Simplified Bible (simplified.bible)
The complete Simplified Bible, a simplified English version of the Holy Bible.
Usage terms: https://simplified.bible/about/#quoting

Genesis 1:1 At the start, God made the sky and the earth.
Genesis 1:2 The earth had no shape and was empty; darkness covered the deep water. And God's Spirit was moving over the water.
Genesis 1:3 God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
Genesis 1:4 God saw the light was good and separated the light from the darkness.
Genesis 1:5 God named the light Day and the dark Night. The evening and morning made up the first day.
Genesis 1:6 God said, "Let there be a space between the waters to separate water from water."
Genesis 1:7 God created the sky and separated the water below the sky from the water above it: and it happened.
Genesis 1:8 God named the sky Heaven. The evening came, then the morning, and that was the second day.
Genesis 1:9 God said, "Let the water under the sky come together in one area, so the dry ground can show," and that happened.
Genesis 1:10 God named the dry land Earth and the collected waters Seas, and God saw it was good.
Genesis 1:11 And God said, let the earth grow grass, plants that make seeds, and trees that make fruit with seeds inside, each kind of plant and tree having its own type of seed, on the earth. And it happened.
Genesis 1:12 The earth produced grass, plants with seeds of their own kind, and trees with fruit containing seeds, each according to its kind. God saw it was good.
Genesis 1:13 The evening and the morning made the third day.
Genesis 1:14 God said, "Let there be lights in the sky to separate the day from the night; and let them serve as signs to mark seasons, days, and years."
Genesis 1:15 Let them be lights in the sky to shine on the earth, and it happened.
Genesis 1:16 God made two big lights; the bigger one to shine during the day, and the smaller one to shine at night. He also made the stars.
Genesis 1:17 God placed them in the sky to shine light on the earth.
Genesis 1:18 To control the day and night, and to separate light from darkness: and God saw it was good.
Genesis 1:19 The evening and the morning made the fourth day.
Genesis 1:20 God said, "Let the water be full of living things that move, and let birds fly above the earth across the sky."
Genesis 1:21 God made big whales and all kinds of animals that move in the water, which the water produced in large numbers, and all kinds of birds with wings. And God saw that it was good.
Genesis 1:22 God blessed them and said, "Have many children, grow in number, fill the sea with life, and let birds increase on the land."
Genesis 1:23 The evening came and then the morning, and that was the fifth day.
Genesis 1:24 God said, "Let the earth produce living creatures of each kind: livestock, crawling things, and wild animals of each kind." And that's what happened.
Genesis 1:25 God created the wild animals, each according to its kind, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the creatures that crawl on the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.
Genesis 1:26 God said, "Let's make humans to look like us and be like us. They will rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, all the earth, and every crawling animal on the earth."
Genesis 1:27 God made humans to look like himself; he made them male and female.
Genesis 1:28 God blessed them and said to them, "Have many children, fill the earth, and control it. Rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, and every creature that moves on the earth."
Genesis 1:29 God said, "Look, I have given you every plant with seeds on the earth and all the trees with fruit with seeds. They will be your food."
Genesis 1:30 God has given every plant for food to all animals on the earth, every bird in the sky, and everything that crawls on the ground with life in it. And that's what happened.
Genesis 1:31 God saw everything He made and it was very good. The evening and morning were the sixth day.

Genesis 2:1 So the sky and the earth were completed, and everything in them.
Genesis 2:2 On the seventh day, God finished the work he had done; he rested on the seventh day from all his work.
Genesis 2:3 God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on that day he rested from all his work of creation.
Genesis 2:4 This lists the times of the sky and the land when they were made, on the day that God created the land and the sky.
Genesis 2:5 Before any plants were in the ground and before any herbs had grown, because God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no one to work the soil.
Genesis 2:6 A mist rose from the earth and watered all the ground.
Genesis 2:7 God made man from the dirt of the ground, breathed life into his nose, and man became alive.
Genesis 2:8 God made a garden in the east part of Eden; and there he placed the man he had created.
Genesis 2:9 God made every beautiful tree with good fruit grow from the ground, as well as the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of knowing good and evil.
Genesis 2:10 A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden; from there it split into four smaller rivers.
Genesis 2:11 The first river is called Pison; it flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
Genesis 2:12 The gold in that land is good; it has bdellium and onyx stones.
Genesis 2:13 The second river's name is Gihon, which flows around the entire land of Ethiopia.
Genesis 2:14 The third river's name is Hiddekel, which flows to the east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
Genesis 2:15 God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and watch over it.
Genesis 2:16 God told the man, "You can eat from any tree in the garden."
Genesis 2:17 Do not eat from the tree that gives knowledge of good and bad, because if you do, you will certainly die.
Genesis 2:18 God said, it's not good for the man to be alone; I will make a suitable helper for him.
Genesis 2:19 From the earth, God made all animals of the land and all birds of the sky; He brought them to Adam to see what he would name them; and whatever Adam named each living thing, that became its name.
Genesis 2:20 Adam named all the animals and birds, but he did not find a suitable helper for himself.
Genesis 2:21 God made Adam fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of Adam's ribs and then closed up the place with flesh.
Genesis 2:22 God used the rib taken from the man to make a woman and brought her to the man.
Genesis 2:23 Adam said, "This one is part of my bones and body. She will be called Woman because she came from Man."
Genesis 2:24 A man will leave his father and mother and join his wife, and they will become one body.
Genesis 2:25 The man and his wife were both naked and were not embarrassed.

Genesis 3:1 The snake was smarter than all the wild animals God made. It said to the woman, "Really, did God say you can't eat from any tree in the garden?"
Genesis 3:2 The woman told the snake, "We can eat the fruit from the trees in the garden."
Genesis 3:3 God has said you must not eat the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden, and you must not touch it, or you will die.
Genesis 3:4 The snake said to the woman, "You will not really die."
Genesis 3:5 God knows that when you eat it, your eyes will open, and you will be like gods, understanding what is good and what is bad.
Genesis 3:6 When the woman saw the tree had good fruit, looked nice, and could make one smart, she took some fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.
Genesis 3:7 Both of their eyes were opened, and they realized they were naked; so they stitched fig leaves together to make coverings for themselves.
Genesis 3:8 They heard God's voice in the garden when the day was cool, and Adam and his wife hid from God among the garden's trees.
Genesis 3:9 God called to Adam and asked, "Where are you?"
Genesis 3:10 He said, "I heard your voice in the garden, and I was scared because I was naked, so I hid."
Genesis 3:11 He asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat from the tree I told you not to eat from?"
Genesis 3:12 The man said, "The woman you put here with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it."
Genesis 3:13 God asked the woman, "What have you done?" The woman answered, "The snake tricked me, and I ate."
Genesis 3:14 God said to the snake, "Because you did this, you are cursed more than all animals, and more than any creature of the field. You will crawl on your belly and eat dust all the days of your life."
Genesis 3:15 I will cause hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers. It will crush your head, and you will strike its heel.
Genesis 3:16 God said to the woman, "I will greatly increase your sadness and your pregnancies; with pain you will give birth to children; you will want your husband, and he will have authority over you."
Genesis 3:17 God said to Adam, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree I told you not to eat from, the ground is cursed because of you. You will have to work hard and suffer all your life to get food from it.
Genesis 3:18 It will also grow thorns and thistles for you; and you will eat the plants of the field.
Genesis 3:19 You will work hard to get food until you die and return to the ground, because you were made from dust, and you will return to dust.
Genesis 3:20 Adam named his wife Eve because she was the mother of all who are alive.
Genesis 3:21 God made clothes from animal skins for Adam and his wife, and dressed them.
Genesis 3:22 God said, "Look, the man has become like one of us in knowing good and evil. Now, so that he does not reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, eat, and live forever:
Genesis 3:23 So God sent him out of the Garden of Eden to work the soil from which he was made.
Genesis 3:24 God sent the man away and put Cherubim to the east of the Eden garden, with a flaming sword that moved in all directions, to guard the path to the tree of life.

Genesis 4:1 Adam was intimate with his wife Eve; she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain, saying, "I have had a son with God's help."
Genesis 4:2 She also gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel took care of sheep, while Cain worked the soil.
Genesis 4:3 After some time, Cain gave some of his crops as an offering to God.
Genesis 4:4 Abel also gave the best of his sheep and their fat. And God respected Abel and his gift.
Genesis 4:5 God did not accept Cain and his offering. Cain became very angry, and his face showed it.
Genesis 4:6 God asked Cain, "Why are you angry? And why do you look upset?"
Genesis 4:7 If you do good, won't you be accepted? But if you don't do good, sin is waiting to enter. It desires to control you, but you must rule over it.
Genesis 4:8 Cain spoke to his brother Abel, and while they were in the field, Cain attacked Abel and killed him.
Genesis 4:9 God asked Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" Cain replied, "I don't know. Am I supposed to look after my brother?"
Genesis 4:10 He asked, "What have you done? Your brother's blood calls out to me from the ground."
Genesis 4:11 You are now cursed from the ground, which opened up to take your brother's blood from your hands.
Genesis 4:12 When you farm the land, it will no longer give you its best crops; you will be a wanderer and a runaway on the earth.
Genesis 4:13 Cain said to God, "My punishment is too much for me to handle."
Genesis 4:14 Look, you have forced me to leave the land today; I will be hidden from you and I will wander the earth; anyone who finds me will kill me.
Genesis 4:15 God said to him, "So, if anyone kills Cain, they will be punished seven times more." And God put a mark on Cain to prevent anyone who found him from killing him.
Genesis 4:16 Cain left God's presence and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Genesis 4:17 Cain was intimate with his wife; she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Then he built a city and named it Enoch, after his son.
Genesis 4:18 Enoch had a son named Irad. Irad had a son named Mehujael. Mehujael had a son named Methusael. Methusael had a son named Lamech.
Genesis 4:19 Lamech married two women: one named Adah and the other named Zillah.
Genesis 4:20 Adah gave birth to Jabal: he became the ancestor of those who live in tents and keep livestock.
Genesis 4:21 His brother's name was Jubal; he was the first musician who played the harp and flute.
Genesis 4:22 Zillah also had Tubalcain, a teacher of all metalworkers in brass and iron, and Tubalcain's sister was Naamah.
Genesis 4:23 Lamech told his wives, Adah and Zillah, "Listen to me; you, Lamech's wives, hear what I say: I have killed a man because he wounded me, and a young man because he hurt me."
Genesis 4:24 If God punishes someone seven times for hurting Cain, then for hurting Lamech, God will punish seventy-seven times.
Genesis 4:25 Adam was close with his wife again, and she had a son named Seth. She said, "God has given me another child to replace Abel, who Cain killed."
Genesis 4:26 Seth also had a son, and he named him Enos. This is when people began to pray to God.

Genesis 5:1 This book lists Adam's descendants. On the day God made humans, he made them to look like himself.
Genesis 5:2 God created them male and female; he blessed them and named them Human when they were created.
Genesis 5:3 Adam lived 130 years, had a son who looked like him, and named him Seth.
Genesis 5:4 Adam lived 800 years after the birth of Seth, and he had other sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:5 Adam lived for 930 years, and then he died.
Genesis 5:6 Seth lived 105 years and had a son named Enos.
Genesis 5:7 After Seth had Enos, he lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:8 Seth lived 912 years, and then he died.
Genesis 5:9 Enos was ninety years old when he became the father of Cainan.
Genesis 5:10 After Enos had his son Cainan, he lived 815 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:11 Enos lived for 905 years; then he died.
Genesis 5:12 Cainan was seventy years old when he became the father of Mahalaleel.
Genesis 5:13 Cainan lived 840 years after he had Mahalaleel, and had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:14 Cainan lived for 910 years, and then he died.
Genesis 5:15 Mahalaleel was sixty-five years old when he became the father of Jared.
Genesis 5:16 After Mahalaleel had Jared, he lived 830 years and had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:17 Mahalaleel lived for 895 years; then he died.
Genesis 5:18 Jared lived 162 years and then had a son named Enoch.
Genesis 5:19 After Jared had Enoch, he lived for 800 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:20 Jared lived 962 years, and then he died.
Genesis 5:21 Enoch was 65 years old when he became the father of Methuselah.
Genesis 5:22 Enoch lived closely with God for 300 years after Methuselah was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:23 Enoch lived for 365 years.
Genesis 5:24 Enoch lived close to God, and then he disappeared because God took him away.
Genesis 5:25 Methuselah lived 187 years and had a son named Lamech.
Genesis 5:26 After Methuselah became the father of Lamech, he lived 782 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:27 Methuselah lived 969 years, then he died.
Genesis 5:28 Lamech lived 182 years and had a son.
Genesis 5:29 He named him Noah, saying, "He will bring us comfort from our hard work and the pain of our hands caused by the ground that God has cursed."
Genesis 5:30 After Lamech had Noah, he lived for 595 more years and had other sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:31 Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.
Genesis 5:32 Noah was 500 years old when he had his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

Genesis 6:1 When people started to increase in number on the earth and they had daughters,
Genesis 6:2 God's sons noticed that human women were beautiful, so they married any they wanted.
Genesis 6:3 God said, "My spirit will not always argue with humans because they are mortal; their lifespan will be 120 years."
Genesis 6:4 There were giants on the earth long ago; and even later, when God's sons married human women, and they had children, those children grew up to be strong and famous old-time heroes.
Genesis 6:5 God saw that people were very wicked on earth, and all the thoughts in their hearts were always only evil.
Genesis 6:6 God regretted making humans on the earth, and he felt deeply sad.
Genesis 6:7 God said, I will wipe out humans whom I made from the earth; along with animals, creatures that crawl, and birds of the sky; because I regret that I made them.
Genesis 6:8 Noah found favor with God.
Genesis 6:9 These are Noah's family records: Noah was a fair and blameless man among his people, and he lived close to God.
Genesis 6:10 Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Genesis 6:11 The world was also bad in God's eyes, and it was full of violence.
Genesis 6:12 God saw the earth, and it was spoiled; all living things had ruined their ways on the earth.
Genesis 6:13 God told Noah, "All living things are about to end because of me; the earth is full of violence because of them; and I will destroy them along with the earth."
Genesis 6:14 Build an ark with gopher wood; make rooms inside, and cover it inside and outside with tar.
Genesis 6:15 Make the boat like this: It should be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Genesis 6:16 Make a window for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from the top; put the door of the ark in its side, and make it with lower, second, and third decks.
Genesis 6:17 Look, I will send a flood to cover the earth and destroy every living thing that breathes; everything on earth will die.
Genesis 6:18 I will make my promise to you; you, your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives will go into the boat with you.
Genesis 6:19 Take two of every kind of living creature, one male and one female, onto the ark to keep them alive with you.
Genesis 6:20 Different kinds of birds, farm animals, and every kind of creature that crawls on the ground will come to you two by two to keep them alive.
Genesis 6:21 Take for yourself every kind of food people eat; collect it, and it will be food for you and for them.
Genesis 6:22 Noah did everything God told him to do.

Genesis 7:1 God said to Noah, "You and your family come into the ark because I have seen you are good in this time."
Genesis 7:2 Take seven pairs of every clean animal, a male and its mate, and one pair of every unclean animal, a male and its mate.
Genesis 7:3 Take seven pairs of each kind of bird, both male and female, to save their species on the earth.
Genesis 7:4 In seven days, I will make it rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out every living thing I have created from the earth.
Genesis 7:5 Noah did everything that God told him to do.
Genesis 7:6 Noah was 600 years old when the great flood came upon the earth.
Genesis 7:7 Noah, his sons, his wife, and their wives all went into the boat because of the floodwaters.
Genesis 7:8 About clean animals, animals that are not clean, birds, and everything that crawls on the ground,
Genesis 7:9 Two by two, males and females, went into the ark to Noah, just as God told Noah to do.
Genesis 7:10 Seven days later, the floodwaters covered the earth.
Genesis 7:11 When Noah was 600 years old, on the 17th day of the second month, all the deep springs burst open, and the rain poured from the sky.
Genesis 7:12 It rained on the earth for forty days and nights.
Genesis 7:13 On that exact day, Noah, his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah's wife, and his sons' three wives all went into the ark.
Genesis 7:14 They, and all animals of their own kinds, all livestock of their kinds, all small creatures that crawl on the ground of their kinds, and all birds of their kinds, every type of bird.
Genesis 7:15 They entered the ark with Noah, two by two, from every creature that has the breath of life.
Genesis 7:16 Those who entered, male and female of every living thing, did so as God had ordered; and God closed the door behind them.
Genesis 7:17 The flood lasted forty days on the earth; the waters grew and lifted the boat, raising it above the ground.
Genesis 7:18 The waters rose high and covered the earth; the ark floated on the surface of the water.
Genesis 7:19 The waters grew very high on the earth, and covered all the tall hills under the sky.
Genesis 7:20 The water rose fifteen cubits high, and it covered the mountains.
Genesis 7:21 All living creatures that moved on the earth died, including birds, livestock, wild animals, all small creatures that crawl on the ground, and every person.
Genesis 7:22 Everyone with the breath of life in their nostrils, on dry land, died.
Genesis 7:23 Every creature on earth died—people, livestock, wildlife, and birds. They were all wiped out; only Noah and those with him on the boat survived.
Genesis 7:24 The water covered the earth for one hundred and fifty days.

Genesis 8:1 God remembered Noah, all living creatures, and all the animals with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters went down.
Genesis 8:2 The deep springs and the sky's windows were closed, and the rain from the sky was held back.
Genesis 8:3 The water went back from the earth slowly, and after 150 days, the water level went down.
Genesis 8:4 The ark stopped on the mountains of Ararat on the seventeenth day of the seventh month.
Genesis 8:5 The water went down non-stop until the tenth month; on the first day of that month, mountain peaks appeared.
Genesis 8:6 After forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark he had built.
Genesis 8:7 He sent out a raven, which kept flying until the water dried up from the earth.
Genesis 8:8 He also sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down from the ground.
Genesis 8:9 The dove couldn't find a place to land because the whole earth was covered with water, so she went back to the ark. Then he reached out his hand, took her, and brought her inside the ark.
Genesis 8:10 He waited another seven days; then he sent the dove out of the boat again.
Genesis 8:11 The dove returned to Noah in the evening with a fresh olive leaf in its mouth, so Noah understood that the floodwaters had gone down.
Genesis 8:12 He waited another seven days and sent out the dove, but it did not come back to him again.
Genesis 8:13 In the six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the water had dried from the earth. Noah took off the ark's cover to look, and saw that the ground was dry.
Genesis 8:14 In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day, the earth was dry.
Genesis 8:15 God spoke to Noah, saying,
Genesis 8:16 Leave the ark, you, your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives with you.
Genesis 8:17 Take with you every living creature with you, from every kind of animal, birds, livestock, and every ground creature; so they can have many offspring, and increase in number on the earth.
Genesis 8:18 Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives all went out together.
Genesis 8:19 Every animal, every crawling creature, and every bird, and everything that crawls on the ground, went out of the ark, each according to its kind.
Genesis 8:20 Noah built an altar to God; he took some of every clean animal and every clean bird and gave burnt offerings on the altar.
Genesis 8:21 God liked the pleasant smell; and God promised himself, I will not put a curse on the land anymore because of people; people think of evil things from when they are young; I will not destroy all living things again as I have done.
Genesis 8:22 As long as the earth exists, there will be planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night will never stop.

Genesis 9:1 God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Have many children, increase in number, and fill the earth."
Genesis 9:2 Every land animal, bird in the sky, creature that moves on the ground, and fish in the sea will be afraid of you; they are all given into your control.
Genesis 9:3 All living creatures that move shall be food for you; just as I have given you all plants.
Genesis 9:4 Do not eat meat that still has its life in it, which is its blood.
Genesis 9:5 I will certainly demand an accounting for human lifeblood; from every animal and from each person I will demand it, and I will require it from anyone who takes another person's life.
Genesis 9:6 Anyone who takes a person's life must have their own life taken by others because God made humans in his own image.
Genesis 9:7 You, be fruitful and increase in number; produce a lot on the earth and grow more.
Genesis 9:8 God spoke to Noah and his sons, saying,
Genesis 9:9 I will make my promise with you and your descendants after you.
Genesis 9:10 And with every animal with you, the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals on earth with you; from all that came out of the ark, to every wild animal on earth.
Genesis 9:11 I will make my promise with you, no living things will be wiped out by a flood again, and there will not be another flood to ruin the earth.
Genesis 9:12 God said, "This is the sign of the promise I make between me and you and every living creature with you, for all time to come."
Genesis 9:13 I put my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of an agreement between me and the earth.
Genesis 9:14 When I bring a cloud over the earth, you will see the bow in the cloud.
Genesis 9:15 I will remember my agreement with you and every living being; never again will the waters turn into a flood to destroy all life.
Genesis 9:16 The rainbow will be in the sky, and when I see it, I will remember the forever promise between God and every living being of all kinds on the earth.
Genesis 9:17 God told Noah, "This is the sign of the promise I made with all living things on earth."
Genesis 9:18 Noah's sons who left the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and Ham was Canaan's father.
Genesis 9:19 Noah had three sons, and from them the whole world was populated.
Genesis 9:20 Noah started to farm and planted a vineyard.
Genesis 9:21 He drank the wine, got drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent.
Genesis 9:22 Ham, Canaan's father, saw his father naked and told his two brothers outside.
Genesis 9:23 Shem and Japheth took a cloth, put it on their shoulders, walked backward, and covered their father's bare body. Their faces were turned away, and they did not see their father unclothed.
Genesis 9:24 Noah woke up from drinking wine and realized what his youngest son had done to him.
Genesis 9:25 He said, "Cursed is Canaan; he will be the lowest servant to his brothers."
Genesis 9:26 He said, "God bless Shem; Canaan will be his servant."
Genesis 9:27 God will make Japheth's land and people grow, and he will live with Shem's family; Canaan will serve him.
Genesis 9:28 Noah lived for 350 years after the flood.
Genesis 9:29 Noah lived for 950 years, then he died.

Genesis 10:1 Here are the family lines of Noah's sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. These sons had their own children after the flood.
Genesis 10:2 Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Genesis 10:3 Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Genesis 10:4 Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Genesis 10:5 These people spread out over the islands and lands of non-Jewish peoples; each group by its language and family, in their own countries.
Genesis 10:6 Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan.
Genesis 10:7 Cush had several sons: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabtechah. Raamah had two sons: Sheba and Dedan.
Genesis 10:8 Cush had a son named Nimrod, who became a powerful leader on Earth.
Genesis 10:9 He was a strong hunter before God; that's why people say, "Like Nimrod, a strong hunter before God."
Genesis 10:10 His kingdom started with Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in Shinar's land.
Genesis 10:11 From that country, Asshur left and built Nineveh, the city Rehoboth, and Calah.
Genesis 10:12 Resen is between Nineveh and Calah; it is a great city.
Genesis 10:13 Mizraim had sons named Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
Genesis 10:14 And the people of Pathrus, Casluh, (from whom the Philistines came), and Caphtor.
Genesis 10:15 Canaan had Sidon, his oldest son, and Heth.
Genesis 10:16 And the Jebusite, the Amorite, and the Girgasite,
Genesis 10:17 The Hivite, the Arkite, and the Sinite,
Genesis 10:18 The Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites were there too. Later, the Canaanite families spread out.
Genesis 10:19 The Canaanites' land started at Sidon, went to Gerar and then to Gaza; from there it reached all the way to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboim, and Lasha.
Genesis 10:20 These are Ham's sons, grouped by their families, languages, lands, and nations.
Genesis 10:21 Shem, the ancestor of all Eber's descendants and Japheth's older brother, also had children.
Genesis 10:22 Shem's children were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
Genesis 10:23 Aram's children were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Genesis 10:24 Arphaxad had a son named Salah, and Salah had a son named Eber.
Genesis 10:25 Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg, because the earth was divided during his life. His brother was named Joktan.
Genesis 10:26 Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
Genesis 10:27 Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah
Genesis 10:28 And Obal, Abimael, and Sheba,
Genesis 10:29 Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab were all Joktan's sons.
Genesis 10:30 Their home was from Mesha to Sephar, a mountain in the east.
Genesis 10:31 These are Shem's sons, by their families, languages, in their countries, and by their nations.
Genesis 10:32 These are the families of Noah's sons, grouped by their descendants, within their countries. And from these families the nations were spread out over the earth after the flood.

Genesis 11:1 Everyone on earth spoke the same language.
Genesis 11:2 As they traveled from the east, they found a flat area in the land of Shinar and they settled there.
Genesis 11:3 They said to each other, "Come, let's make bricks and bake them well." They used bricks instead of stones and tar for mortar.
Genesis 11:4 They said, "Come on, let's build a city and a tower that reaches to the sky, so we can make a name for ourselves and not be spread out over the whole world."
Genesis 11:5 God came down to see the city and the tower that people were building.
Genesis 11:6 God said, "Look, the people are united, and they all speak the same language; this is what they have started to do: now they can do anything they think of."
Genesis 11:7 Let's go down and mix up their language, so they can't understand each other.
Genesis 11:8 So God spread them out from there all over the earth, and they stopped building the city.
Genesis 11:9 So they named it Babel, because there God mixed up everyone's language and scattered them all over the world.

Genesis 11:15 Salah lived for 403 years after Eber's birth and had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 11:16 Eber lived 34 years and then became the father of Peleg.
Genesis 11:17 Eber lived for 430 years after the birth of Peleg and had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 11:18 Peleg was thirty years old when he became the father of Reu.
Genesis 11:19 Peleg lived for 209 years after Reu was born, and he had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 11:20 Reu was thirty-two when he became the father of Serug.
Genesis 11:21 Reu lived for 207 years after Serug was born, and he had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 11:22 Serug was thirty years old when he had Nahor.
Genesis 11:23 Serug lived for 200 years after Nahor was born and had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 11:24 Nahor lived 29 years and had a son named Terah.
Genesis 11:25 After Nahor had his son Terah, he lived 119 more years and had more sons and daughters.
Genesis 11:26 Terah lived for 70 years and had three sons: Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Genesis 11:27 Here are the descendants of Terah: Terah was the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran was the father of Lot.
Genesis 11:28 Haran died before his father Terah in his birthplace, in Ur of the Chaldees.
Genesis 11:29 Abram and Nahor married. Abram's wife was Sarai, and Nahor's wife was Milcah, Haran's daughter, who was also Iscah's father.
Genesis 11:30 Sarai could not have children; she had none.
Genesis 11:31 Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, Abram's wife; and they left Ur of the Chaldees to go to Canaan. But they stopped at Haran and lived there.
Genesis 11:32 Terah lived for 205 years and then he died in Haran.

Genesis 12:1 God told Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives, and your father's home, and go to a land I will show you."
Genesis 12:2 I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great; and you will be a blessing.
Genesis 12:3 I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; through you, all the earth's families will be blessed.
Genesis 12:4 Abram left as God had told him, and Lot went too; Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
Genesis 12:5 Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, everything they owned, and all the people they had in Haran. They set out for Canaan and arrived there.
Genesis 12:6 Abram traveled through the land to Sichem, to the Moreh plain. The Canaanite people were living in the land at that time.
Genesis 12:7 God showed himself to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your children." There Abram built an altar to God who had appeared to him.

Genesis 12:9 Abram traveled on, heading south.

Genesis 12:12 So when the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me but let you live.
Genesis 12:13 Please say you are my sister, so that things will go well for me because of you, and my life will be spared thanks to you.
Genesis 12:14 When Abram arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians saw that his wife was very beautiful.
Genesis 12:15 Pharaoh's leaders saw her, praised her to Pharaoh, and she was brought into Pharaoh's house.
Genesis 12:16 He treated Abram well because of her, giving him sheep, cows, donkeys, male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
Genesis 12:17 God punished Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
Genesis 12:18 Pharaoh called Abram and asked, "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?"
Genesis 12:19 Why did you say, 'She is my sister'? I could have married her because of that. Now, here is your wife, take her and leave.
Genesis 12:20 The king told his men about him, and they made him leave with his wife and all his belongings.

Genesis 14:1 During the time when Amraphel ruled Shinar, Arioch ruled Ellasar, Chedorlaomer ruled Elam, and Tidal ruled many nations;

Genesis 14:3 All these were united in the Siddim Valley, now the Salt Sea.
Genesis 14:4 For twelve years they obeyed Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year, they rebelled.
Genesis 14:5 In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him defeated the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzims in Ham, and the Emins in Shaveh Kiriathaim.
Genesis 14:6 The Horites lived in Seir mountain, reaching to Elparan near the desert.
Genesis 14:7 They went back and came to Enmishpat, known as Kadesh, and defeated all the land of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who lived in Hazezontamar.
Genesis 14:8 The kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela (also called Zoar) went out and fought a battle with them in the Siddim Valley.
Genesis 14:9 With Chedorlaomer, the king of Elam, Tidal, the king of nations, Amraphel, the king of Shinar, and Arioch, the king of Ellasar; four kings joined together against five.
Genesis 14:10 The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ran away, but they fell into the pits. Those who were left ran to the hills.
Genesis 14:11 They took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah, all their food, and left.
Genesis 14:12 They captured Lot, Abram's nephew, who lived in Sodom, along with his possessions, and left.
Genesis 14:13 Someone who had escaped came and told Abram, the Hebrew, who was living near Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and Aner. These men were allies of Abram.
Genesis 14:14 When Abram learned his brother was captured, he equipped his skilled servants, born in his home, 318 in number, and chased the captors to Dan.
Genesis 14:15 He split his group and, with his servants, attacked at night, defeated them, and chased them to Hobah, north of Damascus.
Genesis 14:16 He took back all the items, and also returned his brother Lot, his items, the women, and the people.
Genesis 14:17 The king of Sodom went to meet him after he came back from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, at the Valley of Shaveh, also called the king's valley.

Genesis 14:19 He blessed him and said, "May Abram be blessed by God Most High, owner of heaven and earth."
Genesis 14:20 May God, the Most High, be blessed, for he has given your enemies over to you. And Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
Genesis 14:21 The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and keep the goods for yourself."
Genesis 14:22 Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand to God, the highest God, the owner of heaven and earth."
Genesis 14:23 I won't take anything from you, not even a thread or a shoestring, so you can't say you made Abram rich.
Genesis 14:24 Keep only what the young men have eaten and the share for the men who joined me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; they should get their share.

Genesis 16:1 Sarai, Abram's wife, had no children. She had a servant from Egypt named Hagar.
Genesis 16:2 Sarai said to Abram, "Look, God has kept me from having children. Please sleep with my servant; maybe I can have children through her." And Abram listened to what Sarai said.
Genesis 16:3 Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar, her Egyptian maid, after Abram lived ten years in Canaan, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife.
Genesis 16:4 He slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When she realized she was pregnant, she looked down on her mistress.
Genesis 16:5 Sarai said to Abram, "I'm blaming you for this: I let you be with my servant, but now she's pregnant, she looks down on me. Let God decide who's right, me or you."
Genesis 16:6 But Abram told Sarai, "Look, your servant is under your control; do what you think is best." And when Sarai was harsh with her, she ran away.
Genesis 16:7 God's messenger met her by a water spring in the desert, near the spring on the road to Shur.
Genesis 16:8 He asked, "Hagar, Sarai's servant, where did you come from and where are you going?" She answered, "I'm running away from my mistress Sarai."
Genesis 16:9 The angel of God told her, "Go back to your mistress and do as she says."
Genesis 16:10 God's messenger said to her, I will greatly increase your descendants so much that they will be too many to count.
Genesis 16:11 The angel of God told her, "Look, you are going to have a baby boy and you will name him Ishmael; because God has heard about your troubles."
Genesis 16:12 He will be a wild person; he will fight against everyone, and everyone will fight against him; he will live near all his family members.
Genesis 16:13 She named God who spoke to her, "You are the God who sees me," because she thought, "I have seen the One who sees me."
Genesis 16:14 So they named the well "The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me." It is located between Kadesh and Bered.
Genesis 16:15 Hagar gave birth to Abram's son, and Abram named the son she had, Ishmael.
Genesis 16:16 Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael for Abram.

Genesis 17:1 When Abram was ninety-nine years old, God came to Abram and said, "I am Almighty God; walk with me and be blameless."
Genesis 17:2 I will create an agreement between us, and I will greatly increase your numbers.
Genesis 17:3 Abram lay face down, and God spoke to him.
Genesis 17:4 I promise to support you, and you will become the father of many nations.
Genesis 17:5 Your name will no longer be Abram, but Abraham, because I have made you a father of many nations.
Genesis 17:6 I will make you very fruitful, and you will become nations, and kings will come from you.
Genesis 17:7 I will make my promise between me and you and your descendants after you, for all time to come, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
Genesis 17:8 I will give you and your descendants the land where you are now just a traveler, all the land of Canaan, to own forever; and I will be their God.
Genesis 17:9 God told Abraham, "You must keep my agreement, you and your descendants for generations to come."
Genesis 17:10 This is my agreement, which you must follow, between me and you and your children after you; Every male among you must be circumcised.
Genesis 17:11 You must cut off the skin of your foreskin as a sign of the agreement between me and you.
Genesis 17:12 Every baby boy who is eight days old must be circumcised, including those born in your family or bought with money from a foreigner—even if they are not your biological children.
Genesis 17:13 Anyone born in your house or bought with your money must be circumcised, and this will be a lasting agreement shown in your body.
Genesis 17:14 If a boy is not circumcised, he will be separated from his people because he has broken my agreement.
Genesis 17:15 God said to Abraham, "Don't call your wife Sarai anymore. Her name is now Sarah."
Genesis 17:16 I will bless her and also give you a son by her. I will truly bless her, and she will become the mother of many nations; kings from many people will come from her.
Genesis 17:17 Abraham fell to the ground, laughed, and thought to himself, "Will a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? And will Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?"
Genesis 17:18 Abraham said to God, "I wish that Ishmael may live under your care!"
Genesis 17:19 God said, "Your wife Sarah will truly have a son for you; and you will name him Isaac. I will make my promise with him as a forever promise, and with his descendants after him."
Genesis 17:20 As for Ishmael, I have listened to you. I have blessed him and will make him very fruitful. He will have many descendants and create twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.
Genesis 17:21 I will make my agreement with Isaac, whom Sarah will give birth to for you at this time next year.
Genesis 17:22 He stopped talking to him, and God left Abraham and went away.
Genesis 17:23 Abraham took his son Ishmael, everyone born in his house, and all the males bought with his money, and on that very day, he circumcised them as God had told him to do.
Genesis 17:24 Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised.
Genesis 17:25 Ishmael was thirteen when he got circumcised.
Genesis 17:26 On that same day, Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.
Genesis 17:27 All the men of his household, those born in his house and those bought with money from foreigners, were circumcised with him.

Genesis 18:1 God appeared to him in the fields of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent during the hottest part of the day.
Genesis 18:2 He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he noticed them, he ran from his tent to greet them and bowed down to the ground.
Genesis 18:3 He said, "My God, if I have now found favor with you, please do not leave your servant."
Genesis 18:4 Please bring some water, wash your feet, and rest under the tree.
Genesis 18:5 I will get some bread to refresh you. Then you can move on since you've stopped by your servant's place. They replied, "Go ahead, just as you've said."
Genesis 18:6 Abraham hurried to the tent to Sarah and said, "Quickly prepare three measures of good flour, knead it, and bake some bread on the fire."
Genesis 18:7 Abraham ran to his cattle, took a young and good calf, and handed it to a servant; and the servant hurried to prepare it.
Genesis 18:8 He brought them butter, milk, and the cooked calf, placed it in front of them, and stood by them under the tree while they ate.
Genesis 18:9 They asked him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" He replied, "Look, she's in the tent."
Genesis 18:10 He said, "I will definitely come back to you when the time comes; and then, Sarah your wife will have a son." And Sarah heard this from the entrance of the tent, which was behind him.
Genesis 18:11 Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah could no longer have children.
Genesis 18:12 So Sarah laughed quietly, thinking, "Now that I am old, can I enjoy life again, with my husband old too?"
Genesis 18:13 God said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Can I really have a child when I am old?'"
Genesis 18:14 Is anything too hard for God? I will come back to you at the set time next year, and Sarah will have a son.
Genesis 18:15 Then Sarah denied it, saying, "I didn't laugh," because she was scared. But he said, "No, you did laugh."
Genesis 18:16 The men got up from there, looked toward Sodom, and Abraham walked with them to help them on their way.
Genesis 18:17 God thought, "Should I keep what I am going to do from Abraham?"
Genesis 18:18 Abraham will surely grow into a great and strong nation, and all the nations on earth will be blessed through him.
Genesis 18:19 I know he will tell his children and family to follow God's way and to do what is right and fair, so God can do for Abraham what He promised.
Genesis 18:20 God said, "Because Sodom and Gomorrah's cry is loud and their sin is very bad."
Genesis 18:21 I will go down now to see if what they have done matches the outcry that has reached me; if it doesn't, I will find out.
Genesis 18:22 The men looked away from there and headed toward Sodom, while Abraham still stood in front of God.
Genesis 18:23 Abraham approached and asked, "Will you also destroy the good people along with the bad?"
Genesis 18:24 Maybe if there are 50 good people in the city, will you still destroy it and not save it for the sake of the 50 good people inside?
Genesis 18:25 You would never do such a thing, to kill the good people along with the bad ones, making the good and bad the same. Surely, the Judge of all the earth will do what is right.
Genesis 18:26 And God said, If I find fifty good people in Sodom, I will save the whole city for them.
Genesis 18:27 Abraham replied, "Look, I've decided to talk to God, even though I am only dust and ashes."
Genesis 18:28 What if five righteous people are missing from the fifty? Will you destroy the whole city for just five? And He said, If I find forty-five, I won't destroy it.
Genesis 18:29 He spoke to him once more, saying, "What if only forty are found there?" And He answered, "I will not do it for the sake of the forty."
Genesis 18:30 He said to him, "Please don't be angry, God, and I will speak: Maybe there will be thirty good people found there." And God replied, "If I find thirty there, I will not destroy it."
Genesis 18:31 He said, "Look, I've decided to talk to God. Maybe there will be twenty good people there." God replied, "If I find twenty good people, I won't destroy it for their sake."
Genesis 18:32 He said, "Please don't be mad, God, and I will say this just one more time: What if ten good people are there?" God replied, "I won't destroy it if I find ten."
Genesis 18:33 After talking with Abraham, God left, and Abraham went back to his place.

Genesis 19:1 Two angels came to Sodom in the evening; Lot was sitting at the entrance of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he got up to greet them and bowed down with his face to the ground.
Genesis 19:2 He said, "Please, come to my house and stay the night. Wash your feet, and you can leave early in the morning." But they answered, "No, we'll stay outside all night."
Genesis 19:3 He insisted they stay with him, so they did and went into his house. He prepared a meal for them, baked bread without yeast, and they ate.
Genesis 19:4 Before they went to bed, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, all men, both old and young, from every part of the city.
Genesis 19:5 They called to Lot and asked, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so we can meet them."
Genesis 19:6 Lot went outside to meet them and closed the door behind him.
Genesis 19:7 Please, my friends, don't do this evil.
Genesis 19:8 Look, I have two daughters who have never been with a man. Let me bring them to you, and you can do what you think is right to them. But don't do anything to these men, because they are under the protection of my roof.
Genesis 19:9 They said, "Move back." Then they said, "This man came to stay here and now he wants to judge us. We'll treat you worse than them." They pushed hard against the man, Lot, and came close to breaking the door.
Genesis 19:10 The men reached out their hand, pulled Lot inside the house with them, and closed the door.
Genesis 19:11 They struck the people at the house entrance with blindness, everyone from least to greatest, so they got tired trying to find the door.
