Genesis 19:13 We will destroy this place because their cries have become very loud and God has sent us to destroy it.
Genesis 19:14 Lot went out and talked to his sons-in-law, who were married to his daughters, and said, "Get up, leave this place; because God will destroy this city." But to his sons-in-law, he seemed like he was joking.
Genesis 19:15 When morning came, the angels hurried Lot, saying, "Get up, take your wife and your two daughters who are with you, or you will be swept away in the city's sin."
Genesis 19:16 As he hesitated, the men took his hand, his wife's hand, and the hands of his two daughters because God was kind to him; they led him out and placed him outside the city.
Genesis 19:17 When they took them outside, he said, "Run for your life; don't look back or stop anywhere in the valley; go to the mountains or you will be swept away."
Genesis 19:18 And Lot said to them, "Oh, please no, sir."
Genesis 19:19 Look, I have found favor with you, and you have shown me great kindness by saving my life. But I can't run to the mountain because some harm might catch me, and I would die.
Genesis 19:20 Look, this city is close enough to run to, and it's small. Please let me run there—it's small, right?—and I will live.
Genesis 19:21 He told him, "Look, I have agreed to your request about this matter too, so I will not destroy the city you've spoken for."
Genesis 19:22 Hurry, go there; because I can't do anything until you arrive there. That's why the city was named Zoar.
Genesis 19:23 The sun had risen over the earth when Lot went into Zoar.
Genesis 19:24 God made sulfur and fire rain down on Sodom and Gomorrah from the sky.
Genesis 19:25 He destroyed those cities, the whole area, everyone living in the cities, and everything growing on the land.
Genesis 19:26 His wife looked back and turned into a salt pillar.
Genesis 19:27 Abraham got up early in the morning to the place where he had stood before God.
Genesis 19:28 He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the land of the plain, saw smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
Genesis 19:29 When God destroyed the plain cities, God thought of Abraham and took Lot out of the destruction as he ruined the cities where Lot lived.
Genesis 19:30 Lot left Zoar and lived in the mountains with his two daughters because he was afraid to live in Zoar, so they stayed in a cave.
Genesis 19:31 The older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there are no men around to be with us in the way that is usual everywhere.
Genesis 19:32 Let's get our father to drink wine and sleep with him to keep our family going.
Genesis 19:33 That night they gave their father wine to drink, and the oldest daughter slept with her father without him noticing when she lay down or when she got up.
Genesis 19:34 The next day, the older sister told the younger, "Look, I slept with our father last night. Let's get him drunk with wine again tonight; then you go and sleep with him, so we can have children from our father."
Genesis 19:35 That night they also gave their father wine to drink, and the younger daughter went and slept with him. He didn't notice when she lay down or when she got up.
Genesis 19:36 Both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
Genesis 19:37 The firstborn had a son and named him Moab; he is the ancestor of the Moabites to this day.
Genesis 19:38 The younger daughter also gave birth to a son and named him Benammi. He is the ancestor of the Ammonites.

Genesis 20:1 Abraham traveled from there to the southern lands and lived between Kadesh and Shur, and stayed in Gerar.
Genesis 20:2 Abraham said about his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelech, the king of Gerar, sent for and took Sarah.
Genesis 20:3 God came to Abimelech in a dream at night and said, "You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is already married."
Genesis 20:4 Abimelech had not been with her, and he said, "God, will you also kill a righteous nation?"
Genesis 20:5 Didn't he tell me, 'She is my sister'? And she also said, 'He is my brother.' I did this with a clear heart and clean hands.
Genesis 20:6 God spoke to him in a dream, saying, "Yes, I know you did this with a pure heart. That's why I kept you from sinning against me and did not let you touch her."
Genesis 20:7 Now, give the man back his wife, because he is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. But if you don't return her, know that you will surely die, you and everyone who belongs to you.
Genesis 20:8 So Abimelech got up early in the morning, called all his workers, and spoke about all these things to them; and the men were very scared.
Genesis 20:9 Then Abimelech called Abraham and asked him, "What have you done to us? How have I wronged you, that you have brought a great sin on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not have been done."
Genesis 20:10 Abimelech asked Abraham, "What did you see that made you do this?"
Genesis 20:11 And Abraham said, "I thought, 'This place does not respect God, and they will kill me to take my wife.'"
Genesis 20:12 She really is my sister, my father's daughter but not my mother's, and she became my wife.
Genesis 20:13 When God made me leave my father's home, I told her, "Please be kind to me, and wherever we go, say 'He is my brother.'"
Genesis 20:14 Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, oxen, male servants, and female servants, and returned his wife Sarah to him.
Genesis 20:15 Abimelech said, "Look, my land is in front of you: live wherever you like."
Genesis 20:16 God said to Sarah, "Look, I have given your brother a thousand silver coins. He will protect you in the eyes of everyone with you and everyone else." This was her correction.
Genesis 20:17 Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, so they could have children.
Genesis 20:18 God had made it so no woman in Abimelech's house could have children because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

Genesis 21:1 God visited Sarah as he promised, and did to Sarah what he had said.
Genesis 21:2 Sarah became pregnant and gave birth to a son for Abraham in his old age, at the exact time God had told him.
Genesis 21:3 Abraham named his son, who Sarah gave birth to, Isaac.
Genesis 21:4 Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God told him to do.
Genesis 21:5 Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Genesis 21:6 Sarah said, "God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears this will laugh with me."
Genesis 21:7 She asked, "Who would have thought to tell Abraham that Sarah could nurse children? Yet I have given him a son in his old age."
Genesis 21:8 The child grew and was weaned. Abraham had a big feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
Genesis 21:9 Sarah saw Hagar the Egyptian's son, whom she had given to Abraham, making fun.
Genesis 21:10 So she told Abraham, "Send away this servant woman and her son, because the son of this servant woman will not share the inheritance with my son, Isaac."
Genesis 21:11 Abraham was very upset about his son.
Genesis 21:12 God told Abraham, "Don't be upset because of the boy and your servant. Listen to everything Sarah tells you, because your descendants will be named through Isaac."
Genesis 21:13 I will also make a nation from the son of the servant woman, because he is your descendant.
Genesis 21:14 Abraham got up early in the morning, took some bread and a water bottle, gave them to Hagar, put them on her shoulder along with the child, and sent her off. Then she left and walked around in the Beersheba desert.
Genesis 21:15 The water in the bottle ran out, and she put the child under a bush.
Genesis 21:16 She went and sat down some distance away, about as far as an arrow can fly, because she said, "I can't watch the boy die." So she sat away from him, cried out loud, and wept.
Genesis 21:17 God heard the boy crying, and God's angel spoke to Hagar from heaven, saying, "What's wrong, Hagar? Don't be afraid, because God has heard the boy crying where he is."
Genesis 21:18 Get up, pick up the boy, and hold him; because I will make him into a great nation.
Genesis 21:19 God made her see, and she noticed a water well; she went, filled her jar with water, and gave the boy a drink.
Genesis 21:20 God was with the boy; he grew up, lived in the desert, and became a bowman.
Genesis 21:21 He lived in the Paran desert, and his mother got him a wife from Egypt.
Genesis 21:22 At that time, Abimelech and Phichol, his army commander, told Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do."
Genesis 21:23 Now promise me here before God that you will not lie to me, or to my son, or to my grandson. Instead, treat me and the land where you have lived as a foreigner with the same kindness I have shown you.
Genesis 21:24 Abraham said, "I will make a promise."
Genesis 21:25 Abraham scolded Abimelech about a water well that Abimelech's workers had forcefully taken.
Genesis 21:26 Abimelech said, "I don't know who did this; you didn't tell me, and I haven't heard about it until today."
Genesis 21:27 Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech; and they both made an agreement.
Genesis 21:28 Abraham placed seven female sheep from the flock apart.
Genesis 21:29 Abimelech asked Abraham, "What do these seven young female sheep you have placed apart mean?"
Genesis 21:30 He said, "Take these seven young female sheep from me so they will be proof that I dug this well."
Genesis 21:31 So he named that place Beersheba, because they both made a promise there.
Genesis 21:32 So they agreed on a promise at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phichol, the leader of his army, went back to the land of the Philistines.
Genesis 21:33 Abraham planted trees in Beersheba and prayed to God, who lives forever.
Genesis 21:34 Abraham lived in the Philistines' land for a long time.

Genesis 22:1 After these events, God tested Abraham. He called, "Abraham," and Abraham answered, "Here I am."
Genesis 22:2 He said, "Now take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. There, offer him as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you."
Genesis 22:3 Abraham got up early in the morning, saddled his donkey, took two of his helpers and his son Isaac, cut wood for the sacrifice, and set out for the place God had mentioned to him.
Genesis 22:4 On the third day, Abraham looked up and saw the place from a distance.
Genesis 22:5 Abraham told his servants, "Stay here with the donkey; the boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we'll come back to you."
Genesis 22:6 Abraham put the wood for the offering on his son Isaac; he carried the fire and a knife, and they walked on together.
Genesis 22:7 Isaac said to his father Abraham, "My father?" Abraham replied, "Yes, my son." Isaac asked, "We have the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?"
Genesis 22:8 Abraham said, "My son, God will find a lamb for a sacrifice." So they both went on together.
Genesis 22:9 They reached the place God had mentioned; Abraham made an altar there, arranged the wood, tied up his son Isaac, and put him on the altar on top of the wood.
Genesis 22:10 Abraham reached out his hand, grabbed the knife to kill his son.
Genesis 22:11 God's messenger called to him from the sky, saying, "Abraham, Abraham!" And he answered, "I'm here."
Genesis 22:12 He said, "Don't hurt the boy or do anything to him, because now I see that you respect God. You didn't refuse to give me your only son."
Genesis 22:13 Abraham looked up and saw a ram with its horns stuck in the bushes behind him. He took the ram and sacrificed it as a burnt offering instead of his son.
Genesis 22:14 Abraham named that place "The Lord Will Provide." People still say today, "On God's mountain, it will be provided."
Genesis 22:15 The angel of God called to Abraham from heaven again.
Genesis 22:16 God said, "I promise by myself that, since you have done this and have not kept back your only son from me:
Genesis 22:17 I will surely bless you and increase your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore; your descendants will conquer their enemies' cities.
Genesis 22:18 Through your descendants, all countries of the world will be blessed because you listened to me.
Genesis 22:19 Abraham went back to his servants, and together they got up and traveled to Beersheba; and Abraham lived in Beersheba.
Genesis 22:20 After these events, someone told Abraham, "Look, Milcah has also given birth to children for your brother Nahor."
Genesis 22:21 Huz was his first child, Buz was his brother, and Kemuel was Aram's father.
Genesis 22:22 Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
Genesis 22:23 Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah gave birth to these eight children for Nahor, Abraham's brother.
Genesis 22:24 His companion Reumah also had children: Tebah, Gaham, Thahash, and Maachah.

Genesis 23:1 Sarah lived to be 127 years old.
Genesis 23:2 Sarah died in Kirjatharba, also called Hebron, in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to mourn and cry for her.
Genesis 23:3 Abraham got up from near his deceased and said to Heth's sons,
Genesis 23:4 I am a foreigner and traveler among you. Please let me have a place to bury my dead, so I can bury them and not see them anymore.
Genesis 23:5 The Heth people replied to Abraham, saying to him,
Genesis 23:6 Listen to us, sir: you are a respected leader among us. Choose any of our burial places to bury your dead. No one here will refuse you their grave for you to bury your dead.
Genesis 23:7 Abraham stood up and bowed to the local people, including the Heth family members.
Genesis 23:8 He talked with them, saying, "If you agree that I should bury my dead away from me, listen to me and ask Ephron son of Zohar for help."
Genesis 23:9 He should sell me the cave of Machpelah that he owns, located at the edge of his field. I will pay its full price so it can be my burial site among you.
Genesis 23:10 Ephron lived with the Heth people and in front of them, and all who entered his city's gate, Ephron the Hittite replied to Abraham, saying,
Genesis 23:11 No, my lord, listen to me: I give you the field and the cave in it; I give it to you in front of my people's sons; bury your dead.
Genesis 23:12 Abraham bowed down to the local people.
Genesis 23:13 He spoke to Ephron with the people of the land listening, saying, "But if you will give it, please listen to me: I will pay you money for the field. Accept it from me, so I can bury my dead there."
Genesis 23:14 Ephron replied to Abraham, saying to him,
Genesis 23:15 Sir, please listen to me: the land costs four hundred silver coins; what difference does that make between us? Go ahead and bury your dead.
Genesis 23:16 Abraham listened to Ephron and paid him the 400 silver coins he had mentioned in front of the Heth's sons, which was the usual money used in trade.
Genesis 23:17 Ephron's field in Machpelah, near Mamre, including the field, the cave in it, and all the trees around its edges, was secured.
Genesis 23:18 To Abraham as his own land, seen by the Heth people, in front of everyone at his city gate.
Genesis 23:19 After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave at Machpelah field near Mamre, which is Hebron in Canaan.
Genesis 23:20 The field and the cave in it were guaranteed to Abraham as a burial place by the Heth sons.

Genesis 24:1 Abraham was old and advanced in years, and God had blessed Abraham in every way.
Genesis 24:2 Abraham said to his oldest servant, who managed everything he owned, "Please put your hand under my thigh."
Genesis 24:3 I will make you promise by God, the God of heaven and earth, not to get a wife for my son from the Canaanite girls where I live.
Genesis 24:4 Go to my homeland and my family, and find a wife for my son Isaac.
Genesis 24:5 The servant asked, "What if the woman doesn't want to come back with me to this place? Should I take your son back to the country you came from?"
Genesis 24:6 Abraham told him, "Make sure you don't take my son back there."
Genesis 24:7 God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and my relatives' land, who spoke to me and promised me, saying, 'I will give this land to your descendants,' will send an angel ahead of you, and you will get a wife for my son from there.
Genesis 24:8 If the woman doesn't want to come with you, you are free from my promise. Just don't take my son back there.
Genesis 24:9 The servant placed his hand under his master Abraham's thigh and made a promise to him about this subject.
Genesis 24:10 The servant took ten of his master's camels and left, carrying all his master's wealth. He then set out for Mesopotamia, to Nahor's city.
Genesis 24:11 He made his camels kneel outside the city near a water well when it was evening, the time when women come out to get water.
Genesis 24:12 He said, "God of my master Abraham, please let me be successful today and show kindness to my master Abraham."
Genesis 24:13 Look, I am standing by the water well; and the city men's daughters come out to get water.
Genesis 24:14 Let it happen that the young woman I ask to lower her jar so I can have a drink, and who offers to water my camels too, be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. This is how I will know you have been kind to my master.
Genesis 24:15 Before he finished talking, Rebekah came out. She was born to Bethuel, Milcah's son and Nahor's wife (Abraham's brother), carrying a pitcher on her shoulder.
Genesis 24:16 The young woman was very pretty, had never been with a man, and she went to the well, filled her jar, and came back up.
Genesis 24:17 The servant hurried to her and asked, "Please let me have a little water from your pitcher to drink."
Genesis 24:18 She said, "Drink, sir," and quickly lowered her jar onto her hand to give him a drink.
Genesis 24:19 After she gave him water, she said, "I will also get water for your camels until they finish drinking."
Genesis 24:20 She hurried, poured her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to get more water, and filled it up for all the camels.
Genesis 24:21 The man watched her in silence, wondering if God had made his trip successful.
Genesis 24:22 After the camels finished drinking, the man gave her a gold earring weighing half a shekel and two gold bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels.
Genesis 24:23 He asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there space at your father's house for us to stay?"
Genesis 24:24 She said to him, "I am Bethuel's daughter, Milcah's grandson who gave birth to Nahor's child."
Genesis 24:25 She also told him, "We have plenty of straw and feed, and a place to stay."
Genesis 24:26 The man lowered his head and honored God.
Genesis 24:27 He said, "Praise God of my master Abraham, who has not denied my master his kindness and honesty. While I was on the journey, God guided me to my master's family's home."
Genesis 24:28 The young woman ran and told her mother's family about these things.
Genesis 24:29 Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and Laban hurried out to the man at the well.
Genesis 24:30 When he saw the earring and bracelets on his sister's hands, and heard her saying what the man told her, he went to the man who was standing by the camels near the well.
Genesis 24:31 He said, "Come in, you who are blessed by God; why are you standing outside? I have made the house ready and have space for the camels."
Genesis 24:32 The man entered the house, took off his camels' gear, gave them straw and food, and brought water to wash his own and his companions' feet.
Genesis 24:33 Food was placed in front of him to eat, but he said, "I won't eat until I explain my mission." Then they told him, "Go ahead and speak."
Genesis 24:34 He said, "I am Abraham's servant."
Genesis 24:35 God has blessed my master a lot; he has become very important: and God has given him sheep, cattle, silver, gold, male servants, female servants, camels, and donkeys.
Genesis 24:36 Sarah, my master's wife, had a son for my master when she was old, and he has given him everything he owns.
Genesis 24:37 My master made me promise not to get a wife for his son from the Canaanite women where we live.
Genesis 24:38 Go to my father's house and to my relatives, and find a wife for my son.
Genesis 24:39 And I said to my boss, Maybe the woman won't come with me.
Genesis 24:40 He told me, 'God, whom I follow, will send an angel with you to make your journey successful; and you will find a wife for my son from my relatives and my father's family.'
Genesis 24:41 Then you will be free from my promise when you go to my family; and if they do not give you someone, you will be free from my promise.
Genesis 24:42 I came to the well today and said, "God of my master Abraham, if you will make my journey successful:"
Genesis 24:43 Look, I'm standing by the water well. When a young woman comes to get water, and I ask her for a little drink from her jar,
Genesis 24:44 She said to me, 'Drink, and I will also get water for your camels.' Let her be the one God has chosen for my master's son.
Genesis 24:45 Before I finished thinking to myself, Rebekah came out with a jar on her shoulder. She went down to the well and drew water. Then I asked her, "Please let me have a drink."
Genesis 24:46 She quickly took her jar off her shoulder, said "Drink, and I'll water your camels too." So I drank, and she watered the camels as well.
Genesis 24:47 I asked her, "Who is your father?" She replied, "I am Bethuel's daughter, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah gave birth to for him." Then I put the earring on her face and the bracelets on her hands.
Genesis 24:48 I bowed my head, worshipped God, and blessed God of my master Abraham who guided me correctly to choose my master's brother's daughter for his son.
Genesis 24:49 If you will treat my master with kindness and honesty, tell me. If not, tell me, so I can go either to the right or to the left.
Genesis 24:50 Then Laban and Bethuel replied, "This matter is from God: we cannot say anything bad or good to you."
Genesis 24:51 Look, Rebekah is here; take her and go so she can become the wife of your master's son, as God has said.
Genesis 24:52 When Abraham's servant heard what they said, he bowed down to the ground to worship God.
Genesis 24:53 The servant took out silver and gold jewelry and clothes, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave valuable gifts to her brother and her mother.
Genesis 24:54 They ate and drank, he and the men with him, and stayed all night; they got up in the morning, and he said, Let me go to my master.
Genesis 24:55 Her brother and mother said, "Let the girl stay with us for a few days, at least ten; then she can go."
Genesis 24:56 He said to them, "Don't stop me, since God has made my journey successful; let me go so I can return to my master."
Genesis 24:57 We will ask the young woman what she thinks.
Genesis 24:58 They called Rebekah and asked her, "Will you go with this man?" She said, "I will go."
Genesis 24:59 They sent off their sister Rebekah, her nurse, Abraham's servant, and his men.
Genesis 24:60 They blessed Rebekah and said to her, "You are our sister. May you be the mother of many millions and may your descendants conquer the lands of their enemies."
Genesis 24:61 Rebekah and her maids got up, they rode on the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah and left.
Genesis 24:62 Isaac returned from near the well Lahairoi; he was living in the southern land.
Genesis 24:63 Isaac went out to think in the field in the evening; when he looked up, he saw camels approaching.
Genesis 24:64 Rebekah looked up, and when she saw Isaac, she got down from the camel.
Genesis 24:65 She had asked the servant, "Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?" The servant replied, "It's my boss." So she took a veil and covered herself.
Genesis 24:66 The servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Genesis 24:67 Isaac took Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent, married her, and loved her. Isaac felt better after his mother died.

Genesis 25:1 Abraham married another woman, and her name was Keturah.
Genesis 25:2 She gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah for him.
Genesis 25:3 Jokshan had Sheba and Dedan as sons. Dedan's sons were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
Genesis 25:4 Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abidah, and Eldaah. All these were Keturah's children.
Genesis 25:5 Abraham gave everything he owned to Isaac.
Genesis 25:6 Abraham gave presents to his other sons, whose mother was a concubine, and sent them away from his son Isaac to the east land while he was still alive.
Genesis 25:7 Abraham lived 175 years.
Genesis 25:8 Then Abraham passed away and died at an old age, as an old man who lived a long life, and he joined his ancestors.
Genesis 25:9 Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, buried him in the Machpelah cave, in Ephron the Hittite's field near Mamre.
Genesis 25:10 Abraham bought the field from the Heth sons; there, Abraham and his wife Sarah were buried.
Genesis 25:11 After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac, who lived near Lahairoi well.
Genesis 25:12 Here are the descendants of Ishmael, Abraham's son, born to Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's servant, by Abraham:
Genesis 25:13 These are the names of Ishmael's sons, listed by their names, in order of their birth: Ishmael's first son is Nebajoth, then Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam.
Genesis 25:14 Mishma, Dumah, and Massa,
Genesis 25:15 Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
Genesis 25:16 These are Ishmael's sons, with their names, by their towns and fortresses; twelve leaders for their tribes.
Genesis 25:17 Ishmael lived 137 years. Then he died and joined his ancestors.
Genesis 25:18 They lived from Havilah to Shur, near Egypt on the way to Assyria; and he died with all his brothers around.
Genesis 25:19 These are the descendants of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham was the father of Isaac.
Genesis 25:20 Isaac was 40 when he married Rebekah, who was the daughter of Bethuel from Syria and the sister of Laban, also from Syria.
Genesis 25:21 Isaac prayed to God for his wife because she could not have children, and God answered his prayer, so his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
Genesis 25:22 The babies inside her were fighting, and she wondered, "Why is this happening to me?" So she went to ask God for answers.
Genesis 25:23 God said to her, "Two nations are in your womb, and two different groups of people will come from you; one group will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger."
Genesis 25:24 When the time came for her to give birth, she had twins in her belly.
Genesis 25:25 The first baby was born red and covered with hair like a coat, and they named him Esau.
Genesis 25:26 After that, his brother came out, grabbing Esau's heel, and they named him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when they were born.
Genesis 25:27 The boys grew up: Esau became a skilled hunter, loving the outdoors; Jacob was a quiet man, staying among the tents.
Genesis 25:28 Isaac loved Esau because he ate Esau's wild game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
Genesis 25:29 Jacob cooked stew, and Esau returned from the field, feeling weak.
Genesis 25:30 Esau said to Jacob, "Please give me some of that red stew because I am very tired." That is why he was also called Edom.
Genesis 25:31 Jacob said, Sell me your birthright today.
Genesis 25:32 Esau said, "Look, I'm about to die; what good is my birthright to me?"
Genesis 25:33 Jacob said, "Promise me today"; so he promised to him, and he sold his right as the firstborn to Jacob.
Genesis 25:34 Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; Esau ate, drank, got up, and left, showing he cared little for his birthright.

Genesis 26:1 There was not enough food in the country, in addition to the earlier food shortage during Abraham's time. Isaac went to see Abimelech, the king of the Philistines, in Gerar.
Genesis 26:2 God appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; live in the land I will tell you about."
Genesis 26:3 Stay in this land, and I will be with you and bless you. I will give all these countries to you and your descendants, and I will keep the promise I made to your father Abraham.
Genesis 26:4 I will make your children as many as the stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands; through your descendants, all the world's nations will be blessed.
Genesis 26:5 Abraham listened to me and followed my orders, commands, rules, and laws.
Genesis 26:6 Isaac lived in Gerar.
Genesis 26:7 The local people asked him about his wife; he said, "She is my sister," because he was afraid to say, "She is my wife." He thought they might kill him because of Rebekah, as she was very beautiful.
Genesis 26:8 When he had been there a long time, King Abimelech of the Philistines looked out a window and saw Isaac being affectionate with his wife Rebekah.
Genesis 26:9 Abimelech called Isaac and said, "She is really your wife; why did you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac answered, "I thought I might be killed because of her."
Genesis 26:10 Abimelech asked, "What have you done to us? Someone could easily have slept with your wife, and you would have made us guilty."
Genesis 26:11 Abimelech told everyone, "Anyone who harms this man or his wife will definitely be killed."
Genesis 26:12 Then Isaac planted crops in that land, and in that same year, he got a hundred times more than he planted, and God blessed him.
Genesis 26:13 The man became very successful and continued to prosper until he was extremely wealthy.
Genesis 26:14 He owned many sheep, cattle, and had many workers: the Philistines were jealous of him.
Genesis 26:15 All the wells that his father's servants had dug during Abraham's time, the Philistines had blocked them and filled them with dirt.
Genesis 26:16 Abimelech said to Isaac, "Leave us; you are much stronger than we are."
Genesis 26:17 Isaac left that place and set up his tent in the Gerar valley and lived there.
Genesis 26:18 Isaac reopened the water wells that were dug in his father Abraham's time, because the Philistines had filled them after Abraham died. He named them what his father had named them.
Genesis 26:19 Isaac's workers dug in the valley and found a well with flowing water.
Genesis 26:20 The herders from Gerar fought with Isaac's herders, saying, "The water is ours!" So, he named the well Esek because they argued with him.
Genesis 26:21 They dug another well, and people also fought over it; so he named it Sitnah.
Genesis 26:22 He moved from there, dug another well, and no one fought over it. He named it Rehoboth, saying, "Now God has given us space, and we will grow in this land."
Genesis 26:23 He left that place and went to Beersheba.
Genesis 26:24 That night, God appeared to him and said, "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and give you many descendants to honor my servant Abraham."
Genesis 26:25 He built an altar there, called on God's name, set up his tent, and Isaac's servants dug a well.
Genesis 26:26 Abimelech from Gerar, his friend Ahuzzath, and Phichol, his army's leader, went to him.
Genesis 26:27 Isaac asked them, "Why do you come to me if you hate me and have made me leave you?"
Genesis 26:28 They said, "We clearly saw that God was with you, so we thought, let's make a promise between us and you, and let's agree together."
Genesis 26:29 Please do us no harm, as we have not harmed you and have only treated you well, sending you off peacefully. You are now blessed by God.
Genesis 26:30 He prepared a meal for them, and they ate and drank.
Genesis 26:31 They got up early in the morning, made promises to each other, and then Isaac sent them away, and they left him peacefully.
Genesis 26:32 That same day, Isaac's workers came and told him about the well they had dug, and said to him, "We have found water."
Genesis 26:33 He named it Shebah, so the city is called Beersheba to this day.
Genesis 26:34 Esau was forty when he married Judith, Beeri the Hittite's daughter, and Bashemath, Elon the Hittite's daughter.
Genesis 26:35 They made Isaac and Rebekah very unhappy.

Genesis 27:1 When Isaac got old and could no longer see well, he called for his oldest son Esau and said, "My son." Esau said to him, "Here I am."
Genesis 27:2 He said, "Look, I am old and don't know when I will die."
Genesis 27:3 Please take your weapons, your arrows, and your bow, go to the fields, and get me some deer meat.
Genesis 27:4 Prepare tasty food for me, the kind I like, and bring it to me so I can eat and then bless you before I die.
Genesis 27:5 Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to his son Esau. And Esau went to the field to hunt for deer meat and to bring it back.
Genesis 27:6 Rebekah said to her son Jacob, "Look, I heard your father talking to your brother Esau, saying,
Genesis 27:7 Bring me some deer meat and cook it well so I can eat and give you my blessing before I die.
Genesis 27:8 Now, my son, listen to what I say and do it.
Genesis 27:9 Go to the herd now and bring me two good young goats. I will cook a tasty meal for your father, one he likes.
Genesis 27:10 Bring it to your father to eat, so he can bless you before he dies.
Genesis 27:11 Jacob told his mother Rebekah, "Look, my brother Esau is very hairy, and I have smooth skin."

Genesis 33:15 Esau said, "Can I leave some of my people with you?" But he answered, "Why do that? I just want to be on good terms with you."
Genesis 33:16 So Esau went back to Seir that day.
Genesis 33:17 Jacob traveled to Succoth, built a house for himself, and made shelters for his animals; that's why the place is named Succoth.
Genesis 33:18 Jacob arrived at Shalem, a city near Shechem in Canaan, after traveling from Padanaram and set up his tent outside the city.
Genesis 33:19 He bought a piece of land where he had pitched his tent from Hamor's descendants, the father of Shechem, for a hundred coins.
Genesis 33:20 He built an altar there and named it God of Israel.

Genesis 34:1 Dinah, Leah's daughter whom she had with Jacob, went out to meet the local girls.
Genesis 34:2 When Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite and ruler of the land, saw her, he grabbed her, slept with her, and dishonored her.
Genesis 34:3 He felt a deep connection with Dinah, Jacob's daughter, loved her, and spoke gently to her.
Genesis 34:4 Shechem said to his father Hamor, "Get me this girl to be my wife."
Genesis 34:5 Jacob found out someone had mistreated his daughter Dinah. His sons were out in the fields with the livestock, so Jacob stayed quiet until they returned.
Genesis 34:6 Hamor, Shechem's father, went to talk to Jacob.
Genesis 34:7 Jacob's sons returned from the fields when they heard the news. They felt deeply hurt and very angry because someone did something very foolish in Israel by sleeping with Jacob's daughter, which should never have happened.
Genesis 34:8 Hamor spoke to them, saying, "My son Shechem deeply desires to marry your daughter. Please let her become his wife."
Genesis 34:9 Marry with us, give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves.
Genesis 34:10 You will live with us, and the land will be open to you; live in it, trade in it, and own property in it.
Genesis 34:11 Shechem said to her father and brothers, "I hope you will favor me, and I will give whatever you ask of me."
Genesis 34:12 Ask for any amount of money or gifts for a dowry, and I will pay what you ask; but let me marry the young woman.
Genesis 34:13 Jacob's sons lied to Shechem and his father Hamor when they spoke because Shechem had disgraced their sister Dinah.
Genesis 34:14 They told them, "We can't do this and let our sister marry a man who is not circumcised; that would be shameful for us."
Genesis 34:15 We agree with this condition: if every man among you gets circumcised, like us.
Genesis 34:16 We will let you marry our daughters, and we will marry your daughters, and we will live with you, and we will become one group of people.
Genesis 34:17 But if you won't listen to us and agree to be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and leave.
Genesis 34:18 Hamor and his son Shechem liked what they heard.
Genesis 34:19 The young man did not hesitate to do it because he liked Jacob's daughter, and he was more respectable than everyone in his family.
Genesis 34:20 Hamor and his son Shechem went to the entrance of their city and talked with the men of their city, saying,
Genesis 34:21 These men are friendly towards us; so let them live in the land and do business there; the land is big enough for them; we can marry their daughters, and they can marry ours.
Genesis 34:22 The men will agree to live with us and become one people only if every male among us gets circumcised just like they are.
Genesis 34:23 Won't their animals, belongings, and all their beasts become ours? Just agree with them, and they will live with us.
Genesis 34:24 Everyone in the city listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every man was circumcised just as they were.
Genesis 34:25 On the third day, when they were in pain, Jacob's two sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, each took a sword, attacked the city with courage, and killed all the men.
Genesis 34:26 They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with their swords, took Dinah from Shechem's house, and left.
Genesis 34:27 Jacob's sons attacked the dead men and looted the city because those men had dishonored their sister.
Genesis 34:28 They took their sheep, oxen, donkeys, and everything in the city and fields.
Genesis 34:29 They captured all their riches, children, and wives, and took everything in the house.
Genesis 34:30 Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have caused me problems, making me look bad to the people here, the Canaanites and Perizzites. We are few in number; they will unite against me, attack, and wipe out me and my family."
Genesis 34:31 They asked, "Should he treat our sister like a prostitute?"

Genesis 35:1 God told Jacob, "Get up and go to Bethel to live. There, build an altar to God who showed Himself to you when you were running away from your brother Esau."
Genesis 35:2 Jacob told his family and everyone with him, "Get rid of the foreign gods you have, make yourselves clean, and change your clothes."
Genesis 35:3 Let's get up and go to Bethel. There I will build an altar to God, who helped me when I was in trouble and who has been with me wherever I have gone.
Genesis 35:4 They gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had and their earrings; Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.
Genesis 35:5 They traveled, and God's terror was on the surrounding cities, so they did not chase Jacob's sons.
Genesis 35:6 Jacob arrived at Luz, in Canaan, also known as Bethel, with everyone who was with him.
Genesis 35:7 He made an altar there and named the place Elbethel, because God had shown himself to him as he was running from his brother.
Genesis 35:8 Rebekah's caregiver Deborah died and they buried her under an oak tree near Bethel. They named the place "Oak of Weeping."
Genesis 35:9 God showed Himself to Jacob again after he left Padanaram and blessed him.
Genesis 35:10 God said to him, "Your name is Jacob. Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel will be your name." And he named him Israel.
Genesis 35:11 God told him, "I am God Almighty: have many children and grow into a nation and many nations will come from you, and you will have kings among your descendants."
Genesis 35:12 I will give you and your descendants the land I gave to Abraham and Isaac.
Genesis 35:13 God left him at the place where he had spoken with him.
Genesis 35:14 Jacob put up a stone pillar where he had talked with God. He poured out a drink offering on it, and also poured oil on it.
Genesis 35:15 Jacob named the place where God spoke with him Bethel.
Genesis 35:16 They left Bethel, and were not far from Ephrath when Rachel started to give birth, and it was difficult.
Genesis 35:17 When she was giving birth with difficulty, the midwife told her, "Don't be afraid; you will have another son too."
Genesis 35:18 As she was dying, she named her son Benoni, but his father named him Benjamin.
Genesis 35:19 Rachel died and was buried on the road to Ephrath, now called Bethlehem.
Genesis 35:20 Jacob put up a stone marker on her burial site; this is Rachel's grave marker to this day.
Genesis 35:21 Israel traveled and set up his tent past the Tower of Edar.
Genesis 35:22 When Israel lived in that land, Reuben slept with Bilhah, his father's partner, and Israel found out. Jacob had twelve sons.
Genesis 35:23 Leah's sons: Reuben, Jacob's first son, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
Genesis 35:24 Rachel's sons are Joseph and Benjamin.
Genesis 35:25 Bilhah, Rachel's servant, had two sons: Dan and Naphtali.
Genesis 35:26 Zilpah, Leah's servant, had two sons with Jacob: Gad and Asher. They were born to Jacob in Padanaram.
Genesis 35:27 Jacob went to his father Isaac in Mamre, to the town of Arbah, now called Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had lived.
Genesis 35:28 Isaac lived for 180 years.
Genesis 35:29 Isaac passed away, died, and joined his ancestors, being very old: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

Genesis 36:1 These are the descendants of Esau, also known as Edom.
Genesis 36:2 Esau married Canaanite women: Adah, daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah, granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite through her father Anah.
Genesis 36:3 Bashemath, Ishmael's daughter and Nebajoth's sister.
Genesis 36:4 Adah had Eliphaz for Esau; and Bashemath had Reuel.
Genesis 36:5 Aholibamah had three sons named Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah. These were Esau's sons, born to him in Canaan.
Genesis 36:6 Esau took his wives, sons, daughters, everyone in his house, his livestock, all his animals, and all his belongings, which he had in Canaan, and moved to another place, away from his brother Jacob.
Genesis 36:7 Their wealth was too much for them to live together; the land where they were outsiders could not support them because of their livestock.
Genesis 36:8 Esau lived in the Mount Seir area; Esau is also known as Edom.
Genesis 36:9 These are the descendants of Esau, who was the ancestor of the Edomites in Mount Seir.
Genesis 36:10 These are the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz, son of Adah, Esau's wife, and Reuel, son of Bashemath, Esau's wife.
Genesis 36:11 Eliphaz's sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
Genesis 36:12 Timna was a secondary wife to Eliphaz, Esau's son, and she gave birth to Amalek for Eliphaz. These were the sons of Adah, Esau's wife.
Genesis 36:13 Reuel's sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Bashemath, Esau's wife.
Genesis 36:14 Aholibamah, daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon, was Esau's wife. She had three sons for Esau: Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah.
Genesis 36:15 These were chiefs of Esau's sons: Eliphaz's sons, Esau's first son; Chief Teman, Chief Omar, Chief Zepho, Chief Kenaz.
Genesis 36:16 Chief Korah, Chief Gatam, and Chief Amalek: these are the chiefs from Eliphaz in Edom; these were Adah's sons.
Genesis 36:17 These are the sons of Reuel, Esau's son: Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, Chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs from Reuel in Edom; these are the sons of Bashemath, Esau's wife.
Genesis 36:18 These are the sons of Esau's wife Aholibamah: leaders Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah. These leaders were Aholibamah's sons, who was Anah's daughter and Esau's wife.
Genesis 36:19 These are Esau's sons, who is also known as Edom, and these are their chiefs.
Genesis 36:20 These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who lived in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, and Anah.
Genesis 36:21 Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan were chiefs of the Horites, Seir's descendants in Edom.
Genesis 36:22 Lotan's children were Hori and Hemam; Lotan's sister was Timna.
Genesis 36:23 Shobal's children were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
Genesis 36:24 These are Zibeon's children: Ajah and Anah. Anah is the one who found the mules in the desert while taking care of his father Zibeon's donkeys.
Genesis 36:25 Anah's children were Dishon and his daughter Aholibamah.
Genesis 36:26 These are Dishon's children: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
Genesis 36:27 Ezer's children are Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
Genesis 36:28 Dishan's children are Uz and Aran.
Genesis 36:29 These are the chiefs from the Horites: Chief Lotan, Chief Shobal, Chief Zibeon, Chief Anah.
Genesis 36:30 Chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan: these are the chiefs from the family of Hori, among the chiefs in the land of Seir.
Genesis 36:31 These are the kings who ruled in Edom before any king ruled the Israelites.
Genesis 36:32 Bela, Beor's son, became king in Edom, and his city was called Dinhabah.
Genesis 36:33 Bela died, and Jobab, Zerah's son from Bozrah, became king after him.
Genesis 36:34 Jobab died, and Husham from the land of Temani became king after him.
Genesis 36:35 Husham died, and then Hadad, son of Bedad who defeated Midian in Moab's field, became king. His city was called Avith.
Genesis 36:36 Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah became king after him.
Genesis 36:37 Samlah died, and Saul from Rehoboth near the river became king after him.
Genesis 36:38 Saul died, and Baalhanan, Achbor's son, became king after him.
Genesis 36:39 Baalhanan, Achbor's son, died, and Hadar became king after him. His city was called Pau, and his wife was Mehetabel, Matred's daughter and Mezahab's granddaughter.
Genesis 36:40 Here are the names of the leaders from Esau's family, organized by their groups and places: Leader Timnah, Leader Alvah, Leader Jetheth.
Genesis 36:41 Duke Aholibamah, Duke Elah, Duke Pinon,
Genesis 36:42 Duke Kenaz, Duke Teman, Duke Mibzar,
Genesis 36:43 Chief Magdiel, chief Iram: these are the chiefs of Edom, living in the land they own: he is Esau, the ancestor of the Edomites.

Genesis 37:1 Jacob lived in the land where his father had been a foreigner, in Canaan.
Genesis 37:2 This lists Jacob's family. Seventeen-year-old Joseph was tending sheep with his brothers, the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father's wives. He told his father about the bad things they were doing.
Genesis 37:3 Israel loved Joseph more than his other children because Joseph was born when Israel was already old, and he gave Joseph a colorful coat.
Genesis 37:4 When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than them, they hated him and could not speak kindly to him.
Genesis 37:5 Joseph had a dream and shared it with his brothers, which made them hate him even more.
Genesis 37:6 He said to them, "Please listen to this dream I had."
Genesis 37:7 Look, we were tying up bundles of grain in the field when suddenly my bundle stood up straight. Then your bundles gathered around and bowed to mine.
Genesis 37:8 His brothers asked him, "Will you really rule over us? Will you actually be our boss?" They disliked him even more because of his dreams and what he said.
Genesis 37:9 He had another dream and shared it with his brothers, saying, "Look, I dreamed again; the sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me."
Genesis 37:10 He told his father and brothers, and his father scolded him, saying, "What kind of dream did you have? Will your mother, brothers and I actually come to bow down to you on the ground?"
Genesis 37:11 His brothers were jealous of him, but his father paid attention to what was said.
Genesis 37:12 His brothers went to graze their father's sheep in Shechem.
Genesis 37:13 Israel said to Joseph, "Aren't your brothers pasturing the sheep in Shechem? Come, I'll send you to them." And he replied, "I'm here."
Genesis 37:14 He told him, "Please go and check if your brothers and the flocks are okay; then come back and tell me." So he sent him from the Hebron valley, and he went to Shechem.
Genesis 37:15 A man found him lost in the field and asked, "What are you looking for?"
Genesis 37:16 He said, "I'm looking for my brothers. Please tell me where they are taking care of their sheep."
Genesis 37:17 The man said, "They left this place; I heard them plan to go to Dothan." So Joseph followed his brothers and found them in Dothan.
Genesis 37:18 When they saw him from far away, before he got close to them, they planned together to kill him.
Genesis 37:19 They said to each other, "Look, here comes the dreamer."
Genesis 37:20 Let's go now, kill him, throw him into a pit, and say a wild animal ate him. Then we'll see what happens to his dreams.
Genesis 37:21 Reuben heard them and saved him from their hands, saying, Let's not kill him.
Genesis 37:22 Reuben told them, "Don't kill him. Just throw him into this pit in the desert, but don't hurt him." He planned to save him from them and return him to his father.
Genesis 37:23 When Joseph reached his brothers, they took off his colorful coat that he was wearing.
Genesis 37:24 They grabbed him and threw him into a hole. The hole was empty without any water in it.
Genesis 37:25 They sat down to eat bread, and when they looked up, they saw a group of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead with their camels carrying spices, balm, and myrrh to take to Egypt.
Genesis 37:26 Judah asked his brothers, "What do we gain if we kill our brother and hide his blood?"
Genesis 37:27 Come, let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not hurt him; he is our brother, our own flesh. And his brothers agreed.
Genesis 37:28 Some Midianite traders passed by; they pulled Joseph out of the hole and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty silver coins, and they took Joseph to Egypt.
Genesis 37:29 Reuben went back to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, so he tore his clothes.
Genesis 37:30 He went back to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone; where can I go now?"
Genesis 37:31 They took Joseph's coat, killed a young goat, and dipped the coat in the blood.
Genesis 37:32 They sent the colorful coat and took it to their father, saying, "We found this. See if it's your son's coat or not."
Genesis 37:33 He recognized it and said, "This is my son's coat; a wild animal must have eaten him. Joseph has surely been torn apart."
Genesis 37:34 Jacob tore his clothes, wore rough fabric around his waist, and grieved for his son for many days.
Genesis 37:35 All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he wouldn't be comforted and said, "I will mourn for my son until I die." So he cried for his son.
Genesis 37:36 The Midianites sold him to Potiphar in Egypt, who was an official of the king and the captain of the guard.

Genesis 38:1 At that time, Judah left his brothers and stayed with a man from Adullam named Hirah.
Genesis 38:2 Judah saw a Canaanite man's daughter named Shuah; he married her and slept with her.
Genesis 38:3 She became pregnant, gave birth to a son, and he named him Er.
Genesis 38:4 She became pregnant again and had a son; she named him Onan.
Genesis 38:5 She became pregnant again and had a son. She named him Shelah. She was in Chezib when she gave birth to him.
Genesis 38:6 Judah found a wife for his oldest son Er, whose name was Tamar.
Genesis 38:7 Er, Judah's eldest son, was evil in God's eyes, and God killed him.
Genesis 38:8 Judah said to Onan, "Sleep with your brother's wife, marry her, and have children for your brother."
Genesis 38:9 Onan knew the child would not be his; so when he slept with his brother's wife, he wasted his seed on the ground, to avoid giving a child to his brother.
Genesis 38:10 What he did upset God, so God also took his life.
Genesis 38:11 Judah told Tamar, his daughter-in-law, "Stay a widow at your father's house until my son Shelah grows up." He thought Shelah might die like his brothers. So Tamar went to live in her father's house.
Genesis 38:12 After some time, Judah's wife, the daughter of Shuah, died. Judah felt better and went to see his sheep shearers in Timnath with his friend Hirah, from Adullam.
Genesis 38:13 Someone told Tamar, "Look, your father-in-law is going to Timnath to cut his sheep's wool."
Genesis 38:14 She took off her widow's clothes, covered herself with a veil, wrapped up, and sat down in an open area on the road to Timnath; because she realized that Shelah had grown up and she hadn't been given to him as his wife.
Genesis 38:15 When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute because she had covered her face.
Genesis 38:16 On the road, he turned to her and said, "Please let me sleep with you." (He didn't know she was his daughter-in-law.) And she asked, "What will you give me to sleep with me?"
Genesis 38:17 He said, "I will send you a young goat from the herd." She asked, "Will you give me something to keep until you send it?"
Genesis 38:18 He asked, "What should I give you as a promise?" She replied, "Your seal ring, your arm bands, and your walking stick that you have with you." So he gave them to her, slept with her, and she became pregnant by him.
Genesis 38:19 She got up, left, took off her veil, and dressed in her widow's clothes.
Genesis 38:20 Judah sent the young goat with his friend from Adullam to get his collateral back from the woman, but he could not find her.
Genesis 38:21 He asked the people there, "Where is the prostitute who was out in the open by the road?" But they said, "There is no prostitute here."
Genesis 38:22 He went back to Judah and said, "I can't find her; and the local men said there was no prostitute here."
Genesis 38:23 Judah said, "Let her keep it so we won't be embarrassed. Look, I sent the young goat, but you didn't find her."
Genesis 38:24 Three months later, someone told Judah, "Your daughter-in-law Tamar has acted like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant because of it." Judah said, "Bring her out and let her be burned."
Genesis 38:25 When she was brought out, she sent a message to her father-in-law, saying, "I am pregnant by the man who owns these things." And she asked, "Please, look and see who these belong to—the signet, bracelets, and staff."
Genesis 38:26 Judah recognized them and said, "She has been more right than I, because I did not give her to my son Shelah." He did not sleep with her again.
Genesis 38:27 During her labor, she discovered she was having twins.
Genesis 38:28 When she was giving birth, one baby reached out his hand, and the midwife tied a red string around it, saying, "This one came out first."
Genesis 38:29 As he pulled back his hand, his brother came out. She asked, "How did you come out first?" So he was named Pharez.
Genesis 38:30 Later, his brother came out, the one with the red string on his hand; they named him Zarah.

Genesis 39:1 Joseph was taken to Egypt; Potiphar, an Egyptian officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him there.
Genesis 39:2 God was with Joseph, and he succeeded in everything; he lived in his Egyptian master's house.
Genesis 39:3 His master noticed that God was with him and that God made everything he did successful.
Genesis 39:4 Joseph won his favor and worked for him. He put him in charge of his house and everything he owned was given to him to look after.
Genesis 39:5 From the time he became the manager of the house and everything in it, God blessed the Egyptian's home because of Joseph; everything he owned, both in the home and in the fields, was blessed by God.
Genesis 39:6 He trusted Joseph with everything he had and didn't worry about anything except the food he ate. Joseph was handsome and well-liked.
Genesis 39:7 After some time, his master's wife noticed Joseph and said, "Sleep with me."
Genesis 39:8 But he refused and told his master's wife, "Look, my master doesn't know what I have in the house, and he has entrusted everything he owns to me."
Genesis 39:9 No one in this house is greater than me; he has kept nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How can I then do such a terrible wrong and sin against God?
Genesis 39:10 As she talked to Joseph every day, he did not listen to her or agree to sleep with her or spend time with her.
Genesis 39:11 Around that time, Joseph entered the house to do his work, and none of the men of the house were inside.
Genesis 39:12 She grabbed his clothes and said, "Sleep with me," but he left his clothes in her hand and ran away.
Genesis 39:13 When she saw he had left his clothes with her and ran away,
Genesis 39:14 She called to the men of her house and said to them, "Look, he has brought a Hebrew here to make fun of us. He came to me to sleep with me, but I screamed loudly."
Genesis 39:15 When he heard me raise my voice and cry out, he left his clothes with me and ran away.
Genesis 39:16 She kept his clothing with her until her husband came home.
Genesis 39:17 She said to him, "The Hebrew servant you brought here came to make fun of me."
Genesis 39:18 As I raised my voice and screamed, he left his clothes with me and ran away.
Genesis 39:19 When his master heard what his wife said, "This is how your servant treated me," he became very angry.
Genesis 39:20 Joseph's boss arrested him and put him in the jail where the king's prisoners were kept, and he stayed in the jail.
Genesis 39:21 God was with Joseph, showed him kindness, and made the prison guard like him.
Genesis 39:22 The prison guard put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners; whatever was done there, Joseph did it.
Genesis 39:23 The prison guard did not worry about anything in his care; because God was with Joseph, and God made everything Joseph did successful.

Genesis 40:1 After these events, the Egyptian king's cupbearer and baker upset their king.
Genesis 40:2 The king was very angry with two of his officials, the head of the cupbearers and the head of the bakers.
Genesis 40:3 He put them in jail at the guard captain's house, where Joseph was held.
Genesis 40:4 The guard captain put Joseph in charge of them, and he took care of them. They stayed there for some time.
Genesis 40:5 Both the king's cupbearer and the baker, who were in prison, had a dream on the same night, and each dream had its own meaning.
Genesis 40:6 Joseph came to them in the morning, saw them, and noticed they were sad.
Genesis 40:7 He asked Pharaoh's officials who were with him in his master's prison, "Why do you look so unhappy today?"
Genesis 40:8 They told him, "We had a dream, but no one can explain it." Joseph said to them, "Doesn't God give meanings to dreams? Please share them with me."
Genesis 40:9 The head servant told his dream to Joseph and said, "In my dream, I saw a grapevine in front of me.
Genesis 40:10 The vine had three branches. It looked like it was budding, its flowers bloomed, and its bunches of grapes ripened.
Genesis 40:11 I held Pharaoh's cup and squashed the grapes into it, then I handed the cup to Pharaoh.
Genesis 40:12 Joseph told him, "This is what it means: the three branches represent three days."
Genesis 40:13 In three days, Pharaoh will free you and give you back your job. Then you will serve Pharaoh his drink like you did before when you were his cupbearer.
Genesis 40:14 Please remember me when things go well for you, and be kind to me. Ask Pharaoh to free me from this prison.
Genesis 40:15 I was indeed kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and I have done nothing here to deserve being thrown into a dungeon.
Genesis 40:16 When the head baker saw that the dream reading was good, he told Joseph, "I was also in my dream, and look, I had three white baskets on my head."
Genesis 40:17 In the top basket, there were all kinds of baked goods for the king, and birds ate them from the basket on my head.
Genesis 40:18 Joseph replied, "This is what it means: The three baskets represent three days."
Genesis 40:19 In three days, the king will remove your head and hang you on a tree; the birds will eat your flesh.
Genesis 40:20 On the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, he threw a party for all his workers and honored his main cupbearer and baker in front of them.
Genesis 40:21 He gave the chief butler his job back, and he handed the cup to the Pharaoh.
Genesis 40:22 He executed the chief baker, just as Joseph had explained to them.
Genesis 40:23 The head servant did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.

Genesis 41:1 After two whole years, Pharaoh had a dream: he was standing by the river.
Genesis 41:2 Look, seven healthy and fat cows came out of the river and they ate in a grassy field.
Genesis 41:3 Then seven other skinny and ugly cows came up from the river and stood next to the first cows by the riverbank.
Genesis 41:4 The skinny and ugly cows ate the seven healthy and fat cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.
Genesis 41:5 He slept again and had another dream: seven healthy and full ears of corn grew on one stalk.
Genesis 41:6 Look, seven skinny ears of grain, damaged by the east wind, grew up after them.
Genesis 41:7 The seven skinny heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full heads. Then Pharaoh woke up and realized it was a dream.
Genesis 41:8 In the morning, he was worried, so he called all of Egypt's magicians and wise men. Pharaoh shared his dream with them, but no one could explain it to him.
Genesis 41:9 The head servant spoke to the king and said, "Today, I remember what I did wrong."
Genesis 41:10 The king was angry with his servants and locked me up in the guard captain's house, me and the head baker.
Genesis 41:11 We both had a dream on the same night, me and him; each of our dreams meant something different.
Genesis 41:12 A young Hebrew man, who worked for the guard's commander, was with us. We shared our dreams with him, and he explained what each dream meant for each person.
Genesis 41:13 Just as he explained to us, it happened: he returned me to my job, and he hanged the other man.
Genesis 41:14 Then Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of the prison. He shaved, put on new clothes, and went to Pharaoh.
Genesis 41:15 Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I had a dream and no one can explain it. But I've heard that you can understand and explain dreams."
Genesis 41:16 Joseph said to Pharaoh, "I don't have the power. God will give Pharaoh a peaceful answer."
Genesis 41:17 Pharaoh said to Joseph, "In my dream, I was standing by the river."
Genesis 41:18 Look, seven healthy and good-looking cows came up from the river and grazed in the grassland.
Genesis 41:19 Then seven other cows came up after them, thin, very ugly, and skinny, such as I have never seen in all of Egypt because they were so bad.
Genesis 41:20 The skinny and sickly cows ate up the first seven healthy cows.
Genesis 41:21 After they ate them, you couldn't tell they had eaten; they still looked bad as before. Then I woke up.
Genesis 41:22 I had a dream where seven healthy and full ears of grain grew on a single stalk.
Genesis 41:23 Look, seven thin and dried up ears of grain, damaged by the east wind, grew after the others.
Genesis 41:24 The skinny ears of grain swallowed up the seven healthy ears, and I explained this to the magicians, but no one could tell me what it meant.
Genesis 41:25 Joseph said to Pharaoh, "Pharaoh's dream means the same thing: God has shown Pharaoh what He will do."
Genesis 41:26 The seven good cows are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years: the dream is the same.
Genesis 41:27 The seven skinny and bad-looking cows that followed are seven years, and the seven thin ears of grain ruined by the east wind will be seven years of hunger.
Genesis 41:28 This is what I told Pharaoh: God is showing Pharaoh what he is going to do.
Genesis 41:29 Look, seven years of great abundance will come to the whole land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:30 After those seven good years, seven years of hunger will follow. All the abundance in Egypt will be forgotten, and the hunger will destroy the land.
Genesis 41:31 The abundance will not be noticed in the land because of the coming famine; it will be very severe.
Genesis 41:32 The dream came to Pharaoh two times because God has decided it will happen soon.
Genesis 41:33 So now, Pharaoh should choose a smart and wise man to be in charge of Egypt.
Genesis 41:34 Pharaoh should do this: he should choose leaders for the land and collect one-fifth of Egypt's crops during the seven good years.
Genesis 41:35 Let them collect all the food from the good years that are coming, and store grain under Pharaoh's control, and keep food in the cities.
Genesis 41:36 That food will be kept to supply the land during the seven years of famine that will happen in Egypt, so the land won't be destroyed by the famine.
Genesis 41:37 Pharaoh and all his servants thought the idea was good.
Genesis 41:38 Pharaoh asked his servants, "Can we find anyone like this man who has the Spirit of God in him?"
Genesis 41:39 Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has shown you all this, no one is as smart and wise as you are."
Genesis 41:40 You will be in charge of my house, and all my people will follow your commands; only I will have more power than you because of my throne.
Genesis 41:41 Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Look, I have made you the ruler over all of Egypt."
Genesis 41:42 The king took his ring off his hand, gave it to Joseph, dressed him in fine linen clothes, and put a gold necklace around his neck.
Genesis 41:43 He let him ride in his second chariot, and as he went, people shouted, "Bow down!" He appointed him to rule over all of Egypt.
Genesis 41:44 Pharaoh told Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, and no one in Egypt will do anything without your permission."
Genesis 41:45 Pharaoh named Joseph Zaphnathpaaneah and gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potipherah, the priest of On, as his wife. Joseph traveled all through Egypt.
Genesis 41:46 Joseph was thirty when he appeared before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. He left Pharaoh's presence and traveled all over Egypt.
Genesis 41:47 During the seven good years, the earth produced lots of food.
Genesis 41:48 He collected all the food from the seven years in Egypt and stored it in the cities. He put the food from the fields around each city in that city.
Genesis 41:49 Joseph collected so much grain like the sand of the sea that he stopped keeping track because it was too much to count.
Genesis 41:50 Joseph had two sons before the famine started. Asenath, Potipherah the priest of On's daughter, was their mother.
Genesis 41:51 Joseph named his first son Manasseh because, he said, God has made me forget all my hard work and my family back home.
Genesis 41:52 He named the second one Ephraim, saying, "God has made me fruitful in the land where I suffered."
Genesis 41:53 The seven plentiful years in Egypt came to an end.
Genesis 41:54 The seven years of famine started, just as Joseph had said, and the famine was in every country, but in Egypt, there was still food.
Genesis 41:55 When Egypt was very hungry, the people begged the king for food. The king told the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph; do whatever he tells you."
Genesis 41:56 There was a famine everywhere on earth; Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold food to the Egyptians; and the famine became very severe in Egypt.
Genesis 41:57 People from every country went to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph because the famine was very severe everywhere.

Genesis 42:1 When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he asked his sons, "Why are you just standing around looking at each other?"
Genesis 42:2 He said, "Look, I've heard there's grain in Egypt. Go there and buy some for us, so we can survive and not die."
Genesis 42:3 Joseph's ten brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
Genesis 42:4 Jacob did not send Joseph's brother Benjamin with his other sons, because he feared something bad might happen to him.
Genesis 42:5 The Israelites also came to buy grain because there was a famine in Canaan.
Genesis 42:6 Joseph was the ruler of the land, and he was the one who sold grain to everyone there. When Joseph's brothers arrived, they bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.
Genesis 42:7 Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but he acted like a stranger towards them and spoke harshly to them. He asked them, "Where do you come from?" And they replied, "We come from the land of Canaan to buy food."
Genesis 42:8 Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
Genesis 42:9 Joseph remembered his dreams about them and said to them, "You are spies; you have come to find out about our weak spots."
Genesis 42:10 They said to him, "No, sir, we have come to buy food."
Genesis 42:11 We are all sons of one man; we are honest men, your servants are not spies.
Genesis 42:12 He told them, "No, you have come to see the bareness of the land."
Genesis 42:13 They said, "We are twelve brothers, sons of one man in Canaan. The youngest is with our father today, and one is gone."
Genesis 42:14 Joseph said to them, "This is what I meant when I told you, 'You are spies.'"
Genesis 42:15 This will test you: You will not leave here unless your youngest brother comes.
Genesis 42:16 Choose one of you to go get your brother, and the rest will stay in jail. This will test if you're telling the truth. If not, as sure as Pharaoh lives, you must be spies.
Genesis 42:17 He kept them all together in prison for three days.
Genesis 42:18 On the third day, Joseph said to them, "Do this and you will live, because I respect God."
Genesis 42:19 If you are honest men, have one of your brothers stay tied up in your prison, and the rest of you go bring grain for the hunger in your homes.
Genesis 42:20 Bring your younger brother to me; then I'll know you're telling the truth and you won't die. And they did it.
Genesis 42:21 They said to each other, "We are truly guilty about our brother because we saw his deep distress when he pleaded with us, and we didn't listen. That's why this trouble has come to us."
Genesis 42:22 Reuben replied, "Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen. Now we must answer for his blood."
Genesis 42:23 They did not know that Joseph could understand them, because he was speaking to them through an interpreter.
Genesis 42:24 He turned away from them and cried. Then he went back, talked with them, took Simeon, and tied him up while they watched.
Genesis 42:25 Joseph told them to fill their bags with grain, put each man's money back in his bag, and give them food for their journey. And so he did for them.
Genesis 42:26 They loaded their donkeys with the grain and left that place.
Genesis 42:27 When one of them opened his bag to feed his donkey at the inn, he saw his money; it was right on top inside his bag.
Genesis 42:28 He told his brothers, "My money is back, and look, it's in my bag." Their hearts sank, and they were scared, saying to each other, "What has God done to us?"
Genesis 42:29 They went to their father Jacob in Canaan and told him everything that happened to them, saying,
Genesis 42:30 The man, who rules the land, spoke to us harshly and thought we were spies.
Genesis 42:31 We told him, "We are honest people; we are not spies."
Genesis 42:32 We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is gone, and the youngest is with our father in Canaan today.
Genesis 42:33 The man, the leader of the land, told us, "I will know you are honest men if you leave one of your brothers with me. Take food for your families to survive the hunger and then leave."
Genesis 42:34 Bring your youngest brother to me, so I can know you're not spies but honest men. Then, I will release your brother, and you can trade in the land.
Genesis 42:35 When they emptied their bags, they found that each man's money was in his bag. When they and their father saw the money, they were scared.
Genesis 42:36 Jacob their father said to them, "You have left me without my children: Joseph is gone, Simeon is gone, and now you want to take Benjamin: everything is against me."
Genesis 42:37 Reuben said to his father, "Kill my two sons if I don't bring him back to you. Trust me with him, and I'll return him to you."
Genesis 42:38 He said, "My son won't go with you because his brother is dead, and he's the only one left. If he gets hurt on your journey, you will make me so sad that I will die."

Genesis 47:31 He said, "Promise me." So he promised. And Israel leaned on the top of his bed.

Genesis 48:1 After these events, someone informed Joseph, "Look, your father is ill," so he brought his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, with him.
Genesis 48:2 Someone told Jacob, "Look, your son Joseph is coming to you," and Jacob gathered his strength and sat up in bed.
Genesis 48:3 Jacob told Joseph, "God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in Canaan and blessed me."
Genesis 48:4 He told me, 'Look, I will make you have many children and increase your numbers. I will turn you into a large group of people, and I will give this land to your descendants after you to own forever.'
Genesis 48:5 Your two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, born in Egypt before I arrived, are now mine just like Reuben and Simeon.
Genesis 48:6 Your children born after them will belong to you and take their brothers' family name in the inheritance.
Genesis 48:7 When I was returning from Padan, Rachel died near me in Canaan before we reached Ephrath, and I buried her on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
Genesis 48:8 Israel saw Joseph's sons and asked, "Who are they?"
Genesis 48:9 Joseph told his father, "These are my sons, whom God has given to me here." Then he said, "Please bring them to me, so I can bless them."
Genesis 48:10 Israel's eyes were weak from old age, and he could not see well. He brought them close, kissed them, and hugged them.
Genesis 48:11 Israel said to Joseph, I never expected to see you again, but now, God has let me see your children too.
Genesis 48:12 Joseph took them from between his knees and bowed down with his face to the ground.
Genesis 48:13 Joseph took both Ephraim in his right hand to his father's left, and Manasseh in his left hand to his father's right, and brought them close to him.
Genesis 48:14 Israel reached out his right hand and put it on Ephraim's head, the younger one, and his left hand on Manasseh's head, moving his hands purposely because Manasseh was the older.
Genesis 48:15 He blessed Joseph and said, "God, who my ancestors Abraham and Isaac followed, the God who has taken care of me all my life until today,
Genesis 48:16 The angel who saved me from all harm, bless the boys. Let them carry on my name and the names of my ancestors Abraham and Isaac, and let them become a large group on the earth.
Genesis 48:17 When Joseph saw his father put his right hand on Ephraim's head, he was unhappy. He lifted his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
Genesis 48:18 Joseph said to his father, "No, my father, this one is the oldest; place your right hand on his head."
Genesis 48:19 His father said no, and replied, I know, my son, I know. He too will become a group of people and be great. Yet his younger brother will be even greater, and his descendants will form many nations.
Genesis 48:20 On that day, he gave them a blessing, saying, "Israel will use your name to give blessings, praying, 'May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh,'" and he put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.
Genesis 48:21 Israel said to Joseph, "Look, I am dying, but God will be with you and will take you back to your ancestors' land."
Genesis 48:22 I have also given you an extra share beyond your brothers, which I took from the Amorite using my sword and bow.

Genesis 49:1 Jacob called his sons and said, "Come here so I can tell you what will happen to you in the future."
Genesis 49:2 Come together and listen, children of Jacob; pay attention to Israel, your father.
Genesis 49:3 Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength, the first sign of my power, the best in honor, and the best in force.
Genesis 49:4 Like water, you will not succeed; for you slept in your father's bed and soiled it—he climbed onto my bed.
Genesis 49:5 Simeon and Levi are brothers; tools of violence are in their homes.
Genesis 49:6 My soul, do not join their secrets; do not be part of their group, my respect. In their anger, they killed a person, and in their stubbornness, they destroyed a wall.
Genesis 49:7 Their anger is cursed because it was strong; their rage is cursed because it was harsh. I will separate them in Jacob and spread them out in Israel.
Genesis 49:8 Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hand will be on your enemies' neck; your father's children will bow down to you.
Genesis 49:9 Judah is like a young lion: after hunting, my son, you have rested. He lies down like a lion, and like a mighty lion; who dares to wake him?
Genesis 49:10 Judah will always have a ruler, and a leader will come from his descendants, until Shiloh comes; and the people will follow him.
Genesis 49:11 He tied his young donkey to the grapevine, and his colt to the best vine; he washed his clothes in wine, and his robes in grape juice.
Genesis 49:12 His eyes will look red from wine, and his teeth will be white from milk.
Genesis 49:13 Zebulun will live by the sea port; he will be a safe place for ships, and his land will reach to Sidon.
Genesis 49:14 Issachar is a strong donkey lying down between two loads.
Genesis 49:15 He saw that rest was good and the land beautiful; he bent his shoulder to work and became a laborer who pays taxes.
Genesis 49:16 Dan will judge his people like one of the Israelite tribes.
Genesis 49:17 Dan will be like a snake on the road, a viper on the path, that bites the horse's heels, making its rider fall off.
Genesis 49:18 I have waited for your salvation, God.
Genesis 49:19 Gad will be attacked by a group, but in the end, he will win.
Genesis 49:20 From Asher, his food will be rich, and he will provide fine foods fit for a king.
Genesis 49:21 Naphtali is a free deer; he speaks beautiful words.
Genesis 49:22 Joseph is like a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine near a spring, whose branches climb over the wall.
Genesis 49:23 The archers hurt him badly, shot at him, and hated him.
Genesis 49:24 His bow stayed strong, and his arms got strong by the mighty God of Jacob; from there comes the shepherd, the rock of Israel.
Genesis 49:25 God, your father's God, will help you; the Almighty will bless you with heaven's blessings, the deep's riches, and the fruitfulness of breast and womb.
Genesis 49:26 Your father's blessings are greater than those of my ancestors, reaching to the farthest everlasting hills. They will rest on Joseph's head and on the forehead of the one set apart from his brothers.
Genesis 49:27 Benjamin will hunt like a wolf: in the morning he will eat the prey, and at night he will share the loot.
Genesis 49:28 These are the twelve tribes of Israel: their father spoke to each of them and gave them his blessing.
Genesis 49:29 He gave them instructions, saying, "I will soon join my ancestors: bury me beside my fathers in the cave in Ephron the Hittite's field."
Genesis 49:30 In the cave in Machpelah field, in front of Mamre in Canaan, Abraham bought it with the field from Ephron the Hittite to own as a burial place.
Genesis 49:31 They buried Abraham and his wife Sarah there; they also buried Isaac and his wife Rebekah there; and I buried Leah there.
Genesis 49:32 The buying of the field and the cave in it was from the Heth people.
Genesis 49:33 After Jacob finished giving instructions to his sons, he pulled his legs up onto the bed, passed away, and joined his ancestors.

Genesis 50:1 Joseph laid his face on his father's face, cried over him, and kissed him.
Genesis 50:2 Joseph told his doctors to prepare his father's body, and the doctors did so for Israel.
Genesis 50:3 He was prepared for forty days, as is the custom for the embalmed, and the Egyptians grieved for him seventy days.
Genesis 50:4 After his mourning time ended, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh's officials and said, "If you think well of me, please tell Pharaoh."
Genesis 50:5 My father asked me to promise, saying, "Look, I am dying; bury me in the grave I made for myself in Canaan." So please let me go and bury my father, and then I will come back.
Genesis 50:6 Pharaoh said, "Go and bury your father, just as he made you promise."
Genesis 50:7 Joseph went to bury his father, and all of Pharaoh's servants, the leaders of his household, and the elders of Egypt went with him.
