Genesis 50:8 Everyone from Joseph's family, his brothers, and their father's family went, but they left their young children, sheep, and cattle in Goshen.
Genesis 50:9 Chariots and horsemen went with him, forming a large group.
Genesis 50:10 They reached Atad's threshing floor, across the Jordan River, where they grieved deeply with loud crying; and he mourned his father for seven days.
Genesis 50:11 When the local people, the Canaanites, saw the sadness at Atad's threshing floor, they said, "This is deep sorrow for the Egyptians." That's why they named the place Abelmizraim, which is across the Jordan.
Genesis 50:12 His sons did as he told them to.
Genesis 50:13 His sons took him to Canaan and buried him in Machpelah cave, in the field that Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite, near Mamre.
Genesis 50:14 Joseph went back to Egypt with his brothers and everyone who joined him to bury his father, after they buried his father.
Genesis 50:15 When Joseph's brothers saw that their father had died, they said, "Joseph might hate us and will surely pay us back for all the bad things we did to him."
Genesis 50:16 They sent someone to tell Joseph, "Before your father died, he told us to say,
Genesis 50:17 Tell Joseph, please forgive your brothers' wrongdoing and sin, because they hurt you. And now, please forgive the wrong that God your father's servants have done. Joseph cried when they talked to him.
Genesis 50:18 His brothers also went and bowed down in front of him, saying, "Look, we are your servants."
Genesis 50:19 Joseph said to them, "Don't be afraid. Am I in God's place?"
Genesis 50:20 You planned to do me harm, but God turned it into good, to achieve what we see today: to save many lives.
Genesis 50:21 So do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your children. He reassured them and spoke gently to them.
Genesis 50:22 Joseph lived in Egypt with his family and he lived to be 110 years old.
Genesis 50:23 Joseph saw his great-grandchildren through Ephraim, and Machir's children, Manasseh's descendants, were raised on Joseph's lap.
Genesis 50:24 Joseph told his brothers, "I am about to die, but God will come to you and take you from this land to the land promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."
Genesis 50:25 Joseph made the children of Israel promise, saying, "God will definitely come to you, and you must take my bones from here."
Genesis 50:26 Joseph died at the age of 110, and they preserved his body. He was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

Exodus 1:1 Here are the names of the people of Israel who went to Egypt; each one with his family joined Jacob.
Exodus 1:2 Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
Exodus 1:3 Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin.
Exodus 1:4 Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
Exodus 1:5 Everyone born from Jacob totaled seventy people; Joseph was already in Egypt.
Exodus 1:6 Joseph and all his brothers and everyone from that generation died.
Exodus 1:7 The Israelites grew many, became very strong and filled the land.
Exodus 1:8 A new king came to power in Egypt who did not know about Joseph.
Exodus 1:9 He said to his people, "Look, the Israelites are becoming too numerous and powerful for us."
Exodus 1:10 Let's be smart in handling them so they don't increase in number. If there's a war, they might join our enemies, fight us, and then leave this land.
Exodus 1:11 So they put bosses over them to make them suffer with hard work. And they built storage cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses.
Exodus 1:12 The more they hurt them, the more they increased and became strong. And they were upset because of the children of Israel.
Exodus 1:13 The Egyptians forced the Israelites to work very hard.
Exodus 1:14 They made their lives very hard with tough work, using mortar, bricks, and all sorts of field work; every task they forced them to do was done harshly.
Exodus 1:15 The king of Egypt talked to the Hebrew midwives, named Shiphrah and Puah.
Exodus 1:16 He said, "When you help the Hebrew women give birth and see them on the birthing stools; if it's a boy, you must kill him, but if it's a girl, she can live."
Exodus 1:17 The midwives respected God and did not follow the Egyptian king's orders; instead, they kept the baby boys alive.
Exodus 1:18 The king of Egypt called the midwives and asked them, "Why have you done this and let the boy babies live?"
Exodus 1:19 The midwives told the king, "Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women; they are strong and give birth before the midwives arrive."
Exodus 1:20 So God was good to the midwives, and the people grew and became very strong.
Exodus 1:21 Because the midwives respected God, he gave them homes.
Exodus 1:22 Pharaoh ordered all his people, "Throw every newborn boy into the river, but let every girl live."

Exodus 2:1 A man from Levi's family went and married a woman from Levi's family.
Exodus 2:2 The woman became pregnant and had a baby boy. When she saw he was a fine child, she hid him for three months.
Exodus 2:3 When she couldn't hide her baby anymore, she made a basket from reeds, sealed it with tar and pitch, placed her child inside, and set it among the plants by the river's edge.
Exodus 2:4 His sister stood far away, to see what would happen to him.
Exodus 2:5 Pharaoh's daughter went to bathe in the river; her attendants walked beside the river; when she saw the basket in the reeds, she sent her servant to get it.
Exodus 2:6 When she opened it, she saw the baby crying, and she felt sorry for him, saying, "This is one of the Hebrew babies."
Exodus 2:7 His sister asked Pharaoh's daughter, "Should I go and find a Hebrew woman to nurse the baby for you?"
Exodus 2:8 The princess told her, "Go." So the girl went and called the baby's mother.
Exodus 2:9 Pharaoh's daughter told her, "Take this baby and care for him for me, and I will pay you." So, the woman took the baby and cared for him.
Exodus 2:10 The child grew up, and she took him to the Pharaoh's daughter, who adopted him as her son. She named him Moses, saying, "I pulled him out of the water."
Exodus 2:11 In those days, when Moses was older, he went to his people and saw their hard work. He saw an Egyptian hitting a Hebrew, one of his own people.
Exodus 2:12 He looked around, and seeing no one, he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
Exodus 2:13 On the second day he went out, he saw two Hebrew men fighting. He asked the one who was in the wrong, "Why are you hitting your companion?"
Exodus 2:14 He asked, "Who made you our leader and judge? Do you plan to kill me like you killed the Egyptian?" Moses was scared and thought, "Everyone must know about it."
Exodus 2:15 When the king heard about this, he wanted to kill Moses. But Moses ran away from the king and lived in Midian, where he sat down by a well.
Exodus 2:16 The priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water, filling the troughs to water their father's sheep.
Exodus 2:17 The shepherds arrived and chased them off, but Moses got up, helped the women, and gave their sheep water.
Exodus 2:18 When they returned to their father Reuel, he asked, "Why have you come back so early today?"
Exodus 2:19 They said, an Egyptian saved us from the shepherds and also got plenty of water for us, and gave it to the sheep.
Exodus 2:20 He asked his daughters, "Where is he? Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to eat bread with us."
Exodus 2:21 Moses was happy to live with the man and the man gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as his wife.
Exodus 2:22 She gave birth to a son, and he named him Gershom, saying, "I have been a foreigner in a foreign land."
Exodus 2:23 Over time, the king of Egypt died; the Israelites groaned because they were slaves, they cried out, and their cries reached God because of their slavery.
Exodus 2:24 God heard their cries, and God remembered his promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Exodus 2:25 God saw the Israelites and cared for them.

Exodus 3:1 Moses took care of his father-in-law Jethro's sheep, who was the priest of Midian. He took the sheep far into the desert and came to God's mountain, called Horeb.
Exodus 3:2 An angel of God appeared to him in a fire from inside a bush. He saw that though the bush was on fire, it did not burn up.
Exodus 3:3 Moses said, I will go over and look at this amazing thing, why the bush does not burn up.
Exodus 3:4 When God saw that Moses came to look, God called to him from the bush, "Moses, Moses!" And he answered, "I'm here."
Exodus 3:5 He said, "Don't come any closer. Take off your shoes because the place where you are standing is sacred ground."
Exodus 3:6 He also said, "I am your father's God, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." Moses covered his face because he was scared to look at God.
Exodus 3:7 God said, "I have really seen how my people in Egypt are suffering and have heard them cry out because of their harsh bosses; I know their pain."
Exodus 3:8 I have come to save them from the Egyptians and to take them from that land to a good and big land, a land filled with milk and honey; to the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Exodus 3:9 So now, look, I've heard the people of Israel's cries, and I've seen how the Egyptians are harshly treating them.
Exodus 3:10 Come now, and I will send you to Pharaoh so you can lead my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.
Exodus 3:11 Moses said to God, "Who am I to go to Pharaoh and lead the people of Israel out of Egypt?"
Exodus 3:12 He said, "I will certainly be with you; and this will be the sign to you that I sent you: When you lead the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this mountain."
Exodus 3:13 Moses said to God, "Look, when I go to the Israelites and tell them, 'The God of your ancestors has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is his name?' what should I tell them?"
Exodus 3:14 God told Moses, "I AM WHO I AM." Then he said, "Tell the people of Israel, 'I AM has sent me to you.'"
Exodus 3:15 God also told Moses to say to the Israelites, "The God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This is my name forever, and how I am to be remembered for all generations."
Exodus 3:16 Go, bring together Israel's leaders, and tell them, God, the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, has appeared to me. He said, 'I have carefully watched what has happened to you in Egypt.'
Exodus 3:17 I have said I will take you from the suffering in Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to a land filled with milk and honey.
Exodus 3:18 They will listen to you. You and Israel's leaders will go to Egypt's king and say, 'The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us travel three days into the desert to offer sacrifices to our God.'
Exodus 3:19 I am certain that the king of Egypt won't let you go, not even with great force.
Exodus 3:20 I will reach out my hand and strike Egypt with all the amazing things I will do there, and then they will let you go.
Exodus 3:21 I will make the Egyptians kind to you, and when you leave, you won't leave empty-handed.
Exodus 3:22 Every woman will ask her neighbor and any guest in her home for silver and gold jewelry, and clothes. You will dress your sons and daughters in these, taking wealth from the Egyptians.

Exodus 4:1 Moses answered, "But look, they won't believe me or listen to my voice; they'll say, 'God hasn't appeared to you.'"
Exodus 4:2 God asked him, "What do you have in your hand?" He replied, "A staff."
Exodus 4:3 He said, "Throw it on the ground." So he threw it on the ground, and it turned into a snake; then Moses ran away from it.
Exodus 4:4 God said to Moses, "Reach out your hand and grab its tail." So Moses reached out, caught it, and it turned back into a staff in his hand.
Exodus 4:5 So they may believe that the God of their ancestors, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has shown Himself to you.
Exodus 4:6 God also said to him, "Now put your hand inside your shirt." He put his hand inside his shirt, and when he took it out, it was as white with leprosy as snow.
Exodus 4:7 He said, "Put your hand inside your shirt again." So he put his hand back inside his shirt, and when he took it out, it was normal like the rest of his skin.
Exodus 4:8 If people don't believe you or pay attention to the first sign, they will believe the second sign.
Exodus 4:9 If people don't believe these two signs or listen to you, take some river water and pour it on dry ground. Then, the water from the river will turn into blood on the ground.
Exodus 4:10 Moses said to God, "Oh my God, I am not good at speaking, and I haven't been good at speaking even since you started talking to me. I speak slowly and with difficulty."
Exodus 4:11 God asked him, "Who gave humans their mouths? Who makes them unable to talk or hear, see or blind? Isn't it me, God?"
Exodus 4:12 Go now, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what to say.
Exodus 4:13 He said, "Oh my God, please send someone else to do it."
Exodus 4:14 God was angry with Moses and said, "Isn't Aaron the Levite your brother? I know he speaks well. Look, he is coming to meet you, and when he sees you, he will be happy."
Exodus 4:15 You will talk to him, put words in his mouth; I will help both of you speak and teach you what to do.
Exodus 4:16 He will speak to the people for you, and he will be like your mouth, while you will be like God to him.
Exodus 4:17 You will take this staff in your hand to perform miracles.
Exodus 4:18 Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said, "Please let me go back to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive." Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."
Exodus 4:19 God told Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, for all the men who wanted to kill you are dead."
Exodus 4:20 Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and went back to Egypt, carrying God's staff.
Exodus 4:21 God told Moses, "When you go back to Egypt, make sure you do all the miracles in front of Pharaoh that I have given you the power to do. But I will make his heart stubborn so he won't let the people go."
Exodus 4:22 Tell Pharaoh, God says, 'Israel is my child, my firstborn.'
Exodus 4:23 I tell you, let my son go so he can serve me; but if you don't let him go, I will kill your firstborn son.
Exodus 4:24 On the journey, at the overnight place, God met him and wanted to kill him.
Exodus 4:25 Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off her son's foreskin, threw it at his feet, and said, "You are really a husband of blood to me."
Exodus 4:26 So he released him. Then she said, "You are a husband of blood because of the circumcision."
Exodus 4:27 God told Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." So he went and found Moses on God's mountain and kissed him.
Exodus 4:28 Moses told Aaron everything God had said to him and all the miracles God told him to perform.
Exodus 4:29 Moses and Aaron went and brought together all the elders of the Israelites.
Exodus 4:30 Aaron said everything God told Moses and did the miracles for the people to see.
Exodus 4:31 The people believed when they heard that God had come to help the people of Israel and seen their suffering, so they bowed down and worshiped.

Exodus 5:1 Later, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, "God of Israel says, 'Let my people go, so they can celebrate a festival for me in the desert.'"
Exodus 5:2 Pharaoh said, "Who is God, that I should listen to him and let Israel go? I don't know God, and I will not let Israel go."
Exodus 5:3 They said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go on a three day trip into the desert to offer sacrifices to God, so he won't strike us with sickness or the sword."
Exodus 5:4 The king of Egypt asked Moses and Aaron, "Why are you stopping the people from working? Go back to your tasks."
Exodus 5:5 Pharaoh said, "Look, there are now many people in the land, and you let them stop working on their heavy tasks."
Exodus 5:6 On that day, Pharaoh ordered the slave drivers and their bosses, saying,
Exodus 5:7 You will not provide straw to the people for brick-making anymore. Instead, let them get their own straw.
Exodus 5:8 You must give them the same number of bricks they made before; do not give them less. They are lazy, so they beg to worship their God.
Exodus 5:9 Give the men more work to do so they work harder and ignore useless talk.
Exodus 5:10 The people's bosses and their helpers went out and told them, "This is what Pharaoh says: I will not give you straw."
Exodus 5:11 Go, find straw wherever you can, but your work must not be lessened.
Exodus 5:12 The people spread out all over Egypt to collect stubble because they had no straw.
Exodus 5:13 The overseers rushed them, saying, "Finish your work, your daily jobs, just as when you had straw."
Exodus 5:14 The Egyptian leaders beat the Israelite foremen they had appointed and asked, "Why haven't you made as many bricks yesterday and today as before?"
Exodus 5:15 The leaders of the Israelites went to the king and asked, "Why are you treating us, your servants, like this?"
Exodus 5:16 Your servants are not given straw, yet we are told to make bricks. Look, your servants are beaten, but it is your own people's fault.
Exodus 5:17 But he said, "You are lazy, you are lazy; that's why you say, 'Let's go and make sacrifices to God.'"
Exodus 5:18 Go now and work; you will not be given straw, but you must still produce the same number of bricks.
Exodus 5:19 The leaders of the Israelites saw they were in trouble when they were told, "You must not make fewer bricks each day."
Exodus 5:20 They met Moses and Aaron waiting for them as they left Pharaoh.
Exodus 5:21 They told them, "God watch you and decide; because you've made us hated by Pharaoh and his people, giving them a reason to kill us."
Exodus 5:22 Moses went back to God and said, "God, why have you treated these people badly? Why did you send me?"
Exodus 5:23 Since I went to the king to speak for you, he has treated these people badly; you have not rescued your people at all.

Exodus 6:1 Then God told Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh: he will let the people go because of my powerful action, and he will force them to leave his land."
Exodus 6:2 God spoke to Moses and told him, "I am God."
Exodus 6:3 I showed myself to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty, but they did not know me as Jehovah.
Exodus 6:4 I have also made a promise to them to give them the land of Canaan, where they traveled as outsiders.
Exodus 6:5 I have heard the cries of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians enslave; I remember my promise.
Exodus 6:6 Tell the people of Israel, I am God, and I will free you from the Egyptian's heavy work, and I will save you from their slavery, and I will rescue you with a powerful arm and with mighty acts of judgment.
Exodus 6:7 I will make you my people, and I will be your God. You will know that I am your God who frees you from the Egyptians' heavy work.
Exodus 6:8 I will take you to the land that I promised to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and I will give it to you as your inheritance: I am God.
Exodus 6:9 Moses spoke this way to the Israelites, but they didn't listen to him because they were very sad and suffering from harsh slavery.
Exodus 6:10 God spoke to Moses and said,
Exodus 6:11 Go and talk to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and tell him to let the Israelites leave his country.
Exodus 6:12 Moses spoke to God, saying, "Look, the people of Israel haven't listened to me; so how will Pharaoh listen to me, when I speak so poorly?"
Exodus 6:13 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, and gave them instructions for the Israelites and Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.
Exodus 6:14 These are the leaders of their families: Reuben, Israel's first son, had Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the Reuben families.
Exodus 6:15 Simeon's sons were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, whose mother was from Canaan. These are the Simeon families.
Exodus 6:16 These are the names of Levi's sons by generation: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.
Exodus 6:17 Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimi, for each family group.
Exodus 6:18 Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived for 133 years.
Exodus 6:19 Merari's sons were Mahali and Mushi. These were the Levi families by their generations.
Exodus 6:20 Amram married his aunt Jochebed; she gave birth to Aaron and Moses: Amram lived 137 years.
Exodus 6:21 Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
Exodus 6:22 Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri.
Exodus 6:23 Aaron married Elisheba, Amminadab's daughter and Naashon's sister, and they had Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Exodus 6:24 Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the Korahite family groups.
Exodus 6:25 Eleazar, Aaron's son, married one of Putiel's daughters; she gave birth to Phinehas: they are the leaders of the Levite family heads.
Exodus 6:26 These are Aaron and Moses, whom God told, "Lead Israel's people out of Egypt with their groups."
Exodus 6:27 These are the ones who spoke to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to free the people of Israel from Egypt: they are Moses and Aaron.
Exodus 6:28 One day when God spoke to Moses in Egypt,
Exodus 6:29 God spoke to Moses and said, "I am God; tell the Pharaoh, king of Egypt, everything I tell you."
Exodus 6:30 Moses said to God, "Look, I don't speak well, so how will Pharaoh listen to me?"

Exodus 7:1 God said to Moses, "Look, I have made you like a god to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your spokesperson."
Exodus 7:2 You will say everything I tell you, and your brother Aaron will tell the Pharaoh to let the Israelites go from his land.
Exodus 7:3 I will make Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and increase my miracles and amazing acts in Egypt.
Exodus 7:4 But the king of Egypt will not listen to you, so I can use my power against Egypt, to lead my forces and my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt with strong acts of judgment.
Exodus 7:5 The Egyptians will understand that I am God when I reach out my hand over Egypt and take the Israelites out from among them.
Exodus 7:6 Moses and Aaron did what God told them.
Exodus 7:7 Moses was 80 years old, and Aaron was 83 years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
Exodus 7:8 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Exodus 7:9 When the king of Egypt asks you for a miracle, tell Aaron to throw his staff down in front of the king, and it will become a snake.
Exodus 7:10 Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did as God had ordered: Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and his officials, and it turned into a snake.
Exodus 7:11 Then the king of Egypt called for the wise men and the magicians, and they also did the same things using their magic.
Exodus 7:12 Everyone threw down their rods, which turned into snakes, but Aaron's rod ate their rods.
Exodus 7:13 God made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, so he did not listen to them, just as God had said.
Exodus 7:14 God told Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is stubborn; he won't let the people go."
Exodus 7:15 Go to Pharaoh in the morning; he will go to the water; stand by the river until he arrives; and take the staff that turned into a snake in your hand.
Exodus 7:16 Tell him, "God of the Hebrews sent me to you with this message: 'Let my people go so they can worship me in the desert.' But so far, you haven't listened."
Exodus 7:17 God says, "By this you will know that I am God: see, I will hit the water in the river with the staff in my hand, and it will turn to blood."
Exodus 7:18 The fish in the river will die, the river will smell bad, and the Egyptians will hate to drink the river's water.
Exodus 7:19 God spoke to Moses, "Tell Aaron to take his stick and hold out his hand over the waters of Egypt—their rivers, canals, ponds, and all their water pools—so they will turn into blood. There will be blood everywhere in Egypt, even in wooden and stone containers."
Exodus 7:20 Moses and Aaron did as God commanded. Aaron raised the staff and struck the waters in the river, with Pharaoh and his officials watching. All the river water turned to blood.
Exodus 7:21 The fish in the river died; the river smelled bad, and the Egyptians couldn't drink its water; there was blood all over Egypt.
Exodus 7:22 The Egyptian magicians did the same with their magic tricks, but Pharaoh's heart became stubborn and he did not listen to them, just as God had said.
Exodus 7:23 Pharaoh turned, went into his house, and paid no attention to this either.
Exodus 7:24 All the Egyptians dug near the river for drinking water because they couldn't drink the river water.
Exodus 7:25 Seven days passed after God struck the river.

Exodus 8:1 God spoke to Moses, "Go to the Pharaoh and tell him, 'God says, let my people go so they can serve me.'"
Exodus 8:2 If you don't let them go, I will fill your lands with frogs.
Exodus 8:3 The river will create many frogs, which will enter your home, your bedroom, onto your bed, into your servants' houses, onto your people, into your ovens, and into your dough bowls.
Exodus 8:4 Frogs will come upon you, your people, and all your servants.
Exodus 8:5 God told Moses, "Tell Aaron to stretch out his hand with his staff over the streams, rivers, and ponds to make frogs come up onto the land of Egypt."
Exodus 8:6 Aaron reached out his hand over Egypt's waters, and frogs came and spread all over Egypt.
Exodus 8:7 The magicians used their magic to make frogs come all over Egypt.
Exodus 8:8 Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, "Ask God to remove the frogs from me and my people; and I will let the people go so they can sacrifice to God."
Exodus 8:9 Moses said to Pharaoh, "When should I ask God to get rid of the frogs from you, your servants, and your people, and leave them only in the river?"
Exodus 8:10 He said, "Tomorrow." He replied, "Let it be as you say, so you will know there is no one like our God."
Exodus 8:11 The frogs will go away from you, your houses, your servants, and your people; they will only stay in the river.
Exodus 8:12 Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, and Moses called out to God about the frogs he sent to Pharaoh.
Exodus 8:13 God did what Moses said; the frogs died in the houses, towns, and fields.
Exodus 8:14 They piled them up in heaps, and the land smelled bad.
Exodus 8:15 When Pharaoh saw that the trouble stopped, he became stubborn and did not listen to them, just as God had said.
Exodus 8:16 God told Moses, "Tell Aaron to stretch out his staff and hit the dust on the ground, so it will turn into lice all over Egypt."
Exodus 8:17 They did just that; Aaron reached out his hand with his stick and hit the earth's dust, and it turned into lice on people and animals; all the dust in Egypt turned into lice everywhere.
Exodus 8:18 The magicians tried to use their magic to produce lice, but they failed: so lice were on people and animals.
Exodus 8:19 The magicians told Pharaoh, "This is the work of God." But Pharaoh's heart became stubborn, and he did not listen to them, just as God had said.
Exodus 8:20 God told Moses, "Get up early in the morning, stand in front of Pharaoh; see, he will go to the water; and tell him, 'God says, let my people go so they can worship me.'"
Exodus 8:21 If you don't let my people go, I will make swarms of flies come upon you, your servants, your people, and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with flies, as well as the ground they stand on.
Exodus 8:22 On that day, I will separate the land of Goshen, where my people live, so no swarms of flies will be there. This will let you know that I am God everywhere on earth.
Exodus 8:23 I will make a clear separation between my people and your people: tomorrow this sign will happen.
Exodus 8:24 God did this; a terrible swarm of flies filled Pharaoh's house, his servants' houses, and all of Egypt: the flies ruined the land.
Exodus 8:25 Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God in this land."
Exodus 8:26 Moses said, "It's not right to do this; we will offer sacrifices to God that the Egyptians hate. If we do this in front of them, won't they stone us?"
Exodus 8:27 We will travel for three days into the desert and offer sacrifices to God, as he tells us to.
Exodus 8:28 Pharaoh said, "I will let you go so you can offer sacrifices to your God in the desert, but don't go too far. Pray for me."
Exodus 8:29 Moses said, "Look, I will leave you now and ask God to remove the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people tomorrow. But Pharaoh must not trick us again by not letting the people go to worship God."
Exodus 8:30 Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to God.
Exodus 8:31 God did what Moses asked and took away the flies from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people; not a single fly was left.
Exodus 8:32 The king was stubborn again this time, and he didn't let the people go.

Exodus 9:1 Then God told Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'God of the Hebrews says, let my people go so they can worship me.'"
Exodus 9:2 If you refuse to let them go and still hold them,
Exodus 9:3 Look, God's power is on your livestock in the fields—on the horses, donkeys, camels, cows, and sheep. A severe disease will come.
Exodus 9:4 God will separate the livestock of Israel from the livestock of Egypt, and none of Israel's animals will die.
Exodus 9:5 God decided on a specific time and said, "Tomorrow God will do this in the land."
Exodus 9:6 The next day, God did that, and all of Egypt's cattle died, but not one of Israel's cattle died.
Exodus 9:7 Pharaoh checked, and not one of the Israelites' animals had died. But Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, and he did not let the people go.
Exodus 9:8 God told Moses and Aaron, "Grab handfuls of furnace ashes, and have Moses toss them into the air where Pharaoh can see."
Exodus 9:9 It will turn into fine dust over all of Egypt, causing sores that burst into blisters on people and animals everywhere in Egypt.
Exodus 9:10 They took furnace ashes and stood before Pharaoh; Moses threw them into the air, and they caused sores to break out on people and animals.
Exodus 9:11 The magicians couldn't stay in front of Moses because of the sores, as the sores were on the magicians and all the Egyptians.
Exodus 9:12 God made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he didn't listen to them, just as God had told Moses.
Exodus 9:13 God told Moses, "Get up early in the morning, stand in front of Pharaoh, and tell him, 'God, the God of the Hebrews, says, "Let my people go, so they can worship me."'”
Exodus 9:14 I will now send all my diseases to you, your servants, and your people, so you will know there is no one like me in the whole world.
Exodus 9:15 I will now reach out my hand to strike you and your people with disease, and you will be removed from the earth.
Exodus 9:16 I made you strong for this reason: to show my power through you and to spread my name all over the world.
Exodus 9:17 Are you still proud against my people and refuse to let them go?
Exodus 9:18 Look, tomorrow at this time I will make a very terrible hailstorm happen, like none that has been in Egypt since it was founded until now.
Exodus 9:19 Go now and bring in your animals and everything you have in the fields. If any person or animal is left outside and not brought to a safe place, they will be hit by hail and die.
Exodus 9:20 Anyone who respected God's message among Pharaoh's officials brought their servants and animals inside the houses.
Exodus 9:21 The person who ignored God's word left their workers and animals outside.
Exodus 9:22 God told Moses, "Reach out your hand to the sky so that hail falls over all of Egypt—on people, animals, and every plant in the fields."
Exodus 9:23 Moses raised his staff to the sky, and God made thunder and hail, and fire moved along the ground; and God poured down hail on Egypt.
Exodus 9:24 There was hail and fire mixed with the hail, very terrible, like nothing ever seen in Egypt since it became a country.
Exodus 9:25 The hail hit all over Egypt, hurting people and animals outdoors, and it damaged all the plants and broke all the trees in the fields.
Exodus 9:26 In Goshen, where the Israelites lived, there was no hail.
Exodus 9:27 The king sent for Moses and Aaron, and said to them, I did wrong this time: God is right, and I and my people are bad.
Exodus 9:28 Ask God, because it's enough, to stop the powerful thunder and hail; then I'll let you go, and you won't have to stay longer.
Exodus 9:29 Moses said to him, "Once I leave the city, I will raise my hands to God; the thunder will stop and there will be no more hail. This is to show you that the earth belongs to God."
Exodus 9:30 But I know that you and your servants do not yet fear God.
Exodus 9:31 The flax and barley were destroyed because the barley had heads and the flax had buds.
Exodus 9:32 The wheat and the rye were not damaged because they had not yet grown.
Exodus 9:33 Moses left the city, away from Pharaoh, and reached out his hands to God. Then the thunder and hail stopped, and the rain no longer fell on the land.
Exodus 9:34 When the king saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped, he sinned even more and became more stubborn, along with his officials.
Exodus 9:35 Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, and he wouldn't let the Israelites go, just as God had said through Moses.

Exodus 10:1 God said to Moses, "Go to the Pharaoh, because I have made his heart and his servants' hearts stubborn, so I can display my miracles to them."
Exodus 10:2 So you can tell your son and grandson about what I did in Egypt, and the signs I showed them; so you will know that I am God.
Exodus 10:3 Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, "God of the Hebrews asks, 'How long will you not humble yourself before me? Let my people go to serve me.'"
Exodus 10:4 If you don't let my people go, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your land.
Exodus 10:5 They will spread across the land so no one can see the ground. They will eat what's left after the hail and consume every tree that grows in your fields.
Exodus 10:6 They will fill your houses, the houses of your servants, and the houses of all Egyptians in a way your ancestors or their ancestors have never seen before. After saying this, he left Pharaoh's presence.
Exodus 10:7 Pharaoh's officials said to him, "How long will this man trap us? Let the men go to worship their God. Don't you realize that Egypt is ruined?"
Exodus 10:8 Moses and Aaron were taken back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go, worship your God. But who will go?"
Exodus 10:9 Moses said, "We will go with our young and old, our sons and daughters, and our animals; because we have to celebrate a feast for God."
Exodus 10:10 He told them, "May God be with you, like I will let you and your children go. Be careful; danger is ahead of you."
Exodus 10:11 No, only the men can go and worship God, as you asked. Then they were forced to leave Pharaoh's presence.
Exodus 10:12 God told Moses, "Reach out your hand over Egypt to bring locusts, so they can cover the land and eat every plant, including what the hail has spared."
Exodus 10:13 Moses held out his stick over Egypt, and God sent an east wind across the land all day and night; when morning came, the east wind brought locusts.
Exodus 10:14 The locusts covered all of Egypt and settled everywhere. They were terrible; no other locusts like them had ever been seen before, nor would there ever be again.
Exodus 10:15 They spread over the whole earth, making the land dark; they ate every plant and all the fruit the hail had left. There was no green left on the trees or plants in the fields in Egypt.
Exodus 10:16 Then Pharaoh quickly called for Moses and Aaron; he said, "I have sinned against your God and against you."
Exodus 10:17 Please forgive my sin just this time, and ask God to stop this death from happening to me.
Exodus 10:18 He left Pharaoh and prayed to God.
Exodus 10:19 God sent a powerful west wind that blew the locusts away and into the Red Sea; not a single locust was left in Egypt.
Exodus 10:20 God made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, so he wouldn't let the Israelites go.
Exodus 10:21 God told Moses, "Reach out your hand toward the sky so that darkness spreads over Egypt, a darkness that can be touched."
Exodus 10:22 Moses reached out his hand toward the sky, and there was a deep darkness over all of Egypt for three days.
Exodus 10:23 They couldn't see each other, and nobody left their spot for three days; but all the Israelites had light where they lived.
Exodus 10:24 The Pharaoh called Moses and said, "Go and worship God; but leave your sheep and cattle behind. Take your children with you."
Exodus 10:25 And Moses said, You must give us sacrifices and burnt offerings so we can offer them to God.
Exodus 10:26 We will take our animals with us; not a single hoof will be left behind; we need them to worship God; and we don't know what we will need to worship God until we get there.
Exodus 10:27 God made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he refused to let them go.
Exodus 10:28 Pharaoh said to him, "Go away from me, be careful, and don't see me again; because the day you see my face, you will die."
Exodus 10:29 Moses said, "You've spoken well, I won't see you again."

Exodus 11:1 God told Moses, "I will send one more plague on Pharaoh and Egypt. After that, he will let you leave this place. When he lets you go, he will really force you all out."
Exodus 11:2 Tell the people to ask their neighbors, both men and women, for silver and gold jewelry.
Exodus 11:3 God made the Egyptians like the people. Also, Moses was very important in Egypt to Pharaoh's officials and the people.
Exodus 11:4 Moses said, "God says, 'Around midnight, I will go through Egypt.'"
Exodus 11:5 Every first child in Egypt will die, from the Pharaoh's first child on his throne to the servant girl's first child working at the mill; and every first child of the animals too.
Exodus 11:6 A terrible scream will spread across Egypt like never before and will never be heard again.
Exodus 11:7 No dog will bark at any Israelite, person or animal, so you will see that God treats Israel differently from Egypt.
Exodus 11:8 All your servants will come to me and bow down, saying, 'Leave, with all who follow you.' After that, I'll go. And he left Pharaoh, very angry.
Exodus 11:9 God told Moses, Pharaoh won't listen to you; this is so I can do many amazing things in Egypt.
Exodus 11:10 Moses and Aaron did all these miracles in front of Pharaoh, but God made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, so he wouldn't let the Israelites leave his country.

Exodus 12:1 God spoke to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, saying,
Exodus 12:2 This month will be the start of months for you: It will be your first month of the year.
Exodus 12:3 Tell all the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month, each family must choose a lamb for their household.
Exodus 12:4 If the family is too small for a whole lamb, they must share with a nearby neighbor based on the number of people. Everyone should have enough lamb to eat.
Exodus 12:5 Choose a one-year-old male lamb without any defects, from either the sheep or the goats.
Exodus 12:6 You must keep it until the fourteenth day of the month. Then the whole community of Israel will slaughter it at twilight.
Exodus 12:7 They will take some of the blood and put it on the two side posts and above the door frame of the houses where they will eat it.
Exodus 12:8 They will eat the meat that night, cooked over fire, along with bread without yeast and bitter herbs.
Exodus 12:9 Do not eat it raw or boiled in water, but roast it over a fire with its head, legs, and inner parts.
Exodus 12:10 Do not leave any of it until morning; whatever is left until morning, you must burn.
Exodus 12:11 Eat it ready to travel, with belts on, shoes on your feet, and staffs in hand. Eat quickly, it is God's Passover.
Exodus 12:12 Tonight, I will go through Egypt and strike down every firstborn, both people and animals, and I will judge all the gods of Egypt. I am God.
Exodus 12:13 The blood will be a sign on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you. The plague will not touch you to destroy you when I strike Egypt.
Exodus 12:14 Remember this day and celebrate it as a feast to God for all generations; it is a forever feast by God's rule.
Exodus 12:15 Eat bread without yeast for seven days; on the first day, remove all yeast from your homes. Anyone who eats bread with yeast from the first to the seventh day will be separated from Israel.
Exodus 12:16 On the first day, you will have a special gathering, and on the seventh day, another special gathering. You must not do any work on those days, except for preparing food that everyone needs to eat.
Exodus 12:17 You must celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread because on this very day I led your groups out of Egypt. So, you must keep this day as a lasting rule for all time in your generations.
Exodus 12:18 On the fourteenth day of the first month at evening, you must eat bread without yeast until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month.
Exodus 12:19 For seven days, you must not have any yeast in your homes. Anyone who eats anything with yeast will be separated from the community of Israel, whether they are a visitor or born in the country.
Exodus 12:20 You must not eat anything with yeast; in all the places you live, eat bread without yeast.
Exodus 12:21 Moses gathered all the Israelite leaders and said to them, "Pick out and take a lamb for each family, and slaughter it for the Passover."
Exodus 12:22 Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the bowl, and touch the top and both sides of the doorframe with the blood in the bowl. Do not leave your house until morning.
Exodus 12:23 God will go through to hit the Egyptians; and when He sees the blood on the top and sides of the door frame, God will skip the door, and won't let the destroyer enter your homes to hit you.
Exodus 12:24 You must always follow this rule, you and your children.
Exodus 12:25 When you arrive in the land that God will give you, as He promised, you must perform this service.
Exodus 12:26 When your children ask you, "What does this service mean to you?"
Exodus 12:27 You should say, "It is the sacrifice of God's Passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians and saved our houses." And the people bowed their heads and worshiped.
Exodus 12:28 The Israelites left and did what God told Moses and Aaron to do.
Exodus 12:29 At midnight, God struck down every firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's firstborn who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon; and every firstborn of the animals too.
Exodus 12:30 Pharaoh and all his officials and Egyptians got up during the night, and there was loud crying in Egypt because every house had someone who had died.
Exodus 12:31 During the night, he asked Moses and Aaron to come and told them, "Get up, leave my people with all of you and the Israelites, and go worship God, as you wanted."
Exodus 12:32 Take your livestock and your cattle, as you mentioned, and leave; and give me a blessing too.
Exodus 12:33 The Egyptians strongly urged the people to hurry and leave the land because they said, "We are all going to die."
Exodus 12:34 The people took their dough before it rose, their kneading bowls wrapped in their clothes on their shoulders.
Exodus 12:35 The Israelites did what Moses told them; they asked the Egyptians for silver and gold jewelry and clothes.
Exodus 12:36 God made the Egyptians kind to the people, so they borrowed what they needed. And they took valuable things from the Egyptians.
Exodus 12:37 The Israelites traveled from Rameses to Succoth, with about six hundred thousand men walking, not counting children.
Exodus 12:38 A diverse group also went with them, along with flocks, herds, and many cattle.
Exodus 12:39 They made flat bread without yeast from the dough they took from Egypt. It was unleavened because they had to leave Egypt quickly and had no time to wait or prepare food.
Exodus 12:40 The time the Israelites lived in Egypt was 430 years.
Exodus 12:41 On the very day after 430 years, all of God's people left Egypt.
Exodus 12:42 This is a special night to honor God for leading them out of Egypt: this is the night for all Israelites to remember throughout their generations.
Exodus 12:43 God told Moses and Aaron, "This is the rule of the Passover: No outsider may eat it."
Exodus 12:44 If you buy a man as a servant, after you circumcise him, he can eat of it.
Exodus 12:45 A foreigner and a paid worker shall not eat it.
Exodus 12:46 Eat it in one house; do not take any of the meat outside; and do not break any of its bones.
Exodus 12:47 Every group in Israel must celebrate it.
Exodus 12:48 When a foreigner stays with you and wants to celebrate the Passover to God, have all his males circumcised. Then he can join in and celebrate. He will be like someone born in the country. No uncircumcised person may eat the Passover meal.
Exodus 12:49 The same law applies to everyone born at home and to foreigners living with you.
Exodus 12:50 All the Israelites did as God told Moses and Aaron to do.
Exodus 12:51 On that very day, God led the people of Israel out of Egypt, organized by their groups.

Exodus 13:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 13:2 Set apart for me every firstborn, every first child or animal born among the Israelites: it belongs to me.
Exodus 13:3 Moses told the people, "Remember this day when you left Egypt, the place of slavery. God freed you with his powerful hand: do not eat bread with yeast."
Exodus 13:4 Today you left in the month of Abib.
Exodus 13:5 When God brings you to the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which he promised to your ancestors to give you, a land rich with milk and honey, you must do this service in this month.
Exodus 13:6 Eat bread without yeast for seven days, and on the seventh day there will be a celebration for God.
Exodus 13:7 Eat bread without yeast for seven days; no bread with yeast should be with you, nor yeast anywhere in your living areas.
Exodus 13:8 On that day, you will explain to your son, saying, "We do this because of what God did for me when I left Egypt."
Exodus 13:9 This will be a sign on your hand and a reminder on your forehead to keep God's law in your words, because God freed you from Egypt with great power.
Exodus 13:10 You should therefore follow this rule at the right time every year.
Exodus 13:11 When God brings you to the land of the Canaanites, as he promised you and your ancestors, and gives it to you,
Exodus 13:12 You must dedicate to God everything that is the first to come from a mother, and every firstborn male animal you have; these males belong to God.
Exodus 13:13 You must trade a lamb for every firstborn donkey; if you choose not to trade, then you must kill the donkey. You must also trade for every firstborn child.
Exodus 13:14 When your son asks you in the future, "What is this?" you will tell him, "God freed us from Egypt, where we were slaves, with a strong hand."
Exodus 13:15 When Pharaoh almost didn't let us leave, God killed all the firstborn in Egypt, both people and animals. That's why I sacrifice to God all male firstborn livestock, but I save my firstborn sons.
Exodus 13:16 It will be a sign on your hand and a reminder between your eyes because with strong hand, God brought us out of Egypt.
Exodus 13:17 When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them through the Philistine land, even though it was close. God thought, "Maybe the people will change their minds when they see war and go back to Egypt."
Exodus 13:18 God guided the people through the desert toward the Red Sea, and the Israelites left Egypt prepared for battle.
Exodus 13:19 Moses took Joseph's bones with him because Joseph had made the Israelites promise, saying, "God will definitely come to help you, and you must take my bones from here with you."
Exodus 13:20 They traveled from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the border of the wilderness.
Exodus 13:21 God led them during the day with a cloud pillar to show the way; and at night with a fire pillar to give them light, so they could travel day and night.
Exodus 13:22 He did not remove the cloud pillar by day or the fire pillar by night from in front of the people.

Exodus 14:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 14:2 Tell the Israelites to go and camp in front of Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, across from Baalzephon; you should camp by the sea in front of it.
Exodus 14:3 The Pharaoh will think that the Israelites are trapped in the land, with the wilderness closing them in.
Exodus 14:4 I will make Pharaoh's heart stubborn, so he will chase them; and I will gain respect through Pharaoh and his army. Then the Egyptians will understand that I am God. And they did this.
Exodus 14:5 The king of Egypt was told that the people had escaped. Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about the people and said, "Why did we let Israel leave and stop serving us?"
Exodus 14:6 He prepared his chariot and took his followers with him.
Exodus 14:7 He took six hundred select chariots, all of Egypt's chariots, and leaders for each one.
Exodus 14:8 God made the heart of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, stubborn, and he chased the Israelites. But the Israelites left boldly.
Exodus 14:9 The Egyptians chased them with all of Pharaoh's horses, chariots, riders, and army, and caught up to them as they camped by the sea near Pihahiroth, in front of Baalzephon.
Exodus 14:10 When the king of Egypt came close, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians coming after them. They were very scared and called out to God for help.
Exodus 14:11 They asked Moses, "Were there no graves in Egypt? Have you brought us to the desert to die? Why did you do this to us, taking us out of Egypt?"
Exodus 14:12 Didn't we tell you in Egypt to leave us alone so we could serve the Egyptians? It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the desert.
Exodus 14:13 Moses told the people, "Don't be afraid. Stand firm and you will see how God will save you today. You won't ever see the Egyptians you're seeing today again."
Exodus 14:14 God will fight for you; you must be quiet.
Exodus 14:15 God said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to move forward."
Exodus 14:16 Raise your staff and reach out your hand over the sea to split it, so the Israelites can walk on dry land through the sea.
Exodus 14:17 I will make the Egyptians very stubborn, and they will chase after the Israelites. But I will be honored through Pharaoh and his entire army, his chariots, and his horsemen.
Exodus 14:18 The Egyptians will know that I am God when I gain honor through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.
Exodus 14:19 God's angel, who had been leading Israel's camp, moved and went behind them. The cloud pillar also moved from in front of them and stood behind them.
Exodus 14:20 The cloud stood between the Egyptians and the Israelites. It was dark for the Egyptians but at night it lit up for the Israelites. So they did not come close to each other all night.
Exodus 14:21 Moses reached out his hand over the sea; and God made the sea pull back with a strong east wind all night, turned the sea into dry ground, and split the waters apart.
Exodus 14:22 The Israelites walked into the middle of the sea on dry land, with water like walls to their right and left.
Exodus 14:23 The Egyptians chased them and followed them into the middle of the sea with all Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and riders.
Exodus 14:24 During the morning watch, God saw the Egyptian army through the fire pillar and cloud and disturbed the Egyptian army.
Exodus 14:25 They removed their chariot wheels, making them hard to drive, so the Egyptians said, "Let's run away from Israel; God is fighting for them against us."
Exodus 14:26 God told Moses, "Reach out your hand over the sea so the water comes back on the Egyptians, their chariots, and their horsemen."
Exodus 14:27 Moses reached out his hand over the sea, and the sea became strong again at sunrise; the Egyptians ran from it, and God defeated the Egyptians in the sea.
Exodus 14:28 The waters flowed back and covered the chariots, the riders, and all of Pharaoh's army that had followed them into the sea; not even one of them was left.
Exodus 14:29 The Israelites walked on dry ground through the sea, with water like a wall on their right and left.
Exodus 14:30 So God rescued Israel from the Egyptians that day, and Israel saw the dead Egyptians on the seashore.
Exodus 14:31 Israel saw the amazing thing God did to the Egyptians; the people were afraid of God, and they trusted God and his servant Moses.

Exodus 15:1 Moses and the Israelites sang this song to God, saying, "I will sing to God because he has won a great victory: he has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea."
Exodus 15:2 God gives me strength and joy; he saves me. He is my God, and I will make a home for him; he's the God of my ancestors, and I will lift him high.
Exodus 15:3 God is a warrior; God is his name.
Exodus 15:4 God threw Pharaoh's chariots and army into the sea: even his top leaders are drowned in the Red Sea.
Exodus 15:5 The waters covered them; they sank deep down like a stone.
Exodus 15:6 Your right hand, God, is mighty and wonderful; your right hand, God, has crushed the enemy.
Exodus 15:7 In your great excellence, you threw down those who opposed you: you unleashed your anger, which burned them up like dry grass.
Exodus 15:8 With your strong breath, the waters piled up, the flowing waters stood still like a mound, and the sea's depths became solid.
Exodus 15:9 The enemy said, "I will chase, catch up, and share the goods; I will be fully satisfied with them; I will pull out my sword, and my hand will defeat them."
Exodus 15:10 You blew with your wind, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the powerful waters.
Exodus 15:11 Who is like you, God, among the gods? Who is as glorious and holy, awesome in praise, doing amazing things?
Exodus 15:12 You reached out your right hand, the earth swallowed them up.
Exodus 15:13 In your mercy, you have led the people you saved; you have guided them with your strength to your holy home.
Exodus 15:14 People will hear and be scared; sadness will grip those living in Palestine.
Exodus 15:15 The leaders of Edom will be shocked; the strong people of Moab will shake with fear; everyone in Canaan will lose their courage.
Exodus 15:16 They will be very afraid and scared because of your powerful arm; they will be so still like a stone until your people go by, God, until the people you have chosen go by.
Exodus 15:17 You will bring them and plant them on your own mountain, the place you made for yourself to live, God, in the sanctuary you have built with your hands.
Exodus 15:18 God will rule forever and ever.
Exodus 15:19 Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and riders entered the sea, and God made the sea's waters flow back over them; but the Israelites walked on dry ground through the sea.
Exodus 15:20 Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, held a tambourine and all the women followed her, playing tambourines and dancing.
Exodus 15:21 And Miriam replied, "Sing to God, for He has won a great victory; He has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea."
Exodus 15:22 Moses led Israel from the Red Sea into the Shur desert. They traveled for three days without finding water.
Exodus 15:23 When they arrived at Marah, they couldn't drink the water because it was bitter. That's why it was named Marah.
Exodus 15:24 The people complained to Moses, asking, "What will we drink?"
Exodus 15:25 He called out to God, and God showed him a tree. When he threw it into the water, the water became sweet. There he gave them a rule and a law, and there he tested them.
Exodus 15:26 If you listen carefully to God's voice and do what is right to him, obey his commands, and follow all his rules, I will not bring any of these diseases on you that I gave to the Egyptians, because I am God who heals you.
Exodus 15:27 They arrived at Elim, where there were twelve water wells and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the water.

Exodus 16:1 They left Elim, and all the Israelites reached the Sin desert, between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month since leaving Egypt.
Exodus 16:2 The whole group of Israel's people complained against Moses and Aaron in the desert.
Exodus 16:3 The Israelites said to them, "We wish we had died by God's hand in Egypt, where we sat around pots of meat and ate all the bread we wanted. You have led us into this desert to starve us all to death."
Exodus 16:4 God told Moses, "Look, I will make bread fall from the sky for you. Every day the people must go out and collect what they need for that day. This is to test if they will follow my rules or not."
Exodus 16:5 On the sixth day, they will get ready what they have collected; it will be twice as much as they gather each day.
Exodus 16:6 Moses and Aaron told all the Israelites, "In the evening, you will know that God has taken you out of Egypt."
Exodus 16:7 In the morning, you will see God's glory because he has heard your complaints against him: and who are we that you complain against us?
Exodus 16:8 Moses said, "This will happen when God gives you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you need in the morning; because God hears your complaints which you make against him. And who are we? Your complaints are not against us, but against God."
Exodus 16:9 Moses told Aaron, "Tell all the Israelites to come before God, because he has heard your complaints."
Exodus 16:10 As Aaron was talking to all of Israel's people, they looked at the desert and saw God's glory in the cloud.
Exodus 16:11 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 16:12 I have heard the Israelites complaining. Tell them, 'In the evening you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have all the bread you want. Then you will understand that I am God, your God.'
Exodus 16:13 In the evening, quails flew in and spread over the camp; and in the morning, dew was all around the people.
Exodus 16:14 When the dew disappeared, there was a small, round substance on the desert ground, as tiny as frost.
Exodus 16:15 When the Israelites saw it, they asked each other, "What is it?" because they didn't know what it was. Then Moses told them, "This is the food that God has given you to eat."
Exodus 16:16 God has ordered this: Each person should collect as much as they need to eat, one omer per person, based on the number of people in your tent.
Exodus 16:17 The Israelites did this and collected food, some gathering more, others less.
Exodus 16:18 When they measured it with an omer, those who collected a lot had no extra, and those who collected a little had enough. Each person gathered as much as they needed to eat.
Exodus 16:19 Moses said, "Don't let anyone keep any of it until morning."
Exodus 16:20 Even though they did not listen to Moses, some people kept some until morning, and it got worms and smelled bad; and Moses was angry with them.
Exodus 16:21 They collected it every morning, each person as much as they needed; and when the sun got hot, it melted.
Exodus 16:22 On the sixth day, they collected double the bread, two omers per person, and the leaders of the group told Moses about it.
Exodus 16:23 He told them, "This is what God has said, 'Tomorrow is the Sabbath rest, a holy day for God: cook what you want to cook today, and boil what you want to boil; keep any leftovers to eat tomorrow morning.'"
Exodus 16:24 They kept it until morning, as Moses instructed, and it didn't smell bad or have any worms in it.
Exodus 16:25 Moses said, "Eat that today; for today is a Sabbath to God: you will not find it in the field today."
Exodus 16:26 Gather food for six days, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none.
Exodus 16:27 It happened that on the seventh day some people went out to collect food, but they found nothing.
Exodus 16:28 God asked Moses, "How long will you refuse to follow my commands and laws?"
Exodus 16:29 Look, because God has given you the Sabbath, he gives you two days' worth of bread on the sixth day; stay where you are, nobody should leave their place on the seventh day.
Exodus 16:30 The people rested on the seventh day.
Exodus 16:31 The people of Israel named it Manna; it was like white coriander seed and tasted like honey cakes.
Exodus 16:32 Moses said, "This is what God commands: Take a full omer to save for future generations, so they can see the bread I gave you in the desert when I led you out of Egypt."
Exodus 16:33 Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar, put a full omer of manna in it, and place it before God to save for your descendants."
Exodus 16:34 As God directed Moses, Aaron put it in front of the Testimony to be preserved.
Exodus 16:35 The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they reached an area where people lived; they ate manna until they got to the edge of Canaan.
Exodus 16:36 An omer is one-tenth of an ephah.

Exodus 17:1 The whole group of Israel's children traveled from the Sin desert, moving as God had told them, and they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
Exodus 17:2 So the people argued with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink." And Moses replied, "Why are you arguing with me? Why are you testing God?"
Exodus 17:3 The people were thirsty for water there, and they complained to Moses, saying, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die of thirst, along with our children and animals?"
Exodus 17:4 Moses cried out to God, saying, "What should I do for these people? They are almost ready to stone me."
Exodus 17:5 God told Moses, "Go ahead of the people and bring some of Israel's elders with you; also, take the staff you used to strike the river in your hand and go."
Exodus 17:6 Look, I will be in front of you on the rock at Horeb; hit the rock, and water will come out so the people can drink. Moses did this with the Israelite elders watching.
Exodus 17:7 He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites argued and tested God by asking, "Is God with us or not?"
Exodus 17:8 Amalek came and battled with Israel at Rephidim.
Exodus 17:9 Moses told Joshua, "Pick some men for us, and go fight Amalek. Tomorrow I'll stand on the hilltop with God's staff in my hand."
Exodus 17:10 Joshua did what Moses told him, and fought Amalek. Moses, Aaron, and Hur went to the top of the hill.
Exodus 17:11 When Moses raised his hand, Israel won; when he lowered his hand, Amalek won.
Exodus 17:12 Moses' hands were tired, so they placed a stone under him to sit on. Aaron and Hur helped hold up his hands, one on each side, and his hands stayed steady until sunset.
Exodus 17:13 Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the sword.
Exodus 17:14 God told Moses, "Write this down as a reminder in a book and tell it to Joshua: I will completely erase the memory of Amalek from the earth."
Exodus 17:15 Moses built an altar and named it The Lord Is My Banner.
Exodus 17:16 He said, because God has promised that God will fight Amalek forever, generation after generation.

Exodus 18:1 When Jethro, the religious leader of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard about everything God had done for Moses and the people of Israel, and how God had led Israel out of Egypt;
Exodus 18:2 Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought back Zipporah, Moses' wife, after she had been sent away.
Exodus 18:3 She had two sons. The first was named Gershom, because he said, "I have been a foreigner in another country."
Exodus 18:4 The other's name was Eliezer, for he said, "My father's God was my helper and saved me from Pharaoh's sword."
Exodus 18:5 Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and wife to Moses in the desert, where he camped at God's mountain.
Exodus 18:6 He said to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, have come to you with your wife and her two sons."
Exodus 18:7 Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him; they asked about each other's well-being and then went into the tent.
Exodus 18:8 Moses told his father-in-law everything that God had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel, all their troubles on the journey, and how God saved them.
Exodus 18:9 Jethro was happy about all the good things God did for Israel, saving them from the Egyptians.
Exodus 18:10 Jethro said, "Praise God, who has saved you from the Egyptians and Pharaoh, and has rescued the people from the Egyptians' control."
Exodus 18:11 Now I understand that God is greater than all gods, because where they acted with arrogance, He was superior.
Exodus 18:12 Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all the leaders of Israel came to eat with him in God's presence.
Exodus 18:13 The next day, Moses took his place to make decisions for the people, and they stood around Moses from morning to evening.
Exodus 18:14 When Moses' father-in-law saw everything he was doing for the people, he asked, "What are you doing to the people? Why do you sit alone while everyone waits around you from morning to evening?"
Exodus 18:15 Moses told his father-in-law, "The people come to me to ask about God."
Exodus 18:16 When they have an issue, they come to me; and I decide between them, and I teach them God's rules and laws.
Exodus 18:17 Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good."
Exodus 18:18 You will definitely become exhausted, both you and these people with you, because this task is too much for you; you can't do it all by yourself.
Exodus 18:19 Listen to me, I will advise you, and God will be with you: You be the people's representative before God, and bring their disputes to God.
Exodus 18:20 You should teach them the rules and laws, and show them the path they must follow, and the work they must do.
Exodus 18:21 Choose from all the people capable men who respect God, honest men who dislike greed, and appoint them as leaders over groups of one thousand, one hundred, fifty, and ten.
Exodus 18:22 Let them decide for the people at all times. They will handle big issues with you, but they will handle small ones themselves. This will make things easier for you, and they will share the work with you.
Exodus 18:23 If you do this and if God tells you to, then you will be able to keep going, and all these people will go home peacefully.
Exodus 18:24 Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
Exodus 18:25 Moses picked skilled men from all Israel and appointed them as leaders of the people: chiefs over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
Exodus 18:26 They judged the people at all times: they took difficult cases to Moses, but they decided every small issue themselves.
Exodus 18:27 Moses allowed his father-in-law to leave, and he returned to his own country.

Exodus 19:1 In the third month, after Israel's people left Egypt, they arrived in the Sinai desert on that same day.
Exodus 19:2 They left Rephidim, came to the Sinai desert, and set up camp in the wilderness; there Israel camped at the mountain.
Exodus 19:3 Moses went up to meet God, and God called to him from the mountain, 'This is what you must tell the people of Jacob and say to the Israelites:
Exodus 19:4 You saw what I did to the Egyptians, how I carried you on eagle's wings, and brought you to me.
Exodus 19:5 So now, if you really listen to my voice and keep my agreement, you will be a special treasure for me above everyone because the whole earth is mine.
Exodus 19:6 You will be for me a kingdom of priests and a sacred nation. These are the words you must tell the people of Israel.
Exodus 19:7 Moses came and gathered the leaders of the people, and told them all the words that God had commanded him.
Exodus 19:8 All the people answered at once, saying, "We will do everything God has said." Moses told God what the people said.
Exodus 19:9 God said to Moses, "Look, I will come to you in a dense cloud so the people can hear me talking with you and will always trust you." Then Moses reported to God what the people had said.
Exodus 19:10 God told Moses, "Go to the people, make them holy today and tomorrow, and have them wash their clothes."
Exodus 19:11 Be prepared for the third day because on that day God will come down where everyone can see on Mount Sinai.
Exodus 19:12 Set limits for the people all around, and say, 'Be careful not to go up the mountain or touch its edge. Anyone who touches the mountain will certainly be put to death.'
Exodus 19:13 No one should touch it, or they must be stoned or shot. Whether animal or person, they must not survive. When the trumpet sounds a long blast, they can go up the mountain.
Exodus 19:14 Moses went down from the mountain to the people, made them holy, and they washed their clothes.
Exodus 19:15 He told the people, "Get ready for the third day and do not go near your wives."
Exodus 19:16 On the third morning, there were thunders and lightning, a thick cloud over the mountain, and a very loud trumpet sound; all the people in the camp shook with fear.
Exodus 19:17 Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the lower part of the mountain.
Exodus 19:18 Mount Sinai was completely covered in smoke because God came down on it in fire, and the smoke rose like from a furnace, making the whole mountain shake a lot.
Exodus 19:19 When the trumpet sound grew long and louder, Moses spoke and God replied with a voice.
Exodus 19:20 God came down to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the top; and Moses went up.
Exodus 19:21 God told Moses, "Go down and warn the people not to force their way through to see God, or many of them will die."
Exodus 19:22 Let the priests who approach God make themselves pure, so God doesn't come forcefully upon them.
Exodus 19:23 Moses said to God, "The people can't come up to Mount Sinai because you told us to put limits around the mountain and make it holy."
Exodus 19:24 God told him, "Go down, then come back up with Aaron. But the priests and people must not force their way up to God, or he will punish them."
Exodus 19:25 Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

Exodus 20:1 God said all these words:
Exodus 20:2 I am God, your God, who brought you out from Egypt, from the place where you were slaves.
Exodus 20:3 You should not worship any other gods but me.
Exodus 20:4 Do not make for yourself any carved idol, or any picture of anything in the sky above, or on the earth below, or in the water under the earth.
Exodus 20:5 Do not bow down to them or serve them; for I, your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me.
Exodus 20:6 I show kindness to thousands who love me and follow my rules.
Exodus 20:7 Do not use God's name for no good reason; God will not let anyone who misuses his name go unpunished.
Exodus 20:8 Remember the day of rest, to keep it special.
Exodus 20:9 Work for six days and do all your tasks.
Exodus 20:10 The seventh day is a rest day for God. On that day, you or your son, daughter, servants, animals, or any guest in your home, should not do any work.
Exodus 20:11 In six days, God created the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore, God blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
Exodus 20:12 Respect your father and your mother so you may live a long time in the land God gives you.
Exodus 20:13 Do not kill.
Exodus 20:14 Do not cheat on your spouse.
Exodus 20:15 Do not steal.
Exodus 20:16 Do not tell lies about others.
Exodus 20:17 Do not want your neighbor's house, do not want your neighbor's wife, their worker, their helper, their ox, their donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
Exodus 20:18 Everyone saw the thunder, the lightning, the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; when they saw this, they moved back and stood far away.
Exodus 20:19 They said to Moses, "You talk to us, and we will listen, but don't let God talk to us, or we might die."
Exodus 20:20 Moses told the people, "Don't be afraid. God has come to test you, so that you will respect him and not sin."
Exodus 20:21 The people stayed far away, while Moses went close to the deep darkness where God was.
Exodus 20:22 God told Moses, "Tell the people of Israel, 'You have seen that I have spoken to you from heaven.'"
Exodus 20:23 Do not make silver gods to be with me, and do not make gold gods for yourselves.
Exodus 20:24 Make an earth altar for me and sacrifice your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and cattle on it. Wherever I make my name known, I'll come to you and bless you.
Exodus 20:25 If you make me an altar of stone, do not use cut stones: if you use tools on it, you make it unclean.
Exodus 20:26 Do not climb steps to my altar, so your nakedness is not exposed.

Exodus 21:1 Here are the rules that you should give to them.
Exodus 21:2 If you buy a Hebrew servant, he must work for six years; but in the seventh year, he will be set free without paying anything.
Exodus 21:3 If he entered alone, he will leave alone; if he was married, his wife will leave with him.
Exodus 21:4 If his master gave him a wife, and she had sons or daughters; the wife and her children belong to her master, and he will leave alone.
Exodus 21:5 If the servant clearly says, "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I don't want to be set free":
Exodus 21:6 The owner must take him to the authorities; he will take him to the door or doorpost. There, the owner must pierce his ear with a tool, and he will work for his owner always.
Exodus 21:7 If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she should not leave like the male servants.
Exodus 21:8 If her master is not happy with her and does not make her his wife, he must allow her to be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners because he was not honest with her.
Exodus 21:9 If he has promised her to his son, he should treat her like his own daughter.
Exodus 21:10 If he marries another woman, he must not reduce the first one's food, clothes, or marital rights.
Exodus 21:11 If he does not do these three things for her, then she can go free without paying anything.
Exodus 21:12 Whoever hits a person and kills them must be put to death.
Exodus 21:13 If a man doesn't plan to harm someone, but it happens by accident, I will choose a safe place for him to go.
Exodus 21:14 If someone deliberately attacks and kills another person, take them away from my altar so they can be put to death.
Exodus 21:15 Anyone who hits their father or mother must be put to death.
Exodus 21:16 Whoever steals a person and sells them, or is caught with them, must be put to death.
Exodus 21:17 Whoever curses their father or mother must be put to death.
Exodus 21:18 If men fight and one hits the other with a stone or his fist and the injured man doesn't die but has to stay in bed:
Exodus 21:19 If he gets up and walks around with a cane, then the one who hit him is not guilty. But he must pay for the injured person's lost time and make sure he is completely healed.
Exodus 21:20 If someone hits their servant, male or female, with a rod and the servant dies, the owner must be punished.
Exodus 21:21 However, if the slave survives a day or two, no punishment will happen, because the slave is his owner's property.
Exodus 21:22 If men fight and injure a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely but there is no serious harm, the man must be fined whatever the woman's husband demands and the court allows.
Exodus 21:23 If harm follows, then you must give a life for a life.
Exodus 21:24 Give an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.
Exodus 21:25 Burn for burn, cut for cut, bruise for bruise.
Exodus 21:26 If someone hurts their servant's eye and it is destroyed, they must set the servant free to make up for the lost eye.
Exodus 21:27 If he knocks out his male or female servant's tooth, he must let them go free because of the tooth.
Exodus 21:28 If an ox hurts a man or a woman so they die, the ox must be stoned to death, and no one can eat its meat; but the owner of the ox is not to blame.
Exodus 21:29 If the ox had a habit of attacking with its horn before, and its owner was warned but did not keep it secure, and the ox killed a man or woman, the ox must be stoned and the owner must be put to death.
Exodus 21:30 If he must pay money, he must pay to save his life whatever amount is required.
Exodus 21:31 If the ox hurts a boy or a girl, the same rule will apply to the owner.
Exodus 21:32 If an ox injures a male or female servant, the owner must pay the servant's master thirty silver coins, and the ox must be killed with stones.
Exodus 21:33 If someone digs a hole and doesn't cover it and a cow or donkey falls into it,
Exodus 21:34 The person who owns the pit must pay for the damages and compensate the owner of the animals; the dead animal will then belong to the person who owned the pit.
Exodus 21:35 If one person's ox injures another's ox and it dies, they must sell the live ox and split the money, and they must also split the dead ox.
Exodus 21:36 If it's known that the ox often pushed before, and its owner didn't keep it secured, he must pay an ox for the ox; the dead ox will belong to him.

Exodus 22:1 If someone steals a cow or a sheep, and kills or sells it, they must give back five cows for a cow, and four sheep for a sheep.
Exodus 22:2 If someone catches a thief breaking in and hits him so he dies, no one is guilty of his death.
Exodus 22:3 If the sun has risen when he is caught, he must pay for the harm he did. If he can't pay, he will be sold to make up for what he stole.
Exodus 22:4 If the stolen animal is found alive with him, whether an ox, a donkey, or a sheep, he must pay back twice as much.
Exodus 22:5 If someone lets their animal eat from another person's field or vineyard, they must pay back with the best from their own field or vineyard.
Exodus 22:6 If a fire starts and spreads to thorns, burning up piles of grain, standing grain, or fields, the person who started the fire must pay for the damage.
Exodus 22:7 If someone gives their neighbor money or items to look after, and they are stolen from the person's house; if the thief is caught, they must pay back twice as much.
Exodus 22:8 If the thief is not found, then the homeowner must go to the judges, to find out if he took his neighbor's belongings.
Exodus 22:9 For any kind of wrong, whether it's about an ox, a donkey, a sheep, clothing, or any lost item that someone claims as their own, both people involved should go to the judges. Whoever the judges decide is guilty must pay back their neighbor twice as much.
Exodus 22:10 If someone gives their neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to take care of, and it dies, gets injured, or is lost without anyone seeing it:
Exodus 22:11 Then they both must promise before God that he did not take his neighbor's belongings; the owner must accept this promise, and he will not have to replace them.
Exodus 22:12 If someone steals from him, he must pay back the owner.
Exodus 22:13 If an animal is torn apart, he must show the pieces as proof and he doesn't have to replace the animal that was killed.
Exodus 22:14 If someone borrows something from their neighbor and it gets damaged or dies while the owner is not present, the borrower must definitely replace it.
Exodus 22:15 If the owner is with the animal, he doesn't have to pay; if it's a rented animal, the loss is covered by the rental fee.
Exodus 22:16 If a man seduces a woman who is not engaged and sleeps with her, he must surely make her his wife by providing a dowry.
Exodus 22:17 If her father totally refuses to give her to him, he must pay money as is the custom for a virgin's dowry.
