Exodus 22:18 Do not let a witch live.
Exodus 22:19 Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal must be put to death.
Exodus 22:20 Anyone who offers sacrifices to any god other than the God alone will be completely destroyed.
Exodus 22:21 Do not trouble or be harsh to a foreigner, because you were once foreigners in Egypt.
Exodus 22:22 Do not mistreat any widow or orphan.
Exodus 22:23 If you hurt them in any way and they call out to me, I will certainly hear their cry.
Exodus 22:24 I will become very angry and will kill you with the sword; your wives will become widows and your children will have no fathers.
Exodus 22:25 If you lend money to any of my people who are poor near you, you should not charge them interest.
Exodus 22:26 If you take your neighbor's clothes as a promise, you must return them before the sun sets.
Exodus 22:27 That is his only blanket, his clothing to cover his skin. What will he sleep in? When he calls to me, I will listen, because I am kind.
Exodus 22:28 Do not insult any gods, nor speak ill of your people's leader.
Exodus 22:29 Do not wait to give the first of your harvested fruits and drinks; you must give your firstborn sons to me.
Exodus 22:30 Treat your oxen and sheep the same way: they must stay with their mother for seven days; on the eighth day, you give them to me.
Exodus 22:31 You must be holy for me: do not eat any meat torn by animals in the fields; throw it to the dogs.

Exodus 23:1 Do not spread false rumors or join hands with the wicked to be an unfair witness.
Exodus 23:2 Do not follow a crowd to do wrong; nor should you agree with many to make unfair decisions.
Exodus 23:3 Do not favor a poor man in his case.
Exodus 23:4 If you find your enemy's ox or donkey lost, you must return it to him.
Exodus 23:5 If you see your enemy's donkey lying down under its load, and you might avoid helping, you must help anyway.
Exodus 23:6 Do not treat the poor unfairly in legal matters.
Exodus 23:7 Stay away from lies and don't kill innocent or good people because I will not let the guilty go unpunished.
Exodus 23:8 Do not accept any gifts; gifts blind the wise and twist the words of the good people.
Exodus 23:9 Do not treat foreigners badly because you know how it feels to be a foreigner, as you were foreigners in Egypt.
Exodus 23:10 For six years you should plant your land and collect its crops.
Exodus 23:11 In the seventh year, let the land rest and be still, so the poor can eat. Whatever they don't eat, the wild animals will. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
Exodus 23:12 Work for six days, and rest on the seventh day, so your ox, donkey, your servant's child, and any foreigner can also rest and be refreshed.
Exodus 23:13 Be careful to follow everything I have told you, and do not talk about other gods or even mention their names.
Exodus 23:14 Celebrate a feast for me three times a year.
Exodus 23:15 You must celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread by eating bread without yeast for seven days, as I have told you, during the set time in the month of Abib, because that is when you left Egypt. No one should come to see me without bringing something.
Exodus 23:16 Celebrate the Harvest Festival when you first collect crops from the fields, and the Gathering Festival at the year's end when you gather your work from the fields.
Exodus 23:17 Three times a year, all your men must come before God.
Exodus 23:18 Do not give God a sacrifice mixed with yeast, and do not keep the fat from my offering until morning.
Exodus 23:19 Bring the first of your harvest to God's house. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Exodus 23:20 Look, I am sending an Angel ahead of you to protect you on the journey and to lead you to the place I have prepared.
Exodus 23:21 Be careful around him, listen to what he says, and do not make him angry, because he will not forgive your wrongdoings; for he represents me.
Exodus 23:22 If you really listen to his voice and do everything I say, then I will be against your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
Exodus 23:23 My angel will go ahead of you and lead you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will eliminate them.
Exodus 23:24 Do not bow down to their gods, do not serve them, or follow their ways; instead, you must completely destroy them and break their statues.
Exodus 23:25 You will serve God, and he will bless your food and your water; I will remove sickness from among you.
Exodus 23:26 No animal will miscarry or be infertile in your land; I will allow you to live a full life.
Exodus 23:27 I will make people afraid of you and destroy all the people you meet, and I will make all your enemies run away from you.
Exodus 23:28 I will send hornets ahead of you to chase away the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite.
Exodus 23:29 I will not force them out from in front of you in one year; if I do, the land may become empty, and the wild animals may become too many for you.
Exodus 23:30 Step by step, I will push them out before you, until you grow and take over the land.
Exodus 23:31 I will define your borders from the Red Sea to the Philistine Sea, and from the desert to the river. I will give the people living there to you, and you will force them out.
Exodus 23:32 Do not make a treaty with them or their gods.
Exodus 23:33 They must not live in your land, or they will make you sin against me; if you worship their gods, it will certainly trap you.

Exodus 24:1 He told Moses, "Go up to God, you, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders, and worship from a distance."
Exodus 24:2 Only Moses will go close to God; others will not, nor will the people go up with him.
Exodus 24:3 Moses told the people everything God said, including the laws. Everyone agreed and said, "We will do everything God has told us."
Exodus 24:4 Moses wrote down all of God's words. Early in the morning, he got up, built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and set up twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Exodus 24:5 He sent young Israelites to present burnt offerings and sacrifice oxen as peace offerings to God.
Exodus 24:6 Moses took half of the blood, put it in bowls, and sprinkled the other half on the altar.
Exodus 24:7 He took the book of the agreement and read it to the people. They said, "We will do everything God has said and obey."
Exodus 24:8 Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people, saying, "Look, this is the blood of the agreement God has made with you about all these words."
Exodus 24:9 Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders from Israel went up.
Exodus 24:10 They saw the God of Israel: under his feet was something like a floor made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
Exodus 24:11 God did not harm the leaders of the Israelites; they saw God, and they ate and drank.
Exodus 24:12 God said to Moses, "Come up to the mountain to me, and stay there. I will give you stone tablets, laws, and commands I have written, so you can teach them."
Exodus 24:13 Moses stood up with his helper Joshua and went up the mountain of God.
Exodus 24:14 He told the elders, "Stay here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are with you; if anyone has any issues, they should go to them."
Exodus 24:15 Moses went up the mountain, and a cloud covered the mountain.
Exodus 24:16 God's brightness stayed on Mount Sinai, and a cloud hid it for six days. On the seventh day, He called to Moses from inside the cloud.
Exodus 24:17 The children of Israel saw the glory of God as a consuming fire on the mountaintop.
Exodus 24:18 Moses went into the cloud and climbed up the mountain, and he was on the mountain for forty days and nights.

Exodus 25:1 God spoke to Moses and said,
Exodus 25:2 Tell the people of Israel to give me an offering. You must accept the offering from anyone who gives it willingly from their heart.
Exodus 25:3 Give this as your offering: gold, silver, and bronze.
Exodus 25:4 And blue, purple, red, fine cloth, and goat hair.
Exodus 25:5 Red-dyed ram skins, badger skins, and acacia wood.
Exodus 25:6 Oil for the lamp, spices for the anointing oil, and for the sweet smelling incense.
Exodus 25:7 Onyx stones and stones for setting in the ephod and the breastplate.
Exodus 25:8 Let them build a holy place for me, so I can live with them.
Exodus 25:9 Follow exactly the design I show you for the tent and for all the equipment, and make them that way.
Exodus 25:10 Make an ark from acacia wood: it should be 2.5 cubits long, 1.5 cubits wide, and 1.5 cubits high.
Exodus 25:11 Cover it with pure gold inside and out, and put a gold rim around it.
Exodus 25:12 Make four gold rings for it and attach them to its four corners; two rings on one side and two on the other side.
Exodus 25:13 Make poles from acacia wood and cover them with gold.
Exodus 25:14 Put the poles through the rings on the sides of the chest to carry it with them.
Exodus 25:15 The poles must remain in the rings of the chest; they must not be removed.
Exodus 25:16 Put the laws I give you into the chest.
Exodus 25:17 Make a cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Exodus 25:18 Make two gold cherubs with hammered work at both ends of the cover.
Exodus 25:19 Make one angel on one end and another angel on the other end; you should make the angels from the same piece as the mercy seat, at its two ends. 

(Note: "Globish" typically refers to a simplified version of English designed to be understood by non-native speakers around the world, so the term "cherub" has been translated to "angel" for clarity.)
Exodus 25:20 The cherubim will spread out their wings above, shielding the mercy seat with their wings, and they will face each other; the cherubim's faces should be toward the mercy seat.
Exodus 25:21 Put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and inside the ark, put the laws I will give you.
Exodus 25:22 There I will meet with you, and I will talk to you from above the mercy seat, between the two cherubs on the ark of the testimony, about everything I command you for the people of Israel.
Exodus 25:23 Also make a table from acacia wood: it should be two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
Exodus 25:24 Cover it with pure gold and add a gold border around it.
Exodus 25:25 Make a border one hand's width all around it, and put a gold rim around the border.
Exodus 25:26 Make four gold rings for it and attach them to its four corners at the four legs.
Exodus 25:27 The rings should be right next to the edge to hold the poles that carry the table.
Exodus 25:28 Make poles from acacia wood and cover them with gold so the table can be carried with them.
Exodus 25:29 Make its plates, spoons, pitchers, and bowls for pouring. Make them all of pure gold.
Exodus 25:30 Put bread on the table in front of me always.
Exodus 25:31 Make a lampstand of pure gold. It should be crafted from hammered work: its base, arms, cups, buds, and blossoms must all be one piece.
Exodus 25:32 Six arms will extend from the sides; three arms of the lampstand from one side, and three arms of the lampstand from the other side.
Exodus 25:33 Each of the six branches coming out of the lampstand had three cups shaped like almond flowers, each with buds and petals.
Exodus 25:34 In the lampstands there will be four cups shaped like almonds, with their buds and blossoms.
Exodus 25:35 There will be a bud below two branches of it, a bud below another two branches, and a bud below two more branches, making six branches coming out of the lampstand.
Exodus 25:36 The buds and branches will be one piece with the lampstand, all made from solid gold.
Exodus 25:37 Make seven lamps for it, and set up the lamps so they shine light in front of it.
Exodus 25:38 Its tongs and snuffdishes must be made of pure gold.
Exodus 25:39 He must make it of a talent of pure gold, including all these utensils.
Exodus 25:40 Make sure you make them just like the pattern you were shown on the mountain.

Exodus 26:1 Make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine linen, blue, purple, and red, and with skilled work of cherubim on them.
Exodus 26:2 One curtain should be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide, and all the curtains should be the same size.
Exodus 26:3 The five curtains must be joined together, and the other five curtains must also be joined together.
Exodus 26:4 Make blue loops along the edge of one curtain at the side where it connects, and do the same on the far edge of the other curtain where it connects to the second one.
Exodus 26:5 Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the second curtain so they can fasten together.
Exodus 26:6 Make fifty gold clasps, and join the curtains together with the clasps to form one tent.
Exodus 26:7 Make eleven curtains out of goat hair for the tent's covering.
Exodus 26:8 One curtain should be thirty units long and four units wide, and all eleven curtains should be the same size.
Exodus 26:9 You will connect five curtains on their own, and six curtains on their own, and fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Exodus 26:10 Make fifty loops on the edge of the outer curtain in the set, and fifty loops on the edge of the second curtain that connects to it.
Exodus 26:11 Make fifty brass clasps, put them in the loops, and fasten the tent together so it becomes one piece.
Exodus 26:12 The leftover part of the tent curtains, the half-piece that's left, should cover the back of the dwelling.
Exodus 26:13 Add one foot of cloth on each side of the tent's remaining length so it hangs over the sides of the dwelling place to cover it.
Exodus 26:14 Make a red-dyed ram skin cover for the tent, and put a badger skin cover over it.
Exodus 26:15 Make upright wooden boards for the tent from acacia wood.
Exodus 26:16 Each board must be ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Exodus 26:17 Each board must have two pegs, lined up with each other; do this for all the boards of the shelter.
Exodus 26:18 Make twenty boards for the tabernacle on the south side facing south.
Exodus 26:19 Make forty silver bases for the twenty planks; put two bases under each plank for its two projections.
Exodus 26:20 For the north side of the tent, there will be twenty boards.
Exodus 26:21 They had forty silver bases; each board was supported by two bases.
Exodus 26:22 Make six boards for the west side of the tent.
Exodus 26:23 Make two frames for the corners of the shelter on both sides.
Exodus 26:24 They should be joined together at the bottom and joined at the top to one ring. This is how both will be for the two corners.
Exodus 26:25 There will be eight boards with their bases of silver, sixteen bases in total; two bases under each board.
Exodus 26:26 Make bars from acacia wood; five for the boards on one side of the tent.
Exodus 26:27 Use five bars for one side of the tent, and five bars for the other side of the tent, on the tent's west side.
Exodus 26:28 The center bar inside the panels will stretch from one end to the other.
Exodus 26:29 Cover the boards with gold and make gold rings to hold the bars, then cover the bars with gold too.
Exodus 26:30 Set up the tent as you were shown on the mountain.
Exodus 26:31 Make a curtain of blue, purple, and red, and finely twisted linen with skilled work, decorated with cherubs.
Exodus 26:32 Hang the curtain on four wooden posts covered with gold, with gold hooks, and set them in four silver bases.
Exodus 26:33 Hang the curtain under the clasps, so you can place the ark of the covenant behind the curtain. The curtain will separate the holy place from the most holy place.
Exodus 26:34 Place the mercy seat on top of the ark of the covenant inside the most holy room.
Exodus 26:35 Place the table outside the curtain, and put the lampstand across from the table on the south side of the tent. Place the table on the north side.
Exodus 26:36 Make a curtain for the tent door using blue, purple, red, and good quality linen, decorated with embroidery.
Exodus 26:37 Make five wooden posts and cover them with gold. Their hooks will be gold, and make five bronze bases for them.

Exodus 27:1 Make an altar from acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar should be square, and its height should be three cubits.
Exodus 27:2 Make horns for it on its four corners, and the horns will be made from the same material. Cover it with bronze.
Exodus 27:3 Make pans for carrying ashes, shovels, bowls, meat hooks, and firepans, all out of bronze.
Exodus 27:4 Make a bronze grid for it, and attach four bronze rings at its corners.
Exodus 27:5 Place it under the edge of the altar below, so the net reaches halfway up the altar.
Exodus 27:6 Make poles for the altar from acacia wood and cover them with bronze.
Exodus 27:7 Put the poles into the rings on the altar's sides to carry it.
Exodus 27:8 Make it with boards as a box; just like you were shown on the mountain, that is how they should make it.
Exodus 27:9 Make the courtyard of the tent: on the south side, there should be curtains for the courtyard made of finely woven linen, a hundred cubits long for one side.
Exodus 27:10 The twenty columns and their twenty bases will be made of bronze; the hooks of the columns and their bands will be made of silver.
Exodus 27:11 On the north side, the curtains will be 100 cubits long, with 20 pillars and 20 bronze bases; the hooks and bands of the pillars will be silver.
Exodus 27:12 The west side of the courtyard will have curtains that are 50 units long, with ten posts and ten bases.
Exodus 27:13 The width of the courtyard on the east side will be fifty cubits.
Exodus 27:14 The curtains on one side of the gate will be fifteen units long, with three pillars and three bases.
Exodus 27:15 On the other side, there will be curtains fifteen units long, with three posts and three bases.
Exodus 27:16 The entrance to the courtyard will have a curtain that is 20 cubits long, made of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen with embroidery. It will have four pillars and four bases.
Exodus 27:17 All the poles around the yard must have silver bands; their hooks must be silver, and their bases bronze.
Exodus 27:18 The court will be one hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide all around, and five cubits high made of fine linen, with brass bases.
Exodus 27:19 All the tools for the tent and everything used in its service, along with all its pegs and all the pegs for the courtyard, must be made of bronze.
Exodus 27:20 Tell the people of Israel to bring you pure, crushed olive oil for the lamp so it will keep burning all the time.
Exodus 27:21 In the tent where people meet, outside the curtain in front of the rules, Aaron and his sons will take care of it from night to morning before God. It will be a permanent law for them through all their generations for the people of Israel.

Exodus 28:1 Choose your brother Aaron and his sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, from the Israelites to serve me as priests.
Exodus 28:2 Make special clothes for your brother Aaron that are beautiful and glorious.
Exodus 28:3 You will talk to all the skilled people I have given wisdom to, so they can make special clothes for Aaron that will set him apart to serve me as a priest.
Exodus 28:4 Make these clothes: a chest piece, an ephod, a robe, a decorated tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are sacred clothes for your brother Aaron and his sons, so they can serve me as priests.
Exodus 28:5 They will take gold, blue, purple, red, and good linen.
Exodus 28:6 They will make the ephod with gold, blue, purple, and red threads, and fine linen, with skilled craftsmanship.
Exodus 28:7 It will have two shoulder parts attached on its two sides, and so it will be held together.
Exodus 28:8 The special belt of the ephod, which is part of it, will be made the same way; out of gold, blue, purple, and red threads, and quality linen woven together.
Exodus 28:9 You will take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of Israel's children.
Exodus 28:10 Put six of their names on one stone and the other six names on the second stone, in the order they were born.
Exodus 28:11 Carve the two stones like a stone carver would, with designs like a seal, and engrave on them the names of Israel's children. Put the stones in gold settings.
Exodus 28:12 You will place two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod as memorial stones for the Israelites. Aaron will carry their names on his two shoulders before God to remember them.
Exodus 28:13 Make gold settings.
Exodus 28:14 Make two chains of pure gold, braided like ropes, and attach the braided chains to the settings.
Exodus 28:15 Make a special chest piece for making decisions using skilled craftsmanship. It should be made just like the ephod using gold, blue, purple, red, and quality woven linen.
Exodus 28:16 It will be square and folded double, a hand's breadth long and a hand's breadth wide.
Exodus 28:17 Place stones in it, four rows of them: the first row will have a ruby, a topaz, and a garnet. This will be the first row.
Exodus 28:18 The second row will have a green gem, a blue gem, and a clear, hard gem.
Exodus 28:19 The third row had a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
Exodus 28:20 In the fourth row there will be a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper; they will be placed in gold settings.
Exodus 28:21 The stones will have the names of Israel's twelve sons, each one named like a seal's carving for each of the twelve tribes.
Exodus 28:22 Make chains like braids of pure gold for the chest piece.
Exodus 28:23 Make two gold rings for the chest piece, and attach the rings to the top two corners of the chest piece.
Exodus 28:24 You should attach the two twisted gold chains to the two rings on the edges of the chestpiece.
Exodus 28:25 Attach the other ends of the two twisted chains to the settings and place them on the shoulder straps of the apron at the front.
Exodus 28:26 Make two gold rings and attach them to the two corners of the chest piece, on the inside edge near the vest.
Exodus 28:27 Make two more gold rings and attach them on the lower sides of the ephod, near the front, right across from its other seam, just above its decorative belt.
Exodus 28:28 They will tie the breastplate with its rings to the ephod's rings using a blue cord, so it sits above the ephod's decorative belt and the breastplate doesn't come off the ephod.
Exodus 28:29 Aaron will carry the names of Israel's children on the chestpiece of decision over his heart when he enters the sacred place, to remember them always in front of God.
Exodus 28:30 You will place the Urim and the Thummim inside the breastplate for making decisions; they must be over Aaron's heart when he goes in front of God. Aaron will always carry the decision-making for the Israelites over his heart in front of God.
Exodus 28:31 Make the ephod's robe completely blue.
Exodus 28:32 It will have a hole in the top, in the middle, with a strong woven edge around the hole, like the neck of a piece of armor, so it doesn't tear.
Exodus 28:33 Around the bottom hem, make blue, purple, and red pomegranates and place gold bells between them all around.
Exodus 28:34 A gold bell and a fruit, a gold bell and a fruit, around the bottom edge of the robe.
Exodus 28:35 Aaron must wear it while serving. When he enters the sacred area before God and when he leaves, the sound will be heard so he will not die.
Exodus 28:36 Make a pure gold plate and carve on it, as you would a seal, "Holy to God."
Exodus 28:37 Tie it with a blue cord on the turban, to be on the front of the turban.
Exodus 28:38 It will be on Aaron's forehead, so he can take responsibility for any wrongs related to the sacred offerings the Israelites make. It will always be on his forehead, so the offerings will be acceptable to God.
Exodus 28:39 Make a coat of fine linen with embroidery, a fine linen turban, and a belt with needlework.
Exodus 28:40 Make coats for Aaron's sons, give them sashes, and make hats for them to show honor and beauty.
Exodus 28:41 Dress your brother Aaron and his sons in these clothes. Then pour the special oil on them to make them priests for me.
Exodus 28:42 Make linen shorts for them to cover their bodies from the waist to the thighs.
Exodus 28:43 Aaron and his sons will wear these when they enter the meeting tent or approach the altar to serve in the holy area, so they will not be guilty and die. This is a permanent law for him and his descendants.

Exodus 29:1 Do this to make them holy so they can serve me as priests: Take one young bull and two perfect rams.
Exodus 29:2 Make bread without yeast, flat cakes mixed with oil, and thin breads spread with oil, all from wheat flour.
Exodus 29:3 Put them all in one basket and bring the basket with the young bull and the two male sheep.
Exodus 29:4 Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the meeting tent and wash them with water.
Exodus 29:5 Take the clothes, and dress Aaron in the tunic, the ephod's robe, the ephod, the chestpiece, and tie the special belt of the ephod around him.
Exodus 29:6 You will place the hat on his head, and put the holy crown on the hat.
Exodus 29:7 Then you will take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
Exodus 29:8 Bring his sons and put robes on them.
Exodus 29:9 Dress Aaron and his sons with belts and hats, and they will always serve as priests. Set apart Aaron and his sons to be priests.
Exodus 29:10 Bring a bull to the meeting tent, and Aaron and his sons will place their hands on the bull's head.
Exodus 29:11 Kill the bull in front of God, by the entrance of the meeting tent.
Exodus 29:12 Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the altar's horns with your finger, then pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
Exodus 29:13 You must take all the fat covering the insides, the layer over the liver, and the two kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
Exodus 29:14 Burn the bull's flesh, skin, and waste outside the camp with fire; it is a sin offering.
Exodus 29:15 You must also take one ram; and Aaron and his sons will place their hands on the ram's head.
Exodus 29:16 Kill the ram, take its blood, and sprinkle it all around the altar.
Exodus 29:17 Cut the ram into pieces, wash its insides and legs, and place them with its other pieces and head.
Exodus 29:18 You must burn the entire ram on the altar; it is a burnt sacrifice to God, a pleasing aroma, an offering made with fire to God.
Exodus 29:19 You will take the other ram; Aaron and his sons will place their hands on the ram's head.
Exodus 29:20 Then you must kill the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the top of Aaron's right ear, on the tops of his sons' right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, on the big toes of their right feet, and sprinkle the blood all around the altar.
Exodus 29:21 Take some of the blood on the altar and the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron, his clothes, his sons, and his sons' clothes with him. They and their clothes will be made holy.
Exodus 29:22 You will also take from the ram the fat, the back part, the fat covering the insides, the layer over the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right front leg, because it is a special ram.
Exodus 29:23 One loaf of bread, one cake made with oil, and one thin biscuit from the basket of bread without yeast that is in front of God.
Exodus 29:24 You will put everything in Aaron's hands and in his sons' hands, and wave them as an offering in front of God.
Exodus 29:25 Take them from their hands and burn them on the altar as a burned offering to God for a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to God.
Exodus 29:26 Take the chest part of the ram used for Aaron's dedication and wave it as an offering before God; it will be your portion.
Exodus 29:27 Set apart the chest part of the waved offering and the upper part of the lifted offering from the ram dedicated to God, for Aaron and his sons.
Exodus 29:28 This will always belong to Aaron and his sons as a permanent law: It is a special gift from the Israelites. It will be a special gift from their peace offerings to God.
Exodus 29:29 Aaron's holy clothes will belong to his sons after him; they will be anointed and made holy in them.
Exodus 29:30 The new priest, who is his son, must wear these clothes for seven days when he goes into the meeting tent to serve in the sacred area.
Exodus 29:31 Cook the meat of the dedication ram in a sacred space.
Exodus 29:32 Aaron and his sons will eat the meat of the ram and the bread in the basket near the entrance of the meeting tent.
Exodus 29:33 They shall eat the offerings used to make atonement that set them apart and make them holy; but no outsider may eat them because they are sacred.
Exodus 29:34 If any of the special meat or bread is left until morning, you must burn what is left. Do not eat it because it is sacred.
Exodus 29:35 Do exactly as I told you for Aaron and his sons: Make them holy for seven days.
Exodus 29:36 Every day you must offer a bull as a sin sacrifice to make amends; cleanse the altar after making amends for it, and anoint it to make it holy.
Exodus 29:37 Make the altar holy by performing a cleansing ceremony for seven days; after that, it will be a very holy altar, and anything that touches it will become holy.
Exodus 29:38 You must offer two one-year-old lambs on the altar every day regularly.
Exodus 29:39 You should offer one lamb in the morning and another lamb in the evening.
Exodus 29:40 With each lamb, mix a tenth of an ephah of flour and a quarter of a hin of olive oil; also offer a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
Exodus 29:41 Offer the second lamb in the evening, and prepare it like the morning grain offering and accompanying drink offering, as a pleasing aroma, a fire sacrifice to God.
Exodus 29:42 Keep offering this burnt sacrifice for all your generations at the entrance of the meeting tent before God: that's where I will meet you to talk to you.
Exodus 29:43 I will meet with Israel's people there, and my glory will make the tabernacle holy.
Exodus 29:44 I will make the meeting tent and the altar holy, and I will also make Aaron and his sons holy, so they can serve me as priests.
Exodus 29:45 I will live among the people of Israel and will be their God.
Exodus 29:46 They will understand that I am their God, who led them out of Egypt so I can live with them: I am their God.

Exodus 30:1 Make an altar for burning incense from acacia wood.
Exodus 30:2 The length will be one cubit and the width one cubit; it will be square. The height will be two cubits, and the horns will be part of it.
Exodus 30:3 Cover it with pure gold—the top, sides, and horns—and make a gold border around it.
Exodus 30:4 Make two gold rings for it below its molding on opposite sides to hold the poles used to carry it.
Exodus 30:5 Make the poles from acacia wood and cover them with gold.
Exodus 30:6 Place it in front of the curtain near the Ark of the Agreement, before the cover above the Agreement, where I will meet with you.
Exodus 30:7 Aaron must burn sweet-smelling incense there every morning: when he prepares the lamps, he must burn incense on it.
Exodus 30:8 When Aaron lights the lamps in the evening, he must burn incense on it, a continuous offering of incense before God for all time to come.
Exodus 30:9 Do not burn any other incense, make burnt offerings, or grain offerings on it, nor pour a drink offering on it.
Exodus 30:10 Aaron must make amends on its horns once a year using the blood from the sacrifice for sins. Every year he must do this for all your future generations. It is very holy to God.
Exodus 30:11 God spoke to Moses and said,
Exodus 30:12 When you count the people of Israel, each one must pay God to save their life, so that no disease comes when you count them.
Exodus 30:13 Everyone counted must give this: half a shekel based on the sanctuary's shekel (which is twenty gerahs). Half a shekel is the donation to God.
Exodus 30:14 Everyone who is counted, age twenty and older, must give an offering to God.
Exodus 30:15 Rich people should not give more, and poor people should not give less than half a shekel when they give an offering to God to atone for your souls.
Exodus 30:16 Take the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the work of the meeting tent; it will remind the Israelites of God, who makes amends for your lives.
Exodus 30:17 God spoke to Moses and said,
Exodus 30:18 Make a basin of bronze with a bronze stand for washing. Place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and fill it with water.
Exodus 30:19 Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and feet there.
Exodus 30:20 When they enter the meeting tent, they must wash with water so they will not die; or when they approach the altar to serve, to burn a fire offering to God.
Exodus 30:21 They must wash their hands and feet so they won't die. This rule will last forever for them, their children, and for all future generations.
Exodus 30:22 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 30:23 Get the best spices for yourself: 500 shekels of pure myrrh, half as much sweet cinnamon, which is 250 shekels, and 250 shekels of sweet calamus.
Exodus 30:24 Five hundred shekels of cassia, by the holy shekel, and an hin of olive oil.
Exodus 30:25 Make a holy oil, a mixed ointment like a perfume maker's craft; it will be a sacred anointing oil.
Exodus 30:26 You will use the oil to anoint the tent where people meet and the chest that holds the laws.
Exodus 30:27 The table and all its dishes, the lampstand and its tools, and the altar for burning incense,
Exodus 30:28 The altar for burnt offerings with all its tools, and the washbasin with its base.
Exodus 30:29 Make these things holy, so they will be very holy; whatever touches them will become holy.
Exodus 30:30 You will anoint Aaron and his sons, prepare them, so they can serve me as priests.
Exodus 30:31 Tell the people of Israel: This oil will be special for anointing, to be used for me by all your future generations.
Exodus 30:32 Do not pour it on human skin, and do not make anything similar to it. It is special, and it must be kept special for you.
Exodus 30:33 Anyone who makes something similar, or who puts some on a non-Israelite, must be separated from their community.
Exodus 30:34 God told Moses, "Take sweet spices, stacte, onycha, and galbanum; mix these sweet spices with pure frankincense, using equal weights of each."
Exodus 30:35 Make it a scented mixture, crafted by a perfumer, mixed well, clean and sacred.
Exodus 30:36 Grind some of it into fine powder and place it in front of the covenant box in the tent of meeting, where I will come to you. It shall be very holy for you.
Exodus 30:37 Make the perfume as I have instructed you. Do not make any for yourselves using this recipe. It is special and only for God.
Exodus 30:38 Anyone who makes perfume like that to smell it will be separated from their people.

Exodus 31:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 31:2 Look, I have chosen Bezaleel, Uri's son, Hur's grandson, from the tribe of Judah.
Exodus 31:3 I have filled him with God's spirit, giving him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill in all kinds of work.
Exodus 31:4 To create clever works, to work with gold, silver, and bronze.
Exodus 31:5 In cutting stones to place them, and in shaping wood to make all kinds of things.
Exodus 31:6 I have also given Aholiab, son of Ahisamach from the tribe of Dan, to help him. And I have put wisdom in the minds of all skilled workers so they can make everything I have told you.
Exodus 31:7 The meeting tent, the box of the agreement, the cover on top of it, and all the things inside the tent.
Exodus 31:8 The table and its items, the pure lampstand with all its items, and the incense altar.
Exodus 31:9 The altar for burnt offerings with all its equipment, and the basin and its stand.
Exodus 31:10 The work clothes, the special clothes for Aaron the priest, and the clothes for his sons to serve as priests.
Exodus 31:11 You will also need the special oil for anointing and the fragrant incense for the sacred place; they must do everything I have told you.
Exodus 31:12 God spoke to Moses and said,
Exodus 31:13 Tell the people of Israel this: You must keep my Sabbaths, for they are a sign between us for all time, to show that I, God, make you holy.
Exodus 31:14 Keep the Sabbath because it is sacred to you. Anyone who disrespects it will be put to death. If anyone does work on that day, they will be separated from their people.
Exodus 31:15 You can work for six days; but the seventh day is a rest day, special to God: if anyone works on that day, they must be put to death.
Exodus 31:16 So the children of Israel must keep the Sabbath and always remember to observe the Sabbath as a lasting agreement.
Exodus 31:17 This is a sign between me and the people of Israel forever: because in six days God made the sky and land, and on the seventh day he rested and felt renewed.
Exodus 31:18 God gave Moses two stone tablets with His laws after speaking to him on Mount Sinai.

Exodus 32:1 When the people saw Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they went to Aaron and said, "Get up, make us gods to lead us. We don't know what happened to Moses, who brought us out of Egypt."
Exodus 32:2 Aaron told them, "Take off the gold earrings that your wives, sons, and daughters are wearing, and bring them to me."
Exodus 32:3 Everyone took off their gold earrings and gave them to Aaron.
Exodus 32:4 He took the gold from them, made it into a statue of a young cow with a tool, and they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of Egypt."
Exodus 32:5 When Aaron saw it, he made an altar in front of it; Aaron announced and said, "Tomorrow is a feast to God."
Exodus 32:6 They got up early the next day, gave burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings; then the people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to have fun.
Exodus 32:7 God said to Moses, "Go down, because your people whom you led out of Egypt have become corrupt."
Exodus 32:8 They quickly left the path I ordered them to follow. They made a golden calf, worshiped it, sacrificed to it, and said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of Egypt."
Exodus 32:9 God said to Moses, "I have seen these people, and they are very stubborn."
Exodus 32:10 So now, leave me alone so that my anger can grow strong against them, and I can destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation.
Exodus 32:11 Moses pleaded with God and said, "God, why are you so angry with your people whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?"
Exodus 32:12 Why should the Egyptians say, "He brought them out to harm them, to kill them in the mountains, and to wipe them off the earth"? Stop being so angry and change your mind about this bad plan for your people.
Exodus 32:13 Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you promised by yourself and told them, I will increase your descendants like the stars in the sky, and all this land that I have mentioned, I will give to your descendants, and they will own it forever.
Exodus 32:14 God felt sorry for the bad things he planned to do to his people.
Exodus 32:15 Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two stone tablets of God's law in his hands. These tablets had writing on both sides.
Exodus 32:16 The tablets were made by God, and the writing on them was God's writing, carved into the tablets.
Exodus 32:17 When Joshua heard the people shouting, he told Moses, "There's a sound of fighting in the camp."
Exodus 32:18 He said, "This isn't the sound of victory shouts or defeat cries, but I hear the sound of singing."
Exodus 32:19 When he got close to the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses became very angry. He threw down the stone tablets and broke them at the foot of the mountain.
Exodus 32:20 He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, crushed it into dust, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Exodus 32:21 Moses said to Aaron, "What did these people do to you to make you lead them into such a big sin?"
Exodus 32:22 Aaron said, "Please don't be angry, you know the people are prone to do wrong."
Exodus 32:23 They said to me, "Make gods for us to lead us because we don't know what happened to Moses, who led us out of Egypt."
Exodus 32:24 I told them, "Anyone who has gold, take it off." So they gave it to me. I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf.
Exodus 32:25 When Moses saw that the people had no clothes (because Aaron had let them take off their clothes, making them ashamed in front of their enemies),
Exodus 32:26 Moses stood at the camp entrance and asked, "Who is on God's side? Come to me." Then all the Levites gathered around him.
Exodus 32:27 He told them, "God of Israel says, 'Each man strap on his sword, move around from gate to gate in the camp, and kill every man his brother, friend, and neighbor.'"
Exodus 32:28 The Levi's children followed Moses' instructions, and that day about three thousand men died.
Exodus 32:29 Moses said, "Make yourselves holy for God today, each one of you on your son and brother, so He can give you a blessing today."
Exodus 32:30 The next day, Moses told the people, "You have committed a serious sin. Now, I will go to God; maybe I can make up for your sin."
Exodus 32:31 Moses went back to God and said, "Oh, these people have done a big sin by making gold idols for themselves."
Exodus 32:32 But now, if you will forgive their sin, do so; but if not, please remove my name from your book that you have written.
Exodus 32:33 God said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, I will erase his name from my book."
Exodus 32:34 So now go, lead the people to the place I told you about. An angel will go ahead of you. But when I check on them, I will punish them for their sins.
Exodus 32:35 God punished the people because they created the calf that Aaron made.

Exodus 33:1 God told Moses, "Leave this place and take the people you brought from Egypt to the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying 'I will give it to your descendants.'"
Exodus 33:2 I will send an angel ahead of you; I will push out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Exodus 33:3 To a land filled with plenty and sweetness: because I will not travel with you; you are stubborn people: otherwise I might destroy you on the journey.
Exodus 33:4 When the people heard this bad news, they were sad, and no one put on their jewelry.
Exodus 33:5 God told Moses to tell the Israelites, "You are stubborn. I will suddenly come to you and punish you. So now, take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you."
Exodus 33:6 The Israelites took off their jewelry at Mount Horeb.
Exodus 33:7 Moses set up the tent far outside the camp and named it the Meeting Tent. Anyone who wanted to seek God would go to the Meeting Tent, which was outside the camp.
Exodus 33:8 When Moses went to the meeting tent, all the people stood up, each at their tent entrance, and watched Moses until he entered the tent.
Exodus 33:9 When Moses went into the tent, a cloud came down and stopped at the entrance, and God spoke with Moses.
Exodus 33:10 Everyone saw the cloud pillar at the tent entrance, and they all stood up and worshiped at their own tent doors.
Exodus 33:11 God spoke to Moses directly, as one speaks to a friend. Then Moses went back to the camp, but his helper Joshua, a young man, did not leave the tent.
Exodus 33:12 Moses said to God, "Look, you tell me, 'Take these people up,' but you haven't told me who you will send with me. Still, you have said, 'I know your name, and you have found favor with me.'"
Exodus 33:13 So now, please, if I have your favor, show me your way so I can know you and continue to find favor with you. Remember that this nation is your people.
Exodus 33:14 He said, "My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."
Exodus 33:15 He said to him, "If you don't go with us, don't take us from here."
Exodus 33:16 How can it be known that I and your people are special to you? Isn't it because you are with us? This is what sets us apart from everyone else in the world.
Exodus 33:17 God said to Moses, "I will do what you asked for, because you have gained my favor and I know you by name."
Exodus 33:18 He said, "Please, show me your glory, God."
Exodus 33:19 He said, "I will let my goodness go by in front of you, and I will say God's name to you; I will be kind to those I choose to be kind to, and I will show mercy on those I decide to show mercy."
Exodus 33:20 He said, "You cannot see my face because no one can see me and stay alive."
Exodus 33:21 God said, "Look, there is a place near me, and you will stand on a rock."
Exodus 33:22 When my glory goes by, I will put you in a gap in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed.
Exodus 33:23 I will remove my hand, and you will see my back, but my face will not be seen.

Exodus 34:1 God told Moses, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets that you broke."
Exodus 34:2 Get ready in the morning, go up Mount Sinai, and meet me at the top of the mountain.
Exodus 34:3 No one should go up with you, and no one should be seen anywhere on the mountain; also, do not let sheep or cattle graze in front of that mountain.
Exodus 34:4 He cut two stone tablets like the first ones; Moses got up early in the morning, went up Mount Sinai as God told him, and carried the two stone tablets.
Exodus 34:5 God came down in the cloud, stood with him there, and announced his own name.
Exodus 34:6 God went by him and said, "God, God, kind and forgiving, patient, full of love and truth."
Exodus 34:7 God shows mercy to thousands, forgives wrongdoing, rebellion, and sin, but does not ignore the guilty; He punishes the parents' sins on the children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generation.
Exodus 34:8 Moses quickly bowed his head to the ground and worshiped.
Exodus 34:9 He said, "If I have now found favor with you, God, please, go with us. This is a stubborn people. Forgive our wrongs and sins, and accept us as your own."
Exodus 34:10 He said, "Look, I am making a promise: I will perform amazing acts for your people that have never been done anywhere on Earth or in any nation. All the people around you will see what God will do, and it will be an awesome thing that I'll do with you."
Exodus 34:11 Pay attention to what I order you today: see, I will push out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Exodus 34:12 Be careful not to agree with the people living in the place you're going, so it doesn't become a trap for you.
Exodus 34:13 You must destroy their altars, break their idols, and cut down their sacred places.
Exodus 34:14 You must not worship any other god, because God, who is named Jealous, is a jealous God.
Exodus 34:15 Make sure you don't agree with the people living in the land, or they might follow their own gods, offer sacrifices to them, invite you, and then you eat from their offerings.
Exodus 34:16 If your sons marry their daughters, their daughters will chase after their own gods and will lead your sons to do the same.
Exodus 34:17 Do not make any metal gods for yourself.
Exodus 34:18 Celebrate the feast of bread without yeast. For seven days, eat bread without yeast as I told you, during the month of Abib, because that is when you left Egypt.
Exodus 34:19 Everything born first from a mother is mine, and every first male born from your livestock, whether cow or sheep.
Exodus 34:20 You must trade a lamb for the firstborn donkey. If you don't trade it, then you must kill the donkey. You must also buy back your firstborn sons. No one should come before me with nothing.
Exodus 34:21 Work for six days, but rest on the seventh day; you should rest both when you plow and when you harvest.
Exodus 34:22 Celebrate the Feast of Weeks when you harvest the first wheat, and have a gathering festival at the end of the year.
Exodus 34:23 Three times a year, all your boys must go before God, the God of Israel.
Exodus 34:24 I will force the nations out of your way and expand your territory. No one will want your land when you go to worship God three times a year.
Exodus 34:25 You must not offer the blood of my sacrifice with yeast; and do not let the passover feast sacrifice remain until morning.
Exodus 34:26 Bring the first of your land's early crops to God's house. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Exodus 34:27 God said to Moses, "Write these words down, because with these words I have made an agreement with you and with Israel."
Exodus 34:28 He stayed with God for forty days and nights without eating bread or drinking water. He wrote the Ten Commandments, the words of the agreement, on the tablets.
Exodus 34:29 When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of testimony in his hand, he did not know that his face was radiant because he had spoken with God.
Exodus 34:30 When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, his face was glowing and they were scared to go near him.
Exodus 34:31 Moses called them, and Aaron and all the leaders came back to him, and Moses spoke with them.
Exodus 34:32 Later, all the Israelites approached, and Moses told them everything God had said to him on Mount Sinai.
Exodus 34:33 After Moses finished talking with them, he covered his face with a veil.
Exodus 34:34 But when Moses went to speak with God, he removed the veil until he left. After leaving, he told the people of Israel what he was told to say.
Exodus 34:35 The Israelites saw that Moses' face was glowing, and Moses covered his face with a veil until he went to talk with God again.

Exodus 35:1 Moses brought all the Israelites together and told them, "These are the commands God has given for you to follow."
Exodus 35:2 Work for six days, but the seventh day is a holy day for you, a day of rest for God. Anyone who works on that day will be put to death.
Exodus 35:3 Do not start any fire in your homes on the Sabbath day.
Exodus 35:4 Moses spoke to all the Israelites, saying, "This is what God has commanded."
Exodus 35:5 Bring a gift for God from among yourselves; anyone who wants to give can bring gold, silver, and bronze.
Exodus 35:6 And blue, purple, red, fine cloth, and goat hair.
Exodus 35:7 Red-dyed ram skins, other animal skins, and acacia wood.
Exodus 35:8 Oil for the lamp, spices for the anointing oil, and for the sweet smelling incense.
Exodus 35:9 And onyx stones, and stones for the ephod and breastplate.
Exodus 35:10 Everyone with a wise heart should come and make everything that God has commanded.
Exodus 35:11 God's tent, its covering, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, its posts, and its bases.
Exodus 35:12 The chest, its poles, the lid, and the curtain that covers it,
Exodus 35:13 The table, its poles, all its tools, and the bread on display.
Exodus 35:14 The lampstand for the light, its accessories, its lamps, and the oil for the light.
Exodus 35:15 The altar for incense, its poles, the oil for anointing, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent.
Exodus 35:16 The altar for burning sacrifices, with its bronze grid, its poles, and all its tools, the washbasin and its base,
Exodus 35:17 The curtains of the courtyard, its posts, their bases, and the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard,
Exodus 35:18 The stakes of the tent, and the stakes of the yard, and their ropes,
Exodus 35:19 The special clothes for serving in the sacred space, the holy outfits for Aaron the priest, and the clothes for his sons to serve as priests.
Exodus 35:20 The whole group of Israel's people left from being with Moses.
Exodus 35:21 They came, everyone moved by their heart, and all who felt willing, and they brought God's offering for the work on the meeting tent, all its service, and the holy clothes.
Exodus 35:22 Men and women came, all who wanted to help. They brought gold bracelets, earrings, rings, and other jewelry. Everyone who gave, gave gold gifts to God.
Exodus 35:23 Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet cloth, fine linen, goats' hair, red sheepskins, or leather brought them.
Exodus 35:24 Everyone who gave silver or brass brought it to God, and anyone who had acacia wood for the work brought it.
Exodus 35:25 All the skilled women spun thread with their hands and brought what they made, in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.
Exodus 35:26 All the women who felt inspired and skilled spun goat hair.
Exodus 35:27 The leaders brought onyx stones and other gems for the priest's garment and chest piece.
Exodus 35:28 And spices, and oil for the lamp, and for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
Exodus 35:29 The people of Israel willingly gave offerings to God, each man and woman who wanted to contribute to all kinds of work, which God had instructed Moses to oversee.
Exodus 35:30 Moses told the people of Israel, "Look, God has chosen Bezaleel, Uri's son, Hur's grandson, from the tribe of Judah by name.
Exodus 35:31 He has filled him with God's spirit, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill in all kinds of crafts.
Exodus 35:32 To create intricate designs and to work with gold, silver, and bronze.
Exodus 35:33 In shaping stones to place them, and in carving wood to create any kind of skilled work.
Exodus 35:34 God has given him the ability to teach, both him and Aholiab, Ahisamach's son from the tribe of Dan.
Exodus 35:35 He has given them skilled hearts to do every kind of work: engraving, expert crafting, and embroidering with blue, purple, scarlet thread and fine linen, and weaving. They can do any job and create intricate designs.

Exodus 36:1 Bezaleel, Aholiab, and every skilled person whom God gave wisdom and understanding knew how to do all kinds of work for the sanctuary service, just as God had instructed.
Exodus 36:2 Moses called Bezaleel, Aholiab, and every skilled person whom God had given wisdom, and everyone who felt moved to come and do the work.
Exodus 36:3 They took from Moses all the gifts the Israelites had brought for the sanctuary's service work. And every morning, they also brought voluntary gifts to him.
Exodus 36:4 All the skilled people who did the work for the holy place stopped their own tasks and came.
Exodus 36:5 They said to Moses, "The people are giving more than needed for the work that God ordered us to do."
Exodus 36:6 Moses ordered and they announced in the camp, "No man or woman should make anything more for the sanctuary offering." So the people stopped bringing things.
Exodus 36:7 They had enough materials for all the work, and more than needed.
Exodus 36:8 Every skilled worker among them who made the tabernacle created ten curtains from fine linen, blue, purple, and red fabric, with artistic designs of cherubs woven into them.
Exodus 36:9 One curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide, and all the curtains were the same size.
Exodus 36:10 He joined five curtains together and then joined the other five curtains in the same way.
Exodus 36:11 He made blue loops on the edge of one curtain by the seam, and did the same on the edge of the other curtain where it joined the second.
Exodus 36:12 He made fifty loops on one curtain, and fifty loops on the edge of the second curtain to join them together. The loops connected one curtain to the other.
Exodus 36:13 He made fifty gold clasps and used them to attach the curtains together, so they became one tent.
Exodus 36:14 He made eleven goat hair curtains to cover the tent that was over the sanctuary.
Exodus 36:15 Each curtain was thirty units long and four units wide; all eleven curtains were the same size.
Exodus 36:16 He joined five curtains together, and six curtains together.
Exodus 36:17 He made fifty loops on the very end of one curtain for joining, and fifty loops on the edge of the second curtain to connect them.
Exodus 36:18 He made fifty bronze clasps to connect the tent so it would be one piece.
Exodus 36:19 He made a red-dyed ram skin cover for the tent and another cover of badger skins on top.
Exodus 36:20 He made upright boards for the tabernacle out of acacia wood.
Exodus 36:21 A board was ten units long and one and a half units wide.
Exodus 36:22 Each board had two pegs set evenly apart: he did this for all the tabernacle's boards.
Exodus 36:23 He made panels for the tent; twenty panels for the south side facing south.
Exodus 36:24 He made forty silver bases for the twenty planks; each plank had two bases for its two projections.
Exodus 36:25 For the other side of the tent, facing north, he made twenty boards.
Exodus 36:26 They had forty silver bases; two bases under one plank, and two bases under another plank.
Exodus 36:27 He made six boards for the west side of the tabernacle.
Exodus 36:28 He made two boards for the corners of the tent on both sides.
Exodus 36:29 They were joined at the bottom and connected at the top to one ring. This was done for both of them at the two corners.
Exodus 36:30 There were eight boards; each had two silver sockets underneath, making sixteen sockets in total.
Exodus 36:31 He made poles of acacia wood; five for the panels on one side of the tent.
Exodus 36:32 Make five crossbars for the frames on the other side of the tent and five crossbars for the frames at the west end.
Exodus 36:33 He made the center bar to go through the boards from one end to the other.
Exodus 36:34 He covered the boards with gold, made their rings of gold for the bars, and covered the bars with gold.
Exodus 36:35 He made a curtain of blue, purple, and red, and quality linen, skillfully woven with angel designs.
Exodus 36:36 He made four pillars of acacia wood for it, covered them with gold, with gold hooks, and made four silver bases for them.
Exodus 36:37 He made a curtain for the entrance of the tent with blue, purple, and red colors, and with finely twisted linen, that was sewn.
Exodus 36:38 It had five pillars with hooks, and he covered the tops and bands with gold; the five bases were bronze.

Exodus 37:1 Bezaleel made the ark from acacia wood: it was 2.5 cubits long, 1.5 cubits wide, and 1.5 cubits high.
Exodus 37:2 He covered it with pure gold inside and outside and put a gold border around it.
Exodus 37:3 He made four gold rings for it, placing them at its four corners; two rings on one side and two on the other side.
Exodus 37:4 He made poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold.
Exodus 37:5 He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the chest to carry it.
Exodus 37:6 He made the cover out of pure gold; it was three and a half feet long and two and a quarter feet wide.
Exodus 37:7 He made two gold cherubs from one piece of gold and put them on both ends of the mercy seat.
Exodus 37:8 One angel on one end here, and another angel on the other end there: the angels on both ends were made from the mercy seat.
Exodus 37:9 The cherubim spread their wings up high and covered the mercy seat with their wings, facing each other; their faces were toward the mercy seat.
Exodus 37:10 He made a table of acacia wood: it was two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
Exodus 37:11 He covered it with pure gold and added a gold border around it.
Exodus 37:12 He also made a border about a hand's breadth wide around it, and put a gold rim around the border.
Exodus 37:13 He made four gold rings and attached them to its four corners on the legs.
Exodus 37:14 Next to the edge were the rings, the spots for the poles to carry the table.
Exodus 37:15 He made the poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold to carry the table.
Exodus 37:16 He made the items for the table—his plates, spoons, cups, and lids to cover them—all out of pure gold.
Exodus 37:17 He made the lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand, its base and branches, its cups, buds, and blossoms, were all one piece.
Exodus 37:18 The lampstand has six branches coming from its sides; three branches come out from one side, and three branches come out from the other side.
Exodus 37:19 Each of the six branches has three cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and petals.
Exodus 37:20 The candlestick had four cups shaped like almonds, with buds and blossoms.
Exodus 37:21 Place a knob under two branches, and do the same for each pair of the six branches coming from the lampstand.
Exodus 37:22 Their buds and branches were all one piece; it was all made of pure gold that had been hammered into shape.
Exodus 37:23 He made seven lamps, lamp trimmers, and trays out of pure gold.
Exodus 37:24 He made it of a talent of pure gold, along with all its utensils.
Exodus 37:25 He made the altar for burning incense out of acacia wood. It was one cubit long and one cubit wide, square-shaped, and two cubits high with horns made from the same wood.
Exodus 37:26 He covered it with pure gold, the top, the sides all around, and its horns; he also made a gold border around it.
Exodus 37:27 He made two gold rings below its molding, at its two corners, on both sides, to hold the poles for carrying it.
Exodus 37:28 He made the poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold.
Exodus 37:29 He made the sacred oil for anointing and the pure, sweet-smelling incense, as a perfumer would.

Exodus 38:1 He made the altar for burnt offerings from acacia wood: it was five cubits long and five cubits wide, forming a square, and it was three cubits high.
Exodus 38:2 He made horns on its four corners; the horns were part of it, and he covered it with bronze.
Exodus 38:3 He made all the altar tools—the pots, shovels, basins, meat hooks, and firepans—all of brass.
Exodus 38:4 He made a bronze grate with a mesh design for the altar, to fit under it halfway up.
Exodus 38:5 He put four rings on the four corners of the bronze grate to hold the poles.
Exodus 38:6 He made the poles out of acacia wood and covered them with bronze.
Exodus 38:7 He placed the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar to carry it; he built the altar with hollow boards.
Exodus 38:8 He made the basin of bronze and its stand of bronze, from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Exodus 38:9 He made the courtyard with fine linen curtains, a hundred cubits long, on the south side.
Exodus 38:10 There were twenty pillars and twenty bronze bases; the hooks and bands of the pillars were silver.
Exodus 38:11 For the north side, the curtains were 100 cubits long, with 20 pillars and 20 bronze bases; the hooks of the pillars and the bands were silver.
Exodus 38:12 For the west side, there were curtains fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases; the hooks of the posts and the bands around them were silver.
Exodus 38:13 For the east side, facing east, fifty cubits.
Exodus 38:14 The curtains on one side of the entrance were fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
Exodus 38:15 On both sides of the courtyard gate, there were curtains 15 cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
Exodus 38:16 All the curtains surrounding the courtyard were made of fine twisted linen.
Exodus 38:17 The bases for the pillars were made of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were made of silver; their capitals were covered with silver; and all the pillars of the courtyard were banded with silver.
Exodus 38:18 The curtain for the courtyard gate was made with fine linen and embroidered with blue, purple, and red thread. It was twenty cubits long and five cubits high, just like the other curtains of the courtyard.
Exodus 38:19 They had four pillars with four bronze bases, silver hooks, and their capitals and bands were covered with silver.
Exodus 38:20 All the hooks for the tent and the surrounding courtyard were made of brass.
Exodus 38:21 This is the total of the meeting tent, the tent for witnessing, as it was recorded, as Moses ordered, for the Levites' work, done by Ithamar, Aaron the priest's son.
Exodus 38:22 Bezaleel, Uri's son and Hur's grandson from the Judah tribe, made everything that God told Moses to make.
Exodus 38:23 Aholiab, son of Ahisamach from the tribe of Dan, was with him. He was skilled in engraving and craft work, and he embroidered with blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.
Exodus 38:24 All the gold used for the work in the holy place, including the gold given as an offering, was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels, by the sanctuary's weight standard.
Exodus 38:25 The congregation's counted silver was one hundred talents and 1,775 shekels, by the sanctuary's standard.
Exodus 38:26 Each man must pay half a shekel, using the sanctuary's measure, for the census of everyone 20 years old and above, totaling 603,550 men.
Exodus 38:27 From the hundred pieces of silver, the bases for the holy place and the curtain were made; a hundred bases from the hundred pieces of silver, one piece for each base.
Exodus 38:28 With 1,775 shekels, he made hooks for the columns, covered their tops, and decorated them.
Exodus 38:29 The bronze given as a gift was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
Exodus 38:30 With it, he made the bases for the entrance of the meeting tent, the bronze altar, its bronze grate, and all the tools for the altar.
Exodus 38:31 The bases of the courtyard all around, the bases of the courtyard gate, and all the pegs for the tent, and all the pegs for the courtyard all around.

Exodus 39:1 They made special cloths in blue, purple, and red to serve in the holy area and created holy clothes for Aaron, just as God told Moses.
Exodus 39:2 He made the ephod from gold, blue, purple, and red threads, and fine linen.
Exodus 39:3 They hammered the gold into thin sheets and sliced it into threads to weave into the blue, purple, and red fabrics, and fine linen with skillful design.
Exodus 39:4 They created shoulder parts for it to join it together; it was joined at the two sides.
Exodus 39:5 The decorative belt of his vest, made of gold, blue, purple, and red threads and fine linen, was just like the rest of it, as God told Moses.
Exodus 39:6 They crafted onyx stones set in gold fittings, engraved like seal rings, with the names of Israel's children.
Exodus 39:7 He placed them on the ephod's shoulders to be reminder stones for the Israelites, just as God had instructed Moses.
Exodus 39:8 He made the special chest piece with skilled work, like the ephod's work; using gold, blue, purple, and red threads, and quality linen woven tightly.
Exodus 39:9 It was square; the chest piece was made double-layered: it was a handspan long and a handspan wide when folded.
Exodus 39:10 They placed four rows of stones in it: the first row had a ruby, a topaz, and a garnet; this was the first row.
Exodus 39:11 In the second row there was an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
Exodus 39:12 The third row had a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
Exodus 39:13 The fourth row had a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper, all set in gold frames.
Exodus 39:14 The stones matched the names of Israel's children, twelve for each name, carved like a seal with each one's name, for the twelve tribes.
Exodus 39:15 They put chains of twisted, pure gold on the chest piece corners.
Exodus 39:16 They made two gold clasps and two gold rings; they attached the rings to the two corners of the chest piece.
Exodus 39:17 They attached the two twisted gold chains to the two rings on the edges of the chest piece.
Exodus 39:18 They attached both ends of the twisted chains to the settings and put them on the shoulder straps of the priestly vest, at the front.
Exodus 39:19 They made two gold rings and placed them on the breastplate's two ends, on its edge, next to the ephod inside.
Exodus 39:20 They made two more gold rings and placed them on the ephod's sides, near the front, opposite the other set, above the decorative belt.
Exodus 39:21 They tied the breastplate to the ephod with blue cord, so it would sit above the ephod's decorative belt and not come loose, just as God told Moses.
Exodus 39:22 He made the ephod's robe of woven fabric, all in blue.
Exodus 39:23 The robe had a hole in the middle, like the hole in armor, with a band around it so it wouldn't tear.
Exodus 39:24 They attached blue, purple, and red pomegranates with twisted linen to the edges of the robe.
Exodus 39:25 They made pure gold bells and placed them among the pomegranates on the robe's hem all around.
Exodus 39:26 A bell and a fruit, a bell and a fruit, all around the bottom of the robe for serving, just as God told Moses.
Exodus 39:27 They made fine linen coats with woven designs for Aaron and his sons.
Exodus 39:28 A hat of fine linen, nice caps of fine linen, and linen shorts of fine twisted linen.
Exodus 39:29 A belt of fine linen, twisted with blue, purple, and red threads, embroidered as God told Moses.
Exodus 39:30 They made the holy crown's plate out of pure gold and engraved on it, like a seal, "Holiness to God."
Exodus 39:31 They attached a blue cord to it to tie it to the top of the turban, as God told Moses.
Exodus 39:32 All the work for the tabernacle, the meeting tent, was completed. The Israelites followed all the instructions God gave to Moses.
Exodus 39:33 They brought the sacred tent to Moses, with all its equipment, its hooks, frames, bars, posts, and bases.
Exodus 39:34 The coverings made of red-dyed ram skins, the coverings of sea cow hides, and the curtain of the tent.
Exodus 39:35 The box with God's rules, its poles, and the lid with forgiveness.
Exodus 39:36 The table, all its dishes, and the bread on display,
Exodus 39:37 The clean lampstand and its lamps, the lamps arranged properly, all its tools, and the oil for lighting.
Exodus 39:38 The gold altar, the special oil, the sweet-smelling incense, and the curtain for the tent entrance.
Exodus 39:39 The bronze altar, its bronze grid, its poles, and all its tools, the washbasin and its base,
Exodus 39:40 The curtains of the courtyard, its columns, and bases, the curtain for the gate of the courtyard, its ropes, and stakes, and all the tools used in the service of the meeting tent.
Exodus 39:41 The special clothes for serving in the sacred area, the holy outfits for Aaron the priest, and clothes for his sons to serve as priests.
Exodus 39:42 Just as God told Moses, the Israelites did all the work.
Exodus 39:43 Moses looked at all the work, and saw they had done it just as God had commanded, so he blessed them.

Exodus 40:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 40:2 On the first day of the first month, you will set up the meeting tent's tabernacle.
Exodus 40:3 Place the Ark of the Covenant inside, and hang the curtain in front of the Ark.
Exodus 40:4 Bring in the table and arrange the items on it; then bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.
Exodus 40:5 Place the gold altar for the incense in front of the ark of the covenant and hang the curtain at the entrance of the tent.
Exodus 40:6 Place the altar for burnt offerings in front of the entrance to the tent where people meet with God.
Exodus 40:7 Place the basin between the meeting tent and the altar, and fill it with water.
Exodus 40:8 You will set up the courtyard all around and put up the curtain at the courtyard entrance.
Exodus 40:9 You will take the anointing oil, and anoint the tent of worship, and everything in it, and make it holy, and all its containers: and it will be holy.
Exodus 40:10 You will anoint the altar where offerings are burned, along with all its tools, and make the altar holy: it will be a very holy altar.
Exodus 40:11 Pour oil on the basin and its stand, and make it holy.
Exodus 40:12 Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the meeting tent and wash them with water.
Exodus 40:13 Dress Aaron in the holy clothes, anoint him, and make him holy, so he can serve me as a priest.
Exodus 40:14 Bring his sons and dress them in robes.
Exodus 40:15 You will anoint them just as you anointed their father so they can serve me as priests. Their anointing will be for a priesthood that lasts forever, generation after generation.
Exodus 40:16 Moses did everything just as God had commanded him.
Exodus 40:17 In the first month of the second year, on the first day, the tabernacle was set up.
Exodus 40:18 Moses set up the tent, secured its bases, put up its frames, inserted the crossbars, and raised its posts.
Exodus 40:19 He spread out the tent over the holy tent, and placed the tent's covering on top of it, just as God had instructed Moses.
Exodus 40:20 He took the testimony, placed it in the chest, attached the poles to the chest, and set the cover on top of the chest.
Exodus 40:21 He put the ark in the tent and hung the curtain to cover the ark of the covenant, just as God told Moses to do.
Exodus 40:22 He placed the table in the meeting tent, on the north side of the dwelling, outside the curtain.
Exodus 40:23 He arranged the bread on it before God, as God had instructed Moses.
Exodus 40:24 He placed the lampstand in the meeting tent opposite the table, on the south side of the tent.
Exodus 40:25 He lit the lamps before God as God had told Moses to do.
Exodus 40:26 He placed the gold altar in the meeting tent in front of the curtain.
Exodus 40:27 He burned sweet-smelling incense on it, just as God told Moses.
Exodus 40:28 He put up the curtain at the entrance of the tent.
Exodus 40:29 He placed the altar for burnt sacrifices near the entrance of the meeting tent's tabernacle and gave burnt and grain offerings on it, just as God told Moses.
Exodus 40:30 He placed the basin between the meeting tent and the altar and filled it with water for washing.
Exodus 40:31 Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet there.
Exodus 40:32 When they entered the meeting tent, and as they approached the altar, they washed; just as God told Moses.
Exodus 40:33 He built the courtyard around the tent and the altar, and put up the curtain for the courtyard entrance. So Moses completed the task.
Exodus 40:34 A cloud hid the meeting tent, and God's glory filled the dwelling place.
Exodus 40:35 Moses could not go into the meeting tent because the cloud stayed on it, and God's glory filled the holy tent.
Exodus 40:36 When the cloud lifted above the tent, the Israelites moved forward on their travels.
Exodus 40:37 But if the cloud did not rise, then they did not move until it did.
Exodus 40:38 God's cloud was over the tent during the day, and at night, there was fire in all the Israelites' view during their travels.

Leviticus 1:1 God called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent where people gather, saying,
Leviticus 1:2 Talk to the people of Israel and tell them: If anyone wants to give an offering to God, it should be a farm animal from the herd or flock.
Leviticus 1:3 If he brings a burnt offering from the herd, it must be a flawless male. He must present it by his own choice at the entrance of the meeting tent before God.
Leviticus 1:4 He must place his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on his behalf to forgive him.
Leviticus 1:5 He must kill the bull before God, and Aaron's sons, the priests, will take the blood and sprinkle it all around the altar near the tent of meeting's entrance.
Leviticus 1:6 He will remove the skin of the burned offering and cut it into pieces.
Leviticus 1:7 Aaron's sons, who are priests, will put fire on the altar and arrange the wood on the fire.
Leviticus 1:8 The priests, who are Aaron's sons, will place the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood that is burning on the altar.
Leviticus 1:9 He must wash its inner parts and legs with water. Then the priest will burn everything on the altar as a burnt offering, a fire-made offering with a pleasing aroma to God.
Leviticus 1:10 If his sacrifice comes from the flock, from the sheep or goats, for a burnt offering, he must present a male without defects.
Leviticus 1:11 He will kill the offering on the north side of the altar in front of God, and Aaron's sons, the priests, will sprinkle its blood all around on the altar.
Leviticus 1:12 He will cut it into pieces, including the head and the fat, and the priest will arrange them on the wood that is burning on the altar.
Leviticus 1:13 He must wash the insides and legs with water: then the priest must take and burn it all on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a fire-offering, with a pleasing aroma to God.
Leviticus 1:14 If his burnt offering to God is birds, he must bring turtledoves or young pigeons.
Leviticus 1:15 The priest will take it to the altar, remove its head, and burn it on the altar. The blood will be drained at the side of the altar.
Leviticus 1:16 He will remove its stomach and its feathers and throw them near the altar on the east side, at the place for ashes.
Leviticus 1:17 He should split it to its wings, but not cut it completely. The priest will burn it on the altar with wood on the fire. It is a burnt offering, a fire sacrifice, that smells good to God.

Leviticus 2:1 When someone wants to give a grain offering to God, it must be of fine flour; they are to pour oil on it and add frankincense.
Leviticus 2:2 He must take it to the priests, Aaron's sons. He must scoop out a handful of the flour and oil, along with all the frankincense. The priest will then burn this portion on the altar as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to God.
Leviticus 2:3 Aaron and his sons will get the rest of the grain offering; it is a very holy part of the offerings to God made with fire.
Leviticus 2:4 If you offer a grain gift cooked in an oven, it should be flatbreads without yeast made from fine flour mixed with oil, or thin crackers without yeast spread with oil.
Leviticus 2:5 If your offering is a grain baked in a pan, it should be made of pure flour without yeast, mixed with oil.
Leviticus 2:6 You will cut it into pieces and pour oil on it: it is a food offering.
Leviticus 2:7 If your gift is a grain offering cooked in a pan, make it with fine flour and oil.
Leviticus 2:8 Bring the grain offering made from these things to God. When you give it to the priest, he will take it to the altar.
Leviticus 2:9 The priest will take a part of the grain offering to remember it, and burn it on the altar. It is a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to God.
Leviticus 2:10 Aaron and his sons can have what's left of the grain offering; it is very holy and comes from the offerings made to God by fire.
Leviticus 2:11 Do not use yeast when you make any food offering for God. You must not burn any yeast or honey in a fire offering to God.
Leviticus 2:12 For the offering of the first crops, give them to God, but do not burn them on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
Leviticus 2:13 In all grain offerings you make, you must use salt. Do not forget to add the salt that represents your agreement with God. Include salt with all your offerings.
Leviticus 2:14 If you bring a grain offering of your first crops to God, you must present roasted green heads of grain as the grain offering from your first crops.
Leviticus 2:15 Put oil on it and place frankincense on top: it is a food offering.
Leviticus 2:16 The priest will burn some of the crushed grain and some of the oil, along with all the incense, as a reminder. This is a fire offering to God.

Leviticus 3:1 If his gift is a peace offering sacrifice from the cattle, whether male or female, he must present one without any defects to God.
Leviticus 3:2 He must put his hand on the head of his offering and kill it at the entrance of the meeting tent. Then the sons of Aaron, who are priests, will splash its blood on all sides of the altar.
Leviticus 3:3 He must present part of the peace offering as a fire offering to God; this includes the fat covering the inner parts and all the fat on the inner parts.
Leviticus 3:4 Take out the two kidneys and the fat on them near the flanks, as well as the fatty membrane over the liver along with the kidneys.
