Leviticus 3:5 Aaron's sons will burn it on the altar with the burnt offering that is on top of the wood on the fire. This is a fire offering with a pleasing smell to God.
Leviticus 3:6 If someone presents a peace offering to God from the flock, whether male or female, it must be without any defects.
Leviticus 3:7 If he gives a lamb as his offering, he must present it to God.
Leviticus 3:8 He must put his hand on his offering's head and kill it in front of the meeting tent; and Aaron's sons must splash its blood all around on the altar.
Leviticus 3:9 He must present part of the peace offering as a burnt offering to God; the fat and the entire tail must be removed close to the backbone, along with the fat covering the internal organs and all the fat on the organs.
Leviticus 3:10 God wants the two kidneys and the fat on them, near the belly, and the layer on the liver to be removed along with the kidneys.
Leviticus 3:11 The priest will burn it on the altar; it is the food for the fire offering to God.
Leviticus 3:12 If he brings a goat as his offering, then he must present it before God.
Leviticus 3:13 He will put his hand on its head and kill it in front of the meeting tent. Aaron's sons will splash its blood on the sides of the altar.
Leviticus 3:14 He must present his sacrifice to God, a burnt offering; the fat covering the inner parts and all the fat on the internal organs.
Leviticus 3:15 Take out the two kidneys and the fat on them near the flanks, and the layer on the liver along with the kidneys.
Leviticus 3:16 The priest will burn them on the altar; this is the food of the fire offering that smells sweet: all the fat belongs to God.
Leviticus 3:17 This rule will always apply to all your future families wherever you live: you must not eat fat or blood.

Leviticus 4:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 4:2 Tell the people of Israel, if anyone sins by mistake by breaking any of God's rules about things they should not do, and disobeys any of these rules:
Leviticus 4:3 If the anointed priest sins like the people do, then he must bring a young, perfect bull to God as a sin offering for his sin.
Leviticus 4:4 He must bring the bull to the entrance of the meeting tent in front of God; then he must put his hand on the bull's head and kill it in front of God.
Leviticus 4:5 The priest who is chosen will take some of the bull's blood and bring it to the meeting tent.
Leviticus 4:6 The priest will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before God, in front of the sanctuary's curtain.
Leviticus 4:7 The priest will put some blood on the horns of the incense altar before God, in the meeting tent; and will pour out all the bull's blood at the base of the burnt offering altar, by the entrance of the meeting tent.
Leviticus 4:8 He must remove all the fat from the bull for the sin offering; the fat covering the insides, and all the fat on the insides.
Leviticus 4:9 Take out both kidneys and the fat on them near the flanks, and the fat above the liver with the kidneys.
Leviticus 4:10 The priest took it from the bull used for the peace offering and will burn it on the altar for burnt offerings.
Leviticus 4:11 Take the cow's skin, all its meat, head, legs, insides, and waste.
Leviticus 4:12 Take the entire bull outside the camp to a clean area where ashes are dumped and burn it on wood with fire; burn it where ashes are dumped.
Leviticus 4:13 If the whole community of Israel sins without knowing it, and they do something they should not do against God's commands without realizing it, they are still guilty.
Leviticus 4:14 When the sin they committed becomes known, the people must offer a young bull for the sin and bring it to the tent where they meet.
Leviticus 4:15 The leaders of the people will put their hands on the bull's head before God, and the bull will be killed before God.
Leviticus 4:16 The priest who has been anointed will take some of the bull's blood to the meeting tent.
Leviticus 4:17 The priest will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in front of God, near the curtain.
Leviticus 4:18 He will put some of the blood on the altar's horns in front of God, in the tent where people meet, and pour all the blood at the base of the altar for burnt offerings, near the entrance of the meeting tent.
Leviticus 4:19 He must take all the fat from the animal and burn it on the altar.
Leviticus 4:20 He must treat this bull just like the sin offering bull; the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
Leviticus 4:21 He shall take the bull outside the camp and burn it as he did the first bull: it is a sin offering for the people.
Leviticus 4:22 When a leader sins and unknowingly breaks any of God's commands about things that should not be done, and is guilty;
Leviticus 4:23 If he realizes his sin, he must bring a perfect male goat as his offering.
Leviticus 4:24 He must put his hand on the goat's head and kill it where they sacrifice burnt offerings to God; it is an offering for sin.
Leviticus 4:25 The priest will take some blood from the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the corners of the altar for burnt sacrifices, and then pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar for burnt sacrifices.
Leviticus 4:26 He must burn all the fat on the altar, just like the fat from peace offerings. The priest will then perform a ritual for his sin, and he will be forgiven.
Leviticus 4:27 If someone ordinary sins by mistake, doing something against God's commands that should not be done, that person is guilty.
Leviticus 4:28 If he realizes his sin, he must bring a perfect female goat as an offering for his sin.
Leviticus 4:29 He must put his hand on the sin offering's head and kill it where they kill the burnt offerings.
Leviticus 4:30 The priest will take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the altar's horns, and then pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
Leviticus 4:31 He must remove all the fat just like the fat is removed from the peace offering; the priest will burn it on the altar to please God; the priest will perform a cleansing for him, and he will be forgiven.
Leviticus 4:32 If he offers a lamb as a sin sacrifice, he must bring a perfect female.
Leviticus 4:33 He must put his hand on the sin offering's head and kill it where they sacrifice the burnt offering.
Leviticus 4:34 The priest will take some blood from the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the corners of the altar for burnt sacrifices, and then pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
Leviticus 4:35 He will remove all the fat like the fat removed from the peace offering lamb; the priest will burn it on the altar as a fire offering to God. The priest will perform a ritual to forgive his sin, and he will be forgiven.

Leviticus 5:1 If a person sins, hears someone swear an oath, and is a witness, knowing or seeing what happened, but doesn't speak up, then that person will be guilty.
Leviticus 5:2 If someone touches anything dirty, like the dead body of an unclean animal, or dead unclean livestock, or dead unclean crawling creatures, without realizing it, that person will be unclean and guilty.
Leviticus 5:3 If he touches anything unclean relating to a person, any kind of human uncleanness, and is not aware of it but later realizes it, he is guilty.
Leviticus 5:4 If someone promises to do something bad or good without realizing it, and later they understand what they promised, they are responsible for their promise.
Leviticus 5:5 When he realizes his guilt in any of these matters, he must admit that he has sinned.
Leviticus 5:6 He must bring a guilt offering to God for the sin he committed, either a female sheep or goat, for a sin sacrifice; and the priest will make amends for his sin.
Leviticus 5:7 If he can't afford a lamb, he must bring two doves or two young pigeons to God for his guilt—one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
Leviticus 5:8 He must take them to the priest, who will sacrifice the sin offering first, then twist off its head without separating it from the body.
Leviticus 5:9 He must sprinkle some of the sin offering's blood on the altar's side; the rest of the blood must be poured out at the altar's base: it is a sin offering.
Leviticus 5:10 He must present the second as a burnt offering in the right way. The priest will perform a ritual to forgive his sin, and he will be forgiven.
Leviticus 5:11 If he can't afford two doves or two young pigeons, the person who sinned must bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not add oil or frankincense to it because it is a sin offering.
Leviticus 5:12 He must take it to the priest, and the priest will grab a handful of it as a reminder and burn it on the altar as a fire offering to God; it is an offering for sin.
Leviticus 5:13 The priest will make up for his sin that he sinned in one of these cases, and he will be forgiven; the leftover will belong to the priest, like a food offering.
Leviticus 5:14 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 5:15 If someone does something wrong by mistake against the sacred things of God, they must bring a perfect ram from their flock, estimated in silver shekels according to the holy standards, as a penalty offering to God.
Leviticus 5:16 He must pay for the damage he did to the sacred things, add one-fifth more, and give it to the priest. The priest will use the ram for the guilt offering to make things right for him, and he will be forgiven.
Leviticus 5:17 If someone sins and does something God's commands say not to do, even if they didn't know it, they're still guilty and must accept the consequences.
Leviticus 5:18 He must bring a perfect ram from the flock, valued by you, for a guilt offering to the priest. The priest will perform a ritual to make up for his mistake which he did without knowing, and he will be forgiven.
Leviticus 5:19 It is a guilt offering: he has truly done wrong against God.

Leviticus 6:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 6:2 If someone sins, breaks faith with God, and lies to a friend about something entrusted to them, shared in partnership, stolen, or if they have cheated their friend;
Leviticus 6:3 Or if someone finds something lost and lies about it, or swears falsely, in any of these things that a person does, they sin.
Leviticus 6:4 He must make up for what he did because he sinned and is guilty. He has to return what he stole, what he got by lying, what was given to him to look after, or what he found and kept.
Leviticus 6:5 If someone lies about anything they own, they must give back the original amount plus an extra fifth to the person it belongs to, on the day they present their guilt offering.
Leviticus 6:6 He must bring his guilt offering to God, a perfect ram from the flock, valued by you, as a guilt offering to the priest.
Leviticus 6:7 The priest will ask God to forgive him, and he will be forgiven for any wrong he has done.
Leviticus 6:8 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 6:9 Tell Aaron and his sons, this is the rule for the burnt offering: It remains on the altar burning all night until morning, and the altar's fire must keep burning.
Leviticus 6:10 The priest will wear his linen clothes and linen underwear next to his skin, and he will remove the ashes left by the fire from the burnt offering on the altar and place them next to the altar.
Leviticus 6:11 He must take off his clothes, put on different clothes, and take the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
Leviticus 6:12 The fire on the altar must keep burning; it must not go out. Every morning the priest will add wood to the fire, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat of the fellowship offerings on it.
Leviticus 6:13 The fire on the altar must keep burning; it must not go out.
Leviticus 6:14 This is the rule for the grain offering: Aaron's sons must present it to God in front of the altar.
Leviticus 6:15 He should take a handful of the flour and oil from the grain offering, along with all of its frankincense, and burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma, as a reminder to God.
Leviticus 6:16 Aaron and his sons will eat the rest of it. They must eat it with bread without yeast in a sacred area—the courtyard of the tent where people meet.
Leviticus 6:17 Do not bake it with yeast. I have given it to them as their share of my offerings burned with fire; it is very holy, just like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Leviticus 6:18 Every male in Aaron's family may eat from it. This rule about God's offerings made with fire will last forever for your descendants: anyone who touches them must be holy.
Leviticus 6:19 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 6:20 Aaron and his sons will give this gift to God on the day he is chosen: one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a regular food offering, half in the morning and half at night.
Leviticus 6:21 Cook it in a pan with oil. When it's baked, bring it in. Offer the baked pieces of the grain offering as a pleasing aroma to God.
Leviticus 6:22 The son priest who takes his place and is anointed will offer it: this is a permanent rule for God; it must be completely burned.
Leviticus 6:23 Every food offering for the priest must be completely burned; it must not be eaten.
Leviticus 6:24 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 6:25 Tell Aaron and his sons, 'This is the rule for the sin offering: Kill the sin offering in the same place as the burnt offering—it's very holy, and it must be done before God.
Leviticus 6:26 The priest who sacrifices it for a sin will eat it. It must be eaten in a holy area, inside the courtyard of the meeting tent.
Leviticus 6:27 Anything that touches its meat will be sacred; and if any of its blood is splashed on clothes, you must wash them in a sacred place.
Leviticus 6:28 The clay pot used for boiling must be broken, but if it's boiled in a bronze pot, it must be scrubbed and washed with water.
Leviticus 6:29 Every male priest may eat from it; it is very holy.
Leviticus 6:30 Any sin offering whose blood is taken into the meeting tent to make peace in the holy area must not be eaten; it must be burned up.

Leviticus 7:1 This is the rule for the guilt offering: it is very holy.
Leviticus 7:2 In the spot where they kill the burnt sacrifice, they must also kill the guilt sacrifice, and its blood should be sprinkled all around the altar.
Leviticus 7:3 He must offer all of its fat; the tail and the fat covering the insides.
Leviticus 7:4 Take out the two kidneys with the fat around them near the loins, and the fatty tissue above the liver along with the kidneys.
Leviticus 7:5 The priest will burn them on the altar as an offering to God by fire; it is a guilt offering.
Leviticus 7:6 Every male priest may eat it; it must be eaten in a sacred place; it is very holy.
Leviticus 7:7 The sin offering and the trespass offering are the same; there is one rule for both: the priest who uses it to make amends will keep it.
Leviticus 7:8 The priest who presents someone's burnt sacrifice will keep the skin of that burnt offering for himself.
Leviticus 7:9 All the grain offerings baked in the oven, or cooked in the frying pan, or on a griddle, belong to the priest who offers them.
Leviticus 7:10 Every grain offering, mixed with oil or dry, shall be shared equally among Aaron's sons.
Leviticus 7:11 This is the rule for the peace offering sacrifice that a person will give to God.
Leviticus 7:12 If he brings it to say thank you, then with the thank you offering he must bring bread without yeast mixed with oil, thin crackers without yeast covered with oil, and cakes mixed with oil made of fine flour that are cooked.
Leviticus 7:13 Along with the cakes, he must also present yeast bread as part of his thanksgiving peace offering.
Leviticus 7:14 From the offering, one part should be given as a gift to God, and it belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offerings.
Leviticus 7:15 The meat from his peace offering for giving thanks must be eaten on the day it is offered; none of it should be kept until the next morning.
Leviticus 7:16 If his sacrifice is a promise or a free-will gift, it must be eaten on the day he makes his sacrifice. Any leftovers can be eaten the next day.
Leviticus 7:17 The rest of the meat from the offering must be burned on the third day.
Leviticus 7:18 If someone eats any meat from their peace offering on the third day, it won't be accepted, and the person who offered it won't get credit for it. It will be considered disgusting, and the person who eats it will be guilty.
Leviticus 7:19 Meat that touches anything unclean cannot be eaten; it must be burned: and about the meat, all who are clean can eat it.
Leviticus 7:20 But the person who eats from the peace offering sacrifice that belongs to God while they are unclean, that person will be separated from their people.
Leviticus 7:21 Anyone who touches something unclean, like human impurity, an unclean animal, or any unclean disgusting thing, and then eats from the peace offering dedicated to God, that person will be cut off from their community.
Leviticus 7:22 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 7:23 Tell the people of Israel, you must not eat any fat, from a cow, or a sheep, or a goat.
Leviticus 7:24 You can use the fat of an animal that dies on its own or one killed by other animals for other purposes, but you must not eat it.
Leviticus 7:25 Anyone who eats the fat of an animal that is offered as a fire sacrifice to God will be separated from their community.
Leviticus 7:26 You must not eat any kind of blood, from birds or animals, in any place you live.
Leviticus 7:27 Anyone who eats any kind of blood will be separated from their community.
Leviticus 7:28 God spoke to Moses and said.
Leviticus 7:29 Tell the people of Israel, whoever gives their peace offering to God must present it to God as their peace offering gift.
Leviticus 7:30 He must use his own hands to bring God's offerings burnt by fire, the fat and the breast, so he can wave the breast as a wave offering before God.
Leviticus 7:31 The priest will burn the fat on the altar, but the breast will belong to Aaron and his sons.
Leviticus 7:32 Give the right shoulder to the priest as a lifted gift from your peace offerings.
Leviticus 7:33 The priest from Aaron's descendants who presents the blood and fat of the fellowship offering will get the right shoulder as his share.
Leviticus 7:34 I have taken the breast that is waved and the shoulder that is lifted up from the Israelites, from their peace offering sacrifices, and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as their share forever from the Israelites.
Leviticus 7:35 This is the part for Aaron and his sons from the fire offerings to God, on the day they were brought to serve God as priests.
Leviticus 7:36 God ordered this gift from the Israelites to them on the day they were anointed, as a rule to last for all their future generations.
Leviticus 7:37 This is the rule for the burnt offerings, grain offerings, sin offerings, guilt offerings, dedications, and peace offerings.
Leviticus 7:38 God told Moses on Mount Sinai to command the Israelites to give their offerings to God when they were in the Sinai wilderness.

Leviticus 8:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 8:2 Bring Aaron and his sons, their clothes, the anointing oil, a bull for the sin offering, two rams, and a basket of bread without yeast.
Leviticus 8:3 Bring everyone to the entrance of the meeting tent.
Leviticus 8:4 Moses did what God told him; and the people came together at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Leviticus 8:5 Moses told the people, "This is what God has commanded to be done."
Leviticus 8:6 Moses took Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.
Leviticus 8:7 He put the coat on him, tied the belt around him, dressed him in the robe, placed the ephod on him, fastened the beautifully crafted ephod belt, and secured it to him.
Leviticus 8:8 He put the breastplate on him and placed the Urim and Thummim inside it.
Leviticus 8:9 He placed the turban on his head and on the turban, right on the front, he put the gold plate, the sacred crown, just as God told Moses.
Leviticus 8:10 Moses took the special oil and put it on the tent of worship and everything in it to make them holy.
Leviticus 8:11 He sprinkled it on the altar seven times and put oil on the altar and all its tools, as well as the washbasin and its base, to make them holy.
Leviticus 8:12 He put anointing oil on Aaron's head and made him holy by anointing him.
Leviticus 8:13 Moses brought Aaron's sons, dressed them in coats, tied belts around them, and put hats on their heads, just as God told Moses to do.
Leviticus 8:14 He brought the bull for the sin sacrifice, and Aaron and his sons put their hands on the bull's head for the sin sacrifice.
Leviticus 8:15 He killed the animal; Moses took the blood, touched it to the altar's horns all around with his finger to cleanse it, then poured the blood at the base of the altar to make it holy, so it could be used for making peace with God.
Leviticus 8:16 He took all the fat from the insides, the fatty membrane above the liver, both kidneys and their fat, and Moses burned them on the altar.
Leviticus 8:17 The bull, its skin, meat, and poop, were burned with fire outside the camp, as God told Moses.
Leviticus 8:18 He presented the ram for the burnt sacrifice, and Aaron and his sons put their hands on the ram's head.
Leviticus 8:19 He killed it, and Moses splashed the blood around the altar.
Leviticus 8:20 He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses burned the head, the parts, and the fat.
Leviticus 8:21 He washed the insides and the legs with water. Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. This was a burnt offering that smelled good, and a fire offering to God, just like God told Moses to do.
Leviticus 8:22 He brought the second ram, the dedication ram; and Aaron and his sons put their hands on the ram's head.
Leviticus 8:23 He killed it; Moses took some of its blood and put it on the top of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
Leviticus 8:24 He brought Aaron's sons, and Moses put some blood on the top of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet; and Moses sprayed the blood around the altar.
Leviticus 8:25 He took the fat, the back part, all the fat on the insides, the membrane over the liver, both kidneys and their fat, and the right front leg.
Leviticus 8:26 From the basket of bread without yeast in front of God, he took one piece of unleavened bread, a piece of bread mixed with oil, and one thin cracker, and placed them on the fat and the right shoulder.
Leviticus 8:27 He placed everything on Aaron's hands and on his sons' hands and waved them as an offering before God.
Leviticus 8:28 Moses took them from their hands, burned them on the altar with the burnt offering; they were offerings to please God, a fire sacrifice to God.
Leviticus 8:29 Moses took the chest part of the ram and moved it back and forth as a special offering to God. This was Moses' share from the dedication ram, just as God told Moses to do.
Leviticus 8:30 Moses took some anointing oil and some blood from the altar, and he sprinkled it on Aaron, his clothes, his sons, and their clothes; and this made Aaron, his clothes, his sons, and their clothes holy.
Leviticus 8:31 Moses told Aaron and his sons, "Cook the meat at the entrance of the meeting tent, and eat it there with the bread from the dedication basket, just as I instructed, 'Aaron and his sons shall eat it.'"
Leviticus 8:32 Burn with fire whatever is left of the meat and bread.
Leviticus 8:33 Do not leave the entrance of the tent where the meeting is held for seven days, until your dedication time is finished, because you will be set apart for seven days.
Leviticus 8:34 As he has done today, so God has commanded to be done, to forgive you.
Leviticus 8:35 Stay by the entrance of the meeting tent day and night for seven days, and follow God's instructions so you won't die, because this is what I've been ordered to tell you.
Leviticus 8:36 Aaron and his sons did everything that God told them through Moses.

Leviticus 9:1 On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and Israel's elders.
Leviticus 9:2 He told Aaron, "Take a young calf for a sin offering and a perfect ram for a burnt offering, and present them to God."
Leviticus 9:3 Tell the Israelites to take a young goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb—both one year old and without any defects—for a burnt offering.
Leviticus 9:4 Also a bull and a ram for peace sacrifices, to offer to God; and a food offering mixed with oil: because today God will appear to you.
Leviticus 9:5 They brought what Moses ordered to the tent of meeting, and everyone came close and stood before God.
Leviticus 9:6 Moses said, "Do what God has commanded and God's glory will show itself to you."
Leviticus 9:7 Moses told Aaron, "Go to the altar, give your sin offering and your burnt offering to ask for forgiveness for yourself and the people. Also present the people's offering and ask for forgiveness for them, as God commanded."
Leviticus 9:8 Aaron went to the altar and killed the calf for his own sin offering.
Leviticus 9:9 Aaron's sons brought the blood to him, and he touched it with his finger and put it on the altar's horns, and spilled the rest at the base of the altar.
Leviticus 9:10 He burned the fat, the kidneys, and the covering over the liver of the sin offering on the altar, just as God told Moses.
Leviticus 9:11 He burned the meat and the skin with fire outside the camp.
Leviticus 9:12 He killed the burnt offering; Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splashed it all around the altar.
Leviticus 9:13 They gave him the burnt offering with its parts and the head, and he burned them on the altar.
Leviticus 9:14 He washed the insides and legs, and burned them with the burnt offering on the altar.
Leviticus 9:15 He presented the offering from the people, took the goat that was for the people's sin offering, killed it, and sacrificed it for sin, first of all.
Leviticus 9:16 He presented the burnt offering and did it the proper way.
Leviticus 9:17 He brought the grain offering, took a handful, and burned it on the altar, next to the morning's burnt offering.
Leviticus 9:18 He also killed the bull and the ram as a peace offering sacrifice for the people; Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splashed it on all sides of the altar.
Leviticus 9:19 The fat of the ox and the sheep, the back part, everything covering the insides, the kidneys, and the membrane over the liver.
Leviticus 9:20 They placed the fat on the breasts and burned the fat on the altar.
Leviticus 9:21 Aaron waved the chest and the right shoulder as a wave offering before God, just as Moses had instructed.
Leviticus 9:22 Aaron raised his hand to the people, gave them a blessing, and then stepped down after presenting the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
Leviticus 9:23 Moses and Aaron went into the meeting tent, came out, and blessed the people; then God's glory showed to everyone.
Leviticus 9:24 Fire came from God and burned up the offering and the fat on the altar. When the people saw this, they cheered and fell to the ground with their faces down.

Leviticus 10:1 Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons, each took a censer, added fire and incense, and offered unauthorized fire to God, which He had not instructed them to do.
Leviticus 10:2 Fire came from God, consumed them, and they died in God's presence.
Leviticus 10:3 Then Moses told Aaron, "This is what God said, 'I must be honored by those who come close to me, and I must be respected in front of all the people.'" And Aaron was quiet.
Leviticus 10:4 Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, Uzziel's sons and Aaron's nephews, and said to them, "Come here, take your brothers away from in front of the holy place, out of the camp."
Leviticus 10:5 They went close and took them outside the camp in their coats, just as Moses had instructed.
Leviticus 10:6 Moses said to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons, "Do not uncover your heads or tear your clothes, so you will not die and so anger will not come upon everyone. But let your relatives, all the people of Israel, mourn the fire that God has started."
Leviticus 10:7 Do not leave the entrance of the meeting tent, or you will die, because God's special oil is on you. They did as Moses said.
Leviticus 10:8 God spoke to Aaron, saying,
Leviticus 10:9 Do not drink wine or strong drink, you or your sons, when you enter the meeting tent, so you don't die. This rule is forever for all your descendants.
Leviticus 10:10 So you can tell what is holy from what is not, and what is clean from what is unclean.
Leviticus 10:11 So you can teach the Israelites all the rules that God has given them through Moses.
Leviticus 10:12 Moses said to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons, "Take the leftover grain offering from God's fire offerings and eat it without yeast near the altar, because it is very holy."
Leviticus 10:13 You must eat it in the sacred place, because it is your share and your sons' share from God's sacrifices made by fire: this is what I am told to do.
Leviticus 10:14 Eat the waved breast and the raised shoulder in a clean place; you, your sons, and your daughters with you. These are your share and your sons' share from the peace offerings of the people of Israel.
Leviticus 10:15 Bring the lifted shoulder and the waved chest along with the burned fat offerings to present as a waved offering before God; it will be yours and your sons' forever, as God has ordered.
Leviticus 10:16 Moses carefully looked for the goat for the sin sacrifice and saw it was burned. He was mad at Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons who were still alive, and said,
Leviticus 10:17 Why didn't you eat the sin offering in the holy area when it is very holy, and God has given it to you to take away the people's sins and make them right with God?
Leviticus 10:18 Look, its blood was not taken into the holy place; you should have eaten it there, as I instructed.
Leviticus 10:19 Aaron said to Moses, "Look, today they gave their sin offering and burnt offering to God. Such things have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been okay with God?"
Leviticus 10:20 When Moses heard it, he was happy.

Leviticus 11:1 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, telling them,
Leviticus 11:2 Tell the people of Israel, "You can eat these animals from all the animals on the earth."
Leviticus 11:3 Whatever animal has a split hoof and chews the cud among the animals, you can eat.
Leviticus 11:4 You must not eat these animals that chew the cud or have split hooves: the camel chews the cud but does not have a split hoof; it is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:5 The rock badger, because it chews its food again but does not have split hooves, is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:6 The rabbit, because it chews the cud but does not have split hooves, is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:7 Pigs have split hooves but don't chew their food again; they are not clean for you.
Leviticus 11:8 Do not eat their meat or touch their dead bodies; they are unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:9 You can eat any sea creature with fins and scales from the water, sea, or river.
Leviticus 11:10 All creatures in the sea or rivers that do not have fins and scales, and every living thing in the water, are not to be eaten by you.
Leviticus 11:11 You should find them disgusting; do not eat their meat, and consider their dead bodies disgusting too.
Leviticus 11:12 Anything in the water that doesn't have fins or scales is disgusting to you.
Leviticus 11:13 You must hate these birds and never eat them because they are dirty: the eagle, the vulture, and the kite.
Leviticus 11:14 Also the vulture and every kind of kite.
Leviticus 11:15 All kinds of ravens.
Leviticus 11:16 The owl, the nighthawk, the cuckoo, and the hawk, each of its own kind,
Leviticus 11:17 Also the little owl, the cormorant, and the large owl,
Leviticus 11:18 The swan, the pelican, and the vulture,
Leviticus 11:19 Also the stork, all types of herons, the lapwing, and the bat.
Leviticus 11:20 All birds that crawl on four legs must disgust you.
Leviticus 11:21 You can eat any flying insects that walk on four legs and have joints above their legs to jump on the earth.
Leviticus 11:22 You can eat these: different types of locusts, bald locusts, beetles, and grasshoppers.
Leviticus 11:23 But all other flying insects that have four legs will be disgusting to you.
Leviticus 11:24 You will be unclean if you touch the dead body of these animals until evening.
Leviticus 11:25 Anyone who touches any part of a dead animal must wash their clothes and will be unclean until the evening.
Leviticus 11:26 The bodies of any animals that have split hooves but are not completely split or do not chew their food well are not clean for you; anyone who touches them will be unclean.
Leviticus 11:27 Any animal that walks on its paws among all the four-legged animals is unclean to you; anyone who touches their dead body will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:28 Whoever carries their dead body must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening; they are unclean to you.
Leviticus 11:29 These animals are also unclean for you among the ones that crawl on the ground: the weasel, the mouse, and the tortoise of its kind.
Leviticus 11:30 The ferret, the chameleon, the lizard, the snail, and the mole.
Leviticus 11:31 These crawling creatures are impure to you: anyone who touches them after they die will be impure until evening.
Leviticus 11:32 If any of these dead creatures falls on something, that thing will become unclean. This includes any wooden object, clothes, leather, or bag—anything used for work. It must be put in water and will be unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
Leviticus 11:33 If something unclean falls into a clay pot, everything inside it becomes unclean, and you must break the pot.
Leviticus 11:34 All food that can be eaten will become unclean if water touches it; any drink that can be drunk from any container will become unclean too.
Leviticus 11:35 Anything that touches any part of their dead body will be unclean; this includes ovens and cooking stoves, which must be destroyed because they are unclean and will be unclean to you.
Leviticus 11:36 Even so, a spring or well with lots of water will be clean, but anything that touches a dead body will be unclean.
Leviticus 11:37 If any piece of their dead body touches seeds that are to be planted, the seeds are still clean.
Leviticus 11:38 If water touches the seed and any part of a dead body touches it, it becomes unclean to you.
Leviticus 11:39 If an animal you can eat dies, anyone who touches its dead body will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:40 Anyone who eats from the dead body must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening; and anyone who carries the dead body must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:41 Every crawling creature on earth is unclean and must not be eaten.
Leviticus 11:42 Do not eat any creature that crawls on its belly, walks on all fours, or has many legs. They are not to be eaten because they are disgusting.
Leviticus 11:43 Do not make yourself disgusting with any crawling creature, nor make yourself dirty with them, so you don't become unclean through them.
Leviticus 11:44 I am your God, so make yourselves holy and be holy because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean with any crawling creature on the earth.
Leviticus 11:45 I am God who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. So you must be holy, because I am holy.
Leviticus 11:46 This is the rule for animals, birds, all creatures that live in the water, and every creature that crawls on the ground.
Leviticus 11:47 To show the difference between what is unclean and clean, and between animals you can eat and those you cannot.

Leviticus 12:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 12:2 Talk to the Israelites and say, if a woman has a baby and it is a boy, she will be unclean for seven days, just like when she is on her period.
Leviticus 12:3 On the eighth day, the skin of his private part should be cut.
Leviticus 12:4 She must then wait thirty-three days to be purified from her bleeding. She must not touch anything sacred or go to the holy place until her purification period is over.
Leviticus 12:5 If she gives birth to a girl, she will be unclean for two weeks like during her period. She will stay in the blood of her cleansing for 66 days.
Leviticus 12:6 When the time of her cleansing for a son or daughter is complete, she must bring a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or dove for a sin offering to the entrance of the meeting tent, to the priest.
Leviticus 12:7 Who will present it to God and provide a sacrifice for her; she will then be purified from her bleeding. This is the rule for a woman who has given birth to a boy or a girl.
Leviticus 12:8 If she can't afford a lamb, she must bring two doves or two young pigeons; one for a sacrifice to honor God, and the other for a sin offering. The priest will perform a ceremony to forgive her sins, and then she will be pure.

Leviticus 13:1 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Leviticus 13:2 When a person has a swelling, a rash, or a shiny spot on their skin that may be a sign of leprosy, they must go to Aaron the priest or one of his sons who are priests.
Leviticus 13:3 The priest will check the skin disease: if the hair turns white and the disease seems deeper than the skin, it is leprosy. The priest will see this and say the person is not clean.
Leviticus 13:4 If there's a white bright spot on the skin and it's not deeper than the skin and the hair hasn't turned white, the priest must isolate the person with the sickness for seven days.
Leviticus 13:5 On the seventh day, the priest will examine the person, and if the disease has not spread and is not active, the priest will isolate the person for another seven days.
Leviticus 13:6 On the seventh day, the priest will look at the person again. If the infection looks darker and hasn't spread on the skin, the priest will say they are clean. It's only a scab. Then they must wash their clothes and they will be clean.
Leviticus 13:7 If the scab spreads widely on the skin after the priest has checked him for being clean, the priest must examine him again.
Leviticus 13:8 If the priest sees the scab spreading on the skin, the priest must say he is unclean because it is leprosy.
Leviticus 13:9 If a man has leprosy, he must go to the priest.
Leviticus 13:10 The priest must look at him, and if there's a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is fresh, red skin in the swelling.
Leviticus 13:11 The skin disease is serious and old, and the priest will say he is unclean; he won't isolate him because he is already unclean.
Leviticus 13:12 If someone's skin breaks out with leprosy all over from head to foot, wherever the priest checks;
Leviticus 13:13 The priest will look, and if the skin disease has spread over all the person's skin, he will declare the person with the disease clean because it has all become white; the person is clean.
Leviticus 13:14 But if he sees raw flesh, he must be considered unclean.
Leviticus 13:15 The priest will look at the sore skin and say it is not clean: because sore skin is not clean: it is a disease.
Leviticus 13:16 If the sore heals and turns white, he should go to the priest.
Leviticus 13:17 The priest will look at the person and if the disease has become white, the priest will declare that the person with the disease is clean.
Leviticus 13:18 If someone had a boil on their skin and it healed,
Leviticus 13:19 If there's a white swelling or a bright white and reddish spot where the boil was, show it to the priest.
Leviticus 13:20 If the priest sees that the mark looks deeper than the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest must say the person is unclean. It is a case of leprosy that has come from the sore.
Leviticus 13:21 If the priest sees it and there are no white hairs, and it's not below the skin but a bit dark, then the priest must isolate him for seven days.
Leviticus 13:22 If it spreads a lot on the skin, then the priest must say he is not clean: it is a disease.
Leviticus 13:23 If the bright spot stays the same and does not spread, it is a healed boil; the priest will say he is clean.
Leviticus 13:24 If there is a burning sore on someone's skin and the healed part turns white or reddish-white.
Leviticus 13:25 The priest will look at it, and if the hair in the bright area has turned white and it appears to be deeper than the skin, it is leprosy that has come from the sore. So, the priest will say he is not clean; it is leprosy.
Leviticus 13:26 If the priest sees the spot and there is no white hair in it, if it's not deeper than the skin but is dark, then the priest will isolate the person for seven days.
Leviticus 13:27 On the seventh day, the priest will examine him, and if the skin infection has spread widely, the priest will declare him unclean because it is leprosy.
Leviticus 13:28 If the shiny spot stays the same and does not spread on the skin, but gets a little darker, it is a scar from the burn. The priest will say he is clean because it is just the swelling from the burn.
Leviticus 13:29 If a man or woman has a disease on their head or beard;
Leviticus 13:30 The priest will look at the sore, and if it is deeper than the skin and has a thin yellow hair, the priest will declare the person unclean. It is a dry scaly infection, a form of leprosy on the head or beard.
Leviticus 13:31 If the priest sees the scall infection and it's not deeper than the skin, and there's no black hair in it, then the priest will quarantine the person with the scall infection for seven days.
Leviticus 13:32 On the seventh day, the priest will examine the sore. If it hasn't spread, there's no yellow hair, and it's not deeper than the skin,
Leviticus 13:33 He must shave his hair, but not the scall. The priest will isolate the person with the scall for another seven days.
Leviticus 13:34 On the seventh day, the priest will check the scall. If the scall has not spread on the skin or looks deep, the priest will say he is clean. Then he must wash his clothes and will be clean.
Leviticus 13:35 If the rash spreads on the skin after he is cleaned;
Leviticus 13:36 The priest will look at him and if the scall has spread on the skin, the priest won't look for yellow hair; he is unclean.
Leviticus 13:37 If the sore hasn't spread and black hair has grown in it, the sore is healed and the person is clean; the priest will declare them clean.
Leviticus 13:38 If a man or woman has shiny white spots on their skin;
Leviticus 13:39 Then the priest will look, and if there are light white spots on their skin, it's just a common freckle; they are clean.
Leviticus 13:40 If a man loses his hair and becomes bald, he is still clean.
Leviticus 13:41 Anyone whose hair has fallen out from the front of their head is bald on the forehead but is still clean.
Leviticus 13:42 If there is a white and red sore on the bald head or forehead, it is leprosy that has developed on the bald spot.
Leviticus 13:43 The priest will look at it, and if there is a white-red swelling on his bald head or forehead, it is like leprosy on the skin.
Leviticus 13:44 He has leprosy and is not clean. The priest must say he is completely not clean; his disease is on his head.
Leviticus 13:45 The person with leprosy who has the sickness must tear their clothes, leave their head uncovered, cover their upper lip, and shout, "Unclean, unclean."
Leviticus 13:46 Every day the sickness is in him, he is unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
Leviticus 13:47 The piece of clothing that has leprosy, whether it is made of wool or linen;
Leviticus 13:48 Whether it's in the threads, in linen, in wool, in leather, or in anything made of leather;
Leviticus 13:49 If the infection on the clothes or skin looks green or red, whether on the threads or in the fabric or on something made of skin, it is a sign of leprosy and must be shown to the priest.
Leviticus 13:50 The priest will examine the disease and isolate the affected person for seven days.
Leviticus 13:51 On the seventh day, he will check the disease. If the disease has spread in the fabric, whether the threads or the weave, or in leather, or in anything made of leather, the disease is a harmful skin condition; it is not clean.
Leviticus 13:52 He must burn the clothing, whether it is woven or knitted from wool or linen, or made of leather, if it has the disease on it. It is a persistent infection and must be burned with fire.
Leviticus 13:53 If the priest looks and sees the disease has not spread in the cloth, whether woven or knitted, or in anything made of leather;
Leviticus 13:54 The priest will order them to wash the item with the disease, and he will isolate it for another seven days.
Leviticus 13:55 The priest will look at the sickness after washing it. If the sickness hasn't changed color or spread, it's not clean. You must burn it because the disease is deep, whether it shows on the inside or outside.
Leviticus 13:56 If the priest sees that the spot is darker after it has been washed, he must cut it out of the fabric, leather, or woven or knitted material.
Leviticus 13:57 If the problem remains in the cloth, whether in the threads or in anything made of skin, it is a spreading disease: you must burn the infected item with fire.
Leviticus 13:58 If you wash a piece of clothing, whether woven or knitted, or any leather item, and the disease goes away, you must wash it again and then it will be clean.
Leviticus 13:59 This is the rule for a disease like leprosy in clothes made of wool or linen, whether in the threads or in anything made of skin, to say if it is clean or not clean.

Leviticus 14:1 God spoke to Moses and said,
Leviticus 14:2 This will be the rule for the person with leprosy on the day they are cleansed: They must be taken to the priest.
Leviticus 14:3 The priest will go outside the camp; the priest will look, and if the leprosy sores are healed in the person with leprosy,
Leviticus 14:4 The priest will order to get for the person to be cleaned two live, clean birds, cedar wood, red fabric, and hyssop.
Leviticus 14:5 The priest will order that one bird be killed in a clay pot over flowing water.
Leviticus 14:6 Take the live bird, the cedar wood, the red yarn, and the hyssop, and dip them and the live bird in the blood of the bird that was killed over flowing water.
Leviticus 14:7 He must sprinkle the person to be cleansed from leprosy seven times, declare him clean, and release the live bird into the open field.
Leviticus 14:8 The person who needs to be clean must wash their clothes, shave off all their hair, and bathe in water to become clean. After this, they can return to the camp but must stay outside their tent for seven days.
Leviticus 14:9 On the seventh day, he must shave all the hair from his head, beard, and eyebrows. He must shave off all his hair, wash his clothes, and bathe in water to be clean.
Leviticus 14:10 On the eighth day, he must bring two male lambs with no defects, one female lamb less than a year old with no defects, some fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and some oil.
Leviticus 14:11 The priest who cleans the man will bring him and his offerings to God at the entrance of the meeting tent.
Leviticus 14:12 The priest will take one male lamb and give it as a guilt offering, along with the oil, and lift them up as an offering before God.
Leviticus 14:13 He must kill the lamb where he kills the sin and burnt offerings, in the holy place. Like the sin offering belongs to the priest, so does the guilt offering. It is very holy.
Leviticus 14:14 The priest will take some of the blood from the guilt offering and put it on the top of the right ear, the right thumb, and the right big toe of the person who is being cleansed.
Leviticus 14:15 The priest will take some of the oil and pour it into his own left hand.
Leviticus 14:16 The priest will dip his right finger in the oil in his left hand and sprinkle the oil with his finger seven times in front of God.
Leviticus 14:17 The priest will put the rest of the oil from his hand on the right ear, the right thumb, and the right big toe of the person being cleansed, on top of the blood from the guilt offering.
Leviticus 14:18 The priest will pour the rest of the oil in his hand on the head of the person being cleansed, and will ask God to forgive him.
Leviticus 14:19 The priest will offer the sin sacrifice, and make amends for the one being cleansed from his impurity; then he will sacrifice the burnt offering.
Leviticus 14:20 The priest will offer the burnt and grain offerings on the altar, and the priest will make amends for him, so he will be clean.
Leviticus 14:21 If he is poor and can't afford much, he must bring one lamb as a guilt offering to be waved to ask for forgiveness for him, and a small amount of fine flour mixed with oil for a food offering, plus a small jug of oil.
Leviticus 14:22 Bring two doves or two young pigeons, whichever you can afford. One will be for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
Leviticus 14:23 He must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the meeting tent for his cleansing on the eighth day, before God.
Leviticus 14:24 The priest will take the lamb for the guilt offering and the container of oil, and then wave them as an offering before God.
Leviticus 14:25 He must kill the lamb for the guilt offering. The priest will take some of the lamb's blood and put it on the right ear, right thumb, and right big toe of the person being made clean.
Leviticus 14:26 The priest will pour some oil into his left hand.
Leviticus 14:27 The priest will use his right finger to flick some of the oil in his left hand seven times in front of God.
Leviticus 14:28 The priest will put some of the oil from his hand on the top of the right ear, the right thumb, and the big toe of the right foot of the person being cleansed, where the blood from the guilt offering was put.
Leviticus 14:29 The priest will put the remaining oil on the head of the person who needs to be made clean to atone for him before God.
Leviticus 14:30 He must give either one dove or one young pigeon, whatever he can afford.
Leviticus 14:31 He should bring what he can afford: one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, along with a grain offering. The priest will then make atonement for the person to be cleansed before God.
Leviticus 14:32 This is the rule for someone who has leprosy but cannot afford the things needed for their cleansing.
Leviticus 14:33 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Leviticus 14:34 When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving to you as your own, and I allow a leprosy disease in a house in your land;
Leviticus 14:35 The homeowner should go and say to the priest, "I think there might be a disease in the house."
Leviticus 14:36 The priest will order the house to be emptied before the priest enters to inspect the disease, so that everything inside won't become unclean; then the priest will go in to examine the house.
Leviticus 14:37 He will examine the disease, and, look, if the disease in the house's walls has green or red hollow streaks that appear deeper than the surface;
Leviticus 14:38 Then the priest will leave the house, go to the door, and close the house for seven days.
Leviticus 14:39 On the seventh day, the priest will return and check the house. If the disease has spread on the walls,
Leviticus 14:40 Then the priest will order to remove the stones with the disease and throw them into a dirty place outside the city.
Leviticus 14:41 He must have the house scraped all around inside, and the scraped-off dust must be dumped outside the city in a dirty place.
Leviticus 14:42 They will get new stones to replace the old ones, and use fresh mortar to cover the house.
Leviticus 14:43 If the disease returns and spreads in the house after the stones are removed, the house is scraped, and it is plastered;
Leviticus 14:44 The priest will come to check, and if the disease has spread in the house, it is a harmful leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
Leviticus 14:45 He will tear down the house, its stones, wood, and all its plaster, and take them out of the city to a dirty place.
Leviticus 14:46 Anyone who enters the house while it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 14:47 Anyone who sleeps in the house must wash their clothes; and anyone who eats in the house must wash their clothes.
Leviticus 14:48 If the priest enters, sees that the disease has not spread after the house was plastered, then he will declare the house clean because the disease is healed.
Leviticus 14:49 He must use two birds, cedar wood, scarlet thread, and hyssop to clean the house.
Leviticus 14:50 He will kill one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.
Leviticus 14:51 He must take the cedar wood, hyssop, scarlet cloth, and live bird, dip them into the blood of the dead bird and fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
Leviticus 14:52 He will clean the house with the bird's blood, with flowing water, with the live bird, with cedar wood, with hyssop, and with scarlet fabric.
Leviticus 14:53 He must release the live bird outside the city into the open fields to make up for any wrongs against the house, and then it will be clean.
Leviticus 14:54 This rule is for every kind of leprosy and skin disease.
Leviticus 14:55 For the disease of clothes or a house,
Leviticus 14:56 For swelling, for sores, and for white patches:
Leviticus 14:57 To teach when something is not clean and when it is clean: this is the rule about leprosy.

Leviticus 15:1 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Leviticus 15:2 Tell the people of Israel, if a man has a discharge from his body, he is unclean because of it.
Leviticus 15:3 This is how he will be unclean with his discharge: whether his body has a flow or is blocked from his flow, it is his uncleanness.
Leviticus 15:4 Every bed he lies on with the discharge is unclean, and everything he sits on will be unclean.
Leviticus 15:5 Anyone who touches his bed must wash their clothes, take a bath, and they will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:6 Whoever sits on anything the person with the discharge sat on must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:7 Anyone who touches the skin of the person with the discharge must wash their clothes, take a bath, and will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:8 If someone with a discharge spits on a clean person, the clean person must wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:9 Any saddle that a person with a discharge rides on will be unclean.
Leviticus 15:10 Anyone who touches anything that was beneath the dead person will be unclean until evening; whoever carries any of those things must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:11 Anyone who touches the person with the discharge without having washed their hands must wash their clothes, bathe in water, and will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:12 If someone with the discharge touches a clay pot, it must be broken, and any wooden object must be washed with water.
Leviticus 15:13 When a person with a discharge is healed, they must count seven days for their cleansing, wash their clothes, and bathe in flowing water to be clean.
Leviticus 15:14 On the eighth day, he must bring two doves or two young pigeons to God at the entrance of the meeting tent and give them to the priest.
Leviticus 15:15 The priest will sacrifice them, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering; and the priest will ask God to forgive him for his problem.
Leviticus 15:16 If a man's semen comes out, he must wash his whole body with water and will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:17 Every piece of clothing and every skin touched by bodily fluids must be washed with water, and will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:18 The woman and the man who have sexual relations must both wash with water and will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:19 If a woman has a discharge, and it is blood from her body, she must be separated for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:20 Everything she lies on during her period will be unclean, and everything she sits on will be unclean too.
Leviticus 15:21 Anyone who touches her bed must wash their clothes, take a bath, and will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:22 Anyone who touches anything she sat on must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:23 If it's on her bed or anything she sits on, when he touches it, he will be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:24 If a man sleeps with a woman during her period, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed he lies on will also be unclean.
Leviticus 15:25 If a woman bleeds for many days, not at the time of her period, or if her bleeding lasts longer than her period, she will be unclean as long as she has this bleeding, just like during her period.
Leviticus 15:26 Every bed she lies on during her period will be like her bed during her separation time; and anything she sits on will be unclean, like the uncleanness of her separation.
Leviticus 15:27 Anyone who touches those things will be unclean. They must wash their clothes, bathe in water, and stay unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:28 If she is healed from her condition, she must count seven days for herself, and then she will be clean.
Leviticus 15:29 On the eighth day, she must take two doves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the meeting tent.
Leviticus 15:30 The priest will offer one as a sin sacrifice and the other as a burnt offering; the priest will make amends for her with God for her unclean condition.
Leviticus 15:31 You must help the Israelites stay clean; if they are unclean, they could die, especially if they make my dwelling place among them unclean.
Leviticus 15:32 This is the rule for someone with a bodily discharge, and for a man who has an emission of semen, making him unclean.
Leviticus 15:33 About a woman during her menstrual cycle, and anyone with a discharge, whether male or female, and anyone who has sexual contact with someone who is unclean.

Leviticus 16:1 God spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons died because they made an offering before God and passed away.
Leviticus 16:2 God told Moses to say to his brother Aaron not to come into the most holy place inside the curtain in front of the cover on the ark whenever he wanted, so that he would not die. For God would appear in the cloud over the cover.
Leviticus 16:3 Aaron must enter the sacred area with a young bull for a sin sacrifice and a ram for a burnt offering.
Leviticus 16:4 He must wear the holy linen coat, linen underclothes next to his body, be wrapped with a linen belt, and wear a linen turban. These are sacred clothes, so he must bathe his body in water before putting them on.
Leviticus 16:5 He must take two young goats from the Israelite community for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Leviticus 16:6 Aaron must sacrifice his own bull for a sin offering to ask for forgiveness for himself and his family.
Leviticus 16:7 He will take two goats and bring them to God at the entrance of the meeting tent.
Leviticus 16:8 Aaron will draw lots for the two goats; one lot for God, and the other for the scapegoat.
Leviticus 16:9 Aaron must bring the goat chosen by God's lot and sacrifice it as a sin offering.
Leviticus 16:10 The goat chosen by lot to be the scapegoat will be brought alive before God, to ask for forgiveness with it, and then it will be released into the wilderness.
Leviticus 16:11 Aaron must bring the bull for the sin offering for himself, make amends for himself and his family, and kill the bull for his own sin offering.
Leviticus 16:12 He must take a firepan full of hot coals from the altar before God and a handful of finely ground fragrant incense, and take it inside the curtain.
Leviticus 16:13 He must put the incense on the fire in front of God so that the smoke will cover the cover of the Ark where the sacred stone tablets are kept, so he will not die.
Leviticus 16:14 He must take some blood from the bull and with his finger, sprinkle it on the east side of the cover. He must also sprinkle some blood in front of the cover seven times with his finger.
Leviticus 16:15 Then he must kill the goat that is for the people's sin offering and take its blood inside the curtain. He must do with the blood as he did with the bull's blood and sprinkle it on the atonement cover and in front of it.
Leviticus 16:16 He will make the holy place pure again, because of Israel's people being unclean and their many wrongdoings; he will do the same for the meeting tent that stays with them, surrounded by their uncleanness.
Leviticus 16:17 No one will be in the meeting tent when he goes into the holy place to make atonement, until he comes out after making atonement for himself, his family, and all of Israel's people.
Leviticus 16:18 He will go to the altar in front of God, make it right, and put some bull blood and goat blood on the altar's horns all around.
Leviticus 16:19 He must sprinkle the blood on it seven times with his finger, make it clean, and make it holy from the Israelites' impurity.
Leviticus 16:20 After he finishes making the holy place, the meeting tent, and the altar right with God, he will bring the live goat.
Leviticus 16:21 Aaron will place both hands on the live goat's head and admit all the wrongs and sins of the Israelites, transferring them to the goat. Then he will send the goat away into the desert with a suitable man.
Leviticus 16:22 The goat will carry all their wrongs to an empty place, and he will release the goat in the wild.
Leviticus 16:23 Aaron will enter the meeting tent and take off the linen clothes he wore into the sacred area, leaving them there.
Leviticus 16:24 He must wash his body with water in the sacred area, get dressed, go out, give his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering, and ask for forgiveness for himself and the people.
Leviticus 16:25 He must burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
Leviticus 16:26 The person who releases the goat as the scapegoat must wash their clothes, clean their body with water, and then may return to the camp.
Leviticus 16:27 Take the bull and the goat used for the sin offerings outside the camp after their blood was used for atonement in the holy place, and burn their skin, flesh, and waste in the fire.
Leviticus 16:28 The person who burns them must wash their clothes and bathe in water; then they can enter the camp.
Leviticus 16:29 This rule will always apply to you: on the seventh month's tenth day, you must humble yourselves and not do any work, whether you're a local or a foreigner staying with you.
Leviticus 16:30 On that day the priest will make amends for you to purify you, so you will be clean from all your sins before God.
Leviticus 16:31 It will be a restful Sabbath for you, and you must humble yourselves, by a rule for all time.
Leviticus 16:32 The priest, chosen and set apart to take over his father's duties, will perform the atonement and wear the linen clothes, the sacred outfits.
Leviticus 16:33 He will purify the holy place, the meeting tent, the altar, the priests, and all the people in the community.
Leviticus 16:34 This rule will always apply to you: Make amends for the people of Israel for all their wrongs once every year. He followed what God told Moses to do.

Leviticus 17:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 17:2 Talk to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel, and tell them this is what God has commanded.
Leviticus 17:3 Any person from the house of Israel who kills an ox, lamb, or goat, in the camp or outside of it,
Leviticus 17:4 If someone does not bring their offering to the entrance of the tent where people meet with God to give it to God, he is guilty of taking a life. That person must be excluded from his community.
Leviticus 17:5 So that the Israelites can bring their sacrifices, which they give in the open fields, to God at the entrance of the meeting tent, to the priest, and offer them for peace to God.
Leviticus 17:6 The priest will sprinkle the blood on God's altar at the tabernacle entrance and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to God.
Leviticus 17:7 They will no longer give their sacrifices to demons they chased after. This will be a permanent rule for them for all time.
Leviticus 17:8 Tell them, "Any Israelite or foreigner staying with you who presents a burnt offering or sacrifice,
Leviticus 17:9 If someone doesn't bring their offering to the entrance of the meeting tent to present it to God, that person must be separated from their people.
Leviticus 17:10 Any person from Israel or any foreigner living with you who eats any kind of blood, I will be against them and remove them from their people.
Leviticus 17:11 Life comes from the blood, and I've given it to you on the altar to forgive your sins because blood brings forgiveness.
Leviticus 17:12 So I told the Israelites, none of you may eat blood, nor may any outsider living with you eat blood.
Leviticus 17:13 Any person from Israel or foreigners living with you who hunts and catches an animal or bird that can be eaten must pour out its blood and cover it with dirt.
Leviticus 17:14 The blood is the life of every creature; it is their lifeblood. So I told the people of Israel not to eat the blood of any creature because the life of every creature is its blood. Anyone who eats it must be removed from the community.
Leviticus 17:15 Anyone who eats an animal that died on its own or was killed by other animals, whether they are from your country or a foreigner, must wash their clothes and bathe with water. They will be unclean until the evening; then they will be clean.
Leviticus 17:16 If he doesn't wash them or bathe his body, he must bear his guilt.

Leviticus 18:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 18:2 Tell the people of Israel, 'I am God, your God.'
Leviticus 18:3 Do not follow the customs of Egypt where you lived, nor the customs of Canaan where I am taking you. Do not follow their rules.
Leviticus 18:4 Follow my rules and keep my laws, and live by them. I am God, your God.
Leviticus 18:5 You must follow my rules and decisions: if a person does this, they will have a good life by them: I am God.
Leviticus 18:6 None of you should come close to a relative to see them naked: I am God.
Leviticus 18:7 Do not see your father's or your mother's naked body; she is your mother, so do not look at her nakedness.
Leviticus 18:8 Do not see your father's wife undressed; she is your father's privacy.
Leviticus 18:9 Do not see the private parts of your sister, either your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, whether she was born in the same house or elsewhere.
Leviticus 18:10 Do not see the private parts of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter; their privacy is your privacy.
Leviticus 18:11 Do not have sexual relations with your stepsister, the daughter of your father's wife; she is your sister.
Leviticus 18:12 Do not see your father's sister without clothes; she is your father's close relative.
Leviticus 18:13 Do not see your aunt undressed; she is your mother's close relative.
Leviticus 18:14 Do not see your uncle's nakedness or be close to his wife; she is your aunt.
Leviticus 18:15 Do not see your daughter-in-law without clothes; she is your son's wife; do not see her without clothes.
Leviticus 18:16 Do not see your brother's wife without clothes; it is like seeing your brother without clothes.
Leviticus 18:17 Do not see a woman and her daughter or her granddaughter naked; it is wrong because they are close relatives.
Leviticus 18:18 Do not marry your wife's sister while your wife is alive, to cause her trouble by having both of them.
Leviticus 18:19 Also, do not go near a woman to see her without clothes while she is set apart during her monthly period.
Leviticus 18:20 Do not have sex with your neighbor's wife and make yourself impure.
Leviticus 18:21 Do not let any of your children be burned in sacrifice to Molech, and do not dishonor your God's name: I am God.
Leviticus 18:22 Do not have sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman; it is disgusting.
Leviticus 18:23 Do not have sexual relations with any animal; it makes you unclean. A woman must not offer herself to an animal to have sexual relations with it; this is a perversion.
Leviticus 18:24 Do not make yourselves unclean with any of these actions; for by all these things, the nations I am driving out before you have become unclean.
Leviticus 18:25 The land is dirty: so I punish its wrongs, and the land throws out its people.
Leviticus 18:26 You must follow my laws and decisions, and must not do any of these disgusting things—neither anyone from your people nor any foreigner living with you.
Leviticus 18:27 The people who lived in the land before you did all these terrible things, and they made the land unclean.
Leviticus 18:28 So that the land does not vomit you out when you make it dirty, as it vomited out the nations before you.
Leviticus 18:29 Anyone who does any of these disgusting things will be separated from their community.
Leviticus 18:30 So you must follow my rules and not do any of these disgusting things that were done before you, so you do not become unclean by them: I am God, your God.

Leviticus 19:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 19:2 Tell all the people of Israel, "You must be holy because I, your God, am holy."
