Leviticus 19:4 Do not turn to idols or make metal gods for yourselves. I am your God.
Leviticus 19:5 If you bring a peace offering to God, you should do it because you want to.
Leviticus 19:6 Eat it on the day you offer it and the next day. If any is left on the third day, burn it in the fire.
Leviticus 19:7 If it's eaten on the third day, it is disgusting and won't be accepted.
Leviticus 19:8 Everyone who eats it will be guilty because they have dishonored what is holy to God: that person will be separated from their community.
Leviticus 19:9 When you harvest your land, do not completely harvest the corners of your field, nor collect the leftover crops.
Leviticus 19:10 Do not pick your vineyard clean or collect every grape; leave some for the poor and foreigners: I am God your God.
Leviticus 19:11 Do not steal, be dishonest, or lie to each other.
Leviticus 19:12 Do not make false promises using my name, and do not disrespect your God's name: I am God.
Leviticus 19:13 Do not cheat your neighbor or steal from him; do not keep a worker's pay overnight until morning.
Leviticus 19:14 Do not insult the deaf or put obstacles in the way of the blind but respect your God: I am God.
Leviticus 19:15 Do not be unfair in judgment: do not favor the poor or be in awe of the rich; but judge your neighbor fairly.
Leviticus 19:16 Do not spread rumors among your people or take part in harming your neighbor; I am God.
Leviticus 19:17 You must not hate your brother in your heart. You must definitely correct your neighbor and not let him continue in sin.
Leviticus 19:18 Do not take revenge or hold a grudge against your own people, but love your neighbor as yourself: I am God.
Leviticus 19:19 Follow my rules. Do not breed your animals with different kinds. Do not plant different kinds of seeds together in your field. And do not wear clothes made of both linen and wool mixed together.
Leviticus 19:20 If a man sleeps with a woman who is a slave promised to another man but she has not been bought or given her freedom, she should be punished, but they should not be killed because she was not free.
Leviticus 19:21 He must bring his guilt offering to God, to the entrance of the meeting tent, a ram as a guilt offering.
Leviticus 19:22 The priest will use the ram for the guilt offering to make up for his sin before God, and he will be forgiven for the sin he committed.
Leviticus 19:23 When you enter the land and plant various food trees, consider their fruit as forbidden for three years; do not eat it.
Leviticus 19:24 In the fourth year, all the fruit will be special to honor God.
Leviticus 19:25 In the fifth year, you can eat its fruit so it will give you more: I am God, your God.
Leviticus 19:26 Do not eat anything with blood in it; do not practice magic or tell fortunes.
Leviticus 19:27 Do not cut the hair on the sides of your head or trim the edges of your beard.
Leviticus 19:28 Do not cut your body for the dead or put tattoos on yourselves: I am God.
Leviticus 19:29 Do not make your daughter have sex for money, so she won't become a prostitute; otherwise, the country will turn to prostitution, and be filled with evil.
Leviticus 19:30 You must keep my Sabbaths and respect my holy place: I am God.
Leviticus 19:31 Do not pay attention to those with spirits, or look for wizards, so you don't become unclean by them: I am God, your God.
Leviticus 19:32 Stand up in respect for the elderly and show honor to the aged. Fear your God. I am the Lord.
Leviticus 19:33 If a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not upset him.
Leviticus 19:34 The foreigner living with you should be treated like a native-born among you, and you must love them as you love yourself; remember, you were once foreigners in Egypt. I am your God.
Leviticus 19:35 You must not be unfair when you judge, measure, weigh, or calculate amounts.
Leviticus 19:36 Use fair scales, fair weights, a fair ephah, and a fair hin: I am God who took you out of Egypt.
Leviticus 19:37 So you must follow all my rules and decisions and act on them: I am God.

Leviticus 20:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 20:2 Tell the Israelites, if anyone, whether they are from Israel or a foreigner living in Israel, gives one of their children to Molech, they must be put to death; the locals must stone them.
Leviticus 20:3 I will turn against that person, remove him from his people, because he offered his children to Molech, which polluted my sacred place and disrespected my holy name.
Leviticus 20:4 If the local people ignore someone who offers their child to Molech and do not put him to death:
Leviticus 20:5 I will oppose that man and his family, and I will exclude him and everyone who follows him to worship Molech, from their community.
Leviticus 20:6 The person who follows those with spirits or wizards, chasing after them, I will oppose and remove from their community.
Leviticus 20:7 Make yourselves holy, and be holy, because I am God, your God.
Leviticus 20:8 Keep my rules and follow them: I am God who makes you holy.
Leviticus 20:9 Anyone who curses their father or mother must be put to death. They have cursed their father or mother, and they are responsible for their own death.
Leviticus 20:10 The man who has an affair with another man's wife, including one who has an affair with his friend's wife, both the cheating man and woman will be put to death for sure.
Leviticus 20:11 A man who sleeps with his father's wife dishonors his father. Both of them must be put to death; they are responsible for their own deaths.
Leviticus 20:12 If a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both must be put to death, because they have caused chaos; they are responsible for their own deaths.
Leviticus 20:13 If a man sleeps with another man as he does with a woman, both have done something horribly wrong: they must be put to death, and they are responsible for their own deaths.
Leviticus 20:14 If a man marries both a woman and her mother, it is a terrible act. They all must be burned with fire to remove the evil from among you.
Leviticus 20:15 If a man has relations with an animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal.
Leviticus 20:16 If a woman gets close to an animal to mate with it, you must kill both the woman and the animal. They must be put to death, and they are responsible for their own deaths.
Leviticus 20:17 If a man has sexual relations with his sister, whether she is his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and they see each other naked, it is wrong. They will be punished in front of their people because he has dishonored his sister. He must accept his guilt.
Leviticus 20:18 If a man sleeps with a woman on her period and sees her nakedness, he has exposed her source of bleeding, and she has shown her blood flow; both will be separated from their community.
Leviticus 20:19 You must not see your mother's sister or your father's sister without clothes; this would reveal a close relative. They must face the consequences of their sin.
Leviticus 20:20 If a man sleeps with his uncle's wife, he has disgraced his uncle. They must accept the punishment for their sin; they will have no children.
Leviticus 20:21 If a man marries his brother's wife, it is impure; he has dishonored his brother; they will have no children.
Leviticus 20:22 You must follow all my rules and decisions and obey them, so that the land where I take you to live won't reject you.
Leviticus 20:23 Do not follow the ways of the people I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I disliked them.
Leviticus 20:24 I told you, you will take over their land, and I will give it to you to live in—a land full of milk and honey. I am God, your God, who has set you apart from other nations.
Leviticus 20:25 You must separate clean animals from unclean ones, and unclean birds from clean ones. Do not make yourselves unclean with animals, birds, or anything that crawls on the earth that I have set apart as unclean for you.
Leviticus 20:26 You should be holy for me because I, God, am holy, and I have set you apart from other people to be mine.
Leviticus 20:27 Anyone, man or woman, who consults with spirits or is a wizard, must be put to death; they will be stoned, and they are responsible for their own death.

Leviticus 21:1 God told Moses, "Tell Aaron's priest sons, they must not make themselves unclean for a dead person among their community."
Leviticus 21:2 But for his close family, for his mother, father, son, daughter, and brother.
Leviticus 21:3 He can become unclean for his sister if she has never been married and is close to him.
Leviticus 21:4 He must not make himself unclean, as a leader among his people, and dishonor himself.
Leviticus 21:5 They must not shave their heads, trim the edges of their beards, or cut their skin.
Leviticus 21:6 They must be holy for their God, and not disrespect their God's name: because they present offerings made with fire and food to their God, they must be holy.
Leviticus 21:7 They must not marry a woman who sells her body or is not respected; they should not marry a woman who has been divorced, because he is holy to his God.
Leviticus 21:8 You must make him holy, because he presents the food of your God; he must be sacred to you, for I, who make you holy, am holy.
Leviticus 21:9 If a priest's daughter dishonors herself by becoming a prostitute, she dishonors her father and must be burned to death.
Leviticus 21:10 The chief priest among his brothers, who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and is dedicated to wear the special clothes, must not let his hair be loose or tear his clothes.
Leviticus 21:11 He must not touch any dead person or make himself unclean, even for his father or mother.
Leviticus 21:12 He must not leave the holy place or make it unclean, because he wears the anointing oil from God. I am God.
Leviticus 21:13 He must marry a woman who is a virgin.
Leviticus 21:14 He must not marry a widow, divorced woman, someone unholy, or a prostitute. Instead, he must marry a virgin from his own community.
Leviticus 21:15 He must not dishonor his children among his people, for I, God, make him holy.
Leviticus 21:16 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 21:17 Tell Aaron that anyone from his descendants who has a flaw cannot come near to offer food to God.
Leviticus 21:18 Anyone with a defect must not come near: a blind person, someone who can't walk, anyone with a disfigured face, or any deformity.
Leviticus 21:19 Or a man with a broken foot or broken hand.
Leviticus 21:20 Or curved spine, or a short person, or one with a flawed eye, or with skin disease, or with sores, or with injured testicles;
Leviticus 21:21 A man from Aaron the priest's family with any defect must not come near to offering God's fire sacrifices; he has a defect and cannot offer food to his God.
Leviticus 21:22 He may eat his God's bread, from both the very holy and the holy parts.
Leviticus 21:23 He must not enter behind the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a flaw; he must not make my holy places impure, for I, God, make them holy.
Leviticus 21:24 Moses told Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.

Leviticus 22:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 22:2 Tell Aaron and his sons to stay away from the holy items of the people of Israel, so they do not disrespect my holy name in those things they dedicate to me: I am God.
Leviticus 22:3 Tell them, anyone from your descendants, through all your generations, who approaches the sacred items that the Israelites dedicate to God while unclean, that person must be separated from me: I am God.
Leviticus 22:4 Any descendant of Aaron who has leprosy or a discharge cannot eat the holy food until they are clean. Anyone who touches something unclean because of a dead body or a man's bodily emission;
Leviticus 22:5 Anyone who touches a crawling creature that might make them unclean, or a person who could pass on their impurity, will also become unclean.
Leviticus 22:6 The person who touches any such thing will be unclean until evening and must not eat any sacred food unless they wash their body with water.
Leviticus 22:7 When the sun sets, he will be clean and can then eat the sacred food, because it is his food.
Leviticus 22:8 He must not eat an animal that died on its own or was killed by other animals, so he will not become unclean; I am God.
Leviticus 22:9 They must follow my rules so they won't be punished for sinning and die if they disrespect it: I, God, make them holy.
Leviticus 22:10 No outsider may eat the holy food; only the priest's guest or paid worker may not eat the holy food.
Leviticus 22:11 If the priest buys someone with his money, both he and those born in his house may eat of it.
Leviticus 22:12 If the priest's daughter is married to someone outside the community, she cannot eat from the holy offerings.
Leviticus 22:13 If the priest's daughter is a widow or divorced, without any children, and she goes back to live in her father's home like when she was young, she can eat her father's food. But someone who is not part of the family cannot eat it.
Leviticus 22:14 If someone eats something holy by mistake, they must add one-fifth more to it and give it to the priest with the holy item.
Leviticus 22:15 They must not disrespect the sacred gifts of the Israelite people, which they give to God.
Leviticus 22:16 Do not let them be guilty when they eat their sacred food, for I, God, have made it holy.
Leviticus 22:17 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 22:18 Talk to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, and tell them: Anyone from Israel or any foreigner in Israel who wants to present a gift to God for all his promises or any voluntary offerings must offer it to God as a burnt sacrifice.
Leviticus 22:19 Give freely a perfect male cow, sheep, or goat.
Leviticus 22:20 Do not offer anything with a flaw, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.
Leviticus 22:21 Anyone who gives a peace sacrifice to God to keep a promise, or as a voluntary offering of cattle or sheep, must offer one without any faults to be accepted.
Leviticus 22:22 Do not offer to God animals that are blind, broken, crippled, with warts, with rashes, or with skin diseases, nor burn them as an offering on the altar to God.
Leviticus 22:23 You may offer a cow or a sheep with extra or missing parts as a voluntary gift to God, but such an animal won't be accepted for a promise.
Leviticus 22:24 You must not give to God anything that is bruised, crushed, broken, or cut; you also must not make such offerings anywhere in your land.
Leviticus 22:25 Do not offer to God bread from a stranger's hand, including any of these, for they are corrupt and flawed, and will not be accepted on your behalf.
Leviticus 22:26 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 22:27 When a cow, sheep, or goat is born, it must stay with its mother for seven days; starting from the eighth day, it can be used for a fire offering to God.
Leviticus 22:28 Do not kill a cow or sheep and its baby on the same day.
Leviticus 22:29 When you give a thanksgiving sacrifice to God, do it because you want to.
Leviticus 22:30 Eat it all on that day; don't save any for the next day: I am God.
Leviticus 22:31 So you must follow my commands and do them: I am God.
Leviticus 22:32 Do not disrespect my holy name; instead, I must be honored by the people of Israel: I am God who makes you holy.
Leviticus 22:33 I brought you out of Egypt to be your God: I am God.

Leviticus 23:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 23:2 Tell the people of Israel, tell them about God's festivals that you must announce as sacred gatherings; these are my festivals.
Leviticus 23:3 Work for six days, but the seventh day is a rest day, a special gathering; do no work on that day: it is God's rest day, everywhere you live.
Leviticus 23:4 These are God's special feasts, the sacred meetings you must announce at the right times.
Leviticus 23:5 On the fourteenth day of the first month, in the evening, is God's Passover.
Leviticus 23:6 On the fifteenth day of that month is God's Feast of Unleavened Bread: for seven days you must eat bread without yeast.
Leviticus 23:7 On the first day, you should gather for a special meeting; you must not do any regular work.
Leviticus 23:8 For seven days, you must present a burnt offering to God. On the seventh day, there is a special gathering; you must not do any regular work on that day.
Leviticus 23:9 God spoke to Moses and said,
Leviticus 23:10 Tell the people of Israel, when you enter the land I am giving you and harvest its crops, bring the first bundle of your harvest to the priest.
Leviticus 23:11 He will present the bundle of grain to God for you to be accepted; the next day after the Sabbath, the priest will do this presentation.
Leviticus 23:12 On that day when you present the sheaf, offer a one-year-old male lamb with no defects as a burnt sacrifice to God.
Leviticus 23:13 Its grain offering shall be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, burned as a pleasing aroma to God; and its drink offering shall be wine, one-quarter of a hin.
Leviticus 23:14 Do not eat bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until the same day you bring an offering to God. This rule will last forever for all your descendants wherever you live.
Leviticus 23:15 Count seven full weeks from the day after the Sabbath when you brought the bundle of grain to wave as an offering.
Leviticus 23:16 Count fifty days until the day after the seventh Sabbath; then give a new grain offering to God.
Leviticus 23:17 From your homes, bring two loaves of bread made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with yeast, as an offering to God.
Leviticus 23:18 You must give seven perfect lambs that are one year old, one young cow, and two rams with the bread as a burnt sacrifice to God. Include grain and drink offerings. It will be a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to God.
Leviticus 23:19 You must offer one young goat as a sin offering and two one-year-old lambs as a peace offering.
Leviticus 23:20 The priest will move them and the bread of the first harvest up and down as a special offering in front of God, along with the two lambs. These are holy for God and are for the priest.
Leviticus 23:21 You must announce on that very day, it should be a special gathering for you: do not do any regular work: this rule will last forever where you live, for all your family to follow.
Leviticus 23:22 When you harvest your land, do not completely clear the corners of your field, nor pick up leftovers. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am God your God.
Leviticus 23:23 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 23:24 Tell the people of Israel: On the first day of the seventh month, you must have a day of rest, a special time to remember with trumpet blasts, a sacred gathering.
Leviticus 23:25 Do not do any regular work on that day, but you must present a fire offering to God.
Leviticus 23:26 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 23:27 On the tenth day of the seventh month, you will have a day to make amends. It will be a special meeting for you. You must show sorrow and give a burnt offering to God.
Leviticus 23:28 Do no work on that day, because it is a day to make up for your sins before God.
Leviticus 23:29 Anyone who does not show their sorrow on that day will be separated from their people.
Leviticus 23:30 If anyone works on that day, I will remove that person from their community.
Leviticus 23:31 You must not do any work; this rule will last forever, for all your future family wherever you live.
Leviticus 23:32 This day will be a day of rest for you, and you should humbly reflect on yourselves. Starting on the evening of the ninth day of the month, from one evening to the next, you will observe your day of rest.
Leviticus 23:33 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 23:34 Tell the people of Israel, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, there will be the Feast of Tabernacles to honor God for seven days.
Leviticus 23:35 On the first day, you must have a special gathering; do not do any regular work on that day.
Leviticus 23:36 For seven days, give a fire offering to God. On the eighth day, gather for a special meeting and give another fire offering to God. It is an important gathering, and you must not do any regular work on that day.
Leviticus 23:37 These are God's special celebrations that you must announce as sacred gatherings, where you present offerings made with fire to God, including burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings, each on its proper day.
Leviticus 23:38 Apart from God's Sabbaths, your gifts, all your promises, and all the voluntary offerings you give to God.
Leviticus 23:39 On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you collect the crops, celebrate a festival for God for seven days. The first day is a rest day, and the eighth day is also a rest day.
Leviticus 23:40 On the first day, grab branches from nice trees, palm trees, thick trees, and willow trees by the stream; and be happy in front of God for seven days.
Leviticus 23:41 You will celebrate a festival for God for seven days each year. This will be a permanent law for all your future generations: you must observe it in the seventh month.
Leviticus 23:42 Live in shelters for seven days; every native-born Israelite must live in shelters.
Leviticus 23:43 I want your future families to know that I had the Israelites live in temporary shelters when I led them out of Egypt. I am God, your God.
Leviticus 23:44 Moses told the Israelites about God's festivals.

Leviticus 24:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 24:2 Tell the Israelites to bring you pure, crushed olive oil for the lamps so they will keep burning all the time.
Leviticus 24:3 Aaron must keep the lamps burning from evening until morning before God inside the tent of meeting. This is to be a lasting rule for all your descendants.
Leviticus 24:4 He will arrange the lamps on the clean lampstand before God all the time.
Leviticus 24:5 Take good flour and make twelve cakes; each cake should have two-tenths of an ephah of flour.
Leviticus 24:6 Place them in two lines, six in each line, on the clean table before God.
Leviticus 24:7 Put pure frankincense on each row so it will be on the bread as a reminder, an offering to God.
Leviticus 24:8 Every Sabbath, he should arrange it before God always, as it is an eternal promise from the people of Israel.
Leviticus 24:9 Aaron and his sons will own it, and they will eat it in a sacred place. It is very holy to them as part of God's offerings made with fire, a rule to follow always.
Leviticus 24:10 The son of an Israeli woman and an Egyptian man went out among the Israelis, and he and an Israeli man fought in the camp.
Leviticus 24:11 The son of the Israelite woman spoke against God's name and cursed. They took him to Moses; his mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri from the Dan tribe.
Leviticus 24:12 They kept him in custody to find out what God wanted.
Leviticus 24:13 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 24:14 Take the person who cursed outside the camp; everyone who heard them must touch their head, and then everyone in the assembly must throw stones at them.
Leviticus 24:15 You will tell the people of Israel, if anyone curses their God, they will be guilty of sin.
Leviticus 24:16 Anyone who speaks against God’s name must be put to death. The whole community must stone them. It doesn't matter if they are a foreigner or born in the land; if they speak against God’s name, they must be put to death.
Leviticus 24:17 Whoever kills a person must surely be put to death.
Leviticus 24:18 If someone kills an animal, they must replace it; one animal for another.
Leviticus 24:19 If a person hurts their neighbor, they should be hurt in the same way.
Leviticus 24:20 Injury for injury, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: if someone hurts another, the same hurt will be given to them.
Leviticus 24:21 If someone kills an animal, they must replace it; if someone kills a person, they must be put to death.
Leviticus 24:22 You will have one law, for both the foreigner and the native-born, because I am your God.
Leviticus 24:23 Moses told the Israelites to take the person who cursed outside the camp and throw stones at him. The Israelites did what God told Moses.

Leviticus 25:1 God spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai and said.
Leviticus 25:2 Talk to the people of Israel and tell them, when you enter the land I am giving you, the land must rest for God.
Leviticus 25:3 For six years you should plant your fields, trim your vineyard, and collect its fruit.
Leviticus 25:4 In the seventh year, the land must rest and have a sabbath for God. You must not plant your fields or trim your vineyards.
Leviticus 25:5 Do not cut what grows by itself in your harvest or pick grapes from your unpruned vines; this is a year for the land to rest.
Leviticus 25:6 The land's rest will provide food for you, your servants, your maids, your workers, and any travelers staying with you.
Leviticus 25:7 Your animals and the wild creatures in your land will have all the crops to eat.
Leviticus 25:8 You must count seven sets of seven years, adding up to forty-nine years in total.
Leviticus 25:9 You will blow the trumpet to announce the Jubilee on the tenth day of the seventh month, and on the Day of Atonement, the trumpet will be heard everywhere in your land.
Leviticus 25:10 Make the fiftieth year holy, and announce freedom all over the country to everyone living there: it will be a special celebration for you; and everyone will go back to their own property, and everyone will go back to their own family.
Leviticus 25:11 That fiftieth year will be a special celebration for you: you must not plant seeds, harvest crops that grow on their own, or pick grapes from untrimmed vines.
Leviticus 25:12 It is a special year; it should be sacred to you. You can eat what grows in the fields.
Leviticus 25:13 In the year of this special celebration, each person should go back to their own property.
Leviticus 25:14 If you sell something to your neighbor or buy something from your neighbor's hand, do not cheat each other.
Leviticus 25:15 Based on the years left after the Jubilee, you will buy from your neighbor, and according to the years of crops, he will sell to you.
Leviticus 25:16 The more years there are, the higher the price will be, and the fewer years there are, the lower the price will be, because it's sold based on how many years of crops it can produce.
Leviticus 25:17 Do not treat each other unfairly, but respect your God; for I am your God.
Leviticus 25:18 So you should follow my rules, obey my laws, and act on them; then you will live safely in the land.
Leviticus 25:19 The land will produce its crops, you will eat as much as you need, and you will live there safely.
Leviticus 25:20 If you ask, "What will we eat in the seventh year if we don't plant or harvest our crops?"
Leviticus 25:21 Then I will order my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce crops for three years.
Leviticus 25:22 You will plant crops in the eighth year and eat from the old produce until the ninth year; you will eat from the old supplies until the new crops are ready.
Leviticus 25:23 The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine and you are only travelers and temporary residents with me.
Leviticus 25:24 In all the land you own, you must provide a way to buy it back.
Leviticus 25:25 If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his property, and a relative comes to buy it back, then they should buy back what their brother sold.
Leviticus 25:26 If the man has no one to buy it back for him, but he can afford to buy it back himself;
Leviticus 25:27 Let him calculate the years since he sold it and give back the extra amount to the person he sold it to, so that person can return to his property.
Leviticus 25:28 If he can't pay back, what he sold stays with the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. Then it will be returned, and he will get his property back.
Leviticus 25:29 If someone sells a house in a city with walls, they can buy it back within one year after the sale.
Leviticus 25:30 If the house in the city with walls is not bought back within a year, then it will belong forever to the person who bought it, and it will not be returned in the Jubilee.
Leviticus 25:31 The houses in unwalled villages will be treated like country land: they can be bought back, and they will be freed in the Jubilee.
Leviticus 25:32 Despite this, the Levites can buy back the cities and houses they own at any time.
Leviticus 25:33 If someone buys a house from the Levites, that house in the Levites' town becomes theirs again in the Jubilee year, because the houses in Levite cities are their permanent property among the Israelites.
Leviticus 25:34 But the land around their cities cannot be sold; it is theirs forever.
Leviticus 25:35 If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself with you, you must help him. Even if he is a stranger or a visitor, so he can live with you.
Leviticus 25:36 Do not charge him interest or profit, but respect God, so your brother can survive with you.
Leviticus 25:37 You must not lend him your money with interest, nor give him your food to get more back.
Leviticus 25:38 I am God, your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
Leviticus 25:39 If your nearby brother becomes poor and sells himself to you, don't make him work like a slave.
Leviticus 25:40 Like a paid worker and a temporary resident, he will stay with you and work for you until the Jubilee year.
Leviticus 25:41 He will then leave you, along with his children, and go back to his family and his ancestors' property.
Leviticus 25:42 They are my servants, whom I freed from Egypt; they must not be sold as slaves.
Leviticus 25:43 Do not treat him harshly, but respect your God.
Leviticus 25:44 You can have male and female slaves from the foreign nations around you; you can buy male and female slaves from them.
Leviticus 25:45 You can buy foreigners who live with you and their families born in your land; they will belong to you.
Leviticus 25:46 You will receive them as a heritage for your children after you, to own as property; they will be your servants forever. But do not rule harshly over your fellow Israelites.
Leviticus 25:47 If a foreigner or stranger becomes wealthy among you, and your fellow countryman becomes poor and sells himself to the foreigner living among you, or to a foreigner's family.
Leviticus 25:48 After he is sold, he can be bought back; one of his relatives can buy him back.
Leviticus 25:49 His uncle or his cousin can buy him back, or any close relative from his family can do it; or if he gets the money, he can buy himself back.
Leviticus 25:50 He must calculate with the one who bought him, starting from the year he was sold until the jubilee year. The cost of his sale will depend on how many years are left, just like the wage of a hired worker.
Leviticus 25:51 If many years remain, he must pay back the redemption price from the money he was bought with.
Leviticus 25:52 If only a few years are left until the Year of Jubilee, he must calculate that with him and pay back the cost of his freedom based on the remaining years.
Leviticus 25:53 He shall be treated like a worker hired year by year; he must not be treated harshly in your presence.
Leviticus 25:54 If he is not set free within those years, then he and his children will be released in the Year of Jubilee.
Leviticus 25:55 The people of Israel are my servants; they are the ones I freed from Egypt. I am your God.

Leviticus 26:1 Do not make any idols or carved images for yourselves, do not set up any sculpted stone figures in your land to bow down to, because I am God, your God.
Leviticus 26:2 You must keep my rest days and respect my holy place: I am God.
Leviticus 26:3 If you follow my rules and obey my commands, and follow through with them;
Leviticus 26:4 I will send rain at the right time, and the land will produce crops, and the trees will bear fruit.
Leviticus 26:5 Your grain grinding will last until grape picking, and grape picking will last until planting time. You will have plenty of bread to eat and live safely in your land.
Leviticus 26:6 I will bring peace to the land, and you will rest without fear; I will remove dangerous animals, and no war will enter your land.
Leviticus 26:7 You will chase your enemies, and they will fall in front of you by the sword.
Leviticus 26:8 Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand; your enemies will fall by your sword.
Leviticus 26:9 I will care for you, make you fruitful, increase your numbers, and keep my promise to you.
Leviticus 26:10 You will eat from your stored food and make room for the new by using up the old.
Leviticus 26:11 I will put my tent among you, and I will not reject you.
Leviticus 26:12 I will live with you, be your God, and you will be my people.
Leviticus 26:13 I am God, who brought you out of Egypt so you wouldn't be slaves; I broke the chains of your burden, so you could walk freely.
Leviticus 26:14 But if you don't listen to me and don't follow all these commands;
Leviticus 26:15 If you ignore my laws or hate my rules, and so do not follow all my commands, but break my agreement:
Leviticus 26:16 I will also do this to you: I will send terror, wasting sickness, and fever that will blind you and make your hearts sad. You will plant seeds for nothing because your enemies will eat your crops.
Leviticus 26:17 I will be against you, and you will be killed by your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will run away even when no one is chasing you.
Leviticus 26:18 If you still don't listen to me after all this, I will punish you seven times more for your sins.
Leviticus 26:19 I will break your power's pride; I will make your sky like iron and your land like brass.
Leviticus 26:20 You will use all your energy for nothing: your land won't produce crops and the trees won't give fruit.
Leviticus 26:21 If you act against me and don't listen to me, I will give you seven times more trouble for your sins.
Leviticus 26:22 I will also send wild animals to attack you, take your children, kill your livestock, and reduce your numbers; your roads will be empty.
Leviticus 26:23 If you don't change your ways because of these things but continue to oppose me;
Leviticus 26:24 Then I will also go against you and punish you seven times more for your sins.
Leviticus 26:25 I will send a sword against you to punish you for breaking my agreement. When you are together in your cities, I will bring disease among you, and you will be given over to your enemies.
Leviticus 26:26 When I make your bread supply scarce, ten women will bake your bread in one oven, and they will give you your bread in measured amounts: you will eat but still be hungry.
Leviticus 26:27 If you still don't listen to me and choose to go against my ways;
Leviticus 26:28 Then I will act against you in anger; and I will punish you seven times for your sins.
Leviticus 26:29 You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
Leviticus 26:30 I will destroy your worship places, cut down your statues, throw your dead bodies on your idols' dead bodies, and I will hate you.
Leviticus 26:31 I will turn your cities into ruins, destroy your holy places, and I will not enjoy the scent of your offerings.
Leviticus 26:32 I will make the land empty, and your enemies living there will be shocked by it.
Leviticus 26:33 I will spread you among the nations, and I will chase you with a sword: and your land will be empty, and your cities ruined.
Leviticus 26:34 The land will have its rest days while it's empty, and you are in your enemies' land; the land will rest and have its rest days.
Leviticus 26:35 As long as it is empty, it will rest; because it didn't rest during your Sabbaths when you lived on it.
Leviticus 26:36 I will make those of you who survive feel weak in heart in their enemies' lands; even the sound of a blowing leaf will scare them. They will run away as if running from a sword and they will fall, even though no one is chasing them.
Leviticus 26:37 They will stumble over each other as if fleeing from a sword, even when no one is chasing them; and you will be unable to resist your enemies.
Leviticus 26:38 You will die in foreign lands, and your enemies' land will consume you.
Leviticus 26:39 Those of you who survive will waste away in your enemies' lands because of your sins and your ancestors' sins.
Leviticus 26:40 If they admit their wrongs, and their ancestors' wrongs, and their betrayal against me, and that they have also acted against me;
Leviticus 26:41 I have opposed them and led them into their enemies' land. If their stubborn hearts are humble and they accept their punishment,
Leviticus 26:42 Then I will remember my promise to Jacob, to Isaac, and to Abraham, and I will remember the land.
Leviticus 26:43 The land will be abandoned by them and will rest during its sabbaths while it's empty without them; and they will accept their punishment for their sins because they hated my laws and their hearts rejected my rules.
Leviticus 26:44 Even then, when they are in their enemies' land, I won't reject them or hate them enough to completely destroy them and break my promise to them, because I am their God.
Leviticus 26:45 But for their sake, I will remember the agreement with their ancestors, who I freed from Egypt for all to see, so I could be their God: I am God.
Leviticus 26:46 These are the rules, decisions, and laws that God gave to the Israelites at Mount Sinai through Moses.

Leviticus 27:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Leviticus 27:2 Tell the people of Israel, when someone makes a special promise, the person promised to God must be valued by your standards.
Leviticus 27:3 Your value for a man between twenty and sixty years old shall be fifty silver shekels, using the sanctuary's shekel.
Leviticus 27:4 If it is a female, your value will be thirty shekels.
Leviticus 27:5 If the person is between five and twenty years old, the value is twenty shekels for a male and ten shekels for a female.
Leviticus 27:6 If it is from one month to five years old, then your value for a boy will be five silver coins, and for a girl it will be three silver coins.
Leviticus 27:7 If someone is 60 years old or older, a man’s value is 15 shekels, and a woman's is 10 shekels.
Leviticus 27:8 If he cannot afford your estimate, he shall stand before the priest, who will set a price based on what he can afford.
Leviticus 27:9 If it's an animal that people offer to God, everything that anyone gives like this to God is special.
Leviticus 27:10 He must not replace or exchange a good animal for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If he does exchange one animal for another, both the animal and its replacement will be holy.
Leviticus 27:11 If there is any impure animal that they do not sacrifice to God, then they must bring the animal to the priest.
Leviticus 27:12 The priest will decide its worth, good or bad, and however you, the priest, value it, that is what it will be.
Leviticus 27:13 If he wants to buy it back, he must add one-fifth to your valuation.
Leviticus 27:14 When someone dedicates their house to God, the priest will decide its value, good or bad, and that value will be final.
Leviticus 27:15 If the person who dedicated his house wants to buy it back, he must add one-fifth of the valued price to it, and it will be his.
Leviticus 27:16 If someone dedicates part of their own field to God, its value will be based on how much seed it takes to plant it: a homer of barley seed will be worth fifty silver coins.
Leviticus 27:17 If he sets apart his field from the jubilee year, it will be valued as you estimate.
Leviticus 27:18 If he makes his field holy after the Jubilee, the priest will calculate the cost based on the remaining years until the next Jubilee, and the price will be reduced from your original estimate.
Leviticus 27:19 If the person who made the field holy wants to buy it back, they must add one-fifth to the estimated price and then it will belong to them again.
Leviticus 27:20 If he won't buy back the field, or if he has sold it to someone else, it can't be bought back again.
Leviticus 27:21 But when the field is set free in the Jubilee, it must be holy for God, like a field given to God; the priest will own it.
Leviticus 27:22 If a person dedicates to God a field they have bought, which is not part of their own land,
Leviticus 27:23 Then the priest will calculate the value of your price until the Year of Jubilee, and on that day, you must pay your price as a sacred gift to God.
Leviticus 27:24 In the jubilee year, the field will go back to the person who originally owned it, the one who sold it.
Leviticus 27:25 All your valuations must be based on the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
Leviticus 27:26 The firstborn of animals, which belong to God, no one can set apart, whether it is an ox or sheep; it belongs to God.
Leviticus 27:27 If it is an impure animal, then one must buy it back at your valued price plus a fifth of that amount; if it is not bought back, then it must be sold at your valued price.
Leviticus 27:28 Even so, nothing that a person dedicates to God from everything they own, whether it's a person, an animal, or land, can be sold or bought back; everything dedicated is very sacred to God.
Leviticus 27:29 No one who is set apart for destruction can be bought back; they must be put to death.
Leviticus 27:30 All the tenth part of the land's produce, from crops or trees, belongs to God; it is sacred to God.
Leviticus 27:31 If someone wants to buy back any of their tithe, they must add a fifth of its value to it.
Leviticus 27:32 About the tenth part of the herd or flock, any that passes under the shepherd's rod, every tenth animal is holy and is for God.
Leviticus 27:33 He will not check if it is good or bad, nor will he replace it: and if he does replace it, then both the original and the replacement will be sacred; they cannot be bought back.
Leviticus 27:34 Here are the rules that God gave to Moses for the people of Israel on Mount Sinai.

Numbers 1:1 God spoke to Moses in the Sinai wilderness, in the meeting tent, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after leaving Egypt, saying,
Numbers 1:2 Count all the members of Israel's community by family groups, according to their fathers' houses, and list the names of all the men one by one.
Numbers 1:3 Count everyone in Israel aged 20 and older who can fight in the army, you and Aaron must organize them by their military groups.
Numbers 1:4 You will have one man from each tribe with you; each one will be the leader of his family.
Numbers 1:5 Here are the names of the men who will be with you: from Reuben's tribe, Elizur son of Shedeur.
Numbers 1:6 From the tribe of Simeon: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai.
Numbers 1:7 From Judah came Nahshon, son of Amminadab.
Numbers 1:8 From the tribe of Issachar: Nethaneel, son of Zuar.
Numbers 1:9 From Zebulun: Eliab, son of Helon.
Numbers 1:10 From Joseph's descendants: From Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
Numbers 1:11 From the tribe of Benjamin: Abidan, son of Gideoni.
Numbers 1:12 From Dan: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai.
Numbers 1:13 From the Asher tribe, Pagiel son of Ocran.
Numbers 1:14 From Gad; Eliasaph son of Deuel.
Numbers 1:15 From Naphtali; Ahira, Enan's son.
Numbers 1:16 These were famous leaders of the group, chiefs of their family tribes, and in charge of thousands in Israel.
Numbers 1:17 Moses and Aaron took these men whose names were listed.
Numbers 1:18 They gathered the whole community on the first day of the second month. They listed their family lines by their fathers' houses, by name, starting from age twenty and above, counting each man.
Numbers 1:19 As God told Moses, so he counted them in the Sinai wilderness.
Numbers 1:20 The descendants of Reuben, Israel's oldest son, were organized by their generations, families, and fathers' houses. The list included every man 20 years old and older who could fight in the war.
Numbers 1:21 The tribe of Reuben had 46,500 people counted.
Numbers 1:22 From Simeon's descendants, by their generations and family groups, according to their fathers' houses, the men counted by name, each one over twenty years old and able to fight in war, were listed.
Numbers 1:23 The tribe of Simeon had 59,300 people counted.
Numbers 1:24 From the descendants of Gad, grouped by their generations and family lines, and according to their fathers' households, everyone 20 years old and older who could fight in war was counted.
Numbers 1:25 The total number of the tribe of Gad was 45,650.
Numbers 1:26 From the tribe of Judah, organized by their family lines and ancestors' houses, counting each person by name, all the men aged twenty and above who could fight in the war.
Numbers 1:27 The census counted 74,600 people from the tribe of Judah.
Numbers 1:28 From the tribe of Issachar came men who were listed by their family lines and fathers' houses. Anyone 20 years old or older who could fight in the army was included by name.
Numbers 1:29 The tribe of Issachar had 54,400 people counted.
Numbers 1:30 From the tribe of Zebulun, listed by generations and families, from each father's house, everyone aged twenty or older who could go to war.
Numbers 1:31 The tribe of Zebulun had 57,400 people counted.
Numbers 1:32 From Joseph's descendants, specifically from Ephraim's line, they were counted by generations, family groups, and fathers' houses, including everyone 20 years and older who could fight in wars.
Numbers 1:33 The count of people from the tribe of Ephraim was forty thousand and five hundred.
Numbers 1:34 From the descendants of Manasseh, according to their family lines and their fathers' houses, following the list of names and counting those twenty years old and above, all those fit for military service.
Numbers 1:35 The tribe of Manasseh had 32,200 people counted.
Numbers 1:36 From Benjamin's descendants, by their family lines, according to their fathers' houses, counting each name from age twenty and older, all who could go to war.
Numbers 1:37 The tribe of Benjamin had 35,400 people counted.
Numbers 1:38 From the Dan tribe, sorted by their generations, family groups, and fathers' houses, all the men 20 years old and above who could go to war were counted by their names.
Numbers 1:39 The count of the Dan tribe was 62,700 people.
Numbers 1:40 From the Asher family, according to their generations and family groups, counting by the men's houses, everyone 20 years old and above who could go to war.
Numbers 1:41 The tribe of Asher had 41,500 people counted.
Numbers 1:42 From Naphtali's descendants, by families and father's houses, counting by names, everyone 20 years and older who could fight in war.
Numbers 1:43 The count of the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
Numbers 1:44 These are the people counted by Moses, Aaron, and the twelve leaders of Israel, with one man representing each family.
Numbers 1:45 All the Israelites counted by their families, from age twenty and up, who could fight in war, were included.
Numbers 1:46 All those counted were 603,550.
Numbers 1:47 The Levites from their ancestors' tribe were not counted with them.
Numbers 1:48 God had spoken to Moses, saying,
Numbers 1:49 Do not count the tribe of Levi or include them in the census of the Israelites.
Numbers 1:50 You should put the Levites in charge of the tent of testimony, all its equipment, and everything that belongs to it. They will carry the tent and all its equipment; they will take care of it and camp around the tent.
Numbers 1:51 When it's time to move the tent, the Levites will take it apart, and when it's time to set up the tent, the Levites will put it together. Anyone else who comes close will be killed.
Numbers 1:52 The Israelites will set up their tents, each person near their own group, and each person by their own flag, among their units.
Numbers 1:53 The Levites must camp around the tent of the covenant so that God's anger does not fall on the Israelites, and the Levites are responsible for looking after the tent of the covenant.
Numbers 1:54 The Israelites did everything God told Moses to do.

Numbers 2:1 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Numbers 2:2 Each man from Israel's tribes will camp under his own flag, near the banner of his family: they will set up their tents around the tent where the people meet.
Numbers 2:3 On the east side, where the sun comes up, the tribe of Judah will set up camp under their flag with their army: Nahshon son of Amminadab will lead them.
Numbers 2:4 His army and the counted number of them were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
Numbers 2:5 The group camping next to them will be the Issachar tribe, with Nethaneel son of Zuar as the leader of the Issachar people.
Numbers 2:6 His army and the counted men totaled fifty-four thousand four hundred.
Numbers 2:7 Next, the group from Zebulun: Eliab son of Helon will lead the Zebulun people.
Numbers 2:8 His army, and the counted people in it, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
Numbers 2:9 In Judah's camp, 186,400 soldiers were counted. They will march first.
Numbers 2:10 On the south side, the flag of Reuben's camp will be set up for their military units: and Elizur son of Shedeur will lead Reuben's people.
Numbers 2:11 His army, with everyone counted, was 46,500.
Numbers 2:12 The group camping next to him will be the Simeon tribe, and their leader will be Shelumiel, Zurishaddai's son.
Numbers 2:13 His army, and the counted people in it, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
Numbers 2:14 The group from Gad: Eliasaph, Reuel's son, will lead Gad's descendants.
Numbers 2:15 His army, and the counted ones, were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
Numbers 2:16 In Reuben's camp, 151,450 people were counted, organized in their groups. They will march second.
Numbers 2:17 Then the tent where people meet will move with the Levites' camp in the middle of all the camps. As they camp, they will move, each person in their own spot under their flags.
Numbers 2:18 The west side will have Ephraim's camp flag, with their soldiers, and Elishama son of Ammihud will lead Ephraim's people.
Numbers 2:19 His army and the counted men were forty-five thousand five hundred.
Numbers 2:20 The Manasseh tribe will be with him, and their leader will be Gamaliel, Pedahzur's son.
Numbers 2:21 His army, and the counted number in it, were thirty-two thousand and two hundred.
Numbers 2:22 Then the tribe of Benjamin: and the leader of Benjamin's people will be Abidan, Gideoni's son.
Numbers 2:23 His army, and the counted number of them, was thirty-five thousand four hundred.
Numbers 2:24 The army of Ephraim had 108,100 soldiers. They will march third.
Numbers 2:25 The flag of Dan's camp will be on the north side by their troops, and the leader of Dan's people will be Ahiezer, Ammishaddai's son.
Numbers 2:26 His army and the counted number of them were 62,700.
Numbers 2:27 The group camping next to him will be the Asher tribe, and the Asher tribe leader will be Pagiel, Ocran's son.
Numbers 2:28 His army, and the counted men, were forty-one thousand five hundred.
Numbers 2:29 The Naphtali tribe: Ahira, son of Enan, will be the leader of Naphtali's people.
Numbers 2:30 His army, with those counted, was fifty-three thousand four hundred.
Numbers 2:31 In Dan's camp, there were 157,600 people counted. They will march last under their banners.
Numbers 2:32 These are the numbers of the Israelites counted by their family groups: all of those counted in the camps throughout their groups totaled 603,550.
Numbers 2:33 The Levites were not counted with the Israelites, as God told Moses.
Numbers 2:34 The Israelites did everything God told Moses: they camped under their flags and moved out grouped by family, following their ancestors' houses.

Numbers 3:1 These are also the family records of Aaron and Moses when God spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
Numbers 3:2 These are Aaron's sons' names: Nadab the oldest, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Numbers 3:3 Here are the names of Aaron's sons, the priests who were appointed and set apart to serve as priests.
Numbers 3:4 Nadab and Abihu died in front of God when they offered the wrong kind of fire before God in the Sinai wilderness, and they had no children. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with their father Aaron watching.
Numbers 3:5 God spoke to Moses and said,
Numbers 3:6 Bring the Levi tribe close, and place them before Aaron the priest, so they can serve him.
Numbers 3:7 They must take care of their duties and the duties of the whole community at the Tent of Meeting by doing the work of the Tent.
Numbers 3:8 They must take care of all the tools of the meeting tent and be responsible for serving the people of Israel in the tent.
Numbers 3:9 You will give the Levites to Aaron and his sons: they are completely given to him from the Israelites.
Numbers 3:10 You will choose Aaron and his sons to be priests, and they will serve in this role. If anyone else comes close, they must be put to death.
Numbers 3:11 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 3:12 I have chosen the Levites from the Israelites to take the place of all the firstborn of Israel. So the Levites belong to me.
Numbers 3:13 Every firstborn is mine; when I struck down the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart every firstborn in Israel, from people to animals, as mine: they belong to me: I am God.
Numbers 3:14 God spoke to Moses in the Sinai desert, saying,
Numbers 3:15 Count the Levi tribe members by their fathers' households and families, including every boy one month old and older.
Numbers 3:16 Moses counted them as God had instructed him to do.
Numbers 3:17 These were the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Numbers 3:18 Here are the names of Gershon’s sons by their families: Libni and Shimei.
Numbers 3:19 Kohath's sons in their families were Amram, Izehar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Numbers 3:20 The descendants of Merari by their family groups were Mahli and Mushi. These are the Levite family groups by their ancestors' houses.
Numbers 3:21 Gershon had two families: the Libnites and the Shimites. These are the Gershonite families.
Numbers 3:22 The count of them, every male one month old and above, was seven thousand five hundred.
Numbers 3:23 The Gershonite families must camp behind the sanctuary, towards the west.
Numbers 3:24 The head of the Gershonite family group will be Eliasaph, Lael's son.
Numbers 3:25 The Gershonites are responsible in the meeting tent for the tent itself, its cover, and the curtain at the entrance.
Numbers 3:26 The curtains for the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard near the tent and altar, and the ropes for all its uses.
Numbers 3:27 From Kohath came the Amramite family, the Izeharite family, the Hebronite family, and the Uzzielite family: these are the Kohathite families.
Numbers 3:28 Among the boys one month old and older, there were 8,600 who took care of the holy place.
Numbers 3:29 The families of Kohath's sons will camp on the south side of the tent of worship.
Numbers 3:30 The head of the leading family from Kohath's descendants will be Elizaphan, Uzziel's son.
Numbers 3:31 Their job is to take care of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the holy objects they use in service, along with the curtains and everything related to their use.
Numbers 3:32 Eleazar, Aaron the priest's son, will be the leader of the Levite leaders and will supervise those who take care of the sanctuary.
Numbers 3:33 Merari had two families: the Mahlites and the Mushites. These are the Merari families.
Numbers 3:34 The count of the males one month old and older was 6,200.
Numbers 3:35 The leader of the Merari family group was Zuriel, Abihail's son. They will set up their tents north of the tent of meeting.
Numbers 3:36 The sons of Merari will take care of the tabernacle's frames, crossbars, pillars, bases, and all its equipment and everything related to it.
Numbers 3:37 And the posts around the courtyard, their bases, their pegs, and their ropes.
Numbers 3:38 Those who camp in front of the tent on the east side, in front of the meeting tent, will be Moses, Aaron, and his sons. They will take care of the sanctuary on behalf of the people of Israel. Anyone else who comes close will be put to death.
Numbers 3:39 Everyone counted from the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted by God's command according to their families, all the males one month old and older, totaled 22,000.
Numbers 3:40 God told Moses, "Count all the first-born boys of the Israelites who are one month old or older, and make a list of their names."
Numbers 3:41 You must choose the Levites for me (I am God) in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites; and the Levites' animals in place of all the firstborn animals of the Israelite people.
Numbers 3:42 Moses counted all the firstborn sons of Israel, just as God had told him to.
Numbers 3:43 All the firstborn boys, one month old and older, listed by name, totaled 22,273.
Numbers 3:44 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 3:45 Choose the Levites instead of the firstborn of the Israelites, and take the Levites' animals instead of their animals; the Levites will belong to me: I am God.
Numbers 3:46 And for the 273 firstborn Israelite children who are more than the Levites and must be redeemed.
Numbers 3:47 You should take five shekels for each person, using the sanctuary shekel (which is twenty gerahs).
Numbers 3:48 You must give the money needed to redeem the extra people to Aaron and his sons.
Numbers 3:49 Moses took the extra redemption money from those who were more than the number redeemed by the Levites.
Numbers 3:50 He took money for the firstborn of the Israelites; one thousand three hundred sixty-five sanctuary shekels.
Numbers 3:51 Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, as God had directed, following God's instructions to Moses.

Numbers 4:1 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Numbers 4:2 Count the Kohathite men among the Levites by their families and their fathers' households.
Numbers 4:3 From age thirty to fifty, everyone who joins the group to work at the meeting tent.
Numbers 4:4 The Kohathites will work at the meeting tent, taking care of the most sacred items.
Numbers 4:5 When the camp moves, Aaron and his sons must take down the curtain and use it to cover the Ark of the Agreement.
Numbers 4:6 You will cover it with badger-skin and lay a completely blue cloth on top, and put the carrying poles in place.
Numbers 4:7 On the table of special bread, they shall lay a blue cloth and place the plates, spoons, bowls, and lids on it: and the regular bread shall be on it.
Numbers 4:8 They will spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover that with badger skin, and insert the carrying poles.
Numbers 4:9 They will use a blue cloth to cover the lampstand, its lamps, tongs, snuffdishes, and all the oil containers used for service.
Numbers 4:10 They will cover it and all its tools with badger skins, then put it on a pole.
Numbers 4:11 On the gold altar, they will lay a blue cloth, cover it with badger skin, and attach its carrying poles.
Numbers 4:12 They must take all the service tools they use in the holy place, wrap them in blue cloth, cover them with leather, and carry them on a pole.
Numbers 4:13 They will remove the ashes from the altar and cover it with a purple cloth.
Numbers 4:14 They will put all its tools on it, which they use for service, like the pans, meat forks, shovels, and bowls, all the tools for the altar; and they will cover it with badger skin and put its carrying poles in place.
Numbers 4:15 When Aaron and his sons finish covering the sanctuary and all its items, as the camp prepares to move, the Kohathites must carry them. However, they must not touch the sacred objects, or they will die. This is the Kohathites' responsibility in the tent of meeting.
Numbers 4:16 Eleazar, Aaron's son and a priest, is in charge of the oil for the lamp, the sweet-smelling incense, the daily grain offering, the anointing oil, and looking after the entire tent of meeting, everything in it, the holy place, and its furnishings.
Numbers 4:17 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Numbers 4:18 Do not exclude the Kohathite clan from the Levite tribe.
Numbers 4:19 Do this for them so they will live and not die when they handle the most holy things: Aaron and his sons must go in and assign each one his job and his load to carry.
Numbers 4:20 They must not enter to see the holy items being covered, or they will die.
Numbers 4:21 God spoke to Moses and said,
Numbers 4:22 Count the sons of Gershon too, by their father's houses and by their families.
Numbers 4:23 Count all who are from 30 to 50 years old; these are the ones who will work and serve in the meeting tent.
Numbers 4:24 This is the work of the Gershonite families, to serve and carry loads.
Numbers 4:25 They will carry the tabernacle's curtains, its covering, the extra layer of badger skin on top, and the cloth for the entrance of the meeting tent.
Numbers 4:26 The curtains of the courtyard, the curtain for the entrance of the courtyard gate near the tent and the altar, their ropes, all the tools used for their service, and everything made for them: this is how they will work.
Numbers 4:27 Aaron and his sons will direct all the work of the Gershonites with everything they carry and all their tasks. You must give them responsibility for all they carry.
Numbers 4:28 This is the job of the Gershon family groups in the meeting tent: they will work under Ithamar, Aaron the priest's son.
Numbers 4:29 Count the sons of Merari by their families and their fathers' houses.
Numbers 4:30 Count everyone from 30 to 50 years old who enters to serve and work at the tent of meeting.
Numbers 4:31 This is their duty with all the work they do in the tent of meeting: to take care of the tent's frames, bars, posts, and bases.
Numbers 4:32 The pillars around the courtyard, their bases, pegs, and ropes, with all their tools and everything used in their service: you must list the tools assigned for carrying them by name.
Numbers 4:33 This is the work of the Merari family groups, doing all their tasks at the meeting tent, led by Ithamar, Aaron the priest's son.
Numbers 4:34 Moses, Aaron, and the leader of the assembly counted the Kohathite men by their families and ancestors' houses.
Numbers 4:35 From age thirty to fifty, everyone who enters the service to work in the tent of meeting.
Numbers 4:36 And the count of them by their families was two thousand seven hundred and fifty.
Numbers 4:37 These were the people counted from the Kohathite families, all who could work at the meeting tent, which Moses and Aaron counted as God commanded through Moses.
Numbers 4:38 The sons of Gershon were counted according to their families and their fathers' houses.
Numbers 4:39 From thirty to fifty years old, everyone who enters the service to work in the tent of meeting.
Numbers 4:40 The count of them, by their family and father's house, was two thousand six hundred thirty.
Numbers 4:41 These are the people counted from Gershon's descendants, all who could work in the meeting tent, whom Moses and Aaron counted as God commanded.
Numbers 4:42 The number of people from the Merari family groups, counted by their family lines and fathers' houses,
Numbers 4:43 From age thirty to fifty, anyone who joins the service to work at the tent of meeting.
Numbers 4:44 The count of their family members was three thousand two hundred.
Numbers 4:45 These are the ones counted from the families of Merari's sons, whom Moses and Aaron counted as God commanded through Moses.
Numbers 4:46 Everyone counted from the Levite tribe, whom Moses, Aaron, and Israel's leaders recorded by their families and ancestors' houses,
Numbers 4:47 From age thirty to fifty, everyone who came to serve and carry loads in the meeting tent.
Numbers 4:48 Even those counted among them were 8,580.
Numbers 4:49 God instructed them to count each person by Moses' direction, based on their tasks and responsibilities, and so Moses counted them as God had ordered.

Numbers 5:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 5:2 Tell the Israelites to send out of the camp anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone who is unclean because of a dead body.
Numbers 5:3 Remove both men and women from the camp; do not let them make your camps unclean where I live among you.
Numbers 5:4 The Israelites did what was told and sent them outside the camp; just as God told Moses, that's what the Israelites did.
Numbers 5:5 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 5:6 Tell the Israelites, when a man or woman does any sin that people do and wrongs God, and that person is guilty;
Numbers 5:7 They must admit the sin they committed, then pay back the main amount plus an extra fifth of it to the person they wronged.
Numbers 5:8 If the man has no relative to pay the debt to, give the payment to God, to the priest, plus the ram for making things right with God.
Numbers 5:9 Every gift of the sacred things the Israelites bring to the priest will belong to him.
Numbers 5:10 Everything a man sets apart as holy belongs to him; whatever someone gives to the priest becomes the priest's.
Numbers 5:11 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 5:12 Talk to the people of Israel and tell them, if a man's wife goes away and is unfaithful to him,
Numbers 5:13 If a man sleeps with her sexually, and it is secret from her husband, and it is hidden, and she is unclean, and there is no witness against her, and she is not caught in the act;
Numbers 5:14 If he feels jealous because he thinks his wife has been unfaithful, or if he feels jealous even if she hasn't been unfaithful:
Numbers 5:15 The man must take his wife to the priest, along with her offering, which is a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He must not add oil or frankincense to it because it is a jealousy offering, a reminder offering that brings sin to mind.
Numbers 5:16 The priest will bring her close and place her before God.
Numbers 5:17 The priest will take holy water in a clay pot and then take some dust from the floor of the worship place and add it to the water.
Numbers 5:18 The priest will bring the woman before God, uncover her head, and give her the jealousy offering to hold as a reminder. The priest will also hold the bitter water that brings a curse.
Numbers 5:19 The priest will make the woman take an oath and say to her, "If you have not slept with another man and have not been unfaithful to your husband, you will not be harmed by this cursed bitter water."
Numbers 5:20 But if you have been unfaithful to your husband and have been with another man:
Numbers 5:21 The priest must make the woman take a curse oath, and the priest will say to the woman, "May God make you a cursed example and a warning among your people when God causes your leg to rot and your stomach to swell."
Numbers 5:22 This cursed water will enter your stomach, making it swell and your thigh waste away. And the woman will say, "Yes, yes."
Numbers 5:23 The priest will write down these curses in a book and then wash them away with the bitter water.
Numbers 5:24 He will make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse; this water will go into her and become bitter.
Numbers 5:25 The priest will take the jealousy offering from the woman's hand, wave it in front of God, and put it on the altar.
Numbers 5:26 The priest will take a handful of the sacrifice, remembering it, and burn it on the altar; then he will make the woman drink the water.
Numbers 5:27 After she drinks the water, if she has been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter her, turn bitter, her stomach will swell, her thigh will waste away, and she will become cursed among her people.
Numbers 5:28 If the woman is not impure but is clean, then she is free and will have children.
Numbers 5:29 This is the rule for when a wife is unfaithful to her husband and becomes unclean with another man.
Numbers 5:30 If a man is overcome by a jealous spirit and suspects his wife, he must bring her before God, and the priest will carry out these laws on her.
Numbers 5:31 Then the man will be free from guilt, and the woman will carry her own guilt.

Numbers 6:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 6:2 Tell the people of Israel, if a man or woman chooses to make a special promise to become a Nazarite, dedicated to God.
Numbers 6:3 He must stay away from wine and strong drinks, not drink any kind of vinegar made from wine or strong drinks, and not drink grape juice or eat fresh or dried grapes.
Numbers 6:4 During the time of his commitment, he must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.
Numbers 6:5 Throughout the time of his promise to stay apart, he must not cut his hair. Until the time is complete for which he sets himself apart for God, he must be holy and allow his hair to grow long.
Numbers 6:6 Every day he sets apart for God, he must not be near any dead body.
Numbers 6:7 He must not make himself unclean for his father, mother, brother, or sister when they die, because he is dedicated to God.
Numbers 6:8 Throughout his time of commitment, he is sacred to God.
Numbers 6:9 If someone dies suddenly near a man, making his dedicated hair unclean, he must shave his head on the day he becomes clean, which is the seventh day.
Numbers 6:10 On the eighth day, he must take two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the meeting tent.
Numbers 6:11 The priest will sacrifice one animal for a sin offering and another for a burnt offering to forgive him for touching a dead body, and he will consecrate his head that day.
Numbers 6:12 He must dedicate the days of his separation to God and bring a one-year-old lamb for a guilt offering. But the previous days don't count because his separation became unclean.
Numbers 6:13 This is the rule for a Nazarite when his time of separation ends: he must go to the entrance of the meeting tent.
Numbers 6:14 He must present his offering to God: a one-year-old male lamb without any defects for a burnt offering, a one-year-old female lamb without defects for a sin offering, and a ram without defects for peace offerings.
Numbers 6:15 A basket of bread without yeast, cakes made with fine flour and oil, and thin bread without yeast covered with oil, along with their grain offering and their drink offerings.
Numbers 6:16 The priest will present them to God and offer the sin sacrifice and the burnt offering.
Numbers 6:17 He will offer the ram as a peace sacrifice to God, along with the basket of bread without yeast. The priest will also present his grain offering and his drink offering.
Numbers 6:18 The Nazarite must cut the hair dedicated to God at the entrance of the meeting tent and put that hair in the fire where the peace offerings are burned.
Numbers 6:19 The priest will take the cooked shoulder of the ram, one bread without yeast from the basket, and one flat, yeast-free bread, and place them on the hands of the Nazarite after his special hair has been cut off.
Numbers 6:20 The priest will move them back and forth as a special offering before God. This part is sacred for the priest, including the chest and shoulder parts. After this, the person dedicated to God can drink wine.
Numbers 6:21 This is the rule for the Nazarite who has made a promise, and for his gift to God because of his special commitment. It is in addition to what he can afford. He must follow what he promised to do according to the rules of his commitment.
Numbers 6:22 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 6:23 Talk to Aaron and his sons and tell them, "This is how you should bless the people of Israel. Say to them,
Numbers 6:24 God bless you and protect you.
Numbers 6:25 May God make his face shine on you and be gracious to you.
Numbers 6:26 May God look kindly on you and bring you peace.
Numbers 6:27 They will give my name to the Israelites, and I will bless them.

Numbers 7:1 On the day Moses finished setting up the tent of meeting, he put oil on it, made it holy, and did the same for all its equipment, the altar, and all its tools.
Numbers 7:2 The leaders of Israel, the heads of their families, who were in charge of the tribes and oversaw the counting, gave offerings.
Numbers 7:3 They presented their gift to God: six covered carts and twelve oxen. Each two leaders shared a cart, and each leader had an ox. They brought them in front of the tent of meeting.

Numbers 7:5 Accept it from them so they can work in the meeting tent; give it to the Levites, to each one as his work requires.

Numbers 8:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 8:2 Tell Aaron, when you light the lamps, the seven lamps should shine in front of the lampstand.
Numbers 8:3 Aaron did as told; he lit the lamps facing the lampstand, just as God ordered Moses.
Numbers 8:4 The candlestick was made of hammered gold, from its base to its flowers, just as God had shown Moses.
Numbers 8:5 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 8:6 Choose the Levites from the people of Israel and make them clean.
Numbers 8:7 Do this to make them clean: Sprinkle purifying water on them, have them shave all their body hair, wash their clothes, and they will be clean.
Numbers 8:8 Let them bring a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you must bring another young bull for a sin offering.
Numbers 8:9 Bring the Levites to the tent of meeting and gather all the Israelites.
Numbers 8:10 Bring the Levites before God, and let the Israelites lay their hands on them.
Numbers 8:11 Aaron will present the Levites to God on behalf of the Israelites, so they can do God's work.
Numbers 8:12 The Levites will put their hands on the bulls' heads. You will sacrifice one bull for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering to God, to ask for forgiveness for the Levites.
Numbers 8:13 Place the Levites in front of Aaron and his sons, and present them as an offering to God.
Numbers 8:14 You must set apart the Levites from the rest of the Israelites, and the Levites will belong to me.
Numbers 8:15 After that, the Levites will enter to work in the meeting tent; you must clean them and present them as an offering.
Numbers 8:16 They are completely given to me from the Israelites; in place of those who are the first to be born, I have chosen them for myself.
Numbers 8:17 All the firstborn of Israel's children belong to me, including humans and animals. On the day I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart for myself.
Numbers 8:18 I have chosen the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of the Israelites.
Numbers 8:19 I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from the Israelites, to serve the Israelites in the meeting tent and to seek forgiveness for the Israelites, so that no disease will come to the Israelites when they come close to the holy place.
Numbers 8:20 Moses, Aaron, and all the Israelite community did to the Levites just as God had commanded Moses. So the Israelites followed these instructions with the Levites.
Numbers 8:21 The Levites were made clean, and they washed their clothes. Aaron presented them to God as a gift and made a sacrifice to purify them.
Numbers 8:22 After that, the Levites went to work in the meeting tent before Aaron and his sons, just as God told Moses to do for the Levites.
Numbers 8:23 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 8:24 This means that the Levites, starting at age twenty-five and older, will work and serve at the meeting tent.
Numbers 8:25 At fifty years old they will stop serving and not work anymore.
Numbers 8:26 They should help their brothers at the tent of meeting and carry out their duties, but they should not do the work. This is what you must require of the Levites regarding their responsibilities.

Numbers 9:1 God spoke to Moses in the Sinai wilderness, in the first month of the second year after they left Egypt, saying.
Numbers 9:2 The Israelite children should celebrate Passover at the set time.
Numbers 9:3 On the fourteenth day of this month, at evening, you must celebrate it at the set time: you must follow all its rules and all its ceremonies.
Numbers 9:4 Moses told the Israelites to celebrate the Passover.
Numbers 9:5 They celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month in the evening in the Sinai wilderness, just as God told Moses, and so the Israelites did.
Numbers 9:6 Some men were unclean because they had touched a dead body, so they couldn't celebrate Passover that day. They went to Moses and Aaron that day.
Numbers 9:7 Those men told him, "We are unclean because of a man's dead body. Why should we be stopped from presenting God's offering at the right time among the Israelites?"
Numbers 9:8 Moses said to them, "Stay here, and I will listen to what God will order for you."
Numbers 9:9 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 9:10 Tell the Israelites that if someone is unclean because of touching a dead body, or is on a far journey, they must still celebrate Passover for God.
Numbers 9:11 On the fourteenth day of the second month, in the evening, they must celebrate it, eating the meal with bread without yeast and bitter herbs.
Numbers 9:12 They must not leave any until morning or break any of its bones. They must follow all the rules of the Passover.
Numbers 9:13 If a person is clean and not traveling but doesn't celebrate Passover, they will be separated from their people for not bringing God's offering at the right time; they must accept their wrong.
Numbers 9:14 If a foreigner stays with you and wants to celebrate the Passover for God, they must do it by the rules and ways of Passover. The same rules apply to both the foreigner and the native-born.
Numbers 9:15 On the day they put up the holy tent, a cloud covered it, which was the Tent of the Agreement. In the evening, it looked like fire on the tent until morning.
Numbers 9:16 The cloud always covered it during the day, and at night it looked like fire.
Numbers 9:17 When the cloud lifted from the tent, then the Israelites set out; where the cloud stayed, there the Israelites camped.
Numbers 9:18 By God's command, the Israelites traveled, and by His command, they set up camp: they stayed in their tents while the cloud stayed over the dwelling place.
Numbers 9:19 When the cloud stayed over the tent for many days, the Israelites followed God's command and did not travel.
Numbers 9:20 So when the cloud stayed over the tent for a few days, they followed God's order and stayed in their tents, and when God ordered, they moved on.
Numbers 9:21 When the cloud stayed from evening until morning and lifted in the morning, they traveled. Whenever the cloud lifted, day or night, they traveled.
Numbers 9:22 Whether the cloud stayed over the tent for two days, a month, or a year, the Israelites stayed in their tents and did not travel. But when the cloud lifted, they traveled.
Numbers 9:23 By God's order, they stayed in their tents, and by God's order, they traveled: they followed God's command through Moses.

Numbers 10:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 10:2 Make two silver trumpets from one piece of metal to call the people together and to signal when it's time to move the camps.
Numbers 10:3 When they blow the horns, everyone must gather to you at the tent of meeting entrance.
Numbers 10:4 If they blow one trumpet, then the leaders, who are in charge of Israel's groups of a thousand, will come to you.
Numbers 10:5 When you sound an alarm, the camps on the east side should move ahead.
Numbers 10:6 When you sound the alarm a second time, the camps on the south side will start to travel; they will blow the alarm when they are to move.
Numbers 10:7 When it's time to gather the people, you should blow the trumpets, but do not sound an alarm.
