Numbers 10:8 Aaron's sons, who are priests, will blow the trumpets; this will be a lasting rule for all your future families.
Numbers 10:9 If you fight in your land against the enemy who attacks you, then you must sound an alarm with the trumpets; and you will be thought of by God, and you will be rescued from your enemies.
Numbers 10:10 On happy days, special days, and the start of your months, blow trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace sacrifices as a reminder before your God: I am your God.
Numbers 10:11 On the twentieth day of the second month in the second year, the cloud lifted from above the tent of the law.
Numbers 10:12 The Israelites left the Sinai desert, and the cloud settled in the Paran desert.
Numbers 10:13 They began their journey as God commanded through Moses.
Numbers 10:14 First, the group from the tribe of Judah marched with their flag, and Nahshon son of Amminadab led them.
Numbers 10:15 The leader of Issachar's tribe's army was Nethaneel, Zuar's son.
Numbers 10:16 Eliab, Helon's son, led the army of Zebulun's descendants.
Numbers 10:17 The tent was taken apart; and Gershon's and Merari's sons moved on, carrying the tent.
Numbers 10:18 Reuben's group marched with their banner, and Elizur, Shedeur's son, was in charge of their soldiers.
Numbers 10:19 The leader of Simeon's tribe was Shelumiel, Zurishaddai's son.
Numbers 10:20 Eliasaph, Deuel's son, was in charge of Gad tribe's soldiers.
Numbers 10:21 The Kohathites moved ahead, carrying the sanctuary, and others set up the tent before they arrived.
Numbers 10:22 The group from Ephraim moved forward with their soldiers, and Elishama, Ammihud's son, was their leader.
Numbers 10:23 Gamaliel, Pedahzur's son, led the army of Manasseh's tribe.
Numbers 10:24 Abidan, Gideoni's son, led the army of Benjamin's tribe.
Numbers 10:25 The flag of Dan's camp moved ahead, which was at the back of all the groups, with Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, leading his people.
Numbers 10:26 Pagiel, son of Ocran, was in charge of the group from the Asher tribe.
Numbers 10:27 Ahira, Enan's son, led the army of Naphtali's tribe.
Numbers 10:28 These were the travels of the Israelites by their groups when they moved on.
Numbers 10:29 Moses said to Hobab, Raguel the Midianite's son and Moses' father-in-law, "We are traveling to the place God promised to give us. Come with us, and we'll treat you well. God has promised good things for Israel."
Numbers 10:30 He said to him, "I will not go; instead, I will go back to my own land and to my family."
Numbers 10:31 He said, "Please don't leave us; you know where we can camp in the desert, and you can guide us."
Numbers 10:32 If you come with us, whatever good things God does for us, we will do the same for you.
Numbers 10:33 They left God's mountain and traveled for three days. The chest of God's agreement led them during these three days to find a place to rest.
Numbers 10:34 God's cloud was over them during the day when they left the camp.
Numbers 10:35 When the ark moved, Moses said, "Get up, God, make your enemies go away, and those who hate you run from you."
Numbers 10:36 When it stopped, he said, "Come back, God, to the many thousands of Israel."

Numbers 11:1 When the people complained, it upset God; God heard it, and became angry; God's fire burned among them, and it destroyed those on the edges of the camp.
Numbers 11:2 The people called out to Moses; and when Moses prayed to God, the fire went out.
Numbers 11:3 He named the place Taberah because God's fire had burned there.
Numbers 11:4 The diverse crowd with them started to crave food, and the Israelites cried again, asking, "Who will give us meat to eat?"
Numbers 11:5 We remember eating fish for free in Egypt, along with cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
Numbers 11:6 Now we feel empty inside; all we see is this manna and nothing else.
Numbers 11:7 The manna looked like coriander seed and was the same color as bdellium.
Numbers 11:8 The people collected the food and ground it in mills or crushed it in a bowl, then cooked it on pans to make cakes; it tasted like fresh oil.
Numbers 11:9 When the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna came down with it.
Numbers 11:10 Moses heard the people crying in their families, each man at his tent door, and God became very angry; Moses was also upset.
Numbers 11:11 Moses said to God, "Why have you made things hard for me, your servant? And why don't I have your favor, that you have put the responsibility of all these people on me?"
Numbers 11:12 Did I give birth to all these people? Did I create them, that you tell me to carry them like a father carries a nursing baby, to the land you promised to their ancestors?
Numbers 11:13 Where can I get meat to give to all these people? They are crying to me, 'Give us meat so we can eat.'
Numbers 11:14 I can't handle all these people by myself, it's too much for me.
Numbers 11:15 If you treat me like this, please kill me now, if I have your favor; don't let me see my misery.
Numbers 11:16 God told Moses, "Bring me seventy of Israel's elders, known to you as leaders and officials, to the meeting tent so they can stand with you."
Numbers 11:17 I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them, so they can share the people's weight with you and you won't have to carry it alone.
Numbers 11:18 Tell the people to get ready for tomorrow, and you will eat meat. You cried to God for meat, saying, "Who will give us meat to eat? We had it good in Egypt." So God will give you meat, and you will eat.
Numbers 11:19 You must not eat for one day, two days, five days, ten days, or twenty days.
Numbers 11:20 But even for a whole month, until you are sick of it because it comes out of your nose, and you hate it: you feel this way because you rejected God among you and cried in front of him, asking, 'Why did we leave Egypt?'
Numbers 11:21 Moses said, "The people I am with are 600,000 soldiers; and you have said, 'I will give them meat to eat for a whole month.'"
Numbers 11:22 Should we kill enough flocks and herds to feed them? Or should we gather all the fish from the sea for them to be satisfied?
Numbers 11:23 God said to Moses, "Is God's power weak? You will now see if my promise to you happens or not."
Numbers 11:24 Moses went out, told the people what God said, gathered seventy elders, and placed them around the tent.
Numbers 11:25 God came down in a cloud, spoke to him, and shared his spirit with the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them, they spoke God's message and did not stop.
Numbers 11:26 Two men stayed in the camp, one named Eldad and the other Medad. God's spirit was with them. They were listed to go to the tent but did not go. Instead, they spoke God's word in the camp.
Numbers 11:27 A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp."
Numbers 11:28 Joshua, son of Nun, who served Moses, replied, "Moses, tell them to stop."
Numbers 11:29 And Moses said to him, "Are you jealous for me? I wish that all God's people were prophets and that God would give them his spirit!"
Numbers 11:30 Moses went into the camp with the elders of Israel.
Numbers 11:31 A wind from God blew, and brought quails from the sea, dropping them near the camp, about a day's walk on one side and on the other side, all around the camp, and about two cubits deep on the ground.
Numbers 11:32 The people stood all day, all night, and the next day, collecting quails. The one who collected the least got ten baskets full. They laid them out around the camp.
Numbers 11:33 While the meat was still in their mouths, before they could chew it, God became very angry with the people, and God struck them with a terrible plague.
Numbers 11:34 He named that place Graves of Craving because there they buried the people who had strong desires.
Numbers 11:35 The people traveled from Kibrothhattaavah to Hazeroth and stayed there.

Numbers 12:1 Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because he married a woman from Ethiopia.
Numbers 12:2 They asked, "Has God spoken only through Moses? Hasn't he also spoken through us?" And God heard this.
Numbers 12:3 Moses was the humblest man on earth, more than anyone else.
Numbers 12:4 God spoke suddenly to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, saying, "You three come to the meeting tent." And the three of them went out.
Numbers 12:5 God came down in the cloud pillar, stood at the tabernacle entrance, and called Aaron and Miriam, and they both came out.
Numbers 12:6 He said, "Listen to me: If there's a prophet with you, God will reveal himself in a vision and speak to him in a dream."
Numbers 12:7 My servant Moses is different; he is trustworthy in all my household.
Numbers 12:8 I will talk directly and clearly with him, not in riddles, and he will see a form of God. So why weren't you afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
Numbers 12:9 God became angry with them, and he left.
Numbers 12:10 The cloud moved away from the tent, and Miriam had a skin disease, white like snow. Aaron saw Miriam and she had the skin disease.
Numbers 12:11 Aaron said to Moses, "Sorry, my lord, I ask you, don't blame us for the foolish things we have done and for our sins."
Numbers 12:12 Do not let her be like a newborn that is half dead with rotting flesh.
Numbers 12:13 Moses called out to God, saying, "Please God, heal her now."
Numbers 12:14 God told Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, wouldn't she feel shame for seven days? Keep her out of the camp for seven days, and after that, she can come back."
Numbers 12:15 Miriam had to stay outside the camp for seven days; the people did not move on until Miriam was allowed back in.
Numbers 12:16 Later, the people left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran wilderness.

Numbers 13:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 13:2 Send people to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each ancestral tribe, send one leader.
Numbers 13:3 Moses, following God's command, sent them from the Paran desert: all those men were leaders of the Israelites.
Numbers 13:4 Their names were these: from Reuben's tribe, Shammua, Zaccur's son.
Numbers 13:5 From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat, Hori's son.
Numbers 13:6 Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, was from the tribe of Judah.
Numbers 13:7 From the Issachar tribe, Igal, Joseph's son.
Numbers 13:8 From the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.
Numbers 13:9 From the tribe of Benjamin, Palti, Raphu's son.
Numbers 13:10 From Zebulun's tribe, Gaddiel, Sodi's son.
Numbers 13:11 From Joseph's tribe, that is, from Manasseh's tribe, Gaddi, Susi's son.
Numbers 13:12 From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli.
Numbers 13:13 From Asher's tribe, Sethur, Michael's son.
Numbers 13:14 Nahbi, Vophsi's son, was from the tribe of Naphtali.
Numbers 13:15 From the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
Numbers 13:16 These are the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. And Moses named Oshea, Nun's son, Joshua.
Numbers 13:17 Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan and told them, "Go up from the south and climb into the mountains."
Numbers 13:18 Look at the land and what it's like, and the people living there, whether they are strong or weak, and if there are many or just a few.
Numbers 13:19 Find out about the land where they live, whether it is good or bad, and what kind of cities they live in, whether they are camps or fortified cities.
Numbers 13:20 Describe the land, if it's rich or poor, and if there are trees or not. Be brave and bring back some of the land's fruit. It was the season for early grapes.
Numbers 13:21 They went and explored the land from the Zin desert to Rehob, near Hamath.
Numbers 13:22 They went up from the south and arrived at Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. (Hebron was founded seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
Numbers 13:23 They reached Eshcol's stream, cut a grape branch with one bunch of grapes, carried it on a pole between two, and took pomegranates and figs.
Numbers 13:24 The place was named Eshcol Creek because the Israelites cut a bunch of grapes from there.
Numbers 13:25 They came back from exploring the land after forty days.
Numbers 13:26 They went and returned to Moses, Aaron, and all the Israelites at the Paran desert, near Kadesh, and told them and everyone what they saw and showed them the fruit of the land.
Numbers 13:27 They told him, "We went to the land you sent us to, and it is full of milk and honey; this is its fruit."
Numbers 13:28 But the people living in the land are strong, and their cities have high walls and are very big. Also, we saw the descendants of Anak there.
Numbers 13:29 The Amalekites live in the southern land; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the mountains; and the Canaanites live by the sea and near the Jordan river.
Numbers 13:30 Caleb calmed the people in front of Moses and said, "Let's go right now and take the land; we can definitely conquer it."
Numbers 13:31 But the men who went with him said, "We can't attack those people; they are stronger than us."
Numbers 13:32 They gave a bad report about the land they explored to the Israelites, saying, "The land we went to check out is one that destroys its people, and everyone we saw there is very tall."
Numbers 13:33 We saw giants there, Anak's descendants, who were from the giants. We felt like grasshoppers to ourselves, and that's how we seemed to them.

Numbers 14:1 The whole group raised their voices, cried, and the people cried all night.
Numbers 14:2 All the Israelites complained against Moses and Aaron, and the whole group said to them, "If only we had died in Egypt! Or if only we had died in this desert!"
Numbers 14:3 Why did God bring us to this land to be killed by the sword and to have our wives and children taken away? Wouldn't it have been better to go back to Egypt?
Numbers 14:4 They said to each other, "Let's choose a leader and go back to Egypt."
Numbers 14:5 Then Moses and Aaron fell down with their faces to the ground in front of all the Israelites gathered there.
Numbers 14:6 Joshua, Nun's son, and Caleb, Jephunneh's son, who had explored the land, tore their clothes.
Numbers 14:7 They told all the Israelites, "The land we explored is a very good land."
Numbers 14:8 If God is pleased with us, then he will take us into this land and give it to us; a land filled with milk and honey.
Numbers 14:9 Do not go against God, and do not be afraid of the people in the land; they are like food for us. Their protection is gone, and God is with us. Do not fear them.
Numbers 14:10 The whole group wanted to throw stones at them. Then God's presence showed up at the meeting tent in front of all the Israelites.
Numbers 14:11 God said to Moses, "How long will these people keep annoying me? And how long will it take before they trust me, despite all the miracles I’ve done for them?"
Numbers 14:12 I will strike them with disease, disown them, and make you into a greater and stronger nation than they are.
Numbers 14:13 And Moses said to God, "Then the Egyptians will hear about it, because you brought these people out with your power from among them."
Numbers 14:14 They will tell the people of this land that you, God, are with this group, you are seen directly, and your cloud is over them. You lead them with a cloud column in the day and a fire column at night.
Numbers 14:15 If you kill all these people at once, then the nations who have heard about you will say,
Numbers 14:16 God could not take these people into the land he promised them, so he killed them in the desert.
Numbers 14:17 Now, I ask you, let God's power be great, just as you have said.
Numbers 14:18 God is patient and very merciful, forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion, but not excusing the guilty, making the children bear the sins of their parents to the third and fourth generation.
Numbers 14:19 Please forgive the wrongdoings of these people because of your great mercy, just as you have forgiven them from the time they left Egypt until now.
Numbers 14:20 God said, I have forgiven as you asked.
Numbers 14:21 As sure as I am alive, the whole world will be filled with the glory of God.
Numbers 14:22 Because all those men who saw my glory and the miracles I did in Egypt and the wilderness have tested me ten times and have not listened to my voice;
Numbers 14:23 They will not see the land that I promised to their ancestors, nor will any who angered me see it.
Numbers 14:24 But my servant Caleb, because he was different and followed me completely, I will lead him into the land he explored, and his descendants will own it.
Numbers 14:25 The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow, go back and head into the desert towards the Red Sea.
Numbers 14:26 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying.
Numbers 14:27 How long must I put up with these wicked people who complain against me? I have heard the complaints of the Israelites, which they keep making against me.
Numbers 14:28 Tell them, 'As surely as I am alive,' says God, 'I will do to you exactly what you said to me.'
Numbers 14:29 Your dead bodies will lie in the desert; and everyone of you counted, from age twenty and older who complained against me, will not enter the land.
Numbers 14:30 Certainly, you will not enter the land that I promised you would live in, except for Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
Numbers 14:31 I will bring in your little ones, whom you said would be victims, and they will get to know the land you did not value.
Numbers 14:32 Your dead bodies will fall in this desert.
Numbers 14:33 Your children will walk in the desert for forty years and suffer for your unfaithfulness until your bodies are gone in the desert.
Numbers 14:34 For the same number of days you explored the land, forty days, you will suffer for your wrongs, one year for each day, totaling forty years, and you will understand my broken promise.
Numbers 14:35 I, God, have said I will definitely do it to all this wicked group that has come together against me: they will be destroyed in this desert and they will die there.
Numbers 14:36 The men Moses sent to explore the land came back and made everyone complain about him by spreading false reports about the land.
Numbers 14:37 The men who told the bad news about the land died from sickness in front of God.
Numbers 14:38 But Joshua, Nun's son, and Caleb, Jephunneh's son, who had explored the land, were still alive.
Numbers 14:39 Moses told these words to all the Israelites, and the people felt very sad.
Numbers 14:40 They got up early in the morning, went to the mountain top, and said, "Look, we're here and will go to the place God has promised, because we have sinned."
Numbers 14:41 Moses asked, "Why do you break God's command? It will not succeed."
Numbers 14:42 Do not go up, because God is not with you; so you won't be defeated by your enemies.
Numbers 14:43 The Amalekites and the Canaanites are in front of you, and you will die by the sword because you have turned away from God, so God will not be with you.
Numbers 14:44 But they dared to go up to the hilltop; still, the box of God's agreement and Moses did not leave the camp.
Numbers 14:45 The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill came down, attacked them, and beat them all the way to Hormah.

Numbers 15:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 15:2 Talk to the people of Israel and tell them, "When you arrive in the land where you will live, which I am giving to you,
Numbers 15:3 I will make a fire offering to God, a burnt offering, or a sacrifice for a promise, or a voluntary offering, or during your special feasts, to please God, from the cattle or the sheep.
Numbers 15:4 The person who presents their offering to God must bring a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil.
Numbers 15:5 Prepare one-fourth of a quart of wine as a drink offering with the burnt offering or sacrifice for each lamb.
Numbers 15:6 For a ram, you should make a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of flour mixed with one third of a hin of oil.
Numbers 15:7 For a drink offering, give one-third of a hin of wine as a sweet smell to God.
Numbers 15:8 When you prepare a bull for a burnt offering, or as a sacrifice to keep a promise, or for peace offerings to God:
Numbers 15:9 He must bring a young bull with a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of flour mixed with a half hin of oil.
Numbers 15:10 You should offer half a hin of wine as a drink offering to God, as a fire offering that smells sweet to Him.
Numbers 15:11 Do this for one bull, one ram, one lamb, or one young goat.
Numbers 15:12 Prepare for each person according to the number you have.
Numbers 15:13 Everyone born in the country must follow these rules when they give a fire offering that smells good to God.
Numbers 15:14 If a foreigner stays with you, or anyone else who lives with you through generations, and wants to make a fire offering that smells good to God, they should do it just like you do.
Numbers 15:15 One rule is for all of you in the congregation and for the foreigner staying with you, a lasting rule for all your generations: just like you, the foreigner will be before God.
Numbers 15:16 One rule and one way will be for you and for the foreigner staying with you.
Numbers 15:17 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 15:18 Tell the people of Israel, when you enter the land I am taking you to,
Numbers 15:19 When you eat the bread from the land, you must give a portion as an offering to God.
Numbers 15:20 You must give a piece of the first of your bread dough as a lifted offering: just as you lift the offering from the threshing floor, you must lift this one too.
Numbers 15:21 Give the first part of your dough to God as a special offering throughout your generations.
Numbers 15:22 If you have made a mistake and not followed all these commands that God gave to Moses,
Numbers 15:23 Do everything God told you through Moses, starting from when God gave Moses the instructions, for all future generations.
Numbers 15:24 If the people sin without knowing it, they must bring a young bull as a burnt offering to God, with its grain and drink offerings as usual, and a goat for a sin offering.
Numbers 15:25 The priest will ask God to forgive all of Israel's people, and they will be forgiven because they did not know what they were doing. They must bring their fire offering and sin offering to God because they did not know.
Numbers 15:26 The whole community of Israel's children and the foreigner living with them will be forgiven, because everyone made a mistake without knowing.
Numbers 15:27 If someone sins without knowing, they must offer a one-year-old female goat as a sin offering.
Numbers 15:28 The priest will ask God to forgive the person who sins without knowing, and God will forgive him.
Numbers 15:29 Everyone must follow the same rule for accidental wrongs—this applies to both the native-born Israelites and foreigners living with them.
Numbers 15:30 But the person who deliberately does something wrong, whether they are a native or a foreigner, insults God, and that person will be separated from their community.
Numbers 15:31 Because he has looked down on God's word and broken his command, that person will be completely cut off; his wrongdoings will be on him.
Numbers 15:32 While the Israelites were in the desert, they found a man collecting sticks on the Sabbath.
Numbers 15:33 The people who saw him picking up sticks took him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.
Numbers 15:34 They held him because it was not clear what should be done to him.
Numbers 15:35 God told Moses, "The man must be put to death: everyone must throw stones at him outside the camp."
Numbers 15:36 The whole group took him outside the camp and threw stones at him until he died, just as God had told Moses.
Numbers 15:37 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 15:38 Tell the people of Israel to make tassels on the edges of their clothes for all time, and to add a blue ribbon on each tassel.
Numbers 15:39 It will be a tassel for you to look at and remember all of God's commands and follow them, and not to follow your own desires and sights, which lead you away.
Numbers 15:40 Remember and follow all my commands, and be pure for your God.
Numbers 15:41 I am God, your God, who took you out of Egypt to be your God: I am God, your God.

Numbers 16:1 Now Korah, Izhar's son, Kohath's grandson, Levi's great-grandson, and Dathan and Abiram, Eliab's sons, and On, Peleth's son, all from Reuben's family, gathered people together.
Numbers 16:2 They stood up against Moses, together with some Israelites, 250 leaders of the community, well-known and respected men.
Numbers 16:3 They joined together against Moses and Aaron, and told them, "You are taking on too much power, while the whole community is holy, each one of them, and God is with them. So why do you raise yourselves above God's community?"
Numbers 16:4 When Moses heard this, he fell on his face.
Numbers 16:5 He said to Korah and his group, "Tomorrow God will show who belongs to him and who is holy; he will bring close to him the one he has chosen."
Numbers 16:6 Do this: Take your incense burners, Korah, and everyone with you.
Numbers 16:7 Put fire in it and add incense to it before God tomorrow; the man God chooses will be holy. You are overstepping your boundaries, descendants of Levi.
Numbers 16:8 Moses said to Korah, "Please listen, you Levites."
Numbers 16:9 Do you think it's a small thing that the God of Israel chose you from Israel's people to come close to serve in God's tent and to serve the people?
Numbers 16:10 He brought you close to him, and also all your brother Levites with you: and now do you want to be priests too?
Numbers 16:11 You and your group have come together against God. Why are you complaining about Aaron?
Numbers 16:12 Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, "We will not come."
Numbers 16:13 Is it a small matter that you have led us out of a land filled with milk and honey, to let us die in the desert, unless you want to be our total leader?
Numbers 16:14 You did not bring us to a land filled with milk and honey, nor give us fields and vineyards as our own. Will you blind these men? We will not go up.
Numbers 16:15 Moses was very angry and said to God, "Do not accept their offering: I have not taken a single donkey from them, nor have I harmed any of them."
Numbers 16:16 Moses said to Korah, "You and your group must come before God, along with Aaron, tomorrow."
Numbers 16:17 Each person take their fire pan, add incense to it, and present it before God, 250 fire pans; you and Aaron do the same with your fire pans.
Numbers 16:18 Each man took his censer, filled it with fire, added incense, and stood at the entrance of the meeting tent with Moses and Aaron.
Numbers 16:19 Korah brought the whole community to the entrance of the meeting tent, and God's glory was seen by everyone.
Numbers 16:20 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Numbers 16:21 Stay away from these people so I can destroy them quickly.
Numbers 16:22 They fell to the ground and said, "Oh God, the God of everyone's spirit, if one person sins, will You be angry with everyone?"
Numbers 16:23 God spoke to Moses and said,
Numbers 16:24 Tell the people, "Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."
Numbers 16:25 Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the leaders of Israel went with him.
Numbers 16:26 He told the people, "Please move away from these evil men's tents and don't touch their things, or you might get destroyed because of their sins."
Numbers 16:27 They moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on all sides. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents with their wives, sons, and young children.
Numbers 16:28 Moses said, "You will see that God has sent me to do all these things; I did not do them on my own."
Numbers 16:29 If these men die like everyone else, or if they meet the fate everyone else does, then God has not sent me.
Numbers 16:30 But if God does something new, and the ground opens and swallows them with everything they have, and they fall alive into a hole, then you will know that these men have angered God.
Numbers 16:31 After he finished saying all these things, the ground split open beneath them.
Numbers 16:32 The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their homes, all the men related to Korah, and all their belongings.
Numbers 16:33 They and everything that belonged to them went down alive into the hole, and the earth closed over them. They died and were gone from the community.
Numbers 16:34 Everyone in Israel around them ran away when they heard the shouting, because they were afraid the ground might swallow them too.
Numbers 16:35 A fire came from God and burned up the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense.
Numbers 16:36 God spoke to Moses and said,
Numbers 16:37 Tell Eleazar, Aaron's son and a priest, to pick up the incense burners from the fire and throw the coals far away, because they are holy.
Numbers 16:38 Use the incense burners of these sinners who harmed themselves to make thin sheets to cover the altar. Because they presented them before God, they are now holy, and they will be a reminder to the people of Israel.
Numbers 16:39 Eleazar the priest took the bronze incense holders used by those who died in the fire, and they were shaped into wide sheets to cover the altar.
Numbers 16:40 This will remind the people of Israel that only those from Aaron's family can come close to burn incense before God, so no one will be like Korah and his followers, just as God told Moses.
Numbers 16:41 But the next day, the whole Israelite community complained against Moses and Aaron, saying, "You have killed God's people."
Numbers 16:42 When the people gathered against Moses and Aaron, they looked at the meeting tent and saw a cloud over it; God's glory showed.
Numbers 16:43 Moses and Aaron went to the meeting tent.
Numbers 16:44 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 16:45 Move away from these people, so I can quickly destroy them. And they fell on their faces.
Numbers 16:46 Moses told Aaron, "Take a censer, put fire in it from the altar, add incense, and go fast to the people to ask God to forgive them. God is angry and the sickness has started."
Numbers 16:47 Aaron did as Moses said, hurried to where the people were, and saw that the sickness had started among them. He burned incense and asked God to forgive the people.
Numbers 16:48 He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped.
Numbers 16:49 The ones who died from the sickness were 14,700, not including those who died because of Korah's issue.
Numbers 16:50 Aaron went back to Moses at the entrance of the meeting tent, and the plague stopped.

Numbers 17:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 17:2 Talk to the people of Israel, and get a stick from each one based on their family leader’s house, making twelve sticks in total: write each man's name on his stick.
Numbers 17:3 Write Aaron's name on Levi's staff, because one staff represents the leader of their family.
Numbers 17:4 Put them in the meeting tent in front of the covenant, where I will meet you.
Numbers 17:5 The man's stick I pick will flower, and I will stop the complaints of the Israelites against you.
Numbers 17:6 Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each chief gave him a stick, one for each chief from their family groups, making twelve sticks total, including Aaron's stick among them.
Numbers 17:7 Moses put the rods in front of God in the tent of meeting.
Numbers 17:8 The next day, Moses entered the tent of testimony and saw that Aaron's staff for the Levi family had sprouted, produced buds, flowered, and grown almonds.
Numbers 17:9 Moses brought all the rods from God to the Israelites, and they saw and each man took his own rod.
Numbers 17:10 God told Moses, "Bring Aaron's staff back before the testimony to be saved as a sign for the rebels; and you will completely remove their complaints from me, so they do not die."
Numbers 17:11 Moses did exactly what God told him to do.
Numbers 17:12 The Israelites said to Moses, "Look, we're going to die, we're all going to die."
Numbers 17:13 Anyone who comes close to God's tent will die: are we going to keep dying?

Numbers 18:1 God said to Aaron, "You, your sons, and your family must take responsibility for any wrongs done to the holy place, and you and your sons must also take responsibility for the mistakes in your priestly duties."
Numbers 18:2 Bring your relatives from the Levi tribe, your father's tribe, with you so they can help and serve you. But you and your sons must serve in front of the tent of testimony.
Numbers 18:3 They must take care of your duties and the duties of the whole tent, but they must not touch the holy objects or the altar, so that neither they nor you will die.
Numbers 18:4 They will join you and take care of the meeting tent's duties for all its service, and no outsider will come close to you.
Numbers 18:5 You must take care of the sacred place and the altar, so that God's anger will no longer fall on the people of Israel.
Numbers 18:6 I have chosen your fellow Levites from the Israelites to be a gift to you, so they can serve at the meeting tent for God.
Numbers 18:7 So you and your sons must do the duties of priests for all that concerns the altar and what is inside the curtain. You are to serve: I have given you the job of being priests as a gift. But anyone else who comes close will be killed.
Numbers 18:8 God spoke to Aaron: Look, I have given you responsibility for my lifted offerings, all the holy gifts of the Israelites. I give them to you and your sons as your due, forever, because you are anointed.
Numbers 18:9 These are the very holy gifts set aside for you: their grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings that they give to God will be very holy for you and your sons.
Numbers 18:10 Eat it in the most holy place; every man can eat it; it is sacred for you.
Numbers 18:11 This is yours: the lifted gift and all the Israelites' waved offerings. I have given them to you, and to your sons and daughters, as a law forever. Anyone in your family who is clean may eat it.
Numbers 18:12 I have given you all the finest olive oil, the best wine, and the best wheat, which are the first things they give to God.
Numbers 18:13 Whatever first fruit is harvested from the land, which people bring to God, will belong to you; everyone who is clean in your family can eat it.
Numbers 18:14 In Israel, anything dedicated will belong to you.
Numbers 18:15 Every firstborn of any creature offered to God, human or animal, will be yours. However, you must buy back the firstborn of humans and unclean animals.
Numbers 18:16 You must buy back anyone a month old or older as you have estimated their value, for the price of five shekels in the sanctuary currency, which equals twenty gerahs.
Numbers 18:17 Do not buy back the first baby of a cow, sheep, or goat, because they are holy. You must put their blood on the altar and burn their fat. This is a fire offering that pleases God.
Numbers 18:18 The meat of those animals will be yours, just like the breast that is waved and the right thigh are yours.
Numbers 18:19 I have given you and your sons and daughters all the lifted gifts of the holy items that the people of Israel give to God as a permanent rule: it's a lasting salt agreement before God for you and your descendants.
Numbers 18:20 God spoke to Aaron, "You will not own land among them or have a share with them: I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites."
Numbers 18:21 Look, I have given the Levites all the tithes in Israel as their inheritance for the work they do, the work at the meeting tent.
Numbers 18:22 From now on, the Israelites must not come close to the meeting tent, or they will be guilty of sin and die.
Numbers 18:23 The Levites must work in the meeting tent, and they will be responsible for their wrongs. This rule will last forever for all your descendants, and the Levites will not own any land among the people of Israel.
Numbers 18:24 But I have given the Israelites' tithes, which they give to God, to the Levites as their inheritance. So I told them they will have no property among the Israelites.
Numbers 18:25 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 18:26 Tell the Levites to say this: When you receive the tithes from the Israelites that I have given you as your inheritance, you must give a tenth of that tithe to God as a special offering.
Numbers 18:27 Your special gift will be counted for you as if it were grain from the threshing floor or the full amount of wine from the winepress.
Numbers 18:28 You must also give God a special gift from all the tithes you get from the Israelites; you will give part of that gift to Aaron the priest as God's special offering.
Numbers 18:29 From all the gifts you give, you must present all that is lifted up to God, the very best and holy part of it.
Numbers 18:30 So you will tell them, when you have taken the best part from it, then it will be considered for the Levites as extra from the grain field and extra from the wine-making place.
Numbers 18:31 You can eat it wherever you are, you and your families, because it is your pay for working at the meeting tent.
Numbers 18:32 You will not be guilty if you set aside the best part of it; do not make the Israelites' sacred things unclean, or you will die.

Numbers 19:1 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
Numbers 19:2 This is the rule of the law that God has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red cow that is perfect, with no flaws, and that has never worn a yoke.
Numbers 19:3 Give her to Priest Eleazar to take her outside the camp, and someone will kill her in front of him.
Numbers 19:4 The priest Eleazar will take some of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle it seven times in front of the meeting tent.
Numbers 19:5 Someone will burn the cow while he watches; they will burn her skin, meat, blood, and poop.
Numbers 19:6 The priest will take cedar wood, hyssop, and red yarn and throw them into the heifer's burning fire.
Numbers 19:7 The priest must wash his clothes and bathe himself in water; after that, he can enter the camp, but he will be unclean until evening.
Numbers 19:8 The person who burns her must wash their clothes in water, bathe themselves in water, and will be unclean until evening.
Numbers 19:9 A clean person must collect the cow's ashes and put them outside the camp in a clean area. These ashes are for the Israelite community to use in a special cleansing water. It is used for purifying from sin.
Numbers 19:10 The person who collects the heifer's ashes must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening. This rule will always apply to the Israelites and any foreigners living with them.
Numbers 19:11 Anyone who touches a dead person's body will be unclean for seven days.
Numbers 19:12 He must clean himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he will be clean. But if he does not clean himself on the third day, then he will not be clean on the seventh day.
Numbers 19:13 Anyone who touches a dead person and does not clean themselves, makes God's tent dirty; they will be separated from Israel. If the special water was not used on him, he is unclean; his dirtiness remains.
Numbers 19:14 This rule applies when someone dies in a tent: anyone who enters the tent and everything inside will be not clean for seven days.
Numbers 19:15 Every container without a lid tied on it is not clean.
Numbers 19:16 Anyone who touches someone killed by a sword outside, or a dead body, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
Numbers 19:17 For a person who is not clean, they must take some of the ashes from the burned cow used for sin cleaning, and mix these ashes with fresh water in a container.
Numbers 19:18 A clean person will take hyssop, dip it in water, and sprinkle it on the tent, all the objects, the people there, and anyone who touched a bone, a dead body, or a grave.
Numbers 19:19 A clean person must sprinkle water on the unclean person on the third and seventh days. On the seventh day, the unclean person must wash themselves, clean their clothes, and bathe in water. By evening, they will be clean.
Numbers 19:20 If a person is unclean and does not cleanse himself, he will be removed from the community because he has made God's sanctuary dirty; he has not had the cleansing water sprinkled on him, so he is unclean.
Numbers 19:21 This rule will always apply: the person who uses the special water must wash their clothes; and anyone who touches the special water will be unclean until evening.
Numbers 19:22 Whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and the person who touches it will be unclean until evening.

Numbers 20:1 The Israelites, all of them, came to the Zin desert in the first month. They stayed in Kadesh where Miriam died and was buried.
Numbers 20:2 The people had no water and they complained to Moses and Aaron.
Numbers 20:3 The people argued with Moses and said, "If only we had died like our brothers did in front of God!"
Numbers 20:4 Why did you lead God's people into this desert for us and our animals to die here?
Numbers 20:5 Why did you bring us from Egypt to this bad place? It has no grain, figs, grapevines, pomegranates, or water to drink.
Numbers 20:6 Moses and Aaron left the gathering and went to the entrance of the meeting tent, and they fell on their faces: and God's glory showed to them.
Numbers 20:7 God spoke to Moses and said,
Numbers 20:8 Take the staff, and together with your brother Aaron, gather the people. Then talk to the rock while they watch, and it will release water. You will bring water from the rock for them and their animals to drink.
Numbers 20:9 Moses took the staff from where it was in front of God, just as he was told.
Numbers 20:10 Moses and Aaron brought all the people to the rock, and Moses said to them, "Listen, you rebels, should we get you water from this rock?"
Numbers 20:11 Moses raised his hand and struck the rock two times with his rod, and plenty of water flowed out, so the people and their animals drank.
Numbers 20:12 God spoke to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me enough to show my holiness before the Israelites, you will not bring this group into the land I have given them."
Numbers 20:13 This is the water of Meribah where the people of Israel argued with God, and through this, God showed his holiness among them.
Numbers 20:14 Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying, "Your brother Israel says, 'You know about all the hardships that have happened to us.'"
Numbers 20:15 Our ancestors went to Egypt, we lived there for a long time, and the Egyptians treated us and our ancestors badly.
Numbers 20:16 When we called out to God, He listened to us, sent an angel, and led us out of Egypt. Now, we are in Kadesh, a city at the edge of your territory.
Numbers 20:17 Please let us travel through your land. We won't go through your fields or vineyards, nor will we drink from your wells. We'll stay on the main road and won't turn right or left until we've crossed your borders.
Numbers 20:18 Edom said to him, "You cannot go through my land or I will attack you with the sword."
Numbers 20:19 The Israelites told him, "We will travel on the main road. If we and our animals drink your water, we will pay for it. We will just pass through on foot without doing anything else."
Numbers 20:20 He said, "You cannot pass." Then Edom came out to face him with many people and strong force.
Numbers 20:21 So Edom would not let Israel go through their land, so Israel went a different way from them.
Numbers 20:22 The Israelites, all the people, traveled from Kadesh to Mount Hor.
Numbers 20:23 God spoke to Moses and Aaron on Mount Hor, near the border of Edom, saying,
Numbers 20:24 Aaron will join his ancestors when he dies, because he will not go into the land I have given to the Israelites, since you both disobeyed my command at the waters of Meribah.
Numbers 20:25 Take Aaron and his son Eleazar, and take them up to Mount Hor.
Numbers 20:26 Take off Aaron's clothes and put them on Eleazar, his son. Aaron will then join his ancestors and die there.
Numbers 20:27 Moses did what God told him; they climbed Mount Hor while everyone watched.
Numbers 20:28 Moses took off Aaron's clothes and dressed Eleazar, his son, in them. Aaron died at the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar went down from the mountain.
Numbers 20:29 When everyone saw that Aaron had died, they all mourned for him for thirty days, including all the people of Israel.

Numbers 21:1 When King Arad of Canaan who lived in the south heard that Israel was traveling by the spy's path, he attacked Israel and captured some of them.
Numbers 21:2 Israel made a promise to God, saying, "If you really help me defeat these people, then I will completely destroy their towns."
Numbers 21:3 God listened to Israel's voice, delivered the Canaanites, and they completely destroyed them and their cities; and he named the place Hormah.
Numbers 21:4 They traveled from Mount Hor towards the Red Sea to go around the land of Edom; the people were very tired because of the journey.
Numbers 21:5 The people complained against God and Moses, asking, "Why did you take us out of Egypt to die in the desert? There's no bread or water, and we hate this worthless food."
Numbers 21:6 God sent venomous snakes among the people, and they bit the people; and many of the Israelites died.
Numbers 21:7 So the people went to Moses and said, "We have done wrong because we spoke against God and you. Ask God to remove the snakes from us." And Moses prayed for the people.
Numbers 21:8 God told Moses, "Make a fiery snake and put it on a pole: anyone who is bitten can look at it and live."
Numbers 21:9 Moses made a brass snake and put it on a pole. If anyone was bitten by a snake and looked at the brass snake, they lived.
Numbers 21:10 The Israelites moved on and camped at Oboth.
Numbers 21:11 They traveled from Oboth and camped at Ijeabarim in the desert near Moab, facing the sunrise.
Numbers 21:12 From there they moved and camped in the Zared Valley.
Numbers 21:13 They moved from there and set up camp beyond the Arnon River in the desert that extends from the territory of the Amorites. The Arnon River marks the boundary between Moab and the Amorites.
Numbers 21:14 This is why it is written in the Book of God's Wars, what God did at the Red Sea and in the streams of Arnon.
Numbers 21:15 By the stream of the brooks that flow to Ar's home and run along the edge of Moab.
Numbers 21:16 From there, they traveled to Beer, the well where God told Moses to bring the people together so He could provide them with water.
Numbers 21:17 Then Israel sang this song: "Come up, O well; sing to it."
Numbers 21:18 The leaders dug the well, the noble people dug it, following the lawgiver's orders, using their staffs. Then they traveled from the desert to Mattanah.
Numbers 21:19 From Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
Numbers 21:20 From Bamoth in the valley, in Moab's land, to Pisgah's peak, looking at Jeshimon.
Numbers 21:21 Israel sent messages to Sihon, the Amorite king, saying,
Numbers 21:22 Let me go through your land: we won't enter the fields or vineyards; we won't drink well water; but we'll stay on the main road until we're beyond your borders.
Numbers 21:23 Sihon did not let Israel go through his land. Instead, Sihon brought all his people and went out to the desert to meet Israel. He reached Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Numbers 21:24 Israel defeated him with the sword and took over his land from Arnon to Jabbok, up to the land of the Ammonites, because the Ammonites' border was well-defended.
Numbers 21:25 Israel captured all these towns and lived in the Amorite towns, including Heshbon and its nearby settlements.
Numbers 21:26 Heshbon was King Sihon of the Amorites' city. He fought the previous Moab king and took all his territory up to the Arnon River.
Numbers 21:27 People who use wise sayings tell us, "Go to Heshbon, and let's rebuild Sihon's city."
Numbers 21:28 A fire has started in Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's city; it burned up Ar of Moab, and the rulers on Arnon's hills.
Numbers 21:29 Trouble comes to you, Moab! You are ruined, people of Chemosh: your god has let your surviving sons and daughters be taken captive by Sihon, king of the Amorites.
Numbers 21:30 We attacked them; Heshbon is destroyed up to Dibon, and we ruined them up to Nophah, which extends to Medeba.
Numbers 21:31 Israel lived in the Amorites' land.
Numbers 21:32 Moses sent spies to Jaazer, they captured its villages, and forced out the Amorites living there.
Numbers 21:33 They turned and went toward Bashan, and Og, the king of Bashan, came out to fight them with all his people at Edrei.
Numbers 21:34 God said to Moses, "Don't be afraid of him, for I have given him, his people, and his land into your control; and you will do to him what you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon."
Numbers 21:35 They struck him, his sons, and all his people until nobody was left alive; then they took over his land.

Numbers 22:1 The Israelites moved on and camped in the Moab plains near the Jordan River across from Jericho.
Numbers 22:2 Balak, Zippor's son, saw everything Israel did to the Amorites.
Numbers 22:3 Moab was very scared of the people because there were so many, and Moab was troubled because of the children of Israel.
Numbers 22:4 Moab told Midian's leaders, "This group will consume everything around us like an ox eats the field's grass." At that time, Balak, Zippor's son, was king of Moab.
Numbers 22:5 He sent messengers to Balaam, son of Beor, at Pethor by the river in his homeland, to invite him, saying, "Look, a people has come out of Egypt; they cover the land and are settling near me."
Numbers 22:6 Please come now and curse these people for me because they are too powerful. Maybe then I can defeat them and force them out of the land. I know that anyone you bless is blessed, and anyone you curse is cursed.
Numbers 22:7 The leaders of Moab and Midian left with money for fortune-telling and went to Balaam. They told him what Balak had said.
Numbers 22:8 He told them, "Stay here tonight, and I will give you an answer after I hear what God tells me." So the Moab leaders stayed with Balaam.
Numbers 22:9 God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men with you?"
Numbers 22:10 Balaam said to God, "Balak, Zippor's son and Moab's king, has sent for me, saying,
Numbers 22:11 Look, people have left Egypt and they are everywhere. Come and curse them for me; maybe then I can defeat them and drive them away.
Numbers 22:12 God told Balaam, "Do not go with them; do not curse the people, because they are blessed."
Numbers 22:13 Balaam got up in the morning and told Balak's leaders, "Go back to your country, because God will not let me go with you."
Numbers 22:14 The Moab leaders got up, went to Balak, and said, "Balaam won't come with us."
Numbers 22:15 Balak sent even more princes who were greater and more respected than the first ones.
Numbers 22:16 They went to Balaam and told him, "Balak, Zippor's son, says, 'Please don't let anything stop you from coming to me.'"
Numbers 22:17 I will give you great honor and do what you ask: please come and curse these people for me.
Numbers 22:18 Balaam replied to Balak's servants, "Even if Balak gave me a house full of silver and gold, I can't ignore God's command to do anything less or more."
Numbers 22:19 Please stay here tonight, so I can find out what more God will tell me.
Numbers 22:20 God came to Balaam at night and said, "If the men come to call you, get up and go with them; but you must only do what I tell you to do."
Numbers 22:21 Balaam got up in the morning, put a saddle on his donkey, and left with the leaders of Moab.
Numbers 22:22 God became angry because Balaam went, and God's angel stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and he had two servants with him.
Numbers 22:23 The donkey saw God's angel standing on the path with a sword in his hand, so the donkey left the path and went into the field. Balaam hit the donkey to make her go back on the path.
Numbers 22:24 An angel of God stood in a vineyard path with a wall on each side.
Numbers 22:25 When the donkey saw God's angel, she pushed against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot, and he hit her again.
Numbers 22:26 God's angel went on and stopped in a tight space where there was no room to move right or left.
Numbers 22:27 When the donkey saw God's angel, she lay down with Balaam on her; this made Balaam angry, and he hit the donkey with a stick.
Numbers 22:28 God let the donkey talk, and she asked Balaam, "What did I do to you, that you have hit me three times?"
Numbers 22:29 Balaam said to the donkey, "You have made fun of me. If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
Numbers 22:30 The donkey said to Balaam, "Aren't I your donkey, the one you've ridden on since you got me until today? Have I ever acted this way to you before?" And he said, "No."
Numbers 22:31 Then God let Balaam see, and he noticed God's angel standing in the path with a sword ready in his hand, so he bowed deeply and lay face down.
Numbers 22:32 The angel of God said to him, "Why have you hit your donkey three times? Look, I came to oppose you because you are going the wrong way against my will."
Numbers 22:33 The donkey saw me and moved away from me three times. If she hadn't moved away, I would have surely killed you by now, but let her live.
Numbers 22:34 Balaam said to the angel of God, "I have done wrong because I didn't know you were standing in my way. If you're unhappy, I'll go back."
Numbers 22:35 The angel of God told Balaam, "Go with the men, but say only what I tell you to say." So Balaam went with Balak's leaders.
Numbers 22:36 When Balak found out that Balaam had arrived, he went to meet him at a city in Moab, near the edge of the Arnon River, at the farthest boundary.
Numbers 22:37 Balak said to Balaam, "Didn't I send for you urgently to call you? Why didn't you come to me? Can't I reward you with honor?"
Numbers 22:38 Balaam said to Balak, "Look, I have come to you: can I just say anything? I will speak only what God gives me to say."
Numbers 22:39 Balaam went with Balak to Kirjathhuzoth.
Numbers 22:40 Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent them to Balaam and to the leaders with him.
Numbers 22:41 The next day, Balak took Balaam to the high places of Baal so he could see all the people.

Numbers 23:1 Balaam said to Balak, "Make me seven altars here, and get ready seven oxen and seven rams for me here."
Numbers 23:2 Balak did what Balaam said; Balak and Balaam sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
Numbers 23:3 Balaam said to Balak, "Stay by your burnt offering, and I'll go; maybe God will meet me. Whatever he shows me, I'll tell you." Then he went to a high place.
Numbers 23:4 God met Balaam, and Balaam said, "I have set up seven altars and on each altar I have sacrificed a bull and a ram."
Numbers 23:5 God gave Balaam a message and said, "Go back to Balak, and say this."
Numbers 23:6 He went back to him and saw him standing by his burnt offering with all the leaders of Moab.
Numbers 23:7 He began his message, saying, "King Balak of Moab brought me from Aram, from the eastern mountains, and said, 'Come and curse Jacob for me; come and speak against Israel.'"
Numbers 23:8 How can I curse someone who God has not cursed? Or how can I condemn someone who God has not condemned?
Numbers 23:9 From the high rocks I see him, and from the hills I watch him: look, the people will live apart and will not be counted with other nations.
Numbers 23:10 Who can count Jacob's dust, or know the number of a quarter of Israel's people? I want to die like good people do, and end my life the same as theirs!
Numbers 23:11 Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, but look, you have completely blessed them."
Numbers 23:12 He replied, "Shouldn't I be careful to say what God has given me to speak?"
Numbers 23:13 Balak said to him, "Please come with me to another place. You can see only a part of the people from there, not all of them. Curse them for me from that place."
Numbers 23:14 He took him to Zophim's field, up on Pisgah peak, made seven altars, and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
Numbers 23:15 He told Balak, "Stay here by your burnt offering while I go to meet God over there."
Numbers 23:16 God met Balaam, gave him a message, and said, "Go back to Balak and say this."
Numbers 23:17 When he arrived, he saw him standing by his burnt offering with Moab's leaders. And Balak asked, "What has God said?"
Numbers 23:18 He began his message, saying, "Stand up, Balak, and listen; pay attention to me, son of Zippor:
Numbers 23:19 God is not a man who lies, or someone's son who changes his mind. If He says something, won't He do it? If He speaks, won't He make it happen?
Numbers 23:20 Look, I have been ordered to bless: God has given a blessing, and I cannot change it.
Numbers 23:21 God has not seen any wrong in Jacob, nor has He noticed any evil in Israel; God is with him, and there is the sound of a king among them.
Numbers 23:22 God led them out of Egypt; he has the power like a strong wild ox.
Numbers 23:23 There is no magic that can harm Jacob, nor any fortune-telling against Israel. Now it will be said about Jacob and Israel, "Look at what God has done!"
Numbers 23:24 Look, the people will get up like a strong lion and raise themselves like a young lion: they will not rest until they have eaten their kill and drunk the blood of those they have defeated.
Numbers 23:25 Balak told Balaam, "Don't curse or bless them at all."
Numbers 23:26 But Balaam replied to Balak, "Didn't I tell you that I must do everything God says?"
Numbers 23:27 Balak said to Balaam, "Please come with me to another place; maybe from there you can ask God to curse them for me."
Numbers 23:28 Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, with a view over Jeshimon.
Numbers 23:29 Balaam said to Balak, "Make seven altars for me here, and get ready seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
Numbers 23:30 Balak did what Balaam told him to do, and sacrificed a bull and a sheep on each altar.

Numbers 24:1 When Balaam saw that God wanted to bless Israel, he did not look for magic spells like before, but instead he looked towards the desert.
Numbers 24:2 Balaam looked up and saw Israel camping by their tribes; then God's spirit came on him.
Numbers 24:3 He began his message and said, Balaam, Beor's son, who can see clearly, said:
Numbers 24:4 He said, he heard God's words and saw a vision from God, fell into a trance with his eyes open.
Numbers 24:5 How beautiful are your tents, Jacob, and your shelters, Israel!
Numbers 24:6 Valleys spread out, gardens by the river, trees of aloes that God planted, and cedar trees near the water.
Numbers 24:7 He will pour water from his buckets, and his offspring will thrive in many waters, and his king will be greater than Agag, and his kingdom will be lifted high.
Numbers 24:8 God led him out of Egypt; he has strength like a wild ox: he will defeat his enemy nations, break their bones, and shoot them with his arrows.
Numbers 24:9 He crouched, he lay down like a lion, and like a mighty lion: who will provoke him? Happy is the one who blesses you, and cursed is the one who curses you.
Numbers 24:10 Balak became very angry at Balaam and clapped his hands. Then Balak said to Balaam, "I asked you to curse my enemies, but you have completely blessed them three times instead."
Numbers 24:11 So now, go back home: I planned to give you high honor, but God has kept you from it.
Numbers 24:12 Balaam said to Balak, "Didn't I tell your messengers you sent to me, saying,
Numbers 24:13 If Balak offered me a house full of money, I cannot ignore God's command and decide on my own to do good or bad; I will only say what God tells me to.
Numbers 24:14 Now I am going to my people. Come, and I will tell you what this people will do to your people in the future.
Numbers 24:15 He began his message and said: Balaam, Beor's son, the man with open eyes, speaks:
Numbers 24:16 He said, after hearing God's words and understanding the Most High's knowledge, he saw a vision of God while in a trance, yet his eyes were open.
Numbers 24:17 I will see him, but not soon. I will look at him, but he's not close. A star will come from Jacob, and a ruler will rise from Israel. He will defeat Moab's borders and destroy the descendants of Sheth.
Numbers 24:18 Edom will belong to someone, and Seir will also belong to their enemies; Israel will act bravely.
Numbers 24:19 A ruler will come from Jacob's descendants; he will destroy the survivors of the city.
Numbers 24:20 When he saw Amalek, he told his story and said, Amalek was the first among nations, but in the end, he will be destroyed forever.
Numbers 24:21 He saw the Kenites, and began to tell a story, saying, "Your home is strong, and you place your nest in a rock."
Numbers 24:22 The Kenite people will be destroyed, until Assyria takes you away as prisoners.
Numbers 24:23 He began his story and said, "Oh no, who can survive when God does this!"
Numbers 24:24 Ships will come from the shores of Chittim and they will attack Asshur and Eber, and he too will be destroyed forever.
Numbers 24:25 Balaam got up, went back to his home, and Balak went on his way too.

Numbers 25:1 Israel stayed in Shittim, and the people started to have sex with the women of Moab.
Numbers 25:2 They invited the people to the offerings for their gods, and the people ate and worshiped their gods.
Numbers 25:3 Israel worshiped Baal of Peor, and God became angry with Israel.
Numbers 25:4 God told Moses, "Take the leaders of the people and display them in front of God against the sun, so that God's intense anger can be calmed down from Israel."
Numbers 25:5 Moses told the judges of Israel, "Each of you kill the men who followed Baal of Peor."
Numbers 25:6 Look, an Israelite man brought a Midianite woman to his brothers right in front of Moses and all the Israelites while they were crying at the entrance of the meeting tent.
Numbers 25:7 When Phinehas, who was Eleazar's son and Aaron the priest's grandson, saw this, he stood up from among the people and grabbed a spear.
Numbers 25:8 He followed the Israelite man into the tent and stabbed both of them, the man and the woman, in her belly. This stopped the plague among the Israelites.
Numbers 25:9 Twenty-four thousand people died in the plague.
Numbers 25:10 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 25:11 Phinehas, Eleazar's son and Aaron the priest's grandson, stopped my anger against the Israelites by being passionately loyal to me among them, so I didn't destroy the Israelites in my jealousy.
Numbers 25:12 So say, 'Look, I give him my promise of peace:'
Numbers 25:13 He will have it, and his descendants too—the promise of a lasting priesthood; because he was eager for his God, and covered the sins of the Israelites.
Numbers 25:14 The Israelite man who was killed with the Midianite woman was named Zimri, son of Salu, a leader from a top family among the Simeonites.
Numbers 25:15 The Midianite woman who was killed was named Cozbi, Zur's daughter. Zur was a leader of a tribe and a ruling family in Midian.
Numbers 25:16 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 25:17 Trouble the Midianites and strike them down.
Numbers 25:18 They trouble you with their tricks, which they used to deceive you about Peor, and about Cozbi, the Midianite prince's daughter and their sister, who was killed when the plague came because of Peor.

Numbers 26:1 After the plague, God spoke to Moses and Eleazar, Aaron's son the priest, saying,
Numbers 26:2 Count all the Israelites who are 20 years old and above, from each family, who can fight in battles.
Numbers 26:3 Moses and the priest Eleazar talked to them on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho, saying,
Numbers 26:4 Count the people who are 20 years old and older; do as God told Moses and the Israelites when they left Egypt.
Numbers 26:5 Reuben, Israel's oldest son: Reuben's children; Hanoch, who started the Hanoch family; Pallu started the Pallu family.
Numbers 26:6 From Hezron comes the Hezronite family; from Carmi comes the Carmite family.
Numbers 26:7 These are the Reubenite families, and there were 43,730 of them counted.
Numbers 26:8 Pallu's sons were Eliab.
Numbers 26:9 Eliab's sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram were well-known among the people, who fought against Moses and Aaron with Korah's group when they opposed God.
Numbers 26:10 The ground split open and swallowed them with Korah when they died, as fire consumed 250 men; and they became a warning.
Numbers 26:11 However, Korah's children did not die.
Numbers 26:12 Simeon's sons by their families: Nemuel's family, the Nemuelites; Jamin's family, the Jaminites; Jachin's family, the Jachinites.
Numbers 26:13 From Zerah comes the Zarhite family; from Shaul comes the Shaulite family.
Numbers 26:14 These are the Simeonite families, with a total of 22,200 people.
Numbers 26:15 The Gad family groups included: the Zephon group called Zephonites, the Haggi group called Haggites, and the Shuni group called Shunites.
Numbers 26:16 From Ozni's family, the Oznites; from Eri's family, the Erites.
Numbers 26:17 From Arod comes the Arodite family; from Areli, the Areli family.
Numbers 26:18 These are the groups of Gad's descendants, counted at forty-five thousand.
Numbers 26:19 Judah's sons were Er and Onan, and they died in Canaan.
Numbers 26:20 The families of Judah's sons were: from Shelah, the Shelah family; from Perez, the Perez family; and from Zerah, the Zerah family.
Numbers 26:21 Pharez had sons: from Hezron came the Hezronite family; from Hamul came the Hamulite family.
Numbers 26:22 These are the families of Judah, and the count for them is 76,500.
Numbers 26:23 From the family of Issachar: Tola's descendants were the Tola family; Pua's descendants were the Pua family.
Numbers 26:24 From Jashub comes the Jashubite family; from Shimron comes the Shimronite family.
Numbers 26:25 These are the families of Issachar with their total of 64,300 people counted.
Numbers 26:26 The families of Zebulun's sons are: Sered's family the Sardites, Elon's family the Elonites, and Jahleel's family the Jahleelites.
Numbers 26:27 These are the Zebulun family groups and there are 60,500 people in them.
Numbers 26:28 Joseph's sons and their families were Manasseh and Ephraim.
Numbers 26:29 From the descendants of Manasseh: from Machir's family came the Machirites, and Machir was the father of Gilead, from whom the Gileadites are descended.
Numbers 26:30 These are Gilead's sons: From Jeezer comes the Jeezerite family; from Helek comes the Helekite family.
Numbers 26:31 From the Asriel clan comes the Asrielites; from the Shechem clan comes the Shechemites.
Numbers 26:32 From Shemida came the Shemidaites, and from Hepher came the Hepherites.
Numbers 26:33 Zelophehad, Hepher's son, had no sons, only daughters: their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
Numbers 26:34 These are the groups of Manasseh, and the number in them is 52,700.
Numbers 26:35 Ephraim's sons and their families are: from Shuthelah, the Shuthelah family; from Becher, the Becher family; from Tahan, the Tahan family.
Numbers 26:36 Shuthelah had sons, and one was Eran, which started the family of the Eranites.
Numbers 26:37 These are the family groups of Ephraim's sons, numbering thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are Joseph's sons, grouped by families.
Numbers 26:38 Benjamin's sons by their families: Bela's family, the Belaites; Ashbel's family, the Ashbelites; Ahiram's family, the Ahiramites.
Numbers 26:39 From Shupham comes the Shupham family; from Hupham comes the Hupham family.
Numbers 26:40 Bela's sons were Ard and Naaman: from Ard came the Ardite family, and from Naaman came the Naamite family.
Numbers 26:41 These are Benjamin's sons by their families: the counted number was 45,600.
Numbers 26:42 These are the children of Dan by their families: from Shuham comes the Shuhamite family. These are the Dan families by their families.
Numbers 26:43 All the Shuhamite families, when counted, totaled 64,400.
Numbers 26:44 From Asher's descendants by their families: From Jimna, the Jimna family; from Jesui, the Jesui family; from Beriah, the Beriah family.
Numbers 26:45 From Beriah's sons: Heber's descendants are the Heberites; Malchiel's descendants are the Malchielites.
Numbers 26:46 Asher's daughter was named Sarah.
Numbers 26:47 These are the families of Asher's sons by their numbers; there were 53,400 of them.
Numbers 26:48 From Naphtali's sons by their families: Jahzeel's descendants, the Jahzeelites; Guni's descendants, the Gunites.
Numbers 26:49 From Jezer comes the Jezerite family; from Shillem comes the Shillemite family.
Numbers 26:50 Here are the family groups of Naphtali according to their own families: and the number of people in them was 45,400.
Numbers 26:51 The children of Israel were counted as 603,730.
Numbers 26:52 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 26:53 To these people, the land will be given as an inheritance, based on the number of names.
Numbers 26:54 Give more land to those who have more people, and less land to those with fewer people; each group will get land based on its size.
Numbers 26:55 Despite this, the land will be split up by drawing lots; each tribe will receive land based on their ancestors' names.
Numbers 26:56 The land will be divided by drawing lots, giving pieces to both the large and small groups.
Numbers 26:57 These are the Levites counted by their families: from Gershon, the Gershonite family; from Kohath, the Kohathite family; from Merari, the Merarite family.
Numbers 26:58 These are the Levite families: the Libnites, the Hebronites, the Mahlites, the Mushites, and the Korathites. Kohath was the father of Amram.
Numbers 26:59 Amram's wife was named Jochebed, Levi's daughter, born to Levi in Egypt; and she gave birth to Aaron and Moses, and their sister Miriam for Amram.
Numbers 26:60 Aaron had four sons named Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Numbers 26:61 Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire before God.
Numbers 26:62 There were 23,000 males one month old and older counted. They were not counted among the Israelites because they did not receive any land from the Israelites.
Numbers 26:63 Moses and Priest Eleazar counted these people. They counted the Israelites on the Moab plains by the Jordan River near Jericho.
Numbers 26:64 But none of the men counted by Moses and Aaron, the priest, when they counted the Israelites in the Sinai desert, were among these.
Numbers 26:65 God had said they would definitely die in the wilderness. No man was left except Caleb, Jephunneh's son, and Joshua, Nun's son.

Numbers 27:1 Zelophehad's daughters came to Moses. Zelophehad was Hepher’s son, Gilead's son, Machir's son, and Manasseh's son from Joseph's family. His daughters were named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
Numbers 27:2 They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole community at the entrance of the meeting tent, saying,
Numbers 27:3 Our father died alone in the desert, not with those who turned against God with Korah; he died because of his own sin and had no sons.
Numbers 27:4 Why should our father's name disappear from his family because he has no son? Give us property among our father's brothers.
Numbers 27:5 Moses took their case to God.
Numbers 27:6 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 27:7 Zelophehad's daughters are correct: you must give them property to inherit among their father's brothers, and you must give them their father's inheritance.
Numbers 27:8 Tell the people of Israel, if a man dies and has no son, then you must give his property to his daughter.
Numbers 27:9 If he has no daughter, then you must give his inheritance to his brothers.
Numbers 27:10 If he has no brothers, then you should give his inheritance to his uncles.
Numbers 27:11 If his father has no brothers, give his property to the closest relative in his family, and they will own it. This will be a permanent law for the people of Israel, as God told Moses.
Numbers 27:12 God told Moses, "Go up this mountain Abarim and look at the land I have given to the people of Israel."
Numbers 27:13 When you have seen it, you too will die as your brother Aaron did.
Numbers 27:14 You disobeyed my order in the Zin desert, during the people's argument, to show my holiness at the water in front of them: that is the water of Meribah in Kadesh in the Zin desert.
Numbers 27:15 Moses spoke to God, saying,
Numbers 27:16 Let God, the God of everyone's spirit, choose someone to lead the group.
Numbers 27:17 Who can lead them and bring them back, so God's people won't be like sheep without a shepherd.
Numbers 27:18 God told Moses, "Take Joshua, son of Nun, a man with the spirit, and put your hand on him."
Numbers 27:19 Place him in front of Priest Eleazar and all the people; and give him instructions while they watch.
Numbers 27:20 Give him some of your honor so that all the Israelite community will follow his lead.
Numbers 27:21 He will stand in front of priest Eleazar, who will seek advice for him by consulting the Urim before God. They will follow his commands to leave and to return, he and all the Israelites with him, as well as the whole community.
Numbers 27:22 Moses did what God told him: he took Joshua, put him in front of priest Eleazar, and in front of everyone gathered.
Numbers 27:23 He put his hands on him and gave him instructions, just as God had ordered through Moses.

Numbers 28:1 God spoke to Moses and said,
Numbers 28:2 Tell the people of Israel to give me my offerings and the bread for my burnt sacrifices, that please me, at the proper time.
Numbers 28:3 Tell them, "This is the fire sacrifice you must give to God: two perfect lambs, one year old, each day, for a regular burnt offering."
Numbers 28:4 Offer one lamb in the morning and the other lamb in the evening.
Numbers 28:5 Use one-tenth of an ephah of flour and mix it with one-fourth of a hin of olive oil for a grain offering.
Numbers 28:6 This is a regular burnt offering set up at Mount Sinai to please God, a sacrifice burned for God.
Numbers 28:7 Offer one-fourth of a hin of wine for each lamb as a drink offering in the sacred place for God.
Numbers 28:8 Offer the second lamb in the evening with the same grain and drink offerings as in the morning; it will be a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to God.
Numbers 28:9 On the Sabbath, offer two lambs that are one year old and have no defects, along with two measures of flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and the accompanying liquid offering.
Numbers 28:10 This is the special burnt offering for every Sabbath along with the regular burnt offering and its accompanying drink offering.
Numbers 28:11 At the start of each month, you must give a burnt offering to God: two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs that are one year old and have no defects.
Numbers 28:12 Use three cups of flour mixed with oil for the grain offering for one bull and two cups of flour mixed with oil for the grain offering for one ram.
Numbers 28:13 For one sheep, mix a special amount of flour with oil to offer as food; it is a burnt offering, a pleasant smelling sacrifice to God.
Numbers 28:14 Their drink gifts should be half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. This is the monthly burnt offering for each month of the year.
Numbers 28:15 Offer a goat as a sin offering to God, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
Numbers 28:16 On the fourteenth day of the first month is God's Passover.
Numbers 28:17 On the fifteenth day of this month there is a festival; for seven days you must eat bread without yeast.
Numbers 28:18 On the first day, there will be a special gathering; you must not do any regular work on that day.
Numbers 28:19 You must offer a fire sacrifice to God; two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old lambs without any defects.
Numbers 28:20 Offer their grain offering with oil mixed in: give three-tenths of an ephah for a bull and two-tenths for a ram.
Numbers 28:21 Give one-tenth of a measure of grain for each of the seven lambs.
Numbers 28:22 And one goat as a sin sacrifice to make amends for you.
Numbers 28:23 You should give these along with the morning burnt offering that is given every day.
Numbers 28:24 Offer like this every day for seven days: food for a fire sacrifice that smells good to God. Give it along with the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
Numbers 28:25 On the seventh day, you should gather together for a holy meeting; you should not do any regular work.
Numbers 28:26 On the day of the firstfruits, when you present a fresh grain offering to God after your weeks are done, you shall hold a special gathering; you shall not do any regular work.
Numbers 28:27 Give God a burnt offering that smells good: two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old lambs.
Numbers 28:28 They offer flour mixed with oil as their food gift, three-tenths of an ephah for a bull, two-tenths for a ram.
Numbers 28:29 One portion of grain for each lamb, for all seven lambs.
Numbers 28:30 One young goat to make peace with God for you.
Numbers 28:31 You should give these besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and they must be without any defects, along with their drink offerings.

Numbers 29:1 In the seventh month, on the first day, you will gather for a sacred meeting; you won't do any regular work: it's a day for you to blow trumpets.
Numbers 29:2 You must offer a burnt sacrifice that smells good to God; one young bull, one ram, and seven perfect lambs that are one year old.
Numbers 29:3 Their grain offering will be flour mixed with oil, three-tenths of an ephah for a bull and two-tenths for a ram.
Numbers 29:4 Give one-tenth of flour for each of the seven lambs.
Numbers 29:5 One young goat as a sin offering to ask for God's forgiveness for you.
Numbers 29:6 In addition to the monthly burnt offering with its grain offering, the daily burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings, follow the usual rules to make a pleasing fire sacrifice to God.
Numbers 29:7 On the tenth day of the seventh month, you must come together for a special meeting; you must humble yourselves and not do any work on that day.
Numbers 29:8 You must present a burnt offering to God as a pleasing aroma; one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old lambs with no defects.
Numbers 29:9 Their grain offering should be flour mixed with oil: three-tenths for a bull and two-tenths for a ram.
Numbers 29:10 For each lamb, give one-tenth of a bushel of grain, for all seven lambs.
Numbers 29:11 One young goat for a sin offering, along with the atonement sin offering, the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings.
Numbers 29:12 On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you must gather for a holy meeting; you must not do any regular work, and you must celebrate a festival for God for seven days.
