Numbers 29:14 Their grain offering should be flour mixed with oil, 3 parts for each of the 13 bulls and 2 parts for each of the 2 rams.
Numbers 29:15 Give a tenth of an ephah of flour for each of the fourteen lambs.
Numbers 29:16 One goat for a sin offering, along with the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
Numbers 29:17 On the second day, give twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen perfect one-year-old lambs.
Numbers 29:18 Their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs must match their number, in the usual way.
Numbers 29:19 One young goat for a sin offering; in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
Numbers 29:20 On the third day, they offered eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without any defects.
Numbers 29:21 Their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, should be in line with their number, as is the custom.
Numbers 29:22 Offer one goat as a sin sacrifice in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain and drink offerings.
Numbers 29:23 On the fourth day, ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without any defects.
Numbers 29:24 Offer food and drink for the bulls, rams, and lambs in amounts that match their number, as is the custom.
Numbers 29:25 Offer one young goat for a sin sacrifice, in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
Numbers 29:26 On the fifth day, offer nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without any defects.
Numbers 29:27 Their grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs must match their number, as required.
Numbers 29:28 Offer one goat for a sin offering, along with the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
Numbers 29:29 On the sixth day, eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without any defects.
Numbers 29:30 Offer their grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs according to the number required, following the usual way.
Numbers 29:31 And one goat for a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering, with its grain offering, and its drink offering.
Numbers 29:32 On the seventh day, seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs with no flaws.
Numbers 29:33 The food offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs must match the number of animals, as required.
Numbers 29:34 And one goat for a sin offering; along with the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
Numbers 29:35 On the eighth day, have a special meeting and do not do any regular work.
Numbers 29:36 You must give God a burnt offering, a sacrifice burned with fire that smells good: one bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old lambs without any defects.
Numbers 29:37 Their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs must match the number of animals, as required.
Numbers 29:38 And one goat for a sin offering, plus the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
Numbers 29:39 During your special feasts, do these things for God, in addition to your promises and voluntary gifts, and also for your burnt, food, drink, and peace offerings.

Numbers 30:1 Moses told the leaders of the tribes about the children of Israel, saying, "This is what God has commanded."
Numbers 30:2 If a person makes a promise to God, or takes an oath to commit themselves firmly, they must not go back on their word. They must do everything they said they would.
Numbers 30:3 If a young woman makes a promise to God while she is living at her father's home, and commits herself by that promise;
Numbers 30:4 If her father hears her promise or the obligation she has made for herself, and he says nothing, then all her promises and obligations will remain valid.
Numbers 30:5 But if her father forbids her when he hears about it, none of her promises or commitments will count. God will forgive her because her father forbade her.
Numbers 30:6 If she had a husband when she made a vow or said anything to bind herself by a promise;
Numbers 30:7 If her husband hears her vow and says nothing to her about it, then her vows and the pledge by which she obligated herself will stand.
Numbers 30:8 If her husband says no on the day he learns about it, her promise and the words she spoke that committed her will not stand. God will forgive her.
Numbers 30:9 Every promise a widow or a divorced woman makes, binding herself, must be kept by her.
Numbers 30:10 If she made a promise in her husband's home, or committed herself with a sworn agreement;
Numbers 30:11 When her husband heard it and said nothing to her and did not forbid her, then all her promises will count, and every agreement by which she committed herself will count.
Numbers 30:12 But if her husband canceled them on the day he learned about them; then whatever promises she made, or any pledge, will not be valid: her husband has canceled them; and God will forgive her.
Numbers 30:13 Every promise and every serious oath to deny oneself, her husband can confirm it, or her husband can cancel it.
Numbers 30:14 If her husband says nothing to her from day to day, he agrees to all her promises or commitments. He makes them stand because he said nothing when he first heard them.
Numbers 30:15 If he cancels her promises after hearing them, he must take responsibility for her wrong.
Numbers 30:16 These are the rules that God told Moses, for a man and his wife, and for a father and his young daughter living in her father's house.

Numbers 31:1 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 31:2 Get justice for the Israelites against the Midianites; then you will join your ancestors.
Numbers 31:3 Moses said to the people, "Get some of you ready for battle, and attack the Midianites to take revenge for God."
Numbers 31:4 From every tribe of Israel, send a thousand people to fight in the war.
Numbers 31:5 From the thousands of Israel, a thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand ready for battle, were given.
Numbers 31:6 Moses sent a thousand men from each tribe to fight, including Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy items and trumpets to sound.
Numbers 31:7 They fought against the Midianites, as God told Moses; and they killed all the men.
Numbers 31:8 They killed the Midianite kings along with the others who were killed; the kings were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. They also killed Balaam, Beor's son, with the sword.
Numbers 31:9 The people of Israel captured all the women and children of Midian, and took all their cows, sheep, and possessions.
Numbers 31:10 They burned all the cities they lived in, and all their beautiful strongholds, with fire.
Numbers 31:11 They took everything they captured, including people and animals.
Numbers 31:12 They brought the prisoners, the captured goods, and the stolen items to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the Israelites' assembly at the camp on the Moab plains by the Jordan River, close to Jericho.
Numbers 31:13 Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the people went out of the camp to meet them.
Numbers 31:14 Moses was angry with the army officers, the leaders of thousands and the leaders of hundreds, who returned from the battle.
Numbers 31:15 Moses asked them, "Did you keep all the women alive?"
Numbers 31:16 Look, these people led the Israelites, following Balaam's advice, to sin against God at Peor, and a disease spread among God's people.
Numbers 31:17 Now, kill all the boys and every woman who has slept with a man.
Numbers 31:18 Keep alive all the young girls who have never slept with a man for yourselves.
Numbers 31:19 Stay outside the camp for seven days if you've killed someone or touched a dead body. Clean yourselves and your prisoners on the third and seventh days.
Numbers 31:20 Clean all your clothes, everything made of skin, all goat hair items, and all wooden things.
Numbers 31:21 Priest Eleazar told the soldiers who fought in the battle, "This is the rule of the law that God gave to Moses."
Numbers 31:22 Keep only the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead.
Numbers 31:23 Everything that can withstand fire must be passed through it to become clean; however, it must also be purified with special water. But everything that cannot withstand fire must be passed through water.
Numbers 31:24 On the seventh day, wash your clothes, and then you will be clean. After that, you can return to the camp.
Numbers 31:25 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 31:26 Count all the captured people and animals, you, Eleazar the priest, and the leading elders of the community.
Numbers 31:27 Split the loot into two parts: one for those who fought in the battle, and the other for the whole community.
Numbers 31:28 Collect a tax for God from the soldiers who fought in battle: one out of every five hundred people, cattle, donkeys, and sheep.
Numbers 31:29 Take some from their share and give it to priest Eleazar as a gift for God.
Numbers 31:30 From the Israelites' half, take one out of every fifty people and animals, including cattle, donkeys, and sheep, and give them to the Levites who are responsible for maintaining God's tent.
Numbers 31:31 Moses and Eleazar the priest did as God commanded Moses.
Numbers 31:32 The spoils, which were the remaining things captured by the soldiers, were six hundred and seventy-five thousand sheep.
Numbers 31:33 Seventy-two thousand cows,
Numbers 31:34 Sixty-one thousand donkeys.
Numbers 31:35 In total, thirty-two thousand women who had never slept with a man.
Numbers 31:36 And the half for those who went to battle was 337,500 sheep.
Numbers 31:37 God's share of the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.
Numbers 31:38 There were 36,000 cattle; God's share was 72.
Numbers 31:39 There were thirty thousand and five hundred donkeys, and God's share was sixty-one.
Numbers 31:40 There were 16,000 people; God's share was 32 people.
Numbers 31:41 Moses gave the special gift for God to Priest Eleazar, as God told Moses to do.
Numbers 31:42 From the half belonging to the Israelites, which Moses separated from the soldiers,
Numbers 31:43 The part that belonged to the people was 337,500 sheep.
Numbers 31:44 Thirty-six thousand cattle,
Numbers 31:45 Thirty thousand and five hundred donkeys.
Numbers 31:46 And sixteen thousand people.
Numbers 31:47 From the Israelites' half, Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals and gave them to the Levites, who looked after God's tent, as God told Moses.
Numbers 31:48 The leaders in charge of a thousand soldiers, and the captains of hundreds, approached Moses.
Numbers 31:49 They told Moses, "Your servants have counted all the soldiers we are responsible for, and not one man is missing."
Numbers 31:50 We have brought a gift for God, including gold jewelry like chains, bracelets, rings, earrings, and pendants, to ask forgiveness for our souls before God.
Numbers 31:51 Moses and Priest Eleazar took the gold from them, including all the crafted jewels.
Numbers 31:52 All the gold given to God by the leaders of the thousands and hundreds was 16,750 shekels.
Numbers 31:53 The soldiers had taken loot, each man for himself.
Numbers 31:54 Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the leaders of thousands and hundreds and brought it to the meeting tent as a reminder for the Israelites before God.

Numbers 32:1 The Reubenites and Gadites had many animals. When they saw the land of Jazer and Gilead, they noticed it was good for animals.
Numbers 32:2 The descendants of Gad and Reuben came and spoke to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the people, saying,
Numbers 32:3 Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Shebam, Nebo, and Beon.
Numbers 32:4 Even the land that God struck down before Israel's people is good for livestock, and your servants have livestock.
Numbers 32:5 So they said, if we have gained your favor, let this land be given to your servants as property, and do not take us across the Jordan.
Numbers 32:6 Moses said to Gad's and Reuben's descendants, "Will your brothers go to fight while you stay here?"
Numbers 32:7 Why are you making the Israelites not want to go to the land that God has given them?
Numbers 32:8 Your ancestors did this when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to explore the land.
Numbers 32:9 When they came to the Eshcol Valley and saw the land, they made the Israelites' hearts lose courage so they would not enter the land God had given them.
Numbers 32:10 God became very angry then, and he promised, saying,
Numbers 32:11 No one who came from Egypt, age twenty or older, will see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not fully follow me.
Numbers 32:12 Protect Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, and Joshua son of Nun, because they have completely followed God.
Numbers 32:13 God became angry with Israel and made them wander in the desert for forty years, until all the people who had done wrong in God's eyes had died.
Numbers 32:14 Look, you have taken your fathers' place as a group of sinful people, making God even angrier with Israel.
Numbers 32:15 If you turn away from God, he will leave you in the desert, and you will ruin everyone.
Numbers 32:16 They came to him and said, "We will make places for our sheep and towns for our children here."
Numbers 32:17 We will go armed ahead of the Israelites until they reach their land. Our families will live in protected cities because of the land's people.
Numbers 32:18 We won't go back to our homes until each Israelite has received their share of the land.
Numbers 32:19 We will not own land with them across the Jordan, nor beyond it, because our inheritance has been given to us on this side of the Jordan to the east.
Numbers 32:20 And Moses said to them, "If you do this, if you go ready for battle before God,
Numbers 32:21 All of you, ready for battle, will cross the Jordan River before God until he has forced his enemies out of his way.
Numbers 32:22 When the land is conquered for God, then you can go back home. You will be innocent before God and before Israel, and this land will be yours under God's watch.
Numbers 32:23 If you don't do this, you have sinned against God, and your sin will become known.
Numbers 32:24 Make towns for your children and pens for your sheep; and do what you said you would.
Numbers 32:25 The children of Gad and Reuben said to Moses, "Your servants will do what you command."
Numbers 32:26 Our children, our wives, our herds, and all our animals will stay in the cities of Gilead.
Numbers 32:27 Your servants will cross over, each man ready for war, before God to fight, as my lord says.
Numbers 32:28 Moses told Priest Eleazar, Joshua, Nun's son, and the main leaders of Israel's tribes about them.
Numbers 32:29 Moses told them, "If the Gadites and the Reubenites cross the Jordan River with you, ready to fight in front of God, and the land is conquered, then you should give them the land of Gilead to own."
Numbers 32:30 If they won't cross over fully armed to help you, they must settle among you in Canaan.
Numbers 32:31 The children of Gad and the children of Reuben replied, "We will do as God has told your servants."
Numbers 32:32 We will go across armed in front of God to the land of Canaan, so the land we inherit on this side of the Jordan River will belong to us.
Numbers 32:33 Moses gave the Gadites, the Reubenites, and half of the Manasseh tribe the lands and cities, including the territories of the kingdoms of Sihon and Og.
Numbers 32:34 The Gad people built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer.
Numbers 32:35 And Atroth, Shophan, Jaazer, and Jogbehah,
Numbers 32:36 Bethnimrah and Bethharan were protected cities with sheep pens.
Numbers 32:37 Reuben's descendants built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kirjathaim.
Numbers 32:38 They renamed Nebo, Baalmeon, and Shibmah, and gave new names to the cities they built.
Numbers 32:39 Machir's descendants, who were Manasseh's children, went to Gilead, captured it, and forced out the Amorites living there.
Numbers 32:40 Moses gave Gilead to Machir, Manasseh's son, and he lived there.
Numbers 32:41 Jair, who was from Manasseh's family, captured the small towns and named them Havothjair.
Numbers 32:42 Nobah went and captured Kenath and its surrounding villages, and renamed it Nobah, like his own name.

Numbers 33:1 These are the travels of the Israelites who left Egypt with their soldiers led by Moses and Aaron.
Numbers 33:2 Moses recorded where they traveled from as God instructed; these are their travels based on where they left.
Numbers 33:3 They left Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day; the day after Passover, the Israelites left boldly while all the Egyptians watched.
Numbers 33:4 The Egyptians buried all their firstborn whom God had struck down. God also punished their gods.
Numbers 33:5 The Israelites left Rameses and camped in Succoth.
Numbers 33:6 They left Succoth and set up camp in Etham, at the border of the wilderness.
Numbers 33:7 They left Etham, turned back to Pihahiroth near Baalzephon, and camped in front of Migdol.
Numbers 33:8 They left Pihahiroth, went through the sea to the desert, traveled for three days in the Etham desert, and camped at Marah.
Numbers 33:9 They left Marah and arrived at Elim, where there were twelve water springs and seventy palm trees; they set up camp there.
Numbers 33:10 They left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
Numbers 33:11 They left the Red Sea and camped in the Sin Desert.
Numbers 33:12 They traveled from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
Numbers 33:13 They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
Numbers 33:14 They moved from Alush and camped at Rephidim where there was no water for the people to drink.
Numbers 33:15 They left Rephidim and camped in the Sinai desert.
Numbers 33:16 They left the Sinai Desert and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah.
Numbers 33:17 They left Kibrothhattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
Numbers 33:18 They left Hazeroth and set up camp in Rithmah.
Numbers 33:19 They left Rithmah and set up camp at Rimmonparez.
Numbers 33:20 They left Rimmonparez and camped at Libnah.
Numbers 33:21 They moved from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
Numbers 33:22 They traveled from Rissah and camped in Kehelathah.
Numbers 33:23 They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shapher.
Numbers 33:24 They moved from Mount Shapher and camped in Haradah.
Numbers 33:25 They moved from Haradah and set up camp in Makheloth.
Numbers 33:26 They moved from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
Numbers 33:27 They left Tahath and set up camp at Tarah.
Numbers 33:28 They moved from Tarah and set up camp in Mithcah.
Numbers 33:29 They left Mithcah and set up camp in Hashmonah.
Numbers 33:30 They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
Numbers 33:31 They left Moseroth and camped at Benejaakan.
Numbers 33:32 They moved from Benejaakan and camped at Horhagidgad.
Numbers 33:33 They traveled from Horhagidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
Numbers 33:34 They moved from Jotbathah and set up camp at Ebronah.
Numbers 33:35 They left Ebronah and camped at Eziongaber.
Numbers 33:36 They moved from Eziongaber and camped in the Zin Desert, near Kadesh.
Numbers 33:37 They moved from Kadesh and set up camp on Mount Hor, at the border of Edom.
Numbers 33:38 Aaron the priest went up to Mount Hor because God told him to, and he died there. It was forty years after the people of Israel left Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
Numbers 33:39 Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
Numbers 33:40 The Canaanite King Arad, who lived in the southern part of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
Numbers 33:41 They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
Numbers 33:42 They left Zalmonah and set up camp in Punon.
Numbers 33:43 They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
Numbers 33:44 They left Oboth and camped at Ije Abarim, on the edge of Moab.
Numbers 33:45 They left Iim and set up camp in Dibongad.
Numbers 33:46 They moved from Dibongad and camped at Almondiblathaim.
Numbers 33:47 They moved from Almondiblathaim and camped in the Abarim mountains, near Nebo.
Numbers 33:48 They left the Abarim mountains and camped in the Moab plains by the Jordan near Jericho.
Numbers 33:49 They camped by the Jordan River, from Bethjesimoth to Abelshittim in the Moab plains.
Numbers 33:50 God spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho, saying,
Numbers 33:51 Tell the people of Israel, when you cross the Jordan River into the land of Canaan.
Numbers 33:52 Then you must force all the people of the land to leave, destroy all their images, melt down all their idols, and tear down all their worship places.
Numbers 33:53 You will take over the land and live in it because I have given it to you to own.
Numbers 33:54 You will divide the land by drawing lots to decide which family gets which part: give bigger parts to larger families and smaller parts to smaller families. Each person's land will be where their lot lands, and you will inherit land based on your ancestral tribes.
Numbers 33:55 If you do not force the people of the land to leave, the ones you allow to stay will cause you trouble, hurt your eyes, and bother you where you live.
Numbers 33:56 I will do to you what I planned to do to them.

Numbers 34:1 And God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 34:2 Tell the Israelites, when you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that will be your inheritance, the land of Canaan and its borders.
Numbers 34:3 Your southern area will start from the Zin wilderness, going by Edom's edge, and your southern boundary will be the farthest shore of the Salt Sea to the east.
Numbers 34:4 Your boundary will go from the south up to the Akrabbim Scarp, continue to Zin, and start out from the south to Kadesh Barnea. Then it will move on to Hazar Addar and over to Azmon.
Numbers 34:5 The border will go around from Azmon to the river of Egypt, and it will end at the sea.
Numbers 34:6 Your western border will be the big sea: this is your western edge.
Numbers 34:7 Your northern boundary will start from the Great Sea and go to Mount Hor.
Numbers 34:8 From Mount Hor, you will mark your boundary to the entrance of Hamath; and the end of the boundary will be at Zedad.
Numbers 34:9 The border will continue to Ziphron, and it will end at Hazarenan: this will be your northern boundary.
Numbers 34:10 Mark your eastern border from Hazarenan to Shepham.
Numbers 34:11 The border will extend from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain; it will go down and stretch to the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee.
Numbers 34:12 The boundary will go down to the Jordan River, and end at the Salt Sea. This will be your land, including all its borders.
Numbers 34:13 Moses told the Israelites, "This is the land that you will receive as your inheritance, which God has instructed to be given to the nine and a half tribes."
Numbers 34:14 The Reuben family tribe and the Gad family tribe have gotten their land, and half of the Manasseh family tribe has gotten theirs too.
Numbers 34:15 The two and a half tribes got their land east of the Jordan River by Jericho, toward the sunrise.
Numbers 34:16 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 34:17 Here are the names of the men who will divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua, Nun's son.
Numbers 34:18 You will choose one leader from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance.
Numbers 34:19 The men's names are as follows: From Judah's tribe, Caleb son of Jephunneh.

Numbers 34:21 From the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad, Chislon's son.

Numbers 34:27 The leader from the Asher tribe, Ahihud, Shelomi's son.
Numbers 34:28 The leader from Naphtali's tribe, the son of Ammihud, was Pedahel.
Numbers 34:29 These are the people God told to divide the land for the Israelites to inherit in Canaan.

Numbers 35:1 God spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho, saying,
Numbers 35:2 Tell the Israelites to give the Levites some of their own cities to live in, along with areas around these cities.
Numbers 35:3 They will live in the cities, and the areas around them will be for their cattle, belongings, and all their animals.
Numbers 35:4 The areas around the cities that you give to the Levites should extend a thousand cubits from the city wall all around.
Numbers 35:5 Measure 2,000 cubits outside the city on the east, south, west, and north; the city will be in the center, and this area will be the city's outskirts.
Numbers 35:6 Give six cities to the Levites as safe places for someone who has killed someone by accident to run to. Also give them forty-two more cities.
Numbers 35:7 You will give the Levites forty-eight cities along with the land around them.
Numbers 35:8 The cities you give must come from the lands of the Israelites: those with more must give more cities, those with less give fewer. Everyone must give the Levites cities based on their own share of the land.
Numbers 35:9 God spoke to Moses, saying,
Numbers 35:10 Tell the people of Israel, when you cross the Jordan River into the land of Canaan.
Numbers 35:11 Then you will choose cities to be safe places for you; so someone who accidentally kills another can run there for safety.
Numbers 35:12 These cities will be your safe places from the avenger, so the person who caused a death won't die before they face trial before the community.
Numbers 35:13 You must provide six cities as safe places from the cities you give.
Numbers 35:14 You must give three cities on this side of the Jordan River and three cities in the land of Canaan as safe places.
Numbers 35:15 These six cities will be safe places for the people of Israel, for foreigners, and for travelers among them, so anyone who accidentally kills someone can run there for safety.
Numbers 35:16 If he hits someone with an iron tool and that person dies, he is a murderer: the murderer must be put to death.
Numbers 35:17 If he hits him with a stone that could kill, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
Numbers 35:18 If he hits someone with a wooden weapon that could kill, and the person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
Numbers 35:19 The person who wants revenge must kill the killer; when he finds him, he must kill him.
Numbers 35:20 If he pushes him out of hate or attacks him on purpose, and he dies;
Numbers 35:21 If someone hits another person with hate in their heart and causes death, that attacker must be put to death, because they are a murderer. The one who avenges the killing shall kill the murderer upon meeting them.
Numbers 35:22 If he pushed him accidentally without being enemies or threw something at him without planning to hurt him,
Numbers 35:23 Or if someone accidentally throws a stone that can kill and hits another person without seeing them, causing death, but was not that person's enemy or intending to hurt them:
Numbers 35:24 Then the group will decide between the person who killed and the one seeking revenge based on these rules.
Numbers 35:25 The community will save the person who killed someone from the one who wants to punish with death. They will send him back to the safe city he ran to, and he must stay there until the high priest, who was chosen with holy oil, dies.
Numbers 35:26 If the person who killed someone goes outside the city where he found safety, which he ran to;
Numbers 35:27 If the person seeking revenge kills the killer outside the safe city, he is not guilty of murder.
Numbers 35:28 He should have stayed in the safe city until the chief priest died; after that, the one who killed can go back to his own land.
Numbers 35:29 These rules will be laws for you and your descendants wherever you live.
Numbers 35:30 Anyone who kills a person, the killer must be put to death based on what witnesses say; but no one should be put to death on the testimony of only one witness.
Numbers 35:31 Do not accept any payment to spare the life of a murderer who deserves death; they must be put to death.
Numbers 35:32 You must not accept any payment to let someone who ran to a safe city return home before the priest dies.
Numbers 35:33 Do not make the land you are in unclean, because blood makes the land unclean. The land cannot be made clean from the blood spilled on it, except by the blood of the one who spilled it.
Numbers 35:34 Do not make the land you will live in unclean, where I also live, because I, God, live among the people of Israel.

Numbers 36:1 The leaders of the clans in Gilead's family, who was Machir's son and Manasseh's grandson, both descendants of Joseph, approached and spoke to Moses and the heads of Israel's families.
Numbers 36:2 They said, God told my lord to divide the land among the Israelites by casting lots, and my lord was told by God to give our brother Zelophehad's daughters their inheritance.
Numbers 36:3 If they marry men from other Israelite tribes, their property will be moved from our ancestors' tribe to their husbands' tribe, reducing our inherited land.
Numbers 36:4 When Israel's jubilee comes, their land will join the land of the tribe they have joined, and it will no longer be part of our ancestors' tribal land.
Numbers 36:5 Moses told the Israelites what God had said, and he agreed that the tribe of Joseph's sons had spoken wisely.
Numbers 36:6 God commands this about Zelophehad's daughters: They should marry whoever they want, but they must marry within their father's tribal family.
Numbers 36:7 The lands of Israel's tribes must not be passed from one tribe to another; each person from the tribes of Israel must hold on to the land inherited from their ancestors.
Numbers 36:8 Every daughter who has property in an Israelite tribe must marry someone from her father's tribe, so each Israelite man can keep his family inheritance.
Numbers 36:9 An inheritance must not pass from one tribe to another; each tribe of the children of Israel must hold on to its own inheritance.
Numbers 36:10 Just as God told Moses, the daughters of Zelophehad did the same.
Numbers 36:11 Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins on their father's side.
Numbers 36:12 They married into the families of Manasseh's sons, Joseph's son, and their property stayed in their father's family tribe.
Numbers 36:13 These are the commands and rules that God gave through Moses to the people of Israel in the Moab plains by the Jordan River near Jericho.

Deuteronomy 1:1 These are the words Moses said to all Israel in the desert east of Jordan, near the Red Sea, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
Deuteronomy 1:2 It takes eleven days to go from Horeb to Kadeshbarnea by the Mount Seir road.
Deuteronomy 1:3 In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses told the Israelites everything that God had commanded him to tell them.
Deuteronomy 1:4 After he killed Sihon, the king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan who lived in Astaroth and Edrei:
Deuteronomy 1:5 Moses started to explain this law in the land of Moab, on this side of the Jordan River, saying,
Deuteronomy 1:6 God spoke to us at Horeb and said, "You have stayed on this mountain long enough."
Deuteronomy 1:7 Turn around, start your trip, and head to the Amorite mountains and all the nearby areas, including the flat lands, the hills, the valleys, the south, and the coast, going to the land of the Canaanites, as far as Lebanon, up to the big river, the Euphrates.
Deuteronomy 1:8 Look, I have put the land in front of you: go and take the land that God promised to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them and their children after them.
Deuteronomy 1:9 I told you then, "I can't take care of you all by myself."
Deuteronomy 1:10 God has made you very many, and today you are as countless as the stars in the sky.
Deuteronomy 1:11 May God, the God of your ancestors, increase you a thousand times and bless you as He promised.
Deuteronomy 1:12 How can I alone handle your troubles, your burdens, and your arguments?
Deuteronomy 1:13 Choose wise, understanding, and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will set them as your leaders.
Deuteronomy 1:14 You replied to me, saying, "What you have said is good for us to do."
Deuteronomy 1:15 I chose the best leaders from your groups, wise and respected men, and appointed them as leaders over you: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, leaders of tens, and other officials for your groups.
Deuteronomy 1:16 At that time, I told your judges: Listen to the disputes among your people and make fair decisions between one person and another, and between your people and the foreigners living among you.
Deuteronomy 1:17 Do not treat people unfairly when you judge; listen to the unimportant and the important alike; do not fear anyone, because the decision is God's. If a case is too difficult for you, bring it to me, and I will listen to it.
Deuteronomy 1:18 I told you then all the things you should do.
Deuteronomy 1:19 When we left Horeb, we traveled through the vast and frightening desert that you saw on the way to the Amorites' mountain, just as God told us; and we arrived at Kadeshbarnea.
Deuteronomy 1:20 I told you, you have reached the mountain of the Amorites, which God is giving to us.
Deuteronomy 1:21 Look, God has put the land in front of you: go up and take it, just as the God of your ancestors told you; do not be afraid or lose heart.
Deuteronomy 1:22 You all came to me and said, "We will send men ahead to explore the land and tell us the best way to go and which towns to enter."
Deuteronomy 1:23 I liked the idea, so I chose twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.
Deuteronomy 1:24 They turned, went up the mountain, reached the Eshcol Valley, and explored it.
Deuteronomy 1:25 They carried some of the land's fruit with them, showed it to us, and told us, "The land God is giving us is good."
Deuteronomy 1:26 Despite this, you did not go up and instead went against God's command.
Deuteronomy 1:27 You complained in your tents and said, "Because God hated us, he brought us out of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us."
Deuteronomy 1:28 Where should we go? Our own people have scared us, saying, "The people are bigger and taller than we are; the cities are huge with walls reaching the sky; and we even saw the Anakim's descendants there."
Deuteronomy 1:29 I told you, don't be scared or afraid of them.
Deuteronomy 1:30 God, who leads you, will fight for you, just as he did in Egypt right before you.
Deuteronomy 1:31 In the desert, you saw how God carried you, like a father carries his son, all along the journey until you arrived here.
Deuteronomy 1:32 In this matter, you did not trust God.
Deuteronomy 1:33 Someone went ahead of you to find a place for you to set up your tents. They guided you at night with fire to show you the way, and by day with a cloud.
Deuteronomy 1:34 God heard what you said and became angry, swearing, "
Deuteronomy 1:35 None of these evil people will see the good land that I promised to give to your ancestors.
Deuteronomy 1:36 Except for Caleb, the son of Jephunneh; he will see the land, and I will give him and his children the land he walked on, because he completely followed God.
Deuteronomy 1:37 God was also angry with me because of you, saying, You will not go in there either.
Deuteronomy 1:38 Joshua, son of Nun, who is with you, will go there; support him because he will lead Israel to take over the land.
Deuteronomy 1:39 Also, the young children you thought would be taken, and your kids who don't yet know right from wrong, they will go there, I will give it to them, and they will own it.
Deuteronomy 1:40 But as for you, go back and travel through the desert towards the Red Sea.
Deuteronomy 1:41 Then you replied to me, "We have sinned against God, we will go and fight, just as God our God told us." And when each man had put on his weapons of war, you were prepared to march up the hill.
Deuteronomy 1:42 God told me to tell you, "Do not go up or fight, for I am not with you; otherwise, you will be defeated by your enemies."
Deuteronomy 1:43 I spoke to you, but you did not listen and disobeyed God's command, boldly going up the hill.
Deuteronomy 1:44 The Amorites, who lived in that mountain, came out against you and chased you like bees and defeated you in Seir, all the way to Hormah.
Deuteronomy 1:45 You came back and cried before God, but God did not listen to you or pay attention to you.
Deuteronomy 1:46 You stayed in Kadesh for a long time, as long as you were there.

Deuteronomy 2:1 We turned and traveled through the desert toward the Red Sea, as God told me to do, and we circled Mount Seir for many days.

Deuteronomy 2:20 This land was also known as a home of giants: giants lived there long ago; and the Ammonites named them Zamzummims.
Deuteronomy 2:21 A large, numerous, and tall people, like the Anakim; but God destroyed them, and they took their place and lived there instead.
Deuteronomy 2:22 God did the same to the descendants of Esau who lived in Seir when he eliminated the Horims before them; they took over their land and have lived there to this day.
Deuteronomy 2:23 The Avims who lived in Hazerim, all the way to Azzah, were destroyed by the Caphtorims who came from Caphtor, and then the Caphtorims lived there instead.
Deuteronomy 2:24 Get up, start traveling, and cross the Arnon River. Look, I have placed Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land in your power. Start taking it over and fight him in battle.
Deuteronomy 2:25 Today, I will start making all nations under heaven fear and respect you. They will hear about you, shake with fear, and be very worried because of you.
Deuteronomy 2:26 I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon, the king of Heshbon, with a message of peace, saying,
Deuteronomy 2:27 Let me go through your land: I will stay on the main road and won't turn right or left.
Deuteronomy 2:28 You will sell me food for money so I can eat, and you will give me water for money so I can drink; I will only walk through your land.
Deuteronomy 2:29 Like the descendants of Esau living in Seir and the Moabites in Ar helped me, until I cross the Jordan into the land God is giving us.
Deuteronomy 2:30 But Sihon, the king of Heshbon, wouldn't let us go through his land: for God made his spirit stubborn and his heart tough, so He could give him to you, as you see today.
Deuteronomy 2:31 God said to me, "Look, I have started to give Sihon and his land to you: start to take it over so you can own his land."
Deuteronomy 2:32 Sihon and all his people came out to fight against us at Jahaz.
Deuteronomy 2:33 God gave us victory over him; we defeated him, his sons, and all his people.
Deuteronomy 2:34 We captured all his cities then, completely destroyed everyone—men, women, and children—in every city, leaving no survivors.
Deuteronomy 2:35 We only took the animals and the things from the cities we captured for ourselves.
Deuteronomy 2:36 From Aroer, next to the edge of the Arnon River, including the city near the river, all the way to Gilead, no city was too strong for us; God gave all of them to us.
Deuteronomy 2:37 You didn't go into the land of the Ammon people, the areas around the Jabbok River, the mountain cities, or any place God told us to stay away from.

Deuteronomy 3:1 We turned and traveled to Bashan. King Og of Bashan and his people came to fight us at Edrei.
Deuteronomy 3:2 God told me, "Don't be afraid of him, because I will give you victory over him, his people, and his land. You will deal with him as you dealt with Sihon, the king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
Deuteronomy 3:3 God gave us victory over Og, the king of Bashan, and his people. We defeated them so that no one was left.
Deuteronomy 3:4 We captured all his cities then; we took every single one of them—60 cities in the area of Argob, in Og's kingdom of Bashan.
Deuteronomy 3:5 All these cities had high walls, gates, and bars around them, and there were also many towns without walls.
Deuteronomy 3:6 We completely destroyed them, just as we did to Sihon, king of Heshbon, destroying every man, woman, and child in every city.
Deuteronomy 3:7 We took all the animals and the goods from the cities for ourselves.
Deuteronomy 3:8 At that time, we took the land from the two Amorite kings that was on this side of the Jordan, from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon.
Deuteronomy 3:9 Hermon is called Sirion by the Sidonians and Shenir by the Amorites.
Deuteronomy 3:10 Every city in the plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan, up to Salchah and Edrei, cities of King Og's realm in Bashan.
Deuteronomy 3:11 Only Og, the king of Bashan, was left of the giants. Look at his iron bedstead. Isn't it in Rabbath of the Ammonites? It is nine cubits long and four cubits wide, using the standard cubit.
Deuteronomy 3:12 At that time, we took this land from Aroer by the Arnon River, including half of Mount Gilead and its cities, and I gave it to the people of Reuben and Gad.
Deuteronomy 3:13 I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, Og's kingdom, to the half tribe of Manasseh; that includes all of Argob and the area known as the land of giants.
Deuteronomy 3:14 Jair from the family of Manasseh captured all the area of Argob to the borders of Geshuri and Maachath. He named the places after himself, calling them the Towns of Jair, which they are still called today.

Deuteronomy 3:16 To the Reubenites and Gadites, I gave land from Gilead to the Arnon River, half the valley, and the boundary extends to the Jabbok River, which is the border of the Ammonites.
Deuteronomy 3:17 The flat land, including the area around the Jordan River from Chinnereth to the Dead Sea, with its eastern border below the slopes of Pisgah.
Deuteronomy 3:18 I told you then, "God has given you this land to own: you must go ahead, ready to fight, in front of your fellow Israelites who are fit for battle."
Deuteronomy 3:19 Your wives, children, and animals, because I know you have many animals, can stay in the cities I gave you.
Deuteronomy 3:20 Wait until God has given your brothers rest, just like you, and until they too have taken over the land God has given them across the Jordan. Then each of you can go back to the land I have given you.
Deuteronomy 3:21 I told Joshua then, "You saw what God did to those two kings: God will do the same to all the kingdoms you enter."
Deuteronomy 3:22 Do not be afraid of them: for God will fight for you.

Deuteronomy 3:27 Go up to the top of Pisgah and look to the west, north, south, and east. See the land with your own eyes, because you will not cross the Jordan River.
Deuteronomy 3:28 Tell Joshua to be brave and strong because he will lead the people and help them receive the land you will see.

Deuteronomy 4:1 Listen, Israel, to the rules and decisions I am teaching you. Follow them so you may live and enter and own the land God of your ancestors is giving you.
Deuteronomy 4:2 Do not add anything to what I tell you, and do not take anything away from it, so you can follow God's commands that I give you.
Deuteronomy 4:3 Your eyes saw what God did because of Baalpeor: God destroyed everyone who followed Baalpeor from among you.
Deuteronomy 4:4 But all of you who stayed close to God are still alive today.
Deuteronomy 4:5 Look, I have taught you rules and decisions, just as God, my God, told me, so that you can follow them in the land you are going to make your own.
Deuteronomy 4:6 So keep and follow these laws, because this is how you will show your wisdom and understanding to other nations. When they hear about these rules, they will say, "This great nation is surely wise and understanding."
Deuteronomy 4:7 What nation is so great that has God close to them like our God whenever we call on Him?
Deuteronomy 4:8 What nation is as great as this one, with laws and rules as fair as all these that I give you today?
Deuteronomy 4:9 Be careful and pay close attention to yourself. Work hard to remember what you've seen, so you won't forget it as long as you live. And make sure to teach it to your children and grandchildren.
Deuteronomy 4:10 Especially the day you stood before God at Horeb, when God told me, 'Bring the people together, and I will let them hear my words, so they will learn to respect me all their lives on earth, and they will teach their children.'
Deuteronomy 4:11 You came close and stood at the foot of the mountain; the mountain was on fire up to the middle of the sky, with darkness, clouds, and deep darkness.
Deuteronomy 4:12 God spoke to you from the fire: you heard the sound of words but saw no form; you just heard a voice.
Deuteronomy 4:13 He told you his agreement, which he ordered you to follow, the ten orders; and he wrote them on two stone tablets.
Deuteronomy 4:14 At that time, God told me to teach you rules and laws, so you could follow them in the land you are going to make your own.
Deuteronomy 4:15 Be very careful about how you live; because you did not see anything when God spoke to you at Horeb from the fire.
Deuteronomy 4:16 Be careful not to ruin yourselves by making an idol in the shape of anything, man or woman.
Deuteronomy 4:17 The image of any animal on the ground, the image of any bird with wings that flies in the sky,
Deuteronomy 4:18 The image of anything that crawls on the land, the image of any fish that lives in the water under the earth.
Deuteronomy 4:19 Be careful not to look up at the sky and see the sun, moon, and stars—all the heavenly bodies—and feel tempted to bow down and worship them. These are things God has shared with all nations under heaven.
Deuteronomy 4:20 But God has chosen you and led you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his own people, just as you are today.
Deuteronomy 4:21 God was angry with me because of you and swore that I would not cross the Jordan or enter the good land that God is giving you to inherit.
Deuteronomy 4:22 But I must die in this land, I cannot cross the Jordan River; but you will cross and take over that good land.
Deuteronomy 4:23 Be careful and do not forget the agreement with God, who made it with you. Do not create any carved idol or image of anything that God has told you not to.
Deuteronomy 4:24 God is like a fire that burns everything up, and he is a God who wants your complete loyalty.
Deuteronomy 4:25 When you have children and grandchildren, and have lived in the land for a long time, if you become corrupt and make an idol, or a image of anything, and do wrong in the eyes of God, to make him angry:
Deuteronomy 4:26 I call heaven and earth to witness against you today: you will soon completely die from the land you are crossing Jordan to own; you will not live long there, but will be totally destroyed.
Deuteronomy 4:27 God will spread you out among many countries, and there will be only a few of you left among the nations where God will take you.
Deuteronomy 4:28 And there you will worship gods made by human hands, out of wood and stone, that can't see, hear, eat, or smell.
Deuteronomy 4:29 If you look for God there, you will find him if you search with all your heart and soul.
Deuteronomy 4:30 When you are in trouble and all these things happen to you, even in the future, if you turn to God and listen to his voice;
Deuteronomy 4:31 God is merciful; he will not abandon you or destroy you and will remember the promise he made to your ancestors.
Deuteronomy 4:32 Ask about the past days, before your time, since God made humans on earth, and check from one end of the sky to the other if anything as great as this has ever happened or been heard of.
Deuteronomy 4:33 Has any nation ever heard God's voice speaking from fire, as you have, and survived?
Deuteronomy 4:34 Has God ever tried to create a nation from within another nation, using tests, signs, miracles, war, strong power, an extended reach, and big fears, just as God did for you in Egypt while you watched?
Deuteronomy 4:35 You were shown this so you would know that God is the only God; there is no other besides him.
Deuteronomy 4:36 From heaven, God let you hear his voice to teach you. On earth, he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from inside the fire.
Deuteronomy 4:37 Because God loved your ancestors, he picked their descendants after them and led you out of Egypt with his great power.
Deuteronomy 4:38 To push out nations from in front of you, greater and stronger than you, to bring you in and to give you their land as your own, just like today.
Deuteronomy 4:39 Understand today, and think deeply in your heart, that God is the only God in heaven above and on earth below.
Deuteronomy 4:40 You must follow God's laws and commands that I give you today, so things go well for you and your children, and you live a long time on the land that God gives you forever.

Deuteronomy 4:42 The person who accidentally killed their neighbor, without previous hate, could run to one of these cities to live.
Deuteronomy 4:43 Bezer in the desert, in the flat land for the people of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead for the people of Gad; and Golan in Bashan for the people of Manasseh.

Deuteronomy 4:47 They took over his land and Og's land, the king of Bashan -- lands of two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River, where the sun rises.
Deuteronomy 4:48 From Aroer, by the river Arnon, to Mount Sion, known as Hermon.

Deuteronomy 5:1 Moses gathered all of Israel and told them, "Listen, Israel, to the rules and laws I am telling you today; learn them, follow them, and put them into practice."
Deuteronomy 5:2 God made an agreement with us at Horeb.
Deuteronomy 5:3 God did not make this agreement with our ancestors, but with us, all of us who are alive here today.
Deuteronomy 5:4 God spoke to you directly on the mountain from within the fire.
Deuteronomy 5:5 I stood between God and you at that time to tell you God's message because you were scared of the fire and did not go up the mountain.
Deuteronomy 5:6 I am God, who brought you out of Egypt, the place where you were slaves.
Deuteronomy 5:7 You should not have any other gods besides me.
Deuteronomy 5:8 Do not make for yourself any carved idol or any image of anything in heaven above, on earth below, or in the water under the earth.
Deuteronomy 5:9 Do not bow down to them or serve them, because I, your God, am a jealous God. I will punish the children for the sins of their parents to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me.
Deuteronomy 5:10 And showing kindness to thousands who love me and follow my commands.
Deuteronomy 5:11 Do not use God's name for no good reason; God will not forgive those who misuse his name.
Deuteronomy 5:12 Remember to keep the Sabbath day holy, as God has instructed you.
Deuteronomy 5:13 Work for six days and do all your tasks.
Deuteronomy 5:14 The seventh day is God's rest day: on this day, you or your children, your male and female workers, your oxen, your donkeys, or any other animals, or the foreigners living in your town, should not work. This is so your workers can rest just like you.
Deuteronomy 5:15 Remember you were a servant in Egypt, and God freed you with great power and an outstretched arm; that's why God told you to observe the Sabbath day.
Deuteronomy 5:16 Respect your father and mother, as God has told you, so you may live a long life and have a good life in the land God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 5:17 Do not kill.
Deuteronomy 5:18 Do not cheat on your partner.
Deuteronomy 5:19 Do not steal.
Deuteronomy 5:20 Do not lie about your neighbor.
Deuteronomy 5:21 Do not want your neighbor's wife, do not wish for your neighbor's house, land, servants, ox, donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
Deuteronomy 5:22 God spoke these words to everyone gathered on the mountain from the fire, cloud, and dark fog with a loud voice, and said nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
Deuteronomy 5:23 When you heard the voice from the dark and saw the mountain burning with fire, you all, including the leaders and older people of your tribes, came close to me.
Deuteronomy 5:24 You said, "Look, our God has shown us his glory and power, and we have heard his voice from the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak to people, and they can still live."
Deuteronomy 5:25 So why should we die now? This huge fire will burn us up. If we keep hearing God’s voice, we will die.
Deuteronomy 5:26 Who among all people has heard God speak from the fire like we have and still lived?
Deuteronomy 5:27 Go close and listen to everything that God will tell you; then tell us everything that God says to you, and we will listen and do it.
Deuteronomy 5:28 God heard what you said to me; and God told me, "I have heard what this people said to you, and everything they said is good."
Deuteronomy 5:29 I wish they had a heart to respect me and always follow my commands, so things would go well for them and their children forever.
Deuteronomy 5:30 Go tell them to return to their tents.
Deuteronomy 5:31 Stay here with me and I will tell you all the rules and laws that you must teach the people so they can follow them in the land I am giving them to live in.
Deuteronomy 5:32 You must do as God has commanded you: do not turn right or left.
Deuteronomy 5:33 Follow all the paths God has told you to take so that you may live a good life and have a long time in the land you will own.

Deuteronomy 6:1 Here are the rules, laws, and decisions that God told you to learn, so you can follow them in the land you are going to make your own.
Deuteronomy 6:2 So you will respect God, follow all His rules and commands that I give to you, you, your son, and your grandson, as long as you live; and so that you may have a long life.
Deuteronomy 6:3 Listen, Israel, and be sure to follow the commands, so that things go well for you, and you become very numerous, just as God promised your ancestors, in a land filled with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 6:4 Listen, Israel: Our God is the only God.
Deuteronomy 6:5 Love God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
Deuteronomy 6:6 Keep these words I give you today in your heart.
Deuteronomy 6:7 You should teach them carefully to your children and talk about them when you are at home, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Deuteronomy 6:8 Tie them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a reminder between your eyes.
Deuteronomy 6:9 Write these words on the doorframes of your house and on your gates.
Deuteronomy 6:10 When God brings you to the land He promised your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you large and beautiful cities you did not build,
Deuteronomy 6:11 Homes filled with good things you did not put there, wells you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees you did not plant; when you have eaten and are satisfied.
Deuteronomy 6:12 Be careful not to forget God, who brought you out of Egypt, where you were slaves.
Deuteronomy 6:13 You should respect God, serve him, and make promises in his name.
Deuteronomy 6:14 Do not follow other gods from the nearby peoples.
Deuteronomy 6:15 Because your God is a God who feels very strong about his relationship with you, be careful not to make him angry or he might remove you from the earth.
Deuteronomy 6:16 Do not test God as you did at Massah.
Deuteronomy 6:17 You must carefully follow God's commandments, teachings, and rules that he has given you.
Deuteronomy 6:18 You should do what is right and good in God's eyes: so things will go well for you, and you can enter and take over the good land that God promised to your ancestors.
Deuteronomy 6:19 To drive out all your enemies from before you, just as God has said.
Deuteronomy 6:20 When your son asks you in the future, 'What do the teachings, laws, and rules that God has given you mean?'
Deuteronomy 6:21 Then you will tell your son, We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, but God led us out of Egypt with great power.
Deuteronomy 6:22 God showed amazing and terrible signs and wonders in Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his family, right before our eyes.
Deuteronomy 6:23 He took us out from there to bring us in and give us the land he promised to our ancestors.
Deuteronomy 6:24 God told us to follow these rules and respect God, for our own good at all times, so that we may be kept alive, just as we are today.
Deuteronomy 6:25 We will be doing what is right if we carefully follow all these commands from God, just as he has told us to do.

Deuteronomy 7:1 When God brings you to the land you are going to take over, and has driven out many nations ahead of you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—seven nations bigger and stronger than you;
Deuteronomy 7:2 When God gives them to you, you must defeat them and completely destroy them; you must not make any agreements with them or show them mercy.
Deuteronomy 7:3 Do not marry them; don't give your daughter to their son, and don't take their daughter for your son.
Deuteronomy 7:4 They will lead your son away from following me, so they can worship other gods. Then God will become very angry with you and destroy you quickly.
Deuteronomy 7:5 Deal with them like this: destroy their altars, break their idols, cut down their sacred poles, and burn their carved images with fire.
Deuteronomy 7:6 You are a holy people to your God: your God has chosen you to be his own special people, more than anyone else in the world.
Deuteronomy 7:7 God did not love or choose you because you were the most people; you were actually the fewest of all.
Deuteronomy 7:8 Because God loved you and wanted to keep the promise made to your ancestors, God brought you out with great power and freed you from slavery under Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
Deuteronomy 7:9 Understand then that God, your God, is the true God, the loyal God, who maintains his promise and kindness to those who love him and obey his commands for a thousand generations.
Deuteronomy 7:10 God pays back those who hate Him directly, to destroy them; He will not delay in repaying someone who hates Him, He will confront them.
Deuteronomy 7:11 You should follow the commands, rules, and decisions I give you today and obey them.
Deuteronomy 7:12 So if you listen to these rules and follow them, then God will keep the promise and kindness he swore to your ancestors.
Deuteronomy 7:13 God will love you, bless you, and make you many. He will bless your children and your land's crops, your grain, wine, and oil, the calves of your cows, and the lambs of your sheep, in the land he promised to your ancestors to give to you.
Deuteronomy 7:14 You will be more blessed than any other people: none of you, man or woman, or your animals, will be unable to have children.
Deuteronomy 7:15 God will remove all sickness from you and won't let you suffer from the terrible diseases of Egypt you know about. Instead, He will make those who hate you suffer from them.
Deuteronomy 7:16 You must destroy all the peoples God gives to you; show them no mercy, and do not worship their gods, as it will trap you.
Deuteronomy 7:17 If you think to yourself, "These nations are too many for me; how can I drive them out?"
Deuteronomy 7:18 Do not fear them: but remember well what God did to Pharaoh and all of Egypt.
Deuteronomy 7:19 The big tests you saw, the miracles, the powerful acts, and the strong arm that God used to rescue you: God will do the same to all the people you fear.
Deuteronomy 7:20 God will send hornets to chase them away until all that are left and hiding from you are destroyed.
Deuteronomy 7:21 Do not be scared of them: for God, who is your God, is with you, a powerful and awesome God.
Deuteronomy 7:22 God will drive out those nations before you gradually; you cannot defeat them quickly, or wild animals will grow too numerous for you.
Deuteronomy 7:23 God will hand them over to you and wipe them out completely until they are gone.
Deuteronomy 7:24 God will hand their kings over to you, and you will erase their names from the earth; no one will be able to resist you until you have destroyed them.
Deuteronomy 7:25 Burn the carved idols of their gods: do not want the silver or gold on them or take it, so you won't be trapped by it: it's hated by God.
Deuteronomy 7:26 Do not bring anything hateful into your home, or you will be cursed like it. Hate it completely and find it totally disgusting, because it is cursed.

Deuteronomy 8:1 Follow all the commands I give you today so you can live, grow, and take over the land God promised to your ancestors.
Deuteronomy 8:2 Remember how God guided you through the wilderness for forty years, to humble and test you, and to see if you would follow His commands.
Deuteronomy 8:3 God made you humble, let you feel hunger, and gave you manna to eat, a food you and your ancestors didn't know. This was to teach you that people don't live by bread alone, but by everything God says.
Deuteronomy 8:4 Your clothes did not wear out and your feet did not swell during these forty years.
Deuteronomy 8:5 You should also think to yourself that just as a father disciplines his child, so God disciplines you.
Deuteronomy 8:6 So you must follow God's commands, live as He wants, and respect Him.
Deuteronomy 8:7 God is bringing you into a good land with streams, springs, and deep waters that flow in the valleys and hills.
Deuteronomy 8:8 A land with wheat, barley, grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land with olive oil and honey.
Deuteronomy 8:9 A place where you will eat bread without shortage, you will not lack anything; a place with iron stones and hills where you can dig out copper.
Deuteronomy 8:10 When you have eaten and are full, then you should thank God for the good land he has given you.
Deuteronomy 8:11 Be careful not to forget God by not following his commands, rules, and laws that I give you today.
Deuteronomy 8:12 Be careful not to forget God when you have eaten your fill, built nice homes, and live in them.
Deuteronomy 8:13 When your herds and flocks grow, and your silver and gold increase, and everything you own increases;
Deuteronomy 8:14 Then your heart may become proud, and you forget God who brought you out of Egypt, out of slavery.
Deuteronomy 8:15 Who guided you through the vast and scary desert with poisonous snakes and scorpions, and where there was no water; who made water come out of the hard rock for you;
Deuteronomy 8:16 God fed you in the desert with manna, unknown to your ancestors, to humble you and test you, to ultimately benefit you in the end.
Deuteronomy 8:17 And you think in your heart, My strength and the power of my hand have earned me this wealth.
Deuteronomy 8:18 Remember God, because He gives you the strength to become wealthy, so that He can keep the promise He made to your ancestors, just as it is today.
Deuteronomy 8:19 If you forget God, follow other gods, serve and worship them, I warn you today that you will certainly be destroyed.
Deuteronomy 8:20 Just like the countries God destroys before you, you too will die if you don't listen to God's voice.

Deuteronomy 9:1 Listen, Israel: Today you will cross the Jordan to take over lands with bigger and stronger nations than you, and cities with tall, strong walls.
Deuteronomy 9:2 A great and tall nation, the descendants of the Anakims, whom you know and have heard about, saying, "Who can stand against the children of Anak?"
Deuteronomy 9:3 Know today that God, your God, is the one leading you. Like a fire, he will destroy your enemies, defeating them as you watch. You will quickly drive them out and destroy them, just as God has told you.
Deuteronomy 9:4 Do not think in your heart, after God has driven them out from before you, 'It is because of my goodness that God has let me take this land.' Instead, it's because of the evil of these nations that God is removing them from your path.
Deuteronomy 9:5 You are not going to take over their land because you are righteous or have a pure heart; you are doing it because these nations are wicked, and God wants to remove them for you. This will fulfill the promise God made to your forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Deuteronomy 9:6 Know then that God is not giving you this good land to own because of your goodness; you are a stubborn people.
Deuteronomy 9:7 Remember and don't forget how you made God angry in the desert. From the time you left Egypt until you arrived here, you have been disobedient to God.
Deuteronomy 9:8 At Horeb, you made God very angry, so much that he wanted to destroy you.
Deuteronomy 9:9 I went up the mountain to get the stone tablets, the ones of the agreement that God made with you. I stayed on the mountain for 40 days and nights, without eating bread or drinking water.
Deuteronomy 9:10 God gave me two stone tablets written by God's finger; they had all the words God spoke to you on the mountain from within the fire on the day we gathered.
Deuteronomy 9:11 After 40 days and 40 nights, God gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the agreement.
Deuteronomy 9:12 God told me, "Get up and go down fast from here because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have ruined themselves; they quickly left the path I ordered them to follow; they've made an idol out of melted metal."
Deuteronomy 9:13 God spoke to me and said, "I have seen these people, and they are stubborn."
Deuteronomy 9:14 Leave me alone, so I can destroy them and erase their name from under heaven, and I will create from you a nation stronger and greater than them.
Deuteronomy 9:15 I turned and came down from the mountain, which was burning with fire, holding the two stone tablets of the agreement in my hands.
Deuteronomy 9:16 I saw that you sinned against God by making a metal calf; you quickly left the path God had ordered you to follow.
Deuteronomy 9:17 I took the two tablets, threw them from my hands, and broke them in front of you.
Deuteronomy 9:18 I bowed down before God for forty days and nights, just as before, not eating bread or drinking water, because of all the wrongs you did, making God angry.
Deuteronomy 9:19 I was scared of God's anger and fury, which could have led to your destruction, but God listened to me then too.
Deuteronomy 9:20 God was very angry with Aaron and wanted to destroy him, but I also prayed for Aaron at that time.
Deuteronomy 9:21 I took the calf idol you made, which was your sin, burned it in fire, crushed it, and ground it into fine dust; then I threw the dust into the stream that flowed down the mountain.
Deuteronomy 9:22 At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibrothhattaavah, you made God very angry.
Deuteronomy 9:23 Also, when God sent you from Kadeshbarnea, saying, "Go and take the land I have given you," you did not obey God's command, and you did not trust or listen to Him.
Deuteronomy 9:24 You have been against God since I first knew you.
Deuteronomy 9:25 So I lay prostrate before God for forty days and nights, just like the first time, because God had said he would destroy you.
Deuteronomy 9:26 I prayed to God and said, "O God, do not destroy your people, your own possession, whom you saved by your power, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand."
Deuteronomy 9:27 God, remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and do not pay attention to this people's stubbornness, wickedness, or sin.
Deuteronomy 9:28 So that the people from the land we were taken from don't say, 'God couldn't take them to the land he promised, and because he hated them, he took them out to kill them in the desert.'
Deuteronomy 9:29 They are your people and your heritage, whom you brought out with your great power and your outstretched arm.

Deuteronomy 10:1 At that time, God told me, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones and come up the mountain to meet me, and make a wooden box."
Deuteronomy 10:2 I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets you broke, and you must put them in the chest.
Deuteronomy 10:3 I made a box from acacia wood and cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Then I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
Deuteronomy 10:4 He wrote on the tablets the same ten commandments that God told you on the mountain from the fire on the day we all gathered, and God gave them to me.
Deuteronomy 10:5 I turned around and came down the mountain, and placed the tablets in the chest I had built; and there they are, as God told me.
Deuteronomy 10:6 The Israelites traveled from Beeroth, where Jaakan's people lived, to Mosera. Aaron died and was buried there, and his son Eleazar became the priest in his place.
Deuteronomy 10:7 They traveled from there to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbath, a land with many water streams.
Deuteronomy 10:8 At that time, God chose the tribe of Levi to carry the covenant box, to serve before God, to take care of his needs, and to bless people in his name, which continues even now.
Deuteronomy 10:9 So Levi does not have a share or property like his brothers; God is his share, just as God promised him.
Deuteronomy 10:10 I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights, like before; and God listened to me again, and did not decide to destroy you.
Deuteronomy 10:11 God told me, "Get up, lead the way for the people, so they can enter and take over the land that I promised to give to their ancestors."
Deuteronomy 10:12 Now, Israel, what does God your God ask of you but to respect God, to live in His ways, to love Him, and to serve God with all your heart and all your soul?
Deuteronomy 10:13 To follow God's commands and rules, which I give you today for your benefit?
Deuteronomy 10:14 Look, the sky and even the highest heavens belong to God, and so does the earth and everything in it.
Deuteronomy 10:15 God was pleased with your ancestors and loved them, so he chose you, their descendants, above all others, as it is today.
Deuteronomy 10:16 Cut away the stubbornness from your heart, and don't be stubborn anymore.
Deuteronomy 10:17 Your God is the greatest God and the highest leader, a big and strong God who treats everyone the same and doesn't take bribes.
Deuteronomy 10:18 He carries out justice for orphans and widows, and loves foreigners, by giving them food and clothing.
Deuteronomy 10:19 Love the foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
Deuteronomy 10:20 You should respect God; serve him, stay close to him, and make promises in his name.
Deuteronomy 10:21 He is the one you praise, and he is your God who has done these great and frightening things for you that you have seen.
Deuteronomy 10:22 Your ancestors went to Egypt with seventy people; and now God has made you as many as the stars in the sky.

Deuteronomy 11:1 So you must love God, follow his instructions, laws, decisions, and commands always.
Deuteronomy 11:2 Understand today: I am not talking to your children who have not known or seen how God disciplines, his greatness, his powerful hand, and his extended arm.
Deuteronomy 11:3 God's miracles and what he did in Egypt before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and his whole country;
Deuteronomy 11:4 God did to Egypt's army, their horses, and their chariots; how He made the Red Sea's water flood over them as they chased you, and how God has destroyed them up to today;
Deuteronomy 11:5 And what he did for you in the desert until you arrived here;
Deuteronomy 11:6 And what happened to Dathan and Abiram, Eliab's sons from the Reuben tribe: how the ground opened up and swallowed them, their families, their tents, and all their belongings in front of all Israel.
Deuteronomy 11:7 But your eyes have seen all the great things God did.
Deuteronomy 11:8 So you must obey all the rules I give you today, so that you can be strong and take over the land you are going to live in.
Deuteronomy 11:9 So that you may live longer in the land, which God promised to your ancestors to give to them and their children, a land filled with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 11:10 The land you are going to make your own is not like Egypt, where you came from. There you planted your seeds and used your feet to water them, like a herb garden.
Deuteronomy 11:11 The land where you are going to take over has hills and valleys and gets its water from the rain that comes from the sky.
Deuteronomy 11:12 A land that God takes care of: God's eyes are always on it, from the start of the year to the end of the year.
Deuteronomy 11:13 If you carefully listen to my commands that I give you today, to love God and serve Him with all your heart and soul, it will happen.
Deuteronomy 11:14 I will send rain to your land at the right time, both early and late rains, so you can collect your grain, wine, and oil.
Deuteronomy 11:15 I will make grass grow in your fields for your cattle so you can eat and be satisfied.
Deuteronomy 11:16 Be careful, don't let your heart be fooled, and don't turn away to serve other gods and bow down to them.
Deuteronomy 11:17 If you make God angry, He might close the sky so it won't rain, and the ground won't grow food, and you might quickly die in the good land God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 11:18 Keep these words of mine in your heart and soul, tie them on your hand as a reminder, and let them be like a band on your forehead.
Deuteronomy 11:19 Teach your children these things. Talk about them at home, when you travel, when you go to bed, and when you get up.
Deuteronomy 11:20 Write them on the door frames of your house and on your gates.
Deuteronomy 11:21 May your life and your children's lives be long in the land that God promised to your ancestors, like endless days in heaven on earth.
Deuteronomy 11:22 If you carefully follow all these commands I give you, to do them, to love God, to walk in all his ways, and to hold fast to him;
Deuteronomy 11:23 God will force all these nations to leave before you, and you will take over greater and stronger nations than you.
Deuteronomy 11:24 Every place where you step will belong to you: from the desert and Lebanon, from the Euphrates River to the farthest sea will be your border.
Deuteronomy 11:25 No one will be able to resist you: for God will make everyone fear and dread you wherever you go, just as he has promised you.
Deuteronomy 11:26 Look, today I give you a choice between a blessing and a curse.
Deuteronomy 11:27 You will be blessed if you follow the commands of God that I give you today.
Deuteronomy 11:28 And a curse if you do not follow God's commandments, but turn away from the path I tell you today, to follow different gods, which you do not know.
Deuteronomy 11:29 When God brings you to the land you will take over, you should speak the blessings on Mount Gerizim and the curses on Mount Ebal.
Deuteronomy 11:30 Aren't they across the Jordan River, along the path where the sun sets, in the Canaanites' land, near Gilgal and next to the Moreh fields?
Deuteronomy 11:31 You will cross the Jordan River to take over the land that God gives you, and you will own it and live there.
Deuteronomy 11:32 Obey all the rules and decisions I am giving you today.

Deuteronomy 12:1 Here are the rules and decisions you must follow in the land that God of your ancestors is giving you to own, as long as you live on the earth.
Deuteronomy 12:2 You must completely destroy all the places where the nations you will take over worshiped their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Deuteronomy 12:3 You must knock down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and burn their Asherah poles with fire. You must cut down their idols and wipe out their names from that place.
Deuteronomy 12:4 Do not do this to your God.
Deuteronomy 12:5 Go to the place that God chooses from all your tribes to honor his name, search for his dwelling, and go there.
Deuteronomy 12:6 Take your burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, gifts, promises, voluntary offerings, and the first of your herds and flocks there.
Deuteronomy 12:7 You will eat there in front of God and be happy with all your work, you and your families, because God has blessed you.
Deuteronomy 12:8 You must not do everything we are doing here today, where everyone does what seems right to them.
Deuteronomy 12:9 You have not yet reached the place of rest and the land that God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 12:10 But when you cross the Jordan and live in the land that God your God gives you to inherit, and when he gives you peace from all your enemies around, so that you live in safety;
Deuteronomy 12:11 There will be a place that God will choose for his name to live; there you must bring everything I tell you: your burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, special gifts, and all your chosen promises to God.
Deuteronomy 12:12 You will be happy in front of God, you and your sons, your daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite that lives in your town, because he doesn't own or inherit land like you do.
Deuteronomy 12:13 Be careful to not give your burnt offerings in just any place you see.
Deuteronomy 12:14 But in the place God picks in one of your tribes, there you must present your burnt offerings and do everything I tell you.
Deuteronomy 12:15 You can kill and eat meat anywhere you live, whatever you desire, according to God's blessings given to you; both clean and unclean people can eat it, just like eating deer or gazelle meat.
Deuteronomy 12:16 Do not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground like water.
Deuteronomy 12:17 You must not eat the tenth part of your grain, wine, or oil, or the firstborn of your cattle or sheep, or any offerings you promised to God, or your voluntary gifts, or special offerings in your own places.
Deuteronomy 12:18 You must eat them in the presence of God at the place God will choose. You, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, and the Levite in your town should all rejoice in everything you do.
Deuteronomy 12:19 Be careful not to ignore the Levite as long as you live on the earth.
Deuteronomy 12:20 When God makes your land larger, as he promised you, and you want to eat meat because you crave it, you can eat any meat you desire.
Deuteronomy 12:21 If the place God has chosen for his name is too far from you, then you may slaughter your cattle and sheep that God has given you, as I have instructed, and you can eat what you desire within your own gates.
Deuteronomy 12:22 Just as you can eat deer or gazelle meat, you may eat these animals: both people who are impure and those who are pure can eat them.
Deuteronomy 12:23 Make sure you do not eat the blood because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.
Deuteronomy 12:24 Do not eat it; pour it on the ground like water.
Deuteronomy 12:25 Do not eat it so that things will go well with you and your children, when you do what is right in God's eyes.
Deuteronomy 12:26 Take your holy items and promises, and go to the place God will select.
Deuteronomy 12:27 You must present your burnt offerings, both the meat and the blood, on the altar of God. The blood of your offerings should be spilled on God's altar, and you may eat the meat.
Deuteronomy 12:28 Listen and follow all these instructions I give you, so things will go well for you and your children forever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of God.
Deuteronomy 12:29 When God removes the nations before you, where you are going to take over, and you replace them and live in their land;
Deuteronomy 12:30 Be careful not to be trapped by copying them, after they are defeated in front of you; and don't ask about their gods, wondering how these people worshiped their gods, thinking you might do the same.
Deuteronomy 12:31 Do not act this way towards God, because they have done everything God hates to their gods, even burning their sons and daughters in fire for them.
Deuteronomy 12:32 Do whatever I tell you: don't add to it or take away from it.
