Deuteronomy 13:1 If a prophet or someone who dreams of visions appears among you, and gives you a sign or a miracle,
Deuteronomy 13:2 If the sign or miracle happens that he told you about, saying, "Let's follow other gods you don't know and worship them,"
Deuteronomy 13:3 Do not listen to what that prophet or dreamer says, because God is testing you to see if you love God with all your heart and soul.
Deuteronomy 13:4 Follow God, respect him, follow his rules, listen to him, serve him, and stay close to him.
Deuteronomy 13:5 That prophet or dreamer must be put to death for trying to turn you away from God, who freed you from Egypt and slavery, leading you on the path God commanded. This will remove evil from among you.
Deuteronomy 13:6 If your brother, your mother's son, or your own son or daughter, or the wife close to you, or your friend who is like your own self, tempts you in secret, saying "Let's go and worship other gods," gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known;
Deuteronomy 13:7 From the gods of the nations near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other.
Deuteronomy 13:8 Do not agree with him, do not listen to him, do not feel sorry for him, do not spare him, and do not hide him.
Deuteronomy 13:9 You must definitely kill him; you should be the first to strike him to put him to death, and then everyone else should follow.
Deuteronomy 13:10 You must stone him to death with rocks because he tried to turn you away from God, who led you out of Egypt, where you were slaves.
Deuteronomy 13:11 Everyone in Israel will hear about it, be afraid, and not do such evil things among you anymore.
Deuteronomy 13:12 If you hear someone in one of your cities, which God has given you to live in, saying,
Deuteronomy 13:13 Some bad men from your group have left and convinced the people of their city to follow other gods that you don't know.
Deuteronomy 13:14 Then you should investigate, search carefully, and ask thoroughly; and if you find out it's true and the offense has definitely been done among you;
Deuteronomy 13:15 You must completely destroy the people of that city with your swords, along with everything in it, and also the animals, using your swords.
Deuteronomy 13:16 Gather all the city's goods into its center, burn the city and everything in it for God. It will be ruins forever and never rebuilt.
Deuteronomy 13:17 Do not keep anything cursed; then God will calm his anger, be merciful to you, feel sorry for you, and make your family larger, as he promised your ancestors.
Deuteronomy 13:18 When you listen to God's voice and follow all the commands I give you today, do what is right in God's eyes.

Deuteronomy 14:1 You are God's children: do not cut yourselves or shave the front of your head for the dead.
Deuteronomy 14:2 You are a special people to God, and God has chosen you to be his own unique people, above all the nations on the earth.
Deuteronomy 14:3 Do not eat anything disgusting.
Deuteronomy 14:4 You may eat these animals: the ox, the sheep, and the goat.
Deuteronomy 14:5 The deer, the gazelle, the fallow deer, the wild goat, the antelope, the wild ox, and the mountain goat.
Deuteronomy 14:6 You may eat any animal that has split hooves divided into two parts and that chews the cud.
Deuteronomy 14:7 But you must not eat these animals that chew the cud or have split hooves: camels, rabbits, and hyraxes. They chew the cud but don't have split hooves, so they are unclean for you.
Deuteronomy 14:8 Pigs are unclean for you because they have split hooves but don't chew the cud. You must not eat their meat or touch their dead bodies.
Deuteronomy 14:9 You may eat all from the water that have fins and scales.
Deuteronomy 14:10 You must not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is not clean for you.
Deuteronomy 14:11 You can eat all clean birds.
Deuteronomy 14:12 But these are the birds you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the hawk.
Deuteronomy 14:13 And the gliding bird, the kite, and every kind of vulture.
Deuteronomy 14:14 Each type of raven,
Deuteronomy 14:15 The owl, the nighthawk, the cuckoo, and different kinds of hawks,
Deuteronomy 14:16 The small owl, the big owl, and the swan,
Deuteronomy 14:17 The pelican, the vulture, and the cormorant,
Deuteronomy 14:18 The stork, the heron and its kinds, the lapwing, and the bat.
Deuteronomy 14:19 Every crawling creature that flies is impure to you; do not eat them.
Deuteronomy 14:20 You can eat all clean birds.
Deuteronomy 14:21 Do not eat any animal that dies on its own. You can give it to the foreigners living in your town, so they can eat it, or you can sell it to someone from another country. You are a special people to God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Deuteronomy 14:22 You must give one tenth of all your crops' yearly growth as an offering.
Deuteronomy 14:23 You will eat before God in the place he chooses for his name, the tenth part of your grain, wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep; so you can learn to always respect God.
Deuteronomy 14:24 If the journey is too long for you and you can't carry your offerings, or if the place God chooses for his name is too far, where God has blessed you:
Deuteronomy 14:25 Then you will change it to money, hold the money in your hand, and go to the place that God chooses.
Deuteronomy 14:26 Use that money to buy whatever you want: cattle, sheep, wine, or any drink you desire. Then eat there in the presence of God and celebrate with your household.
Deuteronomy 14:27 Do not neglect the Levite living in your towns, for they have no share or inheritance of their own among you.
Deuteronomy 14:28 After three years, you must take one-tenth of your crops from that year and store it in your town.
Deuteronomy 14:29 The Levite, who has no share or property with you, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow living in your towns may come, eat, and have enough, so that God may bless you in everything you do.

Deuteronomy 15:1 Every seven years, you must forgive debts.
Deuteronomy 15:2 This is how the release works: Everyone who has lent something to their neighbor must forgive the debt; they must not demand it back from their neighbor or relative, because it is known as God's time for forgiveness.
Deuteronomy 15:3 You can require a foreigner to repay a debt, but you must let your own people go free without repayment.
Deuteronomy 15:4 Help those in need until no one is poor among you, because God will bless you greatly in the land God gives you as your own.
Deuteronomy 15:5 If you listen carefully to God's voice and follow all these commands I give you today.
Deuteronomy 15:6 God blesses you as he promised, and you will lend to many nations but not borrow; you will rule over many nations, but they won't rule over you.
Deuteronomy 15:7 If there is a poor man from your people in any of your towns in the land God is giving you, do not be hard-hearted or close your hand to your poor brother.
Deuteronomy 15:8 You should open your hand generously to him and lend him enough for what he needs.
Deuteronomy 15:9 Be careful not to think evil thoughts, like "The seventh year, the year to forgive debts, is near," and then look badly at your poor brother and give him nothing. If he calls out to God against you, it will be a sin for you.
Deuteronomy 15:10 You must definitely give to him, and don't feel sad when you do because God will bless you in everything you do and in all your efforts.
Deuteronomy 15:11 The poor will always be in the land, so I command you to generously help your brother, the poor, and the needy in your land.
Deuteronomy 15:12 If your brother, a Hebrew man or woman, is sold to you and works for you for six years, you must set them free in the seventh year.
Deuteronomy 15:13 When you set him free, do not send him away with nothing.
Deuteronomy 15:14 You should generously provide for him from your flock, your grain, and your winepress. Give to him from the blessings God has given you.
Deuteronomy 15:15 Remember you were a slave in Egypt, and God saved you; that's why I give you this command today.
Deuteronomy 15:16 If he tells you, "I will not leave you," because he loves you and your household and is happy with you;
Deuteronomy 15:17 Then you will take a sharp tool and pierce his ear to the door, and he will be your servant forever. Do the same for your female servant.
Deuteronomy 15:18 It won't feel difficult for you when you set him free; for he was as good as two paid workers for you, working six years: and God will bless you in everything you do.
Deuteronomy 15:19 You must set apart for God all the firstborn male animals from your herds and flocks. Don't use the firstborn of your cow for work, and don't cut the wool of the firstborn of your sheep.
Deuteronomy 15:20 You will eat it in front of God every year at the place God will choose, you and your family.
Deuteronomy 15:21 If it has any flaws, like being lame or blind or having any other serious defect, do not offer it as a sacrifice to God.
Deuteronomy 15:22 You should eat it inside your gates: both people who are unclean and those who are clean can eat it, just like they would eat a gazelle or a deer.
Deuteronomy 15:23 You must not eat the blood; you must pour it out on the ground like water.

Deuteronomy 16:1 Watch for the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to honor God, because in the month of Abib, God freed you from Egypt during the night.
Deuteronomy 16:2 You must therefore sacrifice the Passover to God, from your flocks and herds, at the place God will choose to be honored.
Deuteronomy 16:3 Do not eat any bread with yeast for seven days; eat only unleavened bread, the bread of suffering, because you left Egypt quickly. This way, you will remember the day you left Egypt for as long as you live.
Deuteronomy 16:4 You must not have any yeast bread with you anywhere in your land for seven days. Also, do not keep any of the meat you sacrifice on the first evening until the next day.
Deuteronomy 16:5 You must not sacrifice the Passover in any of your towns that God gives you.
Deuteronomy 16:6 But at the place God chooses for his name to live, there you must offer the Passover sacrifice in the evening, when the sun sets, on the anniversary of your departure from Egypt.
Deuteronomy 16:7 You should cook and eat it in the place God chooses. In the morning, you will return and go to your tents.
Deuteronomy 16:8 For six days you will eat bread without yeast, and on the seventh day there will be a special gathering to honor God. You should not do any work on that day.
Deuteronomy 16:9 Count seven weeks for yourself; start counting the seven weeks when you begin to cut the grain.
Deuteronomy 16:10 Celebrate the Festival of Weeks for God with a gift you choose to give, based on how much God has blessed you.
Deuteronomy 16:11 You will be happy in front of God, together with your son, your daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite who lives in your town, the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows among you, in the place God has chosen for His name to be honored.
Deuteronomy 16:12 Remember you were a slave in Egypt, and you must follow and obey these laws.
Deuteronomy 16:13 Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days after you have collected your grain and wine.
Deuteronomy 16:14 You should be happy during your feast—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns.
Deuteronomy 16:15 Celebrate a special festival for God for seven days at the place God picks, because God will bless all you earn and all you do, so you will be truly happy.
Deuteronomy 16:16 Three times a year, all your men must go to the place God chooses; for the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Tabernacles. They must not come to God empty-handed.
Deuteronomy 16:17 Everyone should give what they can, based on the blessings God has given you.
Deuteronomy 16:18 Appoint judges and officials for each of your towns that God gives you, for all your tribes, and they must make fair decisions for the people.
Deuteronomy 16:19 You must not twist justice; you must not favor certain people, nor accept bribes, because bribes blind the eyes of the wise and twist the words of the good.
Deuteronomy 16:20 Always do what is fair and right so you may live and receive the land God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 16:21 Do not plant any kind of trees close to God's altar that you make for yourself.
Deuteronomy 16:22 Do not set up any idol; God hates that.

Deuteronomy 17:1 Do not offer to God any bull or sheep that has a defect or any bad quality, because that is something God hates.
Deuteronomy 17:2 If you find someone in any of your towns that God gave you, man or woman, who has done evil in God's eyes by breaking his agreement,
Deuteronomy 17:3 He left to serve other gods and worshiped them, the sun, moon, or any stars, which I did not command.
Deuteronomy 17:4 If someone tells you about this and you hear it, then you carefully check and find out it's true and this terrible thing has happened in Israel.
Deuteronomy 17:5 Then you must take the man or woman who did the evil thing to your city gates, and stone them to death.
Deuteronomy 17:6 If two or three people say someone must die, then they can be killed; but if only one person says it, they cannot be killed.
Deuteronomy 17:7 The witnesses must be the first to punish him with death, and then everyone else. This is how you will remove evil from among you.
Deuteronomy 17:8 If you face a difficult case in court, whether it's a dispute about harm, legal claims, or injury, which is causing conflict in your community, then you should go to the location that God has selected.
Deuteronomy 17:9 You will go to the Levite priests and the judge who is in office at that time and ask; and they will tell you the decision of the court.
Deuteronomy 17:10 You must follow the decision the leaders at the place God chooses give you; do everything they tell you.
Deuteronomy 17:11 Follow the law they teach you and the decision they give you without turning to the right or left from what they tell you.
Deuteronomy 17:12 If someone acts arrogantly and does not listen to the priest serving before God, or to the judge, that person must be put to death. This will remove the evil from among you.
Deuteronomy 17:13 Everyone will hear, be afraid, and stop acting arrogantly.
Deuteronomy 17:14 When you arrive in the land that God gives you, and you live there, and you decide, "I want to have a king like the other nations around me;"
Deuteronomy 17:15 You must definitely make the man whom God chooses the king over you; he must be one of your own people. Do not make a foreigner who is not your brother your king.
Deuteronomy 17:16 He should not collect many horses, or make the people go back to Egypt to get more horses, because God told you not to go back that way again.
Deuteronomy 17:17 He must not have many wives so his heart won’t be led astray; nor should he gather lots of silver and gold for himself.
Deuteronomy 17:18 When he becomes king and sits on his throne, he must write for himself a copy of this law from the book in the presence of the Levite priests.
Deuteronomy 17:19 He should keep it with him and read it every day of his life. This will help him respect God and follow all the instructions and rules written in it.
Deuteronomy 17:20 So that he doesn't think he's better than his brothers, and so he doesn't ignore God's commandments, either by going too far right or left, so that he and his children may live a long time ruling over Israel.

Deuteronomy 18:1 The Levite priests and the whole Levi tribe won't have any property or share with Israel. They will eat the food given to God by fire and his share.
Deuteronomy 18:2 So they will not receive land among their brothers; God is their share, as he told them.
Deuteronomy 18:3 The priest should get this from the people who give a sacrifice, whether it's a cow or sheep: they must give the priest the shoulder, both cheeks, and the stomach.
Deuteronomy 18:4 Give the first of your grain, wine, oil, and the first wool from your sheep to him.
Deuteronomy 18:5 God has chosen him from all your tribes to serve in God's name, him and his sons forever.
Deuteronomy 18:6 If a Levite arrives from any of your towns throughout Israel where he has been staying, and he comes with all his heart's desire to the location God has chosen;
Deuteronomy 18:7 He will serve in God's name, like his fellow Levite priests who serve before God.
Deuteronomy 18:8 They will have equal shares to eat, in addition to what comes from selling their family inheritance.
Deuteronomy 18:9 When you go into the land that God is giving you, do not learn to do the terrible things that those nations do.
Deuteronomy 18:10 No one among you should make their son or daughter go through fire, use magic, tell the future, cast spells, or be a witch.
Deuteronomy 18:11 A person who charms, talks to spirits, practices magic, or communicates with the dead.
Deuteronomy 18:12 Everyone who does these things is hated by God, and because of these hateful acts, God pushes them away from you.
Deuteronomy 18:13 You should be without fault with God.
Deuteronomy 18:14 The countries you will take over listened to fortune-tellers and diviners, but God has not allowed you to do that.
Deuteronomy 18:15 God will send a Prophet from among your own people, like me; you should listen to him.
Deuteronomy 18:16 Just as you asked God at Horeb on the gathering day, saying, "I don't want to hear God's voice again, nor see this big fire, so that I won't die."
Deuteronomy 18:17 God told me, "They have said good things."
Deuteronomy 18:18 I will bring up a Prophet from among their brothers, like you, and will put my words in his mouth; he will tell them everything I command him.
Deuteronomy 18:19 If anyone doesn't listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I will hold them accountable.
Deuteronomy 18:20 But the prophet who dares to say something in my name that I didn't tell him to say, or speaks in the name of other gods, will die.
Deuteronomy 18:21 If you think, "How can we tell what words God hasn't spoken?"
Deuteronomy 18:22 When a prophet claims to speak for God, if what they say doesn't happen, it is not a message from God. The prophet spoke arrogantly. You should not fear them.

Deuteronomy 19:1 When God has destroyed the nations whose land God gives you, and you take their place, living in their cities and houses;
Deuteronomy 19:2 You must set aside three cities in the middle of your land that God gives you to own.
Deuteronomy 19:3 Make a road and split your land that God gives you into three parts so anyone who kills can escape there.
Deuteronomy 19:4 This is about the person who accidentally kills someone and runs away to a safe place to stay alive: it’s for someone who kills their neighbor without meaning to and didn't hate them before.
Deuteronomy 19:5 When a man goes to the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and while swinging the axe to chop down the tree, the axe head comes off the handle and hits his neighbor and kills him; the man should run to one of those cities for safety and live.
Deuteronomy 19:6 So that the person seeking revenge doesn't chase the killer while angry, catch him because the distance is far, and kill him, even though the killer didn't deserve to die as he had no previous hatred towards the victim.
Deuteronomy 19:7 So I order you, 'Set aside three cities for yourself.'
Deuteronomy 19:8 If God expands your territory as he promised your ancestors and gives you all the land he promised to them;
Deuteronomy 19:9 If you follow all these commandments I give you today, to love God and always walk in his ways, then you will have three more cities in addition to the three you already have.
Deuteronomy 19:10 Do not let innocent blood be shed in your land, which God gives you as an inheritance, or you will be guilty.
Deuteronomy 19:11 If anyone hates their neighbor, plans to harm them, attacks and kills them, and then runs to one of these cities:
Deuteronomy 19:12 The leaders of his city will send for him, take him from there, and hand him over to the person seeking revenge so that he can be put to death.
Deuteronomy 19:13 Do not feel sorry for him, but remove the guilt of innocent blood from Israel so that things will go well for you.
Deuteronomy 19:14 Do not move the boundary markers set long ago on the land that is your inheritance, which you will receive in the land God has given you to own.
Deuteronomy 19:15 One person alone cannot accuse someone of a wrongdoing or sin; it must be confirmed by the statement of two or three witnesses.
Deuteronomy 19:16 If someone lies about another person, saying they did something bad;
Deuteronomy 19:17 The two men who disagree will stand before God, in front of the priests and judges at that time.
Deuteronomy 19:18 The judges must carefully investigate; and if they find out the witness lied about their brother.
Deuteronomy 19:19 Then you must do to him what he planned to do to his brother; this way you will remove the evil from among you.
Deuteronomy 19:20 Those left will hear, be afraid, and will not do any more evil like that among you.
Deuteronomy 19:21 Do not feel sorry; life must be given for life, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.

Deuteronomy 20:1 When you go to fight against your enemies and you see horses and chariots and a bigger army than yours, don't be scared of them: because God who brought you out of Egypt is with you.
Deuteronomy 20:2 When you are close to the battle, the priest will come forward and talk to the people.
Deuteronomy 20:3 Listen, Israel, today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not be weak-hearted, do not be afraid, do not shake with fear, and do not be scared of them.
Deuteronomy 20:4 God is the one who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.
Deuteronomy 20:5 The leaders will talk to the people and ask, "Is there anyone who has built a new house but hasn't dedicated it yet? He should go home, so he doesn't die in the fight and someone else dedicates his house."
Deuteronomy 20:6 Who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not eaten any of its fruit yet? He should go home, so he doesn't die in battle and someone else eats the fruit.
Deuteronomy 20:7 If a man is engaged to be married and has not yet married her, he should go back to his home so he won't die in the battle and another man marry her.
Deuteronomy 20:8 The leaders will speak again to the people and ask, "Is there anyone who is scared and weak-hearted? He should go back to his home so he doesn't make his fellow soldiers lose courage like he has."
Deuteronomy 20:9 When the officers finish talking to the people, they will appoint leaders to guide the soldiers.
Deuteronomy 20:10 When you come close to a city to battle it, first offer peace to it.
Deuteronomy 20:11 If the city responds peacefully and welcomes you, then everyone in the city will pay you tribute and serve you.
Deuteronomy 20:12 If it does not agree to peace with you and wants to fight, then surround and attack it.
Deuteronomy 20:13 When God gives you victory, you must kill every man there with your sword.
Deuteronomy 20:14 But take the women, children, animals, and everything else in the city for yourself, including all the goods; and you can use what you take from your enemies, which God has given you.
Deuteronomy 20:15 Do this to all the distant cities not part of these nations.
Deuteronomy 20:16 But from the towns of these nations, which God gives you as a possession, you must not let anything that breathes live.
Deuteronomy 20:17 You must completely destroy them: the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, just as God has commanded you.
Deuteronomy 20:18 Make sure they don't teach you to follow their terrible ways that they practice for their gods; if you do, you will sin against God.
Deuteronomy 20:19 When you surround a city for a long time, fighting to capture it, do not ruin its trees by chopping them down with an axe. You can eat their fruit, but do not cut them down, because trees in the field are not your enemy to use in the siege.
Deuteronomy 20:20 Destroy only the trees you know are not for food; cut them down and use them to make defenses against the city at war with you, until it surrenders.

Deuteronomy 21:1 If a dead person is found in the land that God is giving you, lying in the field, and nobody knows who killed him:
Deuteronomy 21:2 Then your leaders and judges will come out, and they will measure to the towns around where the person was killed.
Deuteronomy 21:3 The closest city to the dead man, the city's leaders must take a cow that hasn't worked or pulled a plow.
Deuteronomy 21:4 The leaders of the city must take the cow to a rocky valley that has not been plowed or planted, and they must cut off the cow's head there in the valley.
Deuteronomy 21:5 The Levi priests should come forward; God has chosen them to serve Him and to give blessings in God's name. They will decide all arguments and cases.
Deuteronomy 21:6 All the leaders of the city closest to the man who was killed must wash their hands over the cow that is killed in the valley.
Deuteronomy 21:7 They will reply, "Our hands did not kill this person, and our eyes did not see it."
Deuteronomy 21:8 Be kind, God, to your people Israel, whom you have saved, and do not blame them for the killing of innocent people. Then they will be forgiven for that blood.
Deuteronomy 21:9 Do what is right to clear yourself of any blame for innocent blood, just as God sees right.
Deuteronomy 21:10 When you go out to fight your enemies, and God gives them to you, and you take them as prisoners,
Deuteronomy 21:11 If you see a beautiful woman among the prisoners and want her as your wife;
Deuteronomy 21:12 You will bring her to your house, and she will shave her head and trim her nails.
Deuteronomy 21:13 She must take off her captive clothes, stay in your house, and cry for her parents for a month. After that, you can marry her, and she will be your wife.
Deuteronomy 21:14 If you no longer like her, you must let her go wherever she wants; do not sell her for money or treat her as an item to sell, because you have dishonored her.
Deuteronomy 21:15 If a man has two wives, one he loves and one he does not, and they both have children for him, the loved and the unloved; and if the oldest son is the son of the unloved wife:
Deuteronomy 21:16 When he gives his children what he owns, he must not favor the son of the woman he loves over his first son by the woman he does not love.
Deuteronomy 21:17 He must recognize the son from the unloved wife as the firstborn, giving him twice as much as he has because he was the father's first sign of strength; this son has the right of the firstborn.
Deuteronomy 21:18 If a man has a son who is stubborn and refuses to obey his father or his mother, and does not listen to them even after they correct him:
Deuteronomy 21:19 His father and mother will take him and bring him to the city elders at the town gate.
Deuteronomy 21:20 They will tell the city elders, "Our son is stubborn and won't listen to us. He eats and drinks too much."
Deuteronomy 21:21 Everyone from his town must throw stones at him until he dies. This removes the evil from your community, and all of Israel will hear about it and be afraid.
Deuteronomy 21:22 If a man has done something that deserves death and he is to be executed, and you hang him on a tree:
Deuteronomy 21:23 Do not leave his body on the tree overnight; bury him that same day because anyone hung on a tree is under God's curse. Do this so that your land, which God is giving you as an inheritance, will not become unclean.

Deuteronomy 22:1 If you see your brother's ox or sheep lost, do not ignore them: you must return them to your brother.
Deuteronomy 22:2 If your brother is not close by or you don't know him, then take it to your house. Keep it until he looks for it, then give it back to him.
Deuteronomy 22:3 Treat your neighbor's donkey the same way; do the same with their clothes, and with anything they've lost that you find. You must not pretend you did not see it.
Deuteronomy 22:4 Do not ignore your neighbor's donkey or ox if they fall on the road; help your neighbor to get them back on their feet.
Deuteronomy 22:5 A woman should not wear men’s clothes, and a man should not wear women’s clothes; everyone who does this is doing something God hates.
Deuteronomy 22:6 If you find a bird's nest in a tree or on the ground with chicks or eggs and the mother is with the chicks or eggs, you must not take the mother with the young.
Deuteronomy 22:7 You must definitely let the mother bird go and only take the young birds for yourself; this will lead to your well-being and you will live a longer life.
Deuteronomy 22:8 When you build a new house, make a safety rail for your roof, so no one falls off and causes death, making you responsible.
Deuteronomy 22:9 Do not plant different kinds of seeds in your vineyard: if you do, the crops you have planted and your vineyard's fruits will be ruined.
Deuteronomy 22:10 Do not use an ox and a donkey together for plowing.
Deuteronomy 22:11 Do not wear clothes made of both wool and linen together.
Deuteronomy 22:12 Make tassels on the four corners of the clothes you wear.
Deuteronomy 22:13 If a man marries a woman, is intimate with her, and then dislikes her,
Deuteronomy 22:14 Talk against her, say she has a bad reputation, and claim, "I married this woman, but when I went to her, I discovered she was not a virgin."
Deuteronomy 22:15 Then the girl's father and mother must show proof of her virginity to the city leaders at the gate.
Deuteronomy 22:16 The girl's father will tell the leaders, "I gave my daughter to this man to be his wife, and he hates her."
Deuteronomy 22:17 Look, he claims your daughter was not a virgin, but here is proof of her virginity. They will show this cloth to the city elders.
Deuteronomy 22:18 The leaders of the city will take that man and punish him.
Deuteronomy 22:19 They must fine him one hundred silver coins, give them to the girl's father, because he gave her a bad reputation in Israel: and she must become his wife; he can't divorce her as long as he lives.
Deuteronomy 22:20 If this is true and the girl's proof of virginity is not there:
Deuteronomy 22:21 They will take the girl to the entrance of her father's home, and the men of her town will stone her to death. This is because she did a disgraceful thing in Israel by being sexually immoral in her father's house. This way, you will remove the evil from among you.
Deuteronomy 22:22 If a man is caught sleeping with a married woman, both of them must die, the man and the woman, to remove evil from Israel.
Deuteronomy 22:23 If an engaged woman who is a virgin is found in the city by a man, and he sleeps with her;
Deuteronomy 22:24 Take both of them to the city gate and throw stones at them until they die. The woman because she did not scream for help in the city, and the man because he slept with another man's wife. This way, you will get rid of the evil among you.
Deuteronomy 22:25 If a man meets an engaged woman in the field, forces her, and sleeps with her, only the man who slept with her must die.
Deuteronomy 22:26 Do nothing to the girl; she has committed no sin deserving death. It's like when someone attacks and kills their neighbor; this case is the same.
Deuteronomy 22:27 He found her in the field, the engaged girl screamed, and no one was there to save her.
Deuteronomy 22:28 If a man meets a young woman who is a virgin not promised in marriage, and he seizes her and sleeps with her, and they are discovered;
Deuteronomy 22:29 The man who slept with her must pay the woman's father fifty silver coins, and she will become his wife. Since he dishonored her, he cannot divorce her as long as he lives.
Deuteronomy 22:30 A man must not marry his father's wife or have relations with her.

Deuteronomy 23:1 Anyone with damaged testicles or a severed penis cannot join God's assembly.
Deuteronomy 23:2 A child born outside of marriage cannot join God's assembly; not even their descendants up to ten generations can join.
Deuteronomy 23:3 An Ammonite or Moabite may not join God's people; not even their descendants to the tenth generation can ever join.
Deuteronomy 23:4 Because they did not meet you with food and water when you left Egypt, and because they paid Balaam, son of Beor from Pethor in Mesopotamia, to curse you.
Deuteronomy 23:5 But God didn't listen to Balaam; instead, God changed the curse into a blessing for you, because God loved you.
Deuteronomy 23:6 Do not look for their peace or well-being at any time, forever.
Deuteronomy 23:7 Do not dislike an Edomite; he is your relative. Do not dislike an Egyptian; you were once a foreigner in his country.
Deuteronomy 23:8 The children born to them will be allowed to join God's community in their third generation.
Deuteronomy 23:9 When the army goes out against your enemies, stay away from all evil things.
Deuteronomy 23:10 If anyone among you becomes unclean because of something that happens to him at night, he must go outside the camp and not return.
Deuteronomy 23:11 When evening arrives, he must wash himself with water; and after sunset, he can return to the camp.
Deuteronomy 23:12 You must have a place outside the camp to which you can go as needed.
Deuteronomy 23:13 You should carry a tool with your weapon. When you need to use the bathroom outside, dig a hole with it, do your business, then cover it up afterwards.
Deuteronomy 23:14 God walks in the middle of your camp to save you and to defeat your enemies ahead of you; so your camp must be sacred so that God does not see anything dirty in you and leave you.
Deuteronomy 23:15 Do not return to their owner a servant who has run away from them to you.
Deuteronomy 23:16 He will live with you, in the place he picks within your gates, where he prefers: do not mistreat him.
Deuteronomy 23:17 No woman of Israel shall be a prostitute, and no man of Israel shall be a male prostitute.
Deuteronomy 23:18 Do not bring money earned from a prostitute or from selling a dog to God's house to keep a promise, because both of these are disgusting to God.
Deuteronomy 23:19 Do not charge your brother interest on money, food, or anything else that you lend with interest.
Deuteronomy 23:20 You may charge interest when you lend to a stranger, but not to your own people, so that God may bless everything you do in the land you are entering to own.
Deuteronomy 23:21 When you make a promise to God, you must not delay in fulfilling it, because God will definitely expect it from you; otherwise, it will be a sin for you.
Deuteronomy 23:22 If you choose not to make a promise, you will not be sinning.
Deuteronomy 23:23 Do what you have said; fulfill your voluntary promise to God, just as you vowed with your own words.
Deuteronomy 23:24 When you go into your neighbor's vineyard, you can eat as many grapes as you want for your own enjoyment, but you must not take any away in a container.
Deuteronomy 23:25 When you go into your neighbor's grain field, you can pick ears by hand, but you must not cut your neighbor's grain with a sickle.

Deuteronomy 24:1 When a man gets married and then doesn't like his wife because he sees something wrong with her, he should write her a divorce paper, give it to her, and make her leave his house.
Deuteronomy 24:2 When she leaves his house, she can go and become another man's wife.
Deuteronomy 24:3 If her second husband dislikes her, writes her a divorce paper, gives it to her, and sends her out of his house, or if the second husband dies, who married her.
Deuteronomy 24:4 Her first husband, who divorced her, cannot marry her again after she has been with someone else. This is wrong in God's eyes. Do not make the land God has given you as your own do wrong things.
Deuteronomy 24:5 When a man marries a new wife, he should not have to fight in war or be given any tasks. Instead, he should spend a year at home and make his wife happy.
Deuteronomy 24:6 No one should take the lower or upper millstone as a guarantee; it is like taking a person's livelihood as security.
Deuteronomy 24:7 If someone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite, intending to enslave or sell them, that kidnapper must be put to death to rid your community of this evil.
Deuteronomy 24:8 Be careful with leprosy and follow closely all that the priest Levites tell you to do. Do it just as they were instructed.
Deuteronomy 24:9 Remember what God did to Miriam when you left Egypt.
Deuteronomy 24:10 When you lend something to your brother, do not enter his house to take his collateral.
Deuteronomy 24:11 You will wait outside, and the man you lend to will bring the item he's using for collateral outside to you.
Deuteronomy 24:12 If the man is poor, do not keep his collateral overnight.
Deuteronomy 24:13 You must give back what you took as security from him by sunset so he can sleep in his own clothes and then he will thank you. This will be a good thing for you in the eyes of God.
Deuteronomy 24:14 Do not mistreat a poor and needy worker, whether they are from your own people or from the foreigners in your land.
Deuteronomy 24:15 On the day he does the work, you must pay him, and not let the sun set before you do, because he is poor and needs the money. Otherwise, he might call out to God against you, and you would be guilty of sin.
Deuteronomy 24:16 Parents should not be killed for their children's actions, nor should children be killed for their parents' actions; a person should be killed only for their own wrongdoing.
Deuteronomy 24:17 Do not twist justice for foreigners or orphans, and do not take a widow's clothing as collateral.
Deuteronomy 24:18 Remember you were a slave in Egypt and God saved you from there: that's why I tell you to do this.
Deuteronomy 24:19 When you harvest your crops and forget a bundle in the field, do not go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so God may bless you in all you do.
Deuteronomy 24:20 When you beat your olive tree, don't strip the branches: leave what's left for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
Deuteronomy 24:21 When you pick grapes from your vineyard, don't go back over it: leave what's left for outsiders, orphans, and widows.
Deuteronomy 24:22 Remember you were a slave in Egypt, so I am commanding you to do this.

Deuteronomy 25:1 If people have a dispute and go to court, the judges should decide the case, declare the innocent person right, and find the guilty person at fault.
Deuteronomy 25:2 If a bad person deserves punishment, the judge will make him lie down and be hit in front of him, as many times as his wrong act deserves.
Deuteronomy 25:3 He may be hit with up to forty lashes, but no more, so that your brother is not disgraced in your eyes.
Deuteronomy 25:4 Do not cover the ox's mouth when it is working with the grain.
Deuteronomy 25:5 If two brothers live together and one dies without having children, his widow should not marry an outsider. Her husband's brother should marry her, fulfilling the brother-in-law's responsibility.
Deuteronomy 25:6 The first child she has will take his dead brother's place so his name will not be forgotten in Israel.
Deuteronomy 25:7 If the man does not want to marry his brother's widow, she should go to the town leaders at the gate and say, "My husband's brother won't continue his family name in Israel; he refuses his duty to me as my husband's brother."
Deuteronomy 25:8 The leaders of his town shall call him and talk to him; and if he insists and says, I don't want to marry her;
Deuteronomy 25:9 The brother's wife must come to him before the elders, take off his shoe, spit in his face, and say, "This is what happens to a man who won't carry on his brother's family."
Deuteronomy 25:10 In Israel, people will call his family 'The House of the Man Whose Shoe Was Taken Off.'
Deuteronomy 25:11 When men fight and one's wife tries to save her husband from the one hitting him by reaching out and grabbing his private parts:
Deuteronomy 25:12 Then you must cut off her hand and show her no pity.
Deuteronomy 25:13 You must not have different weights, big and small, in your bag.
Deuteronomy 25:14 Do not keep different sized measures, large and small, in your house.
Deuteronomy 25:15 You must use accurate and fair weights and measures so that you may live a long time in the land God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 25:16 Everyone who does these things, and all who act unfairly, are hated by God.
Deuteronomy 25:17 Remember what Amalek did to you on your journey after you left Egypt.
Deuteronomy 25:18 He attacked you on the journey, hitting all the weakest people at the back when you were tired and weak; he did not respect God.
Deuteronomy 25:19 So when God has given you peace from all your enemies around, in the land God gives you to own, you must erase all memory of Amalek from under the sky; do not forget this.

Deuteronomy 26:1 When you enter the land God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and live there;
Deuteronomy 26:2 You must take some of the first fruits from your harvest, from the land that God gives you, put them in a basket, and go to the place God chooses for his name to live.
Deuteronomy 26:3 You will go to the priest who is serving at that time, and tell him, "I declare today to God that I have arrived in the land God promised to our ancestors to give to us."
Deuteronomy 26:4 The priest will take the basket from your hand and put it in front of God's altar.
Deuteronomy 26:5 You will say in front of God, "My father was a struggling Syrian, and he went down to Egypt and stayed there with just a few people, and there he became a large, strong, and numerous nation."
Deuteronomy 26:6 The Egyptians treated us badly, hurt us, and forced us into harsh slavery.
Deuteronomy 26:7 When we cried to God of our ancestors, God heard us and saw our suffering, our hard work, and our oppression.
Deuteronomy 26:8 God led us out of Egypt with great power, with a strong arm, with fearsome acts, and with miraculous signs.
Deuteronomy 26:9 God has led us to this place and given us this land, a land rich with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 26:10 And now, look, I have brought the first crops of the land that you, God, have given me. You will place them before God, and bow down before God.
Deuteronomy 26:11 You will be happy with every good thing that God has given to you, your family, the Levite, and the foreigner living with you.
Deuteronomy 26:12 When you finish taking a tenth part of all your crops every third year, the year for giving a tenth, and give it to the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows so they can have enough food in your towns and be satisfied.
Deuteronomy 26:13 Then you will say in front of God, "I have removed the sacred things from my house, and I have given them to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not broken your commands, nor have I forgotten them."
Deuteronomy 26:14 I have not eaten any of it while sad, nor have I used any for impure purposes, nor have I given any for the dead. But I have listened to God's voice and done everything you commanded me.
Deuteronomy 26:15 Look from your holy home in heaven and bless your people Israel and the land you gave us, like you promised our ancestors, a land filled with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 26:16 Today, God has told you to follow these rules and decisions: so you must obey them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Deuteronomy 26:17 You have promised today that God is your God, and to follow his ways, keep his rules, commands, and decisions, and to listen to his voice.
Deuteronomy 26:18 Today, God has declared you to be his special people, just as he promised, and you should follow all his commands.
Deuteronomy 26:19 God will make you greater than any other nation He created, in praise, reputation, and honor, so you will be a special people dedicated to God, just as He promised.

Deuteronomy 27:1 Moses and the leaders of Israel told the people, "Follow all the rules I give you today."
Deuteronomy 27:2 On the day you cross the Jordan into the land God is giving you, you must set up large stones and cover them with plaster.
Deuteronomy 27:3 Write all the words of this law on them when you cross over, so you can enter the land that God gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the God of your ancestors promised you.
Deuteronomy 27:4 So when you cross the Jordan River, set up these stones I tell you about today on Mount Ebal and cover them with plaster.
Deuteronomy 27:5 There you will make an altar for God using stones. Do not use any iron tools on the stones.
Deuteronomy 27:6 Make God's altar with unbroken stones, and offer burnt sacrifices to God on it.
Deuteronomy 27:7 Give peace offerings, eat them there, and be happy before God.
Deuteronomy 27:8 You should write all the words of this law clearly on the stones.
Deuteronomy 27:9 Moses and the Levite priests spoke to all Israel, saying, "Pay attention and listen, Israel; today you have become the people of God."
Deuteronomy 27:10 You must listen to God's voice and do what he commands, including his rules that I tell you today.
Deuteronomy 27:11 On that day, Moses gave the people these instructions:
Deuteronomy 27:12 These will stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
Deuteronomy 27:13 These will stand on Mount Ebal to pronounce curses: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
Deuteronomy 27:14 The Levites will speak out and say to all the Israelite men in a loud voice,
Deuteronomy 27:15 May the person who makes any carved or metal idol, which God hates, made by an artist, and hides it, be cursed. And all the people will agree and say, "Amen."
Deuteronomy 27:16 May the one who disrespects his father or mother be cursed. And all the people shall agree, saying, "Yes."
Deuteronomy 27:17 May the person who moves his neighbor's property marker be cursed. All the people shall agree by saying, "Amen."
Deuteronomy 27:18 May the person who leads the blind astray be cursed. And everyone will agree by saying, "Amen."
Deuteronomy 27:19 May the one who twists the justice due to foreigners, orphans, and widows be cursed. And let all the people say, "So be it."
Deuteronomy 27:20 May the person who sleeps with his father's wife be cursed, for he shames his father. And all the people will agree by saying, Amen.
Deuteronomy 27:21 A person who sleeps with an animal is cursed. Everyone must agree to this by saying "Amen."
Deuteronomy 27:22 Let the person who sleeps with his half-sister or stepsister be cursed, and everyone will agree by saying, "Yes."
Deuteronomy 27:23 May the person who sleeps with his mother-in-law be cursed. And everyone will agree, saying, "Yes."
Deuteronomy 27:24 Someone who secretly hurts their neighbor is cursed. And everyone will agree by saying, "Yes."
Deuteronomy 27:25 May the person who takes money to kill an innocent be cursed. And everyone will agree.
Deuteronomy 27:26 Let the person who does not follow all the rules of these laws be cursed. And everyone will agree by saying, "Amen."

Deuteronomy 28:1 If you carefully listen to God and follow all the commands I give you today, God will make you greater than all other nations on Earth.
Deuteronomy 28:2 All these good things will come to you and be yours if you listen to God's voice.
Deuteronomy 28:3 You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the field.
Deuteronomy 28:4 You will be blessed with healthy children, good crops, many cattle, more cows, and lots of sheep.
Deuteronomy 28:5 Your basket and your storage will be blessed.
Deuteronomy 28:6 You will be blessed when you come in, and you will be blessed when you go out.
Deuteronomy 28:7 God will make your enemies who attack you defeated in front of you: they will approach you from one direction, but they will run away from you in seven different ways.
Deuteronomy 28:8 God will order blessings for you on your storage places and on everything you do; and he will bless you in the land God gives you.
Deuteronomy 28:9 God will make you his special people, just as he promised you, if you follow his commands and live as he wants you to.
Deuteronomy 28:10 Everyone on earth will know you are named after God, and they will fear you.
Deuteronomy 28:11 God will make you rich in belongings, in children, in livestock, and in crops on your land—the land God promised to your ancestors to give to you.
Deuteronomy 28:12 God will open his good treasure for you, the sky to send rain to your land at the right time, and he will bless all you do: you will lend to many countries, but you will not need to borrow.
Deuteronomy 28:13 God will make you the leader, not the follower; you will be on top, not on the bottom, if you listen to and follow God's commands that I give you today.
Deuteronomy 28:14 Do not turn away from any of the words I command you today, either to the right or to the left, to follow and serve other gods.
Deuteronomy 28:15 If you do not listen to God and do all his commands and rules that I give you today, then all these curses will come on you and catch you.
Deuteronomy 28:16 You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the field.
Deuteronomy 28:17 Your basket and your storage will be cursed.
Deuteronomy 28:18 Your children, your crops, your cattle, and your sheep will be cursed.
Deuteronomy 28:19 You will be cursed when you come in, and you will be cursed when you go out.
Deuteronomy 28:20 God will make you suffer, trouble you, and scold you in everything you try to do until you are ruined and die soon, all because you did evil things and turned away from me.
Deuteronomy 28:21 God will cause disease to stick to you until it wipes you out from the land you're going to take over.
Deuteronomy 28:22 God will strike you with wasting disease, fever, swelling, severe heat, the sword, blight, and mildew; these will chase you until you die.
Deuteronomy 28:23 The sky above you will be like metal, and the ground beneath you will be as hard as iron.
Deuteronomy 28:24 God will turn the rain of your land into powder and dust: it will come down from the sky on you until you are destroyed.
Deuteronomy 28:25 God will let you be defeated by your enemies: you will attack them from one direction, but run away in seven different directions, and you will be scattered among all the nations of the world.
Deuteronomy 28:26 Your dead body will become food for all the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, and no one will scare them away.
Deuteronomy 28:27 God will punish you with sores, hemorrhoids, scabs, and itching that cannot be cured.
Deuteronomy 28:28 God will strike you with madness, blindness, and deep confusion.
Deuteronomy 28:29 You will feel around at midday like a blind person in the dark, and you will not succeed in what you do: you will always be mistreated and robbed, and no one will rescue you.
Deuteronomy 28:30 You will promise to marry a woman, but another man will be with her; you will build a house, but you won't live in it; you will plant a vineyard, but you won't pick its grapes.
Deuteronomy 28:31 Your ox will be killed while you watch, and you won't eat any of it. Your donkey will be forcefully taken from you and will not be returned. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, and you will have no one to save them.
Deuteronomy 28:32 Your sons and daughters will be given to another people, and you will watch, powerless and longing for them all day long; but you will not be able to do anything.
Deuteronomy 28:33 A nation you do not know will eat the crops from your land and all your hard work; you will be constantly oppressed and crushed.
Deuteronomy 28:34 You will go crazy from what you will see.
Deuteronomy 28:35 God will strike you with painful sores on your knees and legs that can't be cured, from the bottom of your feet to the top of your head.
Deuteronomy 28:36 God will take you and your chosen king to a foreign country that neither you nor your ancestors have heard of; there you will worship man-made gods of wood and stone.
Deuteronomy 28:37 You will become a wonder, a common saying, and an insult among all the nations where God takes you.
Deuteronomy 28:38 You will take a lot of seeds to the field but will harvest only a little because locusts will eat it.
Deuteronomy 28:39 You will plant vineyards and take care of them, but you will not drink the wine or pick the grapes; because worms will eat them.
Deuteronomy 28:40 You will have olive trees all around your land, but you will not use the oil on yourself; because your olives will drop off before they are ready.
Deuteronomy 28:41 You will have sons and daughters, but you won't enjoy them; they will be taken away as captives.
Deuteronomy 28:42 Locusts will eat all the trees and fruit in your land.
Deuteronomy 28:43 The foreigner living among you will rise above you, very high; and you will go down, very low.
Deuteronomy 28:44 He will lend to you, and you will not lend to him: he will be the leader, and you will follow.
Deuteronomy 28:45 All these curses will happen to you. They will chase you and catch you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to God or follow his rules and laws that he gave you.
Deuteronomy 28:46 They will be on you as a sign and a marvel, and on your descendants forever.
Deuteronomy 28:47 Because you did not serve God with joy and a happy heart, even though you had plenty of everything;
Deuteronomy 28:48 You will serve your enemies that God will send against you, in hunger, thirst, being without clothes, and lacking everything. They will put an iron yoke on your neck until they have destroyed you.
Deuteronomy 28:49 God will send a nation against you from far away, from the end of the earth, fast like an eagle flies; a nation whose language you will not understand.
Deuteronomy 28:50 A nation with a scary face, that will not respect old people or be kind to the young.
Deuteronomy 28:51 He will eat your livestock and crops until you are ruined. He will not leave you any grain, wine, or oil, nor will he leave the calves of your cows or the lambs of your sheep until he has ruined you.
Deuteronomy 28:52 He will surround you at all your gateways until your tall and strong walls fall down, where you felt safe, all over your land. And he will surround you at all your gateways all over your land, which God has given you.
Deuteronomy 28:53 You will eat the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your sons and daughters, which God has given you, during the siege and hardship your enemies will cause you.
Deuteronomy 28:54 So the man who is gentle and delicate among you will become hard-hearted against his brother, his beloved wife, and the rest of his children he has left.
Deuteronomy 28:55 So he won't give any of his children's flesh, which he will eat, to others because he has nothing left during the siege and hardship when your enemies pressure you at all your gates.
Deuteronomy 28:56 The soft and gentle woman among you, who would not dare to put her foot on the ground because she is so refined and gentle, will look with hostility at her husband, her son, and her daughter.
Deuteronomy 28:57 She will turn against her newborn baby and the children she has given birth to. She will secretly eat them because she has nothing else during the siege and hardship your enemy will cause within your cities.
Deuteronomy 28:58 If you do not carefully follow all the words of this law written in this book and respect this wonderful and awe-inspiring name, God.
Deuteronomy 28:59 Then God will make your sicknesses very bad, and your descendants will also have serious, lasting diseases and severe, long-term illnesses.
Deuteronomy 28:60 God will cause you to suffer all the sicknesses you feared in Egypt, and they will stick with you.
Deuteronomy 28:61 God will bring upon you every sickness and plague not recorded in this book of law until you are destroyed.
Deuteronomy 28:62 You will become very few in number, though you were as numerous as the stars in the sky, because you did not obey God.
Deuteronomy 28:63 It will happen that just as God was happy to make things good for you and increase your numbers, so God will be happy to ruin you and make you disappear; and you will be taken away from the land you are about to take over.
Deuteronomy 28:64 God will scatter you among all nations, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you will worship other gods that you and your ancestors did not know, made of wood and stone.
Deuteronomy 28:65 In these countries, you will not be at ease, nor will your feet find rest. God will make your heart fearful, your eyesight weak, and your mind sad.
Deuteronomy 28:66 Your life will hang uncertain before you; you will be afraid all day and night, and will have no confidence about living.
Deuteronomy 28:67 In the morning, you will wish it were evening. In the evening, you will wish it were morning because of the fear in your heart and the terrible things you will see.
Deuteronomy 28:68 God will take you back to Egypt in ships, by the path I told you you'd never see again. There, you will be sold to your enemies as slaves, both men and women, but no one will buy you.

Deuteronomy 29:4 But God has not given you a mind to understand, or eyes to see, or ears to hear, until today.
Deuteronomy 29:5 I have guided you for forty years in the desert: your clothes have not worn out, and your shoes have not worn out on your feet.
Deuteronomy 29:6 You haven't eaten bread or drunk wine or strong alcohol so that you may know that I am God.
Deuteronomy 29:7 When you arrived here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan fought against us, and we defeated them.
Deuteronomy 29:8 We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

Deuteronomy 29:12 You should agree to a commitment with God, and to His promise, which God makes with you today.

Deuteronomy 29:14 I am making this promise and agreement not just with you.
Deuteronomy 29:15 But with everyone here today in front of God, and with those who are not here with us today.
Deuteronomy 29:16 You know how we lived in Egypt and how we traveled through the countries you went by.
Deuteronomy 29:17 You have seen their disgusting idols, made of wood, stone, silver, and gold, that were with them.
Deuteronomy 29:18 Make sure no one among you—man, woman, family, or group—turns away from God today to worship the gods of other lands. Make sure there's no one among you that grows bitter and poisonous like a harmful plant.
Deuteronomy 29:19 When he hears the words of this curse, he might tell himself he will be okay, even though he follows his own stubborn desires, leading to more and more wrong.
Deuteronomy 29:20 God will not forgive him, but then God's anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and all the curses written in this book will fall on him, and God will erase his name from under heaven.
Deuteronomy 29:21 God will set him apart for harm from all the tribes of Israel, following all the curses of the agreement written in this book of the law.
Deuteronomy 29:22 So that future generations of your children and newcomers from distant lands will ask, when they see the disasters and diseases that God has brought on the land;
Deuteronomy 29:23 The whole land is full of sulfur, salt, and ash, nothing can be planted, nothing grows, and no grass sprouts, just like when God destroyed Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim in his anger and fury.
Deuteronomy 29:24 All nations will ask, "Why has God acted this way towards this land? What does this fierce anger mean?"
Deuteronomy 29:25 People will say, "It's because they left the agreement with God that their ancestors had, which he made with them when he took them out of Egypt."
Deuteronomy 29:26 They left and served different gods, and bowed to them, gods they didn't know, and that God hadn't given to them.
Deuteronomy 29:27 God became very angry with this land and decided to bring all the curses written in this book upon it.
Deuteronomy 29:28 In anger, wrath, and deep displeasure, God removed them from their land and threw them into another land, where they are to this day.
Deuteronomy 29:29 Hidden things are for God, but what is shown is for us and our kids forever, so we can follow all of this law.

Deuteronomy 30:2 Go back to God, listen to Him, and follow everything I tell you today, you and your children, with all your heart and all your soul.
Deuteronomy 30:3 God will end your captivity, show you mercy, and bring you back from all the nations where God has spread you out.
Deuteronomy 30:4 If any of you are scattered to the farthest skies, God will bring you back from there.
Deuteronomy 30:5 God will take you to the land your fathers owned, you will own it; He will be good to you and increase your numbers more than your fathers.
Deuteronomy 30:6 God will change your heart and the hearts of your descendants so that you love God with all your heart and soul, and you will live.
Deuteronomy 30:7 God will give all these curses to your enemies and to those who hate and trouble you.
Deuteronomy 30:8 You will come back and listen to God, and follow all his orders that I give you today.
Deuteronomy 30:9 God will bless all the work you do, make you have many children, give you many animals, and make your land produce good crops, because God will take joy in making things good for you, just as He did for your ancestors.
Deuteronomy 30:10 If you listen to God's voice and follow His commands and rules written in this book of the law, and if you turn to God with all your heart and all your soul.
Deuteronomy 30:11 This command I give you today is not secret or hard to reach.
Deuteronomy 30:12 It's not up in heaven, so you don't need to ask, "Who will go up to heaven to get it for us, so we can listen and follow it?"
Deuteronomy 30:13 It's not across the sea, so you don't need to ask, "Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us, so we can hear it and do it?"
Deuteronomy 30:14 The message is very close to you, in your mouth and in your heart, so you can do it.
Deuteronomy 30:15 Look, today I put in front of you life and what is good, and death and what is bad.
Deuteronomy 30:16 Today I tell you to love God, follow His paths, and obey His rules and laws, so you can live and have many children. God will bless you in the land you are going to make yours.
Deuteronomy 30:17 If your heart turns away and you don't listen, but instead you are led astray to worship and serve other gods;
Deuteronomy 30:18 I tell you today that you will certainly die and not live long in the land you're crossing the Jordan River to take over.
Deuteronomy 30:19 I tell heaven and earth today to witness against you: I have given you the choice between life and death, and between blessings and curses. So choose life, so that you and your children can live.
Deuteronomy 30:20 So you can love God, obey what he says, and stay close to him because he gives you life and a long time to live, so you can stay in the land God promised to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give to them.

Deuteronomy 31:1 Moses went and said these things to all Israel.
Deuteronomy 31:2 He told them, "Today I am 120 years old; I can't lead you anymore. God also told me, 'You will not cross this Jordan river.'"
Deuteronomy 31:3 God will go ahead of you and will destroy the nations so you can take their land; and Joshua will lead you, just as God has promised.
Deuteronomy 31:4 God will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings, and their land, which he destroyed.
Deuteronomy 31:5 God will let you defeat them so you can follow all the rules I have given you.
Deuteronomy 31:6 Be strong and brave, don't be scared or fear them, because God, your God, is with you; he will not leave you or abandon you.
Deuteronomy 31:7 Moses called Joshua and told him in front of all Israel, "Be strong and brave, for you will lead these people to the land God promised to give their ancestors, and you will help them take it as their own."
Deuteronomy 31:8 God goes before you; He will be with you, He will not leave you or forget you; do not be scared or worried.
Deuteronomy 31:9 Moses wrote down the law and gave it to the Levite priests who carried God's covenant chest, and to all the leaders of Israel.
Deuteronomy 31:10 Moses told them, "Every seven years, at the appointed time in the year of debt cancellation, during the Festival of Shelters,
Deuteronomy 31:11 When all Israel comes to meet God at the place He will choose, you must read this law to all Israel so they can hear it.
Deuteronomy 31:12 Bring everyone together, men, women, and children, and any outsiders living with you, so they can listen, learn to respect God, and follow all the teachings of this law.
Deuteronomy 31:13 So that your children, who do not know anything, can listen and learn to respect God, as you live in the land you are going to take over across the Jordan.
Deuteronomy 31:14 God told Moses, "Look, your time to die is near: call Joshua, and both of you come to the meeting tent, so I can give him instructions." Moses and Joshua went and stood in the meeting tent.
Deuteronomy 31:15 God appeared in the tent as a cloud pillar, and the cloud pillar stayed above the tent's entrance.
Deuteronomy 31:16 God said to Moses, "Look, you will die just like your ancestors did; and these people will betray me and follow the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will leave me and break the agreement I have made with them."
Deuteronomy 31:17 On that day, I'll get very angry with them, leave them, and turn away from them. They will be destroyed and face many bad things and troubles. Then they will realize and say, "These bad things are happening because our God is not with us."
Deuteronomy 31:18 I will definitely hide my face on that day because of all the wrongs they have done, since they have turned to other gods.
Deuteronomy 31:19 Now, write down this song for yourselves and teach it to the people of Israel. Have them sing it, so it will stand as evidence against them.
Deuteronomy 31:20 When I bring them to the land I promised their ancestors, a land rich with milk and honey, they will eat, be satisfied, become prosperous, then they will turn to other gods, worship them, anger me, and break our agreement.
Deuteronomy 31:21 When they face many bad things and troubles, this song will stand as evidence against them because it will not be forgotten by their descendants. I am aware of their thoughts even now, before they enter the land I promised.
Deuteronomy 31:22 Moses wrote this song that day and taught it to the people of Israel.
Deuteronomy 31:23 God commanded Joshua, Nun's son, saying, "Be strong and brave, for you will lead the people of Israel into the land I promised them, and I will be with you."
Deuteronomy 31:24 When Moses finished writing the words of this law in a book,
Deuteronomy 31:25 Moses told the Levites who carried the covenant box of God, saying,
Deuteronomy 31:26 Take this law book and place it beside the covenant box of God, so it can be a witness against you.
Deuteronomy 31:27 I know you are rebellious and stubborn. Even while I am still alive with you today, you have rebelled against God; how much more will you do so after I die?
Deuteronomy 31:28 Bring to me all the tribe leaders and your officials so I can tell them these things and have heaven and earth witness against them.
Deuteronomy 31:29 I know that after I die, you will become corrupt and leave the path I commanded. Bad things will happen to you later because you will do wrong, making God angry with what you do.
Deuteronomy 31:30 Moses spoke to all the Israelites the words of this song until it was finished.

Deuteronomy 32:1 Listen, heavens, and I will talk; and listen, earth, to what I say.
Deuteronomy 32:2 My teaching will fall like rain, my words will settle like dew, like a light rain on new plants, and like showers on the grass.
Deuteronomy 32:3 I will tell everyone about God's name: say our God is great.
Deuteronomy 32:4 He is the Rock, His work is perfect; all His ways are fair. A God of truth, not doing wrong, just and upright is He.
Deuteronomy 32:5 They have made themselves bad; they are not like his children because they are a wrong and twisted group.
Deuteronomy 32:6 Are you repaying God like this, you foolish and senseless people? Isn't He your father who created you? Didn't He make and sustain you?
Deuteronomy 32:7 Think about the past and reflect on the years gone by. Ask your father, and he will teach you; talk to the older people, and they will explain it to you.
Deuteronomy 32:8 When God divided the lands among the nations, when he split up the people, he set the borders based on how many Israelites there were.
Deuteronomy 32:9 God's share is his people; Jacob is the group he has chosen to receive his inheritance.
Deuteronomy 32:10 He found him in a desert land, in a noisy empty wilderness; he led him around, taught him, and protected him like the pupil of his eye.
Deuteronomy 32:11 Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, hovers over its young, spreads its wings, takes them, and carries them on its wings.
Deuteronomy 32:12 God alone guided him, and there was no other god with him.
Deuteronomy 32:13 God let him ride on the earth's high places, to eat the crops from the fields; God let him taste honey from the rock and oil from the hard stone.
Deuteronomy 32:14 Butter from cows, and sheep's milk, with lamb's fat, and Bashan-bred rams, and goats, with wheat's creamy richness; and you drank grape juice, pure and rich.
Deuteronomy 32:15 Jeshurun grew fat and rebelled; you became fat, you got thick, you were filled with fat; then you left God who created you, and didn't value the God who saved you.
Deuteronomy 32:16 They made God jealous with foreign gods, and with hateful acts they made him angry.
Deuteronomy 32:17 They offered sacrifices to demons, not to God; to gods they did not know, to new gods that were recently made, that your ancestors did not fear.
Deuteronomy 32:18 You have forgotten the God who gave you life and ignored the one who made you.
Deuteronomy 32:19 When God saw it, he hated them because they angered his sons and daughters.
Deuteronomy 32:20 He said, "I will turn away from them and see what their future holds, because they are a difficult and unfaithful generation."
Deuteronomy 32:21 They made me jealous with things that are not God; they angered me with their useless actions. And I will make them jealous with those who are not a people; I will make them angry with a foolish nation.
Deuteronomy 32:22 My anger has started a fire that will burn to the deepest hell, destroy the earth and its crops, and set the mountain bases on fire.
Deuteronomy 32:23 I will bring many troubles upon them; I will use up my arrows against them.
Deuteronomy 32:24 They will suffer from severe hunger, extreme heat, and harsh destruction. I will also let wild animals attack them, and snakes from the ground will poison them.
Deuteronomy 32:25 Outside, the sword, and inside, fear, will kill the young man and the young woman, as well as the baby and the old man.
Deuteronomy 32:26 I said I would spread them out and make people forget them completely.
Deuteronomy 32:27 If I were not worried about our enemies' anger, they might act wrongly and claim, "We won by our own power, and God didn't do this."
Deuteronomy 32:28 They are a nation without guidance, and they have no understanding.
Deuteronomy 32:29 If only they were wise and understood this, so they would think about their future!
Deuteronomy 32:30 How can one person chase a thousand, or two people make ten thousand run away, unless their protector has abandoned them and God has trapped them?
Deuteronomy 32:31 Their rock is not like our God, even our enemies agree.
Deuteronomy 32:32 Their vine comes from Sodom's vines, and Gomorrah's fields: their grapes are bitter, their bunches are sour.
Deuteronomy 32:33 Their wine is like dragon poison and very cruel snake venom.
Deuteronomy 32:34 Isn't this kept with me and sealed in my treasures?
Deuteronomy 32:35 I am in charge of revenge and payback; their feet will slip when the time comes: because their disaster day is near, and the things that will happen to them will come quickly.
Deuteronomy 32:36 God will judge his people and change his mind for his servants when he sees their strength is gone and no one is confined or remaining.
Deuteronomy 32:37 He will ask, "Where are their gods, the rock they trusted in?"
Deuteronomy 32:38 Who ate the best parts of your offerings and drank your wine gifts? Let them get up and help you; let them protect you.
Deuteronomy 32:39 Understand now that I am the only God; there is no other god beside me. I can cause death or give life; I can injure or heal, and no one can rescue from my power.
Deuteronomy 32:40 I raise my hand to the sky and say, I will live forever.
Deuteronomy 32:41 If I sharpen my shiny sword, and my hand grabs justice, I will give payback to my enemies and repay those who hate me.
Deuteronomy 32:42 I will make my arrows soaked with blood, and my sword will consume flesh; with the blood of those killed and prisoners, from the first acts of revenge against the enemy.
Deuteronomy 32:43 Celebrate, all you nations, with God's people, because He will take revenge for His servants' blood, pay back His enemies, and be kind to His land and His people.
Deuteronomy 32:44 Moses came and told all the words of this song to the people, along with Hoshea, Nun's son.
Deuteronomy 32:45 Moses finished telling all these words to all Israel.
Deuteronomy 32:46 He told them, "Pay close attention to everything I am telling you today. Teach your children to follow all the instructions of this law."
Deuteronomy 32:47 This is not useless for you; it is your life. By doing this, you will live longer in the land you will own after crossing the Jordan.
Deuteronomy 32:48 On that same day, God spoke to Moses, saying,
Deuteronomy 32:49 Go up to Mount Abarim, to Mount Nebo in Moab, across from Jericho; and look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as their own.
Deuteronomy 32:50 You will die on the mountain you are climbing and join your ancestors, just like your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his ancestors.
Deuteronomy 32:51 Because you disobeyed me among the Israelites at Meribah-Kadesh, in the Zin desert; because you did not honor me in front of the Israelites.
Deuteronomy 32:52 You will see the land in front of you, but you will not enter the land I am giving to the children of Israel.

Deuteronomy 33:1 This is the blessing that Moses, the man of God, gave to the Israelites before he died.
Deuteronomy 33:2 He said, God came from Sinai, appeared from Seir to them, shone from Mount Paran, and arrived with thousands of holy ones. From his right hand, a fiery command for them went out.
Deuteronomy 33:3 Yes, he loves the people; all his holy ones are in your care: and they sit at your feet; everyone will receive your words.
Deuteronomy 33:4 Moses gave us a law, which is the inheritance for the community of Jacob.
Deuteronomy 33:5 He became king in Jeshurun when the leaders and tribes of Israel came together.
Deuteronomy 33:6 Let Reuben live and not die, and may his people be many.
Deuteronomy 33:7 This is Judah's blessing: He said, "Listen, God, to Judah's voice, and bring him to his people. May his hands be strong enough for him, and help him against his enemies."
Deuteronomy 33:8 Of Levi he said, Let your objects of truth and decision stay with your holy one, whom you tested at Massah, and whom you argued with at Meribah's waters.
Deuteronomy 33:9 He told his father and mother, "I haven't seen him." He didn't recognize his brothers or know his children because they followed your instruction and kept your agreement.
Deuteronomy 33:10 They will teach Jacob your rules, and Israel your laws. They will offer incense to you, and complete burnt offerings on your altar.
Deuteronomy 33:11 God, bless his belongings, and accept what he does; strike down those who attack him, and those who hate him, so they don't get up again.
Deuteronomy 33:12 About Benjamin, he said, "God's loved one will live safely with Him; God will protect him always, and he will rest close to His heart."
Deuteronomy 33:13 And about Joseph he said, "May his land be blessed by God with the valuable gifts of heaven, with dew, and with water from beneath the earth."
Deuteronomy 33:14 For the valuable foods grown by the sun, and for the valuable things produced by the moon,
Deuteronomy 33:15 For the best parts of the old mountains, and for the valuable things of the eternal hills.
Deuteronomy 33:16 For the valuable things of the earth and its richness, and for the kindness of God who appeared in the bush: let the blessing rest on Joseph's head, and on the crown of the head of him who was set apart from his brothers.
Deuteronomy 33:17 His majesty is like that of a young bull, and his power is like the horns of unicorns. With it, he will gather people from all over the world. They are the many from Ephraim and the many from Manasseh.
Deuteronomy 33:18 God said about Zebulun, "Be happy, Zebulun, when you go out; and Issachar, be happy in your homes."
Deuteronomy 33:19 They will invite the people to the mountain; there they will give right sacrifices: for they will enjoy the riches of the seas, and the hidden treasures of the sand.
Deuteronomy 33:20 About Gad, he said, "Lucky is the one who makes Gad grow: he lives like a lion and rips off the arm and the top of the head."
Deuteronomy 33:21 He set aside the best land for himself because he took the lead in the law. He joined the leaders and made fair decisions for the people, following God's laws and rules with Israel.
Deuteronomy 33:22 About Dan, he said, "Dan is a young lion; he will jump out from Bashan."
Deuteronomy 33:23 Naphtali, you are content with favor and filled with God's blessings; take the west and the south.
Deuteronomy 33:24 Asher will be blessed with children, loved by his brothers, and have rich land.
Deuteronomy 33:25 Your shoes will be made of iron and brass; and your strength will last as long as your life.
Deuteronomy 33:26 No one is like the God of Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to help you, and shows his greatness in the skies.
Deuteronomy 33:27 The forever God is your safe place, and his arms that last always are holding you up: he will push away your enemies from in front of you, and tell you to wipe them out.
Deuteronomy 33:28 Israel will live safely on its own; Jacob's descendants will have a place with fields of grain and vineyards; their sky will give them dew.
Deuteronomy 33:29 You are lucky, Israel: Who is like you, a people saved by God, your helper's shield and the sword of your greatness! Your enemies will be proven liars to you; and you will walk on their high places.

Deuteronomy 34:1 Moses went up from the Moab plains to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. God showed him all the land of Gilead, as far as Dan.
Deuteronomy 34:2 All Naphtali, Ephraim's land, Manasseh, and all Judah's land, up to the farthest sea,
Deuteronomy 34:3 To the south, the flat land of Jericho's valley, the city with palm trees, up to Zoar.
Deuteronomy 34:4 God said to him, "This is the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I said I would give it to your descendants. I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it."
