Deuteronomy 34:5 Moses, God's servant, died in Moab as God said.
Deuteronomy 34:6 He buried him in a valley in Moab, near Bethpeor, but no one knows his grave location to this day.
Deuteronomy 34:7 Moses was 120 years old when he died; his eyesight was still clear, and he was still strong.
Deuteronomy 34:8 The Israelites cried for Moses in the Moab plains for thirty days; after that, the time for crying and grieving for Moses was over.
Deuteronomy 34:9 Joshua, son of Nun, was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had put his hands on him; so, the Israelites listened to him and did what God had told Moses.
Deuteronomy 34:10 No prophet like Moses has since appeared in Israel, someone whom God knew personally.
Deuteronomy 34:11 In all the miracles and amazing things that God told him to do in Egypt, to Pharaoh, his officials, and his whole country,
Deuteronomy 34:12 And with all the power and amazing acts that Moses performed for all Israel to see.

Joshua 1:1 After Moses, God's servant, died, God spoke to Joshua, Nun's son and Moses' assistant, saying,
Joshua 1:2 Moses, my servant, has died; now get up, cross the Jordan River, you and all these people, to the land I am giving to the Israelites.
Joshua 1:3 Every place where you step, I have given it to you, just as I promised Moses.
Joshua 1:4 From the desert and Lebanon to the big river, the Euphrates, all the Hittite land, and to the big sea where the sun sets, this will be your border.
Joshua 1:5 No one will be able to defeat you as long as you live. Just like I was with Moses, I will be with you; I won't let you down or abandon you.
Joshua 1:6 Be brave and confident, because you will give this nation the land as their inheritance that I promised to their ancestors.
Joshua 1:7 Be strong and brave, follow all the laws Moses gave you without turning from them, and you will succeed wherever you go.
Joshua 1:8 Keep this book of rules always in your speech; think about it all the time so you can be careful to do everything written in it. Then you'll succeed and do well.
Joshua 1:9 Didn't I command you? Be strong and brave; don't be scared or discouraged, for God is with you wherever you go.
Joshua 1:10 Joshua told the people's leaders, "
Joshua 1:11 Go through the camp and tell the people to get their food ready. In three days, you will cross the Jordan River to take over the land that God is giving you.
Joshua 1:12 Joshua spoke to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of the tribe of Manasseh, saying,
Joshua 1:13 Remember what Moses, God's servant, told you: God has given you rest and has given you this land.
Joshua 1:14 Your wives, children, and animals will stay in the land Moses gave you east of the Jordan River; but you must go ahead of your fellow Israelites ready for battle, all the brave soldiers, and help them.
Joshua 1:15 Stay until God gives your brothers rest, as he did for you, and they take over the land that God is giving them. After that, go back to your own land, which Moses, God's servant, gave you on the east side of the Jordan River where the sun rises.
Joshua 1:16 They told Joshua, "We will do everything you command, and we will go wherever you send us."
Joshua 1:17 Just like we listened to Moses in everything, we will listen to you too. But may God be with you just as he was with Moses.
Joshua 1:18 Anyone who disobeys your orders and doesn't listen to your words in everything you tell him must be put to death. Just be strong and brave.

Joshua 2:1 Joshua, Nun's son, sent two spies from Shittim, telling them, "Go, look over the land, especially Jericho." So they went and stayed at a prostitute named Rahab's house.
Joshua 2:2 The king of Jericho was told, "Look, men from Israel came here tonight to explore the land."
Joshua 2:3 The king of Jericho sent a message to Rahab, telling her, "Send out the men who came to you and entered your house, because they came to spy on the whole land."
Joshua 2:4 The woman took the two men, hid them, and said, "Some men came to me, but I didn't know where they were from."
Joshua 2:5 At the time when they closed the gate, at dark, the men left. I don't know where they went. Go after them fast, and you will catch up to them.
Joshua 2:6 She took them to the house's roof and hid them under the flax stalks she had spread out there.
Joshua 2:7 The men chased them toward the Jordan River crossings. When the chasers had passed by, they closed the gate.
Joshua 2:8 Before they went to bed, she went up to the roof to meet them.
Joshua 2:9 She told the men, "I know that God has given you the land, and we are all afraid of you, and everyone in the land is shaking in fear because of you."
Joshua 2:10 We heard how God made the Red Sea dry for you as you left Egypt, and what you did to the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you totally destroyed.
Joshua 2:11 As soon as we heard this, we were very afraid and lost all our courage because of you, for your God is the God in heaven above and on the earth below.
Joshua 2:12 So now, please promise me by God that because I was kind to you, you will also be kind to my family, and give me a sign that you will keep your promise.
Joshua 2:13 Please promise you will keep my father, mother, brothers, sisters, and everything they own safe, and save us from death.
Joshua 2:14 The men said to her, "We will protect your life if you keep our plan secret. When God gives us the land, we will treat you well and honestly."
Joshua 2:15 She lowered them with a rope through the window because her house was on the city wall, where she lived.
Joshua 2:16 She told them, "Go to the mountain so the chasers don't find you; hide there for three days until the chasers go back; then you can leave."
Joshua 2:17 The men told her, "We won't be responsible for your promise that you made us swear to."
Joshua 2:18 Look, when we enter the land, you must tie this red cord in the window you used to help us escape. Then you must bring your father, mother, brothers, and all your family to stay with you.
Joshua 2:19 Anyone who leaves your house and goes into the street will be responsible for their own death, and we will not be to blame. But anyone who stays with you in the house, if they are hurt, we will be responsible.
Joshua 2:20 If you tell others about our agreement, we will be free from the promise you made us give.
Joshua 2:21 She said, "Okay, let's do as you said." She let them go, and they left. Then she tied the red cord in the window.
Joshua 2:22 They went to the mountain and stayed there for three days until those chasing them had gone back. The chasers looked for them everywhere on the road but didn't find them.
Joshua 2:23 The two men went back, came down the mountain, crossed over, and met Joshua, Nun's son, and told him everything that happened to them.
Joshua 2:24 They told Joshua, "God has really given us all the land; the people living there are scared of us."

Joshua 3:1 Joshua got up early in the morning; they left Shittim and went to the Jordan River, he and all the Israelites, and stayed there before crossing over.
Joshua 3:2 Three days later, the officers went among the people.
Joshua 3:3 They told the people, "When you see the Ark of God's covenant and the Levite priests carrying it, leave your spot and follow it."
Joshua 3:4 Stay about two thousand cubits away from it; do not go near it, so you can see the path you should take, because you have never traveled this way before.
Joshua 3:5 Joshua told the people, "Make yourselves holy, because tomorrow God will do amazing things among you."
Joshua 3:6 Joshua told the priests, "Carry the covenant chest and walk ahead of the people." So they carried the covenant chest and went in front of the people.
Joshua 3:7 God said to Joshua, "Today I will start to make you great in front of all Israel, so they will know that I will be with you just like I was with Moses."
Joshua 3:8 Tell the priests carrying God's covenant box, when you reach the edge of the Jordan River, to stand still in the water.
Joshua 3:9 Joshua told the people of Israel, "Come here and listen to what God says to you."
Joshua 3:10 Joshua said, "You will know that God is with you because he will surely push out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites from the land before you."
Joshua 3:11 Look, the box of God's promise, belonging to the God of the whole world, is going ahead of you into the Jordan River.
Joshua 3:12 Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.
Joshua 3:13 When the priests carrying God's covenant box step into the Jordan River, the water flowing from upstream will stop and stand up like a wall.
Joshua 3:14 When the people left their tents to cross the Jordan River, with the priests carrying God's covenant chest ahead of them;
Joshua 3:15 As those carrying the ark reached the Jordan River and the priests carrying the ark dipped their feet at the edge of the water (because the Jordan River overflows its banks during harvest season),
Joshua 3:16 The water flowing from above stopped and piled up far from the city Adam, near Zaretan. The water flowing toward the Salt Sea in the plain was stopped and dried up, and the people crossed over facing Jericho.
Joshua 3:17 The priests carrying God's covenant box stood on dry land in the middle of the Jordan River, and all the Israelites walked on dry land until everyone had completely crossed the Jordan.

Joshua 4:1 After everyone had crossed the Jordan River, God spoke to Joshua, saying,
Joshua 4:2 Choose twelve men from the people, one from each tribe.
Joshua 4:3 Tell them, 'Pick up twelve stones from where the priests stood in the Jordan River, carry them with you, and put them down where you stay tonight.'
Joshua 4:4 Then Joshua called the twelve men he had chosen from the Israelites, one from each tribe.
Joshua 4:5 Joshua said to them, "Go ahead of God's ark into the middle of the Jordan River, and each of you pick up a stone on your shoulder, one for each of the tribes of Israel's children."
Joshua 4:6 This will be a sign for you. When your children ask you in the future, "What do these stones mean to you?"
Joshua 4:7 You will tell them, "The waters of Jordan stopped flowing when the Ark of God's covenant crossed the river. The waters stopped, and these stones will always remind the people of Israel of this."
Joshua 4:8 The Israelites did as Joshua ordered and took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan River, as God told Joshua, one for each tribe of Israel. They brought them to where they were staying and put them down there.
Joshua 4:9 Joshua placed twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan River where the priests carrying the covenant box had stood, and the stones remain there to this day.
Joshua 4:10 The priests who carried the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan River until all was done that God had told Joshua to tell the people, just as Moses had instructed Joshua; and the people hurried and crossed over.
Joshua 4:11 When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of God and the priests crossed in front of the people.
Joshua 4:12 The descendants of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh's tribe crossed over ready for battle ahead of the Israelites, just as Moses had instructed them.
Joshua 4:13 About forty thousand ready for war went across to fight in the flat lands of Jericho before God.
Joshua 4:14 On that day, God made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they respected him just as they respected Moses, for his whole life.
Joshua 4:15 God spoke to Joshua, saying,
Joshua 4:16 Tell the priests carrying God's covenant chest to come up from the Jordan River.
Joshua 4:17 Joshua told the priests, "Come up from the Jordan."
Joshua 4:18 When the priests carrying God's covenant ark stepped out of the Jordan River and onto dry ground, the river's waters flowed back to their place and overflowed its banks as before.
Joshua 4:19 The people left the Jordan River on the tenth day of the first month and set up camp in Gilgal, near the eastern edge of Jericho.
Joshua 4:20 Joshua set up those twelve stones in Gilgal that they had taken from the Jordan.
Joshua 4:21 He told the Israelites, "When your children ask their fathers in the future, 'What do these stones mean?'
Joshua 4:22 You should tell your children, "Israel crossed the Jordan River on dry ground."
Joshua 4:23 God dried up the Jordan River for you to cross, just as He did with the Red Sea, letting us pass through.
Joshua 4:24 So that everyone in the world may know that God's power is great and that you should respect God always.

Joshua 5:1 When all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings by the sea learned that God had dried up the Jordan River so the Israelites could cross, their hearts sank, and they lost their courage because of the Israelites.
Joshua 5:2 At that time, God told Joshua, "Make sharp knives and circumcise the Israelites once more."
Joshua 5:3 Joshua made sharp knives and circumcised the Israelites at Foreskin Hill.
Joshua 5:4 Joshua circumcised the people because all the men who had left Egypt, the soldiers, had died in the desert after leaving Egypt.
Joshua 5:5 All the people who had left Egypt were circumcised, but those born in the desert during the journey from Egypt were not circumcised.
Joshua 5:6 The Israelites traveled in the desert for forty years until all the fighting men who left Egypt had died because they did not listen to God. God had promised he would not let them see the land he had told their ancestors he would give to us, a land filled with milk and honey.
Joshua 5:7 Joshua circumcised their children who replaced them because they were not circumcised since it was not done during their journey.
Joshua 5:8 After they circumcised everyone, they stayed in their camp spots until they were healed.
Joshua 5:9 God said to Joshua, "Today I have taken away the shame of Egypt from you. That's why the place is named Gilgal to this day."
Joshua 5:10 The Israelites camped at Gilgal and celebrated Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month in the Jericho plains.
Joshua 5:11 They ate the old grain from the land the day after Passover, unleavened bread, and roasted grain on that very day.
Joshua 5:12 The manna stopped the day after they ate the old grain of the land; the Israelites no longer had manna; instead, they ate the crops from Canaan that year.
Joshua 5:13 When Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a sword in his hand. Joshua approached him and asked, "Are you on our side or the side of our enemies?"
Joshua 5:14 He said, "No, but as the leader of God's army, I have now come." Then Joshua bowed down to the ground, worshiped, and said to him, "What does my Lord want to tell his servant?"
Joshua 5:15 The leader of God's army told Joshua, "Take off your shoe from your foot; because the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did that.

Joshua 6:1 Jericho was tightly closed because of the Israelites: no one could leave or enter.
Joshua 6:2 God said to Joshua, "Look, I have given you the city of Jericho, its king, and its brave warriors."
Joshua 6:3 You will march around the city, all you soldiers, circling the city one time. Do this for six days.
Joshua 6:4 Seven priests will carry seven ram's horn trumpets in front of the ark, and on the seventh day, you will march around the city seven times while the priests blow the trumpets.
Joshua 6:5 When they blow the ram's horn for a long time, and you hear the trumpet, everyone must shout loudly. Then the city wall will collapse, and the people will go straight into the city.
Joshua 6:6 Joshua, Nun's son, told the priests to carry the covenant box and have seven priests walk in front with seven ram's horn trumpets ahead of God's box.
Joshua 6:7 He told the people, "Move on, go around the city, and let the armed men go ahead of the Ark of God."
Joshua 6:8 After Joshua talked to the people, seven priests with seven ram's horn trumpets walked ahead of God and blew their trumpets, and God's covenant box came behind them.
Joshua 6:9 The soldiers walked ahead of the priests with the trumpets, and the guards followed behind the sacred chest, while the priests kept walking and playing the trumpets.
Joshua 6:10 Joshua told the people, "Do not shout or make any noise with your voice, and do not speak until the day I tell you to shout; then you should shout."
Joshua 6:11 So the ark of God went around the city once, then they returned to the camp and stayed there.
Joshua 6:12 Joshua got up early in the morning, and the priests carried the ark of God.
Joshua 6:13 Seven priests with seven trumpets made from ram's horns walked ahead of God's ark. They kept blowing the trumpets. Soldiers marched in front, while the rear guard followed after God's ark, as the priests continued to blow the trumpets.
Joshua 6:14 On the second day, they walked around the city one time and then went back to their camp. They did this for six days.
Joshua 6:15 On the seventh day, they got up at dawn and walked around the city in the same way seven times, but on that day they walked around the city seven times.
Joshua 6:16 On the seventh time, when the priests played the trumpets, Joshua told the people, "Shout, because God has given you the city."
Joshua 6:17 The city will be cursed, everything in it for God, but Rahab the prostitute will survive, her and everyone with her in her home, because she hid the spies we sent.
Joshua 6:18 Be sure to stay away from the cursed things, so you don't become cursed by taking them and bring trouble to the camp of Israel.
Joshua 6:19 All the silver, gold, and items made of brass and iron are holy to God: they must go into God's treasury.
Joshua 6:20 When the priests blew the trumpets, the people yelled. And when the people heard the trumpet and yelled loudly, the wall collapsed. So they all went into the city, straight ahead, and captured it.
Joshua 6:21 They completely destroyed everything in the city, men, women, children, seniors, oxen, sheep, and donkeys, with their swords.
Joshua 6:22 Joshua told the two men who explored the land, "Go to the prostitute's house and take out the woman and everything she owns, just as you promised her."
Joshua 6:23 The young spies went in, took Rahab, her father, mother, brothers, and everything she owned, brought out all her family, and left them outside Israel's camp.
Joshua 6:24 They set the city on fire, burning everything in it, but they saved the silver, gold, and bronze and iron objects to put in God's house treasury.
Joshua 6:25 Joshua kept Rahab the prostitute and her family safe, along with everything she owned; she lives in Israel to this day because she hid the spies Joshua sent to Jericho.
Joshua 6:26 Joshua warned them, saying, "God will curse anyone who rebuilds the city of Jericho. He will lose his oldest son when he lays the foundations, and his youngest son when he sets up the gates."
Joshua 6:27 God was with Joshua, and his reputation spread across the whole land.

Joshua 7:1 The Israelites did wrong with the cursed item, because Achan, son of Carmi, grandson of Zabdi, great-grandson of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took the cursed item, and God became angry with the Israelites.
Joshua 7:2 Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, near Bethaven, east of Bethel, and told them, "Go and look at the land." The men went and saw Ai.
Joshua 7:3 They went back to Joshua and told him, "Don't send all the people. Just send about two or three thousand men to attack Ai. Don't tire everyone out because Ai has only a few people."
Joshua 7:4 About three thousand men from the people went up there, but they ran away from the men of Ai.
Joshua 7:5 The men of Ai killed about 36 of them; they pursued them from the city gate to Shebarim and attacked them on the slopes. The people's courage dissolved completely.
Joshua 7:6 Joshua tore his clothes, fell to the ground on his face in front of God's ark until evening, along with the leaders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads.
Joshua 7:7 And Joshua said, "Oh no, God, why did you bring us across the Jordan River only to let the Amorites defeat us? I wish we had stayed on the other side of the Jordan!"
Joshua 7:8 God, what can I say when Israel runs away from their enemies?
Joshua 7:9 The Canaanites and everyone living in the land will hear about it, surround us, and wipe out our name from the world: what will you do for your great name then, God?
Joshua 7:10 God said to Joshua, "Get up; why are you lying down on your face?"
Joshua 7:11 Israel has sinned, and they have broken the agreement I gave them: they have taken cursed things, stolen, lied, and put these things with their own belongings.
Joshua 7:12 So, the Israelites couldn't face their enemies and ran away because they were cursed. I won't stay with you unless you get rid of the cursed ones among you.
Joshua 7:13 Get up, make the people holy, and say, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow because God says, "Israel has something cursed among them. You cannot defeat your enemies until you remove the cursed thing from you."
Joshua 7:14 In the morning, you will be brought forward by your tribes. The tribe God chooses will come forward by families. The family God chooses will come forward by households. The household God chooses will come forward one person at a time.
Joshua 7:15 Whoever is caught with the cursed item will be burned with fire, along with everything he owns, because he broke God's agreement and did foolish things in Israel.
Joshua 7:16 Joshua got up early in the morning, gathered Israel by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was chosen.
Joshua 7:17 He brought Judah's family forward; he chose the Zarhite family. He presented the Zarhites one by one, and Zabdi was selected.
Joshua 7:18 He brought his family one by one; and Achan, son of Carmi, grandson of Zabdi, great-grandson of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was chosen.
Joshua 7:19 Joshua said to Achan, "My son, honor the God of Israel, confess to Him; and tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me."
Joshua 7:20 Achan replied to Joshua, "I truly sinned against God of Israel, and this is what I have done:"
Joshua 7:21 When I saw a fine Babylonian robe, two hundred pieces of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty pieces among the loot, I wanted them and took them. They are now buried in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.
Joshua 7:22 Joshua sent messengers, and they hurried to the tent; there, hidden in his tent, was the object with the silver underneath.
Joshua 7:23 They removed them from inside the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before God.
Joshua 7:24 Joshua and all Israel with him took Achan, Zerah's son, the silver, the clothes, the gold bar, his sons, his daughters, his oxen, his donkeys, his sheep, his tent, and everything he owned, and they brought them to Achor Valley.
Joshua 7:25 Joshua asked, "Why have you brought us trouble? God will bring trouble on you today." Then all of Israel threw stones at them and burned them after they had thrown stones.
Joshua 7:26 They put a big pile of stones over him, which is still there today. So God stopped being so angry. That's why they named the place the Valley of Trouble, a name it still has today.

Joshua 8:1 God told Joshua, "Don't be afraid or discouraged. Take all your soldiers and go to Ai. I have given you the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land."
Joshua 8:2 Do to Ai and its king what you did to Jericho and its king. But you can keep the goods and animals for yourselves. Set up an ambush behind the city.
Joshua 8:3 Joshua got up, and all the soldiers with him, to attack Ai. Joshua picked thirty thousand strong, brave men and sent them out at night.
Joshua 8:4 He told them, "Look, wait secretly behind the city. Don't go too far from it, but be ready."
Joshua 8:5 I and all the people with me will go near the city. When they come out to fight us like before, we will run away from them.
Joshua 8:6 They will follow us until we lead them away from the city. They will think we are running away like before, so we will run away from them.
Joshua 8:7 Then you'll get up from the ambush and take the city because God will give it to you.
Joshua 8:8 When you capture the city, you must set it on fire. Do this as God has commanded. Look, I have commanded you.
Joshua 8:9 Joshua sent them out, and they went to set up an ambush. They stayed between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. Joshua spent that night with the people.
Joshua 8:10 Joshua got up early in the morning, counted the people, and he and the leaders of Israel went ahead of them to Ai.
Joshua 8:11 All the people, including the soldiers with him, went up, approached, and arrived in front of the city, camping on the north side of Ai, with a valley between them and Ai.
Joshua 8:12 He took around five thousand men and hid them for an ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the city's west side.
Joshua 8:13 When they positioned the people, all the army to the north of the city and the ambush to the west of the city, Joshua went into the middle of the valley that night.
Joshua 8:14 When the king of Ai noticed, they hurried and got up early, and the city's men came out to fight Israel, he and all his people, at the set time, in front of the open area; yet he did not know there were ambushers waiting for him behind the city.
Joshua 8:15 Joshua and all of Israel acted like they were defeated in front of them and ran away through the wilderness.
Joshua 8:16 Everyone in Ai gathered to chase after them, and they followed Joshua, leading them away from the city.
Joshua 8:17 No man remained in Ai or Bethel; all went after Israel, leaving the city unprotected to chase Israel.
Joshua 8:18 God told Joshua, "Reach out with the spear in your hand toward Ai; I will make sure you conquer it." Joshua reached out with the spear he held toward the city.
Joshua 8:19 The attackers quickly came from their spot, and as soon as he signaled, they ran into the city, captured it, and quickly set it on fire.
Joshua 8:20 When the men of Ai turned around, they saw the city's smoke going up to the sky. They could not run away in any direction, and the people who ran to the wilderness now attacked those chasing them.
Joshua 8:21 When Joshua and all of Israel realized that their hidden soldiers had captured the city and smoke was rising from it, they turned back and killed the men of Ai.
Joshua 8:22 The other army came out of the city to fight them, and Israel was on both sides. They defeated them, allowing none to survive or get away.
Joshua 8:23 They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
Joshua 8:24 When Israel finished killing all of Ai's people in the fields and the wilderness where they had chased them, and after all had died by the sword, all the Israelites went back to Ai and destroyed it with the sword.
Joshua 8:25 On that day, twelve thousand men and women died, all from the city of Ai.
Joshua 8:26 Joshua did not lower his hand, which he had raised with the spear, until he had completely destroyed all the people of Ai.
Joshua 8:27 Israel took only the animals and the goods of that city for themselves, as God had commanded Joshua.
Joshua 8:28 Joshua burned Ai, turning it into a permanent pile of ruins, still desolate to this day.
Joshua 8:29 The king of Ai was hung on a tree until evening; when the sun set, Joshua ordered that they take his body off the tree, throw it at the city gate entrance, and pile up many stones over it, which are still there today.
Joshua 8:30 Then Joshua made an altar for God of Israel on Mount Ebal.
Joshua 8:31 Just as Moses, God's servant, instructed the Israelites, as recorded in Moses' law book, they built an altar of uncut stones that no one had used metal tools on. On it, they made burnt offerings and presented peace offerings to God.
Joshua 8:32 He wrote a copy of Moses' law on the stones in front of the people of Israel.
Joshua 8:33 All of Israel, including their leaders, officials, and judges, stood around the ark in front of the Levite priests, who carried God's covenant ark. This included foreigners and natives alike. Half were facing Mount Gerizim and half facing Mount Ebal, just as Moses, God’s servant, had instructed to bless the people of Israel.
Joshua 8:34 Later, he read all the words of the law—both the blessings and the curses—as they are written in the book of the law.
Joshua 8:35 Joshua read every command that Moses had given to all the people of Israel, including the women, children, and foreigners living with them.

Joshua 9:1 When all the kings near the Jordan River, in the hills, valleys, and along the coast of the great sea next to Lebanon, including the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, heard about it;
Joshua 9:2 They came together to fight Joshua and Israel as one.
Joshua 9:3 When the people of Gibeon heard about what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai,
Joshua 9:4 They acted cleverly, pretending to be messengers, putting old bags on their donkeys, and carrying old, torn, and mended wine skins.
Joshua 9:5 They wore old shoes patched up on their feet and old clothes; all their food was dry and moldy.
Joshua 9:6 They went to Joshua at the Gilgal camp and said to him and the Israelites, "We come from a distant land: so now, make an agreement with us."
Joshua 9:7 The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Maybe you live near us; how can we make an agreement with you?"
Joshua 9:8 They told Joshua, "We are your servants." And Joshua asked them, "Who are you and where do you come from?"
Joshua 9:9 They said to him, "We are your servants from a very distant land. We came because of God's name, for we have heard about his great reputation and everything he did in Egypt."
Joshua 9:10 God did many things to the two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan River: to Sihon, the king of Heshbon, and to Og, the king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
Joshua 9:11 Our leaders and everyone from our land told us, 'Bring food for the trip, go to meet them, and say, "We are your servants; so now, please make an agreement with us."'
Joshua 9:12 We brought this bread hot from our homes as food for the journey when we left to meet you; but now, see, it's dry and moldy.
Joshua 9:13 We filled these wine bottles when they were new, but look, they are torn now. Our clothes and shoes have gotten old because of our very long trip.
Joshua 9:14 The men took some of their food and did not seek advice from God.
Joshua 9:15 Joshua made peace with them and agreed to let them live, and the leaders of the people promised them this.
Joshua 9:16 Three days after they made a peace agreement, they found out that those people were their neighbors living nearby.
Joshua 9:17 The Israelites traveled and reached their cities on the third day. Their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kirjathjearim.
Joshua 9:18 The Israelites did not attack them because their leaders had promised them by God of Israel. But all the people complained against the leaders.
Joshua 9:19 All the leaders told the people, "We promised them before God of Israel: so now we cannot harm them."
Joshua 9:20 We will do this to them; we will let them live so that we don't get punished, because of the promise we made to them.
Joshua 9:21 The leaders told them, "Let them live, but they will cut wood and carry water for the whole community, just as the leaders promised them."
Joshua 9:22 Joshua called them and asked, "Why did you trick us into thinking you were far away when you actually live near us?"
Joshua 9:23 So now you are cursed, and you will always be slaves, cutting wood and carrying water for the temple of my God.
Joshua 9:24 They replied to Joshua, "We were definitely told that your God ordered his servant Moses to give you all the land and to wipe out all the land's people in front of you. So, we were very scared for our lives because of you, and that's why we did this."
Joshua 9:25 Now, look, we are in your power: do to us what you think is good and right.
Joshua 9:26 He did the same for them and saved them from the Israelites, so they were not killed.
Joshua 9:27 On that day, Joshua made them wood cutters and water carriers for the community and God's altar, a job they still do where he chooses.

Joshua 10:1 When Adonizedec, the king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and completely destroyed it, just as he did to Jericho and its king, and that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living with them,
Joshua 10:2 They were very afraid because Gibeon was a big city like the king's cities, larger than Ai, and all its men were strong.
Joshua 10:3 So Adonizedec, the king of Jerusalem, sent a message to Hoham, the king of Hebron; Piram, the king of Jarmuth; Japhia, the king of Lachish; and Debir, the king of Eglon, saying,
Joshua 10:4 Come up to me, and help me, so we can defeat Gibeon because it has made peace with Joshua and the people of Israel.
Joshua 10:5 So the five Amorite kings – the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon – united their armies and camped at Gibeon to attack it.
Joshua 10:6 The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal, saying, "Don't stop helping your servants; come to us fast, and save us, and help us, because all the Amorite kings who live in the mountains have joined together against us."
Joshua 10:7 Joshua went up from Gilgal with all the soldiers and brave warriors.
Joshua 10:8 God said to Joshua, "Don't be afraid of them, because I have given them over to you. Not one of them will be able to resist you."
Joshua 10:9 Joshua quickly went to them, traveling from Gilgal all night.
Joshua 10:10 God confused them before Israel, and killed many at Gibeon, and chased them on the road to Bethhoron, and struck them down to Azekah and Makkedah.
Joshua 10:11 As they ran away from Israel, heading toward Bethhoron, God made large stones fall from the sky onto them up to Azekah, and many died. More were killed by the hailstones than by the Israelites' swords.
Joshua 10:12 Then Joshua spoke to God when God gave the Amorites to Israel, and he said where Israel could see, "Sun, stop over Gibeon; and Moon, in the valley of Ajalon."
Joshua 10:13 The sun stopped, and the moon paused, until the people got revenge on their enemies. Isn't this recorded in the Book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the sky and didn't set for about a full day.
Joshua 10:14 There had never been a day like it before or after, when God listened to a human voice, because God fought for Israel.
Joshua 10:15 Joshua went back, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
Joshua 10:16 But these five kings ran away and hid in a cave at Makkedah.
Joshua 10:17 Someone told Joshua, "The five kings are hiding in a cave at Makkedah."
Joshua 10:18 Joshua said, "Put big rocks over the cave entrance and have men guard it."
Joshua 10:19 Do not stop, but chase your enemies and strike those at the back; do not let them go into their cities: for God has given them into your control.
Joshua 10:20 When Joshua and the Israelites finished killing them until they were all dead, the survivors went to fortified cities.
Joshua 10:21 All the people went back to the camp with Joshua at Makkedah safely; no one said anything bad about the Israelites.
Joshua 10:22 Joshua said, "Open the cave and bring those five kings out to me."
Joshua 10:23 They did that and brought out the five kings to him from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.
Joshua 10:24 When they took the kings to Joshua, Joshua told the Israelite men and the captains of the soldiers with him, "Come close, step on these kings' necks." They came close and stepped on their necks.
Joshua 10:25 Joshua told them, "Don't be afraid or discouraged. Be strong and brave. This is how God will treat all your enemies you fight against."
Joshua 10:26 Afterward, Joshua struck them, killed them, and hung them on five trees, where they stayed until evening.
Joshua 10:27 When the sun was setting, Joshua ordered, and they took the bodies down from the trees, threw them into the cave where they had been hidden and put big rocks at the entrance of the cave, which are still there today.
Joshua 10:28 On that day Joshua captured Makkedah, defeated it with the sword, and completely destroyed its king, everyone in it; he left no one alive. He treated the king of Makkedah just like he did the king of Jericho.
Joshua 10:29 Joshua moved on from Makkedah with all Israel to Libnah and fought against it.
Joshua 10:30 God gave the city and its king to Israel; they struck it with the sword, killing everyone there. No one was left alive, just as they did to the king of Jericho.
Joshua 10:31 Joshua moved from Libnah with all of Israel to Lachish, set up camp there, and fought against it.
Joshua 10:32 God gave Lachish to Israel, and on the second day, they captured it, struck it with the sword, and killed everyone inside, just as they had done to Libnah.
Joshua 10:33 Horam, king of Gezer, came to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his people, leaving no survivors.
Joshua 10:34 Joshua moved from Lachish to Eglon with all Israel, and they set up camp there and attacked it.
Joshua 10:35 On that day, they captured it and struck it with the sword's blade, and he completely destroyed everyone in it, just like he had done to Lachish.
Joshua 10:36 Joshua left Eglon with all the Israelites and went to Hebron, where they battled it.
Joshua 10:37 They captured it and struck it with the sword's edge, including its king, all its cities, and everyone inside. None were left alive, just as they had done to Eglon. They completely destroyed it and everyone inside.
Joshua 10:38 Joshua went back and all Israel with him to Debir, and they fought against it.
Joshua 10:39 He took the city, its king, and all its towns. They struck them with the sword and completely destroyed everyone there. He spared no one. Just as he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and also to Libnah and its king.
Joshua 10:40 Joshua defeated the entire area of the hills, the south, the valleys, and the springs, along with all their kings. He didn't leave anyone alive but completely wiped out every living thing, just as God of Israel had commanded.
Joshua 10:41 Joshua defeated them from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza, and all the area of Goshen, up to Gibeon.
Joshua 10:42 Joshua captured all these kings and their lands at once, because God was fighting for Israel.
Joshua 10:43 Joshua went back, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

Joshua 11:1 When Jabin, the king of Hazor, heard what happened, he sent messages to Jobab, the king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph.
Joshua 11:2 To the kings in the north mountains, the southern plains near Chinneroth, the valley, and near Dor to the west,
Joshua 11:3 To the Canaanite in the east and west, the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Jebusite in the mountains, and Hivite near Hermon in Mizpeh.
Joshua 11:4 They left with all their groups, a huge crowd like the sand on the seashore, with many horses and chariots.
Joshua 11:5 When all these kings joined forces, they gathered and set up camp at Merom's waters to battle Israel.
Joshua 11:6 God told Joshua, "Don't be afraid of them. Tomorrow at this time, I will make sure they are all defeated before Israel. You will disable their horses, and burn their chariots."
Joshua 11:7 Joshua and his soldiers surprised them near the waters of Merom and attacked.
Joshua 11:8 God gave them to Israel, who struck them and chased them to Great Zidon, Misrephothmaim, and the Valley of Mizpeh in the east; they attacked them until no one was left.
Joshua 11:9 Joshua did as God commanded: he crippled their horses and burned their chariots.
Joshua 11:10 Joshua then turned back, captured Hazor, and killed its king with a sword; because Hazor used to be the leader of all those kingdoms.
Joshua 11:11 They killed everyone there with their swords, completely destroying them; no one was left alive. And he burned Hazor down.
Joshua 11:12 Joshua captured all the cities of those kings and defeated them with a sword, destroying them completely, just as Moses, God's servant, had commanded.
Joshua 11:13 Israel did not burn any of the strong cities, except for Hazor; only that city did Joshua burn.
Joshua 11:14 The people of Israel took all the valuables and animals from these cities for themselves; but they killed every person with their swords until none were left alive.
Joshua 11:15 God told Moses what to do, Moses told Joshua, and Joshua did everything God had told Moses.
Joshua 11:16 Joshua captured all that land, including the hills, the southern area, the land of Goshen, the valleys, the plains, and Israel's mountains.
Joshua 11:17 From Halak mountain, going up to Seir, all the way to Baalgad in Lebanon valley, below Mount Hermon: He captured all their kings, struck them, and killed them.
Joshua 11:18 Joshua fought with all those kings for a long time.
Joshua 11:19 Every city fought the children of Israel except the Hivites of Gibeon; they captured all others in battle.
Joshua 11:20 God made their hearts stubborn so they would fight against Israel, and he could completely destroy them without mercy, just as God told Moses.
Joshua 11:21 At that time, Joshua came and removed the Anakim people from the mountains, from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and all the mountains of Judah and Israel. Joshua completely destroyed them along with their cities.
Joshua 11:22 No Anakims were left in Israel's land, only some stayed in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua 11:23 Joshua captured all the land as God told Moses; he gave it to Israel as their tribal inheritance. The land had peace from war.

Joshua 12:1 These are the kings of the country that the Israelites defeated and whose land they took over, on the east side of the Jordan River, from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon, and all the eastern plains.
Joshua 12:2 Sihon, the king of the Amorites, lived in Heshbon and controlled the land from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River, including the middle of the river and half of Gilead, all the way to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites' land.
Joshua 12:3 From the plain to Lake Chinneroth in the east, to the Dead Sea in the east and the road to Beth Jeshimoth, and to the south below the slopes of Pisgah.
Joshua 12:4 The territory of Og, the king of Bashan, was one of the last places of the giants, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Joshua 12:5 They ruled over Mount Hermon, Salcah, and all of Bashan up to the territory of the Geshurites and Maachathites, and half of Gilead, which was up to the land of King Sihon of Heshbon.
Joshua 12:6 Moses, God's servant, and the Israelites defeated them. Moses gave the land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh as their own.
Joshua 12:7 Here are the kings of the land that Joshua and the Israelites defeated west of the Jordan River, from Baalgad in the Lebanon Valley up to Mount Halak leading to Seir. Joshua gave this land to the Israelite tribes as their own, divided among them.
Joshua 12:8 In the mountains, valleys, flat lands, springs, deserts, and the south; the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Joshua 12:9 The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, next to Bethel, one;
Joshua 12:10 The king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one.
Joshua 12:11 The king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
Joshua 12:12 The king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one.
Joshua 12:13 The king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one.
Joshua 12:14 The king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one.
Joshua 12:15 The king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one.
Joshua 12:16 The king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one.
Joshua 12:17 The king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one.
Joshua 12:18 The king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one.
Joshua 12:19 One king of Madon, one king of Hazor.
Joshua 12:20 The king of Shimronmeron, one; the king of Achshaph, one.
Joshua 12:21 The king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one.
Joshua 12:22 The king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
Joshua 12:23 The king of Dor by the sea, one; the king of the peoples at Gilgal, one;
Joshua 12:24 The king of Tirzah, one: a total of thirty-one kings.

Joshua 13:1 Joshua was old with many years; and God said to him, "You are old with many years, and there is still a lot of land to take over."
Joshua 13:2 This is the land that still remains: all the territory of the Philistines, and all of Geshur.
Joshua 13:3 From the River of Egypt to the northern boundary of Ekron, land that is considered Canaanite territory, there are five Philistine rulers: those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron; and also the people of Avvim.
Joshua 13:4 From the south, including all Canaanite territory, and Mearah near the Sidonians, up to Aphek, to the Amorite border:
Joshua 13:5 The land of the Giblites and all of Lebanon, toward the sunrise, from Baalgad at the base of Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
Joshua 13:6 I will make all the people living in the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephothmaim, including the Sidonians, leave the land so that the Israelites can have it. You should divide this land among the Israelites by drawing lots, just as I told you.
Joshua 13:7 Now split this land to give as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Joshua 13:8 The Reubenites and the Gadites got their land on the east side of the Jordan River, which Moses had given them, just as Moses, God's servant, had done.
Joshua 13:9 From Aroer, by the Arnon river bank, the city in the river center, and all the flat land from Medeba to Dibon.
Joshua 13:10 All the cities ruled by Sihon, the king of the Amorites in Heshbon, up to the territory of the Ammonites.
Joshua 13:11 Gilead, the land of the Geshurites and Maachathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan up to Salcah;
Joshua 13:12 Moses defeated Og's whole kingdom in Bashan, which included Ashtaroth and Edrei, where the last of the giants lived, and he drove them out.
Joshua 13:13 But the Israelites did not force out the Geshurites or the Maachathites. So, the Geshurites and the Maachathites live among the Israelites to this day.
Joshua 13:14 God did not give the Levi tribe any land; instead, their inheritance is to receive the burnt sacrifices made to God, just as He promised them.
Joshua 13:15 Moses gave the Reuben tribe their land based on their family groups.
Joshua 13:16 Their land started at Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River, including the city in the middle of the river valley, and all the flat land near Medeba.
Joshua 13:17 Heshbon and all its towns in the flat area; Dibon, Bamoth Baal, and Beth Baal Meon.
Joshua 13:18 And Jahaza, Kedemoth, and Mephaath,
Joshua 13:19 Kirjathaim, Sibmah, and Zarethshahar in the mountain valley,
Joshua 13:20 Bethpeor, Ashdothpisgah, and Bethjeshimoth,
Joshua 13:21 All the cities in the flat land and the entire territory of King Sihon of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon and was defeated by Moses along with Midian's leaders—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, who were rulers under King Sihon and lived in the area.
Joshua 13:22 The Israelites also killed Balaam, Beor's son, who was a fortune-teller, with the sword along with the others they had killed.
Joshua 13:23 The territory of Reuben's descendants was along the Jordan River. This land was their inheritance, including its towns and villages.
Joshua 13:24 Moses gave land to the Gad tribe, to the Gad families.
Joshua 13:25 Their border included Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half of Ammon's land, reaching to Aroer near Rabbah.
Joshua 13:26 From Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the edge of Debir.
Joshua 13:27 In the valley there were Betharam, Bethnimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, which were part of King Sihon of Heshbon's realm. This included the land by the Jordan River, up to the shore of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east side of the Jordan.
Joshua 13:28 This is what the children of Gad received as their families' inheritance: the cities and their villages.
Joshua 13:29 Moses gave land to half of the Manasseh tribe, and this land was owned by the families of that half-tribe.
Joshua 13:30 Their border extended from Mahanaim, including all of Bashan, the entire realm of Og, king of Bashan, and all of Jair's settlements in Bashan, sixty cities.
Joshua 13:31 Half of Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, cities of King Og in Bashan, belonged to the descendants of Machir, son of Manasseh, for one group of Machir's family.
Joshua 13:32 These are the lands that Moses gave out as inheritance in the Moab plains, across the Jordan River, near Jericho to the east.
Joshua 13:33 Moses did not give any land to the tribe of Levi; God was their inheritance, just as he promised them.

Joshua 14:1 These are the lands the Israelite people received in Canaan, which the priest Eleazar, Joshua son of Nun, and the tribe leaders gave to them as their share.
Joshua 14:2 Their land was given to them by drawing lots, as God had ordered through Moses, for the nine and a half tribes.
Joshua 14:3 Moses had given land to two and a half tribes on the other side of the Jordan River, but he did not give any land to the Levites among them.
Joshua 14:4 Joseph's children formed two groups, Manasseh and Ephraim; so they did not give the Levites a share of the land, only towns to live in, along with nearby lands for their animals and belongings.
Joshua 14:5 As God told Moses, the Israelites did, and they split the land.
Joshua 14:6 The people of Judah went to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb, the son of Jephunneh from the Kenaz tribe, said to him, "You know what God told Moses about you and me at Kadesh Barnea."
Joshua 14:7 I was forty years old when Moses, God's servant, sent me from Kadeshbarnea to explore the land, and I reported back to him exactly what I felt.
Joshua 14:8 However, my companions who went with me caused the people to lose courage, but I fully followed God.
Joshua 14:9 And Moses promised on that day, saying, The land where you walked will be your possession and your children's forever, because you have fully followed God.
Joshua 14:10 And now, look, God has kept me alive, just as he promised, for forty-five years since God told Moses this when the Israelites were moving through the desert: and today, I am eighty-five years old.
Joshua 14:11 I am still as strong today as I was when Moses sent me out; my strength for battle, to advance and retreat, is unchanged.
Joshua 14:12 Now give me this mountain, which God talked about before; you heard how the giants lived there and the cities were big and strong. If God is with me, I will push them out, just as God promised.
Joshua 14:13 Joshua blessed Caleb, son of Jephunneh, and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.
Joshua 14:14 Hebron became Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenezite's land because he always followed God of Israel.
Joshua 14:15 Before, Hebron was called Kirjatharba, named after Arba, a great leader of the Anakims. And the land had peace from war.

Joshua 15:1 This was the tribe of Judah's family land; it reached to Edom's border and Zin desert in the south, which was the farthest part of the southern border.
Joshua 15:2 Their southern boundary started at the edge of the Salt Sea, stretching towards the south.
Joshua 15:3 It went to the south toward Maalehacrabbim, then to Zin, and up the south to Kadeshbarnea, moved on to Hezron, up to Adar, and turned toward Karkaa.
Joshua 15:4 From there it went to Azmon, and ended at the river of Egypt; the southern boundary ended at the sea.
Joshua 15:5 The eastern border reached the Salt Sea, up to the end of the Jordan River. And the northern border started at the sea inlet, at the far end of the Jordan.
Joshua 15:6 The border rose to Bethhogla, went north of Betharabah, and rose again to the stone of Bohan, Reuben's son.
Joshua 15:7 The border went up to Debir from Achor Valley, then north, facing Gilgal, near the ascent to Adummim, on the river's south side. The border reached Enshemesh's waters and ended at Enrogel.
Joshua 15:8 The boundary went up through Hinnom Valley to the southern area of the Jebusite city, which is Jerusalem. Then it went up to the mountain peak facing Hinnom Valley to the west, at the end of the Rephaim Valley to the north.
Joshua 15:9 The border went from the hilltop to Nephtoah's water spring, then to the towns of Mount Ephron, and reached Baalah, known as Kirjathjearim.
Joshua 15:10 The border went from Baalah west to Mount Seir, then ran by the side of Mount Jearim, or Chesalon, to the north, continued down to Bethshemesh, and stretched toward Timnah.
Joshua 15:11 The boundary extended to the north side of Ekron, then it went to Shicron, passed by Mount Baalah, and reached Jabneel. The boundary ended at the sea.
Joshua 15:12 The western border reached the big sea and its shoreline. This is the surrounding boundary for the families of Judah's descendants.
Joshua 15:13 God gave Caleb, Jephunneh's son, a place among Judah's people as God told Joshua, including Hebron, the city of Arba, Anak's father.
Joshua 15:14 Caleb forced out the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
Joshua 15:15 He went from there to the people of Debir, which used to be called Kirjathsepher.
Joshua 15:16 Caleb said, Whoever defeats Kirjathsepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife.
Joshua 15:17 Othniel, Kenaz's son and Caleb's brother, captured the city, so he was given Achsah, his daughter, as his wife.
Joshua 15:18 As she came to him, she persuaded him to ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey, and Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
Joshua 15:19 She replied, "Please give me a special gift; you have given me land in the south; now also give me water springs." So he gave her the upper and lower springs.
Joshua 15:20 This is what the family of the tribe of Judah's descendants will inherit.
Joshua 15:21 The farthest towns of Judah's tribe near Edom's southern border were Kabzeel, Eder, and Jagur.
Joshua 15:22 And Kinah, Dimonah, and Adadah,
Joshua 15:23 Kedesh, Hazor, and Ithnan.
Joshua 15:24 Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Joshua 15:25 Hazor, Hadattah, Kerioth, and Hezron, which is also called Hazor,
Joshua 15:26 Amam, Shema, and Moladah.
Joshua 15:27 And Hazargaddah, Heshmon, and Bethpalet,
Joshua 15:28 And Hazarshual, Beersheba, and Bizjothjah,
Joshua 15:29 Baalah, Iim, and Azem.
Joshua 15:30 Eltolad, Chesil, and Hormah,
Joshua 15:31 Ziklag, Madmannah, and Sansannah.
Joshua 15:32 Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon: there are 29 cities in total with their villages.
Joshua 15:33 In the valley were Eshtaol, Zoreah, and Ashnah.
Joshua 15:34 Zanoah, Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam,
Joshua 15:35 Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah,
Joshua 15:36 Sharaim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen cities and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 15:37 Zenan, Hadashah, and Migdalgad,
Joshua 15:38 And Dilean, Mizpeh, and Joktheel,
Joshua 15:39 Lachish, Bozkath, and Eglon.
Joshua 15:40 And Cabbon, Lahmam, and Kithlish,
Joshua 15:41 Gederoth, Bethdagon, Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with their surrounding villages.
Joshua 15:42 Libnah, Ether, and Ashan.
Joshua 15:43 Jiphtah, Ashnah, and Nezib,
Joshua 15:44 Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah, along with their surrounding villages, make nine cities.
Joshua 15:45 Ekron, with its towns and villages:
Joshua 15:46 From Ekron to the sea, all the area near Ashdod along with its villages.
Joshua 15:47 Ashdod with its towns and villages, Gaza with its towns and villages, to the River of Egypt, and the great sea and its border.
Joshua 15:48 In the mountains were Shamir, Jattir, and Socoh.
Joshua 15:49 And Dannah, and the city of Dannah, which is Debir,
Joshua 15:50 Anab, Eshtemoh, and Anim,
Joshua 15:51 Goshen, Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 15:52 Arab, Dumah, and Eshan.
Joshua 15:53 And Janum, Beth-tappuah, and Aphekah,
Joshua 15:54 Humtah, Kirjatharba or Hebron, and Zior; nine cities and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 15:55 Maon, Carmel, Ziph, and Juttah
Joshua 15:56 And Jezreel, Jokdeam, and Zanoah,
Joshua 15:57 Cain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with their areas.
Joshua 15:58 Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor.
Joshua 15:59 And Maarath, Bethanoth, and Eltekon; six towns with their surrounding areas.
Joshua 15:60 Kirjathbaal, also known as Kirjathjearim, and Rabbah; two cities with their surrounding small towns.
Joshua 15:61 In the desert, Betharabah, Middin, and Secacah,
Joshua 15:62 Nibshan, Salt City, Engedi; six cities and their villages.
Joshua 15:63 The people of Judah couldn't make the Jebusites, who lived in Jerusalem, leave; so the Jebusites live with the people of Judah in Jerusalem until now.

Joshua 16:1 Joseph's descendants received land extending from the Jordan at Jericho to the eastern waters of Jericho, reaching to the desert and then to Bethel hill.
Joshua 16:2 It goes from Bethel to Luz, and goes through to the edge of Archi to Ataroth.
Joshua 16:3 It goes down west to Japhleti's border, to Bethhoron the lower border, and to Gezer; its western end is at the sea.
Joshua 16:4 Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their share of the land.
Joshua 16:5 The territory for the families of Ephraim's descendants was this: their land on the east reached from Atarothaddar to Upper Bethhoron.
Joshua 16:6 The border extended toward the sea to Michmethah on the north; it turned east to Taanathshiloh, going past it to Janohah on the east.
Joshua 16:7 It went from Janohah to Ataroth and Naarath, reached Jericho, and ended at the Jordan River.
Joshua 16:8 The boundary started at Tappuah, went west to the Kanah River, and ended at the sea. This was the land for the families of Ephraim's tribe.
Joshua 16:9 The towns set aside for the Ephraim tribe were within the land given to the Manasseh tribe, including all those towns and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 16:10 They did not force the Canaanites who lived in Gezer to leave, but the Canaanites still live among the people of Ephraim today, and they have to pay taxes.

Joshua 17:1 The tribe of Manasseh also received land because Manasseh was Joseph's oldest son. This included land for Machir, Manasseh's oldest son and Gilead's father, who was a warrior, so he got Gilead and Bashan.
Joshua 17:2 There was also a portion for the other descendants of Manasseh according to their families; for the descendants of Abiezer, the descendants of Helek, the descendants of Asriel, the descendants of Shechem, the descendants of Hepher, and the descendants of Shemida: these were the sons of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, grouped by their families.
Joshua 17:3 Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, did not have sons, only daughters. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
Joshua 17:4 They approached Priest Eleazar, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, and said, "God told Moses to grant us land with our brothers." So, following God's order, they received land among their father's brothers.
Joshua 17:5 Manasseh got ten parts of land, not counting Gilead and Bashan, which are across the Jordan River.
Joshua 17:6 The daughters of Manasseh also received a share of the inheritance along with his sons, and the other sons of Manasseh got the land of Gilead.
Joshua 17:7 Manasseh's territory stretched from Asher to Michmethah near Shechem; the boundary continued to the right towards Entappuah's people.
Joshua 17:8 Manasseh owned the land of Tappuah, but the town of Tappuah, on Manasseh's border, belonged to the descendants of Ephraim.
Joshua 17:9 The border went down to the Kanah River, south of the river; these towns of Ephraim are among Manasseh's towns: Manasseh's border was also on the north side of the river, and it ended at the sea.
Joshua 17:10 To the south belonged to Ephraim, to the north belonged to Manasseh, the sea marked their border; they touched Asher to the north and Issachar to the east.
Joshua 17:11 Manasseh had Bethshean and its villages in Issachar and Asher, Ibleam and its villages, the people of Dor and their villages, the people of Endor and their villages, the people of Taanach and their villages, and the people of Megiddo and their villages—three districts in total.
Joshua 17:12 The children of Manasseh could not make the people of those cities leave; the Canaanites insisted on living in that land.
Joshua 17:13 When the Israelites grew strong, they made the Canaanites pay taxes but did not completely force them out.
Joshua 17:14 The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why have you given me only one piece of land when I am a large group, since God has blessed me so far?"
Joshua 17:15 Joshua replied, "If you are a large group, go to the forested area and clear land for yourselves in the territory of the Perizzites and the giants, if the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you."
Joshua 17:16 Joseph's descendants said, "The hill isn't enough for us; even the Canaanites living in the valley have strong iron chariots, in both Bethshean with its villages and the Jezreel Valley."
Joshua 17:17 Joshua said to Joseph's family, including Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a large group with strong power; you will have more than one piece of land."
Joshua 17:18 The mountain will be yours because it is covered with trees, and you can cut them down. You will own everything that comes from it after you drive out the Canaanites, even if they have iron chariots and are strong.

Joshua 18:1 The whole group of Israel's people gathered at Shiloh and put the meeting tent there. The land was brought under their control.
Joshua 18:2 Seven tribes of Israel's children still hadn't gotten their land.
Joshua 18:3 Joshua asked the Israelites, "How long will you delay before going to take over the land that God has given you?"
Joshua 18:4 Choose three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They will travel through the land, map it according to each tribe's share, and then return to me.
Joshua 18:5 They will split it into seven parts: Judah will stay within their southern territory, and Joseph's family will stay within their northern territories.
Joshua 18:6 Divide the land into seven parts and bring the map to me. Here, I will draw lots for you before God.
Joshua 18:7 The Levites don't share land with you because serving God is their inheritance. But Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh got their land across the Jordan River to the east, that Moses, God's servant, gave them.
Joshua 18:8 The men got up and left. Joshua told those who were to map out the land to go, travel through the land, map it out, and return to him so he could draw lots for them in the presence of God at Shiloh.
Joshua 18:9 The men traveled through the region, divided it into seven parts by cities for a record, and returned to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
Joshua 18:10 Joshua threw lots for them in Shiloh before God, and there Joshua divided the land among the Israelites according to their groups.
Joshua 18:11 The land for the tribe of Benjamin's descendants was divided according to their families. Their land was located between the territories of the descendants of Judah and Joseph.
Joshua 18:12 Their northern border started at the Jordan River, went north to Jericho, climbed through the western mountains, and ended in the Bethaven desert.
Joshua 18:13 The boundary line went from there toward Luz, to Luz's edge, also known as Bethel, to the south; and the line went down to Atarothadar, close to the hill on the southern side of lower Bethhoron.
Joshua 18:14 The boundary line went from there, circling around the southern corner of the sea, from the hill facing Bethhoron to the south; it ended at Kirjathbaal, also called Kirjathjearim, a city belonging to the tribe of Judah: this was the western side.
Joshua 18:15 The southern side started from the edge of Kirjathjearim, went west, and reached the spring of water at Nephtoah.
Joshua 18:16 The border went down to the end of the mountain near the Valley of Hinnom, which is by the Valley of the Giants to the north. It went down to Hinnom Valley, by the south side of Jebusi, and went down to Enrogel.
Joshua 18:17 It came from the north to Enshemesh, then on to Geliloth, across from the climb to Adummim, and went down to Bohan son of Reuben's stone.
Joshua 18:18 It moved along the side across from Arabah to the north and went down to Arabah.
Joshua 18:19 The border went by the side of Bethhoglah to the north, and the border ended at the north shore of the Dead Sea at the southern tip of the Jordan River; this was the southern boundary.
Joshua 18:20 The Jordan River was its eastern border. This was the land given to the families of Benjamin's descendants, surrounding it completely.
Joshua 18:21 The towns for the tribe of Benjamin's descendants, grouped by families, were Jericho, Bethhoglah, and the Keziz valley.
Joshua 18:22 And Betharabah, and Zemaraim, and Bethel,
Joshua 18:23 And Avim, Pharah, and Ophrah,
Joshua 18:24 Chepharhaammonai, Ophni, and Gaba; twelve towns with their surrounding areas.
Joshua 18:25 Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth,
Joshua 18:26 And Mizpeh, Chephirah, and Mozah,
Joshua 18:27 Rekem, Irpeel, and Taralah,
Joshua 18:28 Zelah, Eleph, Jebusi (which is Jerusalem), Gibeath, and Kirjath are fourteen cities with their villages. This land is what the families of Benjamin's descendants received as their share.

Joshua 19:1 The second choice was for the tribe of Simeon's descendants, according to their families. Their land was inside the land given to Judah's descendants.
Joshua 19:2 They received Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah as their inheritance.
Joshua 19:3 And Hazarshual, Balah, and Azem.
Joshua 19:4 Eltolad, Bethul, and Hormah,
Joshua 19:5 Ziklag, Bethmarcaboth, and Hazarsusah,
Joshua 19:6 Bethlebaoth and Sharuhen; thirteen cities with their villages.
Joshua 19:7 Ain, Remmon, Ether, and Ashan; four cities with their surrounding villages.
Joshua 19:8 All the small towns near these cities, as far as Baalathbeer and Ramath in the south, were part of the land given to the Simeon tribe's families.
Joshua 19:9 The tribe of Simeon received their land from the allotment of the tribe of Judah because Judah's portion was too large for them, so Simeon's inheritance was within Judah's land.
Joshua 19:10 The third share was for the families of Zebulun, and their territory reached to Sarid.
Joshua 19:11 Their boundary went up to the sea, through Maralah, to Dabbasheth, and to the river near Jokneam.
Joshua 19:12 It turned from Sarid to the east, towards the sunrise, to the edge of Chislothtabor, then continued to Daberath, and went up to Japhia.
Joshua 19:13 It moves on from there to the east toward Gittahhepher, to Ittahkazin, then turns toward Remmonmethoar until it reaches Neah.
Joshua 19:14 The border goes around it on the north side to Hannathon, and ends in the Jiphthahel Valley.
Joshua 19:15 Kattath, Nahallal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages.
Joshua 19:16 This is what the families of Zebulun's children will receive as their inheritance: these cities and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 19:17 The fourth draw was for Issachar, for the families of Issachar's children.
Joshua 19:18 Their boundary went towards Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shunem.
Joshua 19:19 And Haphraim, Shihon, and Anaharath.
Joshua 19:20 And Rabbith, Kishion, and Abez,
Joshua 19:21 And Remeth, Engannim, Enhaddah, and Bethpazzez;
Joshua 19:22 The border touches Tabor, Shahazimah, and Bethshemesh, ending at the Jordan River: sixteen cities and their villages.
Joshua 19:23 This is what the family groups of the tribe of Issachar receive as their inheritance: the towns and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 19:24 The fifth share was for the Asher tribe family groups.
Joshua 19:25 Their boundary included Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph.
Joshua 19:26 Alammelech, Amad, and Misheal; the land goes up to Carmel in the west and to Shihorlibnath.
Joshua 19:27 It turns toward the sunrise at Bethdagon, goes to Zebulun, to the Jiphthahel Valley north of Bethemek and Neiel, and ends at Cabul on the left.
Joshua 19:28 Hebron, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, all the way to great Zidon;
Joshua 19:29 Then the border turns to Ramah and the fortified city of Tyre; the border turns to Hosah, ending at the sea from the border to Achzib.
Joshua 19:30 Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob too: twenty-two cities and their villages.
Joshua 19:31 This is what the Asher tribe's families will receive: These towns and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 19:32 The sixth share was given to the Naphtali people, each family group among them.
Joshua 19:33 Their land extended from Heleph and Allon to Zaanannim, including Adami, Nekeb, and Jabneel, to Lakum, and ended at the Jordan River.
Joshua 19:34 Then the border turns west to Aznothtabor, goes from there to Hukkok, touches Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan River to the east.
Joshua 19:35 The protected cities are Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth.
Joshua 19:36 Adamah, Ramah, and Hazor,
Joshua 19:37 Kedesh, Edrei, and Enhazor,
Joshua 19:38 Iron, Migdalel, Horem, Bethanath, and Bethshemesh; nineteen cities with their villages.
Joshua 19:39 This is what the Naphtali tribe's families will receive as their inheritance: the towns and their surrounding villages.
Joshua 19:40 The seventh share was picked for the Dan tribe families.
Joshua 19:41 Their land included Zorah, Eshtaol, and Irshemesh.
Joshua 19:42 And Shaalabbin, and Ajalon, and Jethlah,
Joshua 19:43 Elon, Thimnathah, and Ekron,
Joshua 19:44 Eltekeh, Gibbethon, and Baalath,
Joshua 19:45 Jehud, Beneberak, and Gathrimmon,
Joshua 19:46 And Mejarkon, and Rakkon, along with the territory facing Japho.
Joshua 19:47 The land for Dan's descendants was too small, so they fought against Leshem, captured it, killed its people, took it over, lived there, and renamed Leshem as Dan after their ancestor Dan.
Joshua 19:48 This is what the Dan tribe's families inherited: these cities and their villages.
Joshua 19:49 After they finished dividing the land for inheritance by their regions, the people of Israel gave a share to Joshua, the son of Nun.
Joshua 19:50 Following God's instructions, they gave him the city he requested, Timnathserah in the hills of Ephraim. He then rebuilt the city and lived there.
Joshua 19:51 These are the lands Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the tribal leaders of Israel's children divided as inheritances by drawing lots in Shiloh before God, at the entrance of the meeting tent. This is how they finished dividing the land.

Joshua 20:1 God also spoke to Joshua, saying,
Joshua 20:2 Tell the people of Israel to choose cities of refuge as I instructed you through Moses.
Joshua 20:3 The person who accidentally kills someone without meaning to can run there for safety, and it will protect you from the person seeking revenge for the blood shed.
Joshua 20:4 When someone runs to one of those cities, he should stand at the city gate entrance and explain his situation to the city elders. They will let him into the city and give him a place to live with them.
Joshua 20:5 If someone seeking revenge chases the killer, they should not hand over the killer to them, because he accidentally killed his neighbor without previous hatred.
Joshua 20:6 He will live in that city until he goes before the people for a decision, and until the high priest dies at that time. Then the person who killed someone can go back to his own city and house, the city he ran from.
Joshua 20:7 They chose Kedesh in Galilee in the Naphtali hills, Shechem in the Ephraim hills, and Kirjatharba, known as Hebron, in the Judah hills.
Joshua 20:8 On the other side of the Jordan by Jericho to the east, they gave Bezer in the desert on the plain to the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead to the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan to the tribe of Manasseh.
Joshua 20:9 These cities were set for all Israelites and any foreigner staying with them so anyone who accidentally killed someone could go there and not be killed by the person seeking revenge until they faced the community.

Joshua 21:1 The leaders of the Levite families approached Priest Eleazar, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the other Israelite families.
Joshua 21:2 They talked to them at Shiloh in Canaan, saying, "God told us through Moses to give us cities to live in, with the surrounding land for our animals."
Joshua 21:3 The Israelites gave the Levites these cities and the land around them from their own land, as God had commanded.
Joshua 21:4 The Kohathite families got their land by casting lots. Aaron's descendants, who were Levites, received thirteen cities from the territories of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
Joshua 21:5 The remaining descendants of Kohath received ten cities by drawing lots from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Joshua 21:6 Gershon's descendants received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and from half of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
Joshua 21:7 The Merari family members received twelve cities from the Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun tribes.
Joshua 21:8 The people of Israel gave cities and surrounding land to the Levites by drawing lots, just as God ordered through Moses.
Joshua 21:9 They gave cities from the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Simeon, which are listed by name here.
Joshua 21:10 Aaron's descendants from the Kohathite clan, who were part of the Levi tribe, received this because they got the first share.
Joshua 21:11 They gave them the city of Arba, Anak's father's city, called Hebron, in Judah's hill country, and the surrounding suburbs.
Joshua 21:12 They gave the land around the city and its villages to Caleb, Jephunneh's son, for him to own.
Joshua 21:13 They gave Aaron's descendants Hebron, a safe city for someone who accidentally killed a person, and the area around it, plus Libnah and its surrounding area.
Joshua 21:14 Jattir and the surrounding area, Eshtemoa and the surrounding area,
Joshua 21:15 And Holon with the land around it, and Debir with the land around it,
Joshua 21:16 And Ain and its surrounding area, Juttah and its surrounding area, and Bethshemesh and its surrounding area; nine cities from those two tribes.
Joshua 21:17 From Benjamin's tribe, the towns Gibeon and Geba with their surrounding areas.
Joshua 21:18 Anathoth and its surrounding area, and Almon and its surrounding area; four cities.
Joshua 21:19 Aaron's descendants, who were priests, had thirteen cities with the land around them.
Joshua 21:20 The Kohathite families, the remaining Levites descended from Kohath, received towns as their share from the tribe of Ephraim.
Joshua 21:21 They gave them Shechem with its surrounding land in the hill country of Ephraim, to be a city of refuge for those who killed someone by accident, and Gezer with its surrounding land.
Joshua 21:22 Kibzaim and its surrounding area, and Bethhoron and its surrounding area; four cities.
Joshua 21:23 From Dan's tribe, Eltekeh and its surrounding lands, Gibbethon and its surrounding lands,
Joshua 21:24 Aijalon and its surrounding land, Gathrimmon and its surrounding land; four cities.
Joshua 21:25 From the half tribe of Manasseh came the towns of Tanach and Gathrimmon, along with the land around them; in total, two towns.
Joshua 21:26 There were ten cities with their surrounding lands for the remaining families of Kohath's children.
Joshua 21:27 They gave the Gershonite Levites from the half-tribe of Manasseh the city of Golan in Bashan and its surrounding lands to be a safe place for those who killed someone by accident; they also gave them Beeshterah and its surrounding lands—two cities in total.
Joshua 21:28 From the tribe of Issachar, Kishon and its surrounding lands, Dabareh and its surrounding lands.
Joshua 21:29 Jarmuth with its surrounding lands, Engannim with its surrounding lands; four cities.
Joshua 21:30 From the Asher tribe, the town of Mishal and the land around it, and the town of Abdon and the land around it.
Joshua 21:31 Helkath and its surrounding lands, and Rehob and its surrounding lands; four cities.
Joshua 21:32 From the Naphtali tribe, the city of Kedesh in Galilee and the surrounding area serve as a safe city for someone who killed another; also, the towns of Hammothdor and Kartan and their surrounding areas; three cities in total.
Joshua 21:33 The Gershonite family groups had thirteen cities with the land around them.
Joshua 21:34 To Merari's descendants, the other Levite families, from Zebulun's tribe, they gave Jokneam and its surrounding land, also Kartah and its surrounding land.
Joshua 21:35 Dimnah and its nearby lands, Nahalal and its nearby lands; four cities.
Joshua 21:36 From the tribe of Reuben, the towns Bezer and Jahazah and the areas around them,
Joshua 21:37 Kedemoth and the land around it, and Mephaath and the land around it; four cities.
Joshua 21:38 From the Gad tribe, the city Ramoth in Gilead and its surrounding land became a safe city for someone who killed another person by accident; and likewise, the city Mahanaim and its surrounding land.
Joshua 21:39 Heshbon and its surrounding lands, Jazer and its surrounding lands; in total, four cities.
Joshua 21:40 All the cities given to Merari's descendants by their families, which were left from the Levite families, totaled twelve cities as their share.
Joshua 21:41 The Levites had 48 towns within Israel's lands, each with surrounding land.
Joshua 21:42 Each of these cities had surrounding areas: that's how all these cities were.
Joshua 21:43 God gave Israel all the land he promised to their ancestors; they took it over and lived there.
Joshua 21:44 God gave them peace on all sides, just as he promised their ancestors. None of their enemies could stand against them; God gave them victory over all their enemies.
Joshua 21:45 Nothing good that God promised to the people of Israel failed; everything happened.

Joshua 22:1 Then Joshua called the people of Reuben, Gad, and the half group from Manasseh,
Joshua 22:2 He told them, "You have followed all that Moses, God's servant, ordered you to do, and you have listened to me in everything I commanded you."
Joshua 22:3 You have not left your relatives all this time until today, but have followed the orders of God's commandment.
Joshua 22:4 Now God has given your brothers peace, just as he promised. So go back to your tents and to your own land that Moses, God's servant, gave you across the Jordan River.
Joshua 22:5 Be careful to follow the command and laws that Moses, God's servant, gave you: love God, walk in all His paths, keep His commands, stay close to Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul.
Joshua 22:6 Joshua blessed them and sent them off, and they went to their tents.
Joshua 22:7 Moses had given one half of the Manasseh tribe land in Bashan. Joshua gave the other half land among their relatives west of the Jordan River. When Joshua sent them to their homes, he blessed them.
Joshua 22:8 He told them, "Go back to your homes with lots of wealth, and lots of cows, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and many clothes: share what you took from your enemies with your brothers."
Joshua 22:9 The families from Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh left their kin from Israel in Shiloh, in Canaan, to return to Gilead, the land given to them as God promised through Moses.
Joshua 22:10 When they reached the Jordan River borders in Canaan, the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built a big altar there by the Jordan.
