Joshua 22:11 The Israelites heard, "Look, the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar near Canaan's land by the Jordan River where the Israelites cross."
Joshua 22:12 When the Israelites heard about it, they all met at Shiloh to prepare for battle against them.
Joshua 22:13 The Israelites sent Phinehas, son of Priest Eleazar, to the people of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead.
Joshua 22:14 With him were ten leaders, one leader from each important family of all Israel's tribes; and each was in charge of their family among the many in Israel.
Joshua 22:15 They went to the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and talked to them, saying,
Joshua 22:16 The whole group of God's people says, "What wrong have you done against the God of Israel by building an altar for yourselves today? Are you turning away from God and rebelling against him?"
Joshua 22:17 Wasn't the sin at Peor enough for us, which we haven't been cleansed from to this day, even though there was a plague among God's people?
Joshua 22:18 But do you have to stop following God today? If you go against God today, He will be angry with all of Israel tomorrow.
Joshua 22:19 If your land is not clean, then go to the land that belongs to God, where God's tent stands, and settle with us. But do not go against God, or us, by making your own altar to compete with God's altar.
Joshua 22:20 Didn't Achan, Zerah's son, do wrong with the cursed item, and all the people of Israel faced anger? And he didn't die alone for his sin.
Joshua 22:21 The children of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh replied to Israel's leaders.
Joshua 22:22 The God of all gods knows, and Israel will come to know; if we are rebelling, or if we are sinning against God, (do not save us today,)
Joshua 22:23 We built an altar not to stop following God, or to burn sacrifices or give grain offerings on it, or to make peace offerings there. If that's wrong, let God deal with it.
Joshua 22:24 If we didn't do it because we were afraid, thinking, 'Later, your kids might tell our kids, "What do you have to do with the God of Israel?"'
Joshua 22:25 God has made the Jordan River a border between us and you, Reuben's and Gad's children; you are not part of God, so your children will cause our children to stop respecting God.
Joshua 22:26 So we decided to make an altar, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices.
Joshua 22:27 Let this be a sign between us, you, and our future generations, so we can serve God in his presence with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings; so your children won't tell our children in the future, "You have no part in God."
Joshua 22:28 We said it would happen, that when later generations or we are asked, we can reply, 'Look at the model of God's altar, built by our ancestors not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a sign between us and you.'
Joshua 22:29 Let's not sin by turning away from God today and making an altar for burnt, grain, or other offerings, apart from the one at God's tent.
Joshua 22:30 When Phinehas the priest, the leaders, and the chiefs of Israel's groups with him heard what the people of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh said, they were happy.
Joshua 22:31 Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, said to the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, "Today we see that God is with us, for you did not do this wrong against God. Now you have saved the people of Israel from God's punishment."
Joshua 22:32 Phinehas, who was the son of the priest Eleazar, and the leaders, came back from the land of Gilead where the Reubenites and the Gadites lived, to Canaan, to tell the Israelites what happened.
Joshua 22:33 The Israelites liked this idea; they praised God and decided not to attack them or ruin the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.
Joshua 22:34 The children of Reuben and the children of Gad named the altar Ed: it will be a sign among us that God is God.

Joshua 23:1 Long after God gave Israel peace from all their enemies, Joshua grew very old.
Joshua 23:2 Joshua called all Israel, their elders, leaders, judges, and officials, and said to them, "I am old and advanced in years."
Joshua 23:3 You have seen everything God has done to these nations for your sake; God has fought for you.
Joshua 23:4 Look, I have given you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan River to the great sea in the west.
Joshua 23:5 God will force them out from in front of you and push them away from your view; and you will take over their land, just as God promised you.
Joshua 23:6 So be very brave to follow and do everything written in Moses' law book, without turning away to the right or the left.
Joshua 23:7 Do not join these nations still living among you; do not speak of their gods, swear by them, serve them, or bow down to them.
Joshua 23:8 Stick close to God, just as you've been doing until now.
Joshua 23:9 God has forced powerful nations out of your way: but no one has been able to defeat you up to now.
Joshua 23:10 One of you will chase a thousand because it is God who fights for you, just as he promised.
Joshua 23:11 Be very careful, then, to love God with all your heart.
Joshua 23:12 But if you turn away and join with the remaining nations among you, and marry them and they marry you:
Joshua 23:13 Be sure that God will not drive out these nations for you anymore. They will be like traps and whips to hurt you, and like thorns in your eyes, until you are gone from this good land God has given you.
Joshua 23:14 Look, today I am following the path of everyone on earth, and you know with all your hearts and souls that not one of the good things God promised you has failed; everything has happened for you, and not one promise has gone unfulfilled.
Joshua 23:15 So it will happen that just as all the good things God promised you have come to you, God will also bring all the bad things until he has destroyed you from this good land that God gave you.
Joshua 23:16 When you break God's agreement that he gave you, and follow and worship other gods, God will get very angry with you, and you will soon be destroyed and taken away from the good land he gave you.

Joshua 24:1 Joshua brought all the Israelite tribes to Shechem, called the Israeli elders, leaders, judges, and officials, and they came before God.
Joshua 24:2 Joshua told all the people, "God says, 'Long ago, your ancestors lived across the river, including Terah, Abraham's father, and Nachor's father, and they worshiped different gods.'"
Joshua 24:3 I brought your father Abraham from across the river, guided him through all of Canaan, increased his descendants, and gave him Isaac.
Joshua 24:4 I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the mountain of Seir to own, but Jacob and his family moved to Egypt.
Joshua 24:5 I sent Moses and Aaron, gave Egypt troubles like I did there, and then I rescued you.
Joshua 24:6 I led your ancestors out of Egypt; you reached the sea, and the Egyptians chased your ancestors with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.
Joshua 24:7 When they called out to God, he made darkness between you and the Egyptians, and he made the sea cover them; you saw what I did in Egypt, and you lived in the desert for a long time.
Joshua 24:8 I brought you into the land of the Amorites who lived across the Jordan River. They fought against you, but I handed them over to you. You took over their land, and I wiped them out before you.
Joshua 24:9 Then Balak, Zippor's son and king of Moab, got up and fought against Israel, and sent for Balaam, Beor's son, to curse you.
Joshua 24:10 But I refused to listen to Balaam; so he continued to bless you, and I saved you from his power.
Joshua 24:11 You crossed the Jordan River and reached Jericho. The people of Jericho, Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites fought you, but I gave you victory over them.
Joshua 24:12 I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it forced the two Amorite kings out, not by your sword or bow.
Joshua 24:13 I have given you land you didn't work for, cities you didn't build, and you live in them. You eat from vineyards and olive groves you didn't plant.
Joshua 24:14 Now respect God and serve him honestly and truly. Stop following the gods your ancestors worshiped across the river and in Egypt, and serve God instead.
Joshua 24:15 If serving God seems bad to you, decide today who you'll serve: the gods your ancestors worshiped beyond the river, or the Amorites' gods where you live. As for me and my family, we will serve God.
Joshua 24:16 The people responded, "No way should we leave God to worship other gods."
Joshua 24:17 For God, our God, is the one who brought us and our ancestors out of Egypt, the place of slavery, and performed those great wonders before our eyes, and protected us on our entire journey, and among all the nations we traveled through.
Joshua 24:18 God drove out from before us all the people, including the Amorites who lived in the land. So we will also serve God, because he is our God.
Joshua 24:19 Joshua told the people, "You cannot serve God because he is a holy God; he is a jealous God; he will not forgive your wrongdoings or your sins."
Joshua 24:20 If you abandon God and serve other gods, then he will change and harm you, destroying you after he has been good to you.
Joshua 24:21 The people told Joshua, "No, we will serve God."
Joshua 24:22 Joshua told the people, "You are your own witnesses that you have picked God to serve Him." And they replied, "We are witnesses."
Joshua 24:23 So he said, "Now get rid of the foreign gods you have, and turn your hearts to God, the God of Israel."
Joshua 24:24 The people told Joshua, "We will serve our God and listen to what he says."
Joshua 24:25 Joshua made an agreement with the people that day and gave them rules and laws in Shechem.
Joshua 24:26 Joshua wrote these words in God's Law Book, and put up a big rock under the oak tree near God's holy place.
Joshua 24:27 Joshua told all the people, "Look, this stone will be our witness. It has heard all of God's words that he spoke to us. It will be a witness for you, so you don't deny your God."
Joshua 24:28 Joshua sent the people away, each to their own land.
Joshua 24:29 After these events, Joshua, son of Nun and God's servant, died at the age of 110.
Joshua 24:30 They buried him in his land at Timnathserah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Joshua 24:31 Israel served God during Joshua's lifetime and the lifetime of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all that God did for Israel.
Joshua 24:32 The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites carried from Egypt, were buried in Shechem, on a piece of land that Jacob purchased from Hamor's sons, Shechem's father, for a hundred silver coins. This land became Joseph's descendants' inheritance.
Joshua 24:33 Eleazar, Aaron's son, died; they buried him on a hill belonging to his son Phinehas, which he received in the Ephraim mountains.

Judges 1:1 After Joshua died, the Israelites asked God, "Who will lead us in battle against the Canaanites first?"
Judges 1:2 God said, "Judah will move forward: see, I have given him control of the land."
Judges 1:3 Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come with me to my land so we can fight the Canaanites; and then I'll go with you to your land." So Simeon went with him.
Judges 1:4 Judah marched forward; God gave them victory over the Canaanites and Perizzites: they killed ten thousand men in Bezek.
Judges 1:5 They found Adonibezek in Bezek and fought him, killing the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Judges 1:6 Adonibezek ran away, but they chased him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.
Judges 1:7 Adonibezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to pick up scraps under my table. Just as I did to them, God has paid me back." They took him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
Judges 1:8 The people of Judah fought against Jerusalem, captured it, struck it with the sword, and burned the city.
Judges 1:9 Later, the people of Judah went to battle the Canaanites living in the mountains, the south, and the valleys.
Judges 1:10 Judah fought against the Canaanites living in Hebron (previously called Kirjatharba) and killed Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
Judges 1:11 He left there to fight the people of Debir. Before, Debir was called Kirjathsepher.
Judges 1:12 Caleb said, "The person who attacks Kirjathsepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Achsah to him as his wife."
Judges 1:13 Othniel, Kenaz's son and Caleb's younger brother, captured the city. So Caleb gave his daughter Achsah to Othniel as his wife.
Judges 1:14 When she approached him, she persuaded him to request a field from her father. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
Judges 1:15 She said to him, "Give me a blessing because you've given me land in the south; also give me water springs." And Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.
Judges 1:16 The Kenite children, who were relatives of Moses' father-in-law, left the city of palm trees with the Judah children. They traveled to the Judah wilderness in the south, near Arad, and lived there among the people.
Judges 1:17 Judah went with his brother Simeon, and they killed the Canaanites living in Zephath, completely destroying the city. The city was then named Hormah.
Judges 1:18 Judah captured Gaza and its surrounding area, as well as Askelon and its area, and Ekron with its area.
Judges 1:19 God was with Judah; he forced out the people of the mountains but could not force out the people of the valley because they had iron chariots.
Judges 1:20 They gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove out the three sons of Anak from there.
Judges 1:21 The Benjamin people did not force the Jebusites out of Jerusalem; instead, the Jebusites lived with the Benjamin people in Jerusalem until now.
Judges 1:22 Joseph's family went to fight against Bethel, and God was with them.
Judges 1:23 Joseph's family sent spies to check out Bethel (which was called Luz before).
Judges 1:24 The spies saw a man leave the city and they said to him, "Please show us how to get into the city, and we'll be kind to you."
Judges 1:25 When he showed them how to get into the city, they struck the city with their swords, but they spared the man and his family.
Judges 1:26 The man went to the Hittites' land, built a city, and named it Luz, which it is still called today.
Judges 1:27 Manasseh did not remove the people of Bethshean and its villages, or those of Taanach and its villages, or those of Dor and its villages, or those of Ibleam and its villages, or those of Megiddo and its villages. Instead, the Canaanites continued to live in that area.
Judges 1:28 When Israel became strong, they made the Canaanites pay taxes but did not completely force them out.
Judges 1:29 Ephraim did not force the Canaanites out of Gezer; instead, the Canaanites lived in Gezer with them.
Judges 1:30 Zebulun did not force the people of Kitron or Nahalol to leave. Instead, the Canaanites lived with them and had to pay taxes.
Judges 1:31 Asher did not force out the people of Accho, Zidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
Judges 1:32 The people of Asher lived with the Canaanites, who were living in the land, because they did not force them out.
Judges 1:33 Naphtali did not force out the people of Bethshemesh or Bethanath; instead, he lived among the Canaanites who were living in the land. However, the people of Bethshemesh and Bethanath paid tribute to them.
Judges 1:34 The Amorites pushed the people of Dan into the mountains because they didn't let them go down to the valley.
Judges 1:35 The Amorites wanted to live in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim, but the people of Joseph were stronger and made them pay taxes.
Judges 1:36 The Amorites' territory started at Akrabbim, went from the rock, and stretched upward.

Judges 2:1 An angel of God came from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I brought you out of Egypt and into the land I promised your ancestors; and I said, I will always keep my promise to you."
Judges 2:2 Do not make agreements with the people of this land; destroy their places of worship. But you did not listen to me: why did you do this?
Judges 2:3 So I said, I won't force them out from your way; but they will be like thorns to bother you, and their gods will trap you.
Judges 2:4 When God's angel said these things to all the Israelites, the people raised their voice and cried.
Judges 2:5 They named that place Bochim and offered sacrifices to God there.
Judges 2:6 After Joshua sent the people away, every Israelite went to their own land to take it over.
Judges 2:7 The people worshiped God during Joshua's lifetime and while the older leaders lived, those who had seen all the great things God had done for Israel.
Judges 2:8 Joshua, Nun's son and God's servant, died at 110 years old.
Judges 2:9 They buried him at the edge of his land in Timnath Heres, in the hills of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Judges 2:10 That whole generation passed away, and a new generation grew up after them who didn't know God or remember what He had done for Israel.
Judges 2:11 The Israelites did bad things that God saw, and they worshipped Baal gods.
Judges 2:12 They left the God of their ancestors who had led them out of Egypt, and chased after other gods from the surrounding peoples, worshiping them and making God angry.
Judges 2:13 They left God and worshiped Baal and Ashtaroth.
Judges 2:14 God was very angry with Israel, so he let raiders come to rob them and sold them to their surrounding enemies, making it impossible for them to resist those enemies.
Judges 2:15 Wherever they went, God's hand was against them for harm, just as God had said and promised, and they were in great trouble.
Judges 2:16 However, God appointed leaders who saved them from their attackers.
Judges 2:17 Still, they wouldn't listen to their judges. They chased after other gods, worshipping them. They quickly left the path their ancestors followed, the one where they obeyed God's commands; but they did not do the same.
Judges 2:18 When God gave them judges, God was with the judge and saved them from their enemies for as long as that judge lived. God felt sorry for them because they were groaning under those who were pressing and troubling them.
Judges 2:19 After the judge died, they turned back and behaved worse than their ancestors, by following and worshiping other gods, and by bowing down to them. They didn't stop their actions or their stubborn behavior.
Judges 2:20 God was very angry with Israel and said, "Because these people have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors and have not listened to me;
Judges 2:21 From now on, I will not force out any of the nations that Joshua left behind when he died.
Judges 2:22 I will test Israel with these commands to see if they will follow God's path as their ancestors did or not.
Judges 2:23 So God did not quickly remove those nations, nor did he hand them over to Joshua.

Judges 3:1 These are the nations God left to test Israel, especially those in Israel who had not experienced all the Canaan wars.
Judges 3:2 The idea was that Israel's descendants should learn about war, especially those who had never known it before.
Judges 3:3 Specifically, five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
Judges 3:4 They were used to test Israel, to see if they would follow God's commands given to their ancestors through Moses.
Judges 3:5 The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Judges 3:6 They married their daughters and gave their daughters to their sons and worshiped their gods.
Judges 3:7 The Israelites did bad things that God saw, forgot God, and worshiped Baal and the Asherah poles.
Judges 3:8 So God was very angry with Israel, and he let the king of Mesopotamia, Chushanrishathaim, defeat them. The people of Israel had to serve Chushanrishathaim for eight years.
Judges 3:9 When the Israelites called out to God, God gave them a rescuer, Othniel the son of Kenaz and Caleb's younger brother, who saved them.
Judges 3:10 God's Spirit came upon him, and he led Israel. He went to battle, and God helped him defeat Chushanrishathaim, the king of Mesopotamia; he overpowered Chushanrishathaim.
Judges 3:11 The land was peaceful for forty years. Then Othniel, Kenaz's son, passed away.
Judges 3:12 The Israelites did wrong before God again, and God gave Eglon, the king of Moab, power over Israel because they had done wrong in God's eyes.
Judges 3:13 He brought together the people of Ammon and Amalek, attacked Israel, and took over the city of palm trees.
Judges 3:14 The Israelites served King Eglon of Moab for eighteen years.
Judges 3:15 When the Israelites called out to God, God gave them a savior, Ehud, Gera's son from the tribe of Benjamin, who was left-handed. Through him, the Israelites sent a gift to Eglon, the king of Moab.
Judges 3:16 Ehud made a two-edged dagger about eighteen inches long and tied it under his clothes on his right thigh.
Judges 3:17 He gave the gift to Eglon, the king of Moab, who was very fat.
Judges 3:18 After he finished giving the gift, he let the people who carried the gift go.
Judges 3:19 However, he turned back from the stone-cutting place near Gilgal and said, "I have a private message for you, king." The king replied, "Be quiet." Then everyone with him left.
Judges 3:20 Ehud went to him while he was sitting alone in a summer room. Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." Then he stood up from his chair.
Judges 3:21 Ehud reached out with his left hand, took the dagger from his right thigh, and stabbed it into his stomach.
Judges 3:22 The handle followed the blade into the body; the fat closed over the blade, so he couldn't pull the knife from his stomach; and the insides spilled out.
Judges 3:23 Then Ehud went out through the entryway, closed the doors of the room behind him, and locked them.
Judges 3:24 After he left, his servants arrived, and seeing the locked room doors, they thought, "He must be resting in his cool room."
Judges 3:25 They waited until they felt embarrassed. When the doors to the room didn't open, they used a key to unlock them and found their master lying dead on the ground.
Judges 3:26 Ehud got away while they waited, went past the stone-cutting places, and ran to Seirath.
Judges 3:27 When he arrived, he sounded a trumpet on Mount Ephraim, and the Israelites followed him down, with him leading the way.
Judges 3:28 He told them, "Follow me, for God has given us victory over the Moabites, our enemies." So they followed him, captured the crossing places of the Jordan River that led to Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross.
Judges 3:29 They killed about ten thousand strong and brave men from Moab at that time, and not a single man escaped.
Judges 3:30 So Moab was defeated that day by Israel, and the land was at peace for eighty years.
Judges 3:31 After him, Shamgar son of Anath killed 600 Philistine men with an ox-goad and he also saved Israel.

Judges 4:1 The Israelites once more did bad things that God saw, after Ehud died.
Judges 4:2 God gave them over to Jabin, the king of Canaan, who ruled in Hazor. Sisera, the commander of his army, lived in Harosheth of the nations.
Judges 4:3 The Israelites cried out to God because he had 900 iron chariots and for twenty years he greatly oppressed the Israelites.
Judges 4:4 Deborah, a prophetess and Lapidoth's wife, led Israel during that time.
Judges 4:5 She lived under Deborah's palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hills of Ephraim, and the Israelites came to her for decisions.
Judges 4:6 She sent for Barak, son of Abinoam, from Kedesh in Naphtali and told him, "Hasn't God of Israel ordered you to go to Mount Tabor and take ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun with you?"
Judges 4:7 I will bring Sisera, the leader of Jabin's army, to you at the Kishon River, with his chariots and troops; and I will give him into your control.
Judges 4:8 Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go; but if you don't go with me, I won't go."
Judges 4:9 She said, "I will definitely go with you. However, this trip you are making won't bring you glory, because God will let a woman defeat Sisera." Then Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Judges 4:10 Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and he led ten thousand troops. Deborah also went with him.
Judges 4:11 Heber the Kenite, from the family of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, had moved away from the Kenites and set up his tent near Kedesh in the Zaanaim area.
Judges 4:12 They told Sisera that Barak, son of Abinoam, had gone up to Mount Tabor.
Judges 4:13 Sisera brought together all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all his men, from Harosheth of the Nations to the Kishon River.
Judges 4:14 Deborah told Barak, "Get up; today is the day God has given Sisera to you. Hasn't God gone ahead of you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him.
Judges 4:15 God confused Sisera and all his chariots and soldiers with the edge of the sword in front of Barak; Sisera got down from his chariot and ran away on foot.
Judges 4:16 But Barak chased the chariots and army to Harosheth of the Nations, and all Sisera's army was killed by the sword; no one survived.
Judges 4:17 However, Sisera ran to Jael's tent, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between King Jabin of Hazor and Heber's family.
Judges 4:18 Jael went to meet Sisera and told him, "Come in, sir, come in to my place; don't be afraid." When he went in to her tent, she covered him with a blanket.
Judges 4:19 He said to her, "Please give me some water to drink; I'm thirsty." She opened a container of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him up.
Judges 4:20 He told her again, "Stand at the tent door. If a man comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?' you must say 'No.'"
Judges 4:21 Jael, Heber's wife, got a tent peg and a hammer, quietly approached him, drove the peg into his head, and pinned it to the ground because he was sound asleep and tired. And so, he died.
Judges 4:22 Look, as Barak chased Sisera, Jael went out to meet him and said, "Come, I will show you the man you are looking for." And when he went into her tent, there lay Sisera dead with a nail in his head.
Judges 4:23 God defeated King Jabin of Canaan that day for the Israelites.
Judges 4:24 The Israelites succeeded and overcame King Jabin of Canaan until they had defeated him completely.

Judges 5:1 Deborah and Barak, Abinoam's son, sang on that day, saying,
Judges 5:2 Praise God for rescuing Israel when the people freely gave themselves to help.
Judges 5:3 Listen, kings; pay attention, princes; I will sing to God; I will praise the God of Israel.
Judges 5:4 God, when you came from Seir, when you marched from Edom's land, the earth shook, and the sky poured rain, the clouds also poured water.
Judges 5:5 The mountains melted before God, including Sinai before the God of Israel.
Judges 5:6 During the time of Shamgar, Anath's son, and when Jael lived, the main roads were empty, and travelers took side paths.
Judges 5:7 People in the villages stopped, they stopped in Israel, until I, Deborah, stood up, until I stood up as a mother in Israel.
Judges 5:8 They picked new gods; then war broke out in the cities: did anyone see a shield or spear among forty thousand in Israel?
Judges 5:9 I care deeply for the leaders of Israel who volunteered among the people. Praise God.
Judges 5:10 Talk, you who ride white donkeys, you who make decisions, and you who travel on the roads.
Judges 5:11 Those saved from the archers' noise by the water wells will talk about God's good deeds, including his kindness to his people in Israel's villages. Then God's people will go to the city gates.
Judges 5:12 Wake up, wake up, Deborah: wake up, wake up, sing a song: get up, Barak, and take your prisoners, you son of Abinoam.
Judges 5:13 Then he let those who were left rule over the leaders of the people: God made me rule over the strong.
Judges 5:14 From Ephraim came warriors against Amalek; following you, Benjamin, with your people; from Machir came leaders, and from Zebulun, those skilled with the writer's pen.
Judges 5:15 The leaders of Issachar supported Deborah; Issachar and Barak too: Barak went down to the valley on foot. The people of Reuben seriously considered their choices.
Judges 5:16 Why did you stay among the sheep pens, listening to the flocks' cries? The people of Reuben deeply questioned themselves.
Judges 5:17 Gilead lived across the Jordan River, and why did Dan stay with ships? Asher stayed by the sea coast and lived in his harbors.
Judges 5:18 Zebulun and Naphtali were people who risked their lives to the point of death on the high parts of the field.
Judges 5:19 Kings came and fought, then Canaan's kings fought near Megiddo's waters; they got no money.
Judges 5:20 They battled from the sky; the stars in their paths battled against Sisera.
Judges 5:21 The Kishon River carried them off, that old river, the Kishon River. Oh, my soul, you have walked on power.
Judges 5:22 Then the horses' hooves were broken from the galloping, the galloping of the strong ones.
Judges 5:23 God's messenger said, "Curse Meroz; curse its people harshly because they did not help God fight against the strong enemies."
Judges 5:24 Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, will be more blessed than other women, and in the tent, she will be the most blessed among women.
Judges 5:25 He asked for water, and she gave him milk; she served cream in a fine bowl.
Judges 5:26 She held the nail and took the worker's hammer in her right hand. With the hammer she hit Sisera, knocked off his head after she had stabbed and gone through his temples.
Judges 5:27 He knelt at her feet, fell, and lay there. Where he knelt, he fell dead.
Judges 5:28 Sisera's mother looked out the window and cried through the lattice, "Why is his chariot taking so long to come? Why are the wheels of his chariot delayed?"
Judges 5:29 Her smart women replied to her, yes, she even answered herself.
Judges 5:30 Did they not hurry? Did they not share the loot, with each man getting a girl or two, and Sisera getting colorful embroidered garments, colorful and richly worked cloths, suitable to wrap around the victors' necks?
Judges 5:31 May all your enemies die, God, but may those who love him shine like the sun at its strongest. And the land was at peace for forty years.

Judges 6:1 The Israelites did bad things in front of God, so God let Midian control them for seven years.
Judges 6:2 The Midianites overpowered Israel, so the Israelites hid in mountain dens, caves, and strongholds.
Judges 6:3 So when Israel planted crops, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the Easterners came to attack them.
Judges 6:4 They camped against them, ruined the crops of the land up to Gaza, and left Israel nothing to eat; no sheep, no oxen, no donkeys.
Judges 6:5 They arrived with their animals and tents, countless like locusts; they and their camels were too many to count, and they invaded the land to ruin it.
Judges 6:6 Israel became very poor because of the Midianites; and the people of Israel called out to God for help.
Judges 6:7 When the Israelites cried out to God because of the Midianites,
Judges 6:8 God sent a prophet to the people of Israel, who told them, "This is what God of Israel says: I took you out of Egypt, and I freed you from slavery."
Judges 6:9 I saved you from the Egyptians and from all who oppressed you, I forced them out of your way, and I gave you their land.
Judges 6:10 I told you, 'I am God, your God; do not fear the gods of the Amorites where you live.' But you did not listen to me.
Judges 6:11 An angel from God came and sat under an oak tree in Ophrah, which belonged to Joash from the Abiezrite family. His son Gideon was beating out wheat near the winepress to keep it hidden from the Midianites.
Judges 6:12 God's messenger appeared to him and said, "God is with you, brave man."
Judges 6:13 And Gideon said to him, "Oh my God, if God is with us, why has all this happened to us? And where are all the miracles that our ancestors told us about, saying, 'Didn't God bring us out of Egypt?' But now God has left us and let the Midianites defeat us."
Judges 6:14 God looked at him and said, "Go with your strength and you will rescue Israel from the Midianites. Haven't I sent you?"
Judges 6:15 He said to him, "Oh my God, how can I save Israel? My family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
Judges 6:16 God said to him, "I will surely be with you, and you will defeat the Midianites as if they were one person."
Judges 6:17 He said to him, "If I have now found favor with you, then show me a sign that you are speaking to me."
Judges 6:18 Please don't leave until I come back to you, bring my gift, and present it to you. And he said, I will wait until you return.
Judges 6:19 Gideon went in, cooked a young goat, and made bread without yeast from a large amount of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the soup in a pot, then took them to the oak tree and gave them to him.
Judges 6:20 God's messenger told him, "Put the meat and bread without yeast on this rock, and pour the soup over them." And he did it.
Judges 6:21 Then the angel of God reached out with the staff in his hand, touched the meat and bread without yeast, and fire came up from the rock and ate up the meat and the bread. Then the angel of God left from his sight.
Judges 6:22 When Gideon realized he was an angel of God, he said, "Oh no, God! I have seen an angel of God face to face."
Judges 6:23 God said to him, "Peace to you; do not be afraid: you will not die."
Judges 6:24 Gideon made an altar there for God and named it "The Lord is Peace." It is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites to this day.
Judges 6:25 That night, God told him, "Take your father's young bull, the seven-year-old second one, and destroy the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and also cut down the wooden image next to it."
Judges 6:26 Make an altar for God on top of this rock where it is supposed to be, and use the second bull to give a burned offering with the wood from the trees you cut down.
Judges 6:27 Gideon took ten of his men and did what God had told him to do. Because he was afraid of his family and the people in the city, he did it at night instead of during the day.
Judges 6:28 When the city people got up early in the morning, they saw the altar of Baal had been knocked over, the trees around it had been chopped down, and the second bull had been sacrificed on the new altar.
Judges 6:29 They asked each other, "Who did this?" When they investigated and asked around, they learned that Gideon, Joash's son, had done it.
Judges 6:30 The city men said to Joash, "Bring out your son so he can die, because he destroyed Baal's altar, and he also cut down the wooden idols near it."
Judges 6:31 Joash said to those against him, "Are you going to argue for Baal? Will you rescue him? Anyone who argues for him should be killed before morning. If Baal is a god, let him argue for himself, since someone has destroyed his altar."
Judges 6:32 So on that day he named him Jerubbaal, meaning, let Baal fight against him because he tore down Baal's altar.
Judges 6:33 All the Midianites, Amalekites, and eastern people gathered and camped in the Jezreel Valley.
Judges 6:34 God's Spirit came on Gideon, and he sounded a trumpet; then Abiezer joined him.
Judges 6:35 He sent messengers through all Manasseh, who joined him. He also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came to meet them.
Judges 6:36 Gideon said to God, "If you will save Israel through me, as you have said,
Judges 6:37 I will place a piece of wool on the ground; if there is dew only on the wool and it's dry everywhere else, then I will know that you will save Israel through me, as you have promised.
Judges 6:38 It happened: He got up early the next morning, squeezed the wool together, and wrung out a bowl full of water from the wool.
Judges 6:39 Gideon said to God, "Please don't be angry with me, and I will speak just this time: let me do one test with the fleece. Let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground around it."
Judges 6:40 God did that night; the wool was dry, but the ground was wet with dew.

Judges 7:1 Jerubbaal, also known as Gideon, and all his companions got up early and set up camp near Harod's well. The Midianite army was to the north of them, near Moreh hill in the valley.
Judges 7:2 God told Gideon, "You have too many people for me to let you defeat the Midianites. Otherwise, Israel will boast and say, 'We saved ourselves.'"
Judges 7:3 Now, go and tell the people, "Anyone who is scared or afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home early." So twenty-two thousand people went back, and ten thousand stayed.
Judges 7:4 God told Gideon, "There are still too many people; take them to the water and I will test them for you there. Whoever I choose for you to take, they will go with you; and whoever I choose not to go, they will not go with you."
Judges 7:5 He led the people to the water, and God told Gideon, "Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel down to drink."
Judges 7:6 Three hundred men scooped water with their hands to drink, but all the others knelt down to drink water directly.
Judges 7:7 God told Gideon, "I will save you by the 300 men who lapped water. I will give you victory over the Midianites. Let all the other people go home."
Judges 7:8 The people took food and their trumpets in their hands. He sent the rest of Israel to their tents, but kept the 300 men. The Midian army was down in the valley below him.
Judges 7:9 That night, God told him, "Get up and go down to the army camp, because I have given it to you."
Judges 7:10 If you're afraid to go, take your servant Phurah with you to the camp.
Judges 7:11 You will listen to what they say, and then you will feel stronger to go to the army. Then he went with Phurah, his servant, to the edge of where the soldiers in the army were.
Judges 7:12 The Midianites, Amalekites, and all the people from the east were spread out in the valley, very numerous like grasshoppers; and there were so many camels, they were as countless as the sand on the seashore.
Judges 7:13 When Gideon arrived, he saw a man who was telling his friend about a dream. He said, "I had a dream where a barley bread loaf rolled into the Midianite camp, hit a tent, knocked it down, and turned it upside down so the tent was flat on the ground."
Judges 7:14 His friend replied, "This is certainly the sword of Gideon, Joash's son, an Israelite man. God has given Midian and their whole army into his hand."
Judges 7:15 When Gideon heard the dream and its meaning, he worshipped, went back to Israel's army, and said, "Get up; for God has given you the army of Midian."
Judges 7:16 He split the three hundred men into three groups and gave each man a trumpet, with empty jars, and torches inside the jars.
Judges 7:17 He told them, "Watch me and do the same. When I get to the camp's edge, do as I do."
Judges 7:18 When I sound the trumpet, me and everyone with me, then you also blow the trumpets around the whole camp and shout, "The sword for God and for Gideon!"
Judges 7:19 Gideon and his 100 men reached the edge of the camp at the start of the middle watch, just after the guards started their shift. They blew their trumpets and smashed the jars in their hands.
Judges 7:20 The three groups sounded the trumpets, broke the jars, held the lamps in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands to blow them: and they shouted, "The sword of God and of Gideon."
Judges 7:21 They stood, each in their spot, around the camp; and the whole army ran, shouted, and ran away.
Judges 7:22 The three hundred blew their trumpets, and God made every man fight against his comrade, and they all fled to Bethshittah in Zererath and near Abelmeholah, as far as Tabbath.
Judges 7:23 The men of Israel came together from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and chased the Midianites.
Judges 7:24 Gideon sent messengers all over the hills of Ephraim saying, "Come fight the Midianites and control the water areas near Bethbarah and the Jordan River." So all the Ephraim men joined together and took control of the water areas near Bethbarah and the Jordan River.
Judges 7:25 They captured two Midianite leaders, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. Then they chased the Midianites and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan River.

Judges 8:1 The men from Ephraim asked him, "Why did you treat us like this, not calling us when you went to fight the Midianites?" And they argued with him strongly.
Judges 8:2 He asked them, "What have I done compared to you? Aren't even the leftovers of Ephraim's grapes better than Abiezer's full harvest?"
Judges 8:3 God has given you control over Midian's leaders, Oreb and Zeeb. What could I have done compared to you? Then they were no longer angry with him after he said this.
Judges 8:4 Gideon reached the Jordan river, crossed it, and with his three hundred men who were tired but still chasing the enemy.
Judges 8:5 He asked the people of Succoth, "Please give some bread to my followers; they're tired, and I'm chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the Midianite leaders."
Judges 8:6 The leaders of Succoth said, "Do you have Zebah and Zalmunna captured already, that we should give bread to your soldiers?"
Judges 8:7 Gideon said, "So when God gives me Zebah and Zalmunna, I'll hurt your skin with wild thorns and prickly plants."
Judges 8:8 He went from there to Penuel and spoke to them in the same way; and the people of Penuel replied just as the people of Succoth had.
Judges 8:9 He also told the men of Penuel, "When I come back safely, I will tear down this tower."
Judges 8:10 Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their armies, about fifteen thousand men, the only survivors from the eastern people's armies, because one hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had died.
Judges 8:11 Gideon traveled along the path near the tent-dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah and attacked the army, because the army felt safe.
Judges 8:12 When Zebah and Zalmunna ran away, he chased them and captured the two Midianite kings, Zebah and Zalmunna, and defeated their whole army.
Judges 8:13 Gideon, Joash's son, came back from the fight before sunrise.
Judges 8:14 They caught a young man from Succoth, asked him questions, and he told them about Succoth's leaders and elders, all seventy-seven men.
Judges 8:15 He went to the people of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. You mocked me before, asking, 'Do you have Zebah and Zalmunna captured so we should give your tired men bread?'"
Judges 8:16 He gathered the city elders, wild thorns, and briers, and with these, he punished the people of Succoth.
Judges 8:17 He destroyed the tower of Penuel and killed the city's men.
Judges 8:18 He asked Zebah and Zalmunna, "What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?" They replied, "They looked like you, every one of them seemed like a prince's son."
Judges 8:19 He said, "They were my brothers, my own mother's sons. If you had let them live, I wouldn't kill you."
Judges 8:20 He told his oldest son Jether, "Get up and kill them." But the boy did not pull out his sword because he was scared, since he was still young.
Judges 8:21 Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Get up and attack us, for a man's power matches his own ability." And Gideon got up, killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and removed the decorations from their camels' necks.
Judges 8:22 The men of Israel said to Gideon, "Be our leader, you, your son, and your grandson, because you saved us from Midian."
Judges 8:23 Gideon said to them, "I will not be your ruler, nor will my son be your ruler: God will be your ruler."
Judges 8:24 Gideon said to them, "I have a favor to ask: please give me the gold earrings you took from your captives." (They had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.)
Judges 8:25 They replied, "We will gladly give them." They laid out a cloth and each man threw in the earrings he had taken.
Judges 8:26 The gold earrings he asked for weighed 1,700 shekels, not counting the fancy clothes, necklaces, purple garments worn by Midianite kings, or the chains on their camels' necks.
Judges 8:27 Gideon made a special vest from them and placed it in his city, Ophrah, and all Israel chased after it, which trapped Gideon and his family.
Judges 8:28 Midian was defeated by the Israelites, so they were no longer a threat. And there was peace in the land for forty years during Gideon's time.
Judges 8:29 Jerubbaal, Joash's son, went and lived in his own house.
Judges 8:30 Gideon had seventy sons of his own, because he had many wives.
Judges 8:31 His companion in Shechem also had a son for him, and he named him Abimelech.
Judges 8:32 Gideon, son of Joash, died at an old age and was buried in his father Joash's tomb, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
Judges 8:33 After Gideon died, the Israelites turned back and followed other gods, choosing Baalberith as their god.
Judges 8:34 The Israelites forgot God, who had saved them from all their enemies around them.
Judges 8:35 They did not show kindness to Jerubbaal's family, Gideon, despite all the good he had done for Israel.

Judges 9:1 Abimelech, Jerubbaal's son, went to Shechem to his mother's brothers, talked with them, and with all his mother's father's family, saying,
Judges 9:2 Please tell everyone in Shechem: What's better for you—to have all seventy sons of Jerubbaal rule over you, or just one person? And remember, I am your own family.
Judges 9:3 His mother's relatives spoke about him to all the men of Shechem, saying all these things: and they felt moved to support Abimelech because they said, "He is our brother."
Judges 9:4 They gave him seventy silver coins from the temple of Baalberith, and with this money, Abimelech paid worthless and reckless men to follow him.
Judges 9:5 He went to his father's home in Ophrah and killed his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, on a single stone. However, Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived because he had hidden.
Judges 9:6 All the men of Shechem and the family of Millo came together and declared Abimelech as king near the tree in Shechem.
Judges 9:7 When they reported this to Jotham, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and shouted, saying to them, "Listen to me, men of Shechem, so that God will listen to you."
Judges 9:8 The trees once set out to choose a king for themselves; they asked the olive tree, "Be our ruler."
Judges 9:9 The olive tree said to them, "Should I give up my richness, which is used to honor both God and people, to rule over the trees?"
Judges 9:10 The trees said to the fig tree, "Come and be our leader."
Judges 9:11 The fig tree answered, "Should I give up my sweetness and good fruit to rule over the trees?"
Judges 9:12 Then the trees said to the grapevine, "Come and be our leader."
Judges 9:13 The vine said to them, "Should I stop making wine, which makes both God and people happy, to rule over the trees?"
Judges 9:14 Then all the trees said to the thorny bush, "Come and be our king."
Judges 9:15 The bramble said to the trees, "If you really make me your king, come and rest in my shade. But if not, let fire come from me and burn the cedars of Lebanon."
Judges 9:16 So, if you have honestly and truly made Abimelech king, and you have treated Jerubbaal and his family well, giving him what his actions deserved;
Judges 9:17 My father fought for you, risked his life greatly, and saved you from the power of Midian.
Judges 9:18 Today, you have turned against my father's family, killed his seventy sons on one stone, and made Abimelech, the maidservant's son, king of Shechem's people because he is your brother.
Judges 9:19 If you have been honest and sincere with Jerubbaal and his family today, then be happy about Abimelech, and let him be happy about you.
Judges 9:20 But if not, let fire come from Abimelech and burn the men of Shechem and the house of Millo; and let fire come from the men of Shechem and the house of Millo and burn Abimelech.
Judges 9:21 Jotham ran away and hid in Beer because he was afraid of his brother Abimelech.
Judges 9:22 After Abimelech had been king of Israel for three years,
Judges 9:23 God sent a bad spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and the men of Shechem betrayed Abimelech.
Judges 9:24 To punish the killing of Jerubbaal's 70 sons, let the guilt fall on their brother Abimelech who killed them, and on the men of Shechem who helped him.
Judges 9:25 The men of Shechem hid on the mountain tops to ambush him, stealing from everyone who passed by, and this was reported to Abimelech.
Judges 9:26 Gaal, Ebed's son, arrived with his brothers and moved to Shechem where the Shechem people started to trust him.
Judges 9:27 They went to the fields, collected grapes from the vineyards, pressed the grapes, celebrated, entered their god's temple, ate, drank, and insulted Abimelech.
Judges 9:28 Gaal, Ebed's son, asked, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem that we must serve him? Isn't he Jerubbaal's son and Zebul his assistant? Serve Hamor's family, Shechem's father. Why should we serve Abimelech?"
Judges 9:29 I wish these people were under my control! Then I would get rid of Abimelech. He told Abimelech, "Get more soldiers and come out to fight."
Judges 9:30 When Zebul, the city leader, heard what Gaal, Ebed's son, said, he became very angry.
Judges 9:31 He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech, saying, "Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are strengthening the city against you."
Judges 9:32 Get up at night, you and the people with you, and hide in the field.
Judges 9:33 In the morning, when the sun comes up, wake up early and get ready to attack the city. And when he and his people come out to fight you, you can do whatever you think is best.
Judges 9:34 Abimelech and all his followers got up at night and set up ambushes around Shechem in four groups.
Judges 9:35 Gaal, Ebed's son, went out and stood at the city gate entrance. Abimelech and his people got up from their hiding place.
Judges 9:36 When Gaal noticed the crowd, he told Zebul, "Look, there are people coming down from the mountain tops." Zebul replied, "You're seeing the mountain shadows looking like people."
Judges 9:37 Gaal spoke again and said, "Look, there are people coming down through the center of the land, and another group is coming by the Plain of Meonenim."
Judges 9:38 Zebul asked him, "Where are your bragging words now? You said, 'Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?' Isn't this the group you looked down on? Please, go out and battle them now."
Judges 9:39 Gaal led the men of Shechem and battled against Abimelech.
Judges 9:40 Abimelech chased him, and he ran away. Many were knocked down and hurt, up to the gate.
Judges 9:41 Abimelech lived at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out so they couldn't live in Shechem.
Judges 9:42 The next day, the people went into the field, and they told Abimelech.
Judges 9:43 He took the people, split them into three groups, hid in the field, watched as the people came out of the city, then attacked and defeated them.
Judges 9:44 Abimelech and his group charged ahead and stopped at the city gate entrance, while the two other groups attacked everyone in the fields and killed them.
Judges 9:45 Abimelech fought against the city all day; he captured the city, killed the people in it, destroyed the city, and covered it with salt.
Judges 9:46 When all the men from Shechem's tower heard that, they went into a strong room in the temple of the god Berith.
Judges 9:47 People told Abimelech that all the men from Shechem's tower had come together.
Judges 9:48 Abimelech and his followers went up Mount Zalmon. He took an axe and cut off a tree branch, put it on his shoulder, and told his followers, "Quickly do as you have seen me do."
Judges 9:49 Everyone cut down branches, followed Abimelech, piled them against the stronghold, and set it on fire. So all the people in Shechem's tower died—about a thousand men and women.
Judges 9:50 Abimelech went to Thebez, camped against it, and captured it.
Judges 9:51 Inside the city, there was a strong tower where all the city's men and women ran to, closed the door, and went up to the top.
Judges 9:52 Abimelech went to the tower, fought it, and got close to the tower's door to set it on fire.
Judges 9:53 A woman dropped a millstone piece on Abimelech's head, breaking it.
Judges 9:54 He quickly called to his young armor-bearer and said, "Pull out your sword and kill me, so people won't say a woman killed me." His assistant stabbed him, and he died.
Judges 9:55 When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech had died, they all went back to their homes.
Judges 9:56 So God paid back Abimelech for the evil he did to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
Judges 9:57 God made the evil men of Shechem pay for their wrongs, and Jotham, Jerubbaal's son, cursed them.

Judges 10:1 After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, Dodo's son from the tribe of Issachar, became a leader to protect Israel. He lived in Shamir in the Ephraim hills.
Judges 10:2 He ruled Israel for twenty-three years, then he died and was buried in Shamir.
Judges 10:3 After him, Jair from Gilead became a leader and judged Israel for twenty-two years.
Judges 10:4 He had thirty sons who rode on thirty young donkeys, and they owned thirty cities called Havothjair, which exist to this day in Gilead.
Judges 10:5 Jair died and was buried in Camon.
Judges 10:6 The Israelites did bad things again before God, worshipped Baal and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, Zidon, Moab, Ammon's children, and the Philistines, and left God and did not worship Him.
Judges 10:7 God became very angry with Israel and handed them over to the Philistines and to the Ammonites.
Judges 10:8 That year they troubled and mistreated the Israelites for eighteen years. This happened to all the Israelites living across the Jordan River in the land of the Amorites in Gilead.
Judges 10:9 The Ammonites crossed the Jordan to also fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the Ephraimites, causing great trouble for Israel.
Judges 10:10 The people of Israel called out to God, saying, "We have sinned against you, for we have left our God and also worshiped Baalim."
Judges 10:11 God asked the Israelites, "Didn't I save you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines?"
Judges 10:12 The people of Sidon, the Amalekites, and the Maonites also troubled you. When you called out to me, I saved you from them.
Judges 10:13 You have left me and served other gods, so I will not save you anymore.
Judges 10:14 Go and call out to the gods you picked; let them save you when you are in trouble.
Judges 10:15 The children of Israel told God, "We have sinned. Do to us whatever you think is best, but please, save us today."
Judges 10:16 They removed the foreign gods from among them and worshiped God; and he felt sorry for Israel's suffering.
Judges 10:17 The people of Ammon came together and set up camp in Gilead. The people of Israel also gathered and set up camp in Mizpeh.
Judges 10:18 The people and leaders of Gilead asked each other, "Who will start the fight against the Ammonites? He will become the leader of everyone in Gilead."

Judges 11:1 Jephthah from Gilead was a brave warrior, and his mother was a prostitute. Gilead was Jephthah's father.
Judges 11:2 Gilead's wife had sons for him; when they grew up, they pushed Jephthah out, telling him, "You won't get any share in our father's home because you are the son of a different woman."
Judges 11:3 Jephthah ran away from his brothers and lived in Tob, where worthless men joined him and followed him.
Judges 11:4 As time went on, the Ammonites started a war with Israel.
Judges 11:5 When the Ammonites fought against Israel, the leaders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob.
Judges 11:6 They said to Jephthah, "Come and be our leader, so we can fight the Ammonites."
Judges 11:7 Jephthah asked the leaders of Gilead, "Didn't you hate me and force me to leave my father's home? Why do you come to me now that you're in trouble?"
Judges 11:8 The Gilead leaders said to Jephthah, "We come back to you now so you can join us, fight the Ammonites, and lead everyone in Gilead."
Judges 11:9 Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you take me back to battle the Ammonites and God lets me win, will I be your leader?"
Judges 11:10 The leaders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "God is our witness that we will do as you say."
Judges 11:11 Jephthah joined the Gilead leaders, and the people chose him as their leader and commander. Jephthah said all he wanted to say to God at Mizpeh.
Judges 11:12 Jephthah sent messengers to the king of Ammon asking, "Why have you come to fight in my land?"
Judges 11:13 The king of the Ammonites replied to Jephthah's messengers, "Israel took my land when they left Egypt, from Arnon to Jabbok and up to the Jordan River. So now, give it back peacefully."
Judges 11:14 Jephthah sent messengers to the king of Ammon's people again.
Judges 11:15 Jephthah says, "Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites."
Judges 11:16 When Israel left Egypt and traveled through the desert to the Red Sea, they reached Kadesh.
Judges 11:17 Israel sent messages to the Edom king, asking, "Please let me go through your land." But the Edom king didn't listen. They asked the same of the Moab king, but he also refused. So, Israel stayed in Kadesh.
Judges 11:18 They traveled through the desert, going around the land of Edom and Moab, and stopped on the east side of Moab, across from the Arnon river, but did not enter Moab's borders because Arnon was the boundary.
Judges 11:19 Israel sent messages to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon, saying, "Please let us pass through your land to our own place."
Judges 11:20 But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his land; instead, Sihon brought all his people together, camped at Jahaz, and battled against Israel.
Judges 11:21 God gave Israel victory over Sihon and his people, and they defeated them. So Israel took over all the land of the Amorites who lived there.
Judges 11:22 They took over all the Amorite territory, from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River, and from the desert to the Jordan River.
Judges 11:23 So now God of Israel has driven out the Amorites for his people Israel, and should you take it over?
Judges 11:24 Wouldn't you take what your god Chemosh gives you to take? So whoever God our God pushes out from before us, we will take their land.
Judges 11:25 Are you any better than Balak, son of Zippor, the king of Moab? Did he ever argue with Israel or fight them?
Judges 11:26 While Israel lived in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the cities near the Arnon River for three hundred years, why didn't you take them back during that time?
Judges 11:27 So I have not sinned against you, but you are doing wrong by fighting me. Let God, the Judge, decide today between the people of Israel and the people of Ammon.
Judges 11:28 But the king of the Ammonites did not listen to the message Jephthah sent him.
Judges 11:29 God's Spirit came to Jephthah, and he went through Gilead and Manasseh, and then through Mizpeh in Gilead, and from there he moved on to fight the Ammonites.
Judges 11:30 Jephthah made a promise to God, saying, "If you really give me victory over the Ammonites,
Judges 11:31 When I come back safely from fighting the Ammonites, whatever comes out of my house to greet me will belong to God, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering.
Judges 11:32 Jephthah went to fight the Ammonite people, and God let him defeat them.
Judges 11:33 He defeated them from Aroer all the way to Minnith, including twenty cities, and as far as the vineyard plains, killing many. So the Ammonites were conquered by the Israelites.
Judges 11:34 Jephthah arrived at Mizpeh at his home, and saw his daughter coming to greet him with drums and dancing; she was his only child, as he had no other sons or daughters.
Judges 11:35 When he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, "Oh no, my daughter! You have made me very sad, and you are causing me problems because I made a promise to God, and I can't take it back."
Judges 11:36 She said to him, "My father, if you made a promise to God, do to me what you have said, because God has given you revenge against your enemies, the Ammonites."
Judges 11:37 She said to her father, "Please do this for me: let me have two months to walk on the mountains and cry because I am a virgin, with my friends."
Judges 11:38 He said, "Go." So he let her go for two months. She left with her friends and mourned her unwed state on the mountains.
Judges 11:39 After two months, she went back to her father, who did as he had promised in his vow: she never knew a man. This became a tradition in Israel.
Judges 11:40 Every year, the women of Israel would mourn for Jephthah the Gileadite's daughter for four days.

Judges 12:1 The men of Ephraim came together, went north, and said to Jephthah, "Why did you go to fight the Ammonites without inviting us? We will burn down your house on top of you."
Judges 12:2 Jephthah told them, "My people and I had big trouble with the children of Ammon; and when I called for your help, you did not rescue me from them."
Judges 12:3 When I saw you didn't save me, I risked my life and confronted the Ammonites. God gave me victory over them. So why have you come to fight me today?
Judges 12:4 Jephthah brought together all the men of Gilead and battled Ephraim: Gilead's men defeated Ephraim because they were called runaways of Ephraim living among the people of Ephraim and Manasseh.
Judges 12:5 The Gileadites captured the Jordan River crossings before the Ephraimites arrived. When any surviving Ephraimites asked to cross over, the Gileadites would ask, "Are you an Ephraimite?" If he answered, "No,"
Judges 12:6 They told him, "Say 'Shibboleth,'" but he said "Sibboleth," because he couldn't say it correctly. Then they captured him and killed him at the Jordan River crossings. At that time, 42,000 Ephraimites died.
Judges 12:7 Jephthah was a judge over Israel for six years. Then he died and was buried in a city of Gilead.
Judges 12:8 After him, Ibzan from Bethlehem led Israel.
Judges 12:9 He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He sent his daughters to marry men from other places and brought in thirty women from other places for his sons to marry. He was a leader of Israel for seven years.
Judges 12:10 Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
Judges 12:11 After him, Elon from Zebulon led Israel; he led for ten years.
Judges 12:12 Elon from Zebulun died and was buried in Aijalon, in Zebulun land.
Judges 12:13 After him, Abdon, Hillel's son from Pirathon, became Israel's judge.
Judges 12:14 He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys, and he was Israel's leader for eight years.
Judges 12:15 Abdon, Hillel's son from Pirathon, died and was buried in Pirathon, in Ephraim's territory, on the Amalekites' hill.

Judges 13:1 The Israelites did bad things again before God, and God let the Philistines rule over them for forty years.
Judges 13:2 A man named Manoah from Zorah, part of the Danite family, had a wife who could not have children.
Judges 13:3 God's messenger appeared to the woman and said to her, "Look, you have no children, but you will become pregnant and have a son."
Judges 13:4 Be careful, please, do not drink wine or strong alcohol, and do not eat anything unclean.
Judges 13:5 Look, you will become pregnant and have a son; his hair must never be cut because he will be dedicated to God as a Nazarite from birth, and he will start to rescue Israel from the Philistines.
Judges 13:6 The woman went and said to her husband, "A man of God came to me with a face like an angel of God, very awe-inspiring. I didn't ask where he was from, and he didn't tell me his name."
Judges 13:7 He told me, "Look, you will get pregnant and have a son. So do not drink wine or strong alcohol, and do not eat anything impure, because the boy will be dedicated to God as a Nazarite from birth until he dies."
Judges 13:8 Then Manoah prayed to God, saying, "Please God, let the man of God you sent us come again and teach us what we should do for the child who will be born."
Judges 13:9 God listened to Manoah's prayer, and God's angel returned to the woman while she was sitting in the field, but her husband Manoah was not with her.
Judges 13:10 The woman quickly ran to her husband, showed him and said, "Look, the man who visited me the other day has appeared to me again."
Judges 13:11 Manoah got up, followed his wife, and met the man. He asked, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?" And the man replied, "I am."
Judges 13:12 Manoah said, "Let your words happen. How should we raise the child and what should we do for him?"
Judges 13:13 The angel told Manoah, "Make sure the woman follows all that I told her."
Judges 13:14 She must not eat anything from the grapevine, drink wine or strong drinks, or eat anything impure: she should follow all that I instructed her to do.
Judges 13:15 Manoah said to God's angel, "Please stay with us until we prepare a young goat for you."
Judges 13:16 The angel said to Manoah, "Even if you keep me here, I won't eat your bread. If you want to give a burnt offering, you must give it to God." Manoah didn't know he was an angel of God.
Judges 13:17 Manoah asked the angel of God, "What is your name, so we can honor you when your words come true?"
Judges 13:18 The angel of God asked him, "Why do you want to know my name, when it is a secret?"
Judges 13:19 Manoah took a young goat with a food offering and sacrificed it on a rock to God; the angel did amazing things, and Manoah and his wife watched.
Judges 13:20 When the fire rose up to the sky from the altar, God's angel went up in the fire of the altar. Manoah and his wife saw this and fell with their faces to the ground.
Judges 13:21 The angel of God did not show up again to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah realized that he was an angel of God.
Judges 13:22 Manoah said to his wife, "We will surely die because we have seen God."
Judges 13:23 But his wife said to him, "If God wanted to kill us, he wouldn't have accepted our burnt and grain offerings, nor would he have shown us all this or told us such things now."
Judges 13:24 The woman had a son and named him Samson. The boy grew up and God blessed him.
Judges 13:25 God's Spirit started to stir him now and then in Dan's camp, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

Judges 14:1 Samson went to Timnath and saw a Philistine woman there.
Judges 14:2 He went and told his father and mother, "I saw a woman in Timnath from the Philistines; now please get her for me to marry."
Judges 14:3 His father and mother asked him, "Can't you find a woman among your relatives or our people? Why do you want to marry a Philistine woman who is not circumcised?" But Samson told his father, "Get her for me; I like her."
Judges 14:4 His parents did not know that God was behind it, as he wanted a reason to confront the Philistines: because the Philistines ruled over Israel then.
Judges 14:5 Samson, his father, and his mother went to Timnath and when they reached the vineyards there, a young lion suddenly roared at him.
Judges 14:6 God's Spirit came powerfully upon him, and he tore the lion apart as easily as one might tear a young goat, but he did not have any weapon in his hand. Yet he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
Judges 14:7 He went down, talked with the woman, and Samson liked her a lot.
Judges 14:8 Later, he went back to marry her, and on the way, he saw the dead lion. Inside it, there were bees and honey.
Judges 14:9 He took some in his hands, ate as he walked, then gave some to his parents, and they ate too. But he didn't tell them he got the honey from the dead lion's body.
Judges 14:10 His father went down to the woman, and Samson had a feast there, as young men usually did.
Judges 14:11 When they saw him, they brought thirty friends to stay with him.
Judges 14:12 Samson told them, "I have a riddle for you: if you can solve it during the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty sheets and thirty sets of clothes."
Judges 14:13 But if you can't tell me the answer, you must give me thirty sheets and thirty sets of clothes. They said to him, "Tell us your riddle so we can hear it."
Judges 14:14 He told them, "From the eater came food, and from the strong came sweet." But they could not solve the riddle in three days.
Judges 14:15 On the seventh day, they told Samson's wife, "Trick your husband into telling us the answer to his riddle, or we'll burn you and your father's home. Did you invite us only to steal from us?"
Judges 14:16 Samson's wife cried in front of him, saying, "You only hate me, you don't love me. You've given a tricky question to my people but haven't told me the answer." He replied, "Look, I haven't even told my father or mother, so why should I tell you?"
Judges 14:17 She cried in front of him for seven days during their feast. On the seventh day, he gave in and told her the answer because she kept pressing him, and she then explained the puzzle to her people.
Judges 14:18 On the seventh day, before sunset, the city men asked him, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" He replied, "If you hadn't used my cow, you wouldn't have solved my riddle."
Judges 14:19 God's Spirit filled him, and he went to Ashkelon, killed thirty men, took their belongings, and gave clothes to those who solved the riddle. He became very angry and went back to his father's home.
Judges 14:20 Samson's wife was given to the friend he had trusted.

Judges 15:1 After some time, during wheat harvest, Samson brought a young goat to his wife and said, "I will go to my wife's room." But her father wouldn't let him enter.
Judges 15:2 Her father said, "I really thought you hated her, so I gave her to your friend. Isn't her younger sister more beautiful? Please take her instead."
Judges 15:3 Samson said about them, "Now I will be less at fault than the Philistines, even though I upset them."
Judges 15:4 Samson caught three hundred foxes, tied their tails together in pairs, and put a torch between each pair of tails.
Judges 15:5 After he lit the torches, he released them into the Philistines' growing grain, and they burned up the stacks and the growing grain, along with the vineyards and olive trees.
Judges 15:6 Then the Philistines asked, "Who did this?" They were told, "Samson, the Timnite's son-in-law, because he took his wife and gave her to his friend." So the Philistines went and burned her and her father to death.
Judges 15:7 Samson told them, "Even though you did this, I will get revenge on you, and then I'll stop."
Judges 15:8 He struck them hard, causing many to die, then went and lived on top of Etam rock.
Judges 15:9 Then the Philistines moved in, camped in Judah, and spread out in Lehi.
Judges 15:10 The men of Judah asked, "Why have you come to fight us?" They replied, "We've come to capture Samson and to do to him what he did to us."
Judges 15:11 Three thousand men from Judah went up to the top of the rock Etam and said to Samson, "Don't you know that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?" He replied, "I did to them what they did to me."
Judges 15:12 They told him, "We have come to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines." Samson said to them, "Promise me that you won't attack me yourselves."
Judges 15:13 They said to him, "No, we won't kill you. But we will tie you up tightly and give you to them." Then they tied him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.
Judges 15:14 When he arrived at Lehi, the Philistines yelled at him; but God's Spirit rushed into him strongly, and the ropes on his arms turned as weak as burnt flax, and the bindings fell off his hands.
Judges 15:15 He found a fresh donkey jawbone, reached out, took it, and killed a thousand men with it.
Judges 15:16 Samson said, "I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men."
Judges 15:17 After he finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand and named that place Ramathlehi.
Judges 15:18 He was very thirsty, and prayed to God, saying, "You have given your servant this great victory; must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of those who are not circumcised?"
Judges 15:19 God split open a space in the jawbone, and water flowed out. After he drank, his strength returned, and he felt better. So he named that place Enhakkore, which is still in Lehi today.
Judges 15:20 He was Israel's leader for twenty years during the time of the Philistines.

Judges 16:1 Samson went to Gaza, saw a prostitute there, and slept with her.
Judges 16:2 The people of Gaza were told, "Samson has come here." So they surrounded him and set a trap at the city gate all night, staying silent, thinking, "In the morning, when it's light, we will kill him."
Judges 16:3 Samson stayed there until midnight, then at midnight he got up, took the city gate doors and the two posts, carrying them, with the crossbar, on his shoulders, and brought them to the top of a hill facing Hebron.
Judges 16:4 Later, he fell in love with a woman named Delilah who lived in the Sorek Valley.
Judges 16:5 The leaders of the Philistines went to her and said, "Trick him, find out where his great strength comes from and how we can beat him. Then we can tie him up and make him suffer. Each of us will give you eleven hundred silver coins."
Judges 16:6 Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me, where does your great strength come from, and how can you be tied up to subdue you?"
Judges 16:7 Samson told her, "If they tie me up with seven fresh ropes that have not been dried, I will become weak and be just like any other man."
Judges 16:8 The leaders of the Philistines gave her seven fresh ropes that were not dry, and she tied him up with them.
Judges 16:9 Men were hiding, waiting in her room. She said to him, "The Philistines are here, Samson." He snapped the ropes as easily as a string snaps when it burns. So no one discovered his strength.
Judges 16:10 Delilah said to Samson, "Look, you have made fun of me and lied to me. Now please tell me how you can be tied up."
Judges 16:11 He told her, "If they tie me up with brand new ropes that have never been used, I will become weak and be like any other man."
Judges 16:12 Delilah took new ropes, tied Samson with them, and said, "The Philistines are attacking you, Samson." Men hiding in the room waited. He snapped the ropes off his arms easily, like a thread.
Judges 16:13 Delilah said to Samson, "You have made fun of me and lied to me. Tell me, how can you be tied up?" And he told her, "If you weave the seven braids of my hair into the cloth."
Judges 16:14 She secured it with the pin and told him, "The Philistines are attacking you, Samson." He woke up, pulled out the beam's pin and the woven fabric, and left.
Judges 16:15 She said to him, "How can you say 'I love you' when your heart isn't with me? You've made fun of me three times and still haven't told me where your great strength comes from."
Judges 16:16 Every day she nagged Samson with her words and kept pressing him until he was so tired that he felt like dying.
Judges 16:17 He shared all his feelings with her and told her, "I've never cut my hair because I've been dedicated to God since birth. If my hair is cut, I'll lose my strength, become weak, and be just like any other man."
Judges 16:18 When Delilah realized that Samson had shared his deepest secret with her, she summoned the Philistine rulers, telling them, "Come here this time because he has revealed his deepest secret to me." So the Philistine rulers went to her, bringing money with them.
Judges 16:19 She made him sleep on her lap, called a man, and had him shave off the seven braids of his hair. She began to weaken him, and his strength left him.
Judges 16:20 She said, "The Philistines are attacking you, Samson!" He woke up and thought, "I'll get up like before and free myself." But he didn't know that God had left him.
Judges 16:21 But the Philistines captured him, blinded him, took him to Gaza, chained him with bronze shackles, and he worked grinding grain in the prison.
Judges 16:22 However, his hair started to grow back after it was cut.
Judges 16:23 The leaders of the Philistines came together to make a big sacrifice to Dagon, their god, and to celebrate. They said, "Our god has given us Samson, our enemy, into our hands."
Judges 16:24 When the people saw him, they praised their god, saying, "Our god has given us our enemy, the one who destroyed our land and killed many of us."
Judges 16:25 When they were happy, they said, "Bring out Samson to entertain us." So they brought Samson from the prison, and he entertained them. They placed him between the columns.
Judges 16:26 Samson told the boy guiding him, "Let me touch the pillars that support the house so I can lean on them."
Judges 16:27 The house was filled with men and women; all the Philistine leaders were there; and about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.
Judges 16:28 Samson cried out to God, "Please remember me and give me strength just this one time, God, so I can get revenge on the Philistines for my eyes."
Judges 16:29 Samson grabbed the two central pillars supporting the house, one in his right hand and the other in his left.
Judges 16:30 Samson said, "Let me die with the Philistines." He pushed with all his strength, and the building collapsed on the rulers and everyone inside. So he killed more people when he died than while he was alive.
Judges 16:31 His brothers and his father's family went down, took him, and brought him back, burying him between Zorah and Eshtaol in his father Manoah's tomb. He had led Israel for twenty years.

Judges 17:1 A man from the hill country of Ephraim was named Micah.
Judges 17:2 He told his mother, "The 1,100 pieces of silver that were stolen from you, which you cursed and told me about, I have it; I took it." His mother said, "You are blessed by God, my son."
Judges 17:3 When he gave back the 1,100 silver coins to his mother, she said, "I fully devoted this silver to God for my son, to make a carved and cast statue; now I will give it back to you."
Judges 17:4 He gave the money back to his mother, and she took two hundred silver coins to the craftsman. He made a carved and a metal idol, which were kept in Micah's house.
Judges 17:5 Micah had a house with idols, made a special vest and household gods, and appointed one of his sons as his priest.
Judges 17:6 During that time, Israel had no king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
Judges 17:7 A young man from Bethlehem in Judah, from the tribe of Judah, who was a Levite, was staying there.
Judges 17:8 The man left the city of Bethlehem in Judah to stay wherever he could find a place. During his travels, he reached the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah's house.
Judges 17:9 Micah asked him, "Where are you from?" He replied, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am traveling to find a place to stay."
Judges 17:10 Micah said to him, "Live with me, be my father and priest, and I'll pay you ten pieces of silver a year, give you clothes, and provide your food." So the Levite stayed.
Judges 17:11 The Levite agreed to live with the man, and the young man was like a son to him.
