1 Samuel 14:28 One person replied, saying, "Your father strictly told the people with a promise, 'Let the man who eats any food today be cursed.' And the people were weak."
1 Samuel 14:29 Jonathan said, "My father has caused problems in the land. Look how my eyes have brightened because I had a little bit of this honey."
1 Samuel 14:30 Wouldn't there have been even more of the Philistines killed if the people had been allowed to eat the food they took from their enemies today?
1 Samuel 14:31 They defeated the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were very tired.
1 Samuel 14:32 The people rushed to take the loot, grabbing sheep, oxen, and young cows. They killed them right there on the ground and ate them, blood and all.
1 Samuel 14:33 Then they informed Saul, "Look, the people are sinning against God by eating meat with blood in it." And he replied, "You have broken the rules: bring a large stone to me today."
1 Samuel 14:34 Saul said, "Spread out among the people and tell them, 'Each of you bring your ox and sheep here. Kill them, eat them, but do not sin against God by eating the blood.' " And that night, everyone brought their ox and killed them there.
1 Samuel 14:35 Saul built an altar for God; it was the first altar he built for God.
1 Samuel 14:36 Saul said, "Let's attack the Philistines at night, take their things until morning, and not leave any of them alive." They replied, "Do whatever you think is best." Then the priest said, "Let's go to God here."
1 Samuel 14:37 Saul asked God for advice, "Should I chase the Philistines? Will you give them to Israel?" But God did not answer him that day.
1 Samuel 14:38 Saul said, "Come here, all the leaders of the people. Find out and see where the sin happened today."
1 Samuel 14:39 Because God lives, who saves Israel, even if it's my son Jonathan, he must die. But no one among the people responded to him.
1 Samuel 14:40 He told all of Israel, "You stay on one side, and my son Jonathan and I will be on the other side." The people told Saul, "Do what you think is best."
1 Samuel 14:41 Therefore, Saul asked God of Israel for a clear answer with lots. Saul and Jonathan were chosen; the others were not.
1 Samuel 14:42 Saul said, "Decide by chance between me and my son Jonathan." And Jonathan was chosen.
1 Samuel 14:43 Then Saul asked Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." Jonathan answered, "I only tasted a little honey with the tip of the stick I was holding, and now I must die."
1 Samuel 14:44 Saul replied, "If God doesn't punish me and even more if you don't die, Jonathan."
1 Samuel 14:45 The people asked Saul, "Should Jonathan die, who has brought this big victory in Israel? No, God wouldn't want that: as long as God lives, not even one hair from his head will drop to the ground; for today he fought alongside God." So, the people saved Jonathan, and he did not die.
1 Samuel 14:46 Then Saul stopped chasing the Philistines, and the Philistines went back to their own land.
1 Samuel 14:47 Saul became king of Israel and fought all his enemies around him, Moab, Ammon's people, Edom, Zobah's kings, and the Philistines. Wherever he went, he defeated them.
1 Samuel 14:48 He assembled an army, defeated the Amalekites, and saved Israel from those who had plundered them.
1 Samuel 14:49 Saul's sons were Jonathan, Ishui, and Melchishua. His two daughters were named Merab, the oldest, and Michal, the younger.
1 Samuel 14:50 Saul's wife's name was Ahinoam, Ahimaaz's daughter, and his army's leader was Abner, Ner's son, Saul's uncle.
1 Samuel 14:51 Kish was Saul's father, and Ner, Abner's father, was Abiel's son.
1 Samuel 14:52 There was intense war with the Philistines throughout Saul's time; whenever Saul saw a strong or brave man, he brought him into his service.

1 Samuel 15:1 Samuel also said to Saul, "God sent me to anoint you as king over his people, over Israel; so now listen to what God says."
1 Samuel 15:2 God says, "I remember what Amalek did to Israel, how he ambushed them on their journey from Egypt."
1 Samuel 15:3 Go and attack Amalek, destroy everything they own, and show no mercy; kill everyone, men and women, babies and children, cows and sheep, camels and donkeys.
1 Samuel 15:4 Saul brought the people together and counted them at Telaim: 200,000 soldiers on foot and 10,000 men from Judah.
1 Samuel 15:5 Saul came to an Amalekite city and hid in the valley.
1 Samuel 15:6 Saul said to the Kenites, "Go away, leave this place away from the Amalekites, so I don't destroy you with them. You were kind to all the Israelites when they left Egypt." So the Kenites moved away from the Amalekites.
1 Samuel 15:7 Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, near Egypt.
1 Samuel 15:8 He captured Agag, the king of the Amalekites, alive and killed all the people with the sword.
1 Samuel 15:9 But Saul and the people saved Agag, the best sheep, cows, fat young animals, lambs, and all the good things, and did not completely destroy them; but everything that was bad and worthless, they completely destroyed.
1 Samuel 15:10 God spoke to Samuel, saying,
1 Samuel 15:11 I regret making Saul king because he stopped following me and didn't obey my commands. This made Samuel sad, and he cried out to God all night.
1 Samuel 15:12 When Samuel got up early to see Saul in the morning, someone told Samuel that Saul went to Carmel, made a memorial there, and then moved on and went down to Gilgal.
1 Samuel 15:13 Samuel went to Saul, and Saul told him, "God bless you; I have done what God commanded."
1 Samuel 15:14 Samuel asked, "What is the meaning of the sheep's bleating and the oxen's lowing that I hear?"
1 Samuel 15:15 Saul said, "They got them from the Amalekites because the people kept the best sheep and cattle to offer to God; and we have completely destroyed the rest."
1 Samuel 15:16 Samuel told Saul, "Wait, and I will tell you what God told me tonight." And Saul said to him, "Go ahead."
1 Samuel 15:17 Samuel said, When you thought you were not important, weren't you chosen to lead the tribes of Israel, and didn't God appoint you as king over Israel?
1 Samuel 15:18 God sent you on a mission, telling you, "Go and completely destroy the sinful Amalekites and battle them until they are wiped out."
1 Samuel 15:19 Why didn't you listen to God's voice, but instead took the loot and did wrong in God's eyes?
1 Samuel 15:20 Saul said to Samuel, "Yes, I did what God told me, and I followed the path God gave me. I captured King Agag of Amalek and completely destroyed the Amalekites."
1 Samuel 15:21 But the people took the best of the sheep and cattle, which were supposed to be completely destroyed, to offer as sacrifices to God in Gilgal.
1 Samuel 15:22 And Samuel said, "Does God enjoy burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as listening to God? Look, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen is better than the best parts of rams."
1 Samuel 15:23 Rebellion is like witchcraft, and being stubborn is like doing wrong and worshiping idols. Since you have rejected God's message, He has also rejected you as king.
1 Samuel 15:24 Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned because I broke God's command and your words, since I was afraid of the people and listened to them."
1 Samuel 15:25 Please forgive my sin now, and come back with me so I can worship God.
1 Samuel 15:26 Samuel told Saul, "I will not go back with you because you ignored God's message, and God has decided you won't be king of Israel anymore."
1 Samuel 15:27 As Samuel was leaving, he grabbed the edge of his robe, and it tore.
1 Samuel 15:28 Samuel said to him, "God has taken the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to someone who lives near you, who is better than you."
1 Samuel 15:29 God, the Strength of Israel, will not lie or change His mind, because He is not a human who would need to change His mind.
1 Samuel 15:30 He said, "I have sinned; but please respect me now in front of my people's leaders and Israel, and come back with me so I can worship God."
1 Samuel 15:31 So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped God.
1 Samuel 15:32 Then Samuel said, "Bring me Agag, the king of the Amalekites." And Agag came to him carefully. And Agag said, "Certainly the worst of death is over."
1 Samuel 15:33 Samuel said, "Just as the sword has left women without children, your mother will be without children among women." And Samuel cut Agag into pieces before God in Gilgal.
1 Samuel 15:34 Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went to his home in Gibeah.
1 Samuel 15:35 Samuel did not visit Saul again until Saul died. But Samuel felt sad for Saul, and God wished he had not made Saul king over Israel.

1 Samuel 16:1 God said to Samuel, "How long will you be sad for Saul, when I have decided he will not be king over Israel? Put oil in your horn and go. I will send you to Jesse of Bethlehem because I have chosen one of his sons to be king."
1 Samuel 16:2 And Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears it, he will kill me." And God said, "Take a young cow with you and say, 'I have come to make a sacrifice to God.'"
1 Samuel 16:3 Invite Jesse to the offering, and I will tell you what to do: you shall anoint for me the one I point out to you.
1 Samuel 16:4 Samuel did as God said and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders shook with fear when he arrived and asked, "Do you come in peace?"
1 Samuel 16:5 He said, "I've come to offer a sacrifice to God peacefully. Get ready and join me in the sacrifice." He set Jesse and his sons apart as holy and invited them to the sacrifice.
1 Samuel 16:6 When they arrived, he saw Eliab and thought, "Certainly, God's chosen one is here."
1 Samuel 16:7 But God told Samuel, Do not look at his face or how tall he is, because I have not chosen him. God does not see the way people see; people look at the outside, but God looks at the heart.
1 Samuel 16:8 Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him walk in front of Samuel. And he said, God has not chosen this one either.
1 Samuel 16:9 Then Jesse had Shammah walk by, but he said, "God has not chosen this one either."
1 Samuel 16:10 Jesse had seven of his sons walk in front of Samuel. Samuel told Jesse, "God has not chosen these."
1 Samuel 16:11 Samuel asked Jesse, "Are all your children here?" Jesse replied, "The youngest is still out, taking care of the sheep." Then Samuel said to Jesse, "Send for him; we won't sit down until he arrives."
1 Samuel 16:12 He sent for him and brought him in. He had red cheeks, a handsome face, and looked good. God said, "Stand up, anoint him; this is the one."
1 Samuel 16:13 Samuel took the oil horn and put oil on David in front of his brothers. God's Spirit came on David from that day on. Then Samuel got up and went to Ramah.
1 Samuel 16:14 God's Spirit left Saul, and a bad spirit from God troubled him.
1 Samuel 16:15 Saul's servants told him, "Look, an evil spirit from God is troubling you."
1 Samuel 16:16 Please tell your servants here to find a skilled harp player. When the bad spirit from God comes on you, he can play and you will feel better.
1 Samuel 16:17 Saul told his servants, "Find a man who can play music well and bring him to me."
1 Samuel 16:18 A servant replied, "Look, I've seen Jesse of Bethlehem's son, who is skilled at playing music, a brave strong man, a fighter, smart in decision-making, good-looking, and God is with him."
1 Samuel 16:19 So Saul sent messages to Jesse, saying, "Send me your son David, who is with the sheep."
1 Samuel 16:20 Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a bottle of wine, and a young goat, and sent them with his son David to Saul.
1 Samuel 16:21 David went to Saul, stood in front of him, Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor carrier.
1 Samuel 16:22 Saul sent a message to Jesse, saying, "Please let David come and see me, because I like him."
1 Samuel 16:23 When the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, David played the harp with his hand, and Saul felt better, and the evil spirit left him.

1 Samuel 17:1 The Philistines brought their armies together to fight and met at Shochoh, part of Judah, setting up camp between Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephesdammim.
1 Samuel 17:2 Saul and the Israelite men came together, camped by the Elah Valley, and arranged their soldiers to fight the Philistines.
1 Samuel 17:3 The Philistines were on one mountain, and Israel was on another, with a valley between them.
1 Samuel 17:4 A great fighter named Goliath from Gath, who was very tall—nine feet and four inches—came out of the Philistine army camp.
1 Samuel 17:5 He wore a bronze helmet and a body armor made of metal, which weighed five thousand bronze coins.
1 Samuel 17:6 He wore bronze armor on his legs and a bronze plate on his back.
1 Samuel 17:7 His spear's handle was like a weaver's large pole; the spear's tip weighed six hundred iron shekels, and a man carrying a shield walked in front of him.
1 Samuel 17:8 He stood and shouted to Israel's armies, "Why have you come to arrange for battle? Am I not a Philistine and you, Saul's servants? Pick a man for yourselves, and let him come down to fight me."
1 Samuel 17:9 If he can fight me and kill me, then we will serve you; but if I beat him and kill him, then you will serve us.
1 Samuel 17:10 The Philistine said, "I challenge Israel's armies today; give me a man to fight with me."
1 Samuel 17:11 When Saul and all Israel heard what the Philistine said, they were upset and very scared.
1 Samuel 17:12 David was the son of an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah, named Jesse, who had eight sons. Jesse was an old man during Saul's time.
1 Samuel 17:13 Jesse's three oldest sons joined Saul in the fight: their names were Eliab the eldest, then Abinadab, and the third, Shammah.
1 Samuel 17:14 David was the youngest, and the three oldest followed Saul.
1 Samuel 17:15 David left Saul and went back to take care of his father's sheep in Bethlehem.
1 Samuel 17:16 The Philistine approached every morning and evening for forty days.
1 Samuel 17:17 Jesse told his son David, "Now take an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the camp."
1 Samuel 17:18 Take these ten cheeses to the commander of their unit, see how your brothers are doing, and bring back something to show they are well.
1 Samuel 17:19 Now Saul, they, and all the Israelite men were in the Elah Valley, fighting the Philistines.
1 Samuel 17:20 David got up early, left the sheep with someone to watch them, and did as Jesse told him. He arrived at the battlefield as the army was heading out to fight and raised a battle cry.
1 Samuel 17:21 Israel and the Philistines arranged their armies for battle, facing each other.
1 Samuel 17:22 David left his supplies with the supply keeper, ran to the soldiers, and greeted his brothers.
1 Samuel 17:23 While he was talking to them, the Philistine warrior from Gath, named Goliath, came out of the Philistine ranks and repeated his challenge, and David heard it.
1 Samuel 17:24 When the men of Israel saw the man, they ran away from him, very scared.
1 Samuel 17:25 The men of Israel asked, "Have you seen this man who has come? He has come to challenge Israel. Whoever kills him will get a lot of wealth from the king, will marry the king's daughter, and will make his family free in Israel."
1 Samuel 17:26 David asked the men near him, "What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? Who does this uncircumcised Philistine think he is to insult the armies of the living God?"
1 Samuel 17:27 The people responded to him, saying, "The man who kills him will be treated this way."
1 Samuel 17:28 When David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking to the men, he became angry at David and asked, "Why did you come here? Who's taking care of the few sheep you have in the desert? I know you're proud and mischievous; you just came to watch the fight."
1 Samuel 17:29 David said, "What did I do now? Isn't there a reason?"
1 Samuel 17:30 He turned away from him to someone else and spoke in the same way. The people replied to him just as they had before.
1 Samuel 17:31 When they heard what David said, they told Saul, and he called for him.
1 Samuel 17:32 David told Saul, "No one should be afraid; I will go and fight this Philistine."
1 Samuel 17:33 Saul told David, "You can't fight this Philistine; you're only a young boy, and he has been a warrior since he was young."
1 Samuel 17:34 David said to Saul, "I, your servant, was watching my father's sheep when a lion and a bear came and took a lamb from the group."
1 Samuel 17:35 I followed and struck him, saving the victim from his mouth. When he attacked me, I grabbed his beard, hit him, and killed him.
1 Samuel 17:36 I killed both the lion and the bear, and this Philistine who has insulted God's army will be like one of them.
1 Samuel 17:37 David also said, "God who saved me from the lion's paw and the bear's paw, will save me from this Philistine's hand." Saul told David, "Go, and may God be with you."
1 Samuel 17:38 Saul gave David his armor; he put a brass helmet on David’s head and a metal coat on him.
1 Samuel 17:39 David put on his sword over his armor and tried to walk, but he wasn't used to them. David told Saul, "I can't walk with these; I'm not used to them." So, David took them off.
1 Samuel 17:40 He took his staff, picked five smooth stones from the stream, placed them in his shepherd's pouch, carried his sling, and approached the Philistine.
1 Samuel 17:41 The Philistine advanced and came close to David, with the shield-bearer in front of him.
1 Samuel 17:42 When the Philistine looked and saw David, he looked down on him because he was just a young boy with a healthy, handsome face.
1 Samuel 17:43 The Philistine said to David, "Do you think I'm a dog that you come at me with sticks?" And the Philistine swore at David by his gods.
1 Samuel 17:44 The Philistine said to David, "Come here, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the animals of the land."
1 Samuel 17:45 David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with a sword, spear, and shield, but I come to you in the name of God, the God of Israel's armies, whom you have insulted."
1 Samuel 17:46 Today, God will let me defeat you. I will strike you down and cut off your head. Then I will give the dead bodies of the Philistine army to the birds and wild animals. And everyone on earth will know that there is a God in Israel.
1 Samuel 17:47 Everyone here will understand that God does not save by sword or spear, because the fight is God's, and he will let us capture you.
1 Samuel 17:48 When the Philistine got up, approached, and came close to David, David quickly ran towards the army to face the Philistine.
1 Samuel 17:49 David reached into his bag, took out a stone, threw it, and hit the Philistine in the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell face down to the ground.
1 Samuel 17:50 David beat the Philistine with a sling and a stone, hitting and killing him, even though David had no sword in his hand.
1 Samuel 17:51 So David ran, stood over the Philistine, took his sword, pulled it out, killed him, and cut off his head. When the Philistines saw their hero was dead, they ran away.
1 Samuel 17:52 The men of Israel and Judah stood up, yelled, and chased the Philistines until they reached the valley and the gates of Ekron. The injured Philistines dropped along the road to Shaaraim, all the way to Gath and Ekron.
1 Samuel 17:53 The Israelites came back from chasing the Philistines and they took things from their tents.
1 Samuel 17:54 David took the Philistine's head to Jerusalem; he stored the armor in his tent.
1 Samuel 17:55 When Saul saw David go to fight the Philistine, he asked Abner, his army commander, "Abner, who is this young man’s father?" And Abner replied, "As sure as you live, king, I don't know."
1 Samuel 17:56 The king said, "Find out who the young man's father is."
1 Samuel 17:57 After David killed the Philistine, Abner brought him to Saul, holding the Philistine's head.
1 Samuel 17:58 Saul asked him, "Who is your father, young man?" And David replied, "I am the son of your servant Jesse from Bethlehem."

1 Samuel 18:1 When he finished talking to Saul, Jonathan felt very close to David and loved him as he loved himself.
1 Samuel 18:2 Saul kept him that day and didn't let him return to his father's house anymore.
1 Samuel 18:3 Jonathan and David made a promise, because Jonathan loved David as much as he loved himself.
1 Samuel 18:4 Jonathan took off his robe, gave it to David, along with his clothes, sword, bow, and belt.
1 Samuel 18:5 David went wherever Saul sent him and acted wisely. Saul put him in charge of the soldiers, and all the people and Saul's helpers liked him.
1 Samuel 18:6 When they arrived, as David came back from killing the Philistine, the women from all the Israeli cities came out to greet King Saul. They were singing, dancing, and playing tambourines and musical instruments with happiness.
1 Samuel 18:7 The women talked to each other as they celebrated and said, "Saul has killed thousands, and David has killed ten thousands."
1 Samuel 18:8 Saul was very angry because he didn't like what was said; he thought, "They credit David with tens of thousands, but me with only thousands. What else can he get but the kingdom?"
1 Samuel 18:9 From that day on, Saul watched David closely.
1 Samuel 18:10 The next day, an evil spirit from God came over Saul, and he started to prophesy in the house. David played his harp as he usually did, with Saul holding a spear in his hand.
1 Samuel 18:11 Saul threw the spear because he thought, "I will hit David and pin him to the wall." But David dodged it twice.
1 Samuel 18:12 Saul feared David because God was with David and had left Saul.
1 Samuel 18:13 So Saul sent him away and put him in charge of a thousand men; he led the people in their movements.
1 Samuel 18:14 David acted wisely in everything he did, and God was with him.
1 Samuel 18:15 So when Saul noticed that he acted very smartly, he became scared of him.
1 Samuel 18:16 All of Israel and Judah loved David because he led them and returned safely.
1 Samuel 18:17 Saul said to David, "Look at my older daughter Merab. I will let you marry her. Just be brave for me and fight God's battles." Saul thought, "I won't hurt him myself, but let the Philistines hurt him."
1 Samuel 18:18 David said to Saul, "Who am I, and what is my life or my father's family in Israel, that I should become the king's son-in-law?"
1 Samuel 18:19 At the time Merab, Saul's daughter, was supposed to marry David, she was married to Adriel the Meholathite instead.
1 Samuel 18:20 Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David; when Saul heard, it made him happy.
1 Samuel 18:21 Saul said, "I will let him marry her so she can trap him, and so the Philistines can fight him." So Saul told David, "Today you will become my son-in-law by marrying one of my daughters."
1 Samuel 18:22 Saul told his servants, "Talk to David in secret and say, 'Look, the king likes you, and all his servants love you. So now become the king's son-in-law.'"
1 Samuel 18:23 Saul's servants told David these things. David asked, "Do you think it's easy to become the king's son-in-law, when I am a poor and little-valued man?"
1 Samuel 18:24 Saul's servants told him, "David spoke in this way."
1 Samuel 18:25 Saul said, "Tell David this: The king doesn't want a dowry, just one hundred Philistine foreskins to get revenge on his enemies." But Saul planned to have the Philistines kill David.
1 Samuel 18:26 When his servants told David this, David was happy to become the king's son-in-law, and the time was not yet over.
1 Samuel 18:27 So David got up and took his men, and they killed two hundred Philistine men; David took their foreskins and presented the full number to the king, so he could become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David as his wife.
1 Samuel 18:28 Saul saw and understood that God was with David, and that Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him.
1 Samuel 18:29 Saul became even more scared of David and remained his enemy all the time.
1 Samuel 18:30 The Philistine leaders went out, and after they did, David acted more wisely than all of Saul's servants, so his reputation grew greatly.

1 Samuel 19:1 Saul told his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David.
1 Samuel 19:2 Jonathan, Saul's son, really liked David. Jonathan warned David, "Saul, my father, wants to kill you. So please be careful and stay hidden in a secret place until morning."
1 Samuel 19:3 I will go out and stand next to my father in the field where you are, and I will talk to my father about you; and what I see, I will tell you.
1 Samuel 19:4 Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul, and said to him, "The king should not do wrong to his servant David; he has not sinned against you, and his actions towards you have been very good."
1 Samuel 19:5 He risked his life, killed the Philistine, and God saved all Israel; you saw it and were happy. So why would you sin and kill innocent David for no reason?
1 Samuel 19:6 Saul listened to what Jonathan said, and Saul promised, saying, "As God lives, he will not be killed."
1 Samuel 19:7 Jonathan called David and showed him everything. Jonathan took David to Saul, and David was with Saul as before.
1 Samuel 19:8 War broke out again: David went and fought the Philistines, killed many, and they ran away from him.
1 Samuel 19:9 An evil spirit from God came upon Saul as he sat in his house with his spear in hand, while David played music.
1 Samuel 19:10 Saul tried to hit David with a spear, aiming to pin him to the wall, but David dodged and the spear stuck in the wall. Then David ran away and got away that night.
1 Samuel 19:11 Saul sent people to David's house to watch and kill him in the morning. David's wife Michal warned him, "If you don't escape tonight, you will be killed tomorrow."
1 Samuel 19:12 Michal helped David escape by lowering him from a window, and he ran away and got away.
1 Samuel 19:13 Michal took an idol, placed it in the bed, put a goat hair pillow under its head, and covered it with a cloth.
1 Samuel 19:14 When Saul sent people to capture David, she said, "He is sick."
1 Samuel 19:15 Saul sent his messengers to check on David again, telling them, "Bring him to me in his bed, so I can kill him."
1 Samuel 19:16 When the messengers entered, they found an idol in the bed with a goat hair pillow as its headrest.
1 Samuel 19:17 Saul asked Michal, "Why did you trick me and let my enemy go so he could escape?" Michal replied to Saul, "He told me, 'Let me go; why should I kill you?'"
1 Samuel 19:18 David ran away, escaped, and went to Samuel in Ramah to tell him everything Saul had done to him. Then David and Samuel stayed in Naioth.
1 Samuel 19:19 Someone told Saul, "Look, David is in Naioth at Ramah."
1 Samuel 19:20 Saul sent people to capture David, but when they saw a group of prophets speaking God's messages and Samuel leading them, God's Spirit came on Saul's messengers, and they started to speak God's messages too.
1 Samuel 19:21 When Saul heard, he sent more messengers, and they also spoke God's messages. Saul sent messengers a third time, and they spoke God's messages as well.
1 Samuel 19:22 He also went to Ramah and arrived at a big well in Sechu. He asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" Someone replied, "Look, they're at Naioth in Ramah."
1 Samuel 19:23 He went to Naioth in Ramah, and God's Spirit was also upon him. He continued to speak God's messages until he reached Naioth in Ramah.
1 Samuel 19:24 He also took off his clothes, and before Samuel, he acted like a prophet. He lay there without clothes all day and night. That's why people ask, "Is Saul also a prophet?"

1 Samuel 20:1 David ran away from Naioth in Ramah, went to Jonathan and asked, "What have I done? What is my wrong? Why does your father want to kill me?"
1 Samuel 20:2 He said to him, "God won't let it happen; you won't die. Look, my father won't do anything, big or small, without telling me. And why would my father keep this from me? It's not true."
1 Samuel 20:3 David promised again and said, "Your father knows well that you like me; and he says, 'Don't tell Jonathan, so he won't be sad.' But as surely as God lives, and as you are alive, I am only a step away from death."
1 Samuel 20:4 Jonathan said to David, "Whatever your heart wants, I will do it for you."
1 Samuel 20:5 David said to Jonathan, "Look, tomorrow is the new moon, and I'm expected to eat with the king. But let me go and hide in the field until the evening of the third day."
1 Samuel 20:6 If your father notices I'm gone, say, "David really needed to go to Bethlehem, his hometown, because there's an annual family sacrifice there."
1 Samuel 20:7 If he says all is well, your servant will be at peace; but if he's really angry, then know he's planning something bad.
1 Samuel 20:8 So you should treat your servant well, because you have made a promise to God with me. But if I've done something wrong, you should punish me yourself; why would you take me to your father?
1 Samuel 20:9 Jonathan said, "Don't think that! If I knew for sure that my father planned to harm you, wouldn't I tell you?"
1 Samuel 20:10 Then David asked Jonathan, "Who will let me know? Or what if your father speaks to you harshly?"
1 Samuel 20:11 Jonathan said to David, "Come on, let's go to the field." So both of them went to the field.
1 Samuel 20:12 Jonathan said to David, "God of Israel, when I talk to my father tomorrow or the day after, if he feels kindly toward David and I don't send you a message to let you know, then..."
1 Samuel 20:13 God will deal with Jonathan severely if he doesn't, but if my father intends to harm you, I will tell you and let you leave safely. May God be with you as He was with my father.
1 Samuel 20:14 While I am still alive, you must show me God's kindness, so I will not die.
1 Samuel 20:15 But you must not stop being kind to my family forever, not even when God has removed all David's enemies from the earth.
1 Samuel 20:16 Jonathan made a promise with David's family, saying, "Let God hold David's enemies responsible."
1 Samuel 20:17 Jonathan made David promise again, because he loved him as much as he loved himself.
1 Samuel 20:18 Jonathan said to David, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed because your seat will be empty."
1 Samuel 20:19 After you've stayed for three days, go down fast and go to the place where you hid before, and stay near the stone Ezel.
1 Samuel 20:20 I will shoot three arrows to the side, as if I were aiming at a target.
1 Samuel 20:21 Look, I will send a boy, telling him, 'Go, look for the arrows.' If I say to the boy, 'Look, the arrows are near you, get them,' then you come back; it means you are safe and nothing is wrong; as God lives.
1 Samuel 20:22 If I tell the young man, 'The arrows are past you,' then leave, because God has sent you away.
1 Samuel 20:23 About the issue we talked about, remember, God will be between you and me forever.
1 Samuel 20:24 David hid in the field, and when the new moon arrived, the king sat down to eat.
1 Samuel 20:25 The king sat on his throne as usual, next to the wall. Jonathan stood up, and Abner sat next to Saul, but David's spot was empty.
1 Samuel 20:26 Saul said nothing that day because he thought, "Something has happened to him; he's not pure; surely he's not pure."
1 Samuel 20:27 The next day, the second day of the month, David's seat was empty. Saul asked his son Jonathan, "Why hasn't Jesse's son come to eat, neither yesterday nor today?"
1 Samuel 20:28 Jonathan replied to Saul, "David really asked for my permission to go to Bethlehem."
1 Samuel 20:29 He said, "Please let me go, because our family has a sacrifice in the city; my brother told me to come, and if you're okay with it, please let me go and see my brothers." That's why he didn't come to the king's table.
1 Samuel 20:30 Saul got angry at Jonathan and said to him, "You son of a stubborn and rebellious woman, don't I know you've picked Jesse's son to your own shame and to the shame of your mother?"
1 Samuel 20:31 As long as Jesse's son lives, you will not secure your position or your kingdom. So send for him now, because he must die.
1 Samuel 20:32 Jonathan answered his father Saul, "Why should he be killed? What did he do?"
1 Samuel 20:33 Saul threw a spear at him to hit him: by this Jonathan knew that his father had decided to kill David.
1 Samuel 20:34 Jonathan got up from the table very angry and didn't eat anything on the second day of the month because he was upset about David, since his father had embarrassed him.
1 Samuel 20:35 In the morning, Jonathan went to the field at the scheduled time with David and a young boy with him.
1 Samuel 20:36 He told his boy, "Run and find the arrows I shoot." While the boy was running, he shot an arrow past him.
1 Samuel 20:37 When the boy reached the place where Jonathan had shot the arrow, Jonathan called out to him, "Isn't the arrow farther than where you are?"
1 Samuel 20:38 Jonathan called out to the boy, "Hurry, run fast, don't stop." And Jonathan's boy picked up the arrows and went back to him.
1 Samuel 20:39 The boy didn't know anything; only Jonathan and David knew about it.
1 Samuel 20:40 Jonathan gave his weapons to his young servant and said to him, "Go, take them to the city."
1 Samuel 20:41 As soon as the boy left, David got up from the southern side, bowed down with his face to the ground three times, and they hugged and cried together until David was overwhelmed.
1 Samuel 20:42 Jonathan told David, "Go in peace, because we both promised in God's name, saying, 'God be between you and me, and between your descendants and my descendants forever.'" Then David left, and Jonathan went back to the city.

1 Samuel 21:1 David went to Nob to see Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech was scared when he saw David and asked, "Why are you alone and no one is with you?"
1 Samuel 21:2 David told Ahimelech the priest, "The king has given me a task and told me, 'Don't let anyone know about the task I'm sending you on, or what I've instructed you to do.' I've told my men to meet at a certain place."
1 Samuel 21:3 What do you have to give me? Please give me five loaves of bread or whatever you have now.
1 Samuel 21:4 The priest replied to David, "I don't have any regular bread, only holy bread. The young men can have some if they have stayed away from women."
1 Samuel 21:5 David replied to the priest, "Honestly, we have not been near women for three days since I left. The young men's belongings are clean, and even though the bread is ordinary, it is like it was made holy today."
1 Samuel 21:6 So the priest gave him sacred bread because only the special bread was there, which had been removed from God's presence to be replaced with fresh bread on the day it was taken out.
1 Samuel 21:7 A man who worked for Saul was there that day, held in God's presence; his name was Doeg, an Edomite, and he was the top shepherd working for Saul.
1 Samuel 21:8 David asked Ahimelech, "Do you have a spear or sword here? I didn't bring mine because I had to hurry for the king's task."
1 Samuel 21:9 The priest said, "Here is Goliath's sword wrapped in cloth behind the vest. If you want it, take it, because it's the only one here." David replied, "There's none like it; give it to me."
1 Samuel 21:10 David got up and ran away that day because he was afraid of Saul, and he went to Achish, the king of Gath.
1 Samuel 21:11 Achish's servants asked him, "Isn't this David, the king of the country? Didn't people sing about him in their dances, saying, 'Saul has killed his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
1 Samuel 21:12 David remembered these words and was very afraid of Achish, the king of Gath.

1 Samuel 22:3 David left and went to Mizpeh in Moab. He said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do for me."

1 Samuel 22:14 Ahimelech replied to the king, "And who is as loyal among all your servants as David, who is the king's son-in-law, does as you ask, and is respected in your household?"

1 Samuel 22:20 One of Ahimelech's sons, named Abiathar, got away and ran to join David.
1 Samuel 22:21 Abiathar told David that Saul had killed God's priests.
1 Samuel 22:22 David told Abiathar, "I knew that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, he would definitely tell Saul. I am responsible for the death of everyone in your father's family."
1 Samuel 22:23 Stay with me, don't be afraid: whoever wants to hurt me wants to hurt you too, but you'll be safe with me.

1 Samuel 23:1 They informed David, "Look, the Philistines are attacking Keilah and stealing from the grain floors."

1 Samuel 23:3 David's men told him, "Look, we're scared here in Judah. How much more scared will we be if we go to Keilah to fight the Philistine armies?"

1 Samuel 23:7 Someone told Saul that David had gone to Keilah. Saul said, "God has given him to me because he's trapped in a town with gates and bars."
1 Samuel 23:8 Saul gathered all the people to fight, to go to Keilah, to surround David and his men.
1 Samuel 23:9 David knew Saul was secretly planning to harm him; he told Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod here."

1 Samuel 23:11 Will the people of Keilah give me to him? Will Saul come, as I have heard? God of Israel, please tell me. And God said, He will come.
1 Samuel 23:12 David asked, "Will the people of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?" And God answered, "They will hand you over."
1 Samuel 23:13 David and his six hundred men got up and left Keilah, going wherever they could. Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, so he stopped pursuing him.
1 Samuel 23:14 David stayed in the wilderness in secure places and was in a mountain in the Ziph wilderness. Saul looked for him every day, but God did not let Saul capture him.
1 Samuel 23:15 David knew Saul had come to take his life, and he was in the Ziph wilderness, hiding in the forest.
1 Samuel 23:16 Jonathan, Saul's son, got up and went to David in the forest, where he encouraged him to trust in God.
1 Samuel 23:17 He told him, "Don't be afraid: my father Saul will not catch you; you will be king of Israel, and I will be right by your side; and my father Saul knows this."
1 Samuel 23:18 They both made a promise before God; David stayed in the forest, and Jonathan went home.
1 Samuel 23:19 The people of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Isn't David hiding in our strongholds in the forest, on the hill of Hachilah, south of Jeshimon?"
1 Samuel 23:20 So now, O king, come down as you wish to come down; and it will be our job to hand him over to the king.
1 Samuel 23:21 Saul said, "God bless you; you have shown me kindness."
1 Samuel 23:22 Please go, get ready, find out exactly where he usually goes, and who has seen him there; because I hear he is very sneaky.
1 Samuel 23:23 Be aware and learn all the hiding spots where he hides, then return to me to confirm, and I will come with you. If he is in the country, I will search for him in all the areas of Judah.
1 Samuel 23:24 They got up and went to Ziph ahead of Saul; David and his men were in the Maon desert, on the south side of Jeshimon.
1 Samuel 23:25 Saul and his men went looking for him. They told David, so he went down to a rock and stayed in the Maon desert. When Saul found out, he chased David in the Maon desert.
1 Samuel 23:26 Saul was on one side of the mountain, David and his men on the other side. David quickly tried to escape because he was afraid of Saul. Saul and his men surrounded David and his men to capture them.
1 Samuel 23:27 A messenger came to Saul and said, "Hurry and come, because the Philistines have attacked the land."
1 Samuel 23:28 So Saul stopped chasing David and fought the Philistines instead. That's why they named that place "Rock of Escape."
1 Samuel 23:29 David left there and lived in the fortresses at Engedi.

1 Samuel 24:1 When Saul came back from chasing the Philistines, he heard, "Look, David is in the Engedi desert."
1 Samuel 24:2 Saul took three thousand picked men from all of Israel and went to look for David and his men on the cliffs where the wild goats live.
1 Samuel 24:3 He reached the sheep pens on the path, where there was a cave; Saul went inside to rest, and David with his men stayed further inside the cave.
1 Samuel 24:4 David's men said to him, "This is the day God told you about, saying, 'I will give your enemy to you, and you can do what you think is right.' " Then David quietly cut a piece from Saul's robe.
1 Samuel 24:5 Later, David felt guilty because he had cut a piece of Saul's robe.
1 Samuel 24:6 He told his men, "God won't let me do this to my master, God's chosen one, by harming him because he is chosen by God."
1 Samuel 24:7 David stopped his men with his words and did not let them attack Saul. But Saul left the cave and continued his journey.
1 Samuel 24:8 David got up later, left the cave, and called out to Saul, "My king." When Saul turned around, David bowed down with his face to the ground.
1 Samuel 24:9 David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to people who say, 'Look, David wants to harm you'?"
1 Samuel 24:10 Look, today your eyes saw that God has given you into my hands in the cave. Some urged me to kill you, but I spared you, saying I won't harm my master because he is God's chosen one.
1 Samuel 24:11 Also, my father, look, yes, look at the piece of your robe in my hand: because I cut the piece of your robe and did not kill you, understand and see that I have no bad intentions or guilt in my actions, and I have not done wrong against you; but still you chase after me to take my life.
1 Samuel 24:12 God will judge between you and me, and God will take revenge for me on you, but I will not harm you.
1 Samuel 24:13 An old saying goes, evil comes from the evil, but I will not hurt you.
1 Samuel 24:14 Who is the king of Israel chasing? Who are you after? Just a dead dog, a flea.
1 Samuel 24:15 So let God be the judge. Let God decide between you and me. Let God look at this, stand up for me, and save me from your power.
1 Samuel 24:16 After David finished speaking to Saul, Saul asked, "Is that your voice, my son David?" Then Saul cried out loud with tears.
1 Samuel 24:17 He told David, "You are better than me because you have done good to me, even though I have done bad to you."
1 Samuel 24:18 Today you showed how you have been good to me; because when God gave me to you, you did not kill me.
1 Samuel 24:19 If someone finds their enemy, would they let them go safely? So, may God reward you well for what you did for me today.
1 Samuel 24:20 And now, I know you will definitely become king, and that you will firmly hold the kingdom of Israel.
1 Samuel 24:21 Promise me now, by God, that you will not end my family line after I am gone, and that you will not erase my name from my father's house.
1 Samuel 24:22 And David promised Saul. Then Saul went home while David and his men went to the fortress.

1 Samuel 25:1 Samuel died; all the people of Israel met, mourned him, and buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David left and went to the Paran wilderness.
1 Samuel 25:2 In Maon, there was a man with a lot of property in Carmel. He was very rich, with three thousand sheep and one thousand goats, and he was cutting the wool off his sheep in Carmel.
1 Samuel 25:3 The man's name was Nabal, and his wife was named Abigail. She was smart and very beautiful, but Nabal was rude and did bad things. He came from Caleb's family.
1 Samuel 25:4 David learned in the desert that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
1 Samuel 25:5 David sent ten young men and told them, "Go to Carmel, visit Nabal, and say hello to him for me."
1 Samuel 25:6 You should tell the person who is doing well, "I wish you peace, and peace to your home, and peace to everything you own."
1 Samuel 25:7 I've heard you're shearing sheep. Your shepherds stayed with us, and we didn't harm them. Nothing was stolen from them the whole time they were in Carmel.
1 Samuel 25:8 Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So please, let your young men be treated well, because we have come on a good day. Please give whatever you can to your servants and to your son David.
1 Samuel 25:9 When David's men arrived, they told Nabal everything David had said and then stopped talking.
1 Samuel 25:10 Nabal replied to David's servants, "Who is David? Who is Jesse's son? Many servants run away from their masters these days."
1 Samuel 25:11 Should I give my bread, water, and meat that I prepared for my shearers to men when I don't know where they come from?
1 Samuel 25:12 David's young men turned back, went to him, and told him everything that was said.
1 Samuel 25:13 David told his men, "Put on your swords." They all put on their swords, and David put on his too. About four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed with their belongings.
1 Samuel 25:14 One of the young men informed Abigail, Nabal's wife, "Look, David sent messengers from the desert to greet our master, but he insulted them."
1 Samuel 25:15 The men were very kind to us, and we were not harmed, nor did we lose anything, while we were with them in the fields.
1 Samuel 25:16 They protected us day and night the whole time we were with them tending the sheep.
1 Samuel 25:17 Now, understand and think about what you will do; for harm is planned against our master and all his family. He is so wicked that no one can talk to him.
1 Samuel 25:18 Abigail quickly took 200 loaves, two bottles of wine, five cooked sheep, five servings of roasted grain, 100 bunches of raisins, and 200 fig cakes, and put them on donkeys.
1 Samuel 25:19 She said to her servants, "Go ahead of me; I'll follow you." But she didn't tell her husband Nabal.
1 Samuel 25:20 As she traveled on the donkey, she passed by the hill's hidden part, and there was David with his men coming toward her; and she met them.
1 Samuel 25:21 David thought, "I protected this man's property in the wilderness for nothing; nothing of his was lost, and yet he has repaid me with harm instead of good."
1 Samuel 25:22 God do the same and more to David's enemies if by morning I leave alive any males.
1 Samuel 25:23 When Abigail saw David, she hurried, got off the donkey, fell in front of David with her face to the ground, and bowed down.
1 Samuel 25:24 She fell at his feet and said, "Let the blame be on me, my lord, let the blame be on me. Please let me, your servant, speak to you, and listen to what I have to say."
1 Samuel 25:25 Please, do not pay attention to this worthless man, Nabal, for he is just like his name suggests: a fool. I, your servant, did not see the men you sent.
1 Samuel 25:26 So now, my lord, since God is alive and your life is safe because God kept you from killing and taking revenge yourself, may your enemies and those who want to harm you become like Nabal.
1 Samuel 25:27 This gift that I, your servant, have brought, let it be given to the young men who follow you.
1 Samuel 25:28 Please forgive your servant's mistake. God will surely give you a lasting home because you fight God's battles, and you've done no wrong throughout your life.
1 Samuel 25:29 A man has come to chase you and wants to take your life, but my lord's life is safe with God, like in a protected bundle; and God will throw your enemies' lives away, like stones from a sling.
1 Samuel 25:30 When God does all the good things he promised you and makes you the leader of Israel;
1 Samuel 25:31 This will not upset you or trouble your heart, if you have killed without reason or taken revenge. But when God is good to you, please remember me.
1 Samuel 25:32 David said to Abigail, "God of Israel is blessed for sending you to meet me today."
1 Samuel 25:33 May your advice be blessed, and may you be blessed for stopping me today from killing and taking revenge by my own hand.
1 Samuel 25:34 Truly, as the God of Israel lives, who stopped me from harming you, if you had not hurried to meet me, by morning, no male in Nabal's household would have survived.
1 Samuel 25:35 David took what she gave him and said to her, "Go home in peace. I have listened to what you said and I accept you."
1 Samuel 25:36 Abigail went to Nabal and saw he was having a big feast in his house like a king. Nabal was happy and very drunk, so she said nothing to him until morning.
1 Samuel 25:37 In the morning, when Nabal was sober and his wife told him what happened, his heart stopped and he became like a stone.
1 Samuel 25:38 About ten days later, God punished Nabal and he died.
1 Samuel 25:39 When David learned Nabal had died, he said, "Praise God, who defended me against Nabal's insults and kept me from doing wrong. God made Nabal's evil come back on him." Then David sent a message to Abigail, asking her to be his wife.
1 Samuel 25:40 When David's servants arrived at Carmel and met Abigail, they told her, "David sent us to bring you to him so you can become his wife."
1 Samuel 25:41 She stood up, bowed down to the ground, and said, "Please, let me be your servant to wash your servants' feet."
1 Samuel 25:42 Abigail hurried, got up, and rode on a donkey, with five of her young women following her. She followed David's messengers and became his wife.
1 Samuel 25:43 David also married Ahinoam from Jezreel, and she became one of his wives too.
1 Samuel 25:44 Saul gave his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Phalti, Laish's son, from Gallim.

1 Samuel 26:1 The Ziphites went to Saul in Gibeah and said, "Isn't David hiding on Hachilah hill, which is near Jeshimon?"
1 Samuel 26:2 Then Saul got up and went to the Ziph desert with three thousand selected Israeli men to look for David in the Ziph desert.
1 Samuel 26:3 Saul camped on Hachilah hill, near Jeshimon. David stayed in the wilderness and knew Saul was following him there.
1 Samuel 26:4 David sent spies and found out that Saul had truly arrived.
1 Samuel 26:5 David got up and went to where Saul was camped. He saw where Saul and Abner, son of Ner and leader of Saul's army, were sleeping. Saul was in a circle trench, and his troops were camped around him.
1 Samuel 26:6 David spoke to Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai, Zeruiah's son and Joab's brother, "Who will come with me to see Saul in the camp?" Abishai replied, "I will go with you."
1 Samuel 26:7 David and Abishai went to the people at night, and saw Saul sleeping in the trench with his spear in the ground by his head, while Abner and the people slept around him.
1 Samuel 26:8 Abishai told David, "Today God has given your enemy to you. Please let me strike him with my spear to the ground in one shot, and I won't need to hit him again."
1 Samuel 26:9 David said to Abishai, "Don't kill him. Who can attack God's chosen one and be innocent?"
1 Samuel 26:10 David also said, "As God lives, God will strike him down, or his time will come to die, or he will go into battle and die."
1 Samuel 26:11 God won't let me harm his chosen one; please take the spear and the water jug near his head, and let's leave.
1 Samuel 26:12 David took the spear and the jug of water from near Saul's head; they left without anyone seeing or knowing, since everyone was asleep because God had made them fall into a deep sleep.
1 Samuel 26:13 David crossed over and stood on top of a distant hill with a wide space between them.
1 Samuel 26:14 David called out to the people and to Abner, son of Ner, saying, "Aren't you going to answer, Abner?" Abner replied, "Who are you, shouting to the king?"
1 Samuel 26:15 David said to Abner, "Aren't you a brave man? Who in Israel is like you? So why didn't you protect the king? Someone from the people came to kill the king."
1 Samuel 26:16 What you did is not good. As God lives, you should die because you didn't protect your master, God's chosen one. Now, look for the king's spear and the jug of water that was near his head.
1 Samuel 26:17 Saul recognized David's voice and asked, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David answered, "Yes, it's my voice, my lord, O king."
1 Samuel 26:18 He asked, "Why does my master chase his servant? What did I do? What wrong is in my hand?"
1 Samuel 26:19 So now, I ask you, let the king listen to his servant. If God has made you angry with me, let Him take a gift. But if people have done it, let God curse them, because they have forced me away today from God's land, telling me, 'Go worship other gods.'
1 Samuel 26:20 So now, don't let my blood spill on the ground in front of God. The king of Israel has come out to chase after me as if I'm just a flea, like someone hunting a bird in the hills.
1 Samuel 26:21 Saul said, "I have sinned. Come back, David my son. I won't hurt you anymore because you valued my life today. I see now that I have been very foolish and made a big mistake."
1 Samuel 26:22 David replied, "Look, here is the king's spear! Let one of the young men come and get it."
1 Samuel 26:23 God rewards everyone for their goodness and loyalty; although God gave you into my power today, I did not want to harm God's chosen one.
1 Samuel 26:24 Look, just as your life was very valuable to me today, so may my life be valuable in God's sight, and may He rescue me from all troubles.
1 Samuel 26:25 Saul said to David, "God bless you, my son David. You will do great things and succeed." Then David left and Saul went back to his home.

1 Samuel 27:1 David thought to himself, "I will one day die by Saul's hand. The best thing I can do is quickly run away to the Philistine territory; then Saul will give up looking for me in Israel, and I will be safe from him."
1 Samuel 27:2 David got up and went with his six hundred men to Achish, son of Maoch, the king of Gath.
1 Samuel 27:3 David lived with Achish in Gath, along with his men and their families, including David's two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, who was Nabal's widow, from Carmel.
1 Samuel 27:4 Saul heard that David had escaped to Gath, so he stopped searching for him.
1 Samuel 27:5 David said to Achish, "If you now favor me, please give me a place in one of the country towns where I can live. Why should I, your servant, live in the capital city with you?"
1 Samuel 27:6 That day, Achish gave him Ziklag, so Ziklag belongs to the kings of Judah to this day.
1 Samuel 27:7 David lived in the land of the Philistines for one year and four months.
1 Samuel 27:8 David and his men went up and attacked the Geshurites, the Gezrites, and the Amalekites, because these people had lived in the area from Shur to Egypt since ancient times.
1 Samuel 27:9 David attacked the land, killed everyone, took the sheep, cows, donkeys, camels, and clothes, then went back to Achish.
1 Samuel 27:10 Achish asked, "Where did you go today?" David answered, "To the southern part of Judah, the southern area of the Jerahmeelites, and the southern territory of the Kenites."
1 Samuel 27:11 David did not let any man or woman live to go and report in Gath, thinking, "They might inform against us, saying, 'This is what David does, and this will be his way as long as he stays in the land of the Philistines.'"
1 Samuel 27:12 Achish trusted David, thinking, "He has made his people Israel completely hate him; so he will be my servant forever."

1 Samuel 28:1 During that time, the Philistines prepared their armies for war to battle Israel. Achish told David, be certain that you and your men will join me in the fight.
1 Samuel 28:2 David said to Achish, "You will see what I can do." And Achish said to David, "So I will make you my bodyguard forever."
1 Samuel 28:3 Samuel had died, all Israel mourned for him, and they buried him in his hometown of Ramah. Saul had also removed all the mediums and fortune-tellers from the land.
1 Samuel 28:4 The Philistines came together and camped in Shunem. Saul brought all of Israel together, and they camped in Gilboa.
1 Samuel 28:5 When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was scared, and his heart shook a lot.
1 Samuel 28:6 When Saul asked God, God did not answer him, not in dreams, not with Urim, and not through prophets.
1 Samuel 28:7 Saul said to his servants, "Find me a woman who can speak with spirits, so I can go to her and ask for her help." His servants told him, "There is a woman who can speak with spirits in Endor."
1 Samuel 28:8 Saul changed his clothes to hide who he was, and took two men with him. They went at night to a woman, and Saul asked her, "Please use your spirit to tell me the future, and call up the person I ask for."
1 Samuel 28:9 The woman said to him, "Look, you know what Saul did; he got rid of the people who talk to spirits and the wizards from the land. So why are you setting a trap for my life, to make me die?"
1 Samuel 28:10 Saul promised her by God, saying, "As God lives, you will not be punished for this."
1 Samuel 28:11 The woman asked, "Who should I call for you?" He replied, "Call Samuel for me."
1 Samuel 28:12 When the woman saw Samuel, she shouted loudly and said to Saul, "Why did you trick me? You are Saul."
1 Samuel 28:13 The king told her, "Don't be scared. What did you see?" The woman said to Saul, "I saw spirits coming up from the ground."
1 Samuel 28:14 He asked her, "What does he look like?" She answered, "An old man is coming up, wearing a cloak." Then Saul knew it was Samuel, and he bowed down with his face to the ground.
1 Samuel 28:15 Samuel asked Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me back?" Saul replied, "I am deeply troubled because the Philistines are fighting me, and God has left me. He doesn't answer me anymore, not through prophets, nor in dreams. So, I've called you to tell me what to do."
1 Samuel 28:16 Then Samuel asked, "Why do you ask me when God has left you and become your enemy?"
1 Samuel 28:17 God did what he said through me: God has taken the kingdom from you and given it to your neighbor, David.
1 Samuel 28:18 Because you did not listen to God's voice or carry out his strong anger against Amalek, God has done this to you today.
1 Samuel 28:19 God will also let Israel fall to the Philistines along with you: tomorrow you and your sons will join me: God will also let the army of Israel fall to the Philistines.
1 Samuel 28:20 Saul immediately fell to the ground, very afraid because of Samuel's words. He had no strength because he had not eaten any food all day or night.
1 Samuel 28:21 The woman approached Saul, noticed he was very troubled, and told him, "Look, I, your servant, have followed your instructions. I risked my life and listened to what you told me."
1 Samuel 28:22 So now, please listen to me, your servant, and let me give you some food. Eat it and gain strength for your journey.
1 Samuel 28:23 He refused, saying, "I won't eat." But his servants and the woman insisted until he listened. Then he got up from the ground and sat on the bed.
1 Samuel 28:24 The woman had a healthy calf at home; she quickly slaughtered it, took flour, made dough, and baked bread without yeast from it.
1 Samuel 28:25 She gave it to Saul and his attendants; they ate, then got up and left that night.

1 Samuel 29:1 The Philistines brought all their armies together at Aphek, while the Israelites set up camp by a spring in Jezreel.
1 Samuel 29:2 The leaders of the Philistines marched by hundreds and by thousands, while David and his men were at the back with Achish.
1 Samuel 29:3 The Philistine leaders asked, "Why are these Hebrews here?" Achish replied to the Philistine leaders, "Isn't this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, who has been with me for some time now, and I have found nothing wrong with him up to today?"
1 Samuel 29:4 The Philistine leaders were angry with him and said, "Send this man back to the place you assigned him. He shouldn't fight with us, or he might turn against us during the battle. How could he win back his master's favor if not by taking the heads of our soldiers?"
1 Samuel 29:5 Isn't this David, the one they celebrated in dances, saying, Saul killed thousands, but David killed tens of thousands?
1 Samuel 29:6 Then Achish spoke to David and said, "As surely as God lives, you have been honest, and your actions with me in the army have been good; I've seen nothing bad in you from when you first came to me until now. But the rulers don't like you.
1 Samuel 29:7 So now, go back and leave in peace, so you don't upset the Philistine leaders.
1 Samuel 29:8 David asked Achish, "What have I done wrong? What fault have you found in me, after all the time I've been with you, that I can't go and fight the king's enemies?"
1 Samuel 29:9 Achish replied to David, "I know you are as good as an angel of God to me. But the Philistine leaders have said, 'He cannot join us in the fight.'"
1 Samuel 29:10 So get up early in the morning with your master's servants who are with you. Once it's early and light, go on your way.
1 Samuel 29:11 David and his men got up early in the morning to leave and go back to the land of the Philistines. The Philistines went to Jezreel.

1 Samuel 30:1 When David and his men arrived at Ziklag on the third day, they found that the Amalekites had attacked the south and Ziklag, defeating Ziklag and setting it on fire.
1 Samuel 30:2 They captured the women there without killing anyone, big or small, and took them away before continuing on their journey.
1 Samuel 30:3 David and his men arrived at the city and saw it was burned down; their wives, sons, and daughters had been kidnapped.
1 Samuel 30:4 David and his followers raised their voices, cried until they could cry no more.
1 Samuel 30:5 David's two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow from Carmel, were kidnapped.
1 Samuel 30:6 David was very upset because the people talked about throwing stones at him, since they were all sad about their sons and daughters. But David found strength in God.
1 Samuel 30:7 David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Please bring me the ephod." And Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
1 Samuel 30:8 David asked God, "Should I chase this group? Will I catch them?" God replied, "Chase them. You will definitely catch them and get everything back."
1 Samuel 30:9 David and his six hundred men went and reached the Besor brook, where those left behind stayed.
1 Samuel 30:10 David and four hundred men chased after them, while two hundred men stayed back because they were too weak to cross Besor Creek.
1 Samuel 30:11 They found an Egyptian in the field, took him to David, and gave him bread to eat; they also gave him water to drink.
1 Samuel 30:12 They gave him some fig cake and two bunches of raisins. After he ate, he felt better because he hadn't eaten any bread or drunk any water for three days and nights.
1 Samuel 30:13 David asked him, "Who are you and where do you come from?" He answered, "I am a young Egyptian, the servant of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me because I got sick three days ago."
1 Samuel 30:14 We attacked the southern Cherethites, the lands of Judah, and Caleb's southern area; and we set fire to Ziklag.
1 Samuel 30:15 David asked him, "Can you lead me to this group?" He replied, "Promise me by God that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master, and I will lead you to them."
1 Samuel 30:16 When he brought him down, they were scattered everywhere on the ground, eating, drinking, and dancing, happy about all the valuable things they had taken from the Philistine and Judah territories.
1 Samuel 30:17 David attacked them from dusk until the evening of the next day; none of them survived except four hundred young men who rode on camels and ran away.
1 Samuel 30:18 David got back everything the Amalekites had taken, and he saved his two wives.
1 Samuel 30:19 They were missing nothing at all, whether big or small, sons or daughters, plunder, or anything they had taken: David got everything back.
1 Samuel 30:20 David took all the sheep and cows, which they led in front of the other animals, and said, "This is what David has captured."
1 Samuel 30:21 David approached the two hundred men who were too weak to follow him and had stayed at Besor Creek. They came out to greet David and his companions. When David got close, he greeted them.
1 Samuel 30:22 The bad men with David replied, "Since they didn't come with us, we won't share the loot we got back, except give each one his wife and kids so they can take them and leave."
1 Samuel 30:23 David said, "My brothers, we must not do this with what God has given us. He has kept us safe and handed over the enemy that attacked us."
1 Samuel 30:24 Who will listen to you about this? Just as the one who fights gets a share, so does the one who stays with the supplies: they will share equally.
1 Samuel 30:25 From that day on, God set it as a rule and law for Israel, and it's still followed today.
1 Samuel 30:26 When David arrived in Ziklag, he sent some of the captured goods to the leaders of Judah, to his friends, with the message, "Here is a gift for you from the goods taken from God's enemies."
1 Samuel 30:27 To those in Bethel, those in south Ramoth, and those in Jattir,
1 Samuel 30:28 To those in Aroer, and to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa,
1 Samuel 30:29 To those in Rachal, those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and those in the cities of the Kenites,
1 Samuel 30:30 To those in Hormah, to those in Chorashan, and to those in Athach,
1 Samuel 30:31 To those in Hebron and all the places where David and his men used to visit.

1 Samuel 31:1 The Philistines battled Israel: the Israelites ran from the Philistines and many were killed on Mount Gilboa.
1 Samuel 31:2 The Philistines chased Saul and his sons closely; they killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Melchishua, Saul's sons.
1 Samuel 31:3 The fight was very bad for Saul, and archers shot him; he was badly hurt by the archers.
1 Samuel 31:4 Saul said to his helper, "Pull out your sword and stab me with it; otherwise these enemies will come and kill me and treat me badly." But his helper wouldn't do it because he was very scared. So Saul took a sword and killed himself with it.
1 Samuel 31:5 When his helper saw Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died with him.
1 Samuel 31:6 Saul died, along with his three sons, his armor bearer, and all his men, on the same day.
1 Samuel 31:7 When the Israelites across the valley and the Jordan River saw that the Israelites were running away and that Saul and his sons had died, they left their towns and ran away; then the Philistines moved in and lived there.
1 Samuel 31:8 The next day, when the Philistines came to take things from the dead bodies, they found Saul and his three sons dead on Mount Gilboa.
1 Samuel 31:9 They cut off his head, took his armor, and sent them throughout the land of the Philistines to show them at the temples of their gods and to the people.
1 Samuel 31:10 They placed his armor in the temple of Ashtaroth and hung his body on the wall of Bethshan.
1 Samuel 31:11 When the people of Jabeshgilead heard what the Philistines did to Saul;
1 Samuel 31:12 All the brave men got up, traveled all night, took Saul's body and his sons' bodies from the Bethshan wall, and went to Jabesh where they burned them.
1 Samuel 31:13 They collected their bones, buried them under a tree at Jabesh, and did not eat for seven days.

2 Samuel 1:1 After Saul died and David came back from defeating the Amalekites, David stayed in Ziklag for two days.
2 Samuel 1:2 On the third day, a man left Saul's camp with torn clothes and dirt on his head. When he reached David, he fell to the ground to show respect.
2 Samuel 1:3 David asked him, "Where did you come from?" He replied, "I escaped from the Israelite camp."
2 Samuel 1:4 David asked him, "What happened? Please tell me." He replied, "The soldiers ran away from the fight, many are dead or dying; and Saul with his son Jonathan are both dead too."
2 Samuel 1:5 David asked the young man who told him, "How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?"
2 Samuel 1:6 The young man who told me said, "I was at Mount Gilboa by chance, and there was Saul leaning on his spear; the chariots and riders were close behind him."
2 Samuel 1:7 When he looked back, he saw me and called to me. I answered, "I'm here."
2 Samuel 1:8 He asked me, "Who are you?" And I replied, "I am an Amalekite."
2 Samuel 1:9 He said to me again, "Please stand on me and kill me, because I'm in great pain and still alive."
2 Samuel 1:10 I stood over him and killed him because I knew he couldn't survive after he fell. I took the crown from his head and the bracelet from his arm, and I brought them here to my lord.
2 Samuel 1:11 Then David grabbed his clothes and tore them; and all the men with him did the same.
2 Samuel 1:12 They were sad, cried, and didn't eat until evening for Saul, for his son Jonathan, for God's people, and for Israel, because they had died in battle.
2 Samuel 1:13 David asked the man who brought him news, "Where are you from?" He replied, "I am the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite."
2 Samuel 1:14 And David asked him, "Weren't you scared to raise your hand to kill God's chosen one?"
2 Samuel 1:15 David called a young man and said, "Go close and attack him." So he struck him, and he died.
2 Samuel 1:16 David said to him, "You are responsible for your own death; your own words have condemned you, saying, 'I killed God's chosen one.'"
2 Samuel 1:17 David mourned for Saul and his son Jonathan with this sad song:
2 Samuel 1:18 He also told them to teach the children of Judah how to use the bow; see, it is written in the book of Jasher.
2 Samuel 1:19 Israel's beauty is killed on your hills: how the strong have fallen!
2 Samuel 1:20 Don't talk about it in Gath, don't announce it in Askelon's streets; so the Philistine girls won't be happy, so the girls of those not circumcised won't celebrate.
2 Samuel 1:21 Mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, or fields for harvests, because there the strong's shield was thrown away without care, Saul's shield, as if he was never anointed with oil.
2 Samuel 1:22 Jonathan's bow did not turn away from the blood of the dead, and the strong ones' fat, and Saul's sword did not come back without success.
2 Samuel 1:23 Saul and Jonathan were kind and nice while they lived, and even in death, they stayed together. They were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
2 Samuel 1:24 Women of Israel, cry for Saul, who dressed you in red with beautiful things, who added gold jewelry to your clothes.
2 Samuel 1:25 The strong have fallen in battle! Oh Jonathan, you were killed on the heights.
2 Samuel 1:26 I am sad for you, my brother Jonathan: you were very kind to me: your love for me was amazing, more than the love of women.
2 Samuel 1:27 The strong have fallen, and the tools of battle are gone!

2 Samuel 2:1 After this, David asked God, "Should I go to one of Judah's cities?" And God told him, "Go." Then David asked, "Which city should I go to?" And God answered, "To Hebron."
2 Samuel 2:2 David went up there with his two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, who was Nabal's wife from Carmel.
2 Samuel 2:3 David took his soldiers and their families to live in the towns near Hebron.
2 Samuel 2:4 The men of Judah came and made David king over Judah. They told David that the men of Jabesh Gilead buried Saul.
2 Samuel 2:5 David sent messengers to the men of Jabeshgilead and said to them, "God bless you for being so kind to your leader Saul by burying him."
2 Samuel 2:6 Now God show you kindness and honesty, and I will also repay you for this kindness because you have done this.
2 Samuel 2:7 So now, make your hands strong and be brave, because your leader Saul has died, and the people of Judah have made me their king.
2 Samuel 2:8 Abner, Ner's son and leader of Saul's army, took Ishbosheth, Saul's son, to Mahanaim.
2 Samuel 2:9 They made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and all of Israel.
2 Samuel 2:10 Ishbosheth, Saul's son, was forty when he started to rule over Israel and ruled for two years. The people of Judah supported David.
2 Samuel 2:11 David ruled as king in Hebron over Judah for seven years and six months.
2 Samuel 2:12 Abner, Ner's son, and Ishbosheth's servants, Saul's son, left Mahanaim for Gibeon.
2 Samuel 2:13 Joab, Zeruiah's son, and David's servants left and met by the pool of Gibeon. They sat down, one group on one side of the pool and the other group on the opposite side.
2 Samuel 2:14 Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men get up and show their skills in front of us." Joab replied, "Let them get up."
2 Samuel 2:15 Then twelve men from Benjamin who were with Ishbosheth, Saul's son, stood up and crossed over, along with twelve of David's servants.
2 Samuel 2:16 They each grabbed their companion by the head and stuck their sword into the other's side, and they fell down together. Therefore, that place was named Field of Swords, in Gibeon.
2 Samuel 2:17 There was a very tough fight that day; and Abner and the Israelites were defeated by David's men.
2 Samuel 2:18 Zeruiah had three sons there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a wild deer.
2 Samuel 2:19 Asahel chased Abner without turning either right or left from following him.
2 Samuel 2:20 Then Abner turned around and asked, "Are you Asahel?" And he replied, "Yes, I am."
2 Samuel 2:21 Abner told him, "Move to your right or left, grab one of the soldiers, and take his armor." But Asahel wouldn't stop chasing him.
2 Samuel 2:22 Abner said to Asahel again, "Stop following me. Why should I hit you and knock you down? How could I then face your brother Joab?"
2 Samuel 2:23 Even though he wouldn't move aside, Abner hit him with the back end of the spear below his chest, so the spear went through him; he collapsed there and died. Everyone who arrived where Asahel had fallen and died stopped in their tracks.
2 Samuel 2:24 Joab and Abishai chased after Abner, and the sun set as they reached the hill of Ammah, near Giah on the road through the desert of Gibeon.
2 Samuel 2:25 The descendants of Benjamin joined together behind Abner, forming one group, and stood on a hilltop.
2 Samuel 2:26 Then Abner called out to Joab, "Can't you see that endless fighting will only bring bitterness in the end? How long will it be before you order your men to stop chasing their own brothers?"
2 Samuel 2:27 Joab said, "As sure as God lives, if you hadn't spoken, by morning the people would have all stopped following their leader."
2 Samuel 2:28 Joab sounded a trumpet, and everyone stopped, no longer chasing Israel or fighting.
2 Samuel 2:29 Abner and his men walked all night across the plain, crossed the Jordan River, traveled through Bithron, and arrived at Mahanaim.
2 Samuel 2:30 Joab stopped chasing Abner. When he brought all the people together, David's servants were missing nineteen men, including Asahel.
2 Samuel 2:31 David's men defeated the Benjamin tribe and Abner's soldiers, so 360 men died.
2 Samuel 2:32 They carried Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb in Bethlehem. Joab and his men traveled all night and arrived at Hebron at dawn.

2 Samuel 3:1 There was a long war between Saul's family and David's family: but David's family became stronger and stronger, while Saul's family became weaker and weaker.
2 Samuel 3:2 David had sons in Hebron. His first son was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel.
2 Samuel 3:3 David's second son was Chileab, with his wife Abigail who was Nabal the Carmelite's widow, and the third son was Absalom, whose mother was Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur.
2 Samuel 3:4 The fourth was Adonijah, Haggith's son; the fifth was Shephatiah, Abital's son.
2 Samuel 3:5 David's sixth son, Ithream, was born from his wife Eglah while they were in Hebron.
2 Samuel 3:6 During the war between Saul's family and David's family, Abner became a strong leader for Saul's family.
2 Samuel 3:7 Saul had a partner named Rizpah, Aiah's daughter. Ishbosheth asked Abner, "Why did you sleep with my father's partner?"
2 Samuel 3:8 Abner was very angry because of Ishbosheth's words and said, "Am I worth nothing, who has been loyal to Saul your father's family, his brothers, and his friends today, and haven't handed you over to David, yet you blame me today for a problem with this woman?"
2 Samuel 3:9 May God do to Abner, and even more, unless I do to him as God has promised to David.
2 Samuel 3:10 To move the kingdom from Saul's family and to establish David's rule over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.
2 Samuel 3:11 He could not reply to Abner at all, because he was afraid of him.
2 Samuel 3:12 Abner sent people to David to speak for him, asking, "Who owns the land?" He also said, "Make a deal with me, and I will support you to unite all of Israel under you."
2 Samuel 3:13 He said, "Okay, I will make an agreement with you. But I demand one thing: you cannot see me unless you bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see me."
2 Samuel 3:14 David sent messengers to Ishbosheth, Saul's son, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I married for a hundred Philistine foreskins."
2 Samuel 3:15 Ishbosheth sent for her and took her from her husband, Phaltiel the son of Laish.
2 Samuel 3:16 Her husband followed her, crying as he went to Bahurim. Then Abner told him, "Go back." And he went back.
2 Samuel 3:17 Abner spoke to the leaders of Israel, saying, "You once wanted David to be your king."
2 Samuel 3:18 Go ahead and do it because God has said about David, "Through my servant David, I will rescue my people Israel from the Philistines and all their enemies."
2 Samuel 3:19 Abner also spoke to the people of Benjamin and then went to tell David in Hebron everything that seemed right to Israel and all the Benjaminites.
2 Samuel 3:20 Abner went to see David in Hebron with twenty men. David gave a feast for Abner and his men.
2 Samuel 3:21 Abner told David, "I will get up and go to bring all of Israel to you, the king, so they can join with you. Then you will rule over everything you want." And David let Abner go, and he left peacefully.
2 Samuel 3:22 David's men and Joab returned from chasing a group and brought back a lot of loot, but Abner was not with David in Hebron; David had let him go, and he left peacefully.
2 Samuel 3:23 When Joab and his army arrived, they told Joab, "Abner, Ner's son, came to the king, and the king let him go, and he left peacefully."
2 Samuel 3:24 Then Joab went to the king and asked, "What have you done? Look, Abner came to you; why did you send him away so he's completely gone?"
2 Samuel 3:25 You know Abner, Ner's son, came to trick you, to find out where you go and what you do.
2 Samuel 3:26 When Joab left David, he sent people to get Abner and they brought him back from Sirah's well, but David didn't know about it.
2 Samuel 3:27 After Abner came back to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside in the gate to talk privately and then struck him below the fifth rib, and Abner died for killing Joab's brother Asahel.
2 Samuel 3:28 After David heard this, he said, "I and my kingdom are innocent before God forever concerning the death of Abner, Ner's son."
2 Samuel 3:29 Let the blame fall on Joab and his family; may his family never be without someone who is sick, has a skin disease, needs a cane to walk, dies by the sword, or goes hungry.
2 Samuel 3:30 Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
2 Samuel 3:31 David said to Joab and all the people with him, "Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and weep for Abner." And King David walked behind the coffin.
2 Samuel 3:32 They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king cried aloud at Abner's grave; all the people also cried.
2 Samuel 3:33 The king mourned for Abner, saying, "Did Abner die like a fool?"
2 Samuel 3:34 Your hands were not tied, nor were your feet chained; like someone falls before evil men, so you fell. And all the people cried for you again.
