2 Samuel 23:17 He said, "I could never do this, God! Isn't this the blood of the men who risked their lives?" So he refused to drink it. This is what the three brave men did.
2 Samuel 23:18 Abishai, Joab's brother and Zeruiah's son, was the leader of the three. He raised his spear against three hundred and killed them, earning fame among the three.
2 Samuel 23:19 Wasn't he the most respected of the three? So he became their leader, but he did not reach the level of the top three.
2 Samuel 23:20 Benaiah, son of Jehoiada and a brave man from Kabzeel, did many brave things. He killed two strong Moabite warriors and also killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day.
2 Samuel 23:21 He killed an Egyptian, a handsome man. The Egyptian carried a spear, but he confronted him with only a stick, took the spear from the Egyptian, and killed him with it.
2 Samuel 23:22 Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, did these things and was famous among the three mighty men.
2 Samuel 23:23 He was more respected than the thirty, but he did not reach the level of the top three. David made him the leader of his bodyguards.
2 Samuel 23:24 Asahel, Joab's brother, was one of the thirty; Elhanan, the son of Dodo from Bethlehem.
2 Samuel 23:25 Shammah from Harod, Elika from Harod,
2 Samuel 23:26 Helez from Palti, Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa,

2 Samuel 24:1 God became angry with Israel again, and he influenced David to count the people of Israel and Judah.
2 Samuel 24:2 The king told Joab, the army commander with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people, so I can know how many there are."
2 Samuel 24:3 Joab said to the king, "May God increase your people a hundred times over, and may you, the king, see it. But why do you, the king, want this?"
2 Samuel 24:4 Despite what the king commanded, Joab and the army leaders went out to count the people of Israel.
2 Samuel 24:5 They crossed the Jordan River and camped in Aroer, to the east of the city by the Gad River, near Jazer.
2 Samuel 24:6 They went to Gilead and the land of Tahtimhodshi, then to Danjaan, and near Zidon.
2 Samuel 24:7 They reached the fortress of Tyre and the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites, then moved south towards Judah, as far as Beersheba.
2 Samuel 24:8 After exploring the whole land for nine months and twenty days, they arrived in Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 24:9 Joab told the king the total number of people, and there were 800,000 brave men with swords in Israel; and 500,000 men in Judah.
2 Samuel 24:10 David felt guilty after he counted the people. David told God, "I have sinned a lot by doing this. Now, I ask you, God, please forgive your servant's wrongdoing, for I have been very foolish."
2 Samuel 24:11 When David got up in the morning, God's message came to the prophet Gad, David's advisor, saying,
2 Samuel 24:12 Go and tell David, God says, I give you three choices; pick one, so I can do it for you.
2 Samuel 24:13 Gad went to David, told him, and asked, "Do you want seven years of hunger in your land, or to run away for three months from your enemies chasing you, or to have three days of disease in your land? Think about it and tell me what reply I should give to the one who sent me."
2 Samuel 24:14 David said to Gad, "I am in big trouble. Let's surrender to God because he is very merciful, and I don't want to be captured by people."
2 Samuel 24:15 God sent a disease on Israel from morning until the set time, and 70,000 men died from Dan to Beersheba.
2 Samuel 24:16 When the angel reached out to destroy Jerusalem, God changed his mind about the harm, and told the angel killing the people, "That's enough, stop now." The angel of God was at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
2 Samuel 24:17 David spoke to God when he saw the angel striking the people and said, "I have sinned, and I have done wrong; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your punishment be on me and my family."
2 Samuel 24:18 Gad went to David that day and told him, "Go, build an altar to God on Araunah the Jebusite's threshing floor."
2 Samuel 24:19 David went up as God had ordered, following Gad's advice.
2 Samuel 24:20 Araunah saw the king and his helpers coming toward him, so Araunah went out and bowed down with his face to the ground before the king.
2 Samuel 24:21 Araunah asked, "Why has the king come to his servant?" David replied, "To buy your threshing floor to make an altar for God, so the sickness can be stopped from hurting the people."
2 Samuel 24:22 Araunah said to David, "Let the king choose and give whatever he wants: see, there are oxen for burning as a sacrifice, and tools for threshing and wood from the oxen equipment."
2 Samuel 24:23 Araunah gave all these things to the king like a king would, and said to the king, "May God accept you."
2 Samuel 24:24 The king told Araunah, "No, I will definitely buy it from you at a fair price; I won't give burnt offerings to God that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty pieces of silver.
2 Samuel 24:25 David built an altar to God there, and gave burnt and peace offerings. So God listened concerning the land, and the plague stopped in Israel.

1 Kings 1:1 King David was old and very weak; they put clothes on him, but he could not get warm.
1 Kings 1:2 So his servants told him, "Let's find a young woman for our king. She will take care of him, lie close to him, and keep him warm."
1 Kings 1:3 They looked for a beautiful young woman all over Israel, found Abishag from Shunem, and took her to the king.
1 Kings 1:4 The young woman was very beautiful, took care of the king, and served him, but the king did not have intimate relations with her.
1 Kings 1:5 Adonijah, Haggith's son, boasted, "I will become king." He organized chariots, riders, and fifty people to run ahead of him.
1 Kings 1:6 His father never asked him why he acted that way and never made him unhappy. He was also very handsome, and he was born to his mother after Absalom.
1 Kings 1:7 He talked with Joab, Zeruiah's son, and Abiathar the priest; they supported Adonijah and helped him.
1 Kings 1:8 But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's strong soldiers did not support Adonijah.
1 Kings 1:9 Adonijah killed sheep, oxen, and well-fed cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, near Enrogel, and invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who served the king.
1 Kings 1:10 Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the strong soldiers, and Solomon his brother were not called by him.
1 Kings 1:11 So Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you heard that Adonijah, Haggith's son, has become king and David doesn't know about it?"
1 Kings 1:12 Now, please come so I can give you advice to save your life and your son Solomon's life.
1 Kings 1:13 Go to King David and ask him, "Didn't you, my lord the king, promise me that your son Solomon would be king after you and would sit on your throne? Why is Adonijah the king now?"
1 Kings 1:14 Look, while you are still talking to the king, I will come in after you and back up what you say.
1 Kings 1:15 Bathsheba entered the king's room, and the king was very old; Abishag from Shunem served the king.
1 Kings 1:16 Bathsheba bowed down to the king, and the king asked, "What do you want?"
1 Kings 1:17 She said to him, "Sir, you promised by God to your servant, 'Certainly, Solomon your son will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne.'"
1 Kings 1:18 Now, Adonijah has become king, and you, my king, do not know about it.
1 Kings 1:19 He has killed many oxen, fat cows, and sheep, and invited all the king's sons, the priest Abiathar, and army commander Joab, but he did not invite your servant Solomon.
1 Kings 1:20 And you, my king, all Israel is watching you, expecting you to say who will take your place as king after you.
1 Kings 1:21 If not, when the king, my lord, dies and joins his ancestors, my son Solomon and I will be treated as criminals.
1 Kings 1:22 While she was still talking to the king, the prophet Nathan arrived.
1 Kings 1:23 They told the king, "Look, here is the prophet Nathan." And when Nathan came in, he bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
1 Kings 1:24 Nathan said, My lord, the king, have you said that Adonijah will be king after me and sit on my throne?
1 Kings 1:25 Today he went down and killed many oxen, fat cows, and sheep. He invited all the king's sons, the army commanders, and the priest Abiathar. They are eating and drinking with him and shouting, "Long live King Adonijah!"
1 Kings 1:26 But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon, he did not call.
1 Kings 1:27 Did the king do this without telling me, who will sit on the throne after him?
1 Kings 1:28 King David replied, "Bring me Bathsheba." She came to see the king and stood in front of him.
1 Kings 1:29 The king promised and said, "As God lives, who has saved me from all trouble,"
1 Kings 1:30 Just as I promised you by the God of Israel, saying, 'Solomon your son will become king after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place,' so I will definitely do today.
1 Kings 1:31 Then Bathsheba knelt down, touched her forehead to the ground, showed deep respect to the king, and said, "May my king, David, live forever."
1 Kings 1:32 King David said, "Get Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, Jehoiada's son." They came to the king.
1 Kings 1:33 The king also told them, "Bring your lord's servants with you and have my son Solomon ride on my own mule, then take him to Gihon."
1 Kings 1:34 Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet make him king over Israel there; blow the trumpet and say, "May God protect King Solomon."
1 Kings 1:35 Then you will follow him, so he can come and sit on my throne; he will be king instead of me, and I have chosen him to rule over Israel and Judah.
1 Kings 1:36 Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, replied to the king, "Yes, may God, the God of my king, agree."
1 Kings 1:37 Just as God was with you, the king, may he also be with Solomon and make his rule even greater than your rule, King David.
1 Kings 1:38 So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down and made Solomon ride on King David's mule and took him to Gihon.
1 Kings 1:39 Priest Zadok took a horn of oil from the tent and put it on Solomon. They sounded the trumpet; and everyone said, May God protect King Solomon.
1 Kings 1:40 Everyone followed him, playing flutes and celebrating so loudly that the sound seemed to shake the ground.
1 Kings 1:41 Adonijah and all his guests heard it when they finished eating. When Joab heard the trumpet, he asked, "Why does the city sound so noisy and upset?"
1 Kings 1:42 While he was still talking, Jonathan, the son of Priest Abiathar, arrived; Adonijah said to him, "Come in, for you are a brave man and bring good news."
1 Kings 1:43 Jonathan replied to Adonijah, "Truly, our king David has made Solomon the king."
1 Kings 1:44 The king sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites with him, and they made him ride the king's mule.
1 Kings 1:45 Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet made him king at Gihon. They came up from there happy, and their joy filled the city. This is the sound you heard.
1 Kings 1:46 Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.
1 Kings 1:47 The king's helpers came to bless our lord King David, saying, "May God make Solomon's name greater than yours, and his throne greater than your throne." Then the king bowed on the bed.
1 Kings 1:48 The king also said, "Praise be to God of Israel, who has given someone to sit on my throne today, while I can still see it."
1 Kings 1:49 All the guests with Adonijah became scared, stood up, and each went their own way.
1 Kings 1:50 Adonijah was afraid of Solomon, so he got up, went and grabbed the corners of the altar.
1 Kings 1:51 Someone told Solomon, "Look, Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon. See, he is holding onto the altar horns and says, 'King Solomon must promise me today that he will not kill his servant with a sword.'"
1 Kings 1:52 Solomon said, "If he acts like a good man, not a single hair from his head will fall to the ground. But if he is found to be wicked, he will die."
1 Kings 1:53 King Solomon sent for him, and they took him from the altar. He came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon told him, "Go to your home."

1 Kings 2:1 David's time to die was near, so he told his son Solomon,
1 Kings 2:2 I am going the same way everyone on earth goes: so be strong and act like a man.
1 Kings 2:3 Follow God's instructions, live by his rules, follow his commands, decisions, and teachings as written by Moses, so you may succeed in everything you do and wherever you go.
1 Kings 2:4 God will keep his promise to me, saying, "If your children pay attention to their behavior and live truthfully with all their heart and soul, you will always have a descendant to rule over Israel."
1 Kings 2:5 You also know what Joab, son of Zeruiah, did to me and what he did to the two leaders of Israel's armies, to Abner, Ner's son, and to Amasa, Jether's son. He killed them and spilt blood as if at war even though it was peacetime. He stained his belt around his waist and his shoes on his feet with their blood.
1 Kings 2:6 So use your wisdom and don't let him die peacefully in old age.
1 Kings 2:7 Show kindness to Barzillai of Gilead's sons and let them eat at your table because they helped me when I ran away from your brother Absalom.
1 Kings 2:8 Look, you have with you Shimei, son of Gera, from the tribe of Benjamin in Bahurim. He cursed me terribly on the day I went to Mahanaim. But he later met me at the Jordan River, and I promised him in God's name, I would not kill him with the sword.
1 Kings 2:9 So now, don't consider him innocent: you're a smart man, you know what you should do to him; make sure he goes to his grave covered in blood.
1 Kings 2:10 David died and was buried in the city of David.
1 Kings 2:11 David ruled over Israel for forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
1 Kings 2:12 Solomon sat on his father David's throne, and his reign became very strong.
1 Kings 2:13 Adonijah, Haggith's son, went to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She asked, "Do you come in peace?" He replied, "Yes, in peace."
1 Kings 2:14 He also said, "I have something to tell you." And she replied, "Go ahead."
1 Kings 2:15 He said, "You know I was supposed to be king, and all Israel looked to me to rule. But now, the kingdom has gone to my brother, because God gave it to him."
1 Kings 2:16 I am asking you for one favor, please don't refuse me. She said to him, Go ahead.
1 Kings 2:17 He said, "Please talk to King Solomon (he won't refuse you) and ask him to let me marry Abishag the Shunammite."
1 Kings 2:18 Bathsheba said, "Okay; I will talk to the king for you."
1 Kings 2:19 Bathsheba went to King Solomon to talk about Adonijah. The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her, sat on his throne, and had a chair placed for his mother; she sat at his right side.
1 Kings 2:20 She said, "I have one small request; please don't say no to me." And the king answered, "Go ahead, my mother, for I will not refuse you."
1 Kings 2:21 She said, "Let Abishag from Shunem be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife."
1 Kings 2:22 King Solomon answered his mother, "Why do you request Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? You might as well ask for the kingdom for him since he's my older brother. And not just for him, but also for Abiathar the priest and Joab, son of Zeruiah.
1 Kings 2:23 King Solomon swore by God, "May God do the same to me, and even more, if Adonijah hasn't said this and put his own life at risk."
1 Kings 2:24 So now, because God is alive, who made me king and put me on my father David's throne, and has given me a home as he promised, Adonijah will be killed today.
1 Kings 2:25 King Solomon sent Benaiah, Jehoiada's son, who attacked and killed him.
1 Kings 2:26 The king said to Abiathar the priest, "Go to your lands in Anathoth, because you deserve to die. But I won't kill you now because you carried God's ark before my father David and suffered where he suffered."
1 Kings 2:27 Solomon removed Abiathar from being a priest for God; this fulfilled what God had said about Eli's family in Shiloh.
1 Kings 2:28 News reached Joab because he had supported Adonijah but not Absalom. Joab ran to God's tent and grabbed the corners of the altar.
1 Kings 2:29 Someone told King Solomon that Joab ran away to God's tent and is now by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah, Jehoiada's son, with the order: Go and kill him.
1 Kings 2:30 Benaiah went to God's tent and told him, "The king says, 'Come out.'" But he replied, "No, I'll die here." Then Benaiah told the king what Joab had said and how he responded.
1 Kings 2:31 The king said to him, "Do what he told you, attack him and bury him. This will remove the guilt of the innocent blood Joab spilled from me and my father's family."
1 Kings 2:32 God will make him responsible for the blood he shed. He attacked and killed two men who were more good and fair than himself without my father David knowing it: Abner, Ner's son and leader of Israel's army, and Amasa, Jether's son and leader of Judah's army.
1 Kings 2:33 Joab and his descendants will always be punished for the bloodshed, but David, his descendants, his family, and his throne will have eternal peace from God.
1 Kings 2:34 Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, went up, attacked him, and killed him. He was buried in his own home in the wilderness.
1 Kings 2:35 The king placed Benaiah, Jehoiada's son, in charge of the army, and Zadok the priest took Abiathar's position.
1 Kings 2:36 The king sent for Shimei and told him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem, live there, and do not go anywhere else."
1 Kings 2:37 On the day you leave and cross Kidron Valley, you will know for sure that you will die; your own actions will be the cause.
1 Kings 2:38 Shimei said to the king, "The words are good: as you, the king, have said, so I, your servant, will do." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for many days.
1 Kings 2:39 After three years, two of Shimei's servants escaped to Achish, Maachah's son, the king of Gath. They informed Shimei, "Look, your servants are in Gath."
1 Kings 2:40 Shimei got up, put a saddle on his donkey, and went to Gath to see Achish to find his servants. Then Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
1 Kings 2:41 Someone told Solomon that Shimei had left Jerusalem for Gath and had returned.
1 Kings 2:42 The king summoned Shimei and said to him, "Didn't I make you promise by God and warn you, saying, 'Be sure of this: the day you leave and go anywhere, you will certainly die'? And you said to me, 'What you said is good.'"
1 Kings 2:43 Why didn't you keep the promise to God and follow the command I gave you?
1 Kings 2:44 The king also told Shimei, "You know all the wrong you kept secret in your heart that you did to my father David. So, God will make sure your wrongs come back on you."
1 Kings 2:45 King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will be set up for all time in God's presence.
1 Kings 2:46 The king told Benaiah, Jehoiada's son, to kill him, and he did. So Solomon's rule was made secure.

1 Kings 3:1 Solomon formed an alliance with Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and married Pharaoh's daughter. He brought her to the city of David until he finished building his palace, God's house, and the wall around Jerusalem.
1 Kings 3:2 People offered sacrifices on high places because no house for God's name had been built at that time.
1 Kings 3:3 Solomon loved God and followed his father David's laws, but he also offered sacrifices and burned incense on high hills.
1 Kings 3:4 The king went to Gibeon to make sacrifices, because that was the most important worship place. Solomon gave a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
1 Kings 3:5 In Gibeon, God appeared to Solomon in a dream at night and said, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."
1 Kings 3:6 Solomon said, "You have shown great kindness to your servant, my father David, because he lived honestly and rightly, and was true-hearted with you; and you have kept this kindness for him by giving him a son to take his place as king, just like today."
1 Kings 3:7 God, you have made me king after my father David, but I am like a little child and do not know how to lead.
1 Kings 3:8 Your servant is among your chosen people, a great number that can't be counted.
1 Kings 3:9 Give me, your servant, a wise heart to govern your people and to know right from wrong, for who can govern this great people of yours?
1 Kings 3:10 God was happy that Solomon asked for this.
1 Kings 3:11 God said to him, because you asked for this, and did not ask for a long life, nor for wealth, nor for the death of your enemies, but for understanding to make the right decisions;
1 Kings 3:12 Look, I did what you asked for: I gave you a wise and understanding heart. There has been no one like you before, and there will be no one like you after.
1 Kings 3:13 I have also given you what you did not ask for—wealth and honor—so no king will be like you all your life.
1 Kings 3:14 If you follow my ways, obey my laws and commands, like your father David did, I will make your life longer.
1 Kings 3:15 Solomon woke up and realized it was a dream. He went to Jerusalem, stood in front of God's covenant chest, gave burnt offerings and peace offerings, and threw a big dinner for all his workers.
1 Kings 3:16 Two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
1 Kings 3:17 One woman said, "Oh sir, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth to a baby while she was there."
1 Kings 3:18 Three days after I gave birth, this woman also had her baby. We were alone in the house; just the two of us, with no one else there.
1 Kings 3:19 This woman's baby died at night because she lay on it too much.
1 Kings 3:20 She got up at midnight, took my son while I, your servant, was sleeping, placed him in her arms, and put her dead baby in my arms.
1 Kings 3:21 When I got up in the morning to feed my baby, I saw it was dead. But when I looked closely later, I saw it wasn't the son I had given birth to.
1 Kings 3:22 The other woman said, "No, the living child is mine and the dead one is yours." The first woman insisted, "No, the dead child is yours and the living child is mine." This is how they argued before the king.
1 Kings 3:23 Then the king said, "One woman claims, 'This living boy is mine, and your son is dead,' while the other says, 'No, your son is dead, and mine is alive.'"
1 Kings 3:24 The king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword to the king.
1 Kings 3:25 The king said, "Cut the living child in two, and give half to one and half to the other."
1 Kings 3:26 The woman with the living baby spoke to the king because she deeply cared for her son and begged, "Please, sir, give her the living baby, don't kill it." But the other woman said, "It should belong to neither of us. Cut it in two."
1 Kings 3:27 The king replied, "Give her the baby that's alive, do not kill it; she's its mother."
1 Kings 3:28 All of Israel heard about the king's decision and they respected the king because they realized God's wisdom was with him to make fair decisions.

1 Kings 4:6 Ahishar was in charge of the household, and Adoniram, Abda's son, was responsible for collecting taxes.

1 Kings 4:9 Dekar's son was over Makaz, Shaalbim, Bethshemesh, and Elonbethhanan.

1 Kings 4:13 Geber's son was in charge of Ramoth in Gilead and the towns of Jair, Manasseh's son, which are in Gilead. He also controlled the area of Argob in Bashan with sixty big cities that have walls and bronze gates.
1 Kings 4:14 Ahinadab, Iddo's son, was in charge of Mahanaim.
1 Kings 4:15 Ahimaaz lived in Naphtali and married Basmath, Solomon's daughter.
1 Kings 4:16 Baanah, Hushai's son, was in Asher and Aloth.
1 Kings 4:17 Jehoshaphat, Paruah's son, was in Issachar.
1 Kings 4:18 Shimei, son of Elah, was from the tribe of Benjamin.
1 Kings 4:19 Geber, Uri's son, was in Gilead, Sihon the Amorite king's land, and Og the Bashan king's land; he was the only official there.
1 Kings 4:20 Judah and Israel had many people, like the sand by the sea, eating, drinking, and being happy.
1 Kings 4:21 Solomon ruled over all kingdoms from the river to the Philistine lands, and to Egypt's border: they gave gifts and served Solomon all his life.
1 Kings 4:22 Solomon's daily food supply was thirty measures of fine flour and sixty measures of grain.
1 Kings 4:23 Ten fat oxen, twenty oxen from the fields, and a hundred sheep, plus deer, roebucks, fallow deer, and fat birds.
1 Kings 4:24 He ruled over all the area by the river, from Tiphsah to Azzah, over all the kings by the river, and he had peace all around him.
1 Kings 4:25 Judah and Israel lived in safety, each person under their own vine and fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, during all of Solomon's time.
1 Kings 4:26 Solomon had 40,000 stalls for his chariot horses and 12,000 riders.
1 Kings 4:27 Those officers supplied food for King Solomon and for everyone who came to King Solomon's table, every man during his month; they were missing nothing.
1 Kings 4:28 They brought barley and straw to the place where the officers were for the horses and camels, each person according to their responsibility.
1 Kings 4:29 God gave Solomon great wisdom, deep understanding, and a big heart, as many as the sands on the seashore.
1 Kings 4:30 Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of everyone in the eastern lands and all the wisdom of Egypt.
1 Kings 4:31 He was smarter than everyone; smarter than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and people everywhere knew about him.
1 Kings 4:32 He spoke three thousand wise sayings, and he had one thousand and five songs.
1 Kings 4:33 He talked about trees, from the tall cedars of Lebanon to the small hyssop plants that grow in walls. He also talked about animals, birds, crawling creatures, and fish.
1 Kings 4:34 People from everywhere came to hear Solomon's wisdom, including all the kings of the earth who had heard about it.

1 Kings 5:1 Hiram, the king of Tyre, sent his servants to Solomon because he heard they had made him king after his father. Hiram always loved David.
1 Kings 5:2 Solomon sent a message to Hiram, saying,
1 Kings 5:3 You know my father David couldn't build a house for God because of the constant wars around him, until God defeated his enemies.
1 Kings 5:4 But now God has given me peace everywhere, with no enemy or bad things happening.
1 Kings 5:5 Look, I plan to build a house for the name of God, as God told my father David, saying, "Your son, who I will put on your throne after you, will build a house for my name."
1 Kings 5:6 So now, tell them to cut cedar trees from Lebanon for me; my workers will work with yours: and I will pay your workers as you decide: because you know we have no one who can cut wood like the Sidonians.
1 Kings 5:7 When Hiram heard Solomon's words, he was very happy and said, "Praise God today, for giving David a wise son to lead this great nation."
1 Kings 5:8 Hiram sent a message to Solomon, saying, "I have thought about what you asked me for, and I will do everything you want with the cedar and fir wood."
1 Kings 5:9 My workers will bring them from Lebanon to the sea, and I'll transport them by sea on rafts to the place you choose for me. There, I'll unload them, and you'll pick them up. You'll fulfill my wish by providing food for my family.
1 Kings 5:10 Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar and fir trees he wanted.
1 Kings 5:11 Solomon gave Hiram 20,000 measures of wheat for his family's food and 20 measures of pure oil. Solomon did this for Hiram every year.
1 Kings 5:12 God gave Solomon wisdom as promised, and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; they both formed a partnership.
1 Kings 5:13 King Solomon gathered workers from all Israel; there were thirty thousand men.
1 Kings 5:14 He sent them to Lebanon in groups of ten thousand each month: they spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of them.
1 Kings 5:15 Solomon had seventy thousand carriers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains.
1 Kings 5:16 In addition to Solomon's main officers in charge of the work, there were 3,300 supervisors managing the workers.
1 Kings 5:17 The king ordered them to bring large, expensive cut stones to lay the house's foundation.
1 Kings 5:18 Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders cut the stones, and the stonecutters helped. They got wood and stones ready to build the house.

1 Kings 6:1 In the year 480 after the Israelites left Egypt, during the fourth year of Solomon's rule over Israel in the month of Zif, which is the second month, he started to build God's house.
1 Kings 6:2 The temple that King Solomon built for God was 60 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
1 Kings 6:3 The entrance hall in front of the temple was 20 cubits long, the same width as the building, and it was 10 cubits wide in front of the building.
1 Kings 6:4 He made windows with thin openings for the house.
1 Kings 6:5 He built rooms along the wall of the house, surrounding the temple and the inner sanctuary, and he added rooms around the outside.
1 Kings 6:6 The lowest room was five cubits wide, the middle one was six cubits wide, and the top one was seven cubits wide. On the outside of the house wall, he made ledges all around so that the beams would not need to be set into the walls of the house.
1 Kings 6:7 The house, during construction, was made from stone prepared beforehand, so no sound of hammer, axe, or any iron tool was heard at the building site.
1 Kings 6:8 The entrance to the middle room was on the right side of the house. They went up through spiral stairs to the middle room, and from there to the third room.
1 Kings 6:9 He built the house, finished it, and covered it with cedar beams and planks.
1 Kings 6:10 He then built rooms all around the house, five cubits tall, and they were supported by cedar wood beams on the house.
1 Kings 6:11 God's message came to Solomon, saying,
1 Kings 6:12 About this house you are building, if you follow my rules, carry out my decisions, and obey all my commands, then I will keep the promise I made to your father David.
1 Kings 6:13 I will live among the people of Israel and will not abandon them.
1 Kings 6:14 Solomon built the house and completed it.
1 Kings 6:15 He built the inside walls of the house with cedar boards, from the floor to the ceiling. He lined the interior with wood and used fir planks for the house's floor.
1 Kings 6:16 He made a twenty-cubit section at the end of the temple, with cedar boards from floor to walls. He built this inner space for the Sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
1 Kings 6:17 The temple, the main part in front, was forty cubits long.
1 Kings 6:18 The inside of the house was decorated with carved bumps and open flowers; it was all made of cedar wood, and no stone was visible.
1 Kings 6:19 He made a special place inside the house for the ark of God's covenant.
1 Kings 6:20 The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. It was covered with pure gold, and the cedar altar was also covered with gold.
1 Kings 6:21 Solomon covered the inside of the temple with pure gold. He put a gold chain barrier in front of the most holy place and covered that with gold too.
1 Kings 6:22 He covered the whole house and the altar near the sacred room with gold until everything was finished.
1 Kings 6:23 Inside the holy place, he made two angels out of olive wood, each fifteen feet tall.
1 Kings 6:24 One wing of the angel was five units long, and the other wing was also five units long; the total span from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other was ten units.
1 Kings 6:25 The other angel was ten units long; both angels were the same size and shape.
1 Kings 6:26 One cherub was ten cubits tall, and the other cherub was also this tall.
1 Kings 6:27 He placed the cherubim inside the inner room, and they spread out their wings. One cherub's wing touched one wall and the other cherub's wing touched the other wall, while their wings touched each other in the middle of the room.
1 Kings 6:28 He covered the cherubim with gold.
1 Kings 6:29 He decorated all the walls of the house with carved images of angels, palm trees, and open flowers, on the inside and outside.
1 Kings 6:30 He covered the floors of the house with gold, inside and outside.
1 Kings 6:31 For the entrance of the holy place, he made doors of olive wood: the top beam and pillars took up one-fifth of the wall.
1 Kings 6:32 The two doors were made of olive wood, and he carved images of angels, palm trees, and open flowers on them. Then he covered them with gold, and put gold on the angels and the palm trees.
1 Kings 6:33 He also made olive wood posts for the temple entrance, one-fourth as thick as the wall.
1 Kings 6:34 The two doors were made of fir wood; each door had two panels that could fold.
1 Kings 6:35 He carved angels, palm trees, and open flowers there, and covered them with gold that was shaped to fit the carvings.
1 Kings 6:36 He made the inner courtyard with three layers of cut stone and one layer of cedar wood.
1 Kings 6:37 In the fourth year, they started building God's house, in the month of Zif.
1 Kings 6:38 In the eleventh year, during Bul, the eighth month, the house was completed in every part and detail. It took seven years to build it.

1 Kings 7:1 Solomon built his own house for thirteen years and he finished the whole house.
1 Kings 7:2 He also built the Lebanon Forest House; it was 100 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high, with four rows of cedar pillars and cedar beams on top of the pillars.
1 Kings 7:3 It was covered with cedar on top of the beams resting on 45 pillars, with 15 pillars in each row.
1 Kings 7:4 There were windows set in three layers, and each row of windows lined up with the opposite ones.
1 Kings 7:5 All the doors and posts were shaped like squares, along with the windows, and light matched light in three rows.
1 Kings 7:6 He built a porch with columns that was fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. This porch was in front, with more columns and a solid beam also in front.
1 Kings 7:7 He built a covered entry for the throne where he could make decisions, the Hall of Justice, and it had cedar from the floor to the ceiling.
1 Kings 7:8 His home, where he lived, had another yard inside the entryway, made in the same style. Solomon also built a home for Pharaoh's daughter, his wife, similar to this entryway.
1 Kings 7:9 All these stones were expensive, cut to size, and sawn smoothly on the inside and outside, from the foundation to the top, and around the outer courtyard.
1 Kings 7:10 The foundation was made of expensive, large stones—some ten cubits and some eight cubits long.
1 Kings 7:11 Above were expensive stones, cut to size, and cedar wood.
1 Kings 7:12 The large courtyard around it had three layers of cut stones and a layer of cedar wood, for both the inner courtyard of God's house and the entrance hall.
1 Kings 7:13 King Solomon sent for Hiram from Tyre.
1 Kings 7:14 He was the son of a widow from Naphtali, and his father was from Tyre, skilled in working with brass. He was very wise, knowledgeable, and skilled in all kinds of brass work. He went to King Solomon and did all the work Solomon asked for.
1 Kings 7:15 He made two brass pillars, each eighteen cubits tall, and a twelve-cubit measuring line could go around each one.
1 Kings 7:16 He created two brass capitals to put on top of the pillars; each capital was five cubits tall.
1 Kings 7:17 Mesh nets and chains were made for the capitals on top of the pillars, seven for each capital.
1 Kings 7:18 He made the columns with two rows of designs around one grate to surround the tops with pomegranates, and he did the same for the other top.
1 Kings 7:19 The tops of the pillars were decorated with carvings of lilies and were four cubits high in the entrance way.
1 Kings 7:20 The tops of the two pillars also had pomegranates above, facing the rounded part next to the meshwork. And there were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around on the other top.
1 Kings 7:21 He put the pillars at the temple entrance: he put the right pillar and named it Jachin; he put the left pillar and named it Boaz.
1 Kings 7:22 On top of the columns was a design of lilies, and so the columns were completed.
1 Kings 7:23 He made a large metal bowl, ten units across from one edge to the other. It was round and five units tall. A measuring line thirty units long could wrap around it.
1 Kings 7:24 Under its edge all around there were small round decorations. There were ten per foot, all around the bowl. The decorations were in two rows and were part of the bowl when it was made.
1 Kings 7:25 It stood on twelve oxen, with three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The sea rested on top of them, and all their back parts pointed inward.
1 Kings 7:26 It was as thick as a hand is wide, and its edge looked like the edge of a cup, decorated with lily flowers. It could hold two thousand baths.
1 Kings 7:27 He made ten brass stands; each one was four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
1 Kings 7:28 The bases were made like this: they had edges, and there were edges between the side supports.
1 Kings 7:29 On the edges between the layers were lions, oxen, and angels; and on the layers was a stand on top: and under the lions and oxen were special details made of delicate designs.
1 Kings 7:30 Each base had four bronze wheels and brass plates. The four corners had supports. There were supports cast in bronze under the basin, next to each side attachment.
1 Kings 7:31 The opening on top of the column, inside the decorative top, was one and a half feet deep; the opening was round, not like the base. The opening also had engravings with square borders, not round.
1 Kings 7:32 Under the edges were four wheels; the wheel axles were connected to the stand, and each wheel was one and a half cubits tall.
1 Kings 7:33 The wheels were made like chariot wheels: their parts—the axles, hubs, rims, and spokes—were all cast metal.
1 Kings 7:34 Each base had four supports at its four corners, and the supports were part of the base itself.
1 Kings 7:35 The base had a round rim at the top half a cubit high; the top of the base, its edges and sides were all one piece.
1 Kings 7:36 On its shelves and edges, he carved angels, lions, and palm trees, each in proper size, with designs all around.
1 Kings 7:37 He made the ten stands in this way: all were made with the same mold, had the same dimensions, and were the same size.
1 Kings 7:38 He made ten brass washbasins; each basin held forty baths and was four cubits; and on each of the ten stands was one basin.
1 Kings 7:39 He placed five stands on the right side of the building and five on the left; and he put the large bowl on the right side of the building, facing south and east.
1 Kings 7:40 Hiram made the washbasins, shovels, and bowls. So Hiram finished all the work he did for King Solomon for God's house.
1 Kings 7:41 The two columns, the two tops of the columns, and the two decorations to cover the tops of the columns.
1 Kings 7:42 And four hundred pomegranates for the two grids, two rows of pomegranates for each grid, to cover the two capitals on top of the pillars.
1 Kings 7:43 The ten stands and ten washbasins on the stands.
1 Kings 7:44 One big bowl, and twelve bulls under the bowl.
1 Kings 7:45 The pots, shovels, and bowls, and all these items that Hiram made for King Solomon for God's house, were made of shiny brass.
1 Kings 7:46 The king molded them in the Jordan Valley, in the clay soil between Succoth and Zarthan.
1 Kings 7:47 Solomon didn't weigh all the objects because there were too many, and no one knew how much the bronze weighed.
1 Kings 7:48 Solomon made all the items for God's house: the gold altar and the gold table for the bread on display.
1 Kings 7:49 The golden candlesticks, five on the right and five on the left, stood in front of the holy place, along with the golden flowers, lights, and tongs.
1 Kings 7:50 The bowls, trimmers, basins, spoons, and incense burners were all made of pure gold, as were the gold door hinges for both the doors of the most sacred part and the doors of the main temple.
1 Kings 7:51 All the work King Solomon did for God's house was finished. Solomon added what his father David had set aside—silver, gold, and items to God's house's treasures.

1 Kings 8:1 Solomon brought together Israel's elders, tribal leaders, and family heads in Jerusalem to move God's covenant chest from David's city, Zion, to King Solomon.
1 Kings 8:2 All the men of Israel gathered around King Solomon for the festival in Ethanim, the seventh month.
1 Kings 8:3 All the leaders of Israel came, and the priests carried the chest.
1 Kings 8:4 They brought God's ark, the meeting tent, and all the sacred items inside the tent; the priests and Levites carried them all.
1 Kings 8:5 King Solomon and all of Israel's people gathered with him stood before the covenant box, offering so many sheep and oxen they couldn't be counted.
1 Kings 8:6 The priests put God's covenant chest in its place in the temple's inner room, right beneath the cherubim angels' wings.
1 Kings 8:7 The cherubim stretched out their two wings over where the ark was and covered the ark and its poles from above.
1 Kings 8:8 They pulled the poles out until the ends were visible in the sanctuary in front of the inner room, but they couldn't be seen from outside, and they are still there today.
1 Kings 8:9 Inside the ark were only the two stone tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb, where God made an agreement with the Israelites after they left Egypt.
1 Kings 8:10 When the priests left the holy place, a cloud filled God's house.
1 Kings 8:11 The priests could not stay to serve because of the cloud, for God's glory had filled God's house.
1 Kings 8:12 Then Solomon said, God would live in deep darkness.
1 Kings 8:13 I have certainly built you a house to live in, a stable home for you to stay in forever.
1 Kings 8:14 The king turned around and blessed all the people of Israel; and all the people stood up.
1 Kings 8:15 He said, "Praise God of Israel, who spoke to my father David and has now done what he promised."
1 Kings 8:16 Since the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I did not choose any city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house for my name; but I chose David to rule over my people Israel.
1 Kings 8:17 David, my father, wanted to build a house for God's name.
1 Kings 8:18 God told David, my father, "Since you wanted to build a house for my name, you did well to have that desire."
1 Kings 8:19 You will not build the house; but your son, who will be born to you, will build the house for my name.
1 Kings 8:20 God did what he said, and I have become king after David my father. I sit on Israel's throne as God promised and have built a house for God's name.
1 Kings 8:21 I have prepared a place for the chest that holds God's agreement, which he made with our ancestors when he led them out of Egypt.
1 Kings 8:22 Solomon stood in front of God's altar in front of all the Israelites and reached his hands up to the sky.
1 Kings 8:23 He said, "God of Israel, no one is like you in heaven or on earth, who keeps promises and shows kindness to your servants who follow you with all their heart."
1 Kings 8:24 You kept your promise to your servant David, my father. You said it with your words, and now you have made it happen with your actions, just like today.
1 Kings 8:25 So now, God of Israel, keep the promise you made to your servant David, my father, when you said, "You will always have a descendant to rule Israel if your children are careful in their actions and follow me just as you have."
1 Kings 8:26 And now, God of Israel, please let your promise to my father David, your servant, come true.
1 Kings 8:27 Can God really live on earth? Even the sky and the highest heavens cannot hold you, so how can this temple I have built?
1 Kings 8:28 Please listen to your servant's prayer and plea, God my God, and hear the cries and prayers I offer to you today.
1 Kings 8:29 Let your eyes be open towards this house day and night, towards the place you said, "My name will be there," so you can listen to the prayers your servant will make facing this place.
1 Kings 8:30 Listen to your servant's prayer and to the prayers of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, your home, and when you hear, forgive.
1 Kings 8:31 If someone wrongs their neighbor and is made to take an oath, and they come to take the oath at your altar in this place:
1 Kings 8:32 Then listen from heaven, act, and decide what your servants deserve. Punish the guilty so they face the consequences of their actions, and reward the good for doing right.
1 Kings 8:33 When your people Israel are defeated by their enemies because they have sinned against you, and then they turn back to you, admit your name, pray, and ask for your mercy in this place:
1 Kings 8:34 Listen from heaven, forgive the sins of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
1 Kings 8:35 When the sky is closed and there is no rain because they have sinned against you; if they pray to this place, admit your name, and stop their sinning when you punish them:
1 Kings 8:36 Listen from heaven and forgive the sins of your servants and your people Israel. Teach them the right path to follow and send rain to the land you have given them as a heritage.
1 Kings 8:37 If there is famine or disease, crop failure, mold, locusts, or caterpillars in the land; if an enemy surrounds them in their land or in their cities; any kind of plague or illness that happens;
1 Kings 8:38 Whatever prayer or plea is made by any person, or by all your people Israel, each knowing the troubles of their own heart, and reaching out their hands toward this temple:
1 Kings 8:39 Listen from heaven, your home, forgive and act, and reward each person according to their actions because you know their heart; only you know every human heart.
1 Kings 8:40 So they will respect you every day they live in the land you gave to our ancestors.
1 Kings 8:41 Also about a foreigner, who is not from your people Israel, but comes from a distant land because of your reputation;
1 Kings 8:42 They will hear about your great name, your powerful hand, and your extended arm; when he comes to pray toward this place.
1 Kings 8:43 Listen in heaven, your home, and do what the foreigner asks of you, so that everyone on earth may know your name and respect you, just like your people Israel; and let them know that this temple I have built is named after you.
1 Kings 8:44 If your people go to fight their enemies wherever you send them, and they pray to God facing the city you have chosen and the house I have built for your name:
1 Kings 8:45 Then listen from heaven to their prayer and plea, and help them.
1 Kings 8:46 If they do wrong against you, because everyone sins, and you get angry with them, and let their enemies take them as prisoners to a far or nearby land;
1 Kings 8:47 But if they think about what they did wrong in the country where they are prisoners, and they turn back to you, and ask for your mercy in the country of their captors, saying, 'We have done wrong, we have acted badly, we have been wicked;'
1 Kings 8:48 Let them come back to you with all their heart and soul from the land of their enemies who took them as captives, and let them pray to you facing their land, which you gave to their ancestors, the city you chose, and the temple I built for your name.
1 Kings 8:49 Listen to their prayers and pleas from heaven, your home, and support their case.
1 Kings 8:50 Forgive your people who have sinned against you, forgive all the wrongs they have done against you, and make their captors show them mercy, so they will also receive mercy.
1 Kings 8:51 They are your people and your inheritance, which you brought out of Egypt, from the iron furnace.
1 Kings 8:52 May your eyes be open to your servant's request and to the prayers of your people Israel, and may you listen to them whenever they call to you.
1 Kings 8:53 You chose them from all the people on earth to be your own, as you said through Moses your servant, when you led our ancestors out of Egypt, O God.
1 Kings 8:54 After Solomon finished praying all this to God, he stood up from the altar of God, where he had been kneeling with his hands raised to heaven.
1 Kings 8:55 He stood up and with a loud voice blessed all the people of Israel, saying,
1 Kings 8:56 God is blessed for giving his people Israel rest, just as he promised. Every single one of his good promises that he made through his servant Moses has come true.
1 Kings 8:57 May God be with us just as he was with our ancestors; may he not leave us or abandon us.
1 Kings 8:58 So he can lead our hearts to him, to follow all his paths, and obey his commands, rules, and decisions, which he gave to our ancestors.
1 Kings 8:59 Let my words, which I have used to ask for help from God, be close to God day and night, so he can support the needs of his servant and his people Israel whenever necessary.
1 Kings 8:60 Everyone on earth may know that God is the only God.
1 Kings 8:61 Keep your heart fully committed to God, follow his rules, and obey his commands, just as you do today.
1 Kings 8:62 The king and everyone in Israel with him made sacrifices to God.
1 Kings 8:63 Solomon gave God a peace offering of 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. The king and everyone in Israel then made the temple holy.
1 Kings 8:64 On that day, the king made the center of the courtyard, in front of God's house, holy because there he gave burnt and grain offerings, and the fat from the peace offerings. This was because the bronze altar in front of God was too small to hold all the burnt and grain offerings, and the fat from the peace offerings.
1 Kings 8:65 At that time, Solomon had a big party, and everyone in Israel joined him, a large crowd, from Hamath to the river of Egypt, in front of God for seven days, and another seven days, totaling fourteen days.
1 Kings 8:66 On the eighth day, he let the people go. They blessed the king and went to their tents, happy and thankful for all the good things God had done for David his servant and for Israel his people.

1 Kings 9:1 When Solomon finished building God's house, his own palace, and everything he wanted to do,
1 Kings 9:2 God appeared to Solomon again, just as he had at Gibeon.
1 Kings 9:3 God said to him, "I have heard your prayer and plea that you made before me. I have made this house holy, which you have built, to place my name there forever; and my eyes and heart will always be there."
1 Kings 9:4 If you walk before me like your father David did, with a pure heart and honesty, doing all I have told you and following my rules and decisions:
1 Kings 9:5 I will make sure your kingdom's throne in Israel lasts forever, just like I promised your father David, when I said, "Your throne in Israel will always have a man to rule."
1 Kings 9:6 If you turn away from following me, you or your children, and do not obey my commands and laws I gave you, but follow and worship other gods:
1 Kings 9:7 I will remove Israel from the land I gave them; and this temple I made holy for my name, I will reject; and Israel will become an example and a common saying among all nations.
1 Kings 9:8 At this tall house, everyone passing by will be shocked and will hiss. They will ask, "Why did God do this to the land and to this house?"
1 Kings 9:9 They will say, 'Because they left God, who freed their ancestors from Egypt, and followed other gods, worshiping and serving them, that's why God let all this bad happen to them.'
1 Kings 9:10 After twenty years, when Solomon finished building the two buildings, God's house and the king's house,
1 Kings 9:11 King Solomon gave King Hiram of Tyre twenty cities in Galilee because Hiram had provided Solomon with cedar and fir trees, and gold, as much as he wanted.
1 Kings 9:12 Hiram left Tyre to see the towns that Solomon gave him, but he did not like them.
1 Kings 9:13 He asked, "What are these towns you've given me, my brother?" He named the area Cabul, a name it still has today.
1 Kings 9:14 Hiram sent the king 120 talents of gold.
1 Kings 9:15 This is why King Solomon collected taxes: to build God's house, his palace, Millo, the walls of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
1 Kings 9:16 The king of Egypt, Pharaoh, attacked and captured Gezer, burned it, killed the Canaanites living there, and gave it as a gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
1 Kings 9:17 Solomon built Gezer and lower Bethhoron.
1 Kings 9:18 And Baalath, and Tadmor in the desert, in the country,
1 Kings 9:19 Solomon had many storage cities, cities for his chariots, cities for his horsemen, and whatever he wanted to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout his lands.
1 Kings 9:20 And all the people remaining from the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not Israelites,
1 Kings 9:21 The children who remained in the land after them, whom the Israelites could not completely destroy, Solomon made those pay forced labor taxes that continue to this day.
1 Kings 9:22 Solomon did not make slaves of the Israelites; instead, they were soldiers, servants, leaders, commanders, chariot officers, and horsemen.
1 Kings 9:23 These were the top supervisors for Solomon's projects, 550, who managed the workers.
1 Kings 9:24 Pharaoh's daughter left David's city and went to the house that Solomon built for her; then he built Millo.
1 Kings 9:25 Solomon made burnt sacrifices and peace sacrifices on the altar he made for God three times a year, and he burned incense on the altar in front of God. So he completed the temple.
1 Kings 9:26 King Solomon built a fleet of ships at Eziongeber, near Eloth, on the coast of the Red Sea, in Edom's territory.
1 Kings 9:27 Hiram sent his sailors, who knew the sea well, with Solomon's servants on the ships.
1 Kings 9:28 They went to Ophir, got 420 talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.

1 Kings 10:1 When the queen of Sheba heard about Solomon’s fame and his relationship with God, she came to test him with difficult questions.
1 Kings 10:2 She went to Jerusalem with a large group, camels carrying spices, lots of gold, and precious stones. When she met Solomon, she talked with him about everything on her mind.
1 Kings 10:3 Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was hidden from the king, which he did not explain to her.
1 Kings 10:4 When the queen of Sheba saw all of Solomon's wisdom and the house he built,
1 Kings 10:5 The food at his table, how his servants sat, how his aides served, their clothes, his cup-bearers, and the way he went up to God's house; it left her breathless.
1 Kings 10:6 She told the king, "The stories I heard in my country about your deeds and your wisdom were true."
1 Kings 10:7 I didn't believe what was said until I came and saw it myself. And what I saw was far greater than I was told; your wisdom and wealth are more than the stories I heard.
1 Kings 10:8 Your men are happy, your servants who always stand before you and hear your wisdom are happy too.
1 Kings 10:9 God blesses you because he took pleasure in you and made you king of Israel; God's love for Israel is eternal, so he made you ruler to carry out fairness and justice.
1 Kings 10:10 She gave the king 120 talents of gold, lots of spices, and valuable stones. No one gave King Solomon as many spices as the Queen of Sheba did.
1 Kings 10:11 Hiram's ships, which carried gold from Ophir, also brought back many almug trees and valuable gems from Ophir.
1 Kings 10:12 The king used almug wood to make columns for God's house and the royal palace, and to make harps and stringed instruments for musicians. There had never been such almug wood before, and none has been seen since then.
1 Kings 10:13 King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba everything she wanted, beyond what he had already generously given her. Then she and her servants went back to her own country.
1 Kings 10:14 Every year, Solomon received 666 talents of gold.
1 Kings 10:15 He also received from the traders, spice sellers, all the kings of Arabia, and the country's leaders.
1 Kings 10:16 King Solomon made 200 large shields of hammered gold; each shield used 600 shekels of gold.
1 Kings 10:17 He made three hundred gold shields; each shield used three pounds of gold. The king placed them in the Lebanon Forest House.
1 Kings 10:18 The king also made a big throne out of ivory and covered it with pure gold.
1 Kings 10:19 The throne had six steps and a round top at the back. There were armrests on both sides of the seat with two lions standing next to the armrests.
1 Kings 10:20 Twelve lions stood on each side of the six steps; nothing like this was made in any other kingdom.
1 Kings 10:21 All of King Solomon's cups were made of gold, and everything in the Lebanon Forest House was pure gold; nothing was made of silver, as silver was not valued much in Solomon's time.
1 Kings 10:22 The king had a fleet of ships for sailing to Tarshish that worked with Hiram's fleet. Every three years, Tarshish's ships came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, monkeys, and peacocks.
1 Kings 10:23 King Solomon was richer and wiser than all other kings on earth.
1 Kings 10:24 Everyone in the world wanted to hear Solomon's wisdom that God had given him.
1 Kings 10:25 Everyone brought gifts, including silver and gold containers, clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules, each year.
1 Kings 10:26 Solomon collected chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. He placed them in chariot cities and with him in Jerusalem.
1 Kings 10:27 The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar trees as plentiful as sycamore trees in the lowlands.
1 Kings 10:28 Solomon got horses from Egypt, and fine thread. The king's traders bought the thread at a cost.
1 Kings 10:29 A chariot was brought from Egypt for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty pieces. This was done for all the Hittite kings and the Syrian kings, brought out by their agents.

1 Kings 11:1 King Solomon loved many foreign women, including Pharaoh's daughter and women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and Hittite lands.
1 Kings 11:2 About the countries which God told the people of Israel, "Do not associate with them, nor let them associate with you, because they will surely turn your hearts towards their gods," Solomon became very attached to them because of love.
1 Kings 11:3 He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred secondary wives, and his wives led his heart astray.
1 Kings 11:4 When Solomon was old, his wives made his heart follow other gods, and his heart was not as faithful to God as his father David's heart was.
1 Kings 11:5 Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the Zidonians' goddess, and Milcom, the Ammonites' hated idol.
1 Kings 11:6 Solomon did bad things that God saw, and he didn't follow God completely like his father David did.
1 Kings 11:7 Solomon built a worship site on the hill facing Jerusalem for Chemosh, the Moabites' detested god, and for Molech, the Ammonites' detested god.
1 Kings 11:8 He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
1 Kings 11:9 God was angry with Solomon because Solomon's heart turned away from the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
1 Kings 11:10 God told him not to follow other gods, but he did not obey what God commanded.
1 Kings 11:11 So God said to Solomon, "Because you have done this and have not followed my agreement and my rules that I gave you, I will certainly take the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant."
1 Kings 11:12 Despite this, I will not do it during your lifetime out of respect for your father David; instead, I will take it away from your son.
1 Kings 11:13 However, I will not take away the entire kingdom; I will give one tribe to your son because of my servant David, and for Jerusalem, which I have chosen.
1 Kings 11:14 God made Hadad the Edomite, of royal blood from Edom, become Solomon's enemy.
1 Kings 11:15 When David was in Edom and Joab, the army commander, had gone to bury the dead after defeating every man in Edom.
1 Kings 11:16 Joab stayed there with all Israel for six months, until he had killed every man in Edom.
1 Kings 11:17 Hadad ran away to Egypt with some of his father's Edomite servants while he was still a young child.
1 Kings 11:18 They left Midian and went to Paran, taking people with them from Paran to Egypt, to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave him a house, food, and land.
1 Kings 11:19 Hadad was liked very much by Pharaoh, so he let him marry his wife's sister, Queen Tahpenes's sister.
1 Kings 11:20 Tahpenes' sister had a son named Genubath for him, and Tahpenes raised Genubath in the Pharaoh's palace; Genubath grew up among the Pharaoh's sons.
1 Kings 11:21 When Hadad in Egypt learned that David had died and that Joab, the army commander, was also dead, he said to Pharaoh, "Let me go back to my own country."
1 Kings 11:22 Then Pharaoh asked him, "What have you missed with me, that you want to go back to your own country?" He replied, "Nothing, but please let me go."
1 Kings 11:23 God raised up another enemy against him, Rezon son of Eliadah, who had run away from his master Hadadezer, the king of Zobah.
1 Kings 11:24 He brought men together, became their leader, and ruled in Damascus after David defeated the people of Zobah. They lived there in Damascus.
1 Kings 11:25 He opposed Israel throughout Solomon's reign, causing trouble like Hadad, hated Israel, and ruled over Syria.
1 Kings 11:26 Jeroboam, Nebat's son from Zereda in Ephraim, who worked for Solomon and whose mother Zeruah was a widow, rebelled against the king.
1 Kings 11:27 He turned against the king because: Solomon had built Millo and fixed the damaged parts of his father David's city.
1 Kings 11:28 Jeroboam was a brave and strong man. Solomon noticed that he was a hard worker, so he put him in charge of all the work for Joseph's descendants.
1 Kings 11:29 At that time, when Jeroboam left Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh found him on the road; Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and they were alone in the field.
1 Kings 11:30 Ahijah took the new clothing he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
1 Kings 11:31 He told Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces: God, the God of Israel, says, 'Look, I will take the kingdom from Solomon's hand and give you ten tribes.'"
1 Kings 11:32 He will keep one tribe for my servant David and for Jerusalem, the city I chose from all the tribes of Israel.
1 Kings 11:33 Because they left me and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites, and did not follow my ways, doing what is right in my sight, and keeping my laws and rules, like David their ancestor did.
1 Kings 11:34 However, I won't take the entire kingdom from him. Instead, I will let him be a leader all his life because of my servant David, whom I selected, since he followed my commands and rules.
1 Kings 11:35 I will take the kingdom from his son's hand and will give it to you, ten tribes.
1 Kings 11:36 I will give one tribe to his son so that my servant David may always have a presence in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to honor my name.
1 Kings 11:37 I will take you, and you will rule as you wish, and be king over Israel.
1 Kings 11:38 If you listen to all I tell you, follow my path, do what is right in my eyes, and keep my laws and commands like my servant David did; then I will be with you, build you a strong home, just like I did for David, and give you Israel.
1 Kings 11:39 I will punish David's descendants for a while, but not forever.
1 Kings 11:40 Solomon wanted to kill Jeroboam. So Jeroboam got up, ran away to Egypt, to King Shishak, and stayed there until Solomon died.
1 Kings 11:41 The other things Solomon did, all his actions, and his wisdom, are they not recorded in the book about Solomon's deeds?
1 Kings 11:42 Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
1 Kings 11:43 Solomon died and was buried in his father David's city, and his son Rehoboam became king after him.

1 Kings 12:1 Rehoboam went to Shechem because all Israel had gathered there to make him king.
1 Kings 12:2 When Jeroboam, son of Nebat, was still in Egypt, he heard about it. He had run away from King Solomon and was living in Egypt.
1 Kings 12:3 They sent for him and called him. Jeroboam and all the people of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
1 Kings 12:4 Your father made our work very hard. Now please make the hard work and the heavy load he put on us lighter, and we will serve you.
1 Kings 12:5 He told them, "Go away for three days, then come back to me." So the people left.
1 Kings 12:6 King Rehoboam asked the elders who had served his father Solomon for advice, saying, "What is your advice on how I should respond to these people?"
1 Kings 12:7 They said to him, "If you agree to serve these people today, help them, listen to them, and say kind things to them, then they will be your servants always."
1 Kings 12:8 He ignored the advice of the older men that they had given him and asked the young men who had grown up with him and who served him for their opinion.
1 Kings 12:9 He asked them, "What advice do you suggest we give to the people who said to me, 'Make the heavy burden your father put on us lighter'?"
1 Kings 12:10 The young men who grew up with him said to him, "This is how you should talk to the people who told you, 'Your father made our work hard, but you should make it easier for us': You should say to them, 'My little finger is stronger than my father's waist.'
1 Kings 12:11 My father made your workload heavy, but I will make it even heavier. He disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
1 Kings 12:12 So Jeroboam and all the people went to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them, "Come back to me on the third day."
1 Kings 12:13 The king spoke harshly to the people and ignored the advice the elders had given him.
1 Kings 12:14 He spoke to them, following the young men's advice, saying, "My father made your workload heavy, and I will make it even heavier. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."
1 Kings 12:15 So the king did not listen to the people, because this was God's plan, to fulfill what God had said through Ahijah from Shiloh to Jeroboam, Nebat's son.
1 Kings 12:16 When all Israel realized that the king did not listen to them, the people told the king, "What share do we have in David? We have no part in Jesse's son: Go to your homes, Israel. Take care of your own family, David." So Israel went back to their homes.
1 Kings 12:17 The children of Israel who lived in the towns of Judah were ruled by Rehoboam.
1 Kings 12:18 Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of taxes, but all the people of Israel stoned him to death. So King Rehoboam hurried to his chariot and escaped to Jerusalem.
1 Kings 12:19 Israel turned against David's family and has done so to this day.
1 Kings 12:20 When all of Israel learned that Jeroboam had returned, they called him to their assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah stayed loyal to David's family.
1 Kings 12:21 When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he gathered the people of Judah and the Benjamin tribe, 180,000 selected soldiers, to battle the people of Israel and return the kingdom to Rehoboam, Solomon's son.
1 Kings 12:22 God's message came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying,
1 Kings 12:23 Tell Rehoboam, Solomon's son and king of Judah, and all the people of Judah and Benjamin, and the others who are left, this message:
1 Kings 12:24 God says, “Do not attack or fight your brothers, the Israelites. Go back to your homes because this is my will." So they listened to God's command and went back home as God had said.
1 Kings 12:25 Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in the hills of Ephraim and lived there. Then he left and built Penuel.
1 Kings 12:26 Jeroboam thought, "Now the kingdom will go back to David's family."
1 Kings 12:27 If these people go to make sacrifices in God's house at Jerusalem, then their loyalty will return to their king, Rehoboam of Judah, and they will kill me and follow Rehoboam king of Judah again.
1 Kings 12:28 The king got advice, then made two gold calves and told the people, "It's too hard for you to go to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of Egypt."
1 Kings 12:29 He placed one idol in Bethel and the other in Dan.
1 Kings 12:30 This action became a sin because the people went to worship the statue, all the way to Dan.
1 Kings 12:31 He built a temple on high places and appointed as priests people of low status who were not from the Levi tribe.
1 Kings 12:32 Jeroboam set up a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day, similar to the one in Judah, and he made sacrifices on the altar. He did this in Bethel, offering to the calves he created, and he appointed priests for the shrines he made in Bethel.
1 Kings 12:33 He made sacrifices on the altar he built in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a date he chose himself; he set up a celebration for the Israelite people and he made offerings on the altar and burned incense.

1 Kings 13:1 A man of God came from Judah to Bethel because God told him to, and Jeroboam was by the altar burning incense.
1 Kings 13:2 He shouted to the altar with God's message: "Listen, altar! God says, 'A boy named Josiah will be born to David's family. He will sacrifice on you the priests from the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones will be burned on you.'"
1 Kings 13:3 That day, he gave a sign, saying, This is the sign God told of; Look, the altar will break, and the ashes on it will be scattered.
1 Kings 13:4 When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God shouted about the altar in Bethel, he reached out from the altar and said, "Grab him." But the hand he reached out withered, so he couldn't pull it back.
1 Kings 13:5 The altar split, and the ashes spilled from it, just as the man of God had predicted by God's message.
1 Kings 13:6 The king replied to the man of God, "Please ask God to heal me so my hand will be fixed." The man of God prayed to God, and the king's hand was healed and became like it was before.
1 Kings 13:7 The king said to the man of God, "Come to my home and rest, and I will give you a reward."
1 Kings 13:8 The man of God told the king, "Even if you offer me half of your house, I will not come inside with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water here."
1 Kings 13:9 I was ordered by God's command, saying, Do not eat bread, do not drink water, and do not go back the same way you came.
1 Kings 13:10 So he went a different way and did not come back by the same path he used to go to Bethel.
1 Kings 13:11 An old prophet lived in Bethel, and when his sons came, they told him everything the man of God did that day in Bethel, including the words he spoke to the king, which they also shared with their father.
1 Kings 13:12 Their father asked them, "Which way did he go?" because his sons had seen the direction the man of God from Judah had taken.
1 Kings 13:13 He told his sons, "Get the donkey ready for me." So they prepared the donkey and he rode on it.
1 Kings 13:14 He followed the man of God, found him sitting under an oak tree, and asked him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" He replied, "I am."
1 Kings 13:15 He said to him, "Come to my house and have some food."
1 Kings 13:16 He said, "I can't go back with you or enter with you. I won't eat bread or drink water with you here."
1 Kings 13:17 God told me not to eat bread, drink water, or go back the same way I came.
1 Kings 13:18 He told him, "I'm a prophet like you; an angel told me by God's command, 'Bring him back to your home so he can have food and water.'" But he was lying to him.
1 Kings 13:19 He returned with him and ate food in his house and drank water.
1 Kings 13:20 As they were sitting at the table, God spoke to the prophet who had brought him back.
1 Kings 13:21 He called out to the man of God from Judah, "This is what God says: Because you did not listen to God's word and did not follow the command that God gave you,
1 Kings 13:22 You came back and ate bread and drank water where God told you not to. Now you will not be buried with your ancestors.
1 Kings 13:23 After he ate bread and drank, he saddled the donkey for the prophet he had brought back.
1 Kings 13:24 After he left, a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body was thrown onto the road, and the donkey and the lion stood beside it.
1 Kings 13:25 Look, men walked by, saw the dead body on the road, and the lion standing near the body; they went and reported it in the town where the old prophet lived.
1 Kings 13:26 When the prophet who had brought him back heard of it, he said, "It is the man of God who did not obey God's command. So God has given him to the lion, which has mauled and killed him, just as God had said."
1 Kings 13:27 He said to his sons, "Get the donkey ready for me." So they got it ready.
1 Kings 13:28 He went and saw the body lying on the road with the donkey and the lion standing by it; the lion had not eaten the body or hurt the donkey.
1 Kings 13:29 The prophet picked up the body of the man of God, put it on the donkey, and took it back. The old prophet returned to the city to grieve and bury him.
1 Kings 13:30 He put his body in his own grave, and they cried for him, saying, "Oh, my brother!"
1 Kings 13:31 After he buried him, he told his sons, "When I die, bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried; put my bones next to his bones."
1 Kings 13:32 The message he shouted by God's command against the altar in Bethel, and against all the worship sites in the Samaria towns, will definitely happen.
1 Kings 13:33 After this, Jeroboam did not stop his bad ways, but again made the least of the people into priests for the high places. Anyone who wanted to, he made holy, and that person became a priest of the high places.
1 Kings 13:34 This act became a sin for Jeroboam's family, leading to its total destruction from the earth.

1 Kings 14:1 At that time, Abijah, Jeroboam's son, became ill.
1 Kings 14:2 Jeroboam said to his wife, "Please get up and change your look so no one knows you are my wife. Go to Shiloh where the prophet Ahijah lives. He's the one who said I would become king of these people."
1 Kings 14:3 Bring with you ten bread loaves, some biscuits, and a jar of honey, and go to him; he will tell you what will happen to the child.

1 Kings 14:19 The other things Jeroboam did, his battles and his rule, are written in the history book of Israel's kings.
1 Kings 14:20 Jeroboam ruled for twenty-two years, then he died, and his son Nadab became king after him.
1 Kings 14:21 Rehoboam, Solomon's son, became king in Judah. He was 41 when he started ruling, and he ruled for 17 years in Jerusalem, the city God chose from all of Israel's tribes to bear His name. His mother was Naamah, from the people of Ammon.
1 Kings 14:22 Judah did bad things that God saw, and their sins made God very jealous, even more than their ancestors had done.
1 Kings 14:23 They also made worship sites, idols, and sacred gardens on every tall hill and under every green tree.
1 Kings 14:24 There were also people doing wrong sexual acts in the land, behaving in all the bad ways of the nations that God had removed before the Israelites.

1 Kings 14:26 He removed the treasures from God's house and the king's palace; he took everything, even all the gold shields Solomon had made.
1 Kings 14:27 King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace the old ones and gave them to the leader of the guard who protected the entrance to the king's palace.
1 Kings 14:28 When the king entered God's house, the guards carried the items and then returned them to the guardroom.
1 Kings 14:29 The other things Rehoboam did and all his actions, aren't they recorded in the book of Judah's kings' histories?
1 Kings 14:30 Rehoboam and Jeroboam were at war for their whole lives.
1 Kings 14:31 Rehoboam died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. His mother's name was Naamah, from Ammon. His son Abijam became king after him.

1 Kings 16:32 He built an altar for Baal in the Baal temple he made in Samaria.
1 Kings 16:33 Ahab built a shrine; Ahab made God, the God of Israel, angrier than any of the previous kings of Israel.
1 Kings 16:34 During Hiel the Bethelite's time, he rebuilt Jericho. He started the work at the cost of his oldest son Abiram's life, and finished it at the cost of his youngest son Segub's life. This happened as God had said through Joshua, Nun's son.

1 Kings 17:1 Elijah from Tishbe in Gilead told Ahab, "As the living God of Israel, before whom I stand, there won't be any dew or rain for these years, unless I say so."
1 Kings 17:2 God's message came to him, saying,
1 Kings 17:3 Go away, turn east, and hide by the Cherith stream, in front of the Jordan.
1 Kings 17:4 You will drink from the stream, and I have told the ravens to bring you food there.
1 Kings 17:5 So he went and did as God had said. He lived by the Cherith stream, which is near the Jordan.
1 Kings 17:6 The birds brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the stream.
1 Kings 17:7 After some time, the stream dried up because there had been no rain in the country.
1 Kings 17:8 God's message came to him, saying,
1 Kings 17:9 Get up, go to Zarephath in Sidon, and stay there. I have told a widow there to take care of you.
1 Kings 17:10 He got up and went to Zarephath. As he arrived at the city entrance, he saw a widow picking up sticks. He asked her, “Please bring me a small amount of water in a container to drink.”
1 Kings 17:11 As she went to get it, he called to her and said, "Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand."
1 Kings 17:12 She said, "As God is alive, I don't have a cake, only a little flour in a jar and a bit of oil in a jug. Look, I'm picking up two sticks to cook it for me and my son, so we can eat it and then die."
1 Kings 17:13 Elijah told her, "Don't be afraid; go ahead and make what you said: but first, please make me a small cake and bring it to me, then make some for yourself and your son."
1 Kings 17:14 God says the jar of flour won't run out, and the jug of oil won't dry up, until the day God sends rain on the land.
1 Kings 17:15 She went and did as Elijah said: she, he, and her family ate for many days.
1 Kings 17:16 The jar of flour didn't run out, nor did the jug of oil dry up, just as God promised through Elijah.
1 Kings 17:17 After these events, the woman's son, who owned the house, became very ill, and he was so sick that he stopped breathing.
1 Kings 17:18 She asked Elijah, "What do you want with me, man of God? Have you come to remind me of my sin and cause my son to die?"
1 Kings 17:19 He said to her, "Give me your son." He took the boy from her arms, went to the upstairs room where he stayed, and laid him on his own bed.
1 Kings 17:20 He called out to God and said, "My God, have you also caused harm to the widow I'm staying with by causing her son to die?"
