1 Kings 17:21 He lay on the child three times, called to God, and said, "O God, please let the child's soul come back to him."
1 Kings 17:22 God heard Elijah's voice, and the child's life returned to him, and he came back to life.
1 Kings 17:23 Elijah took the child, brought him from the room into the house, and gave him to his mother. Elijah said, "Look, your son is alive."
1 Kings 17:24 The woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of God from your mouth is true."

1 Kings 18:1 After a long time, God's message came to Elijah in the third year, saying, "Go, meet Ahab, and I will make it rain on the land."
1 Kings 18:2 Elijah went to meet Ahab, and there was a severe famine in Samaria.
1 Kings 18:3 Ahab asked Obadiah, his house manager, to come. (Obadiah deeply respected God:
1 Kings 18:4 When Jezebel killed God's prophets, Obadiah took one hundred prophets, hid them in groups of fifty in caves, and gave them bread and water.
1 Kings 18:5 Ahab told Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the water springs and streams. Maybe we can find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so we don't lose all the animals."
1 Kings 18:6 They split the land to travel through it: Ahab went one way alone, and Obadiah went a different way alone.
1 Kings 18:7 As Obadiah was on the road, he met Elijah. He recognized him, bowed down to the ground, and asked, "Are you Elijah, my master?"
1 Kings 18:8 He replied, "I am Elijah; go tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"
1 Kings 18:9 He asked, "What did I do wrong that you would let your servant be killed by Ahab?"
1 Kings 18:10 As God, your God, is alive, there isn't any country or kingdom where my master hasn't looked for you. And when they said, "He's not here," he made each country and kingdom promise they hadn't found you.
1 Kings 18:11 Now you say, "Go, tell your master, 'Look, Elijah is here.'"
1 Kings 18:12 When I leave you, God's Spirit will take you to a place I don't know. So when I tell Ahab and he can't find you, he will kill me. But I, your servant, have feared God since I was young.
1 Kings 18:13 Didn't someone tell you, my lord, what I did when Jezebel killed God's prophets? I hid a hundred of God's prophets in caves, fifty in each, and gave them bread and water.
1 Kings 18:14 You say, "Go tell your master, 'Elijah is here,'" but he will kill me.
1 Kings 18:15 Elijah said, "As the living God of all commands, whom I serve, I will definitely show myself to him today."
1 Kings 18:16 Obadiah met Ahab and told him, and then Ahab went to meet Elijah.
1 Kings 18:17 When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, "Are you the one who troubles Israel?"
1 Kings 18:18 He replied, "I have not caused trouble in Israel; it is you and your family because you have ignored God's commands and followed the Baals."
1 Kings 18:19 So now, send a message and bring all of Israel to Mount Carmel, along with the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of the groves who are fed by Jezebel.
1 Kings 18:20 Ahab sent a message to all the Israelites and brought the prophets to Mount Carmel.
1 Kings 18:21 Elijah came to everyone and asked, "How long will you hesitate between two choices? If God is the true God, follow Him; but if Baal is, then follow him." But the people didn't say anything in reply.
1 Kings 18:22 Elijah told the people, "I am the only one left of God's prophets, but there are 450 prophets of Baal."
1 Kings 18:23 So they should give us two young bulls. They can pick one, cut it up, and place it on the wood without setting it on fire. I'll prepare the other bull, put it on the wood, and also not light it.
1 Kings 18:24 Ask your gods for help, and I will ask God for help. The one who sends fire is the true God. And everyone agreed this was a good plan.
1 Kings 18:25 Elijah said to Baal's prophets, "Pick one bull for yourselves, prepare it first since you are many, and pray to your gods, but don't light a fire under it."
1 Kings 18:26 They took the bull given to them, prepared it, and prayed to Baal from morning to noon, saying, "O Baal, listen to us." But there was no reply or anyone who answered. And they jumped on the altar that was built.
1 Kings 18:27 At noon, Elijah made fun of them and said, "Shout louder; maybe your god is busy talking, away on a trip, taking a nap, or needs to wake up."
1 Kings 18:28 They shouted loudly and cut themselves with knives and sharp tools, as was their custom, until blood flowed out on them.
1 Kings 18:29 After midday, they continued to prophesy until the evening sacrifice, but there was no voice, no answer, and no one paid attention.
1 Kings 18:30 Elijah said to everyone, "Come closer to me." So all the people came closer to him. Then he fixed God's altar that was damaged.
1 Kings 18:31 Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of Jacob's sons, because God had said, "Your name will be Israel."
1 Kings 18:32 He used the stones to build an altar for God and dug a ditch around it big enough to hold two measures of seed.
1 Kings 18:33 He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, placed it on the wood, and said, "Fill four barrels with water and pour it over the burnt offering and the wood."
1 Kings 18:34 He said, "Do it again." So they did it again. Then he said, "Do it a third time." And they did it a third time.
1 Kings 18:35 Water flowed around the altar, and the trench was also filled with water.
1 Kings 18:36 When the time came to offer the evening sacrifice, the prophet Elijah stepped forward and prayed, "God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, show everyone today that you are the true God in Israel, that I am your servant, and that I have followed your instructions.
1 Kings 18:37 Listen to me, God, listen to me, so these people will know you are God, and that you have turned their hearts back to you again.
1 Kings 18:38 Then God's fire came down and burned up the offering, the wood, the stones, the dust, and even dried up the water in the ditch.
1 Kings 18:39 When everyone saw this, they fell down and said, "God is the God; God is the God."
1 Kings 18:40 Elijah said to them, "Capture the prophets of Baal and don't let any of them get away." They captured them, and Elijah took them to the Kishon creek and killed them there.
1 Kings 18:41 Elijah told Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink; because I hear the sound of a lot of rain coming."
1 Kings 18:42 So Ahab went to eat and drink. Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel, lay down on the ground, and put his face between his knees.
1 Kings 18:43 He told his servant, "Go up now, look toward the sea." So he went up, looked, and said, "There is nothing." Then he was told, "Go back seven times."
1 Kings 18:44 On the seventh time, he saw a small cloud rising from the sea, like a man's hand. He told the messenger to tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and go before the rain stopped him.
1 Kings 18:45 Meanwhile, the sky turned dark with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain fell. Ahab rode off to Jezreel.
1 Kings 18:46 God's power was with Elijah; he tied up his clothes and ran ahead of Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

1 Kings 19:1 Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah did, including how he killed all the prophets with a sword.
1 Kings 19:2 Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "I hope the gods punish me severely if I don't make your life like one of them by this time tomorrow."
1 Kings 19:3 Seeing that, he got up, ran for his life, and arrived at Beersheba in Judah, where he left his servant.
1 Kings 19:4 He went alone into the desert for a day, sat under a juniper tree, and wished to die, saying, "It is enough; now, God, take my life, for I am no better than my ancestors."
1 Kings 19:5 As he was sleeping under a juniper tree, an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."
1 Kings 19:6 He saw a baked cake on the coals and a jar of water by his head. He ate and drank, then lay down again.
1 Kings 19:7 The angel of God came back a second time, touched him, and said, "Get up and eat, because the trip is too much for you."
1 Kings 19:8 He got up, ate and drank, then traveled with the power from that food for forty days and nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
1 Kings 19:9 He went to a cave to stay, and there God's message came to him. He asked, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
1 Kings 19:10 He said, "I have been very loyal to God, because the people of Israel have broken your agreement, destroyed your places of worship, and killed your messengers with the sword; and I am the only one left; and now they want to kill me too."
1 Kings 19:11 He said, "Go out and stand on the mountain in front of God." Then, as God passed by, a powerful wind tore the mountains apart and shattered the rocks, but God was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but God was not in the earthquake.
1 Kings 19:12 After the earthquake came a fire, but God was not in the fire; and after the fire, a quiet, gentle sound.
1 Kings 19:13 When Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his cloak and went out to stand at the cave entrance. Then a voice came to him and asked, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
1 Kings 19:14 He said, "I have been very loyal to God because the Israelites have broken your agreement, destroyed your places of worship, and killed your messengers with the sword; now I am the only one left, and they want to kill me too."
1 Kings 19:15 God told him, "Go back through the desert to Damascus, and when you arrive, make Hazael king over Syria."
1 Kings 19:16 You must anoint Jehu, Nimshi's son, to be king of Israel, and anoint Elisha, Shaphat's son from Abelmeholah, to be prophet in your place.
1 Kings 19:17 Anyone who escapes Hazael's sword will be killed by Jehu, and anyone who escapes Jehu's sword will be killed by Elisha.
1 Kings 19:18 Still, I have kept 7,000 people in Israel, all who have not bowed to Baal, and all whose mouths have not kissed him.
1 Kings 19:19 He left that place and found Elisha, Shaphat’s son, plowing with twelve pairs of oxen, and he was with the last pair. Elijah went by him and threw his cloak over him.
1 Kings 19:20 He left the oxen, ran to Elijah, and said, "Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you." Elijah replied, "Go back. What have I done to you?"
1 Kings 19:21 He went back, took a pair of oxen, killed them, cooked their meat with the oxen's gear, and gave it to the people to eat. Then he got up, followed Elijah, and helped him.

1 Kings 20:1 Benhadad, the king of Syria, brought all his army together. He was joined by thirty-two kings, with their horses and chariots. He advanced and laid siege to Samaria and attacked it.
1 Kings 20:2 He sent messengers to Ahab, the king of Israel, in the city, telling him, "Benhadad says,
1 Kings 20:3 Your silver and your gold are mine; your wives and children, even the most beautiful, are mine too.
1 Kings 20:4 The king of Israel replied and said, "My lord, O king, as you say, I am yours, and all that I have."
1 Kings 20:5 The messengers came back and said, "Benhadad says, 'Even though I've sent you a message demanding you give me your silver, gold, wives, and children...'"
1 Kings 20:6 I will send my servants to you tomorrow at this time, and they will search your house and your servants' houses. Whatever you like, they will take it.
1 Kings 20:7 The king of Israel called all the leaders and said, "Notice and see how this man wants to cause trouble. He asked for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, and I didn't refuse him."
1 Kings 20:8 All the leaders and everyone told him, "Don't listen to him or agree."
1 Kings 20:9 So he told Benhadad's messengers, "Tell my king I will do all he first asked of me, but I can't do this." The messengers left and reported back to him.
1 Kings 20:10 Benhadad sent a message saying, "May the gods punish me severely if there is enough dust in Samaria for all my followers to grab a handful."
1 Kings 20:11 The king of Israel replied, "Tell him not to brag while putting on his armor like one who takes it off after battle."
1 Kings 20:12 When Ben-hadad heard this message while he was drinking with the kings in their tents, he told his servants to get ready for battle. So they prepared to attack the city.
1 Kings 20:13 Look, a prophet came to Ahab, the king of Israel, and said, "This is what God says: 'Have you seen this huge crowd? I will give them to you today, and you will know that I am God.'"
1 Kings 20:14 Ahab asked, "By whom?" He replied, "God says, 'By the young men of the province leaders.'" Then Ahab asked, "Who will lead the attack?" He answered, "You will."
1 Kings 20:15 He counted the young men from the provincial leaders, totaling 232; then he counted all the others, all the Israelites, and there were 7,000.
1 Kings 20:16 They left at midday. But Benhadad and the thirty-two kings helping him were getting drunk in the tents.
1 Kings 20:17 The young leaders' soldiers went first. Then Benhadad was informed, "Men have come out of Samaria."
1 Kings 20:18 He said, "If they come for peace, capture them alive; if they come for war, capture them alive."
1 Kings 20:19 These young men, who were the leaders' sons, left the city, along with the army that followed them.
1 Kings 20:20 Everyone killed their opponent, the Syrians ran away, Israel chased them, and King Benhadad of Syria escaped on a horse with his cavalry.
1 Kings 20:21 The king of Israel went out, attacked the horses and chariots, and killed many Syrians.
1 Kings 20:22 The prophet went to the king of Israel and told him, "Go, get stronger, pay attention, and be careful with what you do. Because when the year comes around again, the king of Syria will attack you."
1 Kings 20:23 The king of Syria's servants told him, "Their god is a god of the hills; that's why they were stronger than us. But if we fight them on the flat land, we will definitely be stronger than them."
1 Kings 20:24 Do this: Remove the kings, every one from their positions, and appoint captains in their places.
1 Kings 20:25 Count yourself an army, just like the one you lost, with the same number of horses and chariots. Then we will battle them on the flat land, and we will definitely be stronger. He listened to their advice and did it.
1 Kings 20:26 When the year came around again, Benhadad counted the Syrian troops and moved to Aphek to battle Israel.
1 Kings 20:27 The Israelites were counted, all showed up, and fought against them. The Israelites camped in front of them, looking like two small groups of young goats, while the Syrians covered the land.
1 Kings 20:28 A man of God came and spoke to the king of Israel, saying, "This is what God says: 'Because the Syrians believe that God is only the God of the hills and not of the valleys, I will give you victory over this large army, and you will realize that I am God.'"
1 Kings 20:29 They camped facing each other for seven days. On the seventh day, the fight began, and the Israelites killed one hundred thousand Syrian foot soldiers in one day.
1 Kings 20:30 But the others ran away to Aphek, into the city. There, a wall collapsed on twenty-seven thousand of the remaining men. Benhadad also ran away and went into the city, to a room inside.
1 Kings 20:31 His servants told him, "We have heard that Israel's kings are kind. Please let us wear rough cloth around our waists and put ropes on our heads, and go to the king of Israel. Maybe he will spare your life."
1 Kings 20:32 They wrapped rough cloth around their waists, placed ropes on their heads, went to the king of Israel, and said, "Your servant Benhadad asks, please let me live." And he replied, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
1 Kings 20:33 The men watched carefully to see if he would do something. When he gave a sign, they quickly took it. They said, "Your brother Benhadad." He replied, "Go and bring him." So Benhadad came to him, and he helped him into the chariot.
1 Kings 20:34 Ben-hadad told him, "I'll give back the cities my father took from your father; you can build your own neighborhoods in Damascus, like my father did in Samaria." Then Ahab replied, "With this agreement, I'll let you go." So he made an agreement with him and let him go.
1 Kings 20:35 A man from the group of prophets told his friend, speaking for God, "Please hit me." But the man would not hit him.
1 Kings 20:36 He told him, "Because you didn't listen to God, as soon as you leave me, a lion will kill you." And right after he left him, a lion found him and killed him.
1 Kings 20:37 He found another person and said, "Please hit me." So the person hit him, injuring him in the process.
1 Kings 20:38 The prophet left and waited for the king on the road, hiding his face with ashes.
1 Kings 20:39 As the king went by, he called out to the king: "I went into the battle, and a man gave me another man and told me, 'Guard this man. If he goes missing, you'll have to die in his place or pay a talent of silver.'"
1 Kings 20:40 While your servant was busy, he disappeared. The king of Israel said, "That will be your punishment; you have chosen it yourself."
1 Kings 20:41 He hurried to remove the ashes from his face, and the king of Israel recognized that he was one of the prophets.
1 Kings 20:42 He told him, "God says, because you released a man I wanted to destroy, your life will be taken for his life, and your people for his people."
1 Kings 20:43 The king of Israel went home sad and upset, and arrived in Samaria.

1 Kings 21:1 After these events, Naboth, from Jezreel, owned a vineyard next to Ahab's palace, the king of Samaria.
1 Kings 21:2 Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard so I can use it for a garden of herbs since it's close to my house. I'll give you a better vineyard in exchange, or if you prefer, I'll pay you its value in money."
1 Kings 21:3 Naboth said to Ahab, "God won’t allow it. I can’t give you what I inherited from my ancestors."
1 Kings 21:4 Ahab went into his house feeling sad and upset because of what Naboth from Jezreel told him. Naboth had said, "I won't give you my family's land." Ahab lay down on his bed, turned his face to the wall, and refused to eat.
1 Kings 21:5 Jezebel, his wife, came to him and asked, "Why are you so sad that you're not eating?"
1 Kings 21:6 He told her, "I talked to Naboth from Jezreel. I offered to buy his vineyard or trade it for another one if he liked. But he said, 'I won't give you my vineyard.'"
1 Kings 21:7 Jezebel, his wife, said to him, "Are you not ruling Israel? Get up, eat some bread, and cheer up; I will get you Naboth's vineyard."
1 Kings 21:8 She wrote letters using Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the city elders and nobles who lived with Naboth.
1 Kings 21:9 She wrote in the letters, "Announce a fast, and put Naboth in a prominent place among the people."
1 Kings 21:10 Place two wicked men in front of him to accuse him, saying, "You insulted God and the king." Then take him out and throw stones at him until he dies.
1 Kings 21:11 The men of the city, including the elders and leaders who lived there, did what Jezebel told them, following the instructions in her letters.
1 Kings 21:12 They announced a time without food and placed Naboth in a high position among the people.
1 Kings 21:13 Two bad men came and sat in front of him. They lied about Naboth in front of everyone, saying, "Naboth insulted God and the king." So they took Naboth out of the city and threw stones at him until he died.
1 Kings 21:14 They sent a message to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."
1 Kings 21:15 When Jezebel found out that Naboth had been stoned to death, she told Ahab, "Get up and take over Naboth the Jezreelite's vineyard, because he didn't sell it to you. Now that he's dead, it's yours."
1 Kings 21:16 When Ahab learned that Naboth had died, he got up to go to Naboth the Jezreelite's vineyard to take it over.
1 Kings 21:17 God's message came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
1 Kings 21:18 Get up, go meet Ahab, the king of Israel, in Samaria. Look, he is in Naboth's vineyard, where he has gone to take it over.
1 Kings 21:19 You will tell him, 'God says, "Have you murdered and also taken the land?"' And you will say to him, 'God says, "In the spot where dogs licked Naboth's blood, dogs will lick your blood too."'
1 Kings 21:20 Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" Elijah answered, "Yes, I have found you because you have chosen to do evil in God's eyes."
1 Kings 21:21 I will bring bad things on you, take away your future family, and destroy every male belonging to Ahab, whether they are free or trapped in Israel.
1 Kings 21:22 I will make your family like Jeroboam's family, the son of Nebat, and like Baasha's family, the son of Ahijah because you have made me angry and caused Israel to sin.
1 Kings 21:23 God also said about Jezebel, "Dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel."
1 Kings 21:24 Anyone from Ahab's family who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by birds.
1 Kings 21:25 No one was like Ahab; he chose to do evil, watched by God, encouraged by his wife Jezebel.
1 Kings 21:26 He did terrible things by worshiping idols, just like the Amorites, whom God had driven out before the Israelites.
1 Kings 21:27 When Ahab heard those words, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, fasted, lay in sackcloth, and walked quietly.
1 Kings 21:28 God's message came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
1 Kings 21:29 Do you see how Ahab is humbling himself before me? Because he is doing this, I will not cause bad things to happen during his life; instead, I will make them happen during his son's life to his family.

1 Kings 22:1 They had peace for three years without fighting between Syria and Israel.
1 Kings 22:2 In the third year, King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to see the king of Israel.
1 Kings 22:3 The king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth in Gilead belongs to us, yet we do nothing to take it back from the king of Syria?"
1 Kings 22:4 He said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you join me in the fight at Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat replied to the king of Israel, "I am with you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses."
1 Kings 22:5 Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please ask for God's guidance today."
1 Kings 22:6 The king of Israel brought together about four hundred prophets and asked them, "Should I go to war against Ramothgilead or not?" They replied, "Go, for God will give it to the king."
1 Kings 22:7 Jehoshaphat asked, "Isn't there a prophet of God here we can ask?"
1 Kings 22:8 The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man, Micaiah son of Imlah, who can ask God for us. But I hate him because he never predicts anything good about me, only bad." Jehoshaphat replied, "The king shouldn't say that."
1 Kings 22:9 The king of Israel called an officer and said, "Quickly bring Micaiah, Imlah's son, here."
1 Kings 22:10 The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, were sitting on their thrones, dressed in their robes, at an open area by the gate of Samaria, while all the prophets spoke their prophecies in front of them.
1 Kings 22:11 Zedekiah, Chenaanah's son, made iron horns and said, "God says, 'With these, you will push the Syrians until they are defeated.'"
1 Kings 22:12 All the prophets said the same thing: "Go to Ramothgilead and you will succeed, because God will give it to the king."
1 Kings 22:13 The messenger who went to get Micaiah said to him, "Look, all the prophets are telling the king good news with one voice. Please make your words like theirs and say something good."
1 Kings 22:14 Micaiah said, "As God lives, whatever God tells me, I will say."
1 Kings 22:15 He went to the king. The king asked him, "Micaiah, should we fight against Ramothgilead or not?" He replied, "Go and succeed, because God will give it to the king."
1 Kings 22:16 The king said to him, "How many times must I order you to tell me only the truth by God's name?"
1 Kings 22:17 He said, "I saw all Israel spread out on the hills, like sheep without a shepherd. And God said, 'These people have no leader; let them each go back to their own home in peace.'"
1 Kings 22:18 The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I say he would not predict anything good about me, but only bad?"
1 Kings 22:19 He said, "Listen to God's message: I saw God sitting on his throne with all the heavenly beings standing around him on his right and on his left."
1 Kings 22:20 God asked, "Who will convince Ahab to attack Ramothgilead and die there?" One suggested this way, and another suggested that way.
1 Kings 22:21 A spirit came out, stood before God, and said, "I will convince him."
1 Kings 22:22 God asked him, "How?" He replied, "I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets." God said, "You will persuade him and succeed. Go out and do it."
1 Kings 22:23 Now, look, God has placed a lying spirit in the mouths of all your prophets, and God has said bad things about you.
1 Kings 22:24 But Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, came forward, hit Micaiah on the face, and said, "How did God's Spirit leave me to talk to you?"
1 Kings 22:25 Micaiah said, "Look, you will see on that day, when you go into a room to hide."
1 Kings 22:26 The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and take him back to Amon, the city's governor, and to Joash, the king's son."
1 Kings 22:27 Say, "The king orders, put this man in jail and give him only poor bread and water until I return safely."
1 Kings 22:28 Micaiah said, "If you come back safely, God has not spoken through me." And he said, "Listen, everyone."
1 Kings 22:29 The king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to Ramoth-gilead.
1 Kings 22:30 The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "I will hide who I am and go into the fight; but you wear your royal clothes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and joined the battle.
1 Kings 22:31 The king of Syria ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, saying, "Do not fight with anyone, important or not, except the king of Israel."
1 Kings 22:32 When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, "This must be the king of Israel." So they went to attack him, and Jehoshaphat shouted for help.
1 Kings 22:33 When the chariot commanders realized he was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.
1 Kings 22:34 A man randomly shot an arrow and hit the king of Israel in the armor gaps. So he told his chariot driver, "Turn around and take me out of the battle; I'm hurt."
1 Kings 22:35 The fight grew fiercer that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing the Syrians, and he died in the evening; blood flowed from his injury into the middle of the chariot.
1 Kings 22:36 A message went through the camp as the sun was setting, saying, "Everyone go to your own city and your own country."
1 Kings 22:37 The king died and was taken to Samaria; they buried him there.
1 Kings 22:38 Someone washed the chariot at the Samaria pool, and dogs licked up his blood. They also washed his armor, just as God had said.
1 Kings 22:39 The other things Ahab did, what he built, including the ivory house and cities, are they not recorded in the book of the history of Israel's kings?
1 Kings 22:40 So Ahab died as his ancestors did; and his son Ahaziah became king after him.
1 Kings 22:41 Jehoshaphat, Asa's son, became king of Judah in the fourth year of Ahab's rule over Israel.
1 Kings 22:42 Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king; he ruled for 25 years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah, and her father was Shilhi.
1 Kings 22:43 He followed the example of his father Asa and did not turn away from it, doing what was right in God's eyes. However, the high places were not removed; the people still offered and burned incense there.
1 Kings 22:44 Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
1 Kings 22:45 The other things Jehoshaphat did, his power, and his battles are written in the history book of Judah's kings, aren't they?
1 Kings 22:46 He removed the remaining people of sinful practices left from his father Asa's time from the land.
1 Kings 22:47 At that time, Edom had no king; a deputy ruled instead.
1 Kings 22:48 Jehoshaphat built ships to sail to Ophir for gold, but they never went because the ships were wrecked at Eziongeber.
1 Kings 22:49 Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my men go with your men on the ships." But Jehoshaphat did not agree.
1 Kings 22:50 Jehoshaphat died like his ancestors and was buried with them in David's city. Jehoram, his son, became king after him.
1 Kings 22:51 Ahaziah, Ahab's son, became king of Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled over Israel for two years.
1 Kings 22:52 He did wrong in God's eyes, following the path of his father, his mother, and Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who led Israel into sin.
1 Kings 22:53 He worshiped Baal and made him offerings, and angered God, just as his father had done.

2 Kings 1:1 Moab fought against Israel after Ahab died.
2 Kings 1:2 Ahaziah fell through a grid in his upstairs room in Samaria and was injured. He sent messengers and told them, "Go, ask Baalzebub, the god of Ekron, if I will get better from my illness."
2 Kings 1:3 The angel said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up, go to meet the king of Samaria's messengers, and ask them, 'Do you look for advice from Baalzebub, the god of Ekron, because you think there is no God in Israel?'"
2 Kings 1:4 So now, God says, "You will not get up from the bed you are lying on; you will certainly die." Then Elijah left.
2 Kings 1:5 When the messengers returned to him, he asked them, "Why have you come back?"
2 Kings 1:6 They told him, "A man came to meet us and he said, 'Go back to the king who sent you and tell him, "God says, 'Are you asking Baalzebub, the god of Ekron, for help because there's no God in Israel? You won't get up from the bed you're lying on; you will definitely die.'"'"
2 Kings 1:7 He asked them, "What kind of man met you and spoke these words to you?"
2 Kings 1:8 They replied, "He was a hairy man, wearing a leather belt around his waist." And he said, "That's Elijah the Tishbite."
2 Kings 1:9 The king sent a leader of fifty men with his fifty to him. He approached and saw him sitting on the hilltop. He said to him, "Man of God, the king orders you to come down."
2 Kings 1:10 Elijah replied to the officer of fifty, "If I am a man of God, may fire fall from the sky and burn you and your fifty men." And fire fell from the sky and burned him and his fifty men.
2 Kings 1:11 Once more, he sent another captain with his fifty men. He spoke to him, saying, "Man of God, the king orders you to come down at once."
2 Kings 1:12 Elijah replied, "If I am a man of God, may fire fall from the sky and burn you and your fifty men." And God's fire fell from the sky and burned him and his fifty men.
2 Kings 1:13 He sent another leader of fifty with his soldiers. This third leader went to Elijah, knelt down before him, begged him, and said, "Please, man of God, value my life and the lives of these fifty men serving you."
2 Kings 1:14 Look, fire came down from the sky and burned up the two leaders and their groups of fifty; so now, please value my life.
2 Kings 1:15 God's angel said to Elijah, "Go with him. Don't be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went with him to the king.
2 Kings 1:16 He told him, "God says, 'Because you sent messengers to ask Baalzebub, the god of Ekron, instead of asking me, isn't it because you think there's no God in Israel to seek advice from? So, you won't leave the bed you're lying on; you will definitely die.'"
2 Kings 1:17 He died as God told through Elijah. Jehoram became king after him in the second year of Jehoram, Jehoshaphat's son, king of Judah, because he had no son.
2 Kings 1:18 The other things Ahaziah did are written in the history book of Israel's kings, aren't they?

2 Kings 2:1 When God was about to take Elijah to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha left Gilgal together.
2 Kings 2:2 Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here because God has sent me to Bethel." Elisha replied, "As long as God lives and you are alive, I will not leave you." So they went to Bethel.
2 Kings 2:3 The prophet students in Bethel went to Elisha and told him, "Do you know God will take your leader away from you today?" He replied, "Yes, I know; be quiet."
2 Kings 2:4 Elijah told him, "Elisha, please stay here because God has sent me to Jericho." Elisha replied, "As surely as God lives and you are alive, I won't leave you." So they went to Jericho together.
2 Kings 2:5 The prophets' sons in Jericho approached Elisha and asked, "Do you know that God will take your leader away from you today?" He replied, "Yes, I know; be quiet."
2 Kings 2:6 Elijah told him, "Please stay here, because God has sent me to Jordan." He replied, "As surely as God lives, and as you live, I won't leave you." So they both went together.
2 Kings 2:7 Fifty sons of the prophets went and watched from a distance while the two of them stood by the Jordan River.
2 Kings 2:8 Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, struck the water, and it split apart so they both could cross on dry land.
2 Kings 2:9 When they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, "Tell me what I can do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha replied, "Please, let me inherit a double share of your spirit."
2 Kings 2:10 He said, "You've asked for something difficult. But if you see me as I am being taken from you, you will get what you asked for. If you don't see me, you won't get it."
2 Kings 2:11 As they were walking and talking, suddenly a fiery chariot and fiery horses appeared and separated them; then Elijah was taken up into heaven by a whirlwind.
2 Kings 2:12 Elisha saw it and yelled, "My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!" He saw him no more, grabbed his clothes, and tore them in half.
2 Kings 2:13 He picked up Elijah’s cloak that had fallen from him, went back, and stood by the Jordan River’s edge.
2 Kings 2:14 He took Elijah's cloak that dropped, hit the water, and said, "Where is the God of Elijah?" After he struck the water, it split apart, and Elisha crossed over.
2 Kings 2:15 When the prophet students in Jericho saw him, they said, "Elijah's spirit now rests on Elisha." They went to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.
2 Kings 2:16 They said to him, "Look, we have fifty strong men with us. Please let them go and look for your master. Maybe God's Spirit lifted him and put him on a mountain or in a valley." But he answered, "Do not send them."
2 Kings 2:17 When they pressed him until he felt embarrassed, he said, "Go." So they sent fifty men who searched for three days but did not find him.
2 Kings 2:18 When they returned to him (since he stayed in Jericho), he said, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"
2 Kings 2:19 The city men told Elisha, "Please look, the place of this city is nice, as you see: but the water is bad, and the land does not produce."
2 Kings 2:20 He said, "Bring me a new jar and put salt in it." And they brought it to him.
2 Kings 2:21 He went to the water spring, threw in the salt, and said, "God says, 'I have made these waters healthy; from now on, there will be no more death or unfruitful land here.'"
2 Kings 2:22 The waters are still healed today, just as Elisha had said.
2 Kings 2:23 He went from there to Bethel, and as he was walking along the road, some children came out of the city and made fun of him, saying, "Go on up, you baldy! Go on up, you baldy!"
2 Kings 2:24 He turned around, saw them, and cursed them in God's name. Then two bears came out of the woods and attacked forty-two of the youths.
2 Kings 2:25 He left there for Mount Carmel, and then he went back to Samaria.

2 Kings 3:1 Jehoram, Ahab's son, started to rule over Israel in Samaria during Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as Judah's king, and he ruled for twelve years.
2 Kings 3:2 He did bad things in God's eyes, but not as much as his father and mother did. He got rid of the Baal statue his father had made.
2 Kings 3:3 He continued doing the same wrongs as Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin; he did not stop these actions.
2 Kings 3:4 Mesha, the king of Moab, raised sheep and gave the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and 100,000 rams, along with their wool.
2 Kings 3:5 After Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
2 Kings 3:6 King Jehoram left Samaria then and counted all the people of Israel.
2 Kings 3:7 He went and sent a message to Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah: "The king of Moab has revolted against me. Will you join me to fight against Moab?" Jehoshaphat replied, "I will go with you. I am like you, my people are like your people, and my horses like your horses."
2 Kings 3:8 He asked, "Which way should we go up?" He replied, "The way through the Edom desert."
2 Kings 3:9 The king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out and traveled for seven days, but there was no water for the army or the animals with them.
2 Kings 3:10 The king of Israel said, "Oh no! God has brought these three kings together only to let Moab defeat us!"
2 Kings 3:11 Jehoshaphat asked, "Isn't there a prophet of God here so we can ask God for guidance?" And one servant of Israel's king replied, "Elisha, son of Shaphat, who used to help Elijah by pouring water on his hands, is here."
2 Kings 3:12 Jehoshaphat said, "God's message is with him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went to see him.
2 Kings 3:13 Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do I have to do with you? Go to your father's prophets and your mother's prophets." But the king of Israel replied, "No, because God has brought these three kings together to give them to Moab."
2 Kings 3:14 Elisha said, "As the living God commands, I serve Him. Truly, if not for my respect for Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not even look at or see you."
2 Kings 3:15 Now bring me a musician. And when the musician played, God's power came upon him.
2 Kings 3:16 He said, "God tells us to dig many ditches in this valley."
2 Kings 3:17 God says, "You won't see wind or rain, but the valley will get filled with water so you and your animals can drink."
2 Kings 3:18 This is easy for God; He will also give you victory over the Moabites.
2 Kings 3:19 You must attack every protected city and every valuable city, cut down every good tree, block all the water wells, and cover every good piece of land with stones.
2 Kings 3:20 In the morning, when the grain offering was made, suddenly water flowed from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
2 Kings 3:21 When all the people of Moab heard that the kings had come to battle them, they called together everyone who could wear armor, and older, and they took positions at the border.
2 Kings 3:22 They got up early in the morning, the sun shined on the water, and the Moabites saw the water on the other side looking as red as blood.
2 Kings 3:23 They said, "This is blood: the kings must be killed, and they have attacked each other: now, Moab, let's go take their things."
2 Kings 3:24 When they reached Israel's camp, the Israelites got up and struck the Moabites, making them run away. But they kept on attacking the Moabites in their own land.
2 Kings 3:25 They destroyed the cities, threw stones on all the good land, and filled it up; they blocked all the water wells, and cut down the good trees. Only in Kirharaseth did they leave the stones in place; but slingers surrounded it and attacked it.
2 Kings 3:26 When the king of Moab realized the battle was too tough, he took seven hundred swordsmen to try and get to the king of Edom, but they failed.
2 Kings 3:27 He sacrificed his oldest son, who was to become king, as a burnt offering on the wall. This act caused great anger towards Israel, making the people leave and go back to their land.

2 Kings 4:1 A woman whose husband had died, who was one of the prophets' sons, called out to Elisha, "My husband, your servant, is dead. You know he respected God. Now a creditor is here to take my two sons as slaves."
2 Kings 4:2 Elisha asked her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what do you have at home?" She replied, "Your servant has nothing at home except a jar of oil."
2 Kings 4:3 He said, "Go, ask your neighbors for empty jars. Get a lot of them."
2 Kings 4:4 When you enter, close the door behind you and your sons, pour oil into all the jars, and put aside the ones that are full.
2 Kings 4:5 She left him, closed the door behind her and her sons, they brought the containers to her, and she filled them up.
2 Kings 4:6 When the jars were all full, she told her son, "Bring me another jar." But he replied, "There are no more jars." Then the oil stopped flowing.
2 Kings 4:7 She went to the man of God and told him. He said, "Go, sell the oil, pay what you owe, and use the rest to live on with your children."
2 Kings 4:8 One day, Elisha went to Shunem, where a notable woman lived; she urged him to have some bread. From then on, whenever he came by, he would stop there to eat bread.
2 Kings 4:9 She told her husband, "Look, I think this is a holy man of God who keeps passing by us."
2 Kings 4:10 Let's build a small room on the wall. We'll put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp in it for him. So when he visits, he can stay there.
2 Kings 4:11 One day he went there, entered the room, and rested.
2 Kings 4:12 He told his servant Gehazi, "Call this woman from Shunem." When Gehazi called her, she came and stood before him.
2 Kings 4:13 He told him, "Tell her, 'Look, you have done so much for us; what can we do for you? Do you want us to speak to the king or the army commander on your behalf?'" And she replied, "I live among my own people."
2 Kings 4:14 He asked, "So what can be done for her?" Gehazi replied, "Truly, she has no child, and her husband is old."
2 Kings 4:15 He said, "Call her." When he called her, she stood at the door.
2 Kings 4:16 He said, "By this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms." But she replied, "No, my lord, you man of God, do not deceive your servant."
2 Kings 4:17 The woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son at the time Elisha had told her, when it was due.
2 Kings 4:18 When the child grew up, one day he went to his father with the harvesters.
2 Kings 4:19 He told his father, "My head hurts." His father said to a boy, "Take him to his mother."
2 Kings 4:20 After he took him and brought him to his mother, he sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
2 Kings 4:21 She went up, put him on the man of God's bed, closed the door, and left.
2 Kings 4:22 She asked her husband, "Please send one of the young men and a donkey with me so I can go to the man of God and return."
2 Kings 4:23 He asked, "Why do you want to go to him today? It's not the new moon or the Sabbath." She answered, "It will be okay."
2 Kings 4:24 She put a saddle on a donkey, and told her servant, "Go ahead; don't slow down the ride for me unless I tell you to."
2 Kings 4:25 She went to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, "Look, there is the woman from Shunem."
2 Kings 4:26 Please go now and meet her. Ask her if she is okay, if her husband is okay, and if her child is okay. She replied, "All is well."
2 Kings 4:27 When she arrived at the hill where the man of God was, she grabbed his feet. Gehazi tried to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her be; she is deeply troubled, and God has kept the reason hidden from me and hasn't told me."
2 Kings 4:28 Then she said, "Did I ask for a son from you, God? Didn't I say, 'Don't trick me'?"
2 Kings 4:29 He told Gehazi, "Tie your clothes tight, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, don't say hello; if they greet you, don't reply. Put my staff on the child's face."
2 Kings 4:30 The child's mother said, "As long as God lives and you are alive, I won't leave you." So he got up and went with her.
2 Kings 4:31 Gehazi went ahead of them and put the staff on the child's face; but there was no sound or response. So he returned to meet him and told him, "The child has not woken up."
2 Kings 4:32 When Elisha entered the house, he saw the child was dead and lying on his bed.
2 Kings 4:33 He went in, closed the door behind them both, and prayed to God.
2 Kings 4:34 He went up, lay on the child, put his mouth on the child's mouth, his eyes on the child's eyes, his hands on the child's hands, extended himself on the child, and the child's body became warm.
2 Kings 4:35 He went back and forth inside the house, then went up and lay on top of the boy. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
2 Kings 4:36 He called Gehazi and said, "Call this woman from Shunem." So he called her. When she came to him, he said, "Pick up your son."
2 Kings 4:37 She went in, knelt at his feet, bowed down, picked up her son, and left.
2 Kings 4:38 Elisha went back to Gilgal where there was a famine. The prophets' sons were with him. He told his helper, "Put on the big pot and cook some stew for the prophets' sons."
2 Kings 4:39 Someone went to the field to pick herbs, found a wild vine, collected a bunch of wild gourds, and came back to cut them up into the pot of soup, because they didn't know what they were.
2 Kings 4:40 They served the food to the men to eat. But while they were eating the stew, they shouted, "Man of God, there is poison in this stew!" So they could not eat it.
2 Kings 4:41 But he said, "Then bring flour." And he threw it into the pot; and he said, "Serve it to the people, so they can eat." And there was nothing bad in the pot.
2 Kings 4:42 A man from Baalshalisha came and brought the man of God twenty barley loaves and fresh ears of corn. He said, "Give it to the people to eat."
2 Kings 4:43 His servant asked, "How can I feed a hundred men with this?" He answered, "Give it to the people to eat, because God says they will eat and have some left over."
2 Kings 4:44 He placed the food before them, and they ate and left some, as God had said.

2 Kings 5:1 Naaman, the leader of the Syrian king's army, was important to his king and respected because through him, God had let Syria win battles. He was also very brave, but he had leprosy.
2 Kings 5:2 The Syrians had attacked in groups and had taken a young girl prisoner from Israel; she served Naaman's wife.
2 Kings 5:3 She told her mistress, "I wish my master were with the prophet in Samaria, because he could cure his leprosy."
2 Kings 5:4 Someone went and told his master, "The girl from Israel said this and this."
2 Kings 5:5 The king of Syria said, "Go ahead, go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." He left, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand gold coins, and ten sets of clothes.
2 Kings 5:6 He took the letter to the king of Israel, which said, "When you get this letter, know that I have sent my servant Naaman to you so you can heal him of his leprosy."
2 Kings 5:7 When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, able to kill or bring to life, that this man sends someone to me to heal his leprosy? See how he is trying to start a fight with me."
2 Kings 5:8 When Elisha, the man of God, found out that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent a message to the king asking, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he will learn that there is a prophet in Israel."
2 Kings 5:9 Naaman came with his horses and chariot, and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
2 Kings 5:10 Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and bathe in the Jordan River seven times, and your skin will be healed, and you will be clean."
2 Kings 5:11 But Naaman was angry and left, saying, "Look, I thought he would surely come out to me, stand, and pray to God, then wave his hand over the spot and heal the skin disease."
2 Kings 5:12 Aren't Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all Israel's waters? Can't I wash in them and be clean? So he left, angry.
2 Kings 5:13 His helpers came close and spoke to him, saying, "If the prophet had told you to do something big, you would have done it, right? So, shouldn't you do it when he simply tells you, 'Wash and be clean'?"
2 Kings 5:14 He went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan River, as God's man had said. His skin became like a young child's, and he was clean.
2 Kings 5:15 He went back to the man of God with his group. He stood in front of him and said, "Now I understand there is no God anywhere on earth except in Israel. Please accept a gift from me, your servant."
2 Kings 5:16 He said, "As God lives, before whom I serve, I won't take anything." Though he was pressed to accept, he still refused.
2 Kings 5:17 Naaman asked, "Please, can your servant take two mules' load of soil? Because from now on, your servant will not offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to other gods, only to God."
2 Kings 5:18 Please God, forgive me, your servant, for when my boss goes into Rimmon's temple to pray and leans on me, and I kneel down in Rimmon's temple, please forgive me for this.
2 Kings 5:19 He said to him, "Leave in peace." So he left and went a short distance away.
2 Kings 5:20 Gehazi, Elisha's helper, thought, "Look, my boss didn't take what Naaman the Syrian offered. But as God lives, I'll chase after him and get something from him."
2 Kings 5:21 So Gehazi ran after Naaman. When Naaman saw him coming, he got off his chariot to meet him and asked, "Is everything okay?"
2 Kings 5:22 He said, "Everything is fine. My master sent me, saying, 'Look, two young prophets from Mount Ephraim have just come to me. Please give them some silver and two sets of clothes.'"
2 Kings 5:23 Naaman said, "Please, take two talents." He insisted, so he put two talents of silver in two bags, along with two sets of clothes, and placed them on two of his servants; and they carried them ahead of him.
2 Kings 5:24 When he got to the tower, he took the items from their hands, placed them in the house, and allowed the men to leave, and they went away.
2 Kings 5:25 He went in and stood before his boss. Elisha asked him, "Where did you come from, Gehazi?" And he replied, "Your servant didn't go anywhere."
2 Kings 5:26 He asked him, "Didn't I feel it when the man came back from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to take money, clothes, olive groves, vineyards, sheep, cattle, male and female servants?"
2 Kings 5:27 Naaman's leprosy will stick to you and your descendants forever. He left with skin as white as a leper's.

2 Kings 6:1 The prophet's sons said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we stay with you is too small for us."
2 Kings 6:2 Please let us go to the Jordan River, and let each of us take a piece of wood so we can build ourselves a place to stay. And he replied, "Go ahead."
2 Kings 6:3 Someone said, "Please agree and come with your servants." He replied, "I will go."
2 Kings 6:4 He went with them. When they reached the Jordan River, they cut down trees.
2 Kings 6:5 While someone was cutting a tree, the axe head dropped into the water and he shouted, "Oh no, master! It was borrowed."
2 Kings 6:6 The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" He showed him the spot. Then he cut a stick and threw it there, and the iron floated.
2 Kings 6:7 So he said, "Pick it up yourself." Then he reached out his hand and took it.
2 Kings 6:8 The Syrian king fought against Israel and talked with his advisors, saying, "My camp will be in a certain place."
2 Kings 6:9 The man of God warned the king of Israel, "Be careful not to go near that place, because the Syrians have come there."
2 Kings 6:10 The king of Israel went to the place that the man of God had told him about and warned him about, and he kept himself safe there more than once.
2 Kings 6:11 So the king of Syria was very upset about this; he called his servants and asked them, "Won't you tell me who among us is on the side of the king of Israel?"
2 Kings 6:12 One of his servants said, "No, my king; but Elisha, the prophet in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words you speak in your bedroom."
2 Kings 6:13 He said, "Go find out where he is, so I can send someone to get him." They told him, "He is in Dothan."
2 Kings 6:14 So he sent horses, chariots, and a large army there. They arrived at night and surrounded the city.
2 Kings 6:15 When God's man's helper got up early and went outside, he saw an army with horses and chariots surrounding the city. The helper said to him, "Oh no, my master! What will we do?"
2 Kings 6:16 He replied, "Don't be afraid: we have more on our side than they have on theirs."
2 Kings 6:17 Elisha prayed and said, "God, please open his eyes so he can see." And God opened the young man's eyes, and he saw the mountain was full of horses and fiery chariots around Elisha.
2 Kings 6:18 When they got to Elisha, he prayed to God, "Please make these people blind." So God made them blind, just as Elisha had said.
2 Kings 6:19 Elisha said to them, "This is not the right way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for." But he took them to Samaria.
2 Kings 6:20 When they arrived in Samaria, Elisha said, "God, please let these men see." And God let them see, and they saw that they were in Samaria.
2 Kings 6:21 The king of Israel said to Elisha when he saw the men, "My father, should I attack them? Should I attack them?"
2 Kings 6:22 He replied, "Don't hurt them. Would you attack those you've captured with your sword and bow? Give them food and water so they can eat, drink, and return to their leader."
2 Kings 6:23 He made a lot of food for them, and after they ate and drank, he sent them off, and they returned to their leader. So, the Syrian groups did not enter Israel again.
2 Kings 6:24 After this, Benhadad the king of Syria brought together all his army, and they went and surrounded Samaria.
2 Kings 6:25 There was a severe famine in Samaria, and they were surrounded. During the siege, a donkey's head was sold for eighty silver coins, and a small amount of dove manure for five silver coins.
2 Kings 6:26 As the king of Israel walked along the wall, a woman called out to him, saying, "Help me, my lord, O king."
2 Kings 6:27 He said, "If God won't help you, where can I help you from? The threshing floor or the winepress?"
2 Kings 6:28 The king asked her, "What's wrong?" She replied, "This woman told me, 'Give me your son so we can eat him today, and tomorrow we'll eat my son.'"
2 Kings 6:29 We cooked my son and ate him. The next day I told her, "Give us your son to eat," but she hid her son.
2 Kings 6:30 When the king heard what the woman said, he tore his clothes. As he walked along the wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth under his clothes against his skin.
2 Kings 6:31 He said, "May God punish me even more if Elisha, son of Shaphat, keeps his head today."
2 Kings 6:32 Elisha was sitting in his house with the elders when the king sent a man to him. Before the man arrived, Elisha said to the elders, "Can you see that this murderer's son wants to cut off my head? When his messenger arrives, close the door and keep him there. Isn't the sound of his boss's footsteps following him?"
2 Kings 6:33 While he was still talking to them, look, the messenger came to him and said, "Look, this trouble is from God; why should I wait for God any longer?"

2 Kings 7:1 Elisha said, "Listen to God's message: Tomorrow at this time, you can buy a measure of fine flour for one shekel and two measures of barley for one shekel at the gate of Samaria."
2 Kings 7:2 A high-ranking official who the king trusted spoke to the man of God, saying, "Look, even if God could open windows in the sky, could this happen?" The man of God replied, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
2 Kings 7:3 At the gate entrance, there were four men with leprosy. They asked each other, "Why are we sitting here waiting to die?"
2 Kings 7:4 If we say, "Let's go into the city," but there's famine in the city and we'll die there, and if we stay here, we'll die too. So, let's go to the Syrian army. If they spare us, we'll live; if they kill us, we'll just die.
2 Kings 7:5 They got up at dusk to go to the Syrian camp, and when they reached the edge of the Syrian camp, there was no one there.
2 Kings 7:6 God made the Syrian army hear sounds of chariots and horses, and the noise of a large army. They said to each other, "Look, the king of Israel has paid the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack us."
2 Kings 7:7 So they got up and ran away at dusk, leaving their tents, horses, donkeys, and the camp just as it was, running to save their lives.
2 Kings 7:8 When the lepers reached the edge of the camp, they entered a tent, ate, drank, took silver, gold, and clothes, then went and hid them. They returned, went into another tent, took things, and hid those too.
2 Kings 7:9 They said to each other, "We are not doing right. This is a day of good news, yet we are silent. If we wait until morning, trouble will come to us. Let's go now and tell the king's family."
2 Kings 7:10 They went and called to the city gatekeeper, and they said, "We went to the Syrian camp, and look, there was no one there, no sound of anyone, only horses and donkeys tied up, and the tents left just as they were."
2 Kings 7:11 He called the gatekeepers, and they reported it to the king's palace inside.
2 Kings 7:12 The king got up at night and told his servants, "I will show you what the Syrians have done to us. They know we are hungry; so they have left their camp to hide in the field, thinking, 'When they leave the city, we will capture them alive and enter the city.'"
2 Kings 7:13 One of his servants replied, "Please, let's take five of the remaining horses in the city – they're like the few people of Israel still here; just as the rest of the Israelites who are gone – and let's go to find out."
2 Kings 7:14 They used two war horses, and the king sent them to follow the Syrian army, telling them, "Go and look."
2 Kings 7:15 They followed them to the Jordan River, and look, the whole path was covered with clothes and items that the Syrians had thrown away as they fled quickly. The messengers came back and told the king.
2 Kings 7:16 The people went out and took things from the Syrian tents. A unit of good flour was sold for a coin, and two units of barley for a coin, just as God had said.
2 Kings 7:17 The king put the officer he relied on in charge of the gate, but the people trampled him there and he died, just like the man of God had predicted when the king visited him.
2 Kings 7:18 As the man of God told the king, "Tomorrow at this time, two measures of barley or one measure of fine flour will cost a shekel at the gate of Samaria."
2 Kings 7:19 The lord replied to the man of God, "Look, even if God could open windows in the sky, could this happen?" The man of God said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you won't eat any of it."
2 Kings 7:20 And so it happened to him: the crowd stepped on him at the gate, and he died.

2 Kings 8:1 Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had brought back to life, "Get up, take your family and find a place to stay, because God has announced a seven-year famine that will happen in the land."
2 Kings 8:2 The woman got up and did what the man of God said. She left with her family and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
2 Kings 8:3 After seven years, the woman came back from the Philistines' land and begged the king for her house and her land.
2 Kings 8:4 The king spoke with Gehazi, the servant of God's man, and said, "Please tell me about all the amazing things Elisha has done."
2 Kings 8:5 As he was explaining to the king how he brought a dead person back to life, the woman whose son was brought back to life begged the king for her house and land. Gehazi said, "My king, this is the woman, and her son is the one Elisha brought back to life."
2 Kings 8:6 When the king asked the woman, she answered. The king then assigned an officer to her, saying, "Give back everything that belonged to her, and all the crops from her land from the day she left until now."
2 Kings 8:7 Elisha went to Damascus; King Benhadad of Syria was ill; people told him, "The man of God has arrived here."
2 Kings 8:8 The king told Hazael, "Take a gift in your hand, go to the man of God, and ask God through him, 'Will I get better from this illness?'"
2 Kings 8:9 So Hazael went to see him, bringing gifts of the best items from Damascus, enough to load forty camels. He arrived and stood before him and said, "Your son Benhadad, the king of Syria, has sent me to ask, 'Will I get better from this illness?'"
2 Kings 8:10 Elisha told him, "Go and tell him, 'You will surely get well.' But God has shown me that he will definitely die."
2 Kings 8:11 He looked intently until the other felt embarrassed; then the man of God cried.
2 Kings 8:12 Hazael asked, "Why is my master crying?" He replied, "Because I know the bad things you will do to the people of Israel: you will burn down their fortresses, kill their young men with the sword, smash their children, and cut open their pregnant women."
2 Kings 8:13 Hazael asked, "Am I a dog to do such a big thing?" Elisha replied, "God has shown me you will become king of Syria."
2 Kings 8:14 He left Elisha, went to his master, who asked him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He replied, "He told me you would definitely get better."
2 Kings 8:15 The next day, he took a heavy cloth, soaked it in water, and put it over his face until he died; then Hazael became king in his place.
2 Kings 8:16 In the fifth year of Joram, Ahab's son and king of Israel, with Jehoshaphat as king of Judah, Jehoram, Jehoshaphat's son, started to rule as king of Judah.
2 Kings 8:17 He was 32 years old when he became king; he ruled for 8 years in Jerusalem.
2 Kings 8:18 He followed the path of Israel's kings, like Ahab's family did, because he married Ahab's daughter, and he did wrong in God's eyes.
2 Kings 8:19 But God would not destroy Judah for David his servant, because he promised to always give him and his children a light.
2 Kings 8:20 During his reign, Edom rebelled against Judah's control and chose their own king.
2 Kings 8:21 Joram went to Zair with all his chariots. He attacked at night and defeated the Edomites and their chariot leaders who had surrounded him. Then the people ran away to their tents.
2 Kings 8:22 Edom rebelled against Judah and is still rebelling today. At that time, Libnah also rebelled.
2 Kings 8:23 The other things Joram did and his deeds, aren't they written in the record book of Judah's kings?
2 Kings 8:24 Joram died like his ancestors and was buried with them in David's city; then his son Ahaziah became king after him.
2 Kings 8:25 Ahaziah, son of Jehoram and king of Judah, started to rule in the twelfth year of Joram, Ahab's son and king of Israel.
2 Kings 8:26 Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for one year in Jerusalem. His mother was Athaliah, Omri's daughter, the king of Israel.
2 Kings 8:27 He followed Ahab's family's path, and did bad things that God saw, just like Ahab's family did, because he was married into Ahab's family.
2 Kings 8:28 He went with Joram, Ahab's son, to fight Hazael, the king of Syria, at Ramothgilead; and the Syrians hurt Joram.
2 Kings 8:29 King Joram returned to Jezreel to heal from his injuries received from the Syrians at Ramah, during his fight with King Hazael of Syria. Ahaziah, son of King Jehoram of Judah, visited Joram, son of Ahab, in Jezreel because he was ill.

2 Kings 9:1 The prophet Elisha called one of the student prophets and said to him, "Tie up your clothes and take this jar of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead."
2 Kings 9:2 When you get there, find Jehu, the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi. Go inside, ask him to stand up from his brothers, and take him to a private room.
2 Kings 9:3 Take the bottle of oil, pour it on his head, and say, "God says, 'I have made you king over Israel.'" Then open the door, run away, and don't stop.
2 Kings 9:4 The young man, the prophet, went to Ramothgilead.
2 Kings 9:5 When he arrived, he saw the army leaders sitting and said, "I have a message for you, captain." Jehu asked, "Which one of us?" He replied, "For you, captain."
2 Kings 9:6 He got up, went into the house, put oil on his head, and said, "God of Israel says, I have made you king over God's people, over Israel."
2 Kings 9:7 You will strike down the family of Ahab your master, so I can get revenge for the murder of my prophets and all of God's servants killed by Jezebel.
2 Kings 9:8 Everyone from Ahab's family will die; I will destroy every male in Ahab's family, whether free or imprisoned in Israel.
2 Kings 9:9 I will make Ahab's family like Jeroboam's family, the son of Nebat, and like Baasha's family, the son of Ahijah.
2 Kings 9:10 Dogs will eat Jezebel in Jezreel's land, and no one will bury her. He opened the door and ran away.
2 Kings 9:11 Then Jehu went out to his master's servants. One asked him, "Is everything okay? Why did this crazy man come to you?" Jehu replied, "You know the man and what he talks about."
2 Kings 9:12 They said, "That's not true; tell us." He replied, "He told me this: 'God says, I have chosen you to be king of Israel.'"
2 Kings 9:13 They hurried, each man took his clothes, laid them on the steps under him, and blowing trumpets, said, "Jehu is king."
2 Kings 9:14 Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi, plotted against Joram. Joram was defending Ramoth-gilead with all of Israel's help against Hazael, the king of Syria.
2 Kings 9:15 King Joram went back to recover in Jezreel from injuries the Syrians caused him during his battle with Hazael, the king of Syria. Jehu said, "If you agree, make sure no one leaves the city to report this in Jezreel."
2 Kings 9:16 So Jehu rode in a chariot to Jezreel because Joram was there. Ahaziah, the king of Judah, had come to visit Joram.
2 Kings 9:17 A guard on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's group coming and said, "I see a group." Joram said, "Send a horseman to ask if they come in peace."
2 Kings 9:18 Someone rode out to meet him and said, "The king asks, 'Is everything peaceful?'" Jehu replied, "What concern is peace to you? Follow me." The lookout reported, "The messenger reached them but isn't coming back."
2 Kings 9:19 He sent another rider who went to them and said, "The king asks, 'Is everything peaceful?'" Jehu replied, "What does peace matter to you? Follow me."
2 Kings 9:20 The guard reported, "He reached them but hasn't returned; his driving style is like Jehu, Nimshi's son, because he drives very fast."
2 Kings 9:21 Joram said, "Get ready." His chariot was prepared. Joram, king of Israel, and Ahaziah, king of Judah, each rode in their chariots to confront Jehu. They met him on Naboth the Jezreelite's land.
2 Kings 9:22 When Joram saw Jehu, he asked, "Is it peace, Jehu?" Jehu replied, "How can there be peace while your mother Jezebel does so many acts of unfaithfulness and witchcraft?"
2 Kings 9:23 Joram turned around, ran away, and said to Ahaziah, "It's a trap, Ahaziah."
2 Kings 9:24 Jehu pulled his bow with all his strength and hit Jehoram between his arms; the arrow came out through his heart, and he slumped down in his chariot.
2 Kings 9:25 Jehu told his officer Bidkar, "Pick him up and throw him into Naboth the Jezreelite's field. Remember when you and I rode together after Ahab's father, God placed this judgment on him."
2 Kings 9:26 Indeed, I saw yesterday the murder of Naboth and his sons, says God; and I will repay you on this piece of land, says God. Now, take him and throw him onto this piece of land, following God's command.
2 Kings 9:27 But when Ahaziah the king of Judah saw it, he ran through the garden house. Jehu chased him, saying, "Hit him in his chariot too." They did that near Gur, close to Ibleam. He escaped to Megiddo and died there.
2 Kings 9:28 His servants took him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the city of David.
2 Kings 9:29 In the eleventh year of Joram, Ahaziah, Ahab's son, started to rule over Judah.
2 Kings 9:30 When Jehu arrived in Jezreel, Jezebel heard about it. She put makeup on her face, did her hair, and looked out the window.
2 Kings 9:31 As Jehu came through the gate, she asked, "Did Zimri have peace after he killed his master?"
2 Kings 9:32 He looked up at the window and asked, "Who's with me? Who?" Two or three eunuchs peered down at him.
2 Kings 9:33 He said, "Throw her down." So they threw her down, and her blood splattered on the wall and horses, and he trampled her.
2 Kings 9:34 When he came in, he ate and drank, and said, Go and see that cursed woman, and bury her, because she is the daughter of a king.
2 Kings 9:35 They went to bury her, but only found her skull, feet, and the palms of her hands.
2 Kings 9:36 So they returned and reported to him. He said, "This is God's message, which He gave through His servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'In the area of Jezreel, dogs will eat Jezebel's body.'"
2 Kings 9:37 Jezebel's dead body will be like manure on the ground in Jezreel, so no one can say, "This is Jezebel."

2 Kings 10:1 Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria's leaders, the elders, and the caregivers of Ahab's children, saying.
2 Kings 10:2 As soon as you get this letter, since the sons of your master are with you, along with chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons;
2 Kings 10:3 Choose the best and most suitable of your master's sons, put him on his father's throne, and defend your master's house.
2 Kings 10:4 They were very afraid and said, "Look, two kings couldn't stand against him. How can we stand?"
2 Kings 10:5 The person in charge of the house, the city leader, the old men, and those taking care of the children sent a message to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants and will do whatever you tell us; we won't make anyone king: do what you think is best."
2 Kings 10:6 He wrote another letter to them, saying, If you are my followers and listen to me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow. The king's seventy sons were with the city's leaders, who were raising them.
2 Kings 10:7 When they received the letter, they killed the king's seventy sons, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jezreel.
2 Kings 10:8 A messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." He replied, "Put them in two piles by the gate entrance until morning."
2 Kings 10:9 In the morning, he went out, stood, and said to everyone, "You are good people: look, I plotted against my master and killed him; but who killed all these others?"
2 Kings 10:10 Understand that none of God's words about Ahab's family will fail to happen; God has done exactly what he said through his servant Elijah.
2 Kings 10:11 Jehu killed everyone left from Ahab's family in Jezreel, along with all his important men, relatives, and priests, leaving no one alive.
2 Kings 10:12 He got up, left, and went to Samaria. On the way, as he was near the place where sheep are sheared,
2 Kings 10:13 Jehu met Ahaziah's brothers, the king of Judah, and asked, "Who are you?" They replied, "We are Ahaziah's brothers, and we are going to greet the king's and queen's children."
2 Kings 10:14 He said, "Capture them alive." So they captured them alive and killed them at the shearing house pit, all 42 men; he did not spare any of them.
2 Kings 10:15 After he left that place, he met Jehonadab, Rechab's son, who was coming to greet him. He welcomed him and asked, "Is your heart true, as my heart is with yours?" Jehonadab replied, "It is." "If so, give me your hand." Then he reached out his hand, and Jehonadab took it and climbed into the chariot with him.
2 Kings 10:16 He said, "Come with me and see how eager I am for God." So they had him ride in his chariot.
2 Kings 10:17 When he arrived in Samaria, he killed all of Ahab's remaining followers until he had completely destroyed them, just as God had told Elijah.
2 Kings 10:18 Jehu brought all the people together and said to them, Ahab worshiped Baal a little, but Jehu will worship him a lot.
2 Kings 10:19 Now, call all of Baal's prophets, his servants, and his priests to me; make sure no one is missing, because I have a big sacrifice for Baal; whoever is missing will not survive. But Jehu planned this trick to destroy all who worship Baal.
2 Kings 10:20 Jehu said, "Call a special meeting for Baal." And they announced it.
2 Kings 10:21 Jehu sent messages throughout Israel, and all of Baal's followers came, leaving no one behind. They entered Baal's temple, filling it completely.
2 Kings 10:22 He told the one in charge of the clothes, "Get robes for all the Baal worshipers." So he gave them robes.
2 Kings 10:23 Jehu and Jehonadab, Rechab's son, went into Baal's temple and said to Baal's followers, "Check and make sure that none of God's servants are here with you, only Baal's worshippers."
2 Kings 10:24 When they entered to give sacrifices and burn offerings, Jehu set eighty men outside and said, "If any of the men I've delivered to you get away, whoever lets him escape will pay with his own life for the fugitive's life."
2 Kings 10:25 When he finished giving the burnt offering, Jehu told the guards and captains, "Go in and kill them; let no one escape." They killed them with their swords, dragged the bodies out, and then went into Baal's temple.
2 Kings 10:26 They took the idols from the Baal temple and burned them.
2 Kings 10:27 They destroyed the idol of Baal, tore down Baal's temple, and turned it into a public toilet, which it remains to this day.
2 Kings 10:28 Jehu got rid of Baal worship in Israel.
2 Kings 10:29 However, Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, specifically the golden calves in Bethel and Dan.
2 Kings 10:30 God said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what is right in my eyes, and have done to Ahab's family all that I wanted, your descendants up to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel."
2 Kings 10:31 But Jehu did not care to follow God's laws with all his heart: he kept on sinning like Jeroboam, leading Israel to sin.
2 Kings 10:32 At that time, God started to reduce Israel's size: and Hazael attacked them throughout Israel's borders.
2 Kings 10:33 East of the Jordan River, the land of Gilead belonged to the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of the tribe of Manasseh, stretching from Aroer by the Arnon River to Gilead and Bashan.
2 Kings 10:34 The other things Jehu did, all his actions and strength, are they not recorded in the book of the records of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 10:35 Jehu died and was buried in Samaria. Then his son Jehoahaz became the ruler after him.
2 Kings 10:36 Jehu was king of Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.

2 Kings 11:1 When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw her son was dead, she got up and killed all the royal family members.
2 Kings 11:2 Jehosheba, King Joram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister, took Joash, Ahaziah's son, and saved him from the king's sons who were killed. She and a nurse hid him in a bedroom to protect him from Athaliah, so he was not killed.
2 Kings 11:3 He stayed hidden with her in God's house for six years while Athaliah ruled the land.
2 Kings 11:4 In the seventh year, Jehoiada sent for the commanders of units of a hundred, the officers and the guards, and brought them to him in God's house. There, he made an agreement with them and had them swear an oath in God's house. He then showed them the king's son.
2 Kings 11:5 He told them, "Here's what you must do: one-third of you who come on the Sabbath will guard the king's palace."
2 Kings 11:6 One third of you will stand at the gate of Sur, another third at the gate behind the guard, and you will guard the house to prevent it from being broken into.
2 Kings 11:7 Two-thirds of you who go out on the Sabbath must guard God's house around the king.
2 Kings 11:8 Surround the king, everyone with their weapons ready: if someone approaches, kill them. Stay with the king wherever he goes.
2 Kings 11:9 The leaders of the hundreds did everything Priest Jehoiada told them. Each one gathered his men who were to come in on the Sabbath and those going out on the Sabbath and went to Priest Jehoiada.
2 Kings 11:10 The priest gave David's spears and shields, which were in God's temple, to the captains of hundreds.
2 Kings 11:11 The guards stood around the king, each with his weapon in hand, from the temple's right side to the left side, near the altar and the temple.
2 Kings 11:12 He brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, gave him the law; they made him king, anointed him, clapped their hands, and said, "God save the king."
2 Kings 11:13 When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the crowd, she went to where the people were in God's temple.
2 Kings 11:14 When she saw, the king was standing by a column, as was the custom, with the leaders and trumpet players near him. All the people were very happy and played their trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted, "Treason! Treason!"
2 Kings 11:15 Jehoiada the priest told the army leaders, "Take her out beyond the temple area. If anyone follows her, kill them with the sword." He had said, "Don't kill her in God's house."
2 Kings 11:16 They grabbed her, and she took the path that the horses used to enter the king's palace, where she was killed.
2 Kings 11:17 Jehoiada made a promise between God, the king, and the people that they would be God's people, and also between the king and the people.
2 Kings 11:18 Everyone in the land entered Baal's temple, destroyed it, broke his altars and statues completely, and killed Mattan, Baal's priest, by the altars. And the priest set up guards for God’s house.
2 Kings 11:19 He gathered the leaders of hundreds, commanders, guards, and everyone in the land; they took the king from God's house, went through the guard gate to the royal palace, and he sat on the kings' throne.
2 Kings 11:20 All the people of the land were happy, and the city was peaceful; they killed Athaliah with a sword near the king's house.
2 Kings 11:21 Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.

2 Kings 12:1 Jehoash became king in the seventh year of Jehu's rule; he was king for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother was named Zibiah from Beersheba.
2 Kings 12:2 Jehoash did what was right in God's eyes all the days Jehoiada the priest taught him.
2 Kings 12:3 But the high places were not removed: the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense there.
2 Kings 12:4 Jehoash told the priests, "All the dedicated money brought to God's house, including everyone's counted contribution, the set value of each person, and any money given willingly to God's house,
2 Kings 12:5 Let the priests receive it from each person they know and use it to fix any damage found in the house.
2 Kings 12:6 In the twenty-third year of King Jehoash's rule, the priests had not yet fixed the temple's damage.
2 Kings 12:7 King Jehoash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests, and asked them, "Why haven't you fixed the broken parts of the temple? Don't take any more money from your friends, but use it to repair the temple."
2 Kings 12:8 The priests agreed to stop taking money from the people and not to fix the damages to the temple.
2 Kings 12:9 Priest Jehoiada took a box, made a hole in its top, and placed it by the altar on the right side as you enter God's house. The priests guarding the door put all the money given to God's house into the box.
2 Kings 12:10 When they saw a lot of money in the chest, the king's writer and the high priest went to it, put the money in bags, and counted what was found in God's house.
