2 Kings 12:11 They gave the collected money to the workers who oversaw the temple of God, and they paid the carpenters and builders working on the temple of God.
2 Kings 12:12 To stoneworkers and stone cutters, and to buy wood and cut stone to fix the damages of God's house, and for all spent on the house to repair it.
2 Kings 12:13 However, they did not make for God's house any silver bowls, trimming scissors, basins, trumpets, gold items, or silver items with the money that was brought into God's house.
2 Kings 12:14 But they gave it to the workers, who used it to fix God's house.
2 Kings 12:15 Also, they did not check on the men who they gave the money to pay the workers, because they were honest.
2 Kings 12:16 The money from wrongdoings and from sin was not taken into God's house: it belonged to the priests.
2 Kings 12:17 Then Hazael, the king of Syria, attacked and captured Gath, and then he planned to attack Jerusalem.
2 Kings 12:18 King Jehoash of Judah gathered all the holy items that his ancestors, Kings Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah of Judah, had set apart for God, along with his own holy items and all the gold found in God's temple and in the royal palace. He sent them to King Hazael of Syria, who then left Jerusalem.
2 Kings 12:19 The other things Joash did are written in the book of the history of Judah's kings, aren't they?
2 Kings 12:20 His servants got up, made a plot, and killed Joash at the house of Millo, near Silla.
2 Kings 12:21 Jozachar, Shimeath's son, and Jehozabad, Shomer's son, who were his servants, struck him, and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in David's city, and his son Amaziah became king after him.

2 Kings 13:1 In the twenty-third year of Joash, Ahaziah's son, who was king of Judah, Jehoahaz, Jehu's son, started to rule over Israel in Samaria, and he ruled for seventeen years.
2 Kings 13:2 He did evil in God's eyes and followed Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who led Israel into sin; he did not turn away from it.
2 Kings 13:3 God became very angry with Israel, and He allowed Hazael, king of Syria, and Hazael's son Benhadad, to defeat them repeatedly.
2 Kings 13:4 Jehoahaz asked God for help, and God listened to him because he saw that the king of Syria was oppressing Israel.
2 Kings 13:5 God gave Israel a rescuer, so they were freed from Syrian rule, and the Israelites lived in their homes as they used to.
2 Kings 13:6 Still, they did not stop doing the same wrongs that Jeroboam made Israel do; they continued in those ways. The worship place in Samaria stayed too.
2 Kings 13:7 God let Jehoahaz keep only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers because the king of Syria had defeated them and reduced them to dust.
2 Kings 13:8 The other things Jehoahaz did, his actions, and his power, aren't they all written in the history book of Israel's kings?
2 Kings 13:9 Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria; his son Joash became king after him.
2 Kings 13:10 In the thirty-seventh year of Joash's rule in Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king of Israel in Samaria and ruled for sixteen years.
2 Kings 13:11 He did evil things that God saw; he did not stop following Jeroboam Nebat's son's sins, which led Israel to sin, but continued in them.
2 Kings 13:12 The other things Joash did, everything he achieved, and how strongly he fought against King Amaziah of Judah, are all written in the Israelite kings' records, right?
2 Kings 13:13 Joash died like his ancestors; Jeroboam became king; and they buried Joash in Samaria with Israel's kings.
2 Kings 13:14 Elisha became very sick with the illness that would cause his death. Joash, the king of Israel, visited him, cried over him, and said, "Oh my father, my father, you are like the strength and protection of Israel."
2 Kings 13:15 Elisha told him, "Get a bow and some arrows." So he got a bow and some arrows.
2 Kings 13:16 He told the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." So he did, and then Elisha placed his hands on the king's hands.
2 Kings 13:17 He said, "Open the east window," and he opened it. Then Elisha said, "Shoot," and he shot. Elisha declared, "This is God's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Syria. You will defeat the Syrians in Aphek until you destroy them."
2 Kings 13:18 He said, "Take the arrows." So he took them. Then he told the king of Israel, "Hit the ground." The king hit the ground three times and stopped.
2 Kings 13:19 The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times; then you would have defeated Syria completely. But now you will defeat Syria only three times."
2 Kings 13:20 Elisha died and was buried. At the start of the year, Moabite raiders attacked the land.
2 Kings 13:21 While they were burying a man, they saw a group of men coming. They threw the man into Elisha's tomb. When the man touched Elisha's bones, he came back to life and stood up.
2 Kings 13:22 Hazael, the king of Syria, was cruel to Israel all the time Jehoahaz was king.
2 Kings 13:23 God was kind to them, felt sorry for them, and cared about them because of his promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and did not want to destroy them or send them away from him at that time.
2 Kings 13:24 So Hazael the king of Syria died; and his son Benhadad became king after him.
2 Kings 13:25 Joash, son of Jehoahaz, won back from Benhadad, son of Hazael, the towns he had taken from Joash's father Jehoahaz in battle. Joash defeated him three times and took back the Israeli cities.

2 Kings 14:1 Amaziah, son of Joash, became king of Judah in the second year of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
2 Kings 14:2 He was 25 years old when he became king and ruled for 29 years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
2 Kings 14:3 He did what was good in God's eyes, but not as well as David his ancestor did; he acted just like his father Joash.
2 Kings 14:4 However, the high places were not removed: the people still sacrificed and burned incense there.
2 Kings 14:5 As soon as he secured control of the kingdom, he killed the servants who had murdered his father, the king.
2 Kings 14:6 He did not kill the murderers' children. It was in Moses' law book, where God said, "Parents should not die for their children, nor children for their parents; every person should die for their own sin."
2 Kings 14:7 He killed ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, captured Selah through battle, and named it Joktheel, which is still its name today.
2 Kings 14:8 Amaziah sent people to talk to Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz and Jehu, king of Israel, to say, "Come, let's meet face to face."
2 Kings 14:9 King Jehoash of Israel sent a message to King Amaziah of Judah: "The small bush in Lebanon sent a message to the big tree in Lebanon, asking, 'Let your daughter marry my son.' But then a wild animal in Lebanon walked over and crushed the small bush.
2 Kings 14:10 You have truly defeated Edom, and now you are proud. Celebrate this victory but stay home. Why get involved in more conflict that will only bring harm to you and make you and Judah fall?
2 Kings 14:11 Amaziah wouldn't listen. So Jehoash, the king of Israel, went and faced Amaziah, the king of Judah, at Bethshemesh in Judah.
2 Kings 14:12 Judah was defeated by Israel, and everyone ran back to their tents.
2 Kings 14:13 King Jehoash of Israel captured King Amaziah of Judah, the son of Jehoash and grandson of Ahaziah, in Bethshemesh. He went to Jerusalem and broke down its wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a distance of four hundred cubits.
2 Kings 14:14 He took all the gold and silver, every item found in God’s house, and in the king’s treasury, along with hostages, and went back to Samaria.
2 Kings 14:15 The other things Jehoash did, his strength, and his battles with Amaziah, king of Judah, are written in the Israelite Kings' history book, right?
2 Kings 14:16 Jehoash died like his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the Israelite kings; his son Jeroboam became king after him.
2 Kings 14:17 Amaziah, son of Joash the king of Judah, lived 15 years after Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the king of Israel, died.
2 Kings 14:18 Aren't the other things Amaziah did written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 14:19 They planned against him in Jerusalem, so he ran to Lachish, but they followed him to Lachish and killed him there.
2 Kings 14:20 They brought him on horses and buried him in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the city of David.
2 Kings 14:21 All the people of Judah made sixteen-year-old Azariah king after his father Amaziah.
2 Kings 14:22 He built Elath and gave it back to Judah after the king died.
2 Kings 14:23 In the fifteenth year of King Amaziah of Judah, Jeroboam son of King Joash began to rule as king in Israel's Samaria, and he ruled for forty-one years.
2 Kings 14:24 He did what was evil in God's eyes and did not stop doing the same sins Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who led Israel into sin, had done.
2 Kings 14:25 He brought back Israel's border from Hamath to the Sea of Arabah, just as God of Israel had promised through his prophet Jonah, son of Amittai, from Gathhepher.
2 Kings 14:26 God saw Israel's suffering, which was very severe, because no one was confined, abandoned, or able to help Israel.
2 Kings 14:27 God did not say he would erase Israel's name from under heaven; instead, he saved them through Jeroboam, the son of Joash.
2 Kings 14:28 The other things Jeroboam did, his achievements, his battles, and how he won back Damascus and Hamath for Israel—territories that were once Judah's—are these not recorded in the history book of Israel's kings?
2 Kings 14:29 Jeroboam died like his ancestors, the kings of Israel; and his son Zachariah became king after him.

2 Kings 15:1 In the twenty-seventh year of King Jeroboam of Israel, Azariah, the son of King Amaziah of Judah, started his rule.
2 Kings 15:2 He was sixteen when he became king, and he ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jecholiah from Jerusalem.
2 Kings 15:3 He did what was good in God's eyes, just as his father Amaziah had done.
2 Kings 15:4 But the high places were not taken away: the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense on the high places.
2 Kings 15:5 God punished the king with leprosy until he died, and he lived in a separate house. Jotham, the king's son, took charge of the palace and ruled the land's people.
2 Kings 15:6 The other things Azariah did are written in the Judah kings' records, right?
2 Kings 15:7 Azariah died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David; his son Jotham became king after him.
2 Kings 15:8 Zachariah, Jeroboam's son, became king of Israel in Samaria for six months during Azariah's thirty-eighth year as king of Judah.
2 Kings 15:9 He did evil in God’s eyes, just like his ancestors. He continued the sins of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin.
2 Kings 15:10 Shallum, Jabesh's son, plotted against him, struck him down in front of the people, killed him, and then became ruler in his place.

2 Kings 15:15 The other things Shallum did and his plot are recorded in the book of the histories of Israel's kings.
2 Kings 15:16 Menahem attacked Tiphsah, all its people, and the surrounding lands from Tirzah because they didn't let him in. So he destroyed it, and he tore open all the pregnant women there.
2 Kings 15:17 In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule over Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king of Israel and ruled for ten years in Samaria.
2 Kings 15:18 He did evil in God's eyes and never stopped sinning like Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who led Israel into sin.
2 Kings 15:19 The Assyrian King Pul attacked the land. Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so he would support Menahem's rule.
2 Kings 15:20 Menahem forced the rich leaders of Israel to give him money; each man had to pay fifty silver shekels so he could give it to the king of Assyria. Then the king of Assyria left and did not stay in the country.
2 Kings 15:21 The other things Menahem did, aren't they written in the history book of Israel's kings?
2 Kings 15:22 Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king after him.
2 Kings 15:23 In Azariah's fiftieth year as Judah's king, Pekahiah, Menahem's son, became Israel's king in Samaria and ruled for two years.
2 Kings 15:24 He did evil things that God saw; he kept on sinning like Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who led Israel into sin.
2 Kings 15:25 Pekah, Remaliah's son and one of his captains, plotted against him. He attacked and killed him in Samaria, inside the king's palace, with the help of Argob, Arieh, and fifty Gileadite men. Then he took over as king.
2 Kings 15:26 Other things Pekahiah did and his actions are written in the Israel Kings' history book.
2 Kings 15:27 In the fifty-second year of Azariah's rule in Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in Samaria and ruled for twenty years.
2 Kings 15:28 He did evil in God's eyes and did not stop doing the same sins as Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who led Israel to sin.
2 Kings 15:29 During Pekah's time as king of Israel, Tiglathpileser, the Assyrian king, captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, the whole region of Naphtali, and took the people to Assyria as prisoners.
2 Kings 15:30 Hoshea, Elah's son, plotted against Pekah, Remaliah's son, struck him down, killed him, and became king in his place during the twentieth year of Jotham, Uzziah's son.
2 Kings 15:31 The other things Pekah did are all written in the book of Israel's kings' histories.
2 Kings 15:32 In the second year when Pekah, Remaliah's son, was king of Israel, Jotham, Uzziah's son, started to reign as king of Judah.
2 Kings 15:33 He was 25 years old when he started to rule, and he ruled for 16 years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha, Zadok's daughter.
2 Kings 15:34 He did what was right in God's eyes, just like his father Uzziah had done.
2 Kings 15:35 Yet the high places were not taken away: the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense there. He constructed the upper gate of God's house.
2 Kings 15:36 The other things Jotham did and all his actions are written in the book of the records of the kings of Judah, aren't they?
2 Kings 15:37 In those days, God started to send Rezin, the king of Syria, and Pekah, the son of Remaliah, against Judah.
2 Kings 15:38 Jotham died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David his father: and his son Ahaz became king after him.

2 Kings 16:1 In the seventeenth year of Pekah, son of Remaliah, Ahaz, son of Jotham and king of Judah, started his rule.
2 Kings 16:2 Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of God, unlike his ancestor David.
2 Kings 16:3 He followed the path of Israel's kings and even burned his son in the fire, just like the hateful practices of the nations that God had driven out before the Israelites.
2 Kings 16:4 He offered sacrifices and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
2 Kings 16:5 Rezin, the king of Syria, and Pekah, the son of Remaliah and king of Israel, attacked Jerusalem to fight, and they surrounded Ahaz, but they could not defeat him.
2 Kings 16:6 At that time, Rezin, the king of Syria, took back Elath for Syria and forced the Jews out of Elath. Then the Syrians moved into Elath and have lived there ever since.
2 Kings 16:7 Ahaz sent messengers to King Tiglathpileser of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come and save me from the king of Syria and the king of Israel who are attacking me."
2 Kings 16:8 Ahaz took the silver and gold from God's house and the king's treasures and sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.
2 Kings 16:9 The king of Assyria listened to him: because the king of Assyria attacked Damascus, captured it, took its people as prisoners to Kir, and killed Rezin.
2 Kings 16:10 King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet King Tiglathpileser of Assyria and saw an altar there. Ahaz sent Priest Urijah a model of the altar, showing how it was made.
2 Kings 16:11 Priest Urijah built an altar just like King Ahaz ordered from Damascus, and he finished it before King Ahaz returned from there.
2 Kings 16:12 When the king returned from Damascus, he saw the altar. The king went up to the altar and made an offering on it.
2 Kings 16:13 He burned his burnt offering and grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the peace offerings' blood on the altar.
2 Kings 16:14 He moved the bronze altar that was in front of God, from the front of the temple, from between the altar and the temple of God, and placed it on the north side of the altar.
2 Kings 16:15 King Ahaz told Priest Urijah, "On the big altar, burn the morning offering, the evening grain offering, the king's burnt offering and grain offering, with all the people's burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings. Put all the blood of the burnt offerings and other sacrifices on it. I will use the bronze altar for asking God for guidance."
2 Kings 16:16 Urijah the priest did everything that King Ahaz ordered.
2 Kings 16:17 King Ahaz removed the edges of the stands, took the basin off them, and took the large bowl off the bronze bulls that were under it, and set it down on a stone floor.
2 Kings 16:18 He changed the temple's shelter for the Sabbath and the king's outer entrance for the king of Assyria.
2 Kings 16:19 The other things Ahaz did are written in the book of the history of Judah's kings, aren't they?
2 Kings 16:20 Ahaz died like his ancestors and was buried with them in David's city; his son Hezekiah became king after him.

2 Kings 17:1 In the twelfth year of Ahaz, king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah started to rule as king in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
2 Kings 17:2 He did evil things that God did not like, but not as much as the earlier kings of Israel.
2 Kings 17:3 The king of Assyria, Shalmaneser, attacked him; Hoshea became his servant and gave him gifts.
2 Kings 17:4 The king of Assyria discovered that Hoshea was plotting against him because Hoshea had sent messages to the king of Egypt, So, and had not given gifts to the king of Assyria like he did every year. So the king of Assyria arrested Hoshea and put him in jail.
2 Kings 17:5 The king of Assyria attacked all over the country, went to Samaria, and surrounded it for three years.
2 Kings 17:6 In Hoshea's ninth year as king, the king of Assyria conquered Samaria, took the Israelites to Assyria, and settled them in Halah, near the Gozan river, and in the Medes' cities.
2 Kings 17:7 The people of Israel sinned against God, who had freed them from Egypt and the rule of Pharaoh, and they worshipped other gods.
2 Kings 17:8 They followed the customs of the nations that God had driven out before the people of Israel and the idols that the kings of Israel had created.
2 Kings 17:9 The Israelites secretly did wrong things against God, and they built worship places in all their cities, from the lookout towers to the walled cities.
2 Kings 17:10 They put up statues and sacred gardens on every tall hill and under every green tree.
2 Kings 17:11 There they burned incense on all the high places, just like the nations who God had removed before them; and they did evil things that made God angry.
2 Kings 17:12 They worshipped false gods, even though God had told them not to do this.
2 Kings 17:13 God warned Israel and Judah through all the prophets and seers, telling them to stop their bad ways and follow my commands and rules, just as I told your ancestors and as I have sent to you through my prophets.
2 Kings 17:14 Despite this, they refused to listen and made their necks stiff, just like their ancestors who did not trust in God.
2 Kings 17:15 They turned away from his laws, the agreement he made with their ancestors, and the warnings he gave them. They chased after worthless things and became worthless, following the customs of the neighboring peoples, which God had told them not to imitate.
2 Kings 17:16 They abandoned all of God's commands and made metal idols, including two calves, built a shrine, worshiped the stars, and followed Baal.
2 Kings 17:17 They made their sons and daughters go through fire, practiced magic and spells, and gave themselves up to do wrong in God's eyes, making him angry.
2 Kings 17:18 So God was very angry with Israel and took them away from his presence; only the tribe of Judah remained.
2 Kings 17:19 Judah did not follow God's commands but followed the rules Israel made.
2 Kings 17:20 God turned away from all the people of Israel, hurt them, and let enemies take them until he pushed them out of his presence.
2 Kings 17:21 He split Israel from David's family; and they made Jeroboam, Nebat's son, king: and Jeroboam turned Israel away from God, leading them to commit a big sin.
2 Kings 17:22 The Israelites followed all the bad things Jeroboam did; they did not stop doing them.
2 Kings 17:23 God took Israel away from their land, as he had warned through his prophets. So Israel was taken from their land to Assyria, where they remain to this day.
2 Kings 17:24 The king of Assyria moved people from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim to live in the cities of Samaria, replacing the children of Israel; they settled in Samaria and lived in its cities.
2 Kings 17:25 When they first lived there, they did not fear God, so God sent lions that killed some of them.
2 Kings 17:26 So they told the king of Assyria, "The people you moved and settled in the towns of Samaria do not understand how to worship the God of this land, and now he has sent lions among them that are killing them because they don't know how to worship the God of this land."
2 Kings 17:27 The king of Assyria ordered, "Take one of the priests you brought from there, let him live there, and have him teach them how to worship the God of that land."
2 Kings 17:28 A priest they had taken from Samaria came to live in Bethel and showed them how to respect God.
2 Kings 17:29 Every nation created their own gods and placed them in the worship places built by the Samaritans, in each city where they lived.
2 Kings 17:30 The men from Babylon created Succothbenoth, the men from Cuth created Nergal, and the men from Hamath created Ashima.
2 Kings 17:31 The Avites worshiped Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their children in fire to worship Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
2 Kings 17:32 They were afraid of God, and chose the least important among them to be priests at the shrines, who offered sacrifices for them at the worship sites.
2 Kings 17:33 They were afraid of God and worshiped their own gods, following the customs of the people they had taken from other places.
2 Kings 17:34 To this day, they still act in the old ways; they do not fear God, nor follow his laws, rules, or the commands he gave to Jacob's descendants, whom he named Israel.
2 Kings 17:35 God made a promise with them and told them, "Do not be afraid of other gods, do not bow down to them, do not serve them, and do not offer sacrifices to them."
2 Kings 17:36 God, who led you out of Egypt with strong power and a raised arm, you should fear, worship, and offer sacrifices to.
2 Kings 17:37 Keep the rules, laws, and commands God has written for you, and always follow them; don't be afraid of other gods.
2 Kings 17:38 Remember the agreement I made with you and do not fear other gods.
2 Kings 17:39 But you should fear God, and he will save you from all your enemies.
2 Kings 17:40 However, they did not listen and continued acting as they did before.
2 Kings 17:41 These nations respected God but also worshiped their idols, as did their parents and their children still do today.

2 Kings 18:1 In the third year of Hoshea, son of Elah the king of Israel, Hezekiah, the son of Ahaz king of Judah, started to rule.
2 Kings 18:2 He was 25 years old when he started to rule; he ruled for 29 years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi, and she was the daughter of Zachariah.
2 Kings 18:3 He did what was right before God, just like his father David had done.
2 Kings 18:4 He got rid of the worship sites, smashed the idols, chopped down the sacred trees, and broke up the bronze snake Moses had made, because up to that time the Israelites had been burning incense to it. He named it Nehushtan.
2 Kings 18:5 He trusted in God of Israel, so there was no king like him in Judah, neither before nor after him.
2 Kings 18:6 He stuck close to God, didn't stop following Him, and obeyed the commands God gave Moses.
2 Kings 18:7 God was with him; wherever he went he was successful. He opposed the king of Assyria and did not serve him.
2 Kings 18:8 He struck the Philistines all the way to Gaza and its surrounding area, from the watchtower to the protected city.
2 Kings 18:9 In the fourth year of King Hezekiah’s rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah’s rule over Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria attacked Samaria and surrounded it.
2 Kings 18:10 After three years, they captured it: during Hezekiah's sixth year, which was Hoshea king of Israel's ninth year, Samaria was conquered.
2 Kings 18:11 The king of Assyria took the people of Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, Habor by the Gozan river, and in the towns of the Medes.
2 Kings 18:12 They did not listen to God's voice, broke his agreement, and ignored everything God's servant Moses told them. They neither obeyed nor followed his instructions.
2 Kings 18:13 In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah's reign, Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, attacked all the protected cities of Judah and captured them.
2 Kings 18:14 Hezekiah, the king of Judah, sent a message to the king of Assyria in Lachish: "I have done wrong; please leave me alone. I will pay whatever you ask." The king of Assyria told Hezekiah to pay him 300 talents of silver and 30 talents of gold.
2 Kings 18:15 Hezekiah gave him all the silver from God's house and the king's treasure.
2 Kings 18:16 Hezekiah removed the gold from the temple doors and pillars he had covered and gave it to the king of Assyria.
2 Kings 18:17 The king of Assyria sent Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a large army to attack Jerusalem. They went and arrived in Jerusalem. When they got there, they stood next to the water channel of the upper pool, on the road that goes by the washer's field.
2 Kings 18:18 When they called for the king, Eliakim, Hilkiah's son who was in charge of the house, Shebna the secretary, and Joah, Asaph's son the record-keeper, came out to them.
2 Kings 18:19 Rabshakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah that the great king of Assyria asks, 'What are you relying on with such confidence?'"
2 Kings 18:20 You say, (but they are just empty words,) I have advice and power for war. Now who do you trust when you rebel against me?
2 Kings 18:21 Now, see, you rely on the broken staff of Egypt. If someone leans on it, it will stab their hand. That's how Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, is to all who trust in him.
2 Kings 18:22 But if you tell me, 'We trust in God,' isn't that the same God whose shrines and altars Hezekiah removed, telling Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship at this altar in Jerusalem'?
2 Kings 18:23 Please now, I ask you, make a promise to the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you can find enough riders for them.
2 Kings 18:24 How can you then scare off even one of my master's lowest officers and rely on Egypt for chariots and soldiers?
2 Kings 18:25 Did I come to attack this place without God telling me to? God told me to come and destroy this land.
2 Kings 18:26 Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, with Shebna and Joah, said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to us in the Syrian language; we understand it. Do not speak in the Jewish language where the people on the wall can hear."
2 Kings 18:27 But Rabshakeh said to them, "Did my master send me to your master and to you to say these things? Didn't he send me to the people sitting on the wall, so that they will eat their own waste and drink their own urine with you?"
2 Kings 18:28 Then Rabshakeh stood up and shouted in the language of the Jews, "Listen to the message from the great king, the king of Assyria:"
2 Kings 18:29 The king says, "Don't let Hezekiah trick you: he can't save you from his power."
2 Kings 18:30 Don't let Hezekiah convince you to trust in God, telling you, "God will definitely save us, and this city won't be given to the king of Assyria."
2 Kings 18:31 Do not listen to Hezekiah: for the king of Assyria says, Make peace with me by giving a gift, and then come out to me. After that, each of you can eat from your own grapevine, and each can eat from his own fig tree, and drink water from your own well.
2 Kings 18:32 Until I come and take you to a land like yours, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land where olive oil and honey flow, so you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah who tells you that God will save us.
2 Kings 18:33 Did any nation's god rescue its land from the king of Assyria?
2 Kings 18:34 Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Did they save Samaria from my power?
2 Kings 18:35 Which gods of the nations have saved their lands from me, that God should rescue Jerusalem from my power?
2 Kings 18:36 The people stayed quiet and did not respond to him because the king had ordered, "Do not answer him."
2 Kings 18:37 Eliakim, Hilkiah's son who was in charge of the household, together with Shebna the secretary and Joah, Asaph's son the historian, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported to him what Rabshakeh had said.

2 Kings 19:1 When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on rough cloth, and went to God's house.
2 Kings 19:2 He sent Eliakim, the household manager, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests dressed in rough cloth to the prophet Isaiah, Amoz's son.
2 Kings 19:3 They told him, "Hezekiah says, 'Today is a day of trouble, criticism, and disrespect; the babies are ready to be born, but there is no strength to deliver them.'"
2 Kings 19:4 It might be that God will hear all of Rabshakeh's words, which the king of Assyria's master sent to insult the living God, and will correct what God has heard: so pray for the survivors who remain.
2 Kings 19:5 King Hezekiah's servants went to Isaiah.
2 Kings 19:6 Isaiah told them, "Tell your master this: God says, 'Do not be afraid of the words you’ve heard, which the king of Assyria's servants have used to insult me.'"
2 Kings 19:7 I will send a disaster on him, and he will hear a rumor and go back to his land; there he will die by the sword.
2 Kings 19:8 So Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah because he heard that the king had left Lachish.
2 Kings 19:9 When he heard that Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia, was coming to fight him, he sent messengers to Hezekiah with a message.
2 Kings 19:10 Tell King Hezekiah of Judah, "Don't be fooled by your God you trust, who says 'Jerusalem won't be given to the Assyrian king.'"
2 Kings 19:11 Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria did to all the lands, completely destroying them: and will you be saved?
2 Kings 19:12 Did the gods of other nations save those places my ancestors destroyed, like Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the Eden people in Thelasar?
2 Kings 19:13 Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the king of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah?
2 Kings 19:14 Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went to God's house and laid it out before God.
2 Kings 19:15 Hezekiah prayed to God and said, "O God of Israel, who sits among the cherubs, you are the one true God of all the earth's kingdoms; you created the heavens and the earth.
2 Kings 19:16 God, lean down and listen; open your eyes, God, and see; hear the words of Sennacherib, who has sent them to insult the living God.
2 Kings 19:17 Truly, God, the kings of Assyria have ruined other countries and their lands.
2 Kings 19:18 They threw their gods into the fire because they were not real gods, just objects made by human hands from wood and stone, so they destroyed them.
2 Kings 19:19 Now then, our God, I ask you, save us from his power, so all the kingdoms of the world will know that you are God, and only you.
2 Kings 19:20 Isaiah, son of Amoz, sent a message to Hezekiah: "God of Israel says, 'I have heard your prayer about Sennacherib, king of Assyria.'"
2 Kings 19:21 This is what God has said about him; The young woman, the daughter of Zion, looks down on you and laughs at you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
2 Kings 19:22 Who have you insulted and spoken against? Against whom have you raised your voice and looked up with arrogance? It is against the Holy One of Israel.
2 Kings 19:23 Your messengers insulted God, saying, "With my many chariots, I've climbed to the mountain tops, to Lebanon's edges, and I'll chop down its tall cedars and best firs. I'll go into its farthest stays and into its fruitful forest."
2 Kings 19:24 I have dug and drunk from unfamiliar waters, and with my feet I have dried up all the rivers near attacked cities.
2 Kings 19:25 Didn't you hear long ago what I did? Didn't you learn how I planned it long ago? Now I have made it happen, and you have turned fortified cities into piles of rubble.
2 Kings 19:26 So the people living there were weak, they were scared and confused; they were like the grass in the field, and like small plants, like the grass on the rooftops, and like grain destroyed before it fully grows.
2 Kings 19:27 I know where you live, how you leave and return, and how angry you are with me.
2 Kings 19:28 Because you are angry with me and your noise has reached my ears, I will put a hook in your nose and a bit in your mouth, and I will make you go back the way you came.
2 Kings 19:29 This will be a sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself, next year you will eat what grows from that, and in the third year plant crops, harvest them, and plant vineyards to eat their fruit.
2 Kings 19:30 The survivors from Judah's family will grow roots below and produce fruit above.
2 Kings 19:31 From Jerusalem, some will survive, and from Mount Zion, some will escape; God's passionate commitment will make this happen.
2 Kings 19:32 So, God says about the king of Assyria: He won't enter this city, shoot arrows here, approach it with shields, or build a siege ramp against it.
2 Kings 19:33 He will go back the same way he came and will not enter this city, says God.
2 Kings 19:34 I will protect this city and save it for myself and for my servant David.
2 Kings 19:35 That night, God's angel went out and struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. In the morning, they were all found dead.
2 Kings 19:36 So Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, left, went back, and lived in Nineveh.
2 Kings 19:37 While he was praying in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword. Then they ran away to Armenia. After that, his son Esarhaddon became king.

2 Kings 20:1 During that time, Hezekiah became very sick and was about to die. Then the prophet Isaiah, Amoz's son, visited him and said, "This is what God says: 'Get your affairs in order, because you are going to die; you will not recover.'"
2 Kings 20:2 He turned toward the wall and prayed to God, saying,
2 Kings 20:3 I ask you, God, please remember how I have lived truthfully before you with a sincere heart, and have done what is good in your eyes. And Hezekiah cried a lot.
2 Kings 20:4 Before Isaiah had left the inner courtyard, God spoke to him, saying,
2 Kings 20:5 Go back and tell Hezekiah, the leader of my people, "God says, I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. I will make you well. In three days, you will go to God's house."
2 Kings 20:6 I will extend your life by fifteen years; I will save you and this city from the king of Assyria's control; and I will protect this city for myself and for David, my servant.
2 Kings 20:7 Isaiah said, "Get some figs." They got them and put them on the sore, and he got better.
2 Kings 20:8 Hezekiah asked Isaiah, "What is the sign that God will heal me and I will go to God's house on the third day?"
2 Kings 20:9 Isaiah said, "This is the sign from God that he will do what he promised: will the shadow move forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?"
2 Kings 20:10 Hezekiah replied, "It's easy for the shadow to move forward ten steps; rather, let it go back ten steps."
2 Kings 20:11 Prophet Isaiah called out to God, and He made the shadow go back ten steps on King Ahaz's sundial, where it had gone down.
2 Kings 20:12 At that time, Berodachbaladan, Baladan's son and king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah because he had heard that Hezekiah was sick.
2 Kings 20:13 Hezekiah listened to them and showed them everything in his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, his armory, and everything in his treasury. There was nothing in his house or in his entire realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
2 Kings 20:14 The prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and asked, "What did these men say? Where did they come from to visit you?" Hezekiah replied, "They have come from a far country, from Babylon."
2 Kings 20:15 He said, "What did they see in your house?" And Hezekiah replied, "They saw everything in my house. There is nothing in my treasures that I did not show them."
2 Kings 20:16 Isaiah told Hezekiah, "Listen to God's message."
2 Kings 20:17 Look, the time will come when everything in your house, and all your ancestors have stored up until now, will be taken to Babylon; nothing will remain, says God.
2 Kings 20:18 Some of your sons, whom you will father, will be taken away to become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
2 Kings 20:19 Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "God's message that you gave is good." And he added, "Isn't it good if there is peace and honesty during my life?"
2 Kings 20:20 The other things Hezekiah did, his power, and how he built a pool and a channel to bring water into the city, are written in the history book of the kings of Judah, aren't they?
2 Kings 20:21 Hezekiah died and was buried with his ancestors, and his son Manasseh became king after him.

2 Kings 21:1 Manasseh was twelve when he started to rule, and he ruled for fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother was named Hephzibah.
2 Kings 21:2 He did evil things that God hated, imitating the wicked practices of the nations that God had thrown out before the Israelites.
2 Kings 21:3 He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had torn down; he set up altars for Baal and made a sacred garden, just like Ahab king of Israel did; and he worshipped the whole army of heaven and served them.
2 Kings 21:4 He made altars in God's house, where God said, "I will place my name in Jerusalem."
2 Kings 21:5 He made altars for all the sky's stars in the two yards of God's house.
2 Kings 21:6 He made his son walk through fire, tracked seasons for omens, cast spells, and talked with spirits and sorcerers. He did many evil things, making God very angry.
2 Kings 21:7 He placed an idol of the grove he made in the temple, where God told David and his son Solomon, "In this temple and Jerusalem, which I chose from all the Israelite tribes, I will put my name forever."
2 Kings 21:8 I will not make Israel leave the land I gave their ancestors, as long as they follow all my commands and the laws Moses gave them.
2 Kings 21:9 But they did not listen, and Manasseh led them to do more evil than the nations God had destroyed before the Israelites.
2 Kings 21:10 God spoke through his prophets, saying,
2 Kings 21:11 Because Manasseh, the king of Judah, did these terrible things and acted more wickedly than the Amorites before him, making Judah sin with his idols.
2 Kings 21:12 So this is what God of Israel says: Look, I will bring such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that anyone who hears about it will feel their ears buzzing.
2 Kings 21:13 I will judge Jerusalem as I did Samaria and the family of Ahab. I will clean Jerusalem like someone cleans a dish, scrubbing it and flipping it over.
2 Kings 21:14 I will abandon the rest of my people, give them to their enemies, and they will be taken and stolen by all their enemies.
2 Kings 21:15 They did evil things that upset me from the time their ancestors left Egypt until today.
2 Kings 21:16 Manasseh killed many innocent people, filling Jerusalem with blood from one end to the other; this was in addition to the sin of leading Judah to do evil, which was wrong in God's eyes.
2 Kings 21:17 The other things Manasseh did, his actions, and his sins are written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah, right?
2 Kings 21:18 Manasseh died and was buried in his own garden, the garden of Uzza, and his son Amon became king after him.
2 Kings 21:19 Amon was 22 years old when he became king, and he ruled for two years in Jerusalem. His mother was Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.
2 Kings 21:20 He did evil things that God saw, just like his father Manasseh did.
2 Kings 21:21 He followed in his father's footsteps, worshiping the idols his father worshiped.
2 Kings 21:22 He left God of his ancestors and did not follow God's way.
2 Kings 21:23 Amon's servants plotted against him and killed the king in his own home.
2 Kings 21:24 The people of the land killed all who plotted against King Amon, and they made Josiah, his son, king in his place.
2 Kings 21:25 The other things Amon did are written in the book of the history of Judah's kings, aren't they?
2 Kings 21:26 He was buried in his tomb in Uzza's garden, and his son Josiah became king after him.

2 Kings 22:1 Josiah became king when he was eight years old and ruled for thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah from Boscath.
2 Kings 22:2 He did what was good in God's eyes, followed his father David's path, and did not stray to the right or left.
2 Kings 22:3 In the eighteenth year of King Josiah's reign, he sent Shaphan, Azaliah's son and Meshullam's grandson, who was a writer, to God's house with a message.
2 Kings 22:4 Go to Hilkiah the high priest, so he can count the silver that has been brought to God's house, which the doorkeepers have collected from the people.
2 Kings 22:5 Let them hand it over to the workers in charge of God's house and let those workers use it to fix the damages of the house.
2 Kings 22:6 To carpenters, builders, stonecutters, and to buy wood and cut stones to fix the house.
2 Kings 22:7 However, they did not have to explain how they used the money given to them, because they acted honestly.
2 Kings 22:8 Hilkiah the high priest told Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the book of the law in God's house." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, who then read it.
2 Kings 22:9 Shaphan the secretary went to the king, told him news, and said, "Your servants collected the money found in the temple, and gave it to the workers managing the temple repairs."
2 Kings 22:10 The writer Shaphan told the king, "The priest Hilkiah gave me a book," and Shaphan read it to the king.
2 Kings 22:11 When the king heard the words of the law book, he tore his clothes.
2 Kings 22:12 The king told Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam Shaphan's son, Achbor Michaiah's son, Shaphan the writer, and Asahiah, the king's worker, to do this:
2 Kings 22:13 Go ask God for guidance for me, the people, and all of Judah about this book that we found. God is very angry with us because our ancestors did not listen to its words and did not do everything it says we should.
2 Kings 22:14 Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asahiah went to see Huldah the prophet, who was married to Shallum, Tikvah's son and Harhas's grandson, who took care of the clothes. She lived in Jerusalem at the school, and they talked with her.
2 Kings 22:15 She said to them, "God of Israel says, 'Tell the man who sent you to me,'".
2 Kings 22:16 God says, "Look, I will bring disaster on this place and on its people, all the curses written in the book the king of Judah has read."
2 Kings 22:17 Because they left me and worshiped other gods, making me angry with what they did, my anger will burn against this place and will not be put out.
2 Kings 22:18 Tell the king of Judah who sent you to ask God, God of Israel says this about what you have heard.
2 Kings 22:19 Because your heart was soft, and you humbled yourself before God when you heard what I said about this place and its people, that they would be ruined and cursed, and you tore your clothes and cried before me; I have heard you too, says God.
2 Kings 22:20 See, I will bring you to your ancestors, and you will go to your grave in peace; your eyes won't see all the bad things I will cause in this place. They told the king this message.

2 Kings 23:1 The king called and brought together all the senior leaders of Judah and Jerusalem.
2 Kings 23:2 The king went to God's house, and with him went all the men from Judah, everyone from Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, young and old. He read aloud to them everything in the book of the agreement found in God's house.
2 Kings 23:3 The king stood by a pillar and promised before God to follow God, to obey His commands, teachings, and laws with all their heart and soul, and to carry out the agreement written in this book. And all the people agreed to the promise.
2 Kings 23:4 The king told Hilkiah the high priest, the other priests, and the doorkeepers to take all the things made for Baal, the idol grove, and the star gods out of God's temple. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the Kidron Valley and took the ashes to Bethel.
2 Kings 23:5 He removed the false priests, appointed by the kings of Judah to offer incense on the high places in Judah's cities and near Jerusalem, including those who offered incense to Baal, the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the heavenly bodies.
2 Kings 23:6 He took the idol from God's house, outside Jerusalem, to Kidron Valley, burned it there, crushed it to dust, and scattered the dust on the common people's graves.
2 Kings 23:7 He destroyed the houses of the immoral people near God's house where women made tapestries for the shrine.
2 Kings 23:8 He brought all the priests from Judah's towns and made the worship sites unclean. These sites were where they burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He also destroyed the worship sites at the city gates, including the one near Joshua the city governor's gate, which was to the left as you entered the city gate.
2 Kings 23:9 However, the priests from the high places did not go to God's altar in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread with their fellow priests.
2 Kings 23:10 He made Topheth unclean, located in the valley of Hinnom's children, so no one could sacrifice their son or daughter in fire to Molech.
2 Kings 23:11 He removed the horses that Judah's kings had dedicated to the sun, near the entrance of God's house, by the room of Nathanmelech the official, which was in the outer area, and he burned the sun's chariots with fire.
2 Kings 23:12 The king destroyed the altars on the upper room of Ahaz that the kings of Judah built, and the altars Manasseh built in both courtyards of God's house. He tore them down and threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.
2 Kings 23:13 The king made the worship places unclean. These places were near Jerusalem, to the right of the Corruption Hill. King Solomon of Israel had built them for Ashtoreth, the Zidonians' hated god; for Chemosh, the Moabites' hated god; and for Milcom, the Ammonites' hated god.
2 Kings 23:14 He broke the idols, cut down the sacred trees, and filled those places with human bones.
2 Kings 23:15 Furthermore, the altar at Bethel, and the worship site built by Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who led Israel into sin, were destroyed by him; he broke down the altar and worship site, burned the worship site, crushed it to dust, and set the grove on fire.
2 Kings 23:16 When Josiah looked around, he saw the graves on the hill. He had the bones removed from the graves, burned them on the altar, and made the altar unclean. This act fulfilled what the man of God had announced, as God had said.
2 Kings 23:17 He asked, "What is that monument I see?" The city people answered him, "It's the grave of the man of God who came from Judah and predicted what you did to Bethel's altar."
2 Kings 23:18 He said, "Leave him be; don't touch his bones." So they left his bones undisturbed, along with the prophet's bones from Samaria.
2 Kings 23:19 Josiah removed all the worship sites in the towns of Samaria that Israel's kings had built to make God angry, and he did the same things to them that he had done in Bethel.
2 Kings 23:20 He killed all the priests at the high places who were there, burned human bones on the altars, and went back to Jerusalem.
2 Kings 23:21 The king told everyone, "Celebrate the Passover for God, as directed in the covenant book."
2 Kings 23:22 Certainly, there hadn't been a Passover like this since the time of the judges who led Israel, or during the reigns of the kings of Israel or Judah.
2 Kings 23:23 But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, this Passover was celebrated for God in Jerusalem.
2 Kings 23:24 Josiah got rid of the mediums, wizards, idols, and all the bad things found in Judah and Jerusalem, to follow the law written in the book discovered by the priest Hilkiah in God's house.
2 Kings 23:25 There was no king like him before, who followed God with all his heart, soul, and strength, just as Moses' law said; nor did any like him rise after.
2 Kings 23:26 Despite this, God did not turn away from the intensity of His great anger, which He had against Judah because of all the wrongs that Manasseh had done to provoke Him.
2 Kings 23:27 God said, "I will take away Judah from my sight, just as I did with Israel. I will reject Jerusalem, the city I chose, and this temple where I said my name would be."
2 Kings 23:28 The other things Josiah did, aren't they written in the book of Judah's kings' history?
2 Kings 23:29 During his reign, the Egyptian king Pharaoh Necho fought the Assyrian king at the Euphrates River. King Josiah confronted him, but Pharaoh Necho killed Josiah at Megiddo after seeing him.
2 Kings 23:30 His servants took his dead body in a wagon from Megiddo to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb. The locals chose Jehoahaz, Josiah's son, poured oil on his head to make him king after his father.
2 Kings 23:31 Jehoahaz was 23 years old when he became king, and he ruled for three months in Jerusalem. His mother was Hamutal, Jeremiah of Libnah's daughter.
2 Kings 23:32 He did evil things that God saw, just like his ancestors did.
2 Kings 23:33 Pharaoh Nechoh captured him at Riblah in the Hamath region so he couldn't rule in Jerusalem; he made the land pay a hundred silver talents and one gold talent.
2 Kings 23:34 Pharaoh Necho made Eliakim, son of Josiah, king instead of his father Josiah, changed his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away to Egypt, where he died.
2 Kings 23:35 Jehoiakim paid the silver and gold to Pharaoh; he taxed the people to get the money as Pharaoh ordered. He collected the silver and gold from everyone, based on how much they had to pay, to give to Pharaoh Necho.
2 Kings 23:36 Jehoiakim was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. His mother was named Zebudah, and she was the daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.
2 Kings 23:37 He did evil things that God did not like, just like his ancestors had done.

2 Kings 24:1 During his reign, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon attacked, and Jehoiakim served him for three years; then he changed his mind and fought against him.
2 Kings 24:2 God sent groups of Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites to destroy Judah, as God had said through the prophets.
2 Kings 24:3 Certainly, by God's command, this happened to Judah to take them away from His presence because of the sins of Manasseh and everything he did.
2 Kings 24:4 He also spilled innocent blood, filling Jerusalem with it, which God would not forgive.
2 Kings 24:5 The other things Jehoiakim did and all his actions are written in the book of the records of the kings of Judah, aren't they?
2 Kings 24:6 Jehoiakim died like his ancestors, and his son Jehoiachin became king after him.
2 Kings 24:7 The king of Egypt did not leave his country again because the king of Babylon had taken everything the king of Egypt owned from the Egypt river to the Euphrates river.
2 Kings 24:8 Jehoiachin was 18 years old when he started to rule, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 3 months. His mother's name was Nehushta, Elnathan of Jerusalem's daughter.
2 Kings 24:9 He did what was evil in God's eyes, just like his father had done.
2 Kings 24:10 At that time, King Nebuchadnezzar's servants attacked Jerusalem, and the city was surrounded.
2 Kings 24:11 Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, attacked the city, and his soldiers surrounded it.
2 Kings 24:12 King Jehoiachin of Judah, his mother, his servants, his leaders, and his officials all went out to meet the king of Babylon. And in the eighth year of his rule, the king of Babylon captured him.
2 Kings 24:13 He took away all the treasures from God's house and the king's house, and destroyed all the gold objects that King Solomon of Israel had made for God's temple, just as God had said.
2 Kings 24:14 He took all of Jerusalem, the leaders, and the strong warriors—10,000 captives, and all the skilled workers and metalworkers. Only the poorest people stayed in the land.
2 Kings 24:15 He took Jehoiachin to Babylon, along with the king's mother, wives, officials, and the land's important people, from Jerusalem to Babylon as prisoners.
2 Kings 24:16 All the strong men, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and metalworkers, a thousand, all good for battle, were taken to Babylon as prisoners by the king of Babylon.
2 Kings 24:17 The king of Babylon appointed Mattaniah, his uncle, as the new king and renamed him Zedekiah.
2 Kings 24:18 Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. His mother was Hamutal, Jeremiah of Libnah's daughter.
2 Kings 24:19 He did bad things in God's eyes, just like Jehoiakim did.
2 Kings 24:20 Because of God's anger, it happened in Jerusalem and Judah that he made them leave his presence, and then Zedekiah fought against the king of Babylon.

2 Kings 25:1 In the ninth year of his rule, in the tenth month, on the tenth day, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem, surrounded it, and built siege works all around it.
2 Kings 25:2 The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah's reign.
2 Kings 25:3 On the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was severe, and there was no bread for the people of the country.
2 Kings 25:4 The city's defenses were breached, and all the soldiers escaped at night through a gate between two walls near the king's garden. The enemy surrounded the city, and the king fled toward the open country.
2 Kings 25:5 The Chaldean army chased the king and caught him in the flat lands of Jericho; all his soldiers were scattered away from him.
2 Kings 25:6 They captured the king and took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where they passed judgment on him.
2 Kings 25:7 They killed Zedekiah's sons in front of him, blinded Zedekiah, tied him with bronze chains, and took him to Babylon.
2 Kings 25:8 In the fifth month, on the seventh day, which was in king Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon's nineteenth year of rule, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guards and a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
2 Kings 25:9 He burned down God's house, the king's house, all of Jerusalem's houses, and every important person's house with fire.
2 Kings 25:10 The entire Babylonian army, along with the captain of the guard, tore down the walls of Jerusalem all around.
2 Kings 25:11 The captain of the guard, Nebuzaradan, took away the remaining people in the city, those who had run away to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the people.
2 Kings 25:12 The guard captain let some poor people stay to work as grape growers and farmers.
2 Kings 25:13 The Chaldeans broke the bronze pillars, stands, and the large bronze basin in God's house into pieces and took the bronze to Babylon.
2 Kings 25:14 They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and all the brass items used in service.
2 Kings 25:15 The guard captain took away the firepans, bowls, and all things made of gold and silver.
2 Kings 25:16 The two pillars, one large bowl, and the stands that Solomon made for God's house; all these bronze items were too heavy to weigh.
2 Kings 25:17 One pillar was eighteen cubits tall, with a brass top three cubits high. It had braided designs and brass pomegranates all around the top. The second pillar was the same with braided work.
2 Kings 25:18 The guard leader took Seraiah, the main priest, Zephaniah, the second priest, and the three door guards.
2 Kings 25:19 He took from the city a military officer, five of the king's advisors found there, the army's chief secretary who enrolled the land's people, and sixty citizens also found in the city.
2 Kings 25:20 Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
2 Kings 25:21 The king of Babylon attacked and killed them in Riblah, in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken away from their land.
2 Kings 25:22 As for the people left in Judah, whom King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had not taken, he put Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, in charge over them.
2 Kings 25:23 When all the army leaders and their soldiers learned that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor, they went to see Gedaliah in Mizpah. This group included Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Careah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, and Jaazaniah son of a Maachathite, along with their men.
2 Kings 25:24 Gedaliah promised them and their men and said to them, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans: live in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and you will be fine."
2 Kings 25:25 In the seventh month, Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, from the royal family, came with ten men and killed Gedaliah. He also killed the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah.
2 Kings 25:26 All the people, important and not, and the army leaders got up and went to Egypt because they were scared of the Chaldeans.
2 Kings 25:27 In the thirty-seventh year of King Jehoiachin of Judah's captivity, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, freed King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison.
2 Kings 25:28 He spoke nicely to him and put his throne higher than the thrones of the kings with him in Babylon.
2 Kings 25:29 He changed his prison clothes and always ate bread in front of him for the rest of his life.
2 Kings 25:30 The king gave him a regular daily amount for every day of his life.

1 Chronicles 2:1 These are Israel's sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
1 Chronicles 2:2 Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, Asher.
1 Chronicles 2:3 Judah's sons were Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three were born to him by Shua's daughter, a Canaanite woman. Er, Judah's first son, was wicked in God's eyes, so God took his life.
1 Chronicles 2:4 Tamar, his daughter-in-law, gave birth to Pharez and Zerah for him. Judah had a total of five sons.
1 Chronicles 2:5 Pharez's sons were Hezron and Hamul.
1 Chronicles 2:6 Zerah's sons were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara: five in total.
1 Chronicles 2:7 Carmi had a son named Achar, who caused trouble in Israel by sinning with the cursed item.
1 Chronicles 2:8 Ethan's son was Azariah.
1 Chronicles 2:9 Hezron's sons were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
1 Chronicles 2:10 Ram fathered Amminadab; and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, the leader of Judah's descendants.
1 Chronicles 2:11 Nahshon had a son named Salma, and Salma had a son named Boaz.
1 Chronicles 2:12 Boaz had Obed, and Obed had Jesse.
1 Chronicles 2:13 Jesse had his first son Eliab, his second son Abinadab, and his third son Shimma.
1 Chronicles 2:14 Nethaneel was fourth, Raddai was fifth,
1 Chronicles 2:15 Ozem was the sixth, David was the seventh.
1 Chronicles 2:16 His sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's sons were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three in total.
1 Chronicles 2:17 Abigail gave birth to Amasa, and Amasa's father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
1 Chronicles 2:18 Caleb, Hezron's son, had kids with his wife Azubah and Jerioth. Their sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
1 Chronicles 2:19 After Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who gave birth to Hur.
1 Chronicles 2:20 Hur had a son named Uri, and Uri had a son named Bezaleel.
1 Chronicles 2:21 Later, Hezron married the daughter of Machir, father of Gilead, when he was 60 years old, and she gave birth to Segub.
1 Chronicles 2:22 Segub was the father of Jair, who owned twenty-three cities in Gilead.
1 Chronicles 2:23 He captured Geshur and Aram with Jair's villages and Kenath with its surrounding towns, a total of sixty cities. All these were the lands of Machir, Gilead's father.
1 Chronicles 2:24 After Hezron died in Calebephratah, his wife Abiah had a son named Ashur, who became the founder of Tekoa.
1 Chronicles 2:25 Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, had these sons: Ram, his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
1 Chronicles 2:26 Jerahmeel also had another wife named Atarah; she was Onam's mother.
1 Chronicles 2:27 Ram's firstborn Jerahmeel had sons: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
1 Chronicles 2:28 Onam's sons were Shammai and Jada. Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur.
1 Chronicles 2:29 Abishur's wife was named Abihail, and she had two sons for him, Ahban and Molid.
1 Chronicles 2:30 Nadab's sons were Seled and Appaim, but Seled died without having any kids.
1 Chronicles 2:31 Appaim's sons were Ishi, Ishi's sons were Sheshan, and Sheshan's children were Ahlai.
1 Chronicles 2:32 Jada, the brother of Shammai, had two sons: Jether and Jonathan. But Jether died without having any children.
1 Chronicles 2:33 Jonathan's sons were Peleth and Zaza. These were Jerahmeel's sons.
1 Chronicles 2:34 Sheshan had only daughters, not sons. Sheshan's servant was an Egyptian named Jarha.
1 Chronicles 2:35 Sheshan gave his daughter as a wife to Jarha, his servant, and she gave birth to a son named Attai.
1 Chronicles 2:36 Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabad.
1 Chronicles 2:37 Zabad had a son named Ephlal, who had a son named Obed.
1 Chronicles 2:38 Obed had a son named Jehu, and Jehu had a son named Azariah.
1 Chronicles 2:39 Azariah had a son named Helez, and Helez had a son named Eleasah.
1 Chronicles 2:40 Eleasah had a son named Sisamai, and Sisamai had a son named Shallum.
1 Chronicles 2:41 Shallum had a son named Jekamiah, and Jekamiah had a son named Elishama.
1 Chronicles 2:42 Caleb's brother Jerahmeel had sons. Mesha was the oldest, and he became the father of Ziph. Mareshah's sons became the fathers of Hebron.
1 Chronicles 2:43 Hebron's sons were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
1 Chronicles 2:44 Shema had Raham, who became the father of Jorkoam, and Rekem had Shammai.
1 Chronicles 2:45 Shammai's son was Maon, and Maon was Bethzur's father.
1 Chronicles 2:46 Ephah, Caleb's woman, had Haran, Moza, and Gazez; and Haran had Gazez.
1 Chronicles 2:47 Jahdai's sons were Regem, Jotham, Gesham, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
1 Chronicles 2:48 Maachah, who was with Caleb, had two sons named Sheber and Tirhanah.
1 Chronicles 2:49 She also gave birth to Shaaph, who was Madmannah's ancestor, Sheva, who was Machbenah's ancestor, and the ancestor of Gibea; Caleb's daughter was Achsa.
1 Chronicles 2:50 Caleb, Hur's son and Ephratah's oldest, had these sons: Shobal started Kirjathjearim.
1 Chronicles 2:51 Salma was the ancestor of Bethlehem; Hareph was the ancestor of Bethgader.
1 Chronicles 2:52 Shobal, the father of Kirjathjearim, had sons: Haroeh and some of the Manahethites.
1 Chronicles 2:53 The families of Kirjathjearim were the Ithrites, the Puhites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. From these families came the Zareathites and the Eshtaulites.
1 Chronicles 2:54 Salma's children included Bethlehem, the people of Netophah, Ataroth, Joab's family, half of the people of Manahath, and the Zorites.
1 Chronicles 2:55 The families of writers who lived in Jabez were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Suchathites. They are the Kenites who come from Hemath, the ancestor of the Rechab family.

1 Chronicles 3:1 These were David's sons born in Hebron: the first, Amnon, with Ahinoam from Jezreel; the second, Daniel, with Abigail from Carmel.
1 Chronicles 3:2 The third, Absalom, Maachah's son and Talmai the king of Geshur's grandson; the fourth, Adonijah, Haggith's son.
1 Chronicles 3:3 The fifth son was Shephatiah with Abital; the sixth was Ithream with Eglah, his wife.
1 Chronicles 3:4 He had six children in Hebron, where he ruled for seven and a half years; then in Jerusalem, he ruled for thirty-three years.
1 Chronicles 3:5 In Jerusalem, he had four sons by Bathshua, Ammiel's daughter: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
1 Chronicles 3:6 Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet too.
1 Chronicles 3:7 Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia,
1 Chronicles 3:8 Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine.
1 Chronicles 3:9 All these were David's sons, not including the sons from his other women, and their sister Tamar.
1 Chronicles 3:10 Solomon's son was Rehoboam, his son was Abia, his son was Asa, and his son was Jehoshaphat.
1 Chronicles 3:11 Joram's son, Ahaziah's son, Joash's son,
1 Chronicles 3:12 Amaziah's son, Azariah's son, Jotham's son,
1 Chronicles 3:13 Ahaz's son, Hezekiah's son, Manasseh's son,
1 Chronicles 3:14 Amon was his son, and then Josiah was his son.
1 Chronicles 3:15 Josiah's sons were, the oldest Johanan, the next Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, and the youngest Shallum.
1 Chronicles 3:16 Jehoiakim's sons were Jeconiah and then Zedekiah.
1 Chronicles 3:17 Jeconiah's children were Assir and his son Salathiel.
1 Chronicles 3:18 Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah were there too.
1 Chronicles 3:19 Pedaiah had sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's children were Meshullam, Hananiah, and their sister Shelomith.
1 Chronicles 3:20 Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed were five men.
1 Chronicles 3:21 Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah and Jesaiah. Rephaiah's, Arnan's, Obadiah's, and Shechaniah's were their families.
1 Chronicles 3:22 The children of Shechaniah were Shemaiah, and Shemaiah's children were Hattush, Igeal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat—six in total.
1 Chronicles 3:23 Neariah had three sons: Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam.
1 Chronicles 3:24 Elioenai's sons were Hodaiah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Dalaiah, and Anani, seven in total.

1 Chronicles 4:1 Judah's sons were: Pharez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
1 Chronicles 4:2 Reaiah, Shobal's son, had a son named Jahath; Jahath had sons named Ahumai and Lahad. These are the clans of the Zorathites.
1 Chronicles 4:3 These were Etam's descendants: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash; their sister was named Hazelelponi.
1 Chronicles 4:4 Penuel was Gedor's father, and Ezer was Hushah's father. They were Hur's sons, who was Ephrath's first child and Bethlehem's father.
1 Chronicles 4:5 Ashur from Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
1 Chronicles 4:6 Naarah had sons named Ahuzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were Naarah's sons.
1 Chronicles 4:7 Helah's sons were Zereth, Jezoar, and Ethnan.
1 Chronicles 4:8 Coz had children Anub and Zobebah, and the relatives of Aharhel, Harum's son.
1 Chronicles 4:9 Jabez was more respected than his brothers; his mother named him Jabez, saying, "Because I gave birth to him in pain."
1 Chronicles 4:10 Jabez prayed to the God of Israel and said, "Please bless me greatly, expand my territory, be with me, and keep me from harm so that I will not suffer." And God gave him what he asked for.
1 Chronicles 4:11 Chelub, Shuah's brother, had a son named Mehir, who was Eshton's father.
1 Chronicles 4:12 Eshton had sons called Bethrapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, who was father of Irnahash. These men were from Rechah.
1 Chronicles 4:13 Kenaz had two sons named Othniel and Seraiah, and Othniel had a son named Hathath.
1 Chronicles 4:14 Meonothai fathered Ophrah, and Seraiah fathered Joab, who was the leader in the Valley of Craftsmen because they were skilled workers.
1 Chronicles 4:15 Caleb, Jephunneh's son, had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah had a son named Kenaz.
1 Chronicles 4:16 Jehaleleel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel.
1 Chronicles 4:17 Ezra had sons named Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. He also had a daughter named Miriam, another son named Shammai, and Ishbah, who became the father of Eshtemoa.
1 Chronicles 4:18 Jehudijah, his wife, had three sons: Jered, who started the family of Gedor; Heber, who started the family of Socho; and Jekuthiel, who started the family of Zanoah. All of them were the sons of Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, whom Mered married.
1 Chronicles 4:19 Hodiah's sons, Naham's sister and the father of Keilah from Garm and Eshtemoa from Maachah.
1 Chronicles 4:20 Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. Ishi's sons were Zoheth and Benzoheth.
1 Chronicles 4:21 Shelah, Judah's son, had sons: Er, who started Lecah's family; Laadah, who started Mareshah's family; and families who made fine linen in Ashbea's house.
1 Chronicles 4:22 Jokim and the men of Chozeba, Joash, and Saraph ruled in Moab, and Jashubilehem. These are old stories.
1 Chronicles 4:23 These were the potters and the people who lived near the plants and bushes; there they lived and worked for the king.
1 Chronicles 4:24 Simeon's sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
1 Chronicles 4:25 Shallum's son, Mibsam's son, Mishma's son.
1 Chronicles 4:26 Mishma's sons were Hamuel, then Zacchur, and then Shimei.
1 Chronicles 4:27 Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers didn't have many children, nor did their family grow as much as the family of Judah.
1 Chronicles 4:28 They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, and Hazarshual.
1 Chronicles 4:29 In Bilhah, in Ezem, and in Tolad,
1 Chronicles 4:30 In Bethuel, in Hormah, and in Ziklag,
1 Chronicles 4:31 In Bethmarcaboth, Hazarsusim, Bethbirei, and Shaaraim were their cities until David became king.
1 Chronicles 4:32 Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five cities.
1 Chronicles 4:33 They had villages near those cities, up to Baal, where they lived and kept their family records.
1 Chronicles 4:34 Meshobab, Jamlech, and Joshah, who was Amaziah's son,
1 Chronicles 4:35 Joel and Jehu, Josibiah's son, Seraiah's grandson, Asiel's great-grandson.
1 Chronicles 4:36 Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah.
1 Chronicles 4:37 Ziza, son of Shiphi, grandson of Allon, great-grandson of Jedaiah, and descendant of Shimri and Shemaiah.
1 Chronicles 4:38 These named were leaders in their families, and their ancestors' family grew a lot.
1 Chronicles 4:39 They went to Gedor's entrance, to the valley's east side, to find grazing land for their sheep.
1 Chronicles 4:40 They found rich and good grasslands, the land was spacious, calm, and peaceful; for the people from Ham had lived there long ago.
1 Chronicles 4:41 These named people came during Hezekiah's rule in Judah, attacked their tents, destroyed the local dwellings, and lived there since it was good land for their sheep.
1 Chronicles 4:42 Some from Simeon's tribe, five hundred men, went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, Ishi's sons.
1 Chronicles 4:43 They defeated the remaining Amalekites who had escaped, and lived there until today.

1 Chronicles 5:1 Reuben was Israel's first son, but since he dishonored his father's bed, his rights as firstborn were given to Joseph's sons instead, and his family line did not get the firstborn's rights.
1 Chronicles 5:2 Judah became stronger than his brothers, and from him came the main leader, but Joseph received the birthright.
1 Chronicles 5:3 Reuben, Israel's first son, had these sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
1 Chronicles 5:4 Joel's sons were Shemaiah, then Gog, then Shimei.
1 Chronicles 5:5 Micah's son, Reaia's son, Baal's son,
1 Chronicles 5:6 Beerah was his son. The Assyrian king, Tilgathpilneser, took him away as a prisoner. He was a leader of the Reubenites.
1 Chronicles 5:7 His brothers, organized by families, when their family tree was recorded, had as leaders Jeiel and Zechariah.
1 Chronicles 5:8 Bela, son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel, lived in Aroer, reaching to Nebo and Baalmeon.
1 Chronicles 5:9 He lived to the east, up to the desert edge, by the Euphrates River because they had lots of animals in Gilead.
1 Chronicles 5:10 During Saul's time, they fought against the Hagarites, defeated them, and lived in their camps across the eastern region of Gilead.
1 Chronicles 5:11 The Gad children lived across from them in Bashan land up to Salcah.
1 Chronicles 5:12 Joel was the leader, Shapham was second, then Jaanai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
1 Chronicles 5:13 Their family members from their father's house were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Heber—seven in total.
1 Chronicles 5:14 These are the descendants of Abihail: Huri's child, Jaroah's child, Gilead's child, Michael's child, Jeshishai's child, Jahdo's child, Buz's child.
1 Chronicles 5:15 Ahi, son of Abdiel, son of Guni, leader of their family.
1 Chronicles 5:16 They lived in Gilead, in Bashan, its villages, and all the surrounding areas of Sharon, right up to their borders.
1 Chronicles 5:17 All these people were listed in family records during the time of Jotham, king of Judah, and during the time of Jeroboam, king of Israel.
1 Chronicles 5:18 Reuben's sons, the Gadites, and half of the Manasseh tribe, brave men good at fighting, carrying shields and swords, shooting arrows, and skilled in battle, totaled 44,760 warriors ready for war.
1 Chronicles 5:19 They fought against the Hagarites, Jetur, Nephish, and Nodab.
1 Chronicles 5:20 They were helped in the fight against them, and their enemies, the Hagarites, were defeated. Everyone who was with the Hagarites was also defeated, because during the battle they called out to God, and he listened to them since they trusted in him.
1 Chronicles 5:21 They took their animals: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 people.
1 Chronicles 5:22 Many people were killed because the war was directed by God. They lived in those places until they were captured.
1 Chronicles 5:23 The children from part of the Manasseh tribe lived in the land; they grew in numbers from Bashan to Baalhermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
1 Chronicles 5:24 These were the leaders of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, strong and well-known men, leaders of their families.
1 Chronicles 5:25 They sinned against their ancestors' God and chased after the local people's gods, even though God had destroyed those people before them.
1 Chronicles 5:26 God moved the hearts of Pul, the king of Assyria, and Tilgathpilneser, the king of Assyria, who then took the people of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh captive. He brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river Gozan, where they are to this day.

1 Chronicles 7:1 Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimrom.
1 Chronicles 7:2 Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam, and Shemuel, leaders of their family. They were brave and strong. During David's time, their family had 22,600 men.
1 Chronicles 7:3 Uzzi's sons were Izrahiah, and Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah, five leaders in total.
1 Chronicles 7:4 With them, according to their families, were 36,000 soldiers grouped by ancestors, because they had many wives and children.
1 Chronicles 7:5 Their relatives in all the Issachar families were brave and strong warriors, counted in their family records as 87,000 men.
1 Chronicles 7:6 Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.

1 Chronicles 10:6 Saul died, along with his three sons and his whole family.

1 Chronicles 10:14 He did not ask God; so God killed him and gave the kingdom to David, Jesse's son.
