1 Chronicles 17:1 One day, while David was at home, he said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I live in a house made of cedar wood, but God's covenant chest is still under a tent."
1 Chronicles 17:2 Then Nathan told David, "Do all that you want to do; because God is with you."
1 Chronicles 17:3 That night, God spoke to Nathan and said,
1 Chronicles 17:4 Go and tell David my servant, God says, You must not build a house for me to live in.
1 Chronicles 17:5 Since the day I led Israel up to this day, I have not lived in a house; instead, I moved from one tent to another and from one shelter to another.
1 Chronicles 17:6 Everywhere I have gone with all Israel, did I ask any of the leaders of Israel, whom I told to take care of my people, 'Why haven't you built me a cedar house?'
1 Chronicles 17:7 So now, tell my servant David this: God says, "I chose you from the pasture and from tending sheep to be the leader of my people Israel."
1 Chronicles 17:8 I have always been with you wherever you have gone, and I have defeated all your enemies for you. I have given you a reputation as great as any of the famous people on the earth.
1 Chronicles 17:9 I will choose a place for my people Israel and make them settle there. They will live there and not be uprooted again; the children of wickedness will not harm them anymore like before.
1 Chronicles 17:10 Ever since I told judges to lead my people Israel, I will also defeat all your enemies. Also, I tell you that God will build you a house.
1 Chronicles 17:11 When your time ends and you join your ancestors, I will bring up one of your descendants, one of your sons, and make his kingdom strong.
1 Chronicles 17:12 He will build a house for me, and I will make his throne last forever.
1 Chronicles 17:13 I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will not remove my mercy from him as I did with the one before you.
1 Chronicles 17:14 I will establish him in my house and kingdom forever; his throne will be secure forever.
1 Chronicles 17:15 Nathan told David everything just as he had seen and heard.
1 Chronicles 17:16 King David came and sat before God and said, "Who am I, God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?"
1 Chronicles 17:17 Even this was a small thing to you, God; you have also talked about your servant's family for a long time ahead, and you have treated me like someone with high status, O God.
1 Chronicles 17:18 What more can David say to you about the honor of your servant? You know your servant well.
1 Chronicles 17:19 God, for your servant's benefit and following your own will, you have done all these great things and revealed them.
1 Chronicles 17:20 God, no one is like you, and there is no other God except you, just as we have heard.
1 Chronicles 17:21 What other nation on earth is like your people, Israel, whom God saved to be his own, to make himself a great and feared name by removing other nations from before your people whom he rescued from Egypt?
1 Chronicles 17:22 You made Israel your people forever, and you, God, became their God.
1 Chronicles 17:23 So now, God, let what you have said about your servant and his family be true forever, and do as you have promised.
1 Chronicles 17:24 Let it be firm, so your name can be honored forever, as people say, "God commanded the armies is the God of Israel and is a God to Israel." And let David's family, your servant's house, stand strong in your presence.
1 Chronicles 17:25 You, my God, have told your servant that you will build a house for him: so your servant felt moved to pray to you.
1 Chronicles 17:26 And now, God, you are God, and have promised this kindness to your servant.
1 Chronicles 17:27 So now, please bless your servant's house so it will always be before you. Because when you bless, God, it is blessed forever.

Now decide what answer I should take back to the one who sent me.

1 Chronicles 21:18 Then God's angel told Gad to tell David to go and build an altar for God on Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor.
1 Chronicles 21:19 David went up following Gad's instructions, which he gave in God's name.
1 Chronicles 21:20 Ornan turned around, saw the angel, and his four sons with him hid. Ornan was threshing wheat.
1 Chronicles 21:21 When David arrived at Ornan's place, Ornan saw him, left the threshing floor, and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.
1 Chronicles 21:22 David said to Ornan, "Let me have this threshing floor to build an altar for God. Sell it to me at its full price, so that the sickness will stop hurting the people."
1 Chronicles 21:23 Ornan said to David, "Take this and let the king do what seems right to him: Look, I give you the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing tools for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering; I give it all."
1 Chronicles 21:24 King David said to Ornan, "No, I will really buy it for the full price. I won't take what is yours for God or give burnt offerings for free."
1 Chronicles 21:25 David paid Ornan six hundred gold shekels for the land.
1 Chronicles 21:26 David made an altar for God, gave burnt and peace offerings, prayed to God, and God responded with fire from heaven on the burnt offering altar.
1 Chronicles 21:27 God told the angel to put his sword back in its sheath.
1 Chronicles 21:28 At that time, David saw that God had answered him at Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor, and he made sacrifices there.
1 Chronicles 21:29 The tent of God that Moses set up in the desert, and the altar for burnt sacrifices, were then on the hill at Gibeon.
1 Chronicles 21:30 David could not approach to ask God because he was afraid of the angel's sword.

1 Chronicles 28:1 David gathered all the leaders of Israel, the tribal leaders, the group leaders who served the king in shifts, the leaders in charge of a thousand men, the leaders of a hundred men, the managers of the king's property and belongings, his sons, the officials, the strong warriors, and all the brave men in Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles 28:2 King David stood up and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I wanted to build a resting place for the ark of God's covenant and a place for our God's feet, and I prepared for the construction."
1 Chronicles 28:3 God told me, "You must not build a house for my name, because you are a warrior and have spilled blood."
1 Chronicles 28:4 However, God chose me from all my father's family to be king over Israel forever. God picked Judah to lead; from Judah's family, my father's household; and from my father's sons, he preferred me to be king over all Israel.
1 Chronicles 28:5 Out of all my sons, because God has given me many, he has chosen my son Solomon to rule as king over Israel.
1 Chronicles 28:6 He told me, "Your son Solomon will build my house and courts: I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father."
1 Chronicles 28:7 I will make his kingdom last forever if he faithfully follows my commands and decisions, just like today.
1 Chronicles 28:8 So now, in front of all Israel, God's people, and while our God listens, follow and search for all of God's commands. Then you will own this good land and pass it down to your children forever.
1 Chronicles 28:9 And you, Solomon my son, understand your father's God, and serve him with a true heart and an eager mind: for God knows every heart and understands every thought's plan: if you look for him, you will find him; but if you leave him, he will reject you forever.
1 Chronicles 28:10 Be careful now; God has chosen you to build a house for the holy place: be strong, and get it done.
1 Chronicles 28:11 David gave Solomon the designs for the entrance, the buildings, the storerooms, the upper rooms, the inner rooms, and the spot for the mercy seat.
1 Chronicles 28:12 He had a design, inspired by God, for the temple courts, the surrounding rooms, the storerooms of God's house, and the storerooms for the holy items.
1 Chronicles 28:13 Also for the duties of the priests and the Levites, for all the work in God's house, and for all the items used in God's house.
1 Chronicles 28:14 He provided gold, measured by weight, for all the gold items, for every type of service tool; he also gave silver, weighed out, for all the silver tools, for every kind of service.
1 Chronicles 28:15 Even the amount of gold needed for the candlesticks and their gold lamps was measured for each candlestick and its lamps. And the silver candlesticks were weighed, each candlestick and its lamps, according to how each one was to be used.
1 Chronicles 28:16 He gave gold by weight for each table of showbread, and the same with silver for the silver tables.
1 Chronicles 28:17 Also, pure gold for the meat hooks, bowls, and cups; and for the gold basins, he gave gold measured by weight for each basin; and the same with silver for each silver basin.
1 Chronicles 28:18 For the incense altar, pure gold measured by weight; and gold for the model of the cherubim's chariot, which stretched out their wings and covered God's covenant ark.
1 Chronicles 28:19 David said, "God made me understand everything about this design through his guidance, including all the details of the work."
1 Chronicles 28:20 David told Solomon his son, "Be strong and brave, and do the work. Don't be afraid or worried, because God, my God, is with you. He won't let you down or leave you until you finish all the work for God's house."
1 Chronicles 28:21 Look, the groups of priests and Levites will be with you for all of God's house service. Every skilled man who is willing will be with you for any kind of work. The leaders and everyone else will fully follow your orders.

1 Chronicles 29:1 King David told everyone, "My son Solomon, who God chose alone, is still young and unexperienced, and the task is huge. This palace is not for a human, but for God."
1 Chronicles 29:2 I have made ready with all my strength for God's house: gold for the gold items, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, and wood for the wooden items. Also onyx, setting stones, sparkling stones, stones of many colors, all kinds of precious stones, and plenty of marble.
1 Chronicles 29:3 I love my God's house so much that I have given my own gold and silver to it, more than everything else I've provided for the sacred place.
1 Chronicles 29:4 Even three thousand units of gold from Ophir and seven thousand units of pure silver to cover the house walls.
1 Chronicles 29:5 Gold for gold items, silver for silver items, and for all kinds of work done by skilled workers. And who is ready to dedicate their service today to God?
1 Chronicles 29:6 The leaders of the families, the heads of the Israelite tribes, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, along with the supervisors of the king's projects, gave freely.
1 Chronicles 29:7 God gave to serve God's house: 5,000 talents of gold, 10,000 drams, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of brass, and 100,000 talents of iron.
1 Chronicles 29:8 People who had precious stones brought them to God's house treasury, through Jehiel the Gershonite.
1 Chronicles 29:9 The people were happy because they gave freely and with true hearts to God, and King David was also very happy.
1 Chronicles 29:10 David praised God in front of everyone and said, "Praise to you, God of Israel, our father, forever and ever."
1 Chronicles 29:11 Yours, O God, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty: for everything in heaven and on earth is yours; yours is the kingdom, O God, and you are honored as the leader above all.
1 Chronicles 29:12 Wealth and honor come from you, God; you rule over everything. Power and strength are in your hand; you have the ability to make anyone great and strong.
1 Chronicles 29:13 So now, our God, we thank you and honor your wonderful name.
1 Chronicles 29:14 Who am I and who are my people that we can freely give like this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from you.
1 Chronicles 29:15 We are outsiders before you, and travelers, just like our ancestors: our time on earth is like a shadow, with no one staying forever.
1 Chronicles 29:16 God, all these things we've gathered to build a house for your holy name come from your hand, and they are all yours.
1 Chronicles 29:17 I also know, my God, that you test the heart and you like honesty. I have gladly given all this with an honest heart. And now I see with joy your people here giving to you willingly.
1 Chronicles 29:18 O God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors, always keep this in the hearts and minds of your people, and make their hearts loyal to you.
1 Chronicles 29:19 Give my son Solomon a pure heart to follow your commands, your guidance, and your laws, to do everything, and to build the temple for which I have provided.
1 Chronicles 29:20 David told everyone, "Now praise God your God." Everyone praised the God of their ancestors, bowed their heads, and worshiped God and the king.
1 Chronicles 29:21 They offered sacrifices and burnt offerings to God the day after, including a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, along with their drink offerings, and many more sacrifices for all the people of Israel.
1 Chronicles 29:22 They ate and drank with great joy before God that day. They made Solomon, David's son, king again, anointed him to serve God as the supreme leader, and appointed Zadok as the priest.
1 Chronicles 29:23 Then Solomon sat on God's throne as king in place of his father David, succeeded, and all Israel followed him.
1 Chronicles 29:24 All the leaders, strong men, and King David's sons too, accepted Solomon as king.
1 Chronicles 29:25 God made Solomon very great in the eyes of all Israel, and gave him a kind of royal splendor no other king in Israel had ever had.
1 Chronicles 29:26 David, Jesse's son, ruled over all Israel.
1 Chronicles 29:27 He ruled over Israel for forty years; seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles 29:28 He died at a ripe old age, with a long life, wealth, and respect, and his son Solomon became king after him.
1 Chronicles 29:29 The things King David did, from beginning to end, are recorded in Samuel the seer's book, in Nathan the prophet's book, and in Gad the seer's book.
1 Chronicles 29:30 Throughout his rule and power, and the events that happened to him, to Israel, and to all the kingdoms of the lands.

2 Chronicles 1:1 Solomon, David's son, became strong as a king, and God was with him and made him very great.
2 Chronicles 1:2 Then Solomon spoke to all Israel, including the leaders of thousands and hundreds, the judges, every ruler, and all the family heads.
2 Chronicles 1:3 Solomon and all the people with him went to the high place in Gibeon because that's where God's meeting tent, which Moses, God's servant, had made in the desert, was located.
2 Chronicles 1:4 David had moved the ark of God from Kirjathjearim to the spot he had set up for it; he had made a tent for it in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 1:5 The bronze altar made by Bezaleel, Uri's son, Hur's grandson, was placed in front of God's Tabernacle. Solomon and the people went to pray there.
2 Chronicles 1:6 Solomon went to the bronze altar in front of God, which was at the meeting tent, and gave a thousand burnt offerings on it.
2 Chronicles 1:7 That night, God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what you want me to give you."
2 Chronicles 1:8 Solomon said to God, "You have shown great kindness to my father David and have made me king in his place."
2 Chronicles 1:9 Now, God, let your promise to my father David be true, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
2 Chronicles 1:10 Please give me wisdom and knowledge so I can lead your people. Who else can judge such a great group?
2 Chronicles 1:11 God told Solomon, "Since you wanted this and did not ask for money, wealth, honor, or the death of your enemies, and you did not even ask for a long life, but you asked for wisdom and knowledge to make good decisions for my people I have put you in charge of as their king:"
2 Chronicles 1:12 God has given you wisdom and knowledge; and you will receive riches, wealth, and honor more than any kings before you, and no future king will match what you have.
2 Chronicles 1:13 Solomon returned from his trip to the sacred site at Gibeon to Jerusalem, leaving the meeting tent, and ruled over Israel.
2 Chronicles 1:14 Solomon collected chariots and soldiers on horses. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 soldiers on horses. He put them in the chariot cities and near the king in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 1:15 The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar trees as plentiful as the sycamore trees in the lowlands.
2 Chronicles 1:16 Solomon got horses from Egypt and also linen yarn. The king's traders bought the yarn for a certain amount of money.
2 Chronicles 1:17 They brought a chariot from Egypt for six hundred silver coins, and a horse for one hundred and fifty coins: and in this way, they provided horses for all the Hittite and Syrian kings through their connections.

2 Chronicles 2:1 Solomon decided to build a temple for God and a palace for his reign.
2 Chronicles 2:2 Solomon assigned seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand to cut stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to supervise them.
2 Chronicles 2:3 Solomon sent a message to Huram, the king of Tyre, saying, "Just as you helped my father David by sending him cedar wood to build a house to live in, please do the same for me."
2 Chronicles 2:4 Look, I am building a house for the name of God, to dedicate it to him, and to burn sweet incense before him, and for the regular bread offering, and for the burnt offerings every morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, new moons, and holy festivals of God. This is a lasting rule for Israel.
2 Chronicles 2:5 The house I am building is big because our God is greater than all other gods.
2 Chronicles 2:6 But who can build a house for God, when even the highest heavens cannot hold Him? So who am I to build a house for Him, except as a place to offer sacrifices to Him?
2 Chronicles 2:7 Send me a skilled man now who can work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue materials, and who knows how to engrave like the skilled men I have in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David arranged for.
2 Chronicles 2:8 Send me cedar, fir, and algum trees from Lebanon, because I know your workers can cut wood there; and look, my workers will work with your workers.
2 Chronicles 2:9 To provide me with plenty of wood, because the house I will build is going to be very great.
2 Chronicles 2:10 Look, I will give your workers, the woodcutters, twenty thousand bushels of ground wheat, twenty thousand bushels of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.
2 Chronicles 2:11 Huram, the king of Tyre, replied in writing and sent it to Solomon: Because God loves His people, He has made you their king.
2 Chronicles 2:12 Huram also said, "Praise God of Israel, who created heaven and earth, and gave King David a wise son with good judgement and understanding to build a temple for God, and a palace for his kingdom."
2 Chronicles 2:13 I have sent a skilled man with knowledge, from Huram my father.
2 Chronicles 2:14 The son's mother was from the tribe of Dan, and his father was from Tyre, skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, as well as in purple, blue, and fine linen, and red fabrics. He could carve any design and come up with any idea, working with your skilled workers and those of your father David.
2 Chronicles 2:15 Now then, please send the wheat, barley, oil, and wine you mentioned to your servants.
2 Chronicles 2:16 We will chop wood in Lebanon as much as you need and float it by sea to Joppa for you to take to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 2:17 Solomon counted all the foreigners in Israel, using the same method his father David had used; there were 153,600 in total.
2 Chronicles 2:18 He assigned seventy thousand workers to carry loads, eighty thousand to cut stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred supervisors to make sure the people worked.

2 Chronicles 3:1 Solomon started building God's house in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where God had shown himself to David, his father, at the spot David had set up on Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor.
2 Chronicles 3:2 He started to build on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his rule.
2 Chronicles 3:3 These are the details Solomon followed to build God's house: it was 60 cubits long following the original unit, and 20 cubits wide.
2 Chronicles 3:4 The porch in front of the house was as wide as the house, twenty units long, and one hundred twenty units high. He covered the inside with pure gold.
2 Chronicles 3:5 He covered the bigger room with fir wood and coated it with pure gold, then he put palm trees and chains on it.
2 Chronicles 3:6 He decorated the house with beautiful precious stones, and the gold used was from Parvaim.
2 Chronicles 3:7 He also covered the house, its beams, pillars, walls, and doors with gold, and carved cherubs on the walls.
2 Chronicles 3:8 He built the most sacred room, as long as the house was wide, twenty cubits, both in length and width. He covered it with pure gold, weighing six hundred talents.
2 Chronicles 3:9 The nails weighed fifty shekels of gold, and the upper rooms were covered with gold.
2 Chronicles 3:10 In the holiest place, he made two angels of carved images and covered them with gold.
2 Chronicles 3:11 The cherubim had wings that were twenty cubits long. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the house. The other wing, also five cubits long, touched the wing of the second cherub.
2 Chronicles 3:12 One wing of the second angel was five units long, touching the house wall; and its other wing, also five units long, touched the wing of the first angel.
2 Chronicles 3:13 The cherubim's wings stretched out twenty units long. They stood on their feet with their faces turned inward.
2 Chronicles 3:14 He made a curtain of blue, purple, and red, and fine linen, with angels woven into it.
2 Chronicles 3:15 He also made two pillars in front of the temple, each 35 cubits tall, with a capital on top that was 5 cubits high.
2 Chronicles 3:16 He made chains like those in the holy place and put them on top of the pillars; he also made a hundred pomegranates and attached them to the chains.
2 Chronicles 3:17 He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right side, and the other on the left side; he named the right pillar Jachin and the left pillar Boaz.

2 Chronicles 4:1 He also made a brass altar, 20 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 10 cubits high.
2 Chronicles 4:2 He also made a large, round basin ten cubits wide from edge to edge and five cubits tall. A cord thirty cubits long could wrap around it.
2 Chronicles 4:3 Beneath it there were figures of bulls surrounding it all around: ten per cubit, encircling the basin all around. Two rows of bulls were molded into it when it was made.
2 Chronicles 4:4 It rested on twelve oxen, three faced north, three faced west, three faced south, and three faced east; the sea was placed on top of them, and all their back parts faced inward.
2 Chronicles 4:5 Its thickness was as wide as a hand, and its edge was like the edge of a cup decorated with lily flowers; it could contain three thousand baths.
2 Chronicles 4:6 He also made ten basins and put five on the right side and five on the left for washing: whatever they needed for the burnt offerings, they washed in the basins; however, the large basin was for the priests to wash in.
2 Chronicles 4:7 He made ten gold candlesticks in their shape and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.
2 Chronicles 4:8 He also made ten tables and put them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left. He made a hundred gold bowls.
2 Chronicles 4:9 He also made the courtyard for the priests, a large courtyard, and gates for the courtyard, and he covered the gates with bronze.
2 Chronicles 4:10 He placed the sea at the southeast corner.
2 Chronicles 4:11 Huram made the pots, shovels, and bowls. Huram completed the work he had to do for King Solomon for God's house.
2 Chronicles 4:12 That is, the two pillars, the tops, and the caps on the pillars' tops, and the two networks to cover the two tops of the caps on the pillars.
2 Chronicles 4:13 There were 400 pomegranates on the two garlands, with two rows of pomegranates on each garland to cover the two tops of the capitals on the pillars.
2 Chronicles 4:14 He also made stands and placed washbasins on the stands.
2 Chronicles 4:15 One sea and twelve oxen under it.
2 Chronicles 4:16 Huram, his father, made pots, shovels, meat hooks, and all their tools of polished brass for King Solomon for God’s house.
2 Chronicles 4:17 In the Jordan Valley, the king made them, in the clay soil between Succoth and Zeredathah.
2 Chronicles 4:18 Solomon made many of these items, and the brass was so heavy its weight could not be determined.
2 Chronicles 4:19 Solomon made all the items for God's house, the gold altar, and the tables for the bread on display.
2 Chronicles 4:20 Also, the lampstands with their lamps, to burn as required in front of the inner sanctuary, made of pure gold.
2 Chronicles 4:21 He made the flowers, lamps, and tongs out of gold, and it was pure gold.
2 Chronicles 4:22 The trimmers, bowls, spoons, and incense burners were all made of pure gold. The entrance to the temple, the inside doors to the most sacred place, and the doors of the main temple were gold.

2 Chronicles 5:1 So Solomon finished all the work for God's house. He brought in all the special things his father David had given, including the silver, gold, and tools, and placed them in the storerooms of God's house.
2 Chronicles 5:2 Solomon gathered the senior leaders of Israel, the top officials of the tribes, and the heads of the families of Israel's children in Jerusalem. They came to move God's covenant chest from David’s city, which is Zion.
2 Chronicles 5:3 So all the men of Israel gathered around the king during the festival in the seventh month.
2 Chronicles 5:4 All the leaders of Israel came, and the Levites carried the ark.
2 Chronicles 5:5 They carried the chest and the meeting tent, along with all the sacred objects that were in the tent. The priests and Levites did this.
2 Chronicles 5:6 King Solomon and all of Israel's people gathered around the ark gave so many sheep and oxen as sacrifices that they couldn't be counted.
2 Chronicles 5:7 The priests put the Covenant Box of God in its place, inside the inner sanctuary of the temple, under the wings of the cherubim.
2 Chronicles 5:8 The cherubim spread their wings over the ark's spot, covering the ark and its poles from above.
2 Chronicles 5:9 They pulled the poles of the ark out so that their ends could be seen from the ark in front of the most holy place, but they were not seen from outside. And they are still there today.
2 Chronicles 5:10 In the ark there was only the two stone tablets that Moses placed inside at Horeb, where God made an agreement with the Israelites after they left Egypt.
2 Chronicles 5:11 When the priests left the holy place (all the priests there were made holy and didn't follow their usual order):
2 Chronicles 5:12 The Levite singers, from Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, along with their sons and relatives, dressed in white linen and playing cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps, stood at the east side of the altar, accompanied by 120 priests blowing trumpets.
2 Chronicles 5:13 As the musicians and singers unified to praise and thank God, and when they raised their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, saying, "God is good; his love lasts forever," the temple filled with a cloud, the God's temple.
2 Chronicles 5:14 The priests could not stay and serve because of the cloud, for God's glory filled God's house.

2 Chronicles 6:1 Then Solomon said, "God has stated that he would live in deep darkness."
2 Chronicles 6:2 I have built a house for you to live in, and a place where you can stay forever.
2 Chronicles 6:3 The king turned to the people, blessed everyone in Israel, and they all stood up.
2 Chronicles 6:4 He said, "Praise be to God of Israel, who has with His hands completed what He promised my father David with His words, saying,"
2 Chronicles 6:5 Since the day I led my people out of Egypt, I did not pick any city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house for my name, nor did I choose anyone to be the leader over my people Israel.
2 Chronicles 6:6 I have picked Jerusalem for my name to be there and chosen David to rule my people Israel.
2 Chronicles 6:7 David my father wanted to build a house for the name of God of Israel.
2 Chronicles 6:8 But God told David my father, "Because you wanted to build a house for my name, you did well to have this desire."
2 Chronicles 6:9 Even though you won't build the temple, your son that will be born to you, he will build the temple for my honor.
2 Chronicles 6:10 God has done what he said: for I took my father David's place and became king of Israel, just as God promised, and I built a temple for God's name.
2 Chronicles 6:11 I have placed the chest in it, which contains the agreement God made with the people of Israel.
2 Chronicles 6:12 He stood in front of God's altar with all of Israel's people watching and spread out his hands.
2 Chronicles 6:13 Solomon built a brass platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits tall, and placed it in the center of the courtyard. He stood on it, knelt down on his knees before all of Israel's people, and raised his hands to the sky.
2 Chronicles 6:14 And said, O God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth; you keep your promise and show kindness to your servants who follow you with all their hearts.
2 Chronicles 6:15 You have kept your promise to my father David, what you told him you did by your power, just as it is today.
2 Chronicles 6:16 So now, God of Israel, keep the promise you gave to my father David, telling him, "You will always have a descendant to rule over Israel, if your sons are careful to live by my teachings as you have."
2 Chronicles 6:17 Now then, O God of Israel, let your word come true, which you have spoken to your servant David.
2 Chronicles 6:18 Can God really live with people on Earth? Even the highest heavens cannot hold you, so how can this temple I built be enough?
2 Chronicles 6:19 Please listen to your servant's prayer and his plea for help, my God, and hear the cry and the prayer that your servant is making before you.
2 Chronicles 6:20 Let your eyes always be open and watch this house day and night, where you said you would be honored; listen to the prayers your servant offers toward this place.
2 Chronicles 6:21 Listen to the prayers of your servant and your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from your home in heaven, and when you hear, forgive.
2 Chronicles 6:22 If someone does wrong to another person and has to take an oath, and they take that oath at your altar in this temple;
2 Chronicles 6:23 Listen from heaven, act and judge your servants. Punish the wicked by making them face their own actions and declare the good people right by rewarding them for their goodness.
2 Chronicles 6:24 If the people of Israel are defeated by their enemies because they have sinned against you, and if they turn back, admit your name, pray, and ask for mercy in this temple;
2 Chronicles 6:25 Listen from heaven, forgive Israel's sin, and let them return to the land you gave them and their ancestors.
2 Chronicles 6:26 When the sky closes and there is no rain because they have sinned against you; if they pray towards this place, admit your name, and stop sinning when you make them suffer;
2 Chronicles 6:27 Listen from heaven and forgive the sins of your servants and your people Israel when you have shown them the right path to follow; and give rain to the land you have given to your people as their inheritance.
2 Chronicles 6:28 If there is famine in the land, if there is disease, if there is crop damage, or rot, locusts, or caterpillars; if their enemies surround them in their land's cities; whatever pain or whatever illness there is:
2 Chronicles 6:29 Whenever someone or any of your people Israel knows their own pain and sadness, and they reach out their hands in this place, listen to their prayer and plea.
2 Chronicles 6:30 Listen from heaven, your home, forgive, and treat everyone based on their actions because you know their hearts; only you understand people's hearts.
2 Chronicles 6:31 Let them respect you and follow your paths all their days living in the land you gave our ancestors.
2 Chronicles 6:32 About the foreigner, not from your people Israel, who comes from a distant land because of your great name, powerful hand, and extended arm; if they come and pray in this temple;
2 Chronicles 6:33 Listen from heaven, your home, and do what the foreigner asks of you, so that everyone on earth may know your name and respect you, just like your people Israel, and know that this house I have built is named after you.
2 Chronicles 6:34 If your people go to war against their enemies on the path you send them, and they pray to you facing the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name;
2 Chronicles 6:35 Listen to their prayer and plea from heaven, and uphold their cause.
2 Chronicles 6:36 If they sin against you, (since no one is without sin,) and you become angry with them, and let their enemies defeat them, and their enemies take them as prisoners to a land far away or close by;
2 Chronicles 6:37 But if they realize their wrongs in the country where they are prisoners, and turn back and pray to you in that land, saying, "We have sinned, we have done wrong, and we have acted badly";
2 Chronicles 6:38 If they come back to you with all their heart and soul in the land where they are captives, and pray facing their land that you gave to their ancestors, the city you chose, and the temple I built for your name:
2 Chronicles 6:39 Then listen from heaven, your home, to their prayers and pleas, help them, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
2 Chronicles 6:40 Now, my God, please let your eyes be open and your ears listen to the prayer made here.
2 Chronicles 6:41 Now get up, God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your power. May your priests, God, be dressed in salvation, and let your holy people be happy with goodness.
2 Chronicles 6:42 God, do not turn away from your chosen one; remember the kindness you showed to your servant David.

2 Chronicles 7:1 After Solomon finished praying, fire fell from the sky and burned up the offering and sacrifices; and God's glory filled the temple.
2 Chronicles 7:2 The priests could not go into God's house because God's glory filled it.
2 Chronicles 7:3 When all the Israelites saw the fire come down and God's glory on the temple, they knelt on the ground with their faces down, worshiped, and praised God, saying, "He is good; his love lasts forever."
2 Chronicles 7:4 Then the king and all the people gave sacrifices to God.
2 Chronicles 7:5 King Solomon gave a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep; so he and everyone dedicated God's house.
2 Chronicles 7:6 The priests performed their duties: the Levites played musical instruments made by King David to praise God, for His kindness lasts forever. This happened as David gave praise with their help; the priests blew trumpets in front of them, and all Israel stood up.
2 Chronicles 7:7 Solomon made the center of the courtyard in front of the house of God holy because that is where he made burned offerings and the fat from the offerings for friendship. This was because the bronze altar that Solomon built could not hold all the burned offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat.
2 Chronicles 7:8 Solomon and all Israel celebrated the feast for seven days with a very large crowd, from Hamath to the river of Egypt.
2 Chronicles 7:9 On the eighth day, they held a special meeting because they had celebrated the altar dedication for seven days and the feast for seven days.
2 Chronicles 7:10 On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he let the people go to their tents, happy and cheerful because of the kindness that God had shown to David, Solomon, and to the people of Israel.
2 Chronicles 7:11 Solomon completed God's house and the royal palace. Everything Solomon planned to do in God's house and his own, he successfully did.
2 Chronicles 7:12 God came to Solomon in the night and said, "I have heard your prayer and picked this place for myself as a house of sacrifice."
2 Chronicles 7:13 If I close the sky so no rain falls, or if I order the locusts to eat up the crops, or if I send disease among my people;
2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, who are known by my name, humble themselves, pray, seek me, and turn from their bad ways, then I will listen from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
2 Chronicles 7:15 Now my eyes will be open, and my ears will listen to the prayers made in this place.
2 Chronicles 7:16 I have now chosen and made this house holy, so that my name will always be there; and I will always watch over and care for it deeply.
2 Chronicles 7:17 If you follow me as your father David did, and do everything I have told you, and keep my laws and decisions;
2 Chronicles 7:18 I will secure your kingdom's throne, just as I promised David your father, saying, "You will always have a man to rule over Israel."
2 Chronicles 7:19 But if you turn away and ignore my laws and commands that I have given you, and if you go and serve other gods and worship them;
2 Chronicles 7:20 Then I will pull them out of the land I have given them, and this house I have made holy for my name, I will throw away, and it will become a common saying and a joke among all peoples.
2 Chronicles 7:21 This tall house will amaze everyone who sees it. They will ask, "Why did God do this to the land and to this house?"
2 Chronicles 7:22 The answer will be, "Because they abandoned the God of their ancestors, who led them out of Egypt, and they followed and worshiped other gods, and served them, that is why he has brought all this harm to them."

2 Chronicles 8:1 After twenty years, during which Solomon had built God's house and his own house,
2 Chronicles 8:2 Solomon rebuilt the cities Huram had given back to him and made the Israelites live there.
2 Chronicles 8:3 Solomon went to Hamathzobah and conquered it.
2 Chronicles 8:4 He built Tadmor in the desert and all the supply cities he built in Hamath.
2 Chronicles 8:5 He also built Upper Bethhoron and Lower Bethhoron, protected cities with walls, gates, and bars.
2 Chronicles 8:6 Baalath, and every city Solomon used to store things, and all the chariot cities, and the cities for horsemen, and everything Solomon wanted to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and his entire territory.
2 Chronicles 8:7 As for all the people remaining from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not from Israel,
2 Chronicles 8:8 But Solomon made the children of those who remained in the land, whom the Israelites had not destroyed, pay tribute up to today.
2 Chronicles 8:9 Solomon did not make the Israelites work as servants; they were soldiers, leaders of his officers, and commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
2 Chronicles 8:10 These were the top leaders of King Solomon's staff, numbering two hundred and fifty, who governed the people.
2 Chronicles 8:11 Solomon moved Pharaoh's daughter from David's city to her own house he built for her; he thought, "My wife can't live in King David's house of Israel, because it's holy where God's ark has been."
2 Chronicles 8:12 Solomon gave burnt offerings to God on God's altar, which he built in front of the entrance hall.
2 Chronicles 8:13 They made offerings at a set amount each day, as Moses commanded, on sabbaths, new moons, and special festival times, three times a year - during the festival of unleavened bread, the festival of weeks, and the festival of tabernacles.
2 Chronicles 8:14 He set up, as David his father had ordered, the groups of priests for their work, the Levites for their tasks, to praise and help the priests each day as needed; the gatekeepers also in their groups at every gate, because this is what David, a man of God, had instructed.
2 Chronicles 8:15 They did not ignore the king's orders to the priests and Levites about anything, including the treasures.
2 Chronicles 8:16 All of Solomon's work was ready by the time they laid the foundation of God's house and continued until it was completed. So God's house was finished.
2 Chronicles 8:17 Solomon went to Eziongeber and Eloth by the sea in Edom.
2 Chronicles 8:18 Huram sent ships and skilled sailors through his servants to join Solomon's servants. They sailed to Ophir, got 450 talents of gold, and brought them to King Solomon.

2 Chronicles 9:1 When the queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame, she went to test him with difficult questions in Jerusalem. She brought a large group, camels carrying spices, lots of gold, and valuable gems. When she arrived, she talked with Solomon about everything she was thinking.
2 Chronicles 9:2 Solomon answered all her questions, and he hid nothing from her.
2 Chronicles 9:3 When the queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom and the house he built,
2 Chronicles 9:4 The food on his table, the way his servants sat, how his officials served, and their clothes; also his cupbearers, and their clothes; and the steps he took to go up to God's house; all this left her breathless.
2 Chronicles 9:5 She told the king, "The stories I heard in my country about your achievements and your wisdom are true."
2 Chronicles 9:6 I didn't believe what they said until I came and saw for myself. And truly, they didn't tell me even half of how wise you are; you are even greater than what I heard.
2 Chronicles 9:7 Your men are happy, and your servants who always stand before you and listen to your wisdom are happy.
2 Chronicles 9:8 God blesses you because he was pleased to make you king on his throne, for God's sake: God loved Israel and wanted them to last forever, so he made you their king to bring them fairness and justice.
2 Chronicles 9:9 She gave the king 120 talents of gold, lots of spices, and precious stones. No one had ever given such spices as the Queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
2 Chronicles 9:10 Huram's workers and Solomon's workers, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum trees and precious stones.
2 Chronicles 9:11 The king used the algum trees to make balconies for God's house and the royal palace, and he made harps and stringed instruments for musicians. No one had ever seen anything like them in Judah before.
2 Chronicles 9:12 King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba everything she wanted, beyond what she had brought to the king. Then she went back to her land with her servants.
2 Chronicles 9:13 Every year, Solomon received 666 talents of gold.
2 Chronicles 9:14 Merchants and traders brought things. Also, Arabian kings and regional leaders brought gold and silver to Solomon.
2 Chronicles 9:15 King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; each shield used six hundred pieces of gold.
2 Chronicles 9:16 He made three hundred shields out of hammered gold, using three hundred gold coins for each shield. The king placed them in the Lebanon Forest House.
2 Chronicles 9:17 The king made a big throne out of ivory and covered it with pure gold.
2 Chronicles 9:18 The throne had six steps and a gold footrest attached to it, with armrests on each side of the seat and two lions next to the armrests.
2 Chronicles 9:19 Twelve lions were on each side of the six steps; nothing like this was made in any other kingdom.
2 Chronicles 9:20 All of King Solomon's cups were gold, and all items from the Lebanon forest house were pure gold: none were silver, because silver was not valued in Solomon's time.
2 Chronicles 9:21 The king's ships sailed to Tarshish with Huram's servants. Every three years, the Tarshish ships returned with gold, silver, ivory, monkeys, and peacocks.
2 Chronicles 9:22 King Solomon was richer and wiser than all other kings on earth.
2 Chronicles 9:23 All the kings of the world wanted to meet Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had given him.
2 Chronicles 9:24 They each brought gifts: silver and gold items, clothes, gear, spices, horses, and mules, regularly every year.
2 Chronicles 9:25 Solomon had four thousand spaces for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand riders; he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 9:26 He ruled over all the kings from the river to the land of the Philistines, and up to Egypt's border.
2 Chronicles 9:27 The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar trees as plentiful as the sycamore trees in the low plains.
2 Chronicles 9:28 They brought horses to Solomon from Egypt and from all countries.
2 Chronicles 9:29 The other things Solomon did, from beginning to end, are written in Nathan the prophet's book, in Ahijah the Shilonite's prophecies, and in the visions that Iddo the seer had about Jeroboam son of Nebat, right?
2 Chronicles 9:30 Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
2 Chronicles 9:31 Solomon died and was buried in his father David's city. Then his son Rehoboam became king.

2 Chronicles 10:1 Rehoboam went to Shechem because all the people of Israel had come there to make him king.
2 Chronicles 10:2 When Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who had fled to Egypt to avoid King Solomon, heard this, he came back from Egypt.
2 Chronicles 10:3 They sent for him and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel went and talked to Rehoboam, saying,
2 Chronicles 10:4 Your father made our work very hard. Now please make our hard service and the heavy load your father put on us lighter, and we will work for you.
2 Chronicles 10:5 He told them, "Come back to me in three days." Then the people left.
2 Chronicles 10:6 King Rehoboam asked the elders who had advised his father Solomon, "What is your advice on how I should respond to these people?"
2 Chronicles 10:7 They said to him, "If you are kind to these people, make them happy, and say nice things to them, they will serve you forever."
2 Chronicles 10:8 He ignored the advice from the elders and instead asked the young men who grew up with him and served him for their advice.
2 Chronicles 10:9 He said to them, "What advice do you have so we can reply to these people who have asked me to lighten the hard work my father put on them?"
2 Chronicles 10:10 The young men who grew up with him said to him, "This is how you should reply to the people who told you, 'Your father made our work hard, but you should make it easier for us': You should tell them, 'My little finger will be thicker than my father's waist.'"
2 Chronicles 10:11 While my father gave you a heavy burden, I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
2 Chronicles 10:12 Jeroboam and all the people went to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had ordered, saying, "Come back to me on the third day."
2 Chronicles 10:13 The king spoke to them harshly, and King Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older men.
2 Chronicles 10:14 He replied with the young men's advice, saying, "My father made your work hard, but I will make it harder: my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."
2 Chronicles 10:15 The king did not listen to the people because this was God's plan, to fulfill the words God had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam, son of Nebat.
2 Chronicles 10:16 When all the people of Israel saw that the king wouldn't listen to them, they said to the king, "What part do we have in David? We don't have any share in Jesse's son. Everyone go to your homes, Israel. And David, take care of your own family." So all the people of Israel went to their homes.
2 Chronicles 10:17 The Israelites living in Judah's cities were ruled by Rehoboam.
2 Chronicles 10:18 Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was in charge of collecting taxes, but the people of Israel threw stones at him until he died. However, King Rehoboam quickly got into his chariot to escape to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 10:19 Israel has been against David's family up to today.

2 Chronicles 11:1 When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he assembled 180,000 skilled soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin to battle against Israel and take back his kingdom.
2 Chronicles 11:2 God's message came to Shemaiah, God's man, saying,
2 Chronicles 11:3 Tell Rehoboam, Solomon's son and king of Judah, and all the people in Judah and Benjamin, this message:
2 Chronicles 11:4 God says, "Do not go up to fight against your relatives. Everyone go back home, because I made this happen." And they listened to what God said and stopped their advance against Jeroboam.
2 Chronicles 11:5 Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built cities for protection in Judah.
2 Chronicles 11:6 He built Bethlehem, Etam, and Tekoa.
2 Chronicles 11:7 Bethzur, Shoco, and Adullam.
2 Chronicles 11:8 Gath, Mareshah, and Ziph,
2 Chronicles 11:9 Adoraim, Lachish, and Azekah,
2 Chronicles 11:10 Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and Benjamin, are fortified cities.

2 Chronicles 11:15 He appointed priests for the high places, for the demons, and for the statues of calves he made.
2 Chronicles 11:16 After them, people from all Israel's tribes who decided to seek God went to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the God of their ancestors.
2 Chronicles 11:17 They made the kingdom of Judah stronger and made Rehoboam, Solomon's son, strong for three years: for three years they followed the ways of David and Solomon.
2 Chronicles 11:18 Rehoboam married Mahalath, Jerimoth's daughter and David's granddaughter, and Abihail, Eliab's daughter and Jesse's granddaughter.
2 Chronicles 11:19 She had sons with him; Jeush, Shamariah, and Zaham.
2 Chronicles 11:20 After her, he married Maachah, Absalom's daughter, who gave birth to Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith for him.
2 Chronicles 11:21 Rehoboam loved Maachah, Absalom's daughter, more than all his other wives and concubines. He had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
2 Chronicles 11:22 Rehoboam appointed Abijah, Maachah's son, as the leader over his brothers because he planned to make him king.
2 Chronicles 11:23 He acted wisely, spreading his children across the lands of Judah and Benjamin to every protected city, providing them with plenty of food. And he wanted many wives.

2 Chronicles 12:1 When Rehoboam secured the kingdom and grew strong, he and all Israel abandoned God's law.
2 Chronicles 12:2 In the fifth year of King Rehoboam's reign, Shishak the king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem because they had sinned against God.
2 Chronicles 12:3 With twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen; the crowd with him from Egypt couldn't be counted, including the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
2 Chronicles 12:4 He captured the walled cities belonging to Judah and went to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 12:5 The prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and to the leaders of Judah who had come to Jerusalem because of Shishak. He told them, "God says, 'You have abandoned me, so I have allowed Shishak to take control over you.'"
2 Chronicles 12:6 The leaders of Israel and the king bowed down; they said, God is fair.
2 Chronicles 12:7 When God saw that they were humble, God's message came to Shemaiah, saying, 'They have become humble; so I won't destroy them and will give them some relief; my anger will not fall on Jerusalem through Shishak.'
2 Chronicles 12:8 They will still serve him, so they can learn about serving me and serving the rulers of other lands.
2 Chronicles 12:9 Shishak, the king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem and stole all the treasures from God's house and the king's house. He also took the gold shields that Solomon had made.
2 Chronicles 12:10 King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and gave them to the chief of the guards who watched over the entrance to the king's palace.
2 Chronicles 12:11 When the king went into God's house, the guards took them and brought them back to the guardroom.
2 Chronicles 12:12 When he became humble, God's anger moved away from him so he was not completely destroyed; and in Judah, things improved.
2 Chronicles 12:13 King Rehoboam got stronger in Jerusalem and ruled. Rehoboam was 41 when he started to rule, and he ruled for 17 years in Jerusalem, the city that God picked from all the Israel tribes to place his name. His mother was Naamah, from Ammon.
2 Chronicles 12:14 He did wrong because he did not prepare his heart to seek God.
2 Chronicles 12:15 The things Rehoboam did, from beginning to end, are recorded in the writings of the prophet Shemaiah and the historian Iddo, which include family records, right? And Rehoboam and Jeroboam were always fighting wars against each other.
2 Chronicles 12:16 Rehoboam died and was buried in David's city, and his son Abijah became king after him.

2 Chronicles 13:1 Abijah began to rule over Judah in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam's reign.
2 Chronicles 13:2 He ruled for three years in Jerusalem. His mother was Michaiah, Uriel of Gibeah's daughter. Abijah and Jeroboam were at war.
2 Chronicles 13:3 Abijah organized his army with four hundred thousand brave soldiers, and Jeroboam arranged his army against him with eight hundred thousand strong warriors.
2 Chronicles 13:4 Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the region of Ephraim and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam, and all of Israel."
2 Chronicles 13:5 Shouldn't you know that God gave David and his descendants the rule over Israel forever through a salt covenant?
2 Chronicles 13:6 Jeroboam, Nebat's son, who served Solomon, David's son, has risen and rebelled against his master.
2 Chronicles 13:7 A group of worthless men, followers of wickedness, joined him. They stood against Rehoboam, Solomon's son, while he was young and gentle, and he couldn't stand up to them.
2 Chronicles 13:8 Now you believe you can resist God’s kingdom under David's sons' control; you are many, and you have golden calves, which Jeroboam created as your gods.
2 Chronicles 13:9 Haven't you thrown out God's priests, Aaron's descendants, and the Levites, and chosen your own priests like other countries do? So now anyone who comes with a young bull and seven rams can become a priest of false gods.
2 Chronicles 13:10 But for us, God is our God, and we haven't left him; the priests who serve God are Aaron's sons, and the Levites do their work.
2 Chronicles 13:11 Every morning and evening, they burn burnt offerings and sweet incense to God. They also arrange the bread on the clean table and light the gold lampstand with its lamps in the evening. We follow God's commands, but you have abandoned Him.
2 Chronicles 13:12 Look, God is with us as our leader, and his priests with trumpets will sound the alarm against you. Children of Israel, do not fight against the God of your ancestors; you will not succeed.
2 Chronicles 13:13 Jeroboam set up an ambush behind them, so they faced Judah with the ambush behind them.
2 Chronicles 13:14 When Judah turned around, they saw the battle was in front and behind them. They cried out to God, and the priests blew the trumpets.
2 Chronicles 13:15 The men of Judah shouted, and as they shouted, God defeated Jeroboam and all Israel in front of Abijah and Judah.
2 Chronicles 13:16 The Israelites ran away from Judah, and God let Judah capture them.
2 Chronicles 13:17 Abijah and his army defeated them heavily: so five hundred thousand of Israel's best men were killed.
2 Chronicles 13:18 At that time, the Israelites were defeated, while the people of Judah were victorious because they trusted in God, the God of their ancestors.
2 Chronicles 13:19 Abijah chased Jeroboam and captured his cities: Bethel and its villages, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephraim and its villages.
2 Chronicles 13:20 Jeroboam did not regain power during Abijah's time; God struck him down, and he died.
2 Chronicles 13:21 Abijah became powerful, married fourteen women, had twenty-two sons, and sixteen daughters.
2 Chronicles 13:22 The other things Abijah did, his actions, and his words, are in the prophet Iddo's history book.

2 Chronicles 14:1 Abijah died, and they buried him in the city of David. His son Asa became king after him. During his time, the land was peaceful for ten years.
2 Chronicles 14:2 And Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of God.
2 Chronicles 14:3 He removed the altars of the foreign gods, the high places, broke the statues, and chopped down the sacred trees.
2 Chronicles 14:4 He told Judah to look for the God of their ancestors and to follow the law and the command.
2 Chronicles 14:5 He removed the worship sites and idols from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom was peaceful under his rule.
2 Chronicles 14:6 He built protected cities in Judah because the land was at peace and there was no war during those years; God had given him peace.
2 Chronicles 14:7 So he told Judah, "Let's build these cities and protect them with walls, towers, gates, and bars while we still have open land; because we have looked for God's help and found it, and he has given us peace all around." And they built and were successful.
2 Chronicles 14:8 Asa had an army with 300,000 men from Judah who carried large shields and spears, and from Benjamin, 280,000 men who carried small shields and used bows. All these were strong and brave warriors.
2 Chronicles 14:9 Zerah the Ethiopian came against them with an army of a million and three hundred chariots, and advanced to Mareshah.
2 Chronicles 14:10 Then Asa fought against him, and they arranged their armies for battle in Zephathah Valley near Mareshah.
2 Chronicles 14:11 Asa called out to God, saying, "God, it's easy for you to help, whether we have many people or just a few who are weak. Help us, God; we rely on you, and in your name, we face this large group. You are our God; don't let anyone defeat you."
2 Chronicles 14:12 God struck down the Ethiopians in front of Asa and Judah, and the Ethiopians ran away.
2 Chronicles 14:13 Asa and his followers chased them to Gerar, and the Ethiopians were beaten so badly they couldn't fight back; because they were defeated by God and his army, and Asa and his people took a lot of their things.
2 Chronicles 14:14 They attacked all the cities near Gerar because they were afraid of God, and they robbed all the cities, as there was a lot to take.
2 Chronicles 14:15 They also attacked the animal tents, took many sheep and camels, and went back to Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles 15:1 God's Spirit came to Azariah, Oded's son.
2 Chronicles 15:2 He went to meet Asa and said, "Listen to me, Asa, and all of Judah and Benjamin: God is with you when you are with Him. If you look for Him, you will find Him; but if you leave Him, He will leave you."
2 Chronicles 15:3 Israel has been a long time without the real God, without a priest to teach, and without law.
2 Chronicles 15:4 But when they were in trouble and turned to God, and looked for him, they found him.
2 Chronicles 15:5 During those times, people had no peace whether they left or arrived, as everyone living in the countries faced great troubles.
2 Chronicles 15:6 One nation destroyed another, and one city destroyed another; for God troubled them with all kinds of problems.
2 Chronicles 15:7 Stay strong, and don't let your hands get weak: your work will be rewarded.
2 Chronicles 15:8 When Asa heard these words and Oded the prophet's message, he felt brave. He removed the terrible idols from all over Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities he had captured in the hills of Ephraim. He also fixed God's altar in front of God's temple entrance.
2 Chronicles 15:9 He brought together all of Judah and Benjamin, and the foreigners from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, because many from Israel joined him when they saw that God was with him.

2 Chronicles 15:17 But the worship places on the hills were not removed from Israel; still, Asa was completely devoted to God all his life.
2 Chronicles 15:18 He brought into God's house the items his father and he had dedicated: silver, gold, and containers.

2 Chronicles 16:3 We have an agreement, just like our fathers did. Look, I've sent you silver and gold. Now, end your agreement with Baasha, the king of Israel, so he will leave me alone.
2 Chronicles 16:4 Benhadad listened to King Asa and ordered his army leaders to attack Israel's cities; they captured Ijon, Dan, Abelmaim, and all the warehouse cities of Naphtali.

2 Chronicles 16:9 God's eyes move across the whole earth, to show his power to those who are fully committed to him. But you have acted foolishly, and from now on you will face wars.

2 Chronicles 16:11 Look, the deeds of Asa, from beginning to end, are recorded in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
2 Chronicles 16:12 In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, Asa became very sick in his feet, and his sickness got very severe. But even in his sickness, he did not ask God for help, only the doctors.
2 Chronicles 16:13 Asa died after ruling for forty-one years and was buried with his ancestors.
2 Chronicles 16:14 They buried him in his own tomb that he had built for himself in the city of David. They placed him on a bed filled with sweet smells and many spices made by the apothecaries. They had a very big fire for him.

2 Chronicles 18:1 Jehoshaphat was very rich and honored, and he allied with Ahab.
2 Chronicles 18:2 After some years, he visited Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered many sheep and cattle for him and his companions and convinced him to join him in going to Ramothgilead.
2 Chronicles 18:3 King Ahab of Israel said to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, "Will you come with me to fight at Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat replied, "I am with you as you are, my people are as your people, and we will join you in battle."
2 Chronicles 18:4 Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please ask for God's guidance today."
2 Chronicles 18:5 So the king of Israel brought together 400 prophets and asked them, "Should we go to war against Ramothgilead, or should I hold back?" And they answered, "Go ahead, because God will give it into the king's hands."
2 Chronicles 18:6 But Jehoshaphat asked, "Isn't there a prophet of God here we can ask?"
2 Chronicles 18:7 The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man we can ask God through. But I hate him because he never prophesies anything good about me, only bad. He is Micaiah, son of Imla." Jehoshaphat replied, "The king should not say that."
2 Chronicles 18:8 The king of Israel called one of his officers and said, "Go fast and bring Micaiah, son of Imla."
2 Chronicles 18:9 The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, sat on their thrones, dressed in royal robes, at the entrance of Samaria's gate in an open area; and all the prophets were giving their prophecies in front of them.
2 Chronicles 18:10 Zedekiah, Chenaanah's son, made iron horns and said, "God says, 'With these, you will drive out Syria until they are destroyed.'"
2 Chronicles 18:11 All the prophets said the same thing: "Go to Ramothgilead and you will succeed because God will give it to the king."
2 Chronicles 18:12 The messenger who went to get Micaiah said to him, "Look, all the prophets are telling the king good news unanimously; so please make your words like theirs and speak good things."
2 Chronicles 18:13 Micaiah said, "As God lives, I will speak only what my God says."
2 Chronicles 18:14 When he arrived, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we go to fight at Ramothgilead or not?" And he answered, "Go, succeed, and you will conquer them."
2 Chronicles 18:15 The king said to him, "How many times must I tell you to speak only the truth to me in God's name?"
2 Chronicles 18:16 He said, "I saw all Israel spread out on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. God said, 'These people have no leader; let them go back home in peace.'"
2 Chronicles 18:17 The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you he would not predict good things for me, but only bad?"
2 Chronicles 18:18 He said again, "Listen to God's message: I saw God sitting on His throne, with all the heavenly beings standing to His right and left."
2 Chronicles 18:19 God asked, "Who will trick King Ahab of Israel into attacking Ramothgilead and dying there?" One suggested this way, and another that way.
2 Chronicles 18:20 A spirit came out and stood before God and said, "I will trick him." And God asked, "How?"
2 Chronicles 18:21 He said, "I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets." God said, "You will trick him, and you will succeed: go out and do it."
2 Chronicles 18:22 Now, look, God has made your prophets lie, and God has said bad things will happen to you.
2 Chronicles 18:23 Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, came forward, hit Micaiah on the face, and asked, "How did God's Spirit leave me to talk to you?"
2 Chronicles 18:24 Micaiah said, "Look, you will see on that day when you go into a room to hide."
2 Chronicles 18:25 The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah, and take him back to Amon, the city governor, and to Joash, the king's son."
2 Chronicles 18:26 Tell them, "The king says, 'Put this man in jail and give him only enough bread and water to make him suffer until I come back safely.'"
2 Chronicles 18:27 Micaiah said, "If you really come back safely, then God did not speak through me." And he said, "Listen, everyone."
2 Chronicles 18:28 The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, went to Ramoth-gilead.
2 Chronicles 18:29 The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "I will change my look and go to battle, but you wear your royal clothes." So the king of Israel changed his look, and they went to battle.
2 Chronicles 18:30 The king of Syria told his chariot commanders to not fight with anyone, whether they are unimportant or important, except for the king of Israel.
2 Chronicles 18:31 When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought he was the king of Israel. So they surrounded him to attack. But Jehoshaphat yelled, and God helped him, making them leave him alone.
2 Chronicles 18:32 It happened that when the chariot commanders realized it was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.
2 Chronicles 18:33 A man randomly shot an arrow and hit the king of Israel in the gaps of his armor. So the king told his chariot driver, "Turn around and take me out of the battle; I've been hurt."
2 Chronicles 18:34 The fight grew stronger that day, but the Israelite king stood in his chariot facing the Syrians till evening, and at sunset, he died.

2 Chronicles 19:1 King Jehoshaphat of Judah went back to his home in Jerusalem safely.

2 Chronicles 20:7 Aren't you our God, who drove out the people of this land before your people Israel and gave it forever to the descendants of Abraham, your friend?

2 Chronicles 20:16 Tomorrow, go down to fight them. They will climb up by the cliff of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the stream, before the desert of Jeruel.
2 Chronicles 20:17 You don't have to fight in this battle. Just take your positions, stand firm, and watch God save you, Judah and Jerusalem. Don't be afraid or worried. Tomorrow, go face them, because God will be with you.
