Ezra 2:63 The governor told them not to eat the most holy food until a priest with the Urim and Thummim came.
Ezra 2:64 The whole group together was 42,360.
Ezra 2:65 In addition to their servants and maids, who numbered 7,337, there were also 200 men and women who were singers.
Ezra 2:66 They had 736 horses and 245 mules.
Ezra 2:67 They had 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
Ezra 2:68 Some family leaders, when they arrived at God's house in Jerusalem, willingly gave for God's house to rebuild it on its site.
Ezra 2:69 They contributed as much as they could to the project's fund: 61,000 gold coins, 5,000 pounds of silver, and 100 priests' robes.
Ezra 2:70 The priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants lived in their towns, and all the people of Israel lived in their towns.

Ezra 3:1 When the seventh month arrived and the Israelites were in their towns, they all came together in Jerusalem as if they were one person.
Ezra 3:2 Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, stood up and built the altar of the God of Israel to make burnt offerings on it, as the law of Moses, the man of God, says.
Ezra 3:3 They placed the altar on its stands because they were afraid of the people living nearby. They made burnt offerings to God there, both in the morning and in the evening.
Ezra 3:4 They also celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles according to what is written, and they gave the daily burnt offerings in the right amount, following the usual practice for each day's requirement.
Ezra 3:5 Later, they gave the regular burnt offerings for each new moon and for all of God's holy festivals, as well as for anyone who wanted to give a special voluntary offering to God.
Ezra 3:6 From the first day of the seventh month, they started to give burnt offerings to God. But the base of God's temple was not laid yet.
Ezra 3:7 They also paid the builders and woodworkers; and provided food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, so they would bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, as allowed by the decree from Cyrus, king of Persia.
Ezra 3:8 In the second year after they arrived at God's house in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel, Shealtiel's son, and Jeshua, Jozadak's son, began along with the other priests, Levites, and all who had returned from being captives to Jerusalem. They assigned the Levites, aged twenty and older, to start working on God's house.
Ezra 3:9 Jeshua stood with his sons and brothers, Kadmiel with his sons, and the men of Judah to help the workers in God's house; Henadad's sons and their sons and brothers, the Levites, did the same.
Ezra 3:10 When the workers set the foundation of God's temple, they had the priests in their clothes with trumpets and the Levites, Asaph's sons, with cymbals praising God, following King David of Israel's rule.
Ezra 3:11 They sang one by one to praise and thank God because He is good and His love for Israel lasts forever. All the people yelled loudly when they praised God because the foundation of God's house was built.
Ezra 3:12 But many priests, Levites, and family leaders, who were old and had seen the first temple, cried loudly when they saw the foundation of this new temple; while many others shouted with joy.
Ezra 3:13 The people couldn't tell the joyful shouting from the crying because they shouted so loudly, and the sound was heard far away.

Ezra 4:1 When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin found out that the exiles were building a temple for the God of Israel;
Ezra 4:2 Then they approached Zerubbabel and the leaders, and proposed to them, "Let us help you build, because we follow your God just as you do, and we have been offering sacrifices to Him since the time King Esarhaddon of Assyria settled us here."
Ezra 4:3 But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other leaders of Israel told them, "You can't help us build a house for our God. We alone will build it for the God of Israel, as King Cyrus of Persia has told us to do."
Ezra 4:4 The local people discouraged the people of Judah and made it hard for them to build.
Ezra 4:5 They paid advisors to work against them and disrupt their plans during the time Cyrus was king of Persia, up until Darius became king of Persia.
Ezra 4:6 During King Ahasuerus's early rule, they sent him a letter accusing the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
Ezra 4:7 During Artaxerxes' reign, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their associates wrote to King Artaxerxes of Persia. The letter was written and translated in the Syrian language.
Ezra 4:8 Rehum the official and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter about Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes like this:
Ezra 4:9 Rehum the leader and Shimshai the writer, along with their friends, the people from Dina, Apharsathch, Tarpel, Aphars, Archev, Babylon, Susa, Deha, and Elam, all wrote a letter.
Ezra 4:10 And the other nations that the great and important Asnapper moved, and put in the cities of Samaria, and the others near the river, and then.
Ezra 4:11 Here is the letter that they sent to King Artaxerxes: "Your servants, the people near the river, send greetings.
Ezra 4:12 Let the king know that the Jews who left you to come to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that troublesome and wicked city, setting up its walls, and fixing its foundations.
Ezra 4:13 Let the king know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, then they won't pay taxes, fees, or duties, and this will harm the income of the kings.
Ezra 4:14 Since we get our support from the king and it is not right for us to watch the king be dishonored, we have told the king about this.
Ezra 4:15 Look in your ancestors' record book, so you'll find out this city has always been troublesome to rulers and regions, promoting rebellion in the past, which is why it was destroyed.
Ezra 4:16 We tell the king that if this city and its walls are rebuilt, then you will have no control in this area across the river.
Ezra 4:17 The king sent a reply to Rehum the chancellor, Shimshai the scribe, and their friends in Samaria, and to others across the river: "Peace, and for now."
Ezra 4:18 The letter you sent us was clearly read to me.
Ezra 4:19 I ordered a search, and it was found that this city has a history of rebelling against kings, and of revolts and unrest.
Ezra 4:20 Powerful kings have ruled over Jerusalem too, controlling lands across the river; people paid them tolls, taxes, and fees.
Ezra 4:21 Tell them to stop these people and not to build this city until I give another order.
Ezra 4:22 Be careful now to do this so you don't fail: why let harm increase to hurt the kings?
Ezra 4:23 When Rehum, Shimshai the secretary, and their friends heard the letter from King Artaxerxes, they quickly went to Jerusalem to the Jews and forced them to stop working.
Ezra 4:24 Work on God's house in Jerusalem stopped and did not resume until the second year of King Darius of Persia's rule.

Ezra 5:1 The prophets Haggai and Zechariah, son of Iddo, spoke God's message to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem.
Ezra 5:2 Zerubbabel, Shealtiel's son, and Jeshua, Jozadak's son, stood up and started building God's house in Jerusalem. God's prophets were also there, helping them.
Ezra 5:3 At that time, Tatnai, the governor of the region across the river, Shetharboznai, and their associates came to them and asked, "Who gave you permission to build this temple and finish this wall?"
Ezra 5:4 We asked them, "What are the names of the men building this?"
Ezra 5:5 God watched over the Jewish leaders, so no one could stop them until the issue reached Darius. Then they sent a written reply about this.
Ezra 5:6 This is the letter that Tatnai, the governor across the river, Shetharboznai, and their associates, the Apharsachites who were also across the river, sent to King Darius:
Ezra 5:7 They sent him a letter that said: To King Darius, all peace.
Ezra 5:8 We want the king to know that we went to Judea, to the big temple of God. It is made with large stones, and wood is put into the walls. The work is moving quickly and going well.
Ezra 5:9 We asked the elders, "Who told you to build this temple and these walls?"
Ezra 5:10 We also asked for their names to tell you, so we could write down the names of their leaders.
Ezra 5:11 They replied to us, saying, "We serve the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel constructed and established."
Ezra 5:12 But after our ancestors made the God of heaven angry, he let Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon and a Chaldean, defeat them. He destroyed this place and took the people to Babylon.
Ezra 5:13 In the first year of Cyrus, the king of Babylon, King Cyrus ordered that God's house be rebuilt.
Ezra 5:14 The gold and silver items from God's house, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Jerusalem temple to the Babylon temple, were taken by King Cyrus from the Babylon temple. He gave them to Sheshbazzar, the governor he appointed.
Ezra 5:15 God said to him, "Take these items, go, bring them to the temple in Jerusalem, and rebuild God's house where it was."
Ezra 5:16 Sheshbazzar came and started the foundation of God's house in Jerusalem. It has been under construction from then until now, and it's still not finished.
Ezra 5:17 So now, if the king agrees, let someone look in the king's treasury in Babylon to see if King Cyrus made a decree to rebuild God's house in Jerusalem, and let the king tell us what he decides about this.

Ezra 6:1 King Darius gave an order, and they searched the records where the Babylon treasures were stored.
Ezra 6:2 They found a scroll at Achmetha, in the palace in the Medes' region, with this written record:
Ezra 6:3 In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus ordered that God's house in Jerusalem be rebuilt. This is where sacrifices were made. The foundation must be strong. It should be 60 cubits high and 60 cubits wide.
Ezra 6:4 Use three layers of large stones and one layer of fresh wood, and let the cost be covered by the king's funds.
Ezra 6:5 Also, return the gold and silver dishes from God's house, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, and bring them back to the temple in Jerusalem, each to its spot, and put them in God's house.
Ezra 6:6 So now, Tatnai, governor across the river, Shetharboznai, and your fellow officials, the Apharsachites, who are across the river, stay away from there.
Ezra 6:7 Do not interfere with the work on God's house; let the Jewish leader and the Jewish elders rebuild God's house where it stands.
Ezra 6:8 I also make a rule about what you should do for the Jewish leaders who are rebuilding God's house: give them what they need from the king's wealth, including taxes from across the river, so they can keep working without delay.
Ezra 6:9 They need young bulls, rams, lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, also wheat, salt, wine, and oil, as the priests in Jerusalem require. Give these to them every day without fail.
Ezra 6:10 So they may give sweet-smelling sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the king's and his sons' lives.
Ezra 6:11 I have also ordered that if anyone changes this command, wood should be torn from their house and they should be hanged on it, and their house should be turned into a pile of rubbish for this.
Ezra 6:12 God, who has chosen to be honored there, will destroy any kings or nations that try to change or ruin this temple in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have ordered this; let it be done quickly.
Ezra 6:13 Then Tatnai, the governor across the river, Shetharboznai, and their friends did quickly what King Darius had ordered.
Ezra 6:14 The Jewish elders built and succeeded because of the words of the prophet Haggai and Zechariah, Iddo's son. They finished building as God of Israel and kings Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes of Persia had ordered.
Ezra 6:15 This house was completed on the third day of the month Adar, during the sixth year of King Darius's rule.
Ezra 6:16 The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the other people who had been taken captive celebrated the dedication of God's house happily.
Ezra 6:17 At the dedication of God's house, they gave a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs as offerings; and for the sin offering for all Israel, they gave twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel.
Ezra 6:18 They organized the priests into their groups and the Levites into their duties for serving God in Jerusalem, according to what is written in Moses' book.
Ezra 6:19 The exiles celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Ezra 6:20 The priests and Levites had all purified themselves and were clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for the exiles, their fellow priests, and for themselves.
Ezra 6:21 The Israelites who returned from being captives and all who left the pagan ways of the land to seek God, ate.
Ezra 6:22 They celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with happiness because God had filled them with joy and made the king of Assyria favorable to them, helping them in the work of God's house, the God of Israel.

Ezra 7:1 After these events, during King Artaxerxes' rule of Persia, Ezra, who was Seraiah's son, Azariah's grandson, and Hilkiah's great-grandson,
Ezra 7:2 The son of Shallum was Zadok's son, and Zadok was Ahitub's son.
Ezra 7:3 He was Amariah's son, Azariah's grandson, and Meraioth's great-grandson.
Ezra 7:4 Zerahiah's son, Uzzi's son, Bukki's son,
Ezra 7:5 Abishua's son, Phinehas's son, Eleazar's son, Aaron the high priest's son.
Ezra 7:6 Ezra left Babylon; he was a skilled writer in Moses' law, which God of Israel had given. The king gave him everything he asked for because God's favor was with him.
Ezra 7:7 Some Israelites, priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and Nethinim went up to Jerusalem in King Artaxerxes' seventh year.
Ezra 7:8 He arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king's rule.
Ezra 7:9 He started to leave Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month because God was helping him.
Ezra 7:10 Ezra had made up his mind to study God's law, follow it, and teach God's rules and decisions in Israel.
Ezra 7:11 This is the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and scribe, who writes down God's commands and laws for Israel.
Ezra 7:12 King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest, a writer skilled in the law of God in heaven, wishes perfect peace.
Ezra 7:13 I issue an order that all Israelites, priests, and Levites in my kingdom who want to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
Ezra 7:14 Since the king and his seven advisors sent you to find out about Judah and Jerusalem according to your God's law that you have with you;
Ezra 7:15 To bring the silver and gold, which the king and his advisors have willingly given to the God of Israel, who lives in Jerusalem.
Ezra 7:16 Take all the silver and gold you can find in the whole Babylon area, along with the voluntary gifts from the people and priests given freely for their God's temple in Jerusalem.
Ezra 7:17 Use this money to quickly buy bulls, rams, lambs, their grain offerings, and their drink offerings, and sacrifice them on the altar of God's house in Jerusalem.
Ezra 7:18 Do whatever you and your brothers think is best with the remaining silver and gold, according to God's will.
Ezra 7:19 Give the tools provided for the work of your God's house to God in Jerusalem.
Ezra 7:20 Whatever else you need for God's house, give it from the king's treasury.
Ezra 7:21 I, King Artaxerxes, order all the treasurers across the river to quickly do whatever Ezra the priest, who knows God's law, asks of you.
Ezra 7:22 To a hundred talents of silver, a hundred measures of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil, and as much salt as needed.
Ezra 7:23 Do whatever the God of heaven has ordered, carefully and for the good of the God of heaven's temple. Why should anger come upon the king's kingdom and his children?
Ezra 7:24 We also tell you that no taxes, payments, or fees should be put on the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or workers of God's house.
Ezra 7:25 Ezra, use the wisdom of God you have to appoint officials and judges who can rule over the people across the river, all who know God's laws; and teach the laws to those who don't know them.
Ezra 7:26 Anyone who does not follow God's law or the king's law should be punished quickly, whether by death, exile, taking their possessions, or putting them in jail.
Ezra 7:27 May God, the God of our ancestors, be praised for inspiring the king to make the temple in Jerusalem beautiful.
Ezra 7:28 God has shown me mercy in front of the king, his advisors, and all the powerful nobles. I felt strong because God was with me, and I brought together leaders from Israel to go with me.

Ezra 8:1 These are the leaders of their families, and this is the family history of those who came with me from Babylon during King Artaxerxes's rule.
Ezra 8:2 From Phinehas' sons came Gershom; from Ithamar's sons, Daniel; from David's sons, Hattush.
Ezra 8:3 From Shechaniah's family, from Pharosh's descendants, came Zechariah; with him, they counted 150 men on the family list.
Ezra 8:4 From the descendants of Pahathmoab, Elihoenai, son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
Ezra 8:5 Shechaniah's family included Jahaziel's son and three hundred other men.
Ezra 8:6 From Adin's descendants, Ebed, Jonathan's son, came with 50 men.
Ezra 8:7 From the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah came with seventy men.
Ezra 8:8 From the family of Shephatiah, there was Zebadiah, Michael's son, with 80 men.
Ezra 8:9 Joab's descendant Obadiah, Jehiel's son, was with two hundred and eighteen men.
Ezra 8:10 From Shelomith's descendants was Josiphiah's son, with 160 men.
Ezra 8:11 From the descendants of Bebai: Zechariah, Bebai's son, and with him 28 men.
Ezra 8:12 From Azgad's descendants, Johanan son of Hakkatan came, along with one hundred and ten men.
Ezra 8:13 From the last sons of Adonikam, named Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, came sixty men.
Ezra 8:14 From Bigvai's descendants came Uthai and Zabbud, along with seventy other men.
Ezra 8:15 I brought them to the river that flows to Ahava; we camped there for three days. I looked over the people and the priests, but there were no Levites among them.
Ezra 8:16 I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, who were leaders, as well as Joiarib and Elnathan, who were wise men.
Ezra 8:17 I gave orders for them to go to Iddo, the leader in Casiphia, and told them what to say to Iddo and his fellow Nethinims there, to bring us helpers for the house of our God.
Ezra 8:18 With God's good help, they brought us a wise man from the descendants of Mahli, who was Levi's son from Israel's family; and Sherebiah, along with his sons and brothers, totaling eighteen.
Ezra 8:19 Hashabiah, along with Jeshaiah from Merari's descendants, his brothers and their children, were twenty in total.
Ezra 8:20 David and the leaders had assigned 220 Nethinims to help the Levites; each one was listed by name.
Ezra 8:21 I announced a fast by the Ahava River to humble ourselves before God, to ask for a safe journey for us, our children, and all our possessions.
Ezra 8:22 I was embarrassed to ask the king for soldiers and cavalry to protect us from enemies on the journey, because we had told the king, "God's favor is with all who seek Him, but His strength and anger are against those who abandon Him."
Ezra 8:23 We fasted and asked God for this, and he listened to us.
Ezra 8:24 I chose twelve of the leading priests, Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten other priests with them.
Ezra 8:25 He gave them the silver, the gold, and the items, including the gifts for our God's house that the king, his advisors, his nobles, and all the Israelites there had given.
Ezra 8:26 I gave them 650 talents of silver, silver items worth 100 talents, and 100 talents of gold.
Ezra 8:27 Also twenty bowls of gold, weighing a thousand coins, and two fine copper containers, as valuable as gold.
Ezra 8:28 I told them, "You are special to God; the utensils are special too; and the silver and gold are gifts freely given to God, the God of your ancestors."
Ezra 8:29 Stay alert and guard them until you weigh them in front of the priests, the Levites, and the leaders of the Israeli families in Jerusalem, inside the rooms of God's house.
Ezra 8:30 The priests and Levites took the silver, gold, and items to take them to God's house in Jerusalem.
Ezra 8:31 We left from the Ahava River on the twelfth day of the first month, to go to Jerusalem. God's help was with us, and he protected us from enemies and ambushes along the road.
Ezra 8:32 We arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.
Ezra 8:33 On the fourth day, they weighed the silver, gold, and containers in God's house. Meremoth, Uriah's son and priest, did this. Eleazar, Phinehas' son, Jozabad, Jeshua's son, and Noadiah, Binnui's son, who were Levites, were with him.
Ezra 8:34 Each item was counted and weighed, and the weights were recorded then.
Ezra 8:35 The children of the exiles who had returned from captivity gave burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All these were burnt offerings to God.
Ezra 8:36 They gave the king's orders to the king's officers and the rulers on this side of the river. They helped the people and God's house.

Ezra 9:1 After these events, the leaders approached me and reported, "The people of Israel, including the priests and the Levites, have not kept away from the local peoples and their detestable practices, like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites."
Ezra 9:2 They have married women from those nations for themselves and their sons, mixing the sacred race with the local people. Indeed, the leaders and officials have led this wrongdoing.
Ezra 9:3 When I heard this, I tore my clothes and my cloak, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat down shocked.
Ezra 9:4 Everyone who was afraid of God's words because of the wrongdoings of the exiles gathered around me, and I sat shocked until the evening offering.
Ezra 9:5 During the evening offering, I got up from feeling sad; I tore my clothes and my cloak, got down on my knees, and stretched out my hands to God.
Ezra 9:6 I said, "Oh my God, I am so ashamed and embarrassed to look up to you, my God, because our wrongs pile up high, and our sins reach up to the sky."
Ezra 9:7 Since our ancestors' time, we have been greatly sinful up to today; because of our wrongs, we, our rulers, and our priests, have been handed over to the rulers of other lands. We have faced war, captivity, robbery, and shame, just like today.
Ezra 9:8 And now, for a short time, God has shown us grace by allowing some of us to survive, and by giving us a secure place in his sanctuary so that he can brighten our eyes and give us some relief while we are enslaved.
Ezra 9:9 We were slaves, but our God did not abandon us in our slavery. Instead, He showed us kindness by making the kings of Persia look favorably on us. This allowed us to revive, rebuild our God's temple, fix its ruins, and give us protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
Ezra 9:10 And now, our God, what can we say? We have ignored your commands.
Ezra 9:11 God ordered through his prophets that the land you are going to take over is dirty because of the land's people and their disgusting actions. They have made it completely unclean from one end to the other.
Ezra 9:12 So do not let your daughters marry their sons, do not take their daughters for your sons, and do not seek friendship or wealth from them ever, so that you may be strong, enjoy the land's goodness, and pass it down to your children forever.
Ezra 9:13 Even after all our bad actions and serious wrongs, knowing that you, our God, have punished us less than our sins deserve, and have provided us with this rescue.
Ezra 9:14 If we break your commands again and become friendly with the people doing these wrong things, wouldn't you be angry with us until you destroyed us all, leaving no one left or any way to escape?
Ezra 9:15 God of Israel, you are good: we are still here, safe today; we stand before you with our wrongs: we cannot face you because of them.

Ezra 10:1 After Ezra prayed and confessed, crying and falling down in front of God's house, a large crowd of men, women, and children from Israel gathered around him because they were all crying a lot.
Ezra 10:2 Shechaniah, son of Jehiel and from Elam's family, spoke to Ezra, "We have sinned against God by marrying foreign women from this land, but there is still hope for Israel in this matter."
Ezra 10:3 So now, let's make an agreement with God to send away all the foreign wives and their children, based on the advice of my lord and those who respect God's commands; and we'll follow the law in doing this.
Ezra 10:4 Get up; this task is yours to do: we will be with you: be brave and go ahead.
Ezra 10:5 Then Ezra stood up and had the lead priests, the Levites, and all Israel promise to do as he said. And they promised.
Ezra 10:6 Ezra got up from in front of God's house and went into Johanan son of Eliashib's room. There, he didn't eat bread or drink water because he was sad about the sins of the people who were taken away.
Ezra 10:7 They announced throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the exiles that they should come together in Jerusalem.
Ezra 10:8 Anyone who did not come within three days, as the leaders and elders advised, would lose all their belongings and be cut off from the group that had been taken away.
Ezra 10:9 All the men from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem in three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day; and everyone sat in the street by God's house, shaking because of the issue and the heavy rain.
Ezra 10:10 Priest Ezra stood up and said to them, "You have done wrong by marrying foreign women, adding to Israel's guilt."
Ezra 10:11 Now, say sorry to God, the God of your ancestors, and do what makes him happy. Stay away from the local people and from the foreign wives.
Ezra 10:12 Then the whole group replied loudly, "We will do as you have said."
Ezra 10:13 There are many people, and it's raining a lot, so we can't stay outside, and we can't finish this job in one or two days because many of us have done wrong in this matter.
Ezra 10:14 Let our leaders and everyone who married foreign women in our towns meet at set times, along with the elders and judges of each town, until God's strong anger about this is calmed.
Ezra 10:15 Jonathan, son of Asahel, and Jahaziah, son of Tikvah, worked on this issue, with Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite assisting them.
Ezra 10:16 The captives' children did this. Ezra, the priest, with some leaders of the families, grouped by their ancestors' families and each by name, set apart and started to look into the matter on the first day of the tenth month.
Ezra 10:17 They finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
Ezra 10:18 Some priests' sons had married foreign women, including Jeshua's descendants—Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
Ezra 10:19 They promised to send away their wives and, admitting their guilt, they brought a sheep to make up for their wrong.
Ezra 10:20 From Immer's sons: Hanani and Zebadiah.
Ezra 10:21 From Harim's sons were Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
Ezra 10:22 The sons of Pashur were Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethaneel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
Ezra 10:23 From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also called Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
Ezra 10:24 Among the singers was Eliashib; and the gatekeepers were Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
Ezra 10:25 From Israel: sons of Parosh are Ramiah, Jeziah, Malchiah, Miamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
Ezra 10:26 The sons of Elam were Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Eliah.
Ezra 10:27 From Zattu's descendants were Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
Ezra 10:28 From Bebai's sons: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
Ezra 10:29 From Bani's descendants came Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
Ezra 10:30 From the descendants of Pahathmoab were Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
Ezra 10:31 From Harim's descendants came Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchiah, Shemaiah, and Shimeon.
Ezra 10:32 Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
Ezra 10:33 From Hashum's sons: Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
Ezra 10:34 From Bani's descendants: Maadai, Amram, and Uel.
Ezra 10:35 Benaiah, Bedeiah, Chelluh,
Ezra 10:36 Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib.
Ezra 10:37 Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasau,
Ezra 10:38 Bani, Binnui, and Shimei,
Ezra 10:39 Shelemiah, Nathan, and Adaiah,
Ezra 10:40 Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Ezra 10:41 Azareel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Ezra 10:42 Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
Ezra 10:43 From Nebo's descendants: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jadau, Joel, and Benaiah.
Ezra 10:44 All these men married foreign women, and some of them had children with these wives.

Nehemiah 1:1 Nehemiah son of Hachaliah spoke these words. In the month of Kislev during the twentieth year, I was at the palace in Susa.
Nehemiah 1:2 My brother Hanani and some men from Judah came, and I asked them about the Jews who survived the captivity and about Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 1:3 They told me that the survivors from the captivity in the province are suffering a lot and are shamed. The wall of Jerusalem is also destroyed, and its gates are burned with fire.
Nehemiah 1:4 When I heard these words, I sat down and cried, and I was sad for some days, and I didn't eat, and I prayed to the God of heaven.
Nehemiah 1:5 I ask you, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps his promise and kindness for those who love him and follow his commands.
Nehemiah 1:6 Listen carefully and keep your eyes open, so you can hear the prayer I make before you now, day and night, for the people of Israel your servants. I admit the sins of the people of Israel, which we have done wrong against you. Both I and my family have sinned.
Nehemiah 1:7 We have acted very badly towards you and have not followed your commands, laws, or rules that you gave to your servant Moses.
Nehemiah 1:8 Please remember what you told your servant Moses: "If you disobey, I will spread you out among the countries."
Nehemiah 1:9 If you come back to me, follow my rules, and do them, even if you were scattered to the farthest skies, I will bring you back to the place I have chosen for my name to be.
Nehemiah 1:10 These are your servants and your people, whom you have saved with your great power and strong hand.
Nehemiah 1:11 God, I ask you, please listen to your servant's prayer and the prayers of those who respect your name. Help your servant today, give him kindness before this man, because I served the king as his cupbearer.

Nehemiah 2:1 In the month of Nisan, during King Artaxerxes's twentieth year, there was wine in front of him. I picked up the wine and gave it to the king. I had never been sad in front of him before.
Nehemiah 2:2 So the king asked me, "Why do you look sad when you're not ill? This must be deep sadness." I felt very afraid.
Nehemiah 2:3 I told the king, "May the king live always. Why shouldn't I look sad when the city where my ancestors are buried is ruined, and its gates have been destroyed by fire?"
Nehemiah 2:4 Then the king asked me, "What do you request?" So I prayed to God in heaven.
Nehemiah 2:5 I told the king, "If it makes the king happy, and if I have your approval, please let me go to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried, so I can rebuild it."
Nehemiah 2:6 The king asked me, with the queen sitting beside him, "How long will your trip take? And when will you come back?" The king was happy to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
Nehemiah 2:7 Also, I said to the king, "If it's okay with the king, please give me letters for the governors across the river so they can help me travel to Judah."
Nehemiah 2:8 I also wrote a letter to Asaph, who takes care of the king's forest, asking for wood to build beams for the palace gates, the city wall, and the house I will live in. The king gave me what I asked for because God was kind to me.
Nehemiah 2:9 I went to the leaders across the river and gave them the king's letters. The king had sent army officers and cavalry with me.
Nehemiah 2:10 When Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about it, they were very upset that someone had come to help the people of Israel.
Nehemiah 2:11 I came to Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.
Nehemiah 2:12 I got up at night with a few men; I didn't tell anyone what God had inspired me to do in Jerusalem, and I didn't bring any animals except the one I was riding.
Nehemiah 2:13 I went out at night through the valley gate, past the dragon spring and the trash gate, and I looked at Jerusalem's walls, which were torn down, and its gates, which were burned by fire.
Nehemiah 2:14 Then I went to the Fountain Gate and to the king's pool, but there was no room for the animal I was riding to get through.
Nehemiah 2:15 I went up at night by the creek, looked at the wall, turned around, entered through the valley gate, and went back.
Nehemiah 2:16 The leaders did not know where I went or what I did; I had not yet told anything to the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the leaders, or the others working.
Nehemiah 2:17 I told them, "You see the trouble we're in. Jerusalem is ruined, its gates burned by fire. Come, let's rebuild Jerusalem's wall, so we won't be disgraced anymore."
Nehemiah 2:18 I told them how God had helped me and what the king had said to me. They replied, "Let's start building." So they prepared to do this good work.
Nehemiah 2:19 When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian heard this, they laughed at us, looked down on us, and said, "What are you doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
Nehemiah 2:20 I replied to them, "The God of heaven will help us succeed; so we, His servants, will start building. But you have no share, no claim, or any history in Jerusalem."

Nehemiah 3:1 Eliashib, the high priest, got up with his fellow priests, and they built the Sheep Gate; they made it holy, and put in its doors; they made it holy all the way to the Tower of Meah, and to the Tower of Hananeel.
Nehemiah 3:2 Next to him, the men of Jericho built. And beside them, Zaccur, Imri's son, built.
Nehemiah 3:3 The sons of Hassenaah built the fish gate, made its beams, and installed its doors, locks, and bars.
Nehemiah 3:4 Next to them, Meremoth, Urijah's son and Koz's grandson, made repairs. Next to them, Meshullam, Berechiah's son and Meshezabeel's grandson, made repairs. Beside them, Zadok, Baana's son, worked on repairs.
Nehemiah 3:5 Next to them, the people of Tekoa worked on repairs; but their leaders wouldn't help with the work for God.
Nehemiah 3:6 Jehoiada, the son of Paseah, and Meshullam, the son of Besodeiah, fixed the Old Gate. They put in its beams, hung its doors, and installed its locks and bars.
Nehemiah 3:7 Next to them, Melatiah from Gibeon and Jadon from Meronoth, along with the men from Gibeon and Mizpah, fixed the section up to the governor's seat by the river.
Nehemiah 3:8 Next to him, Uzziel, Harhaiah's son and a goldsmith, made repairs. Next to him, Hananiah, the son of a perfumer, also made repairs. Together, they strengthened Jerusalem up to the wide wall.
Nehemiah 3:9 Rephaiah, Hur's son and leader of half of Jerusalem, fixed the next part.
Nehemiah 3:10 Next to them, Jedaiah, Harumaph's son, fixed the wall by his house. Next to him, Hattush, Hashabniah's son, also made repairs.
Nehemiah 3:11 Malchijah, Harim's son, and Hashub, Pahathmoab's son, fixed another section and the oven tower.
Nehemiah 3:12 Next to him, Shallum, son of Halohesh, who was in charge of half of Jerusalem, fixed the wall with his daughters.
Nehemiah 3:13 Hanun and the people of Zanoah fixed the Valley Gate. They built it, put in its doors, locks, and bars, and repaired the wall for a thousand cubits up to the Dung Gate.
Nehemiah 3:14 Malchiah, Rechab's son and leader of a district of Bethhaccerem, fixed the Dung Gate. He built it, installed its doors, locks, and bars.
Nehemiah 3:15 Shallun, Colhozeh's son and leader of a district of Mizpah, fixed the Fountain Gate. He constructed and roofed it, installed its doors, locks, and bars, and rebuilt the wall by the Pool of Siloam near the king's garden, leading to the stairs down from David's City.
Nehemiah 3:16 After him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, leader of half of Bethzur, fixed the area opposite King David's tombs, near the constructed pool, and up to the warriors' house.
Nehemiah 3:17 After him, the Levites, with Rehum son of Bani, made repairs. Next to him, Hashabiah, leader of half of Keilah, made repairs in his area.
Nehemiah 3:18 After him, their relatives fixed it, Bavai son of Henadad, leader of half of Keilah.
Nehemiah 3:19 Ezer son of Jeshua, the leader of Mizpah, fixed the next section near the ascent to the armory at the corner.
Nehemiah 3:20 After him, Baruch, Zabbai's son, worked hard to fix another part of the wall, from the corner to the entrance of Eliashib the high priest's house.
Nehemiah 3:21 After him, Meremoth, Urijah's son and Koz's grandson, fixed another part, from Eliashib's house entrance to the end of Eliashib's house.
Nehemiah 3:22 After him, the priests, the men from the flat land, made repairs.
Nehemiah 3:23 After him, Benjamin and Hashub fixed the area opposite their house. Then, Azariah, son of Maaseiah and grandson of Ananiah, repaired next to his house.
Nehemiah 3:24 After him, Binnui son of Henadad fixed another section, from Azariah's house to where the wall turns, all the way to the corner.
Nehemiah 3:25 Palal son of Uzai worked opposite where the wall turns by the tower that stretches from the royal palace near the prison courtyard. Next was Pedaiah son of Parosh.
Nehemiah 3:26 Also, the temple workers lived on the Ophel hill, near the Water Gate to the east and the projecting tower.
Nehemiah 3:27 After them, the people of Tekoa fixed another part, opposite the big tower that extends out, all the way to the Ophel wall.
Nehemiah 3:28 The priests fixed the section above the Horse Gate, each one opposite his own house.
Nehemiah 3:29 After them, Zadok the son of Immer fixed the area opposite his house. Next, Shemaiah the son of Shechaniah, who was in charge of the east gate, also made repairs.
Nehemiah 3:30 After him, Hananiah, Shelemiah's son, and Hanun, Zalaph's sixth son, fixed another section. Then Meshullam, Berechiah's son, made repairs opposite his room.
Nehemiah 3:31 After him, Malchiah the son of a goldsmith fixed the wall by the area where the Nethinims and merchants live, near the Miphkad Gate, and up to the corner.
Nehemiah 3:32 The goldsmiths and merchants fixed the area from the corner to the Sheep Gate.

Nehemiah 4:1 But when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he became very angry, was greatly upset, and made fun of the Jews.
Nehemiah 4:2 He spoke to his brothers and Samaria's army, asking, "What can these weak Jews do? Can they rebuild their defenses? Can they offer sacrifices? Can they finish in one day? Can they bring the burned stones back to life from the rubble piles?"
Nehemiah 4:3 Tobiah, from Ammon, stood next to him and said, "What they are building is so weak that if a fox climbs it, the wall will fall down."
Nehemiah 4:4 Listen, our God, we are looked down on: make their insults fall on them, and let them be captured in the land they were taken to.
Nehemiah 4:5 Do not overlook their wrongdoing, and do not erase their sin from your presence; for they have made you angry in front of the builders.
Nehemiah 4:6 We built the wall, and the whole wall was connected up to halfway because the people wanted to work.
Nehemiah 4:7 When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites found out that the walls of Jerusalem were being rebuilt and the gaps were getting fixed, they became very angry.
Nehemiah 4:8 They all plotted together to come fight against Jerusalem and to block its progress.
Nehemiah 4:9 We prayed to God and kept guard day and night to protect ourselves from them.
Nehemiah 4:10 Judah said, "The workers are getting weak, and there is a lot of trash; we can't build the wall."
Nehemiah 4:11 Our enemies said, "They won't realize or see until we attack them, kill them, and stop their work."
Nehemiah 4:12 When the nearby Jews came to us, they repeatedly warned us, "No matter where you come from, they will attack you."
Nehemiah 4:13 So I placed people in the lower parts of the wall and on the higher areas according to their families, armed with swords, spears, and bows.
Nehemiah 4:14 I looked, got up, and told the leaders and the rest of the people, "Don't be afraid of them: remember God, who is great and mighty, and fight for your brothers, your children, your wives, and your homes."
Nehemiah 4:15 When our enemies found out that we knew their plan, and that God had stopped their plan from succeeding, we all went back to work on the wall.
Nehemiah 4:16 From then on, half of my servants worked, while the other half carried spears, shields, bows, and body armor; and the leaders stood behind all the people of Judah.
Nehemiah 4:17 The people who built the wall and those who carried loads worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.
Nehemiah 4:18 Each builder worked with a sword tied to their side, and I had the trumpet blower by my side.
Nehemiah 4:19 I told the leaders, officials, and the others, "The task is huge and spread out, and we are far apart on the wall."
Nehemiah 4:20 When you hear the trumpet, come to us; our God will fight for us.
Nehemiah 4:21 We worked hard, and half of us kept holding spears from dawn until the stars came out.
Nehemiah 4:22 I also told the people at that time, "Everyone should stay in Jerusalem with their servants, so they can protect us at night and work during the day."
Nehemiah 4:23 Neither I, nor my brothers, nor my workers, nor the guards with me took off our clothes, except to wash them.

Nehemiah 5:1 The people and their wives raised a loud protest against their fellow Jews.
Nehemiah 5:2 Some people said, "We, our sons, and our daughters are many, so we get corn for them to eat and survive."
Nehemiah 5:3 Some said, "We have put our fields, vineyards, and homes up as security to buy grain because of the famine."
Nehemiah 5:4 Some also said, "We have borrowed money to pay the king's tax, using our fields and vineyards as collateral."
Nehemiah 5:5 Now our bodies are like our relatives' bodies, and our children like theirs. Yet, we must make our sons and daughters slaves, and some of our daughters are already enslaved. We can't free them, because others now own our lands and vineyards.
Nehemiah 5:6 I was very angry when I heard their cries and these words.
Nehemiah 5:7 I thought about it, and I scolded the nobles and officials, saying to them, "You charge your own people interest." Then I called a large meeting to deal with them.
Nehemiah 5:8 I told them, "We have bought back our fellow Jews who were sold to other nations, as much as we could. Now, are you going to sell your own people, or should they be sold to us?" They kept quiet and had nothing to say.
Nehemiah 5:9 I said, "What you are doing isn't right. Shouldn't you live in fear of God to avoid the scorn of our enemies?"
Nehemiah 5:10 I, my brothers, and my workers could also demand from them money and grain: I ask you, please stop charging them interest.
Nehemiah 5:11 Please give back to them today their land, vineyards, olive groves, and homes. Also return the part of the money, grain, wine, and oil you have been taking from them.
Nehemiah 5:12 They said, "We will give everything back and ask for nothing in return; we will do as you say." Then I gathered the priests and made them promise to do this.
Nehemiah 5:13 I shook my clothes and said, "May God remove anyone from their home and job who does not keep this promise. May they be shaken out and left with nothing." Everyone agreed, saying "Amen," and praised God. The people kept the promise.
Nehemiah 5:14 Since I was made governor in Judah, from the 20th to the 32nd year of King Artaxerxes, which is 12 years, neither I nor my brothers have used the food allowance given to the governor.
Nehemiah 5:15 The governors before me made the people pay for their food and wine, and even took forty silver coins; their helpers also took advantage of the people. But I didn't do this because I respected God.
Nehemiah 5:16 Yes, I kept working on this wall; we didn't buy any land, and all my workers came there to work.
Nehemiah 5:17 Also, at my table there were one hundred and fifty Jews and leaders, in addition to the visitors from the nations around us.
Nehemiah 5:18 Every day, I was given one ox, six special sheep, and some birds to eat. Also, every ten days, I received many kinds of wine. But even with all this, I didn't take the governor's food allowance because the people were already working hard.
Nehemiah 5:19 Remember me, my God, for good, for everything I've done for these people.

Nehemiah 6:1 When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian, and our other enemies heard that I had built the wall with no gaps left (though I had not yet installed the doors in the gates at that time),
Nehemiah 6:2 Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message, saying, "Come, let's meet in one of the villages on the plain of Ono." But they planned to hurt me.
Nehemiah 6:3 I sent messengers to them, saying, "I'm doing important work and can't stop to come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to come to you?"
Nehemiah 6:4 They sent me the same message four times; and I replied in the same way each time.
Nehemiah 6:5 Sanballat sent his servant to me for the fifth time with an open letter in his hand.
Nehemiah 6:6 The message said, "The nations are hearing, and Gashmu also says, you and the Jews plan to revolt. That's why you're rebuilding the wall, to become their king, they say."
Nehemiah 6:7 You have also chosen prophets to speak about you in Jerusalem, saying, "There is a king in Judah." And now these words will be reported to the king. So come, let us talk together.
Nehemiah 6:8 Then I sent a message to him, saying, "Nothing like what you are saying is happening; you are making it up in your mind."
Nehemiah 6:9 They all scared us by saying, "Their hands will be too weak to do the work, so it won't be finished." Now, God, give me strong hands.
Nehemiah 6:10 Later, I went to the home of Shemaiah, Delaiah’s son, Mehetabeel’s grandson, who was confined inside. He suggested, "Let's meet at God's house, inside the temple, and close the temple doors because they are coming to kill you; indeed, at night they will come to kill you."
Nehemiah 6:11 I thought, should someone like me run away? And who like me would go into the temple to save his life? I won't go in.
Nehemiah 6:12 I realized that God had not sent him; he made this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat paid him.
Nehemiah 6:13 He was paid to make me scared, so I would sin and they could discredit me with bad things to say.
Nehemiah 6:14 God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done, and also the prophetess Noadiah and the other prophets who tried to scare me.
Nehemiah 6:15 The wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days.
Nehemiah 6:16 When all our enemies and the nations around us heard about this, they felt very discouraged because they realized that our God had done this work.
Nehemiah 6:17 During that time, the leaders of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters came to them.
Nehemiah 6:18 Many people in Judah were loyal to him because he was married to Shecaniah's daughter, Arah's granddaughter, and his son Johanan had married Meshullam's daughter, Berechiah's granddaughter.
Nehemiah 6:19 They also told me about his good works and shared my words with him. Tobiah sent letters to scare me.

Nehemiah 7:1 When the wall was finished, and I had installed the doors, and the gatekeepers, musicians, and Levites had been assigned their tasks,

Nehemiah 8:1 All the people came together as one in the street by the water gate and asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of Moses's Law, which God had given to Israel.
Nehemiah 8:2 Ezra the priest presented the law to the assembly of men and women, and to all who could understand, on the first day of the seventh month.
Nehemiah 8:3 He read to them in front of the Water Gate from morning until noon. Men, women, and others who could understand listened closely to the reading of God's laws.
Nehemiah 8:4 Ezra the teacher stood on a wooden platform built for this reason, and next to him on his right were Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Urijah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, and on his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchiah, Hashum, Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Nehemiah 8:5 Ezra opened the book where everyone could see, because he was higher than everyone else; and when he opened it, everyone stood up.
Nehemiah 8:6 Ezra praised God, the great one. All the people replied, "Yes, yes," raising their hands. They lowered their heads and worshiped God with their faces to the earth.
Nehemiah 8:7 Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites helped the people understand the law, and the people stood where they were.
Nehemiah 8:8 They clearly read from God's law book, explained the meaning, and helped them understand what was read.
Nehemiah 8:9 Nehemiah, the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who instructed the people told everyone, "This day is special for God; don't be sad or cry." Because everyone cried when they heard the law's words.
Nehemiah 8:10 He told them, "Go, eat rich food, drink sweet drinks, and give some to those who have nothing ready. Today is sacred to God. Don't be sad, because the joy of God gives you strength."
Nehemiah 8:11 The Levites calmed everyone, saying, "Be quiet, because this day is sacred; don't be sad."
Nehemiah 8:12 Everyone went to eat, drink, share food, and celebrate with joy because they understood the words that were explained to them.
Nehemiah 8:13 On the second day, the leaders of all the families, the priests, and the Levites came together to Ezra the writer to learn the meaning of the law.
Nehemiah 8:14 They discovered in the law that God gave through Moses, it said the people of Israel must live in shelters during the festival of the seventh month.
Nehemiah 8:15 They should announce in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, "Go to the mountain and get branches from olive trees, pine trees, myrtle trees, palm trees, and other leafy trees to make shelters as it is written."
Nehemiah 8:16 The people went out, brought branches, and made shelters for themselves—on their rooftops, in their yards, in the yards of God's house, by the Water Gate, and by the Ephraim Gate.
Nehemiah 8:17 Everyone who had returned from being captives built shelters and sat under them. They hadn't done this since the time of Joshua son of Nun. And they were very happy.
Nehemiah 8:18 Every day from the start to the end, he read from God's book of laws. They celebrated for seven days, and on the eighth day, they held a special gathering as was the custom.

Nehemiah 9:1 On the twenty-fourth day of this month, the people of Israel gathered together. They fasted, wore rough clothing, and put dirt on themselves.
Nehemiah 9:2 The people of Israel kept away from foreigners, stood up, and admitted their own sins and the wrongdoings of their ancestors.
Nehemiah 9:3 They stood in their spot and read from God's law book for a quarter of the day; for another quarter, they admitted their wrongs and worshiped God.
Nehemiah 9:4 Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani, who were Levites, stood on the stairs and called out to God with loud voices.
Nehemiah 9:5 Then the Levites, Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodijah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, "Stand up and praise God forever and ever; and may your wonderful name be blessed, higher than all blessings and praise."
Nehemiah 9:6 You alone are God; you created the heavens, the highest heavens, and all their stars, the earth, and everything on it, the seas, and everything in them. You keep them all alive, and the heavenly beings worship you.
Nehemiah 9:7 You are God, who chose Abram, took him out of Ur of the Chaldees, and gave him the name Abraham.
Nehemiah 9:8 You saw that his heart was loyal to you, and you made an agreement with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites to his descendants, and you kept your promise, because you are righteous.
Nehemiah 9:9 You saw our ancestors' suffering in Egypt and heard their cries near the Red Sea.
Nehemiah 9:10 You showed miracles and amazing things to Pharaoh, his officials, and everyone in his land because you knew they were arrogant. This made you famous, like you are today.
Nehemiah 9:11 You split the sea for them, so they walked through it on dry ground; and you threw their chasers into the deep, like a stone into strong waters.
Nehemiah 9:12 You also led them in the day with a cloud and at night with a fire to light their path where they should walk.
Nehemiah 9:13 You also came down on Mount Sinai, talked to them from heaven, and gave them fair laws, true rules, and good commands.
Nehemiah 9:14 You made your holy rest day known to them, and gave them rules, decrees, and laws through Moses, your servant.
Nehemiah 9:15 You gave them bread from heaven when they were hungry, and you made water flow from the rock when they were thirsty. You promised them they would enter and own the land you swore to give them.
Nehemiah 9:16 They and our ancestors were proud, stubborn, and did not listen to your commands.
Nehemiah 9:17 They didn't listen or remember the amazing things you did for them; they were stubborn and chose a leader to take them back to being slaves. But you are a forgiving God, kind and merciful, not easily angered, full of love, and you didn't leave them.
Nehemiah 9:18 Yes, when they made a golden calf and said, "This is your God who brought you out of Egypt," and did very bad things.
Nehemiah 9:19 But you, with your great mercy, did not abandon them in the desert: the cloud pillar did not leave them by day, to guide them on their path; nor the fire pillar at night, to give them light and show them the way to go.
Nehemiah 9:20 You also gave them your good spirit to teach them, did not stop giving them manna to eat, and provided them water when they were thirsty.
Nehemiah 9:21 Yes, for forty years you supported them in the desert, so they needed nothing; their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
Nehemiah 9:22 You also gave them kingdoms and countries, splitting them into parts. So they took over the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, the king of Bashan.
Nehemiah 9:23 You made their children as many as the stars in the sky, and you led them to the land you promised their ancestors they would enter and take over.
Nehemiah 9:24 The children entered and took over the land, and you conquered the land's people, the Canaanites, for them, and handed them over with their kings and the people of the land, so they could do as they wanted with them.
Nehemiah 9:25 They captured fortified cities and a rich land, and took over houses filled with all kinds of goods, dug wells, vineyards, olive groves, and plenty of fruit trees. They ate to satisfaction, grew fat, and enjoyed your immense kindness.
Nehemiah 9:26 Despite this, they did not listen and turned against you, throwing your laws aside and killing your prophets who warned them to turn back to you, causing great anger.
Nehemiah 9:27 So you gave them over to their enemies who troubled them, but when they called out to you in their distress, you heard from heaven. Because of your many kindnesses, you sent them rescuers to save them from their enemies.
Nehemiah 9:28 After they rested, they did wrong before you: so you let them stay in their enemies' land, where they were controlled by them. But when they came back and called to you, you heard them from heaven; and you saved them many times because of your mercy.
Nehemiah 9:29 You warned them to follow your laws again, but they acted with pride, and did not listen to your commands. They broke your rules, which if followed, would give life. They turned away and were stubborn, and refused to listen.
Nehemiah 9:30 For many years you were patient with them and warned them through your spirit in your prophets, but they wouldn't listen. So you handed them over to the surrounding peoples.
Nehemiah 9:31 Even though you were very kind, you did not completely destroy them or leave them; because you are a kind and merciful God.
Nehemiah 9:32 So now, our God, the great, the powerful, and the fearsome God, who keeps promises and shows kindness, do not see all the hardships that have come on us, our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all your people, from the days of the Assyrian kings until now, as small.
Nehemiah 9:33 Even though you are fair in everything that happens to us, because you have done what is right, but we have acted badly.
Nehemiah 9:34 Our kings, leaders, priests, and ancestors did not follow your law or listen to your commands and warnings that you gave them.
Nehemiah 9:35 They did not serve you in their own land, and with the great goodness you gave them, and in the rich and fertile land you provided, they did not turn away from their evil deeds.
Nehemiah 9:36 Look, we are servants today, working in the land you gave our ancestors to enjoy its fruits and benefits, but here we are, serving in it.
Nehemiah 9:37 It produces a lot of growth for the kings you put over us due to our sins; they also rule over our bodies and our animals as they like, and we are in great trouble.
Nehemiah 9:38 Because of all this, we make a firm agreement and write it down. Our leaders, Levites, and priests put their seals on it.

Nehemiah 12:26 These events happened when Joiakim, son of Jeshua and grandson of Jozadak, was alive, during the time Nehemiah was governor and Ezra was priest and writer.
Nehemiah 12:27 At the opening of Jerusalem's wall, they invited the Levites from everywhere to celebrate with joy, using thank yous, songs, cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps.
Nehemiah 12:28 The singers' children came together from the area around Jerusalem and from the Netophathi villages.
Nehemiah 12:29 From Gilgal, as well as from Geba and Azmaveth fields, for the singers had built villages around Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 12:30 The priests and the Levites made themselves, the people, the gates, and the wall clean.
Nehemiah 12:31 Then I led the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and organized two large groups of thankful people. One group walked on the right side of the wall towards the Dung Gate.
Nehemiah 12:32 Hoshaiah and half of Judah's leaders followed them.
Nehemiah 12:33 Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
Nehemiah 12:34 Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
Nehemiah 12:35 Some priests' sons had trumpets, including Zechariah, who was Jonathan's son, Shemaiah's grandson, Mattaniah's great-grandson, Michaiah's great-great-grandson, Zaccur's great-great-great-grandson, and Asaph's great-great-great-great-grandson.
Nehemiah 12:36 His brothers Shemaiah, Azarael, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethaneel, and Judah, Hanani, played David's musical instruments, with God’s man Ezra leading them.
Nehemiah 12:37 At the Fountain Gate in front of them, they climbed the stairs to the City of David, went along the wall above David's house, and reached the Water Gate on the east side.
Nehemiah 12:38 The other group that was thanking God went opposite them, with me following, and half of the people were along the wall from past the furnace tower to the wide wall.
Nehemiah 12:39 Above the Ephraim gate, the old gate, the fish gate, the Hananeel tower, and the Meah tower, as far as the sheep gate, they stopped at the prison gate.
Nehemiah 12:40 Two groups of thankful people, along with me and half of the leaders, stood in God's house.
Nehemiah 12:41 The priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Michaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah had trumpets.
Nehemiah 12:42 Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer were there. The singers sang loudly with their leader Jezrahiah.
Nehemiah 12:43 On that day, they gave many sacrifices and were happy because God had made them very joyful. The women and children were happy too. The happiness of Jerusalem was heard from far away.
Nehemiah 12:44 At that time, people were chosen to take care of the storage rooms for the treasures, the offerings, the first crops, and the tithes. They collected from the city fields what was legally given to the priests and Levites: because the people of Judah were happy with the priests and Levites who served.
Nehemiah 12:45 The singers and gatekeepers followed God's orders and the rules for purification, as directed by David and his son Solomon.
Nehemiah 12:46 In the old times of David and Asaph, there were lead singers and songs of praise and thanks to God.
Nehemiah 12:47 During the time of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all of Israel provided daily shares to the singers and gatekeepers. They set apart sacred gifts for the Levites, and the Levites dedicated them to Aaron's descendants.

Nehemiah 13:1 On that day, they read from the book of Moses to the people; it was written that Ammonites and Moabites may never join God's assembly.
Nehemiah 13:2 Because they didn't bring food and water to the Israelites, but paid Balaam to curse them, God changed the curse into a blessing.
Nehemiah 13:3 When they heard the law, they separated all the non-Israelites from Israel.
Nehemiah 13:4 Before this, Eliashib the priest, who was in charge of the storerooms of our God's house, had become close to Tobiah.
Nehemiah 13:5 He set up a big room for him where they used to put the food offerings, incense, containers, and the parts of grain, new wine, and oil that were supposed to go to the Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and the gifts for the priests.
Nehemiah 13:6 During all this time, I wasn't in Jerusalem because in the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes of Babylon, I went to the king, and after a while, I got permission from the king to leave.
Nehemiah 13:7 I came to Jerusalem and learned about the bad thing Eliashib did for Tobiah by setting up a room for him in the courts of God's house.
Nehemiah 13:8 It made me very sad, so I threw all of Tobiah's belongings out of the room.
Nehemiah 13:9 Then I ordered, and they cleaned the rooms. After that, I brought back the items of God's house, along with the grain offering and the incense.
Nehemiah 13:10 I noticed that the Levites did not receive their shares, so the Levites and singers who did the work had all gone back to their own fields.
Nehemiah 13:11 I argued with the leaders and asked, "Why is God's house neglected?" I brought them together and put them in their positions.
Nehemiah 13:12 Then all of Judah brought a tenth of the grain, new wine, and oil to the storerooms.
Nehemiah 13:13 I appointed managers for the storage rooms: Priest Shelemiah, Scribe Zadok, and Pedaiah from the Levites, with Hanan, Zaccur's son and Mattaniah's grandson, beside them. They were trusted, and their job was to hand out supplies to their relatives.
Nehemiah 13:14 God, remember me for this and do not erase the good things I have done for God's house and its duties.
Nehemiah 13:15 During that time, I saw people in Judah working on the Sabbath: they were pressing grapes, carrying grain, loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. I warned them on that day for selling food.
Nehemiah 13:16 People from Tyre also lived there, who brought fish and all kinds of goods, and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 13:17 I argued with Judah's leaders and asked them, "What is this bad thing you are doing to disrespect the Sabbath day?"
Nehemiah 13:18 Didn't your ancestors do the same, and didn't God cause all this trouble for us and this city? Yet you make God even angrier with Israel by not keeping the Sabbath holy.
Nehemiah 13:19 When Jerusalem's gates started to get dark before the Sabbath, I ordered them closed and said they shouldn't open until after the Sabbath. I placed some of my workers at the gates to stop anyone from bringing in loads on the Sabbath day.
Nehemiah 13:20 The traders and sellers of all kinds of goods stayed outside Jerusalem once or twice.
Nehemiah 13:21 I warned them and asked, "Why do you spend the night by the wall? If you do it again, I will arrest you." After that, they did not come on the Sabbath anymore.
Nehemiah 13:22 I told the Levites to make themselves clean, and to guard the gates to keep the Sabbath day holy. God, remember this too and show me mercy because you are very kind.
Nehemiah 13:23 In those days, I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Nehemiah 13:24 Their children spoke partly in Ashdod's language and couldn't speak the Jewish language, but only in the language of their own people.
Nehemiah 13:25 I argued with them, cursed them, hit some of them, pulled out their hair and made them promise by God, saying, "You must not let your daughters marry their sons, or let your sons marry their daughters, or marry them yourselves."
Nehemiah 13:26 Didn't Solomon, the king of Israel, sin because of these things? Still, there was no other king like him among many nations; he was loved by his God, who made him king over all Israel. But foreign women led even him into sin.
Nehemiah 13:27 Should we listen to you and do this terrible thing, sinning against God by marrying foreign women?
Nehemiah 13:28 One of Joiada's sons, who was Eliashib the high priest's son, married Sanballat the Horonite's daughter, so I made him leave.
Nehemiah 13:29 God, remember them because they have made the priesthood unclean and broken the agreement with the priests and Levites.
Nehemiah 13:30 I purified them from all foreigners and set up the duties for the priests and Levites, each to their own task.
Nehemiah 13:31 For the wood given at set times, and for the first crops. God, please remember me kindly.

Esther 1:1 During the time of King Ahasuerus, who ruled over 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia.
Esther 1:2 In those days, when King Ahasuerus was ruling from his throne in his kingdom at the palace in Shushan,
Esther 1:3 In the third year of being king, he prepared a big meal for all his leaders and workers; the important people of Persia and Media and the leaders from the regions were present.
Esther 1:4 He showed off his kingdom's wealth and his great honor for many days, 180 days to be exact.
Esther 1:5 When the days were over, the king held a feast for all the people in Shushan palace, for both important and unimportant, lasting seven days, in the garden area of the king's palace.
Esther 1:6 There were white, green, and blue curtains, tied with fine linen and purple cords to silver rings and marble pillars; the couches were made of gold and silver, set on a floor with red, blue, white, and black marble.
Esther 1:7 They served drinks in golden cups, all different from each other, and gave lots of fine wine, as much as the king allowed.
Esther 1:8 The drinking followed the rule; no one was forced to drink because the king had ordered his household officers to let everyone drink as they wished.
Esther 1:9 Queen Vashti also held a banquet for the women in the palace of King Ahasuerus.
Esther 1:10 On the seventh day, when the king felt happy from wine, he ordered Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, his seven servants, to come to King Ahasuerus.
Esther 1:11 To bring Queen Vashti before the king with the royal crown, to show her beauty to the people and the princes: for she was beautiful to see.
Esther 1:12 But Queen Vashti wouldn't come when the king ordered her through his servants; so the king got very angry, and he burned with rage.
Esther 1:13 The king spoke to the wise men who understood the times, since this was the king's usual way with all who were experts in law and decisions.
Esther 1:14 Next to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven leaders of Persia and Media, who saw the king and were the highest in the kingdom.
Esther 1:15 What should we do to Queen Vashti by law since she did not follow King Ahasuerus's order given through his officials?
Esther 1:16 Memucan spoke to the king and the leaders, saying, "Queen Vashti didn't disrespect just the king, but also all the leaders and everyone in King Ahasuerus' provinces."
Esther 1:17 Because of the queen's action, all women will hear about it and look down on their husbands, thinking, 'The king ordered Queen Vashti to come to him, but she didn't.'
Esther 1:18 The women of Persia and Media will tell the king's leaders today about what the queen has done. This will cause a lot of disrespect and anger.
Esther 1:19 If the king agrees, let him issue a royal order and make it a law of the Persians and Medes, so it cannot be changed: Vashti will not come before King Ahasuerus again; and let the king give her royal position to someone better than her.
Esther 1:20 When the king's order is announced to his whole kingdom (because it is large), all wives will respect their husbands, whether they are high-ranking or not.
Esther 1:21 The king and his officials liked the idea, and the king followed Memucan's advice.
Esther 1:22 He sent letters to all the king's provinces, to each province in its own script, and to every people in their own language, so that every man should be in charge of his own house, and it should be announced in the language of each people.

Esther 2:1 After this, when King Ahasuerus calmed down, he remembered Vashti, what she did, and the decision made against her.
Esther 2:2 The king's servants who served him suggested, "Let's look for beautiful young women for the king."
Esther 2:3 Let the king choose officials throughout his kingdom to bring all the beautiful young women to the palace in Susa, to the women's living quarters, under the care of Hegai, the royal eunuch in charge of the women, and provide them with their beauty treatments.
Esther 2:4 Let the young woman who pleases the king become queen instead of Vashti. The king liked this idea and he followed it.
Esther 2:5 In Shushan palace, there lived a Jew named Mordecai, son of Jair, grandson of Shimei, and great-grandson of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin.
Esther 2:6 Who had been taken from Jerusalem as prisoners with King Jeconiah of Judah, whom King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had taken captive.
Esther 2:7 He raised Hadassah, also called Esther, his cousin, because she had no parents. She was lovely and pretty. When her parents died, Mordecai adopted her as his daughter.
Esther 2:8 It happened that when the king's order was announced, and many young women were brought to the palace of Shushan under the care of Hegai, Esther was also taken to the king's house and placed under Hegai, who was in charge of the women.
Esther 2:9 The young woman pleased him, and he showed her kindness. He quickly provided her with her purification items, what she needed, and seven maids from the king's palace. He moved her and her maids to the best place in the women's quarters.
Esther 2:10 Esther had not revealed her people or family because Mordecai had told her not to tell anyone.
Esther 2:11 Mordecai walked past the women's quarters every day to find out how Esther was doing and what would happen to her.
Esther 2:12 When it was time for each young woman to go to King Ahasuerus, after she had completed twelve months of beauty treatments according to the customs for the women—six months with myrrh oil and six months with sweet scents and other purification methods—
Esther 2:13 Every girl went to the king, and she was given whatever she wanted to take with her from the women's house to the king's house.
Esther 2:14 In the evening, she went, and the next day she went back to the second women's house, under Shaashgaz's care, the king's officer in charge of the concubines. She would not go to the king again unless he enjoyed her company and asked for her by name.
Esther 2:15 When it was Esther's turn, who was adopted by her cousin Mordecai, to meet the king, she asked for only what Hegai, the royal official in charge of the women, suggested. Everyone who saw Esther liked her.
Esther 2:16 Esther was brought to King Ahasuerus at his royal palace in the tenth month, called Tebeth, in the seventh year of his rule.
Esther 2:17 The king loved Esther more than any other woman, and she found more kindness and approval from him than any other virgin. So he put the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
Esther 2:18 The king prepared a large feast for all his leaders and workers, called Esther's feast; he declared a holiday across the regions and presented presents, as befits a king.
Esther 2:19 When the young women were brought together again, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
Esther 2:20 Esther had not told anyone about her family or people, because Mordecai told her not to. She followed Mordecai's orders, just like when she was raised by him.
Esther 2:21 During that time, while Mordecai was at the king's entrance, two of the king's officials, Bigthan and Teresh, who guarded the doorway, became angry and wanted to attack King Ahasuerus.
Esther 2:22 Mordecai learned about it and told Queen Esther; then Esther informed the king, mentioning Mordecai.
Esther 2:23 When they investigated, they discovered the truth; so both men were hanged on a tree, and this was recorded in the king's chronicles.

Esther 3:1 After this, King Ahasuerus promoted Haman, son of Hammedatha the Agagite, raised his rank, and gave him a higher seat than all the other princes with him.
Esther 3:2 All the king's workers at the king's gate bowed and showed respect to Haman because the king ordered it. But Mordecai did not bow or show him respect.
Esther 3:3 The king's servants at the king's gate asked Mordecai, "Why are you disobeying the king's order?"
Esther 3:4 Every day they spoke to him, but he did not listen. So they told Haman to see if Mordecai's behavior would be accepted because he had told them he was a Jew.
Esther 3:5 When Haman noticed that Mordecai did not bow or show him respect, Haman became very angry.
Esther 3:6 He thought it was not enough to hurt only Mordecai; after learning about Mordecai's people, Haman wanted to kill all the Jews in King Ahasuerus's kingdom.
Esther 3:7 In the first month, named Nisan, during King Ahasuerus's twelfth year, they threw dice every day and each month to decide the day, until the last month, called Adar.
Esther 3:8 Haman told King Ahasuerus, "A certain group of people are spread out and scattered among the citizens in all the regions of your kingdom; their rules are different from everyone else's and they don't follow the king's rules: so it's not good for the king to let them be."
Esther 3:9 If the king agrees, let an order be written to kill them, and I will give ten thousand silver coins to the officials to put into the king's treasury.
Esther 3:10 The king took his ring off his hand and gave it to Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
Esther 3:11 The king told Haman, "The money is yours, and the people too. You can do with them what you think is best."
Esther 3:12 On the thirteenth day of the first month, the king's writers were brought in. They wrote down everything Haman ordered for the king's officers, the leaders of each province, and the heads of each people in their own script and language. This was done in King Ahasuerus's name and sealed with his ring.
Esther 3:13 Messages were sent by couriers to all the king's regions to wipe out, kill, and eliminate all Jews—old and young, children and women—on the same day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their belongings.
Esther 3:14 The message about the order was shared in every area to tell everyone to prepare for that day.
Esther 3:15 The messengers rushed out with the king's orders, and the law was announced in Susa, the capital. The king and Haman sat down to have drinks, while the people of Susa were confused.

Esther 4:1 When Mordecai realized everything that had happened, he tore his clothes, dressed in rough fabric with ashes, and went out into the center of the city, crying loudly and bitterly.
Esther 4:2 They came up to the king's entrance, but no one could go through the king's entrance wearing sackcloth.
Esther 4:3 In every area where the king's rule and order went, the Jews mourned deeply, fasted, cried, and wailed; many wore rough cloth and put ashes on themselves.
Esther 4:4 Esther's servants and attendants came and told her. Then the queen was very sad; she sent clothes to dress Mordecai and to remove his sackcloth from him, but he didn't accept them.
Esther 4:5 Esther asked Hatach, one of the king's officials serving her, to go and find out from Mordecai what was happening and why.
Esther 4:6 So Hatach went to Mordecai in the city street in front of the king's gate.
Esther 4:7 Mordecai explained everything that happened to him and how much money Haman agreed to give to the king's treasury to kill the Jews.
Esther 4:8 He also gave him the text of the order issued in Shushan to kill them, so he could show it to Esther, tell her about it, and instruct her to plead with the king and ask him to save her people.
Esther 4:9 Hatach came and told Esther what Mordecai said.
Esther 4:10 Again, Esther spoke to Hatach and told him to give a message to Mordecai.
Esther 4:11 All the king's workers and the people in the king's lands know that anyone, man or woman, who goes to the king in the inner court without being invited must be put to death. The only way they can be saved is if the king shows them the golden scepter so they can live. But I have not been called to see the king for thirty days.
Esther 4:12 They reported Esther's words to Mordecai.
Esther 4:13 Mordecai told Esther, "Don't think you alone will escape from this danger at the palace, more than any other Jews."
Esther 4:14 If you stay silent now, the Jews will get help and freedom from somewhere else; but you and your family will be destroyed. And who knows if you were made queen for a moment like this?
Esther 4:15 Then Esther told them to give Mordecai this reply.
Esther 4:16 Go, get all the Jews in Shushan to fast for me. Don't eat or drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will also fast. Then I'll go to the king, even though it's against the law. If I die, I die.
Esther 4:17 Mordecai left and did everything Esther told him to do.

Esther 5:1 On the third day, Esther dressed in her royal clothes and stood in the inner part of the palace, across from the king's rooms. The king was seated on his royal throne in the palace, facing the entrance.
