Esther 5:2 When the king saw Queen Esther in the courtyard, she won his favor, and he offered her the golden scepter he held. Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter.
Esther 5:3 The king said to her, "What do you want, Queen Esther? What do you ask for? You will be given up to half of the kingdom."
Esther 5:4 Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast I have prepared for him."
Esther 5:5 Then the king ordered, "Hurry Haman, so he can do what Esther asked." So the king and Haman went to the feast Esther had made.
Esther 5:6 The king asked Esther at the wine feast, "What do you want? It will be given to you. What do you ask for? Up to half the kingdom, it will be done."
Esther 5:7 Esther answered, "Here is what I ask for."
Esther 5:8 If the king likes me and agrees to my wish and request, may the king and Haman join the meal I prepare for them, and tomorrow I will follow the king's instructions.
Esther 5:9 Haman left that day happy and cheerful, but when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate not standing or moving for him, he was very angry at Mordecai.
Esther 5:10 Even though Haman held back his anger, when he got home, he called his friends and his wife Zeresh to come over.
Esther 5:11 Haman bragged about how rich he was, how many children he had, all the ways the king had honored him, and how he was higher in rank than the other leaders and workers of the king.
Esther 5:12 Haman also said, "Yes, Queen Esther allowed no one else to come to the feast she prepared for the king, just me; and tomorrow I am invited to join her and the king again."
Esther 5:13 But all this means nothing to me as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.
Esther 5:14 Zeresh, his wife, and all his friends said to him, "Make a tall gallows, fifty cubits high, and tomorrow ask the king to hang Mordecai on it. Then you can go happily with the king to the feast." Haman liked the idea and had the gallows built.

Esther 6:1 That night the king could not sleep, so he ordered the record book of past events to be brought and read to him.
Esther 6:2 It was recorded that Mordecai reported Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's guards, who planned to attack King Ahasuerus.
Esther 6:3 The king asked, "What honor and respect has Mordecai received for this?" The king's servants who served him replied, "Nothing has been done for him."
Esther 6:4 The king asked, "Who is in the court?" Just then, Haman arrived in the outer court of the king’s palace, hoping to talk to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had set up for him.
Esther 6:5 The king's helpers told him, "Look, Haman is standing in the courtyard." And the king said, "Let him come in."
Esther 6:6 So Haman arrived. And the king asked him, "What should be done for the man the king wants to honor?" Haman thought to himself, "Who would the king want to honor more than me?"
Esther 6:7 Haman told the king, "For the man the king likes to honor,
Esther 6:8 Bring the king's fancy clothes, the horse the king rides, and the royal crown that is placed on his head.
Esther 6:9 Give these clothes and horse to one of the king's top princes, so they can dress the man the king wants to honor. Then have him ride through the city streets while they announce, "This is how the man the king wants to honor is treated."
Esther 6:10 The king told Haman, "Hurry and take the clothes and the horse, as you suggested, and do the same for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the palace entrance. Don't leave out anything you mentioned."
Esther 6:11 Haman took the clothes and the horse, dressed Mordecai, and led him on the horse through the city streets, announcing, "This is how the man the king wants to honor will be treated."
Esther 6:12 Mordecai went back to the king's entrance. But Haman hurried to his home, sad, with his head covered.
Esther 6:13 Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his wise friends and his wife Zeresh said to him, "If Mordecai is from the Jewish people, and you have started to lose to him, you will not win against him, but you will definitely lose to him."
Esther 6:14 While they were still chatting with him, the king's attendants arrived and quickly took Haman to the feast Esther had set up.

Esther 7:1 The king and Haman went to dine with Queen Esther.
Esther 7:2 The king spoke to Queen Esther again on the second day during the wine banquet, asking, "What do you wish for, Queen Esther? It will be given to you. What do you want to ask for? It will be done, up to half of the kingdom."
Esther 7:3 Queen Esther answered, "If I have pleased you, O king, and if you wish, please spare my life and save my people, as I have asked."
Esther 7:4 My people and I are sold to be killed and wiped out. If we were just sold as slaves, I would be quiet, even though the loss wouldn't make up for the king's loss.
Esther 7:5 Then King Ahasuerus replied to Queen Esther, "Who is he, and where is he, who dared to do this in his heart?"
Esther 7:6 Esther said, "This evil Haman is our enemy." Then Haman became scared in front of the king and queen.
Esther 7:7 The king, angry after his wine feast, went into the palace garden. Haman stood up to beg Queen Esther to save his life, for he knew the king intended harm against him.
Esther 7:8 Then the king came back from the palace garden to the wine banquet room, and he saw Haman lying on the couch where Esther was. The king asked, "Is he trying to attack the queen right here in front of me in the palace?" As soon as the king finished speaking, they covered Haman's face.
Esther 7:9 Harbonah, one of the king's servants, said to the king, "Look, there are the gallows, fifty cubits tall, which Haman built for Mordecai, who had spoken well of the king, standing at Haman's house." Then the king said, "Hang him on it."
Esther 7:10 They hung Haman on the same gallows he built for Mordecai. This calmed the king's anger.

Esther 8:1 On that day, King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Mordecai came to the king because Esther had explained who he was to her.
Esther 8:2 The king removed his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther made Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
Esther 8:3 Esther spoke to the king again, knelt at his feet, and cried, asking him to stop the evil plans of Haman the Agagite against the Jews.
Esther 8:4 The king reached out his gold staff to Esther. Then Esther got up and stood in front of the king.
Esther 8:5 She said, "If the king agrees and I have his favor, if he thinks it's the right thing to do and he is pleased with me, let an order be made to cancel the plans Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, made. He wrote these plans to kill the Jews in all the king's lands."
Esther 8:6 How can I bear to see the harm that will happen to my people, or watch my relatives be destroyed?
Esther 8:7 Then King Ahasuerus told Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, "Look, I have given Esther Haman's house, and they have hanged him because he attacked the Jews."
Esther 8:8 Write a letter for the Jews in the king's name as you wish, and seal it with the king's ring, because no one can change a letter written and sealed with the king's ring.
Esther 8:9 The king's writers were called in the third month, the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day. Everything Mordecai ordered was written for the Jews, the officials, and the leaders of the 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. Each province got the order in its own script and language, and so did the Jews in their script and language.
Esther 8:10 He wrote in King Ahasuerus' name, sealed it with the king's ring, and sent letters by messengers on horseback and riders on mules, camels, and young camels.
Esther 8:11 The king allowed the Jews in every city to unite and defend their lives, to kill and eliminate any group or region that attacked them, including children and women, and to take their belongings as loot.
Esther 8:12 On one day in all the areas ruled by King Ahasuerus, specifically on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month Adar.
Esther 8:13 The text of the order to be announced in every province was made known to everyone, so the Jews could prepare to defend themselves against their enemies on that day.
Esther 8:14 The messengers who rode on mules and camels left quickly, pushed by the king's order, and the law was announced in Shushan the palace.
Esther 8:15 Mordecai left the king dressed in blue and white royal clothes, with a big gold crown, and clothes of good linen and purple. The city of Shushan was happy and glad.
Esther 8:16 The Jews had brightness, happiness, joy, and respect.
Esther 8:17 In every region and city where the king's orders reached, the Jews felt joy and happiness, celebrated with a feast, and had a good day. Many local people became Jews because they were afraid of the Jews.

Esther 9:1 In the twelfth month, called Adar, on the thirteenth day, as the time for the king's command and law to be acted on came close, when the Jews' enemies hoped to control them, things changed so that the Jews gained power over those who hated them.
Esther 9:2 The Jews came together in their cities in all the king Ahasuerus's provinces to act against those who wanted to harm them, and no one could oppose them because everyone was afraid of them.
Esther 9:3 All the province leaders, assistants, officials, and the king's workers helped the Jews, because they were afraid of Mordecai.
Esther 9:4 Mordecai became very important in the king's palace, and his reputation spread through all the provinces: Mordecai became more and more respected.
Esther 9:5 The Jews defeated all their enemies with swords, killing and destroying them, and did as they pleased to those who hated them.
Esther 9:6 In the palace of Shushan, the Jews killed five hundred men.
Esther 9:7 Parshandatha, Dalphon, and Aspatha,
Esther 9:8 And Poratha, Adalia, and Aridatha,
Esther 9:9 And Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vajezatha,
Esther 9:10 They killed the ten sons of Haman, Hammedatha's son, who was an enemy of the Jews, but they did not take any of the loot.
Esther 9:11 On that day, they told the king how many people were killed in the palace of Shushan.
Esther 9:12 The king said to Queen Esther, "The Jews have killed five hundred men and Haman's ten sons in the palace at Shushan. What have they done in the other parts of the kingdom? Now, what do you want to ask for? It will be given to you. What more do you request? It will be done."
Esther 9:13 Then Esther said, "If the king agrees, let the Jews in Shushan have tomorrow to do as today's order allows, and hang Haman's ten sons on the gallows."
Esther 9:14 The king ordered it, and they announced the law in Shushan; they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
Esther 9:15 The Jews in Shushan came together on the fourteenth day of the month Adar and killed three hundred men in Shushan; however, they did not take any of the things that belonged to those they killed.
Esther 9:16 The other Jews in the king's lands came together, defended their lives, found peace from their enemies, and killed 75,000 of their foes, but they didn't take any of the spoils.
Esther 9:17 On the thirteenth day of the month Adar, and on the fourteenth day, they rested, and they made it a day of feasting and joy.
Esther 9:18 The Jewish people in Shushan gathered on the thirteenth day, and also on the fourteenth; then, on the fifteenth day, they rested and celebrated with a feast and joy.
Esther 9:19 So the Jews living in the villages and towns without walls celebrated the fourteenth day of the month Adar as a happy day with feasting and by giving food to each other.
Esther 9:20 Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Jews in every province of King Ahasuerus, near and far.
Esther 9:21 To make sure they celebrate the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar every year.
Esther 9:22 Like the days when the Jews had rest from their enemies, and when their sadness turned into happiness, and their grieving into celebration, they should make these days full of feasting and happiness, sharing food with each other, and giving presents to the poor.
Esther 9:23 The Jews agreed to continue the tradition they had started, just as Mordecai had instructed them.
Esther 9:24 Because Haman, son of Hammedatha the Agagite who was the enemy of all the Jews, planned to destroy the Jews and cast lots to finish them and wipe them out.
Esther 9:25 But when Esther approached the king, he ordered by letter that his evil plan against the Jews should backfire on him, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
Esther 9:26 That's why they named these days Purim after the word Pur. So because of everything written in this letter, what they had seen about this event, and what had happened to them,
Esther 9:27 The Jewish people decided and agreed, both they and their descendants, and all who would join them, to always observe these two days every year as written and at the set time.
Esther 9:28 These days must be remembered and celebrated by every generation, every family, every region, and every city. The days of Purim should never be forgotten by the Jews, nor should the memory of them disappear from their descendants.
Esther 9:29 Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to make sure this second Purim letter was accepted.
Esther 9:30 He sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of King Ahasuerus's kingdom, with messages of peace and truth.
Esther 9:31 To set these Purim days at their fixed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had told them to, and as they had decided for themselves and their descendants, about the fasts and their pleading.
Esther 9:32 Esther's order made Purim rules official, and they were written down.

Esther 10:1 The king Ahasuerus put a tax on the land and the islands of the sea.
Esther 10:2 Every powerful act and every display of his strength, along with the story of how great Mordecai became, which the king recognized, are all recorded in the history book of the kings of Media and Persia, aren't they?
Esther 10:3 Mordecai the Jew was close to King Ahasuerus, respected by many Jews, and he looked after the well-being of his people and promoted peace among them.

Job 1:1 In the land of Uz, there lived a man named Job. He was blameless and honest, feared God, and avoided evil.
Job 1:2 He had seven sons and three daughters.
Job 1:3 He also had seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a huge family. So he was the richest man in the east.
Job 1:4 His sons had parties in their own homes, each on his special day; and they invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
Job 1:5 When the feasting days were over, Job would make his children holy, get up early, and give burnt offerings for each one. He thought, "Maybe my sons have done wrong and thought bad things about God." Job did this all the time.
Job 1:6 One day, the children of God gathered in front of God, and Satan joined them too.
Job 1:7 God asked Satan, "Where do you come from?" Satan answered God, "I have been roaming around the earth, going back and forth on it."
Job 1:8 God said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth, a perfect and honest man who respects God and avoids evil."
Job 1:9 Then Satan replied to God, "Does Job respect God for nothing?"
Job 1:10 Haven't you protected him, his house, and everything he has on all sides? You have blessed what he does, and his wealth has grown in the land.
Job 1:11 Reach out now and strike everything he owns, and he will surely insult you to your face.
Job 1:12 God said to Satan, "Look, all he has is under your control; but do not hurt him." So Satan left God's presence.
Job 1:13 One day his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the oldest brother's house.
Job 1:14 A messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were eating nearby."
Job 1:15 The Sabeans attacked and captured them; they killed the workers with swords; I alone escaped to tell you.
Job 1:16 While he was still talking, another person came and said, "Fire from God fell from the sky and burned up the sheep and the workers, and I'm the only one who got away to tell you."
Job 1:17 While he was still talking, another person came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three groups, attacked the camels, took them, and also killed the workers with swords; only I have escaped to tell you."
Job 1:18 While he was still talking, another one came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house."
Job 1:19 Suddenly, a strong wind from the desert struck all four sides of the house, and it collapsed on the young men, and they died; I am the only one who got away to tell you.
Job 1:20 Then Job stood up, tore his robe, shaved his head, fell to the ground, and worshiped.
Job 1:21 I was born with nothing, and I will die with nothing: God gave, and God has taken away; praise God's name.
Job 1:22 In all this, Job did not sin or blame God wrongly.

Job 2:1 Once more, a time came when God's children appeared before God, and Satan also arrived with them to present himself before God.
Job 2:2 God asked Satan, "Where did you come from?" Satan replied to God, "I've been roaming around the earth and walking back and forth on it."
Job 2:3 God said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job? There's no one like him on earth. He's a perfect and honest man who respects God and stays away from evil. Yet he keeps his goodness, even though you convinced me to harm him for no reason."
Job 2:4 And Satan replied to God, "Surely one will give everything they have to save their own life."
Job 2:5 Reach out now and hurt his bones and flesh, and he will surely curse you to your face.
Job 2:6 God said to Satan, "Look, he is in your power, but spare his life."
Job 2:7 Satan left from being with God and gave Job painful sores from the bottom of his feet to the top of his head.
Job 2:8 He took a piece of broken pottery to scratch himself with and sat down in the ashes.
Job 2:9 His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your goodness? Curse God and die."
Job 2:10 He told her, "You talk like a foolish woman. Should we accept only good from God and not trouble?" Despite everything, Job did not say anything wrong.
Job 2:11 When Job's three friends learned about all the bad things that had happened to him, each came from his own home: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah. They had agreed to meet and go to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
Job 2:12 When they looked up and didn't recognize him from far away, they cried out loud, tore their clothes, and threw dust on their heads, looking up to the sky.
Job 2:13 They sat with him on the ground for seven days and nights without speaking because they saw his sorrow was very deep.

Job 3:1 After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
Job 3:2 Job spoke and said,
Job 3:3 Let the day I was born disappear, and the night that said, "A baby boy is conceived."
Job 3:4 Let that day be dark; may God not notice it from above, nor let light shine on it.
Job 3:5 Let darkness and death's shadow mark it; let a cloud cover it; let the day's darkness scare it.
Job 3:6 Let that night be dark; may it not be included among the days of the year or counted in the months.
Job 3:7 Look, let that night be alone, let no happy voice be heard in it.
Job 3:8 Let those who curse the day do so, those who are prepared to wake up their sadness.
Job 3:9 Let the stars of its dusk become dark; let it hope for light, yet find none; and let it not witness the break of dawn.
Job 3:10 Because it did not close the doors of my mother's womb or keep sadness from my eyes.
Job 3:11 Why didn't I die at birth? Why didn't I stop breathing when I was born?
Job 3:12 Why did I have knees to sit on, or breasts to feed from?
Job 3:13 By now, I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest.
Job 3:14 With leaders and advisors of the earth, who build ruined places for themselves;
Job 3:15 Or with leaders who had gold, who filled their homes with silver:
Job 3:16 Or I would have been like a baby born too early that never lived, as babies who never saw light.
Job 3:17 There the bad people stop causing trouble; and there the tired people rest.
Job 3:18 There the prisoners find peace; they do not hear the voice of the one who keeps them down.
Job 3:19 Both important and unimportant people are there; and the servant is no longer bound to their boss.
Job 3:20 Why is light given to those in misery, and life to those with bitter hearts?
Job 3:21 They want to die, but it doesn't happen; they search for death more eagerly than for hidden treasures.
Job 3:22 Who are very happy and glad when they find the grave?
Job 3:23 Why is light given to a person whose path is hidden, and whom God has surrounded?
Job 3:24 I sigh before I eat, and my loud cries flow like water.
Job 3:25 What I feared most has happened to me, and what I was scared of has come true.
Job 3:26 I was not safe, nor at rest, nor peaceful; still, trouble came.

Job 4:1 Then Eliphaz from Teman replied,
Job 4:2 If we try to talk with you, will you be upset? But who can stop themselves from speaking?
Job 4:3 Look, you have taught many people, and you have given strength to tired hands.
Job 4:4 Your words have supported the one who was falling, and you have made weak knees strong.
Job 4:5 Now it has happened to you, and you are weak; it affects you, and you are upset.
Job 4:6 Isn't this what you respect, what you trust, what you hope for, and how right you act?
Job 4:7 Please remember, who has ever died being innocent? Or when have the good people been destroyed?
Job 4:8 I have seen that those who do bad things and spread evil will get the same in return.
Job 4:9 With God's powerful breath, they are destroyed, and by his breath, they vanish.
Job 4:10 The lion's roar, the fierce lion's voice, and the young lions' teeth are all broken.
Job 4:11 The old lion dies because it has no food, and the strong lion's cubs are spread out far away.
Job 4:12 Someone secretly told me something, and I heard a bit of it.
Job 4:13 In thoughts from night visions, when deep sleep falls on people,
Job 4:14 I felt afraid and shook all over, making my bones tremble.
Job 4:15 Suddenly, a spirit moved in front of me, and the hair on my body stood up.
Job 4:16 It stood still, but I couldn't see its shape clearly: a figure was in front of my eyes, everything was quiet, and I heard a voice speaking.
Job 4:17 Can a human be more fair than God? Can someone be purer than the one who created him?
Job 4:18 Look, he doesn't trust his servants, and he accuses his angels of errors.
Job 4:19 How much less can those living in clay houses trust in themselves, when their very foundation is dust and they can be destroyed as easily as a moth?
Job 4:20 They are ruined from dawn to dusk; they vanish forever without anyone caring.
Job 4:21 Doesn't their greatness leave them? They die without wisdom.

Job 5:1 Call now; see if anyone will answer you; to which holy person will you turn?
Job 5:2 Anger kills the foolish person, and jealousy kills the naive one.
Job 5:3 I saw the fool grow strong, but quickly I said his home would fail.
Job 5:4 His children are not safe, they are beaten down at the city entrance, and no one is there to save them.
Job 5:5 The hungry eat what they harvest and take it from the thorns, while thieves consume their wealth.
Job 5:6 Trouble doesn't come from the dust, nor does problem grow from the ground.
Job 5:7 A person is born to face trouble, just like sparks rise up.
Job 5:8 I would ask God for help, and to God, I would entrust my problems.
Job 5:9 God does great things beyond understanding and countless wonders.
Job 5:10 God gives rain on the earth and sends water to the fields.
Job 5:11 To lift up those who are down and to raise those who grieve to a place of safety.
Job 5:12 He ruins the plans of the clever, so they can't succeed in what they do.
Job 5:13 God catches the clever in their tricks, and the plans of the deceitful rush to an end.
Job 5:14 They face darkness during the day and fumble at noon as if it were night.
Job 5:15 God saves the poor from violence, from being spoken against, and from the power of the strong.
Job 5:16 So the poor have hope, and wrongdoing is silenced.
Job 5:17 Look, the person whom God corrects is happy, so do not hate God's discipline.
Job 5:18 God causes pain and then heals; He injures, but His hands also heal.
Job 5:19 God will rescue you from six disasters; even in seven, no harm will come to you.
Job 5:20 In hunger, God will save you from death, and in battle, from the sword's force.
Job 5:21 You will be protected from harmful words, and you won't fear disaster when it arrives.
Job 5:22 When disaster and hunger come, you will laugh; you won't be scared of the earth's wild animals.
Job 5:23 You will have an agreement with the stones of the field: and the wild animals will be peaceful with you.
Job 5:24 You will know that your home will be safe; you will check on your place and will not do wrong.
Job 5:25 You will also know that your descendants will be many and your children will cover the earth like grass.
Job 5:26 You will reach old age and die, just like corn is harvested when it's ready.
Job 5:27 Look, we have checked this, so it is true; listen to it, and understand it for your benefit.

Job 6:1 But Job replied and spoke,
Job 6:2 I wish my sorrow could be fully measured, and my troubles put on scales at the same time.
Job 6:3 It's heavier than sea sand now; that's why I can't express my words.
Job 6:4 God's arrows are inside me, their poison drains my spirit; God's terrors line up against me.
Job 6:5 Does the wild donkey call out when it has grass? Or does the ox moo over its feed?
Job 6:6 Can you eat tasteless food without salt? Or is there any flavor in egg whites?
Job 6:7 The things I didn't want to touch now feel like my sad food.
Job 6:8 I wish I could get what I ask for, and that God would give me what I deeply desire.
Job 6:9 I wish God would decide to crush me, release his grip, and end my life.
Job 6:10 Then I would still be comforted. Even though I suffer, I would be brave. Let God not hold back, because I have not hidden the words of God.
Job 6:11 What strength do I have to hope? What is my future that I should extend my life?
Job 6:12 Am I as strong as rocks? Is my body made of bronze?
Job 6:13 Isn't my help within me? And has wisdom completely left me?
Job 6:14 A friend should be kind to someone who is suffering, but he ignores respecting God.
Job 6:15 My brothers have been as unreliable as a stream, like the water in streams that disappears.
Job 6:16 They are dark because of the ice, and snow is hidden in them.
Job 6:17 When they get warm, they disappear; when it's hot, they are gone from where they were.
Job 6:18 Their paths have changed direction; they lead to nowhere and end in destruction.
Job 6:19 The soldiers from Tema searched, and the groups from Sheba waited for them.
Job 6:20 They were confused because they had hope; they went there and felt embarrassed.
Job 6:21 You are now worth nothing; you see my downfall, and you are scared.
Job 6:22 Did I ask you to bring something to me or to give me a gift from what you own?
Job 6:23 Save me from my enemy’s grasp, or rescue me from the clutches of the powerful?
Job 6:24 Instruct me, and I will be quiet; show me where I have made mistakes.
Job 6:25 How powerful are true words! But what does your arguing prove?
Job 6:26 Do you think you can correct mere words when someone in despair speaks as if they are just wind?
Job 6:27 Yes, you overpower the orphans and trap your friend.
Job 6:28 So now, be satisfied and look at me; it is clear to you if I am lying.
Job 6:29 Please come back, don't think it's wrong; yes, come back, my goodness is in it.
Job 6:30 Is there wrongdoing in my words? Can't I tell what is wrong?

Job 7:1 Doesn't everyone have a set time to live on earth? Aren't their days like those of a worker?
Job 7:2 Like a worker who really wants rest, and like an employee eager for their pay.
Job 7:3 I am given months of emptiness and nights of trouble are set for me.
Job 7:4 When I go to bed, I think, "When will I get up and the night be over?" I am restless until morning comes.
Job 7:5 My body is covered with worms and dirt clumps; my skin is cracked and disgusting.
Job 7:6 My days go by faster than a weaver's tool, and they end without hope.
Job 7:7 Please remember my life is like the wind: I will not see happiness again.
Job 7:8 The person who has seen me won't see me again: you watch me, but I'm gone.
Job 7:9 Just like a cloud disappears and is gone, so is the person who dies and will not rise again.
Job 7:10 He will not go back to his home, and his place will not recognize him anymore.
Job 7:11 So I won't hold back my words; I will speak because my spirit is in pain; I will express my soul's deep sorrow.
Job 7:12 Am I the sea, or a big fish, that you keep watch over me?
Job 7:13 When I say, "My bed will comfort me, my sofa will soothe my worries,"
Job 7:14 You frighten me with dreams and scare me with visions.
Job 7:15 So my soul prefers suffocating, and death over my life.
Job 7:16 I hate it; I don't want to live forever: leave me alone; my days are pointless.
Job 7:17 Who is a person that you make so important and think so much about them?
Job 7:18 You visit him every morning and test him every moment?
Job 7:19 How long will you not leave me, or give me a moment's peace?
Job 7:20 I have sinned; what should I do to you, God, protector of people? Why have you made me your target, so that I am a problem to myself?
Job 7:21 Why don't you forgive my wrong and remove my sin? For soon I will lie in the earth; you will look for me in the morning, but I won't be there.

Job 8:1 Bildad the Shuhite replied, saying,
Job 8:2 How long will you keep talking like this? How long will your words blow like a strong wind?
Job 8:3 Does God twist fairness? Or does the Almighty twist what's right?
Job 8:4 If your children sinned against God, and he has rejected them for their wrongdoing;
Job 8:5 If you seek God early and pray to the All-powerful;
Job 8:6 If you were pure and honest, surely now God would act for you and make your righteous home successful.
Job 8:7 Even if you started small, your future will grow a lot.
Job 8:8 Please ask about the past, and get ready to learn from your ancestors.
Job 8:9 We have only been here for a short time and know very little, because our lives on earth are like a passing shadow.
Job 8:10 Won't they teach you, talk to you, and speak heartfelt words to you?
Job 8:11 Can reeds grow without mud? Can plants grow without water?
Job 8:12 While it is still green and not cut, it dries up before any other plant.
Job 8:13 The ways of all who forget God lead to nothing, and the fake person's hope will vanish.
Job 8:14 Those whose hope will get cut off, and who rely on something as weak as a spider's web.
Job 8:15 He will rely on his house, but it won't last; he will hold it tightly, but it won't remain.
Job 8:16 He thrives in the sunlight, and his branches spread out in his garden.
Job 8:17 His roots twist around the pile of rocks and reach into the stony ground.
Job 8:18 If he is destroyed from his place, then it will reject him, saying, I have never seen you.
Job 8:19 Look, this is the happiness of his path, and from the ground others will rise.
Job 8:20 Look, God will not reject a good person, nor will he support those who do wrong.
Job 8:21 Until he makes your mouth laugh and your lips shout with joy.
Job 8:22 Those who hate you will be covered with shame; the home of the evil will become nothing.

Job 9:1 Then Job replied and spoke,
Job 9:2 I know it's true: but how can a person be right with God?
Job 9:3 If he argues with God, he cannot reply to even one out of a thousand questions.
Job 9:4 He is smart in his heart and very strong: who has resisted him and succeeded?
Job 9:5 God moves the mountains without their knowing and turns them over in anger.
Job 9:6 God shakes the earth from its place, making its pillars tremble.
Job 9:7 Who commands the sun not to rise and seals the stars.
Job 9:8 Who alone stretches out the sky and walks on the sea's waves.
Job 9:9 God made the stars Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades and the hidden places of the south.
Job 9:10 God does great things beyond understanding and countless wonders.
Job 9:11 Look, he moves past me, but I don't see him; he goes by, but I don't notice him.
Job 9:12 Look, when God takes something, who can stop Him? Who will ask Him, "What are you doing?"
Job 9:13 If God does not stop being angry, the prideful supporters must bow down to him.
Job 9:14 How much less can I reply to God and carefully select my words to argue with Him?
Job 9:15 Even if I were right, I would not respond but ask for mercy from my judge.
Job 9:16 If I had called and he had answered me, I still wouldn't believe that he listened to my voice.
Job 9:17 He crushes me with a storm and gives me many wounds for no reason.
Job 9:18 He won't let me catch my breath, but fills me with sadness.
Job 9:19 If I talk about power, God is powerful; and if about fairness, who can schedule a time for my case?
Job 9:20 If I claim to be right, my own words will show I'm wrong: if I claim to be perfect, they will show I'm not.
Job 9:21 Even if I were perfect, I still would not understand myself; I would hate my life.
Job 9:22 I said this because God destroys both the good and the bad.
Job 9:23 If a disaster kills unexpectedly, God will mock when the innocent are tested.
Job 9:24 God has let wicked people control the earth; they hide the truth from its judges. If this isn't so, who else could it be?
Job 9:25 Now my days pass faster than a messenger: they rush by and see nothing good.
Job 9:26 They have gone by like fast ships, like an eagle swooping down on its food.
Job 9:27 If I decide to forget my troubles, to put aside my sadness, and to cheer myself up:
Job 9:28 I am scared of all my troubles; I know you will not find me innocent.
Job 9:29 If I am bad, why do I work for nothing?
Job 9:30 If I clean myself with snow and wash my hands very well;
Job 9:31 You will push me into a pit, and my own clothes will disgust me.
Job 9:32 He is not a person like me that I could reply to him or that we could meet in court.
Job 9:33 There is no mediator between us to put a hand on both of us.
Job 9:34 Let him stop using his rod on me, so his fear won't scare me.
Job 9:35 I would talk without being afraid of him; but that is not my situation.

Job 10:1 I am tired of my life; I will not hold back my complaints; I will speak from my heart's bitterness.
Job 10:2 I will tell God, "Do not judge me; tell me why you argue with me."
Job 10:3 Is it right for you to be unfair, to reject what you have created, and to favor the plans of the evil?
Job 10:4 Do you have human eyes? Or do you see as a person sees?
Job 10:5 Are your days like a human's days? Are your years like a person's years?
Job 10:6 You ask about my wrongs and search for my sins?
Job 10:7 You know I am not wicked; no one can rescue from your hand.
Job 10:8 Your hands made and shaped me completely; but now you are destroying me.
Job 10:9 Please remember you created me from clay; will you turn me back into dust?
Job 10:10 Did you not pour me out like milk and thicken me like cheese?
Job 10:11 You dressed me with skin and flesh, and built me with bones and muscles.
Job 10:12 You have given me life and kindness, and your care has kept my spirit safe.
Job 10:13 You have kept these things hidden in your heart; I know you understand this.
Job 10:14 If I do wrong, you notice it, and you will not clear me of my guilt.
Job 10:15 If I am evil, trouble is upon me; and if I am good, I still can't hold my head high. I am totally confused; so see my suffering.
Job 10:16 It grows. You chase me like a fierce lion, and then you do amazing things to me again.
Job 10:17 You create new evidence against me and grow angrier with me; changes and conflict oppose me.
Job 10:18 Why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before anyone saw me!
Job 10:19 I would have been like I never existed; I would have been taken from birth to the grave.
Job 10:20 Aren't my days short? Stop and leave me be, so I can have a little comfort.
Job 10:21 Before I go to a place I cannot come back from, to the land of darkness and death's shadow;
Job 10:22 A land of total darkness, like the deepest darkness; a place of death's shadow, without any order, where even the light is dark.

Job 11:1 Zophar from Naama replied, saying,
Job 11:2 Shouldn't many words get a reply? And should a chatty person be right?
Job 11:3 Do your lies make people stay silent? When you mock, doesn't anyone make you feel ashamed?
Job 11:4 You have said, "My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your sight."
Job 11:5 I wish God would speak and tell you off.
Job 11:6 God wants to show you the deep secrets of wisdom, which are twice as much as what exists. Understand then that God asks from you less than your wrongs deserve.
Job 11:7 Can you find out about God by searching? Can you fully understand the Almighty?
Job 11:8 It's as high as the sky; what can you do? It's deeper than the deepest place; what can you know?
Job 11:9 Its size is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
Job 11:10 If he decides, closes in, or brings together, then who can stop him?
Job 11:11 For he knows foolish people: he sees evil too; won't he think about it?
Job 11:12 Empty-headed people want to seem wise, even though they are born as wild as a donkey's foal.
Job 11:13 If you get your heart ready and reach out your hands to him;
Job 11:14 If you hold wrongdoing in your hand, put it far from you, and do not let evil live in your homes.
Job 11:15 You will be able to hold your head high without guilt; yes, you will be steady and without fear.
Job 11:16 You will forget your troubles, and think of them like water that has gone by.
Job 11:17 Your future will be brighter than midday: you will glow, you will be like the dawn.
Job 11:18 You will be safe because there is hope; yes, you will look around and lie down without fear.
Job 11:19 You will lie down without fear; many will come to ask for your favor.
Job 11:20 The wicked will lose their sight, won't get away, and their hope will vanish like a dying breath.

Job 12:1 Job answered, saying,
Job 12:2 You must be the people, and wisdom will die with you.
Job 12:3 I understand as much as you do; I am not less than you. Indeed, who doesn't know things like these?
Job 12:4 I am like someone mocked by their neighbor, who calls on God, and he answers: the honest, good person is made fun of.
Job 12:5 Someone who is about to fall is like a lamp that someone comfortable looks down on.
Job 12:6 Thieves live comfortably, and those who challenge God feel safe; into their hands, God gives plenty.
Job 12:7 Ask the animals, and they will teach you; ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
Job 12:8 Talk to the earth, it will teach you; and the fish in the sea will tell you.
Job 12:9 Everyone knows that God has done all this.
Job 12:10 God holds the life of every creature and the breath of all people.
Job 12:11 Doesn't the ear test words? And the mouth taste its food?
Job 12:12 Old people have wisdom; with many years comes understanding.
Job 12:13 He has wisdom and power; he gives advice and understanding.
Job 12:14 Look, he destroys, and it cannot be rebuilt; he imprisons a person, and there can be no escape.
Job 12:15 Look, he stops the waters, and they dry up; he also sends them out, and they flood the land.
Job 12:16 He has power and knowledge: both the tricked and the trickster belong to him.
Job 12:17 He leads advisors away as captives and turns judges into fools.
Job 12:18 He frees kings from their chains and ties a belt around their waists.
Job 12:19 He leads rulers away defeated, and overthrows the powerful.
Job 12:20 God takes away the speech of the reliable and removes the wisdom of the old.
Job 12:21 God shows scorn for rulers and reduces the power of the strong.
Job 12:22 He reveals deep truths from darkness and brings the shadow of death into the light.
Job 12:23 He makes nations grow, and then destroys them; he expands nations, and then reduces them.
Job 12:24 God removes the understanding of the world's leaders and makes them wander in a place without paths.
Job 12:25 They feel around in the dark with no light, and he causes them to stumble like a drunk person.

Job 13:1 I have seen all this with my eyes; my ears have heard and understood it.
Job 13:2 I know what you know; I am not less than you.
Job 13:3 I want to talk to God Almighty, and I wish to discuss with God.
Job 13:4 You create lies and your healing is worthless.
Job 13:5 I wish you would all be completely quiet! It would be wise for you.
Job 13:6 Listen to my arguments and pay attention to what I say.
Job 13:7 Will you speak wrongly for God and talk with lies for him?
Job 13:8 Will you favor him? Will you argue for God?
Job 13:9 Is it right for him to investigate you? Like one person teases another, do you tease him?
Job 13:10 God will certainly correct you if you unfairly favor some people in secret.
Job 13:11 Won't his greatness scare you? And his fear come on you?
Job 13:12 Your memories are like ashes, your forms like clay.
Job 13:13 Stay quiet, leave me be, so I can talk, and whatever happens, let it happen.
Job 13:14 Why do I risk my life and take my own life into my hands?
Job 13:15 Even if he kills me, I will still trust in God; but I will defend my own actions to him.
Job 13:16 He will also be my savior, because a hypocrite will not come before Him.
Job 13:17 Listen carefully to what I say and hear my explanation with your ears.
Job 13:18 Look, I have prepared my case; I know I will be proven right.
Job 13:19 Who will argue with me? For if I stay silent now, I will die.
Job 13:20 Please don't do two things to me; then I won't hide from you.
Job 13:21 Stop punishing me, and don't scare me anymore.
Job 13:22 Then you call, and I will answer; or let me talk, and you reply to me.
Job 13:23 What are my wrongs and sins? Show me what I have done wrong and my sin.
Job 13:24 Why do you hide your face and treat me like your enemy?
Job 13:25 Will you break a leaf blown back and forth? And will you chase the dry straw?
Job 13:26 You write harsh things against me and make me inherit the sins of my youth.
Job 13:27 You put my feet in chains and watch all my ways closely; you leave a mark on the soles of my feet.
Job 13:28 He decays like something rotten, like clothing eaten by moths.

Job 14:1 A person born from a woman lives only a short time and has many problems.
Job 14:2 He blooms like a flower and then is trimmed. He also flees like a shadow and does not stay.
Job 14:3 Do you watch such a person and bring me to trial with you?
Job 14:4 Who can make a clean thing from an unclean one? No one.
Job 14:5 God has set the number of his days, and knows how many months he will live. You have decided his limits, which he cannot go beyond.
Job 14:6 Let him alone so he can have peace until he finishes his workday like a worker.
Job 14:7 A tree has hope because if it's cut down, it can grow back, and its new shoots won't stop.
Job 14:8 Even if its roots grow old in the earth and its stump dies in the ground;
Job 14:9 Even if it smells water, it will sprout and grow branches like a plant.
Job 14:10 When a person dies, they decay; when they stop breathing, where do they go?
Job 14:11 As the water disappears from the sea, and a riverbed becomes dry and empty:
Job 14:12 People lie down and do not rise again; until the sky is gone, they will not wake up or be woken from their sleep.
Job 14:13 I wish you would hide me in the grave and keep me hidden until your anger is over, then set a time to remember me.
Job 14:14 If someone dies, will they live again? I will wait for all the days set for me until it is my turn to change.
Job 14:15 You will call, and I will answer you; you will long for what your hands have made.
Job 14:16 You count my steps now; are you not keeping watch on my sin?
Job 14:17 My wrong is locked in a bag, and you stitch up my sin.
Job 14:18 Mountains crumble and disappear, and rocks are moved from their spots.
Job 14:19 Water wears down stones; you wash away the soil's growth; you crush human hopes.
Job 14:20 You always win against him, and he goes away; you change his face, and send him off.
Job 14:21 His sons achieve honor but he doesn't know it; they are humbled, yet he doesn't notice.
Job 14:22 His body will feel pain, and his heart will be sad.

Job 15:1 Eliphaz from Teman replied and said.
Job 15:2 Should a wise person speak empty words and fill themselves with useless thoughts?
Job 15:3 Should he argue with useless words or speak where he can do no good?
Job 15:4 Yes, you throw away respect and stop praying to God.
Job 15:5 Your mouth speaks your wrongs, and you talk like a tricky person.
Job 15:6 Your own words condemn you, not me; your own lips speak against you.
Job 15:7 Are you the first man who was born? Or were you created before the hills?
Job 15:8 Have you heard God's secret? And do you keep wisdom to yourself?
Job 15:9 What do you know that we don't? What do you understand that we don't have in us?
Job 15:10 With us are old men with gray hair, much older than your father.
Job 15:11 Is God's comfort unimportant to you? Is there something you are hiding?
Job 15:12 Why does your heart lead you astray? And what are your eyes signaling?
Job 15:13 Are you turning against God and letting such words come out of your mouth?
Job 15:14 Who is a person, that they can be pure? And someone born of a woman, that they can be right?
Job 15:15 Look, God does not fully trust his holy ones; even the skies are not pure in his eyes.
Job 15:16 How much more disgusting and dirty is a person, who drinks up wrong like water?
Job 15:17 I will show you, listen to me; and I will tell you what I have seen.
Job 15:18 Wise people shared wisdom from their ancestors and did not hide it.
Job 15:19 God gave the earth to them alone, and no outsider went among them.
Job 15:20 The bad person suffers through all his days, and the years he will live are unknown to the bully.
Job 15:21 He hears terrifying noises: even when he's doing well, destruction will hit him.
Job 15:22 He doesn't believe he will escape from darkness, and he is expected to meet the sword.
Job 15:23 He roams around looking for bread, asking, "Where is it?" He knows that times of trouble are close by.
Job 15:24 Worry and distress will scare him; they will overcome him, like a king prepared for battle.
Job 15:25 He reaches out his hand against God, and makes himself strong against the Almighty.
Job 15:26 He charges at him, right at his neck, on the thick parts of his shields.
Job 15:27 Because he covers his face with his fat and gets layers of fat on his sides.
Job 15:28 He lives in empty cities, in houses where no one lives, that are about to turn into ruins.
Job 15:29 He will not become rich, his wealth will not last, nor will he keep its success on earth.
Job 15:30 He will not escape the darkness; the fire will wither his branches, and he will be gone with a puff of breath.
Job 15:31 Don't let the person who is fooled trust in things that have no value, because they will only get emptiness in return.
Job 15:32 It will happen before its time, and its sprout will not be green.
Job 15:33 He will lose his young grapes like a vine, and drop his blossoms like an olive tree.
Job 15:34 The group of fakes will be left empty, and fire will burn down the tents of the corrupt.
Job 15:35 They plan trouble, give birth to empty promises, and their hearts breed lies.

Job 16:1 Then Job replied and spoke,
Job 16:2 I have heard many things like this: you are all terrible at comforting.
Job 16:3 Will empty talk ever stop? What makes you so bold to answer?
Job 16:4 I could talk like you if I were in your place. I could make many accusations against you and shake my head at you.
Job 16:5 I would encourage you with my words, and my talking would ease your sadness.
Job 16:6 Even if I talk, my sadness isn't lessened; and if I stay quiet, how am I comforted?
Job 16:7 But now he has made me tired: you have left all my friends alone.
Job 16:8 You have covered me with wrinkles, which stand as proof against me; my thinness is a testimony to my face.
Job 16:9 He violently attacks me in his anger, hating me; he grinds his teeth at me; my enemy glares at me with sharp eyes.
Job 16:10 They opened their mouths wide at me; they slapped my face in insult; they joined together against me.
Job 16:11 God has given me to the bad people, and put me into the hands of the evil ones.
Job 16:12 I was comfortable, but God has torn me apart; He has grabbed my neck and shattered me, and made me a target.
Job 16:13 His archers surround me, he splits my insides apart, and shows no mercy; he spills my bile on the ground.
Job 16:14 He shatters me, breaking me over and over; he charges at me like a giant.
Job 16:15 I have put rough cloth on my skin, and put my strength in the dirt.
Job 16:16 I cry so much my face is dirty, and my eyelids are dark like death.
Job 16:17 I have done nothing wrong, and my prayer is sincere.
Job 16:18 Earth, do not hide my blood, and do not let my cry go unheard.
Job 16:19 Even now, my witness is in heaven, and my evidence is up high.
Job 16:20 My friends mock me, but I cry to God.
Job 16:21 I wish someone could talk to God for a person, just as someone argues for a friend.
Job 16:22 In a few years, I will go on a path from which I won't come back.

Job 17:1 My breath is bad, my days are over, the graves wait for me.
Job 17:2 Aren't there people who mock me around? And doesn't my eye endure their insults?
Job 17:3 Lie down now, make a promise with me; who will agree and shake hands with me?
Job 17:4 You have kept their heart from understanding; so you will not lift them up.
Job 17:5 Whoever uses smooth talk with friends will find even their children's eyes will fail.
Job 17:6 He has made me a joke among the people; before, I was like a drum.
Job 17:7 My eyes are weak from sadness, and my whole body is like a shadow.
Job 17:8 Good people will be shocked at this, and the honest will stand up against the fake.
Job 17:9 Good people will stay on their path, and those with pure actions will become stronger and stronger.
Job 17:10 But all of you, come back now: I can't find one wise person among you.
Job 17:11 My days are gone, my plans are shattered, and so are the hopes of my heart.
Job 17:12 They turn night into day: daylight ends quickly because of the dark.
Job 17:13 If I wait, the grave becomes my home; I have prepared my bed in the dark.
Job 17:14 I told decay, "You are my father." To the worm, "You are my mother and my sister."
Job 17:15 Where is my hope now? Who will see my hope?
Job 17:16 They will go to the gates of the grave when we all rest in the dust together.

Job 18:1 Bildad the Shuhite replied and said,
Job 18:2 How long until you stop talking? Pay attention, and then we will speak.
Job 18:3 Why are we treated like animals and considered disgusting to you?
Job 18:4 He hurts himself in his anger: should the world be abandoned for you? And should the stone be moved from its spot?
Job 18:5 Yes, the wicked's light will go out, and their fire's spark won't shine.
Job 18:6 The light in his tent will become dark, and his lamp will go out with him.
Job 18:7 His strong steps will become tight, and his own plans will make him fall.
Job 18:8 He is trapped in a net by his own steps and walks on a trap.
Job 18:9 A trap will catch him by the foot, and a thief will defeat him.
Job 18:10 A trap is set for him on the ground, and a snare is in his path.
Job 18:11 Fears will scare him from all around and make him run away.
Job 18:12 His strength will be weakened by hunger, and ruin will stand by his side.
Job 18:13 It will eat away the power of his skin; death's firstborn will consume his power.
Job 18:14 His trust will be pulled up from his home, and it will take him to the king of fears.
Job 18:15 It will live in its tent, for it is not its own; sulfur will be spread over its home.
Job 18:16 His roots will dry up below, and his branches will be cut off above.
Job 18:17 People will forget him on earth, and his name will not be spoken in public.
Job 18:18 He will be forced from light to darkness, and driven away from the world.
Job 18:19 He won't have a son or nephew among his people, or anyone left in his home.
Job 18:20 Those who follow him will be amazed at his time, just as those before were terrified.
Job 18:21 These are surely the homes of the evil, and this is where someone who does not know God lives.

Job 19:1 Then Job replied and spoke,
Job 19:2 How long will you trouble me and crush me with your words?
Job 19:3 You have insulted me ten times; you're not ashamed that you've been treating me like a stranger.
Job 19:4 If I have truly made a mistake, it stays with me.
Job 19:5 If you really want to act superior to me and argue against my disgrace:
Job 19:6 Understand that God has defeated me and has surrounded me with his net.
Job 19:7 I shout because of injustice, but no one listens; I cry out, but there is no fairness.
Job 19:8 God has blocked my path so I can't get through, and has made my ways dark.
Job 19:9 He has taken away my honor and removed the crown from my head.
Job 19:10 God has destroyed me on every side, and I am gone; and he has taken away my hope like a tree.
Job 19:11 He has also ignited his anger against me, and he considers me as one of his enemies.
Job 19:12 His soldiers gather, march against me, and camp around my tent.
Job 19:13 He has made my brothers stay away from me, and my friends have truly become strangers to me.
Job 19:14 My relatives have let me down, and my close friends have ignored me.
Job 19:15 Those who live in my house and my servants see me as a stranger; I am like a foreigner to them.
Job 19:16 I called my worker, but he did not respond; I pleaded with him aloud.
Job 19:17 My wife is disgusted by my breath, even though I pleaded for the sake of my own children.
Job 19:18 Even young children looked down on me; when I stood up, they talked against me.
Job 19:19 All my close friends hate me, and those I loved have turned against me.
Job 19:20 My bones stick to my skin and flesh, and I barely escaped with my life.
Job 19:21 Feel sorry for me, my friends, because God has struck me.
Job 19:22 Why do you attack me like God does, and aren't happy with just hurting my body?
Job 19:23 I wish my words were written down! I wish they were recorded in a book!
Job 19:24 They were carved with an iron tool and filled with lead in the rock forever.
Job 19:25 I know that my savior is alive, and he will stand on the earth on the last day.
Job 19:26 Even after my skin is eaten by worms and my body is gone, I will still see God with my own body.
Job 19:27 I will see God myself, my own eyes will look at him, and not a stranger's; even if I am wasting away inside.
Job 19:28 But you should ask, "Why do we persecute him, when the heart of the problem lies within me?"
Job 19:29 Be afraid of the sword: anger brings sword punishments, so you know there is a judgment.

Job 20:1 Zophar from Naamath spoke and said,
Job 20:2 So my thoughts make me reply quickly.
Job 20:3 I have heard the criticism against me, and my insight makes me respond.
Job 20:4 Don't you know this from long ago, since the time humans were put on earth?
Job 20:5 The success of the wicked is brief, and the happiness of the dishonest lasts only a moment.
Job 20:6 Even if he becomes very important and his pride reaches the sky,
Job 20:7 He will die forever like his waste; those who saw him will ask, "Where is he?"
Job 20:8 He will vanish like a dream and not be found; he will be driven away like a night vision.
Job 20:9 The eye that saw him will never see him again; his place will no longer see him.
Job 20:10 His kids will try to help the poor, and his hands will give back their things.
Job 20:11 His bones carry the sins of his youth, which will go down with him to the dirt.
Job 20:12 Even if wrongdoing tastes sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue;
Job 20:13 Even if he doesn't hurt it but leaves it in his mouth without letting it go:
Job 20:14 The food in his stomach has changed; it is like snake poison inside him.
Job 20:15 He has consumed wealth, and he will spit it out again: God will force it from his stomach.
Job 20:16 He will suck the snake's poison: the viper's tongue will kill him.
Job 20:17 He will not see the rivers, the floods, or the streams of honey and cream.
Job 20:18 He must give back what he worked for and cannot keep it; he will return an amount equal to his wealth, but he will not be happy about it.
Job 20:19 Because he hurt and left the poor; because he took a house by force that he did not build.
Job 20:20 He will not find peace within, nor keep what he wanted.
Job 20:21 All his food will be gone; so no one will search for his possessions.
Job 20:22 When he feels most secure, he will be in trouble; every hand of the wicked will attack him.
Job 20:23 When he's about to eat, God will throw his anger at him and make it fall on him as he eats.
Job 20:24 He will run from the iron weapon, and a steel bow will shoot him.
Job 20:25 It is pulled out, and comes from the body; yes, the shiny sword comes from his liver: fears are on him.
Job 20:26 Darkness will hide in his hidden places; a fire not fanned will eat him up; things will go badly for anyone remaining in his tent.
Job 20:27 The sky will show his wrongs; and the ground will stand against him.
Job 20:28 His wealth will disappear, and his possessions will be lost when God is angry.
Job 20:29 This is what a bad person gets from God, the share given to him by God.

Job 21:1 Job replied,
Job 21:2 Listen carefully to what I say, and let this comfort you.
Job 21:3 Let me speak, and after I have spoken, you can mock me.
Job 21:4 Do I complain to people? If that's true, shouldn't I be upset?
Job 21:5 Listen to me, be amazed, and put your hand over your mouth.
Job 21:6 When I think about it, I get scared, and my body starts to shake.
Job 21:7 Why do bad people live long, grow old, and become very strong?
Job 21:8 Their children are secure with them, and they can see their grandchildren.
Job 21:9 Their homes are safe and not afraid, and God's punishment does not touch them.
Job 21:10 Their bull mates without failing; their cow gives birth and does not miscarry.
Job 21:11 They send out their young like a herd, and their kids dance.
Job 21:12 They play tambourines and harps, and are happy to hear the organ's music.
Job 21:13 They live in riches all their days, but suddenly they die.
Job 21:14 So they tell God to go away, because they don't want to know His ways.
Job 21:15 Who is God that we should serve Him? And what do we gain by praying to Him?
Job 21:16 Look, they have no control over their own welfare; I stay away from the plans of the wicked.
Job 21:17 How often is the wicked person's light extinguished! And how often does ruin fall upon them! God gives out sadness in his anger.
Job 21:18 They are like straw in the wind, and like husks that the storm blows away.
Job 21:19 God saves up the wrongs of someone for their children: He punishes them, and they will realize it.
Job 21:20 He will see his own ruin and drink from God's anger.
Job 21:21 Why would he enjoy his house after he's gone if his life is cut short?
Job 21:22 Can anyone teach God knowledge, since He judges even the powerful?
Job 21:23 Someone dies in their prime, feeling completely peaceful and relaxed.
Job 21:24 His chest is full of milk, and his bones are wet with marrow.
Job 21:25 Another person dies feeling bitter and never enjoys their food.
Job 21:26 They will all rest in the ground, and worms will cover them.
Job 21:27 Look, I know what you are thinking and the plans you are wrongly making against me.
Job 21:28 You ask, "Where is the prince's house? And where do the wicked live?"
Job 21:29 Have you not asked those who pass by? And do you not recognize the signs they know?
Job 21:30 The wicked are kept for the day of destruction; they will be taken to the day of anger.
Job 21:31 Who will tell him what he has done to his face? Who will pay him back for his actions?
Job 21:32 He will be taken to the grave and stay in the tomb.
Job 21:33 The lumps of earth in the valley will be dear to him, and everyone will follow him, just as countless have gone before him.
Job 21:34 So how can you comfort me with nonsense, when your answers are full of lies?

Job 22:1 Then Eliphaz from Teman replied,
Job 22:2 Can a person be useful to God, as a wise person is useful to themselves?
Job 22:3 Does it make God happy when you are good, or does He benefit when you live perfectly?
Job 22:4 Will God correct you because he fears you? Will he go to court with you?
Job 22:5 Isn't your evilness huge? And your sins endless?
Job 22:6 You took a promise from your brother for no reason and took clothes from those with none.
Job 22:7 You did not give water to the tired to drink, and you kept bread from the hungry.
Job 22:8 The strong person owned the land, and the respected person lived on it.
Job 22:9 You sent widows away with nothing, and you have crushed the strength of orphans.
Job 22:10 So traps surround you, and sudden fear upsets you.
Job 22:11 Or darkness, so you can't see, and lots of water covers you.
Job 22:12 Isn't God in the highest part of heaven? And see how high the stars are!
Job 22:13 And you ask, "How does God know? Can he judge behind the dark cloud?"
Job 22:14 Dense clouds hide God so he cannot be seen; and he moves in the sky's expanse.
Job 22:15 Have you noticed the old path that bad people have walked on?
Job 22:16 They were cut down too soon, and their foundation was washed away by a flood.
Job 22:17 They told God to go away: and what can God do for them?
Job 22:18 He filled their homes with good things, but I stay away from the plans of the wicked.
Job 22:19 Good people see it and are happy; those who are not guilty mock them.
Job 22:20 Our resources are not destroyed, but the fire burns what's left of them.
Job 22:21 Get to know God now and find peace; this will bring you goodness.
Job 22:22 Please accept the teachings from God, and keep his words in your heart.
Job 22:23 If you come back to God, you will be restored, and you will keep sin far from your home.
Job 22:24 You will pile up gold like dust, and the gold of Ophir like pebbles from the streams.
Job 22:25 Yes, God will protect you, and you will have lots of silver.
Job 22:26 Then you will find joy in God and you can look up to Him with confidence.
Job 22:27 Pray to God, and he will listen to you, and you must keep your promises.
Job 22:28 You will decide on something, and it will happen for you: light will shine on your path.
Job 22:29 When people feel defeated, you should say, "There is hope"; and God will save the humble.
Job 22:30 He will save the land of the innocent; it is saved because of your clean hands.

Job 23:1 Then Job replied,
Job 23:2 Today my complaint is harsh; my suffering is worse than my groans.
Job 23:3 I wish I knew where to find God so I could go to where he is.
Job 23:4 I would explain my case to God and give many reasons to support it.
Job 23:5 I want to know the words he would reply with, and understand what he would tell me.
Job 23:6 Would he argue with me using his great power? No; instead, he would give me strength.
Job 23:7 There, good people could argue with God; so I would be saved forever from my judge.
Job 23:8 I look ahead, but he's not there; I look behind, but I can't see him.
Job 23:9 On the left side, where he works, I cannot see him; he hides on the right side so I cannot find him.
Job 23:10 God knows the path I follow; when he has tested me, I will come out like gold.
Job 23:11 I have followed his path without turning away.
Job 23:12 I have not turned away from what God commands; I value his words more than my daily bread.
Job 23:13 He has one plan, and no one can change it. Whatever he wants to do, he does.
Job 23:14 He does what he has planned for me, and he has many more things like this.
Job 23:15 So, when I feel God's presence, I get disturbed; when I think about it, I become scared of Him.
Job 23:16 God makes my heart gentle, and the Almighty disturbs me.
Job 23:17 Because I was not taken away before the darkness, nor has he hidden the darkness from my face.

Job 24:1 Why, if God knows all time, do those who know him not recognize his days?
Job 24:2 Some people move boundary stones; they forcefully steal herds of animals and eat from them.
Job 24:3 They chase away the orphan's donkey and take the widow's ox as collateral.
Job 24:4 They push the needy off the road; the world's poor all hide away.
Job 24:5 Look, like wild donkeys in the desert, they go out to work; they get up early to find food: the wild land provides food for them and their children.
Job 24:6 Everyone harvests their grain in the field, and they collect the wicked's grapes.
Job 24:7 They make the naked sleep without clothes, so they have no cover when it's cold.
Job 24:8 They are soaked by the mountain rains and hug the rocks because they have no shelter.
Job 24:9 They snatch away the orphans and demand collateral from the poor.
Job 24:10 They make him go without clothes and take the bundle of grain from the hungry.
Job 24:11 They make oil inside their cities, press their grapes for wine, and still feel thirsty.
Job 24:12 People groan in the city, and the hurt souls cry out; but God does not charge them with wrongdoing.
Job 24:13 They are among those who resist the light; they do not know its ways or stay on its paths.
Job 24:14 The killer gets up at dawn to kill the poor and needy, and at night he acts like a thief.
Job 24:15 The one who is unfaithful with their partner waits for night, thinking no one will see them, and covers their face.
Job 24:16 At night they break into houses they had picked out in the day; they do not know the light.
Job 24:17 Morning feels like the shadow of death to them; when recognized, they are terrified by this shadow of death.
Job 24:18 He is fast like the rivers; their land is cursed on the earth: he does not see the path of the vineyards.
Job 24:19 Dryness and warmth dry up the snow's water; just as the grave takes those who have sinned.
Job 24:20 The body will forget him; worms will eat him up; he will not be remembered; and evil will be broken like a tree.
Job 24:21 He treats the childless woman badly and does not help the widow.
Job 24:22 He pulls in the strong with his power: he stands up, and nobody can be sure of living.
Job 24:23 Even if someone feels safe and relaxed, God still watches their actions.
Job 24:24 They are raised up for a short time, but then they vanish and are brought down; they are removed just like everyone else, and cut off like the tops of the stalks of grain.
Job 24:25 If this is not true now, who will prove me wrong and show that my words are worthless?

Job 25:1 Bildad the Shuhite replied and said,
Job 25:2 God has power and is respected; he makes peace in his heavens.
Job 25:3 Can anyone count his armies? And who doesn't his light shine on?
Job 25:4 How can a person be right with God? How can someone born of a woman be pure?
Job 25:5 Look at the moon, it does not glow; even the stars are not clean in God's eyes.
Job 25:6 How much less is a person, a worm, and a human being, who is also a worm?

Job 26:1 But Job replied and spoke,
Job 26:2 How have you helped the person with no power? How can you save the arm that has no strength?
Job 26:3 How have you advised someone who lacks wisdom? And how have you fully explained the situation as it is?
Job 26:4 Who did you speak to? And who inspired your words?
Job 26:5 Dead things take shape beneath the waters, and those that live there.
Job 26:6 God sees everything in hell, and nothing can hide destruction.
Job 26:7 He stretches out the north over empty space and hangs the earth on nothing.
Job 26:8 He gathers water into his heavy clouds, and the clouds don't break under the weight.
Job 26:9 He covers his throne and puts a cloud over it.
Job 26:10 He has set limits for the waters, until the time when day and night end.
Job 26:11 Heaven's pillars shake and are amazed at his scolding.
Job 26:12 He splits the sea with his strength, and with his wisdom, he defeats the arrogant.
Job 26:13 By his Spirit, he made the skies beautiful; his hand shaped the twisted snake.
Job 26:14 Look, these are some of his actions, but we hear only a small part about him. Who can grasp the greatness of his power?

Job 27:1 Job kept on speaking his story, and said,
Job 27:2 God lives, who has taken away my justice; and the Almighty, who has troubled my soul.
Job 27:3 As long as I breathe, and God's breath is in my nose;
Job 27:4 I will not speak evil, nor will my tongue tell lies.
Job 27:5 I would never agree with you; I will keep my honesty until I die.
Job 27:6 I keep to my righteousness and will not give it up; my heart will not blame me as long as I live.
Job 27:7 Let my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who attacks me be like the unjust.
Job 27:8 What hope does a fake person have, even if they are rich, when God takes their life?
Job 27:9 Will God listen to him when he calls for help during trouble?
Job 27:10 Does he enjoy the Almighty? Will he constantly ask for God's help?
Job 27:11 I will teach you by God's power; I won't hide what is with the Almighty.
Job 27:12 Look, you have all seen it yourselves; so why do you continue to act so foolishly?
Job 27:13 This is what a bad person gets from God, and what bullies will get from the All-Powerful.
Job 27:14 If he has many children, they are for death, and his descendants will not have enough food.
Job 27:15 The ones left of him will be buried when they die, and his widows won't cry.
Job 27:16 Even if he piles up silver like dust and stores up clothes like dirt,
Job 27:17 He might make it ready, but good people will wear it, and those who did nothing wrong will share the money.
Job 27:18 He builds his house like a moth, and like a temporary shelter put up by a caretaker.
Job 27:19 The rich man will lie down but won't be picked up again; he opens his eyes, and he's gone.
Job 27:20 Fears grip him like water, a storm sweeps him away at night.
Job 27:21 The east wind takes him away, and he goes; a storm throws him out of his place.
Job 27:22 God will throw down on him and will not hold back; he really wants to escape from his power.
Job 27:23 People will clap their hands at him and boo him from his spot.

Job 28:1 Surely there is a source for silver and a place where gold is refined.
Job 28:2 Iron comes from the ground, and copper is melted from the rock.
Job 28:3 He ends the darkness and explores every detail: the dark rocks and the shadow of death.
Job 28:4 The flood bursts out from where people live; the waters, once stepped in and forgotten, have dried up and disappeared from human presence.
Job 28:5 The earth gives us bread, and beneath it is heat like fire.
Job 28:6 Its rocks are where sapphires are found, and it has particles of gold.
Job 28:7 There is a path unknown to birds, and unseen by the vulture's eye.
Job 28:8 Young lions have not walked on it, nor has the strong lion crossed over it.
Job 28:9 He reaches out his hand to the rock; he flips the mountains from their base.
Job 28:10 He carves out rivers in the rocks, and his eye sees every valuable thing.
Job 28:11 He stops the rivers from flooding; and he brings hidden things into the light.
Job 28:12 Where can wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?
Job 28:13 No one knows its value; it cannot be found in the land of the living.
Job 28:14 The deep says, 'It's not in me,' and the sea says, 'It's not with me.'
Job 28:15 It can't be bought with gold, nor can you weigh silver to pay for it.
Job 28:16 It can't be compared to Ophir's gold, valuable onyx, or sapphires.
Job 28:17 Gold and crystal are not its equal: you cannot swap it for any gold jewelry.
Job 28:18 People will not talk about coral or pearls; wisdom is worth more than rubies.
Job 28:19 Ethiopia's topaz won't match it, nor can it be compared to fine gold.
Job 28:20 Where does wisdom come from? And where can we find understanding?
Job 28:21 It is hidden from all living creatures and kept secret from the birds in the sky.
Job 28:22 Destruction and death say, "We have heard of its fame with our ears."
Job 28:23 God understands its way and knows its place.
Job 28:24 He looks to the earth's ends and sees everything under the sky.
Job 28:25 To set the weight for the winds; and he measures the waters by amount.
Job 28:26 When he set rules for the rain and a path for the thunder's lightning:
Job 28:27 He saw it, explained it, got it ready, and thoroughly examined it.
Job 28:28 To people he said, "Look, respecting God is wisdom, and avoiding evil is understanding."

Job 29:1 Job kept on speaking in his story, and said,
Job 29:2 I wish I were back in the old days when God took care of me;
Job 29:3 When his light glowed above me, and I walked in the dark by his light;
Job 29:4 When I was young and God's friendship was with me in my home;
Job 29:5 When God was still with me and my children were around me;
Job 29:6 When I washed my feet with cream, and the stones gave me streams of oil;
Job 29:7 When I went through the city to the gate, when I set up my seat in the public square!
Job 29:8 The young men saw me and hid, while the older men stood up in respect.
Job 29:9 The leaders stopped speaking and put their hand over their mouth.
Job 29:10 The important people stayed quiet, and their tongue stuck to the top of their mouth.
Job 29:11 When people heard me, they praised me; when they saw me, they approved of me.
Job 29:12 I helped the poor who called out, the orphan, and the person who had no one to help them.
Job 29:13 The blessing of someone close to death came to me; and I made the widow's heart joyful.
Job 29:14 I wore what was right, and it covered me: my fairness was like a robe and a crown.
Job 29:15 I was eyes for the blind and feet for the lame.
Job 29:16 I was like a father to the poor and I investigated issues that I did not know about.
Job 29:17 I broke the wicked's jaw and took away the stolen goods from his teeth.
Job 29:18 Then I said, I will die peacefully at home, and live as long as the grains of sand.
Job 29:19 My roots stretched out to the water, and the dew stayed on my branches all night.
Job 29:20 My honor was strong within me, and my strength was restored in my grip.
Job 29:21 People listened to me, waited, and stayed quiet for my advice.
Job 29:22 After I spoke, they did not reply; my words fell on them.
Job 29:23 They waited for me like for the rain; and they opened their mouths wide for the late rain.
Job 29:24 If I smiled at them, they did not trust it; they did not make my happy face sad.
Job 29:25 I picked their path, sat as the leader, and lived like a king among the troops, comforting those who grieve.

Job 30:1 Now, younger people mock me, people whose fathers I wouldn't have let sit with my sheepdogs.
Job 30:2 Yes, how could the strength of their hands help me, when they were worn out by old age?
Job 30:3 They were alone, suffering from hunger and need; they ran away to the empty, barren wilderness long ago.
Job 30:4 They gathered plants by the bushes and used juniper roots for food.
Job 30:5 They were forced out from where people lived; people shouted at them as they would at a thief.
Job 30:6 To live in valley cliffs, earth caves, and among the rocks.
Job 30:7 In the bushes they cried out; under the thorns they huddled together.
Job 30:8 They were kids of fools, yes, kids of lowly men; they were worse than dirt.
Job 30:9 Now I am their joke; yes, I am their mocking word.
Job 30:10 They hate me, they run away from me, and they don't hesitate to spit in my face.
Job 30:11 Because he has untied my rope and made me suffer, they have also removed the restraint in my presence.
Job 30:12 Young people gather on my right side; they knock me off my feet, and they build up paths to harm me.
Job 30:13 They block my way, they increase my trouble, they have no helper.
Job 30:14 They attacked me like a flood breaking through: in my ruin, they overwhelmed me.
Job 30:15 Fears attack me; they chase my soul like the wind: and my well-being disappears like a cloud.
Job 30:16 My soul is poured out inside me; days of suffering grip me.
Job 30:17 At night, my bones hurt deeply, and my muscles get no rest.
Job 30:18 My sickness is so strong it changes my clothes; it wraps around me like my coat's collar.
Job 30:19 He has thrown me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
Job 30:20 I call to you, but you don't hear me; I stand up, but you don't notice me.
Job 30:21 You have become harsh to me; with your strong hand, you stand against me.
Job 30:22 You lift me up to the wind; you make me ride on it, and you melt away my strength.
Job 30:23 I know you will lead me to death, to the place set for everyone who lives.
Job 30:24 However, he will not reach out to the grave when they call out as they perish.
Job 30:25 Didn't I cry for the person who was suffering? Wasn't I sad for the poor?
Job 30:26 When I hoped for good, evil came to me; and when I waited for light, darkness arrived.
Job 30:27 I felt deep turmoil inside and could not rest; my days of trouble came before I was ready.
Job 30:28 I walked sadly without the sun; I stood up and cried among the people.
Job 30:29 I am like a brother to wild dragons, and a friend to owls.
Job 30:30 My skin is dark on me, and my bones are hot from burning.
Job 30:31 My harp now plays sad songs, and my flute sounds like the cries of those who are crying.

Job 31:1 I promised myself not to look with desire; so why should I think about a young woman?
Job 31:2 What does a person get from God above? And what does the Almighty give from high up?
Job 31:3 Isn't destruction meant for the wicked, and an unusual punishment for those who do wrong?
Job 31:4 Doesn't God see how I live and count every step I take?
Job 31:5 If I have lived with falsehood or hurried to deceive;
Job 31:6 Let me be measured in a fair scale so God can see my honesty.
Job 31:7 If I have gone off the path, and my heart followed what I saw, and if any stain has stuck to my hands;
Job 31:8 Let me plant seeds, but let someone else eat the harvest; yes, let my descendants be destroyed.
Job 31:9 If my heart was misled by a woman, or if I waited secretly at my neighbor's door;
Job 31:10 Let my wife work for another man, and let other men be with her.
Job 31:11 This is a terrible crime, yes, it's a wrongdoing that the judges must punish.
Job 31:12 It is a fire that burns until everything is destroyed and would remove all my growth.
Job 31:13 If I ignored my male or female servant's complaint against me;
Job 31:14 What should I do when God stands up? And when He comes to check, what will I say to Him?
Job 31:15 Didn't the same God who created me in the womb also create him? And didn't one shape both of us inside the womb?
Job 31:16 If I have denied the poor what they wanted, or made the widow's eyes weary;
Job 31:17 I did not eat my food alone and ignored the orphans; they ate with me.
Job 31:18 Since I was young, he grew up with me like a father, and I've guided her since I was in my mother's womb.
Job 31:19 If I have seen anyone die because they had no clothes, or any poor person without a blanket;
Job 31:20 If he didn't thank me or wasn't warmed by my sheep's wool;
