Job 31:21 If I raised my hand against an orphan when I saw my support at the city gate:
Job 31:22 Let my arm drop off from my shoulder, and my arm be broken from its bone.
Job 31:23 I was scared of being destroyed by God, and because he is so great, I couldn't bear it.
Job 31:24 If I have put my hope in gold or told pure gold, 'You are my trust;'
Job 31:25 If I was happy because I was very rich and my own efforts brought me a lot;
Job 31:26 If I looked at the sun shining or the moon moving brightly;
Job 31:27 My heart was secretly tempted, or my mouth kissed my hand.
Job 31:28 This would also be a sin that a judge must punish, because I would have denied God above.
Job 31:29 If I was happy when my enemy was destroyed, or felt proud when bad things happened to him:
Job 31:30 I have not let my mouth sin by cursing his life.
Job 31:31 If the people in my home never said, "We wish we had his meat!" they are not content.
Job 31:32 The traveler did not sleep in the street; I opened my doors to them.
Job 31:33 If I hid my wrongs like Adam, keeping my sins close to me:
Job 31:34 Was I scared of many people, or did the scorn of families frighten me, so that I stayed quiet and didn't go outside?
Job 31:35 I wish someone would listen to me! Look, what I want is for God to respond to me, and for my opponent to have written down his accusations.
Job 31:36 I would surely carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.
Job 31:37 I would tell him how many steps I have taken; like a leader, I would approach him.
Job 31:38 If my land cries out against me or its furrows also speak out;
Job 31:39 If I have eaten its fruits without paying, or if I have caused the owners to lose their life:
Job 31:40 Let weeds grow instead of wheat, and useless plants instead of barley. Job has finished speaking.

Job 32:1 These three men stopped answering Job because he thought he was right.
Job 32:2 Elihu, Barachel's son from the Buzite family, became very angry with Job because Job made himself look right instead of God.
Job 32:3 God was also angry with Job's three friends because they could not find an answer but still blamed Job.
Job 32:4 Elihu waited until Job finished talking because the others were older than him.
Job 32:5 When Elihu saw that these three men had no answer, he became very angry.
Job 32:6 Elihu, Barachel's son from the Buz family, replied, "I am young, and you are old. That's why I was scared and didn't share my thoughts with you."
Job 32:7 I said, "Time should teach, and many years should bring wisdom."
Job 32:8 Humans have a spirit, and God's breath gives them insight.
Job 32:9 Powerful people are not always smart; old people do not always make good decisions.
Job 32:10 So I said, listen to me; I will also share my thoughts.
Job 32:11 I listened carefully to what you said; I heard your arguments while you found the right words to speak.
Job 32:12 Yes, I listened to you, and there was none among you who proved Job wrong or responded to his words.
Job 32:13 So you might not claim, we have discovered wisdom: it is God who brings him down, not people.
Job 32:14 He has not spoken against me, and I won't reply to him with your words.
Job 32:15 They were surprised and stopped answering; they stopped talking.
Job 32:16 I waited because they were quiet, stood still, and didn't speak anymore.
Job 32:17 I said, I will give my answer, I will also share my opinion.
Job 32:18 I have a lot to say, and the spirit inside me compels me to speak.
Job 32:19 See, my stomach is like unopened wine; it feels like it's going to burst like new wineskins.
Job 32:20 I will talk to feel better: I will open my mouth and reply.
Job 32:21 Please don't let me show favoritism to anyone or use flattering titles for people.
Job 32:22 I don't use flattering titles; if I did, my Creator would quickly end my life.

Job 33:1 So Job, please listen to what I say and pay attention to all my words.
Job 33:2 Look, now I have opened my mouth and my tongue has spoken inside it.
Job 33:3 I will speak what is true and my words will clearly show what I know.
Job 33:4 God's spirit made me, and the Almighty's breath gave me life.
Job 33:5 If you can answer me, arrange your words clearly and stand up.
Job 33:6 Look, I am just as you want, in place of God: I am made from clay too.
Job 33:7 You don't need to fear my terror, nor will my hand be hard on you.
Job 33:8 You have definitely spoken where I could hear, and I have heard what you said.
Job 33:9 I am clean and have not wronged anyone, I am innocent; I have done nothing wrong.
Job 33:10 Look, He finds reasons to accuse me; He considers me His enemy.
Job 33:11 He puts my feet in shackles and watches all the ways I walk.
Job 33:12 Look, you are not right in this: I will tell you that God is greater than a human.
Job 33:13 Why do you argue with God? He doesn't need to explain anything he does.
Job 33:14 God speaks once, even twice, but people do not notice.
Job 33:15 In a dream, during the night, when people are in deep sleep and lying in bed half-asleep;
Job 33:16 Then he opens people's ears and gives them understanding.
Job 33:17 To make a person change their plan and keep them from being proud.
Job 33:18 He protects his soul from the pit and his life from dying by the sword.
Job 33:19 He suffers with pain on his bed, and his bones ache greatly.
Job 33:20 So he hates bread, and he refuses good food.
Job 33:21 His body wastes away, hidden from sight; and his bones, once unseen, now stick out.
Job 33:22 Yes, his soul is close to death, and his life nears those who destroy.
Job 33:23 If a messenger is with him, an interpreter, one in a thousand, to show a person how to be right:
Job 33:24 Then he is kind to him and says, Save him from falling into the pit: I have found a payment.
Job 33:25 His body will be more refreshed than a child's: he will become young again.
Job 33:26 He will pray to God, and God will accept him; he will see God's face with happiness because God will give man what is right.
Job 33:27 He looks at people, and if anyone says, "I have sinned, I have twisted what is right, and it did not benefit me;"
Job 33:28 He will save his soul from falling into the pit, and his life will see the light.
Job 33:29 Look, God often does all these things with humans.
Job 33:30 To save his life from the grave, to enjoy the light of life.
Job 33:31 Pay attention, Job, listen to me: be quiet, and I will talk.
Job 33:32 If you have something to say, reply: speak, because I want to clear you.
Job 33:33 If not, listen to me: be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.

Job 34:1 Elihu replied and said,
Job 34:2 Listen to me, you wise people; pay attention, you who have understanding.
Job 34:3 The ear tests words like the mouth tastes food.
Job 34:4 Let's decide what is fair; let's understand together what is good.
Job 34:5 Job has said, "I am righteous," but God has taken away my right to a fair judgment.
Job 34:6 Should I lie against what is right? My injury is incurable, though I did no wrong.
Job 34:7 Who is like Job, who drinks up mockery as easily as water?
Job 34:8 Who spends time with those who do wrong and walks with evil people.
Job 34:9 He has said, "It benefits a person nothing to enjoy being with God."
Job 34:10 Listen to me, wise men: God would never do evil, and the All-Powerful would never act unjustly.
Job 34:11 God will repay a person for what they have done and give each one what their actions deserve.
Job 34:12 Yes, surely God will not act wrongly, nor will the Almighty twist justice.
Job 34:13 Who has put him in charge of the earth? Or who has arranged the whole world?
Job 34:14 If God decides to focus on a person, if he takes back that person's life and breath;
Job 34:15 Everyone will die at the same time, and humans will become dust again.
Job 34:16 If you understand now, listen to this: pay attention to what I am saying.
Job 34:17 Can someone who hates justice rule? Will you condemn the one who is completely fair?
Job 34:18 Is it right to tell a king, "You are bad" or to rulers, "You are evil"?
Job 34:19 How much less to someone who doesn't favor leaders or value the rich over the poor? For they are all created by God.
Job 34:20 Suddenly they will die, the people will panic at midnight and vanish; and the powerful will be removed effortlessly.
Job 34:21 God watches over people's paths and sees everything they do.
Job 34:22 There is no darkness or shadow of death where the wrongdoers can hide.
Job 34:23 God will not give a person more than is fair, so that they would have to argue with God.
Job 34:24 He will shatter countless strong men and replace them with others.
Job 34:25 So he knows what they do, and he turns things upside down at night, destroying them.
Job 34:26 He strikes them as bad people for all to see.
Job 34:27 They turned away from God and did not think about any of His ways.
Job 34:28 So they make the poor's cries reach God, and he hears the cries of those who are suffering.
Job 34:29 When God brings peace, who can cause trouble? And when God hides, who can see him? It doesn't matter if it's a whole country or just one person.
Job 34:30 Let not the false person rule, so the people won't be trapped.
Job 34:31 It is right to tell God, "I have accepted punishment, I will not sin again."
Job 34:32 Teach me what I do not see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.
Job 34:33 Should it go as you want? God will repay it, whether you refuse or choose; not me. So say what you know.
Job 34:34 Let people with understanding tell me, and let a wise person listen to me.
Job 34:35 Job spoke without understanding, and his words lacked wisdom.
Job 34:36 I want Job to be tested to the limit because of how he answers for evil people.
Job 34:37 He makes his sin worse by rebelling, applauds himself in our presence, and speaks many words against God.

Job 35:1 Elihu spoke again and said,
Job 35:2 Do you think it's right to say, "I am more righteous than God"?
Job 35:3 You said, "What benefit will it be to you?" and, "What will I gain if I am cleansed from my sin?"
Job 35:4 I will answer you and your friends too.
Job 35:5 Look up at the sky and see; look at the clouds so high above you.
Job 35:6 If you sin, what do you do against God? Or if your sins increase, what do you do to Him?
Job 35:7 If you are good, what do you give to God? Or what does He get from what you have?
Job 35:8 Your evil can harm someone like you; your good deeds can help people.
Job 35:9 Because of many harsh acts, the victims cry out; they call for help because of the power of the strong.
Job 35:10 But no one asks, 'Where is God my creator, who provides songs at night?'
Job 35:11 Who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?
Job 35:12 They call out for help, but no one answers, because of the arrogance of wicked people.
Job 35:13 God will not listen to emptiness, nor will the Almighty consider it.
Job 35:14 Even if you say you can't see God, he is still the one to judge; so you should trust in him.
Job 35:15 But now, God has come in anger because it's not as it should be; yet he doesn't realize how harsh it is.
Job 35:16 So Job speaks without reason; he talks a lot but without understanding.

Job 36:1 Elihu continued and spoke,
Job 36:2 Let me speak a bit more, for I still have things to say about God.
Job 36:3 I will bring my knowledge from far away and give credit for being right to my Creator.
Job 36:4 I speak the truth, and someone with perfect understanding is with you.
Job 36:5 Look, God is powerful and does not reject anyone; He is strong and wise.
Job 36:6 He does not keep the wicked alive but gives justice to the poor.
Job 36:7 God never stops watching the good people; he sets them to rule with kings on thrones, making their power secure forever, and they are lifted high.
Job 36:8 If they are tied up in chains and caught in ropes of trouble;
Job 36:9 Then he shows them what they have done and the wrongs they have committed by going too far.
Job 36:10 God opens their ears to instruction and orders them to turn away from wrongdoing.
Job 36:11 If they listen and work for God, they will live with success and enjoy their years.
Job 36:12 If they don't obey, they will die by the sword and will die without understanding.
Job 36:13 The insincere in heart store up anger; they don't cry out when he [God] restrains them.
Job 36:14 They die young, and their life ends among the impure.
Job 36:15 He saves the needy in their trouble and listens to them when they are oppressed.
Job 36:16 God would have taken you from a tight place to a spacious place with no tightness; your table would have been full of richness.
Job 36:17 But you have carried out the punishment of the wicked: punishment and fairness catch up with you.
Job 36:18 Be careful, because if God gets angry, he might punish you, and no large payment can save you.
Job 36:19 Will he value your wealth? No, not gold or any strong army.
Job 36:20 Do not wish for the night when people are taken away from where they are.
Job 36:21 Be careful, don't accept wrongdoing because you prefer it over suffering.
Job 36:22 Look, God lifts up with His power: who can teach like Him?
Job 36:23 Who has directed his path? Or who can say, "You have done wrong"?
Job 36:24 Remember to praise God's work that people see.
Job 36:25 Everyone can see it; people can spot it from far away.
Job 36:26 Look, God is great, and we do not know him, and no one can understand how long he has existed.
Job 36:27 He turns water into tiny drops; they fall as rain matching the mist.
Job 36:28 The clouds pour down and sprinkle plenty of water on people.
Job 36:29 Can anyone understand how the clouds spread out, or the sounds from his home in the sky?
Job 36:30 Look, he spreads his light over it and covers the sea's depths.
Job 36:31 God judges the people by these things; he provides plenty of food.
Job 36:32 He covers the sun with clouds and orders them to block the light.
Job 36:33 The sound of it tells about it, the livestock also about the mist.

Job 37:1 My heart shakes with fear and moves out of its place.
Job 37:2 Listen carefully to his voice and the noise that comes from his mouth.
Job 37:3 He guides it under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
Job 37:4 After it, a voice roars: God thunders with his majestic voice, and does not hold back when his voice is heard.
Job 37:5 God thunders wonderfully with his voice; he does great things we cannot understand.
Job 37:6 He tells the snow to fall on the earth, and the same to the light rain and the heavy rain of his power.
Job 37:7 He closes the hands of every person so everyone can know His deeds.
Job 37:8 Then the animals go into their dens and stay there.
Job 37:9 From the south comes a strong wind, and from the north comes cold.
Job 37:10 God's breath brings frost, and the surface of the waters becomes tight.
Job 37:11 God tires out the heavy cloud by adding water to it; he spreads his light cloud around.
Job 37:12 It moves as God plans, so they can do everything he tells them on the earth.
Job 37:13 He makes it happen, whether for discipline, for his land, or for kindness.
Job 37:14 Listen to this, Job: be still and think about God's amazing deeds.
Job 37:15 Do you know when God arranged them and made the light of his cloud shine?
Job 37:16 Do you know how the clouds stay balanced, the amazing things done by the one who has perfect knowledge?
Job 37:17 Your clothes become warm when God calms the earth with the south wind.
Job 37:18 Have you helped God spread out the sky, which is solid, like a mirror made of melted metal?
Job 37:19 Show us what to say to God; we don't know how to speak properly because we are confused.
Job 37:20 Should I tell God what I say? If someone speaks, they will certainly be overwhelmed.
Job 37:21 People cannot see the bright light in the clouds, but the wind comes and clears them away.
Job 37:22 Clear skies come from the north; with God is awesome greatness.
Job 37:23 About God, we cannot fully understand him: he is great in power, fair in judgment, and full of justice: he does not cause suffering.
Job 37:24 People fear God because he doesn't favor those who think they are wise.

Job 38:1 Then God answered Job from the storm and said,
Job 38:2 Who is this who gives advice with words but has no understanding?
Job 38:3 Get ready like a man; I will question you, and you must answer me.
Job 38:4 Where were you when I set the earth's foundations? Tell me if you understand.
Job 38:5 Who set its measurements, if you know? Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
Job 38:6 Where are its foundations fixed? Or who put its cornerstone in place?
Job 38:7 When the morning stars sang together and all of God's children shouted for joy.
Job 38:8 Who closed in the sea with gates when it burst forth, as though coming out of the womb?
Job 38:9 When I wrapped it in clouds like clothes, and a thick dark blanket covered it,
Job 38:10 I broke open a place for it, and put in bars and doors.
Job 38:11 God said, "You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop."
Job 38:12 Have you ever ordered the morning to begin or shown the dawn its place?
Job 38:13 So it can grab the edges of the world and shake the bad people from it.
Job 38:14 It changes like clay under a seal; and they settle into place like clothes.
Job 38:15 The wicked are denied light, and their strong arm will be broken.
Job 38:16 Have you gone into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked looking for the depths?
Job 38:17 Have you seen the gates of death or the doors where death's shadow falls?
Job 38:18 Have you understood how wide the earth is? Tell me if you know everything about it.
Job 38:19 Where is the place where light lives? And where is the home of darkness?
Job 38:20 You should take it to its limit and know the ways to its home.
Job 38:21 Do you know this because you were born then? Or because you have lived many days?
Job 38:22 Have you entered the storehouses of the snow? Or have you seen the storehouses of the hail?
Job 38:23 I have kept for a time of trouble, for a day of battle and war.
Job 38:24 How is light spread, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
Job 38:25 Who has made channels for the flood, or a path for thunder's lightning?
Job 38:26 To make it rain on the land where no one lives; on the desert where there is no one;
Job 38:27 To make the lonely, barren land fertile and to help young plants start to grow.
Job 38:28 Does the rain have a father? Or who has created the dewdrops?
Job 38:29 Who made ice come from the womb? Who created the frost from the heavens?
Job 38:30 The waters are covered like with a stone, and the surface of the deep water is solid like ice.
Job 38:31 Can you control the beautiful patterns of the stars or untie the ropes of the constellations?
Job 38:32 Can you make the constellations appear in their season? Or can you lead the Great Bear and its cubs?
Job 38:33 Do you know the laws of the sky? Can you establish their rule on the earth?
Job 38:34 Can you call out to the clouds to make them pour down water on you?
Job 38:35 Can you make lightning strike and have it report to you, 'Here we are'?
Job 38:36 Who has placed wisdom inside us? Or who has given the heart understanding?
Job 38:37 Who can count the clouds wisely? Or who can hold back the rain from the sky?
Job 38:38 When the soil turns hard, and lumps stick tightly together?
Job 38:39 Will you hunt food for the lion or satisfy the hunger of the young lions?
Job 38:40 When they crouch in their lairs and stay hidden to ambush?
Job 38:41 Who gives the raven its food? When its young cry out to God, they roam because they have no food.

Job 39:1 Do you know when the wild goats give birth? Can you tell when the deer are having their young?
Job 39:2 Can you count how many months they need? Or do you know when they give birth?
Job 39:3 They bend down, they give birth to their young, they let go of their pain.
Job 39:4 Their young are healthy, they grow up with grain; they leave and do not come back.
Job 39:5 Who set the wild donkey free? Who untied the ropes of the wild donkey?
Job 39:6 I made the wilderness his house and the empty land his home.
Job 39:7 He mocks the city's crowd and ignores the driver's shouts.
Job 39:8 The mountains are where his animals graze, and he looks for every plant that is green.
Job 39:9 Will the unicorn want to work for you or stay by your feeding trough?
Job 39:10 Can you tie the unicorn with a rope in the fields? Or will he plow the valleys behind you?
Job 39:11 Will you trust him because he is strong? Or will you rely on him to do your work?
Job 39:12 Will you trust him to bring back your crops and collect them into your barn?
Job 39:13 Did you give the beautiful wings to the peacocks? Or the wings and feathers to the ostrich?
Job 39:14 She leaves her eggs on the ground and keeps them warm with the dirt.
Job 39:15 And forgets that a foot might crush them, or a wild animal might destroy them.
Job 39:16 She is cold toward her young, as if they were not hers; her hard work is pointless without concern.
Job 39:17 God has not given her wisdom, nor has he given her understanding.
Job 39:18 When she rises up, she looks down on the horse and its rider.
Job 39:19 Did you give the horse its strength? Did you make its neck strong like thunder?
Job 39:20 Can you scare him like a grasshopper? His strong breath is frightening.
Job 39:21 He digs in the valley, happy in his power; he moves towards the armed men.
Job 39:22 He laughs at fear, is not scared, and does not turn away from the sword.
Job 39:23 The arrows shake against him, the shining spear and the shield.
Job 39:24 He charges across the land with anger and fury; he does not think the trumpet sound is real.
Job 39:25 He says among the trumpets, "Ha, ha"; and he senses the battle from far away, the noise of the commanders, and the yelling.
Job 39:26 Does the hawk fly by your wisdom and spread its wings to the south?
Job 39:27 Does the eagle fly up on your order and build her nest up high?
Job 39:28 She lives and stays on the rock, at the top of the cliff, and in the secure spot.
Job 39:29 From there she looks for food, and her eyes see from far away.
Job 39:30 Her young ones also drink blood: and where there are dead bodies, there she is.

Job 40:1 God replied to Job, saying,
Job 40:2 Can a person argue with God and teach Him? Anyone who corrects God should reply.
Job 40:3 Job replied to God and said,
Job 40:4 I realize I am worthless; what can I say to you? I will put my hand over my mouth.
Job 40:5 I have spoken once; I won't reply again; even twice; but I'll say no more.
Job 40:6 God replied to Job from the storm and said,
Job 40:7 Prepare yourself like a man; I will question you, and you must answer me.
Job 40:8 Will you cancel my decision? Will you say I am wrong so you can say you are right?
Job 40:9 Do you have an arm like God? Or can you thunder with a voice like him?
Job 40:10 Dress yourself now with greatness and honor; and put on glory and beauty.
Job 40:11 Throw out your anger and look at all the proud people; bring them down.
Job 40:12 Pay attention to everyone who is proud and make them humble; step on the evil ones where they stand.
Job 40:13 Put them all in the dust; cover their faces in darkness.
Job 40:14 Then I will agree that your own power can save you.
Job 40:15 Look at the behemoth, which I created with you; it eats grass like an ox.
Job 40:16 Look, his power is in his hips, and his strength is in his belly muscles.
Job 40:17 He swings his tail like a cedar tree; the muscles of his thighs are tightly woven.
Job 40:18 His bones are as hard as pieces of brass; his bones are like rods of iron.
Job 40:19 He is the greatest of God's creations; only his maker can threaten him.
Job 40:20 The mountains give him food, and all the wild animals play there.
Job 40:21 He lies under the shade trees, in the hiding place of the reeds and marshes.
Job 40:22 The trees cast their shade over him; the willow trees by the stream surround him.
Job 40:23 Look, he drinks up a river without rushing; he believes he can take the Jordan River into his mouth.
Job 40:24 He sees it with his eyes; his nose detects traps.

Job 41:1 Can you catch Leviathan with a fishhook or tie down its tongue with a rope?
Job 41:2 Can you put a hook in his nose or pierce his jaw with a spike?
Job 41:3 Will he beg you often? Will he speak gently to you?
Job 41:4 Will he agree with you? Will you make him your servant forever?
Job 41:5 Will you play with it like a bird? Or will you tie it up for your girls?
Job 41:6 Will friends feast on him? Will traders divide him up?
Job 41:7 Can you cover his skin with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
Job 41:8 Touch him and remember the fight, do it no more.
Job 41:9 Look, his hope is pointless: won't someone be terrified just by seeing him?
Job 41:10 No one is brave enough to disturb him; who then can face me?
Job 41:11 Who has given to me first, so I need to pay him back? Everything under the whole sky is mine.
Job 41:12 I won't hide his body, his strength, or his good shape.
Job 41:13 Who can reach the edge of his clothing? Or who can approach him with a double bit bridle?
Job 41:14 Who can open the doors of his face? His teeth are terrifying all around.
Job 41:15 His scales are what he is proud of, tight and sealed closely.
Job 41:16 They are so close together that no air can fit between them.
Job 41:17 They are connected to each other, they cling tightly, so they cannot be separated.
Job 41:18 When he sneezes, light shines, and his eyes are like the dawn's first light.
Job 41:19 From his mouth come shining lights, and sparks of fire jump out.
Job 41:20 Smoke comes out of his nose like from a boiling pot or kettle.
Job 41:21 His breath lights up coals, and flames come out of his mouth.
Job 41:22 Strength stays in his neck, and sadness turns to joy in his presence.
Job 41:23 His skin is thick and tight; it is solid and does not move.
Job 41:24 His heart is as strong as a rock, yes, as hard as a lower grinding stone.
Job 41:25 When he stands up, the strong are scared: because of the terror, they try to make themselves clean.
Job 41:26 The warrior's sword won't succeed: neither the spear, the arrow, nor the armor.
Job 41:27 He thinks iron is like straw and brass is like rotten wood.
Job 41:28 Arrows cannot scare him; to him, slingshot stones turn to chaff.
Job 41:29 Arrows seem like straw to him; he laughs at the shaking of a spear.
Job 41:30 He lies on sharp rocks; he scatters spiky things on the mud.
Job 41:31 He makes the depths churn like a boiling pot; he makes the sea stir like a pot of ointment.
Job 41:32 He leaves a shining trail behind him; it seems like the depths have gray hair.
Job 41:33 On earth, there is no one like him; he is made without fear.
Job 41:34 He sees everything that is high up; he is a king over all the proud people.

Job 42:1 Then Job replied to God, saying,
Job 42:2 I know you can do everything, and no thought can be hidden from you.
Job 42:3 Who hides wise plans without understanding? So I spoke of things I did not understand, wonders beyond me that I did not know.
Job 42:4 Please listen, and I will talk: I will ask you questions, and you tell me the answers.
Job 42:5 I have heard about you from others, but now I see you with my own eyes.
Job 42:6 So I dislike myself and change my ways, feeling sad as if I were sitting in dust and ashes.
Job 42:7 After God spoke these words to Job, God said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "I am angry with you and your two friends because you did not speak truthfully about me, as my servant Job did."
Job 42:8 Take seven bulls and seven rams to my servant Job and make a burnt offering for yourselves. Job will pray for you, and I will accept him. Otherwise, I will punish you for your foolish words about me, unlike my servant Job, who spoke what is right.
Job 42:9 Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah went and did what God told them to; God also accepted Job.
Job 42:10 God ended Job's suffering when he prayed for his friends; God also gave Job twice as much as he had before.
Job 42:11 All his brothers and sisters and former friends came to visit him. They ate with him in his home, felt sorry for him, and comforted him because of all the bad things that God had let happen to him. Each person also gave him some money and a gold earring.
Job 42:12 So God blessed Job more in the end than at the start: he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
Job 42:13 He also had seven sons and three daughters.
Job 42:14 He named the first Jemima, the second Kezia, and the third Kerenhappuch.
Job 42:15 In the whole country, no women were as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them property along with their brothers.
Job 42:16 After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children, his grandchildren, and even to four generations.
Job 42:17 Job died when he was very old and had lived a long life.

Psalms 1:1 Happy is the person who does not follow bad advice, does not hang out with sinners, and does not join those who make fun of others.
Psalms 1:2 He enjoys following God's law and thinks about it all day and night.
Psalms 1:3 He will be like a tree by the water that grows fruit at the right time; its leaves will not dry out, and everything he does will succeed.
Psalms 1:4 The wicked are not like this; they are like the dry husks that the wind blows away.
Psalms 1:5 So, the wicked won't stand when judged, nor will sinners be with the group of good people.
Psalms 1:6 God knows the path of good people, but the way of the bad will disappear.

Psalms 2:1 Why do the nations get angry, and the people think up useless plans?
Psalms 2:2 The rulers of the world stand together, and the leaders plan together, against God and his chosen one, saying,
Psalms 2:3 Let's tear off their chains and throw their ropes away from us.
Psalms 2:4 God in heaven will laugh; He will mock them.
Psalms 2:5 Then he will speak to them angrily and trouble them greatly in his upset.
Psalms 2:6 I have placed my king on my holy mountain Zion.
Psalms 2:7 I will tell the rule: God has said to me, "You are my Son; today I have become your father."
Psalms 2:8 Ask me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance and the farthest places on earth as your own.
Psalms 2:9 You will break them with an iron rod; you will smash them like a clay pot.
Psalms 2:10 Understand this, you kings: Listen and learn, you rulers of the world.
Psalms 2:11 Serve God with respect, and be happy with caution.
Psalms 2:12 Show love to the Son, or he may get angry, and you could be destroyed on your path, because his anger can flare up quickly. Happy are those who trust in him.

Proverbs 8:1 Doesn't wisdom call out? And understanding raise her voice?

Proverbs 8:22 God chose me at the start of His path, before His ancient works.

Proverbs 8:25 Before the mountains were in place, before the hills I was born.
Proverbs 8:26 Before God made the earth, the fields, or the highest dust particles of the world.
Proverbs 8:27 When he made the sky, I was there: when he drew a circle on the deep:
Proverbs 8:28 When he made the clouds up high: when he made the deep springs strong:
Proverbs 8:29 When he told the sea its limits, so the waters would not disobey his command, when he set the earth's foundations:
Proverbs 8:30 I was with God, like someone raised with him; I was his joy every day, always happy in his presence.
Proverbs 8:31 I celebrated in the world he made; I enjoyed being with people.
Proverbs 8:32 Listen to me now, children: happy are those who follow my teachings.
Proverbs 8:33 Listen to advice, be smart, and don't ignore it.

Proverbs 8:35 Whoever finds me finds life and will receive favor from God.
Proverbs 8:36 Whoever sins against me hurts their own soul; all who hate me love death.

Proverbs 27:21 Just as a pot is for melting silver and a furnace is for purifying gold, so a person is tested by being praised.

Proverbs 27:26 Use sheep for clothes, and goats to buy a field.
Proverbs 27:27 You will have enough goat's milk for your food, your family's food, and to support your servant girls.

Proverbs 28:1 Bad people run away even when no one chases them, but good people are as brave as a lion.
Proverbs 28:2 When a country sins, it has many rulers, but a wise and knowledgeable man will help it last longer.

Proverbs 28:4 Those who ignore God's laws praise the bad people, but those who follow the laws stand against them.
Proverbs 28:5 Bad people do not understand what is right, but those who look for God understand everything.
Proverbs 28:6 It's better to be poor and honest than to be dishonest and rich.
Proverbs 28:7 Whoever follows the law is a wise child, but he who hangs out with wild people brings shame to his parent.
Proverbs 28:8 Whoever makes money through charging too much interest and unfair profit will end up collecting wealth for someone who cares for the poor.
Proverbs 28:9 Whoever ignores the law, even their prayers are detestable.

Proverbs 28:11 The rich man thinks he is smart, but the poor with insight can see through him.
Proverbs 28:12 When good people are happy, there is great joy; but when bad people gain power, others go into hiding.
Proverbs 28:13 Whoever hides their sins won't succeed, but the one who admits and stops them will receive mercy.
Proverbs 28:14 The person who always respects God is happy, but someone who becomes stubborn will get into trouble.

Proverbs 28:16 A ruler who lacks understanding is also very harsh, but someone who hates greed will live a long time.
Proverbs 28:17 Anyone who hurts another person must run away to a deep hole; nobody should help him.
Proverbs 28:18 Anyone who lives in a good way will be safe, but someone who chooses to do wrong will suddenly fail.
Proverbs 28:19 The one who works their land will have lots of bread, but the one who chases after worthless people will have plenty of poverty.
Proverbs 28:20 A loyal person will have many blessings, but someone rushing to get rich won't stay guiltless.
Proverbs 28:21 Showing favoritism is wrong: a person might sin just for a small piece of food.
Proverbs 28:22 Someone who rushes to get rich has bad intentions and does not realize that they will become poor.
Proverbs 28:23 Someone who corrects a person will later be appreciated more than someone who uses words to flatter.
Proverbs 28:24 Anyone who steals from their father or mother and says it's not wrong is a friend of someone who destroys.
Proverbs 28:25 A person with a proud heart causes conflict, but one who trusts in God will prosper.
Proverbs 28:26 Anyone who trusts only in themselves is foolish, but someone who acts wisely will be safe.
Proverbs 28:27 Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but one who ignores them will face many troubles.
Proverbs 28:28 When bad people gain power, others hide; but when they die, the good grow in number.

Proverbs 29:1 Anyone who keeps making the same mistakes and refuses to accept correction will suddenly be ruined beyond repair.
Proverbs 29:2 When good people lead, everyone is happy; but when bad people rule, everyone is sad.

Proverbs 29:5 Someone who praises their neighbor too much is setting a trap for them.
Proverbs 29:6 When a bad person does wrong, they get caught in a trap, but a good person is happy and sings.
Proverbs 29:7 Good people think about the needs of the poor; but bad people don't care to know them.
Proverbs 29:8 Mocking people trap a city, but wise people calm anger.
Proverbs 29:9 If a wise person argues with a foolish one, whether they get angry or laugh, there is no peace.
Proverbs 29:10 Violent people dislike those who are honest, but righteous people care about their well-being.
Proverbs 29:11 A foolish person says everything they think; but a wise person keeps it to themselves for later.
Proverbs 29:12 If a leader listens to lies, all their followers become bad.
Proverbs 29:13 The poor person and the liar come across each other; God gives light to both of their eyes.

Proverbs 29:19 A worker won't change just by talking to them; even if they get it, they won't respond.
Proverbs 29:20 Do you see someone who talks without thinking? A fool has more hope than him.
Proverbs 29:21 The one who raises his servant with care from a young age will eventually have him as his own son.
