Proverbs 29:27 A dishonest person disgusts the honest, and someone who lives rightly is hated by the wicked.

Proverbs 30:1 Agur, Jakeh's son, said this prophecy: he told Ithiel, and also Ithiel and Ucal.
Proverbs 30:2 I am surely less wise than anyone, and I lack a man's understanding.
Proverbs 30:3 I have not learned wisdom, nor do I know about the holy.
Proverbs 30:4 Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has held the wind in his hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in a cloak? Who has set up all the earth's edges? What's his name, and what's his son's name, if you know it?
Proverbs 30:5 Every word from God is pure; he protects those who trust in him.
Proverbs 30:6 Do not add to his words, or God will correct you, and you will be shown to be a liar.
Proverbs 30:7 I ask you for two things; don't refuse me before I die.
Proverbs 30:8 Keep me away from useless things and dishonesty; don't make me poor or rich; give me just the food I need.
Proverbs 30:9 So I don't become too full, forget you, and ask, "Who is God?" or become poor, steal, and disrespect my God's name.
Proverbs 30:10 Do not blame someone's servant to their boss, or they might curse you and you'll be found at fault.
Proverbs 30:11 A generation curses their father and doesn't bless their mother.
Proverbs 30:12 Some people think they are clean, but they are not free from their dirt.
Proverbs 30:13 A group of people exist who are very proud; they look at others with arrogance.
Proverbs 30:14 Some people are like sword teeth and knife jaws, they eat up the poor and needy from the world and among people.
Proverbs 30:15 The leech has two daughters that cry, "Give, give." There are three things never full, even four that never say, "Enough":
Proverbs 30:16 The grave, the empty womb, the dry earth, and the fire that never says 'Enough.'
Proverbs 30:17 The eye that makes fun of its father, and hates to listen to its mother, the ravens of the valley will pluck it out, and young eagles will eat it.
Proverbs 30:18 There are three things that are amazing to me, yes, four things I don't understand:
Proverbs 30:19 How an eagle flies in the sky; how a snake moves on a rock; how a ship sails in the sea; and how a man acts with a woman.
Proverbs 30:20 This is how an unfaithful woman acts: she eats, cleans her mouth, and says, I've done nothing wrong.
Proverbs 30:21 The earth is troubled by three things, and there are four it can't stand:
Proverbs 30:22 When a servant becomes a leader and a fool gets plenty to eat.
Proverbs 30:23 A disliked woman when she gets married; and a servant girl who inherits from her lady.
Proverbs 30:24 There are four small things on earth, but they are very wise:
Proverbs 30:25 Ants are not strong, yet they gather their food in the summer.
Proverbs 30:26 The rock badgers are weak creatures, yet they make their homes in the rocks.
Proverbs 30:27 The locusts don't have a king, but they all go out in groups.
Proverbs 30:28 The spider uses its hands to make a web and lives in king's homes.
Proverbs 30:29 Three things move gracefully, indeed, four look good as they go:
Proverbs 30:30 A lion, the strongest among animals, doesn't turn away from anything.
Proverbs 30:31 A greyhound; a male goat also; and a king, who cannot be opposed.
Proverbs 30:32 If you acted foolishly by being proud, or if you planned something bad, put your hand over your mouth.
Proverbs 30:33 When you stir milk, you make butter, and when you squeeze a nose, you get blood; so when you force anger, you cause fighting.

Proverbs 31:1 The sayings of King Lemuel, the teaching his mother gave him.
Proverbs 31:2 What should I say, my son? What, child of my body? What, child of my promises?
Proverbs 31:3 Do not give your strength to women, or your paths to what ruins kings.
Proverbs 31:4 Kings should not drink wine, Lemuel, nor should leaders drink strong alcohol.
Proverbs 31:5 They might drink, forget the rules, and twist the justice due to those who are suffering.
Proverbs 31:6 Give hard liquor to someone who is dying, and wine to those who are very sad.
Proverbs 31:7 Let him drink and forget his lack of money, and not recall his troubles anymore.
Proverbs 31:8 Speak up for those who cannot speak, in the defense of all who are headed for ruin.
Proverbs 31:9 Speak up, make fair decisions, and defend the rights of the poor and needy.
Proverbs 31:10 Who can find a good woman? Her value is much higher than jewels.
Proverbs 31:11 Her husband's heart trusts her deeply, so he lacks nothing of value.
Proverbs 31:12 She will treat him well and never badly all her life.
Proverbs 31:13 She looks for wool and flax and works eagerly with her hands.
Proverbs 31:14 She is like the traders' boats; she gets her food from far away.
Proverbs 31:15 She gets up while it's still night, and provides food for her family, and shares with her servant girls.
Proverbs 31:16 She thinks about a field, buys it, and with her own work, she plants a vineyard.
Proverbs 31:17 She wraps her waist with power and makes her arms strong.
Proverbs 31:18 She sees that her goods are valuable; her lamp does not go out at night.
Proverbs 31:19 She puts her hands to the spindle and holds the distaff.
Proverbs 31:20 She extends her hand to the poor; yes, she offers her hands to those in need.
Proverbs 31:21 She is not worried about the cold for her family, because they all wear warm red clothes.
Proverbs 31:22 She makes herself patterned blankets; her clothes are silk and purple.
Proverbs 31:23 Her husband is respected in the community where he meets with the local leaders.
Proverbs 31:24 She makes good linen cloth and sells it; she also delivers belts to the shopkeeper.
Proverbs 31:25 She wears strength and respect; she will be glad in the future.
Proverbs 31:26 She speaks wisely and kindly advice is on her tongue.
Proverbs 31:27 She takes good care of her family and does not waste time doing nothing.
Proverbs 31:28 Her children stand up and call her blessed; her husband too, and he praises her.
Proverbs 31:29 Many women have been good, but you are the best of them all.
Proverbs 31:30 Being liked for charm is misleading, and beauty is shallow: but a woman who respects God will be honored.
Proverbs 31:31 Give her the rewards of her work, and let her actions praise her publicly.

Ecclesiastes 1:1 This is the Preacher's message, David's son and king in Jerusalem.
Ecclesiastes 1:2 Everything is meaningless, says the Teacher; everything is completely meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 1:3 What good does a person get from all the work they do under the sun?
Ecclesiastes 1:4 One generation goes, and another comes, but the earth lasts forever.
Ecclesiastes 1:5 The sun rises and sets, and quickly goes back to where it rose.
Ecclesiastes 1:6 The wind moves south, then turns north; it goes around and around, and comes back to its paths.
Ecclesiastes 1:7 All rivers flow into the sea, but the sea never fills up. The rivers go back to where they came from and start again.
Ecclesiastes 1:8 Everything is hard work; people can't express it: the eye is never happy with what it sees, nor the ear with what it hears.
Ecclesiastes 1:9 What has happened before will happen again; what has been done before will be done again; there's nothing new under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 1:10 Can we say about anything, "Look, this is new"? It has already existed long ago, before our time.
Ecclesiastes 1:11 People do not remember past things; and those to come will not be remembered by those who follow them.
Ecclesiastes 1:12 I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
Ecclesiastes 1:13 I devoted myself to seek and understand by wisdom everything that happens on earth: this difficult task has been given by God to humanity to work on.
Ecclesiastes 1:14 I have seen everything people do on earth, and truly, everything is pointless and frustrating.
Ecclesiastes 1:15 What is twisted cannot be straightened; what is missing cannot be counted.
Ecclesiastes 1:16 I talked to myself, saying, "Look, I have become very wealthy and have gained more wisdom than anyone before me in Jerusalem; yes, my heart has learned much about wisdom and knowledge."
Ecclesiastes 1:17 I devoted myself to understand wisdom, madness, and foolishness and realized that this too is frustrating.
Ecclesiastes 1:18 With much wisdom comes much sadness; gaining more knowledge leads to more sorrow.

Ecclesiastes 2:1 I told myself, "Come on, let's try pleasure and have fun." But this, too, turned out to be meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 2:2 I said about laughter, "It's crazy," and about joy, "What does it do?"
Ecclesiastes 2:3 I decided to enjoy wine while keeping wise, and to embrace foolishness, until I could understand what is truly good for people to do throughout their lives.
Ecclesiastes 2:4 I made great projects; I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.
Ecclesiastes 2:5 I created gardens and orchards for myself, and in them I planted all types of fruit trees.
Ecclesiastes 2:6 I made pools of water to water the forest that grows trees.
Ecclesiastes 2:7 I got myself workers and maids, and had workers born in my house; I also had many herds of large and small animals, more than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
Ecclesiastes 2:8 I collected silver and gold for myself, and special treasures from kings and regions. I got male and female singers, and all kinds of musical pleasures that people enjoy.
Ecclesiastes 2:9 I became very great, more than anyone in Jerusalem before me; my wisdom stayed with me.
Ecclesiastes 2:10 Whatever my eyes wanted, I did not keep from them. I did not deny my heart any joy; my heart was happy in all my work, and this was my reward from all my work.
Ecclesiastes 2:11 I looked at everything I had done and all the hard work I had put in, and I saw that it was all pointless and frustrating, and there was no real gain to be had on earth.
Ecclesiastes 2:12 I looked to understand wisdom, madness, and folly: for what can a person do who follows the king? Only what has already been done.
Ecclesiastes 2:13 I saw that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
Ecclesiastes 2:14 A wise person uses their mind, but a fool lives without guidance. I also noticed that the same things happen to everyone.
Ecclesiastes 2:15 I thought to myself, "What happens to fools will happen to me too. So why have I been so wise?" I realized that this is also meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 2:16 People won't remember the wise more than the fool forever; because what exists now will be forgotten in the future. And the wise person dies just like the fool.
Ecclesiastes 2:17 So I disliked life because the work done under the sun troubled me; it all seemed pointless and frustrating.
Ecclesiastes 2:18 Yes, I hated all my hard work under the sun because I must leave it to the person who will come after me.
Ecclesiastes 2:19 Who knows if he will be wise or foolish? Yet he will control all my hard work where I have been wise. This too is pointless.
Ecclesiastes 2:20 So, I lost hope over all the hard work I had done under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 2:21 There is a person who works with wisdom, knowledge, and fairness; but he will leave what he has worked for to another who hasn't worked for it. This too is meaningless and a big problem.
Ecclesiastes 2:22 What does a person gain from all their work and the troubles that make their heart worry, which they experience in their life under the sun?
Ecclesiastes 2:23 Every day is full of sadness and his work brings grief; even at night, his mind finds no rest. This too is meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 2:24 The best thing for a person is to eat, drink, and enjoy good things from their work. I saw that this too comes from God.
Ecclesiastes 2:25 Who can eat or enjoy life more than I?
Ecclesiastes 2:26 God gives a good person wisdom, knowledge, and happiness, but gives a sinner hard work to collect and pile up wealth only to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless and frustrating.

Ecclesiastes 3:1 Everything has its time, and there is a moment for every purpose under heaven.
Ecclesiastes 3:2 A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pull up what is planted.
Ecclesiastes 3:3 A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to tear down, and a time to build up.
Ecclesiastes 3:4 A time to cry, and a time to laugh; a time to grieve, and a time to dance;
Ecclesiastes 3:5 A time to throw away stones, and a time to collect stones; a time to hug, and a time to avoid hugging.
Ecclesiastes 3:6 A time to gain, and a time to give up; a time to save, and a time to throw away;
Ecclesiastes 3:7 A time to tear, and a time to mend; a time to be quiet, and a time to talk;
Ecclesiastes 3:8 A time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
Ecclesiastes 3:9 What does a person gain from their work?
Ecclesiastes 3:10 I have seen the hard work that God has given to people to do.
Ecclesiastes 3:11 God has made everything beautiful in its time. He also placed the world in their hearts, yet no one can fully understand what God does from start to finish.
Ecclesiastes 3:12 I understand that there is no real benefit for people except to be happy and do good during their lives.
Ecclesiastes 3:13 Everyone should eat, drink, and enjoy the results of their work—this is a gift from God.
Ecclesiastes 3:14 I know that whatever God does will last forever. You can't add or take away from it. And God does it so people will respect Him.
Ecclesiastes 3:15 What has happened is happening now; and what will happen has already happened; and God asks for what has occurred.
Ecclesiastes 3:16 I also saw under the sun the place of judgment, where there was evil, and the place of righteousness, where there was wrong.
Ecclesiastes 3:17 I thought to myself, God will judge the good and the bad, because there is a right time for every plan and action.
Ecclesiastes 3:18 I thought to myself about people's lives, that God tests them so they can see that they are like animals.
Ecclesiastes 3:19 What happens to people happens to animals too. They all have the same fate: as one dies, so does the other. They all have the same spirit. People have no advantage over animals, for everything is meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 3:20 Everyone goes to the same place; everyone comes from dust, and everyone will turn to dust again.
Ecclesiastes 3:21 Who knows if the human spirit rises up and the animal spirit goes down into the earth?
Ecclesiastes 3:22 So I see that there is nothing better than for a person to be happy with their own work; that is their reward. Who can show them what will happen after they are gone?

Ecclesiastes 4:1 I went back and saw all the unfair things happening on earth: I saw the tears of the oppressed, with no one to comfort them; the oppressors had the power, but the oppressed had no comforter.
Ecclesiastes 4:2 So I said that those who have already died are happier than those who are still alive.
Ecclesiastes 4:3 Yes, the one who has not yet been born is better off than both of them, for he has not seen the bad things done in the world.
Ecclesiastes 4:4 I saw that all hard work and success in doing good things can make people jealous of their neighbor. This is also meaningless and frustrating.
Ecclesiastes 4:5 The foolish person does nothing and harms themselves.
Ecclesiastes 4:6 It is better to have a little with peace than a lot with hard work and stress.
Ecclesiastes 4:7 Then I came back and saw that everything is pointless under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 4:8 There is only one person, without a companion; they have no children or siblings. Still, their work never ends; they are never happy with their wealth, and never ask, "Who am I working for, and denying myself enjoyment?" This too is meaningless, a miserable task.
Ecclesiastes 4:9 Two are better than one because they get a good return for their work.
Ecclesiastes 4:10 If they fall, one can help the other up, but pity the person who is alone and falls without someone to help them.
Ecclesiastes 4:11 If two people lie together, they keep warm, but how can one stay warm alone?
Ecclesiastes 4:12 If one person can be defeated, two can stand strong against the enemy; a rope made of three strands is not easily snapped.
Ecclesiastes 4:13 A poor and smart child is better than an old and foolish king who won't listen to advice.
Ecclesiastes 4:14 He comes to rule after being in jail; even someone born in his kingdom may become poor.
Ecclesiastes 4:15 I thought about everyone alive who goes about under the sun, along with the next person who will take their place.
Ecclesiastes 4:16 People never stop coming, even those from before. Those who come later won't be happy with this. This too is pointless and frustrating.

Ecclesiastes 5:1 Be careful when you enter God's house, and be eager to listen rather than to offer the foolish sacrifice of those who don't realize they're doing wrong.
Ecclesiastes 5:2 Don't speak without thinking, and don't be quick to say anything before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so use only a few words.
Ecclesiastes 5:3 Dreams come with lots of activity, and a fool is recognized by too many words.
Ecclesiastes 5:4 When you make a promise to God, do not delay in fulfilling it; for God does not like fools: fulfill the promise you made.
Ecclesiastes 5:5 It's better not to make a promise than to make one and not keep it.
Ecclesiastes 5:6 Do not let your mouth lead you into sin, and don't tell the messenger it was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and ruin what you have done?
Ecclesiastes 5:7 In having many dreams and lots of words, there are also empty things: but respect God.
Ecclesiastes 5:8 If you see the poor being oppressed, and unfairness in law and justice in the land, don't be surprised: because God, who is above the highest authorities, sees everything, and there are powers greater than them.
Ecclesiastes 5:9 The good things the earth gives are for everyone; even the king depends on what the fields produce.
Ecclesiastes 5:10 Whoever loves money will never have enough; loving wealth brings no satisfaction. This is pointless too.
Ecclesiastes 5:11 As wealth grows, so do those who consume it. And what benefit is it to the owners except to look at it with their own eyes?
Ecclesiastes 5:12 A working person sleeps peacefully, whether they eat a little or a lot, but a rich person's wealth keeps them from sleeping well.
Ecclesiastes 5:13 I have seen a terrible problem on Earth: wealth hoarded by its owner to their harm.
Ecclesiastes 5:14 Those riches vanish by bad work: he has a son and has nothing to give him.
Ecclesiastes 5:15 When he was born from his mother, he was naked, and he will go back the same way when he dies, taking nothing of his work with him.
Ecclesiastes 5:16 This is also a terrible wrong: a person leaves the world just as they came into it. So what does someone gain from working for nothing?
Ecclesiastes 5:17 Throughout his life, he eats in the dark, feeling much sadness and anger because of his illness.
Ecclesiastes 5:18 I have seen that it is good and proper for a person to eat, drink, and enjoy the benefits of their work throughout their life under the sun, the life that God has given them, because this is their share.
Ecclesiastes 5:19 Everyone whom God has given wealth and riches, and the ability to enjoy them, to take their share, and to find joy in their work; this is a gift from God.
Ecclesiastes 5:20 He won't think much about his life's days, because God responds to him with joy in his heart.

Ecclesiastes 6:1 I have seen a bad thing everywhere in the world, and it happens often to people.
Ecclesiastes 6:2 A man whom God has given money, possessions, and respect, so he lacks nothing he wants, but if God doesn't let him enjoy these things and a stranger does instead, this is pointless and a terrible sickness.
Ecclesiastes 6:3 If a man has a hundred children and lives a long time, but is not happy or buried when he dies, it is better to be born dead.
Ecclesiastes 6:4 He comes with emptiness, leaves in the dark, and his name will be shrouded in darkness.
Ecclesiastes 6:5 He hasn't seen the sun or learned anything; he has more peace than the other.
Ecclesiastes 6:6 Even if a person lives two thousand years, they still do not experience true happiness. Don't we all end up in the same place after death?
Ecclesiastes 6:7 Everyone works to feed themselves, but no one is ever fully satisfied.
Ecclesiastes 6:8 What advantage does a wise person have over a fool? What does the poor person gain by knowing how to conduct themselves in life?
Ecclesiastes 6:9 Seeing what is in front of you is better than chasing your wishes. This, too, is pointless and frustrating.
Ecclesiastes 6:10 What has happened has already been named, and it is known that it is human; no one can argue with one who is stronger than themselves.
Ecclesiastes 6:11 With so many things that add to emptiness, how is a person improved?
Ecclesiastes 6:12 Who knows what is best for a person in life, during the meaningless days they pass like a shadow? Who can tell anyone what will happen after them under the sun?

Ecclesiastes 7:1 Having a good reputation is better than having expensive perfume, and the day someone dies is better than the day they are born.
Ecclesiastes 7:2 It is better to visit a place where people are sad because of death than a place where people are celebrating. This is because everyone will die someday, and the living should think about this.
Ecclesiastes 7:3 Sadness is better than laughing because a sad face can improve the heart.
Ecclesiastes 7:4 Wise people think about sad times; foolish people think about happy times.
Ecclesiastes 7:5 It is better to listen to the correction from someone smart than to enjoy the music of foolish people.
Ecclesiastes 7:6 Like the noise of thorns burning under a pot, so is a fool's laugh: it's also meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 7:7 Oppression can make a smart person angry; and a bribe can ruin their character.
Ecclesiastes 7:8 The end of something is better than its start, and being patient is better than being proud.
Ecclesiastes 7:9 Don't be quick to get angry, because anger lives in the hearts of fools.
Ecclesiastes 7:10 Do not ask why the old days were better than now; asking this does not show wisdom.
Ecclesiastes 7:11 Having wisdom and an inheritance is good, and it benefits those who live under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 7:12 Wisdom protects us, and so does money, but the best thing about knowledge is that wisdom brings life to those who possess it.
Ecclesiastes 7:13 Think about what God does: who can fix something if God made it bent?
Ecclesiastes 7:14 When times are good, be happy, but when times are bad, think: God has made one as well as the other, so that people can't predict anything about their future.
Ecclesiastes 7:15 In my empty days, I have seen everything: a good person dies despite being good, and a bad person lives long while being bad.
Ecclesiastes 7:16 Don't be too righteous or too wise; why ruin your life?
Ecclesiastes 7:17 Don't be too wicked or foolish; why die before it's your time?
Ecclesiastes 7:18 It is good for you to grasp this and not let go; because one who respects God will succeed in everything.
Ecclesiastes 7:19 Wisdom gives the wise more strength than ten strong men in the city.
Ecclesiastes 7:20 No one on earth is perfect; everyone does some good, but also makes mistakes.
Ecclesiastes 7:21 Don't pay attention to everything people say, or you might hear your servant speaking badly of you.
Ecclesiastes 7:22 Your heart knows that you have also cursed others many times.
Ecclesiastes 7:23 I have tested all these things with wisdom; I thought I could become wise, but it was out of my reach.
Ecclesiastes 7:24 What is far away and very deep, who can discover it?
Ecclesiastes 7:25 I set my heart to understand, to investigate, and to find wisdom and explanations, and to understand foolishness, senselessness, and madness.
Ecclesiastes 7:26 I find a woman whose heart is full of traps and her hands are like chains more bitter than death. Someone who pleases God will avoid her, but a sinner will be caught by her.
Ecclesiastes 7:27 Look, this is what I have discovered, says the teacher, adding one thing to another to find the explanation.
Ecclesiastes 7:28 My soul still searches, but I do not find: I have found one man among a thousand, but not one woman among all.
Ecclesiastes 7:29 Look, I have found only this: God made people good, but they have come up with many schemes.

Ecclesiastes 8:1 Who is as wise as that person? And who understands the meaning of things? A person's wisdom lights up their face, and it softens the hardness of their expression.
Ecclesiastes 8:2 I advise you to obey the king's order, because of your promise to God.
Ecclesiastes 8:3 Don't rush to leave his presence, and don't take part in wrong; for he does whatever he wants.
Ecclesiastes 8:4 Where a king's command is, there is power: and who can ask him, "What are you doing?"
Ecclesiastes 8:5 Anyone who follows the command will not experience anything bad; and a wise person understands the right time and decision.
Ecclesiastes 8:6 Every goal has its right time and way, so people often feel overwhelmed by troubles.
Ecclesiastes 8:7 He does not know what will happen: for who can tell him when it will be?
Ecclesiastes 8:8 No one has power over their spirit to keep it, and no one has control over the day of death. There is no release from that struggle; evil will not save those who are bound to it.
Ecclesiastes 8:9 I have seen all this and given my heart to every deed done under the sun: there is a time when one person rules over another to their harm.
Ecclesiastes 8:10 I saw the bad people buried who went back and forth from the holy place, and they were forgotten in the city where they did these things; this is also meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 8:11 Because punishment for bad actions is not given quickly, people are encouraged to keep doing wrong.
Ecclesiastes 8:12 Even if a sinner does wrong many times and lives a long life, I am sure that things will go well for those who respect God and show their respect for him.
Ecclesiastes 8:13 Things will not go well for the wicked, and he will not live long, like a shadow, because he does not respect God.
Ecclesiastes 8:14 There is a meaningless thing happening on earth: good people get what bad people deserve, and bad people get what good people deserve. I say this is also meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 8:15 I praised fun because the best thing for a person in life is to eat, drink, and enjoy themselves. This happiness will stay with them through their workdays, given by God.
Ecclesiastes 8:16 When I devoted my heart to learn wisdom and to observe the activities done on the earth: (because there are those who do not get sleep day or night:)
Ecclesiastes 8:17 I saw everything God has done, and we can't fully understand all that happens on earth. Even if we work hard to search for it, we won't find it. And even if a wise person thinks they can know it, they won't be able to discover it.

Ecclesiastes 9:1 I thought deeply about all this and decided to explain that the good and wise people, and what they do, are in God's control. No one can understand whether they will experience love or hate based on what they see around them.
Ecclesiastes 9:2 Everything happens to everyone: the same thing happens to good and bad people, to those who are pure and those who are not, to those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. Just as it is with the good person, so it is with the sinner; and it is the same for those who make promises and those who are afraid to.
Ecclesiastes 9:3 This is a bad thing among everything done under the sun: everyone experiences the same fate. Also, people's hearts are full of evil and insanity while they live, and afterward, they die.
Ecclesiastes 9:4 Those who are still alive have hope; a living dog is better than a dead lion.
Ecclesiastes 9:5 People who are alive know they will die, but the dead do not know anything and they no longer get rewards, because they are forgotten.
Ecclesiastes 9:6 Their love, hatred, and jealousy are all gone; they will never again take part in anything that happens on earth.
Ecclesiastes 9:7 Go on your way, enjoy your food, and be happy with your drink; for God accepts what you do now.
Ecclesiastes 9:8 Always wear clean clothes and keep your head oiled.
Ecclesiastes 9:9 Enjoy life with the wife you love all your days, which God has given you under the sun. This is your share in life and in your work while you are here.
Ecclesiastes 9:10 Do whatever your hand finds to do, and do it with all your strength; because there is no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom in the grave where you are headed.
Ecclesiastes 9:11 I came back and saw that being fast doesn't always win the race, being strong doesn't always win the battle, being wise doesn't always bring food, being smart doesn't always bring wealth, and being skilled doesn't always win favor; but time and chance happen to everyone.
Ecclesiastes 9:12 People don't know when their time will come, like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare; just like that, people are caught by sudden trouble.
Ecclesiastes 9:13 I have also seen this wisdom on earth, and it seemed very important to me:
Ecclesiastes 9:14 There was a small city with few people in it, and a great king attacked it, surrounded it, and built large barriers against it.
Ecclesiastes 9:15 In the city, they found a poor but wise man. He used his wisdom to save the city, but nobody remembered that poor man afterward.
Ecclesiastes 9:16 I said that wisdom is better than strength, but people ignore a poor man's wisdom and don't listen to his words.
Ecclesiastes 9:17 Wise people's words are heard better in silence than a ruler's shout among fools.
Ecclesiastes 9:18 Wisdom is better than tools of war, but one wrongdoer can ruin a lot of good.

Ecclesiastes 10:1 Dead flies make the perfumer's oil give off a bad smell; similarly, a little foolishness can ruin the respect of someone known for wisdom and honor.
Ecclesiastes 10:2 A wise person's heart leads them to do what is right; but a foolish person's heart leads them to do what is wrong.
Ecclesiastes 10:3 Yes, when a fool walks on the road, he lacks wisdom, and he tells everyone that he is a fool.
Ecclesiastes 10:4 If a ruler gets angry with you, don't leave your position; staying calm can resolve major problems.
Ecclesiastes 10:5 I have seen a bad thing under the sun; it is a mistake that comes from the leader.
Ecclesiastes 10:6 Foolishness is honored, and the wealthy take the humble seats.
Ecclesiastes 10:7 I have seen workers on horses and rulers walking like workers on the ground.
Ecclesiastes 10:8 Anyone who digs a pit will fall into it; and whoever breaks through a hedge, a snake will bite him.
Ecclesiastes 10:9 Whoever moves stones may get hurt; and whoever splits wood may be in danger from it.
Ecclesiastes 10:10 If the tool is dull and its sharpness is not honed, then one must use more strength; however, wisdom helps to apply effort effectively.
Ecclesiastes 10:11 For sure, a snake will bite if it's not charmed; a chatterer is no different.
Ecclesiastes 10:12 A wise person's words are kind, but a fool's words will ruin him.
Ecclesiastes 10:13 The first things he says are silly, and his final words are crazy and harmful.
Ecclesiastes 10:14 A fool talks too much and no one knows what will happen. Who can say what will come after him?
Ecclesiastes 10:15 The hard work of foolish people tires them all because they don't know how to get to the city.
Ecclesiastes 10:16 Trouble comes to a country when its leader is immature, and its rulers eat early in the day.
Ecclesiastes 10:17 Happy is the country when its king is from a noble family, and its leaders eat at the right time, for strength, and not to get drunk.
Ecclesiastes 10:18 Because of too much laziness, the building falls apart; and because of not using one's hands, the house leaks.
Ecclesiastes 10:19 A feast is for fun, and wine cheers us up, but money solves all problems.
Ecclesiastes 10:20 Do not curse the king, even to yourself; and do not curse the wealthy in your bedroom: because a bird might spread the news, and a creature with wings might reveal what you said.

Ecclesiastes 11:1 Throw your bread on the water, and you will find it again after a long time.
Ecclesiastes 11:2 Share with seven, or even eight, because you do not know what troubles may come on the earth.
Ecclesiastes 11:3 If clouds are full, they pour rain on the earth. If a tree falls south or north, it stays where it fell.
Ecclesiastes 11:4 If you wait for perfect weather, you won't plant seeds; if you look at the clouds, you won't harvest crops.
Ecclesiastes 11:5 You don't know how the spirit comes to the body, or how a baby's bones grow inside a pregnant woman: just like that, you don't understand how God, who makes everything, works.
Ecclesiastes 11:6 Plant your seeds in the morning, and don't stop working in the evening. You can't tell if one will succeed, the other, or if both will be equally good.
Ecclesiastes 11:7 Surely light is sweet, and it's nice for the eyes to see the sun.
Ecclesiastes 11:8 If a person lives for many years and enjoys them, he should still remember there will be many dark days. Everything that happens is meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 11:9 Be happy, young person, while you are young. Let your heart give you joy in your youth. Follow your heart and what you see with your eyes, but remember that God will judge you for all these things.
Ecclesiastes 11:10 So take away sadness from your heart and stop doing bad things with your body, because being young is not so important.

Ecclesiastes 12:1 Remember your Creator while you are young, before bad days arrive and the years come when you will find no joy in them.
Ecclesiastes 12:2 Before the sun, light, moon, or stars grow dark, and the clouds come back after the rain:
Ecclesiastes 12:3 On the day when the guards of the house shake, the strong people bend, the grinders stop because there are only a few, and the ones looking out the windows can't see clearly.
Ecclesiastes 12:4 The doors on the streets will close when the grinding noise is quiet, someone will wake up at the bird's call, and all the music will fade away.
Ecclesiastes 12:5 People will fear high places and be scared on the road. The almond tree will bloom, the grasshopper will drag, and desire will fade away. This is because everyone dies and people mourn in the streets.
Ecclesiastes 12:6 Before the silver cord snaps, or the gold bowl cracks, or the jug shatters at the spring, or the wheel breaks at the well.
Ecclesiastes 12:7 The dust will go back to the earth where it came from, and the spirit will return to God who gave it.
Ecclesiastes 12:8 Everything is meaningless, says the teacher; all is meaningless.
Ecclesiastes 12:9 The teacher was wise and continued to teach the people knowledge. He paid attention and collected many wise sayings, arranging them well.
Ecclesiastes 12:10 The teacher tried to find pleasing words; what was written was honest and true.
Ecclesiastes 12:11 The wise people's words are like prods, and like nails set down by leaders of groups, given by one God.
Ecclesiastes 12:12 Also, my child, be warned: writing many books has no limit; and studying a lot is tiring for the body.
Ecclesiastes 12:13 Listen to the final point: Respect God and follow his rules, because this is everyone's main job.
Ecclesiastes 12:14 God will judge everything we do, even the things we keep secret, whether they are good or bad.

Song of Solomon 1:1 The best song, which is Solomon's.
Song of Solomon 1:2 Let him kiss me with his mouth's kisses: because your love is better than wine.
Song of Solomon 1:3 Because your perfumes smell so good, your name is like perfume spreading out, so young women love you.
Song of Solomon 1:4 Pull me, and we'll run after you. The king brought me into his rooms. We'll be happy and celebrate in you. We will think about your love more than wine. Good people love you.
Song of Solomon 1:5 I am dark and beautiful, O women of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like Solomon's drapes.
Song of Solomon 1:6 Do not stare at me because I am dark, for the sun has darkened me. My siblings were mad at me; they made me watch over the vineyards, but I did not take care of my own vineyard.
Song of Solomon 1:7 Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you feed your flock and where you rest them at noon, for why should I be like one who wanders beside the flocks of your friends?
Song of Solomon 1:8 If you don't know, most beautiful woman, follow the path where the sheep walked, and feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
Song of Solomon 1:9 I have compared you, my love, to a group of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.
Song of Solomon 1:10 Your cheeks look lovely with rows of jewels, your neck with gold chains.
Song of Solomon 1:11 We will create gold borders for you with silver dots.
Song of Solomon 1:12 While the king is at his table, my perfume spreads its fragrance.
Song of Solomon 1:13 My loved one is like a bundle of myrrh to me; he will rest between my breasts all night.
Song of Solomon 1:14 My loved one is to me like a bunch of henna flowers in the vineyards of En Gedi.
Song of Solomon 1:15 Look, you are beautiful, my love; look, you are beautiful; your eyes are like doves.
Song of Solomon 1:16 Look, you are beautiful, my loved one, yes, delightful; our bed is also fresh and green.
Song of Solomon 1:17 The support beams of our house are made of cedar, and the beams of our roof are fir.

Song of Solomon 2:1 I am the rose of Sharon and the lily of the valleys.
Song of Solomon 2:2 Like a lily among thorns, so is my loved one among the women.
Song of Solomon 2:3 Just like an apple tree stands out from the forest trees, so my loved one stands out among other men. I enjoyed sitting in his shade, and his fruit tasted sweet to me.
Song of Solomon 2:4 He took me to a feast, and he showed his love for me like a flag.
Song of Solomon 2:5 Support me with raisins, cheer me up with apples; I am overwhelmed with love.
Song of Solomon 2:6 His left hand is under my head, and his right hand hugs me.
Song of Solomon 2:7 I ask you, young women of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and deer of the fields, not to disturb or awaken my love until he wishes.
Song of Solomon 2:8 I hear my loved one's voice! Look, he's coming, jumping over the mountains, hopping on the hills.
Song of Solomon 2:9 My loved one is like a deer or a young stag: look, he stands behind our wall, he looks in at the windows, showing himself through the trellis.
Song of Solomon 2:10 My loved one spoke and said to me, Get up, my love, my beautiful one, and come with me.
Song of Solomon 2:11 The winter is over, the rain has stopped.
Song of Solomon 2:12 Flowers show up on the earth; it's time for birds to sing, and we hear the turtle dove in our land.
Song of Solomon 2:13 The fig tree grows its young figs, and the grapevines with new grapes smell sweet. Get up, my love, my beautiful one, and come with me.
Song of Solomon 2:14 My dove hiding in the rocks and secret stairways, show me your face, let me hear your voice; your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
Song of Solomon 2:15 Catch the foxes for us, the small foxes that ruin the vineyards; our vineyards are blooming.
Song of Solomon 2:16 My loved one belongs to me, and I belong to him; he grazes among the flowers.
Song of Solomon 2:17 Wait until the day starts and the shadows vanish, then come back, my loved one, and be like a deer or young stag on the Bether hills.

Song of Solomon 3:1 At night in my bed, I searched for the one my soul loves: I searched for him, but did not find him.
Song of Solomon 3:2 I will get up now and walk through the city, in the streets and squares, looking for the one my heart loves. I looked for him but did not find him.
Song of Solomon 3:3 The guards walking through the city found me. I asked them, "Have you seen the one I love deeply?"
Song of Solomon 3:4 I had just left them when I found the one my heart loves. I held him tightly and wouldn't let go until I brought him to my mother's home, to the room of the one who gave birth to me.
Song of Solomon 3:5 I ask you, women of Jerusalem, by the deer and the wild does, do not disturb or wake my love until he wants to.
Song of Solomon 3:6 Who is this coming from the desert like smoke columns, scented with myrrh and incense, with all the spice seller's powders?
Song of Solomon 3:7 Look at his bed, which belongs to Solomon; sixty brave men surround it, the brave ones of Israel.
Song of Solomon 3:8 They all carry swords, skilled in fighting: each man has his sword on his leg because of fear at night.
Song of Solomon 3:9 King Solomon built himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon.
Song of Solomon 3:10 He made its pillars of silver, its base of gold, its cover of purple, and its middle was decorated with love, for the women of Jerusalem.
Song of Solomon 3:11 Go out, daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon wearing the crown his mother gave him on his wedding day, and on the day he was very happy.

Song of Solomon 4:1 Look, you are beautiful, my love; look, you are beautiful; your eyes are like doves' eyes among your hair: your hair is like a group of goats seen on Mount Gilead.
Song of Solomon 4:2 Your teeth are like a group of sheep with even cuts, freshly washed, where each has a twin, and none is without offspring.
Song of Solomon 4:3 Your lips are like a red ribbon, and your words are lovely. Your cheeks are like pieces of pomegranate behind your hair.
Song of Solomon 4:4 Your neck is like a strong tower built to hold weapons, with a thousand shields hanging on it, all belonging to strong warriors.
Song of Solomon 4:5 Your two breasts are like two young deer that are twins, which browse among the lilies.
Song of Solomon 4:6 Until daylight comes and shadows go away, I will go to the myrrh mountain and the frankincense hill.
Song of Solomon 4:7 You are completely beautiful, my love; you have no flaws.
Song of Solomon 4:8 Come with me from Lebanon, my partner, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from where the lions live, from the mountains where the leopards are.
Song of Solomon 4:9 You have captured my heart, my sister, my wife; you have captured my heart with just one look from your eye, with just one necklace around your neck.
Song of Solomon 4:10 Your love is so beautiful, my sister, my partner! Your love is better than wine, and your perfume smells better than all spices!
Song of Solomon 4:11 Your lips, my partner, drip like honeycomb: honey and milk are beneath your tongue; and your clothes smell like the scent of Lebanon.
Song of Solomon 4:12 My sister, my partner, is like a private garden, a locked spring, a sealed fountain.
Song of Solomon 4:13 Your garden is like a pomegranate orchard with nice fruits, henna, and nard plants.
Song of Solomon 4:14 Nard and saffron; sweet cane and cinnamon, along with every frankincense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices.
Song of Solomon 4:15 A garden's fountain, a spring of fresh water, and rivers from Lebanon.
Song of Solomon 4:16 Wake up, north wind; and come, south wind; blow on my garden, so its fragrances spread. Let my loved one enter his garden and enjoy its delicious fruits.

Song of Solomon 5:1 I have come into my garden, my sister, my partner: I have collected my myrrh and spices; I have eaten my honeycomb and honey; I have drunk my wine and milk. Eat, friends; drink, yes, drink a lot, my loved one.
Song of Solomon 5:2 I am asleep, but my heart is awake: it's my loved one's voice knocking, saying, "Let me in, my sister, my love, my pure one, my dove; because my head is wet with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night."
Song of Solomon 5:3 I took off my coat; why should I put it back on? I cleaned my feet; why should I get them dirty again?
Song of Solomon 5:4 My loved one reached in through the door opening, and I was deeply stirred for him.
Song of Solomon 5:5 I got up to open the door for my loved one; my hands dripped with myrrh, and my fingers with fragrant myrrh, on the lock's handles.
Song of Solomon 5:6 I opened the door for my loved one, but he had left and was gone. My heart sank when he spoke. I looked for him but couldn't find him. I called him, but he didn't answer me.
Song of Solomon 5:7 The guards patrolling the city found me and beat me; they hurt me. The wall keepers took my veil away.
Song of Solomon 5:8 I ask you, women of Jerusalem, if you see my loved one, please tell him I am deeply in love.
Song of Solomon 5:9 What makes your beloved better than any other, O most beautiful among women? What makes your beloved stand out that you give us such a command?
Song of Solomon 5:10 My loved one is fair and has a healthy red glow, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
Song of Solomon 5:11 His head is like the finest gold, his hair is thick and black as a raven.
Song of Solomon 5:12 His eyes are like dove's eyes by streams of water, bathed in milk, and perfectly placed.
Song of Solomon 5:13 His cheeks are like a garden of sweet spices, and sweet flowers; his lips are like lilies, dripping with the sweet scent of myrrh.
Song of Solomon 5:14 His hands are like gold rings with beryl stones; his stomach is like polished ivory decorated with sapphires.
Song of Solomon 5:15 His legs are like marble columns on gold bases: his face is like Lebanon, as grand as the cedars.
Song of Solomon 5:16 His words are very sweet; yes, he is completely beautiful. This is my loved one, and this is my friend, O women of Jerusalem.
