Isaiah 1:1 This is the vision that Isaiah, son of Amoz, had about Judah and Jerusalem during the time when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
Isaiah 1:2 Listen, skies, and pay attention, earth: God has spoken, I have raised and cared for children, but they have turned against me.
Isaiah 1:3 The ox knows its owner, and the donkey knows where its master feeds it, but Israel doesn't know, my people don't think about it.
Isaiah 1:4 Oh sinful country, people full of wrongdoing, offspring of those who do evil, kids who spoil things: they have left God, they have made the Holy One of Israel angry, they have turned away.
Isaiah 1:5 Why should you be punished again? You will only rebel more and more: your entire mind is ill, and your entire heart is weak.
Isaiah 1:6 From the bottom of the foot to the top of the head, there is no health in it; only wounds, bruises, and open sores. They have not been cleaned, bandaged, or treated with ointment.
Isaiah 1:7 Your country is empty, your cities are burned: strangers eat up your land in front of you, and it is empty, as destroyed by outsiders.
Isaiah 1:8 The Daughter of Zion is left like a small house in a vineyard, like a shelter in a cucumber field, like a city surrounded by enemies.
Isaiah 1:9 If God had not left us a small group of survivors, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been like Gomorrah.
Isaiah 1:10 Listen to God's message, you leaders of Sodom; pay attention to our God's rules, people of Gomorrah.
Isaiah 1:11 Why do you offer me so many sacrifices? says God. I have had enough of burnt rams and fat from well-fed animals; I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats.
Isaiah 1:12 When you come to meet me, who asked you to walk in my courtyards?
Isaiah 1:13 Stop bringing worthless gifts; I hate the smell of incense. New moon celebrations, Sabbaths, and meetings—I cannot stand them; they are full of sin, even the special gatherings.
Isaiah 1:14 I hate your new moons and celebrations; they bother me, and I am tired of putting up with them.
Isaiah 1:15 When you raise your hands, I will look away from you; even when you pray a lot, I won't listen: your hands have blood on them.
Isaiah 1:16 Clean yourselves, make yourselves pure; stop doing wrong things that I see; stop doing bad things.
Isaiah 1:17 Learn to do good; seek fairness, help those who are suffering, defend orphans, and argue for widows.
Isaiah 1:18 Come now, and let's talk this over, says God: even if your sins are bright red, they will become as white as snow; even if they are deep red like crimson, they will be like wool.
Isaiah 1:19 If you are willing and obey, you will enjoy the best from the land.
Isaiah 1:20 If you refuse and rebel, you will be destroyed by the sword because God has said it.
Isaiah 1:21 How has the loyal city turned into a prostitute! It was once full of fairness; goodness made its home there; but now there are killers.
Isaiah 1:22 Your silver has turned to waste, your wine diluted with water.
Isaiah 1:23 Your leaders are disobedient and friends with thieves: they all love getting gifts and chase after rewards: they do not defend orphans, nor do they care about the needs of widows.
Isaiah 1:24 So God, the powerful One of Israel, says, "I will get relief from my foes and take revenge on my enemies."
Isaiah 1:25 I will intervene for you, completely remove your impurities, and get rid of all your lesser metals.
Isaiah 1:26 I will bring back your judges like before, and your advisors as in the start; then you will be known as the city of rightness, the loyal city.
Isaiah 1:27 Zion will be saved through justice, and those who turn to her will be brought back with fairness.
Isaiah 1:28 The ruin of wrongdoers and sinners will happen at the same time, and those who abandon God will be destroyed.
Isaiah 1:29 They will feel shame for the oak trees you wanted, and you will be embarrassed about the gardens you picked.
Isaiah 1:30 You will be like an oak tree with withering leaves, and like a garden without water.
Isaiah 1:31 The strong will be like tinder, and their creator like a spark; they will both burn, and no one will put them out.

Isaiah 2:1 Isaiah, son of Amoz, had a vision about Judah and Jerusalem.
Isaiah 2:2 In the future, God's house on the mountain will be the highest of all, and all countries will come to it.
Isaiah 2:3 Many people will go and say, "Come, let's go up to God's mountain, to the home of Jacob’s God, and he will teach us his ways, so we can follow his paths." For the law will come from Zion, and God's word from Jerusalem.
Isaiah 2:4 He will judge between the nations and correct many people. They will turn their swords into tools for farming and their spears into cutting tools. One nation will not fight another, nor will they learn about war anymore.
Isaiah 2:5 People of Jacob, come, let's walk in God's light.
Isaiah 2:6 So you have left your people, the house of Jacob, because they follow Eastern ways, act like Philistine fortune-tellers, and are happy with foreign children.
Isaiah 2:7 Their land is filled with silver and gold, with no end to their wealth; it is also full of horses, with no end to their chariots.
Isaiah 2:8 Their land is filled with idols. They bow down to what their own hands have made, to what their own fingers have created.
Isaiah 2:9 The common man bows down, and the important man lowers himself; so do not forgive them.
Isaiah 2:10 Go into the rocks and hide in the ground because you are afraid of God and because of his great power.
Isaiah 2:11 People's proud looks will be lowered, and their arrogance will be brought down, and only God will be lifted high on that day.
Isaiah 2:12 The day of God will come for all the proud and high people, and for everyone raised up; they will be made low.
Isaiah 2:13 On all the tall cedars of Lebanon and all the big oaks of Bashan,
Isaiah 2:14 On all the tall mountains and on all the high hills,
Isaiah 2:15 On every tall tower and every strong wall,
Isaiah 2:16 On all the ships of Tarshish and on all beautiful artworks.
Isaiah 2:17 People's pride will be lowered, and their arrogance will be brought down; only God will be lifted up on that day.
Isaiah 2:18 He will completely destroy the idols.
Isaiah 2:19 They will hide in rock holes and earth caves because they fear God and his majestic glory when he comes to shake the earth greatly.
Isaiah 2:20 On that day, a person will throw away their silver and gold idols, which they made to worship, to the moles and bats.
Isaiah 2:21 To hide in the rock crevices and on high rugged cliffs, because they are afraid of God and in awe of his majestic power, when he stands to make the earth tremble greatly.
Isaiah 2:22 Stop depending on people, who have only breath in their noses. What are they really worth?

Isaiah 3:1 Look, God will remove from Jerusalem and Judah all support, the entire supply of bread, and all the water.
Isaiah 3:2 The strong man, the soldier, the judge, the prophet, the wise person, and the elder,
Isaiah 3:3 The leader of fifty, the respected man, the advisor, the skilled worker, and the good speaker.
Isaiah 3:4 I will make children their leaders, and young ones will rule over them.
Isaiah 3:5 People will mistreat each other, neighbors will act badly towards one another, the young will disrespect the old, and the lowly will act rudely towards the respected.
Isaiah 3:6 If a man grabs his brother from his father's family and says, "You have clothes, be our leader and take charge of this mess."
Isaiah 3:7 On that day, he will promise, saying, "I do not want to heal; for there is neither food nor clothes in my house: do not make me a leader of the people."
Isaiah 3:8 Jerusalem is destroyed, and Judah has fallen, because their speech and actions are against God, angering his glorious presence.
Isaiah 3:9 Their faces show their guilt; they brag about their sins like Sodom and don't hide them. Trouble to them, for they have brought evil upon themselves.
Isaiah 3:10 Tell the good people that things will go well for them, because they will enjoy what their actions have earned.
Isaiah 3:11 Trouble will come to the bad person; he will be paid back for what he has done.
Isaiah 3:12 My people are pushed around by children and ruled by women. My people, your leaders mislead you and ruin your paths.
Isaiah 3:13 God stands up to argue his case and stands to judge the people.
Isaiah 3:14 God will judge the elders and leaders of his people because you have destroyed the vineyard, and the robbed goods of the poor are in your homes.
Isaiah 3:15 Why are you hurting my people and crushing the poor? says God.
Isaiah 3:16 God says, because the women of Zion are proud, walking with their heads high and flirting with their eyes, strutting as they go, and their feet make sounds.
Isaiah 3:17 So God will strike the tops of Zion's daughters' heads with sores, and God will expose their private parts.
Isaiah 3:18 On that day, God will remove their ankle bracelets, headbands, and crescent necklaces.
Isaiah 3:19 The chains, the bracelets, and the scarves,
Isaiah 3:20 The caps, leg accessories, headbands, perfume boxes, and earrings,
Isaiah 3:21 The rings and nose rings
Isaiah 3:22 The different sets of clothes, the cloaks, the headscarves, and the hairpins,
Isaiah 3:23 The eyeglasses, the nice cloth, the head coverings, and the scarves.
Isaiah 3:24 It will happen that where there was once perfume, there will be a bad smell; instead of a belt, torn clothes; instead of nicely done hair, baldness; instead of fine clothes, rough sackcloth; and scars will replace beauty.
Isaiah 3:25 Your men will die by the sword, and your strong will fall in battle.
Isaiah 3:26 Her gates will cry and grieve; and she, being empty, will sit on the ground.

Isaiah 4:1 On that day, seven women will grab one man and say, "We will eat our own food and wear our own clothes; just let us have your name to remove our shame."
Isaiah 4:2 On that day, God's branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the earth's produce will be outstanding and attractive for the survivors in Israel.
Isaiah 4:3 Everyone who stays in Zion and survives in Jerusalem will be called holy, each one listed among the living in Jerusalem.
Isaiah 4:4 When God cleans the dirt from Zion's daughters and removes Jerusalem's blood by judging and burning.
Isaiah 4:5 God will make a cloud and smoke over every home on Mount Zion and over its gatherings by day, and a bright, burning fire by night; all the splendid things will have protection.
Isaiah 4:6 There will be a shelter to provide shade from the heat during the day, and a safe place to protect from storms and rain.

Isaiah 5:1 I will sing a song for my loved one about his vineyard. My loved one has a vineyard on a fertile hill.
Isaiah 5:2 He built a fence around it, removed the stones, planted the best vines, built a tower in the middle, and made a winepress in it. He expected it to grow grapes, but it grew wild grapes instead.
Isaiah 5:3 Now, people of Jerusalem and Judah, please decide who is right—me or my vineyard.
Isaiah 5:4 What more could I have done for my vineyard that I didn't do? Why did it grow wild grapes when I expected it to produce good grapes?
Isaiah 5:5 Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will remove its hedge, and it will be devoured; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.
Isaiah 5:6 I will make it a wasteland: it won't be trimmed or tilled; instead, thistles and thorns will grow. I will tell the clouds not to rain on it.
Isaiah 5:7 God's vineyard is the people of Israel, and the Judah men are his favored plants. He expected fairness, but found abuse; he wanted rightness, but heard pleas for help.
Isaiah 5:8 Pity those who combine house to house and field to field until there's no more space, just to live alone on the land!
Isaiah 5:9 God told me, "Truly, many big and beautiful houses will be empty with no one living in them."
Isaiah 5:10 Indeed, ten acres of vineyard will produce only one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will produce only an ephah of grain.
Isaiah 5:11 Trouble awaits those who get up early to start drinking and keep on until night, until they are heated by wine.
Isaiah 5:12 At their parties, they have harps, violins, drums, flutes, and wine, but they don't care about what God has done or pay attention to what he has made.
Isaiah 5:13 My people have been taken away as captives because they lack knowledge; their leaders are starving, and many are parched with thirst.
Isaiah 5:14 So hell has grown bigger and opened wide its mouth with no limit: and their splendor, crowds, show of wealth, and those who celebrate, will all go down into it.
Isaiah 5:15 The average person will be lowered, and the powerful person will be made humble, and the proud will be brought down.
Isaiah 5:16 God will be honored when he judges, and the holy God will be made pure through justice.
Isaiah 5:17 The lambs will eat as they do, and strangers will eat in the empty lands of the wealthy.
Isaiah 5:18 Trouble awaits those who pull sin along with ropes of useless things, and drag wrongdoings as if with a heavy cart rope.
Isaiah 5:19 Those who say, "Let God hurry; let Him speed up His work so we may see it. And let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come closer and happen, so we may know it!"
Isaiah 5:20 Trouble comes to those who say bad things are good, and good things are bad; who replace light with darkness, and darkness with light; who exchange bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter.
Isaiah 5:21 Pity those who think they are smart and wise by themselves!
Isaiah 5:22 Trouble comes to those who are good at drinking wine and those who mix strong drinks well.
Isaiah 5:23 They declare the guilty innocent for bribes and deny the good their rights!
Isaiah 5:24 So just as fire eats up straw and flames burn up dry grass, their roots will rot, and their flowers will turn to dust because they have rejected God's law and ignored the words of Israel's Holy God.
Isaiah 5:25 So God is angry with his people; he has reached out to punish them and struck them down. The mountains shook, and their bodies lay torn in the streets. Yet even with all this, God's anger has not stopped, and his hand is still raised to strike again.
Isaiah 5:26 He will raise a flag for distant nations and whistle for them from the earth's end. Look, they will quickly and speedily come.
Isaiah 5:27 No one will get tired or fall; no one will rest or sleep; their belts won't come undone, nor will their shoe straps break.
Isaiah 5:28 Their arrows are sharp, their bows ready, their horses' hooves hard as rock, and their wheels spin like a storm.
Isaiah 5:29 Their growling will sound like a lion's; they will roar like young lions; they will growl, grab their catch, take it to a safe place, and no one will rescue it.
Isaiah 5:30 On that day, they will shout at them like the sea's roar. If someone looks at the land, they will see darkness and sadness, and even the sky above will be dark.

Isaiah 6:1 The year King Uzziah died, I saw God on a high and exalted throne, and his robe filled the temple.
Isaiah 6:2 Above it stood the seraphim: each one had six wings; with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
Isaiah 6:3 One called to another, saying, “Holy, holy, holy, is God of all: the whole earth is full of his glory.”
Isaiah 6:4 The door's posts shook with the sound of the shout, and the house was filled with smoke.
Isaiah 6:5 I said, "I'm in trouble! I am ruined because I have dirty lips and live among people with dirty lips, yet I have seen the King, God."
Isaiah 6:6 One of the seraphs flew to me with a live coal in his hand that he took from the altar with tongs.
Isaiah 6:7 He put it on my mouth and said, "See, this has touched your lips; your guilt is gone, and your sin is forgiven."
Isaiah 6:8 I also heard God's voice asking, "Who should I send, and who will go for us?" Then I said, "Here I am; send me."
Isaiah 6:9 He said, "Go and tell these people, 'You may hear, but you will not understand; you may see, but you will not know what you're seeing.'"
Isaiah 6:10 Make these people's hearts dull, their ears deaf, and blind their eyes; so they won't see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn back, and be healed.
Isaiah 6:11 I asked, "God, how long will this last?" And he replied, "Until the cities are empty, the houses have no one living in them, and the land is completely deserted."
Isaiah 6:12 God has taken people far away, and there is a big emptiness in the land.
Isaiah 6:13 In it, a tenth will remain, and it will revive and be used for food. Like a terebinth or an oak tree that keeps its strength even when it loses its leaves, so will the holy people be the strength of the land.

Isaiah 7:1 During the time of Ahaz, Jotham's son, and grandson of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah, Remaliah's son and king of Israel, attacked Jerusalem but could not defeat it.
Isaiah 7:2 The house of David was informed, "Syria has joined forces with Ephraim." Then his and his people's hearts shook like trees in the forest shake in the wind.
Isaiah 7:3 God told Isaiah, "Go out now to meet Ahaz, along with your son Shearjashub, at the end of the water channel of the upper pool on the road to the launderer's field."
Isaiah 7:4 Tell him, "Be careful and stay calm; don't be afraid or weak because of the dying fires of Rezin's anger with Syria, and the son of Remaliah."
Isaiah 7:5 Because Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son have planned something bad against you, saying,
Isaiah 7:6 Let's attack Judah, trouble it, make a gap for us, and place Tabeal's son as king there.
Isaiah 7:7 God says, "It will not happen, nor will it take place."
Isaiah 7:8 Syria's capital is Damascus, and Damascus's leader is Rezin. In 65 years, Ephraim will be destroyed and no longer be a nation.
Isaiah 7:9 Ephraim's capital is Samaria, and the leader of Samaria is Remaliah's son. If you don't believe, you will not last.
Isaiah 7:10 God spoke to Ahaz again, saying,
Isaiah 7:11 Ask for a sign from God; you can ask for it to be deep down or high up.
Isaiah 7:12 Ahaz said, I will not ask, nor will I test God.
Isaiah 7:13 He said, "Listen, family of David; is it not enough for you to tire people? Will you also tire my God?"
Isaiah 7:14 God will give you a sign: A young woman will become pregnant, have a son, and name him Immanuel.
Isaiah 7:15 He will eat butter and honey to learn how to reject what is bad and choose what is good.
Isaiah 7:16 Before the child learns to reject evil and choose good, the land you hate will be abandoned by its two kings.
Isaiah 7:17 God will bring upon you, your people, and your ancestors' house, times unlike any since Ephraim separated from Judah—the king of Assyria included.
Isaiah 7:18 In that day, God will call for the flies from Egypt's farthest rivers and the bees from Assyria.
Isaiah 7:19 They will come and rest in the empty valleys, in the rock crevices, and among all the thorny plants and bushes.
Isaiah 7:20 On that day, God will use a hired razor, from the people across the river, the king of Assyria, to shave the head, the hair on the feet, and also remove the beard.
Isaiah 7:21 On that day, a person will take care of a young cow and two sheep.
Isaiah 7:22 Because there will be so much milk, people will eat butter; everyone left in the land will eat butter and honey.
Isaiah 7:23 On that day, every place with a thousand grapevines, each worth a thousand silver coins, will be overtaken by weeds and thorns.
Isaiah 7:24 People will come there with arrows and bows, because the whole land will be covered with thorns and briers.
Isaiah 7:25 On every hill plowed with tools, there won't be fear of sharp plants; instead, it will be a place for oxen and for smaller animals to walk.

Isaiah 8:1 God told me, "Get a large scroll and write on it with a normal pen about Mahershalalhashbaz."
Isaiah 8:2 I chose trustworthy people to witness, Uriah the priest and Zechariah, Jeberechiah's son.
Isaiah 8:3 I went to the prophetess; she became pregnant and had a son. Then God told me, "Name him Mahershalalhashbaz."
Isaiah 8:4 Before the child learns to say "My father" or "My mother," the wealth of Damascus and the goods of Samaria will be taken by the king of Assyria.
Isaiah 8:5 God spoke to me again, saying,
Isaiah 8:6 Since these people reject the gentle flowing waters of Shiloah and are happy with Rezin and the son of Remaliah;
Isaiah 8:7 Now then, see how God brings the river's strong and many waters against them, including the Assyrian king and his might. He will rise above all his streams and overflow all his banks.
Isaiah 8:8 He will pass through Judah, flooding and crossing over, reaching up to the neck; his stretched-out wings will cover the width of your land, Immanuel.
Isaiah 8:9 Join together, people, and you will be destroyed; listen, all you from distant lands: prepare for battle, and you will be destroyed; prepare for battle, and you will be destroyed.
Isaiah 8:10 Make plans together, but they will fail; say what you want, but it won't happen, because God is with us.
Isaiah 8:11 God spoke to me forcefully and taught me not to follow this people's ways, saying.
Isaiah 8:12 Don't call everything a conspiracy, like these people do, and don't fear what they fear; do not be terrified.
Isaiah 8:13 Make God your only holy one; fear him and be in awe of him.
Isaiah 8:14 He will be a safe place, but also a stumbling stone and a rock that causes offense to both the families of Israel, and a trap and a snare to the people of Jerusalem.
Isaiah 8:15 Many of them will stumble, fall, get hurt, be caught, and be captured.
Isaiah 8:16 Keep the teaching safe, put the law in the hearts of my followers.
Isaiah 8:17 I will wait for God, who hides from the people of Jacob, and I will seek Him.
Isaiah 8:18 Look, I and the children God has given me are for signs and wonders in Israel from God who lives on Mount Zion.
Isaiah 8:19 When people tell you to ask for help from those who talk to spirits and wizards who whisper and murmur, shouldn't you ask for help from your God instead of looking for answers among the dead?
Isaiah 8:20 Refer to God's law and message: if they do not agree with this, it is because they lack understanding.
Isaiah 8:21 They will go through it in great trouble and hunger, and when they are hungry, they will become upset, curse their king and God, and look up.
Isaiah 8:22 They will look to the earth and see distress and darkness, the gloom of suffering, and they will be pushed into darkness.

Isaiah 9:1 Still, the gloom won't be as heavy as the trouble she first had, when God at first only slightly punished the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, and later punished it much more harshly by the sea, past Jordan, in the area of the nations.
Isaiah 9:2 People who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in the land where death casts its shadow, on them the light has shone.
Isaiah 9:3 You have made the nation larger, but not made its joy greater. They are happy in your presence like they are happy at harvest time, and like people rejoicing when they share out what they have taken.
Isaiah 9:4 For you have shattered the weight he carried and the stick on his shoulder, the club of his enemy, just like in the time of Midian.
Isaiah 9:5 Every warrior's battle involves chaos and bloody clothes; but this fight will be with burning and fire's fuel.
Isaiah 9:6 A child is born to us, a son is given to us; he will govern, and he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace.
Isaiah 9:7 His government and peace will grow forever. He will rule on David's throne and over his kingdom, setting it up and making it secure, fair, and just from now on and always. God's passionate commitment will make this happen.
Isaiah 9:8 God sent a message to Jacob, and it arrived in Israel.
Isaiah 9:9 Everyone, including Ephraim and the people of Samaria who speak with pride and strong hearts, will know,
Isaiah 9:10 The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with cut stones; the sycamores have been chopped down, but we will replace them with cedars.
Isaiah 9:11 So God will make Rezin's enemies attack him and cause his foes to unite.
Isaiah 9:12 The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind, will attack and consume Israel completely. Despite this, God remains angry, and his power is still at work.
Isaiah 9:13 The people do not turn to the one who strikes them, nor do they look for God.
Isaiah 9:14 So God will remove the leaders and followers from Israel, as well as everything else, in one day.
Isaiah 9:15 The old and respected person is the leader; and the false teacher is the least important.
Isaiah 9:16 The leaders of these people lead them astray, and those who follow them are ruined.
Isaiah 9:17 So, God will not be happy with their young men, nor will he show kindness to the orphans and widows, because everyone is fake and does bad things, and all they say is foolish. Despite all this, God is still angry and ready to act.
Isaiah 9:18 Evil acts burn like fire: they will consume the briars and thorns, and will spread in the dense parts of the forest, rising up like smoke.
Isaiah 9:19 God's anger has made the land dark, and the people will burn like fuel for the fire; no one will show mercy to his brother.
Isaiah 9:20 He will grab with his right hand and still be hungry; he will eat with his left hand and not be satisfied. Each person will eat the flesh of their own arm.
Isaiah 9:21 Manasseh and Ephraim will fight each other, but together they will fight against Judah. Despite this, God is still angry and continues to punish.

Isaiah 10:1 Trouble comes to those who make unfair laws and write rules that cause suffering.
Isaiah 10:2 To push away the needy from fair treatment, and to take the rights from the poor of my people, so that they can take advantage of widows and steal from children without parents!
Isaiah 10:3 What will you do when the time of punishment comes, and disaster arrives from far away? Who will you run to for help? Where will you leave your riches?
Isaiah 10:4 Without me, they will kneel before the captives, and they will fall among the dead. Despite this, God is still angry, and his hand is still reaching out.
Isaiah 10:5 O Assyrian, you are the stick I use in anger, and the club you hold is my fury.
Isaiah 10:6 I will send him against a nation of pretenders, and to the people I am angry with, I will order him to seize their goods, capture them, and crush them like dirt on the roads.
Isaiah 10:7 He does not intend this, nor does he think this; but he plans to destroy and wipe out many nations.
Isaiah 10:8 He says, "Aren't all my leaders as powerful as kings?"
Isaiah 10:9 Isn't Calno like Carchemish? Isn't Hamath like Arpad? Isn't Samaria like Damascus?
Isaiah 10:10 My hand has conquered idol nations, whose carved idols were superior to those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
Isaiah 10:11 Won't I do to Jerusalem and its idols what I did to Samaria and its idols?
Isaiah 10:12 So, it will happen that when God has finished his work on Mount Zion and Jerusalem, I will punish the proud actions of the king of Assyria and his arrogant pride.
Isaiah 10:13 God says, "With my own power I did this, with my knowledge, because I am wise. I changed the borders of nations, took their treasures, and defeated the people as a brave warrior would."
Isaiah 10:14 My hand found wealth as a nest, and as one picks up abandoned eggs, I collected everything on earth; nobody fluttered a wing or opened their mouth to chirp.
Isaiah 10:15 Can an axe brag to the person using it? Or can a saw act proud toward the one who moves it? It's like a stick moving those who pick it up, or a wooden staff lifting itself as if it isn't wood.
Isaiah 10:16 Therefore, God will make his rich people thin, and he will set a fire under his glory that burns like a fierce fire.
Isaiah 10:17 Israel's light will be like a fire, and its Holy One like a flame; it will burn and consume its thorns and briers in one day.
Isaiah 10:18 God will destroy the beauty of his forest and his fertile land, both inside and out, and they will be like when a flag carrier grows weak.
Isaiah 10:19 The remaining trees of the forest will be so few that a child could count them.
Isaiah 10:20 On that day, the survivors of Israel and those who have escaped from the house of Jacob will no longer rely on the one who attacked them; instead, they will truly depend on God, the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 10:21 The remaining people will come back, Jacob's survivors, to the powerful God.
Isaiah 10:22 Even though there are many people in Israel, like sand by the sea, only a few of them will come back; what is decided will happen and will be done right.
Isaiah 10:23 God will carry out a complete destruction, as planned, throughout the land.
Isaiah 10:24 So this is what God says: My people living in Zion, do not fear the Assyrian. He will hit you with a stick and raise his staff against you, just like it was done in Egypt.
Isaiah 10:25 In a short time, God's anger will end, and my fury in their ruin will stop.
Isaiah 10:26 God will whip him like he did the Midianites at Oreb's rock, and just as he lifted his staff over the sea, he will raise it as he did in Egypt.
Isaiah 10:27 On that day, the heavy load will be lifted from your shoulder, and the harness from your neck, and the harness will be broken because of the blessing.
Isaiah 10:28 He has come to Aiath, he has moved on to Migron; at Michmash he has stored his supplies.
Isaiah 10:29 They have crossed over the path; they are staying in Geba; Ramah is scared; Saul's Gibeah has run away.
Isaiah 10:30 Raise your voice, daughter of Gallim; let it be heard all the way to Laish, you poor Anathoth.
Isaiah 10:31 Madmenah has moved away; the people of Gebim are getting ready to run away.
Isaiah 10:32 He will stay at Nob for that day; he will threaten the mountain of Zion's daughter, the hill of Jerusalem with his hand.
Isaiah 10:33 Look, God, the God of all, will cut off the branches with fear: the tall will be cut down, and the proud will be made low.
Isaiah 10:34 He will chop down the forest thickets with an iron tool, and Lebanon will fall to a powerful one.

Isaiah 11:1 A branch will grow from the stump of Jesse, and a shoot will come up from his roots.
Isaiah 11:2 God's spirit will be with him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of advice and strength, the spirit of knowledge and respect for God.
Isaiah 11:3 He will understand quickly how to respect God, and he won't decide by only what he sees, nor correct by just what he hears.
Isaiah 11:4 He will fairly judge the poor and decide with fairness for the humble of the earth. He will strike the land with his word, and with his speech, he will kill the wicked.
Isaiah 11:5 Righteousness will be his belt, and faithfulness the belt around his waist.
Isaiah 11:6 The wolf will live with the lamb, the leopard will lie down with the baby goat, the calf, the young lion, and the well-fed animal will be together; and a small child will guide them.
Isaiah 11:7 Cows and bears will eat together; their babies will lie down close; and lions will eat grass like oxen.
Isaiah 11:8 The nursing baby will play over the viper's hole, and the child who no longer nurses will put his hand on the snake's nest.
Isaiah 11:9 People will not hurt or destroy anything on my holy mountain, because the earth will be filled with knowledge about God, just as water fills the sea.
Isaiah 11:10 On that day, Jesse's descendant will be like a flag for all peoples; nations will come to him, and his place will be wonderful.
Isaiah 11:11 On that day, God will reach out again to bring back the survivors of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
Isaiah 11:12 He will raise a flag for all countries, and will bring together Israel's scattered people, and collect Judah's spread-out ones from all over the world.
Isaiah 11:13 Ephraim's jealousy will go away, and Judah's enemies will be defeated: Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, and Judah will not bother Ephraim.
Isaiah 11:14 They will soar over the Philistines in the west and take the riches of those in the east. They will take control of Edom and Moab, and the people of Ammon will follow them.
Isaiah 11:15 God will completely destroy the sea by Egypt and, with a strong wind, will sweep his hand over the river, dividing it into seven streams so that people can cross on dry land.
Isaiah 11:16 A road will be made for the survivors of his people left in Assyria, just like the one for Israel when they left Egypt.

Isaiah 12:1 On that day, you will say, "God, I will praise you. Even though you were angry with me, your anger has gone, and you have comforted me."
Isaiah 12:2 Look, God is my savior; I will trust and not fear: for God is my strength and my song; he has also become my savior.
Isaiah 12:3 So with happiness you will get water from the springs of rescue.
Isaiah 12:4 On that day you will say, "Praise God, ask for his help, tell everyone what he has done, and remember that his name is great."
Isaiah 12:5 Sing to God; for He has done wonderful things: this is known all over the earth.
Isaiah 12:6 Shout loudly, you who live in Zion, because the Holy One of Israel is great among you.

Isaiah 13:1 Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw this message about Babylon.
Isaiah 13:2 Raise a flag on the tall mountain, shout out loud to them, wave your hand, so they may enter the gates of the leaders.
Isaiah 13:3 I have ordered my holy ones; I have summoned my warriors to express my wrath, those who delight in my greatness.
Isaiah 13:4 The sound of many people in the mountains, like a large crowd; the loud noise of many countries' kingdoms joining together: God gathers the armies for war.
Isaiah 13:5 They come from a distant land, from the farthest skies, even God and his weapons of anger, to destroy the entire country.
Isaiah 13:6 Cry out, because God's day is near; it will come like destruction from God.
Isaiah 13:7 So everyone's hands will go weak, and each person's heart will feel afraid.

Isaiah 26:7 The path of good people is straight: you, the fairest, judge the way of the good.
Isaiah 26:8 Yes, following your decisions, God, we have waited for you; our soul's longing is for your name and to remember you.
Isaiah 26:9 I long for you with all my heart at night; indeed, I will search for you early with my spirit. When your decisions are known on earth, the people of the world will understand what is right.
Isaiah 26:10 Even if the wicked are shown kindness, they still do not learn what is right. They act unfairly in a good land and do not respect the greatness of God.
Isaiah 26:11 God, when you raise your hand, they don't see it: but they will see and feel shame for their jealousy of the people; indeed, the fire meant for your enemies will consume them.
Isaiah 26:12 God, you will give us peace, because you have done all our deeds for us.
Isaiah 26:13 God, our God, other rulers besides you have ruled over us, but we will only honor your name.
Isaiah 26:14 They are dead, they will not live; they are gone, they will not rise again. So, you have punished and wiped them out, erasing all memory of them.
Isaiah 26:15 You have grown the nation, God, you have made the nation larger; you are honored; you have spread it to the farthest parts of the earth.
Isaiah 26:16 God, in trouble they seek you, they pray deeply when you discipline them.
Isaiah 26:17 Just as a pregnant woman about to give birth hurts and cries out in her pain, so we have been before you, God.
Isaiah 26:18 We have been pregnant, we have been in pain, we have only produced wind; we have not brought any salvation on the earth; nor have the world's people fallen.
Isaiah 26:19 Your dead will live; my dead body and they will rise. Wake up and sing, you in the dust: your dew is like the plants' dew, and the earth will let out the dead.
Isaiah 26:20 Come, my people, go into your rooms and close your doors behind you. Hide for a short time until the anger has passed.
Isaiah 26:21 Look, God is coming from his place to punish the people of the world for their wrongs. The earth will reveal the blood spilled on it and will not hide those who were killed anymore.

Isaiah 27:1 On that day, God with His fierce, mighty sword will punish Leviathan, the sharp serpent, even Leviathan, the twisted serpent; and He will kill the sea dragon.
Isaiah 27:2 On that day, sing to her, "A vineyard of red wine."
Isaiah 27:3 I am God and I take care of it; I will water it all the time so that no one damages it, I will protect it day and night.
Isaiah 27:4 I am not angry: who would challenge me with briers and thorns in battle? I would march through them, I would burn them all.
Isaiah 27:5 Let him grab my power so he can be at peace with me, and he will be at peace with me.
Isaiah 27:6 He will help the descendants of Jacob to grow strong: Israel will bloom and flourish and spread their fruit all over the world.
Isaiah 27:7 Did God strike him as he struck those who attacked him? Or was he killed like those he killed?
Isaiah 27:8 When it grows, you will argue with it, but God calms the strong wind on the east wind's day.
Isaiah 27:9 Through this, Jacob's wrongdoing will be cleansed, and completely removing his sin will come from turning all the altar stones into crushed chalk; the sacred poles and idols will no longer remain standing.
Isaiah 27:10 The protected city will become empty, the place left and forgotten like a desert: there the calf will graze, lie down, and eat its branches.
Isaiah 27:11 When its branches dry up, they get broken off. Women come to burn them. These people don't understand, so the one who created them will not pity them, and the one who shaped them will not be kind to them.
Isaiah 27:12 On that day, God will clear the land from the Euphrates River to the brook of Egypt, and you, the people of Israel, will be gathered one by one.
Isaiah 27:13 On that day, a loud trumpet will sound, and those about to die in Assyria, along with the exiles in Egypt, will return and worship God on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

Isaiah 28:1 Trouble is coming for the proud crown, for the drunk people of Ephraim, whose beautiful glory is like a dying flower, on the head of the rich valleys of those drunk with wine.
Isaiah 28:2 Look, God has a powerful and strong one who, like a hailstorm and a destructive storm, like a big flood of overflowing waters, will throw down to the ground with force.
Isaiah 28:3 The proud crown, the drunk people of Ephraim, will be stepped on.
Isaiah 28:4 The beautiful crown of the fertile valley will wither away like a flower, and be like early fruit before summer; when someone sees it, they will eat it as soon as it's in their hand.
Isaiah 28:5 On that day, God will be like a crown of glory and a beautiful tiara for the remaining people.
Isaiah 28:6 To give discernment to those who judge and power to those who push back enemies to their gates.
Isaiah 28:7 But they have made mistakes because of wine, and strong drink has led them astray; the priest and the prophet have made errors because of strong drink, they are overwhelmed by wine, they wander off the path because of strong drink; they make mistakes in their visions, they trip up in their decisions.
Isaiah 28:8 Every table is covered with vomit and dirty, leaving no clean spot.
Isaiah 28:9 Who will he teach knowledge? Who will he help understand the teachings? Those who have outgrown milk and no longer nurse.
Isaiah 28:10 Rule should be followed by rule; line by line; here a bit, there a bit.
Isaiah 28:11 With unclear speech and a different language, he will talk to these people.
Isaiah 28:12 He said to them, "This is the place where you can give rest to the tired, and here they can be refreshed. But they wouldn't listen."
Isaiah 28:13 God's teaching was given to them bit by bit, rule by rule; here a little, there a little, so they might stumble, fall, and be caught.
Isaiah 28:14 Listen to God's message, you mocking leaders of the people in Jerusalem.
Isaiah 28:15 Because you said, "We have an agreement with death and a deal with the grave; when disaster sweeps by, it won't reach us: for we've made lies our shelter, and under untruths we've hidden."
Isaiah 28:16 So God says, "Look, I place in Zion a stone for a foundation, a tested stone, a valuable cornerstone, a solid foundation. Whoever believes will not rush."
Isaiah 28:17 I will use justice as a measuring line and righteousness as a plumb line; hail will destroy the shelter of lies, and water will flood the hiding place.
Isaiah 28:18 Your deal with death will be canceled, and your pact with the grave will not last; when the sweeping punishment comes through, you will be crushed by it.
Isaiah 28:19 Once it starts, it will sweep over you; every morning and night it will come, and just hearing the news will be very distressing.
Isaiah 28:20 The bed is too short for someone to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around oneself.
Isaiah 28:21 God will rise up like he did at Mount Perazim, he will be angry like he was in the Valley of Gibeon, to do what he must, his unusual work; and to complete his task, his unexpected task.
Isaiah 28:22 So now, don't mock or your punishment will grow. I have heard from God that he has decided to destroy the entire earth.
Isaiah 28:23 Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
Isaiah 28:24 Does the farmer plow all day to plant seeds? Does he break up the lumps of soil on his land?
Isaiah 28:25 When he has smoothed out the ground, doesn't he spread the fitches and scatter the cumin, and put the best wheat, the chosen barley, and the rye where they belong?
Isaiah 28:26 God guides him with wisdom and teaches him.
Isaiah 28:27 You don't use a heavy tool to thresh the fitches, nor do you drive a cart wheel over the cummin; instead, you beat the fitches with a stick and the cummin with a rod.
Isaiah 28:28 Grain for bread is crushed, but not forever; it won't be ground endlessly or broken with the cart's wheel, nor smashed by horse riders.
Isaiah 28:29 This also comes from God, who is amazing in giving advice and outstanding in what He does.

Isaiah 29:1 Sadness to Ariel, the city where David lived! Keep adding year after year; continue the sacrifices.
Isaiah 29:2 I will trouble Ariel, and there will be sadness and pain; and Ariel will be to me as Ariel.
Isaiah 29:3 I will surround you with my camp, attack you with a siege mound, and build towers to besiege you.
Isaiah 29:4 You will be brought low, and you will speak from the ground, and your words will be soft from the dust, and your voice will be like a ghost from the ground, and your words will be a whisper from the dust.
Isaiah 29:5 Many strangers among you will be like tiny dust, and many cruel people will vanish like chaff blown away, and all this will happen quickly, in a moment.
Isaiah 29:6 You will be visited by God with thunder, earthquake, loud noise, storm, tempest, and flames of consuming fire.
Isaiah 29:7 The crowds from all countries battling Ariel, and all attacking her and her defenses, making her suffer, will be like a dream seen in the night.
Isaiah 29:8 It will be like a hungry person who dreams of eating, but wakes up still hungry, or like a thirsty person who dreams of drinking, but wakes up thirsty and weak. This is how it will be for all the nations that fight against God's holy mountain.
Isaiah 29:9 Wait and be amazed; shout out loud, they act drunk, but not from wine; they stumble, but not from strong drink.
Isaiah 29:10 God has made you fall into a deep sleep and has shut your eyes. The prophets and leaders, the seers, he has covered.
Isaiah 29:11 The whole vision is like a sealed book to you. When it is given to someone who can read and they are asked, "Please read this," they say, "I can't, because it is sealed."
Isaiah 29:12 The book is given to someone who can't read, and they are asked, "Please read this," but he answers, "I can't read."
Isaiah 29:13 So God said, "Although these people come close to me with their words and honor me with their lips, their hearts are far from me, and their fear of me is just a human command they've been taught."
Isaiah 29:14 So, I will do an amazing thing for these people, a truly amazing thing that will amaze them: their wise people will lose their wisdom, and their smart people will not be able to understand.
Isaiah 29:15 Trouble awaits those who try to hide their plans from God; they do their deeds in secret and think, "Who sees us? Who knows what we're doing?"
Isaiah 29:16 Thinking you can twist things will be seen as silly as clay questioning the potter: Can what is made say to the one who made it, "You didn't make me"? Or can a creation say to its creator, "You don't know what you're doing"?
Isaiah 29:17 Won't it soon happen that Lebanon becomes a fertile land, and the fertile land will be considered like a forest?
Isaiah 29:18 On that day, the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the blind will see, even from darkness.
Isaiah 29:19 Humble people will find more joy in God, and the needy will celebrate the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 29:20 The dreadful one is defeated, the mocker is destroyed, and all who look for evil are stopped.
Isaiah 29:21 They make a person guilty because of a single word, set traps for those who correct in public, and twist the truth to harm the innocent for no reason.
Isaiah 29:22 So God, who saved Abraham, says about Jacob's family: Jacob won't be ashamed now, nor will his face turn pale.
Isaiah 29:23 But when he sees his children, my creation, around him, they will honor my name, respect the Holy One of Jacob, and fear the God of Israel.
Isaiah 29:24 Those who were confused will understand, and those who complained will learn what to believe.

Isaiah 30:1 Trouble to the stubborn children, says God, who make plans without including me, and who make agreements without my spirit, only adding more wrongdoings to their sins.
Isaiah 30:2 They go to Egypt without asking me, seeking help from Pharaoh's power and putting their trust in Egypt's protection!
Isaiah 30:3 So, relying on Pharaoh will embarrass you, and trusting in Egypt will bring you confusion.
Isaiah 30:4 His leaders were in Zoan, and his messengers went to Hanes.
Isaiah 30:5 They all felt ashamed because of a nation that could not bring them any benefit or help, but only brought them shame and disgrace.
Isaiah 30:6 The heavy loads of the southern animals: they go to a land of trouble and pain, where lions and poisonous snakes live. They will put their wealth on young donkeys and their valuables on camels, and take them to a people who won't help them.
Isaiah 30:7 The Egyptians will try to help, but it will be useless and pointless; that's why I said, "They can only sit still."
Isaiah 30:8 Go, write this down on a tablet in front of them, and record it in a book, so it will last forever and be remembered always.
Isaiah 30:9 These are defiant people, dishonest kids, kids who won't listen to God's teachings.
Isaiah 30:10 They tell the seers, "Don't see," and the prophets, "Don't tell us the truth. Tell us nice things, lie to us."
Isaiah 30:11 Move away from the road, step aside from the path, and stop making us deal with the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 30:12 Therefore, the Holy One of Israel says, because you reject this message and rely on oppression and deceit, and depend on them:
Isaiah 30:13 This wrong will be like a crack in a wall that's about to collapse—a bulge in a tall wall that will break suddenly, without warning.
Isaiah 30:14 He will smash it like a potter's jar shattered into bits; he won't hold back. So, when it breaks, there won't be a piece left to carry coals from the fire or scoop water from a well.
Isaiah 30:15 God, the Holy One of Israel, says this: You will be saved by turning back and resting; your strength will be in calmness and trust, but you did not want this.
Isaiah 30:16 But you said, "No, we will escape on horses." So you will run away. And you said, "We will ride fast horses." So those chasing you will be fast.
Isaiah 30:17 A thousand will run away because one person scolds them; because five scold you, you will run away. You will be left alone like a flag on a mountain, like a banner on a hill.
Isaiah 30:18 So God will wait to be kind to you, and then he will rise up to show you mercy. For God decides what is right; happy are all who wait for him.
Isaiah 30:19 The people will live in Zion in Jerusalem; you will not cry anymore. God will be very kind to you when you call out; when he hears, he will respond to you.
Isaiah 30:20 Even if God gives you hard times and suffering, your teachers won't be hidden away anymore, and you will be able to see your teachers.
Isaiah 30:21 You will hear a voice behind you saying, "This is the path, follow it," whether you go right or left.
Isaiah 30:22 You will also make your silver idols and your gold statues unclean. You will throw them away like a dirty cloth and say to them, "Get away from here."
Isaiah 30:23 God will send rain for your seeds you plant in the soil; you'll have bread from the earth's bounty, and it will be rich and abundant. On that day, your livestock will graze in spacious meadows.
Isaiah 30:24 The oxen and young donkeys that plow the land will eat pure food, which has been sifted with a shovel and a fan.
Isaiah 30:25 On every tall mountain and every high hill, there will be rivers and streams of water on the day of the great killing, when the towers collapse.
Isaiah 30:26 The moon will shine as brightly as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter, like seven days combined, when God repairs his people's harm and heals their injuries.
Isaiah 30:27 Look, God's name comes from afar, blazing with his anger, and the weight is great: his lips are full of wrath, and his tongue is like a consuming fire.
Isaiah 30:28 His breath, like a flood, will come up to the neck, to separate the nations with a useless sieve; and there will be a bit in the mouths of the people, making them wander off course.
Isaiah 30:29 You will sing like on a holy night celebration; your hearts will be joyful like when someone plays a flute going to God's mountain, to the great God of Israel.
Isaiah 30:30 God will make his mighty voice heard and show the striking power of his arm, with fierce anger, and with flames of a consuming fire, with storms, and strong winds, and hailstones.
Isaiah 30:31 Because of God's command, the Assyrian will be defeated, the one who struck with a stick.
Isaiah 30:32 Everywhere the staff touches, as God decides, there will be music with drums and harps; and with it, He will fight in the trembling battles.
Isaiah 30:33 Tophet was set up long ago; it is made ready for the king. It is deep and wide, with a big pile of fire and wood. God's breath, like a sulfur stream, lights it.

Isaiah 32:4 Even impulsive people will learn wisdom, and those who stutter will speak clearly.
Isaiah 32:5 The bad person will not be called generous, and the stingy will not be said to be giving.

Isaiah 32:7 The tools of the mean person are bad: he plans evil schemes to hurt the poor with false words, even when the poor speak the truth.
Isaiah 32:8 The generous person plans generous actions, and through generous actions, they will succeed.
Isaiah 32:9 Stand up, you women who are comfortable; listen to my voice, you daughters who are not worried; pay attention to what I say.
Isaiah 32:10 You will have many troubled days and years, you who are carefree: because there will be no grapes to harvest, and the gathering will not happen.
Isaiah 32:11 Shake with fear, you women who are relaxed; get worried, you who feel secure: take off your clothes, dress in rough sackcloth around your waists.

Isaiah 32:15 Until God gives us His Spirit from above, and the desert becomes a fertile land, and the fertile land is considered a forest.
Isaiah 32:16 Then fair judgment will live in the desert, and goodness will stay in the fertile land.
Isaiah 32:17 Doing what is right will bring peace; and living rightly will bring calm and safety always.
Isaiah 32:18 My people will live in peaceful homes, safe houses, and quiet resting places.
Isaiah 32:19 When it hails, falling on the forest, the city will be down in a low place.
Isaiah 32:20 Happy are you who plant by all waters, who let the ox and donkey work freely.

Isaiah 33:1 How terrible for you who destroy others when you have not been destroyed yourself, who betray others when no one has betrayed you! When you stop destroying, you will be destroyed; when you stop betraying, betrayal will come to you.
Isaiah 33:2 God, be kind to us; we have waited for you. Be their strength every morning, and our rescue when trouble comes.
Isaiah 33:3 When the loud noise came, people ran away; when you showed your power, countries split apart.
Isaiah 33:4 Your loot will be collected as caterpillars do, and like swarms of locusts moving back and forth, it will be taken away.
Isaiah 33:5 God is lifted up; for he lives on high: he has filled Zion with fairness and goodness.
Isaiah 33:6 Wisdom and knowledge will make your times stable, and will be the strength of your safety; respecting God is his treasure.
Isaiah 33:7 Look, their brave people will cry loudly outside; the peacemakers will cry sadly.
Isaiah 33:8 The roads are empty, no one travels on them; he has broken the promise, he has no respect for the cities, he cares about no one.
Isaiah 33:9 The earth is sad and weak: Lebanon is embarrassed and cut down: Sharon is like a desert; and Bashan and Carmel lose their fruit.
Isaiah 33:10 Now I will get up, says God; now I will be lifted high; now I will raise myself up.
Isaiah 33:11 You will get pregnant with useless stuff, you will give birth to waste: your own breath, like fire, will consume you.
Isaiah 33:12 The people will be like lime burning up; like cut thorns, they will be burned in the fire.
Isaiah 33:13 Listen, those who are far away, see what I have done; and those who are close, recognize my power.
