Isaiah 33:15 The person who lives right and speaks fairly, who hates unfair gain, who refuses bribes, who does not listen to plots of murder, and who does not look at evil things.
Isaiah 33:16 He will live in a high place; his fortress will be strong cliffs: He will have bread and a steady water supply.
Isaiah 33:17 Your eyes will see the king in his beauty; they will look at a land that is far away.
Isaiah 33:18 Your heart will think about fear. Where is the writer? Where is the collector? Where is the one who counted the towers?
Isaiah 33:19 You will not see a fierce people, people whose speech is too complex for you to understand; people who speak with a stutter that you cannot comprehend.
Isaiah 33:20 Look at Zion, the city of our celebrations: you will see Jerusalem as a peaceful home, a tent that won't be destroyed; none of its pegs will ever be taken out, and none of its ropes will break.
Isaiah 33:21 In that place, God will be like a land with wide rivers and streams, where no rowboats or great ships will sail.
Isaiah 33:22 God is our judge, God makes our laws, God is our king; he will save us.
Isaiah 33:23 Your ropes are untied; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail. Then the great treasures are shared; even the disabled get a share.
Isaiah 33:24 No one living there will say, "I am sick." The people there will be forgiven for the wrong things they have done.

Isaiah 34:1 Come close, all you countries, to listen; and pay attention, all you peoples: let the earth and everything on it hear; the world and all that comes out of it.
Isaiah 34:2 God is angry with all nations and furious with their armies; he has completely destroyed them and handed them over to be killed.
Isaiah 34:3 Their dead bodies will be thrown away, and they will smell bad. The mountains will flow with their blood.
Isaiah 34:4 Every star in the sky will disappear, and the sky will close up like a scroll. All the stars will fall, like leaves drop from a grapevine, and like figs drop from a fig tree.
Isaiah 34:5 My sword will be ready in the sky; it will fall on Edom and the people I have decided to punish, for punishment.
Isaiah 34:6 God's sword is covered with blood, it is thick with fat, from the blood of lambs and goats, and from the fat of ram's kidneys: because God has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a big killing in the land of Idumea.
Isaiah 34:7 The unicorns will come down with them, and the young bulls with the grown bulls; their land will be wet with blood, and their soil rich with fat.
Isaiah 34:8 It is the day of God's revenge, and the time to pay back for the dispute over Zion.
Isaiah 34:9 Its rivers will turn into tar, its soil into sulfur, and its ground will burn like tar.
Isaiah 34:10 It will not stop burning day or night; its smoke will rise forever. It will remain empty from one generation to another; no one will ever pass through it again.
Isaiah 34:11 The cormorant and bittern will live there; the owl and raven will make it their home. God will mark it with lines of chaos and stones of emptiness.
Isaiah 34:12 They will invite its nobles to rule, but no one will be there, and all its leaders will become nothing.
Isaiah 34:13 Thorns will grow in her palaces, nettles and brambles in her strongholds; it will be a home for dragons and a place for owls.
Isaiah 34:14 Desert animals will meet with island creatures, and goat-demons will call to each other; the night bird will also settle there and find a resting place.
Isaiah 34:15 The great owl will build its nest there, lay eggs, hatch them, and protect them under its wings; vultures will also meet there, each with its partner.
Isaiah 34:16 Look in God's book and read: none of these will be missing, none will be without a partner, because God has ordered it, and his spirit has brought them together.
Isaiah 34:17 He has decided their share by casting lots, and his hand has distributed it to them with measuring lines: they will own it forever, and they will live there from one generation to the next.

Isaiah 35:1 The wild and lonely areas will be happy for them; and the desert will be joyful and bloom like a rose.
Isaiah 35:2 It will bloom a lot and be happy with joy and singing. Lebanon's beauty will belong to it, as well as the greatness of Carmel and Sharon. They will see God's glory and greatness.
Isaiah 35:3 Make weak hands strong and steady shaking knees.
Isaiah 35:4 Tell those who are scared, "Be brave, don't be afraid. Look, your God will come to punish, God will come to repay; he will come and rescue you."
Isaiah 35:5 The eyes of those who cannot see will be opened, and the ears of those who cannot hear will be cleared.
Isaiah 35:6 Then the crippled person will jump like a deer, and the mute person's tongue will sing. For water will flow in the wasteland, and rivers in the dry land.
Isaiah 35:7 The dry ground will turn into pools, and the thirsty earth will have water springs. Where dragons once lived, there will be grass with reeds and rushes.
Isaiah 35:8 A road will be there, a path called the Holy Way. Impure people won't travel on it. It's for God's people; even if they are not wise, they will not go the wrong way.
Isaiah 35:9 No lion or fierce animal will be there, none will be found there; but those saved by God will walk there.
Isaiah 35:10 God's rescued people will come back and arrive at Zion singing, with endless joy. They will be happy and joyful, while sadness and sighing will disappear.

Isaiah 36:1 In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah's rule, Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
Isaiah 36:2 The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to King Hezekiah with a big army. He stood near the water channel of the upper pool on the road by the laundry workers' field.
Isaiah 36:3 Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, the palace manager, Shebna the secretary, and Joah, son of Asaph the record keeper, went to meet him.
Isaiah 36:4 Rabshakeh said to them, Tell Hezekiah, The great king, the king of Assyria, asks, 'What is this trust you have?'
Isaiah 36:5 I say, you claim (but those are just empty words) that I have advice and power for war. Now, who do you rely on when you rebel against me?
Isaiah 36:6 Look, you rely on the support of this weak reed, which is Egypt. If someone leans on it, it will break and stab their hand. That's how Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, is to all who trust in him.
Isaiah 36:7 But if you say to me, "We trust in God our God," isn't it the same one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, telling Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship at this altar"?
Isaiah 36:8 So now, please promise my master, the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you have enough riders for them.
Isaiah 36:9 How can you then scare off even a single one of my master's lowest officers and rely on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
Isaiah 36:10 Have I come to attack this land without God's guidance? God told me to go and destroy it.
Isaiah 36:11 Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please talk to your servants in the Syrian language, because we understand it. Don't talk to us in the Jewish language where the people on the wall can hear."
Isaiah 36:12 But the official said, "Did my master send me to your master and to you to say these things? Didn't he send me to the people sitting on the wall, so that they will have to eat their waste and drink their urine with you?"
Isaiah 36:13 Then Rabshakeh stood up and shouted in the Jewish language, "Listen to the words of the great king, the king of Assyria."
Isaiah 36:14 The king says, don't let Hezekiah trick you; he won't be able to save you.
Isaiah 36:15 Do not let Hezekiah convince you to trust in God, saying, "God will surely save us: this city will not be given to the king of Assyria."
Isaiah 36:16 Do not listen to Hezekiah. The king of Assyria says, "Make a deal with me by giving me a present, and come out to me. Then each of you can eat from your own grapevines and fig trees, and drink water from your own wells."
Isaiah 36:17 Until I come and bring you to a place like your own, a land with grain and wine, a land with bread and vineyards.
Isaiah 36:18 Be careful that Hezekiah doesn't convince you by saying, 'God will save us.' Has any nation's god rescued its land from the king of Assyria?
Isaiah 36:19 Where are the gods of Hamath and Arphad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Could they save Samaria from my power?
Isaiah 36:20 Which gods of these lands have saved their lands from me, that God should save Jerusalem from me?
Isaiah 36:21 They stayed quiet and did not speak a word to him because the king had ordered, "Do not answer him."
Isaiah 36:22 Eliakim, Hilkiah's son who managed the household, Shebna the secretary, and Joah, Asaph's son and the historian, went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him what Rabshakeh had said.

Isaiah 37:1 When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into God's house.
Isaiah 37:2 He sent Eliakim, the household manager, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests in mourning clothes to Isaiah the prophet, Amoz's son.
Isaiah 37:3 They told him, "Hezekiah says, 'Today is a day of trouble, criticism, and disrespect: the babies are ready to be born, but there is no strength to deliver them.'"
Isaiah 37:4 It's possible God will hear what Rabshakeh has said, sent by the king of Assyria to insult the true God, and will correct what God has heard. So, pray for the survivors who remain.
Isaiah 37:5 King Hezekiah's servants went to Isaiah.
Isaiah 37:6 Isaiah told them, "Tell your master, 'God says, Do not fear the words you've heard, which the king of Assyria's servants have used to insult me.'"
Isaiah 37:7 I will send a disaster against him. He will hear a rumor and go back to his land. There, he will die by the sword.
Isaiah 37:8 So Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah because he heard that the king had left Lachish.
Isaiah 37:9 He heard that Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia, was coming to fight you. So he sent messengers to Hezekiah with this message.
Isaiah 37:10 Tell Hezekiah, king of Judah, this: Don't let your God, who you trust, trick you into thinking that Jerusalem won't be handed over to the king of Assyria.
Isaiah 37:11 Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria did to all countries by completely destroying them; can you really be saved?
Isaiah 37:12 Did the gods of other nations save the cities my ancestors destroyed, like Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Isaiah 37:13 Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arphad, and the king of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah?
Isaiah 37:14 Hezekiah got the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went to God's house and laid it out before God.
Isaiah 37:15 Hezekiah prayed to God, saying,
Isaiah 37:16 God of heaven's armies, the God of Israel, who sits above the angelic creatures, you are the only God of all the earth's nations: you created the sky and the land.
Isaiah 37:17 Listen to me, God, and hear; open your eyes, God, and see; and hear everything Sennacherib has said to insult you, the living God.
Isaiah 37:18 Truly, God, the kings of Assyria have destroyed all the nations and their lands.
Isaiah 37:19 They threw their gods into the fire because they were not real gods, just things made by human hands from wood and stone, so they destroyed them.
Isaiah 37:20 So now, our God, save us from his power, so all the countries of the world will know that you are God, and only you.
Isaiah 37:21 Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah, saying, "God of Israel says, because you prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria:
Isaiah 37:22 This is what God has said about him: The young woman, the city of Zion, looks down on you and laughs at you; the city of Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
Isaiah 37:23 Who have you insulted and spoken against? And who have you raised your voice and looked at with pride? Even against the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 37:24 Your servants insulted God, saying, "With my many chariots I climbed mountain peaks, Lebanon's edges; I'll chop its tall cedars, best firs; I'll reach its far heights, Carmel's woods."
Isaiah 37:25 I have dug and drunk water; and with my feet I have dried up all the rivers of the attacked places.
Isaiah 37:26 Didn't you hear a long time ago how I made it happen, and from long ago that I planned it? Now I have made it happen, so that you could turn fortified cities into piles of ruins.
Isaiah 37:27 So the people living there were weak, scared, and confused. They were like field grass, green plants, grass on roofs, and grain wilted before it grows.
Isaiah 37:28 I know where you live, how you go out and come in, and how angry you are with me.
Isaiah 37:29 Because you are angry with me and I have heard your noise, I will put a hook in your nose and a bit in your mouth, and I will make you go back the way you came.
Isaiah 37:30 This will be a sign for you: This year, you will eat what grows by itself; the next year, what comes from that; but in the third year, plant crops, harvest them, grow vineyards, and eat their fruit.
Isaiah 37:31 The survivors from the family of Judah will again put down roots and grow fruit.
Isaiah 37:32 From Jerusalem, a group will survive, and some will flee from Mount Zion; God's intense dedication will make this happen.
Isaiah 37:33 So, God says about the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city, shoot an arrow here, come near it with shields, or build a siege ramp against it.
Isaiah 37:34 He will go back the way he came and will not enter this city, says God.
Isaiah 37:35 I will protect this city and save it for myself and for my servant David.
Isaiah 37:36 Then God's angel went out and struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. When people got up the next morning, everyone was dead.
Isaiah 37:37 So Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, left, went back, and stayed in Nineveh.
Isaiah 37:38 While he was praying in Nisroch's temple, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword and then ran away to Armenia. After that, his son Esarhaddon became the new king.

Isaiah 38:1 Hezekiah was very sick and near death. The prophet Isaiah, Amoz's son, came to him and said, "God says, 'Get your home ready, because you are going to die; you will not survive.'"
Isaiah 38:2 Hezekiah turned to face the wall and prayed to God.
Isaiah 38:3 He said, "Please remember, God, how I have lived in truth before you with a faithful heart, doing what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah cried a lot.
Isaiah 38:4 God spoke to Isaiah, saying,
Isaiah 38:5 Go and tell Hezekiah, 'God, the God of your ancestor David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I will extend your life by fifteen years.'
Isaiah 38:6 I will save you and this city from the king of Assyria's control, and I will protect this city.
Isaiah 38:7 This will be a sign for you from God: God will do what he has said.
Isaiah 38:8 Look, I will make the shadow that has moved down Ahaz's sundial go back ten steps. So the shadow moved back ten steps from where it had gone down.
Isaiah 38:9 This is the message from Hezekiah, the king of Judah, when he was sick and then got better from his illness.
Isaiah 38:10 I said when my life was being cut short, I will go to the gates of death: I will miss out on the rest of my years.
Isaiah 38:11 I said, I will not see God, God, among those alive: I will no longer see people with those on earth.
Isaiah 38:12 My life has passed and is gone like a shepherd's tent: I have ended my own life like a weaver: God will finish me off with wasting illness: from day to night you will end me.
Isaiah 38:13 I thought until morning that, like a lion, he would break all my bones; from day to night you will finish me.
Isaiah 38:14 Like a bird or a swallow, I chirped: I cried like a dove: my eyes are tired from looking up: Oh God, I am overwhelmed; help me.
Isaiah 38:15 What should I say? God has spoken to me and made it happen: I will walk gently all my life feeling the bitterness in my heart.
Isaiah 38:16 God, by these things people live, and in all these is my spirit's life: so you will heal me and let me live.
Isaiah 38:17 Look, I was very bitter when I wanted peace, but because you love me, you saved me from total destruction; you have put all my sins out of sight.
Isaiah 38:18 The grave cannot praise you, death cannot honor you; those who go into the pit cannot hope for your truth.
Isaiah 38:19 Living people will praise you, just like I do today; parents will tell their children about your truth.
Isaiah 38:20 God was ready to save me, so we will sing my songs with stringed instruments every day of our life in God's house.
Isaiah 38:21 Isaiah said, "Let them take a lump of figs and put it on the boil as a poultice, and he will get better."
Isaiah 38:22 Hezekiah also asked, "What is the sign that I will go to God's house?"

Isaiah 39:1 At that time, Merodachbaladan, son of Baladan and king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah because he heard that Hezekiah had been ill and had gotten better.
Isaiah 39:2 Hezekiah was happy with them and showed them his treasury, the silver, gold, spices, fine oil, his armory, and everything in his treasures: he kept nothing hidden from them in his house or his rule.
Isaiah 39:3 Isaiah the prophet went to King Hezekiah and asked him, "What did these men say, and where did they come from to visit you?" Hezekiah replied, "They came to me from a distant country, from Babylon."
Isaiah 39:4 He asked, "What did they see in your house?" And Hezekiah replied, "They saw everything in my house; there's nothing in my treasures I didn't show them."
Isaiah 39:5 Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Listen to the message from God:"
Isaiah 39:6 The time will come when everything in your house and everything your ancestors saved up until now will be taken to Babylon; nothing will remain, says God.
Isaiah 39:7 From your children, whom you will father, they will take some to be eunuchs in the palace of the Babylonian king.
Isaiah 39:8 Hezekiah told Isaiah, "God's message you gave is good. Also, there will be peace and truth while I live."

Isaiah 40:1 Comfort my people, comfort them, says your God.
Isaiah 40:2 Talk kindly to Jerusalem, and tell her that her struggle is over, that her wrongs are forgiven, because she has received from God twice as much as she deserved for all her sins.
Isaiah 40:3 The voice of someone shouting in the wilderness says, "Get ready for God's coming; clear a straight path for our God in the desert."
Isaiah 40:4 Every valley will be lifted up, and every mountain and hill will be brought down; the crooked will be straightened, and the rough areas will be smoothed out.
Isaiah 40:5 God's glory will be shown, and everyone will see it because God has said it would happen.
Isaiah 40:6 The voice said, "Shout." And he asked, "What should I shout?" All people are like grass, and their beauty is like the flowers in the field.
Isaiah 40:7 The grass dries up, the flower wilts when God's breath blows on it; indeed, people are like grass.
Isaiah 40:8 The grass dries up, the flower wilts, but God's word will last forever.
Isaiah 40:9 O Zion, who brings good news, go up the high mountain; O Jerusalem, who brings good news, raise your voice loudly; raise it, do not be afraid; tell the cities of Judah, See your God!
Isaiah 40:10 Look, God will come with power, and his arm will have authority: see, his reward is with him, and his task is in front of him.
Isaiah 40:11 He will care for his flock like a shepherd: he will gather the young lambs with his arm, hold them close, and gently guide the mothers.
Isaiah 40:12 Who has measured the waters in the palm of his hand, and measured the sky with his hand's width, and calculated the earth's dust in a container, and weighed the mountains on scales, and the hills with a balance?
Isaiah 40:13 Who has guided the Spirit of God, or as his advisor, has taught him?
Isaiah 40:14 Who gave him advice, and who taught him, and showed him how to judge rightly, and gave him knowledge, and showed him how to understand?
Isaiah 40:15 Look, the countries are like a drop from a bucket, and they are like fine dust on scales: look, he picks up the islands as if they are very small.
Isaiah 40:16 Lebanon does not have enough wood for a fire, nor enough animals for a sacrifice.
Isaiah 40:17 To God, all nations are nothing; they are worth less than nothing, just emptiness.
Isaiah 40:18 Who will you compare to God? Or what image will you compare to him?
Isaiah 40:19 The worker makes a carved idol, the goldsmith covers it with gold, and makes silver chains for it.
Isaiah 40:20 The poor person without a gift picks a lasting tree and finds a skilled craftsman to make a carved idol that won't fall over.
Isaiah 40:21 Haven't you known? Haven't you heard? Hasn't someone told you from the start? Haven't you understood since the world was made?
Isaiah 40:22 God sits above the circle of the earth, and its people are like grasshoppers; He stretches out the sky like a curtain and spreads it out like a tent for living.
Isaiah 40:23 God reduces rulers to nothing; He makes the judges of the earth worthless.
Isaiah 40:24 Yes, they will not be planted; yes, they will not be sown; yes, their stem will not root in the ground: and when he breathes on them, they will dry up, and the storm will sweep them away like straw.
Isaiah 40:25 Who can you compare to me? Who is my equal? asks the Holy One.
Isaiah 40:26 Look up to the sky and see who made these stars. God brings them out one by one and knows each by name. Because of his great strength and power, not a single one is missing.
Isaiah 40:27 Why do you say, Jacob, and complain, Israel, "My path is hidden from God, and my rights are ignored by my God"?
Isaiah 40:28 Don't you know? Haven't you heard that the eternal God, the creator of the whole earth, never gets tired or weary? No one can understand how deep his wisdom is.
Isaiah 40:29 He gives strength to the tired and gives more power to the weak.
Isaiah 40:30 Young people will get tired and worn out, and young men will stumble and fall.
Isaiah 40:31 Those who trust in God will gain new strength; they will soar high on wings like eagles; they will run without getting tired; they will walk without giving up.

Isaiah 41:1 Stay quiet before me, islands; and let the people get their strength back: let them approach; then let them talk: let's come close to make a decision together.
Isaiah 41:2 Who brought the good man from the east, called him to follow, handed nations to him, and let him govern kings? He made them like dust to his sword and like scattered straw to his bow.
Isaiah 41:3 He chased them and went safely on a path where he had never walked before.
Isaiah 41:4 Who has made and done this, calling the generations from the start? I, God, the first, and with the last; I am the one.
Isaiah 41:5 The islands saw it and were scared; the farthest parts of the earth felt fear, moved closer, and arrived.
Isaiah 41:6 They each helped their neighbor and said to their brother, "Have courage."
Isaiah 41:7 The carpenter cheered on the goldsmith, and the one who hammered helped the one at the anvil, saying, "It's ready to be soldered." Then he nailed it down so it wouldn't move.
Isaiah 41:8 You, Israel, are my servant, you are Jacob, whom I have chosen, the descendant of Abraham, my friend.
Isaiah 41:9 I have brought you from the farthest parts of the earth, called you from its leaders, and said to you, 'You are my servant; I have chosen you and not rejected you.'
Isaiah 41:10 Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not be upset, for I am your God. I will make you strong; yes, I will help you; indeed, I will support you with my righteous right hand.
Isaiah 41:11 Look, all who were angry with you will feel shame and be embarrassed; they will become nothing, and those who fight you will be destroyed.
Isaiah 41:12 You will look for them, but you won't find them—those who fought against you. Those who wage war against you will be nothing, like something that doesn't exist.
Isaiah 41:13 I, God, will hold your right hand and say to you, do not be afraid; I will help you.
Isaiah 41:14 Don't be afraid, Jacob, you weak people of Israel; I will help you, says God, your savior, the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 41:15 Look, I will make you into a new sharp tool with teeth for threshing: you will crush the mountains, break them into pieces, and turn the hills into dust.
Isaiah 41:16 You will scatter them with a fan, and the wind will take them away; the storm will spread them out. And you will be happy with God, celebrating the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 41:17 When the poor and needy look for water and find none, and they are too thirsty to speak, I, God, will listen to them, I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
Isaiah 41:18 I will create rivers on the mountains and springs in the valleys; I will turn the desert into a place with pools of water, and the dry ground into sources of water.
Isaiah 41:19 I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive trees in the wild; I will place fir, pine, and cypress trees together in the desert.
Isaiah 41:20 So they can see, know, think about, and understand that God has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has made it.
Isaiah 41:21 Explain your case, says God; present your best arguments, says the King of Jacob.
Isaiah 41:22 Let them present and tell us what will happen: show us past events, so we can think about them and understand their outcomes; or tell us about the future.
Isaiah 41:23 Show us what will happen in the future so we may know you are gods. Do something, good or bad, so we will be amazed and see it together.
Isaiah 41:24 Look, you are nothing, and your work is worthless; anyone who chooses you is detestable.
Isaiah 41:25 I have brought up someone from the north, and he will come; from where the sun rises, he will call on my name: and he will crush leaders as if they were mortar, just like a potter steps on clay.
Isaiah 41:26 Who has told us from the start, so we can know? And in advance, so we can say, He is good? Truly, no one shows it, no one announces it, no one hears your words.
Isaiah 41:27 The first will tell Zion, "Look, here they are." And I will send to Jerusalem someone who brings good news.
Isaiah 41:28 I looked, and there was no one; no one was there to advise or answer my questions.
Isaiah 41:29 Look, they are all useless; their deeds are worth nothing: their metal idols are just air and chaos.

Isaiah 42:1 Look at my servant, who I support; my chosen one, who pleases me; I have given him my spirit: he will bring fair judgment to the nations.
Isaiah 42:2 He will not shout or raise his voice or make it heard in the street.
Isaiah 42:3 He won't break a hurt reed, and he won't put out a weak flame: he will make sure that justice leads to truth.
Isaiah 42:4 He will not fail or lose heart until he establishes justice on earth; and the islands will look forward to his teachings.
Isaiah 42:5 God says, he who made the sky and stretched it wide; he who laid out the earth and all that grows from it; he who gives breath to its people, and life to those who walk on it:
Isaiah 42:6 I, God, have called you to do right, and will take your hand, and will protect you, and make you a promise to the people, a light for all nations.
Isaiah 42:7 To give sight to the blind, to free the prisoners, and to lead those in darkness out of jail.
Isaiah 42:8 I am God, that is my name; I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to idols.
Isaiah 42:9 Look, what happened before has happened, and now I tell you about new things: before they start to happen, I inform you.

Isaiah 42:12 Let them honor God and tell of his praise on the islands.

Isaiah 42:14 I have been quiet for a long time; I have been still and held back. Now I will cry out like a woman in labor; I will destroy and devour quickly.
Isaiah 42:15 I will destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all their plants; and I will turn rivers into dry land, and I will dry up the ponds.
Isaiah 42:16 I will guide the blind on unfamiliar paths; I will take them on routes they don't know. I will turn the dark into light for them and make the rough places smooth. I will do these things for them and not leave them alone.
Isaiah 42:17 They will turn back and be very ashamed, those who trust in carved idols and tell the metal images, "You are our gods."
Isaiah 42:18 Listen, you who cannot hear; and you who cannot see, look so that you may see.
Isaiah 42:19 Who is blind except my servant? Or who is deaf like the messenger I send? Who is as blind as the one in right standing, and as blind as God's servant?
Isaiah 42:20 You see many things but don't notice; you open your ears but don't hear.
Isaiah 42:21 God is happy because of his goodness; he will make his laws great and respected.
Isaiah 42:22 These people are robbed and looted; they are all trapped in pits and hidden in jails. They are hunted, with no one to save them; they are taken, with no one saying, "Give back."
Isaiah 42:23 Who among you will listen to this? Who will pay attention and listen for the future?
Isaiah 42:24 Who let Jacob be taken and Israel be robbed? Wasn't it God, whom we sinned against? They wouldn't follow His path or obey His rules.
Isaiah 42:25 So God has poured out his anger on him and sent the power of war. It has set him on fire all around, but he did not understand. It burned him, but he did not take it seriously.

Isaiah 43:1 But now, God who made you, Jacob, and shaped you, Israel, says: Don't be afraid, for I have saved you; I have called you by your name; you are mine.
Isaiah 43:2 When you go through the waters, I will be with you; and when you go through the rivers, they won't flood you: when you walk through the fire, you won't be burned; and the flame won't set you on fire.
Isaiah 43:3 I am your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior: I traded Egypt, Ethiopia, and Seba for your freedom.
Isaiah 43:4 Because you are valuable to me, you are honored, and I love you: so I will trade other people for you and give nations in exchange for your life.
Isaiah 43:5 Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
Isaiah 43:6 I will tell the north, 'Let go,' and the south, 'Don't hold back.' Bring my sons from distant places, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
Isaiah 43:7 Everyone who is known by my name, I created for my glory; I shaped them and made them.

Isaiah 43:23 You have not brought me the young animals for your burnt offerings; you have also not honored me with your sacrifices. I have not made you work hard with offerings or tired you with incense.
Isaiah 43:24 You did not buy me sweet cane with money, nor did you offer me the best parts of your sacrifices; but you made me work with your sins, you tired me out with your wrongdoings.

Isaiah 43:28 So I have disgraced the sacred leaders, and let Jacob be cursed, and Israel be insulted.

Isaiah 44:1 Listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen:
Isaiah 44:2 God who created you and shaped you from birth, who will support you, says: Do not be afraid, Jacob, my servant, and Jesurun, whom I have selected.
Isaiah 44:3 I will give water to the thirsty and send streams over the dry land. I will pour my spirit on your descendants and my blessing on your children.
Isaiah 44:4 They will grow like plants in the grass, like willow trees by the streams.
Isaiah 44:5 One will say, "I belong to God"; another will use the name of Jacob for himself; and another will write with his hand, "I am God's," and will take the name of Israel.
Isaiah 44:6 God, the King of Israel, and his rescuer, The Lord of all, says: I am the first, and I am the last; and there is no other God besides me.
Isaiah 44:7 Who else but me can call, announce, and set everything since I chose the old people? Let them reveal the future and what will happen.
Isaiah 44:8 Do not be afraid or scared; haven't I told you before and made it clear? You are my witnesses. Is there any other God besides me? No, there is no other God; I do not know of any.
Isaiah 44:9 People who create idols are without purpose; their cherished objects won't help them; and they testify to their own ignorance, as they cannot see or understand, leading to their shame.
Isaiah 44:10 Who has made a god or cast an idol that is no use at all?
Isaiah 44:11 Look, all his friends will feel shame; and the craftsmen, they are just people: let them all come and stand up; but they will be afraid, and they will all feel shame together.
Isaiah 44:12 The blacksmith uses tongs to work in the coals, shapes it with hammers, and uses his arms' strength; but he gets hungry and weak, doesn't drink water, and feels faint.
Isaiah 44:13 The woodworker measures with a ruler, draws lines, shapes the wood with tools, uses a compass to draw circles, and creates a figure like a person, as beautiful as a person, to stay in the house.
Isaiah 44:14 He cuts down cedars and picks the cypress and oak, which he makes strong among the forest trees: he plants an ash tree, and the rain helps it grow.
Isaiah 44:15 Then it will be used by someone to make a fire; he will take some of it to keep warm, he will start a fire and cook bread. Also, he makes a god and bows down to it; he makes it into an idol and worships it.
Isaiah 44:16 He burns some of it in the fire; with some he eats meat; he cooks a meal and is full. Yes, he warms himself and says, "Ah, I'm warm, I've seen the fire."
Isaiah 44:17 With the rest, he makes an idol, his carved image. He bows down to it, worships it, and prays to it, saying, "Save me, for you are my god."
Isaiah 44:18 They do not know or understand because God has closed their eyes so they cannot see and their hearts so they cannot understand.
Isaiah 44:19 No one thinks to themselves, nor do they realize or understand enough to say, "I have burned some of it in a fire; yes, I have also baked bread on its embers; I have cooked meat and eaten it. Should I then use the rest to make something disgusting? Should I bow down to a piece of wood?"
Isaiah 44:20 He eats ashes: a tricked heart has led him wrong, so he can't save himself, or think, "Isn't there a false thing in my hand?"
Isaiah 44:21 Remember this, Jacob and Israel, because you are my servant. I made you; you are my servant. Israel, I will not forget you.
Isaiah 44:22 I have wiped away your wrongdoings like a heavy cloud, and your sins like a mist. Come back to me, because I have saved you.
Isaiah 44:23 Sing, you heavens, because God has done it; shout, you depths of the earth; burst into song, you mountains, O forest, and every tree in it; for God has saved Jacob and shown his glory in Israel.
Isaiah 44:24 God says, "I am your savior and creator from birth. I am God who makes everything, who stretched out the skies without help, who spread out the earth on my own."
Isaiah 44:25 God frustrates the signs of liars and drives diviners crazy; God makes wise men retreat and turns their knowledge into foolishness.
Isaiah 44:26 God confirms the words of his servant and carries out the plans of his messengers; he tells Jerusalem, "You will be populated," and to the towns of Judah, "You will be rebuilt, and I will restore your ruined places."
Isaiah 44:27 He tells the waters, "Dry up," and I will dry your rivers.
Isaiah 44:28 God calls Cyrus his leader, who will do all that God wants; he will order that Jerusalem be rebuilt and the temple's foundation be laid.

Isaiah 45:2 I will go ahead of you and make the twisted paths straight. I will break the bronze gates into pieces and cut through the iron bars.
Isaiah 45:3 I will give you treasures from dark places and hidden wealth from secret spots so you can know that I, God, who calls you by name, am the God of Israel.
Isaiah 45:4 For the sake of my servant Jacob and my chosen Israel, I have called you by name and given you a special title, even though you do not know me.
Isaiah 45:5 I am God, and there is no other; there is no other God besides me. I gave you strength, even though you did not know me.
Isaiah 45:6 So that people can understand from where the sun rises to where it sets that there is no one except me. I am God, and there is no one else.
Isaiah 45:7 I create light and make darkness; I bring peace and create trouble; I, God, do all these things.
Isaiah 45:8 Heavens above, open up and let the skies rain down goodness; let the earth split open and salvation grow, with goodness rising up at the same time; I, God, have made this happen.
Isaiah 45:9 How terrible for someone who argues with their Creator! Let a broken piece of pottery argue with other broken pieces on the ground. Can the clay question the one shaping it, saying, "What are you making?" or criticize the work, saying, "You have no hands"?
Isaiah 45:10 How terrible for someone who asks their father, "What are you fathering?" or asks a woman, "What are you giving birth to?"
Isaiah 45:11 God, the Holy One of Israel, your Creator, says, "Ask me about the future of my children, and tell me what to do with what I have made."
Isaiah 45:12 I made the earth and created people on it. I stretched out the sky with my own hands, and I command all the stars.
Isaiah 45:13 I have brought him up to be good, and I will guide all he does: he will build my city, and he will release my prisoners, not for money or a gift, says God.
Isaiah 45:14 God says, "Egypt's work and Ethiopia's trade, and the tall Sabean people, will come to you and belong to you. They will follow you, coming in chains. They will bow down to you and beg you, saying, 'Truly, God is with you; there is no other, there is no other god.'"
Isaiah 45:15 Truly, you are a God who hides yourself, O God of Israel, the Savior.
Isaiah 45:16 They will all feel shame and be embarrassed together; those who make idols will be completely confused.
Isaiah 45:17 Israel will be saved by God with eternal salvation; you will never be ashamed or confused forever.
Isaiah 45:18 God, who made the heavens, says: I formed the earth and created it to last. I did not make it for nothing; I made it to be lived in. I am God, and there is no one else.
Isaiah 45:19 I have not spoken in secret or in hidden places on earth. I did not tell Jacob's descendants to look for me without finding me. I, God, speak what is right and announce what is true.
Isaiah 45:20 Gather and come close, you who have survived from other countries. Those who make idols from wood have no understanding, and they pray to a god who cannot rescue them.
Isaiah 45:21 Tell others and bring them close; yes, let them plan together: who announced this long ago? who spoke of it back then? It was I, God, wasn't it? There is no other God besides me; a fair God and a Savior; there is no one else.
Isaiah 45:22 Turn to me and be saved, all you people of the earth, because I am God, and there is no other.
Isaiah 45:23 I have promised by myself, the word has left my mouth in truth and won't come back, that to me every knee will bend, every tongue will promise.
Isaiah 45:24 Someone will definitely say, "I find righteousness and strength in God." People will come to him, and all who are angry with him will be embarrassed.
Isaiah 45:25 All of Israel's descendants will be made right with God and will take pride in Him.

Isaiah 46:1 Bel bends down, Nebo bows, their idols are on the animals and livestock: your carts carry a heavy load; they weigh down the tired animals.
Isaiah 46:2 They bend low, they kneel down together; they cannot save the heavy load, but they themselves are carried off as prisoners.
Isaiah 46:3 Listen to me, O family of Jacob, and all the survivors of the family of Israel, who have been supported by me since birth, whom I have carried since you were born.
Isaiah 46:4 Even when you are old, I am with you; I will support you when your hair turns gray. I created you, and I will take care of you; I will sustain you and save you.
Isaiah 46:5 Who do you think is like me? Who can you say I am equal to or compare me with?
Isaiah 46:6 They pour out gold from their bags, weigh silver on scales, pay a goldsmith to make it into a god; then they bow down and worship it.
Isaiah 46:7 They carry him on the shoulder, they lift him up, and put him in his spot, and he stands; he won't move from his spot. Even if someone calls to him, he can't reply or save that person from their problems.
Isaiah 46:8 Remember this and act like men: think about it again, you who break rules.
Isaiah 46:9 Think about the past, because I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and no one is like me.
Isaiah 46:10 Telling the future from the start, and from long ago the things not yet happened, saying, My plan will last, and I will do all I want.
Isaiah 46:11 God calls a hungry bird from the east, the man who carries out my plans from a distant land: yes, I have said it, and I will make it happen; I have planned it, and I will do it.
Isaiah 46:12 Listen to me, you strong-minded, who are far from doing right:
Isaiah 46:13 I am making my righteousness come soon; it won't be far away, and my help won't be delayed: I will set rescue in Zion, for Israel who I honor.

Isaiah 47:1 Come down and sit in the dirt, you pure girl of Babylon. Sit on the ground. You have no throne, girl of the Chaldeans, because you won't be called soft and gentle anymore.
Isaiah 47:2 Use the grinding stones to make flour, let down your hair, show your legs, reveal your thighs, and cross the rivers.
Isaiah 47:3 Your nakedness will be exposed, and your shame will be seen: I will get revenge, and I will not face you like a human.
Isaiah 47:4 Our rescuer is God, the ruler of all, called the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 47:5 Stay quiet and go into the dark, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for you will no longer be known as the queen of nations.
Isaiah 47:6 I was angry with my people, I have made my inheritance impure, and handed them over to you: you showed them no mercy; you laid a very heavy burden on the old.
Isaiah 47:7 You said, "I will always be a lady," so you didn't take these things seriously or think about what would happen later.
Isaiah 47:8 Listen to this, you who love pleasures and live carelessly, thinking to yourself, "I am the only one; there's no one besides me. I will never be a widow or know the loss of children."
Isaiah 47:9 Two things will suddenly happen to you: you'll lose your children and become a widow. These will fully hit you because of your many magic tricks and spells.
Isaiah 47:10 You trusted in your wrongdoing, thinking no one sees you. Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray, and you told yourself, "I exist, and there is no one else like me."
Isaiah 47:11 Bad things will happen to you; you won't know where they come from. Trouble will hit you, and you won't be able to stop it. Sudden ruin will happen to you, and you won't see it coming.
Isaiah 47:12 Stand now with your magic spells and the many sorceries you've worked on since your youth; perhaps you will succeed, maybe you will inspire fear.
Isaiah 47:13 You are tired from all your advice. Now let the astrologers, the stargazers, and those who predict each month try to stand up and save you from what is going to happen to you.
Isaiah 47:14 Look, they will be like dry grass; the fire will burn them up; they won't be able to save themselves from the flames. There won't be a single coal to warm up by, or a fire to sit in front of.
Isaiah 47:15 They that worked with you and traded with you since your youth will all go their own ways; no one will help you.

Isaiah 48:1 Listen to this, you people of Jacob, named after Israel, who came from Judah's line, who swear by God's name and name the God of Israel, but not honestly or rightly.
Isaiah 48:2 They say they belong to the holy city and rely on the God of Israel; God of the heavenly armies is his name.
Isaiah 48:3 I told about the past from the start; they came from my mouth, I showed them; I acted quickly, and they happened.
Isaiah 48:4 Because I knew you are stubborn, your neck is strong like iron, and your forehead like brass.
Isaiah 48:5 From the start, I told you what would happen; I showed you before it happened so you wouldn't claim your idol or carved or cast image made it happen.
Isaiah 48:6 You have heard, now you see all of this; won't you tell it? I have shown you new things from now on, even secrets you did not know.
Isaiah 48:7 They were made just now, not long ago; before today, you did not hear them, so you can't say, "Look, I knew about them."
Isaiah 48:8 Yes, you did not hear; yes, you did not know; yes, since your ear was not open: because I knew you would be very unfaithful, and you were named a rule-breaker from birth.
Isaiah 48:9 For my reputation, I will hold back my anger, and for my honor, I will stop myself for your sake so I don't destroy you.
Isaiah 48:10 Look, I have made you pure but not like silver; I have picked you in the hard times.
Isaiah 48:11 For my own sake, yes, for my own sake, I will act: why should my name be dishonored? I will not give my glory to anyone else.
Isaiah 48:12 Listen to me, Jacob and Israel, whom I have called; I am the one; I am the first, and I am also the last.
Isaiah 48:13 My hand has set the earth's foundation, and my right hand spread out the skies: when I call them, they rise up at once.
Isaiah 48:14 Everyone, come together and listen; who among them has announced these events? God loves him; he will fulfill his wishes on Babylon, and his power will be against the Chaldeans.
Isaiah 48:15 I, yes I, have spoken; I have called him: I have brought him, and he will succeed on his path.
Isaiah 48:16 Come close to me, listen to this: I have not spoken in secret from the start; I have been there since it began, and now God and his Spirit have sent me.
Isaiah 48:17 God says, "I am your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord your God who teaches you to succeed and guides you on the right path."
Isaiah 48:18 If only you had listened to my commands! Then your peace would be like a river, and your goodness like the sea's waves.
Isaiah 48:19 Your descendants would have been as many as the sand, and the children born to you like its pebbles; their name would not have been erased or wiped out in my presence.
Isaiah 48:20 Leave Babylon, run away from the Chaldeans, sing out loud and announce, share the news everywhere on earth; say, God has saved his servant Jacob.
Isaiah 48:21 They were not thirsty when God guided them through the deserts; he made water flow from the rock for them; he split the rock, and water poured out.
Isaiah 48:22 God says there is no peace for the wicked.

Isaiah 49:1 Listen, islands, to me; pay attention, you people from far away. God has called me from before I was born; from my mother's womb, he has spoken my name.
Isaiah 49:2 God has made my mouth like a sharp sword; he has hidden me in the shadow of his hand and made me like a smooth arrow stored in his quiver.
Isaiah 49:3 He told me, "You are my servant, Israel, and through you I will be honored."
Isaiah 49:4 Then I said, I have worked hard for nothing, I have used my energy for no reason, and it's all been pointless: but for sure, my reward is with God, and my work is with my God.
Isaiah 49:5 God, who made me in the womb to serve Him, to bring Jacob back to Him, says: Even if Israel isn't brought back together, I will still be honored in God's sight, and God will give me strength.
Isaiah 49:6 He said, "It is a small task for you to be my servant, to bring back the people of Jacob and to save the survivors of Israel. I will also make you a light for other nations so that you can be my salvation to the ends of the earth."
Isaiah 49:7 God, who saves Israel and is holy, says to the one people hate and nations reject, who serves rulers: Kings will see you and stand up, princes will see and bow down, because God is faithful and the holy one of Israel has chosen you.
Isaiah 49:8 God says, "I listened to you at the right time, and on the day you were saved, I helped you. I will keep you safe and make you a promise to the people, to rebuild the land and give new life to ruined places."
Isaiah 49:9 So you can tell the captives, "Go out," and to those in the dark, "Come into the light." They will find food along the roads, and they will graze on every hill.
Isaiah 49:10 They will not be hungry or thirsty; neither will the heat or sun hurt them, because the one who has mercy on them will lead them and guide them to water springs.
Isaiah 49:11 I will turn all my mountains into roads, and my paths will be raised up.
Isaiah 49:12 Look, these will come from far away: some from the north and the west, and others from the land of Sinim.
Isaiah 49:13 Sing, heavens, and earth be happy; mountains, burst into song: for God has comforted his people and will show kindness to those who are suffering.
Isaiah 49:14 But Zion said, God has left me, and my God has forgotten me.
Isaiah 49:15 Can a mother forget her baby or not feel love for her own child? Even if she could forget, I will never forget you.
Isaiah 49:16 Look, I have carved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are always in my sight.
Isaiah 49:17 Your children will hurry back; those who destroyed you and left you in ruins will leave you.
Isaiah 49:18 Look around and see: everyone is coming to you. As God lives, says God, you will wear them all like jewelry and dress yourself with them like a bride.
Isaiah 49:19 Because your ruined and empty places, and the land of your ruin, will now be too small for all the people, and those who devoured you will be gone.
Isaiah 49:20 The children you will have, after you've lost the others, will tell you, 'This place is too small for me; make room for me to live.'
Isaiah 49:21 Then you will think to yourself, "Who gave me these children when I lost mine and was all alone, a prisoner, and wandering? And who has raised these?" I was alone; where were these children before?
Isaiah 49:22 God says, "See, I will raise my hand to the nations and show my signal to the peoples. They will carry your sons in their arms and your daughters will be lifted on their shoulders."
Isaiah 49:23 Kings will care for you like fathers, and queens like mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground, and honor you like they are kissing your feet. Then you will know that I am God. Those who wait for me will not be ashamed.
Isaiah 49:24 Can the prize be taken from the strong, or the rightful prisoner set free?
Isaiah 49:25 But this is what God says: Even the prisoners of the strong will be taken, and the victims of the fearsome will be freed. I will fight against those who fight you, and I will save your children.
Isaiah 49:26 I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will be drunk on their own blood as if it were sweet wine. Then everyone will know that I, God, am your Savior and Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.

Isaiah 50:1 God says, "Where is your mother's divorce paper that I sent away? Who is the one I sold you to because of my debts? Look, because of your wrongs you sold yourselves, and because of your mistakes your mother was sent away.
Isaiah 50:2 Why, when I arrived, was no one there? When I called, why did no one respond? Is my power lessened, so that I can't save? Or do I lack the strength to rescue? Look, at my command I dry up the sea, I turn rivers into deserts; their fish rot because there is no water, and they die of thirst.
Isaiah 50:3 I make the skies dark, and I cover them with sackcloth.
Isaiah 50:4 God has given me the tongue of someone who is educated, so I can say the right thing at the right time to those who are tired: he wakes me up every morning, he makes my ear ready to listen like someone who is educated.
Isaiah 50:5 God has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious, nor did I turn back.
Isaiah 50:6 I let people beat my back and pull hair from my face without hiding from shame or spit.
Isaiah 50:7 God will help me, so I won't be confused. I am determined, and I know I won't be ashamed.
Isaiah 50:8 God who declares me right is close; who will argue with me? Let's face each other: who is against me? Let them approach me.
Isaiah 50:9 Look, God will help me; who can declare me guilty? See, they will all wear out like clothes; moths will consume them.
Isaiah 50:10 Who among you respects God, listens to his servant, walks in darkness without light? Let him trust in God's name and rely on his God.
Isaiah 50:11 Look, all who start a fire and surround yourselves with sparks: go ahead and walk in the light of your fire and the sparks you've made. This is what you'll get from me; you will lay down in sadness.

Isaiah 51:1 Listen to me, you who seek what is right, you who look for God: consider the rock from which you were cut and the quarry from which you were dug.
Isaiah 51:2 Look to Abraham your father and Sarah your mother; God called him alone, blessed him, and made him numerous.
Isaiah 51:3 God will comfort Zion: He will make her ruined places better; He will make her wild land like Eden, and her dry land like God's garden; there will be joy and happiness, thankfulness, and beautiful songs.
Isaiah 51:4 Listen to me, my people; and pay attention to me, my nation: because a law will come from me, and I will set my judgment as a light for the people.
Isaiah 51:5 My goodness is close; my rescue has begun, and my strength will decide for the people; the islands will look to me, and they will rely on my strength.
Isaiah 51:6 Look up at the sky, and down at the earth below: for the sky will disappear like smoke, the earth will wear out like clothes, and its people will die too. But my rescue will last forever, and my goodness will never end.
Isaiah 51:7 Listen to me, you who know what is right, you people who have my law in your heart; do not fear the insults of humans or be terrified of their abuse.
Isaiah 51:8 Moths will devour them like clothes, and worms will eat them like wool, but my goodness will last forever, and my rescue will pass on from one generation to the next.
Isaiah 51:9 Wake up, wake up, show your power, arm of God; wake up like you did in the old days, in past generations. Weren't you the one who defeated Rahab and struck the dragon?
Isaiah 51:10 Aren't you the one who dried up the sea, the deep waters, making a path for the saved to cross?
Isaiah 51:11 So, those saved by God will come back, singing to Zion; endless joy will be theirs. They will get happiness and joy; sadness and grief will go away.
Isaiah 51:12 I am the one who comforts you; why should you be afraid of a person who will die or a human who will wither like grass?
Isaiah 51:13 You forget God who made you, who stretched out the sky and set the earth's base; you always fear the anger of your enemy, as if they were about to destroy you, but where is the enemy's anger now?
Isaiah 51:14 The prisoner hurries to be set free so he won't die in the hole or run out of food.
Isaiah 51:15 I am your God, who split the sea with its loud waves; "God of armies" is his name.
Isaiah 51:16 I have put my words in your mouth, and I have protected you with my hand's shadow, so I can create the skies, establish the earth, and tell Zion, 'You are my people.'
Isaiah 51:17 Wake up, stand up, Jerusalem, you've drunk from God's hand the cup of his anger; you've drunk to the last drop the cup that makes you stagger, and poured it out.
Isaiah 51:18 No one is there to lead her among all the children she has had; nor is there anyone to take her hand among all the children she has raised.
Isaiah 51:19 Two disasters have struck you; who will mourn for you? Ruin and destruction, famine and war: who can comfort you?
Isaiah 51:20 Your sons have collapsed; they lie at the entrance of every street, like a wild bull caught in a net. They are overwhelmed with God's anger, the scolding of your God.
Isaiah 51:21 So listen, you who are troubled and as if drunk, but not from wine:
Isaiah 51:22 Your God, who defends his people, says, "Look, I have removed from your hand the cup that makes you tremble, the very worst of my anger's cup; you will never drink it again."
Isaiah 51:23 I will make those who hurt you take it; they told you to lie down so they could walk on you, and you were like the ground or a road for them to walk on.

Isaiah 52:2 Get up from the dust; stand up and sit down, Jerusalem; free yourself from the chains on your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
Isaiah 52:3 God says, "You sold yourselves for nothing, and you will be freed without paying."
Isaiah 52:4 God said, "Long ago, my people went to Egypt to stay for a while; but then, the Assyrian mistreated them for no reason."
Isaiah 52:5 So now, why am I here? asks God, when my people have been taken for nothing? Those who lead them cause them to cry out, says God, and my name is insulted all the time, every day.
Isaiah 52:6 So my people will learn my name; on that day, they will know that I am the one who is speaking: look, it's me.
Isaiah 52:7 How beautiful are the feet of the person on the mountains who brings good news, who announces peace; who brings good news of good things, who announces salvation; who tells Zion, "Your God rules!"
Isaiah 52:8 Your guards will raise their voices; they will sing together because they will see things the same way when God brings back Zion.
Isaiah 52:9 Celebrate with joy, sing together, you deserted parts of Jerusalem: for God has comforted his people, he has saved Jerusalem.
Isaiah 52:10 God has shown his power to all nations; everyone around the world will see God's saving strength.

Isaiah 52:12 You will not leave quickly or run away, because God will lead you, and the God of Israel will protect you from behind.
Isaiah 52:13 Look, my servant will act wisely; he will be raised up, praised, and very honored.
Isaiah 52:14 Many were shocked at him; his face was so disfigured beyond any person, and his appearance beyond that of people.
Isaiah 52:15 He will amaze many nations; kings will be silent because of him; for they will see what was not told to them, and they will think about things they had never heard.

Isaiah 53:1 Who has believed what we said? And to whom has God shown his power?
Isaiah 53:2 He will grow up before God like a young plant and as a root from dry soil. He has no attractive form or beauty; when we see him, nothing in his appearance makes us want him.
Isaiah 53:3 People dislike and ignore him; he is a man who knows sadness and pain: we all turned away from him; he was disliked, and we did not value him.
Isaiah 53:4 He surely took on our pains and carried our sadness, but we thought he was punished by God, hit by him, and suffering.
Isaiah 53:5 He was hurt for our wrongs, he was beaten for our sins. The punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed.
Isaiah 53:6 We all, like sheep, have wandered off; each of us has gone our own way; and God has put on him the wrongs of us all.
Isaiah 53:7 He was mistreated and he suffered, but he did not speak: he is led like a lamb to be killed, and like a sheep is silent before its shearers, so he does not speak.
Isaiah 53:8 He was freed from jail and trial. Who will speak of his descendants? He was removed from the living because my people did wrong, and he suffered for them.
Isaiah 53:9 He was buried with bad people, and although wealthy when he died, he had not been violent or lied.
Isaiah 53:10 God chose to hurt him; God made him suffer. When you offer his life for sin, he will see his children, live a long life, and God's will succeed through him.
Isaiah 53:11 He will see the results of his suffering and be content. Through his understanding, my good servant will make many people right with God, because he will carry their wrongs.
Isaiah 53:12 So I will give him a share with the great, and he will share the winnings with the mighty, because he gave his life to death: he was counted with the wrongdoers; he took on many people's sins and spoke up for the wrongdoers.

Isaiah 54:1 Sing, you who couldn't have children; shout with joy, you who never gave birth. Be happy, because you have more children now than the woman who has a husband, says God.
Isaiah 54:2 Make your tent bigger and stretch out its covers. Don't hold back, make the ropes longer, and make the pegs stronger.
Isaiah 54:3 You will spread out to the right and to the left; your descendants will settle in other nations and live in empty towns.
Isaiah 54:4 Do not be afraid; you will not be embarrassed. Do not feel confused; you will not be disgraced. You will forget the shame of your youth and no longer remember the dishonor of being a widow.
Isaiah 54:5 Your Creator is your partner; God is his name; and your Savior, the Holy One of Israel, will be known as the God of the entire world.
Isaiah 54:6 God has chosen you like a woman abandoned and sad in spirit, like a young wife rejected, says your God.
Isaiah 54:7 I left you alone for a short time, but I will bring you back with great kindness.
Isaiah 54:8 I was upset with you for a short time and turned away; but I will show you endless kindness and compassion, says your God, the Redeemer.
Isaiah 54:9 This is like Noah's flood to me: just as I promised that Noah's flood would never again cover the earth, so I promise I will not be angry with you or scold you.
Isaiah 54:10 Even if the mountains go away and the hills move, my kindness will not leave you and my peace agreement will not move, says God who has mercy on you.
Isaiah 54:11 You who are troubled and storm-tossed, and without comfort, see, I will set your stones with pretty colors and lay your foundations with sapphires.
Isaiah 54:12 I will make your windows out of agate, your gates out of sparkling stones, and all your borders out of beautiful stones.
Isaiah 54:13 All your children will be taught by God, and they will have great peace.
Isaiah 54:14 You will be set up in what is right: you will be safe from being hurt and you won't be scared; and you won't be terrified because it won't get close to you.
Isaiah 54:15 Look, they will definitely come together, but not because of me: anyone who comes together against you will fail because of you.
Isaiah 54:16 Look, I made the blacksmith who fans the coals into flame and forges a tool for his work; I also made the destroyer to ruin.
Isaiah 54:17 No weapon made against you will succeed, and you will prove wrong every tongue that accuses you. This is the right of God's servants, and their goodness comes from God.

Isaiah 55:1 Everyone who is thirsty, come to the water. Even if you have no money, come, buy, and eat. Yes, come and get wine and milk for free, without paying.
Isaiah 55:2 Why spend money on what is not food, and work hard for what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good, and enjoy rich food.
Isaiah 55:3 Lean in to listen, come to me; pay attention, and you will have life. I will promise you forever-lasting kindness, like I did for David.
Isaiah 55:4 Look, I have made him a witness to the people, a leader and commander for them.
Isaiah 55:5 Look, you will call a country you do not know, and countries that did not know you will come to you because of God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he has honored you.
Isaiah 55:6 Look for God while he can be found, call on him while he is close by.
Isaiah 55:7 Let the bad person stop doing wrong and the unjust person change their thoughts. Let them turn back to God, and He will be kind to them; turn to our God because He will fully forgive them.
Isaiah 55:8 My thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways, says God.
Isaiah 55:9 Just as the sky is higher than the ground, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
Isaiah 55:10 Just as rain and snow fall from the sky and do not return without watering the earth, making it sprout and grow, providing seeds for the farmer and food to eat:
Isaiah 55:11 My word that comes out of my mouth will not come back to me empty. Instead, it will do what I want, and it will succeed in what I send it to do.
Isaiah 55:12 You will leave with joy and be guided in peace. The mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees will clap their hands.
Isaiah 55:13 Where there were thorns, the fir tree will grow, and where there were briers, the myrtle tree will grow. This will bring honor to God, a lasting sign that will not be destroyed.

Isaiah 56:1 God says, "Keep fair judgment, and do what is right: for my rescue is close to coming, and my goodness will soon be shown."
Isaiah 56:2 Happy is the person who does this, and the human who holds on to it; who keeps the Sabbath without ruining it, and stops his hand from doing any bad thing.
Isaiah 56:3 A foreigner who has chosen to follow God should not say, "God has totally cut me off from his people." And a eunuch should not say, "Look, I am just a dead tree."
Isaiah 56:4 God says to the eunuchs who follow my Sabbaths, choose what pleases me, and commit to my promise;
Isaiah 56:5 I will give them a place and a name better than sons and daughters within my house and walls; they will have an everlasting name that will never be taken away.
Isaiah 56:6 Foreigners who connect with God to serve Him and love His name, becoming His servants, who keep the Sabbath without spoiling it and follow my agreement.
Isaiah 56:7 I will bring them to my holy mountain and give them joy in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be welcome on my altar, for my house will be known as a house of prayer for everyone.
Isaiah 56:8 God, who brings Israel's scattered people together, says, "I will also bring others to join those I have already gathered."
Isaiah 56:9 All you wild animals of the fields, come to eat; yes, all you animals in the forests.
Isaiah 56:10 His guards are blind; they know nothing. They are all silent dogs; they can't bark. They are sleeping, lying down, and enjoy sleeping.
Isaiah 56:11 Yes, they are greedy dogs that can never get enough, and they are shepherds who do not understand. They all only look out for themselves, each one for his own profit.
Isaiah 56:12 Come on, they say, let's get wine and get drunk on hard liquor; tomorrow will be like today, and even better.

Isaiah 57:1 Good people die, and nobody cares: and kind-hearted people are taken away, with no one understanding that they were spared from coming evil.
Isaiah 57:2 He will find peace: they will rest in their beds, each living righteously.
Isaiah 57:3 Come close, you children of the witch, born of the cheater and the prostitute.
Isaiah 57:4 Who are you mocking? Who are you opening your mouth wide and sticking out your tongue at? Aren't you children of rebellion, offspring of lies?
Isaiah 57:5 Getting excited about idols under every green tree and killing the children in the valleys under the cliffs of the rocks?
Isaiah 57:6 Your share is among the stream's smooth stones; these are your lot. You have poured out a drink to them and offered food. Why should I be comforted by this?
Isaiah 57:7 You put your bed on a tall and high mountain: you even went up there to make a sacrifice.
Isaiah 57:8 You have put up your memorials behind doors and doorposts. You have shown yourself to others, not me, and climbed into bed with them. You made your bed bigger and agreed to be with them; you loved their bed when you saw it.
Isaiah 57:9 You went to the king with oil, added more perfumes, sent your messengers far away, and lowered yourself down to hell.
Isaiah 57:10 You are tired from your long journey, but you didn't say there is no hope; you found strength in your own hands, so you were not sad.
Isaiah 57:11 Who have you been so afraid of that you lied and forgot about me, and didn't care? Haven't I been silent for a long time, yet you still don't fear me?
Isaiah 57:12 I will tell about your goodness and your actions, because they will not help you.
Isaiah 57:13 When you call for help, let your groups save you; but the wind will carry them all off, emptiness will take them. But anyone who trusts in me will own the land and will receive my sacred mountain.
Isaiah 57:14 They will say, "Build up, build up, clear the path, remove the obstacles from my people's way."
Isaiah 57:15 God, the high and eternal one who is called Holy, says: I live in a high and holy place, and also with the person who is sorry and humble, to give new life to the humble spirit and to the hearts of those who are sorry.
Isaiah 57:16 I will not argue forever, nor stay angry always: because the spirit would grow weak before me, and the souls I created would die.
Isaiah 57:17 Because of his greed, I was angry and punished him. I hid myself and was angry, but he kept on doing wrong according to his desires.
Isaiah 57:18 I have seen his actions and will heal him; I will guide him and give peace to him and his mourners.
Isaiah 57:19 I make the words that people say; peace, peace to the one who is far away and to the one who is close, says God; and I will heal him.
Isaiah 57:20 Evil people are like a restless sea that stirs up mud and dirt.
Isaiah 57:21 My God says the bad have no peace.

Isaiah 58:1 Shout loudly, don't hold back, raise your voice like a trumpet, and show my people their wrongs, and the family of Jacob their sins.
Isaiah 58:2 They look for me every day and enjoy learning my ways, like a country that did what's right and didn't ignore their God's laws: they want to know my fair laws; they love to come close to God.
Isaiah 58:3 Why do we fast, they ask, and you don't see? Why do we make ourselves suffer, and you don't notice? Look, on your fast day you seek your own pleasure and make all your workers work hard.
Isaiah 58:4 Look, you fast to cause arguments and fights, and to hit with wicked fists: you should not fast like today if you want your voices heard by God.
Isaiah 58:5 Is this the kind of fasting I have chosen? A day for a person to make themselves suffer? Is it just to hang your head low like a reed and to lie on sackcloth and ashes? Do you call this a fast, a day pleasing to God?
Isaiah 58:6 Isn't this the fast I have chosen: to break the chains of evil, to remove the heavy loads, to set free those who are crushed, and to break every bondage?
Isaiah 58:7 Isn't it to share your food with the hungry, and to welcome the poor who have nowhere to stay into your home? When you see someone without clothes, to give them something to wear; and not to ignore your own relatives?
Isaiah 58:8 Your light will shine like the dawn, and your health will quickly improve; your goodness will lead the way, and God's glory will protect you from behind.
Isaiah 58:9 You will call and God will answer; you will cry and he will say, 'Here I am.' If you stop oppressing others, pointing fingers, and speaking falsely;
Isaiah 58:10 If you give your heart to the hungry and comfort the troubled soul, then your light will shine in the darkness, and your darkest time will be like midday.
Isaiah 58:11 God will always guide you, satisfy you in dry times, make you healthy, and you will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring that never runs dry.
Isaiah 58:12 Your descendants will rebuild the ruined places. You will restore the foundations laid long ago. You will be known as the fixer of broken walls and the restorer of livable streets.
Isaiah 58:13 If you stop doing what you want on my holy day, the Sabbath, and see it as a joyful and special day for God, and respect it by not following your usual routines, seeking your own enjoyment, or talking about everyday matters:
Isaiah 58:14 You will enjoy being close to God; He will let you triumph on the earth's high places and give you the blessings of your ancestor Jacob: this is God's promise.

Isaiah 59:1 Look, God's hand is not too short to save; nor is his ear too dull to hear.
Isaiah 59:2 Your wrongs have come between you and God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so he will not listen.
Isaiah 59:3 Your hands are dirty with blood, and your fingers with wrong; your lips have told lies, your tongue whispers twisted things.
Isaiah 59:4 No one asks for justice or argues for truth; they rely on what's empty and tell lies; they make trouble and cause wrongdoing.
Isaiah 59:5 They hatch poisonous snake eggs and spin spider webs: whoever eats their eggs dies, and when one is stepped on, a viper hatches.
Isaiah 59:6 Their webs can't be made into clothes, nor can they cover themselves with what they do: their actions are sinful, and they do violent things.
Isaiah 59:7 Their feet rush to do bad things, and they hurry to spill innocent blood. They plan sinful things; ruin and damage are on their way.
Isaiah 59:8 They do not know the way to peace; their paths are not fair: whoever walks in them will not find peace.
Isaiah 59:9 So justice is far from us, and fairness doesn't reach us. We hope for light but only find darkness; we look for brightness but walk in gloom.
Isaiah 59:10 We search for the wall like blind people, and we fumble as though we can't see. We trip at midday as if it were dark; we are in empty spaces like the dead.
Isaiah 59:11 We all growl like bears and sadly cry like doves; we hope for fairness, but find none; for rescue, but it's far away from us.
Isaiah 59:12 We have many sins against you, and our wrongs show our guilt; our sins are always with us, and we know our bad acts.
Isaiah 59:13 By breaking rules and lying about God, turning away from our God, talking about hurting others and rebelling, thinking and saying untrue things from our heart.
Isaiah 59:14 Judgment is avoided, and justice is distant because truth has failed in public, and fairness cannot come in.
Isaiah 59:15 Yes, truth is lacking; and those who avoid doing wrong become victims. God saw this and was unhappy because there was no justice.
Isaiah 59:16 He saw no one was there and was surprised no one intervened; so he himself brought salvation, and his goodness supported him.
Isaiah 59:17 He wore fairness like armor on his chest and put on a helmet of rescue on his head; he dressed himself in revengeful clothes and wrapped intense passion around himself like a cape.
Isaiah 59:18 God will pay back everyone based on what they have done; he will show anger to his foes and settle scores with his enemies; he will also repay those who live on the islands.
Isaiah 59:19 People will respect God's name in the west and his greatness where the sun rises. When enemies attack like a rushing water, God's Spirit will raise a flag to stand against them.
Isaiah 59:20 God will come to Zion and to those in Jacob who stop doing wrong, says God.
Isaiah 59:21 I promise you this, says God: My Spirit with you and the words I've given you will always be on your lips and on the lips of your children and grandchildren, now and forever, says God.

Isaiah 60:1 Get up and shine, because your light has come, and God's glory has risen upon you.
Isaiah 60:2 Look, darkness will cover the earth, and deep darkness the people, but God will rise upon you, and His glory will be seen on you.
Isaiah 60:3 People from other nations will come to your light, and rulers will be attracted to the glow of your dawn.
Isaiah 60:4 Look around and see: everyone is coming to you: your sons from far away, and your daughters will be cared for at your side.
Isaiah 60:5 You will see and be happy, and your heart will feel awe and grow big, because the riches of the sea will come to you, and the wealth of the nations will come to you.
Isaiah 60:6 Many camels will be around you, the young camels of Midian and Ephah. Everyone from Sheba will come, bringing gold and incense, and they will praise God.
Isaiah 60:7 All Kedar's sheep will come to you, Nebaioth's rams will serve you; they will be welcome as sacrifices on my altar, and I will honor my glorious temple.
Isaiah 60:8 Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their nests?
Isaiah 60:9 The islands will wait for me, and the ships from Tarshish will come first, to bring your sons from a distance, along with their silver and gold, to honor God, the Holy One of Israel, because he has made you honored.
Isaiah 60:10 Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their rulers will serve you. When I was angry, I punished you, but now I will show you mercy.
Isaiah 60:11 So your gates will always be open; they won't close day or night so that people can bring you wealth from other nations, and their kings led to you.
Isaiah 60:12 Any country or kingdom that does not serve you will be destroyed; indeed, those countries will be totally ruined.
Isaiah 60:13 Lebanon's beauty will come to you, with its fir, pine, and cypress trees, to make my holy place beautiful; and I will make where I stand a glorious place.
Isaiah 60:14 The children of those who hurt you will come to you and bow down. Everyone who looked down on you will fall at your feet. They will call you God's City, the Holy One of Israel's Zion.
Isaiah 60:15 Even though you were abandoned and disliked, and nobody passed through you, I will turn you into an everlasting glory, a delight for many generations.
Isaiah 60:16 You will also drink the milk of nations and nurse at the breasts of kings; and you will know that I, God, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the powerful one of Jacob.
Isaiah 60:17 I will give gold for brass, silver for iron, brass for wood, and iron for stones. I will make your leaders bring peace and your rulers bring fairness.
Isaiah 60:18 There will be no more violence in your land, no wasting or destruction within your borders; you will name your walls Safety, and your gates will be called Praise.
Isaiah 60:19 You will not need the sun for light in the day, nor the moon to shine for you; God will be your eternal light, and your God will be your glory.
Isaiah 60:20 Your sun will never set, your moon will not disappear; for God will be your eternal light, and your sad days will be over.
Isaiah 60:21 Your people will all be good; they will own the land forever. They are my plantings, the work of my hands, to show my greatness.
Isaiah 60:22 A small child will grow into a large group, and a little one will become a powerful nation: God will make it happen quickly at the right time.

Isaiah 61:1 God's Spirit is with me; for God has chosen me to bring good news to the humble; He has sent me to heal those with broken hearts, to announce freedom for the captives, and to open the prison for those who are tied up.
Isaiah 61:2 To announce the year God favors and the day God will take revenge; to comfort all who are sad.
Isaiah 61:3 God aims to comfort those who grieve in Zion, to give them beauty instead of ashes, joyful oil instead of mourning, and clothes of praise instead of a heavy heart, so they will be like strong, good trees planted by God to show his greatness.
Isaiah 61:4 They will rebuild the ruined places, they will restore the old ruins, and they will fix the destroyed cities, the places ruined for many years.
Isaiah 61:5 Foreigners will care for your sheep, and people from other places will farm your land and tend your vineyards.
Isaiah 61:6 You will be called God's priests; people will call you God's servants. You will enjoy the wealth of other nations, and you will take pride in their splendor.
Isaiah 61:7 You will receive twice as much instead of your shame; they will celebrate their share instead of feeling embarrassed. So in their land, they will own twice as much, and they will have endless joy.
Isaiah 61:8 For I, God, love fairness, I hate theft in sacrifices; and I will guide their work in truth, and I will form a lasting agreement with them.
Isaiah 61:9 Their children will be recognized by other nations, and their descendants by all peoples; everyone who sees them will know that they are children whom God has blessed.
