Isaiah 61:10 I will be very happy with God, my soul will be joyful in my God; because he has dressed me in the clothes of rescue, he has wrapped me with the coat of being right, like a groom gets ready with fancy things, and like a bride decorates herself with her gems.
Isaiah 61:11 Just like the earth produces its sprouts and a garden makes its planted seeds grow, God will make fairness and praise blossom in front of all countries.

Isaiah 62:1 For Zion's sake, I will not keep quiet, and for Jerusalem's sake, I will not stop working until its goodness shines out like the dawn, and its rescue blazes like a burning lamp.
Isaiah 62:2 People from other nations will see how good you are, and all rulers will see your honor. You will be given a new name chosen by God.
Isaiah 62:3 You will also be a crown of glory in God's hand, and a royal crown in the hand of your God.
Isaiah 62:4 You will no longer be called Forsaken, nor will your land be called Desolate. Instead, you will be known as Hephzibah, and your land Beulah, for God delights in you, and your land will be married.
Isaiah 62:5 Just as a young man marries a young woman, your sons will marry you. And just as a groom is happy with his bride, God will be happy with you.
Isaiah 62:6 I have placed guards on your walls, Jerusalem, who will never be silent day or night. You who remember God, never stop speaking.
Isaiah 62:7 Don't let him rest until he makes Jerusalem respected all over the world.
Isaiah 62:8 God has promised with his power, "I won't let your enemies eat your grain, or strangers drink the wine you worked for."
Isaiah 62:9 Those who gathered it will eat it and thank God; those who collected it will drink it in the holy places.
Isaiah 62:10 Pass through, pass through the gates; make a path for the people; build up, build up the road; remove the stones; raise a flag for the people.
Isaiah 62:11 Look, God has announced to the world's end, "Tell the people of Zion, 'Look, your rescuer is coming; see, he brings his reward and his work is ahead of him.'"
Isaiah 62:12 People will call them God's holy people, the ones God saved; and you will be known as the city that was searched for and not abandoned.

Isaiah 63:1 Who is this coming from Edom, with colorful clothes from Bozrah, looking splendid in his clothes, moving in his great strength? I am the one who speaks what is right, powerful to save.
Isaiah 63:2 Why are you wearing red clothes and look like someone who has been stomping grapes?
Isaiah 63:3 I have crushed grapes to make wine by myself; no one from the people was with me. I will step on them in my anger, and walk on them in my rage; their blood will splash on my clothes, and I will dirty all my clothing.
Isaiah 63:4 The day for payback is in my heart, and the time has come to save my people.
Isaiah 63:5 I looked, but there was no one to help; I was surprised that no one supported me. So my own strength saved me; my anger kept me going.
Isaiah 63:6 I will step on the people in my anger, make them confused in my rage, and I will knock down their power to the ground.
Isaiah 63:7 I will talk about God's kindness and praise God for all He has given us. He has been very good to Israel's people because of His mercy and great kindness.
Isaiah 63:8 For he said, "They are my people, children who will not deceive." So, he became their Savior.
Isaiah 63:9 In all their troubles, he felt trouble too, and his messenger saved them. With his love and kindness, he freed them; he lifted them up and carried them long ago.
Isaiah 63:10 But they resisted and upset God's Holy Spirit: so He became their foe and fought against them.
Isaiah 63:11 He recalled the past, Moses, and his people, asking, "Where is the one who led them from the sea, the shepherd of his flock? Where is the one who gave them his holy Spirit?"
Isaiah 63:12 God guided them with Moses' strong hand, splitting the water for them, to make his name last forever.
Isaiah 63:13 God guided them through the deep waters, like a horse in the desert, so they would not trip.
Isaiah 63:14 Like an animal that walks down into a low place, God's Spirit made him calm: in the same way, you guided your people to bring honor to your name.
Isaiah 63:15 Look from heaven and see from your holy and glorious home. Where is your passion and your power, the deep feelings and kindness you have for me? Have they been held back?
Isaiah 63:16 You are definitely our father, even if Abraham doesn't know us and Israel doesn't recognize us. You, God, are our father, our savior; your name lasts forever.
Isaiah 63:17 God, why have you made us stray from your paths and made our hearts hard from fearing you? Come back for the sake of your servants, the people who belong to you.
Isaiah 63:18 Your holy people owned the land for only a short time; our enemies have trampled your temple.
Isaiah 63:19 We belong to you; you never ruled over them; they were not called by your name.

Isaiah 64:1 I wish you would tear open the skies and come down, so that the mountains would melt before you.
Isaiah 64:2 Just like a fire melts things and boiling water bubbles, so you show your power to your enemies, making nations shake before you.
Isaiah 64:3 When you did amazing things we didn't expect, you came, and the mountains melted before you.
Isaiah 64:4 From the start of the world, people have not heard or known by hearing, and no eye has seen, O God, what you have made ready for those who wait for you.
Isaiah 64:5 You meet those who are happy and do good, who remember you and your paths. But you are angry because we have sinned. Yet if we continue in this, we will be saved.
Isaiah 64:6 We are all unclean, and our good deeds are like dirty cloths; we all wither like a leaf, and our sins sweep us away like the wind.
Isaiah 64:7 No one calls on your name or makes an effort to hold on to you, for you have hidden your face from us and have let our sins destroy us.
Isaiah 64:8 But now, God, you are our father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
Isaiah 64:9 Don't be very angry, God, and don't remember sins forever. Look, we beg you, we are all your people.
Isaiah 64:10 Your holy cities are empty, Zion is empty, Jerusalem is destroyed.
Isaiah 64:11 Our sacred and lovely home, where our ancestors worshiped you, has been destroyed by fire; and all our nice things are ruined.
Isaiah 64:12 Will you hold back because of these things, God? Will you stay silent and punish us harshly?

Isaiah 65:1 People who did not ask for me are now looking for me; those who did not seek me have found me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that was not called by my name.
Isaiah 65:2 I have reached out all day to stubborn people who follow their own bad paths and thoughts.
Isaiah 65:3 A nation that always makes me angry to my face; they offer sacrifices in gardens and burn incense on brick altars.
Isaiah 65:4 They stay near the graves and sleep in tombs, eat pig meat, and their pots hold disgusting things.
Isaiah 65:5 They say, "Keep away, don't come near me, because I am more holy than you." These people are like irritating smoke in my nose, a fire that keeps burning all day.
Isaiah 65:6 Look, it is recorded before me: I will not stay quiet, but will pay back, even repay into their lap.
Isaiah 65:7 Your wrongs, and your ancestors' wrongs, says God, who worshiped on the mountains and insulted me on the hills: so I will give back their past actions to them.
Isaiah 65:8 God says, "Like new wine in the grape cluster, and someone says, 'Don't destroy it; there's a blessing in it,' I will do the same for my servants, so I won't destroy them all."
Isaiah 65:9 I will produce descendants from Jacob, and from Judah someone to inherit my mountains; those I choose will possess it, and my workers will live there.
Isaiah 65:10 Sharon will be a place for flocks, and the valley of Achor will be a resting place for herds, for my people who have looked for me.
Isaiah 65:11 But you abandon God, forget my holy hill, set a table for idols, and provide drinks for them.
Isaiah 65:12 So I will count you for the sword, and all of you will kneel for killing: because when I called, you did not answer; when I spoke, you did not listen; instead you did bad things in front of me, and chose what I did not like.
Isaiah 65:13 So this is what God says: Look, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry. Look, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Look, my servants will be happy, but you will be ashamed.
Isaiah 65:14 Look, my servants will sing with happy hearts, but you will cry because your hearts are sad, and you will wail because your spirits are troubled.
Isaiah 65:15 You will leave your name as a curse for my chosen ones: because God will kill you, and will give his servants a different name.
Isaiah 65:16 Anyone who asks for a blessing on earth will ask for a blessing from the God of truth. Anyone who makes a promise on earth will promise by the God of truth. The past troubles are forgotten, and they are hidden from my sight.
Isaiah 65:17 Look, I am making new heavens and a new earth: and the old things will not be remembered or thought about anymore.
Isaiah 65:18 Be happy and celebrate always because of what I create. Look, I make Jerusalem a place of joy and its people a delight.
Isaiah 65:19 I will be happy in Jerusalem and delighted with my people. No more will there be the sound of crying or the sound of tears in the city.
Isaiah 65:20 No babies will die young, nor old people before their time. Everyone will live to be at least 100 years old. But if someone at 100 years old is a sinner, they will be cursed.
Isaiah 65:21 They will build houses and live in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Isaiah 65:22 People won't build homes for others to live in, or plant for others to eat. Just like trees live long, my people will have long lives and enjoy what they make with their own hands.
Isaiah 65:23 They will not work for nothing, nor have children for misfortune, because they are the children of God's blessed ones, and their descendants with them.
Isaiah 65:24 Before they even ask, I will respond; while they are still talking, I will listen.
Isaiah 65:25 The wolf and the lamb will eat together, and the lion will eat grass like the ox; the snake will eat dust. They will not harm or ruin anything on my holy mountain, says God.

Isaiah 66:1 God says, "The sky is my throne, and the earth is where I rest my feet. Where is the home you build for me? And where can I rest?"
Isaiah 66:2 God made all these things; they exist because of him. But I will pay attention to the person who is poor and has a humble spirit, who respects my words.
Isaiah 66:3 Whoever kills an ox is like someone who murders a person; whoever sacrifices a lamb is like someone who kills a dog; whoever presents a grain offering is like someone who offers pig blood; whoever burns incense is like someone who worships an idol. Indeed, they follow their own paths, and their souls enjoy their disgusting acts.
Isaiah 66:4 I will also pick the lies they believe and make their fears come true; because when I called, no one answered; when I talked, they didn't listen. Instead, they did bad things in front of me and picked what I didn't like.
Isaiah 66:5 Listen to God's message, you who respect his word; your brothers who hated you and threw you out because of me said, "Let God be honored." Yet he will show himself for your happiness, and they will feel shame.
Isaiah 66:6 A loud sound from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of God that gives payback to his enemies.
Isaiah 66:7 Before she had labor pains, she gave birth; before her pain started, she had a baby boy.
Isaiah 66:8 Has anyone heard of such a thing? Has anyone seen such things? Can the earth produce in one day? Or can a nation be born in a moment? For as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.
Isaiah 66:9 Will I let a baby be born and then not let it come out? asks God. Will I let it come out and then close the womb? asks your God.
Isaiah 66:10 Be happy with Jerusalem and celebrate with her, all who love her; be joyful with her, all who grieve for her.
Isaiah 66:11 So you can feed and be content with the comfort she gives; so you can nurse and be happy with how much she has to give.
Isaiah 66:12 For this is what God says: I will bring peace to her like a river, and the wealth of nations like a flooding stream: then you will nurse, be carried on her hip, and rocked on her knees.
Isaiah 66:13 Like a mother who comforts her child, so will I comfort you; and you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
Isaiah 66:14 When you see this, your heart will be happy, and your bones will grow strong like a plant: and God's support will be clear to his servants, and his anger to his enemies.
Isaiah 66:15 Look, God will come with fire, and with his chariots like a storm, to show his anger with intensity, and his correction with fire.
Isaiah 66:16 God will judge all people with fire and his sword, and many will be killed.
Isaiah 66:17 Those who try to make themselves pure by rituals in gardens, standing behind one particular tree, and eat pork, disgusting things, and mice, will be destroyed together, says God.
Isaiah 66:18 I know what they do and think. I will bring together all countries and languages; they will come and see my greatness.
Isaiah 66:19 I will put a sign among them, and I will send the survivors to different nations – to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, where they use bows, to Tubal and Javan, and to distant islands that have not heard of me or seen my power. They will tell the foreigners about my greatness.
Isaiah 66:20 They will bring all your brothers as a gift to God from every nation by horses, chariots, carts, mules, and fast animals to God's holy mountain, Jerusalem, as God says, like the Israelites bring a gift in a clean container to God's house.
Isaiah 66:21 I will select some of them to be priests and Levites, says God.
Isaiah 66:22 Just like the new heavens and the new earth that I will create will always be with me, says God, so will your children and your name always be.
Isaiah 66:23 Every month and every week, all people will come to worship before me, says God.
Isaiah 66:24 They will go out and see the dead bodies of those who sinned against me. The worms on them will not die, and the fire will not go out. Everyone will hate the sight of them.

Jeremiah 1:1 These are the words of Jeremiah, Hilkiah's son, a priest from Anathoth in Benjamin's territory.
Jeremiah 1:2 God spoke to them when Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his rule.
Jeremiah 1:3 It happened in the time of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, up to the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, Josiah's son, king of Judah, until Jerusalem was taken away as prisoners in the fifth month.
Jeremiah 1:4 God spoke to me, saying,
Jeremiah 1:5 Before I made you in the womb, I knew you; before you were born, I set you apart and appointed you as a prophet to the nations.
Jeremiah 1:6 Then I said, "Oh, God! Look, I can't speak: I am just a child."
Jeremiah 1:7 But God told me, "Don't say, 'I am a child.' You must go wherever I send you and speak whatever I tell you."
Jeremiah 1:8 Don't be scared of their looks: I am with you to save you, says God.
Jeremiah 1:9 Then God reached out His hand and touched my mouth. And God said to me, "Look, I have placed my words in your mouth."
Jeremiah 1:10 Today, I have given you power over nations and kingdoms to uproot, tear down, destroy, and overthrow, to build and to plant.
Jeremiah 1:11 God's message came to me, saying, "Jeremiah, what do you see?" And I said, "I see the branch of an almond tree."
Jeremiah 1:12 Then God said to me, "You have seen correctly, for I will quickly carry out what I have said."
Jeremiah 1:13 God spoke to me again, asking, "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a boiling pot, tilted from the north."
Jeremiah 1:14 Then God said to me, "From the north, a bad thing will spread over all the people living in the land."
Jeremiah 1:15 Look, I will summon all the families from the northern kingdoms, says God. They will come and each will place his throne at the entrance of Jerusalem's gates, around all its walls, and near all the towns of Judah.
Jeremiah 1:16 I will announce my decisions against them for all their evil, because they left me, burned incense to other gods, and worshiped what their hands made.
Jeremiah 1:17 Get ready, stand up, and tell them everything I tell you to say. Don't be afraid of them, or I will confuse you in front of them.
Jeremiah 1:18 Today, I have made you like a protected city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls against the entire country, its kings, leaders, priests, and all the people.
Jeremiah 1:19 They will fight against you, but they won't win, because I am with you, says God, to save you.

Jeremiah 2:1 God spoke to me, saying,
Jeremiah 2:2 Go and tell Jerusalem, 'God says: I remember how kind you were when you were young, and how you loved me when we were newly together, following me in the desert, in a land where nothing was planted.'
Jeremiah 2:3 Israel was sacred to God, and the first of his crops. Anyone who harms Israel will be punished; they will face trouble, says God.
Jeremiah 2:4 Listen to God's message, O family of Jacob, and all the clans of Israel:
Jeremiah 2:5 God asks, "What wrong did your ancestors find in me that made them leave me, follow worthless things, and become worthless themselves?"
Jeremiah 2:6 No one asked, "Where is God who brought us out of Egypt, who led us through the wild land of deserts and pits, through a dry land and dark death's shadow, through a place where no one travels or lives?"
Jeremiah 2:7 I brought you to a fertile land to eat its fruit and enjoy its richness, but when you came in, you made my land dirty and turned my property into something disgusting.
Jeremiah 2:8 The priests didn't ask, "Where is God?" and those who knew the law didn't know me: the leaders also sinned against me, and the prophets spoke for Baal, following things that bring no good.
Jeremiah 2:9 So I will still argue with you, says God, and with your grandchildren too.
Jeremiah 2:10 Travel to the islands of Chittim and look; then go to Kedar, think hard, and see if there's anything like this.
Jeremiah 2:11 Has a nation swapped its gods, which are not really gods? But my people have traded their honor for something that brings no benefit.
Jeremiah 2:12 Be shocked, you heavens, at this, and be terribly scared, be very empty, says God.
Jeremiah 2:13 My people did two bad things; they left me, the source of life-giving water, and dug their own wells, cracked wells that cannot hold water.
Jeremiah 2:14 Is Israel a servant? Is he a slave born in the house? Why is he destroyed?
Jeremiah 2:15 Young lions roared at him, screamed, and left his land empty: his cities are burned with no one living in them.
Jeremiah 2:16 The children from Noph and Tahapanes have damaged the top of your head.
Jeremiah 2:17 Didn't you bring this on yourself by abandoning God, who guided you on your path?
Jeremiah 2:18 Why are you going to Egypt to drink the water of the Nile? Or why are you going to Assyria to drink the water of the Euphrates?
Jeremiah 2:19 Your bad behavior will teach you a lesson, and your wrongdoings will show you your mistake. Understand and realize that it's a bad and painful thing to have left God, and that you don't respect me, says God.
Jeremiah 2:20 Long ago, I removed your heavy yoke and broke your chains; but you said, 'I won't sin.' Yet on every high hill and under every green tree, you wandered and acted unfaithfully.
Jeremiah 2:21 I planted you as a fine vine, all with good seeds: how then have you become a poor vine to me?
Jeremiah 2:22 Even if you use baking soda and lots of soap, your sins are still clearly seen by me, says God.
Jeremiah 2:23 How can you say, 'I am not dirty, I have not followed other gods'? Look at your path in the valley, see what you have done: you are like a fast camel running on her paths.
Jeremiah 2:24 A wild donkey used to the desert, that breathes in the wind as it wants; who can make it change its ways when it's ready? Those who look for it won't get tired; when the time comes, they will find it.
Jeremiah 2:25 Take care of your feet so they're not bare, and don't let yourself be thirsty; but you've said, "There's no hope; I love outsiders, and I'll follow them."
Jeremiah 2:26 Like a thief feels shame when caught, so the people of Israel feel ashamed; including their kings, leaders, priests, and prophets.
Jeremiah 2:27 They say to a piece of wood, "You are my dad," and to a rock, "You gave birth to me." They turn their back on me, not their face. But when they are in trouble, they'll call out, "Get up and save us."
Jeremiah 2:28 Where are the gods you made? Let them help you when you're in trouble. You have as many gods as you have cities, Judah.
Jeremiah 2:29 Why do you argue with me? You have all sinned against me, says God.
Jeremiah 2:30 I have punished your children for nothing; they did not learn their lesson. Your own violence has killed your prophets, like a deadly lion.
Jeremiah 2:31 People of this time, look at God's message. Have I been like a desert to Israel? A place of darkness? Why do my people say, "We are our own masters; we won't come to you anymore"?
Jeremiah 2:32 Can a young woman forget her jewelry, or a bride her wedding clothes? Yet my people have forgotten me for countless days.
Jeremiah 2:33 Why do you change your ways to get love? So you have also taught the bad ones your ways.
Jeremiah 2:34 In your clothes, they found the blood of innocent poor people: it was not hidden, but found on all of these.
Jeremiah 2:35 But you say, "I am innocent, so surely God's anger will stop." I will argue with you because you say, "I have not sinned."
Jeremiah 2:36 Why do you wander around so much to change your path? You will also feel ashamed of Egypt, just as you felt ashamed of Assyria.
Jeremiah 2:37 Yes, you will leave there with your hands on your head, because God has rejected the things you trust in, and you will not succeed with them.

Jeremiah 3:1 People ask, "If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him to be with another man, can he take her back? Won't that make the land very unclean?" But you have been unfaithful with many partners; still, come back to me, says God.
Jeremiah 3:2 Look up to the high places and see where you haven't been with anyone. You have waited along the paths for others, like an Arabian in the desert; and you have made the land impure with your unfaithfulness and your evil ways.
Jeremiah 3:3 So the rains have been stopped, and there was no late rain; your face was like a prostitute's, you refused to feel shame.
Jeremiah 3:4 Won't you from now on call out to me, 'My Father, you have led me since I was young'?
Jeremiah 3:5 Will God stay angry forever? Will he keep his anger to the end? You have said and done bad things as much as you could.
Jeremiah 3:6 God also said to me in King Josiah's time, "Have you seen what unfaithful Israel has done? She has gone up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and there acted like a prostitute."
Jeremiah 3:7 After she did all this, I said, "Come back to me." But she did not return. And her unfaithful sister Judah saw this.
Jeremiah 3:8 I saw that, even though Israel had been unfaithful and I divorced her, her deceitful sister Judah was not afraid and also acted unfaithfully.
Jeremiah 3:9 She became impure because of her many lovers, and she made the land impure too, by worshiping idols made of wood and stone.
Jeremiah 3:10 Despite this, Judah, her unfaithful sister, did not fully turn back to me but only pretended to, says God.
Jeremiah 3:11 God told me, "Israel, even though unfaithful, has proven to be better than the deceitful Judah."
Jeremiah 3:12 Go and speak these words to the north, and say, "Come back, unfaithful Israel," says God, "and I won't let my anger come down on you because I am merciful," says God, "and I won't stay angry forever."
Jeremiah 3:13 Admit your wrongs, admit you've sinned against God, by following foreign customs under every green tree, and not listening to me, says God.
Jeremiah 3:14 Come back to me, you who have turned away, says God; for I am committed to you: I will choose one person from each city and two from each family, and I will bring you to Zion.
Jeremiah 3:15 I will give you leaders who please me, and they will teach you with knowledge and understanding.
Jeremiah 3:16 When you grow and become many in the land, in those days, God says, they will no longer talk about the ark of God's covenant. It will not be thought of, remembered, or visited, and that will not happen again.
Jeremiah 3:17 At that time, people will call Jerusalem God's throne; all nations will come together there to honor God. And they will no longer follow their own evil thoughts.
Jeremiah 3:18 During that time, the people of Judah will join with the people of Israel, and together they will come from the northern lands to the land I gave your ancestors as their inheritance.
Jeremiah 3:19 But I said, "How can I place you among the children and give you a beautiful land, a wonderful inheritance from many nations?" And I said, "You will call me 'My Father,' and will not turn away from me."
Jeremiah 3:20 Just as a wife dishonestly leaves her husband, so you have been dishonest with me, O people of Israel, says God.
Jeremiah 3:21 A cry was heard on the hills, the weeping and prayers of Israel's children: because they have twisted their path, and they have forgotten God.
Jeremiah 3:22 Come back, you who have strayed, and I will heal your wandering. We are returning to you because you are our God.
Jeremiah 3:23 Hoping for rescue from the hills or many mountains is truly useless: only from God is Israel's salvation.
Jeremiah 3:24 Shame has ruined our ancestors' hard work since we were young; their animals, their sons, and their daughters.
Jeremiah 3:25 We lay in our shame, and our disgrace covers us: because we have sinned against God, both we and our ancestors, from our youth to this day, and have not listened to God's voice.

Jeremiah 4:1 If you will come back, Israel, says God, come back to me. And if you will get rid of your bad things so I can't see them, then you will not be moved.
Jeremiah 4:2 You will swear, "God is alive," honestly, fairly, and rightly; and nations will praise themselves in him, and they will take pride in him.
Jeremiah 4:3 God says to the men of Judah and Jerusalem, "Prepare your unused land for planting, and do not sow seeds among thorns."
Jeremiah 4:4 Make your hearts pure for God, you men of Judah and people of Jerusalem, or my anger will burn like a fire that no one can put out because of your bad actions.
Jeremiah 4:5 Announce in Judah and tell everyone in Jerusalem; say, "Sound the trumpet throughout the land: shout loudly, come together, and let's go to the fortified cities."
Jeremiah 4:6 Raise a signal toward Zion. Get away and don't stop, for I will bring disaster from the north, and massive destruction.
Jeremiah 4:7 A lion has come out from his hiding place, and the one who destroys nations is coming; he has left his home to ruin your land; and your cities will be destroyed, with no one living in them.
Jeremiah 4:8 Put on rough cloth to show you are sad, cry loudly and mourn, because God's strong anger has not been turned away from us.
Jeremiah 4:9 On that day, God says, the king will be filled with fear, and so will the princes; the priests will be shocked, and the prophets will be amazed.
Jeremiah 4:10 I said, "Ah, God! You have truly misled these people and Jerusalem by telling them they will have peace, while the threat of death is so near."
Jeremiah 4:11 Then people will say to Jerusalem, "A harsh wind from the desert hills blows towards my people, not to cool or to clean them."
Jeremiah 4:12 A strong wind from there will come to me; now I will also pass judgment on them.
Jeremiah 4:13 Look, he will rise like clouds, his chariots will be like a storm: his horses are faster than eagles. Trouble for us! We are ruined.
Jeremiah 4:14 Jerusalem, clean your heart of evil so you can be saved. How long will your useless thoughts stay in you?
Jeremiah 4:15 A voice announces from Dan, and spreads news of trouble from Mount Ephraim.
Jeremiah 4:16 Tell the nations; look, announce to Jerusalem that guards are coming from a far land, and they shout against the towns of Judah.
Jeremiah 4:17 They surround her like guards in a field because she has rebelled against me, says God.
Jeremiah 4:18 Your actions have caused these things to happen to you; this is your wrongdoing, because it is harsh and it hurts you deeply.
Jeremiah 4:19 I am in deep pain and my heart hurts; it beats loudly inside me. I cannot stay quiet because, my soul, you have heard the war trumpet’s call.
Jeremiah 4:20 Destruction follows destruction; the whole land is ruined: suddenly my tents are destroyed, and my curtains in an instant.
Jeremiah 4:21 How long will I see the flag and hear the trumpet sound?
Jeremiah 4:22 My people are foolish, they don't know me; they are stupid children, without understanding. They are clever at doing wrong, but clueless about doing right.
Jeremiah 4:23 I saw the earth, and it was shapeless and empty; the skies were dark with no light.
Jeremiah 4:24 I saw the mountains, and look, they shook, and all the hills swayed gently.
Jeremiah 4:25 I saw, and look, there was no one, and all the birds of the sky had flown away.
Jeremiah 4:26 I saw that the fertile land had become a desert, and all its cities were destroyed because of God and his intense anger.
Jeremiah 4:27 God has said, the whole land will be empty; but I will not completely destroy it.
Jeremiah 4:28 Because of this, the earth will be sad and the sky will turn dark; for I have said it, planned it, and will not change my mind or go back on it.
Jeremiah 4:29 Everyone in the city will run away because of the noise of the horsemen and archers; they will hide in the bushes and climb the rocks. Every city will be empty, and no one will live there.
Jeremiah 4:30 When you are ruined, what will you do? Even if you wear red clothes, even if you put on gold jewelry, even if you put makeup on your face, it's useless to try to look beautiful; your lovers will hate you, they will want to kill you.
Jeremiah 4:31 I have heard a sound like a woman in labor, the agony of a first-time mother, the sound of Zion's daughter crying out, stretching out her hands and saying, "I am in distress now, for I am exhausted by killers."

Jeremiah 5:1 Go through Jerusalem's streets, look carefully, and search in its open spaces to see if you can find one person who acts justly and seeks truth; if so, I will forgive the city.
Jeremiah 5:2 Even though they say, "God is alive", they are truly lying when they swear.
Jeremiah 5:3 God, don't you look for honesty? You punished them, but they didn't care; you destroyed them, but they wouldn't learn. Their faces are tougher than stone; they wouldn't come back to you.
Jeremiah 5:4 So I thought, these people are poor and unwise because they don't know the way of God or understand His decisions.
Jeremiah 5:5 I will go to the leaders and talk to them; for they know God's path and the rulings of their God: but these people have completely broken off the yoke and torn apart the ties.
Jeremiah 5:6 So a lion from the woods will kill them, a wolf at night will destroy them, and a leopard will guard their cities. Anyone who leaves will be attacked because they have many sins and keep turning away from God.
Jeremiah 5:7 How can I forgive you for this? Your children left me and made promises to false gods. I gave them plenty to eat, but then they cheated on me and gathered at prostitutes' houses.
Jeremiah 5:8 They were like well-fed horses in the morning: each one desired his neighbor's wife.
Jeremiah 5:9 Will I not punish for these things? says God: and will not I take revenge on a nation like this?
Jeremiah 5:10 Climb up her walls and tear them down, but don't completely destroy everything; remove her defenses, for they don't belong to God.
Jeremiah 5:11 The people of Israel and Judah have been very unfaithful to me, says God.
Jeremiah 5:12 They have lied about God, and said, He is not the one; we won't face disaster; we won't see war or hunger.
Jeremiah 5:13 The prophets will turn into wind, and they do not have the word: this is how they will be treated.
Jeremiah 5:14 So God says, because you say this, look, I will turn my words in your mouth into fire, and these people into wood, and the fire will burn them up.
Jeremiah 5:15 Look, I will send a nation against you from far away, O people of Israel, says God: a powerful and old nation, a nation whose language you do not know or understand what they say.
Jeremiah 5:16 Their bag of arrows is like an open grave; they are all strong warriors.
Jeremiah 5:17 They will eat your crops and your bread that your sons and daughters should eat. They will consume your flocks and herds. They will destroy your vineyards and fig trees. They will ruin your protected cities, where you felt safe, with the sword.
Jeremiah 5:18 But in those days, says God, I will not completely destroy you.
Jeremiah 5:19 When you ask, "Why does God do all this to us?" you will say, "Just as you left me to worship other gods in your own land, you will serve foreigners in a land not your own."
Jeremiah 5:20 Tell this to the people of Jacob, and announce it in Judah:
Jeremiah 5:21 Listen to this, you foolish people without understanding; you have eyes but do not see, you have ears but do not hear.
Jeremiah 5:22 Are you not afraid of me? says God. Won't you shake in fear before me, who has set the sand as the sea's limit by a forever command, so it can't go past it? Even if its waves crash around, they still can't win; even if they roar, they cannot cross it.
Jeremiah 5:23 These people have a disobedient and rebellious heart; they have turned away and left.
Jeremiah 5:24 They don't think, "Let's respect God, who sends rain in the right seasons and sets the harvest times for us."
Jeremiah 5:25 Your wrongdoings have pushed away these blessings, and your sins have kept good things from you.
Jeremiah 5:26 Among my people there are bad people: they hide and wait like someone setting traps; they set a trap and catch others.
Jeremiah 5:27 Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of lies; so they have become powerful and very rich.
Jeremiah 5:28 They have grown fat and sleek; indeed, they have gone beyond the evil deeds: they do not defend the rights of orphans, and yet they succeed; they also do not uphold the cause of the poor.
Jeremiah 5:29 Will I not punish them for these acts? says God. Won't I take revenge on a nation like this with my very being?
Jeremiah 5:30 A shocking and terrible thing has happened in the land;
Jeremiah 5:31 The prophets tell lies, and the priests lead with their help; and my people like it that way: but what will you do when it all ends?

Jeremiah 6:1 People of Benjamin, come together to escape from Jerusalem. Sound the horn in Tekoa, and light a beacon in Bethhaccerem. Danger is coming from the north, bringing huge ruin.
Jeremiah 6:2 I have compared Zion's daughter to a lovely and gentle woman.
Jeremiah 6:3 Shepherds and their flocks will come to her; they will set up their tents all around; they will each feed in their own area.
Jeremiah 6:4 Get ready for war against her; stand up, let's attack at noon. Trouble for us! The day is fading, and the evening shadows are getting long.
Jeremiah 6:5 Get up, and we'll go at night to destroy her grand houses.
Jeremiah 6:6 God has said, "Cut down trees and build a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city that must be punished; there is nothing but oppression within her."
Jeremiah 6:7 Like a spring spouts water, she spouts her evil: violence and robbery are heard within her; pain and injury are always before me.
Jeremiah 6:8 Learn your lesson, Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you; I will make you empty, a place with no people.
Jeremiah 6:9 God says, "They will completely pick the remaining people of Israel like a vine: put your hand back like a grape picker into the baskets."
Jeremiah 6:10 Who should I talk to and warn so they will listen? Look, they don't want to hear and can't understand. God's message is offensive to them; they find no joy in it.
Jeremiah 6:11 So I am filled with God's anger, I can't hold it in: I will release it on the kids outside, and on groups of young men: because the husband and wife will be caught, as well as the old person with the very old.
Jeremiah 6:12 Their homes, lands, and wives will be given to others, because I will raise my hand against the people of this land, says God.
Jeremiah 6:13 From the least to the greatest, everyone is greedy; from the prophet to the priest, everyone lies.
Jeremiah 6:14 They have lightly healed my people's wound, saying, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.
Jeremiah 6:15 Did they feel shame when they did something very wrong? No, they did not feel any shame, and they could not even blush. So they will fall like others who fall. When I punish them, they will be brought down, says God.
Jeremiah 6:16 God says, "Stand at the crossroads and look. Ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is, and walk in it. Then you will find peace for yourselves." But they said, "We won't walk in it."
Jeremiah 6:17 I also placed guards over you, saying, "Listen to the trumpet." But they said, "We will not listen."
Jeremiah 6:18 Listen, nations, and understand, community, what is happening among them.
Jeremiah 6:19 Listen, Earth: I will bring trouble on these people, the result of their thinking, because they did not listen to my words or my law, but rejected it.
Jeremiah 6:20 Why do you bring me incense from Sheba and sweet cane from distant lands? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please me.
Jeremiah 6:21 So God says, "Look, I will put obstacles in front of these people. Both fathers and sons will trip over them, and neighbors and friends will be destroyed."
Jeremiah 6:22 God says, "Look, a people is coming from the north land, and a great nation will arise from the far parts of the earth."
Jeremiah 6:23 They will grab bows and spears; they are harsh and show no kindness; their voices are loud like the ocean; they ride on horses, lined up ready to fight you, daughter of Zion.
Jeremiah 6:24 We have heard of its fame; our hands grow weak; distress grips us, and pain like that of a woman giving birth.
Jeremiah 6:25 Do not go into the field or walk on the road; the enemy's sword and fear are all around.
Jeremiah 6:26 My people's daughter, put on rough clothing and roll in the ashes. Cry bitterly as if for an only child, because the destroyer will soon come upon us.
Jeremiah 6:27 I have made you a tower and stronghold among my people so that you can understand and test their ways.
Jeremiah 6:28 They all rebel greatly, spreading lies; they are like brass and iron; they all corrupt.
Jeremiah 6:29 The blowers are scorched, the lead is melted by the fire; the metalworker tries in vain to purify, because the evil are not removed.
Jeremiah 6:30 People will call them worthless silver because God has rejected them.

Jeremiah 7:1 God told Jeremiah,
Jeremiah 7:2 Stand at the entrance of God's house, speak this message, and say, "Listen to God's word, all you from Judah who come through these gates to worship God."
Jeremiah 7:3 God, the ruler of all, says to the people of Israel: Change how you live and act, and I will let you live here.
Jeremiah 7:4 Don't trust in false words that say, "This is God's temple, God's temple, God's temple."
Jeremiah 7:5 If you truly change your ways and actions; if you honestly apply justice between one person and another;
Jeremiah 7:6 If you do not mistreat foreigners, orphans, and widows, and do not kill innocent people here, and do not follow other gods to your own harm:
Jeremiah 7:7 I will let you live in this place, in the land I gave to your ancestors, forever and always.
Jeremiah 7:8 Look, you believe in false words that are of no use.
Jeremiah 7:9 Will you steal, kill, cheat, lie, worship Baal, and follow unknown gods?
Jeremiah 7:10 Come stand before me in this house, named for me, and say, 'We are saved so we can do all these wrong things?'
Jeremiah 7:11 Do you see this house, known as my house, as a thieves' hideout? I have seen it too, says God.
Jeremiah 7:12 Go to the place I chose first in Shiloh, where I made my name known, and see what I did to it because of the evil done by my people Israel.
Jeremiah 7:13 Now, because you have done all these things, says God, I spoke to you again and again, but you did not listen; I called you, but you did not answer.
Jeremiah 7:14 So I will treat this temple, known by my name where you trust, and the place I gave to you and your ancestors, just as I did to Shiloh.
Jeremiah 7:15 I will throw you away from me, like I threw away all your brothers, the entire family of Ephraim.
Jeremiah 7:16 So do not pray for these people, do not beg or plead for them, and do not ask me to help them, because I will not listen to you.
Jeremiah 7:17 Don't you see what they do in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
Jeremiah 7:18 The children collect wood, the fathers start the fire, and the women prepare their bread to make cakes for the queen of heaven, and to offer drinks to other gods, making me angry.
Jeremiah 7:19 Are they making me angry? says God. Aren't they just confusing themselves?
Jeremiah 7:20 So God says, "Look, I will pour out my anger and fury on this place, on people, animals, trees, and crops. It will burn and not be put out."
Jeremiah 7:21 God, the God of Israel, says: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat meat.
Jeremiah 7:22 I did not tell your ancestors, nor did I command them about burnt offerings or sacrifices when I brought them out of Egypt.
Jeremiah 7:23 I told them to obey me, and I will be your God, and you will be my people. Follow all my commands, so things will go well for you.
Jeremiah 7:24 But they didn't listen or pay attention. Instead, they followed their own plans and desires of their evil hearts. They went backwards, not forwards.
Jeremiah 7:25 Since the time your ancestors left Egypt until now, I have sent you my prophets, day after day, getting up early to send them.
Jeremiah 7:26 They did not listen to me or pay attention, but they were stubborn, doing worse than their ancestors.
Jeremiah 7:27 So you must tell them all these words, but they will not listen to you; you must also call to them, but they will not respond to you.
Jeremiah 7:28 You should tell them, "This nation does not listen to God's voice and does not accept correction. Truth is gone and no longer spoken by them."
Jeremiah 7:29 Shave your head, Jerusalem, throw away your hair, and cry on the hills, because God has rejected and abandoned the people he is angry with.
Jeremiah 7:30 The people of Judah have done wrong in my eyes, says God; they have put their disgusting things in the temple that has my name, to make it dirty.
Jeremiah 7:31 They made worship sites at Tophet in Hinnom valley, to burn their sons and daughters in fire; I never told them to do this, and I never thought of such a thing.
Jeremiah 7:32 So, look, days are coming, says God, that it will not be named Tophet, or the valley of Hinnom's son, but the valley of killing: for they will bury in Tophet until there is no space.
Jeremiah 7:33 The dead bodies of these people will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, and no one will scare them away.
Jeremiah 7:34 I will stop the sounds of joy and happiness, and the voices of the bride and groom in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, because the land will be empty.

Jeremiah 8:1 At that time, God says, they will take out the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of the princes, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the people of Jerusalem from their graves.
Jeremiah 8:2 They will lay them out under the sun, and the moon, and all the stars in the sky, which they loved, served, followed, sought after, and worshipped. They won't be collected or buried; they will become like waste on the ground.
Jeremiah 8:3 Those left from this wicked family, in every place where I've sent them, will prefer death over life, says God.
Jeremiah 8:4 Also, tell them, "This is what God says: If they fall, won't they get up? If someone turns away, won't they come back?"
Jeremiah 8:5 Why do the people of Jerusalem keep turning away forever? They cling to lies and won't turn back.
Jeremiah 8:6 I listened and heard, but they did not speak correctly: no one felt sorry for their evil ways, asking, "What have I done?" Everyone kept to their own path, like a horse charging into battle.
Jeremiah 8:7 Yes, the stork in the sky knows her set times; and the dove, the crane, and the swallow keep track of their migration time; but my people do not understand God's laws.
Jeremiah 8:8 Why do you say, "We are wise, and we have God's law"? Look, it was useless for him to write it; the scribes' work is useless.
Jeremiah 8:9 The wise men feel ashamed, confused, and trapped because they have ignored God's word; so, what wisdom do they really have?
Jeremiah 8:10 So I will give their wives to others and their fields to new owners, because everyone, from the least to the greatest, is greedy, and from the prophet to the priest, everyone lies.
Jeremiah 8:11 They have only slightly healed my people's wounds, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace.
Jeremiah 8:12 Did they feel shame when they did wrong? No, they had no shame at all and could not even blush. So they will fall with those who fall; when it's time for their punishment, they will be brought down, says God.
Jeremiah 8:13 God says, "I will certainly destroy them. There will be no grapes on the vines, no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves will wither. Everything I gave them will be taken away."
Jeremiah 8:14 Why are we just sitting here? Let's gather and go into the fortified cities and stay quiet there: for God has made us silent and given us bitter water to drink because we have sinned against God.
Jeremiah 8:15 We hoped for peace, but nothing good happened; we wanted a time of healing, but we found distress!
Jeremiah 8:16 People heard his horses snorting from Dan; the land shook from the noise of his mighty horses. They came, ate up the land, and everything in it, including the city and its people.
Jeremiah 8:17 Look, I will send snakes, venomous ones, among you, which cannot be tamed, and they will bite you, says God.
Jeremiah 8:18 When I try to soothe my sadness, my heart feels weak inside me.
Jeremiah 8:19 Listen to my people's daughter crying out from a distant land: Isn't God in Zion? Isn't her king there? Why have they made me angry with their idols and pointless foreign gods?
Jeremiah 8:20 The harvest is over, the summer has finished, and we are not rescued.
Jeremiah 8:21 I am in pain because my people are suffering; I am deeply sad and shocked.
Jeremiah 8:22 Is there no medicine in Gilead; is there no doctor there? Why then isn't the health of my people restored?

Jeremiah 9:1 I wish my head were full of water, and my eyes were a stream of tears, so I could cry day and night for the people who have been killed.
Jeremiah 9:2 I wish I had a traveler's shelter in the desert so I could leave my people and get away from them; they are all unfaithful, a group of liars.
Jeremiah 9:3 They twist their words like a bow for lies; they are not brave for the truth on earth; they go from one bad act to another and do not know me, says God.
Jeremiah 9:4 Be careful of everyone around you, and don't trust any brother fully; for every brother may betray you, and every neighbor might spread lies.
Jeremiah 9:5 Everyone will trick their neighbor and not tell the truth; they have trained their tongue to lie and exhaust themselves doing wrong.
Jeremiah 9:6 Your home is in the middle of lies; because of these lies, they choose not to know me, says God.
Jeremiah 9:7 So this is what God says: "Look, I will test them and refine them; because what else can I do for my people's children?"
Jeremiah 9:8 Their tongue is like a shot arrow; it tells lies. They talk kindly to their neighbor with their mouth, but in their heart, they set a trap.
Jeremiah 9:9 Won't I punish them for these acts? says God. Won't I take revenge on a nation like this with all my being?
Jeremiah 9:10 I will cry and wail for the mountains, and mourn for the desert settlements, because they are scorched and no one can travel through them; no one can hear the cattle, and the birds of the sky and the animals have fled; they have disappeared.
Jeremiah 9:11 I will turn Jerusalem into piles of rubble, a home for dragons; I will make the towns of Judah empty, with no one living there.
Jeremiah 9:12 Who is the wise person who can understand this? And who has God spoken to so they can explain it, why the land is dying and scorched like a desert, empty and unused?
Jeremiah 9:13 God says, "They have left my law which I gave them, have not listened to my voice, or followed it."
Jeremiah 9:14 But they followed the desires of their own heart and worshiped Baal, as their ancestors taught them.
Jeremiah 9:15 So this is what God, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will make them, this nation, eat bitter plants, and drink poisoned water.
Jeremiah 9:16 I will spread them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known, and I will chase them with a sword until they are destroyed.
Jeremiah 9:17 God says, "Think about this, and ask the weeping women to come; invite the skilled women to come too."
Jeremiah 9:18 Let them hurry and cry for us, so our eyes fill with tears, and our eyelids overflow with water.
Jeremiah 9:19 A sound of crying comes from Zion, "We are ruined! We are totally ashamed because we left our land, our homes have thrown us out."
Jeremiah 9:20 Listen to God's word, women, take in his message, show your daughters how to cry, and teach each other how to mourn.
Jeremiah 9:21 Death has climbed through our windows and entered our palaces, to take away children from outside, and young men from the streets.
Jeremiah 9:22 Say this, God says, "Dead bodies will lie like waste on the ground, like cut grain left by the reaper, with no one to pick them up."
Jeremiah 9:23 God says, "Don't let the wise man boast about his wisdom, don't let the strong man boast about his strength, don't let the rich man boast about his wealth."
Jeremiah 9:24 But if anyone wants to boast, let them boast about this: that they understand and know God, who shows kindness, fairness, and what is right on the earth, because God takes pleasure in these things.
Jeremiah 9:25 Look, a time is coming, says God, when I will punish both the circumcised and the uncircumcised.
Jeremiah 9:26 Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon's children, Moab, and everyone from faraway places living in the desert: all these nations are not circumcised, and all Israel's people are not circumcised in heart.

Jeremiah 10:1 Listen to the message that God is giving you, people of Israel.
Jeremiah 10:2 God says, "Don't follow the heathen's ways, and don't be scared of the sky signs; the heathen are scared of them."
Jeremiah 10:3 The ways of the people are worthless: someone cuts down a tree from the woods, made by a worker using an axe.
Jeremiah 10:4 They decorate it with silver and gold; they use nails and hammers to secure it so it doesn't move.
Jeremiah 10:5 They stand straight like palm trees but cannot speak. They need to be carried since they cannot walk. Do not fear them; they cannot do harm, nor can they do good.
Jeremiah 10:6 No one is like you, God; you are great, and your name is powerful.
Jeremiah 10:7 Who wouldn't respect you, King of nations? It belongs to you; because among all the wise people of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, no one is like you.
Jeremiah 10:8 But they are all senseless and foolish; their idol is just a teaching about worthless things.
Jeremiah 10:9 Silver made into sheets is brought from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz, made by craftsmen and metalworkers. Their clothes are blue and purple, all created by skilled artisans.
Jeremiah 10:10 God is the real God, the living God, and a forever king: when he is angry, the earth will shake, and the countries won't stand his anger.
Jeremiah 10:11 Tell them, "The gods who did not create the sky and the earth will vanish from the earth and from under the sky."
Jeremiah 10:12 God made the earth with his power, set up the world with his wisdom, and spread out the skies with his understanding.
Jeremiah 10:13 When he speaks, many waters form in the sky, and he makes vapors rise from the earth's edges; he creates lightning with rain, and brings wind from his storerooms.
Jeremiah 10:14 Everyone is foolish in what they know; every metal worker is ashamed of their idol, because what they pour as an image is a lie, and there is no life in them.
Jeremiah 10:15 They are worthless and make mistakes; when it's time for them to be judged, they will be destroyed.
Jeremiah 10:16 Jacob's share is not like theirs: he is the maker of everything; and Israel is the tribe he inherits: God of all armies is his name.
Jeremiah 10:17 Collect your belongings from the land, person living in the strong place.
Jeremiah 10:18 God says, "I will throw out the people living in the land this time and trouble them so they realize it."
Jeremiah 10:19 I am in trouble because I am hurt! My injury is serious, but I thought, This is truly sad, and I must endure it.
Jeremiah 10:20 My tent is ruined, all its ropes are snapped; my children have left me, and they are gone. No one is left to put up my tent or hang my curtains.
Jeremiah 10:21 The leaders have become foolish and have not looked for God: so they will not succeed, and all their flocks will be spread out.
Jeremiah 10:22 Look, the sound of the report has arrived, and a big disturbance from the north to leave the towns of Judah empty, and a home for dragons.
Jeremiah 10:23 God, I understand that a person's path is not decided by themselves: it is not for the one who walks to choose their own way.
Jeremiah 10:24 God, correct me fairly, not in anger, or I will be destroyed.
Jeremiah 10:25 Release your anger on the nations that don't know you, and on the peoples who don't pray to you: for they have attacked Jacob, destroyed him, and left his home empty.

Jeremiah 11:1 God told Jeremiah:
Jeremiah 11:2 Listen to the words of this agreement and tell them to the people of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 11:3 Tell them, "This is what God of Israel says: The person who does not follow the words of this agreement will be cursed."
Jeremiah 11:4 On the day I led your ancestors out of Egypt, the land of harsh labor, I told them: "Listen to me and do as I say. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God."
Jeremiah 11:5 I want to keep the promise I made to your ancestors to give them a land rich with milk and honey, just like today. Then I replied, "Let it be so, God."
Jeremiah 11:6 Then God told me, "Announce all these words in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Say, 'Listen to the terms of this agreement and follow them.'"
Jeremiah 11:7 I strongly warned your ancestors when I took them from Egypt, and I've continued until today, telling them to listen to me.
Jeremiah 11:8 They did not obey or listen, instead they followed their own evil desires. So I will make them face all the consequences of the agreement I gave them to follow, but they did not.
Jeremiah 11:9 God told me, "There is a plot among the people of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem."
Jeremiah 11:10 They have returned to the sins of their ancestors, who didn't listen to my words; they followed other gods to worship them: both Israel and Judah have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors.
Jeremiah 11:11 So God says, "I will bring trouble to them that they can't escape. Even if they call out to me, I won't listen."
Jeremiah 11:12 Then the towns of Judah and people of Jerusalem will cry to the gods they burned incense to, but those gods won't rescue them when they're in trouble.
Jeremiah 11:13 Judah, you had as many gods as you had cities; you built as many altars for that disgraceful idol as there are streets in Jerusalem, altars to offer incense to Baal.
Jeremiah 11:14 Do not pray for these people, nor call out or pray for them, because I will not listen when they call to me in their trouble.
Jeremiah 11:15 Why is my loved one in my house when she has done shameful things with many, and the sacred meat is gone from you? When you do wrong, you are happy.
Jeremiah 11:16 God named you a green olive tree, beautiful with good fruit. But with loud noise, he set fire to it, and its branches are broken.
Jeremiah 11:17 God, who planted you, has declared disaster because of the wrongs of Israel and Judah, who angered me by burning incense to Baal.
Jeremiah 11:18 God has given me knowledge of it, and I know it: then you showed me what they have done.
Jeremiah 11:19 But I was like a lamb or an ox led to be killed; I did not know they had planned against me, saying, "Let's destroy the tree and its fruit, and let's cut him off from the world of the living, so that his name will be forgotten."
Jeremiah 11:20 But, God of all, who judges fairly and tests our minds and feelings, let me see your revenge on them, because I have told you my reasons.
Jeremiah 11:21 So, God tells the people of Anathoth who want to kill you, "Do not speak God's words, or we will kill you."
Jeremiah 11:22 So God says, "Look, I will punish them: the young men will die by the sword; their sons and daughters will die by hunger."
Jeremiah 11:23 No one from them will survive because I will bring disaster upon the people of Anathoth when it's time to punish them.

Jeremiah 12:1 You are right, God, when I speak with you. But let me ask you about your decisions: Why do bad people succeed? Why are all the cheaters happy?
Jeremiah 12:2 You have planted them, and they have taken root; they grow and produce fruit. You are on their lips, but far from their hearts.
Jeremiah 12:3 But you, God, know me; you see me and test my heart towards you. Take them away like sheep to be killed, and get them ready for their day of slaughter.
Jeremiah 12:4 How long will the land be sad, and the plants in the fields dry up, because of the bad things the people living there do? The animals and birds are dying, because they think, "God won't see what happens to us in the end."
Jeremiah 12:5 If you have raced with runners and they have tired you, then how can you race against horses? And if you get tired in a peaceful land where you felt safe, then what will you do when the Jordan River overflows?
Jeremiah 12:6 Even your own brothers and your father's family have been unfaithful to you; they have led a crowd against you. Do not trust them, even if they speak nicely to you.
Jeremiah 12:7 I have abandoned my home, I have left my inheritance; I have handed over the one I love deeply to her enemies.
Jeremiah 12:8 My inheritance is like a lion in the woods to me; it yells at me, so I have come to hate it.
Jeremiah 12:9 My inheritance is like a bird with mixed colors, and the other birds are against it; all you animals of the field, come and eat it up.
Jeremiah 12:10 Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard; they have walked all over my land; they have turned my lovely field into an empty wasteland.
Jeremiah 12:11 They have ruined it, and now it's sad and cries out to me; the whole land is ruined, because no one cares.
Jeremiah 12:12 Robbers have attacked all the high places in the desert; God's sword will destroy everything from one end of the land to the other, and no one will be safe.
Jeremiah 12:13 They planted wheat but will harvest thorns; they worked hard for no gain; and they will be embarrassed by your crops because of God's intense anger.
Jeremiah 12:14 God says to all my bad neighbors who interfere with the land I gave to my people Israel: I will remove them from their land, and take out the house of Judah from among them.
Jeremiah 12:15 After I remove them, I will come back, show them kindness, and bring each person back to their own property and land.
Jeremiah 12:16 If they carefully learn the ways of my people and swear by my name, saying 'God lives,' just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be established among my people.
Jeremiah 12:17 If they don't obey, I will completely uproot and destroy that nation, says God.

Jeremiah 13:1 God said to me, "Go and buy a linen belt and wear it around your waist, but do not put it in water."
Jeremiah 13:2 So I took a belt as God had said, and tied it around my waist.
Jeremiah 13:3 God's message came to me again, saying,
Jeremiah 13:4 Take the belt you have, which is around your waist, get up, go to the Euphrates, and hide it in a rock's hole.
Jeremiah 13:5 So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, just as God told me to.
Jeremiah 13:6 After many days, God told me, "Get up, go to the Euphrates and get the belt I told you to hide there."
Jeremiah 13:7 I went to the Euphrates, dug up, and took the belt from where I hid it, and look, the belt was ruined, it was useless.
Jeremiah 13:8 God's message came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 13:9 God says, I will ruin the pride of Judah and the big pride of Jerusalem in this way.
Jeremiah 13:10 These bad people, who won't listen to what I say, who follow their own desires, and worship other gods, serving them, will be like this useless belt.
Jeremiah 13:11 Just as a belt fits tightly around a person's waist, I brought the entire nations of Israel and Judah close to me, declares God, so they would be my people, bring me fame, praise, and honor. But they did not listen.
Jeremiah 13:12 So, tell them this message: God of Israel says, every jar will be filled with wine. And when they ask you, "Don't we already know that every jar will be filled with wine?"
Jeremiah 13:13 Then you will tell them, 'This is what God says: Look, I will make everyone in this land, including the kings on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people of Jerusalem, very drunk.
Jeremiah 13:14 I will smash them against each other, fathers and sons alike, says God. I will show no pity or mercy and will destroy them.
Jeremiah 13:15 Listen and pay attention; don't be proud: for God has spoken.
Jeremiah 13:16 Praise God before he brings darkness, before you trip on the shadowy mountains, and while you seek light, he turns it to deep shadow, and makes it very dark.
Jeremiah 13:17 If you don't listen, I will cry quietly because of your pride; my eyes will cry a lot and overflow with tears, because God's people are taken as prisoners.
Jeremiah 13:18 Tell the king and the queen to be humble and sit down, because their power will fall, including the crown they're proud of.
Jeremiah 13:19 The southern cities will be closed, with no one to open them. Everyone in Judah will be taken away as prisoners, completely taken away.
Jeremiah 13:20 Look up and see those coming from the north: where is the group of sheep given to you, your beautiful sheep?
Jeremiah 13:21 What will you say when God punishes you? You have trained them to lead and command over you; will you not be in pain like a woman giving birth?
Jeremiah 13:22 If you think, "Why are these things happening to me?" It is because of your great sins that you are exposed and humiliated.
Jeremiah 13:23 Can a person change their skin color or a leopard its spots? In the same way, you who always do bad might start doing good.
Jeremiah 13:24 So I will spread them out like straw blown away by the desert wind.
Jeremiah 13:25 This is what you get, the share I have given you, says God; because you forgot me and believed in lies.
Jeremiah 13:26 So I will lift your skirts over your face, and your disgrace will be seen.
Jeremiah 13:27 I have seen your unfaithfulness and your wild desires, the shameful acts of your prostitution, and the disgusting things you do on the hills in the fields. How terrible for you, Jerusalem! Will you ever be clean? When will it happen?

Jeremiah 14:1 The message from God that came to Jeremiah about the drought.
Jeremiah 14:2 Judah is sad, its gates are weak; they look dark to the ground; and Jerusalem's cry has risen.
Jeremiah 14:3 Their leaders sent their young ones for water. They went to the wells and found no water. They came back with their containers empty. They felt shame and disappointment and hid their faces.
Jeremiah 14:4 Because the ground is cracked, since there was no rain on the land, the farmers were embarrassed, and they covered their heads.
Jeremiah 14:5 Yes, the female deer gave birth in the field and left her newborn because there was no grass.
Jeremiah 14:6 The wild donkeys stood on the hills, they breathed in the wind like dragons; they went blind because there was no grass.
Jeremiah 14:7 God, even though our sins speak against us, act for your name's sake, because we have often turned away and have sinned against you.
Jeremiah 14:8 God, the hope of Israel and its savior in times of trouble, why do you seem like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who just stops to stay for one night?
Jeremiah 14:9 Why should you seem like a shocked man, like a strong man who can't save? But you, God, are with us, and we carry your name; don't leave us.
Jeremiah 14:10 God says to these people, "They love to wander and have not stopped their feet, so God does not accept them; he will now remember their wrongs and punish their sins."
Jeremiah 14:11 Then God said to me, "Do not pray for the good of these people."
Jeremiah 14:12 When they go without food, I will not listen to their calls; when they make a burnt offering and gifts, I will not take them. Instead, I will destroy them with war, hunger, and disease.
Jeremiah 14:13 Then I said, "Oh, God! Look, the prophets tell them, 'You won't see war or suffer from hunger; I will give you true peace in this place.'"
Jeremiah 14:14 Then God said to me, "The prophets are telling lies using my name: I did not send them, nor did I tell them to speak, nor have I spoken to them: they are giving you fake visions, using magic, and telling worthless and deceitful things from their own minds.
Jeremiah 14:15 So God says this about the prophets who say they speak for me, but I did not send them: They claim there will be no war or famine in this land, but it's by war and famine that those prophets will be destroyed.
Jeremiah 14:16 The people they tell prophecies to will be thrown onto the streets of Jerusalem because of hunger and war; no one will bury them, their wives, their sons, or their daughters: because I will bring their evil down on them.
Jeremiah 14:17 Tell them this: Let my eyes cry tears day and night without stopping, for my people's young daughter is deeply hurt by a terrible wound.
Jeremiah 14:18 If I go out to the fields, I see those killed by the sword! If I go into the city, I see people suffering from hunger! Yes, both the prophet and the priest wander in a land they do not know.
Jeremiah 14:19 Have you completely rejected Judah? Do you dislike Zion? Why have you hit us, and there's no cure for us? We hoped for peace, but there's nothing good; we waited for a time to heal, but instead, we found trouble!
Jeremiah 14:20 We admit, God, our wrongs and our ancestors' sins, for we have sinned against you.
Jeremiah 14:21 Do not hate us, for the sake of your name, do not dishonor your glorious throne: remember, do not break your promise to us.
Jeremiah 14:22 Do any of the false gods of other nations bring rain? Can the sky itself send down showers? Aren't you the one, our God? So we will wait for you, for you created everything.

Jeremiah 15:1 God said to me, "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, I would not favor these people. Throw them out of my sight and let them leave."
Jeremiah 15:2 If people ask you, "Where should we go?" you should tell them, "God says: those who are to die will die; those who are to be killed by the sword will be killed by the sword; those who are to starve will starve; and those who are to be taken captive will be taken captive."
Jeremiah 15:3 I will set four destroyers against them, God says: the sword to kill, the dogs to rip apart, the birds from the sky, and the animals of the earth to eat and ruin.
Jeremiah 15:4 I will make them be scattered to all countries of the world, because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 15:5 Who will feel sorry for you, O Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will stop to ask how you are?
Jeremiah 15:6 You have left me, says God, you have turned away; so I will reach out my hand against you and destroy you; I am tired of changing my mind.
Jeremiah 15:7 I will scatter them with a fan at the land's entrances; I will take away their children, I will wipe out my people because they do not turn from their ways.
Jeremiah 15:8 More widows have come to me than grains of sand in the sea: I've brought a destroyer at midday against young men's mothers. I made him strike suddenly, bringing fear to the city.
Jeremiah 15:9 The woman who had seven children is weak; she has died. Her life ended unexpectedly early. She is humiliated and distressed. And I will let their remaining people be defeated by their enemies' swords, says God.
Jeremiah 15:10 I am in trouble, my mother, because you gave birth to me as a man who argues and fights with everyone! I haven't borrowed money for interest, nor have I loaned money for interest; but everyone is cursing me.
Jeremiah 15:11 God said, "It will truly be good for your survivors; I will make the enemy treat you well in times of trouble and suffering."
Jeremiah 15:12 Can iron break the iron from the north and the steel?
Jeremiah 15:13 I will give away your wealth and treasures for nothing because of all your sins, throughout your entire land.
Jeremiah 15:14 I will make you go with your enemies to a land you don't know: because a fire has started in my anger that will burn you.
Jeremiah 15:15 God, you know: remember me, visit me, and take revenge for me on those who are after me; don't take me away while you are patient: know that I have been criticized because of you.
Jeremiah 15:16 I found your words and took them to heart; they made me happy and filled my heart with joy because I am known as one of your people, God of all.
Jeremiah 15:17 I did not sit with the mockers or celebrate; I sat by myself because of what you did; you have made me very angry.
Jeremiah 15:18 Why does my pain never end, and my wound cannot be healed and won't get better? Will you be like someone who lies to me, and like water that disappears?
Jeremiah 15:19 So God says, "If you come back, I will bring you back to stand before me. And if you separate the valuable from the worthless, you will be like my spokesperson. Let them come back to you, but do not go back to them."
Jeremiah 15:20 I will make you like a strong bronze wall to these people: they will fight against you, but they won't win over you, because I am with you to save and free you, says God.
Jeremiah 15:21 I will save you from the wicked and rescue you from the terrible.

Jeremiah 16:1 God's message came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 16:2 Do not marry or have sons or daughters here.
Jeremiah 16:3 God says this about the boys and girls born here, about their mothers who gave birth to them, and about their fathers who fathered them in this land;
Jeremiah 16:4 They will die painful deaths; no one will mourn for them; they won't be buried; they'll be like waste on the ground. They will be killed by war and hunger; and their bodies will be food for the birds and wild animals.
Jeremiah 16:5 God says, "Do not go into the house of mourning, nor grieve or weep for them, for I have removed my peace from these people," says God, "along with kindness and compassion."
Jeremiah 16:6 Everyone, both important and unimportant, will die in this land. They won't be buried, and no one will mourn, cut themselves, or shave their heads for them.
Jeremiah 16:7 People will not cut themselves in grief for others or offer comfort for the dead, nor will anyone give a comforting drink for someone's father or mother.
Jeremiah 16:8 Do not go into the place where people feast, to sit with them and eat and drink.
Jeremiah 16:9 God, the God of Israel, says: I will make the sounds of joy and celebration, the voices of the bride and groom, stop in this place before your very eyes during your lifetime.
Jeremiah 16:10 When you tell these people everything I’ve said, they will ask you, "Why has God declared such great disaster for us? What wrong have we done? What sin have we committed against our God?"
Jeremiah 16:11 Then you will tell them, 'Your ancestors left me,' says God, 'followed other gods, served and worshiped them, abandoned me, and didn't follow my laws.'
Jeremiah 16:12 You have acted worse than your ancestors; look, each of you follows their own wicked desires, refusing to listen to me.
Jeremiah 16:13 So I will throw you out of this land into a land you and your ancestors don't know. There you will worship other gods all the time. I will not be kind to you there.
Jeremiah 16:14 So, listen, the days will come, God says, that people will no longer say, "God lives, who brought the Israelites out of Egypt."
Jeremiah 16:15 But God lives, who brought the people of Israel from the northern land and all the places where he scattered them: and I will return them to their own land that I gave to their ancestors.
Jeremiah 16:16 Look, I will send many fishermen, says God, and they will fish for people; then I will send many hunters, and they will hunt for them on every mountain, on every hill, and from the rock holes.
Jeremiah 16:17 I see all their actions; nothing they do is hidden from me, nor is their wrongdoing hidden from my sight.
Jeremiah 16:18 First, I will repay their wrongdoing and sin twice over, because they have polluted my land and filled my inheritance with the dead bodies of their disgusting and hateful things.
Jeremiah 16:19 God, my strength and safe place, when trouble comes, people from all over the world will turn to you and admit that what their ancestors believed was false and useless.
Jeremiah 16:20 Can a person make their own gods when they are not really gods?
Jeremiah 16:21 So, I will let them see who I am this time, let them know my power and strength; and they will understand that my name is God.

Jeremiah 17:1 Judah's sin is deeply engraved on their hearts and on your altars' corners as if written with an iron pen and diamond tip.
Jeremiah 17:2 While their children recall their altars and sacred gardens near the green trees on the tall hills.
Jeremiah 17:3 I will give away all your wealth and treasures, and your worship places in the field because of sin, across your land.
Jeremiah 17:4 You will stop having the land I gave you; and I will make you serve your enemies in a land you don't know: because you have made me very angry, and it will burn forever.
Jeremiah 17:5 God says, "A curse on the person who trusts in other people, who depends on human strength, and turns away from God."
Jeremiah 17:6 He will be like a lonely plant in the desert, not seeing when good comes; he will live in dry areas of the wasteland, in salty land where no one lives.
Jeremiah 17:7 Happy is the person who trusts in God and whose hope is God.
Jeremiah 17:8 He will be like a tree by the water, sending out roots by the stream, not fearing the heat with green leaves, not worrying in dry times, never stopping making fruit.
Jeremiah 17:9 The heart can lie more than anything else and is very bad: who can understand it?
Jeremiah 17:10 I, God, search the heart and test the mind, to reward everyone according to their behavior and the results of their actions.
Jeremiah 17:11 Like a bird that sits on eggs it can't hatch, a person who gets money unfairly will lose it before their life is half over, and in the end, they will be foolish.
Jeremiah 17:12 A magnificent, lofty throne since the start is where our holy place is.
Jeremiah 17:13 God, the hope of Israel, all who leave you will be embarrassed, and those who turn away from me will be named in the dust, because they have left God, the source of living water.
Jeremiah 17:14 Heal me, God, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved; for you are my praise.
Jeremiah 17:15 Look, they ask me, "Where is God's message? Let it come now."
Jeremiah 17:16 As for me, I did not rush to stop being a shepherd to follow you; I did not wish for the terrible day; you know this: what I said was true in your presence.
Jeremiah 17:17 Don't scare me; you are my hope when things are bad.
Jeremiah 17:18 May those who chase me be confused, but keep me from confusion; let them be afraid, but keep me from fear; bring a day of trouble on them, and ruin them completely.
Jeremiah 17:19 God told me to go and stand at the city gate where the people of Judah's kings enter and exit, and at all of Jerusalem's gates.
Jeremiah 17:20 Tell them, "Listen to God's message, you kings of Judah, everyone in Judah, and all who live in Jerusalem and go through these gates."
Jeremiah 17:21 God says: Be careful and do not carry any load on the Sabbath day, or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 17:22 Do not take anything from your homes or do any work on the Sabbath, but keep it as a special day, just as I told your ancestors.
Jeremiah 17:23 But they did not obey or listen; instead, they were stubborn and would not hear or accept teaching.
Jeremiah 17:24 If you carefully listen to me, says God, do not carry any load through the city gates on the Sabbath; respect the Sabbath as a day of rest with no work.
Jeremiah 17:25 Kings and princes will come into the gates of this city. They will sit on David's throne and ride in chariots and on horses, along with their princes, the men of Judah, and the people of Jerusalem. And this city will last forever.
Jeremiah 17:26 People will come from Judah's cities, areas around Jerusalem, Benjamin's land, the plains, the mountains, and the south, bringing burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, and incense, as well as praise offerings, to God's house.
Jeremiah 17:27 If you don't listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy, and not carry any load through Jerusalem's gates on the Sabbath; then I will start a fire in its gates that will destroy Jerusalem's buildings, and it won't be put out.

Jeremiah 18:1 The message that came to Jeremiah from God said,
Jeremiah 18:2 Get up and go to the potter's house, where I will make you hear my message.
Jeremiah 18:3 I went to the potter's house and saw him making something on the wheel.
Jeremiah 18:4 The clay pot the potter was making got ruined in his hands, so he made a different pot in a way he thought was best.
Jeremiah 18:5 Then God spoke to me, saying,
Jeremiah 18:6 People of Israel, can't I deal with you as a potter does? says God. Look, just as clay is in the potter's control, so are you in my control, people of Israel.
Jeremiah 18:7 When I decide to talk about a nation or kingdom, to uproot, tear down, or destroy it;
Jeremiah 18:8 If that country, which I warned, stops doing bad things, I will not punish them as I planned.
Jeremiah 18:9 When I decide to talk about a nation or kingdom, to make it grow and succeed;
Jeremiah 18:10 If it does wrong in my eyes by not listening to me, then I will change my mind about the good I planned to do for them.
