Jeremiah 18:11 Now go and tell the people of Judah and those living in Jerusalem that God says: "Look, I am planning trouble for you and making a plan against you. So turn away from your bad ways and do what is right."
Jeremiah 18:12 They said, "There is no hope. We will follow our own plans and each of us will act on the evil desires of our heart."
Jeremiah 18:13 So God says, ask the nations, has anyone heard of such a thing: the virgin of Israel has done something very awful.
Jeremiah 18:14 Will a man abandon the snow of Lebanon from the mountain fields? Or will he leave behind the cold, flowing waters from afar?
Jeremiah 18:15 Because my people have forgotten me, they have burned incense to worthless things, causing them to stray from the old paths and walk on unmade ways.
Jeremiah 18:16 To turn their land into ruins, always empty; everyone who goes by will be shocked and shake their head.
Jeremiah 18:17 I will scatter them like an east wind before the enemy; I will show them my back, not my face, on their day of trouble.
Jeremiah 18:18 They said, "Come, let's make plans against Jeremiah, because the teachings won't disappear from the priest, advice won't vanish from the wise, and messages won't stop from the prophet. Come, let's attack him with our words and not listen to anything he says."
Jeremiah 18:19 Listen to me, God, and pay attention to the voices of those who argue against me.
Jeremiah 18:20 Should bad be paid back for good? They have made a trap for me. Remember I spoke to you on their behalf to do them good and to keep your anger from them.
Jeremiah 18:21 So give their children to hunger, and let their blood be spilled by the sword; make their wives lose their children and become widows; and kill their men, let their young men die by the sword in war.
Jeremiah 18:22 Let a shout come from their houses when you bring soldiers suddenly against them, because they have dug a hole to capture me and hidden traps for my feet.
Jeremiah 18:23 God, you know their plans to kill me. Do not forgive their wrongs or erase their sins from your view. Let them fail in your presence when you are angry.

Jeremiah 19:1 God says, "Go and get a clay jar from a potter, and bring some of the elders of the people and some of the senior priests."
Jeremiah 19:2 Go to the Valley of Hinnom, near the entrance of the east gate, and announce the words I will give you.
Jeremiah 19:3 Say, "Listen to God's message, kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem: God of the armies of heaven, the God of Israel, says, 'Look, I will bring disaster on this place, and whoever hears about it will have their ears ring.'"
Jeremiah 19:4 Because they left me and made this place strange, and burned incense here to other gods that neither they, their ancestors, nor Judah's kings knew, and filled this place with innocent blood;
Jeremiah 19:5 They also made high places for Baal, to burn their sons as sacrifices to Baal, something I never commanded or mentioned, nor did it ever cross my mind.
Jeremiah 19:6 So, look, the days are coming, says God, when this place will not be called Tophet or the Valley of Hinnom's son, but the Valley of Slaughter.
Jeremiah 19:7 I will ruin the plans of Judah and Jerusalem here; I will make them die by the sword in front of their enemies, by those who want to kill them: and I will leave their dead bodies as food for the birds in the sky, and for the animals on the land.
Jeremiah 19:8 I will make this city empty and a place for hissing; everyone who passes by will be shocked and hiss at all its disasters.
Jeremiah 19:9 I will make them eat their sons' and daughters' flesh, and they will eat their friends' flesh during the siege and hardship that their enemies and those who want to kill them will cause.
Jeremiah 19:10 Then you will break the bottle while the men with you watch.
Jeremiah 19:11 Tell them, 'This is what God says: Just as a clay pot is smashed and can't be fixed, I will break this nation and this city. They will bury the dead in Tophet until there's no more room to bury them.'
Jeremiah 19:12 I will do this to this place, says God, and to its people, and even make this city like Tophet.
Jeremiah 19:13 The homes in Jerusalem and the homes of Judah's kings will be unclean like Tophet because on their roofs they burned incense to the sky's stars and gave drink offerings to other gods.
Jeremiah 19:14 Jeremiah returned from Tophet, where God had sent him to give his message. He stood in the courtyard of God's house and spoke to all the people.
Jeremiah 19:15 God of Israel says, I will make all the bad things happen to this city and its towns that I said would happen, because they were stubborn and did not listen to my words.

Jeremiah 20:1 Now Pashur, the priest Immer's son and head officer in God's house, heard Jeremiah's prophecies.
Jeremiah 20:2 Then Pashur hit Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks near the upper gate of Benjamin next to God's house.
Jeremiah 20:3 The next day, Pashur released Jeremiah from the stocks. Then Jeremiah told him, "God has not named you Pashur, but Magormissabib."
Jeremiah 20:4 God says, "Look, I will make you a terror to yourself and your friends. They will be killed by their enemies' swords, and you will see it. I will give all Judah to the king of Babylon. He will take them to Babylon as captives and kill them with the sword."
Jeremiah 20:5 I will give all of this city's power, all its hard work, all its valuable things, and all the treasures of Judah's kings to their enemies, who will loot them, take them, and bring them to Babylon.
Jeremiah 20:6 You, Pashur, and everyone in your house will be taken as prisoners. You will go to Babylon, die there, and be buried there, along with all your friends who you told lies to.
Jeremiah 20:7 God, you tricked me, and I got tricked; you are stronger than me, and you have won: every day people laugh at me, everyone makes fun of me.
Jeremiah 20:8 Since I started speaking, I've been shouting about violence and destruction; because God's message has brought me insult and mockery every day.
Jeremiah 20:9 I decided I would not talk about God or speak in his name. But his message burned in my heart like fire, and it tired me to hold it in, and I couldn't keep silent.
Jeremiah 20:10 I heard many insulting me; everyone is afraid. "Tell on him," they say, "and we'll tell too." All my friends are waiting for me to slip, thinking, "Maybe he'll be tricked, then we'll beat him and get back at him."
Jeremiah 20:11 God is with me like a powerful warrior; so those who chase me will trip and not win: they will be deeply embarrassed; they won't succeed: their never-ending disgrace will always be remembered.
Jeremiah 20:12 But, O God of all, who tests the good and sees their deepest thoughts and feelings, let me watch your punishment on them; for I have told you my case.
Jeremiah 20:13 Sing to God, praise God; for he has saved the needy from the hands of wrongdoers.
Jeremiah 20:14 Let the day I was born be cursed; don't let the day my mother gave birth to me be happy.
Jeremiah 20:15 May the man who told my father, "You have a new baby boy," making him very happy, be cursed.
Jeremiah 20:16 Let that person be like the cities that God destroyed without regret, and let him hear crying in the morning and yelling at midday.
Jeremiah 20:17 Because he did not kill me before I was born; or my mother's body could have been my grave, always pregnant with me.
Jeremiah 20:18 Why was I born to experience hard work and sadness, only for my time to end in disgrace?

Jeremiah 21:1 God gave a message to Jeremiah when King Zedekiah sent Pashur, son of Melchiah, and Zephaniah, son of Maaseiah the priest, to him, saying,
Jeremiah 21:2 Please ask God for us, because King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon is attacking us; maybe God will act for us by his amazing works, so that he might leave us alone.
Jeremiah 21:3 Jeremiah told them, "Tell Zedekiah this:
Jeremiah 21:4 God of Israel says, "Look, I will make your weapons of war that you use to fight the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans surrounding you outside the walls useless, and I will gather them inside this city."
Jeremiah 21:5 I will fight against you with a powerful hand, strong arm, and with anger, fury, and great wrath.
Jeremiah 21:6 I will strike down the people and animals in this city; they will die from a terrible disease.
Jeremiah 21:7 After that, God says, I will hand over Zedekiah, the king of Judah, his officials, and the people who remain in the city, protecting them from disease, war, and hunger, to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, their enemies, and those wanting to kill them. He will strike them down with his sword; he will not hold back, feel sorry, or show mercy.
Jeremiah 21:8 Tell these people, "God says, 'Look, I give you the choice of life and the choice of death.'"
Jeremiah 21:9 Anyone who stays in this city will die from war, hunger, and disease, but whoever surrenders to the Chaldeans surrounding you will survive and keep their life safe.
Jeremiah 21:10 I have decided to bring disaster, not good, to this city, says God. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
Jeremiah 21:11 Speak about the house of the king of Judah and say, Listen to God's message.
Jeremiah 21:12 Family of David, this is what God says: Judge fairly every morning, and save those who are being robbed by their oppressors; otherwise, my anger will flare up like fire, and burn with no one to put it out, because of your bad actions.
Jeremiah 21:13 Look, I am against you, valley dweller and plain rock, says God; you ask, "Who will attack us? Who will come into our homes?"
Jeremiah 21:14 I will punish you for what you have done, says God, and I will start a fire in your forest, and it will burn everything around it.

Jeremiah 22:1 God says, "Go to the king of Judah's palace and say this message there.
Jeremiah 22:2 Say, "Listen to God's word, King of Judah, you who sit on David's throne, along with your officials and people who come through these gates."
Jeremiah 22:3 God says; Carry out fair justice and do what is right, and rescue those who have been robbed from their oppressors; and do not harm or be violent to foreigners, orphans, or widows, and do not kill innocent people here.
Jeremiah 22:4 If you really do this, then kings who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses, along with their servants and people.
Jeremiah 22:5 If you don't listen to these words, I promise by myself, says God, that this house will be left empty.
Jeremiah 22:6 God says to the royal house of Judah, "You are like Gilead to me, and like the top of Lebanon. But I will surely turn you into a desert and cities without people."
Jeremiah 22:7 I will send destroyers against you, each with their weapons, and they will chop down your best cedar trees and throw them into the fire.
Jeremiah 22:8 Many countries will pass by this city, and each person will ask their neighbor, why has God done this to this great city?
Jeremiah 22:9 They will answer, 'Because they left the agreement with their God and worshiped and served other gods.'
Jeremiah 22:10 Do not cry for the dead or feel sad for them; but cry hard for the one who is leaving, for they will not come back or see their homeland again.
Jeremiah 22:11 God says about Shallum, son of Josiah, king of Judah, who became king after his father Josiah: He has left this place and will not come back.
Jeremiah 22:12 He will die where he has been taken as a captive and will never see this land again.
Jeremiah 22:13 Pity the one who builds his house by unfair means and his rooms by injustice; who makes his neighbor work for free and does not pay him for his labor.
Jeremiah 22:14 Someone says, "I will build myself a big house with spacious rooms, put in windows, line it with cedar wood, and paint it bright red."
Jeremiah 22:15 Will you be king because you surround yourself with cedar? Didn't your father eat, drink, and carry out fair judgment and justice, and then things went well for him?
Jeremiah 22:16 He decided justly for the poor and needy; this brought goodness: isn't this knowing me? says God.
Jeremiah 22:17 Your eyes and heart only want to take things, kill the innocent, oppress, and be violent.
Jeremiah 22:18 So this is what God says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: No one will mourn for him, saying, "Oh, my brother!" or "Oh, my sister!" No one will mourn for him, saying, "Oh, master!" or "Oh, his greatness!"
Jeremiah 22:19 He will be buried like a donkey, dragged away and thrown out beyond Jerusalem's gates.
Jeremiah 22:20 Go to Lebanon and shout; raise your voice in Bashan, and call out from the crossings, because all your friends are ruined.
Jeremiah 22:21 I spoke to you when you were doing well, but you said you wouldn't listen. This has been your way since you were young, not obeying my voice.
Jeremiah 22:22 The wind will destroy all your shepherds, and your friends will be taken away; then you will feel ashamed and embarrassed because of all your evil.
Jeremiah 22:23 You who live in Lebanon and build your nest in the cedar trees, how will you plead for mercy when pain comes, like the pain of a woman giving birth?
Jeremiah 22:24 I swear, says God, even if Coniah son of King Jehoiakim of Judah were like a ring on my right hand, I would still pull you off.
Jeremiah 22:25 I will hand you over to those who want to kill you, to those you are afraid of, to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 22:26 I will throw you and your mother who gave birth to you out to another country where you were not born, and there you will die.
Jeremiah 22:27 But they will not go back to the land they want to return to.
Jeremiah 22:28 Is Coniah a hated, shattered statue? Is he a container that brings no joy? Why are he and his descendants thrown out and sent to a land they do not know?
Jeremiah 22:29 Earth, earth, earth, listen to God's message.
Jeremiah 22:30 God says, "Mark this man as childless, a man who will not succeed in his lifetime: because none of his descendants will succeed, sitting on David's throne or ruling in Judah anymore."

Jeremiah 23:1 God says, "Trouble will come to the leaders who ruin and disperse the sheep of my land!"
Jeremiah 23:2 So this is what God of Israel says to the leaders who take care of my people: You have scattered my sheep and made them run away, and you did not care for them. Look, I will punish you for the bad things you've done, says God.
Jeremiah 23:3 I will bring the remaining ones of my flock from all the countries where I sent them, and they will return to their homes; they will have many children and grow in number.
Jeremiah 23:4 I will put shepherds in charge of them who will take care of them; they will not be afraid or discouraged or be in need anymore, says God.
Jeremiah 23:5 Look, the time will come, God says, when I will bring forth a righteous descendant from David, and a King will rule successfully, carrying out fair and just decisions on the earth.
Jeremiah 23:6 During his time, Judah will be saved and Israel will live in safety. And he will be called God Our Righteousness.
Jeremiah 23:7 So, God says, "Look, the time is coming when people won't say anymore, 'God is alive, who brought the Israelites out of Egypt.'"
Jeremiah 23:8 But God lives, who brought and led the descendants of Israel out of the north and from all countries where I had sent them; and they will live in their own land.
Jeremiah 23:9 My heart is broken because of the prophets; my whole body trembles; I am like a drunk man, beaten by wine, because of God and his holy words.
Jeremiah 23:10 The land is full of cheaters; because of cursing, the land is sad; the nice parts of the desert have dried out, people's actions are bad, and their power is not used rightly.
Jeremiah 23:11 Both the prophet and the priest are unholy; yes, I have seen their evil in my house, says God.
Jeremiah 23:12 So their path will be like slippery roads in the dark: they will be pushed and will fall on it, because I will bring disaster on them, the time when I punish them, says God.
Jeremiah 23:13 I have seen foolishness in Samaria's prophets; they spoke messages from Baal and led my people Israel astray.
Jeremiah 23:14 I have also seen terrible things among Jerusalem's prophets: they are unfaithful and live in lies; they encourage the wicked so no one turns from their evil ways; to me, they are like Sodom and its people like Gomorrah.
Jeremiah 23:15 So this is what God says about the prophets: I will give them bitter food to eat and poison water to drink, because the prophets of Jerusalem have spread corruption throughout the land.
Jeremiah 23:16 God says, "Don't listen to the prophets who speak to you; they fill you with false hopes. They talk about visions from their own minds, not from God."
Jeremiah 23:17 They keep telling those who hate me, "God has said, you will have peace"; and they tell everyone who follows their own desires, "No harm will come to you."
Jeremiah 23:18 Who has been in God's council and understood and listened to his message? Who has paid attention to his message and heard it?
Jeremiah 23:19 Look, a violent storm from God has come out in anger, a terrible storm: it will hit the wicked very hard.
Jeremiah 23:20 God's anger will not stop until He has done what He plans. In the future, you will fully understand this.
Jeremiah 23:21 I did not send these prophets, but they went; I did not speak to them, but they spoke my message.
Jeremiah 23:22 If they had followed my advice and had made my people listen to my words, then they would have turned away from their bad behavior and their wicked actions.
Jeremiah 23:23 Am I not a close God, says God, and not a distant one?
Jeremiah 23:24 Can anyone hide in secret places where I won't see him? says God. Don't I fill heaven and earth? says God.
Jeremiah 23:25 I have heard the prophets who tell lies in my name, saying, "I had a dream, I had a dream."
Jeremiah 23:26 How long will the prophets who tell lies plan this in their hearts? Yes, they are prophets led by their own deceit.
Jeremiah 23:27 They try to make my people forget my name with the dreams they share with each other, just like their ancestors forgot my name for Baal.
Jeremiah 23:28 The prophet who has a dream should share that dream; and whoever has my message should speak it truthfully. What do the worthless bits matter compared to the grain? says God.
Jeremiah 23:29 Isn't my word like a fire? says God, and like a hammer that breaks the rock into pieces?
Jeremiah 23:30 So, I am against the prophets who take my words from each other, says God.
Jeremiah 23:31 Look, I am against the prophets, says God, who speak on their own and claim, 'God says.'
Jeremiah 23:32 Look, I am against those who tell false dreams, says God, and share them, leading my people astray with their lies and carelessness; I did not send them or tell them to do this: so they will not help my people at all, says God.
Jeremiah 23:33 When the people, a prophet, or a priest ask you, "What is God's message?" You should say, "What message? God says He will abandon you."
Jeremiah 23:34 If a prophet, a priest, or anyone else claims, "This is God's message," I will punish that person and his family.
Jeremiah 23:35 Everyone should ask their neighbor and their brother, "What has God answered?" and "What has God said?"
Jeremiah 23:36 You should not talk about God's burden anymore: everyone's own words will be their burden because you have twisted the words of the living God, our God of all.
Jeremiah 23:37 You should ask the prophet, "What has God replied to you?" and "What has God said?"
Jeremiah 23:38 Since you say, "God's message," this is what God says: "Because you call it 'God's message,' even though I told you not to call it 'God's message,'"
Jeremiah 23:39 So, look, I myself will completely forget you, and I will leave you, and the city I gave to you and your ancestors, and I will throw you out of my sight.
Jeremiah 23:40 I will make you suffer lasting shame and disgrace that will never be forgotten.

Jeremiah 24:1 God showed me two baskets of figs in front of the temple. This was after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon took away Jeconiah, son of King Jehoiakim of Judah, the Judah leaders, carpenters, and metalworkers from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Jeremiah 24:2 One basket had very good figs, just like the first ripe ones, and the other basket had very bad figs that could not be eaten because they were so bad.
Jeremiah 24:3 Then God asked me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "Figs; the good ones are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, so bad they can't be eaten."
Jeremiah 24:4 God spoke to me again, saying,
Jeremiah 24:5 God, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, I will recognize the people from Judah that I have sent away as captives to the land of the Chaldeans for their own good.
Jeremiah 24:6 I will watch over them for their good and bring them back to this land. I will rebuild them and not tear them down. I will plant them and not uproot them.
Jeremiah 24:7 I will give them a heart to know me, that I am God; they will be my people, and I will be their God because they will come back to me with all their heart.
Jeremiah 24:8 Like the bad figs that are too rotten to eat, this is what God says: I will do the same to Zedekiah king of Judah, his leaders, the rest of Jerusalem who stay in this land, and those living in Egypt.
Jeremiah 24:9 I will let them be taken to all the kingdoms of the earth to their harm, to be mocked and used in sayings, to be insulted and cursed, wherever I send them.
Jeremiah 24:10 I will send war, hunger, and disease among them until they are wiped from the land I gave to them and their ancestors.

Jeremiah 25:1 God's message came to Jeremiah about all the Judah people in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 25:2 Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to everyone in Jerusalem, saying,
Jeremiah 25:3 Since the thirteenth year of King Josiah of Judah until now, which is twenty-three years, God has been giving me messages, and I have been telling you them early and often, but you have not listened.
Jeremiah 25:4 God has sent you all his messengers, the prophets, arising early and sending them; but you have not listened or paid attention to hear.
Jeremiah 25:5 They said, "Everyone turn from your bad ways and stop doing wrong, then live in the land that God gave you and your ancestors forever."
Jeremiah 25:6 Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them, and do not make me angry with what you do; then I will not harm you.
Jeremiah 25:7 But you have not listened to me, says God; you made me angry with what you have done, which will hurt yourselves.
Jeremiah 25:8 So God Almighty says, "Because you did not listen to my words,"
Jeremiah 25:9 Look, I will send for all the families from the north and for Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant. I will bring them against this land and its people, as well as all the surrounding nations. I will completely wipe them out, make them shocking to see, a target for hissing, and ruin them forever.
Jeremiah 25:10 I will remove their sounds of joy and happiness, the bridegroom and bride's voices, the noise of the mill, and the candle's light.
Jeremiah 25:11 This entire land will become a wasteland and a shock, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
Jeremiah 25:12 When seventy years have passed, I will punish the king of Babylon and their nation, says God, for their wrongs, and the land of the Chaldeans will be forever deserted.
Jeremiah 25:13 I will bring all my words that I have spoken against that land to pass, including everything written in this book that Jeremiah has predicted against all the nations.
Jeremiah 25:14 Many nations and powerful kings will use them for their own purposes, and God will repay them based on their actions and the work of their hands.
Jeremiah 25:15 God of Israel told me to take the cup of anger from His hand and make all the countries I send you to, drink from it.
Jeremiah 25:16 They will drink, stagger, and go crazy because of the sword I will send among them.
Jeremiah 25:17 I took the cup from God's hand and made all the nations drink it, to whom God had sent me.
Jeremiah 25:18 This means Jerusalem, the towns in Judah, their kings, and leaders, to turn them into ruins, something shocking, scorned, and cursed, as they are now.
Jeremiah 25:19 Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt, his officials, his leaders, and all his citizens;
Jeremiah 25:20 All the mixed people, and all the kings of Uz, and all the kings of the Philistine lands, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remaining people of Ashdod,
Jeremiah 25:21 Edom, Moab, and the children of Ammon.
Jeremiah 25:22 All the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the islands across the sea,
Jeremiah 25:23 Dedan, Tema, Buz, and everyone in the farthest places,
Jeremiah 25:24 All the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed people living in the desert,
Jeremiah 25:25 Every king of Zimri, every king of Elam, and every king of the Medes,
Jeremiah 25:26 All the northern kings, from far and close, and every kingdom on earth will drink, and then the king of Sheshach will drink too.
Jeremiah 25:27 Tell them this: God of the armies, the God of Israel, says, "Drink and get drunk, vomit, fall, and don't get up because of the sword I will bring upon you."
Jeremiah 25:28 If they won't take the cup from your hand to drink, then tell them, "God says you will surely drink."
Jeremiah 25:29 Look, I am starting to bring trouble to the city known by my name, and do you think you will go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, because I will send destruction upon all the people of the world, says God.
Jeremiah 25:30 So, speak against them all these words and tell them: God will roar from above and speak from his holy place; he will roar loudly over his home; he will shout like those who crush grapes, against everyone on earth.
Jeremiah 25:31 A sound will be heard across the world; God has a dispute with the countries, he will argue with everyone; he will let the sword kill the wicked, says God.
Jeremiah 25:32 God says, "Look, evil will spread from country to country, and a big storm will come from the edges of the earth."
Jeremiah 25:33 On that day, those God has killed will be scattered from one end of the earth to the other. They won't be mourned or collected or buried; they will be like manure on the soil.
Jeremiah 25:34 Cry out, you leaders of the flock, and weep; roll in the ashes, you important ones, because the time of your defeat and scattering is here; and you will break like a fine vase.
Jeremiah 25:35 The shepherds won't be able to run away, and the leader of the sheep won't be able to escape.
Jeremiah 25:36 Shepherds will cry out, and the leaders of the flock will wail because God has ruined their grazing land.
Jeremiah 25:37 And the peaceful homes are destroyed because of God's intense anger.
Jeremiah 25:38 He has abandoned his hiding place like a lion, because their land is ruined due to the cruel enemy's violence and fierce anger.

Jeremiah 26:1 At the start of Jehoiakim's rule, the son of King Josiah of Judah, God sent this message:
Jeremiah 26:2 God says, "Stand in the yard of God's house, and talk to all the people from the towns of Judah who come to worship in God's house. Tell them everything I tell you to say; don't leave out a single word."
Jeremiah 26:3 If they listen and each person stops doing bad things, then I will change my mind about the punishment I planned for them because of their bad actions.
Jeremiah 26:4 Tell them this: If you don't listen to me and follow the laws I've given you, God says.
Jeremiah 26:5 Listen to my prophets' words that I sent to you, waking them early and sending them, but you did not listen.
Jeremiah 26:6 I will make this house like Shiloh and will make this city a curse to all the countries of the world.
Jeremiah 26:7 The priests, prophets, and everyone heard Jeremiah say these things in God's house.
Jeremiah 26:8 When Jeremiah finished telling the people everything God had commanded him to say, the priests, prophets, and everyone there grabbed him and said, "You will certainly die."
Jeremiah 26:9 Why did you prophesy in God's name, saying, "This place will be like Shiloh, and this city will be empty with no one living here?" And all the people turned against Jeremiah in God's house.
Jeremiah 26:10 When the leaders of Judah heard this news, they went up from the king's palace to God's house and sat at the entrance of the new gate of God's house.
Jeremiah 26:11 The priests and prophets told the leaders and everyone, "This man should be put to death because he spoke against our city, as you all heard."
Jeremiah 26:12 Jeremiah spoke to all the leaders and the people, saying, "God sent me to tell about the coming trouble for this place and this city, all the things you have heard.
Jeremiah 26:13 So now change how you live and act, and listen to God's voice; then God will change his mind about the harm he said he would do to you.
Jeremiah 26:14 As for me, I am in your power: do to me what you think is good and right.
Jeremiah 26:15 But be sure, if you kill me, you will bring innocent blood on yourselves, on this city, and on its people, because God truly sent me to tell you all these things.
Jeremiah 26:16 Then the leaders and all the people said to the priests and prophets, "This man should not be put to death, for he has spoken to us in the name of our God."
Jeremiah 26:17 Some elders stood up and spoke to all the people gathered, saying,
Jeremiah 26:18 Micah, from Moresheth, told God's message when Hezekiah was king of Judah. He said to Judah's people: "God says, 'Zion will be farmed like a field, Jerusalem will turn into piles of rubble, and the Temple hill will be like overgrown hills in the woods.'"
Jeremiah 26:19 Did King Hezekiah of Judah and all of Judah kill him? Didn't he respect God, ask for God's mercy, and God changed his mind about the bad things he said he would do to them? We could bring a lot of trouble on ourselves this way.
Jeremiah 26:20 A man named Urijah, Shemaiah's son from Kirjathjearim, also spoke for God. He said the same things against this city and land as Jeremiah did.
Jeremiah 26:21 When King Jehoiakim, his strong soldiers, and all the leaders heard the prophet's words, the king wanted to kill him. But Urijah became scared when he heard this, ran away, and escaped to Egypt.
Jeremiah 26:22 King Jehoiakim sent Elnathan, the son of Achbor, and some other men to Egypt.
Jeremiah 26:23 They took Urijah from Egypt and brought him to King Jehoiakim, who killed him with a sword and threw his body into the burial place of the ordinary people.
Jeremiah 26:24 Ahikam son of Shaphan helped Jeremiah so that no one handed him over to the people to kill him.

Jeremiah 27:1 At the start of Jehoiakim's rule, Josiah's son and king of Judah, God gave this message to Jeremiah:
Jeremiah 27:2 God told me, "Make ties and yokes, and put them on your neck."
Jeremiah 27:3 Send them to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre, and the king of Sidon, through the messengers who come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah, king of Judah.
Jeremiah 27:4 Tell your masters this message from God, the God of Israel: This is what you should say to your masters;
Jeremiah 27:5 I have created the earth, people, and animals on the ground with my great power and strong arm, and I have given it to those who I thought should have it.
Jeremiah 27:6 I have now given all these lands to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, my servant; I have also given him the animals of the field to serve him.
Jeremiah 27:7 All countries will serve him, his son, and his grandson until the time for his own country comes; then many countries and powerful kings will take advantage of him.
Jeremiah 27:8 Any nation or kingdom that doesn't serve King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon or refuses to submit to him, God will punish with war, hunger, and disease until they are destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar.
Jeremiah 27:9 So don't listen to your prophets, fortune tellers, dream interpreters, magicians, or spell casters who tell you that you won't have to serve the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 27:10 They are lying to you when they say I will force you from your land and you will die.
Jeremiah 27:11 But the countries that accept the rule of the king of Babylon and serve him, I will let them stay in their land, says God; they will farm it and live there.
Jeremiah 27:12 I also spoke to Zedekiah, the king of Judah, with all these words, saying, "Put your necks under the control of the king of Babylon, serve him and his people, and you will live."
Jeremiah 27:13 Why do you and your people want to die by the sword, hunger, and disease, just as God has said would happen to the nation that refuses to serve the king of Babylon?
Jeremiah 27:14 Do not listen to the prophets who tell you, "You do not have to serve the king of Babylon." They are lying to you.
Jeremiah 27:15 God says, "I did not send them, but they tell lies in my name. They do this so you will be forced away and destroyed, along with the prophets who are misleading you."
Jeremiah 27:16 I also told the priests and the people this message from God: "Don't listen to your prophets who say, 'Soon the items from God's house will be brought back from Babylon.' They are lying to you.
Jeremiah 27:17 Don't listen to them; serve the king of Babylon and live. Why should this city be destroyed?
Jeremiah 27:18 But if they are prophets, and if God’s word is with them, let them now pray to God so that the things left in God's house, the king of Judah's house, and in Jerusalem do not go to Babylon.
Jeremiah 27:19 God says this about the pillars, the large water basin, the stands, and the rest of the items left in this city.
Jeremiah 27:20 When Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take them, while he took Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah and all the important people of Judah and Jerusalem as prisoners from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Jeremiah 27:21 Yes, this is what God says about the items left in God's house, and in the palace of Judah's king and Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 27:22 They will be taken to Babylon and will stay there until I decide to bring them back, says God; then I will take them out and return them to this place.

Jeremiah 28:1 That year, when Zedekiah started ruling Judah, in the fourth year, fifth month, the prophet Hananiah, Azur's son from Gibeon, spoke to me in God's house with priests and everyone there, saying,
Jeremiah 28:2 God of Israel says, I have broken the power of the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 28:3 In two years, I will bring back to this place all the items from God's house that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon took away and moved to Babylon.
Jeremiah 28:4 I will bring Jeconiah, son of King Jehoiakim of Judah, and all the Judah captives back from Babylon, says God; for I will break the power of the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 28:5 Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah where the priests and all the people in God's house could hear.
Jeremiah 28:6 The prophet Jeremiah agreed, saying, "Yes, let it happen: may God do this: may God make true what you have predicted, to return the items of God's house, and everyone taken as prisoners, from Babylon to this place."
Jeremiah 28:7 Please listen to this message that I am saying to you and to everyone.
Jeremiah 28:8 Prophets before us long ago spoke against many nations and large kingdoms about war, evil, and disease.
Jeremiah 28:9 The prophet who predicts peace will be recognized as truly sent by God when his prophecy comes true.
Jeremiah 28:10 Then Hananiah the prophet took the wooden bar from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it.
Jeremiah 28:11 Hananiah said to everyone, "This is what God says: 'I will break Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king's, control from all countries in two years.'" And the prophet Jeremiah left.
Jeremiah 28:12 God spoke to the prophet Jeremiah after Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke from Jeremiah's neck, saying,
Jeremiah 28:13 Go and tell Hananiah, 'God says, "You have broken the wooden yokes; now you will make iron yokes to replace them."'
Jeremiah 28:14 God says, "I have put an iron yoke on the necks of all these nations so they will serve Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, and they will serve him. I have also given him the animals of the fields."
Jeremiah 28:15 The prophet Jeremiah said to Hananiah, "Listen, Hananiah, God did not send you; you are making these people believe a lie."
Jeremiah 28:16 So God says, "Look, I will throw you off the earth. This year you will die because you have taught rebellion against God."
Jeremiah 28:17 The prophet Hananiah died that year in the seventh month.

Jeremiah 29:1 This is the message from the letter that the prophet Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the remaining elders who were taken as captives, and to the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem to Babylon as prisoners.
Jeremiah 29:2 After Jeconiah the king, the queen, the officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the carpenters, and the metalworkers left Jerusalem;
Jeremiah 29:3 Through Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, (sent by Zedekiah king of Judah to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon) it said,
Jeremiah 29:4 God, the ruler of all, the God of Israel, says to everyone who was taken as prisoners – whom I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Jeremiah 29:5 Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Jeremiah 29:6 Marry and have sons and daughters; find wives for your sons, and give your daughters to men, so they too can have sons and daughters; this way you will grow in number there, not become fewer.
Jeremiah 29:7 Look for the good of the city where I have sent you as prisoners, and pray to God for it, because if it has peace, you will have peace too.
Jeremiah 29:8 God, the God of Israel, says: Don't let the prophets and fortune-tellers among you trick you, and don't listen to the dreams you encourage them to have.
Jeremiah 29:9 They are falsely claiming to speak for me; I did not send them, says God.
Jeremiah 29:10 God says that after seventy years in Babylon, I will come to see you and make my promise come true by bringing you back here.
Jeremiah 29:11 I know the plans I have for you, says God, plans for peace and not for harm, to give you a hopeful future.
Jeremiah 29:12 You will call to me, go and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
Jeremiah 29:13 You will look for me and find me when you search for me with all your heart.
Jeremiah 29:14 I will let you find me, says God. I will end your captivity and bring you together from all the nations and places where I sent you, says God. I will take you back to where you were taken from.
Jeremiah 29:15 Because you have said, "God has given us prophets in Babylon."
Jeremiah 29:16 Understand that this is what God says about the king sitting on David's throne, about all the people living in this city, and about your relatives who have not been taken away with you as captives.
Jeremiah 29:17 God says: I will send them war, hunger, and disease, and I will make them like bad figs that are so rotten they can't be eaten.
Jeremiah 29:18 I will chase them with war, hunger, and disease, and will make them be scattered to all kingdoms of the earth, to become a curse, a shock, and an object of scorn among all the nations where I have sent them.
Jeremiah 29:19 Because they did not listen to my words, says God, which I sent to them through my prophets, who I sent early and often, but you did not want to listen, says God.
Jeremiah 29:20 Listen to God's message, all of you who were taken from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Jeremiah 29:21 God, the God of Israel, says this about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who tell lies in my name: I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them while you watch.
Jeremiah 29:22 People from Judah who are captives in Babylon will use this curse, saying, "May God make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire."
Jeremiah 29:23 They have done bad things in Israel, been unfaithful with their neighbors' wives, and lied using my name, which I never told them to do. I know and am a witness, says God.
Jeremiah 29:24 You should also tell Shemaiah from Nehelam:
Jeremiah 29:25 God of Israel says, because you sent letters in your name to everyone in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,
Jeremiah 29:26 God has made you priest instead of Jehoiada the priest, so you can be an officer in God's house. If anyone acts crazy and claims to be a prophet, you must put him in jail and in restraints.
Jeremiah 29:27 So why haven't you corrected Jeremiah from Anathoth, who claims to be a prophet to you?
Jeremiah 29:28 So he sent a message to us in Babylon, saying, "This captivity will last a long time: build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit."
Jeremiah 29:29 The priest Zephaniah read the letter to the prophet Jeremiah.
Jeremiah 29:30 God spoke to Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 29:31 Tell all the captives, "God says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Since Shemaiah has been prophesying to you without being sent by me and has made you believe a lie:
Jeremiah 29:32 So God says, "Look, I will punish Shemaiah from Nehelam and his descendants. He will not have a family member to live among the people, nor will he see the good things I will do for my people, says God, because he encouraged rebellion against me."

Jeremiah 30:1 God gave a message to Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 30:2 God of Israel says, "Write down all the words I have told you in a book."
Jeremiah 30:3 Look, the time is coming, says God, when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says God. I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they will own it.
Jeremiah 30:4 Here are the words that God said about Israel and Judah.
Jeremiah 30:5 God says, "We have heard a voice shaking, scared, and not peaceful."
Jeremiah 30:6 Ask now, can a man have a baby? Why do I see every man with his hands on his hips like a woman in labor, with every face turned pale?
Jeremiah 30:7 Oh no! That day will be terrible; there's no other day like it. It's going to be a time of great trouble for Jacob, but he will be rescued from it.
Jeremiah 30:8 On that day, God says, I will remove the yoke from your neck and break your chains, so that strangers will no longer use you for their own gain.
Jeremiah 30:9 But they will serve their God, and their king David, whom I will bring to them.
Jeremiah 30:10 So don't be afraid, my servant Jacob, says God; nor be scared, Israel. Look, I will rescue you from far away, and your descendants from the land where they are captives. Jacob will come back, be at peace, be calm, and no one will frighten him.
Jeremiah 30:11 I am with you, says God, to save you. Even if I completely destroy all the nations where I dispersed you, I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you fairly but will not let you go unpunished.
Jeremiah 30:12 God says your injury has no cure, and your wound is very serious.
Jeremiah 30:13 No one is there to argue for you so you can be healed; you have no medicine to make you better.
Jeremiah 30:14 All your friends have forgotten you; they don't look for you; because I have hurt you like an enemy, with harsh punishment, due to your many sins, which grew too much.
Jeremiah 30:15 Why are you crying about your pain? Your sadness can't be healed because you've done so many wrong things: since you kept sinning, I let this happen to you.
Jeremiah 30:16 So, everyone who eats you up will be eaten; and all your enemies will be captured; those who rob you will be robbed, and all who attack you, I will give as victims.
Jeremiah 30:17 I will make you healthy again and heal your injuries, God says, because they called you an Outcast, saying, "This is Zion, whom no one cares for."
Jeremiah 30:18 God says, "Look, I will bring back the people to Jacob's tents and be kind to their homes. The city will be rebuilt on its ruins, and the palace will stand as it used to."
Jeremiah 30:19 From them will come thanksgiving and joyful voices. I will increase their number, they won't be few; I will honor them, and they won't be unimportant.
Jeremiah 30:20 Their children will be like before, and their community will be secure with me. I will punish all who oppress them.
Jeremiah 30:21 Their leaders will come from among them, and their ruler will rise from their midst; I will bring him close, and he will come to me. Who is the one who devoted himself to come to me? says God.
Jeremiah 30:22 You will be my people, and I will be your God.
Jeremiah 30:23 Look, God's strong wind blows with anger, never stopping; it will come down harshly on the wicked.
Jeremiah 30:24 God's intense anger will not stop until he has finished his work and carried out the plans of his heart. In the future, you will think about this.

Jeremiah 31:1 At that time, says God, I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be my people.
Jeremiah 31:2 God says, "The people saved from the sword found kindness in the desert; this happened to Israel when I led them to a place of rest."
Jeremiah 31:3 God showed himself to me long ago and said, "Yes, I have loved you forever; that's why I've brought you close with kindness."
Jeremiah 31:4 I will rebuild you, and you will be rebuilt, O Israel, young and pure. You will wear your tambourines again and dance with joy.
Jeremiah 31:5 You will plant grapevines again on the mountains of Samaria: the people who plant them will eat the grapes like ordinary food.
Jeremiah 31:6 A day will come when the guards on Mount Ephraim will shout, "Get up, let's go to Zion to our God."
Jeremiah 31:7 God says, "Sing with joy for Jacob, and shout among the leaders of the nations. Share the news, praise, and say, 'God, save your people, the remaining ones of Israel.'"
Jeremiah 31:8 Look, I will bring them from the north and gather them from the ends of the earth. Along with them will be the blind and the lame, pregnant women, and those giving birth. A large crowd will come back here.
Jeremiah 31:9 They will come crying, and I will guide them with their prayers. I will lead them along paths beside flowing waters, on a straight road where they won't trip, because I am Israel's father, and Ephraim is my oldest child.
Jeremiah 31:10 Listen to God's message, all countries, and announce it on distant islands, saying, "He who spread out Israel will bring them back and watch over them like a shepherd with his sheep."
Jeremiah 31:11 God has saved Jacob and rescued him from someone stronger than him.
Jeremiah 31:12 So they will come and sing on the heights of Zion, and gather to enjoy God's blessings – for grain, wine, oil, and the young of sheep and cattle. Their lives will be like a well-watered garden; they will never grieve again.
Jeremiah 31:13 The young woman will be happy dancing, and young and old men will join her: I will change their sadness to happiness, comfort them, and help them find joy instead of their grief.
Jeremiah 31:14 I will satisfy the priests with rich food, and my people will be content with my kindness, says God.
Jeremiah 31:15 God says: A sound was heard in Ramah, crying and loud sorrow; Rachel cried for her children and would not be comforted for her children because they were gone.
Jeremiah 31:16 God says, "Stop crying and wipe your tears away, because your efforts will be rewarded by God; and they will return from the enemy's land."
Jeremiah 31:17 God says you have hope for the future; your children will return to their own land.
Jeremiah 31:18 I have certainly heard Ephraim feeling sorry for himself, saying, "You have disciplined me, and I've learned my lesson, like a young cow not used to the yoke. Help me change, and I will change, because you are my God."
Jeremiah 31:19 After I turned back, I was sorry; after I understood, I hit my thigh in grief. I was ashamed and embarrassed because I carried the shame of my young mistakes.
Jeremiah 31:20 Is Ephraim my dear son? Is he a delightful child? Because after I spoke against him, I still remember him fondly. So, I am deeply moved for him; I will definitely show him mercy, says God.
Jeremiah 31:21 Set up signs for yourself, make tall piles of stones; keep your thoughts on the main road, the path you traveled. Come back, Israel's young woman, come back to your towns.
Jeremiah 31:22 How long will you wander, O disloyal daughter? For God has made something new on earth: a woman will embrace a man.
Jeremiah 31:23 God, the ruler of all, the God of Israel, says: People will still use this language in Judah and its cities when I turn their fortunes around. God bless you, home of justice and holy mountain.
Jeremiah 31:24 Farmers and people who care for flocks will live in Judah and all its cities.
Jeremiah 31:25 I have satisfied the tired person, and I have filled up every sad person.
Jeremiah 31:26 I woke up, looked around, and my sleep had been pleasant to me.
Jeremiah 31:27 Look, the time will come, says God, that I will fill the people of Israel and Judah with many people and animals.
Jeremiah 31:28 It will happen that just as I have watched over them to uproot, break down, throw away, destroy, and hurt, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, says God.
Jeremiah 31:29 In those days, people will no longer say, "The parents ate sour grapes, and now the children's teeth feel rough."
Jeremiah 31:30 Everyone will die for their own wrongs: anyone who eats sour grapes will feel the effect on their teeth.
Jeremiah 31:31 Look, the time will come, says God, when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah.
Jeremiah 31:32 This is not like the promise I made with their ancestors when I led them by the hand out of Egypt; they broke my promise even though I was like a husband to them, says God.
Jeremiah 31:33 This is the promise I will make with Israel's people: After that time, says God, I will put my rules deep inside them, write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Jeremiah 31:34 People will no longer teach their neighbors or their brothers to know God, because everyone from the least to the greatest will know me, since I will forgive their wrongs and never remember their sins again.
Jeremiah 31:35 God says, "I give the sun for light during the day, and the moon and stars for light at night. I stir up the sea to make its waves roar. My name is God of all."
Jeremiah 31:36 If those rules leave my presence, says God, then Israel’s descendants will no longer be a nation before me forever.
Jeremiah 31:37 God says, "If the sky above can be measured and the earth's foundations explored, then I will reject all of Israel's descendants for what they have done," says God.
Jeremiah 31:38 Look, the time will come, God says, that the city will be rebuilt for God from Hananeel Tower to the Corner Gate.
Jeremiah 31:39 The measuring line will still stretch out facing it, on the hill Gareb, and will go around to Goath.
Jeremiah 31:40 The entire valley where dead bodies and ashes are, and all the land to Kidron stream, to the east by the Horse Gate, will be sacred to God; it will never be destroyed or disturbed again.

Jeremiah 32:1 The message that came to Jeremiah from God in the tenth year of Zedekiah, the king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
Jeremiah 32:2 At that time, the Babylonian king's army surrounded Jerusalem, and the prophet Jeremiah was confined in the prison yard inside the king of Judah's palace.
Jeremiah 32:3 King Zedekiah of Judah had imprisoned him, asking, "Why do you prophesy and say, 'God declares, I will give this city to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it'"?
Jeremiah 32:4 Zedekiah, the king of Judah, will not escape from the Chaldeans. He will definitely be given to the king of Babylon. They will talk face to face, and they will look into each other's eyes.
Jeremiah 32:5 God will take Zedekiah to Babylon, where he will stay until I deal with him, says God. Even if you battle the Chaldeans, you will not succeed.
Jeremiah 32:6 Jeremiah said, God spoke to me, saying,
Jeremiah 32:7 Look, your uncle Shallum's son Hanameel will come to you and say, "Buy my field in Anathoth: you have the right to buy it back."
Jeremiah 32:8 So my cousin Hanameel came to me in the prison yard, just as God had said he would, and he told me, "Please buy my field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, because you have the right to inherit it and to buy it back. Buy it for yourself." Then I understood that this was truly from God.
Jeremiah 32:9 I bought the field from Hanameel, my cousin in Anathoth, and paid him the money, exactly 17 silver shekels.
Jeremiah 32:10 I signed the document, sealed it, had witnesses watch, and weighed the money on the scales.
Jeremiah 32:11 I took the proof of my purchase, the sealed documents as required by law, and the unsealed copies.
Jeremiah 32:12 I gave the purchase papers to Baruch, Neriah's son and Maaseiah's grandson, in front of my cousin Hanameel and the witnesses who signed the papers, with all the Jews in the prison courtyard watching.
Jeremiah 32:13 I gave Baruch orders in front of them, saying,
Jeremiah 32:14 God of Israel says, "Take these documents, the sealed and unsealed copies of the property sale, and place them in a clay jar so they will last a long time."
Jeremiah 32:15 God, the ruler of everything, says; People will again own houses, land, and vineyards in this place.
Jeremiah 32:16 After giving Baruch son of Neriah the purchase papers, I prayed to God, saying,
Jeremiah 32:17 Oh God, you have created the sky and the earth with your great power and outstretched arm, and nothing is too difficult for you.
Jeremiah 32:18 You show love to thousands, but bring the fathers' sins onto their children: the Great and Mighty God, God of all, is his name.
Jeremiah 32:19 God is wise in planning and powerful in action: for your eyes see all that humans do: to reward everyone based on their actions and the outcomes of their behavior.
Jeremiah 32:20 You have shown signs and wonders in Egypt to this day, in Israel, and among all people, making a great name for yourself, as seen today.
Jeremiah 32:21 You brought your people Israel out of Egypt with miracles, amazing acts, strong power, an extended arm, and great fear.
Jeremiah 32:22 You gave them this land, which you promised their ancestors, a land filled with milk and honey.
Jeremiah 32:23 They came and took the land, but did not listen to you or follow your laws. They did none of what you told them to do, so you have brought all this trouble on them.
Jeremiah 32:24 Look at the hills, they have come to capture the city; and the city has been handed over to the Chaldeans who are attacking it, because of war, hunger, and disease. What you have said has happened, and you see it.
Jeremiah 32:25 You told me, God, "Buy the field with money and get witnesses, because the city will be handed over to the Chaldeans."
Jeremiah 32:26 God spoke to Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 32:27 Look, I am God, the God of everyone: is anything too difficult for me?
Jeremiah 32:28 So God says, "Look, I will give this city to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, and he will capture it."
Jeremiah 32:29 The Chaldeans fighting this city will come, set it on fire, and burn it along with the houses where they burned incense to Baal on the roofs and offered drinks to other gods, making me angry.
Jeremiah 32:30 The children of Israel and Judah have been doing bad things before me since they were young; they have made me angry by what they do, says God.
Jeremiah 32:31 This city has made me angry and furious since the day it was built, until now; so I want to get rid of it.
Jeremiah 32:32 Because of all the bad things the people of Israel and Judah have done, making me angry, including their kings, leaders, priests, prophets, the men of Judah, and the people of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 32:33 They've turned their backs on me, not their faces. Even though I taught them early and kept teaching, they did not listen to learn.
Jeremiah 32:34 They put their disgusting idols in the house named after me, to make it unclean.
Jeremiah 32:35 They made altars for Baal in the valley of Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters as offerings to Molech; something I did not command, nor did I think they would do such a horrible thing and make Judah sin.
Jeremiah 32:36 So now, God, the God of Israel, says this about the city you claim will be given to the king of Babylon through war, hunger, and disease:
Jeremiah 32:37 Look, I will bring them back from all the countries where I sent them in my anger, fury, and great wrath; I will return them to this place and they will live in safety.
Jeremiah 32:38 They will be my people, and I will be their God.
Jeremiah 32:39 I will give them one heart and one path so they will respect me always, for their own good and for their children's good.
Jeremiah 32:40 I will make a forever promise with them that I won't leave them but do good for them; I will make them respect me so they won't leave me.
Jeremiah 32:41 Yes, I will celebrate by doing good for them, and I will definitely plant them in this land with all my heart and soul.
Jeremiah 32:42 God says: Just as I caused all this big trouble for these people, I will also give them all the good I promised.
Jeremiah 32:43 People will buy land in this country, even though you say it is empty with no people or animals, because it has been taken over by the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 32:44 People will buy land with money, sign legal papers, seal them, and have witnesses in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah, the mountain towns, the valley towns, and the southern towns, because I will restore their fortunes, says God.

Jeremiah 33:1 Again, God spoke to Jeremiah while he was still locked up in the prison yard, saying,
Jeremiah 33:2 God, who made it and shaped it to set it firm, has this to say; God is his name.
Jeremiah 33:3 Ask me, and I will respond to you, and tell you about great and powerful things you do not know.
Jeremiah 33:4 God, the God of Israel, says this about the houses of this city and about the houses of the kings of Judah that are torn down by attackers and by weapons:
Jeremiah 33:5 They come to battle the Chaldeans, only to be filled with the bodies of those I have killed in my anger and fury, and because of all the evil, I have turned away from this city.
Jeremiah 33:6 Look, I will bring them health and healing, and I will heal them and show them a lot of peace and truth.
Jeremiah 33:7 I will bring back the people of Judah and Israel from captivity and rebuild them as before.
Jeremiah 33:8 I will clean them from all their wrongs which made them sin against me; and I will forgive all their sins and offenses against me.
Jeremiah 33:9 It will be known to me as a joyful name, praised and honored by all the nations of the earth. They will hear of all the good I do for them. They will be in awe and shake with fear because of all the goodness and success I bring to it.
Jeremiah 33:10 God says: In this place you think will be empty, with no people or animals, and in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that are empty, with no people or animals living there, you will hear noise again.
Jeremiah 33:11 The sounds of happiness and joy, the sounds of the groom and the bride, the sounds of people saying, "Praise God, for He is good; His kindness lasts forever," and the sounds of those bringing thank-you gifts to God's house. I will bring back the people to their land as before, says God.
Jeremiah 33:12 God says: Once more in this empty place, where no people or animals are, and in all its cities, shepherds will live and have their sheep rest.
Jeremiah 33:13 In the mountain cities, valley cities, southern cities, Benjamin's land, near Jerusalem, and in Judah's cities, flocks will again pass under the hands of the one counting them, says God.
Jeremiah 33:14 Look, the time is coming, says God, when I will do the good thing I promised to the people of Israel and Judah.
Jeremiah 33:15 In those days and at that time, I will make a Righteous Branch sprout for David; he will carry out fair judgment and justice in the land.
Jeremiah 33:16 In those days, Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will live in safety. This is the name by which it will be called: God our righteousness.
Jeremiah 33:17 God says David will always have someone from his family to be king of Israel.
Jeremiah 33:18 The priest Levites will always have someone to offer burnt offerings, prepare grain offerings, and make sacrifices to God.
Jeremiah 33:19 God's message came to Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 33:20 God says, if you can end my agreement with the day and night so they don't happen at the right times;
Jeremiah 33:21 If that happens, my agreement with my servant David might also break, so he won't have a son to rule on his throne, along with the Levite priests, who serve me.
Jeremiah 33:22 Just as you can't count the stars or measure the sand on the beach, I will greatly increase the descendants of my servant David and the priests who serve me.
Jeremiah 33:23 God's message came to Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 33:24 Do you not see what these people are saying? They say, "God has rejected the two families he chose," so they look down on my people as if they aren't a nation anymore.
Jeremiah 33:25 God says, "If my agreement is not with day and night, and if I haven't set the laws of heaven and earth;
Jeremiah 33:26 Then I will reject the descendants of Jacob and David my servant, so I won't choose any of his descendants to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. But I will bring back their captives and show them mercy.

Jeremiah 34:1 God gave a message to Jeremiah when Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, his army, and all the kingdoms he ruled, along with all their people, were fighting against Jerusalem and its cities. He said,
Jeremiah 34:2 God says to Zedekiah, the king of Judah, "I will give this city to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down."
Jeremiah 34:3 You will not avoid capture; you will be caught and handed over to him. You will see the King of Babylon with your own eyes, and he will talk directly to you, and you will go to Babylon.
Jeremiah 34:4 Listen to God's message, O Zedekiah, king of Judah; God says about you, You will not die by the sword.
Jeremiah 34:5 You will die peacefully, and just as they made fires for past kings before you, they will do the same for you. They will mourn for you and say, "Oh, master!" because I, God, have declared it.
Jeremiah 34:6 The prophet Jeremiah told all these words to Zedekiah, the king of Judah, in Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 34:7 When the king of Babylon's soldiers fought against Jerusalem and the remaining cities of Judah, Lachish, and Azekah, these were the fortified cities left in Judah.
Jeremiah 34:8 This is the message that Jeremiah received from God after King Zedekiah had agreed with all the people in Jerusalem to set them free.
Jeremiah 34:9 Every man should release his male servant and every man his female servant, if they are Hebrew, so that no one should use them as servants, specifically a fellow Jew.
Jeremiah 34:10 When all the leaders and people who had agreed to the promise heard that they should let their male and female servants go free and not make them serve anymore, they obeyed and let them go.
Jeremiah 34:11 Later, they changed their minds and forced the men and women they had freed to become slaves again.
Jeremiah 34:12 So God spoke to Jeremiah with this message.
Jeremiah 34:13 God, the God of Israel, says: I made an agreement with your ancestors when I took them out of Egypt, from the place of slavery, saying,
Jeremiah 34:14 At the end of seven years, each of you must free any Hebrew who has been sold to you. After they have served you for six years, you must let them go free. But your ancestors did not listen to me or pay attention.
Jeremiah 34:15 You had changed your ways and done what is right in my eyes by giving freedom to each other; and you had made a promise to me in the temple that is named after me.
Jeremiah 34:16 But you turned away and dishonored my name. You forced every freed servant and maid to come back and made them slaves again.
Jeremiah 34:17 So God says: You did not listen to me when I asked you to give freedom to each other. Now, I declare that you will be free to face war, disease, and hunger. And I will scatter you among all the nations on earth.
Jeremiah 34:18 I will punish the men who broke my agreement, who did not keep the promises they made to me when they cut a calf in half and walked between its pieces.
Jeremiah 34:19 The leaders of Judah, the leaders of Jerusalem, the officials, the priests, and all the people of the country who walked between the calf's pieces.
Jeremiah 34:20 I will let their enemies capture them and those who want to kill them. Their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the land.
Jeremiah 34:21 I will hand King Zedekiah of Judah and his leaders over to their enemies, to those who want to kill them, and to the Babylonian army that has left you.
Jeremiah 34:22 Look, I will give an order, says God, and make them come back to this city; they will attack it, capture it, and burn it down. I will turn the towns of Judah into empty ruins.

Jeremiah 35:1 God's message came to Jeremiah when Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, saying,
Jeremiah 35:2 Go to the Rechabites' house, talk to them, bring them to God's house, into a room, and offer them wine to drink.
Jeremiah 35:3 I brought Jaazaniah, son of Jeremiah, son of Habaziniah, his brothers, all his sons, and the whole Rechabite family.
Jeremiah 35:4 I took them into God's house, to the room of Hanan's descendants, Igdaliah's son, who was a man of God. This room was next to the rulers' room and above Maaseiah son of Shallum's room, who guarded the door.
Jeremiah 35:5 I put pots full of wine and cups in front of the Rechabites' sons and told them, "Drink the wine."
Jeremiah 35:6 But they said, "We will not drink wine, because Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, told us, 'You and your sons must never drink wine.'"
Jeremiah 35:7 Do not build houses, plant seeds, grow vineyards, or own them. But always live in tents, so you can live long in the land where you are visitors.
Jeremiah 35:8 We have followed Jonadab, son of Rechab, our father's command by not drinking wine at any time, not us, our wives, our sons, or our daughters.
Jeremiah 35:9 We didn't build houses to live in, and we don't have vineyards, fields, or seeds.
Jeremiah 35:10 We have lived in tents and followed and done everything that Jonadab our father told us to do.
Jeremiah 35:11 But when Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, invaded our land, we decided to go to Jerusalem to escape the Chaldeans' and Syrians' armies, and now we live in Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 35:12 God spoke to Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 35:13 God, the ruler of all, says; Go and tell the people of Judah and Jerusalem, won't you listen and follow my words? says God.
Jeremiah 35:14 Jonadab, Rechab's son, told his sons not to drink wine, and they don't to this day. They follow their father's rule, but even though I talked to you early and often, you didn't listen to me.
Jeremiah 35:15 I have also sent you all my prophets, telling them to get up early and go to you, saying, 'Turn away from your bad ways, change what you do, and don't follow other gods to worship them, so you can live in the land I gave to you and your ancestors.' But you haven't listened or paid attention to me.
Jeremiah 35:16 Because Jonadab's descendants followed their father's command, but these people did not listen to me.
Jeremiah 35:17 So this is what God, the God of Israel, says: I will bring all the bad things I said would happen to Judah and everyone in Jerusalem, because I spoke to them and they did not listen; I called to them and they did not answer.
Jeremiah 35:18 Jeremiah told the Rechabites, "God says, 'Because you have followed your ancestor Jonadab's orders, keeping his rules and doing everything he commanded you:'"
Jeremiah 35:19 So this is what God, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will always have a descendant to serve me.

Jeremiah 36:1 In the fourth year of King Jehoiakim, Josiah's son, of Judah, this message came to Jeremiah from God:
Jeremiah 36:2 Get a scroll and write down all the words I've told you about Israel, Judah, and all other countries, from the time I first spoke to you during Josiah's reign until now.
Jeremiah 36:3 Perhaps the people of Judah will hear about the bad things I plan to do to them, so they might turn from their wicked ways, and then I can forgive their wrongs and their sin.
Jeremiah 36:4 Jeremiah asked Baruch, Neriah's son, to write down all of God's words that he had spoken to him on a scroll.
Jeremiah 36:5 Jeremiah told Baruch, "I am locked up; I can't go into God's house."
Jeremiah 36:6 So go and read the scroll you wrote from my words to the people in God's house on the day of fasting. Also read it to everyone from Judah who comes from their towns.
Jeremiah 36:7 They might ask God for mercy and stop doing evil, because God is very angry with them.
Jeremiah 36:8 Baruch, Neriah's son, followed all that Jeremiah the prophet told him, reading God's words from the book in God's house.
Jeremiah 36:9 In the fifth year of King Jehoiakim, son of Josiah of Judah, during the ninth month, they announced a fast for everyone in Jerusalem and for all who came from the towns of Judah to Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 36:10 Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the book in God's house, in Gemariah's room, son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper area, near the new gate entrance of God's house, to all the people listening.
Jeremiah 36:11 When Michaiah, son of Gemariah and grandson of Shaphan, heard all of God's words from the book,
Jeremiah 36:12 He went to the king's palace, to the secretary's room, and all the leaders were sitting there, including Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the leaders.
Jeremiah 36:13 Then Michaiah told everyone what he had heard when Baruch read the book to the people.
Jeremiah 36:14 So all the leaders sent Jehudi, Nethaniah's son, Shelemiah's grandson, and Cushi's great-grandson, to Baruch. They said, "Bring the scroll you've been reading to the people, and come here." Baruch, Neriah's son, took the scroll and went to them.
Jeremiah 36:15 They told him, "Please sit and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
Jeremiah 36:16 When they heard all the words, they became very scared and said to Baruch, "We will definitely tell the king all these words."
Jeremiah 36:17 They asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you write down all these words as he spoke them?"
Jeremiah 36:18 Baruch replied to them, "He said all these things to me out loud, and I wrote them down with ink in the book."
Jeremiah 36:19 The leaders told Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah, and don't let anyone know where you are."
Jeremiah 36:20 They entered the king's court and left the scroll in the room of Elishama the secretary, then told the king everything.
Jeremiah 36:21 The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he brought it from Elishama the secretary's room. Then Jehudi read it to the king and all the princes standing near the king.
Jeremiah 36:22 The king was sitting in his winter home during the ninth month, and a fire was burning in front of him.
Jeremiah 36:23 When Jehudi had read three or four pages, he cut them with a penknife and threw them into the fire on the hearth until the whole scroll was burned up in the fire on the hearth.
Jeremiah 36:24 They were not scared, nor did they tear their clothes, not the king, nor any of his servants who heard these words.
Jeremiah 36:25 Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah asked the king not to burn the scroll, but he wouldn't listen to them.
Jeremiah 36:26 The king told Jerahmeel, Hammelech's son, Seraiah, Azriel's son, and Shelemiah, Abdeel's son, to capture Baruch the writer and Jeremiah the prophet; but God protected them.
Jeremiah 36:27 Then God spoke to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll containing the words that Baruch wrote down as Jeremiah dictated, saying,
Jeremiah 36:28 Get another scroll and write on it all the words that were on the first scroll, which King Jehoiakim of Judah burned.
Jeremiah 36:29 Tell King Jehoiakim of Judah that God says: You have burned the scroll because it said that the king of Babylon would come, destroy this land, and take away both people and animals.
Jeremiah 36:30 God says about Jehoiakim, king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on David's throne, and his dead body will be thrown out to the heat by day and the frost by night.
Jeremiah 36:31 I will punish him, his descendants, and his servants for their wrongs. I will bring all the bad things I said would happen to them, to the people of Jerusalem, and to the people of Judah because they did not listen.
Jeremiah 36:32 Jeremiah got another scroll and gave it to Baruch the writer, Neriah's son. He wrote down all the words from Jeremiah that King Jehoiakim of Judah had burned. They added many more similar words as well.

Jeremiah 37:1 King Zedekiah, Josiah's son, became king after Coniah, Jehoiakim's son, whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had made king over Judah.
Jeremiah 37:2 But he, his servants, and the people of the land did not listen to the words of God that He said through the prophet Jeremiah.
Jeremiah 37:3 King Zedekiah sent Jehucal, Shelemiah's son, and Zephaniah, Maaseiah the priest's son, to prophet Jeremiah, saying, "Please pray to God for us."
Jeremiah 37:4 Jeremiah moved freely among the people because he was not imprisoned.
Jeremiah 37:5 The Egyptian army left Egypt, and when the Chaldeans attacking Jerusalem heard about them, they left Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 37:6 God spoke to the prophet Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 37:7 God, the God of Israel, says this: Tell the king of Judah who sent you to ask me, 'The army of Pharaoh that came to help you will go back to Egypt, to their own country.'
Jeremiah 37:8 The Chaldeans will come back, fight against this city, capture it, and set it on fire.
Jeremiah 37:9 God says, "Don't trick yourselves by thinking, 'The Chaldeans will definitely leave us.' They will not leave."
Jeremiah 37:10 Even if you had defeated the entire army of the Chaldeans battling you, and only injured soldiers were left, they would still get up, each in his tent, and set this city on fire.
Jeremiah 37:11 When the Chaldean army left Jerusalem because they were afraid of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah 37:12 Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin and keep himself apart from the people there.
Jeremiah 37:13 While he was at Benjamin's gate, a guard leader named Irijah, son of Shelemiah, grandson of Hananiah, was there. He arrested Jeremiah the prophet, accusing him, "You are defecting to the Chaldeans."
Jeremiah 37:14 Then Jeremiah said, "That's not true; I am not going over to the Babylonians." But he did not listen to him; so Irijah arrested Jeremiah and took him to the officials.
Jeremiah 37:15 So the leaders were angry with Jeremiah, hit him, and put him in jail in Jonathan the writer's house, because they had turned it into a jail.
Jeremiah 37:16 When Jeremiah went into the dungeon and the cells, he stayed there for many days.
Jeremiah 37:17 King Zedekiah sent for him and brought him to his house, where he asked him privately, "Has God given a message?" Jeremiah replied, "Yes, you will be captured by the king of Babylon."
Jeremiah 37:18 Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What have I done wrong to you, to your servants, or to the people that you have locked me up?"
Jeremiah 37:19 Where are your prophets now who told you, 'The king of Babylon will not attack you or this land'?
Jeremiah 37:20 Please listen, I ask you, O king: accept my urgent request not to send me back to Jonathan the scribe's house, so I won't die there.
Jeremiah 37:21 King Zedekiah ordered that Jeremiah be put in the prison yard, and that he get a piece of bread every day from the baker's area until all the city's bread was gone. So Jeremiah stayed in the prison yard.

Jeremiah 38:1 Then Shephatiah, Mattan's son; Gedaliah, Pashur's son; Jucal, Shelemiah's son; and Pashur, Malchiah's son heard what Jeremiah was telling everyone.
Jeremiah 38:2 God says, "Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, hunger, and disease, but whoever goes to the Chaldeans will live; they will escape with their life and survive."
Jeremiah 38:3 God says, "This city will definitely be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and they will capture it."
Jeremiah 38:4 So the leaders said to the king, "Please, let this man be killed because he is making the soldiers who are left in the city and all the people lose courage by saying these things. He is not looking out for the good of the people, but for their harm."
Jeremiah 38:5 King Zedekiah said, "Look, he's in your control; the king can't do anything against you."
Jeremiah 38:6 They took Jeremiah and threw him into Malchiah's son Hammelech's dungeon, in the prison yard. They lowered Jeremiah with ropes. The dungeon had no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
Jeremiah 38:7 When Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's palace, heard that they had thrown Jeremiah into the pit, while the king was sitting at the Benjamin gate;
Jeremiah 38:8 Ebedmelech left the king's house and spoke to the king, saying,
Jeremiah 38:9 Sir, the king, these men have done wrong in everything they did to the prophet Jeremiah by throwing him into a pit, and he will probably die of hunger there because there is no bread left in the city.
Jeremiah 38:10 The king ordered Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, "Take thirty men from here with you, and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the pit before he dies."
Jeremiah 38:11 Ebedmelech took the men and went into the king's house below the treasury. He got some old torn clothes and worn-out rags, and using ropes, lowered them into the dungeon to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah 38:12 Ebedmelech the Ethiopian told Jeremiah, "Place these old torn clothes and rotting rags under your armpits, beneath the ropes." And Jeremiah did that.
Jeremiah 38:13 They pulled Jeremiah out of the pit with ropes and he stayed in the prison courtyard.
Jeremiah 38:14 King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and brought him to the third entrance of God's house. The king told Jeremiah, "I will ask you something; don't hide anything from me."
Jeremiah 38:15 Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, won't you definitely kill me? And if I give you advice, won't you listen to me?"
Jeremiah 38:16 So King Zedekiah secretly promised Jeremiah, saying, "As God lives, who made us this soul, I will not kill you or hand you over to these men who want to take your life."
Jeremiah 38:17 Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "God, the ruler of heaven's armies, the God of Israel, says: If you really go out to meet the king of Babylon's officers, you will live, this city won't be burned down, and you and your family will survive."
Jeremiah 38:18 If you don't go out to meet the king of Babylon's officers, then this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, who will burn it, and you won't escape from them.
