Jeremiah 38:19 King Zedekiah told Jeremiah, "I am scared of the Jews who joined the Chaldeans because I worry they will hand me over to them, and they will make fun of me."
Jeremiah 38:20 Jeremiah said, "They won't hand you over. Please listen to what God is telling you through me: then things will go well for you, and you will stay alive."
Jeremiah 38:21 If you choose not to go out, here is the message God has revealed to me:
Jeremiah 38:22 Look, all the women left in Judah's king's house will be taken to the king of Babylon's officials, and they will say, "Your allies encouraged you and have beaten you: your feet are stuck in the mud, and they have turned away from you."
Jeremiah 38:23 They will bring out all your wives and children to the Chaldeans. You will not escape from them but will be captured by the king of Babylon. You will make this city burn with fire.
Jeremiah 38:24 Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Don't let anyone know about these words and you won't die."
Jeremiah 38:25 If the leaders find out I spoke with you, and they ask you, 'Tell us what you told the king and what he said to you; don't hide it from us and we won't kill you,'
Jeremiah 38:26 Then you should tell them, I asked the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die.
Jeremiah 38:27 All the leaders went to Jeremiah and asked him questions, and he answered with the words that the king had ordered. Then they stopped talking with him because they didn't understand the situation.
Jeremiah 38:28 Jeremiah stayed in the prison courtyard until the day Jerusalem was captured, and he was there when it happened.

Jeremiah 39:1 In the ninth year when Zedekiah was king of Judah, during the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon and his whole army attacked Jerusalem and surrounded it.
Jeremiah 39:2 In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, during the fourth month on the ninth day, the city walls were breached.
Jeremiah 39:3 All the leaders of the king of Babylon entered and sat at the central gate: Nergalsharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, and all the other leaders of the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 39:4 When Zedekiah, the king of Judah, and all the soldiers saw them, they ran away. They escaped from the city at night, through the king's garden and the gate between the two walls, and they took the road to the plain.
Jeremiah 39:5 The army of the Chaldeans chased them and caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. After capturing him, they took him to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, at Riblah in the territory of Hamath, where he was judged.
Jeremiah 39:6 The king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons in Riblah while he watched. He also killed all the important leaders of Judah.
Jeremiah 39:7 He blinded Zedekiah and tied him up with chains to take him to Babylon.
Jeremiah 39:8 The Chaldeans set fire to the king's palace and the people's homes and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 39:9 Then Nebuzaradan, the head guard, took the remaining people in the city as captives to Babylon, along with those who joined him and the rest of the people who were left.
Jeremiah 39:10 Nebuzaradan, the guard captain, left the poor people who had nothing in Judah and gave them vineyards and fields then.
Jeremiah 39:11 The king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar, gave orders about Jeremiah to his chief guard, Nebuzaradan, saying,
Jeremiah 39:12 Take him, watch him carefully, and don't hurt him; but do to him just as he tells you.
Jeremiah 39:13 So Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, sent Nebushasban, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, and all the princes of Babylon's king.
Jeremiah 39:14 They sent for Jeremiah, took him from the prison yard, and handed him over to Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, Shaphan's grandson, to take him home. So he lived with the people.
Jeremiah 39:15 God's message came to Jeremiah when he was locked in the prison yard, saying,
Jeremiah 39:16 Go and tell Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, 'God, the ruler of all, the God of Israel, says: I will make my words come true against this city for harm, not for good; and you will see it happen on that day.'
Jeremiah 39:17 God says, "But on that day, I will save you, and you will not be handed over to the men you fear."
Jeremiah 39:18 I will definitely save you, and you won't die by the sword, but you will have your life as a reward because you trusted in me, says God.

Jeremiah 40:1 God gave a message to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, released him in Ramah. This happened when he had been taken with chains among all the people from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken as prisoners to Babylon.
Jeremiah 40:2 The guard leader took Jeremiah and said to him, "God has declared this disaster on this place."
Jeremiah 40:3 God has made this happen because you sinned against him and didn't listen to him, so this has come upon you.
Jeremiah 40:4 Today, I free you from the chains on your hands. If you want to come with me to Babylon, come; I will take good care of you. But if you don't want to come with me to Babylon, then don't. Look, all the land is open to you: go wherever you think is best and right for you.
Jeremiah 40:5 Before he had gone far, he said, "Return to Gedaliah, Ahikam's son and Shaphan's grandson, whom the king of Babylon appointed as ruler over the towns of Judah. Stay with him and the people, or go anywhere you think is best." Then the guard captain gave him food and a gift and allowed him to leave.
Jeremiah 40:6 Jeremiah went to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, at Mizpah and lived with him among the people who remained in the land.
Jeremiah 40:7 When all the military leaders who were in the open country and their troops heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, as governor over the land and had put under his care men, women, children, and the poorest people who had not been taken as captives to Babylon;
Jeremiah 40:8 They went to Gedaliah at Mizpah, including Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai from Netophah, and Jezaniah son of a Maachathite with their men.
Jeremiah 40:9 Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, Shaphan's grandson, promised them and their people, saying, "Don't be afraid to work for the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the Babylon king, and you will be fine."
Jeremiah 40:10 I will stay in Mizpah to help the Chaldeans when they arrive, but you should collect wine, summer fruits, and oil, store them in containers, and live in the cities you've captured.
Jeremiah 40:11 When all the Jews in Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, and other countries heard that the king of Babylon had allowed some people from Judah to remain and that he had appointed Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam and grandson of Shaphan, to govern them;
Jeremiah 40:12 All the Jews came back from the places they had been scattered to and went to Judah, to see Gedaliah at Mizpah. There, they collected a lot of wine and summer fruits.
Jeremiah 40:13 Johanan, Kareah's son, and all the army leaders in the fields went to see Gedaliah at Mizpah.
Jeremiah 40:14 He asked, “Do you really know that Baalis, the king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, to kill you?” But Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, did not believe it.
Jeremiah 40:15 Johanan, Kareah's son, spoke to Gedaliah in Mizpah in secret. He said, "Please let me go and kill Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, and no one will find out. Why should he kill you, so the Jews with you scatter and the survivors in Judah die?"
Jeremiah 40:16 But Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, told Johanan, Kareah's son, "Don't do this; you're lying about Ishmael."

Jeremiah 41:1 In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, grandson of Elishama of royal descent, and ten leaders with him, went to see Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. There, they all ate bread together in Mizpah.
Jeremiah 41:2 Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, and the ten men with him stood up, attacked Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, Shaphan's grandson, with a sword, and killed him. Gedaliah was the one the king of Babylon had appointed to govern the land.
Jeremiah 41:3 Ishmael killed all the Jews with him and Gedaliah at Mizpah, including the Chaldeans and soldiers there.
Jeremiah 41:4 Two days after he killed Gedaliah, with nobody knowing,
Jeremiah 41:5 Some men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria—eighty of them—with shaved beards, torn clothes, and cuts on their bodies. They brought offerings and incense to take to God's house.
Jeremiah 41:6 Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, left Mizpah to meet them, crying as he walked. When he met them, he told them, "Come to Gedaliah, Ahikam's son."
Jeremiah 41:7 When they entered the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed them and threw their bodies into a pit, along with his men.
Jeremiah 41:8 But ten men were there who said to Ishmael, "Don't kill us: we have hidden treasures in the field, of wheat, barley, oil, and honey." So he spared them and did not kill them with their brothers.
Jeremiah 41:9 The pit where Ishmael threw all the dead men he killed because of Gedaliah was the same one King Asa had dug because he was afraid of Baasha, the king of Israel. Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, filled it with the slain.
Jeremiah 41:10 Ishmael took all the remaining people in Mizpah captive, including the king's daughters and those Nebuzaradan, the guard captain, left with Gedaliah, Ahikam's son. Then Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, led them away to the Ammonites.
Jeremiah 41:11 When Johanan son of Kareah and all the army leaders with him heard about all the bad things Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,
Jeremiah 41:12 They captured all the men and fought against Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, near the large waters in Gibeon.
Jeremiah 41:13 When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan, Kareah's son, and the commanders with him, they were happy.
Jeremiah 41:14 All the people Ishmael took from Mizpah turned around, came back, and went to Johanan, Kareah's son.
Jeremiah 41:15 Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, got away from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.
Jeremiah 41:16 Johanan, Kareah's son, and the leaders with him took all the survivors he saved from Ishmael, Nethaniah's son, from Mizpah after he killed Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, including soldiers, women, children, and eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
Jeremiah 41:17 They left and lived in Chimham's place near Bethlehem, planning to go to Egypt.
Jeremiah 41:18 They feared the Chaldeans because Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor.

Jeremiah 42:1 Then all the army leaders, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and everyone, both small and great, came forward.
Jeremiah 42:2 They said to the prophet Jeremiah, "Please listen to our request and pray to God for us, for all of us who remain, because only a few of us are left from many, as you can see."
Jeremiah 42:3 So that God may show us the path to walk in and what we should do.
Jeremiah 42:4 Then the prophet Jeremiah said to them, "I have listened to you; I will pray to God for you as you have asked; and whatever answer God gives, I will tell you everything; I will hide nothing from you."
Jeremiah 42:5 Then they said to Jeremiah, "May God be a true and trustworthy witness between us, if we do not follow all the instructions that your God gives you for us."
Jeremiah 42:6 Whether it is good or bad, we will listen to God, to whom we sent you; so that things will go well for us when we listen to God's voice.
Jeremiah 42:7 After ten days, God spoke to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah 42:8 He called Johanan, Kareah's son, and all the army leaders with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
Jeremiah 42:9 He said to them, "This is what God, the God of Israel, says, to whom you sent me to offer your request before Him;"
Jeremiah 42:10 If you choose to stay in this land, then I will strengthen you and not destroy you, and I will settle you and not uproot you, because I regret the harm I have caused you.
Jeremiah 42:11 Do not fear the king of Babylon, whom you are scared of; do not fear him, says God: for I am with you to save you and rescue you from his power.
Jeremiah 42:12 I will show you kindness so that you will be shown kindness, and bring you back to your own land.
Jeremiah 42:13 But if you say, "We won't live in this land or listen to the voice of God,"
Jeremiah 42:14 No, we will go to Egypt, where we won't see war, hear the trumpet, or be hungry for bread; and we will live there.
Jeremiah 42:15 So now, listen to what God tells you, you who remain from Judah. This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: If you are fully determined to go to Egypt and live there;
Jeremiah 42:16 It will happen that the sword you were afraid of will catch up with you in Egypt, and the hunger you feared will also reach you there in Egypt; and there you will die.
Jeremiah 42:17 Everyone who goes to live in Egypt will die by war, hunger, and disease. No one will survive or escape the disaster I will bring on them.
Jeremiah 42:18 God of Israel says: Just as my anger has been poured out on the people of Jerusalem, it will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become a curse and a shocking example, and you will never see this place again.
Jeremiah 42:19 God has told you, people left from Judah, do not go to Egypt: be sure that I have warned you today.
Jeremiah 42:20 You pretended in your hearts when you sent me to God, saying, "Ask God to help us, and tell us everything God says, and we will do it."
Jeremiah 42:21 Today I told you, but you did not listen to God or follow what he sent me to tell you.
Jeremiah 42:22 So now, be sure that you will die from war, hunger, and disease in the place you want to go to live.

Jeremiah 43:1 When Jeremiah finished telling the people everything that God had sent him to say to them,
Jeremiah 43:2 Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying: God has not sent you to tell us, 'Do not go to live in Egypt.'"
Jeremiah 43:3 But Baruch, son of Neriah, is turning you against us to hand us over to the Chaldeans, so they can kill us or take us as prisoners to Babylon.
Jeremiah 43:4 So Johanan, Kareah's son, and all the army leaders, and all the people, did not follow God's command to live in the land of Judah.
Jeremiah 43:5 Johanan, Kareah's son, and all the military leaders took all the remaining people of Judah who had come back from the countries where they were scattered to live in the land of Judah.
Jeremiah 43:6 Men, women, children, the king's daughters, and everyone that the captain of the guards, Nebuzaradan, left with Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch, son of Neriah.
Jeremiah 43:7 They entered Egypt because they did not listen to God, and so they reached Tahpanhes.
Jeremiah 43:8 Then God spoke to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
Jeremiah 43:9 Carry large stones in your hand and bury them in the mud at the brick-making place near the entrance of the king's palace in Tahpanhes, where the men of Judah can see you.
Jeremiah 43:10 Tell them this: God, the God of Israel, says, "Look, I will send and bring King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, my servant. I will place his throne on these hidden stones, and he will set up his royal tent over them."
Jeremiah 43:11 When he comes, he will strike the land of Egypt, and those marked for death will die, those marked for captivity will be taken captive, and those marked for the sword will fall by the sword.
Jeremiah 43:12 I will start a fire in the Egyptian gods' temples; it will burn them and take them as prisoners. He will take over Egypt as easily as a shepherd puts on his coat, and then he will leave there safely.
Jeremiah 43:13 He will also destroy the statues in Bethshemesh in Egypt; he will burn down the Egyptian temples.

Jeremiah 44:1 God's message came to Jeremiah for all the Jews living in Egypt, in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph, and the region of Pathros. He said,
Jeremiah 44:2 God says, "You have seen all the bad things I have brought on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah; now they are ruined, and no one lives there."
Jeremiah 44:3 They did evil things to make me angry, like burning incense and worshiping gods they, you, or your ancestors didn't know.
Jeremiah 44:4 Even though I sent you all my prophets, again and again, telling you, "Please don't do this terrible thing that I hate."
Jeremiah 44:5 But they did not listen or turn their ears away from their evil ways, to stop burning incense to other gods.
Jeremiah 44:6 So my anger and fury were poured out and blazed in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and they are ruined and empty to this day.
Jeremiah 44:7 So now this is what God, the God of all, the God of Israel, says: Why do you do this terrible thing against yourselves? It will make every man, woman, baby, and nursing child disappear from Judah, leaving no one left.
Jeremiah 44:8 You make me angry with what you do, burning incense to other gods in Egypt where you've gone to live, making yourselves cut off, cursed, and shamed among all the countries on earth.
Jeremiah 44:9 Have you forgotten how bad your ancestors, the kings of Judah, their wives, you, and your wives were in Judah and Jerusalem?
Jeremiah 44:10 They have not become humble to this day, nor have they shown fear, followed my laws, or obeyed my rules that I gave to you and your ancestors.
Jeremiah 44:11 So this is what God, the God of Israel says: Look, I will turn against you to bring disaster and to completely remove Judah.
Jeremiah 44:12 I will take the few people from Judah who decided to go live in Egypt. In Egypt, they will all be destroyed. They will die by the sword and from hunger. Every one of them, from the least to the greatest, will die by the sword and from hunger. They will become something people curse and are shocked by, and they will be insulted and shamed.
Jeremiah 44:13 I will punish the people in Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem, with war, hunger, and disease.
Jeremiah 44:14 None of the remaining people of Judah who went to live in Egypt will survive or stay alive to go back to Judah, even though they want to live there again; only those who manage to escape will return.
Jeremiah 44:15 All the men who knew their wives worshiped other gods, and all the women near them, along with a large crowd, even all the people living in Egypt, in Pathros, responded to Jeremiah, saying,
Jeremiah 44:16 About what you told us in God's name, we won't listen to you.
Jeremiah 44:17 We will definitely do whatever we said we would, like offering incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out liquid offerings to her, just as we, along with our ancestors, kings, and leaders, did in the towns of Judah and Jerusalem. Back then, we had plenty of food, were healthy, and didn't see any trouble.
Jeremiah 44:18 Since we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been destroyed by war and hunger.
Jeremiah 44:19 When we burned incense to the queen of heaven and gave her drink offerings, did we make cakes for her and pour out drinks without our men?
Jeremiah 44:20 Then Jeremiah spoke to everyone, the men and women, and all who had replied to him, saying,
Jeremiah 44:21 God remembered the incense you and your ancestors, kings, and leaders burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, didn't He?
Jeremiah 44:22 So God could not stand it anymore, because of the evil things you've done, and the terrible things you've done; that's why your land is ruined, shocking, and cursed, with no one living in it, just like today.
Jeremiah 44:23 Because you burned incense and sinned against God, not listening to God's voice or following His laws, rules, or commands, this bad thing has happened to you today.
Jeremiah 44:24 Jeremiah also said to all the people and the women, "Listen to God's message, all of you from Judah living in Egypt."
Jeremiah 44:25 God, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have said with your mouths and done with your hands, "We will surely keep the promises we made to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her." You will indeed keep your promises and do what you vowed.
Jeremiah 44:26 So listen to God's message, all you people of Judah living in Egypt. I promise by my great name, says God, that no one from Judah in Egypt will say 'The living God' anymore.
Jeremiah 44:27 Look, I will look after them for harm, not for good: and all the men of Judah in Egypt will die by the sword and hunger, until they are all gone.
Jeremiah 44:28 A few who escape the sword will come back from Egypt to Judah, and all the remaining people of Judah who went to stay in Egypt will find out which words will last, mine or theirs.
Jeremiah 44:29 This will be a sign to you, says God: I will punish you here, so you will know that my words will certainly come true and bring bad things to you.
Jeremiah 44:30 God says, "Look, I will hand over Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, to his enemies and to those who want to kill him, just as I handed over Zedekiah, king of Judah, to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy, who wanted to kill him."

Jeremiah 45:1 Jeremiah the prophet told Baruch, son of Neriah, these words after Baruch wrote them down as Jeremiah said them. This happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim's rule, Josiah's son, who was the king of Judah.
Jeremiah 45:2 God, the God of Israel, says this to you, O Baruch:
Jeremiah 45:3 You said, "I am in trouble now! For God has made my sadness greater; I grew weak as I sighed, and I can't find peace."
Jeremiah 45:4 Tell him this: God says, "Look, I will destroy what I have built and uproot what I have planted, all across the land."
Jeremiah 45:5 Are you looking for great things for yourself? Don't look for them, because I will bring trouble to everyone, says God, but I will let you escape with your life wherever you go.

Jeremiah 46:1 God's message that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the nations;
Jeremiah 46:2 Against Egypt and Pharaohnecho's army, the king of Egypt, near the Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim's reign, Josiah's son, the king of Judah.
Jeremiah 46:3 Prepare your shields, both large and small, and move forward to fight.
Jeremiah 46:4 Prepare the horses; riders, get ready and put on your helmets; polish the spears and wear your armor.
Jeremiah 46:5 Why have I seen them scared and running away? Their strong ones are defeated, have run quickly, and don't look back because fear was all around, says God.
Jeremiah 46:6 Do not let the fast run away, nor the strong man get away; they will trip and fall by the Euphrates River to the north.
Jeremiah 46:7 Who is this coming up like a flood, with waters swirling like rivers?
Jeremiah 46:8 Egypt rises like a flood, and its waters surge like the rivers. It says, "I will rise and cover the earth. I will destroy the city and its people."
Jeremiah 46:9 Move forward, horses; surge ahead, chariots; and strong warriors step out; the Ethiopians and Libyans with shields; and the Lydians with bows ready.
Jeremiah 46:10 Today is God's day, a day for revenge, so he can fight his enemies. The sword will eat until it is full and drunk with their blood. God has a sacrifice in the land by the Euphrates River.
Jeremiah 46:11 Travel to Gilead and get healing ointment, young woman of Egypt. You will use many treatments in vain; you will not be healed.
Jeremiah 46:12 Countries have heard about your disgrace, and your screams have spread everywhere: because strong people have tripped over each other, and they have both fallen down.
Jeremiah 46:13 God told the prophet Jeremiah how King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon would come and strike the land of Egypt.
Jeremiah 46:14 Tell everyone in Egypt, announce in Migdol, and let Noph and Tahpanhes know: say, "Be strong and get ready; the sword will destroy everything around you."
Jeremiah 46:15 Why were your brave men scattered? They did not stand firm because God drove them away.
Jeremiah 46:16 He caused many to fall, yes, one tumbled onto another; and they said, Get up, let's go back to our own people and the land where we were born, away from the cruel sword.
Jeremiah 46:17 They shouted there, "Pharaoh the king of Egypt is just noise; he missed the scheduled time."
Jeremiah 46:18 I am alive, says the King named God of all. Just like Tabor stands out among the mountains and Carmel at the sea, he will come.
Jeremiah 46:19 You, Egypt's daughter, get ready for captivity: Noph will be ruined and empty without people.
Jeremiah 46:20 Egypt is like a beautiful young cow, but disaster is coming; it is coming from the north.
Jeremiah 46:21 Her paid workers are among her like well-fed bulls; they have turned away and run off together: they did not stay because their disaster came upon them, and their time of punishment.
Jeremiah 46:22 The sound will move like a snake; they will move forward with a military force and attack with axes like woodcutters.
Jeremiah 46:23 They will chop down her forests, says God, even though they are too vast to explore; because they outnumber the grasshoppers and cannot be counted.
Jeremiah 46:24 Egypt's daughter will be ashamed; she will be handed over to the northern people.
Jeremiah 46:25 God, the God of Israel, says, "Look, I will punish the people of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all who trust in him."
Jeremiah 46:26 I will give them over to those who want to kill them, to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and to his officials. Later, it will be lived in again, like in the old times, says God.
Jeremiah 46:27 Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, and do not be discouraged, Israel. I will save you from far away and your descendants from the land where they are captives. Jacob will come back, be peaceful and secure, and no one will frighten him.
Jeremiah 46:28 Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, God says: I am with you. I will completely destroy all the nations where I have sent you, but I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you properly, but I will not let you go unpunished.

Jeremiah 47:1 God's message came to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines before the Pharaoh attacked Gaza.
Jeremiah 47:2 God says, "Look, waters are coming from the north, becoming a flooding river, flooding the land and everything in it; the city and everyone living there. Then people will scream, and everyone in the land will wail."
Jeremiah 47:3 When they hear the loud stomping of his powerful horses, the roar of his chariots, and the rumbling of their wheels, the parents will not turn back to their kids because their hands are too weak.
Jeremiah 47:4 The day is coming to destroy all the Philistines, and to end every remaining helper from Tyre and Sidon: for God will destroy the Philistines, the survivors from the land of Caphtor.
Jeremiah 47:5 Gaza is now bald; Ashkelon and the rest of their valley are destroyed. How long will you hurt yourself?
Jeremiah 47:6 Sword of God, how long until you stop? Go back into your sheath, rest, and be calm.
Jeremiah 47:7 How can it be calm when God has ordered it to attack Ashkelon and the coast? That is where he has sent it.

Jeremiah 48:1 God says this about Moab: "Trouble is coming to Nebo because it's destroyed. Kiriathaim is captured and shamed. Misgab is terrified and upset."
Jeremiah 48:2 Moab will not be praised anymore; in Heshbon, they plan to destroy it. Come, let's wipe it out as a nation. Madmen, you too will be destroyed; the sword will chase you.
Jeremiah 48:3 Cries and loud noises will come from Horonaim, along with destruction and major damage.
Jeremiah 48:4 Moab is ruined; her young children have made a cry heard.
Jeremiah 48:5 As people climb up Luhith, they keep crying. As they go down to Horonaim, enemies hear a loud sound of ruin.
Jeremiah 48:6 Run away, save yourselves, and be like a bush in the desert.
Jeremiah 48:7 Because you trusted in what you did and in your riches, you will be captured: and Chemosh will be taken away as a prisoner with his priests and leaders.
Jeremiah 48:8 The destroyer will come to every city, and every city will not be spared; the valley will also wither, and the flat land will be ruined, as God has said.
Jeremiah 48:9 Give Moab wings to fly away and escape, because its cities will be empty, with no one living in them.
Jeremiah 48:10 Cursed is the one who does God's work with trickery, and cursed is the one who holds back his sword from drawing blood.
Jeremiah 48:11 Moab has lived comfortably since he was young, settled without being disturbed, and has not been moved from one container to another, nor has he been taken captive; so his ways have stayed the same, and his character has not changed.
Jeremiah 48:12 So, look, the time will come, God says, when I will send travelers to him who will make him wander, empty his containers, and smash his jars.
Jeremiah 48:13 Moab will feel shame for Chemosh just as the people of Israel felt shame for their trust in Bethel.
Jeremiah 48:14 How can you say, "We are powerful and strong warriors"?
Jeremiah 48:15 Moab is destroyed, and people have left its towns, and its best young men have been killed, says the King, whose name is God of armies.
Jeremiah 48:16 Moab's disaster is coming soon, and his trouble is speeding up.
Jeremiah 48:17 Everyone around him, mourn for him; and everyone who knows his name, ask, "How is the powerful stick broken, and the lovely stick!"
Jeremiah 48:18 You who live in Dibon, come down from your high place and sit in thirst; for the destroyer of Moab will attack you and break down your safe places.
Jeremiah 48:19 People of Aroer, stand by the road, watch, and ask both the person who is running away and the person who has escaped, "What happened?"
Jeremiah 48:20 Moab is embarrassed; it is destroyed: wail and weep; say it in Arnon, that Moab is ruined.
Jeremiah 48:21 God's judgment has come to the flat land, to Holon, to Jahazah, and to Mephaath.
Jeremiah 48:22 On Dibon, Nebo, and Bethdiblathaim,
Jeremiah 48:23 On Kiriathaim, on Bethgamul, and on Bethmeon,
Jeremiah 48:24 And on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, and on all the cities of Moab, far and near.
Jeremiah 48:25 Moab's strength is gone, and his power is broken, says God.
Jeremiah 48:26 Make him drunk because he acted arrogantly against God. Moab will roll in his own throw-up, and he will be mocked as well.
Jeremiah 48:27 Didn't you mock Israel? Did you catch him with thieves? You've been happy talking about him.
Jeremiah 48:28 You who live in Moab, leave the cities, live in the cliffs, and be like the dove that builds her nest on the edge of a cave's entrance.
Jeremiah 48:29 We have heard how proud Moab is, very proud indeed, of his greatness, his arrogance, his pride, and his conceited heart.
Jeremiah 48:30 I know his anger, says God, but it won't happen like that; his lies won't succeed.
Jeremiah 48:31 So, I will wail for Moab and cry for all of Moab; my heart will grieve for the people of Kirheres.
Jeremiah 48:32 O Sibmah vine, I will cry for you like the cries of Jazer: your branches have spread across the sea, even to Jazer's sea: the destroyer has attacked your summer fruit and harvest.
Jeremiah 48:33 Happiness and joy have been removed from the fertile fields and the land of Moab; I have made the wine stop flowing from the winepresses: no one will step on grapes with cheers; their cheers won't be heard.
Jeremiah 48:34 People are screaming from Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz, and from Zoar to Horonaim, like young cows. Even Nimrim's waters will be empty.
Jeremiah 48:35 I will stop people in Moab from making sacrifices on the high hills and burning incense to their gods, says God.
Jeremiah 48:36 So my heart will cry for Moab like flutes, and my heart will be like flutes for the people of Kir Heres, for the wealth they gained is gone.
Jeremiah 48:37 Every head will be shaved, every beard trimmed; all hands will be scratched, and around the waist, there will be rough cloth.
Jeremiah 48:38 People will mourn on all the rooftops in Moab and in its streets, because I have shattered Moab like a useless pot, says God.
Jeremiah 48:39 They will cry out, "How it is destroyed! How Moab has run away in shame!" So Moab will become a joke and a terror to all nearby.
Jeremiah 48:40 For this is what God says: Look, he will soar like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.
Jeremiah 48:41 Kerioth is captured, and the strongholds are taken by surprise, and on that day, the brave soldiers in Moab will be as scared as a woman having a baby.
Jeremiah 48:42 Moab will be ruined and no longer be a nation because it boasted against God.
Jeremiah 48:43 Danger, a hole, and a trap will come to you, people of Moab, says God.
Jeremiah 48:44 The one who runs from danger will fall into a hole, and whoever climbs out of the hole will get caught in a trap, because I will bring disaster on Moab when I punish them, says God.
Jeremiah 48:45 Those who ran away stayed in the shade of Heshbon because of the enemy. But a fire will start from Heshbon, and a flame from Sihon, and it will burn the edges of Moab and the tops of the noisy people's heads.
Jeremiah 48:46 Sadness comes to you, Moab! The followers of Chemosh are destroyed: your sons are captured, and your daughters are captured.
Jeremiah 48:47 But I will restore Moab from captivity in the future, says God. This is God's judgment on Moab.

Jeremiah 49:1 About the Ammonites, this is what God says: Does Israel have no children? Do they have no one to inherit their land? Why then does the king of the Ammonites take over the land of Gad, and why do his people live in its towns?
Jeremiah 49:2 So, listen, the time will come, God says, when I will make the sound of war heard in Rabbah of the Ammon people; it will become a ruined mound, and its towns will be set on fire. Then Israel will take over the land from those who took their land, God says.
Jeremiah 49:3 Cry out, O Heshbon, because Ai is destroyed: weep, you women of Rabbah, put on rough cloth; mourn, and walk back and forth by the fences; for their king will be taken as prisoner, along with his religious leaders and officials.
Jeremiah 49:4 Why do you boast about your valleys, your fertile valley, you unfaithful city? You trust in your riches and think, 'Who will attack me?'
Jeremiah 49:5 Look, I will cause you to be very afraid, says God of all, from everyone around you; and you will all be forced to leave straight away; and no one will help those who stray.
Jeremiah 49:6 Afterward, God will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites' descendants.
Jeremiah 49:7 About Edom, God says: Has wisdom disappeared from Teman? Has good advice ended for the wise? Is their wisdom gone?
Jeremiah 49:8 Run away, turn around, hide well, people of Dedan; because I will bring Esau's disaster on him, when it's time for me to punish him.
Jeremiah 49:9 If grape pickers come to you, wouldn't they leave some grapes behind? If thieves come at night, they will destroy only until they have enough.
Jeremiah 49:10 I have left Esau exposed, revealed his hiding spots, and he can't hide: his descendants, his brothers, and his neighbors are ruined, and he no longer exists.
Jeremiah 49:11 Leave your children without a father to me; I will keep them safe, and your widows can rely on me.
Jeremiah 49:12 God says, "Look, those who were not supposed to drink from the cup have definitely drunk it; and do you think you will go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but you will certainly drink from it."
Jeremiah 49:13 I promise, says God, that Bozrah will become ruined, shamed, empty, and cursed; all its cities will be forever deserted.
Jeremiah 49:14 I have heard news from God: a messenger has been sent to the nations saying, "Come together and attack her; get ready for battle."
Jeremiah 49:15 I will make you unimportant among the nations and scorned by people.
Jeremiah 49:16 Your fearsomeness has tricked you, with the arrogance of your heart, you who live in the rock cracks and hold the hilltops high. Even if you set your home as high as an eagle's, I will bring you down from there, says God.
Jeremiah 49:17 Edom will become a wasteland; everyone who passes by will be shocked and will scorn its many disasters.
Jeremiah 49:18 Just like when Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns were destroyed, says God, no one will live there, nor will any person stay there.
Jeremiah 49:19 Look, he will rise like a lion from the Jordan's banks against the powerful place: but I will quickly make him flee from there: and who is the capable man I can put in charge of it? Who is equal to me? Who can set a time for me? And who is the shepherd that can face me?
Jeremiah 49:20 Listen to God's plan against Edom and his intentions for the people of Teman: Even the weakest will lead them away; yes, their homes will be made empty and ruined.
Jeremiah 49:21 The earth shakes when they fall, and their loud cry is heard all the way to the Red Sea.
Jeremiah 49:22 Look, he will rise and soar like an eagle, and stretch his wings over Bozrah. On that day, the brave people of Edom will be as scared as a woman in labor.
Jeremiah 49:23 About Damascus: Hamath and Arpad are worried because they have heard bad news. They are afraid; there is sadness on the sea; it cannot calm down.
Jeremiah 49:24 Damascus has become weak and tries to run away; fear has grabbed her, and pain and sorrow have caught her like a woman giving birth.
Jeremiah 49:25 Why is the praised city abandoned, the city of my happiness?
Jeremiah 49:26 So her young men will die in the streets, and all her soldiers will be wiped out on that day, says God.
Jeremiah 49:27 I will start a fire in the walls of Damascus, and it will burn down Benhadad's palaces.
Jeremiah 49:28 About Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon will strike, this is what God says: Get up, attack Kedar, and take the goods of the eastern people.
Jeremiah 49:29 They will take their tents and animals; they will take their covers, all their things, and camels; and they will shout to them, "Fear is all around."
Jeremiah 49:30 Run away, go far away, hide well, people of Hazor, says God; because Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has made plans against you and intends to attack you.
Jeremiah 49:31 Get up and go to the rich country that lives safely, says God, a country without gates or bars, living on its own.
Jeremiah 49:32 They will lose their camels and lots of their livestock; I will scatter those in the far corners to every direction, and disaster will come at them from all sides, says God.
Jeremiah 49:33 Hazor will become a home for wild creatures and will be empty forever; no person will live there, nor will anyone stay there.
Jeremiah 49:34 God's message that came to Jeremiah the prophet about Elam, at the start of King Zedekiah's rule in Judah, was:
Jeremiah 49:35 God says: I will break Elam's strongest weapon, their bow.
Jeremiah 49:36 I will send winds from all four directions against Elam and scatter its people in every direction; there will be no country where its refugees do not go.
Jeremiah 49:37 I will make Elam afraid before their enemies and those who want to kill them. I will bring disaster on them, with my intense anger, says God. I will send the sword after them until they are destroyed.
Jeremiah 49:38 I will put my throne in Elam and destroy their king and leaders, says God.
Jeremiah 49:39 In the future, God will restore Elam's fortunes.

Jeremiah 50:1 God spoke against Babylon and the Chaldeans through the prophet Jeremiah.
Jeremiah 50:2 Tell the nations, announce it, raise a flag; announce it, don't hide it: say, Babylon is captured, Bel is ashamed, Merodach is shattered; her gods are ashamed, her statues are shattered.
Jeremiah 50:3 From the north, a nation will attack her and make her land empty. No one will live there; all people and animals will leave.
Jeremiah 50:4 During that time, God says, the people of Israel and Judah will come together, crying as they travel to look for their God.
Jeremiah 50:5 People will look for the way to Zion and say, "Come, let's join with God in a lasting promise that we'll always remember."
Jeremiah 50:6 My people were like lost sheep. Their leaders led them the wrong way. They made them wander on the mountains, moving from hill to hill, and they forgot where to rest.
Jeremiah 50:7 Everyone who found them ate them up; and their enemies thought, 'We are not guilty, because they sinned against God, who is just and the hope of their ancestors.'
Jeremiah 50:8 Leave Babylon, depart from the land of the Chaldeans, and lead like male goats at the front of the herds.
Jeremiah 50:9 Look, I will bring a group of big nations from the north against Babylon. They will prepare to fight her, and then she will be captured. Their arrows will be like those of a strong skilled warrior; none will miss their target.
Jeremiah 50:10 Chaldea will be robbed, and everyone who robs it will be happy, says God.
Jeremiah 50:11 You were happy and celebrated, you who ruined what I care for, because you have become as fat as a young cow in the field and roar like bulls.
Jeremiah 50:12 Your mother will be very confused; the one who gave birth to you will feel ashamed: look, the least of the nations will become an empty wasteland, a dry place, and a desert.
Jeremiah 50:13 Because God is angry, no one will live there; it will be completely empty. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be shocked and scorn at all its disasters.
Jeremiah 50:14 Get ready to fight against Babylon on all sides: all you archers, shoot at her, don't hold back any arrows: because she has sinned against God.
Jeremiah 50:15 Call out against her from all sides: she has surrendered; her foundations are destroyed, her walls are torn down: because it is God's revenge: repay her; do to her as she has done to others.
Jeremiah 50:16 Remove the farmer from Babylon, and the reaper during harvest time: because of the scary sword, everyone will go back to their own people, and they will each run to their own country.
Jeremiah 50:17 Israel is like a sheep that has been scattered; lions have chased it away: first the king of Assyria ate it up, and now this king Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon has crushed its bones.
Jeremiah 50:18 So God, the God of Israel, says, "Look, I will punish the king of Babylon and his country just like I punished the king of Assyria."
Jeremiah 50:19 I will bring Israel back to their home, and they will eat from Carmel and Bashan, and they will be content on Mount Ephraim and Gilead.
Jeremiah 50:20 During that time, God says, people will look for Israel's wrongs but find none, and search for Judah's sins but they won't be found, because I will forgive those I spare.
Jeremiah 50:21 Attack the land of Merathaim and also the people of Pekod. Destroy them completely as I have told you, says God.
Jeremiah 50:22 The noise of war is in the country, with much destruction.
Jeremiah 50:23 How has the hammer of the whole world been split and shattered! How has Babylon turned into a wasteland among the countries!
Jeremiah 50:24 I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught without knowing; you are found and captured because you fought against God.
Jeremiah 50:25 God has opened his storage of weapons and has taken out the tools of his anger. This is what God of all does in the land of the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 50:26 Attack her from the farthest border, break into her storerooms, pile her up like mounds and completely destroy her; leave nothing remaining.
Jeremiah 50:27 Kill all her bulls; let them be led to the slaughter. Trouble is coming for them, because their day has arrived, the time for them to be punished.
Jeremiah 50:28 The message of those who run away and get out of Babylon, to announce in Zion that God is taking revenge, revenge for his temple.
Jeremiah 50:29 Gather the archers to attack Babylon: all who use bows, surround it and let no one escape. Pay back Babylon for what it has done; treat it just as it has treated others. It has acted arrogantly against God, the Holy One of Israel.
Jeremiah 50:30 So her young men will die in the streets, and all her soldiers will be killed on that day, says God.
Jeremiah 50:31 Look, I am against you, you very proud one, says God: for your day has arrived, the time I will deal with you.
Jeremiah 50:32 The proudest will trip and fall, and no one will help them up: I will start a fire in their cities, and it will consume everything around them.
Jeremiah 50:33 God says: The Israelites and the people of Judah were both oppressed. Their captors held them tightly and would not free them.
Jeremiah 50:34 Their Savior is powerful; God is his name: he will fully defend their case, to bring peace to the land, and trouble to the people of Babylon.
Jeremiah 50:35 God says a sword will strike the Chaldeans, the people of Babylon, its leaders, and its wise men.
Jeremiah 50:36 A sword is against the liars; they will act foolishly. A sword is against her strong men; they will be terrified.
Jeremiah 50:37 War will come to their horses and chariots, and to all the mixed peoples within the city; they will be weak like women: war will come to their riches, and they will be stolen.
Jeremiah 50:38 Her waters face a drought; they will dry up because this is the land of carved images, and they are crazy about their idols.
Jeremiah 50:39 So, the wild animals of the desert and the creatures of the islands will live there, and owls will make their home there. It will never be lived in again, and no one will stay there from one generation to the next.
Jeremiah 50:40 God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities nearby, says God; so no one will live there, nor will anyone stay there.
Jeremiah 50:41 Look, a nation will come from the north, and a great country, and many rulers will rise from the ends of the earth.
Jeremiah 50:42 They will carry bows and spears; they are mean and won't show mercy. Their voices will sound like the ocean. They will ride horses, ready for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
Jeremiah 50:43 The king of Babylon heard the news about them, and his hands became weak; distress gripped him, pain like that of a woman giving birth.
Jeremiah 50:44 Look, he will rise like a lion from the flooded Jordan to the home of the powerful: but I will make them quickly flee from it: and who is the chosen one I can set over it? For who is like me? And who will set a time for me? And what leader will face me?
Jeremiah 50:45 Listen to God's plan against Babylon, and his intentions for the Chaldeans' land: even the smallest sheep will lead them away, and their homes will be destroyed along with them.
Jeremiah 50:46 When Babylon is captured, the earth shakes and nations hear the outcry.

Jeremiah 51:1 God says, "Look, I will send a destructive wind against Babylon and those living there who turn against me."
Jeremiah 51:2 God will send to Babylon people who will scatter her, and will empty her land; for in the time of trouble, they will surround her completely.
Jeremiah 51:3 Let the archer aim at the one who shoots, and at the one who wears armor. Do not spare the young men; completely destroy every soldier.
Jeremiah 51:4 The killed will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and those stabbed will lie in her streets.
Jeremiah 51:5 God has not abandoned Israel or Judah, even though their land was full of sin against the Holy One of Israel.
Jeremiah 51:6 Run away from Babylon, save yourselves; don't get destroyed by her sins. This is the time for God's revenge; he will pay her back.
Jeremiah 51:7 Babylon was like a gold cup in God's hand that made the whole world drunk. The countries drank her wine, so now they are crazy.
Jeremiah 51:8 Babylon has quickly fallen and is destroyed: cry for her; bring medicine for her pain, maybe she can be healed.
Jeremiah 51:9 We wanted to heal Babylon, but it cannot be healed. Leave it, and let's all go back to our own countries. Its punishment is great, reaching up to the sky.
Jeremiah 51:10 God has shown us to be right: come, and let us tell in Zion what God has done.
Jeremiah 51:11 Sharpen the arrows; collect the shields: God has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes: for His plan is to destroy Babylon; it is God's revenge, the revenge for His temple.
Jeremiah 51:12 Raise the flag on Babylon's walls, strengthen the guard, place the lookouts, and get the traps ready: for God has planned and carried out what he said against the people of Babylon.
Jeremiah 51:13 You who live by many waters, rich in treasures, your time has ended, and so has your greed.
Jeremiah 51:14 God has sworn, saying, "I will surely fill you with people, like swarms of caterpillars, and they will raise a loud cheer against you."
Jeremiah 51:15 God made the earth with His power, set up the world with His wisdom, and spread out the sky with His knowledge.
Jeremiah 51:16 When God speaks, many waters form in the sky; He makes steam rise from the earth's edges, creates lightning with rain, and releases the wind from His storehouses.
Jeremiah 51:17 Everyone acts foolish with their own knowledge; every craftsman is ashamed of their idols. The metal idols they make are lies, and there's no life in them.
Jeremiah 51:18 They are worthless, made by mistake; when they are judged, they will be destroyed.
Jeremiah 51:19 Jacob's share is not like others; for he made everything: and Israel is the tribe he chose to inherit: God of all is his name.
Jeremiah 51:20 You are my battle axe and instruments of war: with you I will smash nations, and with you I will ruin kingdoms.
Jeremiah 51:21 I will break the horse and its rider with you; I will break the chariot and its rider with you.
Jeremiah 51:22 I will also smash men and women with you; I will break old and young with you; and I will smash young men and girls with you.
Jeremiah 51:23 I will also crush the shepherd and his sheep with you; with you, I will crush the farmer and his oxen; and with you, I will crush leaders and rulers.
Jeremiah 51:24 I will pay back Babylon and everyone in Chaldea for all the bad things they did in Zion, as you saw, says God.
Jeremiah 51:25 Look, I am against you, you destructive mountain, says God, who ruins the whole earth. I will reach out my hand against you, push you off the cliffs, and turn you into a burned mountain.
Jeremiah 51:26 No one will use any of your stones for corners or bases; you will be empty forever, says God.
Jeremiah 51:27 Put up a sign in the country, sound the horn among the nations, get the nations ready to fight against her, gather the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz against her; choose a leader to face her; make the horses come like hairy locusts.
Jeremiah 51:28 Get the nations ready to fight against her, with the kings of Media, their captains, all their leaders, and all the countries they control.
Jeremiah 51:29 The land will shake and be full of sadness because God's plans will happen to Babylon, making it empty and without people.
Jeremiah 51:30 The strong men of Babylon stopped fighting, stayed in their forts, lost their strength, acted like women, set her homes on fire, and her gates are broken.
Jeremiah 51:31 A messenger will run to meet another, and one will meet another, to tell the king of Babylon that part of his city has been captured.
Jeremiah 51:32 The paths are blocked, the tall grass is burned, and the soldiers are scared.
Jeremiah 51:33 For this is what God of all, the God of Israel, says: The city of Babylon is like a place where grain is crushed. It is time to crush her; soon her time for harvest will come.
Jeremiah 51:34 The king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar, has destroyed me; he has beaten me down; he has left me empty; he has swallowed me like a monster; he has stuffed himself with my treasures; he has thrown me away.
Jeremiah 51:35 Let the people of Zion say that the harm done to me and my body will come back on Babylon, and let Jerusalem say that my blood will be on the people of Chaldea.
Jeremiah 51:36 So this is what God says: "Look, I will fight for you and get revenge for you. I will dry up her sea and make her springs dry."
Jeremiah 51:37 Babylon will turn into ruins, a home for wild creatures, a place of amazement, and be deserted.
Jeremiah 51:38 They will roar together like lions; they will cry out like young lions.
Jeremiah 51:39 In their excitement, I will give them parties, make them drunk so they can be happy, sleep forever, and never wake up, says God.
Jeremiah 51:40 I will make them go down like lambs to be killed, like rams and male goats.
Jeremiah 51:41 Sheshach is captured! The whole earth's praise is seized! How has Babylon become a shocking sight to nations!
Jeremiah 51:42 The sea has risen over Babylon; she is overwhelmed by its many waves.
Jeremiah 51:43 Her cities are deserted, a dry and empty land, a place where no one lives and no one travels through.
Jeremiah 51:44 I will punish the god Bel in Babylon, and I will make him give back what he took. Then, nations will no longer worship him, and Babylon's wall will collapse.
Jeremiah 51:45 My people, leave from inside her and save yourselves from God's fierce anger.
Jeremiah 51:46 So your heart doesn't lose courage, and you don't fear the news that will spread in the country; news will come one year, and then the next year more news, along with violence in the country, leader fighting against leader.
Jeremiah 51:47 So, look, days are coming when I will judge Babylon's idols; her entire land will be in panic, and all her killed will fall within her.
Jeremiah 51:48 The sky and the earth, and everything in them, will sing for Babylon; because destroyers will come to her from the north, says God.
Jeremiah 51:49 Just as Babylon made many in Israel die, so at Babylon many from all over the world will die.
Jeremiah 51:50 You who have escaped the sword, go, don't stop; remember God from far away, and think of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 51:51 We are ashamed because we have faced insults; our faces are covered with shame because outsiders have entered God's holy places.
Jeremiah 51:52 So, look, the time is coming, says God, when I will judge her idols, and throughout her land the injured will moan.
Jeremiah 51:53 Even if Babylon goes up to the sky and strengthens her high places, destroyers will still come to her from me, says God.
Jeremiah 51:54 A cry of distress comes from Babylon, and much ruin from the land of the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 51:55 Because God has ruined Babylon and silenced her loud voice; when her waves roar like big waters, the sound of their roar is heard.
Jeremiah 51:56 Because the destroyer has come upon her, upon Babylon, and her strong men are captured, every one of their bows is broken: for God will surely repay.
Jeremiah 51:57 I will make her leaders, wise people, commanders, officials, and strong men drunk; they will sleep forever and never wake up, says the King named God of all.
Jeremiah 51:58 God says; Babylon's wide walls will be completely destroyed, and her tall gates will burn; the people will work for nothing, and tire themselves out.
Jeremiah 51:59 The message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah, Neriah's son and Maaseiah's grandson, was when he went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah in Zedekiah's fourth year as king. Seraiah was a peaceful leader.
Jeremiah 51:60 Jeremiah wrote in a book all the bad things that would happen to Babylon, all these words written against it.
Jeremiah 51:61 Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you go to Babylon and see and read all these words;
Jeremiah 51:62 Then you will say, O God, you have declared that this place will be completely destroyed, so that no one will live here, not people or animals, and it will be empty forever.
Jeremiah 51:63 When you finish reading this book, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates River.
Jeremiah 51:64 You will say, "Babylon will fall and not rise again because of the disaster I will cause: and people will be tired." These are Jeremiah's words.

Jeremiah 52:1 Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, and she was the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
Jeremiah 52:2 He did bad things in God's view, just like Jehoiakim did.
Jeremiah 52:3 Because of God's anger, this happened in Jerusalem and Judah until he threw them out of his presence, and Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 52:4 In the ninth year of his rule, on the tenth day of the tenth month, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and his whole army came to Jerusalem, surrounded it, camped against it, and built siege works all around it.
Jeremiah 52:5 The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
Jeremiah 52:6 In the fourth month, on the ninth day, the hunger in the city was very bad, and there was no bread for the people.
Jeremiah 52:7 Then the city was breached, and all the soldiers ran away. They left the city at night through a gate between two walls near the king's garden. The Chaldeans surrounded the city, and the soldiers escaped across the plain.
Jeremiah 52:8 The Chaldean army chased the king and caught Zedekiah in the fields of Jericho; his whole army was separated from him.
Jeremiah 52:9 Then they captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the Hamath region, where he passed sentence on him.
Jeremiah 52:10 The king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons in front of him; he also killed all the leaders of Judah in Riblah.
Jeremiah 52:11 He blinded Zedekiah, and the king of Babylon tied him up, took him to Babylon, and put him in jail until he died.
Jeremiah 52:12 In the fifth month, on the tenth day, in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard serving the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 52:13 He burned God's house, the king's house, and all Jerusalem's houses, including the great men's houses, with fire.
Jeremiah 52:14 The entire army of the Chaldeans with the captain broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 52:15 Then Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took some poor people as prisoners, and the rest of the people left in the city, along with those who had joined the king of Babylon, and the remaining crowd.
Jeremiah 52:16 Nebuzaradan, the guard captain, let some poor people stay to work as vineyard keepers and farmers.
Jeremiah 52:17 The Chaldeans broke the brass pillars, bases, and the large brass basin in the house of God, and took all the brass to Babylon.
Jeremiah 52:18 They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, dishes, spoons, and all the bronze tools used in service.
Jeremiah 52:19 The officer in charge took away the bowls, the pans, the jars, the pots, the lampstands, the ladles, and the goblets. He took the gold items as gold and the silver items as silver.
Jeremiah 52:20 Two pillars, one large basin, and twelve bronze bulls under the stands, which King Solomon made for God's house: all this bronze was too heavy to weigh.
Jeremiah 52:21 About the pillars, one pillar was 18 feet tall; a band twelve cubits long wrapped around it; and it was as thick as four fingers and hollow inside.
Jeremiah 52:22 A brass capital was on it; the capital was five cubits high, with a net design and brass pomegranates all around. The second pillar and its pomegranates were the same.
Jeremiah 52:23 There were ninety-six pomegranates on one side; in total, there were one hundred pomegranates all around the netting.
Jeremiah 52:24 The guard leader took Seraiah the head priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.
Jeremiah 52:25 He also took from the city a eunuch who was in charge of the soldiers, and seven men who were close to the king, found in the city; the army's chief secretary who counted the country's people; and sixty men from the land's people, found in the heart of the city.
Jeremiah 52:26 Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, captured them and took them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
Jeremiah 52:27 The king of Babylon struck them down and killed them at Riblah in the Hamath region. So Judah was taken as prisoners from their land.
Jeremiah 52:28 These are the people Nebuchadnezzar took as captives: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Jews.
Jeremiah 52:29 In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, he took 832 people as prisoners from Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 52:30 In the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took 745 Jewish people as prisoners; the total taken was 4,600 people.
Jeremiah 52:31 In the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin king of Judah's captivity, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in his first year as king, freed Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
Jeremiah 52:32 He spoke nicely to him and placed his throne higher than the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
Jeremiah 52:33 He changed his prison clothes and always ate bread in his presence for the rest of his life.
Jeremiah 52:34 The king of Babylon provided him with daily food until he died, every day for the rest of his life.

Lamentations 1:1 How lonely sits the city that was once full of people! How has she become like a widow! She who was important among the nations, and a ruler among the regions, how has she become a servant!
Lamentations 1:2 She cries hard at night, and her tears are on her face. None of her loved ones comfort her; all her friends have betrayed her and turned into her enemies.
Lamentations 1:3 Judah has been taken captive due to suffering and harsh labor. She lives among foreign people and finds no peace. All who chase her have caught her in difficult places.
Lamentations 1:4 Zion's paths are sad because no one comes to the feasts; her gates are empty, her priests are sad, her young women are troubled, and she feels bitter.
Lamentations 1:5 Her enemies are now in control; they are successful because God has punished her for her many sins: her children have been taken away as prisoners by the enemy.
Lamentations 1:6 Zion's daughter has lost all her beauty; her leaders are like deer that find no grass, fleeing weakly from the hunter.
Lamentations 1:7 Jerusalem thought back to the time of her trouble and suffering and all the good things she once had, when her people were defeated by the enemy and no one helped her. Her enemies saw her and laughed at her sacred days.
Lamentations 1:8 Jerusalem has sinned a lot; so she is cast aside. All who respected her now look down on her because they have seen her shame. Yes, she sighs and turns away.
Lamentations 1:9 Her dirtiness clings to her clothes; she forgets what will happen to her in the end, so she falls from her position in a surprising way: she has no one to comfort her. Oh God, see how much I am suffering because the enemy has become very proud.
Lamentations 1:10 The enemy reached out to take all her nice things; she saw that foreigners came into her holy place, the ones you said should not join your people.
Lamentations 1:11 Her people groan, looking for food; they trade their treasures for food to keep alive. Look, God, and see how wretched I've become.
Lamentations 1:12 Doesn't it matter to you, everyone who passes by? Look and see if there is any pain like my pain, which I'm suffering, that God has caused me on the day of his intense anger.
Lamentations 1:13 God sent fire into my bones from above, which overpowered them. He set a trap for my feet, turned me around, and left me empty and weak all day long.
Lamentations 1:14 God holds the heavy burden of my wrongs; it is wrapped around my neck, weighing me down. He has weakened me, and I am handed over to those I cannot escape from.
Lamentations 1:15 God has trampled all my warriors inside my walls; he summoned a group to attack my young men; God has crushed the young woman of Judah like grapes in a winepress.
Lamentations 1:16 I cry over these things; my eyes shed many tears because the one who could calm me is far away: my children are helpless because the foe has won.
Lamentations 1:17 Zion reaches out her hands, but no one comforts her. God has ordered that enemies surround Jacob. Jerusalem is like an unclean woman to them.
Lamentations 1:18 God is good; I did not obey His rules: please listen, everyone, and see how sad I am: my young women and men have been taken away as prisoners.
Lamentations 1:19 I called my lovers, but they tricked me; my priests and elders died in the city when they looked for food to refresh themselves.
Lamentations 1:20 Look, God, I am in trouble; my stomach is in pain, my heart is upset inside me, because I have seriously disobeyed. Outside, violence takes away lives, inside it's like death.
Lamentations 1:21 People know I am sad and no one comforts me. My enemies know about my problems and are happy you did this. But you have set a day, and they will end up like me.
Lamentations 1:22 Let all their evil acts be seen by you, God; treat them as you have treated me for all my wrongs, because I sigh a lot and my heart is weak.

Lamentations 2:1 Why has God covered Zion's people with darkness in his anger? He has thrown down Israel's beauty from the sky to the ground and forgotten his footstool in his anger.
Lamentations 2:2 God has destroyed all of Jacob's homes, without mercy. He has torn down Judah's defenses in anger. He has brought them to the ground and dishonored the kingdom and its rulers.
Lamentations 2:3 God has cut off all of Israel's strength in his fierce anger; he has pulled back his support facing the enemy, and he burned against Jacob like a fire that consumes everything around it.
Lamentations 2:4 He has aimed his bow like an enemy; he stood ready with his right hand like an opponent, and killed everything beautiful in Zion's place of worship; he unleashed his anger like fire.
Lamentations 2:5 God was like an enemy: He swallowed up Israel, destroyed all its palaces, ruined its strongholds, and made the people of Judah mourn and cry.
Lamentations 2:6 He has forcefully taken away his shelter, as if from a garden; he has ruined the meeting places: God made the special feasts and rest days be forgotten in Zion, and has shown anger towards the king and the priest.
Lamentations 2:7 God has rejected his altar, hated his holy place, let enemies take over the palace walls; they are loud in God's house, like during a big celebration.
Lamentations 2:8 God decided to tear down Zion's wall: He marked it for destruction and didn't stop. So, the defenses and wall mourn; they fall apart together.
Lamentations 2:9 Her gates have fallen into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars: her king and leaders are among the nations: there is no law anymore; her prophets also receive no visions from God.
Lamentations 2:10 The leaders of Zion's people sit quietly on the ground. They have thrown dust on their heads and wear rough cloth. The young women of Jerusalem look down sadly.
Lamentations 2:11 I cry until I can cry no more, I am deeply upset, and I feel broken inside because my people are destroyed; even the children and babies are fainting in the city streets.
Lamentations 2:12 They ask their mothers, "Where is food and drink?" when they faint like those hurt in the city streets, when their life spills into their mothers' laps.
Lamentations 2:13 What can I use to testify for you? What can I compare you to, O daughter of Jerusalem? What can I make equal to you to comfort you, O virgin daughter of Zion? Your wound is as big as the sea; who can heal you?
Lamentations 2:14 Your prophets have seen useless and foolish visions for you; they have not revealed your sins to free you from captivity; instead, they have presented you with false troubles and reasons for exile.
Lamentations 2:15 Everyone who goes by claps at you; they hiss and shake their heads at the city of Jerusalem, asking, "Is this the city people say is so beautiful, the joy of the whole world?"
Lamentations 2:16 All your enemies have spoken against you: they hiss and grind their teeth: they say, We have swallowed her up: surely this is the day we waited for; we have found it, we have seen it.
Lamentations 2:17 God did what he planned; he completed his word from long ago: he destroyed without mercy; he let your enemies celebrate over you, he gave strength to your rivals.
Lamentations 2:18 Their heart called out to God, O wall of Zion's people, let tears flow like a river day and night: do not stop; do not let your eyes stop crying.
Lamentations 2:19 Get up, yell out at night: at the start of the guard shifts, pour out your feelings like water before God: raise your hands to him for the lives of your young children, who are weak from hunger on every street corner.
Lamentations 2:20 Look, God, and see who you have done this to. Will women eat their own children, those a hand's breadth long? Will the priest and prophet be killed in God's holy place?
Lamentations 2:21 Both young and old are lying on the streets; my young women and men have been killed by the sword. You have killed them in your anger; you showed no mercy.
Lamentations 2:22 You called my fears around me like on a special day, so that when God was angry, no one escaped or was left: my enemy destroyed those I cared for and raised.

Lamentations 3:1 I am the man who has seen suffering because of his anger.
Lamentations 3:2 He has guided me and taken me to a place of darkness, not light.
Lamentations 3:3 Certainly, he has turned against me; he keeps acting against me all day long.
Lamentations 3:4 He made my skin and flesh old; he broke my bones.
Lamentations 3:5 He has built against me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
Lamentations 3:6 He has put me in dark places, like those long dead.
Lamentations 3:7 God has surrounded me so I can't escape; He has made my chains heavy.
Lamentations 3:8 When I cry and yell, God ignores my prayer.
Lamentations 3:9 He has blocked my paths with cut stone; he has made my ways twisted.
Lamentations 3:10 He was to me like a bear waiting to attack, and like a lion hiding.
Lamentations 3:11 He has changed my path and torn me apart; he has left me lonely.
Lamentations 3:12 He has aimed his bow, and made me the target for his arrow.
Lamentations 3:13 He made the arrows from his bag hit my body.
Lamentations 3:14 I was mocked by all my people; they sang about me all day long.
Lamentations 3:15 God has filled me with bitterness; he has made me very bitter.
Lamentations 3:16 He has also broken my teeth with gravel stones; he has covered me with ashes.
Lamentations 3:17 You took my peace far away; I forgot what good fortune is.
Lamentations 3:18 I said, "My strength and my hope are gone because of God."
Lamentations 3:19 I remember my suffering and my sadness, the bitterness and the poison.
Lamentations 3:20 I still remember them deep in my heart, and I am humbled.
Lamentations 3:21 I remember this and so I have hope.
Lamentations 3:22 It is because of God's kindness that we are not destroyed, for His compassion never ends.
Lamentations 3:23 Every morning they are new; your faithfulness is great.
Lamentations 3:24 God is all I need, says my soul; so I will put my hope in Him.
Lamentations 3:25 God is good to those who wait for Him, to the person who looks for Him.
Lamentations 3:26 It is good for a person to have hope and to wait quietly for God to save.
Lamentations 3:27 It is good for a person to deal with hard times when young.
Lamentations 3:28 He sits alone and stays quiet because he has taken it upon himself.
Lamentations 3:29 He puts his mouth to the ground; perhaps there is hope.
Lamentations 3:30 He offers his face to the one who hits him; he is overwhelmed with insults.
Lamentations 3:31 God will not reject forever.
Lamentations 3:32 Even though God may bring sadness, He will show mercy because of His great kindness.
Lamentations 3:33 God does not cause pain or sadness to people without reason.
Lamentations 3:34 To step on all the captives of the earth.
Lamentations 3:35 To deny a person justice in the presence of God,
Lamentations 3:36 God does not approve of ruining a person's case.
Lamentations 3:37 Who is the one who can make something happen if God has not commanded it?
Lamentations 3:38 Doesn't both good and bad come from the mouth of God?
Lamentations 3:39 Why should a living person complain, a person for being punished for their sins?
Lamentations 3:40 Let's examine our ways, and turn back to God.
Lamentations 3:41 Let's raise our hearts and hands to God in heaven.
Lamentations 3:42 We have done wrong and rebelled; you have not forgiven us.
Lamentations 3:43 You have been angry with us, chased us, killed us without mercy.
Lamentations 3:44 You have surrounded yourself with a cloud, so our prayers cannot get through.
Lamentations 3:45 You have made us like trash and garbage among the people.
Lamentations 3:46 All our enemies have spoken against us.
Lamentations 3:47 Fear and a trap have come upon us, along with ruin and destruction.
Lamentations 3:48 My eyes flow with tears for the ruin of my people.
Lamentations 3:49 My eye cries non-stop without any break.
Lamentations 3:50 Until God looks down from heaven and sees.
Lamentations 3:51 My eyes hurt my heart because of what happens to the girls of my city.
Lamentations 3:52 My enemies chased me hard, like a bird, for no reason.
Lamentations 3:53 They have ended my life in the prison, and thrown a stone at me.
Lamentations 3:54 Water poured over my head; then I thought, I am finished.
Lamentations 3:55 I called your name, God, from the deep pit.
Lamentations 3:56 You have heard my voice; do not ignore me when I sigh and cry out.
Lamentations 3:57 You came close when I called you; you said, Don't be afraid.
Lamentations 3:58 God, you have fought for my soul; you have saved my life.
Lamentations 3:59 God, you have seen the wrong done to me: judge my case.
Lamentations 3:60 You have seen all their revenge and all their plans against me.
Lamentations 3:61 You have heard their insults, God, and all their plans against me.
Lamentations 3:62 The words of those against me and their plans all day long.
Lamentations 3:63 I see them when they sit and when they stand; I am their music.
Lamentations 3:64 Give them what they deserve, God, based on what they have done.
Lamentations 3:65 Make their hearts sad, and put your curse on them.
Lamentations 3:66 Punish and wipe them out in anger from beneath the skies of God.

Lamentations 4:1 The gold has lost its shine! The purest gold is no longer bright! The sacred stones are scattered at the beginning of every street.
Lamentations 4:2 The valuable children of Zion, once worth as much as fine gold, are now treated like common clay pots made by a potter.
Lamentations 4:3 Sea creatures nurse their young, but my people have become heartless, like ostriches in the desert.
Lamentations 4:4 The baby's tongue sticks to the top of its mouth because it's so thirsty; the little children beg for bread, but nobody gives any to them.
Lamentations 4:5 People who ate fine foods are now alone in the streets; those who wore red clothes hug trash heaps.
Lamentations 4:6 The punishment for my people's wrongs is worse than what Sodom faced, which was destroyed suddenly without anyone helping.
Lamentations 4:7 Her holy people were cleaner than snow, they were brighter than milk, their bodies were redder than jewels, and they shone like sapphires.
Lamentations 4:8 Their faces are darker than black; they are unrecognizable in the streets: their skin sticks to their bones; it is dried up and has become like a stick.
Lamentations 4:9 People killed by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger, for the hungry waste away, suffering for lack of food from the fields.
Lamentations 4:10 Compassionate women have cooked their own children; they became their food during my people's ruin.
Lamentations 4:11 God has carried out his anger; he has unleashed his intense wrath and started a fire in Zion that has consumed its foundations.
Lamentations 4:12 Earth's rulers and everyone living in the world would not have believed that the foe and enemy could come into Jerusalem's gates.
Lamentations 4:13 Because her prophets sinned and her priests did wrong, spilling the blood of innocent people among her,
Lamentations 4:14 They wandered around like blind people in the streets; they made themselves dirty with blood, so no one could touch their clothes.
Lamentations 4:15 They called out to them, "Leave; you are unclean; go away, do not touch." As they ran and roamed, among the nations it was said, "They will not stay there anymore."
Lamentations 4:16 God's anger has scattered them; He will no longer look after them: they did not respect the priests, they did not honor the old people.
Lamentations 4:17 We keep looking for help that never comes, and we have waited for a country that cannot rescue us.
Lamentations 4:18 They chase us so we can't walk in our streets; our end is close, our days are over, for our end has arrived.
Lamentations 4:19 Our enemies chase us faster than eagles in the sky; they chased us on the mountains and set traps for us in the desert.
Lamentations 4:20 The one we breathed through, God's chosen one, was captured by them, and we thought we would live safely under his protection even among foreign nations.
Lamentations 4:21 Be happy and glad, you daughter of Edom, living in the land of Uz; the cup will also come to you: you will get drunk and undress.
Lamentations 4:22 Your punishment is finished, daughter of Zion; you won't be taken away anymore: but he will punish your sins, daughter of Edom; he will expose your wrongs.

Lamentations 5:1 Remember, God, what has happened to us; look, and see our disgrace.
Lamentations 5:2 Our property has gone to outsiders, our homes to foreigners.
Lamentations 5:3 We are like children without parents; our mothers are like women whose husbands have died.
Lamentations 5:4 We have to buy our own water to drink; we must pay for the wood we use.
Lamentations 5:5 We are persecuted and work hard without rest.
Lamentations 5:6 We have submitted to the Egyptians and Assyrians to have enough bread.
Lamentations 5:7 Our ancestors did wrong, they are gone; and we suffer for their sins.
Lamentations 5:8 Slaves have become our masters: no one saves us from their power.
Lamentations 5:9 We get our bread at the risk of our lives because of the danger in the desert.
Lamentations 5:10 Our skin turned very dark as if burned because of the terrible hunger.
Lamentations 5:11 They assaulted the women in Zion, and the young women in the towns of Judah.
Lamentations 5:12 Leaders are hung by their hands; the faces of the old are not respected.
Lamentations 5:13 They made the young men work at grinding grain, and the children stumbled under heavy loads of wood.
Lamentations 5:14 The older leaders no longer sit in the city gates, and the young men have stopped their music.
Lamentations 5:15 Our happiness has ended; our dancing has changed to sadness.
Lamentations 5:16 Our crown has fallen: sad for us, because we have done wrong!
Lamentations 5:17 Because of this, we are discouraged; for these things, our vision is blurred.
Lamentations 5:18 Because Mount Zion is empty, foxes walk on it.
Lamentations 5:19 You, God, last forever; your rule goes on from one generation to the next.
Lamentations 5:20 Why do you forget us forever and abandon us for such a long time?
Lamentations 5:21 Bring us back to you, God, and we will return; make our days like they used to be.
Lamentations 5:22 You have completely rejected us; you are very angry with us.

Ezekiel 1:1 In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, while I was with the captives by the Chebar River, the sky opened, and I saw visions from God.
