Ezekiel 1:2 On the fifth day of the month, during the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's capture,
Ezekiel 1:3 God's message came directly to Ezekiel the priest, Buzi's son, in the Chaldeans' land by the Chebar river; and God's power was with him.
Ezekiel 1:4 I looked and saw a storm coming from the north. It had a big cloud and fire swirling inside it. It was shining, and from the center, it glowed like amber in the fire.
Ezekiel 1:5 From within it came four living beings that looked like people.
Ezekiel 1:6 Each one had four faces, and each one had four wings.
Ezekiel 1:7 Their feet were straight, and the bottoms of their feet were like a calf's hoof; they shone like polished bronze.
Ezekiel 1:8 They had human hands under their wings on all four sides, and all four had faces and wings.
Ezekiel 1:9 Their wings touched each other; they did not turn as they moved; each one went straight ahead.
Ezekiel 1:10 Each of them had a human face, and each had a lion's face on the right side. Each also had an ox's face on the left side, and each of them had an eagle's face.
Ezekiel 1:11 Their faces looked like this: their wings stretched up; each had two wings touching another's, and two covered their bodies.
Ezekiel 1:12 They all went straight ahead; wherever the spirit wanted to go, they went, without turning as they moved.
Ezekiel 1:13 The living creatures looked like glowing, burning coals and bright lamps moving up and down among them; the fire was bright and lightning flashed from the fire.
Ezekiel 1:14 The living creatures moved quickly back and forth, like a flash of lightning.
Ezekiel 1:15 As I watched the living beings, I saw one wheel on the ground next to the living beings, with its four sides.
Ezekiel 1:16 The wheels looked and were made like shiny yellow-green stones, and all four were alike; each one seemed to be a wheel inside another wheel.
Ezekiel 1:17 When they moved, they went in four directions and did not turn as they moved.
Ezekiel 1:18 The rims of the wheels were tall and frightening, and they were covered with eyes all around the four of them.
Ezekiel 1:19 When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved with them; and when the living creatures rose from the ground, the wheels also rose.
Ezekiel 1:20 Wherever the spirit wanted to go, they went; that's where their spirit aimed to go, and the wheels rose along with them, because the spirit of the living being was in the wheels.
Ezekiel 1:21 When they moved, these moved; when they stopped, these stopped; and when they rose from the ground, the wheels rose too, because the spirit of the living being was in the wheels.
Ezekiel 1:22 The appearance of the sky above the living creatures' heads was like a frightening, clear crystal spread out over their heads.
Ezekiel 1:23 Under the sky, their wings were straight, facing each other. Each one had two wings covering one side of its body and two wings covering the other side.
Ezekiel 1:24 As they moved, I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of mighty waters, like God's voice, a sound of talking, like the sound of an army: when they stopped, they lowered their wings.
Ezekiel 1:25 A voice came from above the sky when they stood still and lowered their wings.
Ezekiel 1:26 Above the sky above their heads was something that looked like a throne made from blue sapphire, and on that throne was a figure that looked like a man.
Ezekiel 1:27 I saw something that looked like amber, with fire inside and around it, from the middle up and from the middle down; it looked like fire and was bright all around.
Ezekiel 1:28 Like a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the shining light around it. That was what the glory of God looked like. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard someone speaking.

Ezekiel 2:1 He said to me, "Human, stand on your feet, and I will talk to you."
Ezekiel 2:2 The spirit came into me as he spoke to me and put me on my feet, so I could hear the one who was speaking to me.
Ezekiel 2:3 He told me, "Human, I am sending you to the people of Israel. They are a nation that has rebelled against me. Both they and their ancestors have sinned against me up to this very day.
Ezekiel 2:4 They are bold and stubborn children. I am sending you to them; you will tell them, 'This is what God says.'
Ezekiel 2:5 Whether they listen or not (because they are stubborn), they will realize that a prophet has been with them.
Ezekiel 2:6 You, human, don't be scared of them or their words, even if you're with thorns and live among scorpions. Don't fear what they say or get upset by their looks, even if they are defiant.
Ezekiel 2:7 You must tell them my words, whether they listen or not, because they are very rebellious.
Ezekiel 2:8 But you, human, listen to what I tell you; don't be rebellious like those rebels: open your mouth and eat what I give you.
Ezekiel 2:9 When I looked, I saw a hand reaching out to me with a scroll in it.
Ezekiel 2:10 He showed it to me; it had writing on the front and back, and it said there were sadness, crying, and terrible pain.

Ezekiel 3:1 He also told me, "Human, eat what you find; eat this scroll, and then go and talk to the people of Israel."
Ezekiel 3:2 I opened my mouth, and he made me eat the scroll.
Ezekiel 3:3 He said to me, "Human, eat what you find; eat this scroll, and go speak to the house of Israel." So I opened my mouth, and he gave me the scroll to eat. And he said to me, "Son of man, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I give you." So I ate, and it was in my mouth like honey in sweetness.
Ezekiel 3:4 He told me, "Human, go to the people of Israel and talk to them with my words."
Ezekiel 3:5 You are not sent to people with a strange language, but to the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 3:6 Not to people with unfamiliar speech and difficult language that you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
Ezekiel 3:7 But the people of Israel will not listen to you because they don't listen to me; all the people of Israel are stubborn and hard-hearted.
Ezekiel 3:8 Look, I have made your face tough against their faces, and your forehead tough against their foreheads.
Ezekiel 3:9 I have made your forehead as hard as the hardest rock: do not fear them or be frightened by their faces, even if they are a stubborn people.
Ezekiel 3:10 He also told me, "Human, take all my words that I will tell you into your heart, and listen with your ears."
Ezekiel 3:11 Go to the captives, to your people's children, talk to them and say, 'This is what God says,' whether they listen or not.
Ezekiel 3:12 Then the spirit lifted me up, and I heard a loud sound behind me. It said, "Praise the glory of God from where He is."
Ezekiel 3:13 I also heard the sound of the living creatures' wings touching each other, the sound of the wheels beside them, and the sound of a loud rush.
Ezekiel 3:14 The Spirit lifted me up and took me away. I felt bitter and angry inside, but God's hand was powerfully on me.
Ezekiel 3:15 I went to the captives at Telabib, who lived by the Chebar River, and I sat with them. I stayed there, shocked, for seven days.
Ezekiel 3:16 After seven days, God spoke to me, saying,
Ezekiel 3:17 Human, I have appointed you as a lookout for the people of Israel: so listen to what I say and warn them for me.
Ezekiel 3:18 When I tell a bad person they will die and you don't warn them or tell them to stop their bad ways to save their life, that person will die for their wrongs, but I will hold you responsible for their death.
Ezekiel 3:19 But if you warn the bad person, and they do not stop being bad or change their bad ways, they will die because of their sins; but you have saved yourself.
Ezekiel 3:20 When a good person stops doing right and does wrong, and if I make him fall, he will die. Because you did not warn him, he will die for his sin, and his good deeds will be forgotten; but I will hold you responsible for his death.
Ezekiel 3:21 If you warn a good person not to sin, and they don't sin, they will surely live because they listened to the warning, and you have saved yourself too.
Ezekiel 3:22 God's hand was on me, and he said, "Get up, go out to the flat land, and I will speak with you there."
Ezekiel 3:23 I got up and went out to the flat land. I saw God's glory there, just like the glory I saw by the Chebar River, and I fell down with my face to the ground.
Ezekiel 3:24 Then the spirit came into me, stood me on my feet, and talked to me, and said, "Go, lock yourself inside your house."
Ezekiel 3:25 But you, human, see, they will tie you up with ropes, and you will be bound by them, and you will not be able to move around among them.
Ezekiel 3:26 I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so you can't talk or correct them, because they are a disobedient people.
Ezekiel 3:27 But when I talk to you, I will open your mouth, and you will tell them, 'This is what God says: Whoever wants to listen, let them listen; and whoever doesn't, let them not listen.' They are stubborn people.

Ezekiel 4:1 You too, human, get a clay tablet, put it in front of you, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem.
Ezekiel 4:2 Surround it with a siege, make a wall against it, pile up dirt against it; put a camp around it, and place battering rams against it all around.
Ezekiel 4:3 Also, get an iron pan and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Face it and it will be under siege, and you will be the attacker. This will be a sign for the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 4:4 Lie on your left side and take on Israel's sins. For as many days as you lie there, you'll carry their sins.
Ezekiel 4:5 I have put on you the years of their wrongs, equal to the number of days, three hundred and ninety days: so you will carry the wrongs of the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 4:6 After you finish those days, lie on your right side again, and you will carry the sin of Judah's people for 40 days; I have set each day equal to one year.
Ezekiel 4:7 So you will look towards Jerusalem under attack, show your arm, and speak against it.
Ezekiel 4:8 Look, I will tie you up so you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have finished the time of your siege.
Ezekiel 4:9 Gather some wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Put them in a container and use them to make bread for yourself. Eat it for the 390 days you lie on your side.
Ezekiel 4:10 The food you will eat must be weighed—twenty shekels each day. Eat it at regular times.
Ezekiel 4:11 You will also drink a measured amount of water, one-sixth of a hin; you will drink it at set times.
Ezekiel 4:12 You will eat it like barley bread and cook it over human waste where they can see you.
Ezekiel 4:13 God said, "The people of Israel will eat unclean bread among the foreign nations where I will send them."
Ezekiel 4:14 I said, "Oh God! Look, I have kept my soul clean. Since I was young until now, I have never eaten anything that died by itself or was torn apart, nor have I ever put disgusting meat in my mouth."
Ezekiel 4:15 He told me, "Look, I have given you cow poop instead of human poop, and you will use it to cook your bread."
Ezekiel 4:16 He also told me, "Human, look, I will make food scarce in Jerusalem: they will ration bread and eat it anxiously; they will measure water and drink it in shock."
Ezekiel 4:17 They will need bread and water, be shocked at each other, and waste away because of their wrongdoing.

Ezekiel 5:1 You, human, use a sharp knife, use a razor like a barber, and shave your head and beard: then use scales to weigh and separate the hair.
Ezekiel 5:2 You must burn a third of it in the city center when the siege ends. Take another third and hit it with a knife. Scatter the last third in the wind, and I will chase them with a sword.
Ezekiel 5:3 You should also take a few of them and tie them in the hem of your clothing.
Ezekiel 5:4 Then take some more, throw them into the fire, and burn them; from there a fire will spread to all the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 5:5 God says, "This is Jerusalem: I have placed it at the center of the nations and lands that surround it."
Ezekiel 5:6 She has made my rules more evil than the nations, and my laws more than the countries around her: they have rejected my rules and laws, they have not followed them.
Ezekiel 5:7 Therefore, God says: Because you have grown more than the countries around you and have not followed my rules, nor kept my decisions, nor acted according to the rules of the countries around you;
Ezekiel 5:8 So God says: "Look, I am against you. I will judge you where everyone can see."
Ezekiel 5:9 I will do to you what I have never done before, and will never do again, because of all your terrible actions.
Ezekiel 5:10 So parents will eat their children among you, and children will eat their parents. I will judge you, and those of you who survive, I will spread in every direction.
Ezekiel 5:11 So, as I live, says God; because you made my sanctuary unclean with all your hateful things and horrible acts, I will reduce you; I won't look away or feel sorry for you.
Ezekiel 5:12 One third of you will die from disease and hunger in your midst, another third will be killed by the sword surrounding you, and I will scatter the last third to every direction and chase them with a sword.
Ezekiel 5:13 My anger will be fulfilled, and I will place my fury on them until I am satisfied. Then they will realize that I, God, have said this because of my intense passion, once I have carried out my fury on them.
Ezekiel 5:14 I will make you empty and a disgrace among the nearby nations, for everyone passing by to see.
Ezekiel 5:15 It will be a shame and an insult, a lesson and a shock to the countries around you, when I judge you with anger, rage, and harsh warnings. I, God, have said this.
Ezekiel 5:16 When I send the bad arrows of hunger that will destroy you, which I'll send to ruin you, I'll make the famine worse and break your bread supply.
Ezekiel 5:17 I will bring hunger and wild animals to you, and they will take away your people. Disease and bloodshed will sweep through you, and I will attack you with war. I, God, have said this.

Ezekiel 6:1 God spoke to me and said,
Ezekiel 6:2 Human, look towards Israel's mountains and speak against them.
Ezekiel 6:3 Speak, mountains of Israel, listen to God's message. God says to the mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys; I will bring a sword against you and destroy your high places.
Ezekiel 6:4 Your altars will be empty, and your statues will be smashed; I will make your dead bodies fall in front of your idols.
Ezekiel 6:5 I will place the dead bodies of the Israelites in front of their idols, and I will spread your bones around your altars.
Ezekiel 6:6 In all the places you live, the cities will be ruined, and the worship sites will be empty; so your altars will be ruined and left empty, your statues will be smashed and stopped, and your symbols will be chopped down, and your creations will be destroyed.
Ezekiel 6:7 The dead will fall among you, and you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 6:8 I will still leave some of you alive, so you can escape the sword in other nations when you are spread out among the countries.
Ezekiel 6:9 Those who survive among you will remember me in the countries where they are prisoners because I am hurt by their unfaithful hearts that have turned away from me and by their eyes that desire their idols. They will hate themselves for all the wrongs they have done.
Ezekiel 6:10 They will understand that I am God, and that I did not threaten to bring this disaster on them for no reason.
Ezekiel 6:11 God says: Hit with your hand, stomp with your foot, and say, "Oh no, because of all the bad things Israel has done!" They will die by war, hunger, and disease.
Ezekiel 6:12 Someone far away will die from disease; someone close will be killed by the sword; and anyone left and trapped will die from hunger. This is how I will show my anger on them.
Ezekiel 6:13 Then you will know that I am God, when their killed men will be around their idols near their altars, on every high hill, on all mountain peaks, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, where they burned sweet smells for all their idols.
Ezekiel 6:14 I will reach out my hand against them, make their land empty and even more barren than the desert near Diblath, everywhere they live; and they will know that I am God.

Ezekiel 7:1 God's message came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 7:2 Also, you human, this is what God says to the land of Israel: An end has come to all parts of the land.
Ezekiel 7:3 The end has come for you, and I will send my anger on you. I will judge you by your actions and punish you for all your wrongdoings.
Ezekiel 7:4 I will not look away from you or feel sorry for you. I will make you face the results of your actions, and your horrible sins will surround you. Then you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 7:5 God says: An evil, just one evil, is coming.
Ezekiel 7:6 The end has come, the end is here: it waits for you; look, it has arrived.
Ezekiel 7:7 Morning has arrived for you who live in the land: the time has come, a day of trouble is close, and the mountains will not echo with noise again.
Ezekiel 7:8 I will soon pour out my anger on you, finish my anger on you, and I will judge you by your actions and repay you for all your wrongs.
Ezekiel 7:9 I will not show mercy or pity; I will repay you for your actions and the evil deeds among you; then you will know that I am God who strikes.
Ezekiel 7:10 See the day, see, it has come: the morning has started; power has grown, arrogance has appeared.
Ezekiel 7:11 Violence has grown into a tool of evil: none will survive, not the many, nor any individuals; there will be no mourning for them.
Ezekiel 7:12 The time has come, the day is near: buyers should not be happy, nor sellers sad, because anger will affect everyone.
Ezekiel 7:13 The seller won't get back what they sold, even while they're still alive. The prophecy is about everyone, and they won't come back. No one will survive because of their wrongdoing.
Ezekiel 7:14 They have sounded the trumpet to get everyone ready, but no one goes to battle because my anger is on all of them.
Ezekiel 7:15 Outside, there is war, and inside, there is disease and hunger. Whoever is in the fields will die by war, and whoever is in the city will be consumed by hunger and disease.
Ezekiel 7:16 Those who survive will escape and be on the mountains, like valley doves, all of them sad, each one for their own wrongs.
Ezekiel 7:17 Everyone's hands will be limp, and every knee will be as weak as water.
Ezekiel 7:18 They will also wear rough cloth, and terror will cover them; all faces will show shame, and every head will be shaved.
Ezekiel 7:19 They will throw their silver in the streets, and their gold will be taken away. Their silver and gold won't save them on the day of God's anger. They won't satisfy their needs or fill themselves with it, because it is the cause of their sins.
Ezekiel 7:20 About his beautiful jewelry, he wore it with greatness. But they put their disgusting idols and things there: so, I have taken it away from them.
Ezekiel 7:21 I will give it to strangers to take, and to the evil people of the world to steal; and they will make it dirty.
Ezekiel 7:22 I will also turn my face away from them, and they will make my secret place dirty; for invaders will go into it and spoil it.
Ezekiel 7:23 Make a chain, because the country is filled with violent acts, and the city is filled with violence.
Ezekiel 7:24 So I will send the worst foreigners, and they will take over their homes. I will end the pride of the powerful, and their sacred places will be made dirty.
Ezekiel 7:25 Destruction comes; and they will look for peace, but there will be none.
Ezekiel 7:26 Trouble will follow trouble, and rumor will come after rumor; then they will look for guidance from a prophet, but the priest will have lost the law, and the elders will have no advice to give.
Ezekiel 7:27 The king will be sad, the leader will be filled with emptiness, and the people's hands will shake with fear: I will treat them as they have acted, and I will judge them by what they deserve; and they will understand that I am God.

Ezekiel 8:1 In the sixth year, the sixth month, and on the fifth day, while I was sitting in my house and the leaders of Judah were sitting before me, the power of God came over me.
Ezekiel 8:2 I saw something that looked like fire below his waist, and from his waist up, he shone brightly, like amber.
Ezekiel 8:3 He reached out like a hand and grabbed my hair; the spirit lifted me up between the ground and sky, and in a vision from God, took me to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner north gate, where there was a place for the jealousy-causing idol.
Ezekiel 8:4 I saw the glory of Israel's God there, just like the vision I had in the open field.
Ezekiel 8:5 He told me, "Human, look up now to the north." So I looked up to the north, and I saw at the entrance of the altar's gate this idol that makes God jealous.
Ezekiel 8:6 He said to me again, "Human, do you see what they are doing? The terrible things the people of Israel are doing here, making me want to stay far from my holy place? But look again, and you will see even worse things."
Ezekiel 8:7 He took me to the entrance of the courtyard; when I looked, I saw a hole in the wall.
Ezekiel 8:8 Then he said to me, "Human, start digging in the wall." So I began to dig in the wall, and soon I found a door.
Ezekiel 8:9 He said to me, "Go in and see the terrible things they are doing here."
Ezekiel 8:10 So I went inside and saw; and look, all kinds of crawling creatures, horrible animals, and the idols of Israel, drawn on the walls all around.
Ezekiel 8:11 Seventy elders of Israel stood in front of them, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan among them, each holding an incense burner, and a large cloud of incense rose up.
Ezekiel 8:12 He said to me, "Human, have you seen what Israel's elders do in secret, each in their own room of pictures? They say, 'God does not see us; God has left the earth.'"
Ezekiel 8:13 He also told me, "Turn again, and you will see even worse things they are doing."
Ezekiel 8:14 Then he led me to the entrance of God's temple gate facing north; and there, I saw women crying for Tammuz.
Ezekiel 8:15 He said to me, "Have you seen this, human? Look again, and you will see even worse things than these."
Ezekiel 8:16 He took me to the inner yard of God's house, and I saw at the temple door, between the entrance and the altar, about 25 men. They turned their backs to God's temple and faced east, worshiping the sun in the east.
Ezekiel 8:17 He asked me, "Have you seen this, human? Do the people of Judah think it's no big deal that they do such disgusting things here? They fill the land with violence and keep making me angry. Look, they are even insulting me right to my face."
Ezekiel 8:18 So I will act in anger. I won't look away or feel sorry. Even if they cry loudly in my ears, I still won't listen.

Ezekiel 9:1 He also shouted loudly in my ears, saying, "Tell those in charge of the city to come here, each with his weapon for destruction in hand."
Ezekiel 9:2 Look, six men came from the direction of the upper gate to the north, each with a weapon for killing in his hand; one of them was dressed in linen, with a writing kit at his side. They came in and stood by the bronze altar.
Ezekiel 9:3 God's bright presence, which had been over the cherubim, rose to the entrance of the temple. God then spoke to the man in linen clothes who had a writing kit at his side.
Ezekiel 9:4 God told him, "Walk through the center of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the people who are upset and cry about all the bad things happening there."
Ezekiel 9:5 He told the others as I could hear, "Follow him through the city and strike. Show no mercy and feel no pity."
Ezekiel 9:6 Kill all the old and young, girls, little children, and women, but do not hurt anyone with the mark; start at my holy place. Then they started with the elders in front of the house.
Ezekiel 9:7 He told them, "Make the temple unclean and fill the courtyards with the bodies of the dead. Go out." So they went out and killed people in the city.
Ezekiel 9:8 While they were being killed and I was spared, I fell facedown, cried out, and said, "Oh God! Will you wipe out the remaining people of Israel by pouring out your anger on Jerusalem?"
Ezekiel 9:9 He told me, "Israel and Judah's sin is very big, and the land is full of blood, and the city is full of wrongdoing: because they say, 'God has left the earth, and God does not see.'"
Ezekiel 9:10 I will not show mercy or feel sorry either; I will give them what they deserve, and they will feel the consequences of their actions.
Ezekiel 9:11 Look, the man in linen clothes with a writing kit at his side reported back, saying, "I have done what you told me to do."

Ezekiel 10:1 I looked, and saw above the cherubim there was something like a blue sapphire stone above them, looking like a throne.
Ezekiel 10:2 He said to the man in linen clothes, "Go between the wheels, under the cherub, take coals of fire from between the cherubs, and spread them over the city." He did this while I watched.
Ezekiel 10:3 The cherubim were on the right side of the house when the man entered, and a cloud filled the inner yard.
Ezekiel 10:4 Then God's glory rose up from the cherub and paused above the entrance of the temple; the temple became filled with the cloud, and the courtyard shone with the brightness of God's glory.
Ezekiel 10:5 The sound of the cherubim's wings could be heard all the way to the outer courtyard, like the voice of God when he speaks.
Ezekiel 10:6 When he gave the order to the man in linen clothes, "Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim," he went in and stood next to the wheels.
Ezekiel 10:7 One angel reached out from between the angels to the fire that was between them, took some, and put it into the hands of the person dressed in linen; who then took it and left.
Ezekiel 10:8 In the cherubs, there was something that looked like a man's hand below their wings.
Ezekiel 10:9 When I looked, I saw four wheels next to the cherubim, one wheel by each cherub, and the wheels looked like the color of a beryl stone.
Ezekiel 10:10 As for how they looked, all four of them were alike, like a wheel inside another wheel.
Ezekiel 10:11 When they moved, they went on their four sides. They didn't turn when they moved, but followed the direction their head faced without turning as they went.
Ezekiel 10:12 Their whole body, backs, hands, wings, and the wheels were covered with eyes all around, even the wheels each of the four creatures had.
Ezekiel 10:13 The wheels were called 'wheel' as I heard.
Ezekiel 10:14 Each one had four faces: the first was a cherub's face, the second a man's face, the third a lion's face, and the fourth an eagle's face.
Ezekiel 10:15 The cherubim rose up. This is the living being I saw by the Chebar River.
Ezekiel 10:16 When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved with them. And when the cherubim rose up from the ground with their wings, the wheels stayed close beside them without turning away.
Ezekiel 10:17 When they stood still, these also stood still; and when they rose up, these also rose up, because the spirit of the living being was in them.
Ezekiel 10:18 God's glory left the entrance of the temple and hovered above the cherubim.
Ezekiel 10:19 The cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the ground before me: as they moved away, the wheels were next to them. Each one stopped at the entrance of the east gate of God's temple, and God's glory was above them.
Ezekiel 10:20 This is the creature I saw by the river Chebar under Israel's God, and I knew they were cherubim.
Ezekiel 10:21 Each had four faces and four wings, and under their wings were what looked like human hands.
Ezekiel 10:22 The way their faces looked was the same as those I saw by the Chebar river; they looked the same and moved straight ahead.

Ezekiel 11:1 The spirit picked me up and took me to the east entrance of God's house, facing east. There, at the entrance gate, I saw twenty-five men. Among them were Jaazaniah, Azur's son, and Pelatiah, Benaiah's son, who were leaders of the people.
Ezekiel 11:2 He said to me, "Human, these are the people who plan trouble and give evil advice in this city."
Ezekiel 11:3 They say, "It's not close; let's build houses: this city is the pot, and we are the meat."
Ezekiel 11:4 So tell them what will happen, speak out, human.
Ezekiel 11:5 God's Spirit came on me and He said, "Speak: This is what God says; you, the people of Israel, have said these things, and I know every thought that comes into your minds."
Ezekiel 11:6 You have increased the number of your dead in this city, and you have filled its streets with the dead.
Ezekiel 11:7 So God says: "The people you killed and left in the city are like meat, and the city is like a pot. But I will take you out of the city."
Ezekiel 11:8 You have been afraid of the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, says God.
Ezekiel 11:9 I will take you out of there, give you to foreigners, and carry out punishments on you.
Ezekiel 11:10 You will die by the sword; I will judge you at Israel's border; and you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 11:11 This city won't be your cooking pot, nor will you be the meat inside it; instead, I will judge you at Israel's border.
Ezekiel 11:12 You will understand that I am God because you have not followed my laws or done what I said but have acted like the foreigners around you.
Ezekiel 11:13 When I was prophesying, Pelatiah, Benaiah's son, died. I fell face down, shouted loudly, and said, "Ah God! Are you going to completely destroy what's left of Israel?"
Ezekiel 11:14 God spoke to me again, saying,
Ezekiel 11:15 Human, your relatives, your own family, and all the people of Israel are those to whom the people of Jerusalem have said, "Stay away from God: this land is ours to own."
Ezekiel 11:16 So say, God says this: Even though I sent them away among other nations, and I have spread them across different lands, I will still be like a small place of safety for them in the lands where they go.
Ezekiel 11:17 So say this: God says, "I will bring you together from the people, gather you from the countries where you were spread out, and I will give you the land of Israel."
Ezekiel 11:18 They will go there and remove all its disgusting things and all its horrors.
Ezekiel 11:19 I will give them one heart, and put a new spirit in you; I will remove the heart of stone from their body, and give them a heart of flesh.
Ezekiel 11:20 So they can follow my rules, obey my commands, and do them: and they will be my people, and I will be their God.
Ezekiel 11:21 But as for those who follow their wicked hearts and disgusting actions, I will make sure their actions come back on them, says God.
Ezekiel 11:22 Then the cherubim lifted their wings, and the wheels were beside them; and God's glory was above them.
Ezekiel 11:23 God's glory rose from the center of the city and rested on the mountain to the east of the city.
Ezekiel 11:24 Later, the spirit lifted me up. In a vision from God's spirit, I was taken to the land of the exiles in Chaldea. There, the vision I saw left me.
Ezekiel 11:25 Then I told the captives everything that God had shown me.

Ezekiel 12:1 God's message came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 12:2 Human, you live among people who refuse to obey, who have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear, because they are defiant.
Ezekiel 12:3 So, you human, get your things ready for moving. Move during the day while they watch. You will go from one place to another while they watch. Maybe they will think about it, even though they are stubborn.
Ezekiel 12:4 Take your belongings out during the day while they watch, as if you're getting ready to move. Then leave in the evening while they watch, as if you're going into exile.
Ezekiel 12:5 Dig through the wall while they watch, and take stuff out that way.
Ezekiel 12:6 Carry it on your shoulders in front of them and take it out at dusk. Cover your face so you can't see the land, because I have made you a symbol for the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 12:7 I did as I was told. During the day, I took out my things like prisoners do, and at night, I made a hole in the wall with my hands. I took my things out at dusk and carried them on my shoulder while they watched.
Ezekiel 12:8 In the morning, God's message came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 12:9 Human, hasn't the house of Israel, the defiant house, asked you, "What are you doing?"
Ezekiel 12:10 Tell them, 'This is what God says: This message is about the leader in Jerusalem and all the people of Israel who are with him.'
Ezekiel 12:11 I am your sign: just as I did, it will happen to them: they will move and be taken as captives.
Ezekiel 12:12 The leader among them will carry their load on his shoulder at dusk and leave. They will break through the wall to get out. He will cover his face so he can't see the ground.
Ezekiel 12:13 I will also spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my trap. I will take him to Babylon in the land of the Chaldeans, but he will not see it, even though he will die there.
Ezekiel 12:14 I will scatter in all directions everyone who is with him to support him, along with all his troops; and I will chase them with a sword.
Ezekiel 12:15 People will understand that I am God when I spread them among different nations and scatter them across the countries.
Ezekiel 12:16 I will let some of them survive war, hunger, and disease, so they can tell all their sins to the foreign people where they go; then they will understand that I am God.
Ezekiel 12:17 God spoke to me again, saying,
Ezekiel 12:18 Human, eat your bread with shaking, and drink your water with trembling and anxiety.
Ezekiel 12:19 Tell the people of the country, "God says to the people of Jerusalem and Israel: They will eat their bread with worry and drink their water in shock, so their country will be empty of everything, because of the violence of everyone living there."
Ezekiel 12:20 The cities where people live will be destroyed, the land will become empty, and you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 12:21 God spoke to me and said,
Ezekiel 12:22 Human, what is the saying you have in Israel: "Time goes on, and every promise fails"?
Ezekiel 12:23 So tell them, 'This is what God says: I will end this saying, and it will no longer be quoted in Israel. Tell them instead: The time is near when every vision will come true.'
Ezekiel 12:24 There will be no more false visions or flattering predictions in Israel.
Ezekiel 12:25 I am God: I will speak, and what I say will happen; it won't be delayed anymore. In your time, O defiant people, I'll say my word and make it happen, says God.
Ezekiel 12:26 God spoke to me again, saying.
Ezekiel 12:27 Human, look, the people of Israel say, "The vision he sees is for the distant future, and he talks about times that are far away."
Ezekiel 12:28 Tell them this: God says, "My words will not be delayed anymore, but what I have said will happen."

Ezekiel 13:1 God's message came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 13:2 Human, speak against the false prophets of Israel. Tell those who predict from their own thoughts, listen to God's message.
Ezekiel 13:3 God says, "Bad things will come to the silly prophets who follow their own thoughts and have seen nothing!"
Ezekiel 13:4 Israel, your prophets are like foxes in the wastelands.
Ezekiel 13:5 You did not go into the breaks or fix the wall for Israel to hold strong in battle on God's day.
Ezekiel 13:6 They have seen lies and false visions, claiming, "God says," when God has not sent them, and they have led others to hope they would affirm the word.
Ezekiel 13:7 Haven't you seen a false vision and told a false prophecy, claiming God said it when I did not speak?
Ezekiel 13:8 So God says, "Because you have spoken nonsense and seen false things, I am against you," says God.
Ezekiel 13:9 I will act against the false prophets who see empty visions and tell lies. They will not join my people's gatherings, won't be listed among the people of Israel, and won't enter Israel's land. Then you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 13:10 Because they misled my people, saying, "Peace," when there was no peace, and someone built a wall, and others covered it with weak mortar.
Ezekiel 13:11 Tell those who cover it with weak plaster that it will collapse: a heavy rain will pour down, large hailstones will fall, and a fierce wind will tear it apart.
Ezekiel 13:12 Look, when the wall has fallen, won't people ask you, "Where is the plaster you used to cover it?"
Ezekiel 13:13 So God says: I will tear it apart with a violent wind in my anger; there will be a massive rainstorm in my rage, and huge hailstones in my fury to destroy it.
Ezekiel 13:14 I will knock down the wall you've covered with weak mortar, it will fall to the ground, its base will be exposed, it will collapse, and you will be destroyed in its ruin. Then you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 13:15 I will finish my anger on the wall and on those who covered it with weak plaster, and I will tell you, The wall is gone, and so are those who plastered it.
Ezekiel 13:16 The prophets of Israel who speak about Jerusalem and who have visions of peace for it, when there is no peace, says God.
Ezekiel 13:17 You, human, turn to the women of your people who speak their own thoughts as if from God; and speak out against them.
Ezekiel 13:18 Say this, "God says: Bad luck to the women who sew cushions for every wrist and make veils for people of every height to trap lives! Are you trapping my people's lives and saving the lives of others who come to you?"
Ezekiel 13:19 Will you dishonor God among the people for some barley and bread, by killing those who should not die and keeping alive those who should not live, with your lies to those who believe them?
Ezekiel 13:20 So God says: Look, I am against your magic charms, which you use to trap souls like birds. I will rip them from your hands and free the souls you catch with them.
Ezekiel 13:21 I will tear off your veils and rescue my people from your grasp, and they will no longer be prey in your hands; then you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 13:22 You have made good people feel sad with lies, even though I did not make them sad; and you have encouraged the bad people, so they do not stop their wrong ways by promising them life.
Ezekiel 13:23 So you won't see false visions or make predictions anymore, because I will rescue my people from your control, and you will realize that I am God.

Ezekiel 14:1 Some elders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.
Ezekiel 14:2 God's message came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 14:3 Human, these people have placed their idols in their hearts, and set the sin they trip over right before themselves. Should I let them ask for my help at all?
Ezekiel 14:4 Tell them this: God says, "Any Israelite who worships idols in his heart and lets his sins lead him into trouble, and then asks a prophet for advice, I, God, will respond to him in a way that reflects his many idols."
Ezekiel 14:5 I want to capture the hearts of Israel's people, for they have all turned away from me because of their idols.
Ezekiel 14:6 Tell the people of Israel, "God says: Change your ways, stop worshiping idols, and stop doing things that are wrong."
Ezekiel 14:7 Everyone from Israel's people, or any visitor living in Israel, who turns away from me, holds idols in their heart, does wrong, and then asks a prophet about me, I, God, will give them my answer directly.
Ezekiel 14:8 I will oppose that person and make him a warning and a common saying, and I will remove him from my people; and you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 14:9 If a prophet is tricked into saying something, it's because I, God, have allowed the trick, and I will punish that prophet and remove him from among my people Israel.
Ezekiel 14:10 They will be punished for their sins, and the prophet will be punished just like the one who goes to him for advice.
Ezekiel 14:11 So that the people of Israel won't turn away from me or be unclean with their sins anymore; instead, they will be my people, and I will be their God, says God.
Ezekiel 14:12 God spoke to me again, saying,
Ezekiel 14:13 Human, when a country sins greatly against me by breaking my rules, I will reach out against that country. I will take away its supply of food, cause a famine, and remove both people and animals from it.
Ezekiel 14:14 Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were there, they could only save themselves by being good, says God.
Ezekiel 14:15 If I send harmful animals into the country, and they destroy it, making it empty so no one can pass through because of the animals:
Ezekiel 14:16 Even if these three men were there, as I live, says God, they would not save their sons or daughters; only they would be saved, but the land would be empty.
Ezekiel 14:17 If I send a sword into that land and command, "Sword, sweep across the land," and I wipe out both people and animals:
Ezekiel 14:18 Even if these three men were there, God says, they would not save their sons or daughters, but only themselves would be saved.
Ezekiel 14:19 If I send a disease into that land and express my anger with death, to remove both people and animals:
Ezekiel 14:20 Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were there, as I live, says God, they wouldn't save either son or daughter; they would only save themselves by being good.
Ezekiel 14:21 God says: What if I send my four terrible punishments to Jerusalem: war, hunger, wild animals, and disease, to kill its people and animals?
Ezekiel 14:22 Still, some people will survive and be brought out—both sons and daughters. They will come to you, and when you see how they behave and what they do, you will feel better about the disaster I have brought on Jerusalem, and all the hardship I have brought on it.
Ezekiel 14:23 They will comfort you when you see their actions, and you'll understand that I had good reasons for everything I did, says God.

Ezekiel 15:1 God spoke to me, saying,
Ezekiel 15:2 Human, what makes a grapevine better than any other tree or a branch found in the forest?
Ezekiel 15:3 Can wood from it be used to make anything? Or can someone use a piece of it to hang things on?
Ezekiel 15:4 Look, it is thrown into the fire as fuel; the fire burns up both its ends, and its middle is charred. Can it be used for any task?
Ezekiel 15:5 Look, when it was whole, it was not fit for any work: how much less will it be fit for any work now, after the fire has eaten it, and it is burned?
Ezekiel 15:6 So this is what God says: Just as a vine among forest trees that I've set aside to burn is given, so will I treat Jerusalem's people.
Ezekiel 15:7 I will be against them; they will escape one fire, but another fire will consume them; and you will know that I am God when I am against them.
Ezekiel 15:8 I will make the land empty, because they did wrong, says God.

Ezekiel 16:1 God spoke to me again, saying,
Ezekiel 16:2 Human, make Jerusalem aware of her wrongdoings.
Ezekiel 16:3 Say, God tells Jerusalem: You were born in Canaan; your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.
Ezekiel 16:4 About your birth: when you were born, no one cut your umbilical cord, cleaned you with water, rubbed you with salt, or wrapped you in cloth.
Ezekiel 16:5 No one felt sorry for you, to do these things for you, to show you kindness; but you were thrown out into the open field, hated, on the day you were born.
Ezekiel 16:6 As I passed by you and saw you covered in your own blood, I told you to live, even though you were in your blood. Yes, I told you to live.
Ezekiel 16:7 I have made you grow like a plant in the field, and you have grown large and become beautiful: your breasts have developed, and your hair has grown long, when before you were naked and had nothing.
Ezekiel 16:8 When I saw you, I noticed it was time for love. I covered you with my cloak and hid your nudity. I promised you and made an agreement with you, says God, and you became mine.
Ezekiel 16:9 I washed you with water; yes, I completely cleaned your blood off you, and I put oil on you.
Ezekiel 16:10 I dressed you in embroidered clothes, and put shoes of fine leather on you, and wrapped you in fine linen, and draped you in silk.
Ezekiel 16:11 I also gave you jewelry, put bracelets on your wrists, and a necklace around your neck.
Ezekiel 16:12 I placed a jewel on your forehead, earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.
Ezekiel 16:13 You were adorned with gold and silver; your clothes were fine linen, silk, and embroidered fabric; you ate the best flour, honey, and oil: and you were very beautiful, growing into a powerful kingdom.
Ezekiel 16:14 People everywhere talked about your beauty because it was perfect, thanks to the splendor I gave you, says God.
Ezekiel 16:15 You trusted in your beauty and became a prostitute because of your fame, offering yourself to everyone who passed by.
Ezekiel 16:16 You took your clothes to decorate your worship sites with different colors, and you acted like a prostitute there. Such things should not happen, nor should it continue.
Ezekiel 16:17 You took the beautiful jewelry I gave you, made from my gold and silver, and made male idols to worship as gods.
Ezekiel 16:18 You took your embroidered clothes and covered them with it, and you put my oil and incense in front of them.
Ezekiel 16:19 I gave you good food to eat, like fine flour, oil, and honey, but you offered it to others as a sweet smell, says God.
Ezekiel 16:20 You also took your sons and daughters, whom you had for me, and gave them to be eaten. Is this small thing part of your unfaithfulness?
Ezekiel 16:21 You killed my children and made them pass through fire.
Ezekiel 16:22 In all the wrong things you did and your unfaithfulness, you forgot your childhood days when you were naked and dirty.
Ezekiel 16:23 After all your bad behavior, (oh, how terrible for you! says God;)
Ezekiel 16:24 You have also made yourself a prominent place and set up a shrine on every street.
Ezekiel 16:25 You have set up your worship places at every street corner, and made your beauty something disgraceful. You offered yourself to everyone who walked by, multiplying your unfaithfulness.
Ezekiel 16:26 You also slept with the Egyptians, your large-bodied neighbors, and made your unfaithfulness worse, making me angry.
Ezekiel 16:27 Look, I have reached out my hand against you, reduced your daily food, and handed you over to those who dislike you, the Philistines' women, who are embarrassed by your bad behavior.
Ezekiel 16:28 You also acted like a prostitute with the Assyrians, because you were never satisfied; indeed, you acted like a prostitute with them, and still you were not satisfied.
Ezekiel 16:29 You also increased your unfaithfulness in Canaan and towards Chaldea; still, you were not satisfied.
Ezekiel 16:30 How weak is your heart, says God, when you do all these things like a bossy prostitute.
Ezekiel 16:31 You build your high spots at the top of every road and make your worship places on every street, yet you are not like a prostitute because you refuse payment.
Ezekiel 16:32 Like a wife who cheats, who chooses others over her husband!
Ezekiel 16:33 You give gifts to all prostitutes, but you give your presents to all your lovers and pay them to come to you from everywhere for your prostitution.
Ezekiel 16:34 You are different from other women in your wrongdoing because no one follows you in it. You pay others instead of being paid, so you are opposite.
Ezekiel 16:35 So, prostitute, listen to God's message.
Ezekiel 16:36 God says: Because you showed your dirtiness and were seen naked in your acts with your lovers, with all your disgusting idols, and because of the blood of your children that you gave to them;
Ezekiel 16:37 So, I will bring together all your lovers, the ones you enjoyed, and those you loved and hated. I'll have them surround you and show them your nakedness, so they can see you completely exposed.
Ezekiel 16:38 I will judge you like women who cheat in marriage and kill are judged; and I will punish you with bloody anger and jealousy.
Ezekiel 16:39 I will let them capture you, and they will destroy your important places and tear down your worship sites. They will take off your clothes, steal your beautiful jewelry, and leave you naked and empty.
Ezekiel 16:40 A group will also attack you, throw stones at you, and stab you with their swords.
Ezekiel 16:41 They will burn your houses with fire, judge you in front of many women: I will make you stop being a prostitute, and you won't pay for it anymore.
Ezekiel 16:42 I will calm my anger towards you, and my jealousy will leave you. I will be peaceful and not angry with you anymore.
Ezekiel 16:43 Because you did not remember your youth and made me unhappy with all this, I will make you pay for your actions, says God. And you will not do this shameful thing on top of all your other wrongs.
Ezekiel 16:44 Look, everyone who speaks in sayings will say this about you: "Like the mother, so is her daughter."
Ezekiel 16:45 You are your mother's daughter, hating your husband and children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who also hated their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father was an Amorite.
Ezekiel 16:46 Your older sister is Samaria, with her daughters who live to your north; and your younger sister who lives to your south is Sodom, with her daughters.
Ezekiel 16:47 You didn't follow their ways or do their terrible things: but you acted as if that was nothing and became even more corrupt than them in all you do.
Ezekiel 16:48 I am alive, says God. Your sister city, Sodom, and her daughters didn't do what you and your daughters have done.
Ezekiel 16:49 Look, the sin of your sister Sodom was pride, plenty of food, and too much free time, and her and her daughters had this, but they didn't help the poor and those in need.
Ezekiel 16:50 They were proud and did terrible things before me; so I removed them as I thought best.
Ezekiel 16:51 Samaria hasn't done even half of your sins; but you have done many more evil things than they did, and you made your sisters seem right by all the evil things you did.
Ezekiel 16:52 You who judged your sisters must now face your own shame because the sins you did are worse than theirs; they are more righteous than you. Yes, feel ashamed and bear your shame for making your sisters seem just by comparison.
Ezekiel 16:53 When I restore the fortunes of Sodom and its towns, and of Samaria and its towns, I will also restore the fortunes of your captives among them.
Ezekiel 16:54 So you can feel your own shame and be embarrassed by all that you have done, because you have been a comfort to them.
Ezekiel 16:55 When your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, go back to what they used to be, and Samaria and her daughters go back to what they used to be, then you and your daughters will also go back to what you used to be.
Ezekiel 16:56 You did not talk about your sister city Sodom when you were proud.
Ezekiel 16:57 Before your evil ways were exposed, like when you shamed the girls of Syria and everyone around them, including the girls of the Philistines who all look down on you.
Ezekiel 16:58 You have carried your wickedness and your disgusting acts, says God.
Ezekiel 16:59 God says, "I will treat you as you have acted, since you ignored the promise and broke the agreement."
Ezekiel 16:60 Even so, I will remember my promise to you from when you were young, and I will make with you a forever promise.
Ezekiel 16:61 Then you will remember your actions and feel ashamed when you accept your older and younger sisters: I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of your agreement.
Ezekiel 16:62 I will make my promise with you; and you will understand that I am God.
Ezekiel 16:63 So you will remember and feel ashamed, and never speak again because of your shame, when I forgive you for all you have done, says God.

Ezekiel 17:1 God spoke to me, saying,
Ezekiel 17:2 Human, tell a puzzle and share a story with the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 17:3 Say, 'God says: A big eagle with large wings and long feathers, full of many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top branch of the cedar tree.'
Ezekiel 17:4 He cut off the top of the young branches and took it to a land of trade; he placed it in a city of merchants.
Ezekiel 17:5 He also took some seeds from the land and planted them in a fertile area; he put them near a lot of water, like a willow tree.
Ezekiel 17:6 It grew and turned into a wide, low vine. Its branches reached out to him, and its roots were beneath him. So it became a vine, grew branches, and produced new shoots.
Ezekiel 17:7 There was also a big eagle with large wings and lots of feathers, and look, the vine turned its roots toward him and spread out its branches so that he could give it water where it was planted.
Ezekiel 17:8 It was put in good soil near plenty of water so it could grow branches and bear fruit, becoming a fine vine.
Ezekiel 17:9 Say this, "This is what God says: Will it succeed? Will he not pull out its roots and cut off its fruit so it dries up? It will dry up with all the leaves of its growth, even without strong force or many people to uproot it."
Ezekiel 17:10 Yes, look, if it is planted, will it thrive? Won't it completely dry up when the east wind blows on it? It will dry up in the beds where it sprouted.

Ezekiel 17:14 To make the kingdom humble, so it would not rise up, but by following his agreement it would remain stable.
Ezekiel 17:15 He turned against God by sending messengers to Egypt to get horses and many soldiers. Will he succeed? Can he get away with this? Or can he ignore the agreement and still be safe?
Ezekiel 17:16 I swear, says God, the king who rejected his promise and broke his agreement will die in Babylon, where he was made king.

Ezekiel 17:18 Because he looked down on his promise by breaking the agreement, after he had shaken hands, and did all these things, he will not get away.
Ezekiel 17:19 So this is what God says: As surely as I live, I will repay him for ignoring my promise and breaking my agreement right on his own head.
Ezekiel 17:20 I will set my net for him, and he will get caught in my trap. Then I will take him to Babylon and talk to him about the wrong he did to me.
Ezekiel 17:21 Everyone running away with him will be killed by the sword, and those left will be spread out in all directions. Then you will know that I, God, have said this.

Ezekiel 17:23 I will plant it on the high mountain in Israel: it will grow branches, produce fruit, and become a magnificent cedar. All kinds of birds will live underneath it, resting in the shade of its branches.
Ezekiel 17:24 All the trees in the land will know that I, God, have made the tall tree fall, raised the small tree, dried up the green tree, and made the dry tree grow. I, God, have said it and made it happen.

Ezekiel 18:1 God spoke to me once more, saying,
Ezekiel 18:2 Why do you use this saying about Israel's land: The parents ate sour grapes, and now their children's teeth feel rough?
Ezekiel 18:3 God says, as long as I live, you will not use this saying in Israel anymore.
Ezekiel 18:4 Look, every person belongs to me; just as a father's person is mine, so is a child's person mine: the person who sins will die.
Ezekiel 18:5 If a person is fair and does what is legal and right,
Ezekiel 18:6 He has not eaten on the mountains, nor looked up to the idols of Israel, nor been with his neighbor's wife, nor approached a woman during her period.
Ezekiel 18:7 He has not been unkind to others, but has returned the borrower's collateral, has not robbed anyone by force, has shared his food with the hungry, and has given clothes to those without any.
Ezekiel 18:8 He who has not lent money at interest, nor taken extra for himself, who has avoided doing wrong, and has made fair decisions between people,
Ezekiel 18:9 Has followed my rules and has kept my decisions, acting honestly; he is righteous, he will certainly live, says God.
Ezekiel 18:10 If he has a son who steals, kills, and does any of these bad things,
Ezekiel 18:11 Someone who does none of those duties, but also eats on the mountains and dishonors his neighbor's wife,
Ezekiel 18:12 Has mistreated the poor and needy, has robbed by force, has not returned what was borrowed, and has looked up to idols, has done terrible things.
Ezekiel 18:13 Lent money for interest or made a profit from it: can he live? He won't live: he did all these bad things; he will certainly die, and it's his own fault.
Ezekiel 18:14 Now, look, if he has a son who sees all the sins his father has done, thinks about it, and does not do the same,
Ezekiel 18:15 Has not eaten on the mountains, nor looked up to the idols of Israel, has not dishonored another's wife,
Ezekiel 18:16 He has not hurt anyone, has not kept anything owed, has not robbed by force, but has given food to the hungry and has clothed those without clothes.
Ezekiel 18:17 He who does not exploit the poor, who does not take interest or profit, who follows my laws and lives by my rules, will not die because of his father's sins; he will surely live.
Ezekiel 18:18 His father, because he hurt others, robbed his brother by force, and did bad things to his people, will also die for his sins.
Ezekiel 18:19 You ask, "Why doesn't the son get punished for the father's sins?" If the son follows what is legal and right, obeys all my rules, and does them, he will certainly live.
Ezekiel 18:20 The person who sins will die. A child won't be punished for a parent's wrongs, nor a parent for a child's. The good person's goodness will be their own, and the bad person's badness will be their own.
Ezekiel 18:21 If a bad person stops sinning and follows all God's laws, doing what is right and fair, they will live and not die.
Ezekiel 18:22 All the wrongs he did will not be brought up to him; by the good things he has done, he will live.
Ezekiel 18:23 Does God take pleasure in the death of the wicked? No, God wants them to turn from their evil ways and live.
Ezekiel 18:24 When someone good stops doing good, does wrong, and acts like a bad person, will they live? All the good they did won't count anymore. They will die because of their wrongs and sins.
Ezekiel 18:25 But you say, God's way isn't fair. Listen, people of Israel; isn't my way fair? Aren't your ways unfair?
Ezekiel 18:26 When a good person stops doing right and does wrong, and dies because of it, they will die because of the wrong they have done.
Ezekiel 18:27 When a bad person stops doing wrong and starts doing what is lawful and right, he will save his life.
Ezekiel 18:28 Because he thinks about it and stops doing all the wrong things he did before, he will live and not die.
Ezekiel 18:29 The people of Israel say, "God's ways are not fair." O people of Israel, aren't my ways fair? Aren't your ways unfair?
Ezekiel 18:30 So, I will judge you, people of Israel, each according to their actions, says God. Turn back and stop all your sins; then they won't destroy you.
Ezekiel 18:31 Get rid of all the wrong things you have done, and create a new heart and a new spirit for yourself. Why should you die, people of Israel?
Ezekiel 18:32 I don't want anyone to die, says God. So change your ways and live.

Ezekiel 19:3 She raised one of her cubs; it became a young lion and learned to hunt; it ate people.
Ezekiel 19:4 Other countries heard about him; he got caught in their trap, and they took him with chains to Egypt.
Ezekiel 19:5 When she saw her waiting was in vain and her hope was gone, she took another one of her young and raised it to be a young lion.
Ezekiel 19:6 He moved among lions, became a young lion, learned to hunt, and ate people.
Ezekiel 19:7 He knew their empty homes and destroyed their cities; the land was empty and completely ruined by the sound of his roar.
Ezekiel 19:8 Nations from all around trapped him with their nets, and he was caught in their hole.
Ezekiel 19:9 They locked him up with chains and took him to the king of Babylon: they kept him in prison so his voice would not be heard on Israel's mountains anymore.
Ezekiel 19:10 Your mother is like a vine in your life, planted near water; she was productive and had many branches because of the plentiful water.
Ezekiel 19:11 She had sturdy branches fit for rulers' scepters; she stood tall amidst the dense foliage, her height visible with her many branches.
Ezekiel 19:12 But she was yanked up angrily, thrown to the ground, and the east wind dried up her fruit; her strong branches were broken and dried up; the fire burned them up.
Ezekiel 19:13 And now it is planted in a desert, in a dry and parched land.
Ezekiel 19:14 Fire came from one of her branch sticks and burned up her fruit. Now she has no strong branch to be a ruler's scepter. This is a sad song, and it will be used as a sad song.

Ezekiel 20:1 In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the leaders of Israel came to ask God, and they sat down in front of me.
Ezekiel 20:2 Then God spoke to me, saying,
Ezekiel 20:3 Human, talk to Israel's leaders and tell them, "God says, 'Have you come to ask me something? As I live, says God, I will not answer you.'"
Ezekiel 20:4 Will you judge them, human, will you judge them? Show them their fathers' wrongdoings.
Ezekiel 20:5 Tell them this is what God says: On the day I picked Israel, raised my hand to Jacob's descendants, and revealed myself to them in Egypt, I raised my hand and told them, 'I am God, your God.'
Ezekiel 20:6 On the day I raised my hand to them, to lead them out of Egypt into a land I had chosen for them, a land filled with milk and honey, the finest of all lands.
Ezekiel 20:7 I said to them, "Throw away every bad thing you set your eyes on, and do not make yourselves dirty with the idols of Egypt: I am God your God."
Ezekiel 20:8 They resisted me and wouldn't listen: they each kept the hateful things they saw, nor did they leave Egypt's idols behind; then I decided to unleash my anger on them there in Egypt.
Ezekiel 20:9 I acted for the sake of my reputation, so it would not be tarnished in front of the nations where they lived, where I revealed myself to them by leading them out of Egypt.
Ezekiel 20:10 So I made them leave Egypt and led them into the desert.
Ezekiel 20:11 I gave them my laws and taught them my rulings, which if a person follows, they will live by them.
Ezekiel 20:12 I also gave them my days of rest, as a sign between us, so they would know that I am God who makes them holy.
Ezekiel 20:13 The people of Israel disobeyed me in the desert. They did not follow my laws, and they did not respect my decisions, which would give life to anyone who followed them. They badly disrespected my rest days. So, I thought to release my anger on them in the desert and to destroy them.
Ezekiel 20:14 I acted for my own reputation so that it would not be tarnished in the eyes of the nations from whom I rescued my people.
Ezekiel 20:15 I promised them in the wilderness that I would not take them to the land I had given them, a land rich with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.
Ezekiel 20:16 Because they disrespected my laws, did not follow my rules, and made my holy days unclean: for their hearts followed their false gods.
Ezekiel 20:17 But my eye pitied them and did not destroy them or wipe them out in the desert.
Ezekiel 20:18 I told their children in the desert, "Do not follow your fathers' customs, do not keep their rules, and do not make yourselves unclean with their idols."
Ezekiel 20:19 I am God, your God; follow my rules, obey my decisions, and carry them out.
Ezekiel 20:20 Honor my rest days; they will be a sign between us so that you will know that I am your God.
Ezekiel 20:21 Despite this, the children disobeyed me: they did not follow my rules or keep my decisions, which would bring life if followed; they disrespected my rest days: so I decided to fully unleash my anger on them in the desert.
Ezekiel 20:22 Even so, I held back and acted for the sake of my name, so it would not be tarnished in the eyes of the nations among whom I had brought them out.
Ezekiel 20:23 I raised my hand to them in the desert, promising that I would scatter them among the nations and spread them out across the lands.
Ezekiel 20:24 Because they did not follow my decisions, but hated my rules, and did not respect my special rest days, and they desired their ancestors' false gods.
Ezekiel 20:25 So I gave them rules that were not good, and laws that did not bring life.
Ezekiel 20:26 I let them become unclean through their own gifts when they burned their firstborn, which made them empty, so they would know I am God.

Ezekiel 20:28 When I brought them to the land I promised to give them, they saw every tall hill and all the dense trees. There they made their sacrifices, presented their offerings to provoke me, made offerings that smelled sweet, and poured out their drink offerings.
Ezekiel 20:29 Then I asked them, "What is the high place you go to?" It is named Bamah to this day.
Ezekiel 20:30 Tell the people of Israel, God says; Are you dirty like your ancestors? Do you act badly like they did?
Ezekiel 20:31 When you give your gifts and burn your children as sacrifices, you make yourselves unclean with all your gods, even now. Should you expect me to answer your questions, people of Israel? I swear, says God, I will not answer you.
Ezekiel 20:32 What you are thinking won't happen—you won't say, 'Let's be like other nations, serving idols made of wood and stone.'
Ezekiel 20:33 I am alive, says God, and I will rule over you with great power, a reaching arm, and intense anger.
Ezekiel 20:34 I will take you away from the people and collect you from the countries where you are spread out, with great power, with an outreached arm, and with strong anger.
Ezekiel 20:35 I will take you to the people's desert, and there I will talk with you directly.
Ezekiel 20:36 Just as I spoke to your ancestors in the desert of Egypt, I will speak to you, says God.
Ezekiel 20:37 I will make you follow the rules, and I will bring you into the agreement's commitment.
Ezekiel 20:38 I will remove the rebels from among you and those who disobey me: I will take them out of the country where they live, and they will not enter the land of Israel: and you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 20:39 Israel, this is what God says: Go and worship your idols if you wish, but if you won't listen to me, stop disrespecting my holy name with your gifts and idols.
Ezekiel 20:40 In my holy mountain, on Israel's highest mountain, God says, all of Israel, everyone in the land, will serve me. There I will accept them, and there I will ask for your gifts, the first of your offerings, along with all your sacred items.
Ezekiel 20:41 I will welcome you because of your pleasing aroma when I rescue you from the peoples and collect you from the countries where you were spread out; and I will show my holiness through you to the nations.
Ezekiel 20:42 You will know that I am God when I bring you to Israel, the land I promised to give your ancestors.
Ezekiel 20:43 There, you will remember your actions and everything you have done that made you impure; and you will hate yourselves for all the wrongs you have done.
Ezekiel 20:44 You will understand that I am God when I act for the sake of my name, not based on your bad ways or your wrong actions, people of Israel, says God.
Ezekiel 20:45 Also, God's message came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 20:46 Human, look toward the south, speak toward the south, and predict against the forest in the southern land.
Ezekiel 20:47 Tell the southern forest to listen to God's message: God says, "Look, I will start a fire in you. It will burn up all the green trees and all the dry trees. The blazing fire won't be put out, and it will scorch everything from the south to the north."
Ezekiel 20:48 Everyone will see that I, God, have started this fire; it will not be put out.
Ezekiel 20:49 Then I said, "Ah God! They are saying about me, 'Doesn't he just speak in puzzles?'"

Ezekiel 21:5 So that everyone may know that I, God, have taken out my sword from its cover: it will not be put back again.

Ezekiel 21:25 You, evil and unholy ruler of Israel, your time has come when your wrongdoing will stop.

Ezekiel 21:32 You will be fuel for the fire; your blood will be spread across the land; you will be forgotten because I, God, have said so.

Ezekiel 23:1 God spoke to me again, saying,
Ezekiel 23:2 Human, there were two sisters from the same mother:
Ezekiel 23:3 In Egypt, they acted immorally; they were immoral since they were young: their bodies were touched, and their virginity was spoiled.
Ezekiel 23:4 The sisters' names were Aholah the older and Aholibah her sister. They belonged to me and had sons and daughters. Their names mean Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem is Aholibah.
Ezekiel 23:5 Aholah acted like a prostitute while she was with me; she was crazy about her lovers, the Assyrians who lived nearby.
Ezekiel 23:6 They wore blue, were leaders and officials, all handsome young men, horsemen riding on horses.
Ezekiel 23:7 She had relations with them, all the favored men of Assyria, and with everyone she desired; she made herself unclean with all their idols.
Ezekiel 23:8 She did not stop the sexual sins she started in Egypt. When she was young, they slept with her, hurt her virgin breasts, and forced their immorality on her.
Ezekiel 23:9 So, I gave her to her lovers, the Assyrians, whom she adored.
Ezekiel 23:10 They saw her nakedness, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became well-known among women because they carried out justice on her.
Ezekiel 23:11 When Aholibah, her sister, saw this, she became even more immoral in her extreme lust than her sister, and in her unfaithfulness, she surpassed her sister's unfaithfulness.
Ezekiel 23:12 She was attracted to her Assyrian neighbors, handsome young men who were commanders and rulers dressed in beautiful clothes, horsemen riding on horses.
Ezekiel 23:13 Then I saw she was corrupted; they both chose the same path.
Ezekiel 23:14 She grew more unfaithful: she saw pictures of men on the wall, drawings of the Chaldeans colored with red.
Ezekiel 23:15 Wearing belts on their waists, with fancy dyed turbans on their heads, all looking like princes, just like the Babylonians from Chaldea, the place where they were born.
Ezekiel 23:16 As soon as she saw them, she longed for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
Ezekiel 23:17 The people from Babylon went to her bed to make love, and by sleeping with her, they made her unclean. She became dirty from being with them, and then she started to dislike them.
Ezekiel 23:18 She revealed her unfaithfulness and exposed herself; then I became disgusted with her, just as I had with her sister.
Ezekiel 23:19 She increased her unfaithfulness, remembering her youth when she acted as a prostitute in Egypt.
Ezekiel 23:20 She was crazy about her lovers, who were as well-endowed as donkeys and ejaculated like stallions.
Ezekiel 23:21 You remembered your wild days as a young woman, when the Egyptians touched your breasts.
Ezekiel 23:22 So, O Aholibah, this is what God says: Look, I will turn your lovers against you, those you no longer care for, and I will bring them against you from all sides.

Ezekiel 23:27 I will stop your indecency and end the unfaithful ways you brought from Egypt; you will not look to them or think of Egypt again.

Ezekiel 23:32 God says, "You will drink from your sister's big deep cup; you will be mocked and ridiculed; it holds a lot."
Ezekiel 23:33 You will be filled with drunkenness and sadness, with a cup of shock and ruin, with the cup of your sister Samaria.
Ezekiel 23:34 You will drink it, drain it, break its pieces, and tear off your breasts. I have said it, says God.
Ezekiel 23:35 So God says, because you have forgotten me and ignored me, now you must deal with your bad behavior and your unfaithfulness.
Ezekiel 23:36 God said to me, "Human, will you judge Aholah and Aholibah? Yes, tell them about their horrible acts."
Ezekiel 23:37 They were unfaithful, their hands are bloody, they were unfaithful with their idols, and they made their sons, whom they had for me, go through fire, consuming them.
Ezekiel 23:38 They have also done this to me: they have made my holy place dirty on that same day, and they have disrespected my special days of rest.
Ezekiel 23:39 After they killed their children for their idols, they entered my sacred place on that same day to disrespect it; look, this is what they have done in my house.
Ezekiel 23:40 You also called men from far away, to whom you sent a messenger; and look, they came. You bathed, put on eye makeup, and wore jewelry for them.

Ezekiel 23:44 They had sex with her like men do with a prostitute. This is how they treated Aholah and Aholibah, the immoral women.

Ezekiel 23:49 They will punish you for your bad acts, and you will suffer for worshipping your idols: and you will realize that I am God.

Ezekiel 24:4 Collect the parts into it, including every good piece, the leg, and the arm; pack it with the best bones.
Ezekiel 24:5 Choose the best of the flock, burn the bones beneath it, cook it thoroughly, and boil the bones in it.
Ezekiel 24:6 So God says: "Trouble waits for the violent city, for the pot filled with filth that remains inside. Take it apart bit by bit; don't spare any of it."
Ezekiel 24:7 Her blood is inside her; she put it on a rock's top; she didn't pour it on the earth to cover it with dust.
Ezekiel 24:8 I did this to make anger rise and to get revenge; I put her blood on a rock where it can't be hidden.
Ezekiel 24:9 So this is what God says: Trouble to the city of blood! I will make a big fire pile.
Ezekiel 24:10 Put on lots of wood, light the fire, cook the meat, season it well, and burn the bones.
Ezekiel 24:11 Place it empty on the coals so that it gets hot, burns, melts away its dirt, and its scum is removed.
Ezekiel 24:12 She wore herself out with lies, and her deep filth didn't leave her: her filth will burn in the fire.

Ezekiel 24:22 Do as I did: do not cover your lips or eat people's bread.
Ezekiel 24:23 You will wear turbans on your heads and shoes on your feet. You will not mourn or cry, but you will waste away because of your sins and grieve among yourselves.
Ezekiel 24:24 Ezekiel is a sign for you: just as he did, you should do the same. When it happens, you will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 24:25 Also, you human, when I take away their power, the joy of their pride, what they desire most, and all they think about—their sons and daughters.

Ezekiel 24:27 On that day you will be able to speak to the one who has escaped, you will talk and not be silent anymore; you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am God.

Ezekiel 31:5 So he grew taller than all the other trees, his branches spread out, and they got longer because there was plenty of water.
Ezekiel 31:6 Every bird in the sky nested in his branches, all the field animals gave birth under his branches, and all great peoples lived in his shade.
Ezekiel 31:7 He was beautiful in his size, with long branches, because his roots were near much water.
