Ezekiel 31:12 Foreigners, the fierce ones from different countries, cut him down and abandoned him. On the mountains and in all the valleys his branches lie fallen, and his limbs are broken by all the rivers of the land. All the earth's people left his shade and left him alone.
Ezekiel 31:13 All the birds of the sky will stay on his ruins, and all the animals of the field will be on his branches.
Ezekiel 31:14 So that no trees by the water become proud of their height, or grow their tops high among dense branches, and no watered trees stand tall in their height; they are all doomed to die, to go down to the earth's depths, among people, with those who sink to the grave.
Ezekiel 31:15 God says, "On the day he died, I made people mourn. I hid the ocean for him, stopped its floods, and the big waters stopped. I made Lebanon sad for him, and all the trees in the field felt weak for him."
Ezekiel 31:16 I caused countries to tremble when they heard he had fallen. When I threw him down to the grave with those going into the deep pit, all the good trees of Eden and the finest ones from Lebanon, all that need water, felt better deep in the ground.
Ezekiel 31:17 They also went down to the grave with him, to those killed by the sword; and those who supported him, who lived in his protection among the nations.
Ezekiel 31:18 Who are you like in beauty and size among the Eden trees? But you will be cut down and lie below the earth with the Eden trees and the dead who were killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his people, says God.

Ezekiel 32:1 In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, God spoke to me.
Ezekiel 32:2 Human, sing a sad song for the Pharaoh of Egypt, and tell him: You are like a strong lion among the nations, and like a large sea creature in the oceans. You came out with your rivers, stirred up the water with your feet, and made their rivers dirty.
Ezekiel 32:3 God says, "I will spread my net over you with a group of many people; and they will pull you up in my net."
Ezekiel 32:4 I will leave you on the land, throw you into the open field, let birds from the sky sit on you, and fill the animals of the earth with you.
Ezekiel 32:5 I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.
Ezekiel 32:6 I will also soak the land where you swim with your blood, up to the mountains; and the rivers will overflow with you.
Ezekiel 32:7 When I make you go away, I will hide the sky and darken the stars; I will cover the sun with clouds, and the moon will not shine.
Ezekiel 32:8 I will turn off all the bright lights in the sky above you and make your land dark, says God.
Ezekiel 32:9 I will trouble many people's hearts when I bring your ruin to nations, to places you do not know.
Ezekiel 32:10 Yes, I will make many people shocked at you, and their kings will be very scared because of you, when I wave my sword in front of them; and they will shake in fear all the time, each person for their own life, on the day you fall.
Ezekiel 32:11 God says the king of Babylon's sword will come against you.
Ezekiel 32:12 Mighty warriors will use their swords to make your crowds fall, even the most feared from all nations, and they will take away Egypt's splendor; all its masses will be wiped out.
Ezekiel 32:13 I will also wipe out all the animals near the big waters; people will not disturb them again, nor will animal hoofs.
Ezekiel 32:14 I will make their waters deep and their rivers flow smoothly, says God.
Ezekiel 32:15 When I make Egypt empty and the land has nothing left that once filled it, when I strike down all who live there, then they will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 32:16 This is the sad song that people will sing to mourn her: women from different countries will mourn for her and for the many people of Egypt, says God.
Ezekiel 32:17 In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, God's message came to me, saying.
Ezekiel 32:18 Human, cry for the many people of Egypt, and bring them down, her and the daughters of powerful nations, to the depths of the earth, with those who descend into the pit.
Ezekiel 32:19 Who do you surpass in beauty? Go down and lie with those who are not circumcised.
Ezekiel 32:20 They will die among those killed by the sword: she is handed over to the sword: pull her out with all her crowds.
Ezekiel 32:21 The powerful ones will speak to him from the place of the dead, along with his helpers: they have fallen and now lie dead, killed by the sword.
Ezekiel 32:22 Asshur and her group are there; graves surround him, all killed by the sword.
Ezekiel 32:23 Their graves are on the edge of the pit, and her group surrounds her grave: all of them killed, fallen by the sword, which spread fear in the land of the living.
Ezekiel 32:24 Elam and all her people are around her tomb, all killed by the sword, and now lie in the lower parts of the earth, uncut. They spread fear when alive, but now they carry their disgrace with others in the pit.
Ezekiel 32:25 They made her a bed among the dead with her many people: their graves surround her: all of them were not circumcised, killed by the sword: even though they scared people in the land of the living, they carry their disgrace with those who go down to the grave: he is placed among the dead.
Ezekiel 32:26 Meshech, Tubal, and their people are there; their graves surround him. All are uncircumcised, killed by the sword, even though they spread fear among the living.
Ezekiel 32:27 They will not rest with the powerful who have died, those uncircumcised who went to the grave with their weapons of war: they placed their swords under their heads, yet their sins remain with their bones, even though they once scared the strong in the world of the living.
Ezekiel 32:28 Yes, you will be broken among the uncircumcised and will lie with those killed by the sword.
Ezekiel 32:29 Edom, its kings, and all its leaders, with their strength, are with those killed by the sword: they will rest with the uncircumcised and those who go down to the grave.
Ezekiel 32:30 The leaders from the north and all the people from Sidon have gone down with the dead, feeling ashamed of their power. They lie dead, not circumcised, with those killed by the sword, and share their disgrace with those who go down to the grave.
Ezekiel 32:31 Pharaoh will see them and feel better about all his people, even Pharaoh and his whole army killed with the sword, says God.
Ezekiel 32:32 I have brought my fear to the living land: and he will be placed among the uncut with those killed by the sword, including Pharaoh and all his crowds, says God.

Ezekiel 33:1 God spoke to me again, saying,
Ezekiel 33:2 Human, tell your people, "When God sends war to a country, and the people choose someone from their area to be their lookout:
Ezekiel 33:3 If he sees the sword coming to the land and blows the trumpet to alert the people;
Ezekiel 33:4 If someone hears the trumpet but does not take warning, and the sword comes and takes them away, their own blood is on their head.
Ezekiel 33:5 He heard the trumpet but ignored the warning; it will be his own fault. But the one who listens to the warning will save himself.
Ezekiel 33:6 If the guard sees danger coming and doesn't sound the alarm, and the people aren't warned; if danger comes and takes someone away, that person is taken because of their own wrongs; but I will hold the guard responsible for their death.
Ezekiel 33:7 You, human, I have made you a lookout for Israel; so, listen to what I say and tell them my message.
Ezekiel 33:8 When I tell a bad person, "You will definitely die," if you don't warn them to turn from their bad ways, they will die because of their sins; but I will hold you responsible for their death.
Ezekiel 33:9 However, if you warn the bad person to stop doing wrong and he doesn't stop, he will die because of his sins; but you will have saved yourself.
Ezekiel 33:10 So you, human, tell the people of Israel: You say, 'Our wrongs and sins weigh us down, and we are wasting away because of them. How can we live?'
Ezekiel 33:11 Tell them, as surely as I live, says God, I don't enjoy seeing the wicked die; instead, I want the wicked to stop their bad behavior and live. Stop, stop your evil ways; why do you want to die, O people of Israel?
Ezekiel 33:12 So, you human, tell your people: A good person's good acts won't save him when he does wrong, and a bad person won't be ruined by his badness on the day he stops doing bad. Also, a good person can't stay alive because of his good acts if he sins.
Ezekiel 33:13 When I tell a good person they will live, if they depend on their goodness but do wrong, none of their good acts will be remembered. Because of the wrong they did, they will die.
Ezekiel 33:14 When I tell a bad person they will die but they stop sinning and do what is fair and right;
Ezekiel 33:15 If a bad person gives back what he promised, returns what he stole, follows the rules for living right, and does not sin, he will surely live and not die.
Ezekiel 33:16 None of the sins he committed will be remembered against him: he did what is legal and right; he will surely live.
Ezekiel 33:17 Your people's children say, "God's way is not fair." But really, their own way is not fair.
Ezekiel 33:18 When a good person stops doing what is right and does wrong, they will die because of it.
Ezekiel 33:19 If a bad person stops doing wrong and does what is fair and right, they will live because of it.
Ezekiel 33:20 But you say, "God's way is not fair." O people of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your actions.
Ezekiel 33:21 In the twelfth year of our captivity, on the tenth month and the fifth day, someone who escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has been captured."
Ezekiel 33:22 That evening, God's power was on me before the escapee arrived. God had made me able to speak by the time he came in the morning, so I could talk again.
Ezekiel 33:23 God spoke to me, saying,
Ezekiel 33:24 Human, the people living in the ruins of Israel say, "Abraham was alone, and he got the land: but we are many; we are given the land as our own."
Ezekiel 33:25 Tell them this: God says, "You eat meat with blood, look up to your idols, and kill people: do you think you can own the land?
Ezekiel 33:26 You rely on your swords, do terrible things, and each of you dishonors another's wife: do you think you will then get the land?
Ezekiel 33:27 Tell them this: God says, "As I live, surely those in the ruins will die by the sword, the one in the open field I will give to the animals to eat, and those in strongholds and caves will die of disease."
Ezekiel 33:28 I will make the land very empty, and its proud power will end; the mountains of Israel will be empty, so no one will pass through.
Ezekiel 33:29 Then they will realize that I am God when I have made the land very empty because of all the terrible things they have done.
Ezekiel 33:30 You, person, your people are talking about you near the walls and in their homes. They say to each other, "Come, let's hear the message from God."
Ezekiel 33:31 They come to you like a crowd does, and they sit before you as if they're my people. They listen to your words but won't follow them. They act loving with their words, but their heart chases after greed.
Ezekiel 33:32 You are like a beautiful song to them, sung by someone with a nice voice who plays an instrument well: they hear your words, but they do not follow them.
Ezekiel 33:33 When this happens—and it will happen—then they will understand that a prophet was with them.

Ezekiel 34:1 God's message came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 34:2 Human, speak against Israel's leaders, speak and tell them, God says to the leaders: Trouble to you, Israel's leaders, who only take care of yourselves! Shouldn't leaders take care of the people?
Ezekiel 34:3 You eat the fat and wear the wool, you kill the well-fed animals, but you do not take care of the flock.
Ezekiel 34:4 You have not helped the sick get stronger, nor healed the ones who were ill, nor bandaged the ones who were injured, nor brought back the ones who were chased away, nor looked for the ones who were lost; instead, you have ruled them harshly and cruelly.
Ezekiel 34:5 They were spread out because there was no shepherd; and wild animals ate them up when they were spread out.
Ezekiel 34:6 My sheep roamed over all the hills and every high mountain; indeed, my flock spread out across the whole earth, and no one looked for or sought them.
Ezekiel 34:7 So, shepherds, listen to what God says.
Ezekiel 34:8 I am alive, says God, and because my sheep were hunted and eaten by every animal in the field since there was no shepherd, and my shepherds did not look for my sheep but fed themselves instead of my sheep;
Ezekiel 34:9 So, you shepherds, listen to God's message.
Ezekiel 34:10 God says, "Look, I am against the shepherds. I will ask for my sheep back from them, and stop them from feeding the sheep. The shepherds won't feed themselves anymore, because I will save my sheep from them, so they won't be their food."
Ezekiel 34:11 For this is what God says; Look, I myself will search for my sheep and find them.
Ezekiel 34:12 Like a shepherd looks for his sheep when they are spread out, I will look for my sheep and save them from all the places where they have been scattered on a dark and cloudy day.
Ezekiel 34:13 I will take them from among the people, gather them from different countries, and bring them to their own land. I will feed them on Israel's mountains, by the rivers, and in all the places where people live in the land.
Ezekiel 34:14 I will give them good grass to eat, and their sheepfold will be on Israel's tall mountains. There they will rest in a good sheepfold and eat from the rich grass on Israel's mountains.
Ezekiel 34:15 I will feed my sheep, and I will make them rest, says God.
Ezekiel 34:16 I will look for the lost, bring back those who were pushed away, heal the injured, and make the weak strong. But I will get rid of the powerful and rich; I will treat them with fairness.
Ezekiel 34:17 And for you, my sheep, this is what God says: Look, I will decide between one animal and another, between rams and male goats.
Ezekiel 34:18 Do you think it's minor that you've eaten the best grass, but you also crush the rest of the grass with your feet? And you drink clear water, but you dirty the rest with your feet?
Ezekiel 34:19 My sheep eat what you've stepped on and drink what you've dirtied with your feet.
Ezekiel 34:20 So this is what God says to them: "Look, I myself will decide between the fat sheep and the thin sheep."
Ezekiel 34:21 Because you pushed with body and shoulder, and butted all the weak ones with your horns until you scattered them away;
Ezekiel 34:22 I will rescue my sheep so they won't be attacked anymore; I will make fair decisions between one animal and another.
Ezekiel 34:23 I will put one shepherd over them, and he will take care of them, my servant David; he will take care of them and be their shepherd.
Ezekiel 34:24 I, God, will be their God, and my servant David will be a leader among them; I, God, have said this.
Ezekiel 34:25 I will make a peace agreement with them and stop the harmful animals in the land; they will live safely in the wilderness and rest in the forests.
Ezekiel 34:26 I will bless them and the areas near my hill, and I will send rain when it's needed; there will be plenty of blessings with the rain.
Ezekiel 34:27 The trees in the fields will give their fruit, and the earth will give its crops, and the people will be safe in their land. They will know that I am God when I have broken the straps of their yoke and set them free from those who used them.
Ezekiel 34:28 They will no longer be attacked by other nations, nor will wild animals eat them; they will live safely and no one will scare them.
Ezekiel 34:29 I will grow a famous plant for them, and they will not be hungry in the land, nor will they feel the shame from other nations anymore.
Ezekiel 34:30 They will know that I, their God, am with them, and that they, the people of Israel, are my people, says God.
Ezekiel 34:31 You, my sheep, the sheep I care for, are people, and I am your God, says God.

Ezekiel 36:1 You, person of God, speak to Israel's mountains and say, "Israel's mountains, listen to God's message:

Ezekiel 36:19 I spread them among different nations, and they spread across many countries. I judged them based on their actions and their ways.

Ezekiel 36:21 But I felt sorry for my holy name, which the people of Israel had dishonored among the nations where they had gone.

Ezekiel 36:23 I will make my great name holy, which you disrespected among the nations. You have disrespected it among them, and the nations will know that I am God when I show my holiness through you to them.
Ezekiel 36:24 I will take you from the nations, gather you from all countries, and bring you to your own land.
Ezekiel 36:25 I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean: I will cleanse you from all your dirt and idols.
Ezekiel 36:26 I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
Ezekiel 36:27 I will put my spirit in you, and make you follow my rules, and you will obey my decisions, and follow them.
Ezekiel 36:28 You will live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
Ezekiel 36:29 I will save you from all your impurities, and I will make the grain grow more and ensure there is no famine for you.
Ezekiel 36:30 I will make trees and crops grow more so you won't suffer hunger or be shamed by other nations.
Ezekiel 36:31 Then you will remember your bad actions and deeds that were not good, and you will hate yourselves because of your sins and disgusting things.
Ezekiel 36:32 I do this not for you, but let it be known, says God: feel shame and embarrassment because of what you have done, people of Israel.
Ezekiel 36:33 This is what God says: When I have purified you from all your wrongdoings, I will let you live in the cities again, and the ruined places will be rebuilt.
Ezekiel 36:34 The empty land will be farmed, where it was once empty for everyone who went by to see.
Ezekiel 36:35 People will say, "This empty land has turned into a garden like Eden; and the ruined, empty cities are now protected and filled with people."
Ezekiel 36:36 Then the nations around you that remain will know that I, God, rebuild what was destroyed and regrow what was deserted: I, God, have said it, and I will do it.
Ezekiel 36:37 God says: I will still be asked by the people of Israel to help them, and I will give them more people, like a flock.
Ezekiel 36:38 Like a sacred herd, like the herd in Jerusalem during its festivals, the ruined cities will be filled with crowds of people, and they will understand that I am God.

Ezekiel 37:1 God's hand was on me, and he took me out in his spirit and put me down in the middle of a valley full of bones.
Ezekiel 37:2 God made me walk around them, and I saw a lot of bones in the valley; they were very dry.
Ezekiel 37:3 He asked me, "Human, can these bones come to life?" I replied, "God, only you know."
Ezekiel 37:4 He told me again, "Speak to these bones and say, 'You dry bones, listen to God's message.'"
Ezekiel 37:5 God says to these bones, "Look, I will make breath come into you, and you will live."
Ezekiel 37:6 I will put tendons on you, make flesh grow on you, cover you with skin, and give you breath, so you will live; then you will understand that I am God.
Ezekiel 37:7 I did as I was told: and as I spoke, there was a sound, and suddenly a shaking, and the bones moved and joined together, each bone connecting to its matching bone.
Ezekiel 37:8 When I looked, the tendons and flesh grew on them, and skin covered them, but they had no breath.
Ezekiel 37:9 Then he said to me, "Speak to the wind, speak, human, and say to the wind, 'God says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these dead ones, so they may live.'"
Ezekiel 37:10 I did as I was told, and breath entered them. They came to life and stood up on their feet—a very large army.
Ezekiel 37:11 He told me, "Human, these bones represent all of Israel. Look, they say, 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is gone, we are completely cut off.'"
Ezekiel 37:12 So, tell them, 'This is what God says: Look, my people, I will open your graves and lift you out of them, and take you to the land of Israel.
Ezekiel 37:13 You will understand that I am God when I open your graves and bring you out of them, my people.
Ezekiel 37:14 I will put my spirit in you, you will live, and I will put you in your own land. Then you will know that I, God, have said and done this, says God.
Ezekiel 37:15 God spoke to me again, saying,
Ezekiel 37:16 Also, you human, take one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and the Israelites associated with him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph, which is for Ephraim, and for all the Israelite companions.'
Ezekiel 37:17 Put them together, one to the other, into one piece; and they will be united in your hand.
Ezekiel 37:18 When your people's children talk to you and ask, "Won't you explain what these things mean to us?"
Ezekiel 37:19 Tell them, "This is what God says: Look, I will take Joseph's stick, which is in Ephraim's hand, along with his companion tribes of Israel, and put them together with Judah's stick, making them one stick, and they will be one in my hand."
Ezekiel 37:20 Hold the sticks you wrote on in your hand for them to see.
Ezekiel 37:21 Tell them, 'This is what God says: Look, I will take the Israelites from the nations where they have gone, gather them from all around, and bring them back to their own land.'
Ezekiel 37:22 I will make them one country in Israel's land on the mountains; and they will all have one king. They will no longer be two separate countries or split into two kingdoms ever again.
Ezekiel 37:23 They won't make themselves unclean with idols, hateful things, or sins. I will rescue them from all the places they sinned and make them clean. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God.
Ezekiel 37:24 David my servant will be their king; they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my rules and keep and follow my laws.
Ezekiel 37:25 They will live in the land I gave to Jacob, my servant, where your ancestors lived. They, their children, and their grandchildren will live there forever, and David, my servant, will always be their leader.
Ezekiel 37:26 I will make a peace agreement with them that will last forever. I will settle them, increase their numbers, and put my holy place among them always.
Ezekiel 37:27 My tent will be with them; yes, I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Ezekiel 37:28 The nations will understand that I, God, make Israel holy when my holy place is with them forever.

Ezekiel 38:3 Say, God says, "Look, I am against you, Gog, the top ruler of Meshech and Tubal."
Ezekiel 38:4 I will make you turn back, put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out with all your army, with horses and riders, all fully armed, a huge crowd with shields and helmets, all carrying swords.
Ezekiel 38:5 Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya are with them; all are carrying shields and wearing helmets.
Ezekiel 38:6 Gomer and his groups, the family of Togarmah from the north, and all their groups, with many people with you.
Ezekiel 38:7 Get ready and make sure you and all your group gathered around you are prepared, and you keep watch over them.
Ezekiel 38:8 After a long time, you will be visited. In the last years, you will enter the land that has recovered from war, which is collected from many nations, against the mountains of Israel, that have always been deserted. But now it has been taken from the nations, and they all will live there safely.

Ezekiel 38:14 So, human, prophesy and tell Gog, "God says: When my people Israel live in safety, won't you realize it?"
Ezekiel 38:15 You will come from your land in the north with many people, all on horses, a large group and a strong army.

Ezekiel 38:18 When Gog attacks the land of Israel, God says, my anger will show on my face.
Ezekiel 38:19 Because I am jealous and very angry, I have promised that there will be a huge earthquake in the land of Israel on that day.
Ezekiel 38:20 So that the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the animals on the land, all small creatures that crawl on the ground, and all people on earth, will tremble before me, and the mountains will crumble, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.
Ezekiel 38:21 I will send a sword against him over all my mountains, says God: everyone's sword will turn against his brother.
Ezekiel 38:22 I will fight against him with disease and bloodshed; I will pour down on him, his troops, and the many people with him, heavy rain, big hailstones, fire, and sulfur.
Ezekiel 38:23 I will show my greatness and holiness; I will be recognized by many nations, and they will know that I am God.

Ezekiel 39:1 So, you human messenger, speak against Gog and say, 'This is what God says: Look, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Meshech and Tubal.'
Ezekiel 39:2 I will make you turn back, leaving only a sixth of you, and will lead you from the north to the mountains of Israel.
Ezekiel 39:3 I will knock your bow from your left hand and make your arrows drop from your right hand.
Ezekiel 39:4 You will fall on the mountains of Israel, you and all your groups, and the people with you: I will give you to the hungry birds of every kind, and to the wild animals to be eaten.
Ezekiel 39:5 You will fall in the open field because I, God, have said so.
Ezekiel 39:6 I will send fire on Magog and on those living without worry on the islands; they will know that I am God.
Ezekiel 39:7 I will make my holy name known among my people Israel; I will not allow my holy name to be dishonored anymore. And the nations will know that I am God, the Holy One in Israel.
Ezekiel 39:8 Look, it has come, and it is finished, says God; this is the day I have talked about.
Ezekiel 39:9 People living in Israel's cities will go out, burn the weapons - the shields, small shields, bows, arrows, clubs, and spears - and use them for fuel for seven years.
Ezekiel 39:10 They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut down trees from the forests because they will use their weapons for fuel. They will take back what was taken from them and loot those who looted them, says God.
Ezekiel 39:11 On that day, I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, in the valley where people pass by, east of the sea. The smell will be so bad it will block the travelers' noses. There they will bury Gog and all his army, and it will be named The Valley of Hamongog.
Ezekiel 39:12 For seven months, the people of Israel will bury them to clean the land.
Ezekiel 39:13 Yes, all the people of the land will bury them, and they will be honored on the day I am glorified, says God.
Ezekiel 39:14 They will choose people for the full-time job of going through the land to bury with travelers the bodies left on the ground, to clean the land. After seven months, they will start searching.
Ezekiel 39:15 Travelers crossing the land, if someone sees a human bone, must then mark it with a sign until the grave-diggers bury it in Hamongog Valley.
Ezekiel 39:16 The city will be named Hamonah. This is how they will purify the land.
Ezekiel 39:17 You, human, this is what God says: Tell all the birds and animals to come together from everywhere to the big sacrifice I have prepared for you on the hills of Israel. You will eat meat and drink blood.
Ezekiel 39:18 You will eat the meat of the strong and drink the blood of the earth's rulers, including rams, lambs, goats, and bulls, all well-fed from Bashan.
Ezekiel 39:19 You will eat until you are full and drink until you are drunk on the sacrifice I made for you.
Ezekiel 39:20 You will be fed at my table with horses, chariots, strong men, and all warriors, says God.
Ezekiel 39:21 I will show my greatness to the nations, and all the nations will see the justice I have done and the power I have used against them.
Ezekiel 39:22 So the people of Israel will know that I am their God from that day on.
Ezekiel 39:23 The nations will understand that Israel was taken as captives because of their sins; they did wrong to me, so I turned away from them and let their enemies defeat them in battle.
Ezekiel 39:24 Because of their dirtiness and bad actions, I punished them and turned away from them.
Ezekiel 39:25 So God says, "Now I will bring back the people of Jacob from captivity, have mercy on all of Israel, and defend my holy name with passion."
Ezekiel 39:26 After they feel their shame and all their wrongs against me, when they lived safely in their land with no one to scare them.
Ezekiel 39:27 When I bring them back from other peoples and collect them from their enemies' lands, and show my holiness through them to many nations.
Ezekiel 39:28 They will know I am their God, who let them be taken captive to foreign lands, but I have brought them back to their own land and have not left any behind.
Ezekiel 39:29 I will not hide my face from them anymore because I have given my spirit to the people of Israel, says God.

Ezekiel 40:1 In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, at the start of the year, on the tenth day of the month, fourteen years after the city was struck down, on that exact day, God's hand was on me and took me there.
Ezekiel 40:2 In visions from God, he took me to the land of Israel and placed me on a very high mountain where there was something like the structure of a city to the south.
Ezekiel 40:3 He took me there, and I saw a man looking like shiny metal, holding a linen string and a measuring stick, standing at the gate.
Ezekiel 40:4 The man said to me, "Look carefully and listen closely. Pay attention to everything I'm going to show you. You are brought here so I can show them to you. Tell everything you see to the people of Israel."
Ezekiel 40:5 Look, there was a wall outside all around the house, and the man had a measuring stick about ten and a half feet long. He measured the wall; it was ten and a half feet thick and ten and a half feet high.
Ezekiel 40:6 He went to the gate facing east, climbed its steps, and measured the gateway's entrance, which was one reed wide; the other entrance was also one reed wide.
Ezekiel 40:7 Each small room was as long and wide as a reed; there was a space of five cubits between the rooms; and the entrance of the gate near the inner gate porch was also as long as a reed.
Ezekiel 40:8 He also measured the inside gateway entrance, one rod long.
Ezekiel 40:9 He measured the gate's entrance at eight units; the gateposts, two units; and the entrance faced inside.
Ezekiel 40:10 The small rooms of the east gate had three on one side and three on the other; all three were the same size. The pillars on both sides were also the same size.
Ezekiel 40:11 He measured the entrance width, ten units; and the gate length, thirteen units.
Ezekiel 40:12 The area in front of the small rooms was one cubit wide on one side and also one cubit wide on the other side; the small rooms themselves were six cubits wide on both sides.
Ezekiel 40:13 He measured the gate from the top of one small room to the top of another: the width was twenty-five cubits, with doors facing each other.
Ezekiel 40:14 He also made pillars sixty cubits high, up to the entrance of the enclosed yard.
Ezekiel 40:15 From the entrance gate to the inner gate's porch was fifty cubits long.
Ezekiel 40:16 The small rooms, the gate posts, and the curved areas all had narrow windows around them, and windows were all around on the inside too; and on each post, there were images of palm trees.
Ezekiel 40:17 He led me to the outer courtyard, and there I saw rooms and a tiled walkway around the courtyard. There were thirty rooms along the walkway.
Ezekiel 40:18 The ground next to the gates opposite the long sides of the gates was the lower ground.
Ezekiel 40:19 He measured the width from the front of the outer gate to the front of the inner courtyard, a hundred cubits to the east and north.
Ezekiel 40:20 He measured the length and width of the gate of the outer courtyard facing north.
Ezekiel 40:21 The small rooms had three on one side and three on the other; the pillars and arches were like those of the first gate. Its length was fifty cubits and its width twenty-five cubits.
Ezekiel 40:22 Their windows, arches, and palm tree designs matched the size of the eastern gate. There were seven steps leading up to it, and the arches were in front of them.
Ezekiel 40:23 The door of the inside yard faced the north and east doors. He measured from one door to the next, a hundred units.
Ezekiel 40:24 Then he took me to the south side, and I saw a gate on the south. He measured its pillars and its archways by these measurements.
Ezekiel 40:25 The building had windows and arches all around that looked like those windows; it was 50 cubits long and 25 cubits wide.
Ezekiel 40:26 There were seven steps leading up to it, with arches in front: it had palm trees, one on each side of the posts.
Ezekiel 40:27 In the inner yard, there was a gate facing south. He measured from one gate to the other toward the south, a distance of one hundred cubits.
Ezekiel 40:28 He took me to the inner courtyard through the south entrance and measured the south entrance with these dimensions.
Ezekiel 40:29 Its small rooms, pillars, and arches were built to these sizes: it had windows and arches all around. It was 50 cubits long and 25 cubits wide.
Ezekiel 40:30 The arches around were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
Ezekiel 40:31 The archways faced the outer courtyard; there were palm trees on its columns, and eight steps led up to it.
Ezekiel 40:32 He led me to the inner courtyard on the east side, and he measured the gateway using those measurements.
Ezekiel 40:33 Its small rooms, pillars, and arches were built to these sizes: it had windows and rounded arches all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Ezekiel 40:34 Its arches faced the outer courtyard, and there were palm tree decorations on its columns on both sides, with eight steps leading up to it.
Ezekiel 40:35 He took me to the north gate and measured it with these measurements.
Ezekiel 40:36 Its small rooms, pillars, arches, and windows all around: it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Ezekiel 40:37 The pillars faced the outer courtyard; each pillar had palm tree designs on both sides, and the stairway to it had eight steps.
Ezekiel 40:38 The rooms and their doorways were by the gate pillars, where they washed the sacrifice that was burned.
Ezekiel 40:39 In the entrance of the gate were two tables on one side and two on the other side, where they would kill the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings.
Ezekiel 40:40 Outside, by the path leading to the north gate entrance, stood two tables; and on the opposite side, near the gate's porch, there were two more tables.
Ezekiel 40:41 On one side were four tables, and on the other side were four tables next to the gate; altogether eight tables where they killed their offerings.
Ezekiel 40:42 The four tables were made of cut stone for the burnt offerings. They were one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one cubit tall. On these, they placed the tools used to kill the burnt offerings and sacrifices.
Ezekiel 40:43 Inside there were wide hooks, secured all around, and on the tables was the meat of the sacrifice.
Ezekiel 40:44 Next to the inner gate, there were rooms for the singers in the inner courtyard, near the north gate, and they faced south. There was also a room beside the east gate that faced north.
Ezekiel 40:45 He told me, "This room, facing south, is for the priests who take care of the temple."
Ezekiel 40:46 The room facing north is for the priests in charge of the altar. These are Zadok's descendants among the Levites, who can come close to God to serve Him.
Ezekiel 40:47 He measured the yard, a hundred units long and a hundred units wide, square; and the altar in front of the building.
Ezekiel 40:48 He took me to the entrance of the house and measured the pillars, five units wide on one side and five on the other. The gateway was three units wide on one side and three on the other.
Ezekiel 40:49 The porch was 20 units long and 11 units wide, and he led me up the stairs to it. There were columns by the entrance, one on each side.

Ezekiel 41:1 Later, he took me to the temple and measured the entrance posts, which were six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other side, the same width as the tent.
Ezekiel 41:2 The door was ten cubits wide; each side of the door was five cubits, five on one side and five on the other side. He measured the length at forty cubits and the width at twenty cubits.
Ezekiel 41:3 He went inside and measured the doorpost at two cubits; the door itself at six cubits; and the width of the doorway at seven cubits.
Ezekiel 41:4 He measured it to be twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, in front of the temple, and said to me, "This is the holiest place."
Ezekiel 41:5 He measured the house wall, six cubits high; and the width of the side rooms, four cubits, all around the house.
Ezekiel 41:6 The side rooms were three stories high, one above another, with thirty rooms in each row. They were attached to the wall of the main building, encircling it so they could be supported, but they didn't go into the wall of the main building.
Ezekiel 41:7 The rooms became larger as they went up, with a spiral going up around the house. Because of this, the house got wider as it went up, from the lowest to the highest through the middle.
Ezekiel 41:8 I also saw the height of the temple all around: its side rooms were built on a base that was six long cubits high.
Ezekiel 41:9 The wall's thickness for the outside rooms was five cubits, and the space left over was for the inside rooms.
Ezekiel 41:10 Between the rooms was an open area 20 cubits wide all around the building on every side.
Ezekiel 41:11 The doors of the side rooms faced the open area, one door to the north and one to the south, and the open space was five cubits wide all around.
Ezekiel 41:12 The building in front of the separated area on the west side was 70 units wide. Its wall was 5 units thick all around, and it was 90 units long.
Ezekiel 41:13 He measured the temple, one hundred units long; and the outer area, and the structure, with its walls, one hundred units long.
Ezekiel 41:14 The width of the temple front and the area to the east is one hundred cubits.
Ezekiel 41:15 He measured the building's length next to the private area behind it, including its side galleries, a hundred cubits total, along with the inner sanctuary and the courtyards' entryways.
Ezekiel 41:16 The door frames, the small windows, and the surrounding balconies on their three floors, facing the door, were paneled with wood all around, from the floor to the windows, and the windows were covered.
Ezekiel 41:17 Above the door, to the inside of the house, outside, and along every side of the wall, inside and out, measured accurately.
Ezekiel 41:18 It had cherubim and palm trees, and each palm tree was between two cherubim, with each cherubim having two faces.
Ezekiel 41:19 The side of a man's face was toward the palm tree on one side, and the side of a young lion's face was toward the palm tree on the other side; this pattern was repeated all around the house.
Ezekiel 41:20 From the ground up to above the door, there were images of angels and palm trees, and they were on the temple wall.
Ezekiel 41:21 The temple's pillars were square, and so was the front of the holy place; both looked the same.
Ezekiel 41:22 The wooden altar was three feet high and its length was two feet. Its corners, length, and walls were made of wood. He told me, "This is the table in front of God."
Ezekiel 41:23 The temple and the holy place had two doors.
Ezekiel 41:24 Each door had two panels that could swing open; one pair for one door, and another pair for the other door.
Ezekiel 41:25 On the temple doors, they carved cherubim and palm trees like those on the walls, and there were solid beams on the outside of the front porch.
Ezekiel 41:26 There were small windows and palm trees on both sides, along the porch, on the side rooms of the house, and heavy beams.

Ezekiel 42:1 He led me out to the outer courtyard to the north and took me to the room facing the special area, in front of the north-facing building.
Ezekiel 42:2 The north door was 100 cubits long and 50 cubits wide.
Ezekiel 42:3 Opposite the twenty cubits reserved for the inner courtyard, and opposite the pavement for the outer courtyard, there was a three-story gallery facing another gallery.
Ezekiel 42:4 In front of the rooms was a path ten cubits wide inside, one cubit wide; and the doors faced north.
Ezekiel 42:5 The upper rooms were smaller because the walkways were higher than these rooms, the lower, and the middle ones of the building.
Ezekiel 42:6 They had three levels, but no columns like the courtyard columns: so the building was narrower than the bottom and middle levels from the ground.
Ezekiel 42:7 The outside wall, facing the side rooms towards the outer courtyard in front of the rooms, was fifty cubits long.
Ezekiel 42:8 The rooms in the outer courtyard were fifty cubits long, and in front of the temple, they were one hundred cubits.
Ezekiel 42:9 Below these rooms was an entrance on the east side, so one could go into them from the outer courtyard.
Ezekiel 42:10 The rooms were in the thick part of the east side wall of the courtyard, across from the sacred area and the main building.
Ezekiel 42:11 The path in front of them looked like the north-facing rooms, as long and as wide; and all their exits matched their designs and their doors.
Ezekiel 42:12 Near the south-facing rooms, there was an entrance at the beginning of the path, the path that leads straight past the eastern wall as you go into them.
Ezekiel 42:13 He told me, "The rooms to the north and south of the sacred area are holy. The priests who come near to God will eat the most holy offerings there. They will also put the most holy offerings, the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings there, because the place is holy."
Ezekiel 42:14 When the priests go inside, they must not leave the holy area for the outside courtyard. They must leave their special clothes there because they are sacred. They should change into different clothes to serve the people.
Ezekiel 42:15 After he finished measuring the inner house, he took me to the east-facing gate and measured all around it.
Ezekiel 42:16 He measured the east side, five hundred long sticks, all around with the stick.
Ezekiel 42:17 He measured the north side, 500 long sticks, all around with the measuring stick.
Ezekiel 42:18 He measured the south side, five hundred long sticks, with the measuring stick.

Ezekiel 42:20 He measured it on all four sides. It had a wall around it, 500 rods long and 500 rods wide, to separate the holy place from the common area.

Ezekiel 43:1 Later, he took me to the gate that faces east.
Ezekiel 43:2 Look, the glory of God of Israel came from the east, and his voice sounded like loud rushing waters, and the earth glowed with his glory.
Ezekiel 43:3 I saw a vision like the one before, when I came to destroy the city. It was like what I had seen by the Chebar River; I fell face down.
Ezekiel 43:4 God's glory entered the house through the gate facing east.
Ezekiel 43:5 The spirit lifted me up and took me to the inner courtyard; and look, God's glory filled the temple.
Ezekiel 43:6 I heard him talking to me from the house; and the man was standing next to me.
Ezekiel 43:7 He told me, "Human, the spot where my throne rests, and where my feet touch the ground, is where I will live among Israel's people forever. My holy name will not be spoiled by them or their kings again, not by their unfaithfulness or the dead bodies of their kings on their sacred hills.
Ezekiel 43:8 They placed their doorways next to my doorways, their doorposts beside mine, with only a wall between us. They made my holy name dirty with the terrible things they did. That's why I have been angry and punished them.
Ezekiel 43:9 Now, let them stop their unfaithfulness and remove their kings' dead bodies far from me, then I will live among them forever.
Ezekiel 43:10 You, human, show the temple to the people of Israel, so they will feel sorry for their sins, and let them follow the design.
Ezekiel 43:11 If they feel sorry for everything they have done, show them the design of the temple, its appearance, all its exits and entrances, and all its details, rules, and laws. Write these down for them to see, so they can follow the complete design and all the rules and obey them.
Ezekiel 43:12 This is the rule for the temple: The entire area on the mountain top around it will be very holy. This is the rule for the temple.
Ezekiel 43:13 These are the altar's dimensions in units: A unit is a unit plus the width of a hand; the base shall be a unit long and a unit wide, and its surrounding edge shall be the width of a hand; and this will be the top part of the altar.
Ezekiel 43:14 From the floor to the lower ledge will be about three feet high and one and a half feet wide; and from the small ledge to the large ledge, it will be about six feet high and one and a half feet wide.
Ezekiel 43:15 The altar will be four cubits high; and there will be four horns extending upward from the altar.
Ezekiel 43:16 The altar will be twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide, forming a square at each of its four corners.
Ezekiel 43:17 The platform will be fourteen cubits long and fourteen wide on all four sides; the edge around it will be half a cubit wide; the base will be a cubit all around; and its steps will face east.
Ezekiel 43:18 He told me, "Human, this is what God says: These are the rules for the altar when it's built, to burn offerings on it and to splash blood on it."
Ezekiel 43:19 You must give the Levite priests from Zadok's descendants, who come to serve me, a young bull for a sin sacrifice, says God.
Ezekiel 43:20 Take some of its blood and put it on the four horns, on the four corners of the altar, and around the edge. This will clean and purify it.
Ezekiel 43:21 You must take the bull used for the sin offering and burn it in the designated area outside the holy place.
Ezekiel 43:22 On the second day, you must offer a perfect young goat for a sin offering, and they will clean the altar like they did with the young bull.
Ezekiel 43:23 After you finish purifying, offer a young bull and a sheep, both without any faults.
Ezekiel 43:24 You will present them before God, and the priests will sprinkle salt on them, and they will make them a burnt offering to God.
Ezekiel 43:25 For seven days, you must get ready a goat for a sin offering each day. They must also get ready a young bull and a ram from the herd, both without any faults.
Ezekiel 43:26 They must clean the altar for seven days to make it pure; and during this time, they must also set themselves apart as holy.
Ezekiel 43:27 After these days are over, starting on the eighth day, the priests will put your burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar, and God will accept you.

Ezekiel 44:1 Then he led me back to the outer sanctuary gate facing east; it was closed.
Ezekiel 44:2 God told me, "This gate must stay closed and not be opened. Nobody will go through it because God, the God of Israel, has gone through it, so it must stay closed."
Ezekiel 44:3 It is for the leader; the leader will sit there to eat bread in front of God; he will go in through the porch of that gate and leave the same way.
Ezekiel 44:4 He led me to the north gate in front of the temple. I saw the brightness of God filling God's temple, and I fell with my face to the ground.
Ezekiel 44:5 God said to me, "Human, pay close attention and look with your eyes, and listen with your ears to everything I tell you about all the rules of God's house and all its laws; notice carefully the entrance to the house and every exit of the holy place."
Ezekiel 44:6 You will tell the rebels, even the people of Israel, 'God says: People of Israel, you have done enough terrible things.
Ezekiel 44:7 You brought outsiders, with unchanged hearts and bodies, into my holy place, making it unclean, even my house, when you offered my food, the best parts and the blood, breaking my agreement because of all your terrible acts.
Ezekiel 44:8 You did not take care of my sacred things; instead, you chose people to take care of my sacred place for your own benefit.
Ezekiel 44:9 God says: No foreigner, not loyal in heart or body, will enter my holy place among the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 44:10 The Levites who turned away from me when Israel followed other gods; they must carry their guilt.
Ezekiel 44:11 They will serve in my holy place, take care of the doors of the temple, and help in the temple: they will kill the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people, and they will stand before the people to serve them.
Ezekiel 44:12 Because they served them near their idols and made the people of Israel do wrong, I have raised my hand against them, says God, and they will be responsible for their sins.
Ezekiel 44:13 They must not come close to me to serve as priests or approach any of my sacred things or the most holy place. Instead, they must face the embarrassment and the wrong things they have done.
Ezekiel 44:14 But I will make them responsible for taking care of the house, for all its work, and for everything that is done inside it.
Ezekiel 44:15 The priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who took care of my holy place when the Israelites turned away from me, will come close to me to serve me. They will stand before me to give me the fat and the blood, says God.
Ezekiel 44:16 They will go into my holy place, they will come close to my table to serve me, and they will follow my commands.
Ezekiel 44:17 When they go through the gates of the inner courtyard, they must wear linen clothes; no wool is to be on them while they serve inside the inner gates and area.
Ezekiel 44:18 They should wear linen hats on their heads and linen underpants around their waists; they must not wear anything that makes them sweat.
Ezekiel 44:19 When they go out to the outer courtyard, to meet the people, they must take off the clothes they wore to serve and leave them in the holy rooms. Then they must wear other clothes so they don't make the people holy with their clothes.
Ezekiel 44:20 They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long but should only trim their hair.
Ezekiel 44:21 Priests must not drink wine before they go into the inner courtyard.
Ezekiel 44:22 They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only young women from Israel, or a widow who was married to a priest before.
Ezekiel 44:23 They will teach my people the difference between what is holy and what is not holy, and help them to tell apart what is unclean and what is clean.
Ezekiel 44:24 When there is a dispute, they will serve as judges; they will make decisions using my rules. They must follow my laws and instructions during all my gatherings and respect my Sabbaths.
Ezekiel 44:25 They must not touch a dead body and become unclean, except for their father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or a sister who was not married, for these they can become unclean.
Ezekiel 44:26 After he is clean, they will count seven days for him.
Ezekiel 44:27 On the day he enters the inner part of the holy place to serve, he must bring his sin offering, says God.
Ezekiel 44:28 It will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. You must not give them any property in Israel: I am their property.
Ezekiel 44:29 They will eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering; and all dedicated items in Israel will belong to them.
Ezekiel 44:30 Give the priest the first part of every crop and every offering you make. Also give him the first of your bread dough so he can ask God to bless your home.
Ezekiel 44:31 The priests must not eat anything that has died on its own or been killed by other animals, whether it's a bird or another kind of animal.

Ezekiel 45:1 Also, when you divide the land to inherit it, you must set aside a special gift for God, a holy part of the land. It will be 25,000 units long and 10,000 units wide. All around this holy area will be considered sacred.
Ezekiel 45:2 The sacred area will be a square, 500 units long and 500 units wide, with a 50-unit border around it.
Ezekiel 45:3 Measure an area that is twenty-five thousand units long and ten thousand units wide; this will be the location of the holy sanctuary and the most holy place.
Ezekiel 45:4 The special part of the land will be for the priests who serve in the holy place, and who approach to serve God. It will provide space for their homes and a sacred area for the holy place.
Ezekiel 45:5 The area 25,000 units long and 10,000 units wide will also be for the Levites, who serve at the temple, as their own property with twenty rooms.
Ezekiel 45:6 You must set aside for the city an area 5,000 units wide and 25,000 units long, next to the sacred part of the land. This will be for all the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 45:7 A share of land will be for the leader on both sides of the sacred offering area and the city property, in front of the sacred offering area and the city property, from the west end to the east end. The length will match one of the sections, from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.
Ezekiel 45:8 He will own land in Israel, and my leaders will not oppress my people anymore; they will give the rest of the land to the families of Israel.
Ezekiel 45:9 God says, "That's enough, leaders of Israel: stop the violence and destruction, make fair decisions and act justly, stop taking things unfairly from my people," says God.
Ezekiel 45:10 You must use fair scales, a fair ephah, and a fair bath.
Ezekiel 45:11 The ephah and the bath will have the same size, so that the bath holds one-tenth of a homer and the ephah also holds one-tenth of a homer. Their size will be based on the homer.
Ezekiel 45:12 A shekel equals twenty gerahs. Use twenty shekels, plus twenty-five shekels, plus fifteen shekels, for your maneh.
Ezekiel 45:13 Offer this gift: one-sixth of an ephah from a homer of wheat and one-sixth of an ephah from a homer of barley.
Ezekiel 45:14 About the oil rule, for each oil bath, you should give one-tenth of a bath from a cor, which is the same as an homer of ten baths, because ten baths make an homer.
Ezekiel 45:15 Take one lamb from every two hundred from the rich pastures of Israel for a food offering, a burnt offering, and peace offerings to ask for forgiveness for them, says God.
Ezekiel 45:16 Every person in the country must give this offering for the leader in Israel.
Ezekiel 45:17 It is the leader's duty to provide burnt sacrifices, food gifts, and drink gifts during festivals, new moon celebrations, and Sabbaths, at all special times for the people of Israel. He must arrange the sin sacrifice, the food offering, the burnt sacrifice, and the offerings for well-being to ask for forgiveness for the people of Israel.
Ezekiel 45:18 God says: On the first day of the first month, you must take a young bull with no marks and clean the holy place.
Ezekiel 45:19 The priest will take some blood from the sin sacrifice and put it on the doorframes of the house, on the four edges of the altar's base, and on the doorframes of the entrance to the inner yard.
Ezekiel 45:20 On the seventh day of each month, do this for anyone who sins or who does not understand, to make the house clean.
Ezekiel 45:21 In the first month, on the fourteenth day, you must celebrate Passover, a seven-day festival; eat bread without yeast.
Ezekiel 45:22 On that day, the leader will provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
Ezekiel 45:23 For seven days of the festival, he must make a burnt offering to God every day: seven bulls and seven male sheep that are perfect, and one goat every day for a sin offering.
Ezekiel 45:24 He must offer a food gift of an ephah for a bull, an ephah for a ram, and a quart of oil with each ephah.
Ezekiel 45:25 On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he must do the same things during the seven-day festival, just like for the sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil.

Ezekiel 46:1 God says: The gate of the inner yard facing east must be closed during the six workdays. But on the Sabbath, it should be opened, and also on the new moon day, it should be opened.
Ezekiel 46:2 The prince will go in through the gateway's outer porch, stand by the gatepost, and the priests will get his burnt offering and peace offerings ready. He will bow down at the gate's entrance, then leave, and the gate will stay open until evening.
Ezekiel 46:3 The local people must worship at the entrance of this gate on Sabbaths and new moon days, honoring God.
Ezekiel 46:4 The sacrifice the leader gives to God on the Sabbath day should be six perfect lambs and one perfect ram.
Ezekiel 46:5 The grain offering should be an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs, whatever he can afford, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
Ezekiel 46:6 On the day of the new moon, there must be a young, perfect bull and six lambs and a ram, all without any defects.
Ezekiel 46:7 He must bring a grain offering: one ephah for a bull, one ephah for a ram, whatever he can afford for the lambs, and one hin of oil for each ephah.
Ezekiel 46:8 When the prince enters, he will use the entrance of that gate, and he will leave using that same way.
Ezekiel 46:9 When the people come to worship God during the special feasts, anyone who enters through the north gate must leave through the south gate. Anyone who enters through the south gate must leave through the north gate. They should not go back the same way they came in, but leave from the opposite gate.
Ezekiel 46:10 The leader among them must enter when they enter and leave when they leave.
Ezekiel 46:11 During festivals and special ceremonies, offer a bushel of grain with each bull, a bushel with each ram, and as much as you can for each lamb, plus a gallon of oil for each bushel of grain.
Ezekiel 46:12 When the prince wants to give a burnt offering or peace offerings to God by choice, they should open the east-facing gate for him, and he will offer them as he does on the Sabbath. After he leaves, they should close the gate.
Ezekiel 46:13 Every day, you must offer a perfect first-year lamb in a burnt sacrifice to God; do this each morning.
Ezekiel 46:14 Every morning, make a food offering of one-sixth of an ephah of flour and one-third of a hin of oil to mix with the flour. This is to be a regular food offering to God forever.
Ezekiel 46:15 They must get the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil ready every morning for a regular burnt offering.
Ezekiel 46:16 God says, if a ruler gives a gift to his sons, it will belong to them; it will be theirs by right of inheritance.
Ezekiel 46:17 If he gives a servant a gift from his inheritance, it belongs to the servant until the Year of Freedom. Then it goes back to the ruler, but his children keep his inheritance.
Ezekiel 46:18 The leader must not take the people's land by force or push them out of their property; instead, he should give his children land from his own property, so my people aren't forced away from their land.
Ezekiel 46:19 He led me to the side entrance of the gate to the priests' holy rooms facing north. There I saw a space to the west on both sides.
Ezekiel 46:20 He told me, "This is where the priests will cook the guilt and sin offerings and bake the grain offerings, so they don't have to take them to the outer courtyard and make the people holy."
Ezekiel 46:21 He took me out to the outer courtyard and led me to each of its four corners; in every corner, there was a smaller courtyard.
Ezekiel 46:22 In the four corners of the courtyard, there were connected courts, each 40 units long and 30 units wide; all four corners were the same size.
Ezekiel 46:23 There was a row of buildings around them, all four sides, with cooking places built underneath the rows all around.
Ezekiel 46:24 He told me, "These are the kitchens where the temple workers will cook the people's sacrifices."

Ezekiel 47:1 Later, he took me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water flowing out from beneath the entrance toward the east, since the temple faced east. The water was coming down from under the right side of the temple, south of the altar.
Ezekiel 47:2 He led me from the north gate and took me outside to the outer east-facing gate. I saw water flowing on the right side.
Ezekiel 47:3 When the man with the measuring line went east, he measured a thousand units, and led me through water up to my ankles.
Ezekiel 47:4 He measured another thousand and led me through water up to my knees. Then he measured another thousand and led me through water up to my waist.
Ezekiel 47:5 Then he measured a thousand cubits, and it became a river too deep to walk across, with water deep enough to swim in, a river that couldn't be crossed on foot.
Ezekiel 47:6 He said to me, "Human, have you seen this?" Then he took me back to the edge of the river.
Ezekiel 47:7 When I came back, I saw many trees along both sides of the riverbank.
Ezekiel 47:8 He told me, "These waters flow to the eastern region, go down into the desert, and enter the sea. When they reach the sea, its waters will become fresh.
Ezekiel 47:9 Everything that is alive and moves, wherever the rivers flow, will survive. There will be a lot of fish because the waters will flow there and heal them; everything will live where the river goes.
Ezekiel 47:10 Fishers will stand by it, from Engedi to Eneglaim; there they will spread out nets; their fish will be of many types, like the fish of the great sea, very many.
Ezekiel 47:11 But its muddy parts and its swamps will not be healed; they will be left to salt.
Ezekiel 47:12 By the river, on both sides of its bank, all kinds of trees will grow for food. Their leaves won't wither, and their fruit won't run out. They will produce new fruit every month because they are watered by a stream from the holy place. Their fruit will be for eating, and their leaves for healing.
Ezekiel 47:13 God says: This will be the border you use to divide the land for Israel's twelve tribes: Joseph will get two shares.
Ezekiel 47:14 You will all receive it as your own: I promised to give it to your ancestors, and this land will become your inheritance.
Ezekiel 47:15 This will be the northern border of the land: it starts from the Great Sea and goes toward Hethlon and on to Zedad.
Ezekiel 47:16 Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, between the border of Damascus and Hamath; Hazarhatticon, near the coast of Hauran.
Ezekiel 47:17 The border starting at the sea will reach Hazarenan, touch Damascus, and extend to the far north, including Hamath's boundary. This is the northern side.
Ezekiel 47:18 Measure the east side from Hauran, Damascus, Gilead, and the land of Israel by Jordan, to the eastern border. This is the east side.
Ezekiel 47:19 The south border goes from Tamar to the Waters of Strife at Kadesh, then follows the river to the Great Sea. This is the south border.
Ezekiel 47:20 The west side will be the big sea from the border to where you face Hamath. That is the west side.
Ezekiel 47:21 You will split this land among yourselves based on the tribes of Israel.
Ezekiel 47:22 You will divide the land by drawing lots to determine who will inherit it, both for yourselves and for the foreigners who live with you and have children among you. They will be treated like native-born Israelites and will share in the inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
Ezekiel 47:23 When a foreigner lives with any of your tribes, you must give them their share of land, says God.

Ezekiel 48:1 Here are the names of the tribes. Starting from the northern tip, along the road to Hethlon, towards Hamath, and up to Hazar Enan at the northern border of Damascus, to Hamath's edge. These are the eastern and western limits. This is Dan's share.
Ezekiel 48:2 Next to Dan's land, from the east side to the west side, land for Asher.
Ezekiel 48:3 Next to Asher's boundary, from the east side to the west side, there is a part for Naphtali.
Ezekiel 48:4 Next to Naphtali's border, from the east to the west, a piece of land for Manasseh.
Ezekiel 48:5 Next to Manasseh's boundary, from the east side to the west side, comes a section for Ephraim.
Ezekiel 48:6 Next to Ephraim's territory, from the east side to the west side, there will be land for Reuben.
Ezekiel 48:7 Next to Reuben's territory, from the east to the west, there will be a section for Judah.
Ezekiel 48:8 By Judah's border, from the east to the west, you must give a land offering 25,000 reeds wide, and as long as one of the other sections, from the east to the west. The sacred place will be in the center of it.
Ezekiel 48:9 The gift you give to God must be twenty-five thousand units long and ten thousand units wide.
Ezekiel 48:10 This special gift for the priests will be: 25,000 units long in the north, 10,000 units wide in the west, 10,000 units wide in the east, and 25,000 units long in the south; God's holy place will be right in the center.
Ezekiel 48:11 It will belong to the holy priests from Zadok's descendants, who followed my commands and did not go wrong when the Israelites went wrong, unlike the Levites.
Ezekiel 48:12 The land they offer will be very holy for them, next to the Levites' land.
Ezekiel 48:13 Near the priests' area, the Levites will have a space measuring 25,000 units long and 10,000 units wide. The whole area will be 25,000 units long and 10,000 units wide.
Ezekiel 48:14 They must not sell, trade, or give away the first of the crops, because it is sacred to God.
Ezekiel 48:15 The five thousand area left next to the twenty-five thousand area will be a common space for the city, for living, and for the outskirts; and the city will be in the middle of it.
Ezekiel 48:16 The sizes will be; the north side 4,500, the south side 4,500, the east side 4,500, and the west side 4,500.
Ezekiel 48:17 The city's surrounding land will be 250 units to the north, 250 units to the south, 250 units to the east, and 250 units to the west.
Ezekiel 48:18 The remaining length next to the holy area will be ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west. This area next to the holy part will be used to grow food for those who work for the city.
Ezekiel 48:19 Those who work for the city will come from all the tribes of Israel.
Ezekiel 48:20 The offering must be a square, 25,000 by 25,000 units; give this holy offering with the city's land included.
Ezekiel 48:21 The rest will belong to the ruler, on both sides of the sacred offering and the city property, next to the 25,000 units of the offering on the east edge, and on the west, also next to the 25,000 units towards the west edge, lined up with the ruler's own shares. This will be the sacred offering, and the temple will be right in the center.
Ezekiel 48:22 Also, from the land belonging to the Levites and the land of the city, which is in the middle of the prince's land, between Judah's territory and Benjamin's territory, will belong to the prince.

Ezekiel 48:25 Next to Simeon's territory, from the east side to the west side, is Issachar's share.
Ezekiel 48:26 Next to Issachar's territory, from east to west, is Zebulun's land.
Ezekiel 48:27 Next to Zebulun's boundary, from the east to the west, is Gad's share.
Ezekiel 48:28 Next to Gad's territory, on the south, the boundary will run from Tamar to the Meribah waters in Kadesh, then along the river to the big sea.
Ezekiel 48:29 This is the land you will distribute by drawing lots to the tribes of Israel for them to inherit, and these are their shares, says God.
Ezekiel 48:30 Here are the city's northern exit points, 4,500 units long.

Ezekiel 48:33 On the south side, four thousand five hundred units long with three gates: one gate for Simeon, one for Issachar, and one for Zebulun.
Ezekiel 48:34 On the west side, 4,500 units with their three gates: one gate for Gad, one gate for Asher, one gate for Naphtali.
Ezekiel 48:35 The city was 18,000 units around, and from that day on it will be called "God is there."

Daniel 1:1 In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and surrounded it.
Daniel 1:2 God let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, and some of God's house items. Nebuchadnezzar took them to Shinar, to his own god's temple, and placed them in his god's treasury.
Daniel 1:3 The king told Ashpenaz, the head of his servants, to bring some young Israelites from royal families, and young nobles.
Daniel 1:4 Children without flaws, good-looking, wise in all ways, clever in knowledge, understanding science, who could serve in the king's palace, and who could be taught the Chaldeans’ education and language.
Daniel 1:5 The king gave them a daily amount of his own food and wine to eat and drink. He did this for three years so they could be healthy enough to serve him.
Daniel 1:6 Among these were Judah's descendants: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
Daniel 1:7 The head of the eunuchs gave them new names: he named Daniel, Belteshazzar; Hananiah was called Shadrach; Mishael was called Meshach; and Azariah was called Abednego.
Daniel 1:8 Daniel decided in his heart not to make himself unclean with the king's food or the wine he drank. So he asked the chief officer for permission not to make himself unclean.
Daniel 1:9 God made Daniel liked and loved by the chief eunuch.
Daniel 1:10 The official in charge of the servants told Daniel, "I am afraid of the king who has decided what you should eat and drink. What if he sees you looking worse than the other young men your age? Then I could get in trouble with the king."
Daniel 1:11 Daniel spoke to Melzar, who was put in charge of Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah by the chief official.
Daniel 1:12 Test us for ten days: give us only vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Daniel 1:13 Let our faces be examined before you, and the faces of the kids who eat the king's food; and treat us as you see fit.
Daniel 1:14 He agreed to their request and tested them for ten days.
Daniel 1:15 After ten days, they looked healthier and better-fed than any of the young people who ate the king's food.
Daniel 1:16 So Melzar removed their share of meat and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables instead.
Daniel 1:17 God gave these four young people knowledge and skill in all kinds of learning and wisdom, and Daniel could understand all kinds of visions and dreams.
Daniel 1:18 After the time set by the king to bring them in was over, the chief official presented them to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Daniel 1:19 The king spoke with them, but no one was like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, so they served the king.
Daniel 1:20 In every area of wisdom and knowledge where the king tested them, he saw they were ten times better than all the sorcerers and fortune-tellers in his whole kingdom.
Daniel 1:21 Daniel remained until King Cyrus's first year.

Daniel 2:1 In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's rule, he had dreams that upset his mind, and he could not sleep.
Daniel 2:2 Then the king ordered the magicians, astrologers, sorcerers, and Chaldeans to be called to tell him his dreams. So they came and stood in front of the king.
Daniel 2:3 The king said to them, "I had a dream that troubled me and I want to understand it."
Daniel 2:4 The Chaldeans said to the king in their language, "King, may you live forever. Tell us your dream, and we will explain its meaning."
Daniel 2:5 The king replied to the Chaldeans, "I have forgotten the dream. If you do not tell me what I dreamed and what it means, you will be chopped up, and your homes will be turned into piles of rubbish."
Daniel 2:6 If you tell the dream and its meaning, you will get gifts, rewards, and great honor from me: so tell me the dream and its meaning.
Daniel 2:7 They replied and said, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning."
Daniel 2:8 The king replied, "I am sure that you are trying to buy time because you realize I have forgotten the dream."
Daniel 2:9 If you don't tell me the dream, there is only one punishment for you: you have planned to tell me lies and twisted words until things change. So tell me the dream, then I'll know you can explain its meaning to me.
Daniel 2:10 The Chaldeans spoke to the king and said, "No one on earth can explain the king's dream. That's why no king, leader, or ruler has ever asked for such things from a magician, astrologer, or Chaldean."
Daniel 2:11 The king asks for something unusual, and no one else can reveal it to the king except for God, who does not live among humans.
Daniel 2:12 Because of this, the king was very angry and ordered that all the wise men of Babylon be killed.
Daniel 2:13 The order was given to kill the wise men, and they looked for Daniel and his friends to kill them too.
Daniel 2:14 Then Daniel spoke carefully and wisely to Arioch, the captain of the king's guard, who had set out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel 2:15 He replied to Arioch, the king's captain, "Why is the king's order so urgent?" Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
Daniel 2:16 Daniel went to the king and asked for more time to explain the dream's meaning to him.
Daniel 2:17 Daniel went to his house and told his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah about the matter.
Daniel 2:18 They hoped for mercy from the God of heaven about this secret, so Daniel and his friends would not die like Babylon's other wise men.
Daniel 2:19 Daniel learned the secret in a dream at night. Then he praised the God of heaven.
Daniel 2:20 Daniel said, "Praise be to God's name forever and ever, for all wisdom and power belong to him."
Daniel 2:21 He changes the times and seasons; he removes kings and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
Daniel 2:22 He uncovers deep and hidden things: he knows what lies in darkness, and light is with him.
Daniel 2:23 I thank you and praise you, God of my ancestors, for giving me wisdom and strength, and for telling me what we asked of you: you have let us know the king's issue.
Daniel 2:24 So Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had ordered to kill the wise men of Babylon. He said to him, "Do not kill the wise men of Babylon. Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning to the king."
Daniel 2:25 Arioch quickly brought Daniel to the king and said, "I have found a man from the captives of Judah who can explain the dream to the king."
Daniel 2:26 The king said to Daniel, also known as Belteshazzar, "Can you tell me the dream I had and explain its meaning?"
Daniel 2:27 Daniel spoke to the king and said, "The mystery the king asked about is something that wise men, astrologers, magicians, and fortune tellers cannot explain to the king."
Daniel 2:28 There is a God in heaven who reveals secrets and has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the future. Your dream and the visions you had in your bed are about these events.
Daniel 2:29 O king, while in bed, you wondered what the future holds. The one who shows secrets has told you what will happen.
Daniel 2:30 But for me, I wasn't told this secret because I am wiser than anyone else. Instead, it was so I could explain it to the king and so you could understand what's in your heart.
Daniel 2:31 You, O king, saw a huge statue. This huge statue, very shiny and bright, stood in front of you; and it looked frightening.
Daniel 2:32 The statue's head was made of pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, its stomach and hips were bronze.
Daniel 2:33 His legs are made of iron, his feet are a mix of iron and clay.
Daniel 2:34 You saw until a stone was cut out, not by hands, which hit the statue on its feet made of iron and clay, and shattered them.
Daniel 2:35 Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold all broke into pieces at once and turned into dust like what you find at the threshing place in summer. The wind blew it all away without leaving a trace. And the stone that hit the statue grew into a big mountain that filled the whole earth.
Daniel 2:36 This is the dream, and we will explain its meaning to the king.
Daniel 2:37 You, O king, are a king of kings because God in heaven has given you a kingdom, power, and might, and honor.
Daniel 2:38 Wherever people live, God has given you power over all the animals on the land and birds in the sky. You are the ruler of them all. You are like the head of gold.
Daniel 2:39 After you, another less powerful kingdom will rise, followed by a third kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole earth.
Daniel 2:40 The fourth kingdom will be as strong as iron. Just as iron crushes and dominates everything, this kingdom will crush and bruise all.
Daniel 2:41 And as you saw the feet and toes made partly of clay and partly of iron, the kingdom will be split. Yet some of its strength will be like iron, just as you saw iron mixed with clay.
Daniel 2:42 The toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly fragile.
Daniel 2:43 You saw iron mixed with wet clay, they will mix with people, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.
Daniel 2:44 During the time of these kings, God from heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed. This kingdom won't be given to others. Instead, it will crush and end all these kingdoms and last forever.
Daniel 2:45 Because you saw a stone cut from the mountain without hands, and it smashed the iron, brass, clay, silver, and gold to pieces, God has shown the king what will happen in the future: the dream is certain, and its meaning is reliable.
Daniel 2:46 Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell to the ground, honored Daniel, and ordered that they give offerings and pleasant smells to him.
Daniel 2:47 The king said to Daniel, "It's true, your God is the most powerful God, the ruler of kings, and shows deep secrets because you could show this secret."
Daniel 2:48 The king made Daniel very important, gave him lots of gifts, and put him in charge of all of Babylon and the leaders of Babylon's wise men.
Daniel 2:49 Daniel asked the king, and he put Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in charge of the tasks in Babylon. But Daniel stayed working at the king's entrance.

Daniel 3:1 King Nebuchadnezzar made a gold statue sixty cubits tall and six cubits wide and set it up on the plain of Dura in the Babylon region.
Daniel 3:2 King Nebuchadnezzar sent for the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, advisers, sheriffs, and all provincial leaders to attend the dedication of the statue he had erected.
Daniel 3:3 Then the leaders, officials, commanders, judges, money keepers, advisors, officers, and all province rulers gathered for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had raised; and they stood in front of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had raised.
Daniel 3:4 A messenger shouted, "People, countries, and speakers of different tongues, this is an order for you."
Daniel 3:5 When you hear the music of the horn, flute, harp, lyre, zither, pipe, and all other musical sounds, you must bow down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Daniel 3:6 Anyone who does not bow down and worship will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace.
