Daniel 3:7 So at that time, when everyone heard the music from the horn, flute, harp, and other instruments, all the people from different nations and with different languages bowed down and worshipped the gold statue King Nebuchadnezzar had made.
Daniel 3:8 So at that time, some Chaldeans approached and charged the Jews with a crime.
Daniel 3:9 They spoke and said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, may you live forever."
Daniel 3:10 You, king, have ordered that everyone who hears the music of horns, flutes, harps, lyres, and other instruments must bow down and worship the gold statue.
Daniel 3:11 Whoever does not bow down and worship will be thrown into a blazing furnace.
Daniel 3:12 Some Jews you put in charge of Babylon's work, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, O king, don't respect you. They don't worship your gods or bow to the gold statue you made.
Daniel 3:13 Nebuchadnezzar, filled with anger, ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought to him. Then, they were taken to the king.
Daniel 3:14 Nebuchadnezzar spoke and asked them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden statue I have made?"
Daniel 3:15 If you are ready, as soon as you hear the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all music, to fall down and worship the statue I made, good. But if you don't worship, you will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace. And what God can save you from me?
Daniel 3:16 Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to the king, "Oh Nebuchadnezzar, we do not need to defend ourselves in this situation."
Daniel 3:17 If this is true, our God whom we serve can save us from the fiery furnace, and He will rescue us from your power, O king.
Daniel 3:18 If not, know this, O king, we will not serve your gods or bow to the gold statue you made.
Daniel 3:19 Then Nebuchadnezzar became very angry, and his face looked different when he looked at Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. So he ordered that the furnace be heated seven times more than usual.
Daniel 3:20 He ordered the strongest soldiers in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing furnace.
Daniel 3:21 These men were tied up in their jackets, pants, hats, and other clothes, and thrown into the middle of the blazing furnace.
Daniel 3:22 Because the king's order was urgent and the furnace very hot, the fire's flames killed the men who took Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
Daniel 3:23 These three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell into the middle of the blazing furnace tied up.
Daniel 3:24 Then King Nebuchadnezzar was amazed and got up quickly. He said to his advisors, "Didn't we throw three tied-up men into the fire?" They replied to the king, "Yes, it's true, O king."
Daniel 3:25 He replied, "Look, I see four men unbound, walking around in the fire unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of God."
Daniel 3:26 Then Nebuchadnezzar went up to the entrance of the flaming furnace, spoke, and said, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you who serve the highest God, come out and come here." So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego walked out of the fire.
Daniel 3:27 The leaders, officials, and officers, along with the king's advisors, came together and saw that the fire did not hurt these men. Not even their hair was burnt, their clothes were not damaged, and they didn't even smell like smoke.
Daniel 3:28 Then Nebuchadnezzar said, "Praise be to the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel to rescue his followers who trusted in him. They defied the king's command and were willing to give up their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God."
Daniel 3:29 So I order that if anyone from any nation or language says something wrong about Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego's God, they will be punished severely, and their homes will be destroyed because no other god can save like this.
Daniel 3:30 Then the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego higher positions in the province of Babylon.

Daniel 4:1 King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, countries, and languages living on the earth; may you have more and more peace.
Daniel 4:2 I thought it was good to show the signs and wonders that God has done for me.
Daniel 4:3 God's signs are amazing, and his wonders are powerful! His kingdom will never end, and he rules forever.
Daniel 4:4 I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at peace in my home and doing well in my palace.
Daniel 4:5 I had a dream that scared me, and the ideas in my bed and the pictures in my head disturbed me.
Daniel 4:6 So I ordered that all the wise men of Babylon be brought to me to explain the meaning of the dream.
Daniel 4:7 The magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and fortune tellers came in, and I told them my dream, but they couldn't explain what it meant.
Daniel 4:8 Finally, Daniel came to see me, named Belteshazzar after my god, and filled with the spirit of the holy gods: I shared my dream with him, saying,
Daniel 4:9 O Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I am aware that you have the spirit of the holy gods, and nothing secret bothers you. Tell me what my dream means that I saw, and explain it to me.
Daniel 4:10 In my bed, I had these dreams: I looked, and there was a tall tree standing in the center of the world.
Daniel 4:11 The tree grew tall and strong, its top touched the sky, and it could be seen from the farthest parts of the earth.
Daniel 4:12 Its leaves were beautiful, it had lots of fruit, and there was food for everyone. Wild animals found shade under it, birds lived in its branches, and all creatures ate from it.
Daniel 4:13 In my dream, as I lay in bed, I saw a messenger, a holy one, coming down from the sky.
Daniel 4:14 He shouted loudly, "Cut down the tree, trim its branches, shake its leaves off, and spread its fruit around: let the animals leave from under it, and the birds from its branches."
Daniel 4:15 But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, held with a band of iron and bronze, surrounded by young grass; let it be damp with the dew from the sky, and share its place with the animals among the plants of the earth.
Daniel 4:16 Change his heart from a human's to a beast's, and let seven periods of time pass over him.
Daniel 4:17 This decision is by the command of the guardians, and the order from the holy ones, so all people may learn that God has power over human kingdoms, and gives them to anyone he chooses, even to the least important people.
Daniel 4:18 I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had this dream. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means, because all the wise people in my kingdom can't explain it. But you can, because you have the spirit of the holy gods in you.
Daniel 4:19 Then Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, was shocked for an hour, and his thoughts worried him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning upset you." Daniel replied, "My lord, the dream is for those who dislike you, and its meaning is for your foes."
Daniel 4:20 The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, reaching high to the sky and visible to the whole world;
Daniel 4:21 Its leaves were beautiful, it had lots of fruit, and it provided food for everyone; animals lived under it, and birds made their homes in its branches.
Daniel 4:22 You, O king, have grown and become strong; your greatness has increased and extends to the heavens, and your rule to the ends of the earth.
Daniel 4:23 The king saw a guardian and a sacred being coming down from the sky, saying, "Cut the tree down and get rid of it, but leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with iron and bronze in the young grass of the field. Let it get wet with the morning dew, and share the land with the wild animals, until seven periods of time go by."
Daniel 4:24 This is the meaning, O king, and this is God's command that has come to you, the king:
Daniel 4:25 You will be driven away from people, and you will live with the wild animals. You will eat grass like cows, and you will be covered with the dew of the sky. Seven periods of time will pass by for you until you understand that God has power over human kingdoms and gives them to anyone he chooses.
Daniel 4:26 They said to leave the tree's stump and roots; your kingdom will remain yours after you understand that God rules the heavens.
Daniel 4:27 So, king, please accept my advice: stop sinning, do what is right, and be kind to the poor. Maybe then you will have a peaceful life.
Daniel 4:28 Everything happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Daniel 4:29 After twelve months, he walked in the royal palace of Babylon.
Daniel 4:30 The king said, "Isn't this the great Babylon that I built as a royal palace by my mighty power and for the glory of my royal status?"
Daniel 4:31 As the king was speaking, a voice came from the sky, saying, "King Nebuchadnezzar, this message is for you: Your power as king is taken away from you."
Daniel 4:32 They will force you away from people, and you will live with wild animals. You will eat grass like cows, and seven periods will go by until you understand that God rules over the kingdoms of people and gives them to anyone he chooses.
Daniel 4:33 Right away, Nebuchadnezzar's fate happened: he was separated from people, ate grass like cattle, his body got wet with dew, until his hair grew long like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.
Daniel 4:34 At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my mind came back to me. I praised and respected the Most High. I gave honor to him who lives forever. His rule goes on forever, and his kingdom lasts for all time.
Daniel 4:35 Everyone on earth is considered unimportant: and God does what he wants with the heavenly forces and people on earth: and no one can stop his action, or ask him, "What are you doing?"
Daniel 4:36 At that moment, my thinking became clear again. For the good of my kingdom, my honor and my radiance came back to me. My advisers and my nobles searched for me, and I regained my power over my kingdom, with even greater grandeur given to me.
Daniel 4:37 Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and lift up and respect the King of heaven. All his deeds are right, and his paths are fair. He can humble those who are proud.

Daniel 5:1 King Belshazzar made a huge feast for a thousand of his nobles and drank wine in front of them.
Daniel 5:2 While Belshazzar was drinking wine, he ordered to bring the gold and silver cups that Nebuchadnezzar, his father, had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. He wanted the king, his leaders, his wives, and his mistresses to drink from them.
Daniel 5:3 Then they brought the gold cups taken from God's temple in Jerusalem; and the king, his officials, his wives, and his mistresses drank from them.
Daniel 5:4 They drank wine and praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
Daniel 5:5 Right then, fingers like a man's appeared and wrote on the wall by the lampstand in the king's palace. The king saw the hand as it was writing.
Daniel 5:6 The king's face changed and his thoughts scared him, making his hips shake and his knees knock together.
Daniel 5:7 The king shouted to bring the star readers, the Chaldeans, and fortune tellers. The king said to Babylon's wise men, "Whoever reads this writing and explains it to me will be dressed in red, wear a gold chain, and be the third most powerful in the kingdom."
Daniel 5:8 All the king's smart people came in, but they couldn't read the writing or explain its meaning to the king.
Daniel 5:9 King Belshazzar became very worried, his face showed his fear, and his nobles were amazed.
Daniel 5:10 The queen heard what the king and his nobles said and entered the banquet hall. She spoke, "King, may you live forever. Don't be upset or look so troubled."
Daniel 5:11 In your kingdom, there's a man with God's holy spirit. He was known for his wisdom like that of the gods during your father's time. This man, whom King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, put in charge of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and fortune tellers.
Daniel 5:12 Because Daniel has a great spirit, knowledge, and insight, can explain dreams, solve difficult problems, and clear up questions, let him be brought to interpret this.
Daniel 5:13 Daniel was brought to the king. The king said to Daniel, "Are you Daniel from the captives of Judah, whom my father the king brought from the land of the Jews?"
Daniel 5:14 I have heard that God's spirit is in you and that you have knowledge, insight, and great wisdom.
Daniel 5:15 And now, the wise men and astrologers have been presented to me to read this writing and explain its meaning, but they could not reveal what it means.
Daniel 5:16 I have heard you can explain dreams and solve problems. If you can read this writing and explain it to me, you will be dressed in red clothes, wear a gold necklace, and be the third highest leader in the kingdom.
Daniel 5:17 Daniel spoke to the king, "Keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else; but I will read the writing for the king and explain what it means."
Daniel 5:18 O king, the highest God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar a kingdom, greatness, honor, and glory.
Daniel 5:19 Because of the greatness God gave him, all people, countries, and languages were afraid and shook before him. Whoever he wanted to kill, he killed; whoever he wanted to keep alive, he spared; whoever he wanted to raise up, he raised; and whoever he wanted to lower, he lowered.
Daniel 5:20 When he became proud and stubborn, he was removed from his throne and his royal honor was taken away.
Daniel 5:21 He was sent away from people; his mind became like animals' minds, and he lived with wild donkeys. They gave him grass to eat like cows, and his body was wet with the morning dew; until he realized that God, the highest ruler, controls the kingdom of people and chooses whoever he wants to be in charge.
Daniel 5:22 And you, his son Belshazzar, did not humble your heart even though you knew all this.
Daniel 5:23 You have acted proudly against God of heaven. People brought God's house cups to you, and you, your leaders, wives, and girlfriends drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which can't see, hear, or know. Yet, you didn't honor the God who holds your life and controls your actions.
Daniel 5:24 Then the hand was sent by God, and this message was written.
Daniel 5:25 This is the message that was written: Numbered, Numbered, Weighed, Divided.
Daniel 5:26 God has counted your kingdom's days and has brought it to an end.
Daniel 5:27 You have been weighed on the scales and found not good enough.
Daniel 5:28 Your kingdom is split and given to the Medes and Persians.
Daniel 5:29 Belshazzar ordered, and they dressed Daniel in a red robe, put a gold chain around his neck, and announced that he would be the third highest leader in the kingdom.
Daniel 5:30 That night, Belshazzar, the Chaldean king, was killed.
Daniel 5:31 Darius from Media became the king at about 62 years old.

Daniel 6:1 Darius decided to put 120 princes in charge of the whole kingdom.
Daniel 6:2 Three presidents were in charge, with Daniel as the top one, so the leaders would answer to them and the king would not be harmed.
Daniel 6:3 Daniel was chosen over the other leaders because he had an excellent spirit; the king planned to put him in charge of the entire kingdom.
Daniel 6:4 The leaders and officials tried to find a reason to accuse Daniel about how he ran the kingdom, but they couldn't find anything wrong or a mistake, because he was loyal and no error or fault was found in him.
Daniel 6:5 Then these men said, "We will not find any reason to accuse Daniel unless it is about the law of his God."
Daniel 6:6 These leaders and officials went to the king and said, "King Darius, may you live always."
Daniel 6:7 All the leaders, governors, rulers, advisors, and officers of the kingdom agreed to create a royal law and a strong order that if anyone prays to any god or person except you, O king, within thirty days, they will be thrown into the lions' den.
Daniel 6:8 Now, king, set up the law and sign the document so that it cannot be changed, as is the rule of the Medes and Persians that does not change.
Daniel 6:9 So King Darius signed the document and the law.
Daniel 6:10 When Daniel learned that the order had been made official, he went to his home. With his windows open toward Jerusalem, he knelt down three times a day to pray and thank God, just as he always did.
Daniel 6:11 These men gathered and saw Daniel praying and asking favors from his God.
Daniel 6:12 Then they approached and spoke to the king about his order: "Have you not made a rule that for the next thirty days, anyone who prays to any god or person, except you, will be thrown into the lions' den?" The king replied, "Yes, it is true and it follows the unchangeable laws of Media and Persia."
Daniel 6:13 They replied to the king, "Daniel, from the captives of Judah, does not respect you, king, or follow the law you signed; instead, he prays three times a day."
Daniel 6:14 The king, after hearing this, was very upset with himself and was determined to save Daniel. He tried until sunset to rescue him.
Daniel 6:15 Then these men gathered together before the king and said, "King, be aware that according to the law of the Medes and Persians, no rule or law set by the king can be altered."
Daniel 6:16 The king ordered Daniel to be thrown into the lions' den. Then he said to Daniel, "The God you always serve will save you."
Daniel 6:17 They brought a stone and placed it over the den's entrance; the king sealed it with his ring and his nobles' rings, so that Daniel's situation could not be altered.
Daniel 6:18 Then the king went to his palace and spent the night without eating. No music was played for him, and he could not sleep.
Daniel 6:19 The king got up very early in the morning and quickly went to the lions' den.
Daniel 6:20 When he reached the den, he called out sadly to Daniel. The king spoke and said to Daniel, "Oh Daniel, servant of the living God, can your God, whom you always serve, save you from the lions?"
Daniel 6:21 Then Daniel said to the king, "King, may you live forever."
Daniel 6:22 My God sent his angel and closed the lions' mouths so they did not harm me, because I was found innocent by God; and O king, I have also done you no harm.
Daniel 6:23 The king was very happy for Daniel, and ordered them to lift Daniel from the pit. So Daniel was lifted from the pit, and he was not hurt at all, because he trusted in God.
Daniel 6:24 The king ordered and they brought the men who had accused Daniel. They threw them, their children, and their wives into the lions' den. The lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones before they even touched the den's floor.
Daniel 6:25 King Darius wrote to all the people, countries, and language groups living on the earth; may you have lots of peace.
Daniel 6:26 I order that in all parts of my kingdom, people must shake with fear and respect before Daniel's God, because he is the living God who lasts forever. His rule will never end, and his power goes on forever.
Daniel 6:27 God saves and rescues, and he does amazing things in the sky and on the ground, who saved Daniel from the lions' power.
Daniel 6:28 Daniel did well during the time of Darius and also when Cyrus the Persian was in power.

Daniel 7:1 In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and saw visions while on his bed. After that, he wrote down the dream and explained the main points.
Daniel 7:2 Daniel spoke and said, "In my night vision, I saw the four winds of heaven stirring up the great sea."
Daniel 7:3 Four large animals came out of the sea, each different from the others.
Daniel 7:4 The first looked like a lion with eagle's wings. I watched until its wings were torn off, it was raised from the ground, made to stand on two feet like a person, and it was given a human heart.
Daniel 7:5 Look, another beast appeared, a second one that resembled a bear. It lifted itself up on one side and had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. They said to it, "Get up and eat lots of meat."
Daniel 7:6 After this, I saw another creature that looked like a leopard with four wings of a bird on its back; this beast also had four heads, and it was given power.
Daniel 7:7 After this, in my dream at night, I saw a fourth beast, very scary and powerful with big iron teeth. It ate and crushed everything, and it stomped on what was left. It was different from all the animals before it and had ten horns.
Daniel 7:8 I looked at the horns, and I saw a new small horn growing up among them. It replaced three of the first horns that were pulled out completely. This horn had eyes like a human and a mouth that said very important things.
Daniel 7:9 I watched until thrones were thrown down, and the Ancient One sat down, dressed in white as snow, with hair like pure wool. His throne was like a blazing fire, and its wheels were like burning fire.
Daniel 7:10 A river of fire flowed and came out from before God. Thousands upon thousands served him, and countless others stood before him. The court was ready, and the books were opened.
Daniel 7:11 I watched because of the loud words the horn was saying: I watched until the beast was killed, its body destroyed, and thrown into the fiery flame.
Daniel 7:12 The other animals lost their power but were allowed to live for a while longer.
Daniel 7:13 In my night dream, I saw someone like a human coming with the clouds of the sky, approaching the Eternal One, and they led him close to him.
Daniel 7:14 He was given power, honor, and a kingdom, so all people, countries, and languages would serve him: his power will last forever, it won't end, and his kingdom won't be destroyed.
Daniel 7:15 I, Daniel, felt sad deep inside me, and the visions in my mind upset me.
Daniel 7:16 I went up to one of those standing there and asked what all this meant. He explained it and helped me understand what these things signified.
Daniel 7:17 These four large animals represent four kings who will come from the earth.
Daniel 7:18 God's holy people will receive the kingdom and own it forever and ever.
Daniel 7:19 Then I would understand the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others, very frightening, with iron teeth and bronze nails; it ate, crushed, and trampled the rest with its feet.
Daniel 7:20 About the ten horns on its head, and another horn that grew, before which three horns were removed; this horn had eyes and a mouth that said very important things and looked stronger than the others.
Daniel 7:21 I saw the horn fighting against God's holy people, and it was winning over them.
Daniel 7:22 Until the Old One came, and the holy people were given the right to judge; and the time arrived for the holy people to take over the kingdom.
Daniel 7:23 He said the fourth creature will be the fourth kingdom on earth. It will be different from all other kingdoms, and it will consume the whole earth, crush it and break it apart.
Daniel 7:24 The ten horns from this kingdom represent ten kings who will come to power: and then another king will come after them who is different from the earlier ones, and he will overcome three kings.
Daniel 7:25 He will say bad things against God, tire out God's holy people, and try to change special dates and laws. They will be under his power for a set time, two times, and half a time.
Daniel 7:26 The court will be in session, and they will take away his power, to completely destroy it forever.
Daniel 7:27 The kingdom, power, and the vastness of the kingdom under all the sky will be given to the holy people of the Most High God, whose kingdom lasts forever, and everyone will serve and follow Him.
Daniel 7:28 This is the end of the story. I, Daniel, was deeply troubled by my thoughts, and my face showed it, but I kept it to myself.

Daniel 8:1 In the third year of King Belshazzar's rule, I, Daniel, had a vision, after my first one.
Daniel 8:2 I had a vision and when it happened, I was in the city of Shushan at the palace, located in Elam. In the vision, I was standing by the Ulai River.
Daniel 8:3 I looked up and saw a ram with two horns standing by the river; both horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew out last.
Daniel 8:4 I saw the ram pushing to the west, north, and south; no animals could stand against him, nor could anyone rescue from his power; he did as he pleased and became powerful.
Daniel 8:5 As I was thinking, a male goat appeared, coming from the west across the land without touching the ground, and this goat had a large horn between its eyes.
Daniel 8:6 He went to the ram with two horns, which I had seen by the river, and charged at it with great anger.
Daniel 8:7 I saw him approach the ram, full of anger, and he struck the ram, breaking its two horns. The ram had no strength to resist him, and he knocked the ram to the ground and stomped on it. No one could save the ram from him.
Daniel 8:8 So the male goat became very powerful. But when he was at his strongest, his large horn broke off. In its place, four important horns grew toward the four directions of the sky.
Daniel 8:9 From one of them, a small horn grew and became very large, stretching south, east, and toward the beautiful land.
Daniel 8:10 It grew big, up to the army of heaven, and it threw some of the army and the stars down to the earth and stepped on them.
Daniel 8:11 Yes, he made himself as great as the leader of the army, and through him the regular offering was stopped, and the sacred place was overthrown.
Daniel 8:12 An army was given to him to fight against the daily offering because of sin, and it threw the truth to the ground; and it acted and succeeded.
Daniel 8:13 I heard one holy person talking, and another holy person asked the one who spoke, "How long will the vision last about the daily offering and the sin that destroys, allowing the holy place and the people to be trampled?"
Daniel 8:14 He told me, "After 2,300 days, the holy place will be clean again."
Daniel 8:15 When I, Daniel, had seen the vision and was looking for its meaning, suddenly, I saw someone who looked like a man standing before me.
Daniel 8:16 I heard a man's voice by the Ulai Canal calling out, "Gabriel, help this person understand the vision."
Daniel 8:17 He came close to where I was standing. When he approached, I felt scared and dropped to the ground. However, he told me, "Know this, human: the vision will happen at the end time."
Daniel 8:18 As he talked with me, I was deeply asleep with my face down, but he touched me and made me stand up.
Daniel 8:19 He said, "Look, I will tell you what will happen at the very end of the anger: because at the set time, the end will come."
Daniel 8:20 The ram you saw with two horns represents the kings of Media and Persia.
Daniel 8:21 The rough goat represents the king of Greece, and the large horn between its eyes stands for the first king.
Daniel 8:22 After it is broken, four kingdoms will rise from that nation, but they will not have its power.
Daniel 8:23 In the later time of their rule, when the wrongdoers have grown completely, a king with a harsh face and skilled in riddles will rise.
Daniel 8:24 His strength will be great, but not by his own strength. He will cause astounding destruction, succeed, take action, and will ruin powerful and sacred people.
Daniel 8:25 With his clever planning, he will make deceit succeed under his control; he will think highly of himself, and using peace, he will ruin many. He will even stand against the greatest leaders, but he will be defeated by no human power.
Daniel 8:26 The dream about the evening and the morning that was described is true. So, keep the dream secret because it will happen far in the future.
Daniel 8:27 I, Daniel, passed out and was sick for some days. Then I got up and went about the king's work. I was amazed by the vision, but nobody understood it.

Daniel 9:1 In the first year of Darius, son of Ahasuerus, from the Medes' family, who became king of the Chaldean land;
Daniel 9:2 In the first year of his rule, I, Daniel, learned from the writings the number of years God told the prophet Jeremiah that Jerusalem would be in ruins, which was seventy years.
Daniel 9:3 I turned to God, to ask for help with prayers and pleas, fasting, wearing burlap, and sitting in ashes.
Daniel 9:4 I prayed to God, my God, and confessed, saying, "Oh God, the great and awesome God, who keeps His promise and kindness to those who love Him and obey His commands."
Daniel 9:5 We have sinned, done wrong, acted badly, and rebelled by turning away from your commands and laws.
Daniel 9:6 We did not listen to your prophets who spoke in your name to our kings, leaders, ancestors, and everyone in the country.
Daniel 9:7 God, you are righteous, but we are ashamed because we have sinned, both in Judah, in Jerusalem, and among all Israel, near and far, in every country where you have scattered us because of our wrongdoings against you.
Daniel 9:8 God, we deserve to be ashamed because we, our leaders, and our ancestors have sinned against you.
Daniel 9:9 God is kind and forgiving, even when we disobey him.
Daniel 9:10 We have not listened to God's voice or followed his laws given to us through his prophets.
Daniel 9:11 Yes, all Israel has broken your law by turning away and not listening to you; so the curse written in Moses's Law has come upon us because we have sinned against you.
Daniel 9:12 He has made his words come true, which he spoke against us and our leaders who judged us, by bringing a great disaster on us. Nothing like this has ever happened under the whole sky as what has been done to Jerusalem.
Daniel 9:13 The law of Moses says all this bad has happened to us. But we didn't pray to God to turn away from our wrongs and know your truth.
Daniel 9:14 So God has been watching the bad things and let them happen to us because God is fair in everything he does; we did not listen to what he said.
Daniel 9:15 And now, our God, who brought your people out of Egypt with great power and made yourself famous as seen today, we have sinned and acted badly.
Daniel 9:16 God, because of your goodness, I ask you to stop being angry with your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. Our sins and the wrongs of our ancestors have made Jerusalem and your people an embarrassment to everyone around us.
Daniel 9:17 So now, our God, listen to your servant's prayer and plea, and make your temple, that is empty, shine with your presence, for your own sake.
Daniel 9:18 My God, please listen and hear us; look and see our ruins, and the city named after you. We ask for help, not because we are good, but because of your great kindness.
Daniel 9:19 God, hear; God, forgive; God, listen and act; do not delay, for your own sake, my God: for your city and your people bear your name.
Daniel 9:20 While I was talking, praying, admitting my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and asking God for help for his holy mountain;
Daniel 9:21 Yes, as I was praying, the man Gabriel, who I had seen in my earlier vision, came quickly to me just when it was time for the evening offering.
Daniel 9:22 He told me and said, "Daniel, I have come to give you wisdom and insight."
Daniel 9:23 As soon as you started to pray, a message was sent out, and I have come to tell you, for you are very loved. So pay attention to the message and think about the vision.
Daniel 9:24 God has set apart seventy weeks for your people and your holy city to stop their rebellion, end their sins, make up for their wrongs, bring in eternal goodness, complete the vision and prophecy, and dedicate the holiest place.
Daniel 9:25 Understand this: From the time the order is given to rebuild Jerusalem until the leader, the Messiah, comes, there will be seven sets of seven years and sixty-two sets of seven years. The city will be rebuilt with streets and strong defenses, despite the difficult times.
Daniel 9:26 After sixty-two weeks, the Messiah will be killed, not for his own sake. The people of the coming prince will destroy the city and the holy place. The end will come like a flood, and until the war is over, ruins are destined.
Daniel 9:27 He will make a strong agreement with many people for one week. In the middle of the week, he will stop the offerings and sacrifices. Because of widespread wicked acts, he will leave the place empty until the end that is decided pours out on the ruined city.

Daniel 10:1 In the third year when Cyrus was king of Persia, something was shown to Daniel, who was also named Belteshazzar. This thing was true, and it was about a big event in the future. Daniel understood what he saw and what it meant.
Daniel 10:2 During that time, I, Daniel, was sad for three whole weeks.
Daniel 10:3 I didn't eat any good-tasting bread, and I didn't have any meat or drink any wine. I also didn't put any oil on my skin for the full three weeks.
Daniel 10:4 On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was by the side of the great river, called Hiddekel.
Daniel 10:5 I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen with a belt of pure gold around his waist.
Daniel 10:6 His body was like shiny green stone, his face shone like lightning, his eyes were like flaming torches, his arms and legs glowed like polished bronze, and his voice sounded like a big crowd.
Daniel 10:7 I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men with me didn't see it, but they were so scared that they ran away to hide.
Daniel 10:8 So I was alone and saw this amazing sight, and I had no strength left: for my good looks had faded away, and I kept no strength.
Daniel 10:9 I heard his voice speaking, and when I heard it, I was deeply asleep with my face down to the ground.
Daniel 10:10 I felt a hand touch me, which made me get on my knees and hands.
Daniel 10:11 He said to me, "Daniel, you are deeply loved, understand the words I'm speaking to you, and stand up, because I've been sent to you." After he said this to me, I stood up, shaking.
Daniel 10:12 He then told me, "Don't be afraid, Daniel. Because from the first day you decided to understand and humble yourself before God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words."
Daniel 10:13 The leader of Persia's kingdom resisted me for twenty-one days. But then Michael, a main leader, came to help me, and I stayed there with the Persian kings.
Daniel 10:14 I have come to help you understand what will happen to your people in the future: the vision is still for a time far away.
Daniel 10:15 After he said those things to me, I looked down and couldn't speak.
Daniel 10:16 Look, someone who looked like a human touched my lips. Then I opened my mouth and spoke to the one standing in front of me, "Oh sir, because of the vision, I am filled with pain and I have no strength left."
Daniel 10:17 How can I, a servant, speak with you, my lord? I am completely weak and have no breath left in me.
Daniel 10:18 Then someone who looked like a man came and touched me, giving me strength.
Daniel 10:19 He said, "You are very loved, don't be afraid; have peace, be brave, yes, be strong." When he spoke to me, I felt stronger and said, "Please speak, for you have made me strong."
Daniel 10:20 He asked, "Do you know why I have come to you? I will now go back to fight against the prince of Persia. And after I leave, the prince of Greece will come."
Daniel 10:21 I will show you what is written in the book of truth: no one supports me against them except for Michael, your leader.

Daniel 11:1 Also, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood by him to support and strengthen him.
Daniel 11:2 I will now show you the truth. Look, three more kings will rise in Persia; and the fourth will be much richer than the others. With his wealth, he will cause everyone to fight against Greece.
Daniel 11:3 A powerful king will rise, who will rule with a large territory and do as he pleases.
Daniel 11:4 When he rises to power, his kingdom will break apart and spread to the four directions of the sky; it won't go to his descendants or remain as it was under his rule: for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others, not his own family.
Daniel 11:5 The southern king will be powerful, as will one of his leaders; he will become stronger than the king and rule over a vast area.
Daniel 11:6 After some years, they will unite; the southern king's daughter will go to the northern king to form a pact. However, she won't keep her strength, nor will he or his strength last. She, along with her escorts, her father, and her supporter during those times, will be handed over.
Daniel 11:7 From her family's roots, one will rise to take power, bring an army, attack the northern king's stronghold, fight them, and win.
Daniel 11:8 He will also take their gods, leaders, and valuable silver and gold items as captives to Egypt; he will last longer than the king of the north.
Daniel 11:9 The king of the south will come into his kingdom and then go back to his own country.
Daniel 11:10 His sons will rise up and gather a large army. One will come for sure, sweep through and move on. Then he will go back, roused to attack his stronghold.
Daniel 11:11 The southern king will become very angry and will go out to fight the northern king. He will gather a large army, but his army will be defeated.
Daniel 11:12 When he removes many people, he will become proud; he will defeat thousands, but this will not make him stronger.
Daniel 11:13 The king from the north will come back, with a huge crowd bigger than before, and after some years, he will definitely come with a large army and lots of wealth.
Daniel 11:14 During that time, many will oppose the southern king, and your people's rebels will rise to fulfill the prophecy, but they will fail.
Daniel 11:15 The northern king will come, build a siege ramp, and capture the strongest cities. The southern forces won't be able to resist, not even the best troops, nor will they have the power to stand against him.
Daniel 11:16 Whoever attacks him will do as he pleases, and no one can stop him. He will stay in the beautiful country, which he will destroy.
Daniel 11:17 He will determine to come with the full force of his kingdom, bringing with him those who are righteous; this is what he will do: and he will offer him a woman, intending to ruin her: but she will not support him or be on his side.
Daniel 11:18 After this, he will look toward the islands and conquer many: but a ruler will end the insults made by him, making the insults fall back on him without his own dishonor.
Daniel 11:19 He will look toward his country's strongholds, but he will trip, fall, and disappear.
Daniel 11:20 A tax collector will rise to power in the kingdom, but he will be destroyed soon after, not in anger or in war.
Daniel 11:21 A despicable person will rise to power where he was not given royal honors; yet he will gain control peacefully, using smooth talk.
Daniel 11:22 A flood will sweep away everything before him; it will destroy everything, even the leader of the covenant.
Daniel 11:23 After making an agreement, he will act dishonestly: he will rise to power with the help of a few people.
Daniel 11:24 He will calmly enter the richest parts of the land; he will do things his ancestors never did, nor his ancestors before them; he will share the loot, goods, and wealth among them. Yes, he will plan his strategies against the strongholds, for a while.
Daniel 11:25 He will gather his strength and bravery to fight the southern king with a large army; but the southern king, with an even bigger and stronger army, will prepare for battle. Yet, he will fail because they will plan tricks against him.
Daniel 11:26 Yes, those who eat his food will destroy him, and his army will be swept away: many will fall down dead.
Daniel 11:27 Both kings will plan evil and lie while eating together, but they will fail because the end will come at the set time.
Daniel 11:28 Then he will go back to his country with lots of wealth; but he will be against the sacred promise; he will do great things, and return to his country.
Daniel 11:29 At the set time, he will come back and move toward the south; but it won't be like before or after.
Daniel 11:30 Ships from Chittim will attack him; he will be upset, go back, and become angry at the sacred promise. He will act on this; he will go back and work with those who abandon the sacred promise.
Daniel 11:31 Forces will support him, they will corrupt the strong sanctuary, stop the regular offering, and set up the dreadful abomination.
Daniel 11:32 Those who do evil against the agreement will be corrupted by smooth talk, but the people who know their God will be strong and take action.
Daniel 11:33 People with knowledge will teach many, but they will face violence, fire, capture, and loss for a long time.
Daniel 11:34 When they fall, they will get a little help, but many will join them with smooth talk.
Daniel 11:35 Some wise people will stumble to test, cleanse, and refine them until the end time, because it's set for a specific time.
Daniel 11:36 The king will do as he wants; he will raise himself up and make himself greater than any god, and will say amazing things against the God of all gods, and will succeed until the anger is finished: because what is decided will happen.
Daniel 11:37 He will not respect his ancestors' God, the love of women, or any god, because he will consider himself greater than all.
Daniel 11:38 He will honor the god of forces instead of his own god. He will honor a god his ancestors did not know with gold, silver, precious stones, and gifts.
Daniel 11:39 He will act this way in the strongest fortresses with a foreign god, whom he will recognize and honor with glory: he will make them rulers over many and will distribute the land for profit.
Daniel 11:40 At the end time, the southern king will attack him, and the northern king will come like a storm, with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will invade nations, sweeping through and conquering them.
Daniel 11:41 He will also go into the beautiful land, and many nations will be defeated: but Edom, Moab, and the leader of the Ammonites will escape from his power.
Daniel 11:42 He will also reach out his hand over the nations, and Egypt will not escape.
Daniel 11:43 He will control Egypt's gold and silver treasures and all its valuable items; Libyans and Ethiopians will follow him.
Daniel 11:44 News from the east and north will upset him; so he will attack angrily to destroy and kill many.
Daniel 11:45 He will set up his royal tents between the seas at the beautiful holy mountain; but he will meet his end, and no one will help him.

Daniel 12:1 During that time, Michael, the powerful prince who protects your people, will arise. There will be a period of great distress, unlike anything that has happened from the beginning of nations until then. But at that time, your people, everyone whose name is written in the book, will be saved.
Daniel 12:2 Many who are in the ground, asleep, will wake up: some will live forever and some will be forever disgraced.
Daniel 12:3 Wise people will shine like the sky, and those who lead many to do right will be like the stars forever.
Daniel 12:4 Daniel, close the words and seal the book until the end time; many will search eagerly, and knowledge will grow.
Daniel 12:5 Then I, Daniel, saw two others, one on each side of the riverbank.
Daniel 12:6 Someone asked the man dressed in linen, who was standing over the river, "How long until these amazing things end?"
Daniel 12:7 I heard the man in linen clothes above the river raise his right and left hands to the sky and promise by the eternal God that there would be a time, two times, and half a time, and after he breaks the power of the holy people, all will be done.
Daniel 12:8 I heard but did not understand. Then I asked, "My Lord, what will happen in the end?"
Daniel 12:9 He said, "Go on, Daniel: the words are secret and sealed until the end time."
Daniel 12:10 Many will be cleansed, made pure, and tested; but the wicked will keep doing wrong: and the wicked won't understand; but the wise will understand.
Daniel 12:11 Starting when the regular sacrifice is stopped and the terrible idol is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
Daniel 12:12 Happy is the person who waits and reaches 1,335 days.
Daniel 12:13 Keep going until the end: you will rest, and then receive your reward when the days are over.

Hosea 1:1 God's message came to Hosea, Beeri's son, when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah, and during Jeroboam, Joash's son, was king of Israel.
Hosea 1:2 The start of God's message through Hosea. God told Hosea, "Go, marry a woman who has been unfaithful, and have children with her, because the people have been very unfaithful, turning away from God."
Hosea 1:3 He went and married Gomer, daughter of Diblaim, who became pregnant and gave birth to a son for him.
Hosea 1:4 God told him, "Name the child Jezreel; soon I will punish Jehu's family for the bloodshed at Jezreel, and I will end the rule of Israel's kingdom."
Hosea 1:5 On that day, I will break Israel's bow in the Jezreel Valley.
Hosea 1:6 She became pregnant again and had a daughter. God told him, "Name her Loruhamah, because I will no longer show mercy to Israel’s people; I will completely remove them."
Hosea 1:7 I will show kindness to Judah's family and save them through God, their God. I will not save them with bows, swords, battles, horses, or horsemen.
Hosea 1:8 After she finished breastfeeding Loruhamah, she became pregnant and gave birth to a son.
Hosea 1:9 Then God said, "Name him Not My People, because you are not my people, and I will not be your God."
Hosea 1:10 The children of Israel will be as many as the sand by the sea, too many to measure or count. And where they were told, "You are not my people," there they will be called "Children of the living God."
Hosea 1:11 The people of Judah and Israel will unite and choose one leader, and they will rise from the land, for the day of Jezreel will be great.

Hosea 2:1 Tell your brothers, 'My People,' and your sisters, 'Loved One.'
Hosea 2:2 Ask your mother to change her ways, for she is not my wife and I am not her husband. She must stop being unfaithful and not act like an adulterer anymore.
Hosea 2:3 So I don't leave her bare, put her back as she was when born, turn her into a desert, make her like dry land, and kill her with thirst.
Hosea 2:4 I will not show kindness to her children because they are children of unfaithfulness.
Hosea 2:5 Their mother has acted like a prostitute: the one who gave birth to them has behaved disgracefully. She said, "I will chase after my lovers who provide me with food, water, wool, linen, oil, and drinks."
Hosea 2:6 So, I will block your path with thorns and build a wall so she can't find her way.
Hosea 2:7 She will chase her lovers but not catch them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will think, 'I will go back to my first husband because it was better for me then than now.'
Hosea 2:8 She did not realize that I gave her grain, wine, and oil, and increased her silver and gold, which they used for Baal.
Hosea 2:9 So I will go back and take back my grain when it's time and my wine when it's due, and I will take back my wool and flax meant to cover her nakedness.
Hosea 2:10 I will now show her bad behavior to her lovers, and no one can save her from me.
Hosea 2:11 I will also make all her happiness stop, her holidays, her new moon celebrations, her rest days, and all her special festivals.
Hosea 2:12 I will ruin her grapevines and fig trees, which she claimed her lovers rewarded her with; I'll turn them into a wild area where wild animals will feed.
Hosea 2:13 I will punish her for the times she worshiped Baal, when she burned incense to them, wore her earrings and jewelry, chased her lovers, and forgot me, says God.
Hosea 2:14 So, I will attract her, take her to the desert, and speak kindly to her.
Hosea 2:15 I will give her vineyards again, and the valley of Achor will be a door of hope. She will sing there like when she was young and when she left Egypt.
Hosea 2:16 On that day, God says, you will call me 'My Husband' and not call me 'My Master' anymore.
Hosea 2:17 I will remove the names of the Baals from her lips, and their names will not be remembered anymore.
Hosea 2:18 On that day, I will make a promise to them with the wild animals, the birds in the sky, and the insects on the ground: I will remove the bow, the sword, and war from the land, and they will rest in safety.
Hosea 2:19 I will promise to be yours forever; yes, I will promise to be yours with fairness, with justice, with kindness, and with compassion.
Hosea 2:20 I will promise myself to you faithfully, and you will know God.
Hosea 2:21 On that day, I will listen, says God, I will hear the skies, and they will hear the land.
Hosea 2:22 The earth will receive the grain, the wine, and the oil; and they will respond to Jezreel.
Hosea 2:23 I will plant her for myself in the land; I will show love to those who were not loved; and I will tell those who were not my people, 'You are my people,' and they will say, 'You are my God.'

Hosea 3:1 God told me, "Go, show love to a woman loved by her friend but who is unfaithful, just as God loves the people of Israel, even though they turn to other gods and love to drink wine."
Hosea 3:2 I bought her for fifteen silver coins, a large amount of barley, and half that amount again.
Hosea 3:3 I told her, "You must wait for me for many days; you must not be unfaithful, and you must not belong to another man; and so I will be for you."
Hosea 3:4 The Israelites will live for a long time without a king or prince, without sacrifices, statues, special priestly clothes, or household gods.
Hosea 3:5 Later, the people of Israel will come back, look for God, and for David their king; they will respect God and his kindness in the future.

Hosea 4:1 Listen to God's message, people of Israel: God has an issue with the country's people, because they lack truth, kindness, and understanding of God.
Hosea 4:2 By swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and being unfaithful, they run wild, and violence follows violence.
Hosea 4:3 So the land will be sad, and everyone living in it will grow weak, along with the animals on the land, the birds in the sky, and even the fish in the sea will disappear.
Hosea 4:4 Let no one argue or scold another, because your people are like those who argue with a priest.
Hosea 4:5 So you will fall in the daytime, the prophet will also fall with you at night, and I will destroy your mother.
Hosea 4:6 My people are ruined because they don't know enough: because you have ignored knowledge, I will ignore you so you won't be a priest to me: since you have forgotten your God's law, I will also forget your children.
Hosea 4:7 As they grew in number, they also sinned against me: so I will turn their honor into disgrace.
Hosea 4:8 They consume my people's sin and desire their wrongdoing.
Hosea 4:9 People and priests will be alike: I will punish them for their actions and repay them for what they have done.
Hosea 4:10 They will eat but still be hungry; they will be unfaithful but not grow in number because they have stopped paying attention to God.
Hosea 4:11 Immorality, wine, and strong drink can ruin good judgment.
Hosea 4:12 My people look for advice from wooden idols, and their walking sticks tell them what to do. They have been led astray by a desire for false gods and have turned away from their God.
Hosea 4:13 They offer sacrifices on mountain tops and burn incense on hills, under oak, poplar, and elm trees, where it is shady and pleasant. As a result, your daughters will become prostitutes, and your partners will be unfaithful.
Hosea 4:14 I will not punish your daughters when they are unfaithful, nor your wives when they are unfaithful: because they themselves keep company with prostitutes and make offerings with them. So the people who do not understand will stumble.
Hosea 4:15 Even though you are unfaithful, Israel, I hope that Judah will not sin. Do not visit Gilgal, do not go to Bethaven, and do not promise by saying, "God lives."
Hosea 4:16 Israel has slipped away like a stubborn cow; now God will care for them like a lamb in a wide open space.
Hosea 4:17 Ephraim is attached to idols: leave him be.
Hosea 4:18 Their drink has gone bad; they are always unfaithful. Her leaders love disgraceful ways.
Hosea 4:19 The wind has wrapped her in its wings, and they will feel shame for their offerings.

Hosea 5:1 Listen, priests, pay attention, people of Israel, and hear this, royal house, because God will judge you. You have been traps at Mizpah and nets on Tabor.
Hosea 5:2 The rebels are skilled at killing, even though I have warned them all.
Hosea 5:3 I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me: because now, Ephraim, you are unfaithful, and Israel is unclean.
Hosea 5:4 They won't change their actions to return to God because a spirit of unfaithfulness is among them, and they don't know God.
Hosea 5:5 Israel's pride shows clearly, so Israel and Ephraim will fall because of their sins; Judah will also fall with them.
Hosea 5:6 They will go with their sheep and cattle to look for God, but they will not find him; he has pulled away from them.
Hosea 5:7 They have betrayed God: they have had unusual children: now, within a month, they will be destroyed with all they have.
Hosea 5:8 Sound the horn in Gibeah and the trumpet in Ramah; shout loudly at Bethaven, follow you, Benjamin.
Hosea 5:9 Ephraim will be ruined on the day of punishment; I have told the tribes of Israel what will definitely happen.
Hosea 5:10 The leaders of Judah were like those who move boundaries; so I will pour out my anger on them like water.
Hosea 5:11 Ephraim is crushed and judged unfairly because he chose to follow wrong orders.
Hosea 5:12 So I will be to Ephraim like a moth, and to the house of Judah like decay.
Hosea 5:13 When Ephraim noticed his illness, and Judah noticed his injury, Ephraim went to the Assyrian, and sent a message to King Jareb: but he couldn't heal you or fix your injury.
Hosea 5:14 I will be like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to Judah's people. I will attack and leave, I will carry off, and no one can save them.
Hosea 5:15 I will go back to my place until they admit their wrong and look for me. When they are in trouble, they will search for me earnestly.

Hosea 6:1 Come, let's go back to God; He has hurt us, but He will heal us; He has struck us, but He will fix our wounds.
Hosea 6:2 In two days, God will restore us to life; on the third day, he will lift us up, so we can live before him.
Hosea 6:3 Then we will understand if we keep trying to know God. His arrival is certain like the dawn, and He will come to us like the rain, like the late and early rains that water the earth.
Hosea 6:4 Ephraim, what should I do with you? Judah, what should I do with you? Your goodness disappears like the morning clouds and the early dew.
Hosea 6:5 So I have taught them through the prophets; I have struck them down with my words; and your decisions shine like the dawn.
Hosea 6:6 I wanted kindness, not offerings; and understanding God above burnt sacrifices.
Hosea 6:7 They, like humans, have broken the agreement; they have betrayed me there.
Hosea 6:8 Gilead is a city of wrongdoers, covered with blood.
Hosea 6:9 Like bands of thieves hiding to attack, a group of priests kill on the path, agreeing together, because they do shameful things.
Hosea 6:10 I have seen a terrible thing in Israel's house: Ephraim has acted shamefully, and Israel is unclean.
Hosea 6:11 Also, Judah, God has prepared a harvest for you when I bring back my people from captivity.

Hosea 7:1 When I wanted to heal Israel, Ephraim's sin and Samaria's evil were revealed because they lied, thieves broke in, and bands of robbers plundered outside.
Hosea 7:2 They don't think in their hearts that I remember all their bad actions: now what they've done surrounds them; they are in my sight.
Hosea 7:3 They please the king with their bad deeds, and the leaders with their lies.
Hosea 7:4 They are all unfaithful, like an oven the baker heats and then stops stoking after mixing the dough until it rises.
Hosea 7:5 On our king's day, the leaders made him sick with lots of wine; he joined in with those who mock.
Hosea 7:6 They prepare their hearts like a hot oven while they wait in ambush. Their anger smolders all night and in the morning it blazes like a burning fire.
Hosea 7:7 They all burn with anger like an oven and have destroyed their rulers; all their kings have fallen, and none of them call out to me.
Hosea 7:8 Ephraim has mixed himself with other people; Ephraim is like an uncooked cake.
Hosea 7:9 Outsiders have used up his energy, and he doesn't realize it; even with gray hair scattered on him, he still doesn't know.
Hosea 7:10 Israel's pride is shown openly, but they still don't turn back to God or look for Him, despite everything.
Hosea 7:11 Ephraim is like a foolish dove with no understanding: they turn to Egypt, they travel to Assyria.
Hosea 7:12 When they go, I will throw my net over them; I will pull them down like birds of the sky; I will punish them as they have been told.
Hosea 7:13 How terrible for them! They have run away from me. They will be destroyed because they have sinned against me. Even though I saved them, they have still told lies about me.
Hosea 7:14 They haven't truly called out to God; instead, they wail on their beds. They gather together for grain and wine, but they turn against God.
Hosea 7:15 Even though I made their arms strong, they still plan to do bad things against me.
Hosea 7:16 They come back, but not to God; they are like a faulty bow; their leaders will die by the sword because of their angry words; this will make them a joke in Egypt.

Hosea 8:1 Put the trumpet to your lips. An eagle swoops on God's house because they broke my agreement and disobeyed my laws.
Hosea 8:2 Israel will call out to me, "My God, we know you."
Hosea 8:3 Israel has rejected what is good; the enemy will chase after him.
Hosea 8:4 They chose kings without my approval, made leaders I did not recognize, and from their silver and gold, they created idols to be destroyed.
Hosea 8:5 Samaria, your calf has rejected you; I am angry with them. How long until they become innocent?
Hosea 8:6 It came from Israel: a craftsman made it; so it's not God. But the calf of Samaria will be smashed.
Hosea 8:7 They planted wind and will get a storm; it won't grow stalks, blooms won't make flour: if it does yield, outsiders will eat it.
Hosea 8:8 Israel is consumed; now they will be among the nations like an unwanted pot.
Hosea 8:9 They have gone to Assyria, like a wild donkey alone: Ephraim has paid for partners.
Hosea 8:10 Yes, even though they hired help from other nations, I will now bring them together, and they will feel some sadness because of the heavy demands of the king of leaders.
Hosea 8:11 Because Ephraim has made many altars for sinning, these altars will become a way for him to sin.
Hosea 8:12 I wrote to him about the important parts of my law, but they were seen as something odd.
Hosea 8:13 They offer meat for my offerings and eat it, but God does not accept them; now he will remember their sins and punish them: they will go back to Egypt.
Hosea 8:14 Israel has forgotten God and built temples; Judah has built many strong cities, but I will set fire to these cities, and it will destroy their palaces.

Hosea 9:1 Do not celebrate, Israel, like other nations, because you have been unfaithful to God, loving the rewards you get on every threshing floor.
Hosea 9:2 The ground and the wine-making place won't provide for them, and the fresh wine will disappoint her.
Hosea 9:3 They will not live in God's land; but Ephraim will go back to Egypt, and they will eat impure food in Assyria.
Hosea 9:4 They must not give wine offerings to God, nor will these please him. Their sacrifices will be like mourning bread; whoever eats it will be unclean. Their bread for their life cannot enter God's house.
Hosea 9:5 What will you do on the sacred day, and on the day of God's feast?
Hosea 9:6 Look, they have left because they were destroyed. Egypt will collect their bodies, and Memphis will bury them. The nice spots where they kept their money will be taken over by weeds, and thorns will fill their homes.
Hosea 9:7 The time for punishment has come, the time for payback is here; Israel will realize this: the prophet is senseless, the spiritual person is insane, because of your many sins and intense hatred.
Hosea 9:8 Ephraim's guard was with my God, but the prophet is like a hunter's trap on every path, and there is hate in God's house.
Hosea 9:9 They have become very corrupt, like in Gibeah's time: so God will remember their wrongs, and he will punish their sins.
Hosea 9:10 I found Israel like grapes in the desert; I saw your ancestors as the first fruit on the fig tree at its first season: but they went to Baalpeor, turned to that disgrace, and their shameful acts were as they desired.
Hosea 9:11 Ephraim's honor will vanish like a bird, from birth, from pregnancy, and from conception.
Hosea 9:12 Even if they raise their children, I will take them away until none are left. And it will be bad for them when I leave them.
Hosea 9:13 Ephraim is like the city Tyre, set in a nice area, but Ephraim will lead his children to the killer.
Hosea 9:14 God, give them what you will give; give them wombs that cannot bear children and breasts that are dry.
Hosea 9:15 All their bad acts are in Gilgal; there I began to hate them. Because they keep doing evil, I will force them out of my house and stop loving them; all their leaders are rebels.
Hosea 9:16 Ephraim is struck down, their roots are dried up, they will not bear fruit. Even if they do produce, I will kill the precious offspring from their womb.
Hosea 9:17 God will reject them because they did not listen to him, and they will wander among the nations.

Hosea 10:1 Israel is like a vine with no value; it produces fruit for itself. The more fruit it has, the more altars it builds; the better the land, the finer the idols.
Hosea 10:2 Their heart is not united; they will be seen as guilty: God will destroy their altars, God will ruin their statues.
Hosea 10:3 Now they will say, "We have no king, because we did not fear God; what can a king do for us?"
Hosea 10:4 They have said things, lying when they make a promise. So unfairness grows like poison plants in the field's rows.
Hosea 10:5 The people of Samaria will be scared because of the fake gods of Bethaven; they will be sad for them, and the priests who were happy about them will mourn, because their honor is gone.
Hosea 10:6 It will be taken to Assyria as a gift for King Jareb: Ephraim will feel shame, and Israel will be embarrassed by its own advice.
Hosea 10:7 Samaria's king is gone like foam on water.
Hosea 10:8 The worship sites of Aven, Israel's sin, will be ruined: thorns and thistles will grow on their altars; and people will ask the mountains to hide them and the hills to fall on them.
Hosea 10:9 Israel, you have sinned since the time of Gibeah: there they remained: the fight in Gibeah against the wicked people did not defeat them.
Hosea 10:10 I want to punish them, and people will come together against them when they get stuck in their own wrong ways.
Hosea 10:11 Ephraim is like a trained young cow that likes to crush grain; but I will put a yoke on her beautiful neck. I will make Ephraim work; Judah will plow and Jacob will break up the soil.
Hosea 10:12 Plant for yourselves the right way, gather with kindness; prepare your unused land: it's time to look for God, until He comes and showers you with the right way to live.
Hosea 10:13 You have planted evil, you have harvested sin; you have eaten the fruit of lies: because you trusted in your own path, in the strength of your warriors.
Hosea 10:14 So, your people will be in chaos, and all your strongholds will be ruined, just like when Shalman destroyed Betharbel on the day of war: the mother was shattered against her children.
Hosea 10:15 Bethel will do the same to you because of your great evil; by morning the king of Israel will be completely destroyed.

Hosea 11:1 When Israel was young, I loved him and called my son out of Egypt.
Hosea 11:2 When they were called, they ignored it; they made sacrifices to false gods and burned incense to idols.
Hosea 11:3 I also taught Ephraim to walk, holding them by their arms; yet they did not realize that I healed them.
Hosea 11:4 I led them with human ties, with ropes of love. Like one who eases the load on their jaws, I bent down to feed them.
Hosea 11:5 He will not go back to Egypt, and the Assyrian will be his king, because they would not come back.
Hosea 11:6 The sword will stay in his cities, destroy his branches, and eat them up, because of their own plans.
Hosea 11:7 My people love to turn away from me; even when they are called to the Most High, no one praises Him.
Hosea 11:8 How can I let you go, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboim? My heart is changed inside me, and my compassion is stirred up.
Hosea 11:9 I will not act with fierce anger, nor come back to destroy Ephraim because I am God, not a human; the Holy One among you, and I will not come into the city.
Hosea 11:10 They will follow God; He will roar like a lion; when He roars, the children will shake with fear from the west.
Hosea 11:11 They will shake with fear like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from Assyria, and I will put them in their homes, says God.
Hosea 11:12 Ephraim surrounds me with lies, and Israel with deceit; but Judah still rules with God and is loyal with the holy people.

Hosea 12:1 Ephraim chases the wind and follows the east wind: he keeps adding lies and destruction; they make agreements with the Assyrians, and oil is taken to Egypt.
Hosea 12:2 God also has an argument with Judah and will punish Jacob for his actions; He will repay him based on what he has done.
Hosea 12:3 In the womb, he grabbed his brother's heel, and with his strength, he struggled with God.
Hosea 12:4 Yes, he had power over the angel and won; he cried and asked for mercy; he met him in Bethel, where he spoke with us.
Hosea 12:5 Even God of all; God is his name to remember.
Hosea 12:6 So turn to your God: practice kindness and fairness, and always depend on your God.
Hosea 12:7 He is a trader with dishonest scales in his hands; he loves to cheat.
Hosea 12:8 Ephraim said, "I have become rich and gained wealth. In all my work, no one will find any wrong that is sin in me."
Hosea 12:9 I am God, who brought you out of Egypt, and I will make you live in tents again, like during the festival.
Hosea 12:10 I have spoken through the prophets, given many visions, and taught in parables through the prophets' work.
Hosea 12:11 Is there wrongdoing in Gilead? Surely they are worthless; they offer bulls in Gilgal; yes, their altars are like piles of stones in the field rows.
Hosea 12:12 Jacob ran away to Syria, and Israel worked to marry a wife, and to get a wife he took care of sheep.
Hosea 12:13 God led Israel out of Egypt through a prophet, and by a prophet they were kept safe.
Hosea 12:14 Ephraim made God very angry, so God will make him face the consequences of his actions, and will make sure his shame remains on him.

Hosea 13:1 When Ephraim spoke with fear, he became a leader in Israel; but when he sinned with Baal, he died.
Hosea 13:2 They keep sinning more, making silver statues and idols they imagine, all made by craftsmen. They tell those who offer sacrifices to kiss these calf idols.
Hosea 13:3 So they will be like the morning cloud and like the early dew that goes away, like chaff blown away from the threshing floor by the wind, and like smoke from a chimney.
Hosea 13:4 I am God, who brought you out of Egypt, and you should not acknowledge any god except me because there is no one else who can save you.
Hosea 13:5 I knew you in the desert, in the dry land.
Hosea 13:6 As their fields were good, they ate and were satisfied; their hearts grew proud, so they forgot God.
Hosea 13:7 So I will be like a lion to them, and like a leopard, I will watch over them.
Hosea 13:8 I will confront them like a mother bear robbed of her cubs, and will tear open their heart; there I will eat them like a lion, and wild animals will rip them apart.
Hosea 13:9 Israel, you have ruined yourself; but your help is in me.
Hosea 13:10 I will be your king. Where is another who can save you in all your cities? Where are your judges to whom you said, "Give me a king and princes"?
Hosea 13:11 I gave you a king because I was angry, and I took him away because I was furious.
Hosea 13:12 Ephraim's wrongdoing is tied up; his sin is hidden.
Hosea 13:13 He will feel pain like a woman giving birth: he is a foolish son, because he should not stay where babies are born for long.
Hosea 13:14 I will rescue them from the grave's power; I will save them from death: O death, I will bring your diseases; O grave, I will cause your ruin: I will not turn back.
Hosea 13:15 Although he may have success among his brothers, a strong wind will blow in from the desert, and this wind from God will dry up his water source and his well will run dry: all his valuable belongings will be ruined.
Hosea 13:16 Samaria will be ruined because she turned against God: people will die by the sword, babies will be smashed, and pregnant women will be cut open.

Hosea 14:1 Israel, come back to God, for you have stumbled because of your wrongdoings.
Hosea 14:2 Bring your words to God and ask Him to forgive all our sins and accept us with kindness; then we will offer Him our words of praise.
Hosea 14:3 Asshur won't save us; we won't ride on horses. We won't call our handmade idols our gods anymore, because the fatherless find kindness in you.
Hosea 14:4 I will heal their turning away, I will love them without cost: because my anger has turned away from them.
Hosea 14:5 I will be like dew for Israel: he will grow like a lily and send out roots like Lebanon's trees.
Hosea 14:6 His branches will grow wide, his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his scent like that of Lebanon.
Hosea 14:7 Those who live in God's protection will come back; they will flourish like grain, and spread out like a grapevine: their smell will be like Lebanon's wine.
Hosea 14:8 Ephraim will ask, "Why should I deal with idols anymore?" I have listened to God and noticed him. I am like a fresh pine tree. You can find your fruit in me.
Hosea 14:9 Who is wise to understand these things? Who is smart to know them? God's ways are right, and the good will follow them, but the wrongdoers will stumble in them.

Joel 1:1 God's message that came to Joel, Pethuel's son.
Joel 1:2 Listen, old men, and all who live in the land, pay attention. Has anything like this happened in your time or in your ancestors' time?
Joel 1:3 Tell your children about it, let them tell their children, and those children tell the next generation.
Joel 1:4 What the palmerworm did not eat, the locust did; and what the locust did not eat, the cankerworm did; and what the cankerworm did not eat, the caterpillar did.
Joel 1:5 Wake up, you who drink too much, and cry; scream, all of you wine lovers, because the fresh wine is taken away from your lips.
Joel 1:6 A nation has invaded my land, powerful and countless, with teeth like a lion's, and with the fangs of a mighty lion.
Joel 1:7 He has destroyed my vine and stripped my fig tree. He has completely bared it and thrown it aside; its branches are now white.
Joel 1:8 Mourn like a young woman wrapped in rough cloth for the husband of her young days.
Joel 1:9 The food offering and the drink offering are stopped at God's house; the priests, God's servants, are sad.
Joel 1:10 The crops are gone, the earth is sad; the grain is ruined, the new wine is gone, the oil is failing.
Joel 1:11 Feel ashamed, you farmers; cry out, you vine growers, because the wheat and barley are ruined; the field crops are destroyed.
Joel 1:12 The grapevine has dried up, and the fig tree is weak; the pomegranate tree, the palm tree, and the apple tree, all the trees in the fields have dried up because happiness has faded away from people.
Joel 1:13 Get ready and cry, priests; wail, servants of the altar; come, spend the night in mourning, servants of my God, because the grain and drink offerings are no longer brought to your God's temple.
Joel 1:14 Set a special time to fast, call a serious meeting, bring together the leaders and everyone who lives in the land to God's house, and pray to God.
Joel 1:15 Oh no, the day is coming! It's the day of God, and it will bring destruction like a disaster from the powerful one.
Joel 1:16 Isn't the food taken away from us, along with joy and happiness from God's house?
Joel 1:17 The seeds have rotted under the dirt, the storehouses are empty, the barns are ruined; because the grain has dried up.
Joel 1:18 The animals cry out in pain! The herds of cows are confused because there is no grass to eat; even the sheep are left with nothing.
Joel 1:19 God, I will call out to you: because the fire has eaten up the wild land's grass, and the flame has burned every tree in the fields.
Joel 1:20 The wild animals cry out to you because the water streams are dry, and fire has burned the wild grasslands.

Joel 2:1 Play the trumpet in Zion, and ring the alarm on my holy mountain: let everyone in the land shake with fear: for the day of God is coming, for it is very near.
Joel 2:2 A day of darkness and sadness, a day of clouds and deep darkness, like dawn spreading over the mountains: a huge and powerful group of people; nothing like this has ever happened before, nor will it ever happen again, even after many years and generations.
Joel 2:3 A fire consumes in front of them; behind them a flame blazes: the land is like the garden of Eden before them, and behind them it's a ruined wasteland; indeed, nothing can escape them.
Joel 2:4 They look like horses, and like riders, they will run.
Joel 2:5 They will jump like the sound of chariots on mountain tops, like the crackling of fire burning dry plants, as a mighty army ready for battle.
Joel 2:6 The people will feel great pain, and all faces will turn dark.
Joel 2:7 They will run like strong men; they will climb the wall like soldiers; they will all walk on their own paths, and they will not leave their positions.
Joel 2:8 No one will push another; each will walk in his own way: and if they fall on the sword, they will not be hurt.
Joel 2:9 They will run around in the city; they will run on the walls, climb onto the houses; they will enter through the windows like a thief.
Joel 2:10 The earth will shake before them; the sky will quiver; the sun and moon will turn dark, and the stars will stop shining.
Joel 2:11 God will speak before his army: His forces are vast: He is powerful and does what He says: The day of God is immense and very frightening; who can endure it?
Joel 2:12 So now, God says, turn back to me with all your heart, by fasting, crying, and mourning.
Joel 2:13 Tear your heart, not your clothes, and return to God, for he is kind and merciful, slow to get angry, full of love, and changes his mind about the harm.
Joel 2:14 Who knows if God will come back, change his mind, and leave a blessing for you, including food and drink offerings for your God?
Joel 2:15 Sound the trumpet in Zion, declare a fast, call a gathering.
Joel 2:16 Bring the people together, make the group holy, call the old leaders, get the children and the babies: let the man getting married leave his room, and the woman getting married come out of her private place.
Joel 2:17 Let the priests, who serve God, cry between the entrance and the altar. Let them say, "Save your people, God, don't let others insult your chosen ones by ruling over them. Why should others ask, 'Where is their God?'"
Joel 2:18 Then God will care deeply for his land and have compassion on his people.
Joel 2:19 Yes, God will reply to his people, "Look, I will give you grain, wine, and olive oil, and you will have enough: and I will not let you be shamed among the nations anymore."
Joel 2:20 I will take the northern army far away from you and push them into a dry and empty land. Their front will face the eastern sea and their back the farthest sea. Their smell will rise up, their stench too, because they have done great things.
Joel 2:21 Don't be afraid, land; be happy and celebrate: God will do amazing things.
Joel 2:22 Do not fear, you animals of the fields: the wild pastures are growing, and the trees are bearing their fruit, the fig tree and the grapevine are giving their best.
Joel 2:23 Be happy, people of Zion, and be joyful in God: He has given you enough early rain, and He will make sure you get both early and late rain in the first month.
Joel 2:24 The floors will be full of wheat, and the containers will overflow with wine and oil.
Joel 2:25 I will give back to you the years the locusts, the cankerworms, the caterpillars, and the palmerworms have eaten, my great army that I sent to you.
Joel 2:26 You will eat a lot, feel full, and thank God, who has done amazing things for you; and my people will never feel shame.
Joel 2:27 You will know that I am with Israel, and that I am your God and no other; and my people will never be ashamed.
Joel 2:28 Afterward, I will give my spirit to everyone; your sons and daughters will speak of the future, your old men will have dreams, and your young men will see visions.
Joel 2:29 I will pour out my spirit on the servants and maidens in those days.
Joel 2:30 I will show amazing things in the sky and on the earth: blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
Joel 2:31 The sun will become dark, and the moon will turn red, before the great and terrible day of God comes.
Joel 2:32 Whoever calls on God's name will be saved; deliverance will be in Mount Zion and Jerusalem as God promised, and among the survivors God calls.

Joel 3:1 For, look, in those days and at that time, when I bring back the people of Judah and Jerusalem,
Joel 3:2 I will gather all nations and take them to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There, I will argue for my people and my land, Israel, because they have been scattered among the nations and my land has been divided.
Joel 3:3 They have drawn lots for my people, traded a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine to drink.
Joel 3:4 Yes, and what do you have to do with me, O Tyre, Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? Will you pay me back? If you pay me back, I will quickly return your payment on your own head.
Joel 3:5 Because you took my silver and gold, and brought my precious things into your temples:
Joel 3:6 You have sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, so you could send them far from their land.
Joel 3:7 I will lift them from the place where you sold them and bring the consequences back on you.
Joel 3:8 I will sell your sons and daughters to the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, a distant nation, because God has said so.
Joel 3:9 Tell this to the nations: Get ready for battle, wake up the strong fighters, let all the soldiers come close; let them move forward.
Joel 3:10 Turn your farming tools into swords and your cutting tools into spears; let those who feel weak say, I am strong.
Joel 3:11 Come together and join, all you nations, and gather around: call your strong ones to come down, God.
Joel 3:12 Let the nations wake up and come to the Valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Joel 3:13 Use the sickle, the crops are ready: come, gather them; the vat is full, it's overflowing because there is so much evil.
