Joel 3:14 Many people, many people in the valley of choice: for God's day is close in the valley of choice.
Joel 3:15 The sun and the moon will become dark, and the stars will stop shining.
Joel 3:16 God will roar from Zion and shout from Jerusalem; the sky and land will tremble. But God will be a safe place for his people, and a stronghold for the people of Israel.
Joel 3:17 You will know that I am God living in Zion, my holy mountain. Then Jerusalem will be a holy city, and no strangers will pass through it anymore.
Joel 3:18 On that day, the mountains will drip with sweet wine, the hills will overflow with milk, all of Judah's streams will run with water, and a spring will come out of God's house and water the valley of Shittim.
Joel 3:19 Egypt will become ruined, and Edom will turn into a barren wasteland because of the harm done to the people of Judah, since they have spilled the blood of the innocent in their country.
Joel 3:20 Judah will live forever, and Jerusalem will last from one generation to the next.
Joel 3:21 I will purify their blood that I haven't purified before, because God lives in Zion.

Amos 1:1 These are the words of Amos, one of the shepherds from Tekoa. He had visions about Israel when Uzziah was king of Judah, and when Jeroboam, Joash's son, was king of Israel. This happened two years before the earthquake.
Amos 1:2 He said, God will roar from Zion and speak loudly from Jerusalem; the shepherds' homes will be sad, and the top of Carmel will dry up.
Amos 1:3 God says: Because Damascus has sinned many times, I will not stop their punishment. They crushed Gilead with iron tools.
Amos 1:4 I will send a fire to Hazael's house, and it will destroy Benhadad's palaces.
Amos 1:5 I will break the defenses of Damascus, end the people from Aven Valley, and their leaders from Eden. The Syrians will be taken as prisoners to Kir, says God.
Amos 1:6 God says: Because Gaza has sinned many times, I won't stop their punishment. They took away a whole group of captives and handed them over to Edom.
Amos 1:7 I will send a fire against the wall of Gaza, and it will burn down its palaces.
Amos 1:8 I will remove the people from Ashdod and the ruler from Ashkelon, and I will attack Ekron. The remaining Philistines will die, says God.
Amos 1:9 God says, "Because Tyre has sinned many times, I will not stop their punishment. They handed over captives to Edom and forgot their treaty of friendship."
Amos 1:10 I will send a fire on the wall of Tyre that will destroy its palaces.
Amos 1:11 God says: Because Edom sinned many times, I will not stop punishing them. They chased their own family with weapons, showed no mercy, stayed angry all the time, and never forgave.
Amos 1:12 I will send a fire to Teman, and it will burn down the strong houses of Bozrah.
Amos 1:13 God says, "Because the people of Ammon committed three sins, and even four, I will not stop their punishment. They attacked pregnant women in Gilead to expand their own land."
Amos 1:14 I will start a fire in the walls of Rabbah, and it will burn down its palaces amid battle cries on the day of combat, and with a storm on the day of the whirlwind.
Amos 1:15 Their king and his leaders will be captured and taken away, says God.

Amos 2:1 God says, "Because Moab sinned three times, even four, I will not cancel their punishment. They burned the bones of Edom's king to ashes."
Amos 2:2 I will send fire to Moab, and it will burn the palaces of Kirioth. Moab will die amid noise, shouts, and trumpet blasts.
Amos 2:3 I will remove the judge from the middle and kill all the leaders with him, says God.
Amos 2:4 God says this: Because Judah has sinned three times, even four, I won't stop their punishment. They rejected God's law and did not follow His rules. Their lies led them astray, like their ancestors before them.
Amos 2:5 I will send fire to Judah, and it will burn down the palaces of Jerusalem.
Amos 2:6 God says: Because Israel has sinned three and even four times, I won't stop their punishment. They traded innocent people for money and the needy for sandals.
Amos 2:7 They chase after worthless things instead of helping the poor and twist the paths of the humble. Both a man and his father misuse the same girl, dishonoring my sacred name.
Amos 2:8 They lie down on clothes taken as pledges near every altar, and they drink wine taken as fines in the temple of their god.
Amos 2:9 But I destroyed the Amorite before them, who was as tall as cedar trees and as strong as oaks; I destroyed their fruit from above and their roots from below.
Amos 2:10 I also took you out of Egypt and guided you for 40 years in the desert to take over the land of the Amorites.
Amos 2:11 I chose some of your sons to be prophets and some of your young men to be Nazarites. Isn't it true, people of Israel? says God.
Amos 2:12 But you gave the Nazarites wine to drink and told the prophets not to speak God's words.
Amos 2:13 Look, I am weighed down by you, like a cart is weighed down when it is full of grain bundles.
Amos 2:14 So the fast will not escape, the strong will not use their strength, and the brave will not save themselves.
Amos 2:15 The person using the bow won't be able to stand; the fast runner won't save themselves; and the horse rider won't escape.
Amos 2:16 The brave one among the warriors will run away without clothes on that day, says God.

Amos 3:1 Listen to what God has said against you, children of Israel, against the entire family I led out of Egypt:
Amos 3:2 I have known only you among all the families on earth; so I will punish you for all your wrongs.
Amos 3:3 Can two people walk together if they do not agree?
Amos 3:4 Will a lion roar in the woods without catching prey? Will a young lion shout from its den if it has caught nothing?
Amos 3:5 Can a bird be caught in a trap on the ground if no one has set one for it? Can someone lift a trap from the ground if it hasn't caught anything?
Amos 3:6 If a trumpet sounds in the city, won't the people be scared? If there's trouble in a city, isn't it God who has caused it?
Amos 3:7 God will do nothing without revealing his plan to his prophets.
Amos 3:8 The lion has roared, who wouldn't be afraid? God has spoken, who wouldn't tell the message?
Amos 3:9 Announce in the palaces of Ashdod and Egypt, say, "Gather on the Samaria mountains and see the big upsets and the oppressed people there."
Amos 3:10 They do not know how to do right, says God, who keep violence and theft in their homes.
Amos 3:11 So God says: An enemy will surround the country; they will reduce your power, and your grand houses will be robbed.
Amos 3:12 God says, "Like a shepherd saves from the lion's mouth two legs or a piece of an ear, so will the Israelites be saved who live in Samaria on the edge of a bed, and in Damascus on a sofa."
Amos 3:13 Listen and speak out in the house of Jacob, says God, the God of all.
Amos 3:14 On the day I punish Israel for their sins, I will also destroy the altars of Bethel; the altar horns will be cut off and fall to the ground.
Amos 3:15 I will destroy the winter homes and the summer homes; the ivory houses will be gone, and the big houses will end, says God.

Amos 4:1 Listen to this message, you cows of Bashan on Samaria's mountain, who hurt the poor, who crush the needy, and who tell their bosses, "Bring us something to drink."
Amos 4:2 God has promised by his own purity, look, the time will come when you will be taken away with hooks, and your descendants with fishhooks.
Amos 4:3 You will leave through the gaps, each cow heading straight ahead; and you will throw them into the palace, says God.
Amos 4:4 Go to Bethel and sin; keep on sinning at Gilgal. Bring your sacrifices every morning and your tithes every three years.
Amos 4:5 Give thanks with bread that has yeast, tell others, and share freely: this pleases you, people of Israel, says God.
Amos 4:6 I also gave you clean teeth in your cities and lack of bread everywhere, but still you haven't turned back to me, says God.
Amos 4:7 I also kept rain from you when it was three months before harvest. I made it rain on one city but not another. One place got rain and didn't dry up, while the place with no rain withered.
Amos 4:8 Two or three cities went to one city to get water to drink, but it wasn't enough. Still, you haven't turned back to me, says God.
Amos 4:9 I have struck you with blight and decay; when your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees grew, the palmerworm ate them, but still you have not turned back to me, says God.
Amos 4:10 I sent sickness to you like in Egypt: I killed your young men with the sword, took your horses, and made your camps smell bad: still, you did not turn back to me, says God.
Amos 4:11 I destroyed some of you, just like God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were saved from the fire, but still you haven't come back to me, says God.
Amos 4:12 So I will act toward you, Israel, and since I will do this, get ready to face your God, Israel.
Amos 4:13 Look, the one who shapes the mountains, makes the wind, and tells people their thoughts, who turns dawn into darkness and walks on the high parts of the land, God, the commander of heavenly armies, is his name.

Amos 5:1 Listen to this message I speak against you, which is a sad song, O people of Israel.
Amos 5:2 The young woman of Israel has fallen; she will not get up again: she is left alone on her land; there is no one to help her up.
Amos 5:3 God says: The city that sends out a thousand will only have a hundred left, and the one that sends out a hundred will only have ten left for the people of Israel.
Amos 5:4 God says to the people of Israel, "Look for me, and you will live."
Amos 5:5 Do not look for Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, and do not travel to Beersheba. Gilgal will be taken captive, and Bethel will be destroyed.
Amos 5:6 Look for God, and you will live; or he might burst out like fire in Joseph's house, consume it, and no one in Bethel can put it out.
Amos 5:7 You who make fair decisions bitter, and abandon what is right in the world,
Amos 5:8 Look for the one who created the seven stars and Orion, who changes deep darkness into morning, and turns day into night: who commands the sea waters and pours them over the earth: God is his name.
Amos 5:9 God gives power to the weak to stand against the mighty, so the weak can attack the stronghold.
Amos 5:10 They dislike the person who corrects others publicly, and they detest the one who speaks honestly.
Amos 5:11 Since you step on the poor and take their wheat, you build stone houses but won't live in them; you plant vineyards but won't drink their wine.
Amos 5:12 I know your many wrongs and your big sins: they hurt good people, they accept bribes, and they push away the poor from getting their rights at the gate.
Amos 5:13 So the wise will stay quiet at that time, because it is a bad time.
Amos 5:14 Look for good, not bad, so you may live, and then God will be with you as you have said.
Amos 5:15 Dislike what's bad, like what's good, and set up fair decisions in your communities. Maybe then God will show kindness to the survivors of Joseph's family.
Amos 5:16 So God, the Lord of all, says: There will be crying in all the streets and people will say in every road, "Oh no, oh no!" Farmers will be called to grieve, and those good at grieving to cry.
Amos 5:17 In all the grape gardens there will be crying, because I will come through you, says God.
Amos 5:18 You who wish for God's day, why do you want it? That day is dark, not light.
Amos 5:19 It's like a man running from a lion, only to meet a bear; or he goes into his house, rests his hand on the wall, and a snake bites him.
Amos 5:20 Won't God's day be full of darkness, without any light? Very dark, with no brightness at all?
Amos 5:21 I hate and reject your festivals, and I won't enjoy your formal gatherings.
Amos 5:22 Even if you give me burnt sacrifices and food offerings, I will not accept them: I will not consider the peace sacrifices of your fat animals.
Amos 5:23 Stop singing your songs to me; I won't listen to your music.
Amos 5:24 Let fair judgment flow like water, and let justice be strong like a flowing river.
Amos 5:25 Did you give me sacrifices and offerings in the desert for forty years, O people of Israel?
Amos 5:26 You have carried the tent of your god Moloch and the star of your god Chiun, which you made for yourselves.
Amos 5:27 So I will make you captive and send you away beyond Damascus, says God, who is called the God of armies.

Amos 6:1 Trouble awaits those who are comfortable in Zion and rely on Mount Samaria, the famous leaders of the nations where the people of Israel go!
Amos 6:2 Go to Calneh and look; then visit the great city of Hamath, and afterward go to Gath of the Philistines. Are they stronger than these kingdoms? Is their land larger than yours?
Amos 6:3 You who push away the day of punishment and bring violence close.
Amos 6:4 They lie on ivory beds, lounge on their sofas, eat lambs from the flock, and calves from the pen.
Amos 6:5 They sing to the music of the harp and make up their own musical instruments, like David.
Amos 6:6 They drink wine from large bowls and use the finest oils to anoint themselves, but they do not care about the suffering of Joseph's people.
Amos 6:7 So now they will be taken away as prisoners with those who were first taken away, and the feasting of those who lounged will end.
Amos 6:8 God has sworn by himself, says the God of all, I despise Jacob's pride and hate his strongholds: so I will hand over the city and everything in it.
Amos 6:9 If ten people are left in one house, they will die.
Amos 6:10 A man's uncle will carry him, and the one who cremates him, to remove the bones from the house. He will ask anyone nearby, "Is anyone else with you?" When he says, "No," he will be told, "Be quiet; we must not speak of God's name."
Amos 6:11 Look, God commands, and he will strike the big house, making large cracks, and the small house with splits.
Amos 6:12 Can horses run on rocky ground? Can you plow with oxen on rocks? You have made fair decisions bitter, and turned what is right into poison.
Amos 6:13 You who celebrate meaningless things, saying, "Haven't we gained power by our own strength?"
Amos 6:14 But look, I will bring against you a nation, O people of Israel, says God, and they will trouble you from the entrance of Hemath to the wilderness river.

Amos 7:1 God showed me this: I saw him create locusts at the start of the crops' second growth, after the king's harvest.
Amos 7:2 When they finished eating the land's grass, I said, "Please God, forgive us. How can Jacob survive? He is too small."
Amos 7:3 God changed his mind about this: It will not happen, says God.
Amos 7:4 God showed me this: God called for judgment by fire, which consumed the deep waters and ate up the land.
Amos 7:5 I said, "Please stop, God. How can Jacob recover? He is too weak."
Amos 7:6 God changed his mind about this: This will not happen either, says God.
Amos 7:7 He showed me: and look, God stood on a wall built straight with a plumb line, holding a plumb line.
Amos 7:8 God asked me, "Amos, what do you see?" I answered, "A plumbline." God said, "Look, I will put a plumbline among my people Israel; I won't overlook their actions anymore."
Amos 7:9 The special places of Isaac will be empty, and the holy places of Israel will be ruined; and I will attack the family of Jeroboam with a sword.
Amos 7:10 Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent a message to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying, "Amos has plotted against you among the people of Israel: the country cannot handle everything he says."
Amos 7:11 Amos says this: Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will definitely be taken captive from their land.
Amos 7:12 Amaziah told Amos, "You, the seer, go away to the land of Judah, eat your bread there, and give your messages there."
Amos 7:13 Do not prophesy again in Bethel; it is the king's temple and the royal palace.
Amos 7:14 Amos replied to Amaziah, "I was not a prophet or the son of a prophet; I was a shepherd and I picked sycamore fruit."
Amos 7:15 God chose me as I tended the sheep and God told me, "Go, speak my words to the people of Israel."
Amos 7:16 Listen now to God's message: You say, "Do not speak against Israel, and do not say anything against the family of Isaac."
Amos 7:17 So God says: Your wife will be unfaithful in the city, your sons and daughters will be killed with swords, your land will be split up, and you will die in a dirty land. Israel will definitely be taken as prisoners out of their land.

Amos 8:1 God showed me this: Look, a basket of summer fruit.
Amos 8:2 He asked, "Amos, what do you see?" I answered, "A basket of summer fruit." Then God told me, "The end has come for my people Israel; I will not spare them anymore."
Amos 8:3 On that day, the temple songs will turn to wails, says God. Dead bodies will be everywhere; they will be thrown out quietly.
Amos 8:4 Listen, you who trample on the needy and try to destroy the poor of the land.
Amos 8:5 Asking, "When will the new moon pass so we can sell grain? And the Sabbath, so we can offer wheat? Reducing the measure, increasing the price, and cheating with dishonest scales?"
Amos 8:6 So we can buy the poor with money, and the needy for a pair of shoes, and even sell the bad part of the wheat.
Amos 8:7 God has promised because of Jacob's greatness, I will surely remember their deeds always.
Amos 8:8 Won't the earth shake because of this, and all who live in it be sad? It will surge like a river; it will be thrown out and sink like the river of Egypt.
Amos 8:9 On that day, God says, I will make the sun set at noon and darken the earth on a bright day.
Amos 8:10 I will change your celebrations into sadness, and all your music into cries of sorrow; I will make everyone wear rough cloth around their waist, and shave every head; I will make the sadness as deep as for an only child, and the end as bitter as a terrible day.
Amos 8:11 Look, days will come, says God, when I will cause a famine in the land. It won't be for lack of bread or thirst for water, but a famine of hearing God's words.
Amos 8:12 They will wander from sea to sea, and from north to east, they will rush around trying to find God's message, but they will not find it.
Amos 8:13 On that day, the beautiful young women and young men will become weak from thirst.
Amos 8:14 Those who swear by Samaria's sin and say, "Your god, O Dan, is alive," and "The way of Beersheba lives," will fall and never get up again.

Amos 9:1 I saw God standing at the altar. He said, "Hit the top of the door so the pillars tremble. Chop off their heads, all of them. I will kill any who are left with a sword. Those who run won't get far, and those who escape won't be saved."
Amos 9:2 Even if they dig deep into the ground, my hand will still reach and take them; even if they climb up to the sky, I will bring them down.
Amos 9:3 Even if they hide at the top of Carmel, I will find and take them from there; and if they hide from me at the bottom of the sea, I will tell the serpent to bite them.
Amos 9:4 Even if they are taken captive by their enemies, I will order the sword to kill them. I will watch them for harm, not for their good.
Amos 9:5 God has the power to touch the land so it will melt, and everyone living there will be sad. The land will rise like a flood and be covered like in the Egypt flood.
Amos 9:6 He makes his layers in the sky and sets his group on the earth; he calls the sea's waters and spreads them over the earth: God is his name.
Amos 9:7 Aren't you like the children of Ethiopia to me, children of Israel? says God. Didn't I lead Israel out of Egypt? And the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?
Amos 9:8 Look, God is watching the sinful nation, and I will wipe it from the earth; but I will not completely destroy Jacob's descendants, says the Lord.
Amos 9:9 Look, I will give an order, and I will shake the people of Israel among all countries, just like corn is shaken in a strainer, but not even the smallest grain will fall to the ground.
Amos 9:10 Every sinner among my people will die by the sword, those who think harm won't reach or stop us.
Amos 9:11 On that day, I will repair David's fallen shelter, fix its gaps, rebuild its ruins, and restore it like before.
Amos 9:12 So they can own what's left of Edom, and all nations called by my name, says God who does this.
Amos 9:13 Look, a time is coming, says God, when the farmer will catch up with the harvester, and the grape crusher will catch up with the one planting seeds; the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and all the hills will flow.
Amos 9:14 I will bring back my people Israel from captivity. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will also create gardens and eat their fruits.
Amos 9:15 I will put them on their land, and no one will ever remove them from the land I gave them, says God.

Obadiah 1:1 Obadiah's vision. This is what God says about Edom: We've heard a report from God, and a messenger has been sent to the nations, saying, "Get up, and let's fight against Edom."
Obadiah 1:2 Look, I have made you small among the nations: you are very disliked.
Obadiah 1:3 Your proud heart has tricked you, you who live in the mountain cracks and high places, thinking to yourself, "Who can bring me down to the ground?"
Obadiah 1:4 Even if you rise high like an eagle and put your home among the stars, I will bring you down, says God.
Obadiah 1:5 If thieves came to you, if robbers at night, (you are destroyed!) wouldn't they steal only what they needed? If grape pickers came to you, wouldn't they leave some grapes behind?
Obadiah 1:6 People have thoroughly searched Esau's belongings and found his hidden treasures.
Obadiah 1:7 All your allies have led you to the border; the friends who were at peace with you have tricked you and have overcome you; those who shared your bread have set a trap beneath you: there is no wisdom in him.
Obadiah 1:8 On that day, God says, won't I remove the wise from Edom and the understanding from the mountain of Esau?
Obadiah 1:9 Your strong men, O Teman, will be scared so that everyone on Mount Esau will be killed.
Obadiah 1:10 Because you hurt your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be gone forever.
Obadiah 1:11 On the day you stood by, on the day strangers took his people away and outsiders came into his city, throwing dice for Jerusalem, you acted just like them.
Obadiah 1:12 You should not have watched when your brother was in trouble, nor should you have been happy when the people of Judah were destroyed, nor should you have boasted when they were in distress.
Obadiah 1:13 You should not have gone through my people's gate when they were in trouble; indeed, you should not have watched their suffering on that day, nor should you have touched their belongings.
Obadiah 1:14 You should not have waited at the crossroads to kill the survivors, nor should you have handed over the remaining people in their time of trouble.
Obadiah 1:15 God's day is coming soon for all nations; what you have done will be done to you; your actions will come back to you.
Obadiah 1:16 Just as you drank on my sacred hill, so will all the nations keep drinking; they will drink and gulp down until they are like they never existed.
Obadiah 1:17 On Mount Zion there will be rescue, and it will be a holy place; the family of Jacob will take back their belongings.
Obadiah 1:18 Jacob's family will be like a fire, Joseph's family like a flame, and Esau's family like dry grass. They will burn Esau's family and nothing will be left, because God has said so.
Obadiah 1:19 People from the south will take over the land of Esau; those from the flat lands will take over Philistine territory. They will also take the farmlands of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will take over Gilead.
Obadiah 1:20 The people of Israel who were taken away will take over the land of the Canaanites up to Zarephath, and the people from Jerusalem who were taken to Sepharad will take over the southern cities.
Obadiah 1:21 Rescuers will come to Mount Zion to rule over Esau's hill, and the kingdom will belong to God.

Jonah 1:1 God spoke to Jonah, Amittai's son, saying,
Jonah 1:2 Get up, go to Nineveh, the big city, and speak out against it, because their badness has reached me.
Jonah 1:3 Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish to escape from God, and he went to Joppa. There he found a boat going to Tarshish. He paid for the trip and got on board to sail with them to Tarshish, away from God.
Jonah 1:4 But God made a strong wind blow over the sea, and a big storm came up, making the ship nearly break apart.
Jonah 1:5 The sailors were scared and each prayed to his own god. They threw the ship's cargo into the sea to make it lighter. But Jonah had gone below deck, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
Jonah 1:6 The captain went to him and said, "What are you doing sleeping? Get up and pray to your God; maybe God will notice us, and we won't die."
Jonah 1:7 They all said to each other, "Come, let's draw lots to find out who is responsible for this trouble." They drew lots and the lot pointed to Jonah.
Jonah 1:8 They asked him, "Please tell us why this trouble is happening to us. What is your job? Where do you come from? What's your country? And what people do you belong to?"
Jonah 1:9 He told them, "I am a Hebrew; and I respect God, the God of heaven, who created the sea and the land."
Jonah 1:10 The men became very scared and asked him, "Why did you do this?" They knew he was running away from God because he had told them.
Jonah 1:11 Then they asked him, "What should we do to you to make the sea calm for us?" because the sea was stormy and turbulent.
Jonah 1:12 He told them, "Pick me up and throw me into the sea, and then the sea will become calm for you. I know that this big storm has come because of me."
Jonah 1:13 The men rowed hard to reach the land, but they couldn't because the sea got rough and stormy against them.
Jonah 1:14 So they called out to God, saying, "Please, God, we beg you, don't let us die because of this man's life, and don't make us guilty of killing an innocent person: for you, God, have done as you wanted."
Jonah 1:15 So they picked up Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging.
Jonah 1:16 The men became very afraid of God, and they gave a sacrifice to God and promised to do things for Him.
Jonah 1:17 God had sent a big fish to swallow Jonah. Jonah was inside the fish for three days and nights.

Jonah 2:1 Then Jonah prayed to God from inside the fish.
Jonah 2:2 I called out to God because of my suffering, and he listened to me; from deep inside the grave I cried, and you heard my voice.
Jonah 2:3 You threw me into the deep sea; I was surrounded by water; all your waves and billows rolled over me.
Jonah 2:4 Then I said, I am thrown away from your view; but I will look again towards your holy temple.
Jonah 2:5 Water surrounded me, even to my life; deep water closed around me and plants tangled around my head.
Jonah 2:6 I went down to the mountain bases; the earth trapped me forever: but you, God, brought my life up from ruin.
Jonah 2:7 When I felt weak inside, I remembered God, and my prayer reached you in your holy temple.
Jonah 2:8 Those who believe in false things ignore the kindness meant for them.
Jonah 2:9 I will offer sacrifice to you with thankful voice; I will fulfill my promises. Salvation comes from God.
Jonah 2:10 God spoke to the fish, and it threw up Jonah onto dry land.

Jonah 3:1 God spoke to Jonah again, saying,
Jonah 3:2 Get up, go to Nineveh, that big city, and tell them the message I have given you.
Jonah 3:3 Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, as God had told him. Nineveh was a very big city; it took three days to go through it.
Jonah 3:4 Jonah started to go into the city, traveling for one day, and he shouted, "In forty days, Nineveh will be destroyed."
Jonah 3:5 The people of Nineveh trusted God, announced a fast, and wore rough clothes, from the most important to the least.
Jonah 3:6 News reached the king of Nineveh, and he got up from his throne, took off his robe, put on sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
Jonah 3:7 He had it announced and spread through Nineveh by the king's and his nobles' order, saying, "No person or animal, no herd or flock, should eat or drink anything."
Jonah 3:8 Let people and animals wear rough cloth, and call out to God strongly; yes, let everyone stop their bad ways and stop hurting others with their hands.
Jonah 3:9 Who knows if God will change his mind and stop being so angry, so we won't die?
Jonah 3:10 God saw what they did, that they stopped doing evil, so he changed his mind about the punishment he had planned to give them, and he didn't do it.

Jonah 4:1 Jonah was very upset by this, and he became angry.
Jonah 4:2 He prayed to God and said, "I knew this would happen, God. That's why I ran away to Tarshish. I knew you are kind and merciful, not easily angered, full of love, and you change your mind about punishing.
Jonah 4:3 So now, God, please take my life from me; it's better for me to die than to live.
Jonah 4:4 Then God asked, "Is it right for you to be angry?"
Jonah 4:5 Jonah left the city, sat on its east side, built himself a shelter, and sat in its shade to see what would happen to the city.
Jonah 4:6 God made a plant grow over Jonah to give him shade and help him feel better. Jonah was very happy about the plant.
Jonah 4:7 God made a worm come up the next morning, and it attacked the plant so that it dried up.
Jonah 4:8 When the sun rose, God sent a strong east wind; the sun blazed on Jonah's head so much that he became weak, wished to die, and thought, "It's better for me to die than to live."
Jonah 4:9 God asked Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?" And he answered, "Yes, I am right to be angry enough to die."
Jonah 4:10 God said, "You feel sorry for the plant you didn't work for or make grow. It appeared overnight and died overnight."
Jonah 4:11 Shouldn't I have mercy on Nineveh, that large city, with more than 120,000 people who do not know right from left, and many animals too?

Micah 1:1 God's message that came to Micah of Morasheth during the time of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, the kings of Judah, was about Samaria and Jerusalem.
Micah 1:2 Listen, everyone; pay attention, O earth and everything in it: and let God be a witness against you, God from his holy place.
Micah 1:3 Look, God is coming from his place and will step down and walk on the earth's high places.
Micah 1:4 The mountains will melt beneath him, and the valleys will split open, like wax melting before a fire and like water rushing down a slope.
Micah 1:5 All this is because Jacob did wrong, and Israel's house sinned. What did Jacob do wrong? Wasn't it Samaria? And Judah's wrong places, aren't they Jerusalem?
Micah 1:6 So, I will turn Samaria into a pile of rubble in a field, like a cleared vineyard, and I will toss its stones into the valley and expose its foundations.
Micah 1:7 All its carved idols will be smashed, all its earnings will be burned up, and all its idols I will ruin. It collected its wealth by prostitution, and it will be used again for prostitution.
Micah 1:8 I will cry and yell, I will walk bare and naked: I will cry loudly like the dragons, and grieve like the owls.
Micah 1:9 Her injury can't be healed; it has reached Judah and even the entrance of my people in Jerusalem.
Micah 1:10 Do not announce it in Gath, do not cry at all; in the house of Aphrah cover yourself with dust.
Micah 1:11 Go away, you who live in Saphir, with your shame exposed. The people of Zaanan did not leave to mourn for Bethezel; they will get no support from you.
Micah 1:12 The person from Maroth really hoped for something good, but bad things came from God to Jerusalem's gate.
Micah 1:13 You, who live in Lachish, hitch the chariot to the fast horse: you started the sin for Zion's people. Israel's wrongdoings were found in you.
Micah 1:14 So you must give gifts to Moresheth of Gath; the towns of Achzib will deceive the kings of Israel.
Micah 1:15 I will send an enemy to conquer you, people of Mareshah; the nobles of Israel will hide in the cave at Adullam.
Micah 1:16 Shave your head and cut off your hair for your precious children; make your bald spot bigger like an eagle, because they have been taken away from you as captives.

Micah 2:1 Trouble to those who plan bad things and do evil in their beds! When morning comes, they do it because they can.
Micah 2:2 They desire fields and seize them with force; and homes, and take them: so they crush a person and his family, even a person and his inheritance.
Micah 2:3 So God says: Look, I am planning a disaster against this family, which you cannot stop; you will not walk proudly, for this time is bad.
Micah 2:4 On that day someone will tell a story against you, mourn with deep sorrow, and say, "We are completely ruined. He has altered what belonged to our people. How has he taken it away from me? While turning aside, he has split our land."
Micah 2:5 You will have no one to divide land by casting lots in God's assembly.
Micah 2:6 Don't prophesy, they tell the prophets: they must not prophesy, so they won't feel ashamed.
Micah 2:7 You who are known as the family of Jacob, is God's spirit limited? Are these his actions? Don't my words benefit those who live rightly?
Micah 2:8 Recently, my people have turned into enemies: you take the coat and clothes from those who walk by peacefully, like people who dislike war.
Micah 2:9 You have forced the women of my people out of their nice homes, and you have taken my honor away from their children forever.
Micah 2:10 Get up and leave; this place is not your rest: it's unclean and will ruin you with terrible destruction.
Micah 2:11 If a man walks in the spirit and lies, saying, "I will tell you about wine and strong drink," he will be considered a prophet by these people.
Micah 2:12 I will definitely bring together all of you, Jacob; I will gather the leftovers of Israel; I will put them as the sheep in Bozrah, as a group in their pen: they will make a loud sound because there are so many people.
Micah 2:13 The leader has gone ahead of them: they have smashed through, walked through the gate, and left by it: their king will lead them, with God at their front.

Micah 3:1 And I said, please listen, leaders of Jacob and rulers of Israel; isn't it your duty to know what is right?
Micah 3:2 Those who hate good and love evil, who tear off their skin and flesh from their bones.
Micah 3:3 They also eat my people's flesh, peel off their skin, break their bones, and cut them up like meat for cooking in a pot or caldron.
Micah 3:4 Then they will call out to God, but he will not listen to them: he will hide his face from them at that time because they have acted badly in their actions.
Micah 3:5 God says about the prophets who lead my people astray: they promise peace when they have food to eat, but they declare war against those who don't feed them.
Micah 3:6 So you will have a night without visions; it will be dark for you, without divination. The sun will set on the prophets, and the day will turn dark for them.
Micah 3:7 Then the seers will be embarrassed, and the diviners will be confused: yes, they will all cover their mouths; because there is no reply from God.
Micah 3:8 I am truly filled with power by God's spirit, and with judgment and strength, to tell Jacob his wrongdoing, and to Israel his sin.
Micah 3:9 Please listen, leaders of Jacob's family and rulers of Israel, who hate fairness and twist what is right.
Micah 3:10 They construct Zion with violence, and Jerusalem with wrongdoing.
Micah 3:11 Its leaders judge for bribes, its priests teach for a price, and its prophets tell the future for money. Yet they rely on God and say, "Isn't God with us? No disaster will come upon us."
Micah 3:12 So, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will turn into piles of rubble, and the temple hill will become like overgrown hilltops.

Micah 4:1 In the future, God's house on the mountain will be the most important, higher than all other hills, and people will come to it.
Micah 4:2 Many nations will come and say, "Let's go up to God's mountain, to the house of Jacob's God; He will teach us His ways, and we will follow His paths. For teachings will come from Zion, and God's word from Jerusalem."
Micah 4:3 He will judge among many peoples and correct powerful nations from far away; they will turn their swords into tools for farming, and their spears into tools for cutting branches. No country will fight against another, nor will they learn war anymore.
Micah 4:4 Everyone will sit under their own vine and fig tree without fear because God has promised it.
Micah 4:5 Everyone will follow their own god, and we will follow our God forever.
Micah 4:6 On that day, God says, I will bring together those who limp, and I will collect those who have been scattered, and those whom I have hurt.
Micah 4:7 I will make those who limp a small surviving group, and those who were sent away a powerful nation: and God will rule over them on Mount Zion from now on, forever.
Micah 4:8 And you, tower of the sheep, the daughter of Zion's stronghold, power will come to you first; the kingdom will come to the daughter of Jerusalem.
Micah 4:9 Why are you crying out loud? Is there no king within you? Has your advisor died? For pains have gripped you like a woman in labor.
Micah 4:10 Feel pain and work hard to give birth, daughter of Zion, like a woman in childbirth: for now you will leave the city, you will live in the fields, and you will go all the way to Babylon; there you will be rescued; there God will save you from your enemies.
Micah 4:11 Now many countries are against you, saying, "Let her become dirty, and let us see Zion."
Micah 4:12 But they do not know God's thoughts or understand his plan: for he will gather them like bundles of grain on the threshing floor.
Micah 4:13 Get up and crush, O daughter of Zion, for I will make your strength iron, and I will make your feet brass, and you will break many people into pieces, and I will dedicate their wealth to God, and their possessions to the God of the whole earth.

Micah 5:1 Get ready for battle, people of the city; we are under attack. They will strike the leader of Israel on the face with a stick.
Micah 5:2 Though you, Bethlehem Ephratah, are small among the clans of Judah, from you will come for me a ruler over Israel, whose origins are from long ago, from ancient times.
Micah 5:3 So he will let them go until the woman in labor gives birth; then, the rest of his brothers will come back to the people of Israel.
Micah 5:4 He will stand and take care of the sheep with God's power, in the greatness of God's name; and they will live safely, because he will be honored everywhere on earth.
Micah 5:5 This man will bring peace when the Assyrian invades our land; and if he marches into our palaces, we will fight against him with seven leaders and eight top officials.
Micah 5:6 They will destroy Assyria's land with the sword, and Nimrod's land at its borders: so he will save us from the Assyrian when he enters our land and walks inside our borders.
Micah 5:7 Jacob's remaining people will be among many, like dew from God, like rain on the grass, not depending on anyone or waiting for humans.
Micah 5:8 The remaining people of Jacob will live among the nations, with many people, like a lion among the forest animals, like a young lion among sheep. He will pass through, trample, and tear apart, and no one can rescue.
Micah 5:9 Your hand will rise against your enemies, and all your foes will be destroyed.
Micah 5:10 On that day, God says, I will take away your horses and destroy your chariots.
Micah 5:11 I will destroy the cities in your land and knock down all your fortresses.
Micah 5:12 I will remove witchcraft from your hands, and you will no longer have fortune-tellers.
Micah 5:13 I will destroy your idols and images from among you; you will no longer worship what your hands have made.
Micah 5:14 I will pull out your worship places from among you and I will destroy your cities.
Micah 5:15 I will carry out punishment with angry fury on the nations, the likes of which they have never heard.

Micah 6:1 Listen to what God says; stand up, argue your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear what you say.
Micah 6:2 Listen, mountains, to God's argument, and you solid grounds of the earth: for God has a dispute with his people, and he will speak to Israel about it.
Micah 6:3 My people, what have I done to you? How have I tired you? Tell me.
Micah 6:4 I brought you out of Egypt and saved you from slavery; and I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam ahead of you.
Micah 6:5 My people, remember what King Balak of Moab planned and what Balaam son of Beor told him from Shittim to Gilgal; so you understand the goodness of God.
Micah 6:6 How should I come before God and bow down to the High God? Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
Micah 6:7 Will God be happy with thousands of sheep, or with ten thousand gallons of oil? Should I offer my first child for my wrongs, the child of my body for the sin of my soul?
Micah 6:8 God has shown you, person, what is good. What does God ask of you but to act fairly, love kindness, and walk humbly with your God?
Micah 6:9 God's voice calls out to the city, and the wise person will recognize your name: listen to the punishment, and the one who has sent it.
Micah 6:10 Are there still stolen riches in the house of the bad person, and the dishonest short measure that is hated?
Micah 6:11 Can I consider them honest when they use unfair scales and bags of false weights?
Micah 6:12 The rich people there are very violent, the people living there tell lies, and their speech is full of trickery.
Micah 6:13 I will make you sick by striking you and make you empty because of your sins.
Micah 6:14 You will eat but not be full; you will be thrown down within yourself; you will try to save, but you will not succeed; and what you do save, I will let be destroyed by the sword.
Micah 6:15 You will plant seeds, but you will not harvest crops; you will press olives, but you will not use the oil; you will make sweet wine, but you will not drink it.
Micah 6:16 You follow Omri's laws and Ahab's family's deeds, and take their advice; so I will make you a wasteland, and your people will be mocked; therefore, you will suffer the shame of my people.

Micah 7:1 I am in trouble! I am like when people have picked the summer fruits, like the scraps left after grapes are picked: there is no bunch to eat; I really wanted the early ripe fruit.
Micah 7:2 The good person is gone from the world; no one is honest anymore. Everyone is setting traps to hurt others; they are all trying to catch their fellow man like hunting with a net.
Micah 7:3 They eagerly do bad things with both hands. The leader and the judge both want bribes; the powerful person tells of his evil wish, and so they plan it together.
Micah 7:4 Even the best person is like a prickly bush; the most honest is as sharp as a thorn fence. The time for your guards and punishment is coming; soon they will be confused.
Micah 7:5 Do not trust a friend or rely on a leader; be careful what you say around the one close to you.
Micah 7:6 The son disrespects his father, the daughter rebels against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are his own family members.
Micah 7:7 So I will look to God; I will wait for the God who saves me: my God will listen to me.
Micah 7:8 Don't be happy over me, my enemy. If I fall down, I will get up; if I'm in the dark, God will be my light.
Micah 7:9 I will accept God's anger because I sinned against him, until he stands up for me and makes things right for me. He will lead me into the light, and I will see his goodness.
Micah 7:10 Then my enemy will see it, and she will be covered with shame, the one who asked me, "Where is your God?" I will see her then; she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
Micah 7:11 On the day when your walls are to be rebuilt, on that day the order will be ended.
Micah 7:12 On that day, he will come to you from Assyria, from strong cities, from the fortress to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
Micah 7:13 Despite this, the land will become empty because of the people living there, due to the results of their actions.
Micah 7:14 Take care of your people with your guidance, your special flock living alone in the forest, in the heart of Carmel: let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, like in the past.
Micah 7:15 Based on the number of days since you left Egypt, I will show him wonderful things.
Micah 7:16 Nations will see and be shocked by their own power; they will cover their mouths and be unable to hear.
Micah 7:17 They will lick the dust like snakes, they will come out of their holes like earthworms: they will be scared of our God and will be afraid because of you.
Micah 7:18 Who is a God like you, forgiving sin and overlooking the wrongs of those who are left of your people? You do not stay angry forever because you enjoy being merciful.
Micah 7:19 He will come back, he will show us mercy; he will conquer our wrongs; and you will throw all their sins into the sea's depths.
Micah 7:20 You will show your faithfulness to Jacob and love to Abraham, as you promised our ancestors long ago.

Nahum 1:1 The message about Nineveh. The vision that Nahum from Elkosh saw.
Nahum 1:2 God is jealous, and God takes revenge; God takes revenge and is very angry; God will punish those against him, and he keeps anger for his enemies.
Nahum 1:3 God is patient, very strong, and does not let the guilty go free. God moves in the tornado and the storm, and the clouds are like the dust under his feet.
Nahum 1:4 He scolds the sea, makes it dry, and dries up all the rivers: Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flowers of Lebanon also wither.
Nahum 1:5 Mountains shake before him, hills dissolve, and the earth burns at his arrival, including the world and everyone living in it.
Nahum 1:6 Who can withstand his anger? Who can endure his fierce rage? His fury is unleashed like fire, and he shatters rocks.
Nahum 1:7 God is good, a safe place in times of trouble; and he knows those who trust in him.
Nahum 1:8 With a sweeping flood, he will completely destroy that place, and darkness will chase his enemies.
Nahum 1:9 What are you planning against God? He will completely end it; trouble will not happen again.
Nahum 1:10 While they are tangled like thorns and drunk like drunkards, they will be consumed like completely dry straw.
Nahum 1:11 Someone from among you plans evil against God, a wicked advisor.
Nahum 1:12 God says, "Even if they are calm and many, they will be cut down when he comes through. Though I have caused you trouble, I will not do it anymore."
Nahum 1:13 I will now break his control over you and tear apart your chains.
Nahum 1:14 God has commanded that your name will no longer spread. I will destroy the carved and metal idols from your temple. I will prepare your grave because you are wicked.
Nahum 1:15 Look at the mountains—the feet of the one who brings good news and announces peace! O Judah, celebrate your festivals and keep your promises: the evil one will not invade you again; he is completely defeated.

Nahum 2:1 The destroyer has come before you: guard the fortress, watch the road, strengthen your waist, and power up greatly.
Nahum 2:2 God has taken away Jacob's greatness, just like Israel's; because the enemies have stripped them bare and ruined their vine branches.
Nahum 2:3 The warriors' shields are red, the brave wear red clothes: on the day of battle, the chariots will blaze with fire, and the evergreen trees will shake violently.
Nahum 2:4 Chariots will speed through the streets, bumping into each other on wide roads; they will look like bright torches and move as fast as lightning.
Nahum 2:5 He will list his brave men: they will trip as they walk; they will rush to its wall, and the protection will be set up.
Nahum 2:6 The river gates will be opened, and the palace will fall apart.
Nahum 2:7 Huzzab will be captured and taken away; she will be led by her maids who sound like cooing doves, beating on their chests.
Nahum 2:8 Nineveh is an ancient city like a water pond, but its people will run away. "Stop, stop," they will shout, but no one will turn around.
Nahum 2:9 Take the silver loot, take the gold loot; there is no end to the riches and beauty from all the nice things.
Nahum 2:10 It is empty and ruined and destroyed; hearts are faint, knees knock, all hips hurt, and every face grows pale.
Nahum 2:11 Where is the home of the lions and the place where the young lions eat, where the lion, the old lion, walked, and the lion's cub, without fear?
Nahum 2:12 The lion tore enough for his cubs, choked food for his lionesses, and filled his lairs with prey, and his dens with torn animals.
Nahum 2:13 Look, I am against you, says God, and I will burn your chariots in smoke, and the sword will kill your young lions: I will take away your hunted animals from the land, and no one will hear your messengers anymore.

Nahum 3:1 Trouble to the violent city! It is full of lies and theft; the victims never escape.
Nahum 3:2 The sound of a whip, the clatter of wheels, the pounding of horses, and the bouncing of chariots.
Nahum 3:3 The rider raises both the shiny sword and the sparkling spear. There are many killed and lots of dead bodies, with no end to their remains; they trip over their own bodies.
Nahum 3:4 Because the beautiful prostitute did many bad sexual things and used magic to control people, she sold entire nations and families.
Nahum 3:5 I am against you, says God; and I will lift your skirts over your face, I will show the nations your bareness, and the kingdoms your disgrace.
Nahum 3:6 I will throw disgusting dirt on you, make you unwanted, and put you on display for all to see.
Nahum 3:7 Everyone who sees you will run away and say, 'Nineveh is destroyed. Who will feel sorry for her? Where can I find someone to comfort you?'
Nahum 3:8 Are you better than the crowded city of No, which was located by the rivers, surrounded by water, whose defense was the sea, and whose walls were also from the sea?
Nahum 3:9 Ethiopia and Egypt gave her great power, and it had no limit; Put and Lubim were your helpers.
Nahum 3:10 She was taken away and made a prisoner. Her young children were killed in the streets, they drew lots for her leaders, and all her important men were tied up with chains.
Nahum 3:11 You will also get drunk; you will hide yourself; you too will look for strength because of the enemy.
Nahum 3:12 Your strong places will be like fig trees with early figs: if shaken, they will fall right into the eater’s mouth.
Nahum 3:13 Look, your people are weak like women; your land's gates will be wide open to your enemies; fire will burn up your defenses.
Nahum 3:14 Gather water for the siege, strengthen your defenses: go to the clay and step on the mortar, make the brick oven strong.
Nahum 3:15 Fire will consume you; a sword will eliminate you, like a cankerworm it will devour you. Though you increase in number like cankerworms, though you multiply like locusts.
Nahum 3:16 You have more traders than the stars in the sky: the locust destroys and then flies away.
Nahum 3:17 Your leaders swarm like locusts, and your officials are like the big locusts that settle in the walls on a chilly day, but when the sun comes up they fly away, and no one knows where they go.
Nahum 3:18 Your leaders sleep, O Assyrian king: your important people will lie in the dust: your people are spread on the mountains, and nobody brings them together.
Nahum 3:19 Your injury cannot be healed; your wound is severe. Everyone who hears about you will clap their hands because your evil has affected everyone without stopping.

Habakkuk 1:1 The message that the prophet Habakkuk saw.
Habakkuk 1:2 God, how long must I call for help, but you do not listen? I cry to you about violence, but you do not save.
Habakkuk 1:3 Why do you show me wrongdoing, and make me see trouble? Destruction and violence are in front of me; there are people who start fights and arguments.
Habakkuk 1:4 So the law fails, and fair judgment is not carried out because the wicked surround the good; that's why unfair decisions are made.
Habakkuk 1:5 Look among the nations, watch, and be amazed: for I will do something in your time that you won't believe, even if someone tells you.
Habakkuk 1:6 Look, I am bringing the Chaldeans, a fierce and quick-moving people, who will spread across the land and take over homes that do not belong to them.
Habakkuk 1:7 They are frightening and awful: they make their own rules and honor.
Habakkuk 1:8 Their horses are faster than leopards and fiercer than night wolves. The riders will spread out, and they will come from far away. They will swoop down like eagles rushing to feed.
Habakkuk 1:9 They will all come to do violence: their faces will be eager like the east wind, and they will collect captives like the sand.
Habakkuk 1:10 They will mock the kings, and laugh at the princes. They will make fun of every fortress, because they will pile up dirt and capture it.
Habakkuk 1:11 Then he will change his mind, cross over, and do wrong, giving credit for his strength to his god.
Habakkuk 1:12 Aren't you eternal, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. God, you have appointed them for judgment; and, mighty God, you have set them up for discipline.
Habakkuk 1:13 You have purer eyes than to see evil and cannot look at wrongs. So why do you watch those who are dishonest and stay silent when the wicked swallows someone more righteous than himself?
Habakkuk 1:14 You make people like fish in the sea, like crawling creatures with no one to lead them.
Habakkuk 1:15 They catch all of them with a hook, trap them in their net, and collect them with their netting; so they are happy and joyful.
Habakkuk 1:16 So they offer sacrifices to their nets and burn incense to their fishing dragnets, because these things give them rich and abundant food.
Habakkuk 1:17 Will they then keep emptying their net, never stopping the killing of nations?

Habakkuk 2:1 I will stand at my guard post and take my position on the watchtower. I will look to see what God will tell me and how I should respond when I am corrected.
Habakkuk 2:2 God answered me, "Write the vision clearly on tablets, so that anyone who reads it can quickly understand."
Habakkuk 2:3 The dream is set for a specific time, and it will come true at the end without lying. Even if it delays, keep waiting for it; it will certainly happen and won't be late.
Habakkuk 2:4 Look, the person with a proud heart is not right inside, but the righteous person will live by trusting in God.
Habakkuk 2:5 Yes, because he sins with wine, he is an arrogant man who does not stay home, but grows his wants like the grave, and is like death, never satisfied, collecting all nations to himself and piling up all people.
Habakkuk 2:6 Won't everyone use a story against him, mock him, and say, "How terrible for the one who takes what isn't his! How long? And for the one who burdens himself with heavy debts!"
Habakkuk 2:7 Won't they suddenly rise up to bite you, awaken to trouble you, and you will become loot for them?
Habakkuk 2:8 Because you have robbed many nations, all the survivors will rob you; because of people's bloodshed, and violence to the land, the city, and to everyone living there.
Habakkuk 2:9 How terrible for the person who greedily wants wrong things for his home, trying to place his home safe and high to avoid evil's reach!
Habakkuk 2:10 You have brought disgrace to your family by harming many people, and you have wronged your own life.
Habakkuk 2:11 The stone in the wall will cry out, and the wooden beam will respond.
Habakkuk 2:12 Trouble comes to the one who builds a town with bloodshed and starts a city with wrongdoing!
Habakkuk 2:13 Look, isn't it because of God that people work hard for nothing and wear themselves out for no reason?
Habakkuk 2:14 The earth will be full of understanding God's glory, just like water fills the sea.
Habakkuk 2:15 Trouble comes to the one who gives their neighbor drink, pouring from the bottle to get them drunk, so they can gaze upon their nakedness!
Habakkuk 2:16 You are full of shame instead of honor: drink yourself, and show your nakedness: the cup from God's right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.
Habakkuk 2:17 Lebanon's violence will fall on you, and the terror from the animals you scared, because of the bloodshed and the violence in the land, the city, and all who live there.
Habakkuk 2:18 What good is an idol that has been carved? Or a cast image and a spreader of falsehoods, when their creator trusts in them to make silent gods?
Habakkuk 2:19 Bad luck to the person who tells a piece of wood to wake up or a silent stone to get up—it can’t teach. Look, it's covered with gold and silver, but there's no life inside it at all.
Habakkuk 2:20 God is in his holy place: let everyone on earth be quiet before him.

Habakkuk 3:1 Habakkuk the prophet's prayer for troubling times.
Habakkuk 3:2 God, I have heard what you said and was scared: God, make your work live again during the years, let it be known; even when you're angry, please remember to be kind.
Habakkuk 3:3 God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. His brightness filled the sky, and the earth was full of His praise.
Habakkuk 3:4 His brightness was like the light; he had rays shining from his hand: and that's where his power was hidden.
Habakkuk 3:5 A disease spread before him, and fiery sparks shot out from under his feet.
Habakkuk 3:6 He stood and measured the earth; he looked and separated the nations; the ancient mountains crumbled, the eternal hills bowed down; his paths are forever.
Habakkuk 3:7 I saw the tents of Cushan in trouble; and the tents in the land of Midian shook.
Habakkuk 3:8 Was God unhappy with the rivers? Were you angry with the rivers? Were you mad at the sea when you rode on your horses and drove your chariots to save us?
Habakkuk 3:9 Your bow was fully revealed, as promised to the tribes, your word. Pause. You split the earth with rivers.
Habakkuk 3:10 The mountains saw you and shook; the floodwaters swept by; the ocean roared and raised its waves high.
Habakkuk 3:11 The sun and moon stopped in the sky; by the light of your arrows, they moved, and by the glow of your shining spear.
Habakkuk 3:12 You marched through the land in anger, you crushed the nations in your wrath.
Habakkuk 3:13 You went out to save your people, to save your chosen one; you crushed the leader of the wicked house, laying bare the foundation all the way to the neck. Pause.
Habakkuk 3:14 You struck the leaders' heads with their own staffs. They attacked me like a whirlwind, eager to secretly destroy the weak.
Habakkuk 3:15 You walked through the sea with your horses, through the mass of deep waters.
Habakkuk 3:16 When I heard, my stomach shook; my lips shook at the sound: decay spread in my bones, and I shook inside, so I could be calm on the day of trouble: when he rises against the people, he will attack them with his soldiers.
Habakkuk 3:17 Even if the fig tree does not bloom and the grapes don't grow on the vines; if the olive crop fails and the fields make no food; if there are no sheep in the pen and no cattle in the barns;
Habakkuk 3:18 I will be happy in God, I will take joy in the God who saves me.
Habakkuk 3:19 God gives me strength, makes me as sure-footed as a deer, and lets me walk on the heights. For the director of music with stringed instruments.

Zephaniah 1:1 God's message came to Zephaniah, Cushi's son, Gedaliah's grandson, Amariah's great-grandson, and Hizkiah's great-great-grandson, during Josiah's time, Amon's son, who was king of Judah.
Zephaniah 1:2 I will completely destroy everything from the land, says God.
Zephaniah 1:3 I will destroy people and animals; I will destroy the birds in the sky and the fish in the sea, along with the obstacles that the wicked face: and I will wipe out people from the earth, says God.
Zephaniah 1:4 I will reach out my hand against Judah, and against everyone living in Jerusalem; I will eliminate the followers of Baal from this place, along with the idolatrous priests.
Zephaniah 1:5 Those who worship the stars from their rooftops, and those who worship and make promises by God, and those who make promises by Malcham.
Zephaniah 1:6 And those who turned away from God; and those who did not look for God, or ask about Him.
Zephaniah 1:7 Be quiet before God, because God's day is near: God has prepared a sacrifice and invited His guests.
Zephaniah 1:8 On the day of God's sacrifice, I will punish the leaders, the king's children, and all who wear foreign clothes.
Zephaniah 1:9 On that day, I will also punish everyone who jumps over the doorway and fills their master's house with violence and lies.
Zephaniah 1:10 On that day, God says there will be a sound of crying from the Fish Gate, a wailing from the second area, and a loud crash from the hills.
Zephaniah 1:11 Cry out, people of Maktesh, because all the traders are destroyed; everyone who handles silver is wiped out.
Zephaniah 1:12 At that time, I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish those who are comfortable and think God will neither help nor harm.
Zephaniah 1:13 So their possessions will be stolen, and their homes will be empty. They will build houses but not live in them, and they will grow grapes but not drink the wine.
Zephaniah 1:14 God's great day is close, very close, and is coming quickly. Even the shouts on that day will make strong men cry loudly.
Zephaniah 1:15 That day is a day of anger, a day of problems and suffering, a day of destruction and ruin, a day of darkness and sadness, a day of clouds and deep shadow.
Zephaniah 1:16 A day of trumpet blasts and warnings against the walled cities and tall towers.
Zephaniah 1:17 I will cause trouble for people, making them stumble like blind people, because they sinned against God. Their blood will spill like dust, and their bodies will be like waste.
Zephaniah 1:18 Their silver and gold won't save them when God is angry. The whole land will be consumed by the fire of his jealousy. He will quickly remove everyone living in the land.

Zephaniah 2:1 Come together, yes, come together, unwanted nation.
Zephaniah 2:2 Before the command comes out, before the day flies away like husks, before God's strong anger hits you, before the day of God's anger arrives.
Zephaniah 2:3 Look for God, all you humble people of the earth, who have followed his laws; look for doing right and being humble: perhaps you will be kept safe on the day of God's anger.
Zephaniah 2:4 Gaza will be abandoned, Ashkelon will be ruined, they will force Ashdod out at midday, and Ekron will be destroyed.
Zephaniah 2:5 Sorry for you, people by the sea, Cherethite nation! God's message is against you; Canaan, land of the Philistines, I will destroy you so no one will live there.
Zephaniah 2:6 The seashore will become homes and huts for shepherds, and pens for sheep.
Zephaniah 2:7 The land will be for Judah's survivors; they will graze there. At night, they will rest in Ashkelon's homes because God will care for them and end their exile.
Zephaniah 2:8 I have heard Moab's insults and Ammon's children's taunts, as they insult my people and boast against their land.
Zephaniah 2:9 So I promise, as I am alive, says God, Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—a place of weeds and salt pits, a land forever empty. The survivors of my people will take their things, and those left of my people will own their land.
Zephaniah 2:10 They will receive this for their arrogance because they insulted and acted superior to God's people.
Zephaniah 2:11 God will be fearsome to them: for he will starve all the earth's gods; and people will worship him, each from their own place, including all the islands of the nations.
Zephaniah 2:12 You people of Ethiopia will also be killed by my sword.
Zephaniah 2:13 He will reach out his hand to the north to ruin Assyria; he will turn Nineveh into ruins, dry as a desert.
Zephaniah 2:14 Animals will rest inside the city, creatures from every country: birds like pelicans and herons will nest in the high beams; their sounds will fill the windows; ruins will be at the doorways because God will reveal the woodwork.
Zephaniah 2:15 This happy city lived without worries, and thought to herself, "I am alone and there's no one like me." But look how it's now empty, a spot where animals rest! Everyone who goes by will hiss and shake their head.

Zephaniah 3:1 Sadness to the dirty and tainted city, to the one that oppresses!
Zephaniah 3:2 She did not listen; she did not accept correction; she did not trust in God; she did not draw close to her God.
Zephaniah 3:3 Her leaders inside her city are like loud lions; her judges are like wolves at night; they don't even leave bones until the next day.
Zephaniah 3:4 Her prophets are unreliable and deceitful; her priests have made the holy place dirty and have broken the law.
Zephaniah 3:5 The fair God is in the middle of it all; he will not act wrongly: every morning he shows his fair decisions, he does not fail; but the unfair have no shame.
Zephaniah 3:6 I have destroyed the nations: their towers are empty; I have made their streets empty, so no one passes by: their cities are ruined, with no people, with no one living there.
Zephaniah 3:7 I thought, 'You will surely respect God and accept guidance, so your homes won't be destroyed, no matter how I punish you.' But they got up early and ruined everything they did.
Zephaniah 3:8 Wait for me, says God, until the day I come to punish. I plan to bring together nations and kingdoms, so I can unleash my fury and intense anger on them. The whole earth will be consumed by the fire of my jealousy.
Zephaniah 3:9 Then I will give the people a clear language, so they can all call on God's name and serve him together.
Zephaniah 3:10 From beyond Ethiopia's rivers, my worshipers, the scattered people's children, will bring me gifts.
Zephaniah 3:11 On that day, you will not feel shame for all your wrong actions against me; because I will remove from you those who take pride in your arrogance, and you will no longer act superior because of my sacred hill.
Zephaniah 3:12 I will also leave among you a suffering and poor people, and they will trust in God's name.
Zephaniah 3:13 The remaining people of Israel will not do wrong, nor will they tell lies; they will not have deceitful speech: because they will eat and rest, and no one will scare them.
Zephaniah 3:14 Sing, daughter of Zion; yell, Israel; be happy and celebrate with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.
Zephaniah 3:15 God has removed your punishments and thrown out your enemies. The King of Israel, God Himself, is with you; you will not see evil again.
Zephaniah 3:16 On that day, they will tell Jerusalem, "Don't be afraid," and to Zion, "Don't let your hands grow weak."
Zephaniah 3:17 God among you is powerful; he will save you, he will be happy with great joy; he will find peace in his love, he will delight in you with singing.
Zephaniah 3:18 I will bring together those who are sad because of the holy meeting, who belong to you, and felt its disgrace as a heavy load.
Zephaniah 3:19 Look, I will fix everything that hurts you at that time. I will rescue the limping one and bring back those who were scattered. I will give them honor and recognition in all the places where they were disgraced.
Zephaniah 3:20 At that time, I will bring you back when I gather you. I will make your name honored and praised by all people on earth, when I free you and you see it, says God.

Haggai 1:1 In Darius's second year as king, on the first day of the sixth month, God's message came through the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel, Shealtiel's son and the governor of Judah, and to Joshua, Josedech's son and the high priest.
Haggai 1:2 God says, "These people claim it's not the time to build God's house."
Haggai 1:3 God's message came through the prophet Haggai, saying,
Haggai 1:4 Is it time for you to live in your paneled houses while this house remains in ruins?
Haggai 1:5 So now, God says this: Think about what you're doing.
Haggai 1:6 You planted a lot but harvest little; you eat but aren't full; you drink but aren't satisfied; you dress but aren't warm; and you earn money only to put it into a pocket with holes.
Haggai 1:7 God says; Think about what you do.
Haggai 1:8 Go to the mountain, get wood, and make the house; I will enjoy it and be honored, says God.
Haggai 1:9 You expected a lot, but see, it turned out to be little; and when you brought it home, I scattered it. Why? says God. Because my house is ruined, while each of you rushes to care for your own house.
Haggai 1:10 So the sky above you doesn't give dew, and the earth doesn't produce crops.
Haggai 1:11 I called for dryness on the land, the mountains, the grain, the new wine, the oil, the crops, the people, the animals, and all the work they do.
Haggai 1:12 Then Zerubbabel, Shealtiel's son, and Joshua, Josedech's son, the high priest, with all the remaining people, listened to God's voice and Haggai the prophet's words, because God had sent him, and the people respected God.
Haggai 1:13 Then Haggai, God's messenger, delivered God's message to the people, saying, "I am with you," says God.
Haggai 1:14 God motivated the spirit of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, leader of Judah, and Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirits of all the remaining people; and they came and worked on God's house.
Haggai 1:15 On the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in King Darius's second year.

Haggai 2:1 In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day, God's message came through the prophet Haggai, saying,
Haggai 2:2 Talk to Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, the leader of Judah, and to Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest, and to the rest of the people, and say,
Haggai 2:3 Who among you saw this temple when it was first built? And what do you think of it now? Doesn't it seem like nothing compared to before?
Haggai 2:4 Be strong now, Zerubbabel, says God; and be strong, Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all you people of the land, says God, and work: because I am with you, says God.
Haggai 2:5 Based on the promise I made to you when you left Egypt, my spirit stays with you: do not be afraid.
Haggai 2:6 God says: After a little while, I will shake the sky, the earth, the sea, and the land.
Haggai 2:7 I will shake all nations, and what every nation wants will come. I will fill this house with glory, says God.
Haggai 2:8 The silver and the gold belong to me, says God.
Haggai 2:9 The splendor of this new house will be greater than the old one, says God, and here I will bring peace, says God.
Haggai 2:10 On the 24th day of the ninth month, in the second year of King Darius, God's message came through the prophet Haggai, saying,
Haggai 2:11 God says; Now ask the priests about the law and tell them,
Haggai 2:12 If someone carries sacred meat in their clothes and their clothes touch bread, soup, wine, oil, or any food, will it become sacred? The priests said no.
Haggai 2:13 Then Haggai asked, "If someone unclean from a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?" And the priests replied, "It will become unclean."
Haggai 2:14 Haggai replied, "This is how these people and this nation are before God, and so is everything they do; even their offerings are unclean."
Haggai 2:15 Please think about this day and the past, before any stone was set on another in God's temple.
Haggai 2:16 Since that time, when someone went to a pile of twenty measures, there were only ten; when someone went to the wine vat to get fifty containers, there were only twenty.
Haggai 2:17 I struck you with blight, mildew, and hail, which ruined your work; but you still didn't turn to me, says God.
Haggai 2:18 Think about this day and from now on, from the 24th day of the ninth month, since the day the foundation of God's temple was set, think about it.
Haggai 2:19 Is the seed still in the barn? Yes, the grapevine, fig tree, pomegranate, and olive tree haven't produced fruit yet. But from today, I will bless you.
Haggai 2:20 Once more, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, God's message came to Haggai.
Haggai 2:21 Tell Zerubbabel, the leader of Judah, I will shake the sky and the ground.
Haggai 2:22 I will topple the rulers of nations, destroy the power of foreign kingdoms, overturn their war chariots and riders; the horses and riders will fall, each killed by his comrade's sword.
Haggai 2:23 On that day, says God, I will choose you, Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, says God, and I will make you like a seal ring, because I have chosen you, says God.

Zechariah 1:1 In the eighth month, during Darius's second year as king, God sent a message to Zechariah, Berechiah's son and the grandson of Iddo the prophet.
Zechariah 1:2 God was very unhappy with your ancestors.
Zechariah 1:3 Tell them this: 'God of all commands: Come back to me, and I will come back to you,' says God of all.
Zechariah 1:4 Do not be like your ancestors. Before, prophets told them, "God says, 'Now stop your evil ways and actions.' But they did not listen or pay attention to me," says God.
Zechariah 1:5 Where are your ancestors now? And do prophets live forever?
Zechariah 1:6 But my words and my laws, which I gave to my prophets, didn't your ancestors take them to heart? When they did, they turned back and realized, just as God planned to treat us based on our actions and behavior, so he has done to us.
Zechariah 1:7 On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, called Sebat, in the second year of Darius, God spoke to Zechariah, Berechiah's son, Iddo's grandson, the prophet.
Zechariah 1:8 At night, I saw a man on a red horse standing among the myrtle trees in the valley, with red, speckled, and white horses behind him.
Zechariah 1:9 I said, "Oh sir, what are these?" And the angel speaking with me replied, "I will show you what they are."
Zechariah 1:10 The man standing among the myrtle trees replied, "These are the ones God has sent to walk back and forth across the earth."
Zechariah 1:11 They replied to the angel of God standing among the myrtle trees, "We have walked back and forth across the earth, and see, the whole earth is quiet and at peace."
Zechariah 1:12 Then the angel from God replied and said, "God of all, how long will you not show kindness to Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, which you have been angry with for seventy years?"
Zechariah 1:13 God answered the angel who was speaking to me with kind and comforting words.
Zechariah 1:14 The angel talking to me told me to shout this message: "God says, 'I have a strong love for Jerusalem and Zion.'"
Zechariah 1:15 I am very upset with the nations that are calm: because I was only a little upset, but they made the trouble worse.
Zechariah 1:16 So God says, "I have come back to Jerusalem with kindness. My house will be built there," says God, "and Jerusalem will be marked out for building."
Zechariah 1:17 Say again, God of all says: My cities will grow with success; God will comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem again.
Zechariah 1:18 I looked up and saw four horns.
Zechariah 1:19 I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" And he replied, "These are the horns that have spread out Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
Zechariah 1:20 God showed me four carpenters.
Zechariah 1:21 I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He answered, "These horns scattered Judah so no one could raise their head. But these have come to frighten them and to throw out the horns of the nations that raised their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."

Zechariah 2:1 I looked up once more, and saw a man holding a measuring tape.
Zechariah 2:2 Then I asked, "Where are you going?" And he answered me, "To measure Jerusalem, to find out how wide and how long it is."
Zechariah 2:3 The angel who was speaking with me left, and another angel came out to meet him.
Zechariah 2:4 He said to him, "Go quickly, tell the young man, 'Jerusalem will be filled with people and animals, and it won't need walls.'"
Zechariah 2:5 I, says God, will be like a protective wall of fire around her, and I will be the honor within her.
Zechariah 2:6 Come, come, leave the land of the north, says God, for I have scattered you in all directions like the four winds of the sky, says God.
Zechariah 2:7 Save yourself, Zion, who lives among the people of Babylon.
Zechariah 2:8 God, the Lord of all, says this: After the glory, he sent me to the nations that robbed you. Because whoever harms you, harms the apple of his eye.
Zechariah 2:9 Look, I will wave my hand at them, and they will become loot for their own slaves. Then you will know that God has sent me.
Zechariah 2:10 Sing and be happy, daughter of Zion; for look, I am coming and I will live among you, says God.
Zechariah 2:11 Many countries will join with God on that day and will be my people. I will live among you, and you will realize that God has sent me to you.
Zechariah 2:12 God will take Judah as his own in the sacred land and will choose Jerusalem once more.
Zechariah 2:13 Everyone be quiet before God, for he has risen from his sacred home.

Zechariah 3:1 He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before God's angel, and Satan standing at his right side to oppose him.
Zechariah 3:2 God said to Satan, "God corrects you, Satan; God who chose Jerusalem corrects you. Isn't this like a stick saved from the fire?"
Zechariah 3:3 Joshua was wearing dirty clothes and stood in front of the angel.
Zechariah 3:4 He replied to those standing before him, "Remove the dirty clothes from him." Then he said to him, "See, I have taken away your sin, and I will dress you in new clothes."
Zechariah 3:5 I said, "Put a clean turban on his head." So they put a clean turban on his head and gave him clothes to wear. And God's messenger stood by.
Zechariah 3:6 The angel of God warned Joshua, saying,
Zechariah 3:7 God says: If you follow my ways and keep my commands, then you will also govern my house and guard my courts, and I will give you places to walk among those who stand here.
Zechariah 3:8 Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your friends who sit with you: they are men to be marveled at. Look, I will bring out my servant, the Branch.
Zechariah 3:9 Look at the stone I put in front of Joshua. This one stone has seven eyes on it. I will carve its design, says God, and in one day, I will take away the sin of that land.
Zechariah 3:10 On that day, says God, everyone will invite their neighbor to sit together under the vine and the fig tree.

Zechariah 4:1 The angel who was speaking with me came back and woke me up like someone being woken from sleep.
Zechariah 4:2 He asked me, "What do you see?" And I answered, "I see a golden lampstand with a bowl at the top and seven lights on it, with seven tubes going to the lights."
Zechariah 4:3 Two olive trees were next to it, one on the right side of the bowl and one on the left side.
Zechariah 4:4 So I replied to the angel speaking with me, asking, "What are these, sir?"
Zechariah 4:5 The angel speaking with me replied and asked, "Do you not know what these are?" And I answered, "No, sir."
Zechariah 4:6 He replied to me, "This is what God tells Zerubbabel: 'Not by strength or by force, but by my spirit,' says God."
