Zechariah 4:7 Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel, you will become flat land: and he will present the top stone amid shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'
Zechariah 4:8 Also, God spoke to me, saying,
Zechariah 4:9 Zerubbabel's hands have started building this house; his hands will also complete it; and you will know that God has sent me to you.
Zechariah 4:10 Who has looked down on small beginnings? They will celebrate and see the measuring line in Zerubbabel's hand along with the seven; they represent God's eyes, which move throughout the entire world.
Zechariah 4:11 I answered and asked him, "What are these two olive trees on the right and left sides of the lampstand?"
Zechariah 4:12 I replied again and asked him, "What are these two olive branches that pour out golden oil through the two gold pipes?"
Zechariah 4:13 He answered and asked, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, sir."
Zechariah 4:14 He said, "These are the two chosen ones who stand by God of the whole earth."

Zechariah 5:1 Then I turned, raised my eyes, and saw a flying scroll.
Zechariah 5:2 He asked me, "What do you see?" I replied, "I see a flying scroll; it is twenty units long and ten units wide."
Zechariah 5:3 He told me, "This is the curse that will spread across the whole earth: everyone who steals will be punished as shown here; and everyone who lies under oath will be punished as shown there."
Zechariah 5:4 I will make this happen, says God of all, and it will go into the thief's house, and into the house of anyone who lies using my name: it will stay in the middle of his house, and destroy it, with its wood and stones.
Zechariah 5:5 The angel who was speaking to me went out and then said to me, "Look up now and see what is coming out."
Zechariah 5:6 I asked, "What is that?" He replied, "This is a measuring basket that is being sent out." He also said, "This represents them throughout the whole world."
Zechariah 5:7 Then I saw a piece of lead lifted up, and there was a woman sitting inside the basket.
Zechariah 5:8 He said, "This is evil." He threw it into the ephah and put the lead cover over its opening.
Zechariah 5:9 I looked up and saw two women coming with the wind in their wings. They had wings like a stork's wings. They lifted the basket up into the sky, between the earth and heaven.
Zechariah 5:10 Then I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "Where are they taking the basket?"
Zechariah 5:11 He told me to build a house for it in the land of Shinar: it will be set up and stand on its own foundation.

Zechariah 6:1 I turned, looked up, and saw four chariots coming from between two brass mountains.
Zechariah 6:2 In the first cart were red horses; and in the second cart black horses.
Zechariah 6:3 In the third chariot were white horses; in the fourth chariot were speckled and strong brown horses.
Zechariah 6:4 Then I replied to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, sir?"
Zechariah 6:5 The angel replied to me, "These are the four spirits of the sky, sent out from the presence of God who rules over the whole earth."
Zechariah 6:6 The black horses inside go to the north; the white follow them; and the gray head south.
Zechariah 6:7 The horse went out to travel back and forth across the land, and God said, "Go, move back and forth across the land." So they traveled back and forth across the land.
Zechariah 6:8 He called out to me and said, "Look, those going to the north country have calmed my spirit there."
Zechariah 6:9 God's message came to me, saying,
Zechariah 6:10 Choose some men from the captives, from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon. Go on the same day to the house of Josiah, Zephaniah's son.
Zechariah 6:11 Then take silver and gold, make crowns, and put them on the head of Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest.
Zechariah 6:12 Tell him this message from God: Look at the man called The BRANCH; he will rise from where he is and build God's temple.
Zechariah 6:13 He will build God's temple; he will have honor and sit and govern on his throne; he will be a priest on his throne, and peace will be the plan between the two.
Zechariah 6:14 The crowns will be for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen, Zephaniah's son, as a reminder in God's temple.
Zechariah 6:15 People from far away will come and build God's temple, and you will realize that God has sent me to you. This will happen if you carefully listen to and obey God.

Zechariah 7:1 In the fourth year of King Darius, God's message came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chisleu.
Zechariah 7:2 They sent Sherezer, Regemmelech, and their men to the house of God to pray to God.
Zechariah 7:3 Talk to the priests in God's house and to the prophets, asking, "Should I cry and fast in the fifth month like I've been doing for many years?"
Zechariah 7:4 God spoke to me, saying,
Zechariah 7:5 Tell everyone in the land, and the priests, 'When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh month for seventy years, were you really fasting for me?
Zechariah 7:6 When you ate and drank, wasn't it for your own benefit?
Zechariah 7:7 Shouldn't you listen to the words God spoke through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem was full of people and thriving, and the surrounding cities were also populated, including the southern areas and the lowlands?
Zechariah 7:8 God's message came to Zechariah, saying,
Zechariah 7:9 God says, 'Make fair decisions and be kind and compassionate to each other.'
Zechariah 7:10 Do not mistreat widows or orphans, strangers, or the poor; and do not plan to harm your fellow person in your heart.
Zechariah 7:11 But they wouldn't listen, turned their backs, and covered their ears so they couldn't hear.
Zechariah 7:12 Yes, they made their hearts as hard as a diamond so they wouldn't listen to the law and the words that God had sent through his spirit by the earlier prophets; that's why a great anger came from God.
Zechariah 7:13 So, it happened that when he called, they did not listen; so when they called, I did not listen, says God.
Zechariah 7:14 I spread them out with a strong wind to countries they didn't know. The land was empty behind them, with no one going by or coming back, because they made the beautiful land empty.

Zechariah 8:1 God spoke to me once more, saying,
Zechariah 8:2 God says; I felt very jealous for Zion, and my jealousy for her was very strong.
Zechariah 8:3 God says, "I have come back to Zion, and I will live in the heart of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be known as the City of Truth, and God's holy mountain will be called the Sacred Mountain."
Zechariah 8:4 God says: Old men and women will still live in Jerusalem's streets, each with a cane because of their great age.
Zechariah 8:5 The city's streets will be filled with boys and girls playing there.
Zechariah 8:6 God says: Even if this seems amazing to the few people left today, wouldn't it seem amazing to me as well? says God.
Zechariah 8:7 God says, "Look, I will rescue my people from the east and from the west."
Zechariah 8:8 I will bring them to live in the center of Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and fairness.
Zechariah 8:9 God says; Stay strong, all who hear the prophets' words today, spoken since the time the temple foundation was laid, so that the temple can be built.
Zechariah 8:10 Before these days, people and animals did not get paid; there was no peace for anyone going or coming because of the trouble. I made everyone turn against their neighbor.
Zechariah 8:11 But now I will not act towards the remaining people as I did before, says God.
Zechariah 8:12 The seeds will grow well; the vine will produce fruit, the earth will yield its crops, and the sky will give its dew; and I will let the survivors among the people have all these things.
Zechariah 8:13 It will happen that, just as you were a curse among the nations, O people of Judah and Israel, so I will rescue you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid, but be strong.
Zechariah 8:14 God says, "Just as I planned to punish you when your ancestors made me angry, says God, and I did not change my mind."
Zechariah 8:15 So, I have decided once more to be good to Jerusalem and the people of Judah: do not be afraid.
Zechariah 8:16 Do these things: Tell the truth to each other; make honest and peaceful decisions in your communities.
Zechariah 8:17 Do not think of hurting others in your hearts, and do not like lying promises, because I hate all these things, says God.
Zechariah 8:18 God's message came to me, saying,
Zechariah 8:19 God says: The fasts in the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will bring joy, happiness, and cheerful festivals to Judah's people; so love honesty and peace.
Zechariah 8:20 God says; It will happen, that people will come from many cities.
Zechariah 8:21 People from one city will go to another, saying, "Let's go quickly to worship God and to seek God. I will go too."
Zechariah 8:22 Yes, many people and powerful nations will come to look for God in Jerusalem and to pray to God.
Zechariah 8:23 God says, in those days, ten men from different nations and languages will grab the clothes of a Jewish man, saying, "We want to go with you because we've heard that God is with you."

Zechariah 9:1 The heavy message from God is in Hadrach, and Damascus will be its resting place: when people and all the tribes of Israel look to God.
Zechariah 9:2 Hamath will also border there; Tyre and Sidon, even if they are very wise.
Zechariah 9:3 Tyre built a stronghold for itself and piled up silver like dust, and gold like the mud of the streets.
Zechariah 9:4 Look, God will throw her out and destroy her strength in the sea; and she will be consumed by fire.
Zechariah 9:5 Ashkelon will see and be afraid; Gaza will see and be very sad, and so will Ekron, because what they hoped for will fail. The king will be gone from Gaza, and no one will live in Ashkelon.
Zechariah 9:6 A child born out of wedlock will live in Ashdod, and I will end the arrogance of the Philistines.
Zechariah 9:7 I will remove the blood from his mouth and the forbidden things from his teeth; but the one who stays will belong to our God, and will be like a leader in Judah, and Ekron will be like a Jebusite.
Zechariah 9:8 I will protect my house from the army and from anyone coming and going, and no one will oppress them again, because now I have seen it with my own eyes.
Zechariah 9:9 Be very happy, daughter of Zion; cheer, daughter of Jerusalem: see, your King comes to you: he is fair, and brings rescue; humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the young of a donkey.
Zechariah 9:10 I will remove the war chariots from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem; the battle bows will be taken away. He will bring peace to the nations, and his rule will stretch from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth.
Zechariah 9:11 You too, by the blood of your agreement, I have freed your captives from a waterless pit.
Zechariah 9:12 Go to the safe place, you who hope and wait; today I promise to give you back much more than you lost.
Zechariah 9:13 When I have prepared Judah, equipped it with Ephraim, and rallied your children, Zion, against Greece's children, making you like a warrior's sword.
Zechariah 9:14 God will be seen above them, and his arrow will shoot out like lightning: God will sound the trumpet and come with the southern storms.
Zechariah 9:15 God will protect them; they will eat and conquer with slingshot stones; they will drink and shout as if drunk; they will be full like bowls, like the corners of an altar.
Zechariah 9:16 God will save them on that day like a shepherd saves his sheep; they will shine in his land like jewels in a crown.
Zechariah 9:17 How great is God's goodness and beauty! Grain will make young men happy, and new wine will make young women joyful.

Zechariah 10:1 Ask God for rain when the late rains come; then God will send thunderclouds and give everyone rain for the plants in the fields.
Zechariah 10:2 The idols have said meaningless things, and the fortune-tellers have seen lies and told untrue dreams; they offer empty comfort. So the people wandered like sheep, distressed because they had no leader.
Zechariah 10:3 I became angry with the shepherds and punished the goats. God has taken care of his people, Judah, and made them strong like a fine horse in battle.
Zechariah 10:4 From him comes the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, from him the bow for battle, from him every ruler together.
Zechariah 10:5 They will be like strong warriors, stepping on their enemies in the street mud during the fight: and they will battle because God is with them, and the horse riders will be confused.
Zechariah 10:6 I will make the people of Judah strong, and I will rescue the people of Joseph. I will bring them back and settle them because I care for them. They will be as if I had never rejected them. I am God, their God, and I will listen to them.
Zechariah 10:7 The people of Ephraim will be strong, and their hearts will be happy like when drinking wine; yes, their children will see it and be happy; their hearts will be joyful in God.
Zechariah 10:8 I will call them and bring them together; for I have saved them: and they will multiply as they did before.
Zechariah 10:9 I will scatter them among the nations, and in distant lands they will remember me; they will live with their children and return.
Zechariah 10:10 I will bring them back from Egypt and gather them from Assyria; I will take them to Gilead and Lebanon, where there won't be enough room for them.
Zechariah 10:11 He will go through the sea in trouble, hit the sea's waves, and the river's depths will dry up. Assyria's pride will be lowered, and Egypt's power will leave.
Zechariah 10:12 I will make them strong in God; they will live and act in his name, says God.

Zechariah 11:1 Open your doors, Lebanon, so the fire can burn your cedar trees.
Zechariah 11:2 Cry out, pine tree, because the cedar has fallen; the powerful have been destroyed. Cry out, you oaks of Bashan, because the thick forest has been cut down.
Zechariah 11:3 Shepherds cry out because their beauty is ruined; young lions roar because the lush Jordan Valley is ruined.
Zechariah 11:4 God, my God, says: Take care of the sheep that are being killed.
Zechariah 11:5 The people who own them kill them and think they've done nothing wrong. Those who sell them say, "Praise God, I'm rich." And their own shepherds don't care about them.
Zechariah 11:6 I will not feel sorry for the people of the land anymore, says God. I will let everyone be captured by their neighbors and their ruler. They will attack the land, and I won't save them from it.
Zechariah 11:7 I will give food to the doomed sheep, including you, the needy ones. I got myself two sticks; I named one Beauty and the other Unity, and I took care of the sheep.
Zechariah 11:8 I also got rid of three shepherds in one month; I grew tired of them, and they strongly disliked me too.
Zechariah 11:9 I said, I won't take care of you anymore: let what is dying die, and what is to be cut off be cut off; and let the remaining ones eat each other's flesh.
Zechariah 11:10 I took my stick, named Beauty, and broke it to end the agreement I had with all the people.
Zechariah 11:11 It broke that day, and the needy sheep who followed me realized it was God's message.
Zechariah 11:12 I told them, "If you agree, pay me; if not, don't." So they gave me thirty silver coins as my payment.
Zechariah 11:13 God told me, "Throw it to the potter—the splendid price they valued me at." So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter at God's house.
Zechariah 11:14 Then I cut my other staff named Bands to break the unity between Judah and Israel.
Zechariah 11:15 God told me to take the tools of a foolish shepherd.
Zechariah 11:16 Look, I will bring up a shepherd in the land who won't care for the lost, or look for the young, or heal the injured, or feed the healthy, but he will eat the meat of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.
Zechariah 11:17 Pity the bad shepherd who abandons his sheep! He will be hurt in his arm and right eye: his arm will wither, and his right eye will become completely blind.

Zechariah 12:1 God has a message for Israel. God, who created the skies, set the earth's foundations, and made humans' spirit within them, says this message.
Zechariah 12:2 I will make Jerusalem a cup that makes all the surrounding people tremble, when they attack both Judah and Jerusalem.
Zechariah 12:3 On that day, I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for everyone: anyone who tries to lift it will get hurt, even if all the world's people unite against it.
Zechariah 12:4 On that day, God says, I will strike every horse with panic and their riders with madness; I will watch over the people of Judah and make every horse of the nations blind.
Zechariah 12:5 The leaders of Judah will think, "The people of Jerusalem will give me strength through God, who commands heavenly armies."
Zechariah 12:6 On that day, I will make the leaders of Judah like a fire in a fireplace and like a blazing torch in a bundle of grain; they will burn up all the nearby nations on every side. And people will live in Jerusalem again, just like before.
Zechariah 12:7 God will save the homes of Judah first, so that the honor of David's family and Jerusalem's people won't be greater than that of Judah.
Zechariah 12:8 On that day, God will protect Jerusalem's people; the weakest among them will be like David; and David's family will be like God, like God's angel with them.
Zechariah 12:9 On that day, I will try to destroy all the countries that attack Jerusalem.
Zechariah 12:10 I will give the family of David and the people of Jerusalem a spirit of kindness and prayer. They will look at me, the one they have hurt, and they will be sad for him, like the sadness for an only child, and feel deep sorrow for him, like the sorrow for a firstborn.
Zechariah 12:11 On that day, there will be a great sadness in Jerusalem, like the sadness of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddo.
Zechariah 12:12 The land will be sad, each family by itself; David's family by itself, and their wives by themselves; Nathan's family by itself, and their wives by themselves.
Zechariah 12:13 The Levi family separately, and their wives separately; the Shimei family separately, and their wives separately.
Zechariah 12:14 Every remaining family, each on its own, and their wives by themselves.

Zechariah 13:1 On that day, there will be a spring made available to David's family and to the people of Jerusalem for cleansing from sin and impurity.
Zechariah 13:2 On that day, God says, I will remove the idols from the land, and they will be forgotten. I will also get rid of the false prophets and evil spirits from the land.
Zechariah 13:3 When someone still claims to speak for God, his own parents will say, "You must not live because you tell lies in God's name." They will be the ones to end his life for doing so.
Zechariah 13:4 On that day, the prophets will feel shame for every vision when they have prophesied; they won't wear rough clothes to trick people.
Zechariah 13:5 But he will say, "I am not a prophet, I am a farmer; a person taught me to care for animals since I was young."
Zechariah 13:6 Someone will ask him, "What are these wounds on your hands?" And he will reply, "These are the wounds I got at my friends' house."
Zechariah 13:7 Wake up, sword, against my shepherd, and against the man close to me, says God. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will run away; I will act against the small ones.
Zechariah 13:8 God says that in the whole land, two-thirds will be cut off and die, but one-third will be left.
Zechariah 13:9 I will take a third of the people through fire and make them pure like silver, and test them like gold. They will call on me, and I will listen. I will say, 'These are my people,' and they will say, 'God is our God.'

Zechariah 14:1 Look, God's day is coming, and your possessions will be shared out among you.
Zechariah 14:2 I will bring all countries together to fight against Jerusalem; the city will be captured, homes will be looted, and women will be violated; half of the city will be taken prisoner, and the rest of the people will not be separated from the city.
Zechariah 14:3 Then God will go out and battle those nations, just as he did on the day of war.
Zechariah 14:4 On that day, his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The Mount of Olives will split in two from east to west, forming a huge valley. Half of the mountain will move north and half will move south.
Zechariah 14:5 You will run to the mountain valley; this valley will stretch to Azal. Yes, you will run as you did when you escaped the earthquake in Uzziah's time, king of Judah. God will come, and all the holy people with you.
Zechariah 14:6 On that day, the light will neither be bright nor completely dark.
Zechariah 14:7 There will be one day known to God, not day or night, but in the evening there will be light.
Zechariah 14:8 On that day, fresh water will flow from Jerusalem, half to the eastern sea and half to the western sea, in both summer and winter.
Zechariah 14:9 God will be king over the whole earth: on that day, God will be the only one, and his name the only one.
Zechariah 14:10 All the land will become flat from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. It will be raised up and people will live there, from the gate of Benjamin to the location of the first gate, to the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananeel to the king's wine presses.
Zechariah 14:11 People will live there, and there won't be any more total destruction; instead, Jerusalem will be a safe place to live.
Zechariah 14:12 This is the sickness God will use to punish all the people who battled against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are still standing, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
Zechariah 14:13 On that day, a great commotion from God will be among the people; they will all grab their neighbor's hand, and they will turn against each other.
Zechariah 14:14 Judah will also fight at Jerusalem; all the riches of the surrounding nations, gold, silver, and clothes, will be collected in large amounts.
Zechariah 14:15 This is how the disease will affect the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the animals in the tents, just like this disease.
Zechariah 14:16 Everyone remaining from the nations that attacked Jerusalem will go there every year to worship God, the King, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
Zechariah 14:17 If any family on earth does not go to Jerusalem to worship the King, God, they will not get any rain.
Zechariah 14:18 If Egypt's people don't go and don't come because they have no rain, there will be a disease with which God will punish the nations that don't go to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
Zechariah 14:19 This will be the punishment for Egypt and for all nations that do not come to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
Zechariah 14:20 On that day, the horses' bells will have "Holiness to God" on them, and the pots in God's house will be like the bowls at the altar.
Zechariah 14:21 Yes, every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be sacred to God. Everyone who offers a sacrifice will come and use them to boil their offerings. On that day, there will be no Canaanites in God's house.

Malachi 1:1 God's message for Israel through Malachi.
Malachi 1:2 God says, "I have loved you. But you ask, 'How have you loved us?' Wasn't Esau Jacob's brother? But I loved Jacob.
Malachi 1:3 I disliked Esau and destroyed his hills and land, leaving it empty for the wild desert creatures.
Malachi 1:4 Edom says, "We are poor, but we will rebuild the ruins." But God says, "They may build, but I will destroy. They will be known as 'Land of Evil' and 'People God is always angry with.'"
Malachi 1:5 You will see and say, "God will be honored from Israel's border."
Malachi 1:6 A son respects his father, and a servant respects his master. So if I am a father, where is my respect? And if I am a master, where is the fear of me? says God to you, priests, who look down on my name. And you ask, How have we looked down on your name?
Malachi 1:7 You offer dirty bread on my altar, and you ask, "How have we made you dirty?" By saying, "God's table is not important."
Malachi 1:8 If you sacrifice blind animals, isn't that wrong? And if you sacrifice lame or sick ones, isn't that wrong too? Would your governor be happy with that or accept you? says God of all.
Malachi 1:9 And now, please ask God to be kind to us; this happened because of you. Will he respect you? says God Almighty.
Malachi 1:10 Is there anyone among you who would close the doors for nothing? You don't even light a fire on my altar without being paid. I am not pleased with you, says God, and I won't accept your offerings.
Malachi 1:11 From sunrise to sunset, my name will be great among the nations. Everywhere, people will offer incense and pure sacrifices in my name because my name will be great among the nations, says God of hosts.
Malachi 1:12 But you have dishonored it by saying, "God's table is dirty;" and its fruit, even its food, is despised.
Malachi 1:13 You also said, "Look, how tiring this is!" and you scorned it, says God; and you brought the torn, the lame, and the sick animals; you offered this as a gift: should I accept this from you? says God.
Malachi 1:14 Let the trickster be cursed, who has a male in his flock and promises it but sacrifices a damaged one to God instead. For I am a great King, says God, and my name is feared among the nations.

Malachi 2:1 And now, priests, this order is for you.
Malachi 2:2 If you won't listen and don't take seriously giving honor to my name, says God of all, I will send a curse on you, and I will turn your blessings into curses—indeed, I have already done it because you don't take it to heart.
Malachi 2:3 Look, I will ruin your crops and put waste on your faces, the waste from your special feasts; and someone will carry you off with it.
Malachi 2:4 You will understand that I sent this order to you so that my agreement would be with Levi, says God.
Malachi 2:5 I made a promise to him of life and peace; and I gave them to him because he respected me and was in awe of my name.
Malachi 2:6 He spoke the truth, and no wrong was on his lips; he walked with me in peace and fairness, turning many from sin.
Malachi 2:7 The priest's mouth should share knowledge, and people should look for teaching from him, because he is God's messenger.
Malachi 2:8 You have left the right path; you made many people trip over the law; you have ruined the agreement of Levi, says God.
Malachi 2:9 Because of this, I have made you despised and lowly in front of everyone, because you have not followed my ways and have been unfair in applying the law.
Malachi 2:10 Don't we all have one father? Didn't one God make us? Why then do we betray each other, breaking the agreement of our ancestors?
Malachi 2:11 Judah has been unfaithful, and a terrible thing has happened in Israel and Jerusalem; Judah has disgraced the sacredness of God, which he cherished, and has married a woman who worships a different god.
Malachi 2:12 God will remove the man who does this, both the leader and the follower, from the homes of Jacob, and anyone who makes an offering to God of hosts.
Malachi 2:13 You have done this again, making God's altar wet with tears, weeping, and loud crying, so much that God doesn't care about the offerings, or accept them happily from you.
Malachi 2:14 But you ask, "Why?" It is because God has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you have betrayed, although she is your partner, the wife you promised to stay with.
Malachi 2:15 Did not God make them one? Yet he had a spirit left. Why one? To find a godly offspring. So watch over your spirit, and do not betray the wife of your youth.
Malachi 2:16 God, the God of Israel, says he hates divorce: for it covers one's clothes with violence, says God of the armies: so be careful in your spirit, and do not be unfaithful.
Malachi 2:17 You have tired God with your words. But you ask, "How have we tired him?" When you say, "Anyone who does evil is good to God, and he enjoys them," or "Where is the God who judges?"

Malachi 3:1 Look, I will send my messenger, and he will make the path ready for me. And God, whom you are looking for, will quickly come to his temple, the messenger of the agreement you enjoy. Look, he will come, says God of all.
Malachi 3:2 Who can endure the day of his coming? Who will be able to stand when he appears? He is like a fire that purifies and like soap that cleans.
Malachi 3:3 He will sit like someone who cleans and refines silver; he will purify the Levi tribe members, cleaning them like gold and silver, so they can give God a righteous offering.
Malachi 3:4 Then the gifts from Judah and Jerusalem will please God, like in the past and the old years.
Malachi 3:5 I will come close to judge you quickly; I will testify against witches, cheaters, liars, those who cheat workers, widows, orphans, and those who deny justice to foreigners and do not respect me, says God.
Malachi 3:6 I am God, I do not change; so you, the children of Jacob, are not destroyed.
Malachi 3:7 Since your ancestors' time, you have turned away from my rules and haven't followed them. Come back to me, and I will come back to you, says God. But you asked, "How can we come back?"
Malachi 3:8 Can a person steal from God? Yet you have stolen from me. But you ask, 'How have we stolen from you?' Through not giving tithes and offerings.
Malachi 3:9 You are cursed with a curse because you have robbed me, all of you.
Malachi 3:10 Bring all your tithes to the storehouse so there will be food in my house. Test me in this, says God, and see if I don't open the windows of heaven and pour out so many blessings you won't have enough room for them.
Malachi 3:11 I will stop the destroyer for you, so it won't ruin your crops; your vine won't drop its fruit before it’s ready, says God.
Malachi 3:12 Every country will say you are lucky because your land will be wonderful, says God.
Malachi 3:13 You have spoken strongly against me, says God. But you ask, 'What have we said against you?'
Malachi 3:14 You have said, "It's pointless to serve God: and what do we gain from following his rules, and from walking sadly in front of God of all?"
Malachi 3:15 We now say proud people are happy; those who do wrong succeed; those who challenge God are safe.
Malachi 3:16 Those who respected God talked often to each other. God listened and heard them, and a book was written to remember those who respected God and thought about his name.
Malachi 3:17 They will be mine, says God, on that day when I gather my precious ones; I will protect them, like a father protects his serving son.
Malachi 3:18 Then you will come back and understand the difference between the good and the bad, between someone who serves God and someone who does not.

Malachi 4:1 Look, the day is coming, it will burn like a furnace; all the proud and evil-doers will be like dry grass: the coming day will burn them up, God says, leaving them without root or branch.
Malachi 4:2 For those of you who respect my name, the Sun of goodness will rise with healing rays; and you will go out and play freely, like young calves let out of their pens.
Malachi 4:3 You will walk on the wicked; they will be like dust under your feet on the day I do this, says God.
Malachi 4:4 Remember the laws Moses, my servant, gave you, which God told him at Horeb for all Israel, including the rules and decisions.
Malachi 4:5 Look, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of God comes.
Malachi 4:6 He will make fathers' hearts close to their children and children's hearts close to their fathers, so I won't come and punish the earth with a curse.

Matthew 1:1 This book lists Jesus Christ's ancestors. He was from David's and Abraham's family.
Matthew 1:2 Abraham had a son named Isaac; Isaac had a son named Jacob; and Jacob had sons, including Judas and his brothers.
Matthew 1:3 Judas had Phares and Zara with Thamar; Phares had Esrom; and Esrom had Aram.
Matthew 1:4 Aram was the father of Aminadab; Aminadab was the father of Naasson; Naasson was the father of Salmon.
Matthew 1:5 Salmon fathered Boaz with Rahab; Boaz fathered Obed with Ruth; and Obed fathered Jesse.
Matthew 1:6 Jesse was the father of King David; and King David was the father of Solomon, whose mother had been Uriah's wife.
Matthew 1:7 Solomon had a son named Rehoboam; Rehoboam had a son named Abijah; and Abijah had a son named Asa.
Matthew 1:8 Asa fathered Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat fathered Joram; and Joram fathered Uzziah.
Matthew 1:9 Ozias was the father of Joatham, Joatham was the father of Achaz, and Achaz was the father of Ezekias.
Matthew 1:10 Hezekiah fathered Manasseh; Manasseh fathered Amon; and Amon fathered Josiah.
Matthew 1:11 Josias was the father of Jechonias and his brothers around the time they were taken to Babylon.
Matthew 1:12 After they were taken to Babylon, Jechonias became the father of Salathiel, and Salathiel became the father of Zorobabel.
Matthew 1:13 Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud; Abiud was the father of Eliakim; and Eliakim was the father of Azor.
Matthew 1:14 Azor was the father of Sadoc; Sadoc was the father of Achim; and Achim was the father of Eliud.
Matthew 1:15 Eliud was the father of Eleazar, Eleazar was the father of Matthan, and Matthan was the father of Jacob.
Matthew 1:16 Jacob was the father of Joseph, who was married to Mary. Mary gave birth to Jesus, also known as Christ.
Matthew 1:17 There are fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen generations from David to the time they were taken to Babylon, and fourteen generations from then to Christ.
Matthew 1:18 The birth of Jesus Christ happened like this: Before Mary, his mother, and Joseph were together as husband and wife, she was discovered to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Matthew 1:19 Joseph, her husband, was a good man and did not want to embarrass her publicly, so he planned to break up with her quietly.
Matthew 1:20 As he was thinking about all this, an angel from God came to him in a dream and said, "Joseph, descendant of David, do not be afraid to make Mary your wife because the baby in her is from the Holy Spirit."
Matthew 1:21 She will have a son, and you will name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.
Matthew 1:22 All this happened to make true what the prophet had said from God.
Matthew 1:23 Look, a young woman will have a baby, and she will give birth to a son. They will name him Emmanuel, which means God with us.
Matthew 1:24 Joseph woke up, did what God's angel told him to, and took Mary as his wife.
Matthew 1:25 He did not have marital relations with her until she gave birth to her first son; and he named him Jesus.

Matthew 2:1 When Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judah during King Herod's time, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem.
Matthew 2:2 Asking, "Where is the newborn king of the Jews? We saw his star rise and have come to honor him."
Matthew 2:3 When King Herod heard this, he and all of Jerusalem were worried.
Matthew 2:4 When he called all the main priests and teachers of the law, he asked them where Christ was to be born.
Matthew 2:5 They said to him, "In Bethlehem of Judea, because the prophet wrote it like this."
Matthew 2:6 You, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are not the least among the rulers of Judah: because from you will come a leader who will govern my people Israel.
Matthew 2:7 Then Herod secretly met with the wise men and carefully asked them when the star had appeared.
Matthew 2:8 He sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go, look carefully for the child; and when you find him, let me know, so I can come and honor him too."
Matthew 2:9 After listening to the king, they left, and the star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
Matthew 2:10 When they saw the star, they were very happy.
Matthew 2:11 When they entered the house, they saw the young child with his mother Mary, and they knelt down and worshiped him. After opening their treasures, they gave him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Matthew 2:12 God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they went home a different way.
Matthew 2:13 After they left, an angel of God came to Joseph in a dream. The angel said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you to come back, because Herod is going to look for the child to kill him."
Matthew 2:14 He got up, took the child and his mother at night, and left for Egypt.
Matthew 2:15 They stayed there until Herod died. This fulfilled what God had told the prophet: "I called my son out of Egypt."
Matthew 2:16 Then Herod, when he realized the wise men had tricked him, became very angry. He ordered his soldiers to kill all the boys two years old and younger in Bethlehem and the surrounding areas, based on the information he had gotten from the wise men.
Matthew 2:17 Then what the prophet Jeremiah had said came true:
Matthew 2:18 In Rama, a voice was heard, crying, tears, and deep sadness, Rachel cried for her children and couldn't be comforted, because they were gone.
Matthew 2:19 When Herod died, an angel of God appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
Matthew 2:20 Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to Israel because those who wanted to kill the child are dead.
Matthew 2:21 He got up, took the child and his mother, and went to the land of Israel.
Matthew 2:22 But when he heard that Archelaus became king in Judea after his father Herod, he was scared to go there. However, after God warned him in a dream, he went to Galilee instead.
Matthew 2:23 He came and lived in a city named Nazareth so that what the prophets said would come true: He will be called a Nazarene.

Matthew 3:1 In those days, John the Baptist came, teaching in the desert of Judea.
Matthew 3:2 Say you're sorry, because God's kingdom is very near.
Matthew 3:3 This is the one the prophet Isaiah talked about when he said, "A voice calls out in the desert, 'Get the road ready for God, make a straight path for him.'"
Matthew 3:4 John wore clothes made of camel hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
Matthew 3:5 People from Jerusalem, all of Judea, and the area around the Jordan River went to see him.
Matthew 3:6 They were baptized by him in the Jordan River, admitting their sins.
Matthew 3:7 When he saw many Pharisees and Sadducees at his baptism, he said to them, "You brood of snakes, who warned you to escape the coming anger?"
Matthew 3:8 Produce actions that show you have changed for the better.
Matthew 3:9 Don't think to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' I tell you, God can make children for Abraham from these stones.
Matthew 3:10 The axe is now at the tree roots; so any tree that doesn't grow good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
Matthew 3:11 I baptize you with water to show you have changed your heart and life. But the one who comes after me is stronger than I am. I'm not good enough to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
Matthew 3:12 He holds a winnowing fork to clean his threshing area and gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn the chaff with a fire that cannot be put out.
Matthew 3:13 Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan River to be baptized by John.
Matthew 3:14 John stopped him, saying, "I should be baptized by you, and yet you come to me?"
Matthew 3:15 Jesus replied, "Let it happen now; this is how we do what is right." Then he allowed it.
Matthew 3:16 When Jesus was baptized and came up from the water, the sky opened to him, and he saw God's Spirit come down like a dove and land on him.
Matthew 3:17 A voice from heaven said, "This is my dear Son, who makes me very happy."

Matthew 4:1 Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the desert to be tempted by the devil.
Matthew 4:2 After he fasted for forty days and nights, he felt hungry.
Matthew 4:3 When the tempter came to him, he said, "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
Matthew 4:4 He replied, "It is said, 'A person doesn't live only by eating bread, but by all words that come from God.'"
Matthew 4:5 Then the devil took him to the holy city and put him on the highest point of the temple.
Matthew 4:6 He said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. It is said, 'God will command His angels to take care of you. They will lift you up in their hands, so you won't hit your foot on a stone.'"
Matthew 4:7 Jesus told him, "It's also written, 'Don't test God.'"
Matthew 4:8 Once more, the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the world's kingdoms and their splendor.
Matthew 4:9 He says to him, "I will give you all these things if you bow down and worship me."
Matthew 4:10 Jesus said to him, "Go away, Satan: because it is written, You should worship God your God, and only serve him."
Matthew 4:11 Then the devil left him, and look, angels came and helped him.
Matthew 4:12 When Jesus learned that John was put in jail, he went to Galilee.
Matthew 4:13 Leaving Nazareth, he went and lived in Capernaum by the sea, in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Matthew 4:14 This was to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah had said:
Matthew 4:15 The land of Zabulon and the land of Naphtali, near the sea, across the Jordan River, Galilee where the non-Jews live;
Matthew 4:16 The people sitting in darkness have seen a great light, and those sitting in the area and shadow of death have had light shine on them.
Matthew 4:17 From then on, Jesus started to preach, saying, "Change your ways, for heaven's kingdom is near."
Matthew 4:18 Jesus, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Simon called Peter, and his brother Andrew, throwing a net into the sea because they were fishermen.
Matthew 4:19 He said to them, "Follow me, and I will teach you to bring people to me."
Matthew 4:20 They immediately left their nets and followed him.
Matthew 4:21 Moving on from there, he saw two other brothers, James and John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, fixing their nets. He called to them.
Matthew 4:22 They quickly left the boat and their dad, and followed him.
Matthew 4:23 Jesus traveled throughout Galilee, teaching in their places of worship, sharing the good news of the kingdom, and curing every kind of illness and disease among the people.
Matthew 4:24 His fame spread all over Syria: and they brought to him all the sick with various diseases and pains, those with evil spirits, those who were insane, and those who were paralyzed; and he healed them.
Matthew 4:25 Many people followed him from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the area across the Jordan River.

Matthew 5:1 Seeing the crowds, he went up on a mountain. When he sat down, his disciples came to him.
Matthew 5:2 He opened his mouth and began to teach them, saying,
Matthew 5:3 Happy are those who know they are spiritually needy, because the kingdom of heaven belongs to them.
Matthew 5:4 Happy are those who are sad, for they will be comforted.
Matthew 5:5 Happy are the gentle, for they will receive the earth as their own.
Matthew 5:6 Happy are those who really want to do what is right, because they will be satisfied.
Matthew 5:7 Happy are those who show mercy: they will be shown mercy.
Matthew 5:8 Happy are those who have clean hearts, because they will see God.
Matthew 5:9 Happy are those who make peace: because they will be known as God's children.
Matthew 5:10 Happy are those who are treated badly for doing right: heaven belongs to them.
Matthew 5:11 You are blessed when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me.
Matthew 5:12 Be happy and very glad, because you have a big reward in heaven. This is how they treated the prophets who were before you.
Matthew 5:13 You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its flavor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and walked on by people.
Matthew 5:14 You are the world's light. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
Matthew 5:15 People don't light a candle and hide it under a bowl; they put it on a stand, and it shines for everyone in the house.
Matthew 5:16 Let your light shine before others, so they can see your good deeds and praise your Father in heaven.
Matthew 5:17 Don't think that I have come to get rid of the law or the prophets; I haven't come to get rid of them but to complete them.
Matthew 5:18 I tell you the truth, until heaven and earth disappear, not the smallest detail of the law will change until everything is accomplished.
Matthew 5:19 Anyone who breaks even the smallest command and teaches others to do so will be least in heaven, but whoever follows and teaches the commands will be called great in heaven.
Matthew 5:20 I tell you, unless your goodness is greater than that of the teachers of the law and the Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Matthew 5:21 You have heard that long ago people were told, 'Do not kill,' and anyone who kills will face judgment.
Matthew 5:22 I tell you, if anyone is angry with their brother for no reason, they are at risk of being judged. If anyone calls their brother 'worthless', they are at risk of the authorities' anger. But if anyone calls their brother a fool, they are at risk of going to hell.
Matthew 5:23 If you bring your gift to the altar and then remember that your brother has something against you;
Matthew 5:24 Leave your gift in front of the altar and go; first make peace with your brother, and then come and give your gift.
Matthew 5:25 Make peace with your enemy quickly while you're still together before they take you to court, and the court hands you over to the guard, and you get put in jail.
Matthew 5:26 Truly I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last penny.
Matthew 5:27 You have heard that long ago people were told, "Do not cheat on your partner."
Matthew 5:28 I tell you, anyone who looks at a woman with desire has already been unfaithful to her in his heart.
Matthew 5:29 If your right eye causes you to sin, take it out and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into hell.
Matthew 5:30 If your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away, because it is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into hell.
Matthew 5:31 It has been said, if someone wants to divorce his wife, he should give her a divorce paper.
Matthew 5:32 I tell you, if anyone divorces his wife, except for marital unfaithfulness, he makes her commit adultery; and anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Matthew 5:33 You have heard people long ago say, "Do not break your promises, but do what you have vowed to God to do."
Matthew 5:34 I tell you, don't swear at all; not by heaven, because it's God's throne.
Matthew 5:35 Do not swear by the earth, for it is God's footrest; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Matthew 5:36 Do not promise by your head, because you cannot turn one hair white or black.
Matthew 5:37 Let your words be 'Yes, yes' or 'No, no'; anything more than this comes from evil.
Matthew 5:38 You have heard it said, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.
Matthew 5:39 I tell you, don't fight against someone who does you harm. If someone hits you on your right cheek, offer them the other one too.
Matthew 5:40 If someone takes you to court to take your coat, give them your cloak too.
Matthew 5:41 If someone makes you go one mile, go two miles with them.
Matthew 5:42 Give to the person who asks you, and do not turn away from the person who wants to borrow from you.
Matthew 5:43 You have heard it was said, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
Matthew 5:44 I tell you, love your enemies, be kind to those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat and persecute you.
Matthew 5:45 So you may be the children of your Father in heaven: for he makes the sun rise on the wicked and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
Matthew 5:46 If you only love those who love you, what good is that? Even tax collectors do that, don't they?
Matthew 5:47 If you greet only your friends, what makes you different? Don't even tax collectors do that?
Matthew 5:48 Be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.

Matthew 6:1 Be careful not to do good things in front of others just to be noticed, because if you do, you won't get any reward from your Father in heaven.
Matthew 6:2 When you give to the needy, don't announce it loudly like hypocrites in the synagogues and streets for attention. Truly, they've received their reward.
Matthew 6:3 When you give to those in need, don't let one hand know what the other is doing.
Matthew 6:4 Give your help to others quietly, and God, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you openly.
Matthew 6:5 When you pray, don't be like the fakers who like to pray in public places just to be seen by others. Truly, they have gotten all they will get.
Matthew 6:6 When you pray, go into your room and close the door, then pray to your Father who is unseen; and your Father, who sees what's done in secret, will reward you.
Matthew 6:7 When you pray, don't keep on repeating words with no meaning, like other people do. They believe they will be heard because they talk a lot.
Matthew 6:8 Do not be like them, because your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
Matthew 6:9 Pray like this: Our Father in heaven, may your name be honored.
Matthew 6:10 Let your kingdom come, let your will be done on earth, just like it is in heaven.
Matthew 6:11 Give us today the food we need.
Matthew 6:12 Forgive us what we owe, as we forgive those who owe us.
Matthew 6:13 Do not let us be tempted, but save us from evil: for the kingdom, the power, and the glory are yours, forever. Amen.
Matthew 6:14 If you forgive people for what they've done wrong, God in heaven will forgive you too.
Matthew 6:15 If you don't forgive others for their wrongs, God won't forgive your wrongs either.
Matthew 6:16 When you fast, don't be like the fakes who look sad to show others they are fasting. Truly, that's the only reward they will get.
Matthew 6:17 When you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face.
Matthew 6:18 Do not show others that you are fasting; only God, who is unseen, should know. And God, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
Matthew 6:19 Do not store up treasures for yourself on earth, where moths and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
Matthew 6:20 Store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moths and rust cannot destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.
Matthew 6:21 Where you keep your treasure is where your heart will be too.
Matthew 6:22 Your eye is like a lamp for your body. If your eye is clear, your whole body will be bright.
Matthew 6:23 But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If the light inside you is dark, how deep is that darkness!
Matthew 6:24 A person can't serve two bosses: they will either hate one and love the other, or be loyal to one and not like the other. You can't serve God and money.
Matthew 6:25 So I tell you, don't worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Isn't life more than food and the body more than clothes?
Matthew 6:26 Look at the birds of the sky: they don't plant seeds, harvest, or store food in barns, but God feeds them. Aren't you worth more than they are?
Matthew 6:27 Who of you can add an inch to your height by worrying?
Matthew 6:28 Why worry about clothes? Look at the field lilies; they don't work or make cloth.
Matthew 6:29 I tell you, even Solomon in all his splendor was not dressed as beautifully as one of these.
Matthew 6:30 So, if God dresses the grass in the field, which is here today and thrown into the fire tomorrow, won't he dress you even more, you with little faith?
Matthew 6:31 So don't worry, asking, 'What will we eat?' or 'What will we drink?' or 'What will we wear?'
Matthew 6:32 The non-believers chase after all these things, but your Father in heaven knows you need them.
Matthew 6:33 First, look for God's kingdom and do what is right; then, all these things will be given to you.
Matthew 6:34 Do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.

Matthew 7:1 Do not judge others, so you will not be judged.
Matthew 7:2 The way you judge others is how you will be judged, and the amount you give to others will be the amount you get back.
Matthew 7:3 Why do you see the small speck in your brother's eye but not notice the big plank in your own eye?
Matthew 7:4 How can you tell your brother, 'Let me remove the speck from your eye,' when you have a log in your own eye?
Matthew 7:5 You are two-faced. First, take the large piece of wood out of your own eye; then you will see well enough to remove the small speck from your brother's eye.
Matthew 7:6 Don't give holy things to dogs or throw your pearls to pigs, in case they step on them and then attack you.
Matthew 7:7 Ask, and you will receive; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
Matthew 7:8 Everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
Matthew 7:9 Which of you, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
Matthew 7:10 If he asks for a fish, will he get a snake?
Matthew 7:11 If you, even though you are not perfect, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him?
Matthew 7:12 Do to others what you want them to do to you; this is what the rules and the teachings of the prophets mean.
Matthew 7:13 Go in through the narrow gate. The gate is wide and the road is broad that leads to ruin, and many people choose that way.
Matthew 7:14 The gate is tight and the path is narrow that leads to life, and only a few find it.
Matthew 7:15 Be careful of fake prophets who look innocent like sheep but are really hungry wolves inside.
Matthew 7:16 You will recognize them by what they produce. Do people pick grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
Matthew 7:17 Just as a good tree produces good fruit, a bad tree produces bad fruit.
Matthew 7:18 A good tree can't produce bad fruit, and a bad tree can't produce good fruit.
Matthew 7:19 Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
Matthew 7:20 You will know them by their actions.
Matthew 7:21 Not everyone who calls to me, 'God, God,' will enter the kingdom of heaven; only the one who does what my Father in heaven wants.
Matthew 7:22 On that day, many will say to me, "Master, Master, didn't we speak of the future in your name, drive out demons in your name, and do many great things in your name?"
Matthew 7:23 Then I will tell them, I never knew you: go away from me, you who do wrong.
Matthew 7:24 So anyone who listens to my words and follows them will be like a smart person who built their house on solid rock.
Matthew 7:25 The rain fell, the rivers rose, the winds blew, and hit that house; but it didn't fall because it was built on a rock.
Matthew 7:26 Everyone who hears my words and doesn't follow them will be like a foolish person who built their house on sand.
Matthew 7:27 The rain fell, the floods came, the winds blew, and hit that house; and it collapsed: and the collapse was big.
Matthew 7:28 After Jesus finished speaking, the people were amazed at his teaching.
Matthew 7:29 He taught them like someone with authority, not like the scribes.

Matthew 8:1 When he came down from the mountain, many people followed him.
Matthew 8:2 Look, a man with leprosy came and knelt before him, saying, "Sir, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Matthew 8:3 Jesus reached out his hand, touched him, and said, "I am willing; be clean." Right away, his leprosy was healed.
Matthew 8:4 Jesus said to him, "Don't tell anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest, and give the offering Moses told you to, as evidence to them."
Matthew 8:5 When Jesus entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking for help.
Matthew 8:6 He said, "Master, my servant is at home suffering badly from paralysis."
Matthew 8:7 Jesus said to him, I will come and heal him.
Matthew 8:8 The officer replied, "Sir, I am not good enough for you to come into my house. But just say the command, and my servant will get better."
Matthew 8:9 I am a man with authority, with soldiers following me. When I tell one to go, he goes; tell another to come, he comes; and when I tell my servant to do something, he does it.
Matthew 8:10 When Jesus heard this, he was amazed and said to those following him, "Truly, I tell you, I haven't found such strong faith in anyone, even in Israel."
Matthew 8:11 I tell you that many will come from the east and west and will eat with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in heaven's kingdom.
Matthew 8:12 The children of the kingdom will be thrown into deep darkness; there will be crying and grinding of teeth.
Matthew 8:13 Jesus told the centurion, "Go on; just as you believed, it will happen." And his servant was healed that very hour.
Matthew 8:14 When Jesus entered Peter's home, he saw that Peter's mother-in-law was in bed with a fever.
Matthew 8:15 He touched her hand, the fever went away, and she got up and helped them.
Matthew 8:16 When evening came, they brought to him many people who had demons. He drove out the spirits with his command and healed all who were sick.
Matthew 8:17 This happened so the words the prophet Isaiah said would come true: He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases.
Matthew 8:18 When Jesus saw many people around him, he told them to go to the other side.
Matthew 8:19 A teacher of the law came and said to him, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
Matthew 8:20 Jesus said to him, "Foxes have holes, and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to rest his head."
Matthew 8:21 One of his followers said to him, "Teacher, let me go first and bury my father."
Matthew 8:22 Jesus said to him, "Follow me, and let those who are dead bury their own dead."
Matthew 8:23 When he got into a boat, his followers went with him.
Matthew 8:24 Suddenly, a huge storm came up on the sea, so that the waves swept over the boat, but he was sleeping.
Matthew 8:25 His followers came to him, woke him up, and said, "Master, save us: we are dying."
Matthew 8:26 He said to them, "Why are you scared, you with little trust?" Then he got up, scolded the winds and the sea, and everything became very calm.
Matthew 8:27 The men were amazed and said, "Who is this man that even the winds and the sea listen to him?"
Matthew 8:28 When he arrived on the other side in the Gergesenes area, two people with evil spirits, coming from the graves and very violent, met him, so nobody could go that way.
Matthew 8:29 Look, they shouted, "What do you want with us, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to punish us before the time?"
Matthew 8:30 Far from them, there was a large group of pigs eating.
Matthew 8:31 The demons begged him, saying, "If you make us leave, let us go into the pigs."
Matthew 8:32 He said to them, "Go." So they came out and entered the pigs. Then all the pigs rushed down the steep hill into the sea and died in the water.
Matthew 8:33 The people watching them ran away, went into the city, and told everything, including what happened to the demon-possessed man.
Matthew 8:34 Look, everyone from the city came to see Jesus; and when they saw him, they asked him to leave their area.

Matthew 9:1 He got into a boat, crossed over, and arrived at his own city.
Matthew 9:2 Look, they brought to Jesus a man with paralysis, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralyzed man, "Young man, cheer up; your sins are forgiven."
Matthew 9:3 Some teachers of the law thought to themselves, "This man is speaking against God."
Matthew 9:4 Jesus, aware of their thoughts, asked, "Why do you think evil in your hearts?"
Matthew 9:5 Which is simpler: to say 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say 'Get up and walk'?
Matthew 9:6 I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, so he said to the man with paralysis, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home."
Matthew 9:7 He got up and went to his home.
Matthew 9:8 When the crowds saw this, they were amazed and praised God for giving such power to people.
Matthew 9:9 As Jesus left that place, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax office. He said to him, "Follow me." Matthew got up and followed him.
Matthew 9:10 As Jesus was eating in the house, many tax collectors and wrongdoers came and ate with him and his followers.
Matthew 9:11 When the Pharisees saw this, they asked his disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
Matthew 9:12 When Jesus heard this, he said to them, "Healthy people don't need a doctor, but sick people do."
Matthew 9:13 Go and understand this: I desire kindness, not offerings. I came not to call the good people, but sinners to turn away from their sins.
Matthew 9:14 John's followers came to Jesus and asked, "Why do we and the Pharisees often fast, but your disciples do not fast?"
Matthew 9:15 Jesus asked them, "Can wedding guests be sad while the groom is with them? But a time will come when the groom will be taken away, and then they will fast."
Matthew 9:16 No one sews a piece of new fabric onto an old clothing because the patch will pull away from it, making the tear worse.
Matthew 9:17 People don't put new wine into old containers; otherwise, the containers will break, the wine will spill, and the containers will be ruined. Instead, they put new wine into new containers, and both stay good.
Matthew 9:18 While he was speaking to them, look, a leader came and bowed down to him, saying, "My daughter has just died. But if you come and put your hand on her, she will live."
Matthew 9:19 Jesus got up, followed him, and his disciples did too.
Matthew 9:20 Look, a woman who had been sick with bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the edge of his clothes.
Matthew 9:21 She thought, "If I can just touch his clothes, I will be healed."
Matthew 9:22 Jesus turned around, and when he saw her, he said, "Daughter, be encouraged; your faith has healed you." And from that moment, the woman was healed.
Matthew 9:23 When Jesus entered the leader's home and saw the musicians and the noisy crowd,
Matthew 9:24 He told them, "Move aside: the girl is not dead, but sleeping." And they laughed at him.
Matthew 9:25 After the crowd was sent outside, he went in, took her hand, and the girl got up.
Matthew 9:26 News of this spread throughout the entire area.
Matthew 9:27 When Jesus left that place, two blind men followed him, calling out, "Son of David, have mercy on us."
Matthew 9:28 When he entered the house, the blind men approached him, and Jesus asked them, "Do you believe I can do this?" They answered, "Yes, Lord."
Matthew 9:29 He touched their eyes and said, "Let it happen for you as you believe."
Matthew 9:30 Their eyes were opened, and Jesus firmly told them, "Make sure no one finds out about this."
Matthew 9:31 After they left, they told everyone about him everywhere in that area.
Matthew 9:32 As they left, they brought to Jesus a man who could not speak because he had a demon.
Matthew 9:33 When the devil was driven away, the person who could not talk spoke, and the crowds were amazed, saying, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel."
Matthew 9:34 The Pharisees said, He drives out evil spirits using the ruler of the evil spirits.
Matthew 9:35 Jesus traveled through all the cities and villages, teaching in their places of worship, spreading the good news of the kingdom, and curing every illness and disease among the people.
Matthew 9:36 When he saw the crowds, he felt sorry for them because they were weak and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.
Matthew 9:37 He said to his students, "There really is a lot of crop, but there are not many workers."
Matthew 9:38 Ask God, who takes care of the harvest, to send workers for gathering it.

Matthew 10:1 When he gathered his twelve followers, he gave them authority over evil spirits, to drive them out, and to cure every kind of illness and disease.
Matthew 10:2 The twelve apostles' names are: The first is Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James, Zebedee's son, and his brother John.
Matthew 10:3 Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, also called Thaddaeus.
Matthew 10:4 Simon from Canaan, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.
Matthew 10:5 Jesus sent out these twelve and told them, "Do not go to the Gentile areas or enter any Samaritan city.
Matthew 10:6 Go instead to the lost sheep of Israel's family.
Matthew 10:7 As you go, tell others, "God's kingdom is near."
Matthew 10:8 Cure sick people, make lepers clean, bring dead back to life, throw out demons: you got it for free, give it for free.
Matthew 10:9 Don't carry gold, silver, or coins in your wallets.
Matthew 10:10 Don't take a bag for your trip, or two coats, or shoes, or a walking stick: because a worker deserves his food.
Matthew 10:11 When you enter a city or town, find out who is good there and stay with them until you leave.
Matthew 10:12 When you enter a house, greet it.
Matthew 10:13 If the home is good, let your peace rest on it; if not, let your peace come back to you.
Matthew 10:14 If anyone does not welcome you or listen to your words, leave that home or town and shake the dust from your feet.
Matthew 10:15 I truly tell you, on Judgment Day, the land of Sodom and Gomorrah will have an easier time than that city.
Matthew 10:16 I send you out like sheep among wolves: so be as smart as snakes and as kind as doves.
Matthew 10:17 Be careful of people: they will hand you over to councils and whip you in their places of worship.
Matthew 10:18 You will stand before rulers and kings because of me, to witness to them and the nations.
Matthew 10:19 When they arrest you, don't worry about what to say, because you will be told what to say at that time.
Matthew 10:20 It's not you speaking, but your Father's Spirit speaking through you.
Matthew 10:21 A brother will turn in his brother to be killed, and a father will turn in his child. Children will rebel against their parents and have them killed.
Matthew 10:22 Everyone will hate you because of me, but if you keep going to the end, you will be saved.
Matthew 10:23 If people chase you away from one town, run to another. Truly, I tell you, you won't finish visiting the towns of Israel before the Son of Man arrives.
Matthew 10:24 A student is not greater than their teacher, nor is a servant greater than their master.
Matthew 10:25 A student should be like their teacher, and a servant like their boss. If people have called the head of the house Beelzebub, they will call the others in the house even worse names.
Matthew 10:26 Do not be afraid of them: because nothing is hidden that will not be shown; and nothing is secret that will not become known.
Matthew 10:27 What I say to you in secret, you must say in public; and what you hear whispered, you must announce from the rooftops.
Matthew 10:28 Do not be afraid of those who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, be afraid of God who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
Matthew 10:29 Aren't two sparrows sold for a small coin? And none of them will fall to the ground without God knowing.
Matthew 10:30 Every hair on your head is counted.
Matthew 10:31 Do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Matthew 10:32 If anyone tells others about me, I will tell my Father in heaven about them.
Matthew 10:33 Whoever denies me before others, I will also deny them before my God in heaven.
Matthew 10:34 Don't think that I came to bring peace on earth: I didn't come to bring peace, but to bring a sword.
Matthew 10:35 I have come to cause disagreement between a man and his father, between a daughter and her mother, and between a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law.
Matthew 10:36 A person's enemies will be the members of their own family.
Matthew 10:37 If you love your father or mother more than you love me, you are not good enough to be my follower. And if you love your son or daughter more than me, you are not good enough to be my follower.
Matthew 10:38 Anyone who does not take up their cross and follow me is not good enough for me.
Matthew 10:39 Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for me will find it.
Matthew 10:40 Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
Matthew 10:41 If you welcome a prophet because he is a prophet, you will get the same reward as a prophet; and if you welcome a good person because he is good, you will get the same reward as a good person.
Matthew 10:42 Anyone who gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because they are my follower will truly not lose their reward.

Matthew 11:1 When Jesus finished giving instructions to his twelve disciples, he left to teach and spread his message in their towns.
Matthew 11:2 When John, who was in prison, heard about what Christ was doing, he sent two of his followers.
Matthew 11:3 He asked him, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect someone else?"
Matthew 11:4 Jesus replied, "Go tell John what you hear and see."
Matthew 11:5 Blind people can see, and those who can't walk, now do. People with leprosy are healed, and the deaf can hear. The dead are brought back to life, and the poor hear the good news.
Matthew 11:6 Happy is anyone who is not upset because of me.
Matthew 11:7 As they left, Jesus spoke to the crowds about John, asking, "Why did you go out into the desert? To see a reed swayed by the wind?"
Matthew 11:8 What did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear fine clothes live in king's palaces.
Matthew 11:9 But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and even more than a prophet.
Matthew 11:10 This is the one about whom it was written, 'Look, I will send my messenger ahead of you, who will make your path ready for you.'
Matthew 11:11 Truly, I tell you, no one born of a woman is greater than John the Baptist; but even the least in heaven's kingdom is greater than he.
Matthew 11:12 Since John the Baptist's time until now, God's kingdom has faced harshness, and forceful people are trying to seize it.
Matthew 11:13 All the prophets and the law told of what would happen up to the time of John.
Matthew 11:14 If you accept this, he is Elijah who was to come.
Matthew 11:15 If you have ears to listen, then listen.
Matthew 11:16 What can I compare this generation to? They are like children sitting in the marketplaces, calling to their friends.
Matthew 11:17 We played music for you, but you did not dance; we were sad for you, but you did not cry.
Matthew 11:18 John did not come eating or drinking, and they say he has a demon.
Matthew 11:19 The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and people say, 'Look, a man who eats too much and drinks too much wine, a friend of tax collectors and wrongdoers.' But smart actions prove right by their results.
Matthew 11:20 He started to scold the cities where he had done many miracles because they did not repent.
Matthew 11:21 How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the powerful things done in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned from their sins long ago, showing sorrow with rough cloth and ashes.
Matthew 11:22 I tell you, it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon on the judgment day than for you.
Matthew 11:23 Capernaum, you are raised up to the sky, but you will be sent down to the underworld. If the powerful acts done in you had happened in Sodom, it would still exist today.
Matthew 11:24 I tell you, it will be easier for Sodom on judgment day than for you.
Matthew 11:25 At that time, Jesus spoke and said, "I thank you, Father, God of heaven and earth, because you have kept these things from the smart and careful people, and have shown them to children."
Matthew 11:26 Even so, Father, because this is what you wanted.
Matthew 11:27 My Father has given me all things: no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to show him.
Matthew 11:28 Come to me, all who work hard and are burdened, and I will give you rest.
Matthew 11:29 Wear my yoke and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart: and you will find rest for your souls.
Matthew 11:30 My yoke is simple, and my load is not heavy.

Matthew 12:1 One Sabbath, Jesus walked through the grain fields, and his hungry disciples started to pick and eat some heads of grain.
Matthew 12:2 When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, "Look, your disciples are doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath day."
Matthew 12:3 But he said to them, "Haven't you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
Matthew 12:4 He went into God's house and ate the bread that only priests should eat, which was against the law for him and his companions.
Matthew 12:5 Have you not read in the law that on Sabbath days the priests in the temple break the Sabbath rules, yet are not guilty?
Matthew 12:6 I tell you, someone greater than the temple is here.
Matthew 12:7 If you knew what it means 'I want kindness, not offerings,' you wouldn't have judged innocent people.
Matthew 12:8 The Son of man is master even of the Sabbath day.
Matthew 12:9 After he left that place, he went into their place of worship.
Matthew 12:10 Look, there was a man with a crippled hand. They asked, "Is it okay to heal on the Sabbath?" so they could blame him.
Matthew 12:11 He asked them, "Who among you, if you have one sheep and it falls into a hole on the Sabbath, wouldn't grab it and pull it out?"
Matthew 12:12 How much more valuable is a person than a sheep? So, it is right to do good on the Sabbath.
Matthew 12:13 Then he said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and it was healed and became as healthy as the other one.
Matthew 12:14 Then the Pharisees left and planned together how to kill Jesus.
Matthew 12:15 When Jesus realized this, he left that place. Many people followed him, and he healed everyone.
Matthew 12:16 He ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
Matthew 12:17 This happened to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah had said:
Matthew 12:18 Look at my servant, whom I have picked; my loved one, who pleases me so much. I will give him my spirit, and he will bring fairness to all nations.
Matthew 12:19 He will not argue or shout; no one will hear his voice in the streets.
Matthew 12:20 He will not break a bent reed or put out a weak flame until he leads justice to victory.
Matthew 12:21 People from other nations will trust in his name.
Matthew 12:22 Someone controlled by a demon, who could not see or speak, was brought to Jesus, and he cured him so that he could both talk and see.
Matthew 12:23 Everyone was amazed and asked, "Isn't this David's son?"
Matthew 12:24 When the Pharisees heard this, they said, "This man doesn't drive out demons except by Beelzebub, the ruler of demons."
Matthew 12:25 Jesus knew what they were thinking and told them, "A kingdom that fights itself will be ruined; and a city or home that is split will not last."
Matthew 12:26 If Satan drives out Satan, he is fighting against himself; how can his kingdom last?
Matthew 12:27 If I drive out demons using Beelzebub, who do your own people use to drive them out? They will be the ones to judge you.
Matthew 12:28 If I drive out demons with God's Spirit, then God's kingdom has come to you.
Matthew 12:29 How can someone get into a strong man's house and take his stuff unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can rob his house.
Matthew 12:30 If you're not with me, you're against me; if you don't gather with me, you spread things out.
Matthew 12:31 So I tell you, people will be forgiven for all kinds of sins and insults, but insults against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
Matthew 12:32 Anyone who speaks against the Son of man can be forgiven, but anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either now or in the future.
Matthew 12:33 Make the tree good and its fruit will be good, or make the tree bad and its fruit will be bad, because a tree is recognized by its fruit.
Matthew 12:34 You people are like snakes! How can you say good things when you are evil? What fills the heart will come out of the mouth.
Matthew 12:35 A good person, from the good stored in their heart, produces good things; and a bad person, from the bad stored within, produces bad things.
Matthew 12:36 I tell you, everyone must explain all the useless words they speak on judgment day.
Matthew 12:37 What you say can save or condemn you.
Matthew 12:38 Some teachers of the law and Pharisees spoke up, saying, "Teacher, we want to see a miracle from you."
Matthew 12:39 He replied, "A wicked and unfaithful generation wants a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah."
Matthew 12:40 Just as Jonah was in the fish for three days and three nights, the Son of Man will be in the earth for three days and three nights.
Matthew 12:41 The people of Nineveh will stand up at the time of judgment with the people of this time and condemn them: because they turned away from their sins when Jonah preached; and look, someone greater than Jonah is here.
Matthew 12:42 The queen from the south will stand up on judgment day with the people of this time, and she will judge them. She traveled from the farthest part of the earth to listen to Solomon's wisdom; but look, someone greater than Solomon is here.
Matthew 12:43 When an evil spirit leaves a person, it wanders through waterless areas looking for rest but doesn't find any.
Matthew 12:44 Then he says, "I will go back to my house from where I left"; and when he arrives, he finds it empty, clean, and tidy.
Matthew 12:45 Then he goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they come in and live there. So the last condition of that person is worse than at the beginning. This will also happen to this evil generation.
Matthew 12:46 While he was still talking to the people, look, his mother and brothers were standing outside, wanting to talk to him.
Matthew 12:47 Someone told him, "Look, your mother and brothers are outside wanting to talk to you."
Matthew 12:48 He replied to the person who spoke to him, "Who is my mother? And who are my brothers?"
Matthew 12:49 He reached out his hand to his followers and said, "Look, my mother and my brothers!"
Matthew 12:50 Anyone who does what my Father in heaven wants is my brother, sister, and mother.

Matthew 13:1 That day, Jesus left the house and sat by the sea.
Matthew 13:2 Large crowds gathered to him, so he got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the beach.
Matthew 13:3 He told them many stories with hidden meanings, saying, "Look, a farmer went out to plant seeds.
Matthew 13:4 As he was planting, some seeds fell by the path, and the birds came and ate them.
Matthew 13:5 Some seeds fell on rocky ground where there wasn't much soil. They quickly grew because the soil wasn't deep.
Matthew 13:6 When the sun rose, they got burned up and since they had no roots, they dried out.
