Matthew 13:7 Some seeds fell among thorns, and the thorns grew and choked them.
Matthew 13:8 Some seeds fell on good soil and produced crops: some 100 times more, some 60 times more, and some 30 times more.
Matthew 13:9 Anyone who has ears to listen should listen.
Matthew 13:10 The disciples came and asked him, "Why do you talk to the people using stories with hidden meanings?"
Matthew 13:11 He replied, "You are allowed to understand the secrets of heaven's kingdom, but others are not."
Matthew 13:12 Whoever has will get more and have plenty, but whoever does not have will lose even what they have.
Matthew 13:13 So I tell them stories because they look but don't really see, and they listen but don't truly hear or understand.
Matthew 13:14 In them, the prediction of Isaiah comes true, which says, "You will hear but not understand; you will see but not recognize."
Matthew 13:15 This people’s heart has grown hard, their ears can barely hear, and they have shut their eyes; otherwise, they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, turn back, and be healed by me.
Matthew 13:16 Your eyes are blessed because they see, and your ears are blessed because they hear.
Matthew 13:17 Truly, I tell you, many prophets and good people wanted to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
Matthew 13:18 Listen to the story of the farmer who plants seeds.
Matthew 13:19 When someone hears about God's kingdom but doesn't understand it, the evil one comes and takes away what was planted in their heart. This is like the seed that falls on the path.
Matthew 13:20 But the one who gets the seed on rocky ground is the person who hears the message and immediately receives it with happiness.
Matthew 13:21 He doesn't have a deep root inside, but lasts only a short time. When trouble or harassment comes because of the message, he quickly gets upset.
Matthew 13:22 The person who received the seed among thorns is the one who hears the message, but worries of life and the lure of wealth choke the message, making them unproductive.
Matthew 13:23 The person who receives the seed on good soil is the one who listens to the word and understands it; they also produce a harvest, yielding sometimes a hundred times, sometimes sixty, sometimes thirty.
Matthew 13:24 He told them another story, saying, "The kingdom of heaven is like a man who planted good seeds in his field."
Matthew 13:25 While people were sleeping, his enemy came and scattered weeds among the wheat, then left.
Matthew 13:26 But when the plants grew and produced grain, the weeds also showed up.
Matthew 13:27 The workers of the owner came and asked him, "Sir, didn't you plant good seeds in your field? Where did the weeds come from?"
Matthew 13:28 He told them, "An enemy did this." The servants asked him, "Do you want us to go and collect them?"
Matthew 13:29 He said, "No, because if you pull up the weeds, you might also pull out the wheat."
Matthew 13:30 Let both grow until harvest time. At harvest, I will tell the workers, "First collect the weeds and tie them to burn, but bring the wheat into my barn."
Matthew 13:31 He told them another story: "God's kingdom is like a tiny mustard seed that a man planted in his field.
Matthew 13:32 This seed is really the smallest of all seeds, but when it grows, it becomes the largest of garden plants and turns into a tree, so that the birds can come and nest in its branches.
Matthew 13:33 He told them another story: The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman mixed into a large amount of flour until it spread through all of it.
Matthew 13:34 Jesus told all these things to the crowd using stories; he did not tell them anything without using a story.
Matthew 13:35 This was done so the prophet's words would come true, where he said, "I will tell stories to explain things; I will share secrets hidden since the world began."
Matthew 13:36 Jesus sent the crowd home and went inside. His followers came to him and said, "Explain the story of the weeds in the field to us."
Matthew 13:37 He replied to them, "The one who plants the good seeds is the Son of Man."
Matthew 13:38 The field means the world; the good seeds represent the people of God's kingdom, while the weeds are the people of the evil one.
Matthew 13:39 The enemy who planted the seeds is the devil; the harvest time is the end of the world; and the workers who harvest are the angels.
Matthew 13:40 So just as weeds are collected and burned in a fire, it will be at the end of this world.
Matthew 13:41 The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will remove from his kingdom everything that causes sin and all who do evil.
Matthew 13:42 They will throw them into a fiery furnace, where there will be crying and grinding of teeth.
Matthew 13:43 The good people will shine like the sun in God's kingdom. If someone can listen, they should listen.
Matthew 13:44 The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a person finds it, they hide it again. Out of happiness, they sell everything they own and buy that field.
Matthew 13:45 The kingdom of heaven is like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
Matthew 13:46 When he found a very valuable pearl, he went and sold everything he had, and bought it.
Matthew 13:47 The kingdom of heaven is like a net thrown into the sea that caught all kinds of fish.
Matthew 13:48 When the net was full, they pulled it onto the shore. They sat down and put the good fish into containers, but threw the bad ones away.
Matthew 13:49 At the world's end, the angels will come and separate the bad people from the good ones.
Matthew 13:50 They will throw them into a fiery furnace, where there will be crying and grinding of teeth.
Matthew 13:51 Jesus asked them, "Do you understand all these things?" They answered him, "Yes, Lord."
Matthew 13:52 He told them, "So, every teacher trained for the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out new and old treasures from his storage."
Matthew 13:53 After Jesus told these stories, he left that place.
Matthew 13:54 When he returned to his hometown, he taught in their meeting place. People were amazed and asked, "How did this man get such wisdom and the power to do great things?"
Matthew 13:55 Isn't this the son of the carpenter? Isn't his mother named Mary? And his brothers, James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
Matthew 13:56 Doesn't he have all his sisters here with us? So where did this man get all these things?
Matthew 13:57 They were upset because of him. But Jesus told them, a prophet is respected everywhere except in his own town and home.
Matthew 13:58 He did not do many powerful things there because they did not believe.

Matthew 14:1 At that time, Herod the ruler heard about Jesus's fame.
Matthew 14:2 He told his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead, and that's why he can do powerful things."
Matthew 14:3 Herod arrested John, tied him up, and put him in jail because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.
Matthew 14:4 John told him, "You should not have her."
Matthew 14:5 He wanted to kill him but was afraid of the people, because they thought he was a prophet.
Matthew 14:6 On Herod's birthday, Herodias's daughter danced for them and made Herod happy.
Matthew 14:7 He promised with a promise to give her anything she asked for.
Matthew 14:8 Her mother had told her what to say, so she said, "Give me John the Baptist's head on a plate right here."
Matthew 14:9 The king felt sad, but because of his promise and the guests at his table, he ordered that her request be granted.
Matthew 14:10 He sent someone and had John beheaded in the prison.
Matthew 14:11 They brought his head on a platter, gave it to the young woman, and she took it to her mother.
Matthew 14:12 His followers came, picked up the body, buried it, and then went to tell Jesus.
Matthew 14:13 When Jesus learned about it, he left by boat to a remote desert area. Hearing this, the people walked from the towns to follow him.
Matthew 14:14 Jesus went out, saw many people, felt sorry for them, and healed their sick.
Matthew 14:15 In the evening, his followers came to him and said, "This is a remote place, and it's getting late; tell the crowd to leave so they can go to the nearby towns and buy food for themselves."
Matthew 14:16 Jesus said to them, "They don't need to leave; give them something to eat."
Matthew 14:17 They said to him, "We only have five loaves of bread and two fish here."
Matthew 14:18 He said, "Bring them here to me."
Matthew 14:19 He told the people to sit on the grass, took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to the sky, said a blessing, broke the bread, and gave it to his followers, who then gave it to everyone.
Matthew 14:20 Everyone ate and was satisfied, and they gathered twelve baskets full of leftover pieces.
Matthew 14:21 About five thousand men ate, not counting women and children.
Matthew 14:22 Right away, Jesus made his disciples get into a boat and go ahead of him to the other side while he sent the crowds away.
Matthew 14:23 After he told the crowds to go, he went up a mountain by himself to pray. When night came, he was there alone.
Matthew 14:24 The boat was in the middle of the sea, being thrown about by waves, because the wind was against it.
Matthew 14:25 In the last part of the night, Jesus went to them, walking on the water.
Matthew 14:26 When the disciples saw him walking on the water, they were scared and said, "It's a ghost!" and they screamed with fear.
Matthew 14:27 Right away Jesus spoke to them, saying, "Be happy; it's me; don't be scared."
Matthew 14:28 Peter answered, "Lord, if it's really you, tell me to come to you on the water."
Matthew 14:29 He said, "Come." So Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus.
Matthew 14:30 But when he saw the strong wind, he was scared; and starting to sink, he shouted, "God, save me."
Matthew 14:31 Right away, Jesus reached out his hand, grabbed him, and said, "You with little faith, why did you doubt?"
Matthew 14:32 When they got into the boat, the wind stopped.
Matthew 14:33 The people in the boat came to him and honored him, saying, "Truly, you are the Son of God."
Matthew 14:34 After they crossed over, they arrived in the land of Gennesaret.
Matthew 14:35 When the people there recognized him, they spread the word throughout the region and brought all the sick to him.
Matthew 14:36 They asked to touch just the edge of his clothes, and everyone who touched it was completely healed.

Matthew 15:1 Some teachers of the law and Pharisees from Jerusalem came to Jesus and asked,
Matthew 15:2 Why do your followers break the elders' tradition? They don't wash their hands before eating bread.
Matthew 15:3 But he replied and said to them, "Why do you also break God's command by following your tradition?"
Matthew 15:4 God commanded, saying, Respect your father and mother; and, Anyone who speaks badly of their father or mother must be put to death.
Matthew 15:5 But you say, if anyone tells their father or mother, 'What you could have gained from me is a gift to God',
Matthew 15:6 If someone does not respect their father or mother, you say they are free from guilt. This way, you cancel out God's rule because of your tradition.
Matthew 15:7 You pretenders, Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you, saying,
Matthew 15:8 These people come close to me with their words and honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
Matthew 15:9 They worship me for nothing, teaching human rules as if they were God's teachings.
Matthew 15:10 He called the crowd and said to them, "Listen and understand."
Matthew 15:11 What goes into the mouth does not make a person unclean; it's what comes out of the mouth that makes a person unclean.
Matthew 15:12 His disciples came and asked him, "Do you know that the Pharisees were upset when they heard what you said?"
Matthew 15:13 He replied, "Every plant that my Father in heaven did not plant will be pulled out."
Matthew 15:14 Leave them; they are blind guides. If a blind person leads another blind person, both will fall into a hole.
Matthew 15:15 Peter replied and asked him, "Explain this story to us."
Matthew 15:16 Jesus asked, "Do you still not understand?"
Matthew 15:17 Don't you understand that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the stomach and then is eliminated?
Matthew 15:18 The things that come out of the mouth start in the heart, and these make the person unclean.
Matthew 15:19 Evil thoughts, murders, cheating in marriage, sexual misconduct, stealing, lying, and insults all come from the heart.
Matthew 15:20 These things make a person unclean: but eating with unwashed hands does not make a person unclean.
Matthew 15:21 Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
Matthew 15:22 Look, a Canaanite woman came from that area and called out to him, "Please have mercy on me, Sir, son of David; my daughter is suffering terribly because of an evil spirit."
Matthew 15:23 He did not reply to her at all. His followers came and urged him, "Tell her to go away; she keeps shouting at us."
Matthew 15:24 He replied, "I am only sent to the lost sheep of Israel."
Matthew 15:25 She came and worshiped him, saying, "Sir, help me."
Matthew 15:26 But he replied, "It's not right to take the children's bread and throw it to dogs."
Matthew 15:27 She said, "Yes, God, but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their owners' table."
Matthew 15:28 Then Jesus replied to her, "Woman, your faith is strong; let it happen for you as you wish." And her daughter was healed at that moment.
Matthew 15:29 Jesus left that place and went near the Sea of Galilee; He climbed a mountain and sat down there.
Matthew 15:30 Many people came to him, bringing the lame, blind, mute, crippled, and many others, and placed them at Jesus' feet; and he healed them.
Matthew 15:31 The crowd was amazed to see those who couldn't speak talking, the injured healed, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they praised the God of Israel.
Matthew 15:32 Jesus called his followers to him and said, "I feel sorry for all the people because they have been with me for three days and have nothing to eat. I don't want to send them away hungry, or they might get weak on their journey."
Matthew 15:33 His followers asked him, "Where can we get enough bread in this remote place to feed such a large crowd?"
Matthew 15:34 Jesus asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" They replied, "Seven, and a few small fish."
Matthew 15:35 He told the people to sit down on the ground.
Matthew 15:36 He took the seven loaves and the fish, thanked God, broke them, and gave them to his followers, and they gave them to the crowd.
Matthew 15:37 Everyone ate and was satisfied. They collected seven baskets full of leftover pieces.
Matthew 15:38 About four thousand men ate, not counting women and children.
Matthew 15:39 He sent the crowd away, got into a boat, and went to the region of Magdala.

Matthew 16:1 The Pharisees and Sadducees also came to Jesus and, trying to trick him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
Matthew 16:2 He replied, "When the evening comes, you say, 'The weather will be good,' because the sky is red."
Matthew 16:3 In the morning, the weather will be bad today because the sky is red and dark. You hypocrites, you can tell what the sky looks like, but can't you tell what's happening in these times?
Matthew 16:4 A bad and unfaithful generation looks for a sign; no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. Then he left them and went away.
Matthew 16:5 When his disciples reached the other side, they realized they had forgotten to bring bread.
Matthew 16:6 Jesus told them, "Be careful and watch out for the influence of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
Matthew 16:7 They talked to each other, saying, "It's because we didn't bring any bread."
Matthew 16:8 When Jesus noticed, he said to them, "You with little faith, why are you discussing that you have no bread?"
Matthew 16:9 Don't you understand or remember the five loaves for the five thousand people and the number of baskets you gathered?
Matthew 16:10 Don't you remember the seven loaves for the four thousand and how many baskets you collected?
Matthew 16:11 Why don't you understand that I was not talking about bread? Be careful of the Pharisees' and Sadducees' teachings.
Matthew 16:12 Then they realized he was not telling them to watch out for the yeast in bread, but to be cautious of the teachings of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Matthew 16:13 When Jesus arrived in the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his followers, "Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?"
Matthew 16:14 They said, "Some think you are John the Baptist, others Elijah, and others think you are Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
Matthew 16:15 He asks them, "But who do you say I am?"
Matthew 16:16 Simon Peter answered, "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God."
Matthew 16:17 Jesus replied to him, "You are blessed, Simon son of Jonah, because this was not shown to you by humans, but by my Father in heaven."
Matthew 16:18 I also tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell will not overcome it.
Matthew 16:19 I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be released in heaven.
Matthew 16:20 He told his disciples not to tell anyone that he was Jesus the Christ.
Matthew 16:21 From that time, Jesus started to explain to his followers that he had to go to Jerusalem, face many troubles from the leaders, the main priests, and the teachers of the law, be put to death, and come back to life on the third day.
Matthew 16:22 Then Peter took him aside and started to scold him, saying, "Don't let this happen to you, Lord; this must not happen to you."
Matthew 16:23 He turned and said to Peter, "Go away from me, Satan! You are a problem to me because you don't care about what comes from God, but only what comes from people."
Matthew 16:24 Jesus told his followers, "If anyone wants to follow me, they must forget about themselves, carry their cross, and come with me."
Matthew 16:25 Whoever wants to save their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for me will find it.
Matthew 16:26 What good is it for someone to gain the whole world, yet lose their own life? Or what can someone give to get back their life?
Matthew 16:27 The Son of Man will come with the brightness of his Father and his angels; and then he will give each person what they deserve for what they have done.
Matthew 16:28 I tell you the truth, some standing here will not die before they see the Son of Man arriving in his kingdom.

Matthew 17:1 Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John, his brother, up a high mountain by themselves.
Matthew 17:2 He changed form in front of them; his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as light.
Matthew 17:3 Suddenly, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.
Matthew 17:4 Peter replied to Jesus, "Teacher, it's great for us to be here. If you want, we can build three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
Matthew 17:5 While he was still speaking, a bright cloud covered them. And a voice from the cloud said, "This is my dear Son, who makes me happy; listen to him."
Matthew 17:6 When the followers heard this, they fell to the ground, very scared.
Matthew 17:7 Jesus came, touched them, and said, "Get up, and do not be afraid."
Matthew 17:8 When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
Matthew 17:9 As they came down from the mountain, Jesus instructed them, "Don't tell anyone what you saw until the Son of man has risen from the dead."
Matthew 17:10 His followers asked him, "Why do the teachers say that Elijah must come first?"
Matthew 17:11 Jesus answered them, "Elias will indeed come first and restore everything."
Matthew 17:12 I tell you, Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted. In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer by their hands.
Matthew 17:13 Then the followers realized he was talking to them about John the Baptist.
Matthew 17:14 When they reached the crowd, a man came to him, knelt down before him, and said,
Matthew 17:15 God, please have mercy on my son; he has seizures and suffers terribly. Often he falls into the fire and into the water.
Matthew 17:16 I brought him to your followers, but they couldn't heal him.
Matthew 17:17 Then Jesus replied, "You have no faith and are all mixed up. How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to me."
Matthew 17:18 Jesus told the evil spirit to leave, and it left the boy, who was healed from that moment.
Matthew 17:19 The disciples came to Jesus alone and asked, "Why couldn't we drive it out?"
Matthew 17:20 Jesus told them, "It's because you don't believe. Truly, if you have faith even as small as a mustard seed, you can tell this mountain to move to another place and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you."
Matthew 17:21 However, this type can only come out through prayer and fasting.
Matthew 17:22 While they stayed in Galilee, Jesus told them, "The Son of Man will be handed over to people."
Matthew 17:23 They will kill him, and on the third day, he will rise again. They were very sad.
Matthew 17:24 When they arrived in Capernaum, the people who collect the temple tax went to Peter and asked, "Doesn't your teacher pay the tax?"
Matthew 17:25 He said, "Yes." When he entered the house, Jesus spoke first, asking, "What do you think, Simon? Who do the kings of the earth collect taxes or fees from? Their own children or others?"
Matthew 17:26 Peter said to him, "From foreigners." Jesus said to him, "Then the children are free."
Matthew 17:27 Still, we don't want to upset them, so go to the lake, throw in a line, and pull out the first fish you catch. Open its mouth and you'll find some money. Take it and pay them for both of us.

Matthew 18:1 The disciples came to Jesus then, asking, "Who is the greatest in heaven's kingdom?"
Matthew 18:2 Jesus called a child over and had him stand among them.
Matthew 18:3 Truly, I tell you, if you don't change and become like little children, you won't enter the kingdom of heaven.
Matthew 18:4 Anyone who humbles themselves like this child is the greatest in heaven's kingdom.
Matthew 18:5 Anyone who welcomes a little child because of me is welcoming me.
Matthew 18:6 But if anyone hurts one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for them to have a heavy stone tied around their neck and to be drowned in the deep sea.
Matthew 18:7 Trouble comes to the world because of wrongs; wrongs must happen, but trouble comes to the person who causes the wrong.
Matthew 18:8 If your hand or foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It's better to live with one hand or foot than to have two and be thrown into eternal fire.
Matthew 18:9 If your eye causes you to sin, take it out and throw it away. It's better to live with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell.
Matthew 18:10 Be careful not to look down on any of these little ones, because I tell you, their angels in heaven always see the face of my God in heaven.
Matthew 18:11 The Son of Man came to save what was lost.
Matthew 18:12 What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one gets lost, won't he leave the ninety-nine and go to the mountains to look for the lost one?
Matthew 18:13 If he finds it, truly, I tell you, he is happier about that one sheep than about the ninety-nine that did not wander off.
Matthew 18:14 God in heaven does not want even one of these little ones to be lost.
Matthew 18:15 If your brother does wrong to you, go and point out his mistake, just between the two of you. If he listens to you, you have won your brother back.
Matthew 18:16 If he doesn't listen to you, bring one or two others with you, so that the truth of every word can be confirmed by two or three witnesses.
Matthew 18:17 If he ignores them, tell the church. But if he ignores the church, treat him like a stranger or a tax collector.
Matthew 18:18 I tell you the truth, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be released in heaven.
Matthew 18:19 I tell you again, if two of you on earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by my Father in heaven.
Matthew 18:20 When two or three people meet in my name, I am there with them.
Matthew 18:21 Peter came to him and asked, "Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother when he sins against me? Up to seven times?"
Matthew 18:22 Jesus said to him, "I don't mean seven times, but seventy times seven."
Matthew 18:23 The kingdom of heaven is compared to a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
Matthew 18:24 When he started to settle accounts, someone was brought to him who owed him ten thousand coins.
Matthew 18:25 Since he couldn't pay, his master ordered that he, his wife, his children, and everything he owned be sold to pay the debt.
Matthew 18:26 The servant knelt down and begged him, saying, "Master, please wait, and I will pay you everything."
Matthew 18:27 The master of the servant felt sorry for him, set him free, and canceled his debt.
Matthew 18:28 The servant went out and found a fellow servant who owed him a small amount of money. He grabbed him and choked him, saying, "Pay back what you owe me."
Matthew 18:29 His coworker knelt down and begged him, saying, "Please be patient with me, and I will pay you everything."
Matthew 18:30 He refused and put him in jail until he could pay back the money.
Matthew 18:31 When his fellow servants saw what happened, they were very sad and went to tell their master everything that happened.
Matthew 18:32 Then his master, after calling him, said to him, 'You evil servant, I forgave all your debt because you asked me to.
Matthew 18:33 Shouldn't you also have shown mercy to your fellow servant, just as I showed mercy to you?
Matthew 18:34 His master was angry and handed him over to the jailers until he could pay back everything he owed.
Matthew 18:35 In the same way, my Father in heaven will treat you, unless you truly forgive everyone for the wrongs they have done to you.

Matthew 19:1 After Jesus finished speaking, he left Galilee and went to the area of Judea across the Jordan River.
Matthew 19:2 Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
Matthew 19:3 The Pharisees came to him, trying to test him, and asked, "Is it okay for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?"
Matthew 19:4 He replied, "Haven't you read that at the start, the Creator made them man and woman?"
Matthew 19:5 And said, "Because of this, a man will leave his father and mother and stick to his wife, and the two will become one body."
Matthew 19:6 So they are no longer two, but one body. What God has joined, let no one separate.
Matthew 19:7 They asked him, "Then why did Moses tell us to give a divorce paper and send her away?"
Matthew 19:8 He told them, Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts were hard, but it was not like that from the start.
Matthew 19:9 I tell you, if anyone divorces his wife for any reason other than unfaithfulness, and marries someone else, he is committing adultery. Whoever marries the divorced woman is also committing adultery.
Matthew 19:10 His followers said to him, "If this is how it is between a man and his wife, it is better not to get married."
Matthew 19:11 He told them, "Not everyone can accept this teaching, only those who are meant to."
Matthew 19:12 Some people are born unable to have children, some are made that way by others, and some choose to live without marriage for God's kingdom. Whoever can accept this should accept it.
Matthew 19:13 People brought little children to him so he could lay his hands on them and pray, but the disciples scolded them.
Matthew 19:14 Jesus said, Let the little children come to me, don't stop them, because heaven belongs to ones like these.
Matthew 19:15 He put his hands on them and left that place.
Matthew 19:16 Someone came and asked him, "Good teacher, what must I do to get eternal life?"
Matthew 19:17 He asked him, "Why do you call me good? Only God is truly good. But if you want to have life, follow the commandments."
Matthew 19:18 He asked, "Which ones?" Jesus answered, "Do not kill, do not cheat on your spouse, do not steal, do not lie about others,"
Matthew 19:19 Respect your father and mother, and love your neighbor as you love yourself.
Matthew 19:20 The young man said to him, "I have kept all these things since I was young: what do I still need?"
Matthew 19:21 Jesus said to him, "If you want to be perfect, go sell what you own, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven: then come and follow me."
Matthew 19:22 But when the young man heard this, he left feeling sad because he had many things.
Matthew 19:23 Jesus told his disciples, "I tell you the truth, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven."
Matthew 19:24 I tell you again, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom.
Matthew 19:25 When his followers heard this, they were very surprised and asked, "Then who can be rescued?"
Matthew 19:26 Jesus looked at them and said, "For people this is impossible, but for God everything is possible."
Matthew 19:27 Peter replied, "Look, we've left everything to follow you. What will we get for this?"
Matthew 19:28 Jesus told them, "Truly, I tell you, those who have followed me will, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, also sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel."
Matthew 19:29 Everyone who has left homes, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse, children, or fields for my sake will get back much more and will have eternal life.
Matthew 19:30 Many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.

Matthew 20:1 The kingdom of heaven is like a man who owns a house and went out early in the morning to find workers for his vineyard.
Matthew 20:2 After he made a deal with the workers for one penny each day, he sent them to his grape farm.
Matthew 20:3 He went out around nine in the morning and saw others standing around doing nothing in the market.
Matthew 20:4 He said to them, "You go work in the vineyard too, and I will pay you what is fair." So they went.
Matthew 20:5 He went out again around six and nine in the morning and did the same thing.
Matthew 20:6 Around eleven o'clock, he went out, found others standing around doing nothing, and said to them, 'Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?'
Matthew 20:7 They tell him, "No one has given us work." He says to them, "Go work in the vineyard, and you will get what is fair."
Matthew 20:8 When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his manager, "Call the workers, and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired to the first."
Matthew 20:9 When the workers who were hired around 5 p.m. came, each one got a penny.
Matthew 20:10 When the first workers came, they thought they would get more, but they also got one penny each.
Matthew 20:11 When they got it, they complained about the homeowner.
Matthew 20:12 You said, 'These people worked only one hour, but you've treated them the same as us, who worked hard all day in the hot sun.'
Matthew 20:13 He replied to one of them, "Friend, I'm not being unfair to you. Didn't you agree to work for a penny?"
Matthew 20:14 Take what is yours and leave; I will give this last person the same as I gave you.
Matthew 20:15 Isn't it okay for me to do what I want with what's mine? Are you jealous because I am generous?
Matthew 20:16 The last will be first, and the first will be last: many are called, but few are chosen.
Matthew 20:17 Jesus headed to Jerusalem and took the twelve disciples aside on the road and said to them,
Matthew 20:18 Look, we are going to Jerusalem; and the Son of Man will be handed over to the religious leaders and the teachers of the law, and they will sentence him to death.
Matthew 20:19 They will hand him over to foreigners to mock, whip, and crucify him; but on the third day, he will come back to life.
Matthew 20:20 Zebedee's wife came to Jesus with her sons, bowing down to him, and asked him for something.
Matthew 20:21 He asked her, "What do you want?" She replied, "Let my two sons sit with you in your kingdom, one on your right and the other on your left."
Matthew 20:22 But Jesus replied, "You don't understand what you're asking. Can you handle the hard things I'm going to face and go through the tough experience I will go through?" They answered him, "We can."
Matthew 20:23 He tells them, "You will indeed drink from my cup and be baptized like I am. But to sit at my right or left side is not for me to give. That place is for those my Father has prepared it for."
Matthew 20:24 When the ten heard about it, they were very upset with the two brothers.
Matthew 20:25 Jesus called them to him and said, "You know that the leaders of other nations rule over them, and their powerful people have authority over them."
Matthew 20:26 In your group, it should not be like that. Instead, if someone wants to be important, they should serve you.
Matthew 20:27 Whoever wants to be the most important among you must serve the rest.
Matthew 20:28 The Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life to save many people.
Matthew 20:29 As they left Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
Matthew 20:30 Two blind men were sitting by the road. When they heard Jesus was coming by, they shouted, "Please help us, Lord, Son of David!"
Matthew 20:31 The crowd told them to be quiet, but they shouted louder, "Please have mercy on us, God, son of David."
Matthew 20:32 Jesus stopped, called them, and asked, "What do you want me to do for you?"
Matthew 20:33 They said to him, "Lord, let our eyes be opened."
Matthew 20:34 Jesus felt sorry for them, touched their eyes, and right away they could see, and they followed him.

Matthew 21:1 When they got close to Jerusalem and reached Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples.
Matthew 21:2 Tell them, go to the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied up, and a young donkey with her: untie them and bring them to me.
Matthew 21:3 If anyone asks you about it, say, 'God needs them,' and he will send them right away.
Matthew 21:4 This happened to fulfill what the prophet had said.
Matthew 21:5 Tell the people of Zion, look, your King is coming to you, humble, and riding on a donkey, and on a colt, the young of a donkey.
Matthew 21:6 The disciples went and did what Jesus told them to do.
Matthew 21:7 They brought the donkey and the young colt, put their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.
Matthew 21:8 A huge crowd spread their clothes on the road; others cut branches from the trees and scattered them on the road.
Matthew 21:9 The crowds going ahead and those following shouted, "Hosanna to the son of David! He who comes in the name of God is blessed; Hosanna in the highest!"
Matthew 21:10 When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up and asked, "Who is this?"
Matthew 21:11 The crowd said, "This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee."
Matthew 21:12 Jesus entered God's temple and drove out all who were selling and buying there. He flipped over the tables of the money changers and the chairs of those selling doves.
Matthew 21:13 He said to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer,' but you have turned it into a hideout for thieves."
Matthew 21:14 Blind and disabled people came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
Matthew 21:15 When the religious leaders saw the amazing things he did, and heard the children shouting in the temple, "Hosanna to the Son of David," they were very upset.
Matthew 21:16 And said to him, "Do you hear what they are saying?" And Jesus said to them, "Yes; have you never read, 'From the mouths of children and babies you have made perfect praise'?"
Matthew 21:17 He left them, went out of the city to Bethany, and stayed there.
Matthew 21:18 In the morning as he went back to the city, he was hungry.
Matthew 21:19 When he saw a fig tree by the road, he went to it but found no fruit, only leaves. Then he said to it, "May you never grow fruit again." At once, the fig tree dried up.
Matthew 21:20 When the disciples saw it, they were amazed and said, "How quickly has the fig tree dried up!"
Matthew 21:21 Jesus replied, "I tell you the truth, if you believe and don't doubt, you can do not just what was done to the fig tree, but also tell this mountain to move and be thrown into the sea, and it will happen."
Matthew 21:22 When you pray and believe, anything you ask for, you will get.
Matthew 21:23 When he entered the temple, the religious leaders and elders approached him while he was teaching and asked, "What gives you the right to do these things? Who gave you this authority?"
Matthew 21:24 Jesus replied and said to them, "I will ask you one question too, and if you answer me, I will tell you by what authority I do these things."
Matthew 21:25 Where did John's baptism come from? From God or from people? They thought, "If we say, 'From God,' he will ask us, 'Then why didn't you believe John?'"
Matthew 21:26 But if we say, 'From people,' we are afraid of the crowd, because everyone considers John a prophet.
Matthew 21:27 They replied to Jesus, "We don't know." So he said to them, "Then I won't tell you by what authority I do these things."
Matthew 21:28 What do you think? A man had two sons. He went to the first and said, "Son, go work in my vineyard today."
Matthew 21:29 He replied, "I won't." But later he changed his mind and went.
Matthew 21:30 He went to the second and said the same thing. The second one answered, "I will go, sir," but he did not go.
Matthew 21:31 Which of the two did what his father wanted? They answered, "The first." Jesus told them, "I tell you the truth, the tax collectors and prostitutes will enter God's kingdom ahead of you."
Matthew 21:32 John came to you living right, but you didn't believe him. Tax collectors and prostitutes did believe, and even after seeing this, you didn't change your minds to believe him.
Matthew 21:33 Listen to another story: A man owned a house, planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, made a place to press grapes, built a watchtower, rented it to farmers, and then he went to a distant land.
Matthew 21:34 When it was almost time to pick the fruit, he sent his workers to the farmers to collect the fruit.
Matthew 21:35 The farmers took his workers, beat one, killed another, and threw stones at another.
Matthew 21:36 He sent more servants than before, and they were treated the same way.
Matthew 21:37 Last of all, he sent them his son, thinking, "They will respect my son."
Matthew 21:38 When the workers saw the son, they said to each other, "This is the one who will inherit everything. Let's kill him and take his inheritance."
Matthew 21:39 They grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
Matthew 21:40 When the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those workers?
Matthew 21:41 They tell him, God will terribly destroy those bad men, and will rent his vineyard to other farmers, who will give him the crops at the right times.
Matthew 21:42 Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the scriptures that the stone the builders did not want became the cornerstone? This was done by God, and it is amazing to us?"
Matthew 21:43 I tell you, God's kingdom will be taken from you and given to a people who produce its fruits.
Matthew 21:44 Anyone who falls on this stone will break, but if it falls on anyone, it will crush them into dust.
Matthew 21:45 When the chief priests and Pharisees heard his stories, they understood he was talking about them.
Matthew 21:46 But when they tried to arrest him, they were afraid of the crowd, because the people believed he was a prophet.

Matthew 22:1 Jesus answered and told them another story using parables. He said,
Matthew 22:2 God's kingdom is like a king who arranged a wedding for his son.
Matthew 22:3 He sent his servants to invite those who had been asked to the wedding, but they did not want to come.
Matthew 22:4 He sent more servants and said, "Tell the invited guests, 'Look, I've made my dinner ready: my oxen and fattened animals are butchered, and everything is set. Come to the wedding feast.'"
Matthew 22:5 But they ignored it and went away, one to his farm, another to his business.
Matthew 22:6 The remaining people took his servants, treated them badly, and killed them.
Matthew 22:7 When the king heard this, he was angry. He sent his armies to kill those murderers and burn their city.
Matthew 22:8 He said to his servants, "The wedding is ready, but the guests who were invited were not worthy."
Matthew 22:9 Go to the main roads and invite everyone you find to the wedding.
Matthew 22:10 The servants went out to the roads and brought back everyone they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
Matthew 22:11 When the king entered to look at the guests, he noticed a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.
Matthew 22:12 He said to him, "Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding outfit?" And he had nothing to say.
Matthew 22:13 The king told his servants, "Tie up his hands and feet, take him out, and throw him into the dark place, where there will be crying and grinding of teeth."
Matthew 22:14 Many are invited, but few are selected.
Matthew 22:15 Then the Pharisees went and planned how to trap him with his words.
Matthew 22:16 They sent their followers to him with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know you are honest and teach God's way truthfully. You don't favor anyone because you pay no attention to who they are."
Matthew 22:17 Tell us then, what do you think? Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?
Matthew 22:18 But Jesus knew they were being evil and asked, "Why are you trying to trick me, you fakers?"
Matthew 22:19 Show me the tax money. And they brought him a coin.
Matthew 22:20 He asks them, "Whose picture and name are on this?"
Matthew 22:21 They said to him, "Caesar's." Then he said to them, "Give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God."
Matthew 22:22 After hearing his words, they were amazed, then they left and went on their way.
Matthew 22:23 That day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and asked him.
Matthew 22:24 Teacher, Moses said, "If a man dies without children, his brother should marry the widow and have children for his brother."
Matthew 22:25 Seven brothers were with us. The first brother died after he got married, and since he had no children, his wife became his brother's.
Matthew 22:26 The second one did the same, and the third, up to the seventh.
Matthew 22:27 Finally, the woman died too.
Matthew 22:28 So, at the resurrection, whose wife will she be, since all seven were married to her?
Matthew 22:29 Jesus answered them, "You are mistaken, because you don't know the Scriptures or God's power."
Matthew 22:30 In the resurrection, people do not marry or are married off, but are like God's angels in heaven.
Matthew 22:31 But about rising from the dead, haven't you read what God told you, saying,
Matthew 22:32 I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. God is not for the dead, but for the living.
Matthew 22:33 When the crowd heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.
Matthew 22:34 When the Pharisees heard that he had made the Sadducees quiet, they came together.
Matthew 22:35 One of them, a lawyer, asked him a question to test him, saying,
Matthew 22:36 Teacher, what is the most important command in the law?
Matthew 22:37 Jesus told him, "You should love God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind."
Matthew 22:38 This is the most important command.
Matthew 22:39 The second command is similar: Love your neighbor the same way you love yourself.
Matthew 22:40 All the laws and the teachings of the prophets are based on these two commandments.
Matthew 22:41 While the Pharisees were together, Jesus asked them,
Matthew 22:42 Asking, "What do you think about the Messiah? Who's his father?" They answered, "David's son."
Matthew 22:43 He asks them, "So why does David, inspired by the Spirit, call him 'Lord,' saying?
Matthew 22:44 God said to my master, "Sit at my right side until I make your enemies a place for your feet."
Matthew 22:45 If David calls him Lord, how is he David's son?
Matthew 22:46 No one could reply to him at all, nor did anyone dare to ask him more questions from that day on.

Matthew 23:1 Jesus spoke to the crowd and to his followers.
Matthew 23:2 The teachers of the Law and the Pharisees have authority like Moses.
Matthew 23:3 Do what they tell you to follow, but don't copy their actions. They talk but don't act.
Matthew 23:4 They put heavy and hard loads on people's shoulders but won't lift a finger to help them.
Matthew 23:5 They do all their actions to be seen by people: they wear wide scripture boxes and make the edges of their clothes long.
Matthew 23:6 They like the best places at feasts and the most important seats in the synagogues.
Matthew 23:7 They like to be greeted in the marketplaces and to have people call them 'Teacher, Teacher.'
Matthew 23:8 Don't let anyone call you 'Teacher,' because you have only one Teacher, Christ, and you are all brothers and sisters.
Matthew 23:9 Do not call anyone on earth your father; you have one Father, and he is in heaven.
Matthew 23:10 Don't be called leaders, because you have only one leader, Christ.
Matthew 23:11 The one who is the greatest among you must be your helper.
Matthew 23:12 Anyone who makes himself important will be made humble, and he who makes himself humble will be made important.
Matthew 23:13 But trouble comes to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, pretenders! You lock the door to God's kingdom so no one can enter. You don't go in, and you don't let those trying to enter get in.
Matthew 23:14 Trouble awaits you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, fakers! You take advantage of widows and their homes, and pretend to be holy by praying long prayers. Because of this, you will face harsher punishment.
Matthew 23:15 You are in trouble, teachers of the law and Pharisees, fakers! You travel over sea and land to win one follower, and when you do, you make them twice as much a child of hell as you are.
Matthew 23:16 Trouble to you, blind leaders, who say, if anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the temple's gold, they must keep their promise!
Matthew 23:17 You fools and blind, which is more important, the gold or the temple that makes the gold holy?
Matthew 23:18 Anyone who swears by the altar is not committing to anything, but whoever swears by the offering on it is responsible.
Matthew 23:19 You fools and blind: which is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy?
Matthew 23:20 Anyone who swears by the altar, is swearing by it and everything on it.
Matthew 23:21 Anyone who swears by the temple is swearing by it and by God who lives in it.
Matthew 23:22 Whoever swears by heaven is swearing by God's throne and by the one who sits on it.
Matthew 23:23 You are in trouble, teachers and religious leaders, pretenders! You give a tenth of your spices like mint, anise, and cumin, but you ignore the more important things in God's law—justice, kindness, and trust. You should do these without forgetting the others.
Matthew 23:24 You blind leaders, who filter out a small insect but swallow a camel.
Matthew 23:25 Trouble comes to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, fakers! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
Matthew 23:26 You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and dish so that the outside can be clean too.
Matthew 23:27 Trouble comes to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, fakers! You are like painted tombs that look nice on the outside but inside are full of dead people's bones and all kinds of filth.
Matthew 23:28 You might look good to others, but inside you are full of fakeness and wrong.
Matthew 23:29 Trouble to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you fakers! You build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the graves of the good people.
Matthew 23:30 And say, If we had lived when our ancestors did, we wouldn't have helped them kill the prophets.
Matthew 23:31 So you show by your own actions that you are descendants of those who killed the prophets.
Matthew 23:32 Complete what your ancestors started.
Matthew 23:33 You snakes, you family of vipers, how can you avoid being condemned to hell?
Matthew 23:34 So, look, I will send to you prophets, wise people, and writers; and some of them you will kill and hang on crosses; and some of them you will beat in your places of worship, and chase from town to town.
Matthew 23:35 So that the punishment for all the good people's blood spilled on the earth will fall on you, from the good Abel's blood to the blood of Zacharias, Barachias's son, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
Matthew 23:36 I truly tell you, all these things will happen to this generation.
Matthew 23:37 Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, how often I wanted to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you didn't want that!
Matthew 23:38 Look, your house is left empty.
Matthew 23:39 I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, "Blessed is he who comes in God's name."

Matthew 24:1 Jesus left the temple, and when his disciples approached, they pointed out the temple buildings to him.
Matthew 24:2 Jesus said to them, "Don't you see all these things? Truly, I tell you, not one stone will be left on another here; all will be knocked down."
Matthew 24:3 As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him in private and said, "Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign of your coming, and of the end of the world?"
Matthew 24:4 Jesus replied and told them, "Be careful that no one tricks you."
Matthew 24:5 Many will come using my name, claiming to be Christ, and they will fool many people.
Matthew 24:6 You will hear about wars and talk of wars: don't be afraid: all these things have to happen, but it's not the end yet.
Matthew 24:7 Country will fight against country, and kingdom against kingdom; there will be food shortages, diseases, and earthquakes in different places.
Matthew 24:8 All these things are the start of troubles.
Matthew 24:9 They will hand you over to suffer and will kill you. All nations will hate you because of me.
Matthew 24:10 Then many will feel hurt, betray each other, and hate one another.
Matthew 24:11 Many false prophets will appear and trick many people.
Matthew 24:12 Because there will be more wrongdoing, many people's love will grow cold.
Matthew 24:13 But the one who keeps going until the end will be saved.
Matthew 24:14 This good news of the kingdom will be told everywhere in the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
Matthew 24:15 When you see the terrible thing that causes destruction, mentioned by the prophet Daniel, standing in the sacred place, (if you read this, try to understand:)
Matthew 24:16 If you are in Judea, run to the mountains.
Matthew 24:17 If you're on the roof, don't go down to get anything from your house.
Matthew 24:18 If someone is in the field, they should not go back to get their clothes.
Matthew 24:19 Trouble will come to pregnant women and mothers nursing babies in those days!
Matthew 24:20 Pray that you don't have to run away in the winter or on the Sabbath day.
Matthew 24:21 Then there will be a great hardship, like nothing that has ever happened from the start of the world until now, and will never happen again.
Matthew 24:22 If those days were not made shorter, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be made shorter.
Matthew 24:23 If anyone tells you, 'Look, here is Christ,' or 'There he is,' don't believe it.
Matthew 24:24 False Christs and false prophets will come and perform great signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even God's chosen people.
Matthew 24:25 Look, I have already told you.
Matthew 24:26 So if someone tells you, 'Look, he is in the desert,' don't go there; or 'Look, he is hiding inside,' don't believe it.
Matthew 24:27 Just like lightning starts in the east and flashes to the west, so will the arrival of the Son of Man be.
Matthew 24:28 Wherever the dead body is, that's where the eagles will come together.
Matthew 24:29 Right after those hard times, the sun will get dark, the moon won't shine, stars will fall from the sky, and the forces in the heavens will be shaken.
Matthew 24:30 Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky, all the peoples of the earth will be sad, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
Matthew 24:31 He will send his angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will bring his chosen people from everywhere, from all parts of the sky.
Matthew 24:32 Learn from the story of the fig tree: When its branch becomes soft and grows leaves, you know summer is near.
Matthew 24:33 In the same way, when you see all these things, understand that it is close, right at the door.
Matthew 24:34 Truly I tell you, this group of people will not disappear until all these things happen.
Matthew 24:35 Heaven and earth will disappear, but my words will never disappear.
Matthew 24:36 No one knows the day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, only God does.
Matthew 24:37 Just as in Noah's time, so will the arrival of the Son of Man be.
Matthew 24:38 Before the flood, people were eating, drinking, getting married, and giving others in marriage, until Noah went into the ark.
Matthew 24:39 They did not know until the flood came and swept them all away; so will it be when the Son of Man comes.
Matthew 24:40 Two people will be in the field; one will be taken, and the other will be left behind.
Matthew 24:41 Two women will be working at the mill; one will be taken, and the other will be left behind.
Matthew 24:42 Stay alert, because you do not know when your Lord will come.
Matthew 24:43 Understand this: if the owner of the house knew when the thief would come, he would have stayed alert and not let his house be broken into.
Matthew 24:44 Be ready too, because the Son of Man will come at a time you don't expect.
Matthew 24:45 Who then is a loyal and smart servant, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give them food at the right time?
Matthew 24:46 Happy is the servant who is doing his work when his master comes.
Matthew 24:47 I truly tell you, he will put him in charge of all his property.
Matthew 24:48 If the bad servant thinks, "My master is taking a long time to come back;"
Matthew 24:49 He will start to hurt his fellow servants and to eat and drink with the drunk.
Matthew 24:50 The master of that servant will come on a day when he is not expecting him, and at an hour he does not know.
Matthew 24:51 He will cut him to pieces and place him with the fakes, where there will be crying and grinding of teeth.

Matthew 25:1 Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.
Matthew 25:2 Five of them were smart, and five were foolish.
Matthew 25:3 The foolish ones took their lamps but didn't bring any oil.
Matthew 25:4 The smart ones took oil in containers along with their lamps.
Matthew 25:5 While the groom was delayed, they all dozed off and slept.
Matthew 25:6 At midnight someone shouted, "Look, the groom is coming; go out to meet him."
Matthew 25:7 Then all those young women got up and made their lamps ready.
Matthew 25:8 The foolish ones said to the wise, "Give us some of your oil; our lamps have gone out."
Matthew 25:9 The wise replied, "No, there might not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves."
Matthew 25:10 While they were buying oil, the groom arrived; those prepared went with him to the wedding, and the door was closed.
Matthew 25:11 Later, the other young women came too, saying, "Sir, Sir, open the door for us."
Matthew 25:12 He replied, "Truly, I tell you, I don't know you."
Matthew 25:13 Stay alert, because you don't know the day or the time when the Son of Man will come.
Matthew 25:14 The kingdom of heaven is like a man going to a distant land, who called his servants and gave them his possessions.
Matthew 25:15 God gave one person five talents, another two, and another one, each according to their own ability; and then he left immediately.
Matthew 25:16 The person who got five talents went and did business with them and earned five more talents.
Matthew 25:17 The person who got two also made two more.
Matthew 25:18 The person who got one coin went, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master's money.
Matthew 25:19 After a long time, the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
Matthew 25:20 The person who got five talents came and brought five more, saying, God, you gave me five talents; look, I've earned five more talents in addition.
Matthew 25:21 His master said to him, "Good job, you're a good and loyal worker. You've been loyal with a few things, I'll put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness."
Matthew 25:22 The person who got two talents also came and said, "Master, you gave me two talents; look, I've earned two more talents in addition."
Matthew 25:23 His master said to him, "Well done, good and loyal servant; you have been loyal with a few things, I will put you in charge of many things: come and share your master's happiness."
Matthew 25:24 The person who got one talent came and said, "Master, I knew you are a tough man, taking what you didn't plant and collecting what you didn't scatter."
Matthew 25:25 I was scared, so I went and buried your money in the ground. Look, here is what belongs to you.
Matthew 25:26 His master replied, "You bad and lazy servant, you knew that I harvest where I haven't planted, and gather where I haven't scattered seed.
Matthew 25:27 You should have put my money with the bankers, so when I came back I could have gotten it back with interest.
Matthew 25:28 So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.
Matthew 25:29 Everyone who has something will receive more and have plenty. But the person who has nothing will lose even the little they have.
Matthew 25:30 Throw the useless servant into the deep darkness, where there will be crying and grinding of teeth.
Matthew 25:31 When the Son of Man comes in his glory, with all the angels, he will sit on his glorious throne.
Matthew 25:32 Before him all nations will be gathered, and he will separate them from each other, just like a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
Matthew 25:33 He will put the sheep on his right side and the goats on his left.
Matthew 25:34 The King will say to those on his right side, "Come, you who are blessed by my Father, receive the kingdom made ready for you since the world was made."
Matthew 25:35 I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me something to drink; I was a stranger, and you welcomed me.
Matthew 25:36 I was naked, and you gave me clothes; I was sick, and you looked after me; I was in prison, and you came to see me.
Matthew 25:37 The good people will answer, "God, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?"
Matthew 25:38 When did we see you as a stranger and welcome you, or without clothes and dress you?
Matthew 25:39 When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?
Matthew 25:40 The King will reply, 'Truly, I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.'
Matthew 25:41 Then he will also say to those on the left, 'Go away from me, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire made for the devil and his angels.'
Matthew 25:42 I was hungry, and you gave me nothing to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink.
Matthew 25:43 I was a stranger, and you did not welcome me: without clothes, and you did not dress me: ill, and in jail, and you did not visit me.
Matthew 25:44 Then they will also answer, saying, "God, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or without clothes, or sick, or in jail, and did not help you?"
Matthew 25:45 He will reply, 'I tell you, when you did not help one of the least important people, you did not help me.'
Matthew 25:46 These will go to eternal punishment, but the good people to eternal life.

Matthew 26:1 After Jesus said all this, he spoke to his followers.
Matthew 26:2 You know that in two days the Passover feast will happen, and the Son of Man will be betrayed to be crucified.
Matthew 26:3 The chief priests, scribes, and elders of the people gathered at the high priest's palace, whose name was Caiaphas.
Matthew 26:4 They planned secretly to capture Jesus and kill him.
Matthew 26:5 But they said, "Not during the feast, so there won't be a riot among the people."
Matthew 26:6 When Jesus was in Bethany, at Simon the leper's house,
Matthew 26:7 A woman came to him with a jar of very expensive perfume and poured it on his head while he was eating.
Matthew 26:8 When his followers saw this, they were upset, asking, "Why this waste?"
Matthew 26:9 This perfume could have been sold for a good price and the money given to the poor.
Matthew 26:10 When Jesus knew this, he said to them, "Why do you bother this woman? She has done a good thing for me."
Matthew 26:11 You will always have the poor among you, but you will not always have me.
Matthew 26:12 Because she put this perfume on me, she did it for when I am buried.
Matthew 26:13 I truly tell you, wherever this good news is shared in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told to remember her.
Matthew 26:14 One of the twelve disciples, named Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests.
Matthew 26:15 He asked them, "What will you pay me to hand him over to you?" So they agreed to give him thirty silver coins.
Matthew 26:16 From then on, he looked for a chance to betray him.
Matthew 26:17 On the first day of the festival of unleavened bread, the followers came to Jesus and asked, "Where do you want us to get ready for you to eat the Passover meal?"
Matthew 26:18 He said, "Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, 'The Teacher says, My time is near; I will celebrate the Passover at your house with my followers.'"
Matthew 26:19 The disciples did what Jesus told them, and they prepared for the Passover.
Matthew 26:20 When evening came, he sat down with the twelve.
Matthew 26:21 While they were eating, he said, "I tell you the truth, one of you will betray me."
Matthew 26:22 They were very sad, and each one started asking him, "Lord, is it me?"
Matthew 26:23 He replied, "The one who dips his hand in the bowl with me will betray me."
Matthew 26:24 The Son of Man is going as it has been told about him, but how terrible for the person who betrays the Son of Man! It would have been better for that person if he had never been born.
Matthew 26:25 Then Judas, who betrayed him, answered and said, "Teacher, is it me?" He replied to him, "You have said so."
Matthew 26:26 While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, "Take and eat; this is my body."
Matthew 26:27 He took the cup, thanked God, and gave it to them, saying, "Drink all of it."
Matthew 26:28 This is my blood of the new agreement, poured out for many to forgive sins.
Matthew 26:29 I tell you, I won't drink this wine again until the day I drink new wine with you in my Father's kingdom.
Matthew 26:30 After singing a hymn, they went to the Mount of Olives.
Matthew 26:31 Jesus said to them, "All of you will be troubled because of me tonight, as it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'"
Matthew 26:32 After I come back to life, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.
Matthew 26:33 Peter replied to him, "Even if everyone is upset because of you, I will never be upset."
Matthew 26:34 Jesus told him, "I tell you the truth, tonight before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you don't know me."
Matthew 26:35 Peter said to him, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never deny you." All the other disciples said the same.
Matthew 26:36 Jesus came with them to a place named Gethsemane and said to the disciples, "Stay here while I go over there to pray."
Matthew 26:37 He brought Peter and Zebedee's two sons with him, and started to feel sad and very troubled.
Matthew 26:38 He said to them, "My soul is very sad, as if I'm about to die. Stay here and keep watch with me."
Matthew 26:39 He went on a bit more, fell face down, and prayed, "My Father, if it's possible, let this cup be taken away; but not what I want, your will be done."
Matthew 26:40 He came to his followers, found them sleeping, and said to Peter, "What, you couldn't stay awake with me for one hour?"
Matthew 26:41 Stay alert and pray so you don't give in to temptation. You want to do what's right, but it's hard to follow through.
Matthew 26:42 He went to pray again, saying, "My Father, if I must go through this and cannot avoid it, let your will happen."
Matthew 26:43 He came and saw them sleeping again because their eyes were tired.
Matthew 26:44 He left them, went away again, and prayed for the third time, saying the same things.
Matthew 26:45 He then goes to his disciples and tells them, "Keep sleeping and resting. Look, the time is near when the Son of Man will be handed over to sinners."
Matthew 26:46 Get up, let's go; look, the one who will betray me is near.
Matthew 26:47 While he was still talking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived with a large crowd carrying swords and clubs sent by the religious leaders and elders.
Matthew 26:48 The one who betrayed Jesus told them, "The man I kiss is the one you want. Grab him and don't let go."
Matthew 26:49 He immediately went to Jesus, said "Hello, teacher," and kissed him.
Matthew 26:50 Jesus said to him, "Friend, why have you come?" Then they came, grabbed Jesus, and arrested him.
Matthew 26:51 Suddenly, one with Jesus reached out, pulled out a sword, hit the high priest's servant, and cut off his ear.
Matthew 26:52 Jesus said to him, "Put your sword back in its place. Everyone who uses a sword will die by a sword."
Matthew 26:53 Do you think I cannot ask my Father for help, and he would quickly send me more than twelve legions of angels?
Matthew 26:54 But how then will what the Scriptures say come true, that it has to happen this way?
Matthew 26:55 At that time, Jesus said to the crowds, "Did you come to arrest me with swords and clubs as if I were a thief? I was with you every day teaching in the temple, and you didn't seize me."
Matthew 26:56 All this happened to fulfill what the prophets wrote. Then all the followers left him and ran away.
Matthew 26:57 Those who captured Jesus took him to Caiaphas, the high priest, where the teachers of the law and the elders were gathered.
Matthew 26:58 Peter followed him from a distance to the high priest's house, entered, and sat with the servants to see what would happen.
Matthew 26:59 The religious leaders, elders, and council looked for lies about Jesus to have a reason to kill him.
Matthew 26:60 They found none, even though many liars came. Finally, two liars came.
Matthew 26:61 He said, "This man claimed, 'I can tear down God's temple and rebuild it in three days.'"
Matthew 26:62 The high priest stood up and said to Jesus, "Aren't you going to answer? What are these accusations these people are making against you?"
Matthew 26:63 But Jesus stayed silent, and the high priest said to him, "I order you by the living God to tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God."
Matthew 26:64 Jesus told him, "You have said it. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of Power and coming on heaven's clouds."
Matthew 26:65 The high priest tore his clothes and said, "He has spoken disrespectfully against God; do we need more witnesses? You all heard the disrespect."
Matthew 26:66 What do you think? They replied, "He deserves to die."
Matthew 26:67 They spit in his face, hit him, and others slapped him with their hands.
Matthew 26:68 Tell us, you Messiah, who hit you?
Matthew 26:69 Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a girl came up to him and said, "You were also with Jesus from Galilee."
Matthew 26:70 He denied it in front of everyone, saying, "I don't know what you're talking about."
Matthew 26:71 After he went out to the entryway, another girl saw him and told the people there, "This man was with Jesus from Nazareth."
Matthew 26:72 He again denied, promising with a strong promise, "I don't know the man."
Matthew 26:73 After some time, those standing nearby came to Peter and said, "You must be one of them; your way of talking gives you away."
Matthew 26:74 He started to curse and swear, "I don't know the man." Right away, a rooster crowed.
Matthew 26:75 Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times." Then he went outside and cried hard.

Matthew 27:1 When morning came, all the leading priests and elders planned together to kill Jesus.
Matthew 27:2 After they tied him up, they took him and handed him over to the governor, Pontius Pilate.
Matthew 27:3 Judas, who had betrayed Jesus, felt sorry when he saw Jesus was going to be punished. He returned the thirty silver coins to the religious leaders and elders.
Matthew 27:4 "I have done wrong by betraying someone innocent," he said. "That's your problem," they replied.
Matthew 27:5 He threw the silver coins in the temple, left, and went to hang himself.
Matthew 27:6 The chief priests took the silver and said, "We can't put this in the treasury because it's blood money."
Matthew 27:7 They made a plan and used the money to buy the potter's field as a burial place for foreigners.
Matthew 27:8 That's why they call the field the Field of Blood to this day.
Matthew 27:9 Then what the prophet Jeremiah had said came true: "They took the thirty silver coins, the price set on him by some of the people of Israel."
Matthew 27:10 They used the money to buy the potter's field, as God told me to do.
Matthew 27:11 Jesus stood in front of the governor, who asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" Jesus replied, "You say so."
Matthew 27:12 When the leading priests and elders accused him, he did not respond.
Matthew 27:13 Pilate asked him, "Don't you hear how many things they are accusing you of?"
Matthew 27:14 He did not reply at all, which amazed the governor very much.
Matthew 27:15 At that festival, the governor usually freed a prisoner chosen by the people.
Matthew 27:16 They had a well-known prisoner named Barabbas.
Matthew 27:17 So when they all came together, Pilate asked them, "Who do you want me to set free for you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called the Christ?"
Matthew 27:18 He knew they had handed him over because they were jealous.
Matthew 27:19 When he sat on the judge's bench, his wife sent a message to him, saying, "Don't get involved with that innocent man, because I had a lot of trouble in a dream about him today."
Matthew 27:20 The religious leaders and officials convinced the people to choose Barabbas and to get rid of Jesus.
Matthew 27:21 The leader answered and asked them, "Which of the two do you want me to set free for you?" They said, "Barabbas."
Matthew 27:22 Pilate asked them, "What should I do with Jesus who is called the Christ?" They all answered, "Crucify him."
Matthew 27:23 The governor asked, "Why? What bad thing has he done?" But they shouted louder, "Crucify him."
Matthew 27:24 When Pilate realized he was getting nowhere and that a riot was starting, he washed his hands in front of the people and said, "I am not responsible for this man's death; you deal with it."
Matthew 27:25 Then all the people answered, "Let the responsibility for his death fall on us and our children."
Matthew 27:26 He set Barabbas free for them, and after he had whipped Jesus, he handed him over to be crucified.
Matthew 27:27 The governor's soldiers took Jesus to a big room and all the soldiers came together around him.
Matthew 27:28 They took off his clothes and put a red robe on him.
Matthew 27:29 After making a crown of thorns, they placed it on his head and a stick in his right hand. They knelt down in front of him and made fun of him, saying, "Hello, King of the Jews!"
Matthew 27:30 They spat on him, took the stick, and hit him on the head.
Matthew 27:31 After mocking him, they removed his robe, dressed him in his own clothes, and took him to be crucified.
Matthew 27:32 As they were leaving, they met a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry the cross.
Matthew 27:33 When they arrived at a place called Golgotha, which means a place of a skull,
Matthew 27:34 They gave him sour wine mixed with bitter herbs, and when he tasted it, he refused to drink.
Matthew 27:35 They nailed him to a cross and divided his clothes, throwing dice to decide who would get each piece. This happened to fulfill what the prophet said: "They divided my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment."
Matthew 27:36 They sat down and watched him there.
Matthew 27:37 They placed a sign above his head with the charge against him written on it: THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Matthew 27:38 Two thieves were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left.
Matthew 27:39 People walking by insulted him, shaking their heads.
Matthew 27:40 They said, "You who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself. If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross."
Matthew 27:41 The religious leaders also made fun of him, along with the teachers of the law and the older leaders, and said,
Matthew 27:42 He saved others; he cannot save himself. If he is Israel's king, let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
Matthew 27:43 He trusted in God; let God rescue him now, if He wants him: because he said, I am the Son of God.
Matthew 27:44 The robbers who were crucified with him also insulted him.
Matthew 27:45 From noon until three in the afternoon, there was darkness over the entire land.
Matthew 27:46 Around the ninth hour, Jesus shouted loudly, saying, Eli, Eli, why have you left me alone?
Matthew 27:47 Some people standing there heard this and said, "This man is calling for Elijah."
Matthew 27:48 Right away one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a stick, and offered it to him to drink.
Matthew 27:49 The others said, "Leave it, let's see if Elijah comes to save him."
Matthew 27:50 Jesus, after crying out loudly, died.
Matthew 27:51 Look, the curtain in the temple tore in two from top to bottom; the ground shook, and the rocks split.
Matthew 27:52 The graves opened, and many holy people who had died came back to life.
Matthew 27:53 They came out of the tombs after he was raised from the dead, and went into the holy city, where many people saw them.
Matthew 27:54 When the army officer and his companions guarding Jesus felt the earthquake and saw what happened, they were very afraid and said, "This really was God's Son."
Matthew 27:55 Many women were there watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
Matthew 27:56 Included were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
Matthew 27:57 When evening arrived, a wealthy man from Arimathaea called Joseph, who was also Jesus' follower, came.
Matthew 27:58 He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body. Then Pilate ordered that the body be given to him.
Matthew 27:59 When Joseph got the body, he wrapped it in a clean cloth.
Matthew 27:60 He placed it in his own new grave that he had carved from the rock, and he rolled a big stone in front of the grave's entrance, then left.
Matthew 27:61 Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting across from the tomb.
Matthew 27:62 The next day, after the preparation day, the chief priests and Pharisees met with Pilate.
Matthew 27:63 They said, "Sir, we recall that the deceiver claimed he would rise again three days after his death."
Matthew 27:64 So, make the tomb secure until the third day, so that his followers cannot come at night, take him, and tell everyone, 'He has risen from the dead.' This would make the last mistake worse than the first.
Matthew 27:65 Pilate said to them, "You have a guard; go and make it as secure as you know how."
Matthew 27:66 They went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone and placing guards.

Matthew 28:1 At the end of the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was starting, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the tomb.
Matthew 28:2 Look, there was a big earthquake because an angel from God came down from heaven, moved the stone from the entrance, and sat on it.
Matthew 28:3 His face shone like lightning, and his clothes were as white as snow.
Matthew 28:4 The guards were so afraid of him that they trembled and became like men who were dead.
Matthew 28:5 The angel said to the women, "Don't be afraid. I know you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified."
Matthew 28:6 He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see where he was lying.
Matthew 28:7 Go fast, and tell his disciples he has risen from the dead. Look, he is going ahead of you to Galilee. You will see him there. I have told you now.
Matthew 28:8 They left the tomb quickly, feeling afraid yet very happy, and ran to tell his disciples.
Matthew 28:9 As they were going to tell his disciples, Jesus met them and said, "Greetings." They came, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
Matthew 28:10 Jesus told them, "Don't be scared. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and they will see me there."
Matthew 28:11 As they were leaving, look, some of the guards went into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.
Matthew 28:12 When they met with the leaders and made their plan, they paid the soldiers a lot of money.
Matthew 28:13 Say, "His followers came at night and took him while we were sleeping."
Matthew 28:14 If the governor hears about this, we will talk to him and protect you.
Matthew 28:15 They took the money and did what they were told, and people still tell this story among the Jews today.
Matthew 28:16 Then the eleven followers went to Galilee, to a mountain where Jesus had told them to go.
Matthew 28:17 When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some were unsure.
Matthew 28:18 Jesus came and said to them, "I have been given all authority in heaven and on earth."
Matthew 28:19 Go and teach all people, baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
Matthew 28:20 Teach them to follow everything I have told you: and remember, I am with you always, to the end of time. Amen.

Mark 1:1 The start of the good news about Jesus Christ, God's Son;
Mark 1:2 The prophets wrote, "Look, I will send my messenger ahead of you to get things ready for you."
Mark 1:3 A voice cries out in the desert, "Get ready for God's coming, make a straight path for him."
Mark 1:4 John baptized in the desert and taught about baptism for forgiveness of sins.
Mark 1:5 Everyone from the area of Judaea and the city of Jerusalem went to him, and they were all baptized by him in the Jordan River while admitting their sins.
Mark 1:6 John wore camel hair clothes with a leather belt around his waist and ate locusts and wild honey.
