Mark 1:7 He preached, "Someone more powerful than me is coming after me, and I'm not even worthy to bend down and untie his shoes."
Mark 1:8 I have baptized you with water; but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.
Mark 1:9 During that time, Jesus traveled from Nazareth in Galilee and John baptized him in the Jordan River.
Mark 1:10 Right after coming up from the water, he saw the sky open, and the Spirit like a dove coming down on him.
Mark 1:11 A voice from heaven said, "You are my dear Son, and I am very pleased with you."
Mark 1:12 Right away, the spirit led him into the desert.
Mark 1:13 He was in the desert for forty days, tempted by Satan, with wild animals, and angels helped him.
Mark 1:14 After John was put in jail, Jesus went to Galilee and preached the good news about God's kingdom.
Mark 1:15 They are saying, "The right time has come, and God's kingdom is near: change your ways and trust in the good news."
Mark 1:16 As he walked by the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew throwing a net into the sea because they were fishermen.
Mark 1:17 Jesus said to them, "Follow me, and I will make you become fishers of people."
Mark 1:18 Right away they left their nets and followed him.
Mark 1:19 After he went a little further from there, he saw James, Zebedee's son, and John his brother, who were in the boat fixing their nets.
Mark 1:20 Immediately he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, and followed him.
Mark 1:21 They went to Capernaum; immediately on the Sabbath, he went into the meeting place and taught.
Mark 1:22 They were amazed at his teaching because he spoke with authority, not like the teachers of the law.
Mark 1:23 In their meeting place, there was a man with an evil spirit; and he shouted,
Mark 1:24 They said, "Leave us alone; what do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, the Holy One of God."
Mark 1:25 Jesus scolded him, saying, "Be quiet and come out of him."
Mark 1:26 When the evil spirit had hurt him and shouted loudly, it left him.
Mark 1:27 Everyone was amazed and asked each other, "What is this? A new teaching? He gives orders to evil spirits with power, and they listen to him."
Mark 1:28 Right away, his fame spread all over the area around Galilee.
Mark 1:29 Right after leaving the synagogue, they went into Simon and Andrew's house, along with James and John.
Mark 1:30 Simon's mother-in-law was in bed with a fever, and they quickly told Jesus about her.
Mark 1:31 He came, took her hand, helped her stand; at once the fever was gone, and she served them.
Mark 1:32 In the evening, when the sun set, they brought to him all who were sick and those who had demons.
Mark 1:33 Everyone in the city came together at the door.
Mark 1:34 He healed many who were sick with different diseases and drove out many demons; he did not let the demons talk because they knew who he was.
Mark 1:35 In the morning, long before sunrise, he got up, left the house, went to a quiet place, and prayed.
Mark 1:36 Simon and his companions went after him.
Mark 1:37 When they found him, they told him, "Everyone is looking for you."
Mark 1:38 He said to them, "Let's go to the nearby towns so I can preach there too; because that's why I came."
Mark 1:39 He taught in their meeting places all over Galilee and drove out demons.
Mark 1:40 A man with leprosy came to him, asking for help, knelt down, and said, "If you want to, you can make me clean."
Mark 1:41 Jesus, feeling sorry for him, reached out, touched him, and said, "I want to; be clean."
Mark 1:42 Right after he spoke, the leprosy left him, and he was clean.
Mark 1:43 He strictly told him and immediately sent him away.
Mark 1:44 He said to him, "Don't tell anyone, but go and show yourself to the priest and offer what Moses told you to for your cleansing, as proof to them."
Mark 1:45 He left and started to spread the news widely, so much that Jesus couldn't go into the town publicly but stayed in remote areas. And people came to him from everywhere.

Mark 2:1 He went back to Capernaum after a few days, and people heard that he was at home.
Mark 2:2 Right away, many people came together, so much that there was no space for them, not even near the door, and he shared God's message with them.
Mark 2:3 They came to him, carrying a man paralyzed by sickness, who was carried by four people.
Mark 2:4 When they couldn't get close to him because of the crowd, they opened up the roof above where he was. After they made a hole, they lowered the mat where the person with paralysis was lying.
Mark 2:5 When Jesus saw how much they believed, he said to the man who could not move, "Son, your sins are forgiven."
Mark 2:6 Some teachers were sitting there, thinking to themselves.
Mark 2:7 Why does this man speak such insults? Who can forgive sins except God alone?
Mark 2:8 Right away, when Jesus knew in his spirit that they were thinking this way inside, he asked them, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?"
Mark 2:9 Is it easier to tell someone with paralysis, "Your sins are forgiven," or to say, "Get up, take your mat, and walk?"
Mark 2:10 So you may know that the Son of man has the power on earth to forgive sins, he said to the sick man with paralysis.
Mark 2:11 I tell you, get up, take your bed, and go home.
Mark 2:12 Right away he got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of everyone. They were all so amazed, they praised God, saying, "We've never seen anything like this."
Mark 2:13 He went out again by the sea, and all the people came to him, and he taught them.
Mark 2:14 As he walked by, he saw Levi, Alphaeus' son, sitting at the tax booth and told him, "Follow me." Levi got up and followed him.
Mark 2:15 As Jesus was eating in his house, many tax collectors and wrongdoers were also eating with him and his followers, because there were a lot of them, and they followed him.
Mark 2:16 When the teachers of the law and Pharisees saw him eating with tax collectors and sinners, they asked his followers, "Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Mark 2:17 When Jesus heard this, he said to them, "Healthy people don't need a doctor, but sick people do. I didn't come to call the good, but sinners to change their ways."
Mark 2:18 John's followers and the Pharisees often fast, and they came and asked him, "Why do John's followers and the Pharisees fast, but your followers do not fast?"
Mark 2:19 Jesus asked them, "Can wedding guests fast while the groom is with them? As long as they have the groom, they can't fast."
Mark 2:20 But a time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them, and then they will fast on those days.
Mark 2:21 No one sews a new piece of cloth onto an old piece of clothing. If they do, the new patch pulls away from the old and the tear gets bigger.
Mark 2:22 No one puts new wine into old bottles; otherwise, the new wine will burst the bottles, the wine will spill out, and the bottles will be ruined. But new wine should be put into new bottles.
Mark 2:23 He walked through the cornfields on the Sabbath, and as they walked, his followers started to pick corn ears.
Mark 2:24 The Pharisees asked him, "Look, why do they do things on the Sabbath day that are not allowed?"
Mark 2:25 He asked them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, along with his companions?"
Mark 2:26 He entered God's house when Abiathar was high priest, ate the sacred bread, which only priests can legally eat, and shared it with his companions.
Mark 2:27 He said to them, "The sabbath was made for people, not people for the sabbath."
Mark 2:28 So, the Son of Man is also the ruler of the Sabbath.

Mark 3:1 He went into the synagogue again, and there was a man there with a crippled hand.
Mark 3:2 They watched to see if he would heal the man on the Sabbath so they could accuse him.
Mark 3:3 He said to the man with the crippled hand, "Stand up."
Mark 3:4 He asked them, "Is it right to do good on the Sabbath, or to do bad? To save a life, or to kill?" But they were silent.
Mark 3:5 When he saw them with anger, upset because their hearts were hard, he told the man, "Stretch out your hand." He did so, and his hand was healed and became like the other one.
Mark 3:6 The Pharisees left and immediately planned with the Herodians how to get rid of him.
Mark 3:7 Jesus went away to the sea with his disciples, and a large crowd from Galilee and Judea followed him.
Mark 3:8 From Jerusalem, from Idumaea, from across the Jordan, and from around Tyre and Sidon, a large crowd came to him when they heard about the amazing things he did.
Mark 3:9 He told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him to keep the crowd from crowding him.
Mark 3:10 He had healed so many people that they crowded around him, hoping to touch him, all those who were sick with diseases.
Mark 3:11 Evil spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and shouted, "You are the Son of God."
Mark 3:12 He strongly ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
Mark 3:13 He went up a mountain and called those he chose, and they went to him.
Mark 3:14 He chose twelve to stay with him and to send them out to teach.
Mark 3:15 To have the ability to cure diseases and drive out demons.
Mark 3:16 Simon was nicknamed Peter.
Mark 3:17 James, Zebedee's son, and John, James' brother, were named by him Sons of Thunder.
Mark 3:18 Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
Mark 3:19 Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him, was also there; and they entered a house.
Mark 3:20 The crowd gathered again, so much that they couldn't even eat.
Mark 3:21 When his friends heard this, they came to take control of him because they said, "He is out of his mind."
Mark 3:22 The teachers of the law who came from Jerusalem said, "He has Beelzebub, and by the ruler of demons he drives out demons."
Mark 3:23 He called them over and told them using simple stories, "How can Satan drive out Satan?"
Mark 3:24 If a kingdom fights within itself, that kingdom cannot last.
Mark 3:25 If a house is split within, that house can't last.
Mark 3:26 If Satan fights against himself and is split apart, he cannot last, but will come to an end.
Mark 3:27 No one can go into a strong man's house and take his things unless he first ties up the strong man; then he can rob his house.
Mark 3:28 I tell you the truth, all sins and insults against God will be forgiven for people.
Mark 3:29 Whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven and is at risk of never-ending punishment.
Mark 3:30 They said he has a bad spirit.
Mark 3:31 His brothers and mother came and, standing outside, they sent someone in to call him.
Mark 3:32 A crowd sat around him, and they told him, "Look, your mother and your brothers outside are looking for you."
Mark 3:33 He replied to them, "Who is my mother or my brothers?"
Mark 3:34 He looked around at those sitting nearby and said, "Look, here are my mother and my brothers!"
Mark 3:35 Anyone who does what God wants is like my brother, my sister, and my mother.

Mark 4:1 He started teaching by the sea again, and so many people came to him that he got into a boat and sat on the water, while all the people stayed on the shore.
Mark 4:2 He taught them many things using stories and explained his teachings to them.
Mark 4:3 Listen; Look, a farmer went out to plant seeds.
Mark 4:4 As he was planting seeds, some dropped on the path, and birds flew down and ate them.
Mark 4:5 Some seeds fell on rocky soil where there wasn't much dirt; they quickly grew because the soil was shallow.
Mark 4:6 When the sun rose, it burned the plant, and because the plant had no roots, it dried up.
Mark 4:7 Some seeds fell among thorns, and when the thorns grew, they choked the seeds so they produced no fruit.
Mark 4:8 Some seeds fell on good soil and grew, making more seeds. They produced thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times more.
Mark 4:9 He told them, "If anyone can hear, listen carefully."
Mark 4:10 When he was alone, the people with the twelve disciples asked him about the parable.
Mark 4:11 He told them, "You are given the knowledge of God's kingdom's secret, but to outsiders, everything is told in stories."
Mark 4:12 They can look but not see, and listen but not understand, so they won't turn back and be forgiven for their wrongs.
Mark 4:13 He asked them, "Don't you understand this story? How then will you understand any story?"
Mark 4:14 The farmer plants the message.
Mark 4:15 These are the ones near the path where the message is planted; but as soon as they hear it, Satan comes quickly and removes the message that was planted in their hearts.
Mark 4:16 These are also the ones planted on rocky soil; they hear the message and quickly accept it with joy.
Mark 4:17 They have no strong root, and only last for a while. When trouble or persecution comes because of the message, they quickly get upset.
Mark 4:18 These are the people whose seed fell among thorns; they are those who hear the message,
Mark 4:19 Worries about life, the trickery of wealth, and wanting other things crowd out God's message, making it unproductive.
Mark 4:20 These are the ones planted on good soil: they hear the message, accept it, and produce crops—some thirty times what was sown, some sixty times, and some a hundred times.
Mark 4:21 He asked them, "Do you bring a candle to hide it under a bowl or a bed? Shouldn't it be placed on a candle holder?"
Mark 4:22 Nothing hidden will stay that way; what was secret will become known.
Mark 4:23 If anyone can hear, let them listen.
Mark 4:24 He told them, "Be careful what you listen to: the way you give to others will be the way you get from others, and if you listen well, you will receive even more."
Mark 4:25 Whoever has will receive more, and whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away.
Mark 4:26 He said, “God's kingdom is like when a man plants seeds in the soil.”
Mark 4:27 He sleeps and wakes, day and night, and the seed sprouts and grows, but he doesn't know how.
Mark 4:28 The earth produces its own crops: first the plant, then the head of grain, then the fully developed grain in the head.
Mark 4:29 But when the fruit is ready, right away he uses the sickle, because it's time to harvest.
Mark 4:30 He asked, "What can we compare God's kingdom to? What example can we use to describe it?"
Mark 4:31 It is like a tiny mustard seed that, when planted in the ground, is smaller than all the other seeds in the ground.
Mark 4:32 When it's planted, it grows and becomes bigger than all the plants, and it spreads out big branches so birds can rest in its shade.
Mark 4:33 Using many stories like these, he shared his message with them, as much as they could understand.
Mark 4:34 He always taught using stories, but when alone with his followers, he explained everything.
Mark 4:35 That same day, when evening came, he said to them, "Let's go across to the other side."
Mark 4:36 After sending the crowd away, they went with him on the boat just as he was. There were also other small boats with him.
Mark 4:37 A big storm came with strong winds, and the waves hit the boat until it was full of water.
Mark 4:38 He was at the back of the boat, sleeping on a cushion. They woke him and said, "Teacher, don't you care if we drown?"
Mark 4:39 He got up, told the wind to stop, and said to the sea, "Quiet, be calm." Then the wind stopped, and it was very calm.
Mark 4:40 He asked them, "Why are you so scared? Why don't you have faith?"
Mark 4:41 They were very afraid and asked each other, "Who is this man that even the wind and the sea listen to him?"

Mark 5:1 They crossed the sea and reached the land of the Gadarenes.
Mark 5:2 As soon as he stepped out of the boat, a man with an evil spirit came from the tombs to meet him.
Mark 5:3 He lived among the graves, and no one could tie him up, even with chains.
Mark 5:4 Because he had often been tied up with chains and shackles, and he had torn the chains apart and broken the shackles, no one could control him.
Mark 5:5 He was always in the mountains and graves, night and day, yelling and hurting himself with stones.
Mark 5:6 When he saw Jesus from far away, he ran and bowed down to him.
Mark 5:7 He shouted loudly, "Jesus, Son of the highest God, what do you want with me? I beg you in God's name, don't torture me."
Mark 5:8 He told the unclean spirit, "Come out of the man."
Mark 5:9 He asked him, "What is your name?" He replied, "My name is Legion, because there are many of us."
Mark 5:10 He begged him a lot not to make them leave the area.
Mark 5:11 Near the mountains there was a large group of pigs eating.
Mark 5:12 All the demons begged him, "Please send us into the pigs, so we can go into them."
Mark 5:13 Immediately, Jesus allowed it. The evil spirits left and went into the pigs. The large group of pigs rushed down the steep hill into the water (there were about two thousand), and they drowned in the water.
Mark 5:14 The people taking care of the pigs ran away and reported this in the town and the countryside. Then everyone came to see what had happened.
Mark 5:15 They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by a demon, who had many inside him, sitting, wearing clothes, and in his clear mind; and they were scared.
Mark 5:16 The people who saw it explained what happened to the man with the demon and about the pigs.
Mark 5:17 They started to ask him to leave their area.
Mark 5:18 When he got into the boat, the man who had been controlled by the evil spirit begged to go with him.
Mark 5:19 However, Jesus did not allow him, but said to him, "Go back to your friends, and tell them about the great things God has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you."
Mark 5:20 He left and started to tell everyone in Decapolis about the great things Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.
Mark 5:21 When Jesus went back by boat to the other side, many people came to him, and he was near the sea.
Mark 5:22 Look, one of the synagogue leaders named Jairus comes, and when he sees Jesus, he falls at his feet.
Mark 5:23 He begged him earnestly, "My young daughter is very sick and close to death. Please come and touch her so she can get better and live."
Mark 5:24 Jesus went with the man, and many people followed and crowded around him.
Mark 5:25 A certain woman had been bleeding for twelve years.
Mark 5:26 She had endured a lot from many doctors, spent all her money, and was not getting better but instead became worse.
Mark 5:27 When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
Mark 5:28 She thought, "If I can just touch his clothes, I will be healed."
Mark 5:29 Right away her bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was cured of her illness.
Mark 5:30 Jesus immediately felt power had left him, turned around in the crowd, and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"
Mark 5:31 His followers asked him, "You see the crowd pressing around you, and yet you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
Mark 5:32 He looked around to see the woman who had done this.
Mark 5:33 The woman, scared and shaking and knowing what had happened to her, came, knelt down before him, and told him the whole truth.
Mark 5:34 He told her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you; go in peace, and be free from your sickness."
Mark 5:35 While he was still talking, someone from the synagogue leader's house came and said, "Your daughter is dead; why bother the Teacher anymore?"
Mark 5:36 As soon as Jesus heard the news, he told the synagogue leader, "Don't be scared, just have faith."
Mark 5:37 He allowed only Peter, James, and John, James's brother, to follow him.
Mark 5:38 He came to the leader's house of the place of worship and saw the commotion, and people crying and wailing a lot.
Mark 5:39 When he came in, he asked them, "Why are you making so much noise and crying? The girl is not dead, but sleeping."
Mark 5:40 They laughed at him. But after sending everyone out, he took the girl's parents and his companions, and went to where the girl was lying.
Mark 5:41 He took the girl's hand and said to her, "Talitha cumi," which means, "Girl, I tell you, get up."
Mark 5:42 Right away the girl got up and walked because she was twelve years old. Everyone was amazed with a huge amazement.
Mark 5:43 He strictly told them to keep it secret and ordered that they give her something to eat.

Mark 6:1 He left that place, went to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.
Mark 6:2 When the Sabbath came, he started to teach in the synagogue. Many who heard him were amazed and asked, "Where did this man get these things?" and "What kind of wisdom has been given to him that he can do such great deeds?"
Mark 6:3 Isn't this the carpenter, Mary's son, and the brother of James, Joses, Juda, and Simon? Aren't his sisters here with us? They were upset by him.
Mark 6:4 Jesus told them, "A prophet is respected everywhere except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own home."
Mark 6:5 He could not do any great deeds there, except he touched a few sick people with his hands and healed them.
Mark 6:6 He was amazed at their lack of faith. He traveled through the towns, teaching.
Mark 6:7 He called the twelve to him and started to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over evil spirits.
Mark 6:8 He told them to take nothing for their trip, except a walking stick; no bag, no food, no money in their wallet.
Mark 6:9 Wear sandals, but don't wear two coats.
Mark 6:10 He told them, "Whenever you go into a house, stay there until you leave that place."
Mark 6:11 If anyone does not welcome you or listen to you, when you leave there, shake off the dust under your feet as a warning to them. Truly, I tell you, it will be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah on judgment day than for that town.
Mark 6:12 They left and told people to change their ways.
Mark 6:13 They forced out many demons, put oil on many sick people, and healed them.
Mark 6:14 King Herod heard about Jesus because his name was well known. Herod thought that John the Baptist had come back to life, which is why such great miracles were happening through Jesus.
Mark 6:15 Some people said, "It is Elijah." And others said, "It is a prophet, or one of the prophets."
Mark 6:16 When Herod heard about it, he said, "It's John, whom I cut off his head; he has come back to life."
Mark 6:17 Herod had John arrested and put in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, since Herod had married her.
Mark 6:18 John told Herod, "It's not right for you to be with your brother's wife."
Mark 6:19 Herodias was angry with him and wanted to kill him, but she couldn't.
Mark 6:20 Herod was afraid of John because he knew he was a good and holy man, so he protected him. When he listened to John, he often followed his advice and enjoyed listening to him.
Mark 6:21 When a good day came, Herod had a dinner on his birthday for his important guests, military leaders, and the top people of Galilee.
Mark 6:22 When Herodias's daughter came in and danced, making Herod and his guests happy, the king told the young woman, "Ask me for anything you want, and I'll give it to you."
Mark 6:23 He promised her, "Whatever you ask of me, I will give it to you, up to half of my kingdom."
Mark 6:24 She went and asked her mother, "What should I ask for?" Her mother replied, "Ask for the head of John the Baptist."
Mark 6:25 She quickly went to the king and asked, "I want you to give me John the Baptist's head on a platter right away."
Mark 6:26 The king was very sorry; but because of his promise and the guests with him, he would not say no to her.
Mark 6:27 The king quickly sent an executioner to cut off his head and bring it. He did this in the prison.
Mark 6:28 They brought his head on a platter, gave it to the girl, and she gave it to her mother.
Mark 6:29 When his followers found out, they came, picked up his body, and placed it in a tomb.
Mark 6:30 The apostles came to Jesus and told him everything they had done and taught.
Mark 6:31 He told them, "Go alone to a quiet place and rest for a bit, because there were so many people coming and going, they didn't even have time to eat."
Mark 6:32 They left for a quiet place by boat, alone.
Mark 6:33 The people saw them leaving, and many recognized him. They ran on foot from all the cities, got there ahead of them, and gathered around him.
Mark 6:34 When Jesus came out, he saw many people and felt sorry for them because they were like sheep without a shepherd, so he started to teach them many things.
Mark 6:35 When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him and said, "This place is empty, and it's already very late."
Mark 6:36 Tell them to leave so they can go to the nearby countryside and towns, and buy their own food, because they have nothing to eat.
Mark 6:37 He replied, "Give them something to eat." They asked him, "Should we go and spend two hundred coins on bread to feed them?"
Mark 6:38 He asks them, "How many bread loaves do you have? Go and check." After checking, they answer, "Five, and two fish."
Mark 6:39 He told them to have everyone sit in groups on the green grass.
Mark 6:40 They sat in groups, in hundreds and fifties.
Mark 6:41 He took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, gave thanks, broke the bread, and gave it to his disciples to give to the people. He also shared the two fish with everyone.
Mark 6:42 Everyone ate and was satisfied.
Mark 6:43 They picked up twelve baskets full of the broken pieces and the fish.
Mark 6:44 About five thousand men ate the bread.
Mark 6:45 Right away, he made his followers get into the boat and go ahead to the other side toward Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd away.
Mark 6:46 After he sent them off, he went up a mountain to pray.
Mark 6:47 When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
Mark 6:48 He saw them struggling to row because the wind was against them. Near the fourth watch of the night, he came to them, walking on the sea, and was about to pass by them.
Mark 6:49 When they saw him walking on the sea, they thought he was a ghost and shouted.
Mark 6:50 They all saw him and were scared. But he quickly spoke to them and said, "Be happy: it's me; don't be afraid."
Mark 6:51 He got into the boat with them, and the wind stopped; they were extremely surprised and amazed.
Mark 6:52 They did not understand the miracle of the bread because their hearts were hard.
Mark 6:53 After they crossed over, they arrived in the land of Gennesaret and approached the shore.
Mark 6:54 As soon as they got off the boat, they recognized him immediately.
Mark 6:55 They ran throughout all the area and started to bring the sick on their beds to wherever they heard he was.
Mark 6:56 Wherever he went—into towns, cities, or the countryside—they placed the ill people in the streets and asked him to let them touch just the edge of his clothes, and everyone who touched him was healed.

Mark 7:1 The Pharisees and some teachers of the Law who were from Jerusalem gathered around him.
Mark 7:2 When they saw some of his followers eating bread with dirty hands, they criticized them.
Mark 7:3 The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they often wash their hands, following the elders' tradition.
Mark 7:4 When they return from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. They also follow many other rules, like washing cups, pots, metal bowls, and tables.
Mark 7:5 The Pharisees and teachers of the law asked Jesus, "Why don't your disciples follow the elders' traditions, but eat bread with dirty hands?"
Mark 7:6 He replied, "Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you fakes, as it is written, 'These people show me respect with their words, but their hearts are not with me.'"
Mark 7:7 They worship me for nothing, teaching human rules as if they were God's teachings.
Mark 7:8 You ignore God's command to follow human traditions, like washing pots and cups, and you do many other similar things.
Mark 7:9 He told them, "You completely ignore God's command to follow your own tradition."
Mark 7:10 Moses said, Respect your father and mother; and anyone who speaks badly of their father or mother must be put to death.
Mark 7:11 But you say, if someone tells their father or mother, 'It is Corban'—which means 'a gift'—so you cannot benefit from me; then they don’t have to help.
Mark 7:12 And you don't let him do anything for his father or mother anymore.
Mark 7:13 You make God's word useless with your tradition that you've passed down, and you do many things like that.
Mark 7:14 When he gathered everyone around, he told them, "Listen to me, all of you, and understand:"
Mark 7:15 Nothing outside a person can make them unclean by going into them. Rather, it is what comes out of a person that makes them unclean.
Mark 7:16 If anyone can hear, let them listen.
Mark 7:17 After he went into the house away from the crowd, his followers asked him about the story.
Mark 7:18 He asked them, "Do you also not understand? Don't you realize that nothing entering a person from outside can make them unclean?"
Mark 7:19 It doesn't go into his heart but into his stomach and then out of the body, cleaning out all foods.
Mark 7:20 He said, What comes out of a person is what makes them unclean.
Mark 7:21 From inside, from people's hearts, come bad thoughts, cheating in marriage, sexual sins, and killings.
Mark 7:22 Stealing, wanting what others have, bad behavior, lying, inappropriate desires, looking to harm others, speaking against God, thinking too highly of oneself, acting without sense.
Mark 7:23 All these bad things start inside a person and make them unclean.
Mark 7:24 He got up from there, went to the area near Tyre and Sidon, went into a house, and did not want anyone to know it, but he could not stay hidden.
Mark 7:25 A woman whose daughter had an evil spirit heard about him, went to him, and knelt down.
Mark 7:26 The woman was Greek, from Syria-Phoenicia. She begged Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
Mark 7:27 Jesus said to her, "Let the children eat first; it's not right to take the children's food and give it to the dogs."
Mark 7:28 She replied, "Yes, God, even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
Mark 7:29 He told her, "Because of your words, go; the evil spirit has left your daughter."
Mark 7:30 When she got home, she saw that the demon had left, and her daughter was lying on the bed.
Mark 7:31 Leaving the region of Tyre and Sidon, he went to the Sea of Galilee, passing through the area of Decapolis.
Mark 7:32 They brought to him a person who was deaf and had trouble speaking, and they asked him to touch him.
Mark 7:33 He took the man away from the crowd, put his fingers in the man's ears, spit, and touched the man's tongue.
Mark 7:34 Looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, "Ephphatha," which means, "Be opened."
Mark 7:35 Right away his ears could hear, his tongue was freed, and he spoke clearly.
Mark 7:36 He told them not to tell anyone, but the more he insisted, the more they spread the news.
Mark 7:37 They were extremely amazed and said, "He does everything well: he makes the deaf hear and the mute speak."

Mark 8:1 During that time, there was a large crowd with nothing to eat, so Jesus called his followers to him and said to them,
Mark 8:2 I feel sorry for all these people because they have been with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
Mark 8:3 If I send them home hungry, they might collapse on the way, because some of them have come from a long distance.
Mark 8:4 And his followers asked him, "Where can anyone get enough bread to feed these people in this remote place?"
Mark 8:5 He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven."
Mark 8:6 He told the people to sit on the ground. He took the seven loaves, thanked God, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to give to the people; and the disciples gave the bread to the people.
Mark 8:7 They had a few little fish; he gave thanks for them and told them to put these before the people too.
Mark 8:8 So they ate, were satisfied, and gathered seven baskets of leftover pieces.
Mark 8:9 About four thousand people had eaten, and he sent them away.
Mark 8:10 Right away he got into a boat with his followers and went to the area of Dalmanutha.
Mark 8:11 The Pharisees came out and started to question him, wanting a sign from heaven to test him.
Mark 8:12 He sighed deeply and said, "Why does this generation look for a sign? Truly, I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation."
Mark 8:13 He left them, got back into the boat, and went to the opposite shore.
Mark 8:14 The followers had forgotten to bring bread and had only one loaf with them on the boat.
Mark 8:15 He warned them, "Be careful and watch out for the Pharisees' yeast and Herod's yeast."
Mark 8:16 They talked to each other, saying, "It's because we don't have bread."
Mark 8:17 When Jesus realized this, he asked them, "Why are you worried about not having bread? Don't you see or understand? Is your heart still hard?"
Mark 8:18 You have eyes but don't see, and ears but don't hear? Don't you remember?
Mark 8:19 When I divided the five loaves for five thousand people, how many baskets of leftover pieces did you gather? They answered him, "Twelve."
Mark 8:20 When you fed the four thousand, how many full baskets of leftovers did you gather? They said, "Seven."
Mark 8:21 He asked them, "Why don't you understand?"
Mark 8:22 He came to Bethsaida; people brought a blind man to him and asked him to touch the man.
Mark 8:23 He took the blind man's hand, guided him out of the town, spat on his eyes, put his hands on him, and asked if he could see anything.
Mark 8:24 He looked up and said, "I see people like walking trees."
Mark 8:25 Then he put his hands on the man's eyes again, and told him to look up. The man's sight returned, and he could see everyone clearly.
Mark 8:26 He sent him home with the instruction, "Don't go into the town or tell anyone there."
Mark 8:27 Jesus and his followers went to the towns of Caesarea Philippi. On the way, he asked them, "Who do people say I am?"
Mark 8:28 They replied, "John the Baptist; but some say Elijah; and others, one of the prophets."
Mark 8:29 He asks them, "But who do you say I am?" And Peter answers, "You are the Christ."
Mark 8:30 He told them not to tell anyone about him.
Mark 8:31 He started to teach them that the Son of Man had to go through a lot of suffering, be turned away by the elders, the main priests, and the writers, be killed, and then come back to life after three days.
Mark 8:32 He spoke those words clearly. Peter took him aside and started to correct him.
Mark 8:33 When he turned around and saw his followers, he scolded Peter, saying, "Get away from me, Satan; you do not care about what God wants, but what people want."
Mark 8:34 When he gathered the crowd and his students, he told them, "If anyone wants to follow me, they must forget about their own desires, carry their own cross, and come with me."
Mark 8:35 Anyone who wants to save their life will lose it, but anyone who loses their life for me and the good news will save it.
Mark 8:36 What good is it for someone to have everything in the world but lose their own life?
Mark 8:37 What can a person offer to buy back their life?
Mark 8:38 Anyone who is ashamed of me and my words in this unfaithful and sinful time, I, the Son of Man, will also be ashamed of when I come with the glory of my Father and the holy angels.

Mark 9:1 He told them, "Truly, I tell you, some standing here won't die before they see God's kingdom come with power."
Mark 9:2 Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a tall mountain alone. There, he changed in appearance before them.
Mark 9:3 His clothes became very bright and white, whiter than anyone in the world could make them.
Mark 9:4 Elias and Moses appeared to them and were talking with Jesus.
Mark 9:5 Peter replied to Jesus, "Teacher, it's good that we are here. Let's make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
Mark 9:6 He did not know what to say because they were very afraid.
Mark 9:7 A cloud covered them, and a voice from the cloud said, "This is my dear Son: listen to him."
Mark 9:8 Suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one else except Jesus with them.
Mark 9:9 As they came down from the mountain, he told them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
Mark 9:10 They kept those words to themselves, wondering what "rising from the dead" meant.
Mark 9:11 They asked him, "Why do the teachers say that Elijah must come first?"
Mark 9:12 He replied, "Elijah truly comes first to restore everything; but it is written that the Son of Man must endure many hardships and be ignored."
Mark 9:13 I tell you, Elijah has already come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.
Mark 9:14 When he came to his disciples, he saw a large crowd around them and the scribes asking them questions.
Mark 9:15 Right away, when the people saw him, they were very surprised and ran up to greet him.
Mark 9:16 He asked the teachers, "What are you discussing with them?"
Mark 9:17 Someone in the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought you my son who has a mute spirit."
Mark 9:18 Wherever it takes him, it throws him into fits. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes weak. I asked your followers to drive it out, but they couldn't.
Mark 9:19 He replied, "You untrusting people, how much longer must I stay with you? How much longer must I put up with you? Bring the boy to me."
Mark 9:20 They brought the boy to Jesus, and as soon as the evil spirit saw Jesus, it threw the boy into a fit. He fell to the ground, rolling around and foaming at the mouth.
Mark 9:21 He asked his father, "How long has he had this?" His father replied, "Since he was a child."
Mark 9:22 Many times it has thrown him into the fire and water to kill him. But if you can do anything, have pity on us and help.
Mark 9:23 Jesus told him, "If you can believe, everything is possible for the one who believes."
Mark 9:24 Right away, the child's father cried out with tears, "God, I believe; help me with my doubt."
Mark 9:25 When Jesus saw the crowd running to join them, he told off the evil spirit, saying, "You silent and hearingless spirit, I command you, come out of him and never go back into him again."
Mark 9:26 The spirit screamed, hurt him badly, and left him. He looked like he was dead, so many people said, "He is dead."
Mark 9:27 Jesus took his hand, helped him up, and he stood.
Mark 9:28 When he entered the house, his followers asked him in private, "Why couldn't we drive it out?"
Mark 9:29 He told them, "This kind can only go out through prayer and fasting."
Mark 9:30 They left that place, traveled through Galilee, and he didn't want anyone to know about it.
Mark 9:31 He taught his followers, telling them, "The Son of Man will be handed over to people, and they will kill him; but after he is dead, he will rise on the third day."
Mark 9:32 But they did not understand what he meant, and were scared to ask him.
Mark 9:33 He came to Capernaum, and in the house, he asked them, "What were you arguing about on the road?"
Mark 9:34 But they kept quiet because on the way they had argued about who should be the most important.
Mark 9:35 He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, "If anyone wants to be first, they must be last of all and serve everyone."
Mark 9:36 He picked up a child and placed him among them. Holding him in his arms, he said to them,
Mark 9:37 Anyone who welcomes a child like this because of me is also welcoming me. And anyone who welcomes me is not just welcoming me but also the one who sent me.
Mark 9:38 John replied, "Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons using your name, and he doesn't join us. So we stopped him because he doesn't join us."
Mark 9:39 Jesus said, Do not stop him, because if someone does a miracle in my name, he will not easily say bad things about me.
Mark 9:40 Anyone who is not against us is with us.
Mark 9:41 Anyone who gives you a drink of water because you follow Christ will truly not miss out on their reward.
Mark 9:42 Whoever hurts one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for them to have a heavy stone tied around their neck and to be thrown into the sea.
Mark 9:43 If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It's better to live with one hand than to have two hands and go to hell, where the fire never goes out.
Mark 9:44 Their worms never die, and the fire never goes out.
Mark 9:45 If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off: it is better for you to enter life with a limp than to have two feet and be thrown into hell, where the fire never goes out.
Mark 9:46 Their worms never die, and the fire never goes out.
Mark 9:47 If your eye causes you to sin, take it out. It is better to go into God's kingdom with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell fire.
Mark 9:48 Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not put out.
Mark 9:49 Everyone will be purified with fire, and every offering will be seasoned with salt.
Mark 9:50 Salt is good, but if the salt becomes tasteless, how can you make it salty again? Keep salt within you and live peacefully with each other.

Mark 10:1 He got up from there and went to the region of Judea across the Jordan. People came to him again, and as usual, he taught them.
Mark 10:2 The Pharisees went to him and asked, "Is it okay for a man to divorce his wife?" to test him.
Mark 10:3 He replied and asked them, "What did Moses tell you to do?"
Mark 10:4 They said, Moses allowed to write a divorce paper, and to send her away.
Mark 10:5 Jesus answered them, "Because your hearts were hard, he gave you this rule."
Mark 10:6 Since the start of creation, God made them as man and woman.
Mark 10:7 A man will leave his father and mother and be united with his wife.
Mark 10:8 The two will become one body, so they are not two anymore, but one body.
Mark 10:9 So what God has united, let no one separate.
Mark 10:10 In the house, his disciples questioned him once more about that topic.
Mark 10:11 He tells them, "Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman is unfaithful to her."
Mark 10:12 If a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she cheats on him.
Mark 10:13 People brought little children to Jesus so he could touch them. But his followers scolded those who brought the children.
Mark 10:14 But when Jesus saw this, he was very upset and said to them, "Let the children come to me, do not stop them: for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these."
Mark 10:15 Truly I tell you, anyone who doesn't accept the kingdom of God like a small child will not get in.
Mark 10:16 He picked them up, touched them with his hands, and gave them his blessing.
Mark 10:17 As he started on his way, someone ran up, knelt before him, and asked, "Good Teacher, what must I do to get eternal life?"
Mark 10:18 Jesus asked him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone."
Mark 10:19 You know the commands: Do not cheat on your partner, do not kill, do not steal, do not lie, do not cheat others, respect your father and mother.
Mark 10:20 He replied, "Teacher, I have followed all these since I was young."
Mark 10:21 Jesus looked at him with love and said, "You're missing one thing: go, sell everything you own, and give the money to the poor. Then you will have riches in heaven. Come, carry the cross, and follow me."
Mark 10:22 He felt sad when he heard this and left feeling upset because he owned a lot.
Mark 10:23 Jesus looked around and said to his followers, "How difficult it is for those with wealth to enter God's kingdom!"
Mark 10:24 The followers were amazed at his words. But Jesus spoke again, and said to them, "Children, how difficult it is for those who rely on their wealth to get into God's kingdom!"
Mark 10:25 It's simpler for a camel to pass through a needle's eye than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom.
Mark 10:26 They were extremely surprised and asked each other, "Then who can be saved?"
Mark 10:27 Jesus looked at them and said, "For people it's impossible, but not for God; with God all things are possible."
Mark 10:28 Then Peter started to say to him, "Look, we have left everything and followed you."
Mark 10:29 Jesus replied, "I tell you the truth, no one who has left home, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or fields for me and the good news.
Mark 10:30 He will get a hundred times more now in this time: homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields, along with troubles; and in the future world, eternal life.
Mark 10:31 Many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.
Mark 10:32 They were traveling to Jerusalem. Jesus was leading them. They were amazed and scared as they followed him. He gathered the twelve disciples and started to explain what would happen to him.
Mark 10:33 Look, we are going to Jerusalem; and the Son of man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law; they will find him guilty of death and will hand him over to the foreigners.
Mark 10:34 They will make fun of him, whip him, spit on him, and kill him. But on the third day, he will come back to life.
Mark 10:35 James and John, Zebedee's sons, came to Jesus and said, "Teacher, we want you to do whatever we ask."
Mark 10:36 He asked them, "What do you want me to do for you?"
Mark 10:37 They asked him, "Let us sit with you in your glory, one on your right side and the other on your left side."
Mark 10:38 But Jesus told them, You don't understand what you're asking. Can you drink the cup I drink? And be baptized with the baptism I am baptized with?
Mark 10:39 They said to him, "We can." And Jesus told them, "You will truly drink the cup I drink from; and you will be baptized with the baptism I am baptized with."
Mark 10:40 But to sit at my right or left side isn't for me to give; it will be given to those it's ready for.
Mark 10:41 When the ten other disciples heard this, they became very upset with James and John.
Mark 10:42 Jesus called them over and said, "You know that the ones who are considered rulers over the people have power over them, and the important people have authority over them."
Mark 10:43 However, among you it should be different: whoever wants to be important must serve you.
Mark 10:44 Anyone who wants to be the most important among you must serve everyone.
Mark 10:45 Even the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life to save many people.
Mark 10:46 They arrived at Jericho. As he was leaving Jericho with his followers and many people, a blind man named Bartimaeus, Timaeus's son, was sitting by the road asking for money.
Mark 10:47 When he heard it was Jesus from Nazareth, he started shouting, "Jesus, son of David, please have mercy on me."
Mark 10:48 Many people told him to be quiet, but he shouted even louder, "Son of David, have mercy on me."
Mark 10:49 Jesus stopped and told them to call the man. They called the blind man, saying, "Cheer up, get up; he is calling you."
Mark 10:50 He threw off his coat, got up, and went to Jesus.
Mark 10:51 Jesus answered, "What do you want me to do for you?" The blind man said, "I want to see again."
Mark 10:52 Jesus said to him, "Go; your faith has healed you." Right away, he could see, and he followed Jesus on the path.

Mark 11:1 When they got close to Jerusalem, near Bethphage and Bethany, by the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his followers.
Mark 11:2 He says to them, "Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter, you will see a young donkey tied up that no one has ridden. Untie it and bring it here."
Mark 11:3 If anyone asks you why you are doing this, tell them God needs it, and he will send it right away.
Mark 11:4 They went, found the young donkey tied up outside by a door at a crossroads, and untied it.
Mark 11:5 Some people standing there asked them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"
Mark 11:6 They told them just as Jesus had instructed, and they let them go.
Mark 11:7 They brought the young donkey to Jesus, put their clothes on it, and he sat on it.
Mark 11:8 Many people spread their clothes on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and scattered them on the road.
Mark 11:9 Those who were ahead and those who followed shouted, "Hosanna; blessed is the one who comes in God's name."
Mark 11:10 Let us praise the kingdom of our father David, that comes in God's name: Hosanna in the highest.
Mark 11:11 Jesus went into Jerusalem and the temple. After looking at everything and evening came, he left for Bethany with his twelve disciples.
Mark 11:12 The next day, after they left Bethany, he felt hungry.
Mark 11:13 Seeing a fig tree with leaves from a distance, he went to see if he could find any fruit on it. But when he got there, he found only leaves, because it was not the season for figs.
Mark 11:14 Jesus replied, "From now on, no one will eat your fruit again." His disciples heard this.
Mark 11:15 They came to Jerusalem: Jesus entered the temple and started to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He flipped over the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves.
Mark 11:16 He did not allow anyone to carry items through the temple.
Mark 11:17 He taught them, "Isn't it written, my house will be known as a place of prayer for all nations? But you have turned it into a hideout for thieves."
Mark 11:18 The teachers of the law and the leading priests heard what Jesus said and looked for a way to kill him. They were afraid of him because everyone was amazed at his teaching.
Mark 11:19 When evening came, he left the city.
Mark 11:20 In the morning, when they walked by, they saw that the fig tree had withered from the roots.
Mark 11:21 Peter remembered and said to him, "Teacher, look, the fig tree you cursed has withered."
Mark 11:22 Jesus replied, "Trust in God."
Mark 11:23 I tell you the truth, anyone who tells this mountain to move and fall into the sea, and does not doubt but believes what they say will happen, it will be done for them.
Mark 11:24 So I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe you have received it, and it will be yours.
Mark 11:25 When you stand and pray, forgive anyone you have something against, so that God in heaven may forgive your wrongs.
Mark 11:26 If you don't forgive others, God in heaven won't forgive your wrongs.
Mark 11:27 They return to Jerusalem: and while he is walking in the temple, the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the elders come to him.
Mark 11:28 Tell him, "What authority allows you to do these actions? And who gave you this authority?"
Mark 11:29 Jesus replied, "I have one question for you. Answer me, and I'll tell you by what authority I do these things."
Mark 11:30 Was John's baptism from God or from people? Tell me.
Mark 11:31 They thought to themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will ask, 'Then why didn't you believe him?'"
Mark 11:32 But if we say, "From people," they are afraid of the crowd, because everyone believed John was truly a prophet.
Mark 11:33 They replied to Jesus, "We don't know." And Jesus said to them, "Then I won't tell you with what authority I do these things."

Mark 12:1 He started to tell them stories. A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, made a pit for the grape juice, built a watchtower, rented it to farmers, and then he went away to another place.
Mark 12:2 During the right time, he sent a worker to the farmers to collect some of the vineyard's fruit from them.
Mark 12:3 They grabbed him, hit him, and sent him away with nothing.
Mark 12:4 He sent them another servant, but they threw stones at him, hurt his head, and sent him away badly treated.
Mark 12:5 He sent another, whom they killed, and many more, beating some and killing others.
Mark 12:6 Still having one beloved son, he sent him to them last, thinking, They will respect my son.
Mark 12:7 But the farmers said to each other, "This is the heir; come, let's kill him, and the inheritance will be ours."
Mark 12:8 They seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
Mark 12:9 What will the owner of the vineyard do then? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.
Mark 12:10 Have you not read this part of the Scripture: The stone the builders did not want is now the most important stone.
Mark 12:11 This was what God did, and it is amazing to us.
Mark 12:12 They tried to arrest him but were afraid of the crowd because they knew the story was about them, so they left him and went away.
Mark 12:13 Some Pharisees and Herodians were sent to trap him by what he said.
Mark 12:14 When they arrived, they said to him, "Teacher, we know you are honest and don't favor anyone, because you don't judge by appearances but teach God's way truthfully: Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
Mark 12:15 Should we pay, or shouldn't we? But knowing they were fake, he said to them, "Why are you testing me? Show me a coin so I can look at it."
Mark 12:16 They brought it to him. He asked them, "Whose picture and title is this?" They answered, "Caesar's."
Mark 12:17 Jesus replied, "Give to the leader what belongs to the leader, and to God what belongs to God." They were amazed at him.
Mark 12:18 The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and asked him, saying,
Mark 12:19 Teacher, Moses told us that if a man dies and leaves a wife but no children, his brother should marry the widow and have children for his brother.
Mark 12:20 There were seven brothers. The first married but died without having children.
Mark 12:21 The second brother married her and then died, leaving no children; and the same happened with the third brother.
Mark 12:22 All seven men married her and had no children. Finally, the woman also died.
Mark 12:23 In the resurrection, when they come back to life, whose wife will she be among them? Because all seven were married to her.
Mark 12:24 Jesus answered them, "Aren't you mistaken because you don’t know the scriptures or God's power?"
Mark 12:25 When they rise from the dead, they don't marry or are married off; they are like the angels in heaven.
Mark 12:26 About the dead, that they come back to life: haven't you read in Moses' book, how in the bush God spoke to him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
Mark 12:27 He is not the God of those who are dead, but the God of those who are alive; you are making a big mistake.
Mark 12:28 A teacher of the law came forward. After hearing them discuss, and noticing Jesus had given good answers, he asked, "What is the most important commandment?"
Mark 12:29 Jesus replied, "The most important commandment is, 'Listen, Israel: God is our only Lord.'"
Mark 12:30 You should love God with all your heart, all your soul, all your mind, and all your strength: this is the first commandment.
Mark 12:31 The second command is this: Love your neighbor as yourself. No other commandment is greater than these.
Mark 12:32 The teacher said to him, "Good, Teacher, you have spoken the truth: there is only one God, and no one else but Him."
Mark 12:33 To love God with all your heart, mind, soul, and strength, and to love others as you love yourself, is more important than any burnt offerings and sacrifices.
Mark 12:34 When Jesus saw he answered wisely, he said to him, "You are close to God's kingdom." After that, no one dared to ask him more questions.
Mark 12:35 Jesus replied while teaching in the temple, "Why do the teachers say that the Messiah is David's son?"
Mark 12:36 David himself, inspired by the Holy Spirit, said, "God told my lord, 'Sit at my right side until I make your enemies a place to rest your feet.'"
Mark 12:37 David himself calls him Lord; so how is he his son? And the people liked listening to him.
Mark 12:38 He taught them, "Be careful of the teachers of the law who like to wear long robes and enjoy being greeted with respect in the marketplaces."
Mark 12:39 The best seats in the meeting places, and the places of honor at banquets:
Mark 12:40 They eat up widows' homes and pretend to be pious with long prayers; they will face stricter punishment.
Mark 12:41 Jesus sat opposite the money box and watched how people put money into it; many rich people gave a lot.
Mark 12:42 A poor widow came and put in two small coins, worth a little.
Mark 12:43 He called his followers and told them, "I truly tell you, this poor widow has given more than anyone else who has donated to the treasury."
Mark 12:44 Everyone else gave from their wealth, but she, in her poverty, gave everything she had to live on.

Mark 13:1 As he left the temple, one of his disciples said to him, "Teacher, look at the size of these stones and these buildings!"
Mark 13:2 Jesus answered him, "Do you see these large buildings? Not one stone will be left on top of another; every one will be thrown down."
Mark 13:3 As he was sitting on the Mount of Olives across from the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew spoke to him in private.
Mark 13:4 Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that all these things are about to be completed?
Mark 13:5 Jesus replied to them, saying, "Be careful so that no one tricks you."
Mark 13:6 Many will come using my name, claiming they are Christ, and will trick many people.
Mark 13:7 When you hear about wars and talk of wars, don't be worried: these things must happen, but it's not the end yet.
Mark 13:8 One country will fight against another, and one kingdom against another. There will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and troubles. These are the first signs of suffering.
Mark 13:9 Be careful: people will hand you over to local courts; you will be whipped in synagogues; and you will stand before leaders and rulers because of me, to prove them wrong.
Mark 13:10 The good news has to be shared with all countries first.
Mark 13:11 When they take you and turn you over, don't worry ahead of time about what to say. Just say what is given to you at that time, because it's not you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
Mark 13:12 Now a brother will betray his brother to death, and a father his son; children will turn against their parents and have them killed.
Mark 13:13 Everyone will hate you because of me, but if you keep going until the end, you will be saved.
Mark 13:14 When you see the terrible thing that causes destruction, as the prophet Daniel talked about, in a place it should not be, (the reader should pay attention,) then those in Judea should run away to the hills.
Mark 13:15 If you are on the roof, do not go down into the house or enter to take anything out.
Mark 13:16 And let the person in the field not go back to get their coat.
Mark 13:17 But it will be hard for pregnant women and those nursing babies in those days!
Mark 13:18 Pray that you don't have to run away during winter.
Mark 13:19 In those days, there will be suffering unlike anything since God created the world, and there will never be anything like it again.
Mark 13:20 If God had not made those days shorter, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he has picked, he has made the days shorter.
Mark 13:21 If anyone tells you, "Look, here's Christ," or "There he is," don't believe it.
Mark 13:22 Fake saviors and false prophets will appear and perform miracles and wonders to trick people, if they could, even those chosen by God.
Mark 13:23 Be careful: I have already told you everything.
Mark 13:24 But in those days, after the suffering ends, the sun will become dark, and the moon will not shine.
Mark 13:25 The stars from the sky will fall, and the forces in the sky will be shaken.
Mark 13:26 People will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.
Mark 13:27 Then he will send his angels to collect his chosen people from everywhere on earth to the farthest parts of heaven.
Mark 13:28 Learn from the story of the fig tree: When its branch gets soft and grows leaves, you know that summer is close.
Mark 13:29 In the same way, when you see these things happening, understand that it is close, right at the door.
Mark 13:30 I truly tell you, this generation will not disappear until all these things happen.
Mark 13:31 The sky and the earth will disappear, but my words will never go away.
Mark 13:32 No one knows the day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, only the Father.
Mark 13:33 Be careful, stay alert, and pray, because you do not know when the time will come.
Mark 13:34 The Son of Man is like someone who went on a long trip, left his home, gave his workers power, each one a job, and told the doorkeeper to stay alert.
Mark 13:35 Stay alert, because you don't know when the owner of the house will come back; it could be in the evening, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.
Mark 13:36 Be careful that he doesn't come suddenly and find you asleep.
Mark 13:37 I tell you and everyone: Stay alert.

Mark 14:1 In two days it would be the Passover festival and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The religious leaders and teachers of the law were trying to find a sneaky way to arrest and kill him.
Mark 14:2 But they said, "Not during the festival, or there may be a riot among the people."
Mark 14:3 While he was in Bethany at Simon the leper's house and eating, a woman came with a very valuable jar of spikenard perfume. She opened the jar and poured the perfume on his head.
Mark 14:4 Some people were upset and asked, "Why was this perfume wasted?"
Mark 14:5 It could have been sold for more than three hundred coins and the money given to the poor. They complained about her.
Mark 14:6 Jesus said, "Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a good thing for me."
Mark 14:7 You will always have poor people with you, and you can help them whenever you want, but you won't always have me.
Mark 14:8 She did what she could: she came early to put oil on my body for burial.
Mark 14:9 I tell you, wherever this good news is shared all over the world, what she has done will also be told to remember her.
Mark 14:10 Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.
Mark 14:11 When they heard this, they were happy and agreed to give him money. He then looked for a good chance to betray him.
Mark 14:12 On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his followers asked him, "Where do you want us to go and get ready for you to eat the Passover meal?"
Mark 14:13 He sent two of his disciples and told them, "Go into the city, and you will meet a man carrying a water jug; follow him."
Mark 14:14 Wherever he enters, tell the owner of the house, 'The Teacher asks, where is the guest room where I can eat the Passover with my followers?'
Mark 14:15 He will show you a big upstairs room furnished and ready: there get things ready for us.
Mark 14:16 His followers left, went into the city, and found everything just as he had told them; and they prepared for the Passover.
Mark 14:17 In the evening, he arrives with the twelve.
Mark 14:18 While they were eating, Jesus said, "Truly, I tell you, one of you eating with me will betray me."
Mark 14:19 They started to feel sad and asked him one by one, "Is it me?" and another asked, "Is it me?"
Mark 14:20 He replied, "It's one of the twelve, who is sharing the bowl with me."
Mark 14:21 The Son of man will go as it is written about him, but how terrible for the man who betrays the Son of man! It would be better for him if he had never been born.
Mark 14:22 While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "Take and eat; this is my body."
Mark 14:23 He took the cup, thanked God, gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
Mark 14:24 He told them, "This is my blood of the new agreement, poured out for many."
Mark 14:25 I tell you the truth, I will not drink from the grapevine again until the day I drink it fresh in God's kingdom.
Mark 14:26 After they sang a song, they went to the Mount of Olives.
Mark 14:27 Jesus said to them, "All of you will turn away from me tonight, because it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered."
Mark 14:28 After I have risen, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.
Mark 14:29 But Peter told him, "Even if everyone else is upset, I will not be."
Mark 14:30 Jesus said to him, "Truly, I tell you, today, even tonight, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times."
Mark 14:31 He spoke even more strongly, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never deny you." All the others said the same thing.
Mark 14:32 They reached a place called Gethsemane, and he told his disciples, "Stay here while I go to pray."
Mark 14:33 He took Peter, James, and John with him and started to feel deeply amazed and very sad.
Mark 14:34 He said to them, "My heart is very sad, to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch."
Mark 14:35 He went a little farther, fell to the ground, and prayed that, if it could happen, the difficult time might go away from him.
Mark 14:36 He said, "Daddy, Father, you can do anything; please take this suffering away from me. But let it be what you want, not what I want."
Mark 14:37 He came and found them asleep. He said to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn't you stay awake for one hour?"
Mark 14:38 Stay alert and pray, so you don't fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.
Mark 14:39 He left again, prayed, and said the same things.
Mark 14:40 When he came back, he saw they were sleeping again because they were very tired, and they didn't know what to say to him.
Mark 14:41 He came back a third time and said to them, "Keep sleeping and resting. It's enough, the time has come; look, the Son of Man is being handed over to sinners."
Mark 14:42 Get up, let's go; look, the one who will betray me is close by.
Mark 14:43 Right away, as he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived with a large crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the elders.
Mark 14:44 The one who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, "The one I kiss is the man; arrest him and take him away without hurting him."
Mark 14:45 As soon as he arrived, he went right up to him, said, "Teacher, teacher," and kissed him.
Mark 14:46 They put their hands on him and arrested him.
Mark 14:47 Someone standing nearby pulled out a sword, hit the high priest's servant, and cut off his ear.
Mark 14:48 Jesus replied, "Did you come out with swords and clubs to capture me as if I were a thief?"
Mark 14:49 Every day I was with you in the temple teaching, but you did not arrest me. However, the scriptures needed to be fulfilled.
Mark 14:50 They all left him and ran away.
Mark 14:51 A young man, wearing only a linen cloth, was following Jesus; but when some men grabbed him,
Mark 14:52 He left the cloth behind and ran away naked.
Mark 14:53 They took Jesus to the high priest, and there all the top priests, elders, and teachers of the law came together.
Mark 14:54 Peter followed him from a distance, all the way to the high priest's palace. He sat with the servants and warmed himself by the fire.
Mark 14:55 The religious leaders and their council looked for evidence against Jesus to kill him; but they found none.
Mark 14:56 Many told lies about him, but their stories did not match.
Mark 14:57 Some people stood up and lied about him, saying,
Mark 14:58 We heard him say, "I will tear down this temple made by hands, and in three days I will make another one not made by hands."
Mark 14:59 Their testimonies did not match either.
Mark 14:60 The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, "Aren't you going to answer? What are these charges that these people are bringing against you?"
Mark 14:61 He stayed silent and did not reply. The high priest questioned him again, asking, "Are you the Messiah, the Son of God?"
Mark 14:62 Jesus said, "I am. You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of power and coming in the clouds of heaven."
Mark 14:63 The high priest tore his clothes and said, "Do we need any more witnesses?"
Mark 14:64 You heard the disrespectful words: what do you think? They all found him guilty and deserving of death.
Mark 14:65 Some started to spit on him, cover his face, hit him, and told him to prophesy. The servants slapped him with their hands.
Mark 14:66 While Peter was downstairs in the courtyard, a servant girl of the high priest came.
Mark 14:67 When she saw Peter warming himself, she stared at him and said, "You were also with Jesus from Nazareth."
Mark 14:68 He denied it, saying, "I don't know or understand what you're talking about." Then he went out to the porch, and the rooster crowed.
Mark 14:69 A servant girl saw him, and started to tell those standing nearby, "This man is one of them."
Mark 14:70 He denied it again. Soon after, the people standing nearby said to Peter once more, "You must be one of them because you are from Galilee, and the way you talk shows it."
Mark 14:71 But he started to curse and swear, "I don't know this man you're talking about."
Mark 14:72 The rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered Jesus's words to him, "Before the rooster crows twice, you will disown me three times." And he started to cry.

Mark 15:1 Early in the morning, the chief priests met with the elders and teachers of the law and the whole council. They tied up Jesus, took Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
Mark 15:2 Pilate asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" He replied, "You say that I am."
Mark 15:3 The religious leaders accused him of many things, but he did not reply.
Mark 15:4 Pilate asked him another time, "Aren't you going to answer? See how many accusations they are making against you."
Mark 15:5 But Jesus still did not answer anything, so Pilate was amazed.
Mark 15:6 At the festival, he set free for them any one prisoner they wanted.
Mark 15:7 There was a man named Barabbas, who was in prison with others who had started a rebellion, and he had killed someone in that rebellion.
Mark 15:8 The crowd loudly started to ask him to do what he always did for them.
Mark 15:9 Pilate answered them, "Do you want me to release the King of the Jews to you?"
Mark 15:10 He knew the chief priests had handed him over because they were jealous.
Mark 15:11 The leading priests convinced the crowd to ask for Barabbas to be released instead.
Mark 15:12 Pilate answered and asked them again, "What do you want me to do to the one you call the King of the Jews?"
Mark 15:13 They shouted again, "Crucify him."
Mark 15:14 Then Pilate asked them, "Why, what wrong has he done?" But they shouted even louder, "Crucify him."
Mark 15:15 So Pilate, wanting to please the crowd, let Barabbas go and handed Jesus over to be nailed to a cross after he had whipped him.
Mark 15:16 The soldiers took him inside the building named Praetorium and gathered all the troops there.
Mark 15:17 They dressed him in purple, made a thorn crown, and placed it on his head.
Mark 15:18 They started to greet him, saying, "Hello, King of the Jews!"
Mark 15:19 They hit him on the head with a stick, spat on him, and kneeling down, pretended to worship him.
Mark 15:20 After they made fun of him, they took off the purple robe, dressed him in his own clothes, and took him out to nail him to a cross.
Mark 15:21 They forced Simon from Cyrene, who was just passing by from the fields and was father to Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
Mark 15:22 They took him to a place called Golgotha, which means Skull Place.
Mark 15:23 They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
Mark 15:24 After they nailed him to the cross, they divided his clothes by casting lots to decide what each one would get.
Mark 15:25 It was nine in the morning when they nailed him to the cross.
Mark 15:26 The sign of his charge was written above: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Mark 15:27 They crucified two thieves with him, one on his right and the other on his left.
Mark 15:28 The scripture that says, "He was counted among the lawbreakers," came true.
Mark 15:29 People walking by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, "Oh, you who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,"
Mark 15:30 Save yourself and come down from the cross.
Mark 15:31 The leading priests also made fun of him, talking with the teachers of the law, saying, "He saved others, but he can't save himself."
Mark 15:32 Let the King of Israel, Christ, come down from the cross now, so we can see and believe. Those who were on the crosses next to him insulted him.
Mark 15:33 When it was noon, the whole country became dark until three in the afternoon.
Mark 15:34 At three in the afternoon, Jesus shouted loudly, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" which means, "My God, my God, why have you left me alone?"
Mark 15:35 Some people standing nearby heard this and said, "Look, he's calling for Elijah."
Mark 15:36 Someone ran and soaked a sponge with vinegar, put it on a stick, and offered it to him to drink, saying, "Wait; let's see if Elijah will come to save him."
Mark 15:37 Jesus shouted loudly and then died.
Mark 15:38 The curtain in the temple tore in two from top to bottom.
Mark 15:39 When the army officer standing in front of him saw that he shouted like this and then died, he said, "Truly, this man was God's Son."
Mark 15:40 Women were also watching from far away, including Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome.
Mark 15:41 She, while in Galilee, followed him and helped him; and many other women who went with him to Jerusalem did the same.
Mark 15:42 Now when evening came, since it was the time to get ready, which is the day before the Sabbath,
Mark 15:43 Joseph from Arimathaea, a respected leader who was also looking forward to God's kingdom, went bravely to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body.
Mark 15:44 Pilate was surprised that he was already dead. He called the centurion to ask if he had been dead for some time.
Mark 15:45 When he learned it from the officer, he gave the body to Joseph.
Mark 15:46 He bought good cloth, took him down, wrapped him in it, put him in a tomb cut from rock, and rolled a stone to the tomb's entrance.
Mark 15:47 Mary Magdalene and Mary, Joses's mother, saw where he was placed.

Mark 16:1 After the Sabbath ended, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought sweet spices to anoint him.
Mark 16:2 Early on the first day of the week, they went to the tomb at sunrise.
Mark 16:3 They asked each other, "Who will move the stone away from the tomb's entrance for us?"
Mark 16:4 When they looked, they saw the stone was moved aside because it was very big.
Mark 16:5 When they went into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, wearing a long white robe, and they were scared.
Mark 16:6 He tells them, "Don't be scared. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look at the place where they put him."
Mark 16:7 Go and tell his followers and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you.
Mark 16:8 They quickly left the tomb, shaking and amazed. They didn't say anything to anyone because they were afraid.
Mark 16:9 When Jesus rose early on the first day of the week, he first appeared to Mary Magdalene, who he had freed from seven demons.
Mark 16:10 She went and told those who had been with him while they were sad and crying.
Mark 16:11 When they heard she had seen him alive, they did not believe it.
Mark 16:12 Later, he showed himself in a different way to two of them as they were walking into the countryside.
Mark 16:13 They went and told the others, but the others did not believe them.
Mark 16:14 Later, he showed up to the eleven disciples while they were eating and scolded them for their lack of faith and stubbornness, because they didn't believe those who had seen him after he came back to life.
Mark 16:15 He told them, "Go into the whole world and tell the good news to everyone."
Mark 16:16 Anyone who believes and is baptized will be saved; but anyone who does not believe will be condemned.
Mark 16:17 People who believe will have these signs: They will drive out demons in my name; they will speak in new languages.
Mark 16:18 They will pick up snakes; and if they drink something poisonous, it will not harm them; they will touch the sick, and they will get better.
Mark 16:19 After the Lord spoke to them, he went up to heaven and sat at the right side of God.
Mark 16:20 They went out and shared the message everywhere, with God helping them, and showed that it was true by the miracles that happened. Amen.

Luke 1:1 Many people have tried to write down the events that we fully believe.
Luke 1:2 Just as those who were there from the start and saw it with their own eyes gave it to us, and they were those who shared the message;
Luke 1:3 I also thought it was a good idea, since I have a full understanding of everything from the start, to write it down for you in an organized way, dear Theophilus.
Luke 1:4 I am making this translation so you can be sure about what you have been taught.
Luke 1:5 During King Herod's time in Judaea, there was a priest named Zacharias who belonged to Abia's priest group. His wife came from Aaron's family, and her name was Elisabeth.
Luke 1:6 They both lived good lives before God, following all God's commands and rules without fault.
Luke 1:7 They had no child because Elisabeth could not have babies, and they were both very old.
Luke 1:8 While he served as priest before God during his assigned time,
Luke 1:9 Following the priest's tradition, his duty was to burn incense when he entered God's temple.
Luke 1:10 The whole crowd of people was praying outside during the time for burning incense.
Luke 1:11 An angel of God appeared to him, standing to the right of the incense altar.
Luke 1:12 When Zacharias saw him, he was upset, and became very afraid.
Luke 1:13 But the angel said to him, "Don't be afraid, Zacharias: your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elisabeth will have a son for you, and you will name him John."
Luke 1:14 You will be happy and joyful; and many will be glad when he is born.
Luke 1:15 He will be great in God's eyes and will not drink wine or strong drinks; he will be filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb.
Luke 1:16 He will turn many Israelites back to God.
Luke 1:17 He will go ahead with the spirit and power of Elijah to bring fathers closer to their children and to guide the disobedient towards what is right, making people ready for God.
Luke 1:18 Zacharias asked the angel, "How can I be sure of this? I am old and my wife is also very old."
Luke 1:19 The angel replied, "I am Gabriel, who stands in God's presence, and I have been sent to talk to you and to tell you this good news."
Luke 1:20 Look, you will not be able to talk until the day these things happen because you did not believe my words, which will come true at the right time.
Luke 1:21 The people waited for Zacharias and wondered why he stayed so long in the temple.
Luke 1:22 When he came out, he could not speak to them; they understood he had seen a vision in the temple because he gestured to them and stayed silent.
Luke 1:23 After finishing his time of service, he went back to his home.
Luke 1:24 After that time, Elisabeth, his wife, became pregnant and kept herself hidden for five months, saying,
Luke 1:25 God has done this for me; he noticed me and took away my shame in front of others.
Luke 1:26 In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city in Galilee called Nazareth.
Luke 1:27 A young woman promised in marriage to a man named Joseph, from David's family line; and the young woman's name was Mary.
