Luke 1:28 The angel came to her and said, "Hello, you are greatly blessed, God is with you: you are honored more than other women."
Luke 1:29 When she saw him, she was upset by his words and wondered what kind of greeting this could be.
Luke 1:30 The angel told her, "Don't be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God."
Luke 1:31 Look, you will become pregnant, have a baby boy, and name him JESUS.
Luke 1:32 He will be great and called the Son of the Most High. God will give him the throne of his ancestor David.
Luke 1:33 He will rule over Jacob's family forever; his kingdom will never end.
Luke 1:34 Mary asked the angel, "How can this happen since I've never been with a man?"
Luke 1:35 The angel said to her, "The Holy Spirit will come to you, and God's power will cover you. So the holy child born from you will be called the Son of God."
Luke 1:36 Look, your cousin Elisabeth is also having a baby boy in her old age; she's been pregnant for six months even though people said she couldn't have children.
Luke 1:37 With God, nothing is impossible.
Luke 1:38 Mary said, "Look, I'm God's servant; let it happen to me as you said." Then the angel left her.
Luke 1:39 Mary got up at that time and quickly went to a town in the hill country of Judah.
Luke 1:40 She went into Zacharias's house and greeted Elizabeth.
Luke 1:41 When Elisabeth heard Mary greet her, the baby jumped inside her, and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Luke 1:42 She spoke loudly and said, "You are blessed among women, and the child you will have is blessed."
Luke 1:43 Why should I be honored with a visit from the mother of my Lord?
Luke 1:44 When I heard your greeting, the baby in my belly jumped for joy.
Luke 1:45 Happy is she who believed, because what God told her will happen.
Luke 1:46 Mary said, "My soul praises God greatly."
Luke 1:47 My spirit is happy in God my Savior.
Luke 1:48 God has noticed his servant's humble state; from now on, all generations will say I am blessed.
Luke 1:49 The Mighty One has done great things for me; and His name is holy.
Luke 1:50 God's kindness is for those who respect him, always and forever.
Luke 1:51 He has shown strength with his arm; he has spread out the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
Luke 1:52 He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up those who were humble.
Luke 1:53 He has given good things to the hungry; but the rich he has turned away with nothing.
Luke 1:54 He has helped his servant Israel, remembering his mercy.
Luke 1:55 He spoke to our ancestors, to Abraham, and to his descendants forever.
Luke 1:56 Mary stayed with her for about three months and then went back to her own home.
Luke 1:57 Elizabeth's time arrived to give birth, and she had a son.
Luke 1:58 Her neighbors and relatives heard how God had shown her great mercy, and they were happy for her.
Luke 1:59 On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the baby and they named him Zacharias, like his father.
Luke 1:60 His mother replied, "No, he will be named John."
Luke 1:61 They told her, "No one in your family has this name."
Luke 1:62 They gestured to his father to ask what name he wanted for the boy.
Luke 1:63 He asked for something to write on, and wrote, "His name is John." Everyone was amazed.
Luke 1:64 Right away, his mouth was opened, his tongue was set free, and he spoke and praised God.
Luke 1:65 Everyone living nearby was afraid, and people talked about these events all over the hill country of Judea.
Luke 1:66 Everyone who heard these things kept them in mind, thinking, "What kind of child will this be?" And God's hand was with him.
Luke 1:67 His father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God's message.
Luke 1:68 Praise God of Israel, for he has come to and saved his people.
Luke 1:69 And has given us a strong savior in the family of his servant David;
Luke 1:70 God spoke through his holy prophets long ago, from the beginning of the world.
Luke 1:71 We should be rescued from our enemies and from all who hate us.
Luke 1:72 To show the kindness promised to our ancestors and to remember his sacred agreement;
Luke 1:73 The promise God made to our father Abraham,
Luke 1:74 He would let us be free from our enemies so we can serve him without fear.
Luke 1:75 Living holy and right before God, every day of our life.
Luke 1:76 And you, child, will be called the prophet of God, because you will go before God to prepare his paths.
Luke 1:77 To teach his people how to be saved by forgiving their sins.
Luke 1:78 Because of our God's kind mercy, a new light from heaven has come to us.
Luke 1:79 To shine light on those in darkness and near death, to lead our steps toward peace.
Luke 1:80 The child grew up, became strong in spirit, and lived in the deserts until the time came to show himself to Israel.

Luke 2:1 At that time, Caesar Augustus ordered that everyone in the world should be counted and taxed.
Luke 2:2 This tax first happened when Cyrenius was the ruler of Syria.
Luke 2:3 Everyone went to register for taxes, each to their own city.
Luke 2:4 Joseph also left Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to go to Judea, to the town called Bethlehem, the city of David, because he belonged to David's family line.
Luke 2:5 To register for taxes with Mary, his fiancée, who was pregnant.
Luke 2:6 While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
Luke 2:7 She gave birth to her first son, wrapped him in baby clothes, and put him in a feeding trough because there was no space for them in the guesthouse.
Luke 2:8 In that area, shepherds were in the fields, staying with their sheep at night.
Luke 2:9 Suddenly, an angel of God appeared to them, and God's brightness shone all around them: and they were very scared.
Luke 2:10 The angel told them, "Don't be afraid; look, I have good news for you, a big joy that will be for everyone."
Luke 2:11 Today in David's city, a Savior is born for you, who is Christ the Lord.
Luke 2:12 This will be a sign for you; you will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a feeding trough.
Luke 2:13 Suddenly, many angels from heaven appeared with the angel, all praising God and saying,
Luke 2:14 Praise God in the highest, and on earth peace, kindness to people.
Luke 2:15 After the angels left and went to heaven, the shepherds said to each other, "Let's go to Bethlehem and see what has happened that God has told us about."
Luke 2:16 They hurried and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in a feeding trough.
Luke 2:17 After they saw it, they shared the message that was told to them about this child.
Luke 2:18 Everyone who heard it was amazed at what the shepherds told them.
Luke 2:19 Mary remembered all these things and thought deeply about them in her heart.
Luke 2:20 The shepherds went back, praising and thanking God for everything they heard and saw, just as they had been told.
Luke 2:21 Eight days after the child was born, when it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus. This is the name the angel had given before he was born.
Luke 2:22 When her time of cleansing as required by Moses' law was completed, they took him to Jerusalem to present him to God.
Luke 2:23 The law of God says every first-born boy shall be considered sacred to God.
Luke 2:24 To give a sacrifice as the law of God says, two turtledoves or two young pigeons.
Luke 2:25 Look, there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. This man was fair and devoted, looking forward to Israel's comfort, and the Holy Spirit was with him.
Luke 2:26 God's Spirit told him he would not die before he saw God's promised Savior.
Luke 2:27 He was led by the Spirit to the temple. When Jesus' parents came to do as the law required,
Luke 2:28 He picked him up, blessed God, and said.
Luke 2:29 God, now you let your servant go in peace, as you promised.
Luke 2:30 My eyes have seen your salvation.
Luke 2:31 You have made ready before all people;
Luke 2:32 A light to make the non-Jews see, and the honor of your people Israel.
Luke 2:33 Joseph and his mother were amazed at what was said about him.
Luke 2:34 Simeon blessed them and told Mary his mother, "Look, this child is destined to cause many in Israel to fall and rise again; and to be a sign that will be opposed."
Luke 2:35 Yes, a sword will go through your own heart too, so that the secrets of many hearts will be shown.
Luke 2:36 Anna was a prophet, the daughter of Phanuel, from the Aser tribe. She was very old and had been married for seven years since she was young.
Luke 2:37 She was a widow of about 84 years old who never left the temple and served God with fasting and prayer day and night.
Luke 2:38 At that moment, she came in and thanked God too. She talked about him to everyone in Jerusalem waiting for salvation.
Luke 2:39 After they had done everything the law of God required, they went back to Galilee, to their home town of Nazareth.
Luke 2:40 The child grew up, became strong in spirit, was full of wisdom, and God's favor was with him.
Luke 2:41 His parents went to Jerusalem every year for the Passover feast.
Luke 2:42 When he was twelve, they went to Jerusalem for the festival as was their tradition.
Luke 2:43 After the days were complete and they were going back, Jesus stayed in Jerusalem without Joseph and his mother knowing.
Luke 2:44 But they thought he was with the group, so they traveled for a day. Then they looked for him among their relatives and friends.
Luke 2:45 When they didn't find him, they went back to Jerusalem to look for him.
Luke 2:46 Three days later, they found him in the temple. He was sitting with the teachers, listening to them and asking questions.
Luke 2:47 Everyone who heard him was amazed at his understanding and replies.
Luke 2:48 When they saw him, they were surprised. His mother asked him, "Son, why have you treated us this way? Look, your father and I have been searching for you with heavy hearts."
Luke 2:49 He asked them, "Why were you looking for me? Didn't you know that I need to do my Father's work?"
Luke 2:50 They did not understand what he said to them.
Luke 2:51 He went with them to Nazareth and obeyed them. His mother remembered all these things in her heart.
Luke 2:52 Jesus grew wiser and taller, and became liked by both God and people.

Luke 3:1 In the fifteenth year when Tiberius Caesar ruled, Pontius Pilate was the governor of Judaea, Herod ruled Galilee, his brother Philip ruled Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias ruled Abilene.
Luke 3:2 During the time Annas and Caiaphas were high priests, God spoke to John, Zacharias's son, in the desert.
Luke 3:3 He went through the whole region around the Jordan River, teaching about a baptism for repentance to forgive sins.
Luke 3:4 The book of the prophet Isaiah says, "A voice calls out in the desert, 'Get ready for God's way, make a straight path for him.'"
Luke 3:5 Every low place will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be made low; the winding roads will be made straight, and the rough paths will be made smooth.
Luke 3:6 Everyone will see how God saves.
Luke 3:7 He told the crowd coming to be baptized, "You brood of snakes, who warned you to escape the coming anger?"
Luke 3:8 Produce actions that show you have changed for the better, and don't think you can say, 'We have Abraham as our ancestor,' because I tell you, God can turn these stones into descendants for Abraham.
Luke 3:9 The axe is now at the root of the trees: every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
Luke 3:10 The people asked him, "What should we do?"
Luke 3:11 He answered and said to them, "If you have two coats, give one to the person who has none; and if you have food, do the same."
Luke 3:12 Tax collectors also came to be baptized and asked him, "Teacher, what should we do?"
Luke 3:13 He told them, "Don't take more than what you are told to."
Luke 3:14 The soldiers also asked him, "What should we do?" He told them, "Don't hurt anyone, don't lie about others, and be happy with your pay."
Luke 3:15 As the people waited and wondered to themselves if John might be the Christ,
Luke 3:16 John replied to everyone, "I baptize you in water, but someone more powerful than me is coming. I'm not good enough to untie his shoes. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire."
Luke 3:17 He holds a winnowing fan to clean his threshing area and he will bring the wheat into his barn, but he will burn the chaff with a fire that cannot be put out.
Luke 3:18 He preached many other things to encourage the people.
Luke 3:19 But Herod the ruler, being corrected by him for taking Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and for all the bad things Herod had done,
Luke 3:20 He also did this: he put John in jail.
Luke 3:21 After everyone was baptized, when Jesus was also baptized and was praying, the sky opened up.
Luke 3:22 The Holy Spirit came down in the form of a dove on him, and a voice from heaven said, "You are my dear Son; I am happy with you."
Luke 3:23 Jesus started to be about thirty years old, and people thought he was Joseph's son, who was Heli's son.
Luke 3:24 He was the son of Matthat, who was Levi's son, who was Melchi's son, who was Janna's son, who was Joseph's son.
Luke 3:25 He was the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Naum, the son of Esli, the son of Nagge.
Luke 3:26 He was the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semei, the son of Joseph, the son of Juda.
Luke 3:27 He was the son of Joanna, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri.
Luke 3:28 He was the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodam, and the son of Er.
Luke 3:29 He was the son of Jose, who was the son of Eliezer, who was the son of Jorim, who was the son of Matthat, who was the son of Levi.
Luke 3:30 He was the son of Simeon, the son of Juda, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim.
Luke 3:31 He was the son of Melea, the son of Menan, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David.
Luke 3:32 He was the son of Jesse, who was the son of Obed, who was the son of Boaz, who was the son of Salmon, who was the son of Nahshon.
Luke 3:33 He was the son of Aminadab, who was the son of Aram, who was the son of Esrom, who was the son of Phares, who was the son of Judah.
Luke 3:34 He was Jacob's son, who was Isaac's son, who was Abraham's son, who was Thara's son, who was Nachor's son.
Luke 3:35 He was the son of Saruch, who was the son of Ragau, who was the son of Phalec, who was the son of Heber, who was the son of Sala.
Luke 3:36 He was the son of Cainan, who was the son of Arphaxad, who was the son of Shem, who was the son of Noah, who was the son of Lamech.
Luke 3:37 He was the son of Methuselah, who was the son of Enoch, who was the son of Jared, who was the son of Mahalaleel, who was the son of Cainan.
Luke 3:38 He was Enos's son, Seth's grandson, Adam's great-grandson, and God's descendant.

Luke 4:1 Jesus, filled with the Holy Spirit, came back from the Jordan River and was guided by the Spirit into the desert.
Luke 4:2 He was tempted by the devil for forty days. During that time, he ate nothing. After it ended, he felt hungry.
Luke 4:3 The devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
Luke 4:4 Jesus replied, "It is said, people do not live only by eating bread, but by every word from God."
Luke 4:5 The devil took him to a high mountain and showed him all the world's kingdoms in an instant.
Luke 4:6 The devil told him, "I will give you all this power and its glory because it has been given to me, and I can give it to anyone I choose."
Luke 4:7 If you worship me, everything will be yours.
Luke 4:8 Jesus replied, "Go away from me, Satan, because it is said, 'You must worship only God and serve him alone.'"
Luke 4:9 He took him to Jerusalem, put him on the highest point of the temple, and said, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here."
Luke 4:10 It is written, God will command his angels to protect you.
Luke 4:11 They will carry you in their hands so that you won't hit your foot on a stone.
Luke 4:12 Jesus replied, "It is written, 'Do not test God.'"
Luke 4:13 After the devil finished all the tempting, he left him for a while.
Luke 4:14 Jesus came back to Galilee with the Spirit's power, and news about him spread through the whole area.
Luke 4:15 He taught in their gathering places, and everyone praised him.
Luke 4:16 He went to Nazareth, where he grew up, and on the Sabbath, as he usually did, he entered the synagogue and stood up to read.
Luke 4:17 He received the book of the prophet Isaiah. When he opened the book, he found the section that said,
Luke 4:18 God's Spirit is on me, because he has chosen me to tell good news to the poor; he has sent me to fix broken hearts, to say to the captives 'You are free,' and to help blind people see, to free those who have been hurt.
Luke 4:19 To announce God's year of favor.
Luke 4:20 He closed the book, gave it back to the assistant, and sat down. Everyone in the synagogue stared at him.
Luke 4:21 He started to tell them, "Today, this scripture has come true as you heard it."
Luke 4:22 Everyone listened to him and was amazed at the kind words he spoke. They asked, "Isn't this Joseph's son?"
Luke 4:23 He told them, "You will definitely tell me this saying, 'Doctor, cure yourself:' do here in your hometown what we heard you did in Capernaum."
Luke 4:24 He said, "Truly I tell you, no prophet is welcomed in his hometown."
Luke 4:25 But I tell you truly, there were many widows in Israel during Elijah's time, when the sky was closed for three and a half years and there was a severe famine everywhere in the country.
Luke 4:26 Elijah was not sent to any of them but to a widow in the city of Sarepta in Sidon.
Luke 4:27 Many people with leprosy lived in Israel when Elisha was a prophet; but only Naaman the Syrian was healed.
Luke 4:28 Everyone in the synagogue became very angry when they heard this.
Luke 4:29 They got up, pushed him out of the city, took him to the edge of the hill where their city was built, to throw him down.
Luke 4:30 He walked right through the crowd and went on his way.
Luke 4:31 He went down to Capernaum, a city in Galilee, and taught them on the Sabbath days.
Luke 4:32 They were amazed at his teaching, because his words had authority.
Luke 4:33 In the meeting place, there was a man with an evil spirit, and he shouted loudly.
Luke 4:34 Leave us alone; what do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are; the Holy One of God.
Luke 4:35 Jesus scolded the demon, saying, "Be quiet and leave him." And after the demon threw the man down in front of everyone, it came out without injuring him.
Luke 4:36 Everyone was amazed and said to each other, "What kind of teaching is this? He gives orders to evil spirits with authority and power, and they leave."
Luke 4:37 News about him spread all over the surrounding region.
Luke 4:38 He got up from the synagogue and went into Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law had a high fever, and they asked him to help her.
Luke 4:39 He stood by her, told the fever to go away, and it did. Right away she got up and took care of them.
Luke 4:40 When the sun was going down, everyone with sick friends brought them to Jesus; he touched each one and healed them.
Luke 4:41 Evil spirits came out of many people, shouting, "You are the Christ, the Son of God." But he scolded them and did not allow them to speak because they knew he was the Christ.
Luke 4:42 When day came, he left and went to a deserted place. The people looked for him, found him, and begged him not to leave them.
Luke 4:43 He told them, "I must tell other cities about God's kingdom, too: that's why I was sent."
Luke 4:44 He taught in the meeting places of Galilee.

Luke 5:1 As the crowd gathered to listen to God's message, he stood by the Lake of Gennesaret.
Luke 5:2 He saw two boats by the lake, but the fishermen had left them and were cleaning their nets.
Luke 5:3 He went onto Simon's boat and asked Simon to push off a little from shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.
Luke 5:4 After he finished talking, he told Simon, "Go out into the deep water and let down your nets to catch some fish."
Luke 5:5 Simon replied, "Teacher, we worked hard all night and caught nothing, but because you say so, I will let down the net."
Luke 5:6 After they did this, they caught a large number of fish; the net tore.
Luke 5:7 They signaled to their friends in the other boat to come and help them. They came and both boats were so full that they started to sink.
Luke 5:8 When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus' knees and said, "Go away from me, because I am a sinful man, God."
Luke 5:9 He was amazed, and so was everyone with him, at the large number of fish they caught.
Luke 5:10 James and John, Zebedee's sons, who worked with Simon, were there too. Jesus told Simon, "Don't be afraid; from now on you will catch people."
Luke 5:11 When they brought their boats to shore, they left everything and followed him.
Luke 5:12 When Jesus was in a city, a man with leprosy saw him, fell on his face, and begged, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Luke 5:13 He reached out his hand, touched him, and said, "I'm willing; be clean." Right away, the leprosy left him.
Luke 5:14 He told him not to tell anyone, but to go show himself to the priest, and offer a cleansing sacrifice as Moses directed, as proof to them.
Luke 5:15 But his fame spread even more, and large crowds gathered to listen and to be healed by him of their sicknesses.
Luke 5:16 He went to a quiet place and prayed.
Luke 5:17 One day, as he was teaching, there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting nearby, from every town of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. And God's power was there to heal them.
Luke 5:18 Look, some people carried a man on a bed who was paralyzed. They tried to bring him in and place him in front of Jesus.
Luke 5:19 When they couldn't find a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles right in front of Jesus.
Luke 5:20 When he saw how much they believed, he said to him, "Man, your sins are forgiven."
Luke 5:21 The teachers of the law and the Pharisees started to think, saying, "Who is this that says bad things against God? Who can forgive sins except God alone?"
Luke 5:22 When Jesus knew what they were thinking, he said to them, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?"
Luke 5:23 Which is easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
Luke 5:24 So you can know the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, he told the man with palsy, "I tell you, get up, take your bed, and go home."
Luke 5:25 Right away, he stood up in front of everyone, picked up the mat he was lying on, and went home, praising God.
Luke 5:26 Everyone was amazed, they praised God, and were very afraid, saying, "We have seen amazing things today."
Luke 5:27 After this, he went out, saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, "Follow me."
Luke 5:28 He left everything, got up, and followed him.
Luke 5:29 Levi held a big dinner at his home; many tax collectors and others ate with them.
Luke 5:30 But their teachers and religious leaders complained about his followers, asking, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and bad people?"
Luke 5:31 Jesus replied, "Healthy people don't need a doctor; only the sick do."
Luke 5:32 I did not come to call good people, but sinners to turn away from their sins.
Luke 5:33 They asked him, "Why do John's followers and the Pharisees' disciples fast and pray often, but your followers eat and drink?"
Luke 5:34 He asked them, "Can you expect the wedding guests to fast while the groom is with them?"
Luke 5:35 But a time will come when the groom will be taken from them, and then they will fast on those days.
Luke 5:36 He also told them a story: No one sews a patch from a new piece of clothing on an old one. If they do, the new piece will tear, and it will not match the old clothing.
Luke 5:37 No one puts new wine into old bottles; otherwise, the new wine will break the bottles, spill out, and the bottles will be ruined.
Luke 5:38 New wine must go into new wineskins; then both stay good.
Luke 5:39 Someone who has drunk old wine doesn't immediately want new wine. They think the old one is better.

Luke 6:1 On the second Saturday following the first, Jesus walked through the grain fields. His followers picked some heads of grain, rubbed them in their hands, and ate them.
Luke 6:2 Some Pharisees asked them, "Why are you doing what's not allowed on the Sabbath?"
Luke 6:3 Jesus replied to them, "Haven't you read what David did when he and his followers were hungry?
Luke 6:4 He entered God's house, took and ate the bread on display, and also gave it to his companions, though only priests are allowed to eat it.
Luke 6:5 He told them that the Son of Man is also Lord of the Sabbath.
Luke 6:6 On another Sabbath, he went into the synagogue and taught. A man was there with a crippled right hand.
Luke 6:7 The teachers of the law and the Pharisees watched Jesus to see if he would heal on the Sabbath, so they could accuse him.
Luke 6:8 But he knew what they were thinking and said to the man with the weak hand, "Get up and stand here." And he got up and stood there.
Luke 6:9 Jesus said to them, I have one question for you: Is it right to do good or bad on the Sabbath? To save a life or to destroy it?
Luke 6:10 He looked at them all and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He did, and his hand was healed, just like the other one.
Luke 6:11 They were overcome with anger and discussed with each other what they should do to Jesus.
Luke 6:12 At that time, he went to a mountain to pray, and spent the whole night talking to God.
Luke 6:13 When it became daytime, he called his disciples to him and out of them, he picked twelve, whom he also called apostles.
Luke 6:14 Simon, who was also called Peter, and his brother Andrew, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Luke 6:15 Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called the Zealot,
Luke 6:16 Judas, James's brother, and Judas Iscariot, who was the traitor.
Luke 6:17 He came down with them and stood on the flat land with his followers and a large crowd from all over Judea and Jerusalem, and from the coast of Tyre and Sidon. They came to listen to him and to be cured of their sicknesses.
Luke 6:18 People troubled by evil spirits were healed.
Luke 6:19 The whole crowd wanted to touch him because healing power came from him and healed everyone.
Luke 6:20 He looked at his followers and said, "Happy are you who are poor: for the kingdom of God belongs to you."
Luke 6:21 Happy are you who are hungry now, because you will be satisfied. Happy are you who are crying now, because you will laugh.
Luke 6:22 You are blessed when people hate you, avoid you, insult you, and say you are evil because of the Son of man.
Luke 6:23 Be happy on that day and jump for joy, because your reward in heaven is big; their ancestors treated the prophets the same way.
Luke 6:24 But bad luck to you who are rich, because you have already gotten your comfort.
Luke 6:25 Trouble to you who are full, because you will be hungry. Trouble to you who laugh now, because you will be sad and cry.
Luke 6:26 Trouble comes to you when everyone says good things about you, because that's what they did for the fake prophets.
Luke 6:27 I tell you who are listening: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you.
Luke 6:28 Be kind to those who curse you, and pray for those who are mean to you.
Luke 6:29 If someone hits you on one cheek, let them hit the other one too; and if someone takes your jacket, don't stop them from taking your shirt as well.
Luke 6:30 Give to everyone who asks you, and if someone takes your belongings, don't ask for them back.
Luke 6:31 Do to others what you would want them to do to you.
Luke 6:32 If you love only those who love you, what reward do you get? Even sinners love those who love them.
Luke 6:33 If you are good only to those who are good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do that.
Luke 6:34 If you lend money to those you expect to pay you back, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, hoping to get back the same amount.
Luke 6:35 Love your enemies, do good, and lend without expecting anything back; your reward will be large, and you will be children of the Most High because God is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
Luke 6:36 Be kind, just as your Father is kind.
Luke 6:37 Do not judge, and you won't be judged. Do not condemn, and you won't be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Luke 6:38 Give, and you will receive; you will be given a lot, packed tight and overflowing, into your arms. Because the same amount you give will be given back to you.
Luke 6:39 He told them a story: If a blind person guides another blind person, won't they both fall into a hole?
Luke 6:40 A student is not greater than their teacher, but anyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher.
Luke 6:41 Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the log that is in your own eye?
Luke 6:42 How can you tell your brother, 'Brother, let me take out the speck in your eye,' when you don't see the log in your own eye? You are acting fake. First, remove the log from your eye. Then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.
Luke 6:43 A good tree does not produce bad fruit, and a bad tree does not produce good fruit.
Luke 6:44 Every tree is recognized by its fruit. People don't pick figs from thorns, or grapes from bramble bushes.
Luke 6:45 A good person brings good things from the good in their heart, and a bad person brings bad things from the bad in their heart. What they have plenty of in their heart, their mouth talks about.
Luke 6:46 Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and not do what I say?
Luke 6:47 Anyone who comes to me, listens to what I say, and follows it, I will show you what they are like:
Luke 6:48 He is like a person who built a house, dug deep, and set its base on rock: when the flood came, the water hit that house hard, but could not move it because it was built on rock.
Luke 6:49 But the person who listens and doesn't act is like someone who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the river hit it hard, the house quickly fell apart, and was completely destroyed.

Luke 7:1 After finishing all his teachings in front of the people, he went into Capernaum.
Luke 7:2 A centurion had a servant he cared for deeply, who was ill and close to death.
Luke 7:3 When he heard about Jesus, he sent Jewish leaders to ask him to come and heal his servant.
Luke 7:4 When they reached Jesus, they urgently asked him, saying, "He deserves your help."
Luke 7:5 He loves our people and has built us a place to worship.
Luke 7:6 Then Jesus went with them. When he was almost at the house, the centurion sent friends to say to him, "Sir, do not bother coming in, because I am not good enough for you to come under my roof.
Luke 7:7 That's why I didn't feel worthy to come to you myself; just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
Luke 7:8 I am also a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one, 'Go,' and he goes; to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it.
Luke 7:9 When Jesus heard this, he was amazed and turning to the crowd following him, he said, "I tell you, I haven't found such strong faith even in Israel."
Luke 7:10 The messengers returned to the house and found the sick servant completely well.
Luke 7:11 The next day, he went to a city named Nain with many of his followers and a large crowd.
Luke 7:12 As he approached the city gate, he saw a group carrying out a dead man, the only son of his mother, who was a widow. Many people from the city were with her.
Luke 7:13 When God saw her, he felt sorry for her and said, "Don't cry."
Luke 7:14 He came and touched the coffin, and the people carrying it stopped. He said, "Young man, I tell you, get up."
Luke 7:15 The dead person sat up and started to talk. Then he was given back to his mother.
Luke 7:16 Everyone became afraid and praised God, saying, "A great prophet has appeared among us," and, "God has come to help his people."
Luke 7:17 News about him spread all over Judaea and the surrounding area.
Luke 7:18 John's followers told him about all these things.
Luke 7:19 John sent two of his disciples to ask Jesus, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect someone else?"
Luke 7:20 When the men got to him, they said, "John the Baptizer sent us to ask you, are you the one we should expect, or should we wait for someone else?"
Luke 7:21 In that hour, he healed many people of their sicknesses and diseases, and of evil spirits; and he gave sight to many who were blind.
Luke 7:22 Jesus replied, "Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind can see, the lame can walk, people with leprosy are healed, the deaf can hear, the dead are brought back to life, and the good news is told to the poor."
Luke 7:23 Happy is anyone who does not get upset because of me.
Luke 7:24 After John's messengers left, he started talking to the people about John, asking, "Why did you go out into the wilderness? To see a reed swayed by the wind?"
Luke 7:25 Why did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those in fancy clothes and living in luxury are in royal palaces.
Luke 7:26 But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and even more than a prophet.
Luke 7:27 He is the one about whom it was written: Look, I send my messenger ahead of you to get things ready for you.
Luke 7:28 I tell you, among all born from women, no one is a greater prophet than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in God's kingdom is greater than he.
Luke 7:29 Everyone who heard him, including the tax collectors, acknowledged that God was right by getting baptized with John's baptism.
Luke 7:30 The Pharisees and legal experts did not accept God's plan for them because they were not baptized by him.
Luke 7:31 God asked, "What can I compare the people of this time to? What are they like?"
Luke 7:32 They are like children sitting in the market, calling to each other, saying, "We played music for you, but you didn't dance; we cried for you, but you didn't cry."
Luke 7:33 John the Baptist didn't eat bread or drink wine, and you say he has a demon.
Luke 7:34 The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look, a man who eats too much and drinks too much wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
Luke 7:35 Wisdom is shown to be right by all who follow her.
Luke 7:36 A Pharisee wanted Jesus to have a meal with him. So Jesus went to the Pharisee's home and sat down to eat.
Luke 7:37 Look, a woman in the town who had done wrong things knew that Jesus was eating at a Pharisee's home, so she came with a jar of perfume.
Luke 7:38 She stood behind him at his feet crying, washed his feet with her tears, dried them with her hair, kissed his feet, and put perfume on them.
Luke 7:39 When the Pharisee who invited Jesus saw this, he thought, "If this man were a prophet, he would know what kind of woman is touching him, because she is a sinner."
Luke 7:40 Jesus replied to him, "Simon, I have something to tell you." And he said, "Teacher, go ahead."
Luke 7:41 A lender had two people who owed him money: one owed five hundred coins, and the other owed fifty.
Luke 7:42 When they couldn't pay, he freely forgave them both. So, which one will love him more?
Luke 7:43 Simon answered, "I think the one who was forgiven the most." And he said to him, "You have judged correctly."
Luke 7:44 He looked at the woman and said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? When I came into your home, you didn't give me water for my feet. But she has washed my feet with her tears and dried them with her hair."
Luke 7:45 You did not give me a kiss, but this woman hasn't stopped kissing my feet since I arrived.
Luke 7:46 You did not put oil on my head, but this woman has put perfume on my feet.
Luke 7:47 So I tell you, her many sins are forgiven because she loved a lot; but one who is forgiven little, loves little.
Luke 7:48 He told her, "Your sins are forgiven."
Luke 7:49 The people eating with him started to think, "Who is this who can also forgive sins?"
Luke 7:50 He told the woman, "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."

Luke 8:1 After that, he traveled to every city and village, teaching and sharing the good news of God's kingdom, and the twelve were with him.
Luke 8:2 Some women who were healed from evil spirits and sicknesses, including Mary called Magdalene who had seven demons come out of her,
Luke 8:3 Joanna, Chuza the manager of Herod's house, and Susanna, along with many others, used their own resources to help him.
Luke 8:4 When many people came together from different cities to be with him, he told them a story with a lesson.
Luke 8:5 A farmer went out to plant his seeds: as he scattered them, some dropped along the path; they were stepped on, and the birds ate them.
Luke 8:6 Some seeds fell on rocky ground, and when they grew, they dried up because they had no water.
Luke 8:7 Some seeds fell among thorns; the thorns grew with them and choked the seeds.
Luke 8:8 Some seeds fell on good soil, grew, and produced fruit a hundred times more. After saying this, he shouted, "If you have ears to listen, then listen."
Luke 8:9 His followers asked him, "What does this story mean?"
Luke 8:10 He said, "You are allowed to know God's kingdom secrets. But others get stories, so they look but don't see, and they listen but don't understand."
Luke 8:11 The story means this: The seed stands for God's message.
Luke 8:12 The ones along the path are those who hear the message, but then the devil comes and takes the message from their hearts so they won't believe and be saved.
Luke 8:13 Those on the rock are the ones who hear the word and accept it with joy, but they have no strong foundation. They believe for a while, but when they face hard times, they give up.
Luke 8:14 The seeds that fell among thorns represent those who hear the message, but then life's worries, wealth, and pleasures stop them from growing, and they don't produce any good results.
Luke 8:15 The seeds that fell on good soil represent those who, with a true and good heart, listen to God's message, hold onto it, and steadily produce good results.
Luke 8:16 When someone lights a candle, they don't hide it under a bowl or put it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a stand so that people coming in can see the light.
Luke 8:17 Nothing that is secret will stay hidden; everything that is hidden will be brought to light and made known.
Luke 8:18 Be careful how you listen: for whoever has, will receive more; and whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away.
Luke 8:19 Then his mother and brothers came to him, but they couldn't get close because of the crowd.
Luke 8:20 Some people told him, "Your mother and your brothers are outside, wanting to see you."
Luke 8:21 He replied, "My mother and brothers are those who listen to God's word and follow it."
Luke 8:22 One day, he got into a boat with his followers and said to them, "Let's go across to the other side of the lake." So they set out.
Luke 8:23 While they were sailing, he fell asleep. A windstorm came on the lake, the boat filled with water, and they were in danger.
Luke 8:24 They came to him, woke him up, and said, "Teacher, teacher, we're going to die!" So he got up, told the wind and the wild water to stop, and they stopped, and everything was calm.
Luke 8:25 He asked them, "Where is your faith?" Filled with fear and amazement, they said to each other, "Who is this man? Even the winds and water obey him!"
Luke 8:26 They reached the area of the Gadarenes, across from Galilee.
Luke 8:27 When he went onto land, a man from the city who had been troubled by evil spirits for a long time, who wore no clothes and did not live in a house but in the tombs, met him.
Luke 8:28 When he saw Jesus, he shouted and fell down in front of him, and said loudly, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the most high God? Please don't torture me."
Luke 8:29 He had told the evil spirit to leave the man. The spirit often took control of him, and though he was tied up with chains and leg irons, he would break free, and the devil drove him into lonely places.
Luke 8:30 And Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" He replied, "Legion," because many demons had gone into him.
Luke 8:31 They begged him not to order them to go into the abyss.
Luke 8:32 There was a large group of pigs eating on the hill, and they asked him to let them go into the pigs. And he let them.
Luke 8:33 The demons left the man and went into the pigs. The pigs then ran down the hill into the lake and drowned.
Luke 8:34 When the people taking care of them saw what had happened, they ran away, and went to tell about it in the city and the countryside.
Luke 8:35 Then they went to see what had happened; they came to Jesus, and saw the man who had been freed from demons sitting at Jesus' feet, dressed and in his right mind, and they were scared.
Luke 8:36 People who saw it explained how the man with demons was healed.
Luke 8:37 The whole crowd from the area of the Gadarenes asked him to leave because they were very afraid. So he got into the boat and went back.
Luke 8:38 The man who was freed from the demons asked to go with Jesus, but Jesus sent him away, saying.
Luke 8:39 Go back to your home, and tell how much God has done for you. So he left and told everyone in the city how much Jesus had done for him.
Luke 8:40 When Jesus came back, the people happily welcomed him because they were all waiting for him.
Luke 8:41 Look, a man named Jairus came, who was a leader in the synagogue. He knelt down before Jesus and begged him to come to his house.
Luke 8:42 He had just one daughter, who was about twelve, and she was very sick. As he went, the crowds pressed around him.
Luke 8:43 A woman who had been bleeding for twelve years and had spent all her money on doctors could not be healed by anyone.
Luke 8:44 She came up behind him, touched the edge of his clothes, and right away her bleeding stopped.
Luke 8:45 Jesus asked, "Who touched me?" When everyone said they hadn't, Peter and his friends told him, "Master, there are so many people crowding and pushing against you, and you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
Luke 8:46 Jesus said, "Someone touched me, because I felt power go out from me."
Luke 8:47 When the woman realized she could not hide, she came shaking with fear. She knelt before Him and told everyone why she had touched Him, and how she was healed at once.
Luke 8:48 He said to her, "Daughter, relax, your faith has healed you; go peacefully."
Luke 8:49 While he was still talking, someone from the synagogue leader's house came and said, "Your daughter is dead; don't bother the Teacher anymore."
Luke 8:50 When Jesus heard this, he said, "Don't be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed."
Luke 8:51 When he entered the house, he did not allow anyone to come in except Peter, James, John, and the girl's father and mother.
Luke 8:52 Everyone cried and mourned for her, but he said, "Don't cry; she isn't dead, she's just sleeping."
Luke 8:53 They laughed at him, knowing she was dead.
Luke 8:54 He sent everyone out, took her hand, and said, "Girl, get up."
Luke 8:55 Her spirit returned, and she got up right away; and he told them to give her something to eat.
Luke 8:56 Her parents were amazed, but he told them not to tell anyone what had happened.

Luke 9:1 He gathered his twelve followers and gave them the power and authority to cast out all demons and to heal sicknesses.
Luke 9:2 He sent them to tell about God's kingdom and heal the sick.
Luke 9:3 He told them, "Don't take anything for your trip, not a walking stick, not a bag, not bread, not money, and don't have two shirts each."
Luke 9:4 When you enter a house, stay there until you leave.
Luke 9:5 If anyone does not welcome you, leave that town and shake the dust off your feet as a warning to them.
Luke 9:6 They left and traveled through the towns, sharing the good news and healing everywhere.
Luke 9:7 Herod the ruler heard about everything Jesus did. He was confused because some people said that John had come back to life.
Luke 9:8 Some people thought Elijah had appeared, while others believed one of the past prophets had come back to life.
Luke 9:9 Herod said, "I beheaded John, but who is this I hear about?" And he wanted to see him.
Luke 9:10 The apostles came back and told Jesus everything they did. He took them to a quiet place in the desert near Bethsaida.
Luke 9:11 When the people found out, they followed him. He welcomed them, talked to them about God's kingdom, and healed those who needed healing.
Luke 9:12 As the day was ending, the twelve disciples came to him and said, "Send the crowd away so they can go to the nearby towns and countryside to find places to stay and get food, because we are in a remote place."
Luke 9:13 He said to them, "You give them something to eat." But they replied, "We only have five loaves of bread and two fish, unless we go and buy food for everyone."
Luke 9:14 There were about five thousand men. He told his disciples to have them sit down in groups of fifty.
Luke 9:15 They did as told and had everyone sit down.
Luke 9:16 He took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to give to all the people.
Luke 9:17 They ate, were all satisfied, and collected twelve baskets of leftover pieces.
Luke 9:18 While he was praying alone, his disciples joined him. He asked them, "Who do people say I am?"
Luke 9:19 They replied, "John the Baptist; but some think Elijah; and others that a prophet from long ago has come back to life."
Luke 9:20 He asked them, "But who do you say I am?" Peter replied, "The Messiah of God."
Luke 9:21 He strictly told them and ordered them not to tell anyone about that thing.
Luke 9:22 The Son of Man must go through a lot of suffering, be turned away by the elders, the top priests, and the teachers of the law, be killed, and come back to life on the third day.
Luke 9:23 He told everyone, "If anyone wants to follow me, they must forget about their own needs, carry their cross every day, and come with me."
Luke 9:24 Whoever tries to keep their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will save it.
Luke 9:25 What good is it for a person to get the whole world, but lose themselves or be thrown away?
Luke 9:26 Whoever feels ashamed of me and my teachings, the Son of Man will feel ashamed of that person when he comes in his glory, his Father's glory, and the glory of the holy angels.
Luke 9:27 I tell you the truth, some standing here will not die before they see God's kingdom.
Luke 9:28 About eight days after saying this, he took Peter, John, and James and went up a mountain to pray.
Luke 9:29 While he was praying, his face changed, and his clothes became very white and shiny.
Luke 9:30 Two men, Moses and Elias, talked with him.
Luke 9:31 Who appeared in glory and talked about his death that he would complete in Jerusalem.
Luke 9:32 Peter and his friends were very sleepy, but when they woke up, they saw his brightness and the two men with him.
Luke 9:33 After they left him, Peter said to Jesus, "Teacher, it's good for us to be here. Let's make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah," without understanding what he was saying.
Luke 9:34 While he was speaking, a cloud came and covered them, and they were afraid as they went into the cloud.
Luke 9:35 A voice came from the cloud, saying, "This is my dear Son: listen to him."
Luke 9:36 After the voice ended, only Jesus was there. They kept quiet about it and didn’t tell anyone at that time what they had seen.
Luke 9:37 The next day, when they came down from the hill, many people met him.
Luke 9:38 Look, a man in the crowd shouted, "Teacher, please pay attention to my son because he is my only child."
Luke 9:39 Suddenly, a spirit seizes him, and he cries out loudly; it shakes him violently, makes him foam at the mouth, hurts him badly, and only leaves after a struggle.
Luke 9:40 I asked your followers to drive him out, but they couldn't.
Luke 9:41 Jesus answered, "You unbelieving and wrong-thinking people, how long must I stay with you and put up with you? Bring your son here."
Luke 9:42 As he was still approaching, the devil knocked him down and attacked him. Jesus scolded the evil spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
Luke 9:43 Everyone was amazed at the great power of God. But as they were all wondering about everything Jesus did, he spoke to his disciples.
Luke 9:44 Listen carefully to these words: the Son of Man will be handed over to people.
Luke 9:45 They did not understand what he meant, and it was kept secret from them so they could not realize it; and they were afraid to ask him about it.
Luke 9:46 They started to argue about which one of them was the most important.
Luke 9:47 Jesus knew what they were thinking, so he took a child and had him stand next to him.
Luke 9:48 Jesus told them, "Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me also welcomes the one who sent me. The least one among you all will be the greatest."
Luke 9:49 John replied, "Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons using your name; we tried to stop him because he is not one of us."
Luke 9:50 Jesus said to him, "Don't stop him, because if he is not against us, he is with us."
Luke 9:51 When the time came for him to be taken up to heaven, he firmly decided to go to Jerusalem.
Luke 9:52 He sent messengers ahead of him, and they went to a Samaritan village to prepare for his arrival.
Luke 9:53 They did not welcome him because he looked like he was headed for Jerusalem.
Luke 9:54 When James and John, his followers, saw this, they asked, "Do you want us to call down fire from heaven to destroy them, like Elijah did?"
Luke 9:55 He turned, corrected them, and said, "You don't know what kind of spirit you belong to."
Luke 9:56 The Son of man did not come to end people's lives, but to rescue them. Then they moved on to another town.
Luke 9:57 As they traveled, a man said to him, "Lord, I will follow you wherever you go."
Luke 9:58 Jesus said to him, "Foxes have holes, and birds in the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to rest his head."
Luke 9:59 He said to another, "Follow me." But he replied, "Please let me go and bury my father first."
Luke 9:60 Jesus told him, "Let the dead bury their own dead. Instead, go and spread the message of God's kingdom."
Luke 9:61 Someone else said, "God, I will follow you, but first let me say goodbye to those at my home."
Luke 9:62 Jesus said to him, "Anyone who starts to plow but keeps looking back isn't ready for God's kingdom."

Luke 10:1 After this, God chose 70 more people and sent them in pairs to every city and place where he planned to go.
Luke 10:2 He told them, "The harvest is really big, but there are not many workers. So, ask God, who is in charge of the harvest, to send more workers to gather it."
Luke 10:3 Go: I am sending you like lambs among wolves.
Luke 10:4 Don't take a money bag, a backpack, or extra shoes; and don't greet anyone on the road.
Luke 10:5 Whenever you go into a house, first say, "Peace to this house."
Luke 10:6 If a peaceful person is there, your peace will stay with them; if not, it will come back to you.
Luke 10:7 Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they offer, because workers deserve their pay. Do not move from house to house.
Luke 10:8 When you go into any city and people welcome you, eat what they give you.
Luke 10:9 Cure the sick there and tell them, God's kingdom is near you.
Luke 10:10 Whenever you go into a city and they don't welcome you, leave and say in its streets,
Luke 10:11 We even wipe off your city's dust that sticks to us, but remember, God's kingdom is very close to you.
Luke 10:12 I tell you, on that day it will be easier for Sodom than for that city.
Luke 10:13 How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the powerful deeds that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned away from their sins long ago, wearing rough clothing and sitting in ashes.
Luke 10:14 Tyre and Sidon will have an easier time on judgment day than you will.
Luke 10:15 You, Capernaum, raised up to heaven, will be pushed down to hell.
Luke 10:16 Whoever listens to you listens to me; whoever disrespects you disrespects me; and whoever disrespects me disrespects the one who sent me.
Luke 10:17 The seventy came back happy, saying, "God, even the demons listen to us because of your name."
Luke 10:18 He told them, "I saw Satan fall from heaven like a flash of lightning."
Luke 10:19 Look, I give you the power to step on snakes and scorpions, and over all the enemy's power: and nothing will hurt you at all.
Luke 10:20 Don't be happy just because spirits obey you; be happier because your names are written in heaven.
Luke 10:21 At that time, Jesus felt very happy and said, "Thank you, Father, God of heaven and earth, because you kept these things from the smart and careful people, but showed them to little children. Yes, Father, this is what you wanted."
Luke 10:22 God has given me all things: and no one knows the Son, except God; and no one knows God, except the Son, and anyone the Son chooses to show him to.
Luke 10:23 He turned to his followers and quietly said, "Happy are the eyes that see what you see."
Luke 10:24 I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
Luke 10:25 A lawyer stood up to test Jesus and asked, "Teacher, what must I do to get eternal life?"
Luke 10:26 He asked him, "What is written in the law? How do you read it?"
Luke 10:27 He replied, "You should love God with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and all your mind; and love your neighbor as yourself."
Luke 10:28 He told him, "You have answered correctly: do this and you will live."
Luke 10:29 But he wanted to prove himself right and asked Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?"
Luke 10:30 Jesus replied, "A man was going from Jerusalem to Jericho, and robbers attacked him, took his clothes, hurt him, and left him almost dead."
Luke 10:31 By chance, a priest was going that way, and when he saw the man, he crossed to the other side and walked past.
Luke 10:32 A Levite also came to the place, saw the man, and went by on the other side.
Luke 10:33 A Samaritan on his journey saw the hurt man and felt sorry for him.
Luke 10:34 He went to him, treated his wounds with oil and wine, put him on his own animal, took him to a hotel, and looked after him.
Luke 10:35 The next day, when he left, he gave the innkeeper two coins and said, "Look after him. If you spend more, I'll pay you back when I return."
Luke 10:36 Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who was attacked by robbers?
Luke 10:37 He said, "The one who was kind to him." Then Jesus told him, "Go and act the same way."
Luke 10:38 As they traveled, he came to a village where a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
Luke 10:39 She had a sister named Mary, who also sat at Jesus' feet and listened to his teaching.
Luke 10:40 Martha was busy with a lot of serving and went to him and said, "Lord, don't you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me."
Luke 10:41 Jesus answered her, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things:
Luke 10:42 Only one thing is important, and Mary has chosen it. It will not be taken from her.

Luke 11:1 As he was praying in a certain place, when he stopped, one of his followers asked him, "Teach us to pray, just like John taught his followers."
Luke 11:2 He told them, "When you pray, say, 'Father in heaven, your name is holy. Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.'"
Luke 11:3 Give us our bread every day.
Luke 11:4 Forgive our sins, as we forgive everyone who does wrong to us. Don't let us be tempted, but save us from evil.
Luke 11:5 He asked them, "If one of you has a friend and goes to him at midnight to ask, 'Friend, give me three loaves of bread;'
Luke 11:6 A friend of mine on a trip has come to me, and I have nothing to give him.
Luke 11:7 The person inside will reply, "Don't bother me. The door is closed, and my kids are in bed with me; I can't get up to give you anything."
Luke 11:8 I tell you, even if he won't get up and help him because they're friends, he will get up and give him what he needs because he keeps asking.
Luke 11:9 I tell you, ask and you will receive; look and you will find; knock and the door will be opened for you.
Luke 11:10 Everyone who asks receives; whoever seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
Luke 11:11 If a child asks for bread from one of you who is a parent, will you give them a stone instead? Or if they ask for a fish, will you give them a snake?
Luke 11:12 If he asks for an egg, will he be given a scorpion?
Luke 11:13 If you, even though you are not perfect, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will God in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him?
Luke 11:14 He was driving out a demon that could not speak. When the demon left, the once-silent person began to speak, and the crowd was amazed.
Luke 11:15 Some of them said, "He drives out demons by the power of Beelzebub, the leader of the demons."
Luke 11:16 Some people, testing him, asked him for a sign from the sky.
Luke 11:17 He knew what they were thinking and said to them, "A kingdom fighting against itself will be ruined; and a family split apart will fall."
Luke 11:18 If Satan fights against himself, how can his kingdom last? This is because you claim I force out demons using Beelzebub's power.
Luke 11:19 If I drive out demons using Beelzebub, who do your own people use to drive them out? So they will judge you.
Luke 11:20 If I use God's power to drive out demons, then God's kingdom has surely come to you.
Luke 11:21 When a strong man with weapons guards his home, his belongings are safe.
Luke 11:22 When someone stronger attacks and beats him, he takes away all his weapons that he relied on, and shares what he has taken.
Luke 11:23 Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not help me gather, spreads everything out.
Luke 11:24 When the evil spirit leaves a person, it wanders through dry areas, looking for a place to rest; not finding one, it says, I will go back to the home I left.
Luke 11:25 When he comes, he finds it clean and tidy.
Luke 11:26 Then he goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than himself; they go inside and live there. So the person ends up in a worse situation than before.
Luke 11:27 As he was speaking, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, "Happy is the mother who gave birth to you and the breasts you nursed from."
Luke 11:28 But he said, "Yes, even more blessed are those who hear God's word and follow it."
Luke 11:29 When many people came together, he started to say, "This is a bad generation: they want a sign; but no sign will be given to them, except the sign of Jonah the prophet."
Luke 11:30 Just as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, so will the Son of Man be to this generation.
Luke 11:31 The queen from the south will stand up at the time of judgment with the people of today, and accuse them because she traveled from far away to listen to Solomon's wisdom; and look, someone greater than Solomon is here.
Luke 11:32 People from Nineveh will stand up with this generation on judgment day and condemn it because they changed their ways after hearing Jonah's message. But now, someone greater than Jonah is here.
Luke 11:33 When someone lights a candle, they don't hide it or put it under a bowl but on a candle holder so that people coming in can see the light.
Luke 11:34 The eye is the lamp of the body. So, if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be dark.
Luke 11:35 Be careful that the light inside you is not actually darkness.
Luke 11:36 If your whole body is full of light, with no dark part, it will all be bright, like when a candle's glow gives you light.
Luke 11:37 While he was speaking, a Pharisee invited him to have dinner with him. So he went in and sat down to eat.
Luke 11:38 When the Pharisee saw this, he was amazed that he didn't wash before eating.
Luke 11:39 God said to him, "You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and evil."
Luke 11:40 You fools, didn't the one who made the outside also make the inside?
Luke 11:41 Instead, give to the poor from what you have; and then everything will be pure for you.
Luke 11:42 But trouble will come to you, Pharisees! You give a tenth of your mint, rue, and all other herbs, but you ignore justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.
Luke 11:43 Trouble comes to you, Pharisees, because you like the best seats in the synagogues and to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces.
Luke 11:44 Trouble to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, pretenders! You are like hidden graves that people walk over without knowing.
Luke 11:45 One of the legal experts replied, "Teacher, when you say these things, you insult us too."
Luke 11:46 He said, "How terrible for you lawyers! You load people with hard-to-carry burdens, but you don't help carry these burdens at all."
Luke 11:47 You are in trouble because you make tombs for the prophets, but your ancestors killed them.
Luke 11:48 You really show that you agree with what your ancestors did; they killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
Luke 11:49 So God's wisdom said, "I will send them prophets and messengers, and they will kill and mistreat some of them."
Luke 11:50 So that this generation will be held responsible for the blood of all the prophets that has been spilled since the world began.
Luke 11:51 From Abel's death to Zacharias's death, who died between the altar and the temple, I tell you, this generation will be held responsible.
Luke 11:52 Pity you, lawyers! You've removed the key to knowledge: you didn't go in yourselves, and you blocked others who were trying to enter.
Luke 11:53 As he spoke to them, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees started to strongly challenge him, trying to get him to talk about many topics.
Luke 11:54 Waiting for him, they wanted to hear him say something wrong so they could accuse him.

Luke 12:1 While a huge crowd was gathering and people were stepping on each other, he started to tell his disciples, "Be careful of the Pharisees' yeast, which is their fake behavior."
Luke 12:2 Everything hidden will be uncovered, and every secret will be known.
Luke 12:3 Whatever you have said in secret will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in private rooms will be shouted from the rooftops.
Luke 12:4 I tell you, my friends, don't be scared of those who can kill the body but can't do anything more after that.
Luke 12:5 But I will tell you who to be afraid of: Be afraid of the one who, after killing, has the power to throw you into hell; yes, I am telling you, be afraid of him.
Luke 12:6 Aren't five sparrows sold for two small coins, and God doesn't forget even one of them?
Luke 12:7 God knows the number of hairs on your head. So don't be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Luke 12:8 I tell you, if anyone acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man will also acknowledge them before God's angels.
Luke 12:9 Whoever denies me before others will be denied before God's angels.
Luke 12:10 Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven, but anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
Luke 12:11 When they take you to the synagogues, to leaders, and authorities, don't worry about how you will defend yourselves or what to say.
Luke 12:12 The Holy Spirit will teach you at that time what you should say.
Luke 12:13 Someone in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell my brother to share the inheritance with me."
Luke 12:14 He said to him, "Person, who appointed me to be a judge or to split property between you?"
Luke 12:15 He told them, "Be careful and avoid greed: a person's life is not about having a lot of possessions."
Luke 12:16 He told them a story: A rich man's land produced a lot of crops.
Luke 12:17 He thought to himself, "What should I do? I don't have enough space to store my crops."
Luke 12:18 He said, "I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my crops and possessions."
Luke 12:19 I will tell myself, "You have plenty of things stored up for many years; relax, eat, drink, and have fun."
Luke 12:20 God said to him, "You fool, tonight your life will be taken from you. Then who will get what you have prepared?"
Luke 12:21 This is like someone who saves wealth for themselves but isn't generous towards God.
Luke 12:22 He told his disciples, "That's why I'm telling you not to worry about your life, what you will eat; or about your body, what you will wear.
Luke 12:23 Life is more important than food, and the body is more important than clothes.
Luke 12:24 Look at the ravens: they don't plant or harvest; they have no storage or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds?
Luke 12:25 Who among you can grow taller by worrying about it, even by a little bit?
Luke 12:26 If you can't do even the smallest task, why worry about the rest?
Luke 12:27 Look at the flowers and how they grow: they don't work hard or make cloth; but I tell you, not even Solomon in all his splendor was dressed as beautifully as one of these.
Luke 12:28 If God dresses the grass in the field today, which is thrown into the fire tomorrow, won't he give you clothes, you who have little faith?
Luke 12:29 Don't worry about what you will eat, drink, or be uncertain about.
Luke 12:30 All the countries in the world go after these things, and God knows you need them.
Luke 12:31 Instead, look for God's kingdom, and all these things will be given to you.
Luke 12:32 Don't be afraid, small group; because God is happy to give you the kingdom.
Luke 12:33 Sell what you own and give to the poor; make for yourselves money bags that do not wear out, a treasure in heaven that never fails, where no thief can come near and no moth destroys.
Luke 12:34 Where you keep what you value most, that's where your heart will be too.
Luke 12:35 Be ready and keep your lamps lit.
Luke 12:36 Be like people waiting for their master to come back from a wedding, so when he arrives and knocks, they can open the door for him right away.
Luke 12:37 Happy are the servants who are found alert by God when he arrives; truly, I tell you, God will prepare himself, have them sit for a meal, and come out to serve them.
Luke 12:38 If he comes during the second or third watch and finds them ready, those servants are blessed.
Luke 12:39 Know this: if the homeowner knew when the thief would come, he would have stayed awake and not let his house be broken into.
Luke 12:40 So be ready too, because the Son of Man will come at a time you do not expect.
Luke 12:41 Then Peter asked him, "God, are you telling this story to us or to everyone?"
Luke 12:42 God asked, "Who is the trustworthy and sensible manager that his master will put in charge of his household to give them their food at the right time?"
Luke 12:43 Happy is the servant whom his master finds working when he returns.
Luke 12:44 I tell you the truth, he will put him in charge of everything he owns.
Luke 12:45 But if that servant thinks, 'My master is taking a long time to come back,' and starts to hit the other servants, and eats and drinks too much and gets drunk;
Luke 12:46 The master of that servant will come on a day when he's not expecting him, at a time he doesn't know, and will punish him severely, assigning him a place with the disbelievers.
Luke 12:47 The servant who knew what his master wanted but didn't get ready or do what his master wanted will be punished severely.
Luke 12:48 The person who did not know and did wrong will get a light punishment. When someone has been given a lot, a lot will be expected from them. And when people have been trusted with a lot, they will be asked to give even more.
Luke 12:49 I have come to bring fire on the earth; and how I wish it was already burning!
Luke 12:50 But I must go through a baptism; and I feel pressured until it's done!
Luke 12:51 Do you think I came to bring peace on earth? I tell you, no; I came to divide.
Luke 12:52 From now on, five people in one family will be split, three against two and two against three.
Luke 12:53 A father will be against his son, and a son against his father; a mother will be against her daughter, and a daughter against her mother; a mother-in-law will be against her daughter-in-law, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
Luke 12:54 He also told the people, "When you see a cloud coming from the west, right away you say, 'A rain is coming'; and that's what happens."
Luke 12:55 When you see the south wind, you say, "It will be hot," and it happens.
Luke 12:56 You pretenders, you can understand the look of the sky and the earth; but why can't you understand what's happening now?
Luke 12:57 Yes, and why don't you judge for yourselves what is right?
Luke 12:58 When you go to court with your opponent, try hard to settle the matter before you get there. If you don't, your opponent might drag you to the judge, the judge might hand you over to the guard, and the guard might put you in jail.
Luke 12:59 I tell you, you will not leave there until you have paid the very last penny.

Luke 13:1 At that time, some people told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Luke 13:2 Jesus answered them, "Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered this way?"
Luke 13:3 I tell you, no: but unless you change your ways, you will all die just as well.
Luke 13:4 Do you think those eighteen people the tower in Siloam fell on and killed were worse sinners than all the other people living in Jerusalem?
Luke 13:5 I tell you, no: but if you don't change your ways, you will all die just as they did.
Luke 13:6 He also told this story: A man had a fig tree in his vineyard; he looked for fruit on it but found none.
Luke 13:7 He said to the vineyard worker, "Look, for three years I've been looking for fruit on this fig tree and haven't found any. Cut it down; why should it waste the soil?"
Luke 13:8 He replied, "Master, leave it alone for one more year. I will dig around it and put fertilizer on it."
Luke 13:9 If it produces fruit, good; if not, then you should cut it down.
Luke 13:10 He was teaching in a synagogue on the Sabbath.
Luke 13:11 Look, there was a woman who had been sick for eighteen years, bent over and unable to straighten up at all.
Luke 13:12 When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said, "Woman, you are freed from your sickness."
Luke 13:13 He touched her, and right away she could stand up straight and she praised God.
Luke 13:14 The leader of the synagogue was upset because Jesus healed on the Sabbath. He told the people, "There are six days to work, so come to be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath."
Luke 13:15 God answered him, "You hypocrite! Doesn't each of you untie his ox or donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead it to drink water?"
Luke 13:16 Shouldn't this woman, a daughter of Abraham, who has been tied by Satan for eighteen years, be set free from this bond on the Sabbath day?
Luke 13:17 After he said this, all his enemies felt ashamed, and everyone was happy because of the wonderful things he did.
Luke 13:18 He asked, "What is God's kingdom like? What can I compare it to?"
Luke 13:19 It is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a big tree, and the birds made nests in its branches.
Luke 13:20 He said again, "What can I compare God's kingdom to?"
Luke 13:21 It is like yeast that a woman mixed into a large amount of flour until it spread through all of it.
Luke 13:22 He traveled through towns and villages, teaching, and headed towards Jerusalem.
Luke 13:23 Someone asked him, "Sir, are only a few people going to be saved?" And he replied to them,
Luke 13:24 Try hard to go through the narrow door, because I tell you, many will try to enter and will not be able to.
Luke 13:25 When the owner of the house gets up and closes the door, and you start standing outside and knocking on the door, saying, "Sir, Sir, let us in," he will answer, "I don't know where you come from."
Luke 13:26 Then you will start to say, "We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets."
Luke 13:27 But he will say, I tell you, I do not know you or where you come from; go away from me, all you who do wrong.
Luke 13:28 You will cry and grind your teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God's kingdom, but you are thrown out.
Luke 13:29 People will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit in God's kingdom.
Luke 13:30 Look, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.
Luke 13:31 That day some Pharisees came and said to him, "Leave this place and go away, because Herod wants to kill you."
Luke 13:32 He said to them, "Go, tell that fox, 'Look, I drive out demons and heal people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will complete my work.'"
Luke 13:33 I must go on my way today, tomorrow, and the next day, because it's not possible for a prophet to die outside of Jerusalem.
Luke 13:34 Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you; how often I wanted to bring your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you didn't want that!
Luke 13:35 Look, your house is now empty: and I tell you, you won't see me until you say, 'Welcome is the one who comes in God's name.'

Luke 14:1 As he entered a leading Pharisee's home to share a meal on the Sabbath, they observed him closely.
Luke 14:2 Look, there was a man in front of him with swelling in his body.
Luke 14:3 Jesus replied to the lawyers and Pharisees, asking, "Is it allowed to heal on the Sabbath?"
Luke 14:4 They stayed quiet. He took the man, healed him, and released him.
Luke 14:5 He replied, "If one of you has a donkey or an ox that falls into a hole, wouldn't you immediately help it out on the Sabbath day?"
Luke 14:6 They could not reply to him after this.
Luke 14:7 He told a story to the invited guests when he noticed how they picked the best seats, and said to them.
Luke 14:8 When you are invited by someone to a wedding, do not take the best seat; someone more important than you might have been invited by them.
Luke 14:9 The person who invited you and the other man might come and say to you, "Give your seat to this man," and then you will feel embarrassed to move to the least important place.
Luke 14:10 When you are invited, go and sit in the least important place so that the host might come to you and say, “Friend, move to a better seat.” Then you will be honored in front of the other guests.
Luke 14:11 Whoever makes himself important will be made humble; and the one who makes himself humble will be made important.
Luke 14:12 He also told the person who invited him, "When you host a dinner or a meal, don't just invite your friends, family, or rich neighbors; otherwise, they might invite you back and repay you."
Luke 14:13 When you have a feast, invite the poor, the hurt, the crippled, and the blind.
Luke 14:14 You will be blessed because they can't repay you; you will be repaid when good people are raised from death.
Luke 14:15 When someone eating with him heard this, he said to him, "Happy is the one who will eat bread in God's kingdom."
Luke 14:16 He told him, "A man prepared a big dinner and invited many people."
Luke 14:17 He sent his servant at dinner time to tell the invited guests, 'Come, everything is ready now.'
Luke 14:18 They all unanimously started to give excuses. The first one told him, "I have bought some land, and I really need to go see it; please excuse me."
Luke 14:19 Another person said, "I have bought five pairs of oxen and I'm going to try them out. Please excuse me."
Luke 14:20 Someone else said, "I just got married, so I can't come."
Luke 14:21 The servant went and told his master what happened. The master, angry, said to his servant, "Go fast into the city streets and paths, and bring here the poor, the injured, the lame, and the blind."
Luke 14:22 The servant said, "Master, I did what you told me, and there's still space left."
Luke 14:23 God told the servant, "Go out to the roads and fences, and make them come in, so my house will be full."
Luke 14:24 I tell you, none of those men invited will enjoy my dinner.
Luke 14:25 Lots of people followed him: then he turned around and spoke to them.
Luke 14:26 If anyone comes to me and does not put aside love for their father, mother, spouse, children, siblings, and even their own life, they cannot be my student.
Luke 14:27 Whoever does not carry their own cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
Luke 14:28 Which one of you, planning to build a tower, doesn't first sit down and figure out the cost to see if you have enough money to complete it?
Luke 14:29 So that if he lays the foundation and can't finish the building, everyone who sees it will make fun of him.
Luke 14:30 He said, "This person started to build but couldn't finish it."
Luke 14:31 What king, about to fight another king, doesn't sit first and think if he can face an army of twenty thousand with his ten thousand?
Luke 14:32 Otherwise, while the other is still far away, he sends messengers and asks for terms of peace.
Luke 14:33 Just as well, anyone of you who does not give up everything they have cannot be my follower.
Luke 14:34 Salt is good, but if salt loses its taste, how can it be made salty again?
Luke 14:35 It's not good for the soil or the manure pile; it's just thrown away. If someone can listen, they should listen.

Luke 15:1 All the tax collectors and sinners came close to listen to him.
Luke 15:2 The Pharisees and teachers complained, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
Luke 15:3 He told them this story:
Luke 15:4 Which one of you, if you have a hundred sheep and one gets lost, wouldn't leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go search for the lost one until you find it?
Luke 15:5 When he finds it, he puts it on his shoulders, happy.
Luke 15:6 When he gets home, he invites his friends and neighbors over and says to them, "Be happy with me because I found my lost sheep."
Luke 15:7 I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven for one sinner who turns from their wrong ways than for ninety-nine good people who don't need to change.
Luke 15:8 If a woman has ten silver coins and loses one, doesn't she light a lamp, clean the house, and look carefully until she finds it?
Luke 15:9 When she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors and says, "Be happy with me; I've found the coin I lost."
Luke 15:10 I tell you, there is happiness among God's angels when one sinner decides to change their ways.
Luke 15:11 He said, "A man had two sons."
Luke 15:12 The younger son said to his father, "Father, give me my share of the property." So the father divided his wealth between them.
Luke 15:13 Soon after, the younger son collected all he had, traveled to a distant land, and there squandered his wealth with wild living.
