Luke 15:14 After he spent everything, a great famine hit that country, and he started to need things.
Luke 15:15 He went and worked for a local person, and that person sent him to his fields to take care of pigs.
Luke 15:16 He really wanted to fill his stomach with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him any.
Luke 15:17 When he realized his situation, he said, "My father's workers have more than enough bread, while I am starving!"
Luke 15:18 I will get up and go to my father, and will say to him, Father, I've done wrong against heaven and in your sight.
Luke 15:19 I am not worthy to be called your son; treat me like one of your paid workers.
Luke 15:20 He got up and went to his father. When he was still far away, his father saw him, felt sorry for him, ran to him, hugged him, and kissed him.
Luke 15:21 The son said to him, "Father, I have done wrong against heaven and before you, and I am no longer good enough to be called your son."
Luke 15:22 But the father told his servants, Get the best coat and put it on him; and put a ring on his finger, and shoes on his feet.
Luke 15:23 Bring the fat calf here, kill it, let's eat, and be happy.
Luke 15:24 My son was gone, and now he's back to life; he was lost, and now he's found. And they started to celebrate.
Luke 15:25 His older son was out in the fields. As he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
Luke 15:26 He asked one of the workers what was happening.
Luke 15:27 He told him, "Your brother has come back, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf because he got him back healthy and well."
Luke 15:28 He was angry and refused to go in, so his father came out and pleaded with him.
Luke 15:29 He replied to his father, "Look, I have served you for many years and never disobeyed your orders, yet you never gave me a goat to enjoy with my friends.
Luke 15:30 But when this son of yours came back, who wasted your money with prostitutes, you prepared a feast for him with the best calf.
Luke 15:31 He said to him, "Son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours."
Luke 15:32 It was right for us to celebrate and be happy: because your brother was dead, and now he is alive; he was lost, and now he is found.

Luke 16:1 He also told his disciples, "There was a rich man who had a manager accused of wasting his property."
Luke 16:2 He called him and asked, "Why am I hearing these things about you? Explain your management because you might not be the manager anymore."
Luke 16:3 The manager thought to himself, "What should I do? My master is taking away my job. I can't dig, and I'm too ashamed to beg."
Luke 16:4 I have decided what to do so that when I lose my job, people will welcome me into their homes.
Luke 16:5 He called each of his boss's debtors and asked the first one, "How much do you owe my boss?"
Luke 16:6 He said, "A hundred barrels of oil." Then he told him, "Take your bill, sit down fast, and write fifty."
Luke 16:7 Then he asked another, "How much do you owe?" And he replied, "A hundred measures of wheat." So he told him, "Take your bill and write eighty."
Luke 16:8 God praised the unfair manager, because he acted smartly: for the people of this world are smarter in their own time than the people of light.
Luke 16:9 I tell you, use your wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it's gone, they will welcome you into eternal homes.
Luke 16:10 Someone faithful in small things is also faithful in big things; and someone unfair in small things is also unfair in big things.
Luke 16:11 So if you have not been reliable with dishonest wealth, who will trust you with true riches?
Luke 16:12 If you have not been trustworthy with someone else's property, who will give you property of your own?
Luke 16:13 A worker can't work for two bosses: he will hate one and like the other, or be loyal to one and not care for the other. You can't work for God and money at the same time.
Luke 16:14 The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all he said and made fun of him.
Luke 16:15 He told them, "You try to show people you are right, but God knows your hearts. What people value highly is disgusting to God."
Luke 16:16 Before John, there were the law and the prophets; now the kingdom of God is taught, and everyone is trying to enter it.
Luke 16:17 It is simpler for heaven and earth to disappear than for the smallest part of God's law to be wrong.
Luke 16:18 Anyone who divorces his wife and marries someone else is unfaithful, and anyone who marries a woman divorced from her husband is unfaithful.
Luke 16:19 There was a rich man who wore purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day.
Luke 16:20 A poor man named Lazarus, who was covered in sores, was placed at his gate.
Luke 16:21 He wanted to eat the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table. Even dogs came and licked his wounds.
Luke 16:22 The poor man died and the angels took him to be with Abraham. The rich man also died and was buried.
Luke 16:23 In hell, he opened his eyes, suffering in pain, and saw Abraham far away with Lazarus close to him.
Luke 16:24 He called out, "Father Abraham, please have pity on me. Send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am suffering in this fire."
Luke 16:25 Abraham said, "Son, remember that you had good things in your life, and Lazarus had bad things. But now he is comforted, and you are suffering."
Luke 16:26 Moreover, there is a big gap between us and you: so those who want to go from here to you can't, nor can anyone cross over to us from there.
Luke 16:27 He then said, "Please, father, send him to my father's house."
Luke 16:28 I have five brothers; he should warn them, so they won't come to this place of suffering.
Luke 16:29 Abraham says to him, "They have Moses and the prophets; they should listen to them."
Luke 16:30 And he said, "No, Father Abraham. But if someone from the dead goes to them, they will change their ways."
Luke 16:31 He told him, "If they don't listen to Moses and the prophets, they won't be convinced even if someone rises from the dead."

Luke 17:1 He told his followers, "It's impossible to avoid problems, but bad things will happen to the person who causes them!"
Luke 17:2 It would be better for him to have a heavy stone tied around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to hurt one of these little ones.
Luke 17:3 Be careful with yourselves: If your brother does wrong to you, correct him; and if he is sorry, forgive him.
Luke 17:4 If he wrongs you seven times in a day, and seven times he comes back to you and says, 'I am sorry,' you must forgive him.
Luke 17:5 The apostles said to God, "Make our faith grow."
Luke 17:6 And God said, "If you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you could tell this mulberry tree, 'Be pulled out by the roots and planted in the sea,' and it would listen to you."
Luke 17:7 Which of you, if you have a servant plowing or taking care of the animals, will tell him as soon as he comes in from the field, 'Go and sit down to eat'?
Luke 17:8 Won't you instead tell him, 'Prepare my dinner, put on your apron, and serve me while I eat and drink; after that, you can eat and drink'?
Luke 17:9 Does he thank the servant for doing what was commanded? I don't think so.
Luke 17:10 In the same way, when you have done everything you were told to do, say, 'We are servants who have not earned any favor; we have only done our duty.'
Luke 17:11 As he was going to Jerusalem, he went through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
Luke 17:12 As he went into a village, ten men with leprosy met him and stood at a distance.
Luke 17:13 They raised their voices and said, "Jesus, Teacher, please help us."
Luke 17:14 When he saw them, he told them, "Go show yourselves to the priests." As they went, they were healed.
Luke 17:15 When one of them saw he was healed, he came back praising God loudly.
Luke 17:16 He fell with his face to the ground at Jesus' feet, thanking him, and he was a Samaritan.
Luke 17:17 Jesus replied, "Weren't ten people cleansed? But where are the other nine?"
Luke 17:18 No one else came back to thank God, only this foreigner.
Luke 17:19 He said to him, "Get up, go on your way; your faith has healed you."
Luke 17:20 When the Pharisees asked him when God's kingdom would come, he replied, "God's kingdom doesn't come in a way you can see it."
Luke 17:21 No one will say, 'Look here!' or 'Look there!' because God's kingdom is inside you.
Luke 17:22 He told the disciples, "A time will come when you'll want to see just one of the days of the Son of man, but you won't be able to."
Luke 17:23 People might tell you, 'Look here!' or 'Look there!' Don't go or follow them.
Luke 17:24 Just like lightning that flashes from one part of the sky and shines to the other part, so will the Son of Man be on his day.
Luke 17:25 First, he must go through a lot and be rejected by this generation.
Luke 17:26 Just like in Noah's time, it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
Luke 17:27 They ate, they drank, they got married, they were given for marriage, until the day Noah went into the ark, and the flood came and wiped them all out.
Luke 17:28 Just like in Lot's time, people ate, drank, bought, sold, farmed, and built.
Luke 17:29 On the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained from the sky and destroyed everyone.
Luke 17:30 It will be the same on the day when the Son of man is shown.
Luke 17:31 On that day, if someone is on the rooftop and their belongings are inside, they should not go down to get them. And if someone is in the field, they should not go back either.
Luke 17:32 Remember Lot's wife.
Luke 17:33 Anyone trying to save their life will lose it, and anyone who loses their life will keep it.
Luke 17:34 I tell you, that night two men will be in one bed; one will be taken, and the other will be left.
Luke 17:35 Two women will be grinding grain together; one will be taken, and the other left behind.
Luke 17:36 Two people will be in the field; one will be taken, and the other will be left behind.
Luke 17:37 They replied, "Where, Lord?" He said to them, "Wherever there is a dead body, that's where the eagles will gather."

Luke 18:1 He told them a story to show that they should always pray and never give up.
Luke 18:2 Someone said, "In a city, there was a judge who did not fear God or care about people."
Luke 18:3 In that city, there was a widow; she approached him and said, "Get justice for me from my opponent."
Luke 18:4 He didn't want to for some time, but later he thought, "Even though I don't fear God or care about people;
Luke 18:5 Since this widow keeps bothering me, I will help her so she won't keep coming and wear me out.
Luke 18:6 God said, "Listen to what the unfair judge says."
Luke 18:7 Won't God protect his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night, even though he is patient with them?
Luke 18:8 I tell you, God will quickly make things right for them. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find people with faith on the earth?
Luke 18:9 He told this story to some who were sure they were good people and looked down on everyone else:
Luke 18:10 Two men went to the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
Luke 18:11 The Pharisee stood up and prayed quietly to himself, 'God, I am thankful that I am not like other people—cheaters, unjust, unfaithful in marriage, or even like this tax collector.
Luke 18:12 I skip eating twice a week, I give part of everything I have.
Luke 18:13 The tax collector stood at a distance, wouldn't even look up to heaven, but hit his chest and said, "God, have mercy on me, a sinner."
Luke 18:14 I tell you, this man went home right with God rather than the other: for everyone who lifts himself up will be put down, and he who lowers himself will be lifted up.
Luke 18:15 They also brought babies to him, so he could touch them. But when his followers saw this, they told them off.
Luke 18:16 Jesus called them to him and said, "Let little children come to me, and don't stop them: for God's kingdom belongs to ones like these."
Luke 18:17 I tell you the truth, anyone who doesn't accept God's kingdom like a little child will never enter it.
Luke 18:18 A leader asked him, "Good Teacher, what must I do to have eternal life?"
Luke 18:19 Jesus asked him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God."
Luke 18:20 You know the commands: Don't cheat in marriage, don't kill, don't steal, don't lie about others, respect your father and mother.
Luke 18:21 He said, "I have followed all these since I was young."
Luke 18:22 When Jesus heard this, he told him, "You still need one thing: sell everything you own, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me."
Luke 18:23 When he heard this, he became very sad because he was very rich.
Luke 18:24 When Jesus saw how sad the man was, he said, "It's really hard for rich people to get into God's kingdom!"
Luke 18:25 It is easier for a camel to pass through the hole of a needle than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom.
Luke 18:26 Those who heard this asked, "Then who can be saved?"
Luke 18:27 He said, What is impossible for people is possible with God.
Luke 18:28 Then Peter said, "Look, we have left everything and followed you."
Luke 18:29 He told them, "Truly, I tell you, no one who has left home, parents, brothers, wife, or children for God's kingdom,
Luke 18:30 Who will not get much more in this time, and in the future eternal life.
Luke 18:31 He gathered the twelve disciples and said to them, "Look, we're going to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will happen."
Luke 18:32 He will be handed over to non-Jews, laughed at, badly treated, and spit on.
Luke 18:33 They will whip him, kill him, and on the third day, he will rise again.
Luke 18:34 They did not understand any of these things; the meaning was hidden from them, and they did not know what was said.
Luke 18:35 As he approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road, begging.
Luke 18:36 Hearing the crowd go by, he asked what it was about.
Luke 18:37 They told him that Jesus from Nazareth is passing by.
Luke 18:38 He shouted, "Jesus, son of David, please be kind to me."
Luke 18:39 The people in front told him to be quiet, but he shouted even louder, "Son of David, have mercy on me."
Luke 18:40 Jesus stood up and ordered that the man be brought to him. When the man came close, Jesus asked him.
Luke 18:41 Asking, "What do you want me to do for you?" He replied, "Sir, I want to see again."
Luke 18:42 Jesus said to him, "Get your sight back; your faith has healed you."
Luke 18:43 Right away he could see, and he followed him, praising God; and when all the people saw this, they also praised God.

Luke 19:1 Jesus went into Jericho and passed through it.
Luke 19:2 Look, there was a man called Zacchaeus, who was the top tax collector, and he was wealthy.
Luke 19:3 He wanted to see who Jesus was but couldn't because of the crowd and because he was short.
Luke 19:4 He ran ahead and climbed a fig tree to see him, because Jesus was going to pass that way.
Luke 19:5 When Jesus reached the spot, he looked up, saw Zacchaeus, and said, "Hurry and come down, Zacchaeus; I need to stay at your house today."
Luke 19:6 He hurried, came down, and welcomed him happily.
Luke 19:7 When they saw this, everyone complained, saying, "He has gone to stay with a man who is a sinner."
Luke 19:8 Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, I give half of what I own to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will pay back four times as much."
Luke 19:9 Jesus told him, "Today, salvation has come to this house, because he too is a descendant of Abraham."
Luke 19:10 The Son of Man has come to look for and save what was lost.
Luke 19:11 As they listened, he told them a story because he was close to Jerusalem and they believed that God's kingdom would soon start.
Luke 19:12 He therefore said, "A nobleman went to a distant country to get a kingdom for himself, and then come back."
Luke 19:13 He called his ten workers, gave them ten pounds each, and said to them, "Work with this until I return."
Luke 19:14 His people hated him and sent a message behind him, saying, "We don't want this man to rule over us."
Luke 19:15 When he returned after receiving the kingdom, he asked the servants he had given money to come to him, so he could find out how much each one had earned from trading.
Luke 19:16 The first one came and said, "Master, your money has earned ten more."
Luke 19:17 He said to him, "Good job, you good servant. Since you were loyal with a little, you will be in charge of ten cities."
Luke 19:18 The second one came and said, "Master, your money has earned five more."
Luke 19:19 He also said to him, "You will be in charge of five cities."
Luke 19:20 Another person came and said, 'Sir, look, here is your money, which I kept wrapped in a cloth.'
Luke 19:21 I was afraid of you, because you are a strict man. You take what you didn't leave, and you harvest what you didn't plant.
Luke 19:22 He said to him, "I will judge you by your own words, you bad servant. You knew that I am a strict man, collecting what I didn't deposit, and gathering what I didn't plant."
Luke 19:23 Why didn't you put my money in the bank so I could have collected it with interest when I returned?
Luke 19:24 He told those standing there, "Take the pound from him and give it to the one who has ten pounds."
Luke 19:25 They said to him, "Master, he has ten coins."
Luke 19:26 I tell you, whoever has something will get more; whoever has nothing, even what they have will be taken away.
Luke 19:27 Bring my enemies, who didn't want me to be their ruler, here and kill them in front of me.
Luke 19:28 After he said this, he went ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
Luke 19:29 When he got close to Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his followers.
Luke 19:30 Say, go to the village ahead of you; as you enter, you will find a tied colt no one has ever ridden; untie it and bring it here.
Luke 19:31 If anyone asks you why you are untying the animal, tell them, 'God needs it.'
Luke 19:32 The ones sent went and found everything just as he told them.
Luke 19:33 As they untied the colt, its owners asked them, "Why are you untying the colt?"
Luke 19:34 They said, God needs him.
Luke 19:35 They brought him to Jesus, and they threw their clothes on the young donkey and put Jesus on it.
Luke 19:36 As he walked, they laid their clothes on the road.
Luke 19:37 When he got close, just as he was coming down the Mount of Olives, all the followers started to joyfully praise God loudly for all the powerful things they had seen.
Luke 19:38 "Saying, 'God bless the King who comes in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory to the highest.'"
Luke 19:39 Some Pharisees in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell your followers to stop."
Luke 19:40 He answered and said to them, "I tell you, if they keep quiet, the stones will cry out right away."
Luke 19:41 When he got close, he saw the city and cried for it.
Luke 19:42 Saying, if you had known, even you, at least on this day, the things that bring you peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
Luke 19:43 A time will come when your enemies will surround you with barriers and enclose you from all sides.
Luke 19:44 God will level you to the ground, and your children with you; not one stone will be left on another, because you did not recognize the time when God came to you.
Luke 19:45 He entered the temple and started to drive out those who were selling and buying there.
Luke 19:46 He told them, "It is written, 'My house is a house of prayer,' but you have turned it into a hideout for thieves."
Luke 19:47 He taught every day in the temple. But the religious leaders, the teachers of the law, and the important people wanted to kill him.
Luke 19:48 They didn't know what to do because all the people were listening carefully to him.

Luke 20:1 One day, while he was teaching the people in the temple and sharing the good news, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders approached him.
Luke 20:2 He spoke to him, asking, "Tell us, by what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority?"
Luke 20:3 He replied and said to them, "I will ask you one thing too; answer me:"
Luke 20:4 Did John's baptism come from God or from people?
Luke 20:5 They thought to themselves, "If we say, 'From God,' he will ask, 'Then why didn't you believe him?'"
Luke 20:6 But if we say, 'From people,' everyone will stone us because they are convinced John was a prophet.
Luke 20:7 They replied that they did not know where it came from.
Luke 20:8 Jesus said to them, "I won't tell you by what authority I do these things."
Luke 20:9 He started to tell the people this story: A man planted a vineyard, rented it to farmers, and went away for a long time.
Luke 20:10 During the right time, he sent a worker to the farmers, asking for some of the vineyard's fruit; but the farmers beat him and sent him back with nothing.
Luke 20:11 He sent another servant, but they also beat him, treated him badly, and sent him away with nothing.
Luke 20:12 He sent another servant, but they hurt this one too and threw him out.
Luke 20:13 Then the owner of the vineyard said, "What should I do? I will send my beloved son; maybe they will respect him when they see him."
Luke 20:14 When the farmers saw him, they talked to each other and said, "This is the heir. Let's kill him so we can have his inheritance."
Luke 20:15 They threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. So, what will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
Luke 20:16 He will come and get rid of those farmers, and he will give the vineyard to others. When they heard this, they said, "May God not let that happen."
Luke 20:17 He looked at them and asked, "What does this mean that is written, 'The stone that the builders did not want has become the most important cornerstone'?"
Luke 20:18 Anyone who falls on that stone will break; but if it falls on someone, it will crush that person to dust.
Luke 20:19 The religious leaders and teachers wanted to arrest Jesus right away, but they were scared of the crowd because they knew he told this story about them.
Luke 20:20 They kept an eye on him and sent out spies pretending to be good men to catch his words, so they could hand him over to the governor's control.
Luke 20:21 They asked him, "Teacher, we know you speak and teach what is right, and you don't favor anyone, but teach God's way truthfully."
Luke 20:22 Is it right for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?
Luke 20:23 He saw their trickery and asked them, "Why are you testing me?"
Luke 20:24 Show me a coin. Whose picture and inscription are on it? They replied, "Caesar's."
Luke 20:25 He told them, "Give back to the ruler what belongs to the ruler, and give to God what belongs to God."
Luke 20:26 They couldn't catch him in his words before everyone; they were amazed at his reply and kept quiet.
Luke 20:27 Some Sadducees, who say there's no resurrection, came to him and asked him a question.
Luke 20:28 Teacher, Moses told us, if a man dies and has a wife but no children, his brother should marry the widow and have children for his brother.
Luke 20:29 So there were seven brothers. The first married but died without having any kids.
Luke 20:30 The second one married her, and he died without having children.
Luke 20:31 The third brother married her; and the same happened with all seven brothers: they had no children and then passed away.
Luke 20:32 Finally, the woman died too.
Luke 20:33 So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven were married to her.
Luke 20:34 Jesus replied, "People in this world get married and are married off."
Luke 20:35 But those who are considered worthy to be part of that world and to be raised from the dead will neither marry nor be married off.
Luke 20:36 They cannot die anymore because they are like the angels and are God's children, as they belong to the resurrection.
Luke 20:37 Now that the dead are raised, Moses showed at the bush, when he called God the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
Luke 20:38 He is not a God of the dead, but of the living; everyone lives for him.
Luke 20:39 Some teachers of the law replied, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
Luke 20:40 After that, they did not dare to ask him any more questions.
Luke 20:41 He asked them, "Why do people say the Christ is David's son?"
Luke 20:42 David himself says in the book of Psalms, "God said to my lord, 'Sit at my right side,'"
Luke 20:43 Until I make your enemies a place to rest your feet.
Luke 20:44 David calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?
Luke 20:45 In front of everyone, he spoke to his disciples,
Luke 20:46 Be careful of the teachers of the law who like to wear long robes and enjoy being greeted in the marketplaces, having the best seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
Luke 20:47 They cheat widows out of their homes and pretend to be pious by making long prayers. These people will be punished more severely.

Luke 21:1 He looked up and saw the wealthy people putting their gifts into the treasury.
Luke 21:2 He also saw a poor widow put in two small coins.
Luke 21:3 He said, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has given more than everyone else."
Luke 21:4 All these people gave from their wealth to God's offerings, but she, in her poverty, gave all she had to live on.
Luke 21:5 As some talked about the temple, how it was decorated with beautiful stones and offerings, he said.
Luke 21:6 Look at these things you see, a time will come when not one stone will be left on another; each one will be knocked down.
Luke 21:7 They asked him, "Teacher, when will these things happen, and what sign will there be when these things are about to take place?"
Luke 21:8 He said, "Be careful not to be fooled. Many will come saying 'I am the Christ,' and will tell you the time is close. Do not follow them."
Luke 21:9 When you hear about wars and turmoil, don't be afraid; these things must happen first, but it doesn't mean the end is right away.
Luke 21:10 He told them, "Nation will fight against nation, and kingdom against kingdom."
Luke 21:11 Big earthquakes will happen in different places, along with famines and diseases; and there will be scary things and big signs from the sky.
Luke 21:12 Before these things happen, people will capture you and mistreat you. They will take you to religious places and jails, and you will stand before leaders and authorities because of me.
Luke 21:13 It will become a witness for you.
Luke 21:14 Decide in your hearts not to worry beforehand about what to say in your defense.
Luke 21:15 I will give you words and wisdom that none of your enemies will be able to oppose or reject.
Luke 21:16 You will be betrayed by your parents, brothers, relatives, and friends; some of you will even be killed.
Luke 21:17 Everyone will hate you because of me.
Luke 21:18 Not one hair on your head will be lost.
Luke 21:19 Be patient and keep control of yourselves.
Luke 21:20 When you see armies surrounding Jerusalem, know that its ruin is near.
Luke 21:21 Those in Judea should run to the mountains; those in the city should leave; and those in the countryside should not go into the city.
Luke 21:22 These are the days of revenge when everything written will come true.
Luke 21:23 But trouble will come to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days, for there will be great trouble in the country and anger against these people.
Luke 21:24 They will be killed by the sword and taken as prisoners to all nations. Jerusalem will be trampled on by foreigners until the period of the foreigners is complete.
Luke 21:25 There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; on earth, nations will be in distress and confused; the sea and its waves will roar.
Luke 21:26 People will faint from fear and worry about what is coming upon the world, because the powers of the skies will be disturbed.
Luke 21:27 Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
Luke 21:28 When these events start happening, look up and raise your heads because your rescue is near.
Luke 21:29 He told them a story: Look at the fig tree and all the other trees.
Luke 21:30 When they start growing, you see and understand by yourselves that summer is almost here.
Luke 21:31 In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that God's kingdom is very close.
Luke 21:32 I truly tell you, this group of people will not disappear until everything happens.
Luke 21:33 Heaven and earth will disappear, but my words will never disappear.
Luke 21:34 Be careful not to let your hearts get weighed down with excess, drunkenness, and the worries of life, so that day won't catch you by surprise.
Luke 21:35 It will come like a trap on everyone living on the entire earth.
Luke 21:36 Stay alert and pray at all times so that you may be considered worthy to avoid all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.
Luke 21:37 During the day, he taught in the temple, and at night, he left and stayed on the hill known as the Mount of Olives.
Luke 21:38 All the people came early in the morning to the temple to hear him.

Luke 22:1 The time for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, also known as Passover, was near.
Luke 22:2 The high priests and teachers of the law wanted to find a way to kill him; they were afraid of the people.
Luke 22:3 Satan entered into Judas, known as Iscariot, one of the twelve disciples.
Luke 22:4 He went and talked with the chief priests and officers about how he could hand him over to them.
Luke 22:5 They were happy and agreed to pay him money.
Luke 22:6 He promised and looked for a chance to hand him over to them when the crowd was not around.
Luke 22:7 The day came for the bread without yeast when it was time for the Passover lamb to be sacrificed.
Luke 22:8 He sent Peter and John, telling them, "Go and get the Passover ready for us to eat."
Luke 22:9 They asked him, "Where do you want us to prepare?"
Luke 22:10 He told them, "Look, when you go into the city, a man carrying a water jar will meet you; follow him into the house he enters."
Luke 22:11 You will tell the owner of the house, 'The Teacher asks you, where is the guest room where I can eat the Passover meal with my followers?'
Luke 22:12 He will show you a big room upstairs that's ready: prepare there.
Luke 22:13 They went and found everything just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
Luke 22:14 When the time came, he sat down with the twelve apostles.
Luke 22:15 He said to them, "I have really wanted to eat this Passover meal with you before I go through hard times."
Luke 22:16 I tell you, I won't eat it again until it comes true in God's kingdom.
Luke 22:17 He took the cup, thanked God, and said, "Take this and share it among you."
Luke 22:18 I tell you, I won't drink from the grapevine until God's kingdom comes.
Luke 22:19 He took bread, thanked God, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body given for you; do this to remember me."
Luke 22:20 After supper, Jesus took the cup and said, "This cup represents the new agreement in my blood, poured out for you."
Luke 22:21 Look, the hand of the one who will betray me is with mine on the table.
Luke 22:22 Truly, the Son of Man will go as planned, but how terrible it will be for the man who betrays him!
Luke 22:23 They started to ask each other which one of them would do this.
Luke 22:24 There was also an argument among them about who should be considered the greatest.
Luke 22:25 He told them, "The rulers of the nations rule over them, and those with power over the people are called good leaders."
Luke 22:26 But you must not be like that: instead, whoever is the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and whoever leads should be like someone who serves.
Luke 22:27 Who is more important, the one who sits and eats, or the one who serves? Isn't it the one who sits and eats? But I am with you as one who serves.
Luke 22:28 You are those who have stayed with me through my trials.
Luke 22:29 I give you a kingdom, just as my Father has given one to me.
Luke 22:30 You may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
Luke 22:31 God said, "Simon, Simon, listen, Satan wants to take you, to shake you like wheat."
Luke 22:32 I have prayed for you that your faith will not fail; and when you turn back, help your brothers be strong.
Luke 22:33 He said to him, "Master, I am ready to follow you, even to jail and to death."
Luke 22:34 He said, "I tell you, Peter, before the rooster crows today, you will deny three times that you know me."
Luke 22:35 He asked them, "When I sent you without money, bag, or sandals, did you need anything?" And they answered, "No."
Luke 22:36 He then told them, "But now, if you have a purse, take it, and your bag too; if you don't have a sword, sell your clothes to buy one."
Luke 22:37 I tell you that what is written must happen to me. I must be counted among the wrongdoers, for what is said about me is coming to an end.
Luke 22:38 And they said, "Master, look, here are two swords." And he replied, "That's enough."
Luke 22:39 He came out and went to the Mount of Olives, as he usually did, and his disciples followed him.
Luke 22:40 When he was there, he told them, "Pray so you won't give in to temptation."
Luke 22:41 He moved away from them about as far as you can throw a stone, kneeled down, and prayed.
Luke 22:42 Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me: but let your will, not mine, be done.
Luke 22:43 An angel from heaven appeared to him, giving him strength.
Luke 22:44 Feeling very troubled, he prayed even harder, and his sweat was like big drops of blood falling to the ground.
Luke 22:45 After praying, he went to his disciples and saw they were asleep because they were sad.
Luke 22:46 He asked them, "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray so you don't give in to temptation."
Luke 22:47 While he was still talking, a crowd appeared, and Judas, one of the twelve, led them to Jesus to kiss him.
Luke 22:48 But Jesus said to him, "Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?"
Luke 22:49 When the people around him saw what was going to happen, they asked, "Master, should we attack with our swords?"
Luke 22:50 One of them struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear.
Luke 22:51 Jesus responded, "Allow this for now." He then touched the man's ear and healed him.
Luke 22:52 Then Jesus said to the chief priests, the temple guards, and the elders who came to him, "Did you come out with swords and clubs as if I were a thief?"
Luke 22:53 When I was with you every day in the temple, you did not try to hurt me. But now is your time, and darkness has power.
Luke 22:54 They took him, led him, and brought him to the high priest's house. Peter followed from a distance.
Luke 22:55 When they made a fire in the middle of the room and sat together, Peter sat with them.
Luke 22:56 A servant girl saw him sitting by the fire, stared at him, and said, "This man was with him too."
Luke 22:57 He denied knowing him, saying, "Woman, I don't know him."
Luke 22:58 After a short time, someone else saw Peter and said, "You are one of them too." But Peter replied, "No, I am not."
Luke 22:59 About an hour later, another person strongly said, "For sure, this man was with him too: because he is from Galilee."
Luke 22:60 Peter said, "I don't know what you're talking about." And right away, as he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
Luke 22:61 God turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered what God had told him: "Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times."
Luke 22:62 Peter went out and cried a lot.
Luke 22:63 The men who were holding Jesus made fun of him and hit him.
Luke 22:64 After they covered his eyes, they hit him in the face and asked, "Guess who hit you?"
Luke 22:65 They said many other disrespectful things against him.
Luke 22:66 As soon as it was morning, the leaders and the head priests and the teachers of the law met together and took him into their meeting, asking,
Luke 22:67 Are you the Messiah? Tell us. And he said to them, If I tell you, you will not believe.
Luke 22:68 If I ask you too, you won't answer or let me go.
Luke 22:69 From now on, the Son of Man will sit at the right side of God's power.
Luke 22:70 They all asked, "Are you the Son of God?" He answered, "You say that I am."
Luke 22:71 They asked, "Do we need more evidence? We've heard it from his own mouth."

Luke 23:1 The whole crowd got up and took him to Pilate.
Luke 23:2 They started to accuse him, saying, "We caught this man corrupting the nation and telling people not to pay taxes to Caesar, claiming he is Christ, a king."
Luke 23:3 Pilate asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" He replied, "You say so."
Luke 23:4 Pilate said to the religious leaders and the people, "I find nothing wrong with this man."
Luke 23:5 They became even angrier, saying, "He causes trouble among the people, teaching all over Judea, starting from Galilee to here."
Luke 23:6 When Pilate heard about Galilee, he asked if the man was from Galilee.
Luke 23:7 As soon as he found out that he was under Herod's authority, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem then.
Luke 23:8 When Herod saw Jesus, he was very happy, because he had wanted to see him for a long time after hearing so much about him; he also hoped to see Jesus perform a miracle.
Luke 23:9 He asked him many questions, but he gave no answer.
Luke 23:10 The leading priests and teachers of the law stood and strongly accused him.
Luke 23:11 Herod and his soldiers ignored Jesus, made fun of him, dressed him in a fancy robe, and sent him back to Pilate.
Luke 23:12 On that day, Pilate and Herod became friends; before that, they had been enemies.
Luke 23:13 Pilate gathered the chief priests, leaders, and the people.
Luke 23:14 He said to them, "You have brought this man to me as someone who corrupts the people. But look, I have questioned him in front of you and have found him not guilty of the accusations you make against him."
Luke 23:15 No, not even Herod, because I sent you to him, and look, he has done nothing that deserves death.
Luke 23:16 I will punish him and then let him go.
Luke 23:17 He had to release one prisoner to them during the feast.
Luke 23:18 They all shouted together, "Get rid of this man and free Barabbas for us."
Luke 23:19 He was put in jail for causing a riot in the city and for murder.
Luke 23:20 So Pilate, wanting to let Jesus go, spoke to them again.
Luke 23:21 They shouted, "Crucify him, crucify him."
Luke 23:22 He asked them a third time, "What wrong has he done? I've found no reason to kill him. So, I'll punish him and then release him."
Luke 23:23 They urgently shouted, wanting him to be crucified. And their voices, along with the chief priests', were stronger.
Luke 23:24 Pilate decided to do what they asked.
Luke 23:25 He freed the one they wanted who was in prison for causing trouble and murder, but he handed Jesus over to do what they wished.
Luke 23:26 As they took him away, they grabbed Simon from Cyrene, who was coming from the fields, and gave him the cross to carry behind Jesus.
Luke 23:27 A large crowd followed him, including women who mourned and cried for him.
Luke 23:28 Jesus turned to them and said, "Women of Jerusalem, don't cry for me, but cry for yourselves and your children."
Luke 23:29 Look, the time is coming when people will say, "Happy are those who cannot have children, the wombs that never gave birth, and the breasts that never nursed."
Luke 23:30 Then they will start to tell the mountains, "Fall on us," and to the hills, "Hide us."
Luke 23:31 If this happens to a living tree, what will happen to a dead one?
Luke 23:32 Two other criminals were also led with him to be executed.
Luke 23:33 When they reached the place known as Calvary, they nailed him to the cross along with the criminals, one on his right and the other on his left.
Luke 23:34 Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, because they don't know what they're doing." They shared out his clothes by throwing dice.
Luke 23:35 The people watched. The leaders mocked him, saying, "He saved others; let him save himself if he is the Messiah, the one chosen by God."
Luke 23:36 The soldiers also made fun of him, went up to him, and gave him vinegar.
Luke 23:37 They said, "If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself."
Luke 23:38 A sign was also put above him with the words in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew, "This is the King of the Jews."
Luke 23:39 One of the criminals hanging beside Jesus insulted him, saying, "If you are the Christ, save yourself and us."
Luke 23:40 But the other one scolded him, saying, "Don't you respect God since you are also being punished the same way?"
Luke 23:41 We are punished fairly, for we are getting what our actions deserve; but this man has done nothing wrong.
Luke 23:42 He told Jesus, "Remember me when you come into your kingdom."
Luke 23:43 Jesus said to him, "I tell you the truth, today you will be with me in paradise."
Luke 23:44 It was around noon, and darkness covered the whole earth until about three in the afternoon.
Luke 23:45 The sun turned dark, and the temple's curtain ripped down the middle.
Luke 23:46 When Jesus shouted loudly, he said, "Father, I give my spirit to you." After saying this, he died.
Luke 23:47 When the army officer saw what happened, he praised God, saying, "This man was truly good."
Luke 23:48 All the people who gathered to see what happened beat their chests and then went away.
Luke 23:49 All his friends and the women who had followed him from Galilee stood at a distance watching these things.
Luke 23:50 Look, there was a man named Joseph, who was a counselor; he was good and fair.
Luke 23:51 He did not agree with their plan and action; he came from Arimathaea, a Jewish city, and he also waited for God's kingdom.
Luke 23:52 This man went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body.
Luke 23:53 He took the body down, wrapped it in cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut out of rock where no one had ever been laid before.
Luke 23:54 That day was for getting ready, and the Sabbath was about to start.
Luke 23:55 The women who had come with him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how his body was placed.
Luke 23:56 They went back and got spices and ointments ready. Then they rested on the Sabbath day, as the rule said.

Luke 24:1 On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they went to the tomb with the spices they had made, and some others were with them.
Luke 24:2 They saw that the stone was moved from the tomb's entrance.
Luke 24:3 They went in and did not find the body of Jesus.
Luke 24:4 While they were very confused about this, suddenly two men in bright clothes stood beside them.
Luke 24:5 As they were scared and looked down at the ground, they asked them, "Why are you looking for the living among the dead?"
Luke 24:6 He is not here; he has risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee.
Luke 24:7 The Son of Man must be handed over to sinners, be crucified, and rise on the third day.
Luke 24:8 They remembered what he said.
Luke 24:9 They came back from the tomb and told everything to the eleven disciples and to all the others.
Luke 24:10 Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and other women with them told the apostles these things.
Luke 24:11 What they said sounded like nonsense, and they did not believe it.
Luke 24:12 Peter got up and ran to the tomb; bending over, he saw the linen wrappings lying alone, and he left, amazed at what had happened.
Luke 24:13 Two of them went to a village named Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem, that day.
Luke 24:14 They talked about all these things that had happened.
Luke 24:15 While they were talking and discussing, Jesus himself came close and walked along with them.
Luke 24:16 But they could not recognize him because their eyes were prevented.
Luke 24:17 He asked them, "What are you discussing so intently as you walk along, looking so sad?"
Luke 24:18 One of them, named Cleopas, replied, "Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who doesn't know the things that have happened here these days?"
Luke 24:19 He asked them, "What things?" They answered, "About Jesus from Nazareth, who was a powerful prophet in actions and words before God and all the people."
Luke 24:20 The leading priests and our leaders handed him over to be sentenced to death and crucified him.
Luke 24:21 We hoped he was the one to save Israel, and what's more, today is the third day since this all happened.
Luke 24:22 Yes, some women from our group also surprised us; they were at the tomb early in the morning.
Luke 24:23 When they did not find his body, they came back saying they had seen a vision of angels who told them he was alive.
Luke 24:24 Some of us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but we did not see him.
Luke 24:25 Then he told them, "You are foolish and slow to trust what the prophets have said:"
Luke 24:26 Shouldn't Christ have suffered these things and entered into his glory?
Luke 24:27 Starting with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them what was said about himself in all the Scriptures.
Luke 24:28 They got close to the village where they were headed, and it seemed like he wanted to keep going.
Luke 24:29 But they urged him, saying, "Stay with us, because it is almost night, and the day is almost over." So he went in to stay with them.
Luke 24:30 While he was eating with them, he took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them.
Luke 24:31 Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; then he disappeared from their sight.
Luke 24:32 They said to each other, "Didn't our hearts feel warm as he talked to us on the road and explained the scriptures to us?"
Luke 24:33 They got up that same hour, went back to Jerusalem, and found the eleven and those with them all together.
Luke 24:34 They said, "The Lord has really risen and has shown himself to Simon."
Luke 24:35 They shared what happened on the road and how they recognized him when he broke the bread.
Luke 24:36 While they were talking, Jesus himself appeared among them and said to them, "Peace to you."
Luke 24:37 They were very scared and thought they had seen a ghost.
Luke 24:38 He asked them, "Why are you worried? And why do you have doubts in your hearts?"
Luke 24:39 Look at my hands and my feet, it's really me. Touch me and see; a spirit doesn't have flesh and bones like you see I have.
Luke 24:40 After saying this, he showed them his hands and feet.
Luke 24:41 While they still couldn't believe because of their happiness, and were amazed, he asked them, "Do you have any food?"
Luke 24:42 They gave him some cooked fish and honeycomb.
Luke 24:43 He took it and ate it in front of them.
Luke 24:44 He told them, "These are the words I told you when I was still with you: everything written about me in Moses' law, the prophets, and the psalms must come true."
Luke 24:45 He opened their minds so they could understand the scriptures.
Luke 24:46 He told them, "It is written that Christ must suffer and rise from the dead on the third day."
Luke 24:47 People should be taught to change their ways and be forgiven for their sins in his name everywhere, starting from Jerusalem.
Luke 24:48 You are witnesses of these things.
Luke 24:49 Look, I will send you what my Father promised, but stay in the city of Jerusalem until you receive power from above.
Luke 24:50 He led them to Bethany, raised his hands, and blessed them.
Luke 24:51 While he was blessing them, he left them and went up into heaven.
Luke 24:52 They worshiped him and went back to Jerusalem feeling very happy.
Luke 24:53 They were always in the temple, praising and thanking God. Amen.

John 1:1 At the start, the Word existed, the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
John 1:2 He was with God from the start.
John 1:3 God made everything; nothing was made without him.
John 1:4 In him was life, and that life was the light for everyone.
John 1:5 The light shines in the dark, but the dark did not understand it.
John 1:6 God sent a man named John.
John 1:7 He came as a witness to tell about the Light, so that everyone might believe through him.
John 1:8 He was not the Light, but came to testify about the Light.
John 1:9 That was the real Light, giving light to everyone coming into the world.
John 1:10 He was in the world, and he made the world, but the world did not know him.
John 1:11 He came to his own people, but they did not accept him.
John 1:12 But as many as accepted him, to them he gave the right to become God's children, even to those who believe in his name.
John 1:13 They were born, not from human origin or human desire, but from God.
John 1:14 The Word became a human and lived with us, and we saw his glory, the glory of God's one and only Son, full of kindness and truth.
John 1:15 John gave witness about him, shouting, "This is who I was talking about when I said, 'The one who comes after me ranks higher than me because he existed before me.'"
John 1:16 From his fullness, we have all received one blessing after another.
John 1:17 Moses gave the law, but Jesus Christ brought grace and truth.
John 1:18 No one has ever seen God, but the unique Son, who is close to the Father's heart, has made him known.
John 1:19 This is John's testimony when the Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"
John 1:20 He admitted and did not deny; he admitted, I am not the Christ.
John 1:21 They asked him, "What then? Are you Elijah?" He said, "I am not. Are you the prophet?" He answered, "No."
John 1:22 They asked him, "Who are you? We need to give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"
John 1:23 He said, "I am someone shouting in the desert, 'Prepare the path for God,' just as the prophet Isaiah said."
John 1:24 The people who were sent came from the Pharisees.
John 1:25 They asked him, "Why do you baptize if you are not the Messiah, Elijah, or the prophet?"
John 1:26 John replied to them, "I baptize with water, but there is someone among you who you do not recognize.
John 1:27 He is the one who comes after me, but is greater than me, and I am not good enough to untie his sandal.
John 1:28 These things happened in Bethabara across the Jordan River, where John was baptizing.
John 1:29 The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, "Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the world's sin."
John 1:30 This is the person I was talking about. A man comes after me who is more important than I am because he existed before me.
John 1:31 I did not know him, but I came to baptize with water so that he might be shown to Israel.
John 1:32 John testified, saying, "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove, and it stayed on him."
John 1:33 I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water told me, 'The person you see the Spirit coming down on and staying with is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'
John 1:34 I saw and confirmed that this is God's Son.
John 1:35 The next day John was there again with two of his followers.
John 1:36 Seeing Jesus walking, he said, Look, the Lamb of God!
John 1:37 The two followers heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
John 1:38 Jesus turned around, saw them following, and asked, "What are you looking for?" They answered, "Teacher, where are you staying?"
John 1:39 He said to them, "Come and see." They came and saw where he lived and stayed with him that day; it was about four o'clock in the afternoon.
John 1:40 One of the two people who heard John and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.
John 1:41 He first finds his brother Simon and tells him, "We have found the Messiah," which means Christ.
John 1:42 He took him to Jesus. When Jesus saw him, he said, "You are Simon, son of Jonah. You will be called Cephas," which means a rock.
John 1:43 The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee, where he met Philip and said to him, "Follow me."
John 1:44 Philip came from Bethsaida, the hometown of Andrew and Peter.
John 1:45 Philip found Nathanael and told him, "We have found the one Moses in the law, and the prophets wrote about, Jesus from Nazareth, Joseph's son."
John 1:46 Nathanael asked him, "Can anything good come from Nazareth?" Philip answered, "Come and see."
John 1:47 Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him and said about him, "Look, a true Israelite, who is not deceitful!"
John 1:48 Nathanael asked him, "How do you know me?" Jesus replied, "Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you."
John 1:49 Nathanael answered him, "Teacher, you are God's Son; you are the king of Israel."
John 1:50 Jesus replied, "Do you believe because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see things even greater than that."
John 1:51 He said to him, "Truly, truly, I tell you, you will see heaven open and God's angels going up and down on the Son of Man."

John 2:1 On the third day, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and Jesus' mother was there.
John 2:2 Jesus and his followers were invited to the wedding.
John 2:3 When they ran out of wine, Jesus' mother told him, "They have no wine."
John 2:4 Jesus said to her, "Woman, why involve me? My time hasn't come yet."
John 2:5 His mother told the servants, "Whatever he tells you to do, do it."
John 2:6 Six stone water jars were placed there, used by the Jews for ritual washing, each holding two or three firkins.
John 2:7 Jesus told them, "Put water in the jars." And they filled them to the top.
John 2:8 He said to them, "Take some out now, and give it to the master of the banquet." So they did.
John 2:9 When the person in charge of the party tasted the water that had turned into wine, without knowing where it came from (though the servants who got the water knew), the leader of the party called the groom.
John 2:10 He said to him, "Everyone first serves the good wine, and when people have had enough to drink, they bring out the cheaper wine. But you have saved the good wine for now."
John 2:11 Jesus did his first miracle in Cana, Galilee, showing his glory; his followers then believed in him.
John 2:12 After this, he went to Capernaum with his mother, brothers, and disciples, and they stayed there for a short time.
John 2:13 The Jewish Passover was coming soon, and Jesus went to Jerusalem.
John 2:14 He found in the temple people selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers sitting down.
John 2:15 He made a whip from cords and chased everyone out of the temple, along with the sheep and cattle. He spilled the money changers' coins and flipped over their tables.
John 2:16 He said to those selling doves, "Take these things away; do not turn my Father's house into a place for selling goods."
John 2:17 His followers remembered the scripture: "Passion for your house consumes me."
John 2:18 The Jews replied to him, "What sign can you show us to prove you have the right to do these things?"
John 2:19 Jesus replied to them, "Tear down this temple, and in three days I will rebuild it."
John 2:20 The Jewish leaders said, "It took forty-six years to build this temple, and you can raise it in three days?"
John 2:21 He was talking about the temple of his body.
John 2:22 So when he had risen from the dead, his followers remembered he had told them this; and they believed the scripture and what Jesus had said.
John 2:23 While he was in Jerusalem during the Passover festival, many people trusted in him because they saw the miracles he performed.
John 2:24 But Jesus didn't trust himself to them because he knew everyone.
John 2:25 He didn't need anyone to tell him about people because he knew what was in everyone.

John 3:1 A Pharisee named Nicodemus was a Jewish leader.
John 3:2 He came to Jesus at night and said, "Teacher, we know you have come from God because no one can do the miracles you do unless God is with him."
John 3:3 Jesus replied, "Truly, I tell you, unless a person is born again, they cannot see God's kingdom."
John 3:4 Nicodemus said to him, "How can an old man be born again? Can he go back into his mother's womb and be born a second time?"
John 3:5 Jesus replied, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, they cannot enter God's kingdom."
John 3:6 What comes from the body is body; and what comes from the Spirit is spirit.
John 3:7 Don't be surprised when I tell you, you must be born again.
John 3:8 The wind blows where it wants, and you hear the sound of it, but you can't tell where it comes from or where it goes: so it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
John 3:9 Nicodemus replied and asked him, "How can this happen?"
John 3:10 Jesus answered him, "Are you a teacher of Israel and don't know these things?"
John 3:11 Truly, truly, I tell you, we talk about what we know and share what we have seen, but you do not accept our testimony.
John 3:12 If I have spoken to you about things of this world and you do not believe, how will you believe if I speak to you about things of heaven?
John 3:13 No one has gone up to heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven.
John 3:14 Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the desert, the Son of Man must also be lifted up.
John 3:15 Everyone who believes in him will not die but have forever life.
John 3:16 God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not die but have eternal life.
John 3:17 God did not send his Son into the world to judge it, but to save the world through him.
John 3:18 Whoever believes in him is not judged, but whoever does not believe is already judged, because they have not believed in the name of God's only Son.
John 3:19 This is the judgment: Light has come into the world, but people loved darkness more than light because their actions were bad.
John 3:20 Everyone who does bad things hates the light and doesn't come to the light, so their actions won't be criticized.
John 3:21 But the person who does what is true comes to the light, so that it can be clearly seen that their actions have been done through God.
John 3:22 After this, Jesus and his followers went to the area of Judea; there he stayed with them and performed baptisms.
John 3:23 John was also baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there; so people came and were baptized.
John 3:24 John had not yet been put in prison.
John 3:25 A dispute about how to purify oneself arose between some of John's followers and the Jewish people.
John 3:26 They went to John and said, "Teacher, the one you talked about on the other side of the Jordan River is now baptizing, and everyone is going to him."
John 3:27 John replied, "A person can only get what is given to them from heaven."
John 3:28 You can testify that I said I am not the Christ, but I am sent ahead of him.
John 3:29 The one with the bride is the groom; but the groom's friend, who stands by and listens, is very happy to hear the groom's voice. So my happiness is complete.
John 3:30 He must become greater, but I must become less.
John 3:31 The one who comes from above is greater than all; the one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and talks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is greater than all.
John 3:32 What he has seen and heard, he tells; but no one accepts what he says.
John 3:33 The one who accepts what he has said shows that God is truthful.
John 3:34 The one God sends speaks God's words because God gives the Spirit without limit to him.
John 3:35 God loves the Son and has given everything into his control.
John 3:36 Anyone who believes in the Son has eternal life; but anyone who doesn't believe in the Son won't have life, and God's anger stays on them.

John 4:1 When God knew that the Pharisees heard Jesus was making and baptizing more followers than John,
John 4:2 Jesus himself did not baptize, but his followers did.
John 4:3 He left Judea and went back to Galilee.
John 4:4 He had to go through Samaria.
John 4:5 He came to a city in Samaria named Sychar, close to the land Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
John 4:6 Jacob's well was there. Jesus, tired from his trip, sat on the well. It was about noon.
John 4:7 A Samaritan woman came to get water; Jesus said to her, "Give me a drink."
John 4:8 His followers had gone to the city to buy food.
John 4:9 The Samaritan woman asked him, "Why do you, a Jew, ask me for a drink when I am a Samaritan woman? Jews don't associate with Samaritans."
John 4:10 Jesus replied to her, "If you knew God's gift and who is saying to you, 'Give me a drink,' you would have asked him and he would have given you living water."
John 4:11 The woman said to him, "Sir, you have nothing to get water with, and the well is deep. Where can you get that living water?"
John 4:12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did his children and his animals?
John 4:13 Jesus replied to her, "Anyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again."
John 4:14 Anyone who drinks the water I give them will never be thirsty again; the water I give them will become a source inside them, flowing up into eternal life.
John 4:15 The woman said to him, "Sir, give me this water so I won't be thirsty or have to come here to get water."
John 4:16 Jesus said to her, "Go, get your husband, and come back here."
John 4:17 The woman replied, "I don't have a husband." Jesus told her, "You are right to say 'I don't have a husband.'"
John 4:18 You've had five husbands; and the man you're with now is not your husband. You spoke the truth about that.
John 4:19 The woman said to him, "Sir, I see that you are a prophet."
John 4:20 Our ancestors worshipped on this mountain, but you say that Jerusalem is where people should worship.
John 4:21 Jesus said to her, "Woman, trust me, the time is coming when you won't worship the Father on this mountain or in Jerusalem.
John 4:22 You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know because salvation comes from the Jews.
John 4:23 The time is coming, and it is now, when true worshipers will worship God in spirit and truth: for God looks for such people to worship him.
John 4:24 God is a Spirit, and those who worship Him should worship in spirit and truth.
John 4:25 The woman said to him, "I know the Messiah is coming, the one called Christ: when he comes, he will explain everything to us."
John 4:26 Jesus said to her, "I who am talking to you am he."
John 4:27 His disciples arrived and were surprised to see him talking with a woman, but no one asked, "What do you want?" or "Why are you talking with her?"
John 4:28 The woman left her water jar and went back to the city. She said to the people,
John 4:29 Come, see a man who told me everything I've done: could this be the Christ?
John 4:30 They left the city and came to him.
John 4:31 While this was happening, his followers asked him, "Teacher, please eat."
John 4:32 He told them, "I have food to eat that you don't know about."
John 4:33 The followers asked each other, "Did anyone bring him something to eat?"
John 4:34 Jesus said to them, "My food is to do what God wants, who sent me, and to complete his work."
John 4:35 Do not say, "There are still four months until the harvest." I tell you, look at the fields, they are ready to be harvested now.
John 4:36 The person who harvests gets paid and collects fruit for eternal life, so that the one who plants and the one who harvests can be happy together.
John 4:37 And this saying is true: one person plants, another one harvests.
John 4:38 I sent you to harvest where you did not work; others did the work, and you are taking over what they did.
John 4:39 Many people from that city believed in Jesus because of what the woman said when she told them, "He told me everything I've done."
John 4:40 When the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them, and he stayed there for two days.
John 4:41 Many more people believed because of what he said.
John 4:42 They said to the woman, "We believe now, not just because of what you said. We have heard him ourselves and know that he truly is the Christ, the Savior of the world."
John 4:43 Two days later, he left and went to Galilee.
John 4:44 Jesus himself said, a prophet is not respected in his own homeland.
John 4:45 When he arrived in Galilee, the people there welcomed him because they had seen all he did in Jerusalem during the festival, since they had gone to the festival too.
John 4:46 Jesus returned to Cana in Galilee, where he had turned water into wine. A nobleman's son was ill in Capernaum.
John 4:47 When he heard that Jesus had come from Judaea to Galilee, he went to him and asked him to come and heal his son, because his son was about to die.
John 4:48 Jesus said to him, "If you don't see miracles and amazing things, you won't believe."
John 4:49 The nobleman said to him, "Sir, please come before my child dies."
John 4:50 Jesus said to him, "Go on; your son is alive." The man believed what Jesus had said to him and left.
John 4:51 As he was heading down, his servants met him and told him, "Your son is alive."
John 4:52 He asked them at what time he started to get better. They told him, "The fever went away yesterday at one in the afternoon."
John 4:53 The father realized it was the exact time Jesus told him, "Your son will live." He and his whole family believed.
John 4:54 This is the second miracle Jesus performed after he left Judaea for Galilee.

John 5:1 After this, the Jews had a festival, and Jesus went to Jerusalem.
John 5:2 In Jerusalem near the sheep trading area, there is a pool named Bethesda in Hebrew, with five covered walkways.
John 5:3 In this place, many sick people, blind, lame, and paralyzed, waited for the water to move.
John 5:4 An angel sometimes went into the pool and stirred up the water. The first person to get in after the water was stirred was healed of any illness they had.
John 5:5 A man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
John 5:6 When Jesus saw him lying there and knew he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, "Do you want to get well?"
John 5:7 The weak man said to him, "Sir, I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred, and while I am trying to get there, someone else goes in before me."
John 5:8 Jesus said to him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and walk."
John 5:9 Right away, the man got well, picked up his mat, and walked. That day was the Sabbath.
John 5:10 The Jewish people said to the man who was healed, "It is the Sabbath day; you are not allowed to carry your bed."
John 5:11 He replied, "The one who healed me told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
John 5:12 Then they asked him, "Who is the man who told you, 'Pick up your mat and walk'?"
John 5:13 The healed man did not know who had cured him, because Jesus had slipped away due to the crowd in that place.
John 5:14 Later, Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, "Look, you are healed. Don't sin again or something worse may happen to you."
John 5:15 The man left and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
John 5:16 So the Jews were against Jesus and wanted to kill him because he did these things on the Sabbath.
John 5:17 But Jesus replied, "My Father has always been at work to this very day, and I too am working."
John 5:18 So the Jews wanted even more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath but also claimed that God was his Father, making himself equal to God.
John 5:19 Jesus replied to them, "I tell you the truth, the Son can do nothing by himself. He only does what he sees God doing. Whatever God does, the Son does the same."
John 5:20 God loves the Son and shows him everything he does: and he will show him even greater things than these, so that you will be amazed.
John 5:21 Just as God brings the dead back to life, the Son also gives life to whoever he chooses.
John 5:22 God does not judge anyone, but has given all judgment to the Son.
John 5:23 Everyone should respect the Son just like they respect the Father. If someone doesn't respect the Son, they don't respect the Father who sent him.
John 5:24 Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears my word and believes in the one who sent me, has eternal life and will not be judged; but has moved from death to life.
John 5:25 Truly, truly, I tell you, the time is coming, and it is now, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
John 5:26 Just as the Father has life in himself, so he has granted the Son to have life in himself.
John 5:27 God has given him power to judge because he is the Son of Man.
John 5:28 Don't be surprised: a time will come when all in the graves will hear his voice.
John 5:29 People who have done good will rise to live; those who have done bad will rise to be judged.
John 5:30 I can do nothing by myself; I make judgments based on what I hear, and my judgments are fair because I don't follow my own desires, but the desires of God who sent me.
John 5:31 If I speak for myself, my words are not true.
John 5:32 Someone else speaks for me, and I know that what he says about me is true.
John 5:33 You sent people to John, and he told the truth.
John 5:34 I don't accept praise from people, but I tell you this so you can be saved.
John 5:35 He was a bright and shining light, and for a while you were happy to enjoy his light.
John 5:36 I have proof stronger than John's: the tasks God gave me to complete, which I am doing, show that God has sent me.
John 5:37 God, who sent me, has testified about me. You have never heard his voice or seen his form.
John 5:38 You don't keep God's message inside you, because you don't believe the one he sent.
John 5:39 Look in the Bible; you believe it has the words for eternal life, and it tells about me.
John 5:40 You don't come to me to have life.
John 5:41 I do not seek praise from people.
John 5:42 But I know you do not have God's love in you.
John 5:43 I came in my Father's name, but you do not accept me. If someone else comes using his own name, you will accept him.
John 5:44 How can you believe when you accept praise from each other but don't look for the praise that comes only from God?
John 5:45 Don't believe I will blame you before God: Moses, who you trust, is the one who accuses you.
John 5:46 If you had believed Moses, you would believe me because he wrote about me.
John 5:47 If you don't believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?

John 6:1 After this, Jesus crossed the Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Tiberias.
John 6:2 Many people followed him because they saw the amazing things he did for the sick.
John 6:3 Jesus went up a mountain and sat there with his followers.
John 6:4 The Passover, a Jewish celebration, was near.
John 6:5 When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward him, he asked Philip, "Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?"
John 6:6 He said this to test him, because he already knew what he was going to do.
John 6:7 Philip told him, "Even two hundred coins worth of bread wouldn't be enough for them so that each person can have a small piece."
John 6:8 One of Jesus' followers, Andrew, who was Simon Peter's brother, said to him,
John 6:9 Here is a boy with five loaves of barley bread and two small fish, but how far will they go among so many people?
John 6:10 Jesus said, "Have the men sit down." There was a lot of grass there. So the men sat down, about five thousand in total.
John 6:11 Jesus took the bread, thanked God, gave it to his disciples, and they gave it to the seated people. They did the same with the fish, giving as much as everyone wanted.
John 6:12 When they had enough to eat, he told his disciples, "Pick up the leftover pieces so nothing is wasted."
John 6:13 So they collected and filled twelve baskets with leftover pieces of the five barley breads after everyone had eaten.
John 6:14 When the men saw the miracle Jesus performed, they said, "Truly, this is the prophet who was to come into the world."
John 6:15 When Jesus knew they wanted to force him to be their king, he went away to a mountain by himself.
John 6:16 When evening came, his followers went to the sea.
John 6:17 They got into a boat and sailed across the lake to Capernaum. It was night, and Jesus had not yet joined them.
John 6:18 The sea got rough because a strong wind was blowing.
John 6:19 After they had rowed about five or six kilometers, they saw Jesus walking on the water, coming near the boat; and they were scared.
John 6:20 He said to them, "It's me; don't be scared."
John 6:21 They happily let him into the boat, and right away the boat reached the shore where they were going.
John 6:22 The next day, when the people on the other side of the sea noticed that there was no other boat except the one his disciples had gotten into, and that Jesus had not gone with his disciples in the boat but his disciples had left by themselves;
John 6:23 But other boats from Tiberias came near the place where they ate bread after God had given thanks.
John 6:24 When the people saw that Jesus and his followers were not there, they took boats and went to Capernaum to look for Jesus.
John 6:25 When they found him across the sea, they asked him, "Teacher, when did you get here?"
John 6:26 Jesus replied, "Truly, truly, I tell you, you look for me not because you saw the miracles but because you ate the bread and were satisfied."
John 6:27 Work not for food that spoils, but for food that lasts forever, which the Son of Man will give you. For God has confirmed his authority.
John 6:28 They asked him, "What should we do to do God's work?"
John 6:29 Jesus answered them, "The work God wants is that you believe in the one He has sent."
John 6:30 They therefore said to him, "What sign do you show us, so we can see and believe you? What do you do?"
John 6:31 Our ancestors ate manna in the desert; it is said, God gave them bread from heaven to eat.
John 6:32 Jesus told them, "Truly, I tell you, Moses did not give you the bread from heaven; but my Father gives you the real bread from heaven."
John 6:33 God's bread is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.
John 6:34 Then they said to him, "Sir, always give us this bread."
John 6:35 Jesus said to them, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty."
John 6:36 I told you that you have seen me but you do not believe.
John 6:37 Everyone the Father gives to me will come to me; and I will never reject anyone who comes to me.
John 6:38 I came from heaven not to do what I want, but to do what God, who sent me, wants.
John 6:39 God wants me to lose nothing he has given me, but to bring it back to life on the last day.
John 6:40 God wants that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him will have eternal life, and I will bring him back to life on the final day.
John 6:41 The Jews complained about him because he said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven."
John 6:42 They asked, "Isn't this Jesus, Joseph's son, who we know his parents? How can he say, 'I came from heaven'?"
John 6:43 Jesus answered them, "Do not complain to each other."
John 6:44 No one can come to me unless God who sent me draws them: and I will lift them up on the last day.
John 6:45 The prophets wrote, 'Everyone will be taught by God.' So everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to me.
John 6:46 No one has seen the Father, except the one from God; he has seen the Father.
John 6:47 Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me has eternal life.
John 6:48 I am the bread of life.
John 6:49 Your ancestors ate manna in the desert, and they died.
John 6:50 This is the bread that comes down from heaven so that a person can eat it and not die.
John 6:51 I am the bread of life that came from heaven; if anyone eats this bread, they will live forever; and the bread I will give is my body, which I will give to save the world.
John 6:52 The Jews argued with each other, asking, "How can this man offer us his flesh to eat?"
John 6:53 Jesus told them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the Son of man's flesh and drink his blood, you do not have life in you."
John 6:54 Anyone who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day.
John 6:55 My body is real food, and my blood is real drink.
John 6:56 Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood lives in me, and I live in them.
John 6:57 The living God sent me, and I live because of God: just as he who eats my flesh will live because of me.
John 6:58 This is the bread that came down from heaven; it's not like the manna your ancestors ate and then died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.
John 6:59 He said these things while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
John 6:60 Many of his followers, when they heard this, said, "This teaching is difficult; who can accept it?"
John 6:61 When Jesus realized that his followers were complaining about it, he asked them, "Does this upset you?"
John 6:62 What if you see the Son of Man go up to where he was before?
John 6:63 The Spirit gives life; the body gives nothing of value: the words I tell you are Spirit and they are life.
John 6:64 But some of you do not believe. Jesus knew from the start who did not believe and who would betray him.
John 6:65 He said, "This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless my Father allows it."
John 6:66 From then on, many of his followers left and no longer walked with him.
John 6:67 Jesus then asked the twelve, "Do you want to leave as well?"
John 6:68 Simon Peter replied, "Master, who else can we turn to? You have the message of everlasting life."
John 6:69 We believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
John 6:70 Jesus replied, "Didn't I pick you twelve, and isn't one of you evil?"
John 6:71 He spoke about Judas Iscariot, Simon's son because he was the one who would betray him, even though he was one of the twelve.

John 7:1 After this, Jesus stayed in Galilee because he did not want to be in Judea where the Jewish leaders wanted to kill him.
John 7:2 The Jewish festival of shelters was coming soon.
John 7:3 His brothers told him, "Leave this place and go to Judea, so your followers can see what you are doing."
John 7:4 No one does things secretly if they want to be known publicly. If you do these things, let everyone see you.
John 7:5 His brothers did not believe in him.
John 7:6 Then Jesus told them, "My time has not come yet, but your time is always here."
John 7:7 The world cannot hate you; but it hates me because I say that its actions are evil.
John 7:8 Go to this festival; I am not going yet because my time has not fully come.
John 7:9 After he spoke to them, he stayed in Galilee.
John 7:10 After his brothers left, he also went to the festival, not publicly, but in secret.
John 7:11 During the festival, the Jewish people looked for him and asked, "Where is he?"
John 7:12 Many people whispered about him: some said, "He is good," while others said, "No, he tricks the people."
John 7:13 However, no one talked about him publicly because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders.
John 7:14 During the festival, Jesus went to the temple and taught.
John 7:15 The Jews were amazed and asked, "How does this man know so much when he has never been taught?"
John 7:16 Jesus told them, "My teaching is not my own, but belongs to the one who sent me."
John 7:17 If anyone chooses to do God's will, they will understand the teaching and know whether it comes from God or if I am speaking on my own.
John 7:18 Someone who talks about themselves wants their own praise. But if a person seeks to honor the one who sent them, they are true, and there's nothing wrong in them.
John 7:19 Didn't Moses give you the law, but none of you follow it? Why do you want to kill me?
