John 7:20 The people replied, "You are crazy: who is trying to kill you?"
John 7:21 Jesus replied to them, "I did one thing, and you are all amazed."
John 7:22 Moses gave you the practice of circumcision; (though it didn't start with Moses, but with the ancestors;) and you even circumcise a man on the Sabbath day.
John 7:23 If a man is circumcised on the Sabbath so the law of Moses isn't broken, why are you mad at me for healing a man completely on the Sabbath?
John 7:24 Do not judge by how things look, but judge with fair judgment.
John 7:25 Some people from Jerusalem asked, "Isn't this the man they want to kill?"
John 7:26 Look, he speaks openly, and no one says anything to him. Do the leaders really know that he is the Christ?
John 7:27 We know where this man comes from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from.
John 7:28 Jesus shouted in the temple as he was teaching, saying, "You all know me, and you know where I'm from. I didn't come on my own, but the one who sent me is real, and you don't know him.
John 7:29 I know him because I come from him, and he sent me.
John 7:30 They tried to seize him, but no one touched him because his time had not yet come.
John 7:31 Many people believed in him and asked, "When the Messiah comes, will he perform more miracles than this man has?"
John 7:32 The Pharisees heard the people whispering these things about him; so the Pharisees and the head priests sent guards to arrest him.
John 7:33 Jesus said to them, "I will be with you a little longer, then I will go to the one who sent me."
John 7:34 You will look for me but won't find me; and you can't go where I am.
John 7:35 Then the Jews said to each other, "Where is he planning to go that we can't find him? Will he go to the scattered Jews among the non-Jews and teach the non-Jews?"
John 7:36 What does he mean by saying, "You will look for me, but you won't find me: and you can't come where I am"?
John 7:37 On the final day, the big feast day, Jesus stood up and shouted, "If anyone is thirsty, come to me and drink."
John 7:38 Whoever believes in me, just as the scripture has said, streams of living water will flow from within them.
John 7:39 He said this about the Spirit, which believers in him would receive: The Spirit had not yet come, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
John 7:40 So when the people heard this, many said, "Truly, this is the Prophet."
John 7:41 Some people said, "This is the Christ." But others asked, "Does the Christ come from Galilee?"
John 7:42 Doesn't the scripture say that Christ will come from David's family, and from Bethlehem, the town where David lived?
John 7:43 People were divided because of him.
John 7:44 Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one touched him.
John 7:45 The officers went to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they asked, "Why didn't you bring him?"
John 7:46 The officers replied, "No one ever spoke like this person."
John 7:47 The Pharisees replied, "Have you been tricked too?"
John 7:48 Have any leaders or Pharisees believed in him?
John 7:49 But these people who do not know the law are cursed.
John 7:50 Nicodemus, who had visited Jesus at night and was one of the group, said to them.
John 7:51 Does our law judge anyone before it hears him and knows what he is doing?
John 7:52 They replied to him, "Are you from Galilee too? Look and see: no prophet comes from Galilee."
John 7:53 Everyone went to their own home.

John 8:1 Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
John 8:2 Early in the morning, he went back to the temple, and all the people came to him. He sat down and taught them.
John 8:3 The teachers of the law and the Pharisees brought to him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand in front of everyone.
John 8:4 They told him, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of cheating on her husband."
John 8:5 Moses told us in the law that we should stone such people: but what do you say?
John 8:6 They said this to test him, so they could find a reason to blame him. But Jesus bent down and wrote on the ground with his finger, pretending not to hear them.
John 8:7 When they kept asking him, he stood up and said to them, "If any of you have never sinned, you can throw the first stone at her."
John 8:8 He bent down again and wrote on the ground.
John 8:9 Those who heard it, feeling guilty themselves, left one after another, starting with the oldest to the youngest: and only Jesus and the woman standing there were left.
John 8:10 When Jesus stood up and saw only the woman, he said to her, "Woman, where are your accusers? Didn't anyone condemn you?"
John 8:11 She said, "No one, God." And Jesus told her, "I don't condemn you either: go and don't sin again."
John 8:12 Jesus spoke to them again, saying, "I am the light of the world: whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life."
John 8:13 The Pharisees said to him, You speak about yourself; your words are not true.
John 8:14 Jesus answered them, "Even though I speak for myself, my words are true. I know where I came from and where I am going, but you don't know where I come from or where I am going."
John 8:15 You judge by human standards; I judge no one.
John 8:16 If I decide something, it is right because it's not just me, but also God who sent me.
John 8:17 Your law also says that if two men agree in their story, it is true.
John 8:18 I testify about myself, and the Father who sent me also testifies about me.
John 8:19 They asked him, "Where is your father?" Jesus replied, "You don't know me or my father. If you knew me, you would know my father as well."
John 8:20 Jesus said these words in the temple room where offerings were kept while he was teaching, and no one tried to arrest him because it was not the right time for that yet.
John 8:21 Jesus spoke to them again, saying, "I am leaving, and you will look for me, but you will die in your sins. Where I am going, you cannot come."
John 8:22 The Jews asked, "Is he going to kill himself?" because he says, "Where I am going, you cannot follow."
John 8:23 He said to them, "You are from below; I am from above. You belong to this world; I do not belong to this world."
John 8:24 I told you that you will die in your sins; if you don't believe that I am the one, you will die in your sins.
John 8:25 They asked him, "Who are you?" And Jesus answered, "I am who I have told you from the start."
John 8:26 I have a lot to say about you and to judge you by: but God who sent me is truthful, and I tell the world what I've heard from him.
John 8:27 They did not understand that he was talking to them about God.
John 8:28 Jesus said to them, "When you have raised up the Son of Man, you will know that I am the one, and I do nothing on my own. I speak what my Father has taught me."
John 8:29 The one who sent me is with me: God has not left me by myself; because I always do what pleases him.
John 8:30 When he said this, many people believed in him.
John 8:31 Jesus said to the Jews who believed in him, "If you keep following my teachings, you are truly my followers."
John 8:32 You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
John 8:33 They replied, "We are Abraham's descendants and have never been slaves to anyone. How can you say, 'You will be set free'?"
John 8:34 Jesus told them, "Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever does sin is a slave to sin."
John 8:35 The servant does not stay in the house forever, but the Son stays forever.
John 8:36 If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free.
John 8:37 I know you are Abraham's descendants; but you want to kill me because my message has no room in you.
John 8:38 I tell what I have seen with my God, and you do what you have seen with your father.
John 8:39 They replied, "Abraham is our father." Jesus said to them, "If you were really Abraham's children, you would do what Abraham did."
John 8:40 But now you want to kill me, a man who has told you the truth from God. Abraham did not do this.
John 8:41 You act like your father. Then they said to him, We were not born out of wedlock; we have one Father, God.
John 8:42 Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love me, because I came from God. I didn't come on my own; He sent me."
John 8:43 Why don't you understand what I'm saying? It's because you can't really listen to my message.
John 8:44 You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to do what he desires. He was a killer from the start and has never stood for truth, because there's no truth in him. When he lies, he's speaking his native language, because he is a liar and the source of all lies.
John 8:45 Because I tell you the truth, you do not believe me.
John 8:46 Who among you can prove I have sinned? If I'm telling the truth, why don't you believe me?
John 8:47 Whoever is from God listens to God's words: you don't listen because you are not from God.
John 8:48 The Jewish people replied, asking him, "Don't we speak the truth saying you are a Samaritan and are possessed by a demon?"
John 8:49 Jesus replied, "I don't have a demon; I respect my Father, but you disrespect me."
John 8:50 I do not look for my own honor; there is one who looks for it and judges.
John 8:51 Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone follows my teaching, they will never experience death.
John 8:52 The Jews said to him, "Now we know you have a demon. Abraham and the prophets died, yet you claim, 'If anyone follows my teachings, they will never die.'"
John 8:53 Are you greater than our ancestor Abraham, who died? And the prophets are dead too: who do you think you are?
John 8:54 Jesus answered, "If I praise myself, my praise means nothing. It is my Father who praises me; you claim He is your God."
John 8:55 You don't know him, but I do. If I said I didn't know him, I would be lying just like you. But I do know him and follow his teachings.
John 8:56 Your father Abraham was happy to see my time: he saw it and was joyful.
John 8:57 The Jewish people said to him, "You're not even fifty years old yet, have you seen Abraham?"
John 8:58 Jesus told them, "Truly, I tell you, before Abraham was born, I am."
John 8:59 They picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid and left the temple, walking through the crowd, and passed by.

John 9:1 As Jesus walked by, he saw a man who was born blind.
John 9:2 His followers asked him, "Teacher, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born without sight?"
John 9:3 Jesus said, "This man and his parents did not sin. It's so that God's work can be shown in him."
John 9:4 I need to do the tasks of the one who sent me while it is day; night is coming when no one can work.
John 9:5 As long as I am in the world, I am the world's light.
John 9:6 After saying this, he spit on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and put it on the blind man's eyes.
John 9:7 He told him, "Go wash in the pool of Siloam (which means 'Sent')." So he went, washed, and came back able to see.
John 9:8 So the neighbors and those who had seen him before when he was blind asked, "Isn't this the same man who used to sit and beg?"
John 9:9 Some said, "This is him"; others said, "He looks like him"; but he himself said, "I am the one."
John 9:10 So they asked him, "How were your eyes opened?"
John 9:11 He replied, "A man named Jesus put mud on my eyes and told me, 'Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.' So I went, washed, and then I could see."
John 9:12 They asked him, "Where is he?" He answered, "I don't know."
John 9:13 They took the man who used to be blind to the Pharisees.
John 9:14 It was the Sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened the man's eyes.
John 9:15 The Pharisees asked him again how he got his sight back. He told them, "He put mud on my eyes, I washed it off, and now I can see."
John 9:16 Some Pharisees said, "This man is not from God because he doesn't keep the Sabbath." But others asked, "How can a sinner do such amazing things?" So they disagreed among themselves.
John 9:17 They asked the blind man again, "What do you think about him, since he healed your eyes?" He replied, "He is a prophet."
John 9:18 The Jews didn't believe that he had been blind and could now see until they asked his parents.
John 9:19 They asked them, "Is this your son, who you say was born blind? How can he see now?"
John 9:20 His parents answered, "We know this is our son and that he was born unable to see."
John 9:21 We don't know how he can now see, or who healed his eyes. He's an adult; ask him, and he will answer for himself.
John 9:22 His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders. The leaders had decided that if anyone said he was the Christ, they would be banned from the synagogue.
John 9:23 So his parents said, "He's old enough; ask him."
John 9:24 They called the man who had been blind again, and told him, "Praise God: we know this man is a sinner."
John 9:25 He replied, "I don't know if he is a sinner; all I know is I was blind, and now I can see."
John 9:26 They asked him again, "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
John 9:27 He told them, "I already told you, and you didn't listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to be his followers?"
John 9:28 They insulted him and said, "You are his follower; but we follow Moses."
John 9:29 We know that God spoke to Moses, but we don't know where this man comes from.
John 9:30 The man replied, "It's amazing that you don't know where he comes from, yet he healed my eyes."
John 9:31 We know that God does not listen to sinners, but if someone worships God and does what He wants, God listens to him.
John 9:32 No one has ever heard of anyone giving sight to a person born blind since the world began.
John 9:33 If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.
John 9:34 They replied to him, "You were completely born in sin, and now you try to teach us?" So they threw him out.
John 9:35 Jesus knew they threw him out; when he found him, he asked, "Do you believe in the Son of God?"
John 9:36 He replied, "Who is he, God, so that I might believe in him?"
John 9:37 Jesus said to him, "You have seen him, and he is the one speaking with you."
John 9:38 He said, "God, I believe." And he honored him.
John 9:39 Jesus said, "I have come to bring judgment to the world so that those who cannot see may see, and those who can see may become blind."
John 9:40 Some Pharisees with him heard this and asked, "Are we also blind?"
John 9:41 Jesus told them, "If you were blind, you wouldn't be guilty of sin. But now you claim, 'We can see,' so your sin stays with you."

John 10:1 Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who does not enter the sheep pen by the gate but climbs in by another way is a thief and a robber.
John 10:2 The one who comes in through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
John 10:3 The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
John 10:4 When he leads his sheep out, he walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow him because they recognize his voice.
John 10:5 They will not follow a stranger but will run away from him because they do not recognize a stranger's voice.
John 10:6 Jesus told them this story, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.
John 10:7 Jesus told them again, "Truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep."
John 10:8 Everyone who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
John 10:9 I am the door. If anyone enters through me, they will be saved. They will come in and go out and find food.
John 10:10 The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I have come so that they can have life, and have it fully.
John 10:11 I am the good shepherd; the good shepherd gives his life for the sheep.
John 10:12 But the person who works only for pay and is not the shepherd, who does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, runs away, and the wolf catches and scatters the sheep.
John 10:13 The worker runs away because he is just a worker and does not care about the sheep.
John 10:14 I am the good shepherd; I know my sheep and my sheep know me.
John 10:15 Just as the Father knows me, I also know the Father; and I give up my life for the sheep.
John 10:16 I have other sheep that are not from this pen. I must bring them too, and they will listen to my voice; then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
John 10:17 So my Father loves me because I give up my life and then take it back.
John 10:18 No one takes it from me; I give it up by my choice. I have the power to give it up, and I have the power to take it back. This order I got from my Father.
John 10:19 So the Jews were divided again because of these words.
John 10:20 Many people said, "He is possessed by a demon and is crazy; why do you listen to him?"
John 10:21 Others said, "These aren't the words of someone with an evil spirit. Can an evil spirit make blind people see?"
John 10:22 It was winter during the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem.
John 10:23 Jesus walked in the temple on Solomon's porch.
John 10:24 The Jews gathered around him and asked, "How long will you keep us guessing? If you are the Christ, tell us clearly."
John 10:25 Jesus replied, "I told you, but you did not believe. The things I do, done in my Father's name, show who I am."
John 10:26 But you don't believe because you are not my sheep, as I told you.
John 10:27 My sheep listen to me, I know them, and they follow me.
John 10:28 I give them forever life; they will never die, and no one can take them from my hand.
John 10:29 My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than everyone; and no one can take them from my Father's hand.
John 10:30 My Father and I are the same.
John 10:31 The Jews picked up stones once more to throw at him.
John 10:32 Jesus answered them, "I have shown you many good things from God; for which of those good things do you want to punish me with stones?"
John 10:33 The Jews replied, "We're not going to stone you for doing good things; we're doing it for disrespecting God, because you, a man, claim to be God."
John 10:34 Jesus replied, "Isn't it written in your law, 'I said, you are gods'?"
John 10:35 If he named them gods, to whom God's message came, and the scripture cannot be changed;
John 10:36 Are you saying that the one whom God has made holy and sent into the world is speaking blasphemy because I said, 'I am God's Son'?
John 10:37 If I don't do what my Father does, don't believe me.
John 10:38 But if I do them, even if you don't believe me, believe the things I do. Then you will understand and believe that God is in me, and I am in God.
John 10:39 So they tried again to seize him, but he got away from them.
John 10:40 He went back to the area beyond the Jordan River, where John first baptized people, and stayed there.
John 10:41 Many people came to him and said, "John didn't perform any miracles, but everything John said about this man was true."
John 10:42 Many people there believed in him.

John 11:1 A man named Lazarus from the town of Bethany, where Mary and her sister Martha lived, was sick.
John 11:2 Mary, who put perfume on Jesus and dried his feet with her hair, had a brother named Lazarus who was ill.
John 11:3 So his sisters sent a message to him, saying, "Lord, look, the one you love is sick."
John 11:4 When Jesus heard this, he said, "This illness will not lead to death. It is for God's glory, so that God's Son may be honored through it."
John 11:5 Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
John 11:6 After hearing that he was sick, he stayed two more days in the same place he was.
John 11:7 After that, he said to his disciples, "Let's go back to Judea."
John 11:8 His followers asked him, "Teacher, recently the Jews wanted to stone you; and you're going back there?"
John 11:9 Jesus answered, "Isn't there twelve hours in a day? If someone walks during the day, they won't stumble because they see the world's light."
John 11:10 If someone walks at night, they trip because there's no light inside them.
John 11:11 He said these things, and then he told them, "Our friend Lazarus is sleeping; but I am going to wake him up."
John 11:12 Then his followers said, "Master, if he is sleeping, he will get better."
John 11:13 However, Jesus was talking about his death; but they thought he was talking about resting by sleeping.
John 11:14 Jesus told them clearly, "Lazarus is dead."
John 11:15 I am happy for you that I wasn't there, so you might believe; but let's go to him now.
John 11:16 Then Thomas, also known as Didymus, told the other disciples, "Let's go too, so we can die with him."
John 11:17 When Jesus arrived, he found that the man had been in the tomb for four days.
John 11:18 Bethany was close to Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs away.
John 11:19 Many Jews visited Martha and Mary to comfort them about their brother.
John 11:20 Martha, when she heard Jesus was coming, went to meet him; but Mary stayed in the house.
John 11:21 Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
John 11:22 I know that even now, whatever you ask from God, He will give it to you.
John 11:23 Jesus said to her, Your brother will live again.
John 11:24 Martha said to him, "I know he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day."
John 11:25 Jesus told her, "I am the one who brings people back to life, and I am life itself. Anyone who believes in me will live, even if they die.
John 11:26 Anyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?
John 11:27 She said to him, "Yes, Lord: I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world."
John 11:28 After saying this, she left and quietly told her sister Mary, "The Teacher has arrived and is asking for you."
John 11:29 As soon as she heard that, she got up fast and went to him.
John 11:30 Jesus had not entered the town yet; he was still in the place where Martha met him.
John 11:31 The Jews who were with her in the house, comforting her, saw Mary get up quickly and leave. They followed her, saying, "She is going to the tomb to cry."
John 11:32 When Mary arrived where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
John 11:33 When Jesus saw her crying and the Jews who came with her crying too, he felt deeply moved and was upset.
John 11:34 And asked, "Where have you placed him?" They replied, "Sir, come and see."
John 11:35 Jesus cried.
John 11:36 Then the Jewish people said, "Look how much he cared for him!"
John 11:37 Some of them asked, "Couldn't this man, who made blind people see, have stopped this man from dying?"
John 11:38 Jesus, feeling deep sadness again, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone placed over the entrance.
John 11:39 Jesus said, "Remove the stone." Martha, the sister of the man who had died, said to him, "God, by now there will be a bad smell because he has been dead for four days."
John 11:40 Jesus said to her, "Didn't I tell you that if you believed, you would see God's glory?"
John 11:41 They removed the stone from where the dead person was placed. Jesus looked up and said, "Father, I thank you for hearing me."
John 11:42 I know you always hear me, but I said this for the people here, so they will believe you sent me.
John 11:43 After he said this, he shouted, "Lazarus, come out!"
John 11:44 The dead man came out, tied up at the hands and feet with burial cloths, and his face was wrapped in a cloth. Jesus told them, "Untie him and let him go."
John 11:45 Many Jews who visited Mary and saw what Jesus did started to believe in him.
John 11:46 Some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
John 11:47 The chief priests and Pharisees met and said, "What should we do? This man performs many miracles."
John 11:48 If we leave him alone, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away our positions and our country.
John 11:49 One of them, named Caiaphas, who was the high priest that year, told them, "You don't understand anything."
John 11:50 We must realize it's better for us that one man dies for the people, so the whole nation doesn't get destroyed.
John 11:51 He didn't say this on his own; as the high priest that year, he predicted that Jesus would die for the nation.
John 11:52 Not just for that nation, but also to unite all of God's children who were spread out.
John 11:53 From that day on, they planned together to kill him.
John 11:54 So Jesus didn't walk openly among the Jews anymore. Instead, he went to a region near the wilderness, to a city named Ephraim, and stayed there with his followers.
John 11:55 The Jewish Passover was soon to happen, and many people left the countryside to go to Jerusalem before the Passover to make themselves clean.
John 11:56 They looked for Jesus and asked each other as they stood in the temple, "What do you think, will he not come to the celebration?"
John 11:57 The chief priests and the Pharisees had ordered that if anyone knew where he was, they should tell so they could arrest him.

John 12:1 Six days before Passover, Jesus went to Bethany, where Lazarus lived, whom he had brought back to life after death.
John 12:2 There they prepared a dinner for him; Martha served, while Lazarus was one of those who sat at the table with him.
John 12:3 Mary took a pound of very expensive spikenard perfume, put it on Jesus' feet, and wiped his feet with her hair. The smell of the perfume filled the house.
John 12:4 One of his followers, Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, who would later betray him, said
John 12:5 Why wasn't this perfume sold for three hundred coins and given to the poor?
John 12:6 He said this not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief, held the money bag, and took what was placed in it.
John 12:7 Jesus said, Leave her alone; she saved this for the day of my burial.
John 12:8 You will always have poor people with you, but you will not always have me.
John 12:9 Many Jewish people knew he was there, so they came not just for Jesus, but also to see Lazarus whom he brought back to life.
John 12:10 The leading priests planned to kill Lazarus too.
John 12:11 Because of him, many Jews left and believed in Jesus.
John 12:12 The next day, many people who had come to the celebration heard that Jesus was heading to Jerusalem.
John 12:13 They took palm tree branches, went out to meet him, and shouted, "Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel who comes in God's name."
John 12:14 Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, as the scripture says.
John 12:15 Don't be afraid, people of Zion: look, your King is coming, riding on a young donkey.
John 12:16 At first, his disciples did not understand these things. But after Jesus was honored, they remembered that these things were written about him, and that they had happened to him.
John 12:17 The people with him when he called Lazarus out of his tomb and woke him from the dead, witnessed it.
John 12:18 The people came to meet him because they heard he had performed this miracle.
John 12:19 The Pharisees then said to each other, "Do you see that we are not succeeding at all? Look, everyone is following him."
John 12:20 Some Greeks who were there to worship at the festival were among them.
John 12:21 This person came to Philip from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked, "Sir, we want to see Jesus."
John 12:22 Philip came and told Andrew, and then Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
John 12:23 Jesus replied to them, "The time has come for the Son of man to be honored."
John 12:24 Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the soil and dies, it stays single; but if it dies, it produces lots of seeds.
John 12:25 Whoever loves their life will lose it; and whoever hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
John 12:26 If someone serves me, he should follow me; and where I am, my servant will be too: if someone serves me, God will honor him.
John 12:27 My soul is troubled; what should I say? Father, rescue me from this time. Yet this is why I came to this moment.
John 12:28 Father, make your name honored. Then a voice from heaven spoke, "I have honored it, and I will honor it again."
John 12:29 The people standing nearby who heard it said it thundered; others said an angel spoke to him.
John 12:30 Jesus replied, "This voice was not for me, but for you."
John 12:31 The time has come to judge this world; now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.
John 12:32 If I am raised up from the earth, I will attract everyone to me.
John 12:33 He said this to show what kind of death he was going to die.
John 12:34 The people replied, "We know from the law that Christ will live forever. So why do you say that the Son of Man must be raised up? Who is this Son of Man?"
John 12:35 Jesus told them, "The light will be with you for just a short time. Walk while you have the light, before darkness overtakes you. Anyone walking in darkness doesn't know where they are going."
John 12:36 While you have light, trust in it, so you can be children of light. After saying this, Jesus left and hid from them.
John 12:37 Even though he had performed many miracles in front of them, they still did not believe in him.
John 12:38 So that what the prophet Isaiah said would come true, he asked, "God, who has believed what we said? And to whom has God shown his power?"
John 12:39 So they couldn't believe, because Isaiah had said before,
John 12:40 God has made their eyes blind and their hearts hard; so they cannot see with their eyes or understand with their hearts, and turn to me so I can heal them.
John 12:41 Isaiah said these things when he saw God's glory and spoke about him.
John 12:42 Many leaders also believed in him, but they did not admit it because of the Pharisees; they were afraid of being expelled from the synagogue.
John 12:43 They liked people's approval more than God's approval.
John 12:44 Jesus cried out and said, "Anyone who believes in me does not just believe in me, but in the one who sent me."
John 12:45 Whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.
John 12:46 I have come as a light into the world so that everyone who believes in me will not stay in darkness.
John 12:47 If anyone hears my words and does not believe, I do not judge them, because I did not come to judge the world, but to save it.
John 12:48 Whoever rejects me and does not accept my words has something that will judge them: the words I have spoken will be their judge on the last day.
John 12:49 I don't speak for myself; the Father who sent me commanded me what to say and speak.
John 12:50 I know that God's command leads to eternal life. So, whatever I say is just as the Father told me to say.

John 13:1 Before the Passover feast, when Jesus realized his time had come to leave this world and go to the Father, he showed endless love for his followers who were in the world.
John 13:2 After dinner, the devil had already persuaded Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray Jesus.
John 13:3 Jesus knew that God had given him power over everything, and that he had come from God and was going back to God.
John 13:4 He got up from dinner, took off his clothes, and wrapped a towel around himself.
John 13:5 Then he poured water into a basin and started to wash his followers' feet, drying them with the towel he was wearing.
John 13:6 Then he came to Simon Peter, and Peter asked him, "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
John 13:7 Jesus answered him, "What I am doing you do not understand now, but you will understand later."
John 13:8 Peter said to him, "You will never wash my feet." Jesus replied, "If I do not wash you, you have no share with me."
John 13:9 Simon Peter said to him, "Lord, not just my feet, but also my hands and my head."
John 13:10 Jesus said to him, "Someone who has bathed only needs to wash their feet to be completely clean. And you are clean, but not all of you."
John 13:11 He knew who would betray him; that is why he said, "Not all of you are clean."
John 13:12 After he washed your feet, put on his clothes, and sat down again, he asked them, "Do you understand what I have done for you?"
John 13:13 You call me Teacher and God, and you are right, because that's what I am.
John 13:14 If I, your leader and teacher, have washed your feet, you should also wash each other's feet.
John 13:15 I have set an example for you, so you should do as I have done to you.
John 13:16 Truly, truly, I tell you, a servant is not more important than his master; nor is the one who is sent more important than the one who sent him.
John 13:17 If you know these things, you will be happy if you do them.
John 13:18 I am not talking about all of you: I know the ones I picked: but so the scripture comes true, the one who shares my bread has turned against me.
John 13:19 I tell you now, before it happens, so when it does happen, you will believe that I am the one.
John 13:20 Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who welcomes the person I send welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
John 13:21 After Jesus said this, he felt very upset and declared, "Truly, I tell you, one of you will betray me."
John 13:22 The followers looked at each other, not sure who he was talking about.
John 13:23 One disciple, who Jesus loved, was resting on Jesus' chest.
John 13:24 Simon Peter motioned to him to ask which one Jesus meant.
John 13:25 He, resting on Jesus' chest, asked him, "Master, who is it?"
John 13:26 Jesus answered, "The one I give the piece of bread to after I dip it." After dipping the bread, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, Simon's son.
John 13:27 After he took the piece of bread, Satan came into him. Then Jesus told him, "Do what you're going to do, do it fast."
John 13:28 No one at the table knew why he said this to him.
John 13:29 Some thought Jesus told Judas, who kept the money, to buy what was needed for the festival or give money to the poor.
John 13:30 After taking the piece of food, he quickly left, and it was night.
John 13:31 So when he left, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is honored, and God is honored in him."
John 13:32 If God is honored through him, God will honor him in return, and will do it soon.
John 13:33 Kids, I'll be with you for a little longer. You will look for me, and like I told the Jewish people, where I'm going, you can't come; I'm telling you this now too.
John 13:34 I give you a new command: love each other just as I have loved you, so you also should love each other.
John 13:35 Everyone will know you are my followers if you love each other.
John 13:36 Simon Peter asked him, "Where are you going?" Jesus replied, "Where I am going, you cannot follow me now, but you will follow me later."
John 13:37 Peter said to him, "God, why can't I follow you now? I will give up my life for you."
John 13:38 Jesus replied, "Are you ready to give up your life for me? Truly, I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times."

John 14:1 Don't be worried in your heart; you trust in God, trust also in me.
John 14:2 In my Father's house, there are many homes. If it wasn't true, I would have told you. I am going to get a place ready for you.
John 14:3 If I go and get a place ready for you, I will come back and take you with me; so you can be where I am too.
John 14:4 You know where I'm going and you know the way.
John 14:5 Thomas said to him, "Lord, we don't know where you are going; how can we know the way?"
John 14:6 Jesus said to him, "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me."
John 14:7 If you had known me, you would have known my Father too. From now on, you do know him and have seen him.
John 14:8 Philip said to him, "Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us."
John 14:9 Jesus said to him, "Have I been with you for so long, and you still don't know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen God; so why do you say, 'Show us God'?"
John 14:10 Don't you believe that I am in God, and God is in me? The words I tell you are not just from me: it's God living in me who does the works.
John 14:11 Trust that I am in God, and God is in me; if not, trust because of the things I have done.
John 14:12 Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I do, and they will do even greater works, because I am going to my Father.
John 14:13 Whatever you ask for in my name, I will do it so that the Father may be honored through the Son.
John 14:14 If you ask for anything in my name, I will do it.
John 14:15 If you love me, follow my commands.
John 14:16 I will ask God, and he will give you another Helper to be with you always.
John 14:17 The Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot accept because it does not see or know him: but you know him, for he lives with you and will be in you.
John 14:18 I will not leave you alone: I will come to you.
John 14:19 Soon, the world will not see me; but you will see me. Because I am alive, you will live too.
John 14:20 On that day, you will understand that I am with my Father, and you are with me, and I am with you.
John 14:21 The one who has my commands and follows them truly loves me; and the one who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and show myself to him.
John 14:22 Judas, not Iscariot, asked him, "Lord, how will you show yourself to us but not to the world?"
John 14:23 Jesus replied, "If someone loves me, he will follow my teachings. Then my Father will love him, and we will come to him and live with him."
John 14:24 Anyone who doesn't love me doesn't follow my teachings. The message you hear isn't mine, but it comes from the Father who sent me.
John 14:25 I have said these things to you while I am still with you.
John 14:26 The Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom God will send in my name, will teach you everything and remind you of all I have told you.
John 14:27 I leave you peace, my peace I give you. Not the way the world does, do I give to you. Don't let your heart be troubled or afraid.
John 14:28 You have heard me say I will leave and come back to you. If you loved me, you would be happy because I am going to the Father, who is greater than me.
John 14:29 I have told you beforehand so that when it happens, you may believe.
John 14:30 From now on, I won't talk much with you because the ruler of this world is coming, and he has no power over me.
John 14:31 I want the world to know I love God; I follow His commands. Let's get up and go.

John 15:1 I am the real vine, and my Father takes care of it.
John 15:2 Every branch in me that does not produce fruit, God removes. Every branch that does produce fruit, God cleans so it will make even more fruit.
John 15:3 You are clean now because of the words I have spoken to you.
John 15:4 Stay with me, and I with you. Just as a branch can't produce fruit alone without being part of the vine, you can't either unless you stay with me.
John 15:5 I am the vine, you are the branches. Anyone who remains in me, and I in them, will produce a lot of fruit. Without me, you can do nothing.
John 15:6 If someone does not remain in me, he is thrown away like a dead branch; people pick it up, throw it into the fire, and it burns.
John 15:7 If you remain in me and my words stay in you, you can ask for anything you want, and it will be done for you.
John 15:8 In this, my Father is honored: when you produce a lot of fruit, then you are truly my followers.
John 15:9 Just as the Father loves me, I also love you. Stay in my love.
John 15:10 If you follow my commands, you will remain in my love, just as I follow my Father's commands and remain in his love.
John 15:11 I have told you these things so that my joy stays in you and your joy is complete.
John 15:12 My command is this: Love each other as I have loved you.
John 15:13 No one has greater love than to give up their life for their friends.
John 15:14 You are my friends if you do everything I tell you to do.
John 15:15 From now on, I don't call you servants, because a servant doesn't know what their master is doing. Instead, I have called you friends, because everything I learned from my Father, I have told you.
John 15:16 You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and produce lasting fruit. So whatever you ask of God in my name, he will give to you.
John 15:17 I instruct you to love each other.
John 15:18 If the world hates you, know that it hated me before it hated you.
John 15:19 If you belonged to the world, the world would love you as its own. But you do not belong to the world, because I have chosen you out of the world. That's why the world hates you.
John 15:20 Remember what I told you: A servant isn't above their master. If they have mistreated me, they will mistreat you too; if they have followed my teachings, they will follow yours as well.
John 15:21 They will do all these things to you because of me, since they do not know the one who sent me.
John 15:22 If I hadn't come and spoken to them, they wouldn't be guilty of sin; but now they can't hide their sin.
John 15:23 Whoever hates me also hates my Father.
John 15:24 If I had not done works among them that no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have seen and hated both me and my Father.
John 15:25 This happens so that what is written in their law comes true: They hated me for no reason.
John 15:26 But when the Helper comes, whom I will send to you from God, the Spirit of truth who goes out from God, he will tell about me.
John 15:27 You will also testify because you have been with me from the start.

John 16:1 I have told you these things so you won't be upset.
John 16:2 They will throw you out of the synagogues; yes, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think they are serving God.
John 16:3 They will do these things to you because they do not know the Father or me.
John 16:4 I have told you these things so that when the time comes, you will remember that I warned you. I didn't tell you this from the start because I was with you.
John 16:5 Now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you is asking me, "Where are you going?"
John 16:6 Because I told you this, sadness has filled your heart.
John 16:7 I'm telling you the truth: It's better for you that I leave. If I don't go, the Helper won't come to you. But if I go, I'll send him to you.
John 16:8 When he comes, he will show the world their sin, what is right, and how they are judged.
John 16:9 About sin, because they do not believe in me;
John 16:10 About being right with God, because I am going to my Father, and you won't see me again;
John 16:11 About judgment, because the leader of this world has been judged.
John 16:12 I have many more things to tell you, but you can't handle them now.
John 16:13 However, when the Spirit of truth comes, he will lead you to all truth. He won't speak on his own but will say what he hears, and he will show you what is to come.
John 16:14 He will honor me because he will take from what is mine and show it to you.
John 16:15 Everything that the Father has is mine; that's why I said He will take what's mine and show it to you.
John 16:16 Soon you will not see me, but then soon after, you will see me again because I am going to the Father.
John 16:17 Some of his followers asked each other, "What does he mean by saying, 'In a little while, you won't see me, but then after a little while, you will see me,' and 'Because I am going to the Father'?"
John 16:18 So they asked, "What does he mean by 'a little while'? We don't understand what he is saying."
John 16:19 Jesus knew they wanted to ask him questions. He said to them, "Are you wondering about what I meant when I said, 'Soon you won't see me, and then after a little while, you will see me again'?"
John 16:20 Truly, truly, I tell you, you will cry and be sad, while the world will be happy. You will feel sorrow, but your sorrow will become joy.
John 16:21 A woman feels pain when she is giving birth because her time has arrived; but once the baby is born, she forgets the pain because she is happy that a baby has come into the world.
John 16:22 You are sad now, but I will see you again, and you will be happy, and no one will take away your happiness.
John 16:23 On that day you will not ask me anything. Truly, I tell you, whatever you ask God in my name, he will give to you.
John 16:24 Until now, you have asked for nothing in my name; ask and you will receive, so that your happiness may be complete.
John 16:25 I have told you these things in riddles, but a time will come when I will not use riddles. Instead, I will tell you clearly about God.
John 16:26 On that day you will ask in my name, and I am not saying that I will ask God for you.
John 16:27 God loves you himself because you have loved me and believed that I came from God.
John 16:28 I came from the Father and entered the world; now I leave the world and return to the Father.
John 16:29 His followers said to him, "Look, now you are speaking clearly and not using difficult sayings."
John 16:30 We are now certain that you know everything and don't need anyone to question you. This makes us believe that you came from God.
John 16:31 Jesus answered them, "Do you now believe?"
John 16:32 Soon, you will all go your separate ways and leave me alone, but I am not really alone because God is with me.
John 16:33 I told you these things so you can have peace in me. You will face trouble in the world, but stay positive; I have beaten the world.

John 17:1 Jesus spoke these words, looked up to heaven, and said, "Father, the time has come; honor your Son, so your Son may honor you."
John 17:2 You have given him power over everyone, so he can give eternal life to all you have given to him.
John 17:3 Eternal life is to know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, who you sent.
John 17:4 I have honored you on earth by finishing the work you gave me to do.
John 17:5 And now, Father, make me glorious with your own glory, the glory I had with you before the world existed.
John 17:6 I have shown your name to the people you gave me from the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have followed your word.
John 17:7 Now they understand that everything you have given me comes from you.
John 17:8 I gave them the words you gave me; they accepted them and know for sure I came from you, and they believe you sent me.
John 17:9 I ask for them: I do not ask for everyone, but for those you have given me; because they are yours.
John 17:10 Everything that is mine is yours, and everything that is yours is mine; and I am honored through them.
John 17:11 Now I am not in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, protect them with your name, the ones you gave me, so they can be united just as we are.
John 17:12 While I was with them, I protected them in your name: I took care of those you gave me, and none were lost, except the one doomed to destruction, so the scripture would come true.
John 17:13 I am coming to you now, and I say these things while I am in the world so that they can have my joy completely within them.
John 17:14 I have given them your message; and the world has hated them, because they are not part of the world, just as I am not part of the world.
John 17:15 I ask not for you to take them from the world, but to protect them from evil.
John 17:16 They do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world.
John 17:17 Make them holy by your truth; your message is truth.
John 17:18 Just as you sent me into the world, I have sent them into the world too.
John 17:19 I make myself pure for them so they can be made pure by the truth.
John 17:20 I don't only pray for these people, but also for those who will believe in me because of their message.
John 17:21 They should all be one; just as you, Father, are in me and I am in you, so they should also be one in us. This way, the world will believe you sent me.
John 17:22 The honor you gave me, I have given to them, so they can be united just as we are united.
John 17:23 I am in them, and you are in me, so that they can be completely one. And so the world can know that you sent me and have loved them as you have loved me.
John 17:24 Father, I want those you have given me to be with me where I am, so they can see my glory, the glory you gave me because you loved me before the world began.
John 17:25 Good Father, the world has not known you; but I have known you, and these know that you sent me.
John 17:26 I have told them your name and will continue to, so that the love you have for me may be in them, and I in them.

John 18:1 After Jesus said these things, he and his disciples crossed the Cedron stream and went into a garden there.
John 18:2 Judas, who betrayed Jesus, knew the place because Jesus often went there with his followers.
John 18:3 Judas, after getting a group of men and leaders from the top priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
John 18:4 Jesus, knowing everything that was going to happen to him, went out and asked them, "Who are you looking for?"
John 18:5 They replied to him, "Jesus from Nazareth." Jesus said to them, "I am the one." Judas, who betrayed him, was also standing with them.
John 18:6 As soon as he told them, "I am he," they stepped back and fell to the ground.
John 18:7 He asked them again, "Who are you looking for?" They answered, "Jesus of Nazareth."
John 18:8 Jesus answered, "I have told you that I am the one you're looking for. So if you want me, let these others go."
John 18:9 This was to fulfill what he said, "I have not lost any of those you gave me."
John 18:10 Simon Peter, with a sword, pulled it out, hit the high priest's helper, and cut off his right ear. The helper's name was Malchus.
John 18:11 Jesus said to Peter, "Put your sword back in its place. Shouldn't I drink the cup that my Father has given me?"
John 18:12 The group, their leader, and the Jewish officials arrested Jesus and tied him up.
John 18:13 They took him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
John 18:14 Caiaphas was the one who advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die for the people.
John 18:15 Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. The other disciple knew the high priest, so he went with Jesus into the high priest's house.
John 18:16 Peter stayed outside by the door. Then the other disciple, who the high priest knew, went out, talked to the woman guarding the door, and brought Peter inside.
John 18:17 Then the girl watching the door said to Peter, "Aren't you one of this man's followers?" He answered, "No, I'm not."
John 18:18 The servants and guards were standing there, having made a coal fire because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. Peter also stood with them and warmed himself.
John 18:19 The high priest then asked Jesus about his followers and his teaching.
John 18:20 Jesus replied, "I spoke clearly to everyone; I always taught in the synagogues and at the temple where the Jews gather; I never said anything in secret."
John 18:21 Why do you ask me? Ask those who heard what I said to them: they know what I said.
John 18:22 After he said this, one of the officers standing there hit Jesus with his hand, asking, "Do you talk back to the high priest like that?"
John 18:23 Jesus replied, "If I said something wrong, show what it was. But if I spoke rightly, why did you hit me?"
John 18:24 Annas had sent him tied up to Caiaphas, the high priest.
John 18:25 Simon Peter stood warming himself. They asked him, "Aren't you one of his followers?" He denied it, saying, "I am not."
John 18:26 A servant of the high priest, who was related to the man whose ear Peter cut off, asked, "Didn't I see you in the garden with him?"
John 18:27 Peter denied it once more, and right then a rooster crowed.
John 18:28 They took Jesus from Caiaphas to the courthouse early in the morning. They didn't go inside the courthouse to avoid becoming unclean and to be able to eat the Passover meal.
John 18:29 Pilate went out to them and asked, "What charges are you making against this man?"
John 18:30 They replied and said to him, "If he were not a criminal, we wouldn't have handed him over to you."
John 18:31 Pilate told them, "Take him and judge him by your own law." But the Jews answered, "We are not allowed to put anyone to death."
John 18:32 This was to fulfill what Jesus had said, showing how he would die.
John 18:33 Pilate went back into the courthouse, called Jesus, and asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?"
John 18:34 Jesus answered, "Are you asking this on your own, or did others talk to you about me?"
John 18:35 Pilate answered, "Am I a Jew? Your own people and the religious leaders handed you over to me. What have you done?"
John 18:36 Jesus answered, "My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom belonged to this world, my helpers would fight to prevent me from being handed over to the Jewish leaders. But my kingdom is not from here."
John 18:37 Pilate asked him, "So you are a king?" Jesus replied, "You say I am a king. I was born for this purpose, and I came into the world to tell the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice."
John 18:38 Pilate asked him, "What is truth?" After saying this, he went out to the Jews and said, "I find no fault in him at all."
John 18:39 You have a tradition that I let one prisoner go during Passover. Do you want me to release the King of the Jews to you?
John 18:40 They all shouted again, "Not this man, but Barabbas." Barabbas was a thief.

John 19:1 Then Pilate took Jesus and whipped him.
John 19:2 The soldiers twisted a thorn crown, put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
John 19:3 They said, "Hello, King of the Jews!" and hit him with their hands.
John 19:4 Pilate came out again and said to them, "Look, I am bringing him out to you to show that I find no fault in him."
John 19:5 Jesus came out wearing a crown of thorns and a purple robe. Pilate said to them, "Look at the man!"
John 19:6 So when the religious leaders and their helpers saw him, they shouted, "Crucify him, crucify him!" Pilate told them, "You take him and crucify him, because I don't find him guilty."
John 19:7 The Jews told him, "We have a law, and according to our law, he should die because he claimed to be God's Son."
John 19:8 When Pilate heard this, he became even more afraid.
John 19:9 He went back into the court and asked Jesus, "Where do you come from?" But Jesus did not answer him.
John 19:10 Then Pilate said to him, "Don't you talk to me? Don't you know that I have the power to crucify you and the power to set you free?"
John 19:11 Jesus answered, "You would have no power over me if it weren't given to you from above. So the one who handed me over to you has a bigger sin."
John 19:12 From then on, Pilate tried to set him free, but the Jews shouted, "If you let this man go, you're not loyal to Caesar. Anyone who claims to be a king is against Caesar."
John 19:13 When Pilate heard this, he brought Jesus outside and sat on the judge's bench at a place called the Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.
John 19:14 It was the time to get ready for the Passover, about six in the morning, when he said to the Jewish people, "Look, here is your King!"
John 19:15 But they shouted, "Take him away, take him away, crucify him!" Pilate said to them, "Should I crucify your King?" The chief priests answered, "We have no king but Caesar."
John 19:16 So he handed Jesus over to them to be crucified. They took Jesus and led him away.
John 19:17 He carried his cross to a place known as Skull Hill, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
John 19:18 They crucified him there with two others, one on each side, and Jesus in the middle.
John 19:19 Pilate wrote a sign and put it on the cross. It said, "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews."
John 19:20 Many of the Jewish people read this title because the place where Jesus was crucified was close to the city. It was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.
John 19:21 The Jewish leaders told Pilate, "Don't write 'The King of the Jews,' but write that he claimed, 'I am King of the Jews.'"
John 19:22 Pilate answered, "What I've written, I've written."
John 19:23 After the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took his clothes and divided them into four parts, giving each soldier a part. They also took his coat, which was seamless and woven in one piece from top to bottom.
John 19:24 So they said to each other, "Let's not tear it. Let's throw dice to see who gets it." This was to fulfill what was written: "They divided my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment." And that's what the soldiers did.
John 19:25 Near Jesus' cross stood his mother, her sister, Mary married to Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
John 19:26 When Jesus saw his mother and his close friend standing nearby, he said to his mother, "Woman, here is your son!"
John 19:27 Then he said to the follower, "Here is your mother!" And from that time, the follower took her into his home.
John 19:28 After this, Jesus, knowing that everything was done and the scripture would be complete, said, "I am thirsty."
John 19:29 A jar full of sour wine was there; they soaked a sponge in the sour wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and held it up to his mouth.
John 19:30 When Jesus took the vinegar, he said, "It is finished." Then he bowed his head and passed away.
John 19:31 So the Jewish leaders, because it was the day to get ready, and since they did not want bodies to stay on the crosses during the Sabbath (which was a special day), asked Pilate to have their legs broken and the bodies removed.
John 19:32 Then the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man and the other who was crucified with him.
John 19:33 But when they reached Jesus and saw he was already dead, they did not break his legs.
John 19:34 A soldier stabbed his side with a spear, and blood and water flowed out right away.
John 19:35 The one who saw it has testified, and his testimony is true: and he knows he's telling the truth, so you may believe.
John 19:36 These things happened so that what was written would come true: None of his bones will be broken.
John 19:37 Another part of the Bible says, "They will look at the one they stabbed."
John 19:38 After this, Joseph from Arimathaea, who followed Jesus but kept it secret because he was afraid of the Jewish leaders, asked Pilate for permission to take Jesus's body. Pilate allowed it, so he came and took Jesus's body away.
John 19:39 Nicodemus, who first visited Jesus at night, also came, bringing about a hundred pounds of a mix of myrrh and aloes.
John 19:40 They took Jesus' body and wrapped it in linen with spices, as is the Jewish way to bury.
John 19:41 Near where he was crucified was a garden, and in it, a new tomb where no one had been laid before.
John 19:42 They placed Jesus there because it was the Jewish day of preparation, and the tomb was close by.

John 20:1 Mary Magdalene came to the tomb early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, and saw that the stone had been removed from the tomb.
John 20:2 She ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple, who Jesus loved, and said to them, "They have taken away God from the tomb, and we don't know where they have put him."
John 20:3 Peter and another disciple went out and came to the tomb.
John 20:4 They both ran, but the other disciple ran faster than Peter and reached the tomb first.
John 20:5 He bent over, looked inside, and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
John 20:6 Simon Peter arrived later, went into the tomb, and saw the linen wrappings lying there.
John 20:7 The cloth that had been on his head wasn't lying with the other linen, but was folded up by itself separately.
John 20:8 The other disciple who arrived first at the tomb also went inside, saw, and believed.
John 20:9 They did not yet understand the Scripture that said he had to rise from the dead.
John 20:10 The followers then went back to their own homes.
John 20:11 Mary stood outside the tomb crying, and as she cried, she bent over to look inside the tomb.
John 20:12 She sees two angels in white sitting, one at the head and the other at the feet, where Jesus's body had been.
John 20:13 They ask her, "Woman, why are you crying?" She answers them, "Because they have taken away my Lord, and I don't know where they have put him."
John 20:14 After saying this, she turned around, saw Jesus standing there, but did not recognize it was Jesus.
John 20:15 Jesus asked her, "Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for?" Thinking he was the gardener, she said to him, "Sir, if you have taken him away, tell me where you've put him and I will get him."
John 20:16 Jesus said to her, "Mary." She turned around, and said to him, "Teacher."
John 20:17 Jesus said to her, "Don't touch me, because I haven't gone up to my Father yet. But go to my brothers and tell them, 'I am going up to my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God.'"
John 20:18 Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen God, and that he had spoken these things to her.
John 20:19 On that evening, which was the first day of the week, the disciples were together with the doors closed because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders. Then, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you."
John 20:20 After saying this, he showed them his hands and side. The disciples were happy when they saw God.
John 20:21 Jesus said to them again, "Peace to you. Just as my Father sent me, I send you."
John 20:22 After he said this, he breathed on them and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit."
John 20:23 If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven; if you do not forgive them, they are not forgiven.
John 20:24 Thomas, who was one of the twelve disciples and also called Didymus, wasn't there when Jesus appeared.
John 20:25 The other followers told him, "We have seen God." But he replied, "Unless I see the nail marks in his hands, put my finger where the nails were, and place my hand in his side, I won't believe."
John 20:26 Eight days later, Jesus's followers were inside again, and Thomas was with them. Even though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace to you."
John 20:27 He said to Thomas, "Put your finger here and look at my hands. Put your hand into my side. Stop doubting and believe."
John 20:28 Thomas replied to him, "My Lord and my God."
John 20:29 Jesus said to him, "Thomas, because you have seen me, you believe. Happy are those who have not seen and still believe."
John 20:30 Jesus did many other miracles in front of his disciples that are not recorded in this book.
John 20:31 These are written so you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, God's Son, and by believing, you may have life in his name.

John 21:1 After these events, Jesus appeared again to his followers by the Sea of Tiberias; and he showed himself like this.
John 21:2 Simon Peter, Thomas also known as Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, Zebedee's sons, and two more disciples were all together.
John 21:3 Simon Peter tells them, "I'm going fishing." They respond, "We'll come with you." So they leave, get on a boat right away, and that night they don't catch anything.
John 21:4 When morning came, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
John 21:5 Jesus asked them, "Children, do you have any food?" They replied, "No."
John 21:6 He told them, "Throw the net on the right side of the boat, and you will catch fish." They did so, and they couldn't pull it in because there were so many fish.
John 21:7 So the disciple Jesus loved told Peter, "It's the Lord." When Simon Peter heard it was the Lord, he put on his fishing jacket (because he was not wearing clothes) and jumped into the water.
John 21:8 The other followers arrived in a small boat; they were not far from shore, about two hundred cubits away, towing the net full of fish.
John 21:9 As soon as they reached the shore, they saw a coal fire with fish on it, and bread.
John 21:10 Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish you just caught."
John 21:11 Simon Peter pulled the net full of large fish onto the shore, 153 in total, and even though there were so many, the net did not tear.
John 21:12 Jesus said to them, "Come and eat." And none of the friends dared to ask him, "Who are you?" knowing it was God.
John 21:13 Jesus came, took bread, gave it to them, and also gave them fish.
John 21:14 This is now the third time Jesus showed himself to his followers after he rose from the dead.
John 21:15 After they ate, Jesus asked Simon Peter, "Simon, son of Jonas, do you love me more than these?" He answered, "Yes, God; you know that I love you." Jesus told him, "Take care of my lambs."
John 21:16 He asked him a second time, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?" He answered, "Yes, Lord; you know I love you." He said to him, "Take care of my sheep."
John 21:17 He asked him for the third time, "Simon, son of Jonas, do you love me?" Peter felt sad because he asked him three times, "Do you love me?" And he told him, "God, you know everything; you know I love you." Jesus told him, "Take care of my sheep."
John 21:18 I tell you the truth, when you were young, you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and take you where you don't want to go.
John 21:19 He said this to show the kind of death by which he would honor God. After saying this, he told him, "Follow me."
John 21:20 Then Peter turned around and saw the disciple Jesus loved following them. This was the same one who had been close to Jesus at the meal and had asked, "Lord, who will betray you?"
John 21:21 Peter, seeing him, says to Jesus, "Master, what will this man do?"
John 21:22 Jesus said to him, "If I want him to stay until I come back, what does that matter to you? You follow me."
John 21:23 This message spread among the followers: they thought that disciple would not die. But Jesus didn't say he wouldn't die; he said, "If I want him to remain until I return, what concern is that of yours?"
John 21:24 This is the follower who tells about these events and wrote them down: and we are sure that what he says is true.
John 21:25 Jesus did many other things too. If someone wrote them all down, I think the whole world couldn't hold all the books that would be written. Amen.

Acts 1:1 I wrote before, Theophilus, about all Jesus began to do and teach.
Acts 1:2 Until the day he was taken up to heaven, after he had given instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles he had chosen.
Acts 1:3 He also showed himself alive to them after his suffering through many sure proofs, being seen by them for forty days, and talking about the things regarding God's kingdom.
Acts 1:4 While together with them, he ordered them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for what the Father promised, which, he said, you have heard about from me.
Acts 1:5 John baptized with water, but soon you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
Acts 1:6 So when they met, they asked him, "Teacher, will you now give the kingdom back to Israel?"
Acts 1:7 He told them, "You do not need to know the times or periods that God has decided by His own authority."
Acts 1:8 You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; then you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, all of Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
Acts 1:9 After he said this, as they watched, he went up; and a cloud hid him from their view.
Acts 1:10 As they watched Jesus going up to heaven very closely, suddenly they saw two men in white clothes standing near them.
Acts 1:11 They also said, "You men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up at the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you saw him go into heaven."
Acts 1:12 Then they went back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, which is about a Sabbath day's walk from the city.
Acts 1:13 When they arrived, they went to a room upstairs, where Peter, James, John, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas brother of James were staying.
Acts 1:14 They all joined together constantly in prayer, along with the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
Acts 1:15 In those days, Peter stood up among the followers and said, "There are about 120 of us here."
Acts 1:16 Friends, this scripture had to be fulfilled. The Holy Spirit spoke through David about Judas, who led those who arrested Jesus.
Acts 1:17 He was counted among us and had a share in our work.
Acts 1:18 This man bought a field with the money he got from doing wrong. He fell forward, split open, and all his insides spilled out.
Acts 1:19 Everyone in Jerusalem knew about it, and they called that field in their own language Aceldama, which means Blood Field.
Acts 1:20 The Psalms book says, "Let his home become empty with no one living there; and let another person take his leadership role."
Acts 1:21 So, from the men who have been with us the whole time that Jesus was with us,
Acts 1:22 Starting with John's baptism until the day he ascended, someone must be chosen to join us as a witness of his resurrection.
Acts 1:23 They chose two men, Joseph known as Barsabas, also named Justus, and Matthias.
Acts 1:24 They prayed and said, "You, God, who knows everyone's heart, show us which one of these two you have chosen."
Acts 1:25 So that he can share in this service and role of apostle, which Judas lost by sinning, to go to where he belongs.
Acts 1:26 They drew lots, and Matthias was chosen. He became one of the twelve apostles.

Acts 2:1 When Pentecost Day arrived, they were all together in one place.
Acts 2:2 Suddenly a loud sound like a strong wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting.
Acts 2:3 They saw something like flames of fire that were split in two touching each person.
Acts 2:4 Everyone was filled with the Holy Spirit and started to speak in different languages, as the Spirit helped them to speak.
Acts 2:5 In Jerusalem, there were Jews, religious men from every country in the world, living there.
Acts 2:6 When news of this spread, a large crowd gathered, and they were amazed because each person heard them speaking in their own language.
Acts 2:7 Everyone was amazed and surprised, asking each other, "Look, aren't all these people who are speaking from Galilee?"
Acts 2:8 How can we each hear them speaking in our own native language?
Acts 2:9 People from Parthia, Media, Elam, Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
Acts 2:10 Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, areas of Libya near Cyrene, visitors from Rome, Jews, and new believers,
Acts 2:11 People from Crete and Arabia, we hear them telling in our own languages the amazing deeds of God.
Acts 2:12 They were all surprised and confused, asking each other, "What does this mean?"
Acts 2:13 Others making fun said, These men have drunk too much wine.
Acts 2:14 But Peter stood up with the eleven, raised his voice, and said to them, "You men of Judaea and everyone in Jerusalem, listen to me and hear my words:
Acts 2:15 They are not drunk as you think, since it is only nine in the morning.
Acts 2:16 This is what the prophet Joel talked about.
Acts 2:17 In the last days, God says, I will give my Spirit to everyone: your sons and daughters will tell of the future, your young men will have visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
Acts 2:18 I will pour out my Spirit on my servants and maidens in those days, and they will prophesy.
Acts 2:19 I will show amazing things in the sky above and signs on the earth below; there will be blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
Acts 2:20 The sun will turn dark, and the moon will turn red, before the great and important day of God comes.
Acts 2:21 Whoever calls on God's name will be saved.
Acts 2:22 People of Israel, listen to this: Jesus from Nazareth was a man shown to be from God to you through miracles, wonders, and signs, which God did through him among you, as you know.
Acts 2:23 God planned for him to be handed over to you, and you took him and had evil men kill him by nailing him to a cross.
Acts 2:24 God raised him up, freeing him from the grip of death, because it was not possible for death to keep holding him.
Acts 2:25 David says about him: "I always see God before me. He is at my right side so I will not be shaken."
Acts 2:26 So my heart was happy, and my tongue was joyful; and even my body will rest with hope.
Acts 2:27 Because you will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you let your Holy One decay.
Acts 2:28 You have shown me the paths of life; you will fill me with joy by being with me.
Acts 2:29 Friends, I want to talk openly to you about our ancestor David. He died, was buried, and his tomb is still here today.
Acts 2:30 Because he was a prophet and knew that God had promised with a strong promise that a descendant from his own body would become the Christ and sit on his throne.
Acts 2:31 He foresaw this and spoke about Christ being raised from the dead. His soul wasn't left in the grave, and his body didn't decay.
Acts 2:32 God raised Jesus, and we all saw it.
Acts 2:33 So, God raised him to His right side and after getting the Holy Spirit as promised by the Father, he has poured out what you now see and hear.
Acts 2:34 David did not go up to heaven, but he said, "God told my lord, 'Sit at my right side.'"
Acts 2:35 Until I make your enemies your footstool.
Acts 2:36 So all the people of Israel should clearly understand that God made Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.
Acts 2:37 When they heard this, their hearts felt troubled, and they said to Peter and the other apostles, "Friends, what should we do?"
Acts 2:38 Peter said to them, "Change your ways, and be baptized each one of you in Jesus Christ's name to have your sins forgiven, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit."
Acts 2:39 The promise is for you, your children, and everyone far away, as many as God will call.
Acts 2:40 He strongly urged with many other words, "Save yourselves from this wicked generation."
Acts 2:41 People who happily accepted the message were baptized. That day, about three thousand people joined them.
Acts 2:42 They stayed devoted to the teachings of the apostles, to sharing with each other, to eating meals together, and to praying.
Acts 2:43 Everyone felt afraid, and the apostles performed many miracles and signs.
Acts 2:44 Everyone who believed was together and shared everything.
Acts 2:45 They sold their belongings and shared with everyone, giving to each as they needed.
Acts 2:46 They met together every day in the temple, and went from home to home to share meals. They ate happily and with sincere hearts.
Acts 2:47 Praising God and being liked by everyone. And God added to the group every day those who would be saved.

Acts 3:1 Peter and John went to the temple together to pray at three in the afternoon.
Acts 3:2 A man who couldn't walk since birth was brought and placed every day at the temple gate named Beautiful to ask for money from those going into the temple.
Acts 3:3 Seeing Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked for help.
Acts 3:4 Peter, with John, looked straight at him and said, "Look at us."
Acts 3:5 He paid attention to them, hoping to get something from them.
Acts 3:6 Peter said, "I don't have silver or gold, but I will give you what I do have: In Jesus Christ of Nazareth's name, get up and walk."
Acts 3:7 He took his right hand and helped him up; at once his feet and ankles became strong.
Acts 3:8 He jumped up, stood, and walked. He went into the temple with them, walking, jumping, and praising God.
Acts 3:9 Everyone saw him walking and thanking God.
Acts 3:10 They knew he was the one who used to sit and ask for help at the Beautiful gate of the temple, and they were amazed at what had happened to him.
Acts 3:11 When the man who could not walk and was healed clung to Peter and John, everyone rushed to them in the area known as Solomon's Porch, filled with amazement.
Acts 3:12 When Peter saw this, he said to the people, "People of Israel, why are you surprised by this? Or why do you stare at us as if we made this man walk by our own power or goodness?"
Acts 3:13 God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our ancestors, has honored his Son Jesus, whom you handed over and rejected before Pilate, even when he decided to release him.
Acts 3:14 But you rejected the Holy and Righteous One, and chose a murderer to be freed for you.
Acts 3:15 They killed the leader of life, but God raised him from the dead; we have seen this ourselves.
Acts 3:16 Believing in his name has made this man strong, whom you all see and know; yes, faith in him has healed him completely before all of you.
Acts 3:17 And now, friends, I know that you did it without understanding, just as your leaders did.
Acts 3:18 God has made happen what he told through all his prophets before, that Christ would suffer.
Acts 3:19 Turn away from your sins and change your ways so that they can be erased when the time comes for God to bring renewal.
Acts 3:20 God will send Jesus Christ, who was already told about to you.
Acts 3:21 Heaven must keep him until the time when everything is made right again, as God promised through all his holy prophets long ago.
Acts 3:22 Moses told our ancestors that God will send you a prophet from your own people, just like me, and you should listen to everything he tells you.
Acts 3:23 Everyone who doesn't listen to that prophet will be removed from the people.
Acts 3:24 Yes, and all the prophets starting with Samuel and those who came after him, as many as have spoken, also predicted these times.
Acts 3:25 You are the prophets' children and belong to the promise God gave to our ancestors, telling Abraham, "Through your descendants, all families on earth will be blessed."
Acts 3:26 First, God raised his Son Jesus and sent him to bless you by turning each of you away from your sins.

Acts 4:1 While they were talking to the people, the priests, the temple leader, and the Sadducees confronted them.
Acts 4:2 They were upset because they taught the people and proclaimed through Jesus that the dead would rise again.
Acts 4:3 They arrested them and kept them in custody until the next day because it was evening.
Acts 4:4 However, many who heard the message believed, and the count of the men was around five thousand.
Acts 4:5 The next day, their leaders, older men, and writers,
Acts 4:6 Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and all the high priest's relatives met in Jerusalem.
Acts 4:7 They placed them in the center and asked, "With what power or by whose name did you do this?"
Acts 4:8 Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "You leaders of the people and elders of Israel,"
Acts 4:9 If today we are being asked how the man who could not walk was healed;
Acts 4:10 Let everyone, and all the people of Israel, know that this man stands before you healed because of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified and whom God raised from the dead.
Acts 4:11 This stone that you builders ignored has now become the cornerstone.
Acts 4:12 There is no salvation through anyone else, for there is no other name under heaven given to people by which we must be saved.
Acts 4:13 When people saw how brave Peter and John were, and realized they were not formally educated, they were amazed; they recognized that Peter and John had been with Jesus.
Acts 4:14 Seeing the man who was healed standing with them, they could not argue against it.
Acts 4:15 When they told them to leave the meeting, they talked with each other.
Acts 4:16 They said, "What should we do with these men? Everyone in Jerusalem knows they performed a remarkable miracle, and we can't deny it."
Acts 4:17 To stop this from spreading among the people, let's firmly warn them not to speak to anyone in this name anymore.
