Acts 4:18 They called them and ordered them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Acts 4:19 But Peter and John replied, "Decide for yourselves if it's right before God to listen to you more than to God.
Acts 4:20 We must speak about what we have seen and heard.
Acts 4:21 After threatening them more, they released them. They found no way to punish them because everyone praised God for what had happened.
Acts 4:22 The man was over forty years old when this healing miracle happened to him.
Acts 4:23 After they were released, they returned to their friends and told them everything the chief priests and elders had said to them.
Acts 4:24 When they heard this, they all spoke to God together, saying, "Lord, you are God, who made the sky, the land, the sea, and everything in them."
Acts 4:25 God said through your servant David, "Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot foolish things?"
Acts 4:26 The kings of the earth rose up, and the leaders met together against God and his chosen one.
Acts 4:27 Truly, Herod, Pontius Pilate, the non-Jewish people, and the people of Israel united against your holy child Jesus, whom you chose.
Acts 4:28 To do whatever your hand and plan had already decided should happen.
Acts 4:29 And now, God, see their threats: and let your servants speak your word with all courage.
Acts 4:30 By reaching out your hand to heal; and that miracles and amazing things may happen in the name of your holy child Jesus.
Acts 4:31 After they prayed, the place where they were gathered trembled; they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God's word confidently.
Acts 4:32 The many people who believed were united in heart and mind. No one claimed that their possessions were only their own. Instead, they shared everything they had.
Acts 4:33 The apostles showed the resurrection of Jesus with great power, and all of them had a lot of grace.
Acts 4:34 Everyone had what they needed because those who owned land or houses sold them and brought the money from the sales.
Acts 4:35 They put the gifts at the apostles' feet, and it was shared out to each person as they needed.
Acts 4:36 And Joses, called Barnabas by the apostles (which means Son of Encouragement), a Levite from Cyprus,
Acts 4:37 Someone who owned land sold it, brought the money, and placed it at the apostles' feet.

Acts 5:1 A man named Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold something they owned.
Acts 5:2 He held back some of the money, his wife knew about it, and he gave part of it and put it at the apostles' feet.
Acts 5:3 Peter said, Ananias, why has Satan made you lie to the Holy Spirit and hold back some of the money from the land?
Acts 5:4 Before you sold it, wasn't it yours? And after you sold it, wasn't the money yours to control? Why did you decide to do this? You haven't lied to people but to God.
Acts 5:5 Ananias heard these words, fell down, and died. Everyone who heard about it was very afraid.
Acts 5:6 The young men got up, wrapped him up, took him out, and buried him.
Acts 5:7 About three hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Acts 5:8 Peter asked her, "Did you sell the land for this amount?" And she replied, "Yes, for that amount."
Acts 5:9 Then Peter said to her, "Why did you both decide to test the Spirit of God? Look, the ones who buried your husband are at the door, and they will take you out too."
Acts 5:10 She immediately fell down at his feet, died, and when the young men came in, they found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
Acts 5:11 Everyone in the church and all who heard about these events were filled with great fear.
Acts 5:12 Through the apostles, many miracles and amazing things happened among the people; they were all together in Solomon's Porch.
Acts 5:13 No one else dared to join them, but the people praised them.
Acts 5:14 More believers, both men and women, were added to God in large numbers.
Acts 5:15 They brought the sick into the streets and placed them on beds and mats so that even Peter's shadow might fall on some as he walked by.
Acts 5:16 Many people came from nearby towns to Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by evil spirits, and all of them were healed.
Acts 5:17 The high priest stood up, and everyone with him, who were the Sadducees group, were very angry.
Acts 5:18 They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
Acts 5:19 At night, God's angel opened the prison doors, took them out, and said.
Acts 5:20 Go, stand in the temple, and tell the people everything about this life.
Acts 5:21 When they heard that, they went into the temple early in the morning and taught. The high priest and his group gathered the council and the whole Israeli senate and sent for the prisoners to be brought.
Acts 5:22 When the guards arrived and didn't find them in jail, they went back and reported it.
Acts 5:23 We found the jail securely locked and the guards standing outside the doors, but when we opened it, there was no one inside.
Acts 5:24 When the high priest, the temple captain, and the chief priests heard all this, they were unsure what it would lead to.
Acts 5:25 Someone came and said, "Look, the men you put in jail are in the temple, teaching the people."
Acts 5:26 The captain and his men went and brought them back without using force, because they were afraid the people might throw stones at them.
Acts 5:27 When they brought them in, they stood before the leaders, and the chief priest questioned them.
Acts 5:28 We clearly ordered you not to teach in this name, yet you have spread your teaching all over Jerusalem and want to make us responsible for this man's death.
Acts 5:29 Peter and the other apostles replied, "We must obey God instead of people."
Acts 5:30 God of our ancestors brought Jesus back to life, who you killed and hung on a tree.
Acts 5:31 God has raised him up with his right hand to be a leader and a savior, to give Israel a chance to change their ways and to forgive their sins.
Acts 5:32 We are his witnesses of these things, and the Holy Spirit, which God has given to those who obey him, is also a witness.
Acts 5:33 When they heard that, they felt deeply hurt and planned to kill them.
Acts 5:34 A Pharisee named Gamaliel, a respected teacher of the law, stood up in the council and ordered that the apostles be taken outside for a short time.
Acts 5:35 He told them, "People of Israel, be careful about what you plan to do to these men."
Acts 5:36 Before this time, Theudas appeared, claiming to be important. About four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all his followers were scattered and came to nothing.
Acts 5:37 After him, Judas from Galilee appeared during the tax times and attracted many followers. He died too, and all who followed him were scattered.
Acts 5:38 I tell you now, stay away from these men and leave them be; because if their plan or action is from people, it will fail.
Acts 5:39 But if it's from God, you can't defeat it; you might be found fighting against God.
Acts 5:40 They agreed with him. After calling the apostles and whipping them, they ordered them not to talk about Jesus and then released them.
Acts 5:41 They left the council, happy because they were considered deserving to endure shame for his name.
Acts 5:42 Every day in the temple and at home, they never stopped teaching and telling the good news about Jesus Christ.

Acts 6:1 During that time, as the number of followers grew, the Greek-speaking followers complained against the Hebrew-speaking followers because their widows were not being helped every day.
Acts 6:2 The twelve gathered all the disciples and said, it isn't right for us to stop teaching God's word to help with meals.
Acts 6:3 Brothers, choose seven men from among you who are known to be honest, filled with the Holy Spirit and wise, so we can put them in charge of this task.
Acts 6:4 We will keep praying and serving the message of God.
Acts 6:5 Everyone liked the idea, so they picked Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, who had converted to their faith.
Acts 6:6 They presented these men to the apostles, and after praying, the apostles placed their hands on them.
Acts 6:7 God's message spread; the group of followers grew a lot in Jerusalem; and many priests started to follow the faith.
Acts 6:8 Stephen, full of trust and strength, performed amazing deeds and miracles among the people.
Acts 6:9 Some people from the synagogue called the synagogue of the Freedmen, along with Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and those from Cilicia and Asia, started to argue with Stephen.
Acts 6:10 They could not argue against the wisdom and spirit he spoke with.
Acts 6:11 They influenced some people to lie, who said, "We heard him say disrespectful things about Moses and about God."
Acts 6:12 They roused the people, the elders, and the teachers of the law, then they attacked him, seized him, and took him to the council.
Acts 6:13 They found lying witnesses who said, "This man never stops speaking against this holy place and the law."
Acts 6:14 We heard him claim that this Jesus from Nazareth will destroy this place and will alter the traditions that Moses gave us.
Acts 6:15 Everyone in the council stared at him and saw his face shining like an angel's.

Acts 7:1 Then the high priest asked, "Is this true?"
Acts 7:2 He said, "Listen, men and fathers, the glorious God appeared to our ancestor Abraham in Mesopotamia before he lived in Haran.
Acts 7:3 God told him, "Leave your country and your relatives, and go to the land I will show you."
Acts 7:4 He left the land of the Chaldeans, lived in Haran, and after his father died, God moved him to this land where you live now.
Acts 7:5 God did not give him any land to own, not even a place to step on. But God promised to give it to him and to his children after him, even though he had no child yet.
Acts 7:6 God said in this way: That his descendants would live in a foreign land; and they would be made slaves and treated badly for four hundred years.
Acts 7:7 God said: I will judge the nation where they are slaves, and afterwards, they will come out and worship me here.
Acts 7:8 God made a promise with Abraham about circumcision: So Abraham had a son, Isaac, and circumcised him on the eighth day; Isaac had Jacob; and Jacob had twelve sons who became leaders.
Acts 7:9 The family leaders, jealous of Joseph, sold him as a slave to Egypt; but God stayed with him.
Acts 7:10 God saved him from all his troubles, gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and Pharaoh made him ruler over Egypt and his whole house.
Acts 7:11 A famine spread over all of Egypt and Canaan, bringing much suffering, and our ancestors couldn't find food.
Acts 7:12 When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there first.
Acts 7:13 Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers a second time, and his family became known to Pharaoh.
Acts 7:14 Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, 75 people in total.
Acts 7:15 Jacob went to Egypt and he and our ancestors died there.
Acts 7:16 They were taken to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father.
Acts 7:17 As the time for God's promise to Abraham came near, the people increased and became many in Egypt.
Acts 7:18 A new king came to power who did not know about Joseph.
Acts 7:19 This person tricked our relatives and treated our ancestors badly, making them throw out their babies so they would not survive.
Acts 7:20 During this time, Moses was born, was very beautiful, and was cared for in his father's home for three months.
Acts 7:21 When he was thrown away, Pharaoh's daughter picked him up and cared for him as her own son.
Acts 7:22 Moses knew all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speaking and acting.
Acts 7:23 When he was 40 years old, he felt the urge to see his fellow Israelites.
Acts 7:24 He saw someone being treated unfairly, so he defended him, took revenge for the one who was hurt, and struck down the Egyptian.
Acts 7:25 He thought his brothers would realize that God would use him to save them, but they didn't understand.
Acts 7:26 The next day he appeared to them as they were fighting, wanting to reconcile them, saying, "Friends, you are brothers; why are you hurting each other?"
Acts 7:27 The person who wronged his neighbor pushed him away, asking, "Who made you our ruler and judge?"
Acts 7:28 Will you kill me like you killed the Egyptian yesterday?
Acts 7:29 Moses ran away after hearing this and lived as a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he had two sons.
Acts 7:30 After forty years passed, he saw an angel of God in a fire inside a bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
Acts 7:31 When Moses saw it, he was amazed at the sight. As he went closer to look, God's voice spoke to him.
Acts 7:32 I am the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses shook with fear and did not dare to look.
Acts 7:33 God said to him, "Take off your shoes because the place where you are standing is holy ground."
Acts 7:34 I have seen my people's suffering in Egypt, heard their cries, and have come to rescue them. Now go, I will send you to Egypt.
Acts 7:35 They rejected Moses, asking, "Who made you a leader and judge?" But God chose him to be their leader and rescuer, with the help of the angel who met him in the bush.
Acts 7:36 God led them out after showing them amazing things and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the desert for forty years.
Acts 7:37 This is Moses, who told the Israelites, "God will bring up a prophet like me from among your brothers; you must listen to him."
Acts 7:38 This is the one who was with the angel in the church in the wilderness, on Mount Sinai, and with our ancestors: he received the living messages to give to us.
Acts 7:39 Our ancestors did not want to obey him. Instead, they pushed him away and wanted to return to Egypt in their hearts.
Acts 7:40 Tell Aaron to make us gods to lead us: for this Moses who took us out of Egypt, we don't know what happened to him.
Acts 7:41 They made a calf back then, gave offerings to the idol and were happy with what they had done.
Acts 7:42 God let them worship the stars of the sky. As the prophets wrote, "People of Israel, did you bring me animal sacrifices for forty years in the desert?"
Acts 7:43 Yes, you carried the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Remphan, idols you made to worship them: and I will take you away beyond Babylon.
Acts 7:44 Our ancestors had the tent of testimony in the desert, as God commanded, telling Moses to make it like the design he had seen.
Acts 7:45 Our ancestors, including Joshua, took over the land of the nations, which God had cleared away for them, all the way until the time of David.
Acts 7:46 He found favor with God and wanted to build a home for the God of Jacob.
Acts 7:47 Solomon built a house for God.
Acts 7:48 However, the highest does not live in buildings made by hands, as the prophet says.
Acts 7:49 Heaven is where I sit as king, and the earth is a place to rest my feet. What kind of home could you build for me? What place could be my resting spot?
Acts 7:50 Didn't my hand make all these things?
Acts 7:51 You are stubborn and closed in your heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your ancestors did.
Acts 7:52 Which prophets did your ancestors not attack? They killed those who told about the arrival of the Righteous One, whom you have now betrayed and murdered.
Acts 7:53 They received the law given through angels but have not followed it.
Acts 7:54 When they heard this, they felt deep pain in their hearts and gritted their teeth at him.
Acts 7:55 He, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw God's glory, with Jesus standing at God's right side.
Acts 7:56 And said, Look, I see the sky opened, and the Son of man standing at God's right side.
Acts 7:57 They shouted loudly, covered their ears, and all rushed at him together.
Acts 7:58 They threw him out of the city and stoned him. The witnesses left their coats near a young man named Saul.
Acts 7:59 They threw stones at Stephen, who called out to God, saying, "Lord Jesus, take my spirit."
Acts 7:60 He kneeled and shouted, "God, do not hold this sin against them." After he said this, he passed away.

Acts 8:1 Saul agreed to his death. There was a big persecution against the church in Jerusalem; and everyone was scattered across Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.
Acts 8:2 Faithful people took Stephen to bury him and cried a lot for him.
Acts 8:3 Saul caused great trouble for the church, going into houses and dragging out men and women to put them in jail.
Acts 8:4 So those who were spread out went all around telling God's message.
Acts 8:5 Philip went to the city of Samaria and told the people about Christ.
Acts 8:6 The people unanimously paid attention to what Philip said, listening and watching the miracles he performed.
Acts 8:7 Many people with evil spirits shouted loudly as the spirits left them. And many who could not move or walk were healed.
Acts 8:8 The city was filled with great happiness.
Acts 8:9 A man named Simon lived in that city before. He practiced magic, amazing the people of Samaria, and claimed to be someone important.
Acts 8:10 Everyone listened to him closely, from the least important to the most important, saying, "This man has great power from God."
Acts 8:11 They respected him because for a long time he had amazed them with his magic.
Acts 8:12 When people believed what Philip was saying about God's kingdom and Jesus Christ, they got baptized, both men and women.
Acts 8:13 Simon also believed and after his baptism, he stayed with Philip, amazed by the miracles and signs he saw.
Acts 8:14 When the apostles in Jerusalem learned that Samaria had accepted God's word, they sent Peter and John to them.
Acts 8:15 When they arrived, they prayed for them so they could receive the Holy Spirit.
Acts 8:16 Because none of them had received the Holy Spirit yet; they had only been baptized in the name of Jesus.
Acts 8:17 They placed their hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit.
Acts 8:18 When Simon noticed that the Holy Spirit was given after the apostles laid their hands on people, he offered them money.
Acts 8:19 Give me this power too, so anyone I touch can receive the Holy Spirit.
Acts 8:20 Peter told him, "May your money be lost with you, because you believed that God's gift can be bought with money."
Acts 8:21 You have no part or share in this matter, because your heart is not right with God.
Acts 8:22 Turn away from your evil ways and ask God to forgive the thoughts of your heart.
Acts 8:23 I see that you are full of bitterness and trapped in sin.
Acts 8:24 Simon answered, "Please pray to God for me so that none of the things you talked about will happen to me."
Acts 8:25 After they told about God and shared his message, they went back to Jerusalem and spoke about Jesus in many Samaritan towns.
Acts 8:26 God's messenger spoke to Philip, saying, "Get up and go south on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza, which is in the desert."
Acts 8:27 He got up and went, and there was a man from Ethiopia, a high-ranking official under Queen Candace of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her wealth and had come to Jerusalem to worship.
Acts 8:28 He was coming back, sitting in his chariot, and reading the prophet Isaiah.
Acts 8:29 Then the Spirit told Philip, "Go close and join this chariot."
Acts 8:30 Philip ran to him, heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and asked, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
Acts 8:31 He asked, "How can I understand unless someone explains it to me?" So he invited Philip to come up and sit beside him.
Acts 8:32 The part of the scripture he read said, "He was led like a sheep to be killed, and like a quiet lamb before someone cutting its wool, he did not open his mouth."
Acts 8:33 In his low state, he was denied justice: and who can speak of his descendants? For his life is taken from the earth.
Acts 8:34 The eunuch asked Philip, "Please, who is the prophet talking about? Himself or someone else?"
Acts 8:35 Then Philip started speaking and, using that part of the Bible, told him about Jesus.
Acts 8:36 As they traveled, they found some water. The eunuch said, "Look, here's water. What's stopping me from getting baptized?"
Acts 8:37 Philip said, "If you believe with all your heart, you can." And he replied, "I believe Jesus Christ is God's Son."
Acts 8:38 He told the chariot to stop. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
Acts 8:39 After they came up from the water, God's Spirit took Philip away, and the eunuch didn't see him again but continued on his journey happily.
Acts 8:40 Philip appeared in Azotus, and as he traveled, he shared the message in all the cities until he reached Caesarea.

Acts 9:1 Saul, still making threats and wanting to kill the followers of the Lord, went to the high priest.
Acts 9:2 He asked for letters to the Damascus places of worship, so that if he found anyone who followed this path, man or woman, he could take them tied up to Jerusalem.
Acts 9:3 As he traveled, he approached Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven shone around him.
Acts 9:4 He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
Acts 9:5 He asked, "Who are you, God?" And God replied, "I am Jesus, the one you are hurting. It's tough for you to fight against what's urging you."
Acts 9:6 He, shaking and amazed, said, "God, what do you want me to do?" God told him, "Get up, go into the city, and you will be told what you need to do."
Acts 9:7 The men traveling with him stood silently, hearing a voice but seeing no one.
Acts 9:8 Saul got up from the ground; when he opened his eyes, he couldn't see anyone. So they took him by the hand and led him into Damascus.
Acts 9:9 He could not see for three days and did not eat or drink.
Acts 9:10 In Damascus there was a follower named Ananias. In a vision God called to him, "Ananias." He answered, "Here I am, God."
Acts 9:11 God told him, "Get up, go to the street named Straight, and ask at Judas' house for a man named Saul from Tarsus because he is praying."
Acts 9:12 In a vision, he saw a man named Ananias come in and touch him so he could see again.
Acts 9:13 Then Ananias answered, "God, I have heard from many about this man, how much harm he has done to your holy people in Jerusalem."
Acts 9:14 He has permission from the high priests to arrest everyone who prays to you.
Acts 9:15 But God said to him, "Go on your way, because he is my chosen tool to bring my name to non-Jews, rulers, and the people of Israel."
Acts 9:16 I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.
Acts 9:17 Ananias went to the house, put his hands on Saul, and said, "Brother Saul, Jesus, who you saw on your way here, sent me so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
Acts 9:18 Right away, something like scales fell from his eyes, and he could see. Then he got up and was baptized.
Acts 9:19 After he ate food, he gained strength. Then Saul spent some days with the followers in Damascus.
Acts 9:20 Right away, he told people in the synagogues that Jesus is God's Son.
Acts 9:21 Everyone who heard him was amazed and asked, "Isn't this the man who was destroying those who called on this name in Jerusalem, and didn't he come here to take them as prisoners to the priests?"
Acts 9:22 Saul grew stronger and confused the Jews living in Damascus by showing that Jesus is truly the Christ.
Acts 9:23 After many days, the Jews planned to kill him.
Acts 9:24 Saul knew they were waiting to ambush him. They guarded the city gates day and night to kill him.
Acts 9:25 The followers took him at night and lowered him down the city wall in a basket.
Acts 9:26 When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to meet with the followers, but they were all scared of him and didn't believe he was really a follower.
Acts 9:27 Barnabas took him to the apostles and told them how he saw Jesus on his journey, that Jesus spoke to him, and how he bravely preached in Jesus' name in Damascus.
Acts 9:28 He was with them when they entered and left Jerusalem.
Acts 9:29 He spoke bravely in the name of Jesus and argued with the Greeks, but they tried to kill him.
Acts 9:30 When the followers learned this, they took him to Caesarea and sent him on to Tarsus.
Acts 9:31 The churches in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace, grew stronger, lived in respect for God, and, encouraged by the Holy Spirit, increased in number.
Acts 9:32 As Peter traveled through different places, he also visited the holy people living in Lydda.
Acts 9:33 There he met a man named Aeneas who had been bedridden for eight years because he was paralyzed.
Acts 9:34 Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you: get up and prepare your bed." And he got up at once.
Acts 9:35 Everyone living in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to God.
Acts 9:36 In Joppa, there was a follower named Tabitha, also known as Dorcas, who did many good deeds and helped the poor.
Acts 9:37 In those days, she became ill and died. After they washed her body, they placed her in an upstairs room.
Acts 9:38 Because Lydda was close to Joppa and the followers knew Peter was there, they sent two men to ask him to come quickly.
Acts 9:39 Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him to the upstairs room where all the widows were crying and showing him the clothes and robes Dorcas had made while she was alive.
Acts 9:40 Peter sent everyone out, knelt down, and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
Acts 9:41 He took her hand, helped her stand, and after calling the believers and widows, showed her to them alive.
Acts 9:42 News spread all over Joppa; many people believed in God.
Acts 9:43 He stayed in Joppa for many days with a man named Simon, who was a leather worker.

Acts 10:1 In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a captain of the Italian group.
Acts 10:2 A religious man who respected God with his whole family, gave lots of charity to others, and always prayed to God.
Acts 10:3 In a clear vision around three in the afternoon, he saw an angel of God come to him and say, "Cornelius."
Acts 10:4 When he saw him, he was scared and asked, "What is it, God?" And God answered, "Your prayers and gifts to the poor have been remembered by God."
Acts 10:5 Now, send people to Joppa and ask for a man named Simon, also known as Peter.
Acts 10:6 He is staying with Simon, a leather worker, whose house is by the sea. He will tell you what you should do.
Acts 10:7 After the angel who spoke to Cornelius left, he summoned two of his servants and a loyal soldier who served him regularly.
Acts 10:8 After he explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.
Acts 10:9 The next day, as they were traveling and getting close to the city, Peter went up to the rooftop to pray around noon.
Acts 10:10 He became very hungry and wanted to eat, but as they were preparing the food, he fell into a deep dream.
Acts 10:11 He saw heaven open and a vessel coming down to him, like a large sheet tied at the four corners, being lowered to the ground.
Acts 10:12 In it were all kinds of four-legged animals, wild creatures, crawling things, and birds of the sky.
Acts 10:13 A voice came to him saying, "Get up, Peter; kill and eat."
Acts 10:14 Peter said, "No, God; I have never eaten anything not pure or clean."
Acts 10:15 The voice spoke to him a second time, "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean."
Acts 10:16 This happened three times, and then the container was taken back up into heaven.
Acts 10:17 While Peter was wondering what his vision meant, the men Cornelius sent asked for Simon's house and were standing at the gate.
Acts 10:18 They called and asked if Simon, also known as Peter, was staying there.
Acts 10:19 As Peter was thinking about the vision, the Spirit told him, "Look, three men are looking for you."
Acts 10:20 Get up, go down, and go with them without doubting, because I have sent them.
Acts 10:21 Then Peter went to the men who Cornelius sent to him and said, "Look, I'm the one you're looking for. Why have you come?"
Acts 10:22 They said, "Cornelius, a fair officer, who respects God and is well spoken of by all the Jewish people, was told by God through a holy angel to invite you to his home and listen to what you have to say."
Acts 10:23 He invited them in to stay. The next day Peter left with them, and some believers from Joppa went along.
Acts 10:24 The next day they arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had gathered his relatives and close friends.
Acts 10:25 As Peter entered, Cornelius met him, knelt before him, and honored him as if he were God.
Acts 10:26 Peter helped him up, saying, "Get up; I am just a man like you."
Acts 10:27 As he chatted with him, he entered and saw many people had gathered.
Acts 10:28 He told them, "You are aware that it's not allowed for a Jewish man to associate with or visit someone from a different nation. However, God has shown me that I should not consider any person impure or unclean."
Acts 10:29 So I came to you without arguing, as soon as I was called. Why did you call for me?
Acts 10:30 Cornelius said, "Four days ago, I was fasting until this time. At three in the afternoon, I was praying in my home, when suddenly a man in shining clothes stood in front of me.
Acts 10:31 Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your acts of charity are remembered before God.
Acts 10:32 Go to Joppa and ask for Simon, also known as Peter, who is staying at the home of Simon the leatherworker by the sea. When he arrives, he will talk to you.
Acts 10:33 I sent for you right away; you did right to come. Now we're all here before God to listen to everything God has told you to tell us.
Acts 10:34 Then Peter began to speak, "I truly understand that God does not show favoritism to anyone.
Acts 10:35 In every country, anyone who respects God and does what is right is accepted by Him.
Acts 10:36 God sent a message to the people of Israel, telling them about peace through Jesus Christ: (he is the ruler of all.)
Acts 10:37 You know the message that spread through all Judea, starting in Galilee after the baptism John preached.
Acts 10:38 God gave Jesus of Nazareth the Holy Spirit and power. He went around doing good and healing all who were under the devil's control, because God was with him.
Acts 10:39 We saw everything he did in the Jewish lands and in Jerusalem. They killed him and hung him on a tree.
Acts 10:40 God raised him up on the third day and showed him openly.
Acts 10:41 Not to everyone, but to chosen witnesses before God, to us who ate and drank with him after he came back to life.
Acts 10:42 He told us to speak to the people and to say that he is the one chosen by God to judge the living and the dead.
Acts 10:43 Every prophet agrees that anyone who believes in him will have their sins forgiven through his name.
Acts 10:44 While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came upon all who heard the message.
Acts 10:45 The believers who were Jews were amazed because the Holy Spirit was given to the non-Jewish people who had come with Peter.
Acts 10:46 They heard them speaking in different languages and praising God. Then Peter replied.
Acts 10:47 Can anyone stop these people from being baptized with water? They have received the Holy Spirit just like us.
Acts 10:48 He ordered them to be baptized in God's name. Then they asked him to stay for some days.

Acts 11:1 The apostles and believers in Judea heard that non-Jews also accepted God's message.
Acts 11:2 When Peter arrived in Jerusalem, those who were circumcised argued with him.
Acts 11:3 You are accused of going to uncircumcised men and eating with them.
Acts 11:4 But Peter explained the story from the start, and told it to them step by step, saying,
Acts 11:5 I was in Joppa praying when I fell into a trance and saw a vision. I saw something like a large sheet coming down from heaven, held by its four corners, and it came down to me.
Acts 11:6 I looked closely and saw animals with four feet, wild creatures, crawling things, and birds of the air.
Acts 11:7 I heard a voice telling me, "Get up, Peter; kill and eat."
Acts 11:8 But I said, "No, God, because I have never eaten anything that is not pure or clean."
Acts 11:9 The voice from heaven told me again, "What God has made clean, do not call ordinary."
Acts 11:10 This happened three times, and then everything was taken back up into heaven.
Acts 11:11 Look, right away three men who had been sent to me from Caesarea arrived at the house where I was staying.
Acts 11:12 The Spirit told me to go with them without doubting. Also, these six friends came with me, and we went into the man's house.
Acts 11:13 He showed us how he saw an angel in his house who stood and said to him, "Send men to Joppa and ask for Simon, also known as Peter."
Acts 11:14 Someone will tell you messages by which you and your whole family will be saved.
Acts 11:15 As I started to talk, the Holy Spirit came on them, just like it did on us at first.
Acts 11:16 I remembered what God said: John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
Acts 11:17 Since God gave them the same gift as he gave us who believed in Jesus Christ, who was I to oppose God?
Acts 11:18 When they heard this, they became quiet and praised God, saying, "So God has also given to non-Jews the chance to turn from their sins and receive life."
Acts 11:19 Those forced away by the troubles starting with Stephen went to places like Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, telling God's message only to Jews.
Acts 11:20 Some of them were from Cyprus and Cyrene, and when they arrived in Antioch, they spoke to the Greeks, telling them about Jesus.
Acts 11:21 God helped them, and many people believed and turned to God.
Acts 11:22 News about these events reached the church in Jerusalem, so they sent Barnabas to go to Antioch.
Acts 11:23 When he arrived and saw God's grace, he was happy and encouraged everyone to stay loyal to God with a determined heart.
Acts 11:24 He was a good man, filled with the Holy Spirit and faith, and many people joined God.
Acts 11:25 Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
Acts 11:26 When he found him, he took him to Antioch. For a whole year, they met with the church and taught many people. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
Acts 11:27 During this time, prophets traveled from Jerusalem to Antioch.
Acts 11:28 One of them, named Agabus, stood up and showed by the Spirit that a big famine would happen all over the world, and it did happen when Claudius Caesar was in power.
Acts 11:29 The followers decided to send help to their fellow believers in Judaea, each one giving as much as they could.
Acts 11:30 They did this and sent it to the leaders through Barnabas and Saul.

Acts 12:1 At that time, King Herod started to bother some people from the church.
Acts 12:2 He killed James, John's brother, with a sword.
Acts 12:3 Seeing that it made the Jews happy, he decided to arrest Peter too. (It was the time of the Feast of Unleavened Bread.)
Acts 12:4 After arresting him, he put him in jail and handed him over to four groups of four soldiers to guard him, planning to present him to the people after Passover.
Acts 12:5 Peter was kept in jail, but the church constantly prayed to God for him.
Acts 12:6 When Herod planned to bring him out, that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, tied with two chains, and guards by the door were watching the jail.
Acts 12:7 An angel from God came to him, and a light shone in the jail. The angel hit Peter on the side and lifted him up, saying, "Get up fast." And his chains fell off his hands.
Acts 12:8 The angel told him, "Get dressed and put on your sandals." He did that. Then the angel said, "Put on your coat and follow me."
Acts 12:9 He went out and followed, not knowing the angel had really done this; he thought he was seeing a vision.
Acts 12:10 After they passed the first and second guard posts, they reached the iron gate leading to the city; it opened by itself for them. They went out, walked down one street, and right away the angel left him.
Acts 12:11 When Peter realized what happened, he said, "Now I'm certain that God has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod's control and from what the Jewish people expected."
Acts 12:12 After thinking about it, he went to Mary's house, the mother of John also called Mark, where many people were meeting and praying.
Acts 12:13 While Peter knocked at the gate door, a young woman named Rhoda came to listen.
Acts 12:14 When she recognized Peter's voice, she didn't open the gate because she was so happy, but she ran inside and told everyone that Peter was at the gate.
Acts 12:15 They told her, "You're crazy." But she kept saying it was true. So they said, "It must be his angel."
Acts 12:16 Peter kept knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were amazed.
Acts 12:17 But he, signaling to them with his hand to be quiet, told them how God had helped him escape from jail. He said, "Go tell these things to James and the others." Then he left and went to a different place.
Acts 12:18 As soon as it was morning, the soldiers were very upset about what had happened to Peter.
Acts 12:19 When Herod couldn't find him, he questioned the guards and ordered them to be killed. Then he left Judea, went to Caesarea, and stayed there.
Acts 12:20 Herod was very unhappy with the people of Tyre and Sidon. But they joined together and went to him, and after winning over Blastus, the king's servant, they asked for peace because their land depended on the king's land for food.
Acts 12:21 On a certain day, Herod, dressed in his royal clothes, sat on his throne and spoke to the people.
Acts 12:22 The people shouted, "This is the voice of a god, not a human."
Acts 12:23 Right away, God's angel struck him down because he didn't honor God: so worms ate him, and he died.
Acts 12:24 God's word spread and increased widely.
Acts 12:25 Barnabas and Saul came back from Jerusalem after completing their work and brought John Mark with them.

Acts 13:1 In the Antioch church, there were some prophets and teachers like Barnabas, Simeon also known as Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen who grew up with Herod the ruler, and Saul.
Acts 13:2 While they served God and went without food, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart Barnabas and Saul for the job I have chosen them for."
Acts 13:3 After they fasted, prayed, and put their hands on them, they sent them off.
Acts 13:4 They were sent by the Holy Spirit and went to Seleucia; from there they sailed to Cyprus.
Acts 13:5 When they were in Salamis, they shared God's message in the Jewish synagogues and John helped them.
Acts 13:6 After they traveled across the island to Paphos, they met a magician who was a fake prophet and a Jew named Barjesus.
Acts 13:7 He was with the governor of the region, Sergius Paulus, a wise man. He asked for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God's message.
Acts 13:8 Elymas the magician tried to stop them and wanted to keep the governor from believing.
Acts 13:9 Then Saul, also known as Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked straight at him.
Acts 13:10 And said, "Oh, you are very tricky and evil, you child of the devil and enemy of everything good, will you not stop twisting the true paths of God?"
Acts 13:11 Now, look, God's power is on you, and you will be blind and not see the sun for a while. Suddenly, he was covered in a fog and darkness, and he walked around looking for someone to guide him by the hand.
Acts 13:12 When the governor saw what happened, he believed and was amazed at God's teaching.
Acts 13:13 When Paul and his friends sailed from Paphos, they arrived at Perga in Pamphylia. John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
Acts 13:14 After leaving Perga, they arrived in Antioch in Pisidia, entered the synagogue on the Sabbath, and sat down.
Acts 13:15 After the reading of the law and the prophets, the synagogue leaders sent a message to them, saying, "Friends, if you have any encouraging message for the people, please speak."
Acts 13:16 Paul stood up, waved his hand, and said, "People of Israel and all who respect God, listen to me."
Acts 13:17 God chose our ancestors, honored the people while they lived as foreigners in Egypt, and with great power led them out of there.
Acts 13:18 For forty years God put up with their behavior in the desert.
Acts 13:19 After he defeated seven nations in Canaan, he gave their land to them by drawing lots.
Acts 13:20 After that, he gave them leaders for about 450 years, until Samuel the prophet.
Acts 13:21 Later they wanted a king, so God gave them Saul, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.
Acts 13:22 After removing him, God made David their king and testified about him, saying, "I have found David, Jesse's son, a man who shares my desires and will do everything I want."
Acts 13:23 God promised to bring Israel a Savior, Jesus, from this man's descendants.
Acts 13:24 Before Jesus came, John told all the people of Israel to turn away from their sins and be baptized.
Acts 13:25 As John finished his work, he asked, "Who do you think I am? I am not the one. But look, someone is coming after me, and I'm not good enough to untie his sandals."
Acts 13:26 Friends and descendants of Abraham, and all who honor God, this message of salvation is for you.
Acts 13:27 The people living in Jerusalem and their leaders didn't recognize him or understand what the prophets said, even though they read their words every Sabbath. By condemning him, they made these prophecies come true.
Acts 13:28 Even though they could not prove he deserved to die, they still asked Pilate to have him killed.
Acts 13:29 After completing all that was written about him, they removed him from the cross and placed him in a tomb.
Acts 13:30 God raised him from the dead.
Acts 13:31 He was seen for many days by those who went with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who now tell the people about him.
Acts 13:32 We share with you good news about the promise given to our ancestors.
Acts 13:33 God has done what he promised our ancestors by raising Jesus from the dead, as it's written in the second psalm: "You are my Son; today I have become your father."
Acts 13:34 About raising him from the dead, never to decay again, he said, I will give you the faithful blessings promised to David.
Acts 13:35 That's why it is said in another psalm, "You will not let your Holy One decay."
Acts 13:36 David served his time by God's will, then he died, was buried with his ancestors, and his body decayed.
Acts 13:37 But he, who was raised by God, did not decay.
Acts 13:38 Let it be clear to you then, friends, that through this man the forgiveness of sins is announced to you.
Acts 13:39 By him, all who believe are made right with God from everything that the law of Moses could not make right.
Acts 13:40 Be careful, so what the prophets said doesn't happen to you.
Acts 13:41 Look, you who scoff, be amazed and vanish: because I am doing something in your days, something you will never believe, even if someone explains it to you.
Acts 13:42 After the Jews left the synagogue, the non-Jews asked to hear these teachings the following Sabbath.
Acts 13:43 After the meeting ended, many Jews and believers followed Paul and Barnabas. They talked to them and encouraged them to keep living in God's kindness.
Acts 13:44 On the next Sabbath, nearly the whole city gathered to hear God's message.
Acts 13:45 When the Jews saw the crowds, they felt jealous and spoke against what Paul was saying, arguing and insulting God.
Acts 13:46 Paul and Barnabas became brave and said, "It was important to speak God's word to you first. But since you reject it and think you're not worthy of eternal life, now we will speak to other people."
Acts 13:47 God has instructed us, saying, I have made you a light for the non-Jews, so that you may bring salvation to the farthest places of the world.
Acts 13:48 When the non-Jews heard this, they were happy and praised God's message. All those chosen for eternal life believed.
Acts 13:49 God's message spread all over the area.
Acts 13:50 The Jews convinced the religious and respected women and the city's leaders to persecute Paul and Barnabas and forced them to leave their region.
Acts 13:51 They brushed the dust from their feet as a warning to them and went to Iconium.
Acts 13:52 The followers were filled with happiness and the Holy Spirit.

Acts 14:1 In Iconium, they both went into the Jewish synagogue, and spoke so well that many Jews and Greeks believed.
Acts 14:2 But the Jews who did not believe upset the non-Jews and turned their thoughts against the believers.
Acts 14:3 They stayed there a long time, speaking bravely about God, who showed that their message of kindness was true by letting them perform miracles and wonders.
Acts 14:4 The people in the city were split: some sided with the Jews, and some with the apostles.
Acts 14:5 When both the non-Jews and the Jews with their leaders attacked them to abuse and stone them,
Acts 14:6 They realized it and ran away to the cities of Lystra and Derbe in Lycaonia, and to the surrounding area.
Acts 14:7 There they shared the good news.
Acts 14:8 In Lystra, there was a man who couldn't use his feet. He had been unable to walk since he was born.
Acts 14:9 Paul spoke and a man listened; he looked straight at him, saw he believed, and could be healed.
Acts 14:10 Spoke loudly, "Get up on your feet." And he jumped up and walked.
Acts 14:11 When the people saw what Paul did, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, "The gods have come down to us looking like humans."
Acts 14:12 People named Barnabas as Jupiter and Paul as Mercury because Paul was the main speaker.
Acts 14:13 The priest of Jupiter from their city brought bulls and wreaths to the gates and wanted to offer a sacrifice with everyone.
Acts 14:14 When the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard this, they tore their clothes and ran into the crowd, shouting.
Acts 14:15 And asking, "Friends, why do you do these things? We are just like you, feeling the same things, and we tell you to stop worshipping these worthless things and turn to the real God who created the sky, the land, the sea, and everything in them."
Acts 14:16 In the past, God allowed all nations to follow their own paths.
Acts 14:17 But God didn't leave without evidence, doing good, giving us rain from the sky, and seasons of bounty, filling our lives with food and joy.
Acts 14:18 With these words, they barely stopped the people from offering sacrifices to them.
Acts 14:19 Some Jews from Antioch and Iconium arrived and convinced the people to stone Paul. They thought he was dead, so they dragged him out of the city.
Acts 14:20 Even though the followers were standing around him, he got up, went into the city, and the next day he left with Barnabas to Derbe.
Acts 14:21 After they shared the good news with that city and taught many people, they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
Acts 14:22 Strengthening the believers and encouraging them to stay true to the faith, and saying that we must go through many hard times to enter God's kingdom.
Acts 14:23 After they chose leaders for each church and prayed with fasting, they trusted these leaders to God, in whom they believed.
Acts 14:24 After they traveled through Pisidia, they arrived in Pamphylia.
Acts 14:25 After they shared God's message in Perga, they traveled to Attalia.
Acts 14:26 From there, they sailed to Antioch, where they had been entrusted to God's care for the task they completed.
Acts 14:27 When they arrived and brought the church together, they told everyone what God had done with them and how He had made it possible for non-Jews to believe.
Acts 14:28 They stayed there a long time with the followers.

Acts 15:1 Some men from Judaea came and told the believers, "You must be circumcised like Moses taught, or you cannot be saved."
Acts 15:2 So when Paul and Barnabas had a big argument with some people, they decided that Paul, Barnabas, and a few others should go to Jerusalem to talk to the apostles and elders about this matter.
Acts 15:3 The church helped them on their journey, and they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the non-Jews had turned to God, which brought great happiness to all the believers.
Acts 15:4 When they arrived in Jerusalem, the church, the apostles, and the elders welcomed them, and they shared everything God had done with them.
Acts 15:5 Some Pharisees who believed stood up and said that it was necessary to circumcise the men and to tell them to follow the Law of Moses.
Acts 15:6 The apostles and leaders met to discuss this issue.
Acts 15:7 After much discussion, Peter stood up and said to them, "Friends, you know that some time ago God chose me so that the non-Jews could hear the message of the good news from me and believe.
Acts 15:8 God, who knows the hearts, showed approval of them by giving the Holy Spirit, just as God did to us.
Acts 15:9 God made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts through faith.
Acts 15:10 So why are you testing God by putting a heavy burden on the followers' necks that neither our ancestors nor we could carry?
Acts 15:11 We believe that by the kindness of Jesus Christ, we will be saved just like them.
Acts 15:12 Everyone was quiet and listened to Barnabas and Paul as they explained the amazing things God had done through them among the non-Jews.
Acts 15:13 After they were quiet, James spoke, saying, "Listen to me, friends and brothers:
Acts 15:14 Simeon has explained how God first visited the non-Jews to choose some of them to be his people.
Acts 15:15 The prophets' words agree with this; it is written,
Acts 15:16 I will come back and rebuild David's fallen shelter; I will repair its ruins and restore it.
Acts 15:17 So that the rest of people might look for God, and all the non-Jews who are called by my name, says God, who does all these things.
Acts 15:18 God knows all his works since the world began.
Acts 15:19 So I decide that we should not bother the Gentiles who turn to God.
Acts 15:20 We should write to them to stay away from idol pollution, sexual immorality, strangled animals, and blood.
Acts 15:21 Since long ago, Moses has had people in every city who teach about him; his writings are read in the synagogues every Sabbath.
Acts 15:22 The apostles, elders, and the whole church agreed to send some of their own men to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, also known as Barsabas, and Silas, who were leaders among the believers.
Acts 15:23 The apostles, elders, and fellow believers send greetings to the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
Acts 15:24 We've heard some who left us have upset you with their words, turning your hearts away, telling you to be circumcised and follow the law, which we did not tell them to do.
Acts 15:25 We agreed together to send some chosen friends to you along with our dear Barnabas and Paul.
Acts 15:26 Men who risked their lives for Jesus Christ.
Acts 15:27 We have sent Judas and Silas to tell you the same things in person.
Acts 15:28 The Holy Spirit and we have decided not to give you any heavy burdens besides these important things.
Acts 15:29 Avoid eating food given to idols, blood, strangled animals, and stay away from sexual sin. If you do this, you will be doing well. Take care.
Acts 15:30 After they were sent off, they went to Antioch, and when they had brought everyone together, they gave them the letter.
Acts 15:31 After they read it, they were happy because it comforted them.
Acts 15:32 Judas and Silas, who were also prophets, encouraged the believers with many words and strengthened them.
Acts 15:33 After staying there for a while, they left peacefully to go to the apostles, sent by the believers.
Acts 15:34 Silas was happy to stay there.
Acts 15:35 Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and telling others about God's message, along with many others.
Acts 15:36 Some days later, Paul said to Barnabas, "Let's go back and see how our friends in every city where we shared God's message are doing."
Acts 15:37 Barnabas decided to bring John, called Mark, with them.
Acts 15:38 But Paul thought it was not a good idea to take him along, because he had left them in Pamphylia and had not continued with them in their work.
Acts 15:39 They argued so much that they split up: Barnabas took Mark and went to Cyprus.
Acts 15:40 Paul chose Silas and left, with the brothers' blessing to God's grace.
Acts 15:41 He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

Acts 16:1 He went to Derbe and Lystra. There, he met a follower named Timothy, whose mother was a Jewish believer, but whose father was Greek.
Acts 16:2 He had a good reputation among the believers in Lystra and Iconium.
Acts 16:3 Paul wanted him to travel with him, so he circumcised him because of the Jews in that area, since they all knew his father was Greek.
Acts 16:4 As they traveled through the towns, they gave out the rules to follow that the apostles and elders in Jerusalem had decided on.
Acts 16:5 The churches were strengthened in their faith and grew in number every day.
Acts 16:6 After they traveled through Phrygia and Galatia, the Holy Spirit did not allow them to preach the word in Asia.
Acts 16:7 After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go to Bithynia, but the Spirit did not allow them.
Acts 16:8 They went through Mysia and came to Troas.
Acts 16:9 Paul had a vision at night; a Macedonian man stood there, asking him, "Please come to Macedonia and help us."
Acts 16:10 After seeing the vision, we immediately tried to go to Macedonia, confident that God had called us to share the good news with them.
Acts 16:11 So we sailed away from Troas and went directly to Samothrace, and the following day to Neapolis.
Acts 16:12 From there we went to Philippi, the main city of that part of Macedonia and a colony. We stayed in that city for several days.
Acts 16:13 On the Sabbath, we left the city to a riverside where people often prayed; we sat down and talked with the women who came there.
Acts 16:14 A woman named Lydia, who sold purple cloth and lived in Thyatira, worshipped God and listened to us because God opened her heart to pay attention to what Paul said.
Acts 16:15 After she and her family were baptized, she asked us, "If you think I am loyal to God, please come to my home and stay." And she insisted we go.
Acts 16:16 As we were going to pray, we met a girl with a spirit of telling the future, who made a lot of money for her owners by predicting things.
Acts 16:17 She followed Paul and us, shouting, "These men are servants of the most high God, who show us how to be saved."
Acts 16:18 She did this for many days. But Paul, upset, turned and told the spirit, "I order you in Jesus Christ's name to leave her." And it left her that hour.
Acts 16:19 When her owners realized they could no longer make money from her, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them to the authorities in the public square.
Acts 16:20 They brought them to the officials, saying, "These men are Jews and are causing a lot of trouble in our city."
Acts 16:21 They teach practices that we, as Romans, cannot accept or follow.
Acts 16:22 The crowd stood up together against them. The officials tore their clothes and ordered them to be beaten.
Acts 16:23 After they whipped them many times, they threw them into jail and told the jailer to watch them carefully.
Acts 16:24 The guard, given this order, put them into the innermost cell and clamped their feet in wooden blocks.
Acts 16:25 At midnight, Paul and Silas prayed and sang songs to God, and the other prisoners listened to them.
Acts 16:26 Suddenly, there was a big earthquake that shook the prison's foundations: right away, all the doors opened, and everyone's chains came loose.
Acts 16:27 When the prison guard woke up and saw the doors open, he took out his sword to kill himself because he thought the prisoners had escaped.
Acts 16:28 Paul shouted loudly, "Don't hurt yourself; we are all still here."
Acts 16:29 He asked for a light, jumped in, shook with fear, and knelt before Paul and Silas.
Acts 16:30 He led them out and asked, "Sirs, what should I do to be saved?"
Acts 16:31 They said, "Trust in Jesus Christ, and you and your family will be saved."
Acts 16:32 They told him and everyone in his house what God had said.
Acts 16:33 He took them at night, cleaned their wounds, and he and everyone with him were immediately baptized.
Acts 16:34 When he brought them into his home, he gave them food, and was very happy, trusting in God with everyone in his home.
Acts 16:35 When daylight came, the officers told the guards, "Release those men."
Acts 16:36 The prison guard told Paul, "The officials have sent word to release you: so now you can leave and go peacefully."
Acts 16:37 But Paul said to them, "They beat us in public without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens. They threw us in jail, and now they want to send us away secretly? No, certainly not. Let them come and take us out themselves."
Acts 16:38 The officers reported these things to the officials, and they became afraid when they learned that the men were Romans.
Acts 16:39 They came and asked them, then led them out, and asked them to leave the city.
Acts 16:40 They left the prison, went to Lydia's home, saw the other believers, cheered them up, and then left.

Acts 17:1 After they traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they arrived in Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
Acts 17:2 Paul, as he usually did, met with them and for three Saturdays discussed the scriptures with them.
Acts 17:3 Explaining and proving that Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead; and that this Jesus, who I tell you about, is the Christ.
Acts 17:4 Some believed and joined Paul and Silas, including many god-fearing Greeks and several influential women.
Acts 17:5 But the Jews who did not believe, jealous as they were, gathered some wicked men from the streets, formed a mob, started a riot in the city, attacked Jason's house, and tried to bring them out to the crowd.
Acts 17:6 When they couldn't find them, they dragged Jason and some other followers to the city authorities, shouting, "These people who have been causing trouble all over the world have now come here too."
Acts 17:7 Jason has welcomed them, and they all act against Caesar's laws, claiming there is another king named Jesus.
Acts 17:8 They upset the people and city leaders when they heard this.
Acts 17:9 After they got a promise from Jason and the other person, they released them.
Acts 17:10 The brothers quickly sent Paul and Silas away at night to the city of Berea, and when they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
Acts 17:11 They were more open-minded than the people in Thessalonica because they eagerly accepted the message and examined the scriptures every day to see if it was true.
Acts 17:12 So many people believed, including respected Greek women and quite a few men.
Acts 17:13 When the Thessalonica Jews learned that Paul was spreading God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble among the people.
Acts 17:14 Right away, the followers sent Paul to the sea, while Silas and Timothy stayed there.
Acts 17:15 The people guiding Paul took him to Athens. After telling Silas and Timothy to hurry and join him, they left.
Acts 17:16 While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he felt deeply troubled when he saw that the city was full of idol worship.
Acts 17:17 So he argued in the church with the Jews and with the religious people, and every day in the town center with those who spent time with him.
Acts 17:18 Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers met him. Some asked, "What is this chatterer trying to say?" Others said, "He seems to talk about foreign gods," because he was telling them about Jesus and the resurrection.
Acts 17:19 They took him to Areopagus and asked, "Can we find out what this new teaching you speak of is?"
Acts 17:20 You are telling us about some new and strange things, and we want to understand what they mean.
Acts 17:21 The people of Athens and the visitors there only used their time to talk about or listen to the latest news.
Acts 17:22 Paul stood in the middle of Mars Hill and said, "People of Athens, I see that you are very religious in every way."
Acts 17:23 As I walked by and saw your religious statues, I noticed one altar with the words, 'To the Unknown God.' You worship without knowing; this is the God I'm telling you about.
Acts 17:24 God, who created the world and everything in it, is the ruler of heaven and earth and does not live in buildings made by people.
Acts 17:25 God is not served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He gives life, breath, and everything to everyone.
Acts 17:26 God made all people from one family to live everywhere on earth, and set the times and limits of where they live.
Acts 17:27 They should look for God, hoping they might reach out to find him, because he is not far from any of us.
Acts 17:28 In him we exist, move, and are alive; as some of your poets have said, we are his children too.
Acts 17:29 Since we are God's children, we should not believe that God is like gold, silver, or stone, shaped by skill and human design.
Acts 17:30 In the past, God overlooked such ignorance, but now He commands everyone everywhere to change their ways.
Acts 17:31 God has set a day when he will fairly judge everyone by the man he has chosen, and he has proven this to everyone by raising him from the dead.
Acts 17:32 When they heard about the dead coming back to life, some laughed, and others said, "We will listen to you talk about this again later."
Acts 17:33 So Paul left them.
Acts 17:34 However, some men stuck with him and believed. Among them was Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

Acts 18:1 After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
Acts 18:2 They met a Jew named Aquila from Pontus, who had just arrived from Italy with his wife Priscilla. This was after Emperor Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome. They went to see them.
Acts 18:3 Because he had the same job, he stayed with them and worked, since they were all tentmakers by trade.
Acts 18:4 He discussed in the meeting place every Saturday, convincing both the Jews and the non-Jews.
Acts 18:5 When Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia, Paul was deeply moved and told the Jews that Jesus was the Messiah.
Acts 18:6 When they argued and said disrespectful things about God, he shook his clothes and told them, "Your actions are your own responsibility; I am not guilty. From now on, I will go to non-Jewish people."
Acts 18:7 He left that place and went into the house of a man named Justus, who worshiped God, and his house was right next to the synagogue.
Acts 18:8 Crispus, the main leader of the synagogue, believed in God with his whole family; and many people in Corinth, after listening, also believed and were baptized.
Acts 18:9 One night God spoke to Paul in a dream, "Don't be scared, but talk and don't stop speaking."
Acts 18:10 I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.
Acts 18:11 He stayed there one and a half years, sharing God's message with them.
Acts 18:12 When Gallio was the governor of Achaia, the Jews united against Paul and took him to the court.
Acts 18:13 He is saying, "This man is convincing people to worship God in a way that is against the law."
Acts 18:14 When Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, "If this were a case of crime or bad behavior, Jews, it would make sense for me to listen to you.
Acts 18:15 If it's about words, names, and your law, you handle it; I won't judge these things.
Acts 18:16 He forced them away from the judge's bench.
Acts 18:17 Then all the Greeks grabbed Sosthenes, the head of the synagogue, and hit him in front of the judge's bench. But Gallio did not care about any of those things.
Acts 18:18 Paul stayed there for a long time, then said goodbye to the brothers, sailed to Syria with Priscilla and Aquila, and he cut his hair at Cenchrea because of a promise.
Acts 18:19 He went to Ephesus, left them there, but went into the synagogue and talked with the Jews.
Acts 18:20 When they asked him to stay longer with them, he did not agree.
Acts 18:21 He said goodbye, telling them, "I really must celebrate this upcoming festival in Jerusalem: but I plan to come back to you, if God allows." Then he left from Ephesus.
Acts 18:22 When he arrived at Caesarea, after going up to greet the church, he went down to Antioch.
Acts 18:23 After staying there for a while, he left and traveled through the regions of Galatia and Phrygia, encouraging all the followers.
Acts 18:24 A Jewish man named Apollos, from Alexandria, who was an excellent speaker and very knowledgeable in the scriptures, went to Ephesus.
Acts 18:25 This man learned about God's way; he was passionate, and he talked and taught about God's teachings with care, knowing only John's baptism.
Acts 18:26 He started to speak confidently in the synagogue. When Aquila and Priscilla heard him, they welcomed him and explained God's way to him more clearly.
Acts 18:27 When he wanted to go to Achaia, the believers sent letters asking the followers there to welcome him. When he arrived, he helped those who through God's kindness had believed a lot.
Acts 18:28 He strongly persuaded the Jews in public, using the scriptures to show that Jesus was the Messiah.

Acts 19:1 While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland areas and arrived in Ephesus, where he met some disciples.
Acts 19:2 He asked them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit after you believed?" They replied, "We haven't even heard if there is a Holy Spirit."
Acts 19:3 He asked them, "Then what baptism did you receive?" They replied, "John's baptism."
Acts 19:4 Paul said, John truly baptized with a baptism to show repentance, telling the people to believe in the one coming after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.
Acts 19:5 When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of Jesus.
Acts 19:6 When Paul put his hands on them, God's Spirit came upon them; they spoke in different languages and gave God's messages.
Acts 19:7 There were about twelve men in total.
Acts 19:8 He went to the meeting place and spoke confidently for three months, discussing and convincing people about God's kingdom.
Acts 19:9 But when some people became stubborn and did not believe, and talked badly about the faith in front of many, he left them, took the believers aside, and discussed with them every day in the school of Tyrannus.
Acts 19:10 This went on for two years, so that everyone living in Asia heard the message of Lord Jesus, including Jews and Greeks.
Acts 19:11 God did amazing miracles through Paul.
Acts 19:12 People took cloths and aprons from his body to the ill, and their sicknesses left them, and the bad spirits came out.
Acts 19:13 Some wandering Jewish people who cast out demons tried to use the name of Jesus that Paul talks about, saying to the evil spirits, "We command you by Jesus to come out."
Acts 19:14 There were seven sons of a Jewish man named Sceva, a high priest, who did the same.
Acts 19:15 The evil spirit spoke back, "I know Jesus and I know Paul; but who are you?"
Acts 19:16 The man with the evil spirit jumped on them, beat them, and was too strong for them, so they ran away from the house naked and hurt.
Acts 19:17 Everyone in Ephesus, both Jews and Greeks, learned about this; they all became afraid, and they praised the name of Jesus greatly.
Acts 19:18 Many who believed came, admitted their actions, and showed what they had done.
Acts 19:19 Many people who practiced magic collected their books and burned them in front of everyone. They added up the value of the books and it was fifty thousand silver coins.
Acts 19:20 God's message spread powerfully and won.
Acts 19:21 After finishing these tasks, Paul decided to travel through Macedonia and Achaia and then go to Jerusalem. He said, "After visiting there, I must go to Rome too."
Acts 19:22 So he sent two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed in Asia for a while.
Acts 19:23 At that time, there was quite a commotion about that way.
Acts 19:24 A man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver temples for Diana, earned a lot of money for the craftsmen.
Acts 19:25 He gathered the craftsmen of the same trade and said, "Friends, you know that we earn our living from this skill."
Acts 19:26 You see and hear that not only in Ephesus but also across Asia, this Paul has convinced and led many people away by saying that handmade things are not gods.
Acts 19:27 So, our work is at risk of being ignored; and the temple of the great goddess Diana may be looked down on, and her grandness ruined, which all Asia and the world worships.
Acts 19:28 When they heard this, they became very angry and started shouting, "Diana of the Ephesians is great!"
Acts 19:29 The whole city was confused, and they grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians and Paul's travel friends, and all together they ran to the theater.
Acts 19:30 When Paul wanted to meet with the people, the disciples did not allow him.
Acts 19:31 Some of the Asian leaders who were his friends sent him a message, asking him not to risk going into the theater.
Acts 19:32 So some in the crowd shouted one thing, some another. The group was mixed up, and most didn't know why they had gathered.
Acts 19:33 They pulled Alexander from the crowd, the Jews pushing him to the front. Alexander waved his hand, wanting to explain himself to the people.
Acts 19:34 When they realized he was a Jew, everyone shouted together for about two hours, "Diana of the Ephesians is great!"
Acts 19:35 When the city clerk made the crowd quiet, he said, "People of Ephesus, everyone knows that our city worships the great goddess Diana and the statue that came down from the god Jupiter."
Acts 19:36 Since these facts are undeniable, you should stay calm and not act hastily.
Acts 19:37 You have brought these men here who have not stolen from churches or spoken against your goddess.
Acts 19:38 If Demetrius and the other workers have a complaint against someone, they can go to court, where the officials are: they should argue their case there.
Acts 19:39 If you ask about other issues, a legal meeting will decide them.
Acts 19:40 We are at risk of being questioned about today's chaos, as there is no reason to explain this crowd.
Acts 19:41 After saying this, he sent the people away.

Acts 20:1 After the disturbance stopped, Paul gathered the disciples, hugged them, and left to go to Macedonia.
Acts 20:2 After he traveled through those areas and encouraged the people a lot, he went to Greece.
Acts 20:3 He stayed there three months. When the Jews planned to catch him as he prepared to sail to Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.
Acts 20:4 Going with him to Asia were Sopater from Berea; from Thessalonica, Aristarchus and Secundus; Gaius from Derbe; Timothy; and from Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
Acts 20:5 Those who went ahead waited for us in Troas.
Acts 20:6 We left Philippi after the Festival of Unleavened Bread and reached Troas in five days, where we stayed for seven days.
Acts 20:7 On the first day of the week, when the followers met to share a meal, Paul spoke to them, planning to leave the next day. He kept talking until midnight.
Acts 20:8 There were many lamps in the upstairs room where they met.
Acts 20:9 A young man named Eutychus was sitting in a window and fell into a deep sleep while Paul was speaking for a long time. He fell asleep, dropped from the third story, and was picked up dead.
Acts 20:10 Paul went down, hugged him, and said, "Don't worry; he's still alive."
Acts 20:11 After he returned, shared food, ate, and talked for many hours until morning, he left.
Acts 20:12 They brought the young man back alive, and they were very comforted.
Acts 20:13 We went ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos to pick up Paul, as he had planned to join us there on foot.
Acts 20:14 When he joined us at Assos, we brought him aboard and sailed to Mitylene.
Acts 20:15 We sailed from there and reached Chios the next day; the following day we went to Samos and stopped at Trogyllium, and the day after, we arrived at Miletus.
Acts 20:16 Paul decided to pass by Ephesus because he did not want to stay in Asia. He hurried to try to be in Jerusalem for Pentecost.
Acts 20:17 From Miletus, he sent a message to Ephesus and invited the church leaders.
Acts 20:18 When they arrived, he told them, "You are aware, from the first day I arrived in Asia, how I have always acted with you."
Acts 20:19 Serving God with complete humility, and with many tears and trials that happened to me because of the Jews' secret plots.
Acts 20:20 I held back nothing useful for you, but showed and taught you openly and in homes.
Acts 20:21 Telling Jews and Greeks to turn to God and believe in our Lord Jesus Christ.
Acts 20:22 And now, I go to Jerusalem, tied by the spirit, not knowing what will happen to me there.
Acts 20:23 The Holy Spirit warns me in every city that chains and troubles are waiting for me.
Acts 20:24 These things do not bother me, and I do not consider my life important to myself, so I can complete my work happily, and the service I received from Lord Jesus, to share the good news of God's kindness.
Acts 20:25 Now I know that all of you, whom I have taught about God's kingdom, will not see me again.
Acts 20:26 Today, I tell you that I am innocent of harming anyone.
Acts 20:27 I have not avoided telling you everything God wants you to know.
Acts 20:28 Be careful to look after yourselves and everyone in your group, because the Holy Spirit has made you leaders to care for God's church that he bought with his blood.
Acts 20:29 I know that after I leave, fierce wolves will come among you and not be kind to the sheep.
Acts 20:30 From among you, some will come, saying wrong things to lead followers to themselves.
Acts 20:31 So be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you, day and night, with tears.
Acts 20:32 Now, friends, I entrust you to God and to his kind message, which can strengthen you and provide you with a share among all who are made holy.
Acts 20:33 I have not desired anyone's money, gold, or clothes.
Acts 20:34 Yes, you know that these hands have worked for my needs and for those with me.
Acts 20:35 I have shown you in every way, by working hard you must help the weak and remember what Jesus said, "It is better to give than to get."
Acts 20:36 After saying this, he knelt down and prayed with everyone.
Acts 20:37 They all cried hard, hugged Paul, and kissed him.
Acts 20:38 They were very sad because he said they would never see him again. And they went with him to the boat.

Acts 21:1 After we had left them and set sail, we went straight to Kos, then the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
Acts 21:2 We found a ship going to Phoenicia, boarded it, and set sail.
Acts 21:3 After we saw Cyprus, we passed it on our left, sailed to Syria, and arrived at Tyre, where the ship was supposed to unload its cargo.
Acts 21:4 We met followers and stayed there seven days. They told Paul by the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
Acts 21:5 After we finished those days, we left and went on our journey; everyone came with us, including wives and children, until we were outside the city; then we knelt on the beach and prayed.
Acts 21:6 After we said goodbye, we boarded a ship and they went back home.
Acts 21:7 After we sailed from Tyre, we arrived in Ptolemais, greeted the believers, and stayed with them for one day.
Acts 21:8 The next day, we who were with Paul left and went to Caesarea. We went to the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.
Acts 21:9 The man had four daughters who were virgins and could prophesy.
Acts 21:10 While we stayed there for several days, a prophet named Agabus came to us from Judea.
Acts 21:11 When he arrived, he took Paul's belt, tied his own hands and feet, and said, "The Holy Spirit says, 'This is how the Jews in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt and hand him over to non-Jewish people.'"
Acts 21:12 When we heard this, we and the local people begged him not to go to Jerusalem.
Acts 21:13 Paul replied, "Why are you crying and making me so sad? I am willing to be arrested and even die in Jerusalem for Jesus."
Acts 21:14 When he wouldn't change his mind, we stopped and said, "Let God's will be done."
Acts 21:15 After that time, we packed our belongings and went to Jerusalem.
Acts 21:16 Some disciples from Caesarea went with us, and they brought Mnason from Cyprus, an early follower, to stay with.
Acts 21:17 When we arrived in Jerusalem, the fellow believers welcomed us happily.
Acts 21:18 The next day, Paul went with us to see James, and all the leaders were there.
Acts 21:19 After greeting them, he explained in detail what God had done among the non-Jews through his work.
Acts 21:20 When they heard this, they praised God and said to him, "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews believe, and they are all very devoted to the law."
Acts 21:21 They have been told that you teach all the Jews living among non-Jews to abandon Moses's teachings by saying they shouldn't circumcise their kids or follow Jewish traditions.
Acts 21:22 So what should we do? A lot of people will gather because they will hear you have come.
Acts 21:23 Do what we tell you: We have four men who have made a promise.
Acts 21:24 Join them, make yourself pure with them, and help pay for their expenses, so they can cut their hair. Then everyone will know that what they heard about you is not true, and that you also live by the law and keep it.
Acts 21:25 Regarding the non-Jewish believers, we have decided they do not have to follow such rules, except they should avoid food given to idols, blood, animals not properly killed, and sexual immorality.
Acts 21:26 Paul went with the men and the following day, they all purified themselves and went into the temple. There, they showed that the days of purification were finished and waited until a sacrifice was made for each of them.
Acts 21:27 When the seven days were almost over, the Asian Jews saw him in the temple, they upset everyone, and grabbed him.
Acts 21:28 Calling out, Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people, the law, and this place. He has also brought Greeks into the temple, making this holy place unclean.
Acts 21:29 They had earlier seen Trophimus from Ephesus with Paul in the city and thought Paul had taken him into the temple.
Acts 21:30 The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and immediately the doors were closed.
Acts 21:31 As they were trying to kill him, news reached the commander of the soldiers that the whole city of Jerusalem was in chaos.
Acts 21:32 He quickly got some soldiers and officers and ran to them. When they saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped hitting Paul.
Acts 21:33 The commander came close, took him, and ordered him to be tied up with two chains; then he asked who he was and what he had done.
Acts 21:34 Different people in the crowd were shouting different things, and because of the noise, he couldn't understand what was happening, so he ordered the man to be taken into the fort.
Acts 21:35 When he reached the stairs, the soldiers carried him because of the crowd's violence.
