Acts 21:36 Many people followed, shouting, "Take him away!"
Acts 21:37 As Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, "May I talk to you?" The commander replied, "You know Greek?"
Acts 21:38 Aren't you the Egyptian who recently caused a commotion and led four thousand murderers into the desert?
Acts 21:39 But Paul said, "I am a Jewish man from Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, and I am from an important city. Please let me speak to the people."
Acts 21:40 After getting permission, Paul stood on the steps and signaled to the people with his hand. When everyone was quiet, he spoke to them in Hebrew, saying,

Acts 22:1 Friends and fathers, listen to my defense that I am presenting to you now.
Acts 22:2 When they heard he was speaking Hebrew to them, they became even quieter, and he said,
Acts 22:3 I am truly a man who is a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, but raised in this city, taught by Gamaliel in the full way of our ancestors' law, and very devoted to God, just like all of you today.
Acts 22:4 I persecuted followers of this way to death, arresting and jailing both men and women.
Acts 22:5 The high priest and all the leaders can confirm this. They gave me letters for the believers, and I went to Damascus to arrest those there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
Acts 22:6 As I was traveling and getting close to Damascus around midday, suddenly a bright light from the sky shone all around me.
Acts 22:7 I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
Acts 22:8 I asked, "Who are you, God?" And he told me, "I am Jesus of Nazareth, the one you are persecuting."
Acts 22:9 Those with me saw the light and were scared, but they didn't hear the voice that spoke to me.
Acts 22:10 I asked, "What should I do, God?" And God told me, "Get up and go to Damascus, and there you will be told about everything you are meant to do."
Acts 22:11 When the bright light made me blind, those with me guided me by hand into Damascus.
Acts 22:12 A man named Ananias, who was religious and respected the law, was well spoken of by all the Jewish people living there.
Acts 22:13 He came to me, stood by me, and said, "Brother Saul, you can see now!" Right away, I could see him.
Acts 22:14 He said, "The God of our ancestors has picked you to know His will, see the Righteous One, and hear what He says."
Acts 22:15 You will tell everyone what you have seen and heard as his witness.
Acts 22:16 Why are you waiting? Get up, be baptized, and clean away your sins by calling on God's name.
Acts 22:17 When I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance.
Acts 22:18 I saw him telling me, "Hurry and leave Jerusalem quickly because they won't accept your testimony about me."
Acts 22:19 I said, God, they know I locked up and hit those in every synagogue who believed in you.
Acts 22:20 When Stephen, who was killed for his faith, bled, I was there too, agreeing to his death and watching over the clothes of those who killed him.
Acts 22:21 He said to me, "Go away, because I will send you far off to the non-Jewish people."
Acts 22:22 They listened to him until he said this, then they shouted, "Get rid of him! He should not be allowed to live."
Acts 22:23 As they shouted, they took off their clothes and threw dust into the air.
Acts 22:24 The commander ordered that he be taken into the fort and told them to find out why people were shouting against him by whipping him.
Acts 22:25 As they tied Paul with straps, he asked the officer standing nearby, "Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen who has not been found guilty?"
Acts 22:26 When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, "Be careful what you do, because this man is a Roman."
Acts 22:27 The commanding officer approached and asked him, "Are you a Roman citizen?" He answered, "Yes."
Acts 22:28 The commander said, "I paid a lot to become free." Paul replied, "But I was born free."
Acts 22:29 As soon as they realized he was a Roman citizen, those who were about to interrogate him backed off. The commander was also scared because he had tied him up.
Acts 22:30 The next day, wanting to understand exactly why he was accused by the Jews, he released him from his shackles, ordered the high priests and their whole council to meet, took Paul down, and placed him in front of them.

Acts 23:1 Paul looked intently at the council and said, "Friends, I have lived with a clear conscience before God up to today."
Acts 23:2 The high priest Ananias ordered those standing nearby to hit him on the mouth.
Acts 23:3 Paul said to him, "God will strike you, you painted wall. Do you sit to judge me by the law, yet you order me to be hit against the law?"
Acts 23:4 The bystanders asked, "Are you insulting God's chief priest?"
Acts 23:5 Paul said, "Brothers, I didn't know he was the high priest; because it's said, 'You must not say bad things about the leader of your people.'"
Acts 23:6 But when Paul realized that some were Sadducees and some Pharisees, he shouted in the meeting, "Friends, I am a Pharisee, born from Pharisees. I am on trial because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead."
Acts 23:7 After he said this, a disagreement started between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the crowd split up.
Acts 23:8 The Sadducees believe there is no resurrection, angels, or spirits, but the Pharisees believe in all of these.
Acts 23:9 A loud shout went up, and the Pharisees' legal experts stood, arguing, "We find nothing wrong with this man. If a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, we shouldn't oppose God."
Acts 23:10 When a big argument started, the commander, worried Paul might be torn apart by the crowd, ordered the soldiers to go down, forcefully take him from the people, and bring him into the fortress.
Acts 23:11 The next night, God stood by him and said, "Cheer up, Paul. Just as you told people about me in Jerusalem, you must also speak about me in Rome."
Acts 23:12 When daylight came, some Jews made a pact, swearing not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
Acts 23:13 Over forty people were involved in this plan.
Acts 23:14 They went to the religious leaders and said, "We have made a serious promise not to eat anything until we have killed Paul."
Acts 23:15 So now, tell the commander with the council to bring him to you tomorrow, pretending you want to ask him more questions. And before he gets there, we will be ready to kill him.
Acts 23:16 When Paul's nephew found out about the ambush, he went into the fort and told Paul.
Acts 23:17 Paul called one of the officers over and said, "Take this young man to the commander; he has something important to tell him."
Acts 23:18 He took him and brought him to the commander, saying, "Paul the prisoner asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you."
Acts 23:19 The leader took his hand, led him to a quiet place, and asked, "What do you need to tell me?"
Acts 23:20 He said, "The Jews want to ask you to bring Paul to the council tomorrow, as if they will ask him more questions."
Acts 23:21 But don't give in to them. Over forty men are hiding, ready to kill him. They took an oath not to eat or drink until they do. Now they're waiting for your word.
Acts 23:22 So the commander let the young man go and ordered him, "Don't tell anyone that you have told me this."
Acts 23:23 He called two army commanders and said, "Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horse riders, and two hundred spearmen to leave for Caesarea at three o'clock in the morning."
Acts 23:24 Give them animals to put Paul on, to take him safely to Governor Felix.
Acts 23:25 He wrote a letter like this:
Acts 23:26 Claudius Lysias sends greetings to the honored governor Felix.
Acts 23:27 The Jews had seized this man and were about to kill him when I came with soldiers and saved him because I learned he was a Roman.
Acts 23:28 I brought him to their meeting to understand why they were accusing him.
Acts 23:29 I saw he was accused about their law issues, but nothing was charged against him deserving death or prison.
Acts 23:30 When I heard that the Jews were planning to ambush the man, I immediately sent him to you and ordered his accusers to present their case against him to you. Goodbye.
Acts 23:31 The soldiers followed orders, took Paul, and moved him at night to Antipatris.
Acts 23:32 The next day they let the horsemen go with him and went back to the fort.
Acts 23:33 When they got to Caesarea and gave the letter to the governor, they also brought Paul before him.
Acts 23:34 After the governor read the letter, he asked which area he was from. When he learned that it was Cilicia;
Acts 23:35 I will listen to you, he said, when your accusers arrive. And he ordered him to be held in Herod's court.

Acts 24:1 Five days later, the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a speaker named Tertullus, who accused Paul to the governor.
Acts 24:2 When he was brought out, Tertullus started to accuse him, saying, "Because of you we have much peace, and good things are done for our nation by your care."
Acts 24:3 We always accept it everywhere, most respected Felix, with great thanks.
Acts 24:4 But so I don't bother you too much, I ask you kindly to listen to us for just a moment.
Acts 24:5 We have found this man to be a troublemaker, stirring up rebellion among Jews everywhere, and the leader of the Nazarene group.
Acts 24:6 He also tried to disrespect the temple; we caught him and wanted to judge him by our law.
Acts 24:7 The commander Lysias came and with strong force took him from us.
Acts 24:8 Telling his accusers to appear before you, so you can find out about all the things we are accusing him of by questioning him yourself.
Acts 24:9 The Jews agreed, saying that this was true.
Acts 24:10 Then Paul, when the governor signaled him to speak, replied, "Knowing that you have been a judge for this nation for many years, I happily defend myself."
Acts 24:11 I want you to understand that I went up to Jerusalem to worship only twelve days ago.
Acts 24:12 They did not find me arguing with anyone at the temple, or stirring up the crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city.
Acts 24:13 They cannot show proof of what they accuse me of now.
Acts 24:14 I admit to you that I worship the God of my ancestors in the way they call heresy, believing in everything written in the law and the prophets.
Acts 24:15 Have hope in God, as they do, that the dead will rise, both good and bad people.
Acts 24:16 I always try to keep a clear conscience before God and everyone.
Acts 24:17 After many years, I came to bring help and gifts to my people.
Acts 24:18 Some Jews from Asia saw me clean in the temple, without a crowd or commotion.
Acts 24:19 They should have been here to accuse me in front of you, if they had any charge against me.
Acts 24:20 Or let these people here tell if they found any wrong in me when I was before the council.
Acts 24:21 I am on trial before you today just because I said, while standing among them, that the dead are raised.
Acts 24:22 When Felix heard this, knowing more about the way, he postponed the decision, saying, "When Captain Lysias comes, I will fully examine your case."
Acts 24:23 He ordered a captain to guard Paul, allow him freedom, and let his friends visit and help him.
Acts 24:24 After some time, Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, arrived. He called for Paul to listen to him talk about faith in Christ.
Acts 24:25 As he talked about being right, self-control, and the future judgment, Felix became scared and said, "Leave now; when I find the right time, I will send for you."
Acts 24:26 He also hoped that Paul would give him money to release him, so he sent for him more often and talked with him.
Acts 24:27 Two years later, Porcius Festus replaced Felix. Felix, wanting to please the Jews, kept Paul in chains.

Acts 25:1 When Festus arrived in the area, three days later he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
Acts 25:2 The high priest and the Jewish leaders told him about Paul and asked him.
Acts 25:3 They asked for a favor against him, wanting him to be brought to Jerusalem, planning to ambush and kill him on the way.
Acts 25:4 Festus replied that Paul should stay in Caesarea and that he would go there soon.
Acts 25:5 So he said, "Those of you who can, come with me and accuse this man if he has done anything wrong."
Acts 25:6 After staying with them for over ten days, he went to Caesarea; the following day, he sat on the judge's bench and ordered that Paul be brought in.
Acts 25:7 When he arrived, the Jews from Jerusalem gathered around him and made many serious accusations against Paul that they could not prove.
Acts 25:8 While speaking for myself, I have done nothing wrong against the Jewish law, the temple, or the ruler.
Acts 25:9 But Festus, wanting to please the Jews, replied to Paul, "Do you want to go to Jerusalem and be judged for these matters there with me present?"
Acts 25:10 Paul said, "I am standing before Caesar's court, where I should be judged. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, and you know this very well."
Acts 25:11 If I have done something wrong that deserves death, I'm not afraid to die. But if I'm not guilty of what they accuse me of, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I want to go to Caesar.
Acts 25:12 Then Festus, after talking with his advisors, said, "Have you asked to go to Caesar? To Caesar you will go."
Acts 25:13 After some time, King Agrippa and Bernice went to Caesarea to greet Festus.
Acts 25:14 After spending several days there, Festus explained Paul's situation to the king, saying, "Felix left a man in jail."
Acts 25:15 In Jerusalem, the Jewish leaders and chief priests told me about him, wanting him to be judged.
Acts 25:16 I replied, "Romans do not hand over anyone to death without letting the accused meet the accusers and defend themselves against the charges."
Acts 25:17 So, when they arrived here, I wasted no time the next day and sat on the judge's bench, and ordered the man to be brought in.
Acts 25:18 When the accusers stood up against him, they did not bring any charges like I thought they would.
Acts 25:19 They had some issues with their own beliefs and about Jesus who had died, but Paul claimed he was alive.
Acts 25:20 Since I was unsure about such issues, I asked him if he wanted to go to Jerusalem and be judged there on these matters.
Acts 25:21 When Paul asked to wait for a trial before Augustus, I ordered him to be held until I could send him to Caesar.
Acts 25:22 Agrippa said to Festus, "I also want to hear the man myself." "Tomorrow," he said, "you will hear him."
Acts 25:23 The next day, Agrippa and Bernice arrived with much show. They went into the hearing room with the top officers and leading men of the city. At Festus' order, Paul was brought in.
Acts 25:24 Festus said, "King Agrippa, and everyone here with us, look at this man. All the Jewish people have come to me about him, in Jerusalem and here too, shouting that he should not live anymore."
Acts 25:25 When I discovered he did nothing deserving death and he has asked to go to Augustus, I decided to send him.
Acts 25:26 I have nothing specific to report to you about him. So I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after we question him, I can have something to write.
Acts 25:27 To me, it seems unfair to send a prisoner without stating the charges against him.

Acts 26:1 Then Agrippa told Paul, "You may now speak for yourself." So Paul reached out his hand and began to explain his side.
Acts 26:2 I am happy, King Agrippa, because today I get to explain to you everything the Jews accuse me of.
Acts 26:3 I know you're skilled in all Jewish customs and issues, so I ask you to listen to me patiently.
Acts 26:4 Since I was young, I have lived in my own country, in Jerusalem, and all the Jews know how I have lived.
Acts 26:5 Those who have known me for a long time would say that I strictly followed our religion's rules as a Pharisee.
Acts 26:6 I am here on trial because of the hope in the promise God made to our ancestors.
Acts 26:7 Our twelve tribes hope to receive what God promised, as they serve God constantly, day and night. For this hope, King Agrippa, I am being accused by the Jews.
Acts 26:8 Why is it hard for you to believe that God can bring the dead back to life?
Acts 26:9 I truly believed that I should do many things against Jesus of Nazareth.
Acts 26:10 I also did this in Jerusalem: I locked up many of God's holy people in prison, with the chief priests' permission; and when they were killed, I was against them.
Acts 26:11 I often punished them in every synagogue and forced them to speak against God; I was very angry with them and chased them even to foreign cities.
Acts 26:12 While I was going to Damascus with the chief priests' permission and orders,
Acts 26:13 At noon, O king, I saw a light from the sky brighter than the sun shining all around me and those traveling with me.
Acts 26:14 When we all fell to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in Hebrew, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It's hard for you to fight against what's right."
Acts 26:15 And I asked, "Who are you, God?" And he replied, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting."
Acts 26:16 Stand up and stay on your feet. I have shown myself to you to appoint you as a servant and a witness of what you have seen and what I will show you.
Acts 26:17 Saving you from the people and from the non-Jews, to whom I now send you.
Acts 26:18 To make them see, and to change them from darkness to light, and from Satan's control to God, so they can have their sins forgiven and share in the blessings with those made holy by trusting in me.
Acts 26:19 So, King Agrippa, I followed the vision from heaven.
Acts 26:20 God first revealed himself to the people of Damascus, then in Jerusalem, all over Judaea, and to non-Jewish people, telling them to change their ways, turn to God, and do things that show they are sorry for their sins.
Acts 26:21 For these reasons, the Jews grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
Acts 26:22 So, with God's help I am still here today, telling everyone, both important and not, only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
Acts 26:23 Christ had to suffer, be the first to rise from the dead, and bring light to the people and the non-Jews.
Acts 26:24 As he defended himself, Festus shouted, "Paul, you're out of your mind; your great learning is driving you insane."
Acts 26:25 He replied, "I am not crazy, respected Festus; I am speaking words of truth and seriousness."
Acts 26:26 The king knows about these things, and I can speak openly to him: I am sure he is aware of them, because this was not done secretly.
Acts 26:27 King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.
Acts 26:28 Agrippa said to Paul, "You almost convince me to become a Christian."
Acts 26:29 Paul said, "I wish to God that not only you but also everyone listening today could be almost exactly like me, except for being in chains."
Acts 26:30 After he said this, the king stood up, along with the governor and Bernice, and everyone sitting with them.
Acts 26:31 After they left, they said to each other, "This man hasn't done anything to deserve death or imprisonment."
Acts 26:32 Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been freed if he had not asked to go to Caesar."

Acts 27:1 When it was decided that we would sail to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a man named Julius, who was a captain in Augustus' army.
Acts 27:2 We got on a boat from Adramyttium and set sail to pass by the coasts of Asia, with a man named Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia joining us.
Acts 27:3 The next day we arrived at Sidon. Julius kindly treated Paul and allowed him to visit his friends to rest.
Acts 27:4 After we left there, we sailed near Cyprus because the winds were against us.
Acts 27:5 After crossing the sea near Cilicia and Pamphylia, we arrived at Myra, a city in Lycia.
Acts 27:6 The officer found a ship from Alexandria going to Italy and put us on it.
Acts 27:7 After sailing slowly for many days and barely passing Cnidus because the wind was against us, we sailed below Crete, near Salmone.
Acts 27:8 After barely getting past it, they reached a place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
Acts 27:9 After a lot of time had passed, and sailing had become risky because the time of fasting was over, Paul warned them.
Acts 27:10 He said to them, "Friends, I see that this trip will bring harm and much loss, not just to the cargo and the ship, but to our lives too."
Acts 27:11 The officer trusted the ship's captain and owner more than what Paul said.
Acts 27:12 Since the harbor wasn't good for staying the winter, most people suggested leaving to try to reach Phoenix and spend the winter there; it's a harbor on Crete, facing southwest and northwest.
Acts 27:13 When the south wind gently blew, thinking they had achieved their goal, they left and sailed near Crete.
Acts 27:14 Soon after, a strong storm called Euroclydon came up against it.
Acts 27:15 When the ship was trapped and couldn't sail into the wind, we let it go wherever it was pushed.
Acts 27:16 Sailing close to an island named Clauda, we worked hard to secure the lifeboat.
Acts 27:17 After they lifted it, they supported the ship with ropes. Worried about hitting the sandbanks, they lowered the sails and let the wind carry them.
Acts 27:18 We were greatly shaken by a storm, so the next day they threw cargo overboard to lighten the ship.
Acts 27:19 On the third day, we threw the ship's equipment overboard with our own hands.
Acts 27:20 When the sun and stars did not show for many days and a big storm was upon us, we lost all hope of being saved.
Acts 27:21 But after not eating for a long time, Paul stood up among them and said, "Friends, you should have listened to me and not left Crete, then we could have avoided this trouble and loss."
Acts 27:22 I encourage you to stay positive because no one will lose their life, only the ship will be lost.
Acts 27:23 Last night, God's angel, who I belong to and serve, stood by me.
Acts 27:24 "God says, 'Don't be afraid, Paul. You will be taken to Caesar, and God has granted the safety of everyone sailing with you.'"
Acts 27:25 So, friends, cheer up: for I trust God, that it will happen just as I was told.
Acts 27:26 We have to land on a certain island.
Acts 27:27 On the fourteenth night, as we were still being tossed around in the sea near Adria, around midnight the sailors thought we were getting close to land.
Acts 27:28 They measured and found it was twenty fathoms deep. After going a bit further, they measured again and it was fifteen fathoms deep.
Acts 27:29 Afraid we might hit rocks, they threw four anchors from the back of the ship and hoped for daylight.
Acts 27:30 As the sailors were trying to escape from the ship by lowering the lifeboat into the sea, pretending they were going to drop anchors from the front of the ship,
Acts 27:31 Paul told the officer and soldiers, "If these men don't stay on the ship, you won't be saved."
Acts 27:32 Then the soldiers cut the ropes of the boat and let it drift away.
Acts 27:33 As the day began, Paul urged everyone to eat, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day you've waited and fasted without eating anything."
Acts 27:34 So I ask you to eat some food, because it is good for you. Not even a single hair from your heads will be lost.
Acts 27:35 After saying this, he took some bread, thanked God in front of everyone, broke it, and started to eat.
Acts 27:36 Then they all felt encouraged and ate some food.
Acts 27:37 There were 276 of us on the ship.
Acts 27:38 After they ate enough, they made the ship lighter by throwing the wheat into the sea.
Acts 27:39 When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they saw a bay with a beach and decided to try to drive the ship onto it if they could.
Acts 27:40 After they lifted the anchors, they let themselves go on the sea, released the steering ropes, raised the main sail to catch the wind, and headed for the shore.
Acts 27:41 They crashed the ship where two seas came together; the front stuck firm and wouldn't move, while the back part broke from the strong waves.
Acts 27:42 The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to prevent any from swimming away and escaping.
Acts 27:43 The officer, wanting to save Paul, stopped them from their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump into the sea and go to shore first.
Acts 27:44 The others held onto planks or pieces of the ship, and this way, everyone safely reached shore.

Acts 28:1 After they were safe, they learned that the island's name was Melita.
Acts 28:2 The local people were very kind to us. They made a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
Acts 28:3 When Paul collected some sticks and put them on the fire, a snake came out from the warmth and bit his hand.
Acts 28:4 When the local people saw the poisonous snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, "Surely this man is a killer. Even though he survived the sea, justice will not let him live."
Acts 28:5 He threw the snake into the fire and was not hurt.
Acts 28:6 They expected him to swell up or suddenly drop dead, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
Acts 28:7 In that area, the island's leader, named Publius, owned land. He welcomed us and kindly let us stay for three days.
Acts 28:8 Publius's father was sick with a fever and severe diarrhea. Paul went to him, prayed, put his hands on him, and healed him.
Acts 28:9 After this happened, more people on the island who were sick came and were healed.
Acts 28:10 They also showed us much respect and gave us what we needed when we left.
Acts 28:11 After three months, we left on a ship from Alexandria that had spent the winter on the island, marked with the symbols Castor and Pollux.
Acts 28:12 We landed at Syracuse and stayed there for three days.
Acts 28:13 From there we circled around and reached Rhegium. After one day, a south wind started blowing, and the next day we arrived at Puteoli.
Acts 28:14 We met fellow believers who asked us to stay with them for seven days; then we continued on to Rome.
Acts 28:15 From there, when the believers heard about us, they came to meet us all the way to the Market of Appius and the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and felt encouraged.
Acts 28:16 When we arrived in Rome, the centurion handed the prisoners over to the guard's commander, but Paul was allowed to live alone with a soldier guarding him.
Acts 28:17 After three days, Paul gathered the Jewish leaders. Once they assembled, he told them, "Friends, although I did nothing against our people or our ancestors' ways, I was still handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem to the Romans."
Acts 28:18 After they questioned me, they wanted to release me because they found no reason to kill me.
Acts 28:19 But when the Jews spoke against me, I had to ask for Caesar's judgment; not because I had any charges against my people.
Acts 28:20 I called for you so I could see and talk with you, because I am chained up due to the hope of Israel.
Acts 28:21 They told him, "We haven't gotten any letters from Judea about you, and none of our friends who have come here have spoken or said anything bad about you."
Acts 28:22 We want to hear what you think, because people everywhere speak against this group.
Acts 28:23 When they set a day, many came to his place. He explained the kingdom of God to them, convincing them about Jesus using the laws of Moses and the prophets, all day long.
Acts 28:24 Some believed what was said, and some did not believe.
Acts 28:25 When they could not agree, they left after Paul said, "The Holy Spirit was right to speak to our ancestors through the prophet Isaiah."
Acts 28:26 Go to these people and tell them, "Though you listen, you will not understand; though you look, you will not really see."
Acts 28:27 The hearts of these people have become hard, their ears are hard to hear, and they have shut their eyes. Otherwise, they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn to me, and be healed by me.
Acts 28:28 Know this: God's salvation is sent to the non-Jews, and they will listen to it.
Acts 28:29 After he said this, the Jews left and had intense discussions with each other.
Acts 28:30 Paul lived for two full years in a house he rented, and he welcomed everyone who visited him.
Acts 28:31 Teaching about God's kingdom and explaining things about the Lord Jesus Christ with full confidence, and no one stopping him.

Romans 1:1 Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, chosen to be an apostle, set apart for the good news of God,
Romans 1:2 He promised this before through his prophets in the holy writings.
Romans 1:3 About his son Jesus Christ our Lord, who was born from David's descendants in the flesh;
Romans 1:4 Shown to be God's Son with power, by being raised from the dead, according to the spirit of holiness.
Romans 1:5 Through him, we received kindness and the task to bring people from all countries to follow the faith, all for his honor.
Romans 1:6 You are also called to belong to Jesus Christ.
Romans 1:7 To everyone in Rome loved by God and called to be holy: May you have kindness and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ.
Romans 1:8 First, I thank God through Jesus Christ for all of you because people around the world are talking about your faith.
Romans 1:9 God is my witness, whom I serve with my heart in telling the good news about his Son, that I always mention you in my prayers without stopping.
Romans 1:10 Asking if maybe now at last I could have a successful trip, if God is willing, to visit you.
Romans 1:11 I really want to see you, so I can give you a spiritual gift to help strengthen your faith.
Romans 1:12 I want us to be encouraged by the faith we share.
Romans 1:13 I don't want you to be unaware, friends, that I have often planned to visit you, but was prevented until now, so that I could have some success with you, just as I have had with other non-Jews.
Romans 1:14 I owe something to both Greeks and non-Greeks, to the educated and the uneducated.
Romans 1:15 I am ready to share the good news with you in Rome, as much as I can.
Romans 1:16 I am not embarrassed about the good news of Christ because it is God's power to save everyone who believes, first the Jew and also the Greek.
Romans 1:17 In it, God's goodness is shown, starting with faith and leading to more faith: it's said, people who are fair will have life through faith.
Romans 1:18 God's anger comes from heaven against all the badness and wrongs of people who live against the truth.
Romans 1:19 What can be known about God is clear to them, because God has shown it to them.
Romans 1:20 God's invisible qualities have been clearly seen since the world was created, understood through what has been made, including his eternal power and nature, leaving no one with an excuse.
Romans 1:21 Even though they knew God, they did not honor him as God or give thanks. Instead, they thought up useless ideas, and their senseless minds became dark.
Romans 1:22 Claiming to be smart, they turned into fools.
Romans 1:23 They turned the honor of the eternal God into pictures of humans, birds, animals, and reptiles.
Romans 1:24 So God let them follow their hearts' desires, which led to impurity and dishonoring their own bodies with each other.
Romans 1:25 Who turned God's truth into a lie, and worshiped and served what was created instead of the Creator, who is always blessed. Amen.
Romans 1:26 Because of this, God let them follow shameful desires. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.
Romans 1:27 Men also left natural relations with women and were consumed with desire for each other. Men did shameful things with other men and suffered in themselves the due penalty for their wrongs.
Romans 1:28 Since they did not think it worthwhile to keep God in their understanding, God let them follow their own thinking, which leads to wrong actions.
Romans 1:29 Filled with every kind of wrong, sexual sin, evil, greed, meanness; full of jealousy, killing, fighting, lying, ill-will; gossips,
Romans 1:30 People who talk badly about others, those who hate God, spiteful people, the proud, those who brag, creators of bad things, and those who do not obey their parents,
Romans 1:31 Lacking understanding, promise breakers, heartless, relentless, unkind:
Romans 1:32 People who know God's judgment understand that those doing such things deserve to die. They not only do these things but also enjoy seeing others do them.

Romans 2:1 So, you can't be excused, person, whoever you are that judges others: because when you judge someone else, you are judging yourself, since you do the same things.
Romans 2:2 We are certain that God's judgment is true and fair against those who do such things.
Romans 2:3 Do you think, man, that if you judge others for doing certain things and then do them yourself, you will avoid God's judgment?
Romans 2:4 Do you look down on the wealth of his kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God's goodness is meant to lead you to change your ways?
Romans 2:5 By being stubborn and unwilling to change, you are storing up anger for yourself for the day when God will show his fair judgment.
Romans 2:6 God will give to each person according to what they have done.
Romans 2:7 To those who keep on doing good and seek glory, honor, and never-ending life, God will give eternal life.
Romans 2:8 But for those who argue and don't follow the truth, but choose what's wrong, there will be anger and punishment.
Romans 2:9 Hard times and suffering will come to every person who does bad things, starting with the Jews and also to non-Jews.
Romans 2:10 But glory, honor, and peace to everyone who does good, first to the Jew and also to the non-Jew.
Romans 2:11 God does not show favoritism.
Romans 2:12 Everyone who sins without knowing God's law will still die, and those who sin knowing God's law will be judged by it.
Romans 2:13 It's not just those who hear the law who are right with God, but those who follow the law will be considered right.
Romans 2:14 For when people who do not have God's law naturally follow what it says, even without the law, they are their own guide.
Romans 2:15 They show that God's law is written in their hearts, their own conscience agrees, and their thoughts either accuse them or tell them they are right.
Romans 2:16 On the day God judges people's secrets through Jesus Christ, following my good news.
Romans 2:17 Look, you are known as a Jew, rely on the law, and take pride in God.
Romans 2:18 You know God's will, and you choose what is best, because you are taught by the law.
Romans 2:19 You are sure that you can guide the blind and be a light for those in the dark.
Romans 2:20 A teacher of the simple, a trainer of the young, who has the outline of knowledge and truth in the law.
Romans 2:21 So you, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who say people should not steal, do you steal?
Romans 2:22 You who say a person should not cheat in marriage, do you cheat? You who hate idols, do you disrespect holy things?
Romans 2:23 You who brag about the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
Romans 2:24 Because of you, people who are not Jews speak badly about God, just like it is written.
Romans 2:25 Being circumcised is good if you follow the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision becomes worthless.
Romans 2:26 So if a person who is not circumcised follows the law's rules, won't that be just like being circumcised?
Romans 2:27 Won't the uncircumcised person by birth, if they follow the law, be able to judge you, who even with the written law and circumcision, break the law?
Romans 2:28 He is not a true Jew if he is only one outwardly, nor is true circumcision something external and physical.
Romans 2:29 A true Jew is one inside; and real circumcision is in the heart, by the spirit, not by written rules. Their praise comes not from people, but from God.

Romans 3:1 What advantage does the Jew have? Or what benefit comes from circumcision?
Romans 3:2 In many ways, mostly because God's messages were entrusted to them.
Romans 3:3 What if some do not believe? Does their lack of belief cancel out God's faithfulness?
Romans 3:4 Absolutely not! Yes, God is truthful, and all people are liars; as the scripture says, "So that you may be right in your words and win when you are judged."
Romans 3:5 If our wrongs show how right God is, what can we say? Is God wrong when He punishes? (I'm speaking like a human.)
Romans 3:6 Certainly not, because then how would God judge the world?
Romans 3:7 If God's truth has spread more because of my lie to his glory, then why am I still judged as a sinner?
Romans 3:8 And instead of being falsely accused, as some claim we say, "Let's do bad things so that good may happen"? Those who say this deserve to be punished.
Romans 3:9 So what? Are we better than them? Not at all: because we have already shown that both Jews and non-Jews are all guilty of sin.
Romans 3:10 It is written, no one is good, not even one.
Romans 3:11 No one understands; no one looks for God.
Romans 3:12 Everyone has strayed from the right path; they have all become useless; not even one person does good.
Romans 3:13 Their throat is like an open grave; they lie with their tongues; there is snake venom under their lips.
Romans 3:14 Their mouth is full of curses and bitterness.
Romans 3:15 Their feet quickly lead them to harm others.
Romans 3:16 Trouble and suffering are in their paths.
Romans 3:17 They do not know the way of peace.
Romans 3:18 They do not fear God at all.
Romans 3:19 We know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who follow the law, so that no one can argue and the whole world is accountable to God.
Romans 3:20 No one will be seen as right by God only by following the law's rules, because the law shows us what sin is.
Romans 3:21 Now, God's goodness is shown without the law, and the law and prophets tell us about it.
Romans 3:22 God's righteousness comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe, there is no difference.
Romans 3:23 Everyone has sinned and falls short of God's glory.
Romans 3:24 We are made right with God for free by His kindness because of the rescue that comes through Jesus Christ.
Romans 3:25 God presented him as a sacrifice to forgive sins through faith in his blood, to show his righteousness by forgiving past sins because of God's patience.
Romans 3:26 I am telling now about God's goodness: so He can be fair and make right those who trust in Jesus.
Romans 3:27 Where can we boast, then? It is shut out. Through what rule? The rule of actions? No, but through the rule of trust.
Romans 3:28 We believe that a person is made right with God through faith, not by following the law's actions.
Romans 3:29 Is he only the God of the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the non-Jews? Yes, he is also the God of the non-Jews.
Romans 3:30 Since there is only one God, he will make both the circumcised right by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
Romans 3:31 By having faith, do we cancel the law? No, we make the law stand.

Romans 4:1 What can we say about what Abraham, our ancestor according to the flesh, discovered?
Romans 4:2 If Abraham was made right by what he did, he could be proud, but not in God's view.
Romans 4:3 What does the scripture say? Abraham trusted God, and it was accepted as his righteousness.
Romans 4:4 To the person who works, the reward is not counted as a free gift, but as something owed.
Romans 4:5 But for the one who does not work, yet believes in God who makes the ungodly right, their faith is accepted as righteousness.
Romans 4:6 David speaks of the happiness of the person whom God considers right without their works.
Romans 4:7 Saying, "Happy are those whose wrongdoings are forgiven, and whose sins are hidden."
Romans 4:8 Happy is the person who God will not count sin against.
Romans 4:9 Does this blessing come only to the circumcised, or also to the uncircumcised? We say that Abraham's faith was counted as righteousness.
Romans 4:10 How was it counted then? When he was circumcised, or not circumcised? Not when circumcised, but when not circumcised.
Romans 4:11 He got the sign of circumcision as proof of his faith's righteousness before he was circumcised, so he could be the father of all who believe without circumcision, and they could also be considered righteous.
Romans 4:12 The father of circumcised people is not just for those who are circumcised, but also for those who follow the faith that Abraham had before he was circumcised.
Romans 4:13 The promise that he would inherit the world was not given to Abraham or his descendants through the law, but through having faith and doing what is right.
Romans 4:14 If those who rely on the law are heirs, then faith means nothing, and the promise is worthless.
Romans 4:15 The law brings anger because where there is no law, there is no wrongdoing.
Romans 4:16 So it depends on faith, so that it may be given freely, and the promise may be guaranteed to all Abraham's descendants; not only to those who follow the law, but also to those who share Abraham's faith. He is the father of us all.
Romans 4:17 It is written, I have made you a father of many nations, in the presence of the God he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and names things that do not exist as though they do.
Romans 4:18 Even when there seemed to be no reason for hope, he kept hoping—believing that he would become the father of many nations, as God had said, "Your descendants will be as many as the stars."
Romans 4:19 He did not weaken in faith, even though he was about a hundred years old and thought about how his body had no strength left, and Sarah could not have children.
Romans 4:20 He did not doubt God's promise because of disbelief; instead, he was strong in his faith, praising God.
Romans 4:21 He was completely sure that God could do what he had promised.
Romans 4:22 So it was counted to him as righteousness.
Romans 4:23 It wasn't just for him that it was counted as his.
Romans 4:24 But also for us, who will be counted as righteous, if we believe in God who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
Romans 4:25 He was given up for our wrongs and raised to life so we could be made right with God.

Romans 5:1 Because we are made right with God by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Romans 5:2 Through faith in him, we have been brought into this favor in which we now stand, and we celebrate in expectation of God's glory.
Romans 5:3 We not only do this, but we also take pride in our troubles, because we know that trouble produces patience.
Romans 5:4 Patience brings experience, and experience brings hope.
Romans 5:5 Hope does not disappoint us because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us.
Romans 5:6 When we were still weak, at the right time, Christ died for the sinful.
Romans 5:7 It's rare that someone would die for a righteous person, but for a good person, someone might be brave enough to die.
Romans 5:8 God shows his love for us in that, even when we were sinning, Christ died for us.
Romans 5:9 Even more, now that we are made right by his blood, we will be rescued from punishment through him.
Romans 5:10 If we became friends with God when we were his enemies because his Son died for us, we will surely be saved now that we are his friends and because his Son lives.
Romans 5:11 We not only do this, but we also find joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Through him, we have now received reconciliation.
Romans 5:12 Because one man brought sin into the world, and death came because of sin, death spread to all people since everyone has sinned.
Romans 5:13 Before the law, sin was in the world, but sin is not counted where there is no law.
Romans 5:14 Death ruled from Adam to Moses, even over those who did not sin like Adam, who represents the one who was to come.
Romans 5:15 The free gift is not like the wrongdoing. If many have died because one person did wrong, God's kindness and the gift he gives freely through one man, Jesus Christ, have reached many more.
Romans 5:16 The gift isn't like the result of one person's sin; the verdict for that one sin was guilt, but God's gift, after many sins, brings us right with Him.
Romans 5:17 If one man's mistake let death rule because of him, even more, those who get lots of kindness and the free gift of being right will live and rule through one person, Jesus Christ.
Romans 5:18 Because one person's mistake led to everyone being judged guilty, the good act of one person gave everyone a free gift leading to life being seen as right.
Romans 5:19 Because one man disobeyed, many became sinners, but because one man obeyed, many will be made good.
Romans 5:20 The law was given so that wrongdoing could increase. But where sin increased, God's kindness increased even more.
Romans 5:21 Just as sin ruled leading to death, so grace also might rule through being right, leading to eternal life, because of Jesus Christ our Lord.

Romans 6:1 So what should we say? Should we keep sinning so that God's kindness can increase?
Romans 6:2 Of course not! How can we, who have died to sin, still live in it?
Romans 6:3 Don't you know that all of us who were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?
Romans 6:4 We are buried with him through baptism into death so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by God's glory, we too may live a new life.
Romans 6:5 If we have died with him, we will also live with him.
Romans 6:6 Understand that our old self was put to death with him so that our sinful nature could be done away with, and from now on we should not be slaves to sin.
Romans 6:7 When someone dies, they are free from sin.
Romans 6:8 If we have died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him.
Romans 6:9 Knowing that Christ was raised from the dead, he won't die again; death no longer rules over him.
Romans 6:10 When he died, he died to sin once, but now that he lives, he lives for God.
Romans 6:11 Think of yourselves as truly dead to sin, but alive to God because of Jesus Christ our Lord.
Romans 6:12 Do not let sin control your body that must die, making you obey its desires.
Romans 6:13 Do not use your body parts as tools for doing wrong and sinning, but give yourselves to God as people who have been brought back to life from death, and use your body parts as tools for doing right for God.
Romans 6:14 Sin will not control you, because you are not under the law, but under God's kindness.
Romans 6:15 So what? Should we keep sinning because we are not controlled by the law but by God's kindness? Certainly not!
Romans 6:16 Don't you know that when you give yourselves to someone as obedient servants, you are the servants of the one you obey, whether you're serving sin, which leads to death, or following obedience, which leads to righteousness?
Romans 6:17 Thank God that you used to be slaves to sin, but now you have followed the teaching given to you with all your heart.
Romans 6:18 After being set free from sin, you became servants of doing right.
Romans 6:19 I talk in human terms because of your weak bodies: just like you used to offer yourselves as slaves to impurity and more and more wrongdoing, now offer yourselves as slaves to right living that leads to holiness.
Romans 6:20 When you served sin, you were not bound by righteousness.
Romans 6:21 What did you gain from the things you are now ashamed of? Those things lead to death.
Romans 6:22 Now that you are free from sin and are servants to God, your actions lead to a holy life and result in eternal life.
Romans 6:23 The payment for sin is death, but God's gift is eternal life in Jesus Christ our Lord.

Romans 7:1 Don't you know, friends, (because I am talking to those who understand law,) that the law has authority over a person as long as they are alive?
Romans 7:2 A married woman is legally tied to her husband while he is alive, but if he dies, she is free from her husband's laws.
Romans 7:3 If her husband is alive and she marries another man, she will be called an adulteress. But if her husband is dead, she is not breaking the law and is not an adulteress, even if she marries another man.
Romans 7:4 So, my friends, you too have died to the law through Christ's body, so that you can belong to another, the one who was raised from the dead, so that we can produce good results for God.
Romans 7:5 When we lived following our human nature, our sins, stirred up by the law, were active in our bodies, leading to death.
Romans 7:6 But now we are free from the law, which we were bound by when it was in effect; so we can serve in a new and spiritual way, not in the old way of following the written rules.
Romans 7:7 What should we say, then? Is the law wrong? Absolutely not. Indeed, I would not have recognized sin if it weren't for the law; I wouldn't have known what desire was if the law hadn't said, "Do not want what others have."
Romans 7:8 Sin used the command to produce all kinds of wrong desires in me. Without the law, sin is powerless.
Romans 7:9 Before I knew the law, I was alive; but when I learned the commandment, sin came back to life, and I died.
Romans 7:10 The rule that was meant to give life, I discovered leads to death.
Romans 7:11 Sin used the command to trick me, and through it killed me.
Romans 7:12 So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, right, and good.
Romans 7:13 Did the good thing cause my death? No way! But it was sin, using the good thing, that caused death in me. This was to show sin as truly sinful through the commandment.
Romans 7:14 We know that the law is spiritual, but I am human, trapped by sin.
Romans 7:15 I don't understand why I do the things I do: I don't do what I know is right, instead I do the things I hate.
Romans 7:16 If I do what I don't want to do, I agree that the law is good.
Romans 7:17 Now it's not me doing it, but the sin that lives in me.
Romans 7:18 I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my body. I want to do what is right, but I can't do it.
Romans 7:19 I don't do the good I want to do, but I do the bad I don't want to do.
Romans 7:20 If I do what I don't want to, it's not really me doing it, but the sin that lives in me.
Romans 7:21 I discover a rule: when I want to do good, evil is there with me.
Romans 7:22 I enjoy following God's laws with my heart.
Romans 7:23 I notice another rule in my body fighting against my mind's rule, making me a prisoner to the rule of sin in my body.
Romans 7:24 I am a miserable person! Who will rescue me from this body that brings death?
Romans 7:25 I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. I serve God's law with my mind, but with my body, I follow the law of sin.

Romans 8:1 So now, there is no punishment for those who are with Christ Jesus, who do not follow human desires, but follow the Spirit.
Romans 8:2 The Spirit's law of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death.
Romans 8:3 The law could not do everything because human weakness made it weak. But God sent his own Son, who was like sinful humans, to deal with sin and to stop sin's power over the body.
Romans 8:4 So that the law's goodness is complete in us, who live not by our selfish desires, but by the Spirit.
Romans 8:5 People who follow their human desires think about human things; but those who follow the Spirit think about spiritual things.
Romans 8:6 Thinking about physical things leads to death, but thinking about spiritual things brings life and peace.
Romans 8:7 The human mind ruled by sin is hostile to God; it does not obey God's laws, and it cannot.
Romans 8:8 Those living by their human nature cannot please God.
Romans 8:9 You are not living according to your selfish desires, but by the Spirit, if God's Spirit truly lives in you. If someone doesn't have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Him.
Romans 8:10 If Christ lives in you, your body is dead due to sin, but the Spirit gives life because of righteousness.
Romans 8:11 If the Spirit of God who raised Jesus from death lives in you, then the one who raised Christ will also give life to your dying bodies through his Spirit within you.
Romans 8:12 So, friends, we do not owe anything to our bodily desires, to live controlled by them.
Romans 8:13 If you follow selfish desires, you will die. But if by the Spirit you put to death the body's wrong actions, you will live.
Romans 8:14 Everyone guided by God's Spirit is a child of God.
Romans 8:15 You have not gotten a spirit that makes you slaves and afraid again; instead, you have gotten a spirit that lets us be God's children, and because of this spirit, we call out, "Daddy, Father."
Romans 8:16 The Spirit itself shows with our spirit that we are God's children.
Romans 8:17 If we are children, then we are heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, if we indeed share in his sufferings so that we may also share in his glory.
Romans 8:18 I believe that our current sufferings are nothing compared to the future glory that will be shown in us.
Romans 8:19 All creation eagerly waits for God's children to be revealed.
Romans 8:20 The creation was made to live a pointless life, not because it wanted to, but because God decided, yet gave it hope.
Romans 8:21 The creation itself will also be freed from the chains of decay into the wonderful freedom of God's children.
Romans 8:22 We know that all creation has been groaning as if in pain up to this time.
Romans 8:23 Not just them, but we also, who have the first of the Spirit, sigh deep inside, waiting to be fully brought into God's family, that is, to have our bodies completely freed.
Romans 8:24 We are saved by hope: but if we see what we hope for, it isn't really hope. Why would anyone hope for something they already have?
Romans 8:25 If we hope for what we can't see, we patiently wait for it.
Romans 8:26 The Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we do not know what to pray for as we should, but the Spirit itself speaks for us with sighs too deep for words.
Romans 8:27 The one who knows what we truly think also understands the Spirit's desires, because he speaks to God for the holy people as God wants.
Romans 8:28 We know that everything works for the good of those who love God, who are called according to his plan.
Romans 8:29 God knew some people in advance, and he chose them to become like his Son so that his Son would be the first among many brothers and sisters.
Romans 8:30 God chose some people in advance; those he chose, he also invited. Those he invited, he made right with himself. And those he made right, he also shared his glory with.
Romans 8:31 What can we say about these things? If God supports us, who can stand against us?
Romans 8:32 God did not hold back his own Son, but gave him up for us all; won't he also freely give us everything else with him?
Romans 8:33 Who can accuse those chosen by God? God is the one who declares them right.
Romans 8:34 Who can condemn us? Christ, who died and more than that, rose again is at God's right side, and also pleads for us.
Romans 8:35 Who can take us away from Christ's love? Can troubles, or hardship, or attacks, or hunger, or having no clothes, or danger, or violence?
Romans 8:36 It is written, for you we are being killed all day; we are treated like sheep going to be killed.
Romans 8:37 No, in all these things we win completely because of the one who loved us.
Romans 8:38 I am sure that nothing - not death or life, not angels or rulers, not now or later,
Romans 8:39 Not high places, deep places, or any other being can separate us from God's love in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Romans 9:11 Before the children were born and had done anything good or bad, God's plan was based on his choice, not their actions, but on his call.

Romans 9:28 God will complete the work and quickly do it with fairness; for God will carry out a brief task on the earth.

Romans 9:30 What can we say then? The non-Jews, who did not pursue being right with God, have achieved it through faith.
Romans 9:31 Israel, which chased the law of right living, did not reach the law of right living.

Romans 9:33 It is written, "Look, I put in Zion a stone that makes people fall, and a rock that makes them trip: but anyone who trusts in him will not feel shame."

Romans 12:2 Do not follow this world's ways: instead, change by renewing your mind to know God's good, pleasing, and perfect will.
Romans 12:3 I tell you, with the kindness given to me, to not think too highly of yourself, but to think sensibly, as God has given each of us a certain amount of faith.
Romans 12:4 Just as we have many parts in one body, and not all parts have the same function:
Romans 12:5 We, though many, are one body in Christ, and each one is a part of each other.
Romans 12:6 Since we have different gifts based on the grace given to us, if it is to prophesy, let us do so in proportion to our faith.
Romans 12:7 If we serve others, let's focus on our service; if we teach, let's focus on our teaching.
Romans 12:8 If you encourage others, do it earnestly. If you give, do it generously. If you lead, do it diligently. If you show kindness, do it happily.
Romans 12:9 Love sincerely. Hate what is evil; hold on to what is good.
Romans 12:10 Show genuine kindness and love to each other like brothers and sisters; give each other more honor.
Romans 12:11 Not lazy in work; passionate in spirit; serving God.
Romans 12:12 Happy in hope; enduring in trouble; always praying.
Romans 12:13 Sharing with those in need; welcoming to others.
Romans 12:14 Be kind to those who are unkind to you; do not wish them harm.
Romans 12:15 Be happy with those who are happy, and cry with those who are crying.
Romans 12:16 Have the same attitude towards each other. Don't aim for high status, but be willing to associate with people of lower position. Don't think you know everything.
Romans 12:17 Don't pay back anyone with harm for harm. Do what is right in everyone's eyes.
Romans 12:18 If you can, try to live in peace with everyone.
Romans 12:19 Dear friends, do not take revenge, but leave room for anger; for it is written, "It is my right to avenge; I will pay back," says God.
Romans 12:20 If your enemy is hungry, give them food; if they are thirsty, give them water; because by doing this, you will make them feel ashamed.
Romans 12:21 Do not let evil defeat you, but defeat evil by doing good.

Romans 13:4 He serves God to do good to you. But if you do evil, be scared; he doesn't carry the sword for no reason: he serves God to punish those who do evil.
Romans 13:5 You must obey, not only to avoid punishment, but also to have a clear conscience.
Romans 13:6 You should pay taxes too because tax collectors are serving God by doing this important work.

Romans 13:8 Don't owe anyone anything, except to love each other, because the one who loves another has done what the law requires.
Romans 13:9 Do not cheat in marriage, do not kill, do not steal, do not lie, do not desire what others have; all other rules are included in this one: Love others as much as you love yourself.
Romans 13:10 Love does no harm to others, so love fulfills the law.

Romans 13:14 Wear the ways of Jesus Christ, and don't make plans for self-indulgence to satisfy its desires.
