Romans 16:21 Timothy, my coworker, and Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives, send their greetings to you.
Romans 16:22 I, Tertius, the writer of this letter, greet you in God.
Romans 16:23 Gaius, my host and the host of the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city's treasurer, greets you, and so does Quartus, our brother.
Romans 16:24 May our Lord Jesus Christ's kindness be with everyone. Amen.
Romans 16:25 Now to him who has the power to strengthen you according to my good news, and the message about Jesus Christ, following the revealing of the secret that was hidden since the beginning of the world,
Romans 16:26 Now it is clearly shown, and through the writings of the prophets, by the order of the forever God, made known to all countries for them to obey in faith.
Romans 16:27 God, the only wise one, gets glory through Jesus Christ forever. Amen.

1 Corinthians 1:1 Paul, chosen as a messenger of Jesus Christ by God's will, and our brother Sosthenes,
1 Corinthians 1:2 To God's church in Corinth, to those made holy in Christ Jesus, called to be God's people, along with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ everywhere: theirs and ours.
1 Corinthians 1:3 May you have kindness and peace from God our Father and from Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 1:4 I always thank God for you because of His kindness given to you through Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 1:5 In every way, you have been made rich by God, in all your speaking and in all your understanding.
1 Corinthians 1:6 Just as the message about Christ was proven true among you:
1 Corinthians 1:7 So you lack no gift as you wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to come.
1 Corinthians 1:8 God will also strengthen you to the end, so that you may be without fault on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 1:9 God is trustworthy, and He called you to join in the life with His Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord.
1 Corinthians 1:10 I ask you, friends, in the name of Jesus Christ, to all agree and not be divided; be completely united with the same thoughts and the same opinions.
1 Corinthians 1:11 I have been told by Chloe's people that there are arguments among you, my brothers and sisters.
1 Corinthians 1:12 I tell you, everyone says, "I follow Paul," or "I follow Apollos," or "I follow Cephas," or "I follow Christ."
1 Corinthians 1:13 Is Christ split into parts? Was Paul put on the cross for you? Or were you baptized in Paul's name?
1 Corinthians 1:14 I thank God I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius.
1 Corinthians 1:15 So no one could claim that I baptized using my own name.
1 Corinthians 1:16 I also baptized Stephanas's family, but I don't know if I baptized anyone else.
1 Corinthians 1:17 Christ did not send me to baptize, but to share the good news; not with fancy words, so the work of Christ on the cross is not made useless.
1 Corinthians 1:18 Talking about the cross seems silly to those who are dying, but to us who are saved, it shows God's power.
1 Corinthians 1:19 It is written, I will ruin the wisdom of the wise, and I will make the knowledge of the smart people worthless.
1 Corinthians 1:20 Where is the wise? Where is the writer? Where is the debater of this age? Hasn't God made the world's wisdom look foolish?
1 Corinthians 1:21 Because the world did not know God through its own wisdom, God chose to save those who believe through the simple message of preaching.
1 Corinthians 1:22 Jews ask for a sign, and Greeks look for wisdom.
1 Corinthians 1:23 We tell people about Christ, who was nailed to a cross. This causes Jewish people to trip and seem silly to Greek people.
1 Corinthians 1:24 But for those who are called, both Jews and non-Jews, Christ is God's power and God's wisdom.
1 Corinthians 1:25 Even what seems foolish in God is wiser than human wisdom, and what seems weak in God is stronger than human strength.
1 Corinthians 1:26 You see, friends, that not many wise by human standards, not many powerful, not many of high status are chosen.
1 Corinthians 1:27 God chose the foolish things in the world to confuse the wise; God chose the weak things in the world to confuse the strong.
1 Corinthians 1:28 God has chosen the lowly and despised things of the world, even things that are not, to make nothing of the things that are.
1 Corinthians 1:29 No one should boast before God.
1 Corinthians 1:30 Through Christ Jesus, you have received from God wisdom, righteousness, holiness, and freedom from sin.
1 Corinthians 1:31 So, as it is written, "If anyone wants to boast, they should boast about God."

1 Corinthians 2:1 When I came to you, friends, I did not use fancy talking or great wisdom to tell you about God.
1 Corinthians 2:2 I decided to focus only on knowing about Jesus Christ and his crucifixion when I was with you.
1 Corinthians 2:3 I was with you feeling weak, scared, and shaking a lot.
1 Corinthians 2:4 My speaking and preaching weren't with fancy words of human wisdom, but with clear evidence of the Spirit and power.
1 Corinthians 2:5 Your faith should not be based on human wisdom, but on God's power.
1 Corinthians 2:6 We talk about deep understanding with the mature, but it's not the knowledge of this world or its leaders, which will all end.
1 Corinthians 2:7 We talk about God's wisdom that is secret and hidden, wisdom that God decided before the world began for our glory.
1 Corinthians 2:8 The rulers of this world did not understand this; if they had, they would not have crucified the glorious Lord.
1 Corinthians 2:9 People have not seen, heard, or even imagined what God has ready for those who love Him.
1 Corinthians 2:10 God has shown these things to us through his Spirit, because the Spirit explores everything, even the deep things of God.
1 Corinthians 2:11 Who knows what a person thinks except their own spirit? Just like that, no one knows God's thoughts except God's Spirit.
1 Corinthians 2:12 We have received, not the world's spirit, but the spirit from God; so we can know what God has freely given us.
1 Corinthians 2:13 We speak about these things not with words taught by human wisdom, but with those taught by the Holy Spirit, explaining spiritual truths with the help of the Spirit.
1 Corinthians 2:14 A person without the Spirit does not accept what comes from God's Spirit, because it seems foolish to them. They cannot understand it because it must be understood in a spiritual way.
1 Corinthians 2:15 The spiritual person can assess everything, but no one can judge him.
1 Corinthians 2:16 Who has understood God's thoughts, that they could teach Him? But we think like Christ.

1 Corinthians 3:1 Brothers and sisters, I could not talk to you as spiritual people but as worldly, as if to babies in Christ.
1 Corinthians 3:2 I have given you milk, not solid food, because until now you were not ready for it, and even now you cannot handle it.
1 Corinthians 3:3 You are still worldly because you have jealousy, arguments, and divisions among you. Doesn't this show that you are worldly and behave like ordinary people?
1 Corinthians 3:4 When one of you says, "I follow Paul," and another, "I follow Apollos," aren't you acting like mere humans?
1 Corinthians 3:5 Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but servants through whom you believed, as God gave to each person?
1 Corinthians 3:6 I planted, Apollos watered, but God made it grow.
1 Corinthians 3:7 So the one who plants or the one who waters is not important, but God who makes things grow is.
1 Corinthians 3:8 The person who plants and the person who waters are working together, and each will get a reward based on their own work.
1 Corinthians 3:9 We work together with God: you are God's field, you are God's construction.
1 Corinthians 3:10 God has given me grace, so like a skilled architect, I laid a foundation for others to build on. But everyone should be careful about how they build on it.
1 Corinthians 3:11 No one can lay any other foundation than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 3:12 If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,
1 Corinthians 3:13 Everyone's work will become clear: the day will show it because fire will reveal it; and the fire will test what kind of work each person has done.
1 Corinthians 3:14 If someone's work lasts which they have built on it, they will get a reward.
1 Corinthians 3:15 If someone's work is burned up, they will lose it: but they themselves will be saved, but only as if through fire.
1 Corinthians 3:16 Don't you know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit lives in you?
1 Corinthians 3:17 If anyone ruins God's temple, God will ruin that person; because God's temple is sacred, and that temple is you.
1 Corinthians 3:18 Do not trick yourself. If someone thinks they are wise by this world's standards, they should become like they know nothing, so they can truly become wise.
1 Corinthians 3:19 The wisdom of this world is silly to God. It is said, He catches the clever in their tricks.
1 Corinthians 3:20 God knows the thoughts of the smart people, that they are useless.
1 Corinthians 3:21 So don't boast about following people. Everything belongs to you.
1 Corinthians 3:22 Whether Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, things now, or things in the future; all belong to you.
1 Corinthians 3:23 You belong to Christ; and Christ belongs to God.

1 Corinthians 4:1 Think of us as Christ's servants and as keepers of God's secrets.
1 Corinthians 4:2 It is expected that those who take care of things must be trusted.
1 Corinthians 4:3 I care very little if you or anyone else judges me; in fact, I don't even judge myself.
1 Corinthians 4:4 I don't know of any wrong I've done; but that doesn't make me innocent. The one who judges me is God.
1 Corinthians 4:5 So, don't judge anything too soon, until God comes, who will reveal what's hidden in darkness and show people's true intentions. Then, each person will get praise from God.
1 Corinthians 4:6 I've used myself and Apollos as examples for your benefit, so you can learn from us not to think too highly of people, following what is written, and so that none of you will feel superior to someone else.
1 Corinthians 4:7 Who makes you different from others? What do you have that you didn't get? If you did get it, why do you boast as if you didn't?
1 Corinthians 4:8 Now you are satisfied, now you are wealthy, you have ruled like kings without us: and I wish you did rule, so we could rule with you.
1 Corinthians 4:9 I believe that God has placed us apostles last, like those sentenced to death. We've become a show for everyone—people, angels, and the world.
1 Corinthians 4:10 We are foolish because of Christ, but you are smart in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are respected, but we are looked down on.
1 Corinthians 4:11 Right now, we are hungry, thirsty, have no clothes, are treated roughly, and have no sure place to live.
1 Corinthians 4:12 We work hard with our hands. When people insult us, we are kind; when we are persecuted, we endure it.
1 Corinthians 4:13 We are insulted, but we ask nicely; we are treated like the world's garbage, like the dirt everyone scrapes off their shoes, right up to this moment.
1 Corinthians 4:14 I'm not writing this to embarrass you, but to warn you as my dear children.
1 Corinthians 4:15 Even if you had ten thousand teachers in Christ, you don't have many fathers. In Christ Jesus, I became your father through the good news.
1 Corinthians 4:16 So I ask you, please follow my example.
1 Corinthians 4:17 I have sent Timothy to you for this reason. He is my dear son and loyal to God. He will remind you of how I live in Christ, as I teach in all the churches.
1 Corinthians 4:18 Some are arrogant, thinking I won't come to you.
1 Corinthians 4:19 I will come to you soon, if God wants, and I will see, not how they talk proudly, but their true strength.
1 Corinthians 4:20 God's kingdom is not just in words, but in power.
1 Corinthians 4:21 What do you want? Should I come to you with punishment, or with love and a gentle spirit?

1 Corinthians 5:1 People often say that sexual immorality is happening among you, the kind not even non-believers talk about, like someone living with his stepmother.
1 Corinthians 5:2 You have become arrogant instead of mourning, so that the one who did this should be removed from among you.
1 Corinthians 5:3 Although I am not there in person, I am with you in spirit and have already made my decision about the person who did this.
1 Corinthians 5:4 In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you gather and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
1 Corinthians 5:5 To hand someone over to Satan to destroy their flesh so that their spirit can be saved on the day of Jesus.
1 Corinthians 5:6 Your boasting is not good. Don't you know that a little yeast works through the whole batch of dough?
1 Corinthians 5:7 Get rid of the old yeast, so you can be a fresh batch of dough, since you are without yeast. Just as Christ, our Passover lamb, has been offered for us.
1 Corinthians 5:8 Let's celebrate the festival not with old yeast or with yeast of evil and badness, but with bread without yeast that is pure and true.
1 Corinthians 5:9 I wrote to you in a letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
1 Corinthians 5:10 Don't completely avoid people in this world who sin sexually, are greedy, cheat others, or worship idols; if you did, you would have to leave this world.
1 Corinthians 5:11 I have told you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral, greedy, worships idols, insults others, drinks too much, or cheats people. Do not even eat with such a person.
1 Corinthians 5:12 Why should I judge those outside? Don't you judge those inside?
1 Corinthians 5:13 God judges those who are outside. So remove the evil person from among you.

1 Corinthians 6:1 Would any of you, with a dispute against another, sue in a court with unfair judges instead of bringing the case to God's people?
1 Corinthians 6:2 Don't you know that God's holy people will judge the world? And if you will judge the world, can't you handle small issues?
1 Corinthians 6:3 Don't you know we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life?
1 Corinthians 6:4 If you have to decide on matters of this life, choose those who are least important in the church to be the judges.
1 Corinthians 6:5 I am telling you this to make you ashamed. Isn't there one wise person among you who can resolve disputes among brothers?
1 Corinthians 6:6 A brother takes another brother to court, and this happens in front of people who don't believe.
1 Corinthians 6:7 Now you have a big problem because you sue each other. Wouldn't it be better to accept being wronged? Why not rather let yourselves be cheated?
1 Corinthians 6:8 No, you do wrong and cheat, and you do this to your brothers.
1 Corinthians 6:9 Don't you know that wrongdoers will not get into God's kingdom? Do not be fooled: people who have sex without being married, worship idols, cheat on their spouses, act in unmanly ways, or use others for sexual acts,
1 Corinthians 6:10 Thieves, greedy people, drunk people, people who insult others, and those who cheat others will not inherit God's kingdom.
1 Corinthians 6:11 Some of you were like that, but now you are clean, made holy, and made right with God in the name of Jesus, and by God's Spirit.
1 Corinthians 6:12 I can do anything, but not everything is good for me: I can do anything, but I won't be controlled by anything.
1 Corinthians 6:13 Food is for the stomach, and the stomach for food, but God will end both. The body is not for sexual immorality, but for God, and God is for the body.
1 Corinthians 6:14 God raised up the Lord and will also raise us up by his power.
1 Corinthians 6:15 Don't you know that your bodies are parts of Christ? Should I then take the parts of Christ and join them to a prostitute? No way.
1 Corinthians 6:16 Do you not know that a person who joins with a prostitute becomes one body with her? For two people, God says, will become one flesh.
1 Corinthians 6:17 Whoever is united with God is one in spirit.
1 Corinthians 6:18 Run away from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside their body, but someone who is sexually immoral sins against their own body.
1 Corinthians 6:19 Don't you know that your body is the home of the Holy Spirit who is in you, given by God, and that you do not belong to yourselves?
1 Corinthians 6:20 You were bought for a price: so honor God with your body and spirit, which belong to God.

1 Corinthians 7:1 About what you wrote to me: It's good for a man not to be with a woman.
1 Corinthians 7:2 To avoid wrong sexual acts, every man should have a wife and every woman should have a husband.
1 Corinthians 7:3 The husband should be kind to his wife, and the wife should be kind to her husband.
1 Corinthians 7:4 A wife does not control her own body, but her husband does; and in the same way, a husband does not control his own body, but his wife does.
1 Corinthians 7:5 Do not cheat each other, unless you both agree to stop having sex for a while to focus on fasting and praying. Then come back together so that Satan won't tempt you because you can't control yourselves.
1 Corinthians 7:6 I say this as a suggestion, not as an order.
1 Corinthians 7:7 I wish that all people were just as I am. But each person has their own special gift from God, one in this way, and another in that way.
1 Corinthians 7:8 I tell unmarried people and widows that it's good for them to stay single, like I am.
1 Corinthians 7:9 If they can't control themselves, they should get married, because it's better to marry than to have strong desires.
1 Corinthians 7:10 To the married, I give this order (not me, but God): A wife should not leave her husband.
1 Corinthians 7:11 If she leaves, she should stay single or get back with her husband; and the husband shouldn't divorce his wife.
1 Corinthians 7:12 I say this, not God: If a man has a wife who does not believe, but she agrees to live with him, he should not leave her.
1 Corinthians 7:13 If a woman has a husband who does not believe, but he wants to live with her, she should not leave him.
1 Corinthians 7:14 The husband who does not believe is made holy through his wife, and the wife who does not believe is made holy through her husband; otherwise your children would be impure, but now they are holy.
1 Corinthians 7:15 If someone does not believe and wants to leave, let them leave. A brother or sister is not bound in such situations: God wants us to live in peace.
1 Corinthians 7:16 Wife, how do you know if you can save your husband? Or husband, how do you know if you can save your wife?
1 Corinthians 7:17 But as God has given to each person, as God has called each one, let them live that way. This is what I instruct in all churches.
1 Corinthians 7:18 If a man is already circumcised when he is called, he should not try to reverse it. If he is uncircumcised when called, he should not get circumcised.
1 Corinthians 7:19 Circumcision doesn't matter, and not being circumcised doesn't matter, but obeying God's commands does matter.
1 Corinthians 7:20 Everyone should remain in the life situation they were in when God called them.
1 Corinthians 7:21 Are you called while a servant? Don't worry about it: but if you can become free, choose that instead.
1 Corinthians 7:22 When someone serves and follows God, they become free, and a person who is free but follows Christ becomes His servant.
1 Corinthians 7:23 You were bought at a price; do not become slaves to people.
1 Corinthians 7:24 Friends, stay as you are when God calls you.
1 Corinthians 7:25 About unmarried women, I don't have a direct order from God, but I offer my opinion as someone who God has shown kindness to be trustworthy.
1 Corinthians 7:26 I believe that, given our current troubles, it is good for a person to stay as they are.
1 Corinthians 7:27 Are you married? Don't try to get a divorce. Are you divorced? Don't look for a wife.
1 Corinthians 7:28 If you get married, you haven't sinned; and if an unmarried woman gets married, she hasn't sinned. However, they will have problems in life. But I want to spare you this.
1 Corinthians 7:29 I tell you, friends, time is running out. It's important that those with wives should live as if they had none.
1 Corinthians 7:30 People who cry should act as if they're not crying; those who are happy should act as if they're not happy; and those who buy things should act as if they don't own them.
1 Corinthians 7:31 People should use this world without misusing it, because this world's way will disappear.
1 Corinthians 7:32 I want you to be free from worries. A single person cares about how to please God.
1 Corinthians 7:33 But a married person cares about worldly things, how to make their spouse happy.
1 Corinthians 7:34 A wife and a virgin are different. The single woman cares about God's work, to be pure in body and spirit, but the married woman cares about worldly things, to please her husband.
1 Corinthians 7:35 I say this for your benefit, not to trap you, but to promote what is proper, and so you can focus on God without distraction.
1 Corinthians 7:36 If a man believes he is acting improperly towards his fiancée, if she is past her prime age and it is necessary, he can do as he chooses, he does not sin: they should get married.
1 Corinthians 7:37 The person who is firm in their decision, not forced but in control of their desire, and decides to stay unmarried, does well.
1 Corinthians 7:38 So the person who helps her get married does good, but the person who does not help her get married does better.
1 Corinthians 7:39 The wife must follow the law while her husband is alive; but if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wants, as long as it is with a believer.
1 Corinthians 7:40 But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my opinion, and I believe I have God's Spirit.

1 Corinthians 8:1 About food given to idols, we understand that we all have knowledge. Knowledge makes one proud, but love builds up.
1 Corinthians 8:2 If someone thinks they know something, they don't know it as well as they should.
1 Corinthians 8:3 If anyone loves God, that person is known by God.
1 Corinthians 8:4 About eating food given to idols, we understand that an idol means nothing in the world, and there is only one God.
1 Corinthians 8:5 Even though some are known as gods, whether in heaven or on earth (and there are many gods and many lords),
1 Corinthians 8:6 For us, there is only one God, the Father, from whom everything comes, and we live for him; and there is one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom everything is made, and through whom we live.
1 Corinthians 8:7 However, not everyone knows this: some people still think of the meat as connected to the idol and eat it with that belief. Because their understanding is weak, it makes them feel guilty.
1 Corinthians 8:8 Eating food does not make us closer to God; if we eat, we are not better; if we don't eat, we are not worse.
1 Corinthians 8:9 But be careful that your freedom does not cause those who are weak to stumble.
1 Corinthians 8:10 If someone sees you with knowledge eating in the temple of an idol, won't a person with a weak conscience feel encouraged to eat food offered to idols?
1 Corinthians 8:11 Will your knowledge cause your weak brother to be lost, for whom Christ died?
1 Corinthians 8:12 But when you do wrong to your brothers and sisters, hurting their weak understanding, you also do wrong to Christ.
1 Corinthians 8:13 If food causes my brother to sin, I will not eat meat as long as the world exists, so I don't make my brother sin.

1 Corinthians 9:1 Am I not a messenger? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Leader? Are you not my work in God?
1 Corinthians 9:2 Even if I am not an apostle to others, I definitely am to you, for you prove my work as an apostle is true in God.
1 Corinthians 9:3 My answer to those who question me is this:
1 Corinthians 9:4 Don't we have the right to eat and drink?
1 Corinthians 9:5 Don't we have the right to bring along a believing wife like the other apostles, the Lord's brothers, and Peter do?
1 Corinthians 9:6 Don't I and Barnabas have the right not to work?
1 Corinthians 9:7 Who goes to war at their own expense? Who plants a vineyard and doesn't eat its grapes? Or who tends sheep and doesn't drink the milk from the sheep?
1 Corinthians 9:8 Do I say these things on my own, or does the law say the same thing too?
1 Corinthians 9:9 It is written in the Law of Moses, "Do not put a muzzle on the ox when it is treading the grain." Does God care about oxen?
1 Corinthians 9:10 Does he say this for us, indeed? Without a doubt, it is written for us: the one who plows should plow with hope, and the one who threshes with hope should share in the results of his hope.
1 Corinthians 9:11 If we have shared spiritual things with you, is it too much to ask for material things in return?
1 Corinthians 9:12 If others share this authority over you, shouldn't we even more? Yet we haven't exercised this authority; instead, we endure everything so we won't block the message of Christ.
1 Corinthians 9:13 Don't you know that those who serve in holy places get their living from the temple things? And those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar?
1 Corinthians 9:14 God has decided that those who share the good news should be supported by the good news.
1 Corinthians 9:15 I haven't used any of these rights, and I’m not writing this to get such help. I'd rather die than let anyone take away my reason for pride.
1 Corinthians 9:16 Even though I share the good news, I can't boast about it because I must do it; if I don't share the good news, it will be bad for me!
1 Corinthians 9:17 If I do this willingly, I get a reward. But if I do it unwillingly, I am still trusted to share God's message.
1 Corinthians 9:18 What then is my reward? Truly, it is this: when I share the good news, I offer it for free so that I do not misuse my rights in spreading the good news.
1 Corinthians 9:19 Although I am free from everyone, I have become a servant to all, so that I might win more people.
1 Corinthians 9:20 I became like a Jew to win over the Jews. To those following the law, I lived like someone under the law to win them over.
1 Corinthians 9:21 To those not following the law, I lived as if I didn't follow the law (although I am not free from God's law but am under Christ's law) so that I might win over those not following the law.
1 Corinthians 9:22 I became weak for the weak people, so I could win them over. I became everything for everyone, so I could save some by any possible way.
1 Corinthians 9:23 I do this for the good news, so I can share in it with you.
1 Corinthians 9:24 Don't you know that everyone who runs in a race does run, but only one gets the prize? Run in such a way that you may win it.
1 Corinthians 9:25 Everyone who competes in games exercises self-control in everything. They do it to win a perishable crown, but we for an imperishable one.
1 Corinthians 9:26 I run with purpose, not aimlessly; I fight, not like someone just hitting the air.
1 Corinthians 9:27 But I discipline my body and keep it under control, so that after telling others, I myself will not be disqualified.

1 Corinthians 10:1 My friends, I want you to know that all our ancestors were under the cloud and all went through the sea.
1 Corinthians 10:2 They were all baptized as followers of Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
1 Corinthians 10:3 Everyone ate the same spiritual food.
1 Corinthians 10:4 Everyone drank the same spiritual drink because they drank from the spiritual rock that went with them, and that rock was Christ.
1 Corinthians 10:5 God was not happy with many of them because they were defeated in the wilderness.
1 Corinthians 10:6 These things happened to them as examples for us, so we wouldn't desire bad things like they did.
1 Corinthians 10:7 Do not worship idols like some of them did; as the Scripture says, "The people ate and drank, then got up to have fun."
1 Corinthians 10:8 Let's not have sex outside of marriage, like some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand died.
1 Corinthians 10:9 Let's not test Christ, as some of them did and were killed by snakes.
1 Corinthians 10:10 Do not complain as some of them did and were killed by the destroyer.
1 Corinthians 10:11 All these things happened to them as examples and are written to warn us, who are living in the last days.
1 Corinthians 10:12 So, if someone thinks they are standing firm, they should be careful not to fall.
1 Corinthians 10:13 No temptation has come to you that isn't normal for people. But God can be trusted not to let you be tempted more than you can handle. He will also give you a way out so you can endure it.
1 Corinthians 10:14 So, my dear friends, run away from worshipping idols.
1 Corinthians 10:15 I talk to you as if you are wise; think about what I'm saying.
1 Corinthians 10:16 The cup we give thanks for, isn't it sharing in Christ's blood? The bread we break, isn't it sharing in Christ's body?
1 Corinthians 10:17 We are many, but we are one loaf of bread and one body, because we all share that one loaf.
1 Corinthians 10:18 Look at the people of Israel: aren't those who eat the sacrifices sharing in the altar?
1 Corinthians 10:19 What am I saying, then? That an idol is worth anything, or that food offered to idols means anything?
1 Corinthians 10:20 I say that what non-Jews sacrifice, they offer to evil spirits, not to God, and I don't want you to be associated with evil spirits.
1 Corinthians 10:21 You cannot drink from God's cup and from the cup of demons; you cannot share in God's table and the table of demons.
1 Corinthians 10:22 Are we making God jealous? Are we stronger than God?
1 Corinthians 10:23 I can do anything, but not everything is good for me: I can do anything, but not everything is helpful to others.
1 Corinthians 10:24 Don't just look out for your own interests, but look out for the interests of others too.
1 Corinthians 10:25 Eat anything sold in the market, without worrying about it for the sake of your conscience.
1 Corinthians 10:26 The Earth belongs to God, and everything in it.
1 Corinthians 10:27 If someone who doesn't believe invites you to a dinner and you want to go, eat whatever they serve you without asking questions, to keep a clear conscience.
1 Corinthians 10:28 If someone tells you, "This food was sacrificed to idols," don't eat it for the sake of the person who mentioned it and for conscience. Because the world belongs to God, and everything in it.
1 Corinthians 10:29 I mean your conscience should consider not just yourself, but others too: for why should my freedom be limited by someone else's conscience?
1 Corinthians 10:30 If I have received a gift from God and am thankful for it, why do people criticize me for it?
1 Corinthians 10:31 No matter what you eat, drink, or do, do everything to honor God.
1 Corinthians 10:32 Do not offend anyone, not Jews, not non-Jews, nor God's church.
1 Corinthians 10:33 I try to please everyone in every way, not looking for my own benefit, but for the good of many so that they may be saved.

1 Corinthians 11:1 Follow me, just as I follow Christ.
1 Corinthians 11:2 I am happy, friends, that you remember me in everything and follow the teachings just as I gave them to you.
1 Corinthians 11:3 I want you to understand that Christ leads every man, the man leads the woman, and God leads Christ.
1 Corinthians 11:4 Every man who prays or speaks God's words with his head covered shames his head.
1 Corinthians 11:5 Every woman who prays or speaks God's messages with her head not covered dishonors her head; it's just like if she had her head shaved.
1 Corinthians 11:6 If a woman does not wear a covering, she should cut her hair. But if it is shameful for a woman to have short hair or be shaved, she should cover her head.
1 Corinthians 11:7 A man should not cover his head because he is made in God's image and reflects God's glory. But a woman reflects a man's glory.
1 Corinthians 11:8 The man does not come from the woman, but the woman comes from the man.
1 Corinthians 11:9 The man was not created for the woman, but the woman for the man.
1 Corinthians 11:10 For this reason, a woman should have a symbol of authority on her head, because of the angels.
1 Corinthians 11:11 Still, neither is man complete without woman, nor woman without man, in God.
1 Corinthians 11:12 Just as a woman comes from a man, so does a man come through a woman; but everything comes from God.
1 Corinthians 11:13 Think for yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
1 Corinthians 11:14 Doesn't nature itself show you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him?
1 Corinthians 11:15 If a woman has long hair, it is her pride, because her hair is given to her as a covering.
1 Corinthians 11:16 If anyone likes to argue, we don't have that habit, and neither do God's churches.
1 Corinthians 11:17 In telling you this, I do not praise you, because when you meet, it's not for the good but for the bad.
1 Corinthians 11:18 First, when you meet as a church, I've heard there are splits among you, and I believe it somewhat.
1 Corinthians 11:19 There must also be false beliefs among you, so that those who are true can be clearly seen.
1 Corinthians 11:20 When you meet together in one place, it is not to eat God's supper.
1 Corinthians 11:21 When they eat, some people go first and take their own meal, leaving others hungry while some have too much to drink.
1 Corinthians 11:22 Do you not have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you look down on God's church and embarrass those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I commend you for this? I do not commend you.
1 Corinthians 11:23 I got from God what I also passed on to you: on the night Jesus was betrayed, he took bread.
1 Corinthians 11:24 After thanking God, he broke the bread and said, "Take and eat; this is my body given for you. Do this to remember me."
1 Corinthians 11:25 In the same way, he took the cup after supper and said, "This cup is the new agreement in my blood; do this whenever you drink it, to remember me."
1 Corinthians 11:26 Every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you show the death of God until he comes.
1 Corinthians 11:27 So anyone who eats this bread and drinks this cup of God in a wrong way will be guilty of sinning against God's body and blood.
1 Corinthians 11:28 A person should check themselves before they eat the bread and drink from the cup.
1 Corinthians 11:29 Anyone who eats and drinks without respecting the body of God eats and drinks judgment on themselves.
1 Corinthians 11:30 Because of this, many of you are weak and ill, and a number have died.
1 Corinthians 11:31 If we judge ourselves, we won't be judged by others.
1 Corinthians 11:32 When God corrects us, it's so we won't be punished along with the world.
1 Corinthians 11:33 So, my friends, when you gather to eat, wait for each other.
1 Corinthians 11:34 If anyone is hungry, they should eat at home so that when you meet, it doesn't lead to judgment. I will take care of the other matters when I arrive.

1 Corinthians 12:1 About spiritual gifts, friends, I don't want you to be unaware.
1 Corinthians 12:2 You know that before, as non-Jews, you followed silent idols wherever you were taken.
1 Corinthians 12:3 I want you to know that no one led by God's Spirit says Jesus is cursed, and no one can say Jesus is Lord without the Holy Spirit.
1 Corinthians 12:4 There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
1 Corinthians 12:5 There are different ways to serve, but the same God.
1 Corinthians 12:6 There are different ways of working, but it is the same God who does all the work in everyone.
1 Corinthians 12:7 The Spirit shows itself in each person for the common good.
1 Corinthians 12:8 One person receives wisdom from the Spirit; another gets knowledge from the same Spirit.
1 Corinthians 12:9 To one person the Spirit gives strong faith; to another person the same Spirit gives the power to heal.
1 Corinthians 12:10 One is given the power to perform miracles; another can prophesy; another can distinguish between spirits; another can speak in different languages; and yet another can interpret those languages.
1 Corinthians 12:11 But the same Spirit does all these things, giving to each person different gifts as he chooses.
1 Corinthians 12:12 Just as a body is one unit but has many parts, and all these parts make up one body, it is the same with Christ.
1 Corinthians 12:13 Through one Spirit, we were all baptized into one body, no matter if we are Jews or non-Jews, slaves or free; and we were all given the same Spirit to drink.
1 Corinthians 12:14 The body is not just one part, but many parts.
1 Corinthians 12:15 If the foot says, "Since I am not the hand, I don't belong to the body," does that mean it's not part of the body?
1 Corinthians 12:16 If the ear says, "Because I'm not the eye, I don't belong to the body," does that mean it's not part of the body?
1 Corinthians 12:17 If the whole body were an eye, how could we hear? If it were all ear, how could we smell?
1 Corinthians 12:18 God has placed each part of the body as he wanted.
1 Corinthians 12:19 If they were all one part, where would the body be?
1 Corinthians 12:20 Now there are many parts, but only one body.
1 Corinthians 12:21 The eye can't tell the hand, "I don't need you," and the head can't tell the feet, "I don't need you."
1 Corinthians 12:22 No, even those parts of the body that seem weaker are important.
1 Corinthians 12:23 We give more honor to the parts of the body we think are less worthy, and our less attractive parts get more attention to look better.
1 Corinthians 12:24 Our attractive parts don't need anything, but God has put the body together, giving extra honor to the parts that were lacking.
1 Corinthians 12:25 The body should have no divide; but its parts should care equally for each other.
1 Corinthians 12:26 If one part hurts, all parts hurt with it; if one part is honored, all parts are happy with it.
1 Corinthians 12:27 You are now the body of Christ, each one of you a part of it.
1 Corinthians 12:28 God has placed in the church first apostles, then prophets, next teachers, then those who do miracles, followed by those with healing gifts, helpers, leaders, and different kinds of language speakers.
1 Corinthians 12:29 Are all messengers? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Does everyone perform miracles?
1 Corinthians 12:30 Does everyone have healing gifts? Does everyone speak in different languages? Does everyone explain what is said?
1 Corinthians 12:31 Desire greatly the best gifts; but I will show you an even better way.

1 Corinthians 13:1 If I speak in human and angel languages but don't have love, I am only a loud horn or a clanging cymbal.
1 Corinthians 13:2 Even if I can prophesy, understand all secrets, know everything, and have enough faith to move mountains, but don't have love, I am nothing.
1 Corinthians 13:3 Even if I give away everything I own to help the poor, and even if I sacrifice my body, but do not have love, it does me no good.
1 Corinthians 13:4 Love is patient and kind; love does not envy; love does not boast and is not proud.
1 Corinthians 13:5 Doesn't act improperly, doesn't seek its own benefit, isn't easily angered, doesn't think of doing wrong.
1 Corinthians 13:6 Does not delight in wrong, but celebrates the truth.
1 Corinthians 13:7 Bears everything, believes everything, hopes for everything, endures everything.
1 Corinthians 13:8 Love never ends. But if there are prophecies, they will stop; if there are languages, they will end; if there is knowledge, it will go away.
1 Corinthians 13:9 We know some things and we tell about the future as much as we know.
1 Corinthians 13:10 When the perfect thing comes, the imperfect things will disappear.
1 Corinthians 13:11 When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. But when I grew up, I stopped doing childish things.
1 Corinthians 13:12 Now we see unclearly, as in a mirror; but then we will see clearly, face to face. Now I know only a little; but then I will fully understand, just as I am fully understood.
1 Corinthians 13:13 Now faith, hope, and love remain, these three; but the most important of these is love.

1 Corinthians 14:1 Chase after love and want spiritual gifts, especially to prophesy.
1 Corinthians 14:2 When someone speaks in a language no one knows, they are not speaking to people but to God, because no one can understand them. However, they are saying secret things in their spirit.
1 Corinthians 14:3 The person who prophesies speaks to people to build them up, encourage them, and give them comfort.
1 Corinthians 14:4 Anyone who speaks in a language not known improves himself; but one who prophesies builds up the church.
1 Corinthians 14:5 I wish you could all speak in different languages, but it's better to share God's messages. The one sharing God's messages is more helpful than one speaking in languages, unless they explain it, so the church can learn and grow.
1 Corinthians 14:6 Now, friends, if I come to you speaking in different languages, how will it help you unless I bring you some revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?
1 Corinthians 14:7 Even lifeless things that make noise, like pipes or harps, need to make different sounds. If they don't, how can you tell what is being played?
1 Corinthians 14:8 If the trumpet makes a confusing sound, who will get ready for the fight?
1 Corinthians 14:9 In the same way, if you don't speak clear words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you're saying? Otherwise, you're just talking to the air.
1 Corinthians 14:10 In the world, there might be many different sounds, and each one has its own meaning.
1 Corinthians 14:11 So if I don't understand what someone is saying, I am like a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker is like a foreigner to me.
1 Corinthians 14:12 In the same way, since you are eager for spiritual gifts, try to be the best at building up the church.
1 Corinthians 14:13 So, if someone speaks in a language others don't know, they should pray for the ability to explain it.
1 Corinthians 14:14 If I pray in a language I don't know, my spirit prays but I can't understand it.
1 Corinthians 14:15 So what should be done? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
1 Corinthians 14:16 If you give thanks with your spirit, how can someone who doesn't know what you're saying join in and say "Amen" to your prayer of thanks?
1 Corinthians 14:17 You truly give thanks well, but the other person is not helped.
1 Corinthians 14:18 I thank God, I speak in different languages more than all of you.
1 Corinthians 14:19 In church, I prefer to say five words that I understand to teach others, rather than ten thousand words in a language nobody knows.
1 Corinthians 14:20 Friends, don't be childish in understanding. Yet in bad intentions be like children, but in understanding be adults.
1 Corinthians 14:21 The law says, "I will speak to these people through people with different languages and lips, but even then, they will not listen to me," says God.
1 Corinthians 14:22 So, speaking in different languages is a sign for unbelievers, not believers, while prophesying is for believers, not unbelievers.
1 Corinthians 14:23 So if the whole church meets in one place and everyone starts speaking in different languages, and people who don't understand or don't believe come in, won't they think you are crazy?
1 Corinthians 14:24 If everyone prophesies and an unbeliever or someone who doesn't know about this comes in, they are convinced by everyone and judged by everyone.
1 Corinthians 14:25 The secrets of his heart become clear; he falls down on his face to worship God, saying truly God is with you.
1 Corinthians 14:26 So, friends, when you meet, each of you brings a song, a teaching, a language, a revelation, or an explanation. Make sure that all of these build up the group.
1 Corinthians 14:27 If someone speaks in a language not known, they should do so two or three at a time, taking turns; and there should be one person to explain it.
1 Corinthians 14:28 If there is no interpreter, he should remain quiet in the church; he can speak to himself and to God.
1 Corinthians 14:29 Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others evaluate.
1 Corinthians 14:30 If something is shown to another person sitting nearby, the first person should stop talking.
1 Corinthians 14:31 You can all give messages from God one at a time, so everyone can learn and be encouraged.
1 Corinthians 14:32 The prophets' spirits are under the prophets' control.
1 Corinthians 14:33 God does not create confusion, but peace, in all the churches of the holy people.
1 Corinthians 14:34 Women should keep quiet in churches: they are not allowed to speak, but must be submissive, as the law also says.
1 Corinthians 14:35 If they want to learn something, they should ask their husbands at home, because it's shameful for women to talk in the church.
1 Corinthians 14:36 Did God's message originate with you? Or was it given to only you?
1 Corinthians 14:37 If someone believes they are a prophet or spiritual, they should accept that what I am writing to you are God's commands.
1 Corinthians 14:38 If someone does not know, let them not know.
1 Corinthians 14:39 Friends, want to prophesy and do not stop others from speaking in different tongues.
1 Corinthians 14:40 Do everything properly and in an organized way.

1 Corinthians 15:1 Friends, I tell you the good news I gave you, which you accepted and still follow.
1 Corinthians 15:2 You are saved by this too, if you remember what I told you, unless your belief was for nothing.
1 Corinthians 15:3 I first told you what I was also told: Christ died for our sins as the writings said.
1 Corinthians 15:4 He was buried and rose again on the third day, just as the scriptures said.
1 Corinthians 15:5 He was seen by Cephas, then by the twelve.
1 Corinthians 15:6 After that, more than five hundred followers saw him at one time; most of them are still alive today, though some have died.
1 Corinthians 15:7 After that, James saw him; then all the apostles did.
1 Corinthians 15:8 Lastly, he was seen by me too, like someone born at the wrong time.
1 Corinthians 15:9 I am the least of the apostles and not worthy to be called an apostle because I persecuted God's church.
1 Corinthians 15:10 Because of God's kindness, I am who I am, and his kindness to me was not wasted; I worked harder than all of them, yet it was not me, but God's kindness with me.
1 Corinthians 15:11 So whether it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
1 Corinthians 15:12 If we preach that Christ rose from the dead, why do some of you say that the dead are not raised?
1 Corinthians 15:13 If the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised.
1 Corinthians 15:14 If Christ has not been raised, then our teaching is useless, and so is your faith.
1 Corinthians 15:15 Yes, and we are proven liars about God; because we claimed that God brought Christ back to life, which He didn't do if it's true that the dead don't come back to life.
1 Corinthians 15:16 If the dead don't rise, then Christ has not been raised either.
1 Corinthians 15:17 If Christ has not been raised, your faith is useless; you are still guilty of your sins.
1 Corinthians 15:18 Then those who have died believing in Christ are also lost.
1 Corinthians 15:19 If we only hope in Christ for this life, we are the most unhappy of all people.
1 Corinthians 15:20 Now Christ has risen from the dead and is the first to rise from those who have died.
1 Corinthians 15:21 Death came through a person, and the raising of the dead also came through a person.
1 Corinthians 15:22 Just as everyone dies because of Adam, so everyone will be given life because of Christ.
1 Corinthians 15:23 Everyone will be raised to life in their own turn: Christ was the first; then, when he comes, those who belong to him will be raised to life.
1 Corinthians 15:24 The end comes when he hands over the kingdom to God, the Father, after he ends all control, authority, and power.
1 Corinthians 15:25 He must rule until he has defeated all his enemies.
1 Corinthians 15:26 The final enemy to be destroyed is death.
1 Corinthians 15:27 God has placed everything under his control, but when it is said that everything is under him, it's clear that this does not include God who put everything under his control.
1 Corinthians 15:28 When everything is under his control, then the Son will also be under the one who gave him power over everything, so that God will be everything to everyone.
1 Corinthians 15:29 What will those who are baptized for the dead do if the dead are not raised at all? Why are they baptized for the dead?
1 Corinthians 15:30 Why do we risk our lives every hour?
1 Corinthians 15:31 I assure you by the happiness I have in Christ Jesus our God, I face death every day.
1 Corinthians 15:32 If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus just as people do, what good is it to me if the dead don't rise again? Let's eat and drink, because tomorrow we will die.
1 Corinthians 15:33 Don't be fooled: bad company ruins good character.
1 Corinthians 15:34 Wake up to what is right, and do not sin; because some do not know God: I say this to make you ashamed.
1 Corinthians 15:35 Someone might ask, "How are the dead brought back to life? And what kind of body will they have?"
1 Corinthians 15:36 You fool, what you plant won't come to life unless it dies first.
1 Corinthians 15:37 When you plant, you do not plant the full-grown plant, but just a seed, maybe wheat or another kind.
1 Corinthians 15:38 God gives it a body as he wants, and to every seed its own body.
1 Corinthians 15:39 Not all living beings have the same body: humans have one kind, animals another, fish another, and birds another.
1 Corinthians 15:40 There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies: the beauty of the heavenly is one kind, and the beauty of the earthly is another kind.
1 Corinthians 15:41 The sun has one kind of beauty, the moon another, and the stars another; and each star is different in its beauty.
1 Corinthians 15:42 The resurrection of the dead is like this: What is buried decays, but what is raised cannot decay.
1 Corinthians 15:43 It is planted with shame; it is raised with honor: it is planted weak; it is raised strong.
1 Corinthians 15:44 A physical body is planted; a spiritual body is raised. There is a physical body, and there is a spiritual body.
1 Corinthians 15:45 The first man, Adam, became a living being; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
1 Corinthians 15:46 The natural life comes first, not the spiritual one; the spiritual life comes after.
1 Corinthians 15:47 The first man comes from the earth and is made of earth; the second man comes from heaven and is the Lord.
1 Corinthians 15:48 People from the earth are like the earth; those from heaven are like heaven.
1 Corinthians 15:49 We have carried the likeness of the earthly, and we will also carry the likeness of the heavenly.
1 Corinthians 15:50 I tell you, friends, that our physical bodies cannot enter God's kingdom; and what is perishable cannot become imperishable.
1 Corinthians 15:51 Look, I tell you a secret; not all of us will die, but we will all be changed.
1 Corinthians 15:52 In a moment, in a quick blink, when the final trumpet sounds, the trumpet will blow, the dead will rise never to die again, and we will be different.
1 Corinthians 15:53 This body that can be destroyed must become one that cannot be destroyed, and this body that can die must become one that cannot die.
1 Corinthians 15:54 When what can decay becomes undying, and what can die becomes immortal, then the saying that is written will happen: Death is overcome by triumph.
1 Corinthians 15:55 Death, where is your sting? Grave, where is your victory?
1 Corinthians 15:56 Death hurts because of sin; and sin is powerful because of the law.
1 Corinthians 15:57 Thank God, who gives us victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 15:58 So, my dear friends, remain firm, unshaken, always doing plenty in God’s work, because you know that what you do for God is never useless.

1 Corinthians 16:1 About the money being gathered for God's people, do as I told the churches in Galatia to do.
1 Corinthians 16:2 On the first day of the week, each of you should set aside some money in keeping with how much God has blessed you, so that we won't need to collect money when I arrive.
1 Corinthians 16:3 When I arrive, whoever you choose and recommend in your letters, I will send them to take your gift to Jerusalem.
1 Corinthians 16:4 If it's right that I go too, they will go with me.
1 Corinthians 16:5 I will come to you after I travel through Macedonia because I am going through Macedonia.
1 Corinthians 16:6 I might stay and spend the winter with you, so you can help me continue my trip wherever I go.
1 Corinthians 16:7 I won't visit you now as I travel; but I hope to stay with you for a bit, if God allows.
1 Corinthians 16:8 But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost.
1 Corinthians 16:9 A big and powerful opportunity has come to me, and there are many opponents.
1 Corinthians 16:10 If Timothy comes, make sure he can be with you without fear, because he is doing God's work, just like I am.
1 Corinthians 16:11 Don't let anyone look down on him. Send him off in peace so he can come to me, because I am expecting him with the others.
1 Corinthians 16:12 About our friend Apollos, I really wanted him to visit you with the others, but he did not want to come right now. He will come when he has a good time.
1 Corinthians 16:13 Stay alert, stand firm in your belief, be brave and strong.
1 Corinthians 16:14 Do everything with love.
1 Corinthians 16:15 I ask you, friends, you know Stephanas's family was the first to believe in Achaia, and they have dedicated themselves to serving God's people.
1 Corinthians 16:16 Submit to such people, and to everyone who works and labors with us.
1 Corinthians 16:17 I am happy Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus came because they have provided what you could not.
1 Corinthians 16:18 They have uplifted my spirit and yours; so recognize those like them.
1 Corinthians 16:19 The churches in Asia send their greetings to you. Aquila and Priscilla send a warm greeting in God, along with the church that meets in their home.
1 Corinthians 16:20 All the friends send their greetings. Greet each other with a sacred kiss.
1 Corinthians 16:21 I, Paul, greet you with my own hand.
1 Corinthians 16:22 If someone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let that person be cursed.
1 Corinthians 16:23 May the kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
1 Corinthians 16:24 My love is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

2 Corinthians 1:1 Paul, a messenger of Jesus Christ chosen by God, and Timothy our brother, to God's church in Corinth and all God's holy people throughout Achaia:
2 Corinthians 1:2 May you have kindness and peace from God our Father and from Jesus Christ.
2 Corinthians 1:3 Praise God, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the giver of mercy, and the source of all comfort.
2 Corinthians 1:4 God comforts us in all our troubles so we can comfort others in trouble with the same comfort we receive from God.
2 Corinthians 1:5 Just as we have many sufferings like Christ, we also have much comfort through Christ.
2 Corinthians 1:6 When we face troubles, it's to help and save you. This help works when you patiently go through the same pains we also have. And when we are comforted, it's to help and save you too.
2 Corinthians 1:7 We are sure of our hope for you, knowing that just as you share in the sufferings, you will also share in the comfort.
2 Corinthians 1:8 We don't want you, friends, to be unaware of the hardships we faced in Asia. We were under great pressure, beyond our ability to endure, so much that we lost hope of living.
2 Corinthians 1:9 We felt like we were sentenced to die, so that we wouldn't rely on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.
2 Corinthians 1:10 God saved us from a terrible death, continues to save us, and we trust will keep on saving us.
2 Corinthians 1:11 You also help us by praying together, so many can give thanks for the gift given to us through many people.
2 Corinthians 1:12 We are happy because we know in our hearts that we have lived in the world with simplicity and sincere faith in God, not with human wisdom but by God's grace, and especially so in our behavior towards you.
2 Corinthians 1:13 We write nothing else to you than what you read and understand, and I hope you will understand fully to the end.
2 Corinthians 1:14 You have recognized that we are your reason to be proud, just as you are ours when Jesus returns.
2 Corinthians 1:15 I planned to visit you first so you could be blessed twice.
2 Corinthians 1:16 I plan to go through your area to Macedonia, then return from Macedonia to you, and then have you help me on my journey to Judea.
2 Corinthians 1:17 So when I decided this, did I do it lightly? Or do I make plans in a worldly way, so that in the same breath I say both "Yes, yes" and "No, no"?
2 Corinthians 1:18 But as God is truthful, our message to you wasn't yes and no.
2 Corinthians 1:19 God's Son, Jesus Christ, who we told you about—me, Silvanus, and Timotheus—wasn't sometimes yes and sometimes no; in him, it was always yes.
2 Corinthians 1:20 All of God's promises in him are yes, and in him, so be it, to show the greatness of God through us.
2 Corinthians 1:21 God makes us strong with you in Christ and has chosen us.
2 Corinthians 1:22 God has also sealed us and given us the Spirit as a promise in our hearts.
2 Corinthians 1:23 I tell you before God, I did not come to Corinth yet to avoid being hard on you.
2 Corinthians 1:24 We don't control your faith, but help bring you joy: you stand strong because of faith.

2 Corinthians 2:1 I decided not to visit you again while feeling sad.
2 Corinthians 2:2 If I make you sad, who can cheer me up except the one I’ve made sad?
2 Corinthians 2:3 I wrote this to you so that when I come, I won't be sad about those I should be happy about, trusting that what makes me happy also makes all of you happy.
2 Corinthians 2:4 I wrote to you with a heavy heart and many tears, not to make you sad, but to show you how much I love you.
2 Corinthians 2:5 If someone has caused sadness, they haven't deeply saddened me, but only to a small extent, so as not to weigh you all down too much.
2 Corinthians 2:6 This punishment, given by many, is enough for that person.
2 Corinthians 2:7 So instead you should forgive and comfort him, so he isn't overcome with too much sadness.
2 Corinthians 2:8 So I urge you to show him your love clearly.
2 Corinthians 2:9 I wrote for this reason too, so I could see if you would follow all instructions.
2 Corinthians 2:10 If you forgive anyone, I also forgive them. If I have forgiven anything, I did it for you in the way of Christ.
2 Corinthians 2:11 So Satan won't outsmart us: we know his tricks.
2 Corinthians 2:12 When I went to Troas to tell people about Christ, God opened an opportunity for me.
2 Corinthians 2:13 I could not rest because I did not find my brother Titus. So, I said goodbye and went to Macedonia.
2 Corinthians 2:14 Thank you to God, who always leads us to victory in Christ and shows the value of his knowledge through us everywhere.
2 Corinthians 2:15 We are like a pleasing fragrance of Christ to God, among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.
2 Corinthians 2:16 To some, we smell like death leading to more death; to others, we smell like life leading to more life. Who is fit for such tasks?
2 Corinthians 2:17 We are not like some who misuse God's words. We speak with honesty, as from God and in God's presence, we speak in Christ.

2 Corinthians 3:1 Are we starting to praise ourselves again? Do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to or from you?
2 Corinthians 3:2 You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by everyone.
2 Corinthians 3:3 It is clear that you are Christ's letter, delivered by us, not written with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on the human heart's living pages.
2 Corinthians 3:4 We have this confidence in God through Christ.
2 Corinthians 3:5 We are not capable on our own to consider anything as coming from ourselves; our ability comes from God.
2 Corinthians 3:6 God has also made us skilled servants of the new agreement; not by the written laws, but by the spirit: because the written laws can cause death, but the spirit gives life.
2 Corinthians 3:7 But if the service of death, written on stones, was so bright that the people of Israel could not look straight at Moses's face because of its shine, which was passing away:
2 Corinthians 3:8 How could serving in the Spirit not be more glorious?
2 Corinthians 3:9 For if the service that brings condemnation is glorious, the service that brings righteousness is far more glorious.
2 Corinthians 3:10 Even what used to be glorious has no glory now compared to the greater glory.
2 Corinthians 3:11 If something that ends was great, then what stays is even greater.
2 Corinthians 3:12 Since we have this hope, we speak very clearly.
2 Corinthians 3:13 Unlike Moses, who covered his face with a veil to prevent the Israelites from seeing the end of the fading glory.
2 Corinthians 3:14 Their minds were closed. Even today, the same covering stays when they read the old covenant, not removed because it is taken away through Christ.
2 Corinthians 3:15 But even now, when people read about Moses, their hearts are covered like with a veil.
2 Corinthians 3:16 When people turn to God, the veil will be removed.
2 Corinthians 3:17 Now God is that Spirit, and where God's Spirit is, there is freedom.
2 Corinthians 3:18 We all, with uncovered faces, look at God's glory as if looking in a mirror and are transformed to become more like Him, from one degree of glory to another, by God's Spirit.

2 Corinthians 4:1 Because we are given this service and have received kindness, we do not lose heart.
2 Corinthians 4:2 We have turned away from secret and shameful ways; we do not use trickery, nor do we distort God's message. Instead, by clearly showing the truth, we prove ourselves to everyone's conscience in God's presence.
2 Corinthians 4:3 If our good news is hidden, it's hidden from those who are lost.
2 Corinthians 4:4 The god of this world has made the minds of unbelievers so they can't see. This way, the bright Good News about Christ, who is like God, doesn't shine on them.
2 Corinthians 4:5 We do not speak about ourselves, but we speak about Jesus Christ as the Lord; and we are your servants because of Jesus.
2 Corinthians 4:6 God, who made light shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts to give us the understanding of God's glory shown in Jesus Christ's face.
2 Corinthians 4:7 We hold this treasure in clay jars, so that the power shown is God's and not ours.
2 Corinthians 4:8 We face troubles on all sides but are not crushed; we are confused but not hopeless.
2 Corinthians 4:9 Chased, but not abandoned; knocked down, but not ruined;
2 Corinthians 4:10 Always carrying in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be shown in our body.
2 Corinthians 4:11 We who are alive are always facing death for Jesus so that Jesus' life can also be shown in our dying bodies.
2 Corinthians 4:12 So death is active in us, but life is in you.
2 Corinthians 4:13 We have the same spirit of faith, just as it is written, "I believed, and so I spoke." We also believe, and so we speak.
2 Corinthians 4:14 Understanding that God, who raised Jesus, will also raise us with Jesus, and will bring us together with you.
2 Corinthians 4:15 Everything is for you, so that God's great kindness can spread to more people, making them grateful and honoring God.
2 Corinthians 4:16 We don't lose heart, for even if our bodies are failing, our true self is renewed every day.
2 Corinthians 4:17 Our small troubles, which last only a short time, are earning us a much greater and lasting glory.
2 Corinthians 4:18 We focus not on what can be seen, but on what cannot be seen. What is seen is temporary; what is unseen is forever.

2 Corinthians 5:1 We know that if our earthly body is destroyed, we have a home from God, a place not built by hands, lasting forever in heaven.
2 Corinthians 5:2 In this we deeply long to be covered by our heavenly home.
2 Corinthians 5:3 If we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
2 Corinthians 5:4 We who live in this body sigh because we feel heavy, not because we want to remove our bodies, but to add to them so that our dying can be completely absorbed by life.
2 Corinthians 5:5 God made us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a guarantee.
2 Corinthians 5:6 So we always feel sure, because we know that while we live in our bodies, we are away from God.
2 Corinthians 5:7 We live by trusting, not by seeing.
2 Corinthians 5:8 We are sure and would prefer to be away from our body and to be with God.
2 Corinthians 5:9 We work hard so that, whether we are with him or away from him, we may be pleasing to God.
2 Corinthians 5:10 We all must stand before Christ to be judged; so that each person receives what they did on Earth, good or bad.
2 Corinthians 5:11 Understanding God's awesome power, we try to convince people; we are clearly seen by God, and I hope we are also clear in your hearts.
2 Corinthians 5:12 We are not praising ourselves to you again, but we are giving you a reason to be proud of us so you can have something to say to those who take pride in what they look like, rather than what is in their heart.
2 Corinthians 5:13 Whether we seem crazy, it's for God, or if we act sensibly, it's for you.
2 Corinthians 5:14 Christ's love compels us; we believe that since one died for everyone, then everyone was dead.
2 Corinthians 5:15 He died for everyone, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and came back to life.
2 Corinthians 5:16 From now on, we don't know anyone in a worldly way; even if we once knew Christ in this way, we don't know him like that anymore.
2 Corinthians 5:17 So if anyone is with Christ, they are a new person: the old has gone, and everything is new.
2 Corinthians 5:18 Everything comes from God, who brought us back to himself through Jesus Christ and has given us the task of bringing others back to him.
2 Corinthians 5:19 God was in Christ, bringing the world back to himself, not holding people's sins against them; and he has trusted us with the message of reconciliation.
2 Corinthians 5:20 We are Christ's representatives, and it's as if God is asking you through us: we urge you on behalf of Christ, make peace with God.
2 Corinthians 5:21 God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the goodness of God.

2 Corinthians 6:1 We, as partners with God, urge you not to take God's kindness for nothing.
2 Corinthians 6:2 God says, "I have listened to you at the right time, and on the day of rescue, I have helped you. Look, now is the right time; now is the day of rescue."
2 Corinthians 6:3 Not causing trouble in anything, so that no one can criticize our service.
2 Corinthians 6:4 We show we are God's servants in everything by being patient, during troubles, when we need things, and in hard times.
2 Corinthians 6:5 Through beatings, jail time, riots, hard work, sleepless nights, and times without food;
2 Corinthians 6:6 Through purity, understanding, patience, kindness, the Holy Spirit, and genuine love,
2 Corinthians 6:7 By the true message, by God's power, by the right ways to act on both sides,
2 Corinthians 6:8 Through praise and criticism, by bad and good reputation: seen as liars, but truthful.
2 Corinthians 6:9 Although unknown, we are well recognized; although we face death, see, we live; although disciplined, we are not put to death.
2 Corinthians 6:10 Feeling sad but always happy; being poor but making many rich; owning nothing but having everything.
2 Corinthians 6:11 People of Corinth, we speak openly to you; our hearts are full of love for you.
2 Corinthians 6:12 You are not limited by us, but you are limited by your own feelings.
2 Corinthians 6:13 Now, to repay me in the same way, (I'm speaking to you as my children,) you should also open your hearts to us.
2 Corinthians 6:14 Don't team up with those who don't believe: what do good and bad have in common? Or what can light share with darkness?
2 Corinthians 6:15 What agreement does Christ have with Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
2 Corinthians 6:16 What deal does God's temple have with idols? You are the living God's temple. God said, I will live in them and be with them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
2 Corinthians 6:17 So leave them and be different, says God, and do not touch dirty things; then I will accept you.
2 Corinthians 6:18 I will be a Father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters, says God Almighty.

2 Corinthians 7:1 So with these promises, dear friends, let's clean ourselves from every dirty thing of body and spirit, making our holiness complete by respecting God.
2 Corinthians 7:2 Accept us; we have not wronged anyone, we have not corrupted anyone, we have not cheated anyone.
2 Corinthians 7:3 I am not saying this to blame you: I have already told you that you are so dear to us, we would happily live or die with you.
2 Corinthians 7:4 I speak to you with great confidence, and I take great pride in you. I am filled with comfort and am very happy, even during our troubles.
2 Corinthians 7:5 When we arrived in Macedonia, we had no peace. We faced problems everywhere; there were conflicts outside and fears inside.
2 Corinthians 7:6 God, who comforts the discouraged, cheered us up with Titus's arrival.
2 Corinthians 7:7 Not just his arrival, but also the comfort he got from you made me happy, as he shared your strong desire, your sadness, and your warm feelings for me; this made me even happier.
2 Corinthians 7:8 Even though my letter made you sad, I don't regret it, even though I did feel sorry before. I see now that the letter made you sad, but only for a little while.
2 Corinthians 7:9 I'm glad not because you were upset, but because your sadness led to change. Your sorrow was for the right reasons, so it didn't harm you because of us.
2 Corinthians 7:10 Feeling truly sorry for our wrongs leads to a change of heart that brings us to be saved, and we won't regret it; but worldly sadness only leads to death.
2 Corinthians 7:11 Look at how seriously you took your sadness, leading to earnestness, a desire to clear yourselves, anger at wrong, fear of doing wrong, strong longing to do right, passion for truth, and a determination to make things right! You have shown that you are innocent in this matter.
2 Corinthians 7:12 I wrote to you not because of the person who did wrong, or the person who was wronged, but to show you our concern for you before God.
2 Corinthians 7:13 So we were cheered up by your encouragement and even more happy about Titus's joy, because you all made him feel better.
2 Corinthians 7:14 If I have praised you to him, I am not embarrassed; just as everything we told you was true, our praises to Titus about you are also true.
2 Corinthians 7:15 His deep feelings for you are very strong as he remembers how all of you obeyed and welcomed him with respect and nervousness.
2 Corinthians 7:16 I am happy because I trust you in everything.

2 Corinthians 8:1 Also, friends, we want you to know about the kindness God gave to the churches in Macedonia.
2 Corinthians 8:2 They were very joyful in hard times, and though very poor, they were very generous.
2 Corinthians 8:3 They gave as much as they could, I can testify, and even beyond their ability, they did it willingly on their own.
2 Corinthians 8:4 They asked us earnestly to accept the gift and share in serving the holy people.
2 Corinthians 8:5 They did this, not in the way we expected, but they first offered themselves to God, and then to us, because God wanted it that way.
2 Corinthians 8:6 We really wanted Titus to complete the good work he started with you.
2 Corinthians 8:7 So, as you excel in everything, in faith, speech, knowledge, complete effort, and love for us, make sure you also excel in this kindness.
2 Corinthians 8:8 I'm not telling you this as a rule, but to show how eager others are, and to test how genuine your love is.
2 Corinthians 8:9 You know about the kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, that even though he was rich, he became poor for your sake, so that by his poverty you could become rich.
2 Corinthians 8:10 I offer this advice: it is good for you, who started to give last year, to not only continue but also to be eager to finish.
2 Corinthians 8:11 So now, do what you have planned; just as you were eager to want to do it, make sure you also complete it with what you have.
2 Corinthians 8:12 If someone is willing to give, it is appreciated for what they can afford, not for what they cannot.
2 Corinthians 8:13 I don't want others to have it easy while you are burdened.
2 Corinthians 8:14 Let there be fairness so your plenty can help others who need it, and in turn, their plenty can help you when you need it, so that everyone has what they need.
2 Corinthians 8:15 It is written, whoever collected a lot had nothing extra, and whoever collected a little did not fall short.
2 Corinthians 8:16 Thank God, who placed the same sincere concern in Titus's heart for you.
2 Corinthians 8:17 He truly welcomed the encouragement, but being more eager, he went to you on his own initiative.
2 Corinthians 8:18 We have sent him along with our brother, who is well known in the churches for his work in sharing the good news.
2 Corinthians 8:19 And not only that, but he was also picked by the churches to go with us with this kindness, which is given by us for the honor of God, and to show your willingness.
2 Corinthians 8:20 We avoid any blame about how we handle this large amount by being careful.
2 Corinthians 8:21 Taking care of what is right, not just before God, but also before people.
2 Corinthians 8:22 We've sent our brother with them. We've often found he works hard in many things, but now he's even more careful because I trust you a lot.
2 Corinthians 8:23 If anyone asks about Titus, he is my partner and helper for you. If they ask about our brothers, they are the church's messengers and show Christ's honor.
2 Corinthians 8:24 Show them, and all the churches, how much you love and that we were right to boast about you.

2 Corinthians 11:6 Even if I speak simply, it doesn't mean I lack knowledge; we have clearly shown you this in everything.

2 Corinthians 11:15 So it's not surprising if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of what is right; their end will match their actions.

2 Corinthians 11:17 What I am saying, I do not say as God would want but rather, I speak foolishly, as if I am confident and proud.

2 Corinthians 11:22 Are they Hebrews? I am too. Are they Israelites? I am too. Are they descendants of Abraham? I am too.
2 Corinthians 11:23 Are they serving Christ? (I talk like a foolish person) I serve even more. I've worked harder, been whipped more, jailed more, and faced death often.
2 Corinthians 11:24 I was whipped with 39 lashes by the Jews five times.
2 Corinthians 11:25 I was beaten with rods three times, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, and I spent a night and a day in the ocean.
2 Corinthians 11:26 Often traveling, facing dangers from floods, robbers, my own people, foreigners, city dangers, wilderness risks, sea threats, and among those pretending to be friends.
2 Corinthians 11:27 Feeling tired and pain, staying awake a lot, being hungry and thirsty, fasting many times, feeling cold and without enough clothes.
2 Corinthians 11:28 Apart from outside matters, I face daily the concern for all the churches.
2 Corinthians 11:29 Who is weak without me feeling weak? Who is upset without me being angry?
2 Corinthians 11:30 If I must boast, I will boast about my weaknesses.
2 Corinthians 11:31 God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is forever blessed, knows I am not lying.
2 Corinthians 11:32 In Damascus, the governor working for King Aretas guarded the city with soldiers because he wanted to arrest me.
2 Corinthians 11:33 Through a window in a basket, I was lowered down the wall and got away from him.
