Galatians 1:1 Paul, an apostle not chosen by people or through a person, but by Jesus Christ and God who brought him back from the dead.
Galatians 1:2 Me and all the friends here send greetings to the churches in Galatia.
Galatians 1:3 May you have kindness and peace from God the Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.
Galatians 1:4 He gave himself for our sins so he could save us from this evil world, as God our Father wanted.
Galatians 1:5 May glory be to God forever and ever. Amen.
Galatians 1:6 I am amazed that you are quickly turning away from God who called you by Christ's grace to a different good news.
Galatians 1:7 This is not really a different gospel, but some are troubling you, wanting to twist Christ's good news.
Galatians 1:8 Even if we or an angel from heaven tell you a different good news than what we already told you, that person should be considered cursed.
Galatians 1:9 I told you before, and I say it again, if anyone teaches a different message than what you received, they should be rejected.
Galatians 1:10 Am I now trying to win over people or God? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I wouldn't be Christ's servant.
Galatians 1:11 I assure you, friends, that the good news I shared was not made by people.
Galatians 1:12 I did not get it from any person, nor was I taught it, but Jesus Christ revealed it to me.
Galatians 1:13 You have heard about how I lived long ago, following the Jewish religion, and how I persecuted God's church greatly and tried to destroy it.
Galatians 1:14 I advanced in the Jewish faith more than many peers in my country, being much more passionate about the traditions of my ancestors.
Galatians 1:15 But when God, who set me apart from birth and called me by his kindness,
Galatians 1:16 To show his Son through me, so I could tell about him to non-believers; I did not immediately consult with any person.
Galatians 1:17 I did not go to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me; instead, I went to Arabia and then came back to Damascus.
Galatians 1:18 Three years later, I went to Jerusalem to meet Peter and stayed with him for fifteen days.
Galatians 1:19 I did not see any other apostles, only James, the brother of the Lord.
Galatians 1:20 I am telling you the truth, I am not lying, and God knows this.
Galatians 1:21 Next, I went to the areas of Syria and Cilicia.
Galatians 1:22 The churches in Judea that belonged to Christ did not know me by face.
Galatians 1:23 They had only heard that the one who used to persecute us now preaches the faith he once tried to destroy.
Galatians 1:24 They praised God because of me.

Galatians 2:1 Fourteen years later, I went back to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and I also brought Titus with me.
Galatians 2:2 I went up because God showed me to do so, and I explained to them the good news I share with non-Jews, but only to those with high status, to avoid my efforts being useless.
Galatians 2:3 Titus, who was with me and is Greek, was not forced to be circumcised.
Galatians 2:4 This is because some fake friends were secretly brought in to check on the freedom we have in Jesus Christ, to try and make us slaves again.
Galatians 2:5 We did not submit to them, not even for a moment, so that the truth of the good news would remain with you.
Galatians 2:6 But those who seemed important—whatever they were, it doesn't matter to me; God does not show favoritism—did not add anything to my message.
Galatians 2:7 But on the other hand, when they realized that I was trusted with the message for the non-Jewish people, just as Peter was for the Jewish people;
Galatians 2:8 For the same power that worked in Peter to serve the Jews worked powerfully in me to serve the non-Jews.
Galatians 2:9 When James, Cephas, and John, who appeared to be leaders, saw the grace given to me, they offered me and Barnabas a welcoming handshake; agreeing that we'd go to the non-Jews and they to the Jews.
Galatians 2:10 They only asked us to remember the poor, which I was also eager to do.
Galatians 2:11 When Peter came to Antioch, I confronted him directly because he was wrong.
Galatians 2:12 Before some people came from James, Peter ate with non-Jews. But when they arrived, he pulled back and kept away because he was afraid of the group that insisted on circumcision.
Galatians 2:13 The other Jews also pretended like him; even Barnabas was led to join them in their pretense.
Galatians 2:14 When I saw they were not living right according to the gospel's truth, I told Peter in front of everyone, "If you, a Jew, live like the Gentiles and not like the Jews, why do you force the Gentiles to follow Jewish ways?"
Galatians 2:15 We who are born Jewish, and not Gentile sinners,
Galatians 2:16 Understanding that a person is not made right by following the law, but by believing in Jesus Christ, we too have put our faith in Jesus Christ so we can be made right by trusting in Christ, not by following the law, because no one will be made right by following the law.
Galatians 2:17 But if we try to be accepted by Christ and are still found as sinners, does that mean Christ supports sin? Definitely not.
Galatians 2:18 If I rebuild what I destroyed, I show that I was wrong.
Galatians 2:19 Through the law, I am as if dead to it, so that I might live for God.

Philippians 1:14 Many believers in God, seeing my imprisonment, are now much braver to talk about God's message fearlessly.
Philippians 1:15 Some people spread the message about Christ because they are jealous and like to argue; but others do it with good intentions.
Philippians 1:16 Some preach about Christ with bad intentions, not honestly, thinking they will make my imprisonment harder.
Philippians 1:17 But the other preaches out of love, knowing that I stand to defend the gospel.
Philippians 1:18 So what? In every way, whether fake or real, Christ is talked about; and I'm happy about this, yes, and I'll keep being happy.
Philippians 1:19 I know that this will lead to my rescue because of your prayers and Jesus Christ's Spirit's help.
Philippians 1:20 I really hope and expect that I won't be ashamed in any way. I want to be very brave now as I always have been, and have Christ honored in my body, whether I live or die.
Philippians 1:21 For me, living means following Christ, and dying is a benefit.
Philippians 1:22 If I continue living in my body, this means I can keep working. But I do not know what I should choose.
Philippians 1:23 I am torn between two choices: wanting to leave and be with Christ, which is much better.
Philippians 1:24 Staying alive is more important for your sake.
Philippians 1:25 Because I am sure of this, I know that I will stay and be with all of you to help your faith grow and to share joy in believing.
Philippians 1:26 I want you to be happier about Jesus Christ because of my visit to you again.
Philippians 1:27 Make sure you live in a way that fits with the good news about Christ. This way, whether I visit you or I'm away, I can hear about you. I want to know that you are standing strong together with one purpose, working as a team for the faith the good news brings.
Philippians 1:28 Don't be scared of your enemies at all: to them it's a clear sign they'll be ruined, but for you it means being saved, which comes from God.
Philippians 1:29 God has granted you the gift not only to believe in Christ but also to endure hardship for him.
Philippians 1:30 You are facing the same struggle that you saw I had, and now you hear that I still have.

Philippians 2:1 So, if there is any comfort from being united with Christ, if any love brings comfort, if we share in the Spirit, if there is any warmth and kindness,
Philippians 2:2 Make my joy complete by agreeing with each other, sharing the same love, and being united in thoughts and purpose.
Philippians 2:3 Do nothing out of fighting or empty pride; instead, with humble minds, value others more than yourselves.
Philippians 2:4 Don't just look out for your own interests, but also for the interests of others.
Philippians 2:5 Have the same mindset as Jesus Christ did.
Philippians 2:6 Even though he was like God, he did not see being equal with God as something to hold onto.
Philippians 2:7 He made himself humble, became a servant, and was born as a human.
Philippians 2:8 Being found as a man, he became humble and obeyed to the point of death, even dying on a cross.
Philippians 2:9 So God has lifted him high and given him a name greater than any other name.
Philippians 2:10 Everyone should kneel to honor Jesus' name - those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.
Philippians 2:11 Everyone should agree that Jesus Christ is the Lord to honor God the Father.
Philippians 2:12 So, my dear friends, just as you have always followed, not only when I am with you but even more now that I'm not, keep working on your own rescue with respect and care.
Philippians 2:13 God is the one who makes you want to do and actually do what pleases Him.
Philippians 2:14 Do everything without complaining or arguing.
Philippians 2:15 So that you may be pure and good, children of God, without fault, in a wicked and twisted world, where you shine like stars.
Philippians 2:16 Offering the message of life; so I can be joyful when Christ comes, knowing my efforts were not wasted.
Philippians 2:17 Yes, and if I am like a drink offering on the offering and service of your faith, I am happy and share joy with all of you.
Philippians 2:18 For this reason, you too be glad and share my joy.
Philippians 2:19 I hope Jesus will let me send Timothy to you soon, so I can feel better after learning how you are doing.
Philippians 2:20 I have no one else who truly cares for your well-being.
Philippians 2:21 Everyone looks out for their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
Philippians 2:22 You know how he has shown himself, like a son with his father, working with me to spread the good news.
Philippians 2:23 So I plan to send him to you soon, once I know what will happen with me.
Philippians 2:24 I trust in God that I will also come soon.
Philippians 2:25 I thought it was important to send Epaphroditus to you – my brother, coworker, and fellow soldier – who is also your messenger and has helped me with my needs.
Philippians 2:26 He really missed you all and was very worried because you heard he was ill.
Philippians 2:27 He was really sick, almost dying, but God showed mercy on him; not just on him, but on me too, so I wouldn't have even more sadness.
Philippians 2:28 I sent him with extra care so that when you see him again, you can be happy and I can be less sad.
Philippians 2:29 Welcome him in the name of God with joy; and respect such people.
Philippians 2:30 He was near death because of his work for Christ, risking his life to help me when you could not.

Philippians 3:1 Friends, be happy in God. Writing the same things to you is not hard for me and it keeps you safe.
Philippians 3:2 Be careful of dogs, be careful of bad people, be careful of those who cut the body.
Philippians 3:3 We are the people who serve God with our hearts, find joy in Jesus, and do not trust in our own power.
Philippians 3:4 I could also trust in human ability. If anyone else thinks they can trust in human ability, I have even more reason to:
Philippians 3:5 Circumcised on the eighth day, from Israel's people, from the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born from Hebrews; and concerning the law, a Pharisee.
Philippians 3:6 Eager to defend my beliefs, I attacked the church; but following the law's rules, I was faultless.
Philippians 3:7 The things that were valuable to me, I now consider worthless because of Christ.
Philippians 3:8 Yes, I consider everything a loss compared to the great value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For him, I've lost all things and see them as trash, so that I can have Christ.
Philippians 3:9 Be in unity with him, not with my own goodness from following the law, but with the goodness that comes through faith in Christ, the goodness from God that relies on faith.
Philippians 3:10 So I can know him, the power of his rising again, sharing in his sufferings, and becoming like him in his death.
Philippians 3:11 I hope somehow to be raised to life after death.
Philippians 3:12 It's not like I've already succeeded or am already perfect, but I keep trying to reach what Jesus Christ chose me for.
Philippians 3:13 Friends, I don't consider that I have fully understood everything. But I do one thing: I forget what is behind and strive for what is ahead.
Philippians 3:14 I strive for the goal to win the prize that God calls us to through Christ Jesus.
Philippians 3:15 Let's think this way, those of us who are mature. And if you think differently about something, God will make that clear to you.
Philippians 3:16 Let's follow the same rules and think the same way for what we've already achieved.
Philippians 3:17 Friends, follow my example together, and notice those who live as you have us as a model.
Philippians 3:18 Many people live in a way I often warned you about, and now I say it crying, they are against Christ's cross.
Philippians 3:19 Their end is ruin, their god is their appetite, they take pride in what should bring shame, and they focus on worldly things.
Philippians 3:20 Our citizenship is in heaven, and from there we eagerly await our Savior, Jesus Christ.
Philippians 3:21 Who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, using his power to bring everything under his control.

Philippians 4:2 I ask Euodias, and I ask Syntyche, to agree with each other in God.

Philippians 4:4 Be happy in God always, and I say again, be happy.
Philippians 4:5 Let everyone see that you are considerate. God is near.
Philippians 4:6 Don't worry about anything; instead, with thankful prayers, tell God what you need.
Philippians 4:7 God's peace, beyond all we can understand, will guard your hearts and thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Philippians 4:11 I'm not saying this because I need anything; I have learned to be happy with whatever I have.

Philippians 4:14 You did well to help me in my trouble.
Philippians 4:15 You Philippians remember that when I first started spreading the good news and left Macedonia, no church helped me with gifts except for you.
Philippians 4:16 You helped me with my needs in Thessalonica more than once.
Philippians 4:17 I don't want a gift; I want you to have benefits that grow for you.
Philippians 4:18 I have everything I need and more. I am satisfied because I received from Epaphroditus what you sent – a sweet-smelling offering, a sacrifice pleasing to God.
Philippians 4:19 My God will meet all your needs with the wealth of his glory in Jesus Christ.

Colossians 1:1 Paul, sent by Jesus Christ because God wanted it, and Timothy our brother,
Colossians 1:2 To God's holy and loyal followers in Christ who are in Colosse: May you have kindness and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ.
Colossians 1:3 We thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you.
Colossians 1:4 We heard about your faith in Jesus and your love for all God's people.
Colossians 1:5 You have hope stored for you in heaven, which you learned about before through the true message of the good news.
Colossians 1:6 It has come to you, as it has to the whole world, and it is producing results, just as it has been in you since the day you heard about it and understood God's true kindness.
Colossians 1:7 You also learned from Epaphras, our dear coworker, who serves you faithfully as a minister of Christ.
Colossians 1:8 They also told us about your love through the Spirit.
Colossians 1:9 Because of this, since the day we learned about it, we keep praying for you. We hope that you will fully understand God's will and gain all wisdom and spiritual insight.
Colossians 1:10 Live a life worthy of God, doing good at every chance, and growing in understanding of God.
Colossians 1:11 Filled with all strength, given by God's glorious power, to be completely patient and able to endure, with joy.
Colossians 1:12 Thanking God, who has prepared us to share in the inheritance of the holy people in the light:
Colossians 1:13 God saved us from darkness and brought us into the kingdom of his beloved Son.
Colossians 1:14 In him, we are set free by his blood, and our sins are forgiven.
Colossians 1:15 He is the image of the unseen God, the first of all creation.
Colossians 1:16 Through him, all things were made in heaven and on earth, seen and unseen, including rulers and authorities. All things were made by him and for him.
Colossians 1:17 He exists before everything, and through him, everything holds together.
Colossians 1:18 He is the head of the body, the church; he is the start, first to rise from the dead; so he is most important in everything.
Colossians 1:19 God was happy to have all completeness live in him.
Colossians 1:20 He made peace with his cross's blood and brought everything back to God, things on earth and in heaven.
Colossians 1:21 And you, once distanced and hostile in your thoughts because of evil deeds, now God has made peace with you.
Colossians 1:22 Through his death in a human body, to present you as holy, without blame, and free from accusation before him:
Colossians 1:23 If you keep your faith strong and steady, and don't give up the hope given by the good news you've heard, which has been told to every living being under the sky, and for which I, Paul, have become a servant.
Colossians 1:24 I am happy to suffer for you, and I share in Christ's sufferings in my own body for the good of the church, which is his body.
Colossians 1:25 I am chosen to serve because God gave this task to me for your benefit, to complete God's message.
Colossians 1:26 The secret that was hidden for so long, even from many people long ago, is now shown to God's holy people.
Colossians 1:27 God wants to show you the riches and glory of this mystery among the non-Jewish people: Christ is in you, giving you the hope of glory.
Colossians 1:28 We teach about Christ, warning everyone and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so that we can present everyone as perfect in Christ Jesus.
Colossians 1:29 I also work hard and struggle, using the great strength that God works in me.

Colossians 2:1 I want you to know about the big struggle I have for you, for those in Laodicea, and for all who have not met me in person.
Colossians 2:2 So that their hearts may be encouraged and united in love, leading to a complete confidence and understanding of God's secret plan, which is Christ himself.
Colossians 2:3 In this one, all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
Colossians 2:4 I say this so no one will trick you with persuasive words.
Colossians 2:5 Even though I am not there in person, I am with you in spirit, happy to see your discipline and firm faith in Christ.
Colossians 2:6 Since you accepted Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to live in Him.
Colossians 2:7 Grown deep in him and built up, strong in your faith as you were taught, filled with thankfulness.
Colossians 2:8 Be careful that no one misleads you with philosophy and empty lies, following human traditions and worldly principles instead of Christ.
Colossians 2:9 In him, the complete nature of God lives in a human form.
Colossians 2:10 You are made whole in him, who is the leader of all rulers and authorities.
Colossians 2:11 In Christ, you also were spiritually circumcised, not by a physical procedure but by stripping away the sinful nature's control over the body.
Colossians 2:12 In baptism, you were buried with him and also raised with him because you believe in God, who brought him back from the dead.
Colossians 2:13 You were dead because of your sins and because your flesh was not circumcised, but God made you alive with Christ and forgave all your sins.
Colossians 2:14 Erasing the written laws that were against us, which opposed us, and removed them, fixing them to his cross;
Colossians 2:15 He disarmed the rulers and authorities, displayed them publicly, and won a victory over them through it.
Colossians 2:16 Don't let anyone criticize you about what you eat or drink, or about celebrating religious festivals, observing the new moon, or keeping the Sabbath.
Colossians 2:17 These are a preview of what will happen; but the real thing belongs to Christ.
Colossians 2:18 Do not let anyone cheat you of your prize by pretending to be humble and worshipping angels, getting involved with things they have never seen, foolishly inflated by their human thinking.
Colossians 2:19 Not staying connected to the Head, from whom the whole body, supported and held together by its ligaments and sinews, grows as God causes it to grow.
Colossians 2:20 So if you have died with Christ and are free from the world's basic rules, why do you still follow its rules as if you belonged to the world?
Colossians 2:21 Do not touch; do not taste; do not handle;
Colossians 2:22 These are all destined to be used up and discarded, according to human rules and teachings.
Colossians 2:23 These things may seem wise because they require strong devotion, humility, and harsh treatment of the body, but they provide no help in controlling selfish desires.

Colossians 3:2 Focus on things above, not on earthly things.
Colossians 3:3 You are dead, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
Colossians 3:4 When Christ, who is our life, comes, you will also be with him in glory.
Colossians 3:5 So, make dead the parts of you that are earthly: sexual sin, impurity, strong lust, evil desires, and greed, which is like worshiping idols.
Colossians 3:6 Because of these things, God's anger comes upon the disobedient people.
Colossians 3:7 You once lived this way when you followed these practices.
Colossians 3:8 Now you should also stop all these things: anger, rage, hate, insulting others, and dirty talk from your mouth.
Colossians 3:9 Do not lie to each other, because you have taken off your old self and its behaviors.
Colossians 3:10 And have put on the new self, which is renewed in knowledge to be like God who created him.
Colossians 3:11 There is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or not, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free; but Christ is everything and in everyone.
Colossians 3:12 Therefore, as God's chosen ones, holy and loved, put on a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.

Colossians 3:14 Above everything, wear love, which binds everything together in perfect unity.
Colossians 3:15 Let God's peace lead in your hearts, which you are called to as one group; and be thankful.
Colossians 3:16 Let Christ's message live in you fully, with all wisdom, and teach and warn each other with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing thankfully in your hearts to God.
Colossians 3:17 In everything you say or do, do it all for Jesus, thanking God through him.
Colossians 3:18 Wives, obey your husbands, as it is right with God.
Colossians 3:19 Husbands, love your wives and don't be harsh with them.
Colossians 3:20 Kids, listen to your parents in everything, because this makes God happy.
Colossians 3:21 Parents, do not make your children angry, so they do not get discouraged.
Colossians 3:22 Workers, obey your earthly bosses in everything; not just when they're watching, like people who just want to please others, but with a true heart and respect for God.
Colossians 3:23 Do everything with all your heart, as if you're doing it for God, not for people.
Colossians 3:24 Understand that from God you will get the reward of what is kept for you in heaven, because you serve Christ.
Colossians 3:25 Whoever does wrong will be paid back for their wrong, and everyone is treated the same.

Colossians 4:18 I, Paul, am writing this greeting with my own hand. Remember that I am in chains. May God's kindness be with you. Amen.

1 Thessalonians 1:1 Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the Thessalonian church in God and Jesus Christ: may you have grace and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ.
1 Thessalonians 1:2 We always thank God for all of you, remembering you in our prayers.
1 Thessalonians 1:3 We constantly remember your faith in action, love's hard work, and hopeful patience in our Lord Jesus Christ, before God our Father.
1 Thessalonians 1:4 Dear friends, know that God has chosen you.
1 Thessalonians 1:5 Our good news didn't come to you just by words, but also with power, God's Spirit, and strong confidence; as you know how we acted among you for your benefit.
1 Thessalonians 1:6 You followed our example and God's, accepting the message in great trouble yet with Holy Spirit's joy.
1 Thessalonians 1:7 So you became examples to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.
1 Thessalonians 1:8 From you, the message of God has spread not only in Macedonia and Achaia but also everywhere your faith in God is known; so we don't need to say anything more.
1 Thessalonians 1:9 People tell how we came to you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the true and living God.
1 Thessalonians 1:10 To wait for his Son from heaven, whom God raised from the dead, Jesus who saves us from the coming anger.

1 Thessalonians 2:1 You know, friends, that our visit to you was not a waste.
1 Thessalonians 2:2 Even though we had already suffered and were badly treated in Philippi, as you know, we were brave in our faith to tell you God's good news, despite strong opposition.
1 Thessalonians 2:3 Our encouragement did not come from lies, impurity, or trickery.
1 Thessalonians 2:4 God trusted us with the good news, so we speak to please not people, but God who tests our hearts.
1 Thessalonians 2:5 We never used flattery or were greedy, and you know it; God saw it all.
1 Thessalonians 2:6 We did not seek praise from people, not from you or anyone else, even though we could have made demands as Christ's apostles.
1 Thessalonians 2:7 We were kind to you, just like a nurse who takes care of her children.
1 Thessalonians 2:8 We really wanted to share with you, not only God's message, but also our own lives because you were so important to us.
1 Thessalonians 2:9 Brothers and sisters, you remember our hard work and struggle: because we worked day and night and didn't want to be a burden to any of you, we shared with you God's message.
1 Thessalonians 2:10 You are witnesses, and God too, how we acted holy, justly, and without blame among you who believe.
1 Thessalonians 2:11 You know how we encouraged, comforted, and urged each of you, like a father does his children.
1 Thessalonians 2:12 You should live in a way that honors God, who invites you to His kingdom and splendor.
1 Thessalonians 2:13 We always thank God because when you accepted the message you heard from us, you didn't think of it as human words but as God's truth, which also powerfully works in those who believe.
1 Thessalonians 2:14 You, brothers and sisters, followed the example of God's churches in Judea that are in Christ Jesus: you also suffered from your own people, just as they did from the Jews.
1 Thessalonians 2:15 They killed both Jesus and their own prophets and have persecuted us; they do not please God and oppose everyone.
1 Thessalonians 2:16 Stopping us from talking to the non-Jews so they can be saved, to make their sins fully complete: because God's anger has fully come upon them.
1 Thessalonians 2:17 We, brothers, were separated from you for a little while in person, not in spirit, and tried very hard to see you because we really wanted to.
1 Thessalonians 2:18 We wanted to come to you, I, Paul, tried more than once; but Satan stopped us.
1 Thessalonians 2:19 What is our hope, joy, or reason to be proud? Aren't you with our Lord Jesus Christ when he comes?
1 Thessalonians 2:20 You are our pride and happiness.

1 Thessalonians 3:1 So when we couldn't wait any longer, we decided to stay alone in Athens.
1 Thessalonians 3:2 We sent Timothy, our brother, who serves God and works with us to spread the good news about Christ, to strengthen and encourage you in your faith.
1 Thessalonians 3:3 No one should be upset by these troubles, because you know we are meant to go through them.
1 Thessalonians 3:4 Truly, when we were with you, we warned you that we would face troubles; and it happened, just as you know.
1 Thessalonians 3:5 Because I couldn't wait any longer, I sent to ask about your faith, in case the tempter had tempted you and our work would be useless.
1 Thessalonians 3:6 But now Timothy has come to us from you and told us about your faith and love. He said you always remember us well and really want to see us, just as we want to see you.
1 Thessalonians 3:7 So, friends, your faith made us feel better, even with all our troubles and hardships.
1 Thessalonians 3:8 We live fully if you remain strong in faith.
1 Thessalonians 3:9 How can we thank God enough for you, for all the happiness we feel because of you in the presence of God?
1 Thessalonians 3:10 Day and night we pray deeply to see you and to strengthen what is missing in your faith.
1 Thessalonians 3:11 May God himself, our Father, and Jesus Christ, our Lord, guide us to you.
1 Thessalonians 3:12 May God help you grow and overflow with love for each other and for everyone, just as we do for you.
1 Thessalonians 3:13 So that God may make your hearts strong and pure in the sight of God, our Father, when our Lord Jesus Christ comes with all his holy people.

1 Thessalonians 4:1 We ask you, friends, and encourage you in Jesus' name, to live as we taught you, so you can please God and keep growing in it.
1 Thessalonians 4:2 You know the commands we gave you from Jesus.
1 Thessalonians 4:3 God wants you to be holy and avoid sexual immorality.
1 Thessalonians 4:4 Each of you should know how to live with your body in a way that is holy and respectful.
1 Thessalonians 4:5 Do not follow strong sexual desires, like the non-believers who do not know God.
1 Thessalonians 4:6 Let no one take advantage of or cheat their fellow in any matter; for God punishes all such acts, as we have already warned and confirmed to you.
1 Thessalonians 4:7 God has not called us to be unclean, but to be holy.
1 Thessalonians 4:8 So, if someone disrespects, they don't disrespect people but God, who has also given us his Holy Spirit.
1 Thessalonians 4:9 Regarding loving others like brothers, you don't need me to write to you, because God has taught you to love each other.
1 Thessalonians 4:10 You are showing love to all God's people in Macedonia, but we urge you, friends, to do so more and more.
1 Thessalonians 4:11 Work hard and mind your own business, just as we told you.
1 Thessalonians 4:12 Live honestly with those outside your group, so you won't need anything from others.
1 Thessalonians 4:13 I want you to understand, friends, about those who have died, so you won't be sad like others who have no hope.
1 Thessalonians 4:14 If we believe that Jesus died and came back to life, then God will also bring with him those who have died believing in Jesus.
1 Thessalonians 4:15 We tell you, by God's message, that those of us who are alive and left until God's return will not go ahead of those who have died.
1 Thessalonians 4:16 God will come down from heaven with a shout, with the archangel's voice, and with God's trumpet: and those who believed in Christ and have died will come back to life first.
1 Thessalonians 4:17 We who are alive and left will be lifted up with them in the clouds to meet God in the sky, and we will always be with God.
1 Thessalonians 4:18 Therefore, encourage each other with these words.

1 Thessalonians 5:1 About the times and dates, friends, you don't need me to write to you.
1 Thessalonians 5:2 You know very well that the day of God will come like a thief in the night.
1 Thessalonians 5:3 When people say, "Peace and safety," then sudden ruin will hit them, like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they won't escape.
1 Thessalonians 5:4 But friends, you are not in the dark, so that the day should surprise you like a thief.
1 Thessalonians 5:5 You are all children of light and of the day; we are not of the night or of darkness.
1 Thessalonians 5:6 So let's not sleep like others; instead, let's stay alert and clear-headed.
1 Thessalonians 5:7 People who sleep, sleep at night; and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.
1 Thessalonians 5:8 Let us who live in the light be clear-minded, wearing faith and love as a protective vest, and the hope of being saved as a helmet.
1 Thessalonians 5:9 God has not chosen us for anger, but to gain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Thessalonians 5:10 He died for us so that, awake or asleep, we might live with him.
1 Thessalonians 5:11 Encourage each other and build each other up, just as you are already doing.
1 Thessalonians 5:12 We ask you, friends, to recognize those who work hard among you, who guide you in the Lord, and who warn you.
1 Thessalonians 5:13 Value them greatly with love because of their work and live peacefully with each other.
1 Thessalonians 5:14 We urge you, friends, to warn those who are not following the rules, encourage those who are discouraged, help those who are weak, and be patient with everyone.
1 Thessalonians 5:15 Make sure no one pays back wrong for wrong to anyone; but always try to do what is good, for each other and for everyone else.
1 Thessalonians 5:16 Be happy always.
1 Thessalonians 5:17 Keep praying all the time.
1 Thessalonians 5:18 In everything, be thankful: because this is what God wants for you in Christ Jesus.
1 Thessalonians 5:19 Do not put out the Spirit's fire.
1 Thessalonians 5:20 Do not look down on prophecies.
1 Thessalonians 5:21 Test everything; keep what is good.
1 Thessalonians 5:22 Stay away from anything that looks evil.
1 Thessalonians 5:23 May the God of peace make you completely holy, and I hope God keeps your spirit, soul, and body without fault until our Lord Jesus Christ comes.
1 Thessalonians 5:24 God, who calls you, is faithful and will do what he promises.
1 Thessalonians 5:25 Brothers and sisters, pray for us.
1 Thessalonians 5:26 Say hello to all the brothers and sisters with a holy kiss.
1 Thessalonians 5:27 I ask you seriously in God's name to make sure this letter is read to all the believers.
1 Thessalonians 5:28 May the kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

2 Thessalonians 1:1 Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and Jesus Christ:
2 Thessalonians 1:2 May you have grace and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ.
2 Thessalonians 1:3 We must always thank God for you, brothers, because it is right. Your faith is growing a lot, and the love you all have for each other is increasing.
2 Thessalonians 1:4 We are proud of you among God's churches because of your patience and faith during all the persecutions and troubles you go through.
2 Thessalonians 1:5 This clearly shows God's fair judgment, so that you can be seen as fit for God's kingdom, which you are also suffering for.
2 Thessalonians 1:6 God thinks it is fair to give trouble to those who trouble you.
2 Thessalonians 1:7 If you are troubled, find rest with us when the Lord Jesus comes from heaven with his powerful angels.
2 Thessalonians 1:8 With fiery flames, punishing those who do not know God and do not follow the teachings of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Thessalonians 1:9 They will be punished with never-ending ruin, away from God and his mighty glory.
2 Thessalonians 1:10 When he comes to receive glory in his holy people and to be marveled at among all who have believed (because you believed our testimony to you) on that day.
2 Thessalonians 1:11 So we always pray for you that God will think you worthy of his call, and will complete every good thing you desire and your work of faith with strength.
2 Thessalonians 1:12 May our Lord Jesus Christ's name be honored through you, and you through him, by the kindness of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2 Thessalonians 2:1 We ask you, friends, because of the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our meeting with him,
2 Thessalonians 2:2 Make sure you are not quickly upset or worried, whether by a spirit, something someone says, or a letter seeming to be from us, claiming that the day of Christ is already here.
2 Thessalonians 2:3 Don't let anyone trick you in any way: for that day will not come unless there is first a turning away from God, and the sinful man, the doomed son, is shown.
2 Thessalonians 2:4 He challenges and lifts himself above everything named God or worshiped; so he, as God, sits in God's temple, acting like he is God.
2 Thessalonians 2:5 Don't you remember that when I was still with you, I told you these things?
2 Thessalonians 2:6 And now you know what is holding back his revelation until the right time.
2 Thessalonians 2:7 The secret power of wrongdoing is already at work: but he who is holding it back will continue to do so until he is removed.
2 Thessalonians 2:8 Then the evil one will be shown, whom God will defeat with his word and destroy with the glory of his coming.
2 Thessalonians 2:9 He will come after Satan, with all power, signs, and false miracles.
2 Thessalonians 2:10 They will be deceived by evil because they did not love the truth that could save them.
2 Thessalonians 2:11 For this reason, God will let them be fooled, so they will believe what is false.
2 Thessalonians 2:12 So that everyone who did not believe the truth, but enjoyed doing wrong, might be judged.
2 Thessalonians 2:13 We must always thank God for you, brothers loved by God, because God chose you from the start for salvation by making you holy through the Spirit and by your belief in the truth.
2 Thessalonians 2:14 God called you through our good news to gain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Thessalonians 2:15 So, friends, stand strong and keep the teachings you have learned, whether by speaking or by our letter.
2 Thessalonians 2:16 Now our Lord Jesus Christ and God, our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope by grace,
2 Thessalonians 2:17 Encourage your hearts and strengthen you in all good words and actions.

2 Thessalonians 3:1 Friends, please pray for us, so that God's message can spread freely and be honored, just like with you.
2 Thessalonians 3:2 So that we can be rescued from people who are unfair and evil: not everyone has faith.
2 Thessalonians 3:3 God is faithful and will make you strong and protect you from evil.
2 Thessalonians 3:4 We trust in God about you, that you are and will continue to follow the instructions we give you.
2 Thessalonians 3:5 May God guide your hearts to love God and to wait patiently for Christ.
2 Thessalonians 3:6 We tell you, friends, speak for Jesus Christ and stay away from anyone who does not follow the teachings we gave and does not act right.
2 Thessalonians 3:7 You know how you should imitate us: we did not act improperly among you.
2 Thessalonians 3:8 We did not eat anyone's bread without paying; we worked hard day and night so we would not be a burden to any of you.
2 Thessalonians 3:9 Not because we lack the authority, but to be an example for you to imitate us.
2 Thessalonians 3:10 Even when we were with you, we told you: If anyone won't work, they shouldn't eat.
2 Thessalonians 3:11 We hear that some among you are acting out of line, not working at all, but meddling in others' business.
2 Thessalonians 3:12 We tell and encourage those people, by Jesus Christ, to work calmly and eat their own food.
2 Thessalonians 3:13 Friends, don't get tired of doing good.
2 Thessalonians 3:14 If anyone does not follow our instructions in this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with him, so he may feel ashamed.
2 Thessalonians 3:15 Don't see him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.
2 Thessalonians 3:16 May God, the Lord of peace, give you peace at all times and in every way. May God be with all of you.
2 Thessalonians 3:17 This is my greeting in every letter, all written by me, Paul.
2 Thessalonians 3:18 May the kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ be with everyone. Amen.

1 Timothy 1:1 Paul, a messenger of Jesus Christ, by God our Savior's order, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who is our hope.
1 Timothy 1:2 To Timothy, my true son in faith: May you have kindness, compassion, and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
1 Timothy 1:3 I asked you to stay in Ephesus when I went to Macedonia, so you could tell some people not to teach different teachings.
1 Timothy 1:4 Don't pay attention to myths and never-ending family histories that cause arguments instead of building up God's work, which is done in faith.
1 Timothy 1:5 The goal of this command is love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and genuine faith.
1 Timothy 1:6 Some people have strayed and turned to meaningless talk.
1 Timothy 1:7 Wanting to be teachers of the law without understanding what they are talking about or what they strongly claim to be true.
1 Timothy 1:8 We know the law is good if someone uses it correctly.
1 Timothy 1:9 Understand this: the law isn't for good people, but for those who break the law and don't obey, for godless and sinful people, for those who aren't holy and who disrespect, for those who kill their fathers or mothers, and for murderers.
1 Timothy 1:10 This is for those who are sexually immoral, those who engage in homosexuality, those who kidnap, those who lie, those who make false promises, and anything else that goes against correct teaching.
1 Timothy 1:11 According to the wonderful good news of the happy God, which was given to me to take care of.
1 Timothy 1:12 I thank Jesus our Lord who gave me strength because he trusted me and chose me to serve Him.
1 Timothy 1:13 I used to speak against God, hurt people, and do harm. But I received mercy because I did it without knowing and without belief.
1 Timothy 1:14 God's grace was very great, filled with faith and love in Christ Jesus.
1 Timothy 1:15 This true statement should be fully accepted: Christ Jesus came into the world to save wrongdoers, and I am the worst of them.
1 Timothy 1:16 However, I received mercy for this reason: so that in me, Jesus Christ could fully display his patience as an example for those who would later believe in him for eternal life.
1 Timothy 1:17 Now to the King who is forever, who cannot die, who no one can see, the only smart God, be honor and praise forever and ever. Amen.
1 Timothy 1:18 I give you this task, Timothy, my son, following the prophecies about you, so that you can fight the good fight well.
1 Timothy 1:19 Keep faith and a clear conscience; some have rejected these and ruined their faith.
1 Timothy 1:20 I have handed over Hymenaeus and Alexander to Satan so they can learn not to speak against God.

1 Timothy 2:1 I encourage, then, that above all, requests, prayers, asking for others, and thanks should be given for everyone.
1 Timothy 2:2 For rulers and all in power; so we can live quietly and peacefully with true faith and honesty.
1 Timothy 2:3 This is good and okay to God who saves us.
1 Timothy 2:4 God wants everyone to be saved and to understand the truth.
1 Timothy 2:5 There is one God and one go-between for God and people, the man Christ Jesus.
1 Timothy 2:6 He gave himself as a ransom for everyone, to be shown at the right time.
1 Timothy 2:7 I am chosen to be a preacher and an apostle, speaking the truth in Christ without lying, and a teacher of the non-Jews in faith and truth.
1 Timothy 2:8 I want men to pray everywhere, raising holy hands, without anger or doubt.
1 Timothy 2:9 Women should also dress simply and with modesty, acting with decency and self-control, not with fancy hairstyles, gold, pearls, or expensive clothes.
1 Timothy 2:10 But (fitting for women who claim to honor God) by doing good deeds.
1 Timothy 2:11 Let the woman learn quietly and obey fully.
1 Timothy 2:12 I do not allow a woman to teach or have control over a man; she must be quiet.
1 Timothy 2:13 Adam was created first, then Eve.
1 Timothy 2:14 Adam was not tricked, but the woman was deceived and did wrong.
1 Timothy 2:15 She will be saved through having children, if they keep their faith, love, and holiness with good sense.

1 Timothy 3:1 It is true that if someone wants to be a leader in the church, they want to do a good thing.
1 Timothy 3:2 A church leader must be without fault, married to one woman, watchful, clear-minded, well-behaved, welcoming to guests, and skilled in teaching.
1 Timothy 3:3 Doesn't drink too much, isn't violent, not chasing dirty money; but is patient, doesn't like to fight, and isn't greedy.
1 Timothy 3:4 Someone who leads their own family well, keeping their children respectful and serious.
1 Timothy 3:5 If a man can't manage his own family, how can he take care of God's church?
1 Timothy 3:6 Someone new should not be given a high position, because if they become proud, they might be judged as the devil was.
1 Timothy 3:7 He must also have a good reputation among outsiders to avoid falling into disgrace and the devil's trap.
1 Timothy 3:8 Deacons must be serious, not lie, not drink too much wine, and not want dirty money.
1 Timothy 3:9 Keeping the secret of faith with a clear conscience.
1 Timothy 3:10 First, these should be tested; then if they are found faultless, they can serve as deacons.
1 Timothy 3:11 Their wives must be serious, not spreading rumors, clear-minded, and trustworthy in everything.
1 Timothy 3:12 Deacons should have one wife and manage their children and homes well.
1 Timothy 3:13 Those who serve well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves and great confidence in their faith in Christ Jesus.
1 Timothy 3:14 I write these things to you, hoping to visit you soon.
1 Timothy 3:15 But if I'm delayed, you will know how to act in God's house, which is the living God's church, the support and foundation of truth.
1 Timothy 3:16 There's no doubt, the secret of being good is great: God appeared in human form, proved right by the Spirit, seen by angels, told to outsiders, trusted in by people everywhere, taken up into greatness.

1 Timothy 4:1 The Spirit clearly says that in later times some will turn away from faith, listening to misleading spirits and teachings of demons.
1 Timothy 4:2 Telling lies and pretending to be good, while their consciences are numb as if burned with a hot iron.
1 Timothy 4:3 Stopping people from marrying and telling them not to eat certain foods, which God made for believers who know the truth to eat with thanks.
1 Timothy 4:4 Every creature from God is good and should not be rejected if it is accepted with thanks.
1 Timothy 4:5 It is made holy by God's word and prayer.
1 Timothy 4:6 If you remind the believers about these teachings, you will be a good servant of Jesus Christ, grown strong through the words of faith and good teaching that you have followed.
1 Timothy 4:7 Avoid disrespectful and silly stories, and instead train yourself to be godly.
1 Timothy 4:8 Exercising your body helps a little, but living a godly life is useful for everything, giving hope for our current life and the future.
1 Timothy 4:9 This saying is true and should be fully accepted.
1 Timothy 4:10 We work hard and are criticized because we trust in God, who saves everyone, especially those who believe.
1 Timothy 4:11 Give these instructions and teach them.
1 Timothy 4:12 Don't let anyone look down on you because you are young, but be an example for the believers in your speech, in your life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
1 Timothy 4:13 Until I arrive, focus on reading, encouraging others, and teaching.
1 Timothy 4:14 Do not ignore the gift you have, which was given to you when the elders laid their hands on you and prophesied.
1 Timothy 4:15 Think deeply about these things and fully dedicate yourself to them so that everyone can see your progress.
1 Timothy 4:16 Be careful about how you live and what you teach; keep on doing these things. By doing so, you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.

1 Timothy 5:1 Don't scold an older person, but ask him kindly like a father; treat the younger men like brothers.
1 Timothy 5:2 Treat older women like mothers; younger women like sisters, with complete respect.
1 Timothy 5:3 Respect women who are truly alone without husbands.
1 Timothy 5:4 If a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first take care of their own family and repay their parents, because this pleases God.
1 Timothy 5:5 A true widow who is alone puts her hope in God and prays day and night.
1 Timothy 5:6 A woman who enjoys life too much is like she's dead even when she's alive.
1 Timothy 5:7 Instruct them in these matters so they can be without fault.
1 Timothy 5:8 If someone does not take care of their family, especially those living at home, they have rejected the faith and are worse than someone who does not believe.
1 Timothy 5:9 Do not include a widow who is less than sixty years old and has been married to only one man.
1 Timothy 5:10 Known for good acts; if she has raised children, welcomed guests, washed believers' feet, helped those in trouble, and eagerly done all kinds of good work.
1 Timothy 5:11 Do not accept the younger widows; when their desires grow strong, they want to marry again.
1 Timothy 5:12 They face punishment because they have abandoned their early belief.
1 Timothy 5:13 They also learn to be lazy, moving from house to house; and they are not just lazy, but also gossips and meddlers, talking about things they should not.
1 Timothy 5:14 I want younger women to get married, have children, manage their homes, and not give critics any reason to speak badly.
1 Timothy 5:15 Some have already turned away following Satan.
1 Timothy 5:16 If any believer, man or woman, has widows in their family, they should help them so that the church isn't burdened and can assist those who are truly in need.
1 Timothy 5:17 Respect the leaders who guide well greatly, and give extra respect to those who work hard teaching God's message and beliefs.
1 Timothy 5:18 The Bible says, you should not cover the ox's mouth when it is working with the grain. Also, a worker deserves to be paid for their work.
1 Timothy 5:19 Do not accept a charge against an older person unless it is supported by two or three witnesses.
1 Timothy 5:20 Tell everyone when someone does wrong so that others will be afraid to do the same.
1 Timothy 5:21 I tell you before God, Jesus Christ, and the chosen angels, to follow these instructions fairly, treating everyone the same, without favoring anyone.
1 Timothy 5:22 Don't quickly accuse anyone, and don't share in the wrongs of others; stay clean yourself.
1 Timothy 5:23 Stop drinking only water, but have a little wine for your stomach and your frequent sicknesses.
1 Timothy 5:24 Some people's sins are obvious, leading directly to judgment, while the sins of others become clear later.
1 Timothy 5:25 Similarly, the good deeds of some people are clear from the start, and those that are not will still be seen.

1 Timothy 6:1 All servants under someone should respect their masters fully, so that God’s name and teaching are not spoken of badly.
1 Timothy 6:2 If you have a boss who believes, respect them because they are your brothers and sisters. Serve them well because they are faithful and loved, sharing in the good things. Teach and encourage these things.
1 Timothy 6:3 If someone teaches differently and doesn't agree with the good words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the teaching that leads to a godly life;
1 Timothy 6:4 He is arrogant and knows nothing, but obsesses over arguments and fights about words, which lead to jealousy, conflict, insults, and suspicious thoughts.
1 Timothy 6:5 Twisted arguments from people with corrupt minds, who lack the truth and think that profit is the same as being godly: stay away from them.
1 Timothy 6:6 Living a godly life and being content with what you have is truly valuable.
1 Timothy 6:7 We brought nothing into this world, and we can surely take nothing with us when we leave.
1 Timothy 6:8 With food and clothing, let us be content.
1 Timothy 6:9 People who want to be rich fall into temptations, traps, and many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction.
1 Timothy 6:10 Loving money too much leads to all kinds of wrongs; some people wanting it have wandered from their beliefs and brought themselves many pains.
1 Timothy 6:11 But you, man of God, run away from these things; and chase after being right, godly, faithful, loving, patient, and gentle.
1 Timothy 6:12 Battle well in your faith, grab hold of forever life, to which you were invited and have claimed well in front of many people.
1 Timothy 6:13 I instruct you before God, who gives life to everything, and Jesus Christ, who spoke the truth before Pontius Pilate.
1 Timothy 6:14 Make sure you follow this command without fault or blame until Jesus Christ appears.
1 Timothy 6:15 In his own time, he will show who is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of all kings and Lord of all lords.
1 Timothy 6:16 Only God has eternal life, lives in light that no one can get close to, whom no one has seen or can see. To Him be honor and lasting power. Amen.
1 Timothy 6:17 Tell those who are wealthy in this world not to be proud or to rely on their unstable wealth, but on God, who generously gives us everything for our enjoyment.
1 Timothy 6:18 Let them do good, be rich in good deeds, ready to share, and eager to be generous.
1 Timothy 6:19 Saving up for themselves a good base for the future, so they may grasp eternal life.
1 Timothy 6:20 Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you, stay away from godless chatter and the false knowledge that some claim.
1 Timothy 6:21 Some who claim to follow have wandered away from the faith. May kindness be with you. Amen.

2 Timothy 1:1 Paul, a messenger of Jesus Christ chosen by God, based on the promise of life found in Christ Jesus.
2 Timothy 1:2 To Timothy, my dear son: May you have kindness, compassion, and peace from God the Father and from Christ Jesus our Lord.
2 Timothy 1:3 I thank God, who I serve like my ancestors did with a clear conscience, that I always remember you in my prayers day and night.
2 Timothy 1:4 I really want to see you, remembering your tears, so I can be full of joy.
2 Timothy 1:5 I remember your true faith, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice, and I am convinced it is in you as well.
2 Timothy 1:6 I remind you to awaken the gift from God you have, which was given to you when I laid my hands on you.
2 Timothy 1:7 God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind.
2 Timothy 1:8 Don't be ashamed of our Lord's message, or of me, his prisoner. But share in the hardships of the good news by the power of God.
2 Timothy 1:9 God saved us and called us with a special calling—not because of what we have done but because of his own plan and kindness given to us in Jesus Christ long ago.
2 Timothy 1:10 But now it is made clear by the coming of our Savior Jesus Christ, who has destroyed death, and has shown us the way to life and eternal life through the good news.
2 Timothy 1:11 I am chosen to be a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher to non-Jews.
2 Timothy 1:12 I suffer for this reason, but I'm not ashamed because I know who I believe in, and I'm sure he can guard what I've entrusted to him until that day.
2 Timothy 1:13 Keep the pattern of true words you heard from me, with faith and love in Christ Jesus.
2 Timothy 1:14 Protect the good message given to you by the Holy Spirit living in us.
2 Timothy 1:15 You know that everyone in Asia has turned against me, including Phygellus and Hermogenes.
2 Timothy 1:16 God show kindness to Onesiphorus's family because he often helped me and was not embarrassed by my imprisonment.
2 Timothy 1:17 When he was in Rome, he looked for me carefully and found me.
2 Timothy 1:18 May God give him mercy from God on that day, and you know very well how much he helped me in Ephesus.

2 Timothy 2:1 You, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Jesus Christ.
2 Timothy 2:2 The teachings you have heard from me, in front of many witnesses, pass on to trustworthy people who can also teach others.
2 Timothy 2:3 So, be strong like a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
2 Timothy 2:4 A person fighting in a war does not get involved with everyday life activities, so they can please the one who chose them to be a soldier.
2 Timothy 2:5 If someone competes in contests, they are not awarded a crown unless they compete according to the rules.
2 Timothy 2:6 The farmer who works hard should be the first to enjoy the fruits of his work.
2 Timothy 2:7 Think about what I say, and may God help you understand everything.
2 Timothy 2:8 Remember that Jesus Christ, who came from David's family, was brought back to life as told in my good news.
2 Timothy 2:9 I face hardship as if I were a criminal, even to the point of being chained; yet God's message is not chained.
2 Timothy 2:10 I put up with everything for the chosen people's sake, so they can also find the salvation in Christ Jesus that comes with eternal glory.
2 Timothy 2:11 This saying is true: If we died with him, we will also live with him.
2 Timothy 2:12 If we go through hard times, we will also rule with him; if we reject him, he will also reject us.
2 Timothy 2:13 If we don't believe, he remains faithful; he cannot contradict himself.
2 Timothy 2:14 Remind them of these things and tell them in God's presence not to argue about words. It doesn't help anyone and ruins those who listen.
2 Timothy 2:15 Make an effort to be acceptable to God, a worker with no need to be ashamed, properly understanding and teaching the true message.
2 Timothy 2:16 Stay away from disrespectful and pointless talk; it leads to more wrong behavior.
2 Timothy 2:17 Their teaching will spread like a disease. It includes Hymenaeus and Philetus.
2 Timothy 2:18 They are wrong about the truth, claiming the resurrection has already happened, and they destroy the faith of some.
2 Timothy 2:19 God's foundation stands firm, with this mark: God knows who belongs to Him. And anyone who calls on Christ's name should turn away from wrongdoing.
2 Timothy 2:20 In a big house, there are not just containers of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay; some are for special use, and some for everyday use.
2 Timothy 2:21 If a person cleans himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, made holy, and ready for the owner's use, prepared for every good action.
2 Timothy 2:22 Run away from young people's strong desires. But chase after living right, trusting, being kind, and peace with those who ask God for help with a clean heart.
2 Timothy 2:23 Stay away from silly and ignorant questions, because they lead to arguments.
2 Timothy 2:24 God's servant should not argue, but be kind to everyone, able to teach, and patient.
2 Timothy 2:25 Gently teach those who disagree with themselves; if perhaps God will grant them a change of heart to recognize the truth.
2 Timothy 2:26 So they can escape the devil's trap, who has captured them to do his will.

2 Timothy 3:1 Understand that in the last days, dangerous times will come.
2 Timothy 3:2 People will love themselves, desire too much, brag, be arrogant, disrespect God, not obey parents, not be thankful, and not be respectful.
2 Timothy 3:3 Unloving, promise-breakers, liars, without self-control, violent, haters of the good,
2 Timothy 3:4 People who betray others, act without thinking, are full of themselves, and love fun more than they love God.
2 Timothy 3:5 They act religious but reject its true power. Stay away from these people.
2 Timothy 3:6 These people sneak into homes and take control of weak-willed women burdened with sins and swayed by various desires.
2 Timothy 3:7 Always learning, but never able to understand the truth.
2 Timothy 3:8 Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these people also reject the truth: they are corrupt thinkers and fail to accept the faith.
2 Timothy 3:9 They won't get any further: everyone will see their foolishness, just as others' was seen.
2 Timothy 3:10 You fully know my teaching, way of life, goal, faith, endurance, love, and patience.
2 Timothy 3:11 Hard times and troubles that happened to me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra, the tough situations I went through: but God rescued me from them all.
2 Timothy 3:12 Everyone who wants to live a good life in Christ Jesus will face troubles.
2 Timothy 3:13 Bad people and tricksters will become more and more wicked, cheating others and being cheated themselves.
2 Timothy 3:14 Keep following the teachings you have learned and are sure of, knowing who taught them to you.
2 Timothy 3:15 From childhood, you have known the sacred writings that can teach you to be saved through faith in Christ Jesus.
2 Timothy 3:16 All scripture comes from God's inspiration and is useful for teaching, for showing mistakes, for improving, and for training in right living.
2 Timothy 3:17 So the person who serves God can be complete, fully equipped for every good action.

2 Timothy 4:1 I command you before God and Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead when he comes and begins his kingdom;
2 Timothy 4:2 Share the message; always be ready, whether it's convenient or not; correct, scold, and encourage with patience and teaching.
2 Timothy 4:3 A time will come when people won't accept true teaching; instead, they will follow their own desires and collect teachers who tell them what they want to hear.
2 Timothy 4:4 They will stop listening to the truth and instead believe in made-up stories.
2 Timothy 4:5 Stay alert in everything, be patient with hardships, do the work of a messenger of good news, and fully carry out your service.
2 Timothy 4:6 I am ready to be sacrificed, and the time for me to leave is close.
2 Timothy 4:7 I have fought well, I have completed my race, I have stayed true to my beliefs.
2 Timothy 4:8 From now on, a crown of goodness is waiting for me, which God, the fair judge, will give me on that day; and not just to me, but to all who look forward to seeing Him.
2 Timothy 4:9 Make an effort to come to me soon.
2 Timothy 4:10 Demas left me because he loved this world and has gone to Thessalonica; Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
2 Timothy 4:11 Only Luke is with me. Bring Mark with you, because he is helpful to me in the work.
2 Timothy 4:12 I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
2 Timothy 4:13 Bring the coat I left in Troas with Carpus when you come, and the books, but mainly the scrolls.
2 Timothy 4:14 Alexander the metalworker caused me a lot of harm; may God repay him for what he has done.
2 Timothy 4:15 Be careful of him too; he has strongly opposed our message.
2 Timothy 4:16 At my first defense, no one was with me; everyone left me. I hope God will not hold it against them.
2 Timothy 4:17 Despite everything, God was with me and gave me strength, so that the message could be completely spread, and all non-Jewish people could hear it; and I was saved from the lion's mouth.
2 Timothy 4:18 God will rescue me from all evil deeds and keep me safe for his heavenly kingdom. To God be glory forever. Amen.
2 Timothy 4:19 Say hello to Prisca and Aquila, and to the family of Onesiphorus.
2 Timothy 4:20 Erastus stayed in Corinth, but I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
2 Timothy 4:21 Try hard to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers send their greetings.
2 Timothy 4:22 May Jesus Christ be with your spirit. May you have grace. Amen.

Titus 1:1 Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, follows the faith of God's chosen ones and recognizes the truth that leads to a godly life.
Titus 1:2 Hoping for eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before the world started.
Titus 1:3 God showed his message at the right time through preaching, which was given to me by the order of God our Savior.
Titus 1:4 To Titus, my true son in our shared faith: May you have kindness, compassion, and peace from God the Father and Jesus Christ our Savior.
Titus 1:5 I left you in Crete so you could fix what was needed and appoint leaders in each town, as I told you.
Titus 1:6 If anyone is without fault, married to one wife, and has trustworthy children who are not accused of being wild or disobedient.
Titus 1:7 A leader in the church must be without fault, as God's manager; not stubborn, not quick to anger, not addicted to alcohol, not violent, not greedy for money.
Titus 1:8 But someone who welcomes guests, likes good people, is self-controlled, fair, holy, and disciplined;
Titus 1:9 Sticking to the true message as taught to him, so he can use solid teaching to encourage and prove wrong those who disagree.
Titus 1:10 There are many who do not obey, who talk for no good reason and trick others, especially those who insist on circumcision.
Titus 1:11 These people who confuse entire families by teaching wrong things for dishonest gain must be silenced.
Titus 1:12 One of their own prophets said, 'People from Crete are always lying, they're bad creatures, and they are lazy.'
Titus 1:13 This testimony is true. So correct them firmly, so they will have a strong faith.
Titus 1:14 Do not pay attention to Jewish stories or human rules that turn people away from the truth.
Titus 1:15 To the pure, everything is pure; but to those who are spoiled and don't believe, nothing is pure because their minds and hearts are spoiled.
Titus 1:16 They claim to know God, but their actions deny Him, being hateful, disobedient, and useless for any good work.

Titus 2:1 Teach what matches with good teaching.
Titus 2:2 Older men should be self-controlled, serious, wise, strong in faith, loving, and patient.
Titus 2:3 Older women should also act in a way that fits with a holy life, not spreading rumors, not drinking too much, and teaching what is good.
Titus 2:4 To help young women be sensible, love their husbands, and love their children.
Titus 2:5 To be wise, pure, take care of their homes, kind, and listen to their husbands, so God's message is not spoken against.
Titus 2:6 Advise young men also to be self-controlled.
Titus 2:7 In everything, be an example of good actions: teach with honesty, seriousness, and truthfulness.
Titus 2:8 Speak clearly and rightly so no one can find fault with you, and those who disagree might feel embarrassed because they can't say anything bad about you.
Titus 2:9 Tell workers to listen to their bosses, try hard to make them happy in everything, and not talk back.
Titus 2:10 Do not steal, but show complete loyalty, so that in everything you may make the teachings of God our Savior attractive.
Titus 2:11 God's grace that offers salvation has been shown to everyone.
Titus 2:12 This teaches us to say no to ungodly ways and worldly desires, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in this world.
Titus 2:13 Waiting for the happy hope and the wonderful coming of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ.
Titus 2:14 He gave himself for us, so he could rescue us from all wrongs and clean us for himself, to be his special people who are eager to do good.
Titus 2:15 Talk about these things, encourage others, and correct them with full authority. Don't let anyone look down on you.

Titus 3:1 Remind them to follow rulers and authorities, to listen to leaders, and to be prepared for all good actions.
Titus 3:2 Don't say bad things about anyone, avoid fighting, be kind, and show humbleness to everyone.
Titus 3:3 We were once foolish, disobedient, misled, chasing many desires and pleasures, living with meanness and jealousy, full of hate, and hating each other.
Titus 3:4 But then God our Savior showed us kindness and love.
Titus 3:5 We are not saved by our good deeds, but by God's kindness. He saved us by giving us a new birth and a fresh start through the Holy Spirit.
Titus 3:6 He gave to us generously through Jesus Christ our Savior.
Titus 3:7 Being made right with God by His kindness, we should become inheritors based on the hope of everlasting life.
Titus 3:8 This true saying I want you to always confirm: those who trust in God should work hard to do good. These actions are good and helpful to people.
Titus 3:9 Stay away from silly questions, family histories, arguments, and fights about the law; they are useless and pointless.
Titus 3:10 Turn away from someone who keeps causing divisions after being warned once and then again.
Titus 3:11 Understand that someone like that has gone wrong, is sinning, and has judged himself guilty.
Titus 3:12 When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make sure to join me in Nicopolis, because I plan to stay there during the winter.
Titus 3:13 Take care to help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey carefully, so they lack nothing.
Titus 3:14 Let ours also learn to do good deeds for important needs, so they are not unproductive.
Titus 3:15 Everyone with me says hello to you. Say hi to those who love us because of our shared faith. May kindness be with all of you. Goodbye.

Philemon 1:1 Paul, a prisoner for Jesus Christ, and Timothy, our brother, to Philemon, our dear friend and coworker.
Philemon 1:2 To our dear friend Apphia, and Archippus our comrade in arms, and the church that meets in your home:
Philemon 1:3 May you have kindness and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ.
Philemon 1:4 I thank God, always mentioning you in my prayers.
Philemon 1:5 Hearing about your love and faith in Jesus, and for all God's people;
Philemon 1:6 May your faith become strong as you realize all the good things we have in Jesus.
Philemon 1:7 We are very happy and comforted by your love, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of God's holy people.
Philemon 1:8 Although I could be confident in Christ to instruct you to do what is right,
Philemon 1:9 For love's sake, I prefer to ask you kindly, since I am Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner for Jesus Christ.
Philemon 1:10 I ask you for my son Onesimus, who became my child while I was in chains.
Philemon 1:11 Before, this was not useful to you, but now it is useful to both of us.
Philemon 1:12 I have sent him back to you, so please welcome him, as he is dear to me.
Philemon 1:13 I wanted to keep him with me so he could help me while I am imprisoned for spreading the gospel, doing your work.
Philemon 1:14 I wouldn't do anything without your agreement, so your kindness is freely given, not forced.
Philemon 1:15 Maybe he left for a while so you could have him back forever.
Philemon 1:16 No longer as a servant, but more than a servant, a dear brother, especially to me, but even more to you, in person and in God.
Philemon 1:17 If you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would me.
Philemon 1:18 If he has wronged you or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
Philemon 1:19 I, Paul, wrote this with my own hand and will pay it back. But I won't remind you that you owe me your very self as well.
Philemon 1:20 Yes, brother, let me find joy in you through God: give me comfort and support in God.
Philemon 1:21 Trusting in your willingness to follow, I wrote to you, knowing you will do even more than I ask.
Philemon 1:22 Please also get a room ready for me, because I believe that thanks to your prayers, I will be able to come to you.
Philemon 1:23 Epaphras, who is in prison with me for following Jesus, sends you greetings.
Philemon 1:24 Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow workers.
Philemon 1:25 May the kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

Hebrews 1:1 God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets at different times and in various ways in the past.
Hebrews 1:2 In these last days, God has spoken to us through his Son, whom he made the heir of everything and who also created the universe.
Hebrews 1:3 He shines with God's glory and is the exact likeness of God, holding everything together with his powerful word. After he had cleaned away our sins, he sat down at the place of honor beside the great God in heaven.
Hebrews 1:4 He is made much better than the angels because he inherited a more excellent name than theirs.
Hebrews 1:5 To which angel did God ever say, "You are my Son, today I have become your Father"? And again, "I will be his Father, and he will be my Son"?
Hebrews 1:6 When he brings his firstborn into the world, he says, "Let all God's angels worship him."
Hebrews 1:7 About the angels, God says, "He makes his angels spirits, and his servants flames of fire."
Hebrews 1:8 God says to the Son, "Your throne, O God, lasts forever and ever; a scepter of righteousness is the scepter of your kingdom."
Hebrews 1:9 You have loved what is right and hated what is wrong; therefore, God, your God, has chosen you and made you happier than your friends with the oil of joy.
Hebrews 1:10 And, you, God, at the start created the earth's foundation; and you made the skies with your hands.
Hebrews 1:11 They will disappear, but you will last; and they will all grow old like clothes.
Hebrews 1:12 Like clothes you roll up, they will be changed, but you stay the same, and your years will never end.
Hebrews 1:13 But to which angel did God ever say, "Sit at my right side until I make your enemies a place to rest your feet"?
Hebrews 1:14 Aren't they all serving spirits, sent to help those who will inherit salvation?

Hebrews 2:1 So we should pay careful attention to what we have heard, so that we don't forget it.
Hebrews 2:2 If the message given by angels was firm, and every wrongdoing and disobedience got a fair punishment;
Hebrews 2:3 How can we escape if we ignore such a great salvation; first announced by the Lord, and confirmed to us by those who heard him?
Hebrews 2:4 God also showed support for them with signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, as God wanted.
Hebrews 2:5 God did not give angels control of the future world we talk about.
Hebrews 2:6 Someone in a certain place said, "What is man, that you think about him? Or a human being that you take care of him?"
Hebrews 2:7 You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honor, and you put him in charge of all you made.
Hebrews 2:8 You have placed everything under his control. Because by making everything under his control, you did not leave anything out of his control. But now we do not see everything under his control yet.
Hebrews 2:9 We see Jesus, made a bit lower than angels to suffer death, now crowned with glory and honor; so by God's kindness, he might experience death for everyone.
Hebrews 2:10 It was right for God, for whom and by whom everything exists, to bring many children to glory by making the leader of their salvation perfect through what he suffered.
Hebrews 2:11 The one who makes holy and those being made holy all have the same Father. That's why he isn't embarrassed to call them brothers.
Hebrews 2:12 I will tell my brothers about you, God; I will sing your praises in the church.
Hebrews 2:13 I will trust in God again. And again, look at me and the children God has given me.
Hebrews 2:14 Since the children have flesh and blood, he too shared in their humanity so that by his death he could defeat the one who had the power of death, that is, the devil.
Hebrews 2:15 Free those who, because they were afraid of death, were slaves their whole lives.
Hebrews 2:16 Truly, he did not take on an angel's nature, but he took on the nature of Abraham's descendants.
Hebrews 2:17 So in every way he had to become like his brothers and sisters, so he could be a kind and trustworthy high priest in matters related to God, and to bring about forgiveness for the people's sins.
Hebrews 2:18 Because he himself was tempted and suffered, he can help those who are tempted.

Hebrews 3:1 Therefore, holy brothers and sisters, who share in the call from heaven, think about Jesus, the messenger and high priest we profess.
Hebrews 3:2 He was loyal to God who chose him, just like Moses was loyal in every part of God's house.
Hebrews 3:3 This man was considered more glorious than Moses, because the one who builds the house is more honored than the house itself.
Hebrews 3:4 Every house is built by someone, but God is the one who built everything.
Hebrews 3:5 Moses was truly loyal in all God's house as a servant, to witness what would be said later.
Hebrews 3:6 But Christ is like a son in charge of his own home, and we are that home if we keep our courage and the joy of our hope strong until the end.
Hebrews 3:7 Therefore, (as God says, today if you listen to his voice,
Hebrews 3:8 Do not make your hearts hard as you did when you tested me in the desert.
Hebrews 3:9 When your ancestors tested me, they saw what I could do for forty years.
Hebrews 3:10 So I was upset with those people and said, "They always go wrong in their hearts; they have never understood my ways."
Hebrews 3:11 I swore in my anger, they will not enter my place of rest.
Hebrews 3:12 Be careful, friends, so none of you have an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
Hebrews 3:13 Encourage each other every day, while it is still called "Today," so that none of you become stubborn because of sin's trickery.
Hebrews 3:14 We share in Christ if we keep our first confidence firm to the end.
Hebrews 3:15 Today, if you will listen to his voice, do not harden your hearts as you did during the rebellion.
Hebrews 3:16 Some who heard God's message made him angry, but not everyone who left Egypt with Moses did so.
Hebrews 3:17 But who made God upset for 40 years? Was it not those who sinned, whose bodies dropped dead in the desert?
Hebrews 3:18 And who did God promise would not enter his place of rest? It was those who did not believe.
Hebrews 3:19 So we understand they couldn't go in because they did not believe.

Hebrews 4:1 Let us be careful then that none of you fail to reach the rest that God promised.
Hebrews 4:2 The good news was told to us just like it was to them. But the message they heard didn't help them, because they didn't trust when they listened.
Hebrews 4:3 We who believe enter into rest, just as God said, "I swore in my anger they would not enter my rest," even though the works were done since the beginning of the world.
Hebrews 4:4 He talked about the seventh day like this: God rested on the seventh day from all his work.
Hebrews 4:5 And in this place again, if they will enter into my peace.
Hebrews 4:6 So, it's clear some people will still enter, but those who first heard the message did not because they did not believe.
Hebrews 4:7 He sets a specific day, calling it "Today," as David did after a long time, saying, "If you hear God's voice today, do not make your hearts stubborn."
Hebrews 4:8 If Jesus had given them rest, he would not have spoken about another day later on.
Hebrews 4:9 So there is still a rest for God's people.
Hebrews 4:10 Whoever enters into rest also stops working just like God did from his own.
Hebrews 4:11 Let us work hard to enter that rest so that no one will fall by following the same path of disbelief.
Hebrews 4:12 God's message is alive, strong, and sharper than any double-edged sword. It cuts deep, even separating the soul and spirit, joints and marrow, and it can tell what the heart thinks and wants.
Hebrews 4:13 No creature is hidden from God; everything is completely exposed to his view.
Hebrews 4:14 Since we have a great priest who has gone into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let's keep strongly to our faith.
Hebrews 4:15 We don't have a high priest who can't understand our weaknesses; He was tempted in every way just like us, but He did not sin.
Hebrews 4:16 Let us then go confidently to God's throne of grace to receive mercy and find grace that will help us when we need it.

Hebrews 5:1 Every high priest chosen from people is appointed for people in matters related to God, so he can present both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
Hebrews 5:2 Who can understand those who don't know, and those who have lost their way? Because that person also has weaknesses.
