Hebrews 5:3 For this reason, he must offer sacrifices for sins for the people and also for himself.
Hebrews 5:4 No one takes this honor for themselves, but only those called by God, just like Aaron was.
Hebrews 5:5 Christ did not give himself the honor of becoming a high priest; but God, who told him, "You are my Son, today I have become your father," did.
Hebrews 5:6 God also says in another place, "You are a priest forever in the way of Melchizedek."
Hebrews 5:7 During his time on earth, when he prayed and pleaded with loud crying and tears to God, who could save him from death, he was heard because he respected God.
Hebrews 5:8 Even though he was a son, he learned to obey through what he went through.
Hebrews 5:9 When he became perfect, he caused everlasting salvation for all who obey him.
Hebrews 5:10 God chose him to be a high priest like Melchisedec.
Hebrews 5:11 We have much to say about this, but it is difficult because you are slow to listen.
Hebrews 5:12 By now you should be teachers, but you need someone to teach you the basics of God's message again. You're like babies who need milk, not solid food.
Hebrews 5:13 Everyone who drinks milk is not experienced in the teaching of right living because they are like a baby.
Hebrews 5:14 Solid food is for grown-ups, who have trained their senses to tell right from wrong through practice.

Hebrews 6:1 So, moving beyond the basic teachings about Christ, let's grow towards complete understanding, without going over the beginning lessons about turning away from useless actions and believing in God again.
Hebrews 6:2 About the teaching of baptisms, the act of placing hands, the rising of the dead, and forever judgment.
Hebrews 6:3 We will do this if God allows it.
Hebrews 6:4 It's impossible for those who once understood, enjoyed the gift from heaven, and shared in the Holy Spirit.
Hebrews 6:5 And have experienced the good message of God and the powers of the future world.
Hebrews 6:6 If they turn away again after knowing the truth, it's impossible to bring them back to change their ways; because they are like they are crucifying God's Son all over again, and shaming him publicly.
Hebrews 6:7 The land that soaks up the frequent rain and produces useful plants for the people who take care of it gets blessings from God.
Hebrews 6:8 The plant that grows thorns and briers is useless, close to being cursed, and its fate is to be burned.
Hebrews 6:9 Dear friends, we are confident of better things in your case, things that go with being saved, even though we talk like this.
Hebrews 6:10 God is fair and won't forget the work and love you showed for His name by serving His holy people, and you still serve them.
Hebrews 6:11 We want each of you to show the same hard work to be fully sure of your hope until the end.
Hebrews 6:12 Work hard and follow those who, with faith and patience, receive what God has promised.
Hebrews 6:13 When God promised Abraham, because there was no one greater to swear by, he swore by himself.
Hebrews 6:14 I will surely bless you and give you many descendants.
Hebrews 6:15 After waiting patiently, he received the promise.
Hebrews 6:16 People truly make promises by someone greater, and an oath ends all arguments for them.
Hebrews 6:17 God, wanting to show the heirs of the promise his unchanging plan more clearly, guaranteed it with an oath.
Hebrews 6:18 Through two unchangeable things, where it is impossible for God to lie, we can have strong comfort, as we have run to take hold of the hope offered to us.
Hebrews 6:19 We have hope as an anchor for the soul, strong and secure, that reaches behind the curtain.
Hebrews 6:20 Jesus, our forerunner, has entered there for us and become a high priest forever, in the same way as Melchizedek.

Hebrews 7:1 Melchizedek, the king of Salem and priest of God most high, met Abraham as he returned from defeating the kings and blessed him.
Hebrews 7:2 Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. He is first called the King of Righteousness, then also the King of Salem, meaning King of Peace.
Hebrews 7:3 Without a father or mother, without family history, having no start or end to life; but made similar to God's Son; remains a priest forever.
Hebrews 7:4 Think about how important this man was, to whom even Abraham, the ancestor, gave a tenth of the goods he won.
Hebrews 7:5 Truly, the descendants of Levi who become priests are commanded to collect a tenth part of the people's goods by the law, even from their own relatives who are also descendants of Abraham.
Hebrews 7:6 The person who did not come from Abraham's family line still got a tenth of what Abraham had, and blessed Abraham who had been given God's promises.
Hebrews 7:7 Without any doubt, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
Hebrews 7:8 Here, people who will die collect tithes; but there, God collects them, who is known to be alive.
Hebrews 7:9 I can also say that Levi, who gets tithes, paid tithes through Abraham.
Hebrews 7:10 He was still in his father's body when Melchisedec met him.
Hebrews 7:11 So if the Levitical priests could have made everything perfect, (because under them the people got the law,) why did we need another priest like Melchisedec instead of one from Aaron's family?
Hebrews 7:12 When the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
Hebrews 7:13 He about whom these things are said belongs to a different tribe, one that has no one serving at the altar.
Hebrews 7:14 It is clear that our Lord came from the tribe of Judah, a tribe Moses said nothing about regarding priests.
Hebrews 7:15 It's even clearer that another priest comes who is like Melchisedec.
Hebrews 7:16 He was chosen not by the rule of a physical command, but by the power of a life that never ends.
Hebrews 7:17 He says, "You are a priest forever, following the way of Melchizedek."
Hebrews 7:18 Truly, the old rule is cancelled because it was weak and useless.
Hebrews 7:19 The law made nothing perfect, but a better hope did, and through this we come close to God.
Hebrews 7:20 Because God made a promise, he became a priest.
Hebrews 7:21 The previous priests became priests without a promise, but this priest was chosen with a promise when God said to him, "I have promised, and I will not change my mind: you will be a priest forever, just like Melchizedek."
Hebrews 7:22 Jesus became a guaranteed promise of a better agreement.
Hebrews 7:23 There were many priests, because they could not continue their work when they died.
Hebrews 7:24 This man has a permanent priesthood because he lives forever.
Hebrews 7:25 He can fully save those who come to God through him, because he always lives to speak for them.
Hebrews 7:26 A high priest like this suits us, holy, innocent, pure, apart from sinners, and raised above the heavens.
Hebrews 7:27 He doesn't need to offer sacrifices every day like the high priests, who first do it for their own sins, then for the people’s sins. He did this once for all when he sacrificed himself.
Hebrews 7:28 The law appoints men as high priests even though they have weaknesses; but the promise that came after the law appoints the Son, who is made perfect forever.

Hebrews 8:1 Here's the main point of what we've said: We have a high priest who sits at the right side of the throne of God in heaven.
Hebrews 8:2 A servant of the holy place and the real tent that God set up, not humans.
Hebrews 8:3 Every high priest is chosen to give gifts and sacrifices, so this man must have something to offer too.
Hebrews 8:4 If he were on earth, he wouldn't be a priest because there are already priests who give gifts following the law.
Hebrews 8:5 Those who serve are working with a copy and shadow of the things in heaven, just as Moses was warned by God when he was about to build the tent: God told him, "Make sure you make everything according to the design shown to you on the mountain."
Hebrews 8:6 He now has a greater service because he is the mediator of a better agreement, which is based on better promises.
Hebrews 8:7 If the first agreement had been perfect, there would be no need to look for a second one.
Hebrews 8:8 Because he found faults with them, God says, "Look, the time is coming when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and the people of Judah."
Hebrews 8:9 This is not like the agreement I made with their ancestors when I took their hand to guide them out of Egypt; they did not keep my agreement, so I ignored them, says God.
Hebrews 8:10 This is the agreement that I will set up with the people of Israel after that time, says God; I will place my rules in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Hebrews 8:11 They won't need to teach their neighbors or their brothers, saying, 'Know God,' because everyone, from the least to the greatest, will know me.
Hebrews 8:12 I will be kind to their wrongs, and I will not remember their sins and bad acts anymore.
Hebrews 8:13 By saying "a new agreement," he has made the first one old. And what is getting old and wearing out will soon disappear.

Hebrews 9:1 Truly, the first agreement also had rules for worshiping God, and a sanctuary on earth.
Hebrews 9:2 They set up a tent; the first part had a lampstand, a table, and bread on display; this area is called the holy place.
Hebrews 9:3 Beyond the second curtain was the part of the tent called the Most Holy Place.
Hebrews 9:4 It had the golden incense burner and the gold-covered covenant chest, which held the gold jar of manna, Aaron's staff that sprouted leaves, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
Hebrews 9:5 Above it were glorious angels covering the mercy seat; we cannot discuss this in detail now.
Hebrews 9:6 After these rules were set, the priests regularly entered the first part of the tent to perform God's work.
Hebrews 9:7 The high priest alone went into the second room once a year, and always with blood, which he offered for himself and the people's mistakes.
Hebrews 9:8 The Holy Spirit shows that the way into the most holy place was not clear while the first tent was still in use.
Hebrews 9:9 This represented the present time, where gifts and sacrifices were given that could not make the worshiper completely clear in conscience.
Hebrews 9:10 This referred only to food, drinks, various cleansings, and physical rules given to them until a time of change.
Hebrews 9:11 But Christ has come as a high priest of the good things that will happen, through a greater and more perfect place of worship, not built by hand, that is, not of this creation.
Hebrews 9:12 Not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, he went into the holy place once and got forever salvation for us.
Hebrews 9:13 If the blood of bulls and goats and the ashes of a young cow sprinkled on the unclean make the body clean.
Hebrews 9:14 How much more will Christ's blood, who offered himself to God without any fault through the eternal Spirit, clean your conscience from useless actions so you can serve the living God?
Hebrews 9:15 For this reason, he is the mediator of the new agreement, so that through death, to free those who sinned under the first agreement, those who are invited can receive the promised eternal inheritance.
Hebrews 9:16 For there to be a will, the person who made it must die.
Hebrews 9:17 A will only takes effect when someone dies; it has no power while the person who made it is alive.
Hebrews 9:18 The first agreement was not made without using blood.
Hebrews 9:19 After Moses told all the rules to the people, he took the blood of calves and goats with water, red wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled it on the book and all the people.
Hebrews 9:20 This is the blood of the agreement which God has commanded for you.
Hebrews 9:21 He also sprinkled blood on both the tent and all the items used for service.
Hebrews 9:22 Almost everything is cleansed with blood by the law; and without blood being shed, there is no forgiveness.
Hebrews 9:23 So it was essential to clean the copies of heavenly things with these methods, but the heavenly things needed better offerings than these.
Hebrews 9:24 Christ did not enter a sanctuary made by humans, which is only a copy of the real one, but into heaven itself to be with God on our behalf.
Hebrews 9:25 He doesn't need to offer himself many times, like the high priest who goes into the sacred place every year with blood that is not his own.
Hebrews 9:26 Since the world began, he would have had to suffer many times. But now, he has come once at the end of the ages to remove sin by sacrificing himself.
Hebrews 9:27 Everyone is meant to die once and after that comes judgment.
Hebrews 9:28 Christ was offered once to take away the sins of many; and he will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to bring salvation to those who are waiting for him.

Hebrews 10:1 The law has only a shadow of the good things that will come, not the real things themselves. So it can never make perfect those who come to God by the same sacrifices they offer continually every year.
Hebrews 10:2 If that were true, wouldn't the offerings have stopped? Because the worshippers would be cleansed and no longer feel guilty for their sins.
Hebrews 10:3 In those sacrifices, they recall sins every year.
Hebrews 10:4 Bull and goat blood cannot remove sins.
Hebrews 10:5 When he enters the world, he says, "You did not want sacrifices and offerings, but you prepared a body for me."
Hebrews 10:6 You did not find joy in burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.
Hebrews 10:7 I said, "Look, I am coming to do your will, God, as it is written about me in the book."
Hebrews 10:8 God did not want sacrifices, burnt offerings, or sin offerings, which are given according to the law.
Hebrews 10:9 He said, "Look, I come to do your will, God. He removes the first to set up the second."
Hebrews 10:10 Through this will, we are made holy by the sacrifice of Jesus Christ's body, once for all.
Hebrews 10:11 Every priest stands every day to serve and often gives the same sacrifices that can never remove sins.
Hebrews 10:12 This man offered one sacrifice for sins forever and then sat down at God's right side.
Hebrews 10:13 From now on waiting until his enemies are turned into his footrest.
Hebrews 10:14 With one sacrifice, he has made perfect forever those who are made holy.
Hebrews 10:15 The Holy Spirit is also a witness to us because he had previously said,
Hebrews 10:16 This is the promise I will make with them after that time, says God: I will place my laws in their hearts, and I will write them in their minds.
Hebrews 10:17 I will not remember their sins and wrongs anymore.
Hebrews 10:18 When these have been forgiven, there is no need for any more sacrifices for sin.
Hebrews 10:19 So, friends, we can confidently go into the most sacred place because of Jesus' blood.
Hebrews 10:20 Through a new and living way he made for us, going through the curtain, which is his body.
Hebrews 10:21 We have a great priest in charge of God's house.
Hebrews 10:22 Let's come close with a true heart, fully sure of our faith, with hearts cleaned from bad thoughts, and bodies washed with clean water.
Hebrews 10:23 Let's firmly keep our faith without doubting; (because God who promised is trustworthy;)
Hebrews 10:24 Let's think about each other to encourage love and good deeds.
Hebrews 10:25 Don't stop meeting together, as some do, but encourage each other, especially as you see the day coming closer.
Hebrews 10:26 If we choose to sin after knowing the truth, there is no more sacrifice left for sins.
Hebrews 10:27 A scary expectation of judgment and burning anger, which will consume the enemies.
Hebrews 10:28 Anyone who ignored Moses' law was put to death without pity on the testimony of two or three people.
Hebrews 10:29 How much worse punishment do you think will be given to someone who has stepped on the Son of God, treated the blood of the agreement that made him holy as nothing special, and insulted the Spirit of kindness?
Hebrews 10:30 We know the one who said, "It is my job to take revenge; I will pay them back," says God. And again, "God will judge his people."
Hebrews 10:31 Being in the power of the living God can be very frightening.
Hebrews 10:32 Remember the early days when, after you were enlightened, you faced many hard struggles.
Hebrews 10:33 You were publicly shamed and suffered, and you stood by those who were treated the same way.
Hebrews 10:34 You felt sorry for me in my chains, and happily accepted losing your things because you knew you have something better and lasting in heaven.
Hebrews 10:35 Do not give up your confidence; it will bring a great reward.
Hebrews 10:36 You need patience, so that after doing God's will, you can receive what was promised.
Hebrews 10:37 In just a short time, the one who will come, will come and won't delay.
Hebrews 10:38 The good person will live by trusting in God; but if someone turns away, God will not be pleased with that person.
Hebrews 10:39 We are not those who turn back and are destroyed, but those who have faith and save their souls.

Hebrews 11:1 Faith is being sure of what we hope for and certain of what we do not see.
Hebrews 11:2 By it, the older people earned praise.
Hebrews 11:3 By believing, we know that God made the worlds with His command, so that what we see was not made from what we can see.
Hebrews 11:4 By trusting, Abel gave God a better offering than Cain, and it showed he was good, with God confirming his gifts; even after his death, he still speaks through it.
Hebrews 11:5 Through faith, Enoch was taken up so he wouldn't experience death; and he was not found, because God had taken him up. Before he was taken up, it was known that he pleased God.
Hebrews 11:6 Without faith, you cannot please God: whoever approaches God must believe that God exists and that he rewards those who earnestly search for him.
Hebrews 11:7 Trusting in God, Noah, who was warned about things still unseen, built an ark out of fear to save his family; by doing this, he showed the world was wrong and became the rightful owner of the goodness that comes from faith.
Hebrews 11:8 Abraham trusted God, and when he was told to go to a land he would later get as his own, he obeyed and left, even though he didn't know where he was going.
Hebrews 11:9 Through trust, he lived as a foreigner in the promised land, staying in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who were also promised the same inheritance.
Hebrews 11:10 He was looking for a city with solid foundations, built by God.
Hebrews 11:11 Sarah's faith gave her the power to have a child, even when she was too old, because she believed God who promised it.
Hebrews 11:12 From just one man, almost dead, came as many descendants as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand by the sea—too many to count.
Hebrews 11:13 All these people died still believing what God had promised them. They did not receive what was promised, but they saw it all from a distance and welcomed it. They agreed that they were just visitors and travelers on earth.
Hebrews 11:14 People who say these things make it clear that they are looking for a homeland.
Hebrews 11:15 Truly, if they had thought of the country they left, they could have found a chance to go back.
Hebrews 11:16 But now they want a better place, that is, a heavenly one. So, God is not ashamed to be called their God because he has made a city for them.
Hebrews 11:17 Abraham, because of his faith, when tested, was willing to sacrifice Isaac. And this man, who was given God's promises, was ready to sacrifice his only son.
Hebrews 11:18 God said your descendants will be named through Isaac.
Hebrews 11:19 Believing that God could bring him back to life, even from death; which is also how he figuratively got him back.
Hebrews 11:20 With trust, Isaac gave blessings to Jacob and Esau for their future.
Hebrews 11:21 In faith, when Jacob was near death, he gave a blessing to both of Joseph's sons and worshiped God, resting on his staff.
Hebrews 11:22 Joseph, trusting in God, talked about the Israelites leaving Egypt before he died, and gave instructions about what should be done with his bones.
Hebrews 11:23 Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born because they saw he was a special child and they were not scared of the king's order.
Hebrews 11:24 By faith, when Moses grew up, he chose not to be called Pharaoh's daughter's son.
Hebrews 11:25 Choosing to endure hardship with God's people instead of enjoying short-lived sinful pleasures.
Hebrews 11:26 Valuing the shame of following Christ as greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, because he looked forward to the reward.
Hebrews 11:27 Through trust, he left Egypt, not scared of the king's anger; because he stayed strong, as if seeing God who can't be seen.
Hebrews 11:28 By believing, he held the passover and put blood on the doorposts so the destroyer of the first children would not touch them.
Hebrews 11:29 Through faith, they crossed the Red Sea on dry ground, but when the Egyptians tried to do the same, they drowned.
Hebrews 11:30 By believing, the walls of Jericho fell after people marched around them for seven days.
Hebrews 11:31 By trusting, Rahab the prostitute did not die with those who did not believe, when she welcomed the spies peacefully.
Hebrews 11:32 What more can I say? I don't have enough time to talk about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
Hebrews 11:33 People with faith overcame kingdoms, did what is right, received what was promised, and shut lions' mouths.
Hebrews 11:34 Put out fires, avoided being killed by swords, became strong from being weak, grew brave in battle, and made foreign armies run away.
Hebrews 11:35 Women got back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured and did not accept rescue, so they could have a better resurrection.
Hebrews 11:36 Others faced mean teasing and whippings, and were also put in chains and jail.
Hebrews 11:37 They were hit with stones, cut into pieces, tested, and killed with swords. They moved around in sheep and goat skins, poor, suffering, and in pain.
Hebrews 11:38 The world did not deserve them: they roamed through deserts, in mountains, and in holes and caves of the ground.
Hebrews 11:39 Even though they were praised for their faith, they did not receive what God promised.
Hebrews 11:40 God has prepared something better for us, so that they would not reach perfection without us.

Hebrews 12:1 Since we are surrounded by so many examples, let's get rid of every burden and the sin that trips us up, and run with endurance the race ahead of us.
Hebrews 12:2 Focusing on Jesus, the starter and completer of our faith; who, because of the joy awaiting him, went through the suffering of the cross, ignored its disgrace, and is now seated at the place of honor beside God's throne.
Hebrews 12:3 Think about how he put up with so much opposition from sinners, so you won't get tired and give up in your minds.
Hebrews 12:4 You haven't fought against sin to the point of shedding blood.
Hebrews 12:5 You have forgotten the encouragement that speaks to you like children, "My child, do not hate God's discipline, nor give up when you are corrected by him."
Hebrews 12:6 God corrects those he loves and disciplines every child he accepts.
Hebrews 12:7 If you accept discipline, God treats you like children; because what child is not disciplined by their father?
Hebrews 12:8 If you are not disciplined, which everyone undergoes, then you are not true children but are like those without a father.
Hebrews 12:9 We had earthly fathers who disciplined us and we respected them. Shouldn't we submit even more to the Father of our spirits and live?
Hebrews 12:10 They disciplined us for a short time as they thought best; but God does it for our good, so that we can share in his holiness.
Hebrews 12:11 At the moment, discipline doesn't seem pleasant but painful. But later, it gives those who are trained by it a peaceful reward of doing right.
Hebrews 12:12 So, raise your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees.
Hebrews 12:13 Make straight paths for your feet, so the injured may not be led astray but may heal instead.
Hebrews 12:14 Seek peace with everyone and live a holy life, because without holiness no one will see God.
Hebrews 12:15 Watch carefully so no one misses out on God's grace; so that no bitter root grows and causes you trouble, making many impure.
Hebrews 12:16 Make sure no one is sexually immoral or godless like Esau, who sold his rights as the firstborn for a single meal.
Hebrews 12:17 You know that later, when he wanted to receive the blessing, he was turned away because he could not change what had happened, even though he cried and tried hard to.
Hebrews 12:18 You have not come to a mountain you can touch, one that burns with fire, or to darkness, gloom, and storms.
Hebrews 12:19 They heard the trumpet and a voice speaking words; those who heard the voice begged that no more words would be spoken to them.
Hebrews 12:20 They couldn't stand the command that if even an animal touched the mountain, it must be stoned or shot with an arrow.
Hebrews 12:21 The sight was so frightening that Moses said, "I am very scared and shaking."
Hebrews 12:22 You have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to countless angels.
Hebrews 12:23 To the main gathering and community of the first children, whose names are in heaven, and to God the Judge of everyone, and to the spirits of good people made complete,
Hebrews 12:24 And to Jesus the go-between of the new agreement, and to the blood that was sprinkled, which speaks of better things than Abel's blood.
Hebrews 12:25 Make sure you do not ignore the one who is speaking. If those who ignored the one who spoke on earth did not get away, we will certainly not get away if we turn away from the one who speaks from heaven.
Hebrews 12:26 God's voice shook the earth before. But now he has promised, saying, "Once more I will shake not just the earth, but also the heavens."
Hebrews 12:27 This message, "Once more," means that what can be shaken will be removed, so that what cannot be shaken will stay.
Hebrews 12:28 Since we are given a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us be grateful, so that we can worship God in a way that pleases Him, with respect and awe.
Hebrews 12:29 Our God is like a fire that burns everything up.

Hebrews 13:1 Keep loving each other like brothers and sisters.
Hebrews 13:2 Don't forget to welcome strangers, because by doing this some people have welcomed angels without realizing it.
Hebrews 13:3 Remember those in prison as if you were there with them, and think of those who are mistreated as if you were suffering too.
Hebrews 13:4 Marriage is respected by everyone, and the marriage bed should be kept pure. But God will judge those who sell sex and cheat in marriage.
Hebrews 13:5 Speak without wanting more, and be happy with what you have: because God has promised, I will always be with you and never abandon you.
Hebrews 13:6 We can say confidently, God helps me, so I will not be afraid of what anyone does to me.
Hebrews 13:7 Remember your leaders who taught you God's message; copy their faith, looking at how their lives ended.
Hebrews 13:8 Jesus Christ is the same in the past, today, and forever.
Hebrews 13:9 Do not be led away by various and strange teachings. It is good for our hearts to be strengthened by kindness, not by food rules which have not helped those who follow them.
Hebrews 13:10 We have an altar that those who work in the place of worship have no right to eat from.
Hebrews 13:11 The bodies of those animals, whose blood the high priest brings into the holy place for sin, are burned outside the camp.
Hebrews 13:12 So Jesus, to make the people holy with his blood, suffered outside the city gate.
Hebrews 13:13 Let's go out to him outside the camp, carrying his shame.
Hebrews 13:14 We have no lasting city here, but we look for one in the future.
Hebrews 13:15 So let us always offer to God our praise, which is saying thanks to him with our words.
Hebrews 13:16 Don't forget to do good and to share with others: God is very pleased with these kinds of sacrifices.
Hebrews 13:17 Listen to those who lead you, and follow their guidance; they are responsible for your well-being and must explain their actions, so let them do so happily, not sadly, because that would be bad for you.
Hebrews 13:18 Pray for us, because we believe we have a clear conscience and want to live right in everything.
Hebrews 13:19 I urge you to do this so I can return to you more quickly.
Hebrews 13:20 Now the God of peace, who brought back our Lord Jesus from the dead, the great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the eternal promise,
Hebrews 13:21 Help you be complete in every good action to do his will, doing in you what pleases him, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Hebrews 13:22 And I ask you, friends, to accept these words of encouragement, for I have written a short letter to you.
Hebrews 13:23 Understand that our brother Timothy has been freed; if he arrives soon, I will visit you with him.
Hebrews 13:24 Greet all who lead you and all of God's people. Those in Italy send you greetings.
Hebrews 13:25 May God's kindness be with everyone. Amen.

James 1:1 James, a servant of God and Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes spread out, hello.
James 1:2 My friends, consider it a joy when you face many kinds of trials.
James 1:3 Understand that testing your faith develops patience.
James 1:4 Let patience finish its work so that you may be complete and whole, lacking nothing.
James 1:5 If anyone needs wisdom, ask God, who gives freely to all without criticizing, and it will be given to you.
James 1:6 Ask with strong belief, without doubting. Because someone who doubts is like a wave in the sea, blown and thrown by the wind.
James 1:7 Let that person not expect to receive anything from God.
James 1:8 A person with two minds is unsteady in everything they do.
James 1:9 Let the humble brother be happy because he is lifted up.
James 1:10 The rich person becomes humble, for like a flower in the grass they will fade away.
James 1:11 As soon as the sun rises with its hot heat, it dries up the grass, the flowers fall, and their beauty disappears: in the same way, the rich person will wilt in their life's path.
James 1:12 Happy is the person who keeps going through hard times because when he passes the test, he will get the reward of life that God has promised to those who love Him.
James 1:13 No one should say when they are tempted, "I am being tempted by God," because God cannot be tempted by evil, and he does not tempt anyone.
James 1:14 A person is tempted when they are pulled by their own desires and trapped.
James 1:15 When desire becomes strong, it leads to sin, and sin, when it's fully grown, results in death.
James 1:16 Don't make a mistake, my dear friends.
James 1:17 Every good and perfect gift comes from above, from the God of light, who never changes or casts shifting shadows.
James 1:18 God, by His own choice, gave us new life through the true message, so we might be the first and best of all He created.
James 1:19 My dear friends, everyone should be quick to listen, slow to talk, and slow to get angry.
James 1:20 Human anger does not produce the goodness that God wants.
James 1:21 Set aside all dirtiness and excess badness, and with humility accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.
James 1:22 Do what the message says, not just listen to it, or you will be fooling yourselves.
James 1:23 If someone listens to God's word but doesn't put it into practice, they are like a person who looks at their face in a mirror.
James 1:24 He looks at himself, then leaves, and quickly forgets what kind of person he was.
James 1:25 Whoever looks into the perfect law that gives freedom and keeps doing it, not forgetting what they heard but doing the work, will be blessed in what they do.
James 1:26 If someone appears to be religious but doesn't control their speech and fools themselves, their religion is worthless.
James 1:27 True and perfect religion in God's sight is this: to help orphans and widows when they are in need, and to keep oneself free from the world's corruption.

James 2:1 My brothers and sisters, do not combine faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, who is glorious, with favoritism.
James 2:2 If a man wearing a gold ring and fine clothes comes into your meeting, and a poor man in dirty clothes also comes in;
James 2:3 You favor the one in fancy clothes, telling him, "Sit here in a good spot," while you tell the poor person, "Stand there," or, "Sit by my feet."
James 2:4 Aren't you showing favoritism and judging with wrong thoughts?
James 2:5 Listen, my dear friends, hasn't God chosen the world's poor to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
James 2:6 You have looked down on the poor. Don't rich people bully you and drag you to court?
James 2:7 Aren't they insulting the honorable name you bear?
James 2:8 If you follow the important rule in the scripture, "Love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
James 2:9 If you show favoritism, you sin and break the law.
James 2:10 Anyone who follows all of God's laws but fails in one aspect is guilty of breaking them all.
James 2:11 For the one who said, "Do not cheat in marriage," also said, "Do not kill." So if you don't cheat but you do kill, you are still breaking the law.
James 2:12 Talk and act like people who will be judged by the law of freedom.
James 2:13 He will be judged without mercy if he has not been merciful; but mercy triumphs over judgment.
James 2:14 What good is it, my friends, if someone claims to have faith but doesn't act on it? Can faith alone save him?
James 2:15 If a brother or sister has no clothes and lacks everyday food,
James 2:16 If one of you tells them, "Go in peace, stay warm and well fed," but doesn’t give them what their body needs, what good is it?
James 2:17 Likewise, if faith does not have actions, it is dead by itself.
James 2:18 Someone might say, "You have faith, and I do things." Show me your faith without doing anything, and I'll show you my faith by what I do.
James 2:19 You believe there is one God; that's good: even demons believe that, and they shake with fear.
James 2:20 Do you want to understand, foolish person, that faith without actions is useless?
James 2:21 Wasn't Abraham our father proved right by his actions when he was about to sacrifice his son Isaac on the altar?
James 2:22 Do you see how faith worked together with his actions, and through actions faith was made complete?
James 2:23 The scripture came true that says, Abraham trusted God, and it was counted to him as being right with God: and he was named God's Friend.
James 2:24 You see then that a person is made right by what they do and not by faith alone.
James 2:25 Rahab, the prostitute, was also accepted for her actions when she took in the messengers and sent them off by a different path, right?
James 2:26 Just like a body without its spirit is dead, so is faith without actions.

James 3:1 My friends, don't all try to be teachers, because we know that we will be judged more strictly.
James 3:2 We all make many mistakes. If someone does not make mistakes when they speak, they are perfect and can control their whole body too.
James 3:3 Look, we put pieces in horse's mouths so they follow us; we guide their whole body.
James 3:4 Look at the ships too. Even though they are big and strong winds push them, a tiny rudder can steer them wherever the pilot chooses.
James 3:5 The tongue is small, yet it talks about big things. See how a small fire can start something so huge!
James 3:6 The tongue is like a fire; it is full of wrong. It can spoil your whole life and is itself set on fire by hell.
James 3:7 Every kind of animal, bird, snake, and sea creature can be tamed and has been tamed by humans.
James 3:8 No one can control the tongue; it is a restless evil, filled with deadly poison.
James 3:9 We use our words to bless God, the Father, and with those same words, we curse people who are made to look like God.
James 3:10 From the same mouth come both blessings and curses. My brothers, this should not be the case.
James 3:11 Can a spring pour out both fresh and bitter water from the same opening?
James 3:12 My friends, can a fig tree produce olives, or a grapevine produce figs? Just as a spring can't give both salty and fresh water.
James 3:13 Who is wise and has knowledge among you? Let them show their good actions with a humble attitude that comes from wisdom.
James 3:14 If you feel bitter jealousy and conflict in your hearts, don't boast or deny the truth.
James 3:15 This wisdom does not come from heaven but is from the earth, appealing to our senses, and evil.
James 3:16 Where jealousy and conflict exist, confusion and all kinds of wrong actions are found.
James 3:17 The wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceful, kind, willing to listen, full of mercy and good actions, fair, and sincere.
James 3:18 The good results of right living are planted in peace by those who work for peace.

James 4:1 Where do your wars and battles with each other come from? Do they not come from your desires that battle within you?
James 4:2 You want things but don't have them. You kill and are jealous but still cannot get what you want. You argue and fight but don't have because you don't ask.
James 4:3 You ask but don't receive because you ask with wrong motives, wanting only to satisfy your desires.
James 4:4 You unfaithful men and women, don't you know that loving this world means being God's enemy? So if anyone chooses to be the world's friend, they become God's enemy.
James 4:5 Do you think the scripture says without reason that the spirit in us longs for what others have?
James 4:6 He gives more kindness. So he says, God opposes the proud, but gives kindness to the humble.
James 4:7 Obey God, then. Stand up against the devil, and he will run away from you.
James 4:8 Come close to God, and He will come close to you. Wash your hands, you sinners, and make your hearts pure, you who are unsure.
James 4:9 Feel sad, cry, and weep: may your laughter become crying, and your happiness become sadness.
James 4:10 Lower yourselves before God, and he will raise you up.
James 4:11 Do not speak badly about each other, friends. Whoever talks badly about a friend and judges them, speaks against the rules and judges the rules. But if you judge the rules, you are not following them but judging them.
James 4:12 There is one lawmaker, who can save and destroy: who are you to judge someone else?
James 4:13 Listen, those who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to this city, stay there for a year, trade, and make a profit":
James 4:14 You don't know what will happen tomorrow. What is your life? It is like a mist that appears for a short while and then disappears.
James 4:15 You should say, "If God wants, we will live and do this or that."
James 4:16 But now you are happy with your bragging: all this kind of happiness is bad.
James 4:17 So if someone knows what is good to do and does not do it, for them it is wrong.

James 5:1 Listen now, you rich people, cry and wail because of the troubles that are going to happen to you.
James 5:2 Your wealth has gone bad, and your clothes have been eaten by moths.
James 5:3 Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be evidence against you and eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up wealth for the last days.
James 5:4 Look, the pay of the workers who harvested your fields, which you unfairly kept from them, is calling out; and their cries have reached God's ears.
James 5:5 You have enjoyed life on Earth and lived recklessly; you have filled your hearts, as if it were a day to kill animals for feasting.
James 5:6 You condemned and killed the righteous person; he did not fight against you.
James 5:7 So, my friends, wait patiently for the Lord to come. Think about farmers who wait for their valuable crops to grow. They wait patiently for the rain in the fall and spring.
James 5:8 Be patient too; make your hearts strong because God's coming is near.
James 5:9 Do not hold grudges against each other, brothers, or you may be judged: see, the judge is right at the door.
James 5:10 Look at the prophets who spoke for God as examples of those who suffered and were patient.
James 5:11 Look, we think those who endure are happy. You have heard about Job's patience, and you know how God's story ended; God is very compassionate and kind.
James 5:12 My friends, don't make promises using the name of heaven or earth or anything else. Just say "yes" when you mean yes, and "no" when you mean no, so you won't be judged.
James 5:13 If any of you are having trouble, pray. If anyone is happy, sing songs of praise.
James 5:14 If anyone among you is sick, they should call for the church leaders to pray over them and anoint them with oil in God's name.
James 5:15 The faithful prayer will heal the sick, God will lift him up, and if he has sinned, he will be forgiven.
James 5:16 Admit your mistakes to each other, and pray for each other, so you can be healed. The powerful and earnest prayer of a good person has great impact.
James 5:17 Elijah was a person with feelings like ours, and he prayed hard for no rain: and it did not rain on the land for three years and six months.
James 5:18 He prayed once more, and the sky sent rain, and the land produced its crops.
James 5:19 Friends, if anyone of you wanders away from the truth and someone brings them back,
James 5:20 Let him understand that one who turns a sinner from the wrong path will save a soul from death and cover many sins.

1 Peter 1:1 Peter, a messenger of Jesus Christ, to the people living far away in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
1 Peter 1:2 Chosen by God the Father who knows everything ahead of time, through being made holy by the Spirit, to obey and to be cleansed by the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be given to you in large amounts.
1 Peter 1:3 Praise be to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, because of his great mercy, has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
1 Peter 1:4 You will receive an inheritance that cannot be destroyed, stained, or fade, which is kept in heaven for you.
1 Peter 1:5 You are protected by God's power through faith for a salvation that will be revealed in the end.
1 Peter 1:6 You are very happy, even though now, for a little while, you may have to be sad because of many tests.
1 Peter 1:7 The test of your faith is much more valuable than gold that can be destroyed, even though it is tested by fire, so that it may result in praise, honor, and glory when Jesus Christ appears.
1 Peter 1:8 Even though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and even though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and are filled with a joy that is so great you cannot describe it, and this joy is glorious.
1 Peter 1:9 Getting the result of your faith, the rescue of your souls.
1 Peter 1:10 The prophets who told about the grace that was to come to you searched carefully, wanting to know about this salvation.
1 Peter 1:11 They wanted to know what time or situation the Spirit of Christ within them was talking about when it predicted Christ's sufferings and the future glory.
1 Peter 1:12 It was shown to them that they were not serving themselves, but us, by telling the messages now given to you by those who shared the good news with you through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—messages even angels long to understand.
1 Peter 1:13 Prepare your mind for action, stay alert, and keep your hope fully on the kindness you will receive when Jesus Christ is revealed.
1 Peter 1:14 As obedient children, do not shape your lives by the desires you had before, when you did not know better.
1 Peter 1:15 But since God who called you is holy, you too should be holy in every aspect of your life.
1 Peter 1:16 It is written, "Be holy, because I am holy."
1 Peter 1:17 If you ask God for help, who judges everyone fairly by their actions, live your time here with respect and caution.
1 Peter 1:18 You know you were not saved with things that can spoil, like silver and gold, from the empty way of life handed down to you from your ancestors.
1 Peter 1:19 With the valuable blood of Christ, like that of a perfect and spotless lamb:
1 Peter 1:20 He was truly chosen before the world was made, but now has been shown for you in these last days.
1 Peter 1:21 Through Jesus, you believe in God who brought him back from death and honored him, so your faith and hope can be in God.
1 Peter 1:22 Since you have made your souls pure by following the truth with the Spirit's help, leading to sincere love for others, make sure you love each other deeply and truly.
1 Peter 1:23 Being born again comes not from perishable seed, but imperishable, through God's word, which lives and lasts forever.
1 Peter 1:24 Everyone is like grass, and all their achievements are like the flowers of the field. The grass dries up, and its flowers fall off.
1 Peter 1:25 God's message lasts forever. And this is the message that is shared with you through the good news.

1 Peter 2:1 So put away all meanness, trickery, pretending, jealousy, and talking about others badly.
1 Peter 2:2 Like new babies, crave pure spiritual milk so you can grow because of it.
1 Peter 2:3 If you have experienced God's kindness.
1 Peter 2:4 Come to Him like you would to a living stone, which people have rejected but which God has chosen and values highly.
1 Peter 2:5 You too, like living stones, are being made into a spiritual temple, a sacred group of priests, to give spiritual offerings that please God through Jesus Christ.
1 Peter 2:6 The scripture says, "Look, I put a very important and chosen cornerstone in Zion. Whoever believes in him will not be embarrassed."
1 Peter 2:7 So for you who believe, he is valuable, but for those who don't obey, the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
1 Peter 2:8 A stumbling block and a rock that makes them fall, even for those who stumble over the message because they do not obey: this is what they were destined for.
1 Peter 2:9 You are a special group, chosen to be kings' priests and a holy nation, different from others; so you can show everyone how great God is, who brought you from darkness into his wonderful light.
1 Peter 2:10 Before, you were not a people, but now you are God's people; before, you did not receive mercy, but now you have received mercy.
1 Peter 2:11 Dear friends, I urge you as outsiders and travelers, to avoid bodily desires, which fight against the soul.
1 Peter 2:12 Live well among non-believers so even if they accuse you of doing wrong, they will see your good deeds and honor God when he examines us.
1 Peter 2:13 Obey all human laws for God's sake, whether they come from the king, who is highest.
1 Peter 2:14 Or to leaders, as to those sent by God to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right.
1 Peter 2:15 God wants you to do good so you can silence the foolish talk of ignorant people.
1 Peter 2:16 As free, but don't use your freedom to hide bad actions, instead live as God's servants.
1 Peter 2:17 Respect everyone. Love your fellow believers. Be in awe of God. Respect the leader.
1 Peter 2:18 Workers, obey your bosses with full respect; not just the kind and fair ones, but also the difficult ones.
1 Peter 2:19 It is good if someone bears pain for doing right because of their conscience toward God, even if they suffer unfairly.
1 Peter 2:20 What good is it if you endure punishment for doing wrong? But if you do right and still suffer for it, and endure it, this pleases God.
1 Peter 2:21 You were called to this because Christ suffered for us, giving us an example to follow his steps.
1 Peter 2:22 He did not sin and no deceit was in his mouth.
1 Peter 2:23 When people insulted him, he did not insult back; when he was hurt, he did not threaten them but trusted in God who judges fairly.
1 Peter 2:24 He carried our sins in his body on the cross so that we, free from sins, can live a good life. By his wounds, you have been healed.
1 Peter 2:25 You were like lost sheep; but now you have come back to the Shepherd and Guardian of your souls.

1 Peter 3:1 Wives, respect your husbands so that even if some do not believe the message, they may be convinced by their wives' way of life without needing words.
1 Peter 3:2 As they see your pure way of life with respect.
1 Peter 3:3 Don't focus on decorating yourself by braiding your hair, wearing gold jewelry, or dressing in fine clothes.
1 Peter 3:4 Let your inner self be gentle and calm, a lasting beauty precious to God.
1 Peter 3:5 In the past, holy women who trusted in God also made themselves beautiful by accepting their husbands' guidance.
1 Peter 3:6 Just like Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord, you are her daughters if you do good and are not frightened by anything scary.
1 Peter 3:7 Husbands, live with your wives wisely. Respect them as the weaker partner, sharing the gift of life together, so nothing will block your prayers.
1 Peter 3:8 Finally, all of you should agree with each other, be kind to one another, love like brothers and sisters, be compassionate, and be polite.
1 Peter 3:9 Do not repay evil with evil, or insults with insults. Instead, give blessings, because you are called to inherit a blessing.
1 Peter 3:10 To enjoy life and have good days, one should keep their tongue from evil and their lips from telling lies.
1 Peter 3:11 Avoid evil and do good; seek peace and follow it.
1 Peter 3:12 God watches over good people, and He listens to their prayers, but He opposes those who do wrong.
1 Peter 3:13 Who would want to hurt you if you are doing good?
1 Peter 3:14 If you suffer for doing right, you are blessed. Don't be scared or upset by their threats.
1 Peter 3:15 Set apart God in your hearts and always be prepared to explain your hope to anyone who asks, doing so gently and respectfully.
1 Peter 3:16 Keep a clear conscience so that those who speak badly of you as wrongdoers may feel ashamed for wrongly criticizing your good behavior as a follower of Christ.
1 Peter 3:17 It is better, if it is God's will, to suffer for doing good than for doing bad.
1 Peter 3:18 Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring us to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive by the Spirit.
1 Peter 3:19 He also went and spoke to the spirits in prison.
1 Peter 3:20 People who did not obey long ago, when God patiently waited during Noah's time while the ark was being built, were saved by water, only a few, that is, eight people.
1 Peter 3:21 This symbol, baptism, now saves us too—not by cleaning our bodies from dirt, but by giving us a clear conscience toward God, because of Jesus Christ's resurrection.
1 Peter 3:22 He has gone to heaven and sits at God's right side, with angels, authorities, and powers under his control.

1 Peter 4:1 Since Christ suffered for us in a human body, prepare yourselves with the same attitude: because anyone who has gone through such suffering is done with sin.
1 Peter 4:2 He should not spend the rest of his life following human desires, but following God's will.
1 Peter 4:3 The time we already lived is enough for us doing what non-believers do, when we followed desires, overdrank, partied, and worshipped idols in terrible ways.
1 Peter 4:4 They find it odd that you don't join them in their wild ways, and they speak badly of you.
1 Peter 4:5 Who must explain their actions to God, who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
1 Peter 4:6 The good news was also told to those who are dead, so they could be judged like living people, but live by God's ways in the spirit.
1 Peter 4:7 Everything is about to end, so be clear-minded and stay alert for prayer.
1 Peter 4:8 Above everything, love each other deeply because love covers many sins.
1 Peter 4:9 Welcome each other into your homes without complaining.
1 Peter 4:10 Each person has been given a gift; use it to help each other, as good caretakers of God's various blessings.
1 Peter 4:11 If someone speaks, they should speak as if speaking God's words; if anyone serves, they should do so with the strength God provides, so that in everything God may be praised through Jesus Christ. To him be the glory and power forever and ever. Amen.
1 Peter 4:12 Dear friends, do not be surprised at the hard test you are facing, as if something unusual is happening to you.
1 Peter 4:13 Be happy because you share in Christ's sufferings, so when his glory is shown, you can be very joyful too.
1 Peter 4:14 If people insult you because of Christ, you are blessed; because the glorious Spirit of God rests on you. They may speak badly of him, but you honor him.
1 Peter 4:15 Don't let any of you suffer for being a murderer, a thief, doing bad things, or interfering in other people's business.
1 Peter 4:16 If anyone suffers because they are a Christian, they should not feel ashamed; instead, they should praise God for it.
1 Peter 4:17 The time has come for God's judgment to start with us, God's people. And if it starts with us, what will happen to those who don't follow God's good news?
1 Peter 4:18 If it's hard for the good person to be saved, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner?
1 Peter 4:19 So those who suffer because it's God's plan should trust God with their lives, as they continue to do good, just like they would trust a reliable maker.

1 Peter 5:1 I urge you, the older leaders among you, as I am also an older leader, a witness of Christ's sufferings, and one who will share in the glory to come.
1 Peter 5:2 Take care of God's flock that is with you, watch over them because you want to, not because you must, and not for money, but because you are eager to.
1 Peter 5:3 Not as bosses over God's people, but as examples to the group.
1 Peter 5:4 When the main Shepherd comes, you will get a crown of glory that never fades.
1 Peter 5:5 Young people, respect those who are older. Everyone should treat each other with respect and be humble, because God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
1 Peter 5:6 So be humble under God's powerful hand, and he will lift you up when the time is right.
1 Peter 5:7 Give all your worries to God, because he cares for you.
1 Peter 5:8 Stay alert and watchful, because your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to eat.
1 Peter 5:9 Stand firm against him by being strong in your faith, knowing that believers all over the world are going through the same kind of suffering.
1 Peter 5:10 God, full of all grace, who has called you to his eternal glory through Christ Jesus, will, after you have suffered for a little while, make you perfect, firm, strong, and steady.
1 Peter 5:11 May he have glory and power forever. Amen.
1 Peter 5:12 Through Silvanus, who I believe is a loyal friend to you, I've written a short letter to encourage you and affirm that you are experiencing God's true kindness.
1 Peter 5:13 The church in Babylon, chosen with you, sends greetings; and so does Mark, my son.
1 Peter 5:14 Say hello to each other with a friendly kiss. May peace be with all of you who belong to Christ Jesus. Amen.

2 Peter 1:1 Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to those who share our valuable faith, given through the goodness of God and Jesus Christ our Savior.
2 Peter 1:2 May grace and peace grow for you by knowing God and Jesus our Lord.
2 Peter 1:3 God's divine power has given us everything we need for life and goodness, through knowing him who called us to glory and excellence.
2 Peter 1:4 God has given us very great and valuable promises, so that through them you can share in God's nature, free from the world's corruption caused by human desires.
2 Peter 1:5 Also, try your best and add goodness to your faith; and to goodness, add knowledge.
2 Peter 1:6 Add self-control to your knowledge; and to self-control, add patience; and to patience, add devotion to God.
2 Peter 1:7 Add to being godly, kindness to others; and to kindness to others, love.
2 Peter 1:8 If these things are in you and grow, they will make sure you are not empty or unproductive in knowing our Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Peter 1:9 But if someone doesn't have these qualities, they are blind, can't see far, and have forgotten they were cleansed from their past sins.
2 Peter 1:10 So, my friends, work hard to confirm your calling and choice, because if you do these things, you will never stumble.
2 Peter 1:11 This way, you will be given a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
2 Peter 1:12 So I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are firm in the truth you have now.
2 Peter 1:13 Yes, I believe it's right, as long as I'm in this body, to remind you and keep you thinking.
2 Peter 1:14 I know that soon I must leave this body, just as Jesus Christ has shown me.
2 Peter 1:15 I will try to make sure that after I die, you can always remember these things.
2 Peter 1:16 We didn't follow cleverly made-up stories when we told you about the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; we saw his greatness with our own eyes.
2 Peter 1:17 He got honor and glory from God the Father when a voice from the magnificent glory said to him, "This is my dear Son, who makes me happy."
2 Peter 1:18 We heard this voice from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.
2 Peter 1:19 We also have a more certain message from the prophets. You do well to pay attention to it, like a light shining in a dark place, until the day breaks and the morning star rises in your hearts.
2 Peter 1:20 Understand this: No prophecy in the Bible comes from someone's own explanation.
2 Peter 1:21 The prophecy did not come long ago by human will, but holy men spoke from God as they were inspired by the Holy Spirit.

2 Peter 2:1 But there were fake prophets among the people, just as there will be fake teachers among you. They will secretly introduce harmful false teachings, even denying God who saved them, and cause quick destruction for themselves.
2 Peter 2:2 Many will follow their harmful ways, and because of them, the way of truth will be badly spoken of.
2 Peter 2:3 Greedy people will use fake words to exploit you. Their punishment, long overdue, won't be delayed, and their destruction is not asleep.
2 Peter 2:4 If God did not spare the angels who sinned but threw them into hell and put them in dark chains to be kept for judgment;
2 Peter 2:5 God did not spare the ancient world, but He saved Noah, the eighth person, who was a preacher of doing right, by bringing a flood on the world of the wicked.
2 Peter 2:6 God turned Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, punishing them as a warning to those who would live wickedly.
2 Peter 2:7 God rescued good man Lot, who was troubled by the evil peoples' dirty behavior.
2 Peter 2:8 The good man lived among them, and he felt troubled every day by the wrong things he saw and heard them do.
2 Peter 2:9 God knows how to save good people from trials and keep the wrongdoers for punishment on the judgment day.
2 Peter 2:10 Mostly those who follow their desires in impure lust and scorn authority are bold and stubborn, not fearing to insult those with honor.
2 Peter 2:11 Even angels, stronger and more powerful, don't bring harsh accusations against others before God.
2 Peter 2:12 These people, like wild animals born to be caught and killed, speak badly about what they don't understand and will completely die in their own corruption.
2 Peter 2:13 They will get the punishment for wrongdoing because they think it's fun to go wild in broad daylight. They are like stains and flaws, enjoying their tricks while they eat with you.
2 Peter 2:14 They have eyes full of cheating and can't stop sinning; they trick weak people and have hearts trained in greed; they are cursed.
2 Peter 2:15 They left the right path and went wrong, following the path of Balaam, son of Beor, who loved getting paid for doing wrong.
2 Peter 2:16 But was corrected for his wrong: the silent donkey speaking with a human voice stopped the prophet's craziness.
2 Peter 2:17 These are like empty wells and clouds blown away by storms; they are headed for the darkest darkness forever.
2 Peter 2:18 When they speak big, empty words, they tempt people with fleshly desires and reckless behavior, those who had barely gotten away from those making mistakes.
2 Peter 2:19 They promise freedom, but they are slaves to corruption. For if something defeats a person, that person is enslaved by it.
2 Peter 2:20 If, after they have escaped the world's corruption by knowing Jesus Christ, they get caught and overcome by it again, their final state is worse than their first.
2 Peter 2:21 It would have been better if they had never known the right way, than to know it and then turn away from the holy command they were given.
2 Peter 2:22 What happened to them is just like the true saying, "A dog goes back to its vomit," and, "A washed pig returns to roll in the mud."

2 Peter 3:1 My dear friends, I am writing to you again to awaken your clean thoughts by helping you remember.
2 Peter 3:2 So you will remember the words spoken before by the holy prophets and the command given by us, the apostles of the Lord and Savior.
2 Peter 3:3 First, know that in the last days, people who mock others will come, following their own desires.
2 Peter 3:4 They ask, "Where is the promise of his coming? For ever since our ancestors died, everything goes on just as it has since the world was created."
2 Peter 3:5 They willingly ignore that long ago, by God's command, the heavens came to be and the earth was formed out of water and by water.
2 Peter 3:6 The world at that time was flooded with water and destroyed.
2 Peter 3:7 The heavens and earth that exist today are maintained by God's command, saved for fire when the time comes for judging and destroying sinful people.
2 Peter 3:8 Dear friends, don't forget this one thing: with God, one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like one day.
2 Peter 3:9 God is not slow to fulfill His promise, as some think of slowness, but is patient with us, not wanting anyone to die, but for everyone to turn from their sins.
2 Peter 3:10 God's day will come like a thief at night. Then the sky will disappear with a loud bang, and the basic parts of the world will dissolve from extreme heat. The earth and everything on it will be burned up.
2 Peter 3:11 Since everything will be destroyed, how should you live? Live a holy and godly life.
2 Peter 3:12 Waiting for and hurrying the arrival of God's day when the skies will burn and vanish and everything will melt from intense heat.
2 Peter 3:13 We expect new heavens and a new earth, as God promised, where goodness lives.
2 Peter 3:14 So, dear friends, since you are looking forward to this, try hard to be found by God in peace, clean, and without fault.
2 Peter 3:15 Understand that our God's patience means salvation, just as our dear brother Paul also wrote to you with the wisdom given to him.
2 Peter 3:16 In all his letters, he talks about these topics. Some ideas are hard to grasp. The uneducated and unsure people distort them, like they do with other parts of the Bible, and this leads to their ruin.
2 Peter 3:17 So, dear friends, since you already know this, be careful not to be led astray by the wrong of wicked people and lose your strong position.
2 Peter 3:18 Keep growing in kindness and in understanding our leader and rescuer, Jesus Christ. May he be honored now and always. Amen.

1 John 1:1 What was there from the start, which we have heard, seen with our own eyes, and touched with our hands, is about the message of life.
1 John 1:2 The life appeared, we have seen it, and we tell you about it. We show you the eternal life that was with God and was shown to us.
1 John 1:3 We tell you what we've seen and heard so you can join us. Our friendship is with God and his Son Jesus Christ.
1 John 1:4 We write these things to you so that your joy can be complete.
1 John 1:5 We heard a message from him and now tell you: God is light, with no darkness at all.
1 John 1:6 If we claim to have a close relationship with God but live in the wrong way, we are lying and not living by the truth.
1 John 1:7 But if we live in the truth, as he is in the truth, we share a bond with each other, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleans us from all sin.
1 John 1:8 If we claim we have no sin, we lie to ourselves, and we don't have the truth.
1 John 1:9 If we admit our sins, God is loyal and fair to forgive us our sins, and to make us clean from all wrongdoing.
1 John 1:10 If we say we haven't sinned, we call God a liar, and his message isn't in us.

1 John 2:1 Dear children, I write this to you so you don't sin. But if anyone does sin, we have someone who speaks to God for us, Jesus Christ the good one.
1 John 2:2 He is the sacrifice for our sins, not only ours but also for the whole world's.
1 John 2:3 We know we know God if we follow his commands.
1 John 2:4 The person who says, "I know God," but doesn't follow his commands is lying, and doesn't have the truth in them.
1 John 2:5 But whoever keeps his word truly has God's love made perfect in them: by this we know we are with him.
1 John 2:6 Whoever says they live in him should also walk just as he did.
1 John 2:7 Friends, I am not writing a new rule to you, but an old rule you've known from the start. This old rule is the message you've heard since the start.
1 John 2:8 I am giving you a new command: what I tell you is true in both him and you. The dark times are over, and now the real light is shining.
1 John 2:9 Anyone who claims to be in the light but hates their brother or sister is still in the dark.
1 John 2:10 The person who loves their brother lives in the light, and there is nothing in them that causes falling.
1 John 2:11 Whoever hates their brother lives in the dark, walks in the dark, and doesn't know where they're going, because the dark has made them blind.
1 John 2:12 I write to you, young ones, because God has forgiven your sins for the sake of His name.
1 John 2:13 I write to you, fathers, because you know the one who is from the start. I write to you, young men, because you have beaten the evil one. I write to you, children, because you know the Father.
1 John 2:14 I wrote to you, fathers, because you know the one from the start. I wrote to you, young men, because you are strong, God's message stays in you, and you have beaten the evil one.
1 John 2:15 Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, God's love is not in them.
1 John 2:16 Everything in the world, the cravings of the body, the desires of the eyes, and life's arrogance, does not come from God but from the world.
1 John 2:17 The world ends, and its desires too: but the person who does what God wants lives forever.
1 John 2:18 Little children, this is the final hour. You have heard that the enemy of Christ is coming, and now many such enemies are already here. This shows us that it is truly the final hour.
1 John 2:19 They left us because they were not truly with us. If they were, they would have stayed. Their leaving showed they weren't really part of us.
1 John 2:20 You have a special gift from the Holy One, and you know everything.
1 John 2:21 I have written to you not because you don't know the truth, but because you do know it and that no lie comes from the truth.
1 John 2:22 Who lies except the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? He is against Christ, who denies both the Father and the Son.
1 John 2:23 Anyone who denies the Son does not have God; but whoever accepts the Son has God too.
1 John 2:24 Keep what you've heard from the start in you. If what you've heard from the start stays in you, you will also stay in the Son and in God.
1 John 2:25 This is the promise he made to us: eternal life.
1 John 2:26 I have written these things to you about those who mislead you.
1 John 2:27 The special blessing you got from God stays in you, and you don't need anyone to teach you. That very blessing teaches you everything, and it's true, not a lie. Just as it has taught you, stay close to God.
1 John 2:28 And now, little children, stay close to him; so that when he comes, we can be brave and not feel embarrassed in front of him.
1 John 2:29 If you know that God is good, you know that anyone who does good things is God's child.

1 John 3:1 Look at how much love God has given us, so we can be called God's children. That's why the world doesn't recognize us, because it didn't recognize him.
1 John 3:2 Friends, now we are children of God, and it's not yet clear what we will become. But we know that when he comes, we will be like him because we will see him as he truly is.
1 John 3:3 Everyone who has this hope in him makes himself clean, just as God is clean.
1 John 3:4 Anyone who sins also breaks the law, because sin is breaking the law.
1 John 3:5 You know he appeared to remove our sins, and he has no sin.
1 John 3:6 Anyone who stays true to God does not sin; anyone who sins has not seen or known God.
1 John 3:7 Kids, don't let anyone trick you: if someone does what is right, they are good, just like God is good.
1 John 3:8 Anyone who sins belongs to the devil because the devil has been sinning from the start. The Son of God came to destroy the devil's work.
1 John 3:9 Anyone born of God does not keep on sinning because God's nature stays in them; they can't keep sinning because they are born of God.
1 John 3:10 This shows who are God's children and who are the devil's children: anyone who does not act righteously is not from God, nor is the one who does not love their brother.
1 John 3:11 This is the message you have heard from the start: we should love each other.
1 John 3:12 Unlike Cain, who belonged to the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his actions were bad, and his brother's were good.
1 John 3:13 Do not be surprised, my friends, if the world hates you.
1 John 3:14 We understand that we have moved from death to life because we love our fellow believers. Whoever does not love their sibling remains in death.
1 John 3:15 Anyone who hates their brother or sister is a killer, and you know that no killer has eternal life in them.
1 John 3:16 We understand God's love because He gave up His life for us, and we should be willing to give up our lives for others.
1 John 3:17 If someone has what they need in this world and sees their brother in need but does not care for him, how can God's love be in that person?
1 John 3:18 My dear children, let's not love just with words or speech, but with actions and truth.
1 John 3:19 We know we belong to the truth, and we can calm our hearts before God.
1 John 3:20 If we feel guilty, God is bigger than our feelings and knows everything.
1 John 3:21 Dear friends, if we don't feel guilty, we have trust in God.
1 John 3:22 Whatever we ask for, we get from God because we follow his commands and do what makes him happy.
1 John 3:23 This is God's command: we must believe in his Son, Jesus Christ, and love each other as he told us to.
1 John 3:24 Whoever follows his commands lives in God, and God in him. This is how we know God remains in us: by the Spirit he gave us.

1 John 4:1 Dear friends, do not believe all spirits, but test the spirits to see if they are from God, for many false prophets have spread throughout the world.
1 John 4:2 You know God's Spirit if it says Jesus Christ came as a human.
1 John 4:3 Any spirit that does not admit Jesus Christ has come as a human is not from God. This is the spirit of the enemy of Christ you have heard about, which is already in the world.
1 John 4:4 You belong to God, little children, and have defeated them: because the one in you is greater than the one in the world.
1 John 4:5 They belong to the world, so they talk about worldly things, and the world listens to them.
1 John 4:6 We belong to God: anyone who knows God listens to us; anyone who does not belong to God does not listen to us. This is how we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of falsehood.
1 John 4:7 Dear friends, let's love each other, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves is God's child and understands God.
1 John 4:8 Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
1 John 4:9 God showed his love for us by sending his one and only Son into the world so we could have life through him.
1 John 4:10 Love is this: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the sacrifice for our sins.
1 John 4:11 Dear friends, if God loved us so much, we should also love each other.
1 John 4:12 No one has ever seen God. If we love each other, God lives in us and his love becomes complete in us.
1 John 4:13 We know we live in God and God lives in us because he has given us his Spirit.
1 John 4:14 We have seen and tell others that God sent his Son to save the world.
1 John 4:15 Anyone who says Jesus is the Son of God lives with God, and God lives with him.
1 John 4:16 We know and trust God's love for us. God is love; anyone living in love lives in God, and God lives in them.
1 John 4:17 Our love is made complete by this, so that we can be confident on judgment day: because we are like him in this world.
1 John 4:18 Love has no fear; true love gets rid of fear because fear brings pain. Someone who is afraid doesn't have complete love.
1 John 4:19 We love God because God loved us first.
1 John 4:20 If someone says, "I love God," but hates his brother, he is lying. If he doesn't love his brother who he can see, how can he love God who he cannot see?
1 John 4:21 We have this rule from God: Anyone who loves God should love their brother too.
